body:
## Context

This repo writes logs into the same Grafana Cloud Loki tenant as `opnsense-exporter` and
`graph2otel`. That repo has five promoted index labels; this one has **none**, and cannot have
any as currently built. This issue records why, and what it would cost if that is ever worth
changing. **It is reference, not queued work** — the honest current answer is probably that it is
not worth it.

The shared naming contract lives at
<https://github.com/rknightion/opnsense-exporter/blob/main/docs/otlp-attribute-contract.md>.

## Why nothing here can be promoted today

Loki's `otlp_config` has an `index_label` action **only** under `resource_attributes`.
`scope_attributes` and `log_attributes` accept `structured_metadata` and `drop`, and nothing else.
So a log attribute can never become an index label, whatever the tenant config says.

This exporter's `buildResource()` in `internal/telemetry/provider.go` sets `service.name`, an
optional `service.version`, `service.instance.id`, and the `WithTelemetrySDK`/`WithOS`/`WithProcess*`
detectors. **No custom attribute reaches the resource.** Every domain dimension is set on the
record, so all of it arrives as structured metadata — queryable with `|`, never as a stream
selector.

Nothing is broken by this. Structured metadata is exactly where a non-promoted attribute would land
anyway; the only cost is query scan.

## What promotion would take

Not a rename. An OTLP resource binds to a `LoggerProvider`, not to a record, so **N distinct values
of a dimension means N `LoggerProvider`s**. `opnsense-exporter`'s `internal/logship/sink_otlp.go` is
what that looks like in practice: a provider map keyed on a resource key, one shared exporter so
partitioning costs no extra connections, deterministic per-partition flush ordering, a
`maxLogResources` cap, and a degrade path that drops the custom attributes once the cap is hit —
which had to be raised from 64 to 256 there, and where overshooting silently destroys the labels
that already work.

That is materially more than a config change, and it buys query scan only. Loki bills on volume;
promotion does not reduce ingest cost at all.

## Naming, if it ever happens

Per the contract: namespace under an emitter prefix, never bare unnamespaced names, never squat a
semconv namespace with a foreign meaning, and use a genuine semconv name where the meaning actually
matches. Dimensions stay emitter-specific rather than shared — a unified label whose values mean
different things per exporter leaves `service.name` as the only disambiguator, which is what you
already had.

## The slot question, settled

An earlier framing held that the three exporters compete for a tenant-wide pool of ~15 promotion
slots, and that each one namespacing its own dimensions would exhaust it. **That was wrong.** The 15
is `max_label_names_per_series` — the maximum label names on a *single stream*, enforced by the
distributor at ingest. A stream from this exporter never carries an `opnsense_*` label, so the
pools were never shared and each exporter independently gets its own 15.

The genuinely shared resource is the tenant's promoted-attribute *list*, capped well above what
three exporters need. Adding entries to it is additive and cannot affect another exporter's streams,
but it is one list, so edits are coordinated and must be GET-merge-PUT rather than a blind partial
write.

## If this is ever picked up

- [ ] Decide which dimensions are worth a stream selector rather than a `|` filter, from real query
      patterns rather than in the abstract
- [ ] Check the distinct-value count of each — a `LoggerProvider` per combination is the cost
- [ ] Hoist onto the resource under a `<emitter>.*` namespace, following the `sink_otlp.go` pattern
      including the cap and the degrade path
- [ ] Add the dotted attribute names to the tenant `otlp_config` list, GET-merge-PUT
- [ ] Verify with `gcx datasources loki series` — presence there is proof of promotion, since
      structured metadata cannot appear in `series` output

Filed from rknightion/opnsense-exporter#477.

comments.body:
## Recorded in `docs/signals.md` (`0811619`) — and two claims in this issue's body did not survive contact with the code

This landed as a new reference section under *"Querying the logs in Loki"*: **"Why no log attribute can ever be promoted, and what promotion would cost"**. The core constraint is recorded exactly as filed — Loki's `otlp_config` exposes the `index_label` action only under `resource_attributes`, so `event_name`, `ingest_transport` and `tenant_id` can never become stream labels whatever the tenant config says.

Three corrections, made because this issue was filed from `rknightion/opnsense-exporter#477` and its body describes **that** repo:

**1. "No custom attribute reaches the resource" is not true here.** `graph2otel.event_domain` has been on the logs resource since `3cbd879` (#402) — one `sdklog.LoggerProvider` per domain, all sharing a single OTLP exporter. So graph2otel already has exactly one promotion-capable attribute, and the "what promotion would take" section describes machinery this repo has already built rather than hypothetical work.

**2. `buildResource()` does not set `service.instance.id`.** It sets `service.name`, an optional `service.version`, and the `WithTelemetrySDK`/`WithOS`/`WithHost`/`WithProcess*` detectors. Checked against `internal/telemetry/provider.go` rather than copied across.

**3. The slot correction was the valuable part, and this page was carrying the wrong version.** `docs/signals.md` said the promotion slots are *"shared with other exporters pushing to the same tenant"*. Replaced with the settled finding: the 15 is `max_label_names_per_series`, the maximum label names on a **single stream**, enforced by the distributor at ingest. A graph2otel stream never carries an `opnsense_*` label, so the budgets were never shared. The genuinely shared resource is the tenant's promoted-attribute *list*, capped well above what three exporters need — additive, but one list, so edits are GET-merge-PUT.

The same wrong claim was in #402's body and has been struck through there.

### Live state, checked rather than assumed

A read-only `series` query against the `cloud` stack — the only test that proves promotion, since structured metadata cannot appear in `series` output:

```
{service_name="graph2otel"} -> {"service_name":"graph2otel"}
                               {"service_name":"graph2otel","__stream_shard__":"0"}
                               {"service_name":"graph2otel","__stream_shard__":"1"}
                               {"service_name":"graph2otel","__time_shard__":"…"}
```

`graph2otel.event_domain` is **not** promoted and `__stream_shard__` is still present, so #402's final acceptance criterion remains open and remains `needs-rob`. Recorded on that issue too.

Closing: this issue's purpose was to be the record, and the record now lives in the docs where a future reader will actually meet it.

title: docs: record why no log attribute here can be promoted to a Loki index label

body:
## Symptom

The **`coverage (Codacy)`** job of CI failed on `b4fcaec`:

```
FAIL	github.com/rknightion/graph2otel/internal/annotations	600.010s
make: *** [Makefile:275: coverage] Error 1
```

`600.010s` is the default `go test` package timeout, so the package's test binary **hung** rather than failing an assertion. Every other job in that run passed, including `build / vet / test` (which runs `-race`) and `Grafana assets + generated docs`. The required `ci-success` check **passed** — the Makefile documents this job as non-gating — so `main` is not blocked. That is why this is a separate issue rather than a revert.

## What has already been ruled out

- **Not reproducible locally.** `go test -covermode=atomic -coverprofile=... ./internal/annotations/` passes in **1.4s**, and `-count=6` passes in 2.4s. `go test -race ./...` passes. `make check` exits 0.
- **Not a real network call.** `testConfig()` sets `URL = "https://grafana.example.com"`, which looks like a live-egress hazard, but every `Start()` call in the tests overrides it with an `httptest` server URL. The one exception (`TestStartIsACleanNoOpWhenUnconfigured`) uses an empty URL and returns before any client is built. The HTTP client also carries `Timeout: cfg.Timeout` (10s by default), so a blackholed connection should bound at 10s, not 600s.
- **Not `Close` on an unstarted Annotator.** `Close` blocks on `<-a.workerDone`, which would deadlock if `run` never launched — but `New` returns `nil, err` when preflight fails, so no caller can reach `Close` in that state.

## Where to look next

The package runs one worker goroutine (`Annotator.run`) with a 1s ticker, a bounded queue, and a `Close` that cancels, waits on `workerDone`, then **drains the queue calling `write` with the caller's ctx**. Candidates, in rough order:

1. **`Close`'s drain loop.** It calls `a.write(ctx, …)` for every queued annotation using the ctx passed to `Close`, *after* the internal ctx was cancelled. If a test's `httptest` server is already closed by a `defer` that ran first, each drained annotation performs an HTTP request against a dead listener. Should fail fast, but worth proving rather than assuming.
2. **A goroutine leak across tests** — the worker survives its parent ctx by design (`context.WithoutCancel`), so a test that never calls `Close` leaves a live goroutine with a 1s ticker. Under coverage instrumentation on a loaded runner, many of those could interact badly.
3. **Coverage instrumentation timing.** `-covermode=atomic` slows every counter increment; a test that assumes a tick or a bounded wait completes quickly may not. `TestPublishNeverBlocksACollectorGoroutine` has a 10s bound; nothing else has an explicit deadline.

## How to get the actual answer cheaply

The hang panics with a full goroutine dump at the timeout, and that dump names the blocked line. It is in the CI log for run [30301556020](https://github.com/rknightion/graph2otel/actions/runs/30301556020) — **read that dump first** rather than re-deriving from the source. If the re-run passes, it is a flake and the dump is still the only real evidence available, so capture it before it ages out.

Locally, `go test -covermode=atomic -count=20 -timeout 60s ./internal/annotations/` plus `-race` under CPU contention (`GOMAXPROCS=2`) is the closest approximation of the runner.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The goroutine dump from the failing run is read and the blocked line named, or the failure is demonstrated to be a flake with the dump recorded here either way.
- [ ] Any test that leaves a worker goroutine running calls `Close`, or the leak is shown to be harmless with a reason.
- [ ] `go test -covermode=atomic -count=20 ./internal/annotations/` passes under CPU contention.
- [ ] If `Close`'s drain can block, it gets a bounded context rather than the caller's.

## Context

`internal/annotations` is new in `186b981` (#400, the opt-in Grafana annotation writer). It is opt-in and inert unless `grafana_annotations.url` is set, so **no shipped deployment runs this code by default** — the blast radius of the underlying defect, if there is one, is limited to deployments that have switched annotations on.

comments.body:
## Re-run of the same SHA passed — this is a FLAKE, not a hard failure

Re-ran the failed job on the unchanged commit `b4fcaec`: [run 30301556020](https://github.com/rknightion/graph2otel/actions/runs/30301556020) is now **success**, including `coverage (Codacy)`. So `main` is fully green on all eight workflows and nothing is blocked.

That downgrades the urgency but **not** the issue. A test binary that hangs for the full 10 minutes once is a real defect that happened to not happen the second time — it is a timing-dependent block, not a wrong assertion, and the same conditions will recur on a loaded runner. Treating an intermittent 10-minute hang as "passed on retry" is how a genuine goroutine-lifetime bug gets normalised.

The goroutine dump from the **first** attempt remains the only concrete evidence and is the cheapest path to the answer. Read it before re-deriving anything from the source.

Priority: low, because the package is opt-in and inert unless `grafana_annotations.url` is set, so no default deployment runs it.

## Root cause: a teardown deadlock in the test, not in the publisher. Fixed in `31a30ec`.

### The dump, read from attempt 1

Attempt 1's log is still retrievable (`gh api repos/rknightion/graph2otel/actions/runs/30301556020/attempts/1/logs`). The blocked line is the test's own:

```
goroutine 99 [sync.WaitGroup.Wait]:
net/http/httptest.(*Server).Close(0x2a2b5d8120e0)
	.../net/http/httptest/server.go:279
github.com/rknightion/graph2otel/internal/annotations.TestPublishNeverBlocksACollectorGoroutine(...)
	.../internal/annotations/annotations_test.go:940      <-- defer srv.Close()

goroutine 41 [chan receive]:
...TestPublishNeverBlocksACollectorGoroutine.func1(...)
	.../internal/annotations/annotations_test.go:906      <-- the handler, parked on <-stall
```

`httptest.Server.Close` waits for outstanding requests. The handler was parked on `<-stall`, and `close(stall)` was registered as the **first** defer, so it ran **last** — behind the wait that only it could release. Nothing in the publisher was blocked: `Annotator.run` was idle in its select (goroutine 104), and `Close` had not been reached.

None of the three candidates in the body was it. The drain, the leaked worker and coverage timing were all innocent.

### Why it was intermittent

The deadlock only fires if the worker reached the handler before the test body returned. The worker dequeues immediately (`case annotation := <-a.queue`), but the test body finishes microseconds after the `Publish` loop, so locally the worker usually lost that race — the server had no in-flight request and `Close` returned at once. Under `-covermode=atomic` on a loaded runner the 1000-iteration `Publish` loop is slow enough that the worker reliably wins. Same mechanism, opposite outcome, same SHA.

That race also means the test **was not testing what it says**: most runs never published anything against a stalled destination.

### Reproduced deterministically before fixing

Making the handler signal that it had parked, and waiting for that signal before the `Publish` loop, turned the flake into a hard hang locally with a stack identical to CI's:

```
httptest.Server blocked in Close after 5 seconds, waiting for connections:
  *net.TCPConn ... in state active
panic: test timed out after 30s
```

### What changed

- The handler now closes a `stalled` channel on its first stalling request and the test waits for it, so the worker is genuinely parked inside an HTTP call before `Publish` is measured.
- Teardown moved to `t.Cleanup`, registered so it unwinds `close(stall)` -> `a.Close` -> `srv.Close`. Comment on the site says why the order is load-bearing.
- **Separate real defect, found while checking acceptance criterion 4:** `Close`'s drain was documented as "bounded by ctx", but `main.go:301` closes with `context.Background()`. A stalled Grafana therefore cost one request timeout per queued annotation — worst case 512 x 10s, over an hour of shutdown. `Close` now derives its own deadline (one write's budget for the whole drain, caller's ctx still wins if it is shorter). New test `TestCloseDrainIsBoundedWhenGrafanaStalls` was watched failing at 2.01s against the old code first.

### Acceptance criteria

- [x] Goroutine dump read; blocked line named (`annotations_test.go:940`, `httptest.Server.Close`).
- [x] No test leaves a worker running without `Close` — audited every `Start` call site in `internal/annotations` and `cmd/graph2otel`; `signalgate_test.go` already unwinds in the correct order, and the two `Start` calls without a `Close` return `nil` (unconfigured) or an error.
- [x] `GOMAXPROCS=2 go test -covermode=atomic -count=20 ./internal/annotations/` -> `ok, 7.579s, coverage 87.0%`.
- [x] Drain bounded, by `Close` rather than by the caller.
- [x] `make check` exit 0.

body:
## Problem

All graph2otel logs land in **one Loki stream**, and that stream is hot enough that Loki is auto-sharding it: live streams for `{service_name="graph2otel"}` carry `__stream_shard__` with values `0` and `1`. Stream sharding is a per-stream ingest-rate response, so this is not cosmetic — the single stream is at a limit.

There is no bounded resource attribute to split it on. Every dimension worth selecting on (`event_name`, `ingest_transport`, `tenant_id`) is a **log-record** attribute and therefore lands in structured metadata, which can never become an index label.

## The constraint (verified, not assumed)

Loki's `index_label` action exists **only** under `otlp_config.resource_attributes`. `log_attributes` accepts `structured_metadata` or `drop` and nothing else. So promoting an attribute to a stream label requires it to be on the **OTLP resource** first.

graph2otel's logs resource (`internal/telemetry/provider.go` `buildResource`) currently carries only `service.*` identity plus the SDK/OS/host/process detectors. Nothing domain-specific.

## Measured evidence

Live `grafanacloud-logs`, 2026-07-27:

| fact | value |
|---|---|
| volume | 97,430 lines / 5.9 MB per 6h (~23 MB/day) |
| mean body | 86 B |
| live streams | 1 logical, split into 2 by `__stream_shard__` |
| structured-metadata keys | **266** distinct across a 800-line sample |
| `event_name` distinct (6h) | **73** |
| `ingest_transport` distinct | 2 (`blob`, `graph`) |
| `detected_level` distinct | 5 |
| `tenant_id` distinct | 1 |

`event_name` at 73 values over 6h is **too many** to promote directly: it would mint ~73 streams for 23 MB/day, i.e. tiny streams with poor chunk utilisation, and the value set grows as collectors are added.

## Proposed change

Add a **coarse, closed, code-defined** `graph2otel.event_domain` resource attribute — the domain prefix of the event name (`defender`, `entra`, `intune`, `m365`, `mdca`, `purview`, …, ~6–8 values), derived in code from the same constant that produces `event_name`. Hoist it onto the logs resource so it is promotable; leave `event_name` where it is, as structured metadata.

Rationale for a derived prefix rather than the raw name: it splits the hot stream by roughly the axis an investigation starts from, stays a closed set that only changes when a collector family is added, and keeps the stream count in single digits at this volume.

Expected result: **~6–8 streams** instead of 1 sharded one, +1 tenant label slot.

## Scope

- Derive `event_domain` from the existing event-name constants; do not parse strings at emit time per record if a table lookup will do.
- Add it to the **logs** resource only. It must not reach the metrics resource — that would put `event_domain` on every series (see the `service.version` reasoning already in `buildResource`).
- Keep `event_name` as structured metadata; this is additive, no query breaks.
- Bound it: a test must assert the domain set is closed and derived from the same source as `event_name`, so a new collector cannot introduce an unbounded value.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `graph2otel.event_domain` is on the logs resource, absent from the metrics resource
- [ ] The value set is closed, code-defined, and asserted by a test against the event-name catalogue
- [ ] `event_name` remains available as structured metadata (no query regressions)
- [ ] Docs record that promoting it to an index label is a tenant-side opt-in that costs the exporter nothing when not promoted
- [ ] Measured after the tenant promotion: stream count for `{service_name="graph2otel"}` is single-digit and `__stream_shard__` is gone

## Maintainer-only follow-up (`needs-rob`)

The promotion itself is a **tenant** change in Grafana Cloud (Logs → OTLP label promotion), not a repo change. Current populated promotions on that tenant: `service_name`, `service_instance_id`, `opnsense_source`, `opnsense_subsystem`, `opnsense_action`.

> **CORRECTION 2026-07-28 (#404).** ~~The 15 promotion slots are shared across the whole Loki tenant — `opnsense-exporter`, `tailscale2otel` and `graph2otel` all sit in it.~~ **That was WRONG.** The 15 is `max_label_names_per_series` — the maximum label names on a **single stream**, enforced by the distributor at ingest. A graph2otel stream never carries an `opnsense_*` label, so the budgets were never shared and each exporter independently gets its own. The genuinely shared resource is the tenant's promoted-attribute *list*, capped well above what three exporters need; edits to it are additive but must be GET-merge-PUT. Recorded in `docs/signals.md`.

## Context

Filed from a cross-project Loki label/promotion assessment covering all three OTLP senders on the `m7kni` tenant. graph2otel is 0.4% of tenant log volume (opnsense-exporter is 98.7%), so this is a query-ergonomics and stream-health change, not a cost change. Promotion does not reduce ingest billing — volume does.

~~Not started. Filed for scheduling only.~~ **Superseded 2026-07-28:** the code half shipped in `3cbd879` — see the comments. Only the tenant-side promotion remains, and it is `needs-rob`.

comments.body:
## Blocker found before implementation: a resource attribute cannot vary per log record

The proposal is "derive `graph2otel.event_domain` from the event name and hoist it onto the logs resource". That is not implementable as written, and the reason is structural rather than a detail of how graph2otel is wired.

**In the OTEL Go SDK, the resource belongs to the `LoggerProvider`, not to the record.** Verified against the pinned SDK (`go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/log` v0.20.0, `go doc`):

```
func WithResource(res *resource.Resource) LoggerProviderOption
    WithResource associates a Resource with a LoggerProvider. This Resource
    represents the entity producing telemetry and is associated with all Loggers
    the LoggerProvider will create.
```

`sdklog.Record` exposes `Resource() *resource.Resource` — a getter with **no corresponding setter**. Every other field on `Record` has a `SetX`; resource does not, because it is stamped from the provider that created the logger.

graph2otel builds exactly one (`internal/telemetry/provider.go:273`):

```go
lp := sdklog.NewLoggerProvider(
    sdklog.WithResource(logRes),
    sdklog.WithProcessor(sdklog.NewBatchProcessor(logExp)),
)
```

So every log record this process emits necessarily carries the same resource. `event_domain` varies per record by definition — that is the whole point of it — so it cannot live there without changing the structure that produces records. The issue's own analysis is right that Loki will only promote a **resource** attribute; the gap is that it then assumes the exporter can put a per-record value there, and it cannot.

Everything else in the issue stands: the measured stream state, the 73-distinct `event_name` count, the reasoning for a coarse ~6-8 value domain rather than the raw event name, and the metrics-resource exclusion. Only the mechanism is wrong.

## Three ways to actually get there, with their real costs

**A. One `LoggerProvider` per event domain.** Six to eight providers, each `WithResource(base + event_domain=<d>)`, each with its own `BatchProcessor`, all sharing the one exporter. The emitter routes to a provider by the domain it already derives.

Honest cost: each `BatchProcessor` carries its own queue (SDK default 2048 records), so the worst-case buffered set multiplies by the number of domains — order 16k records instead of 2k. camden runs `mem_limit: 256m` with `GOMEMLIMIT=230MiB`, so queue sizes would need lowering in step, and per-domain batching means smaller, more frequent export payloads. It also means shutdown must flush N processors, and the delivery/degraded self-obs wrapper currently assumes one.

**B. Group by attribute inside the forked OTLP/HTTP log exporter.** `third_party/otlploghttp` is already a maintained fork with a provenance gate. The transform step could partition a batch into multiple `ResourceLogs`, promoting a chosen log attribute onto each synthesized resource. One process, one provider, one queue, no memory multiplication.

Honest cost: it deepens a fork that currently exists to track upstream closely, and it puts a graph2otel-specific behaviour inside a vendored OTLP exporter — exactly the kind of thing that makes the next upstream rebase expensive. It is also a wire-shape change invisible from the Go API, so it needs its own golden test.

**C. Do nothing in the exporter; split at the collector.** If an Alloy/OTel Collector hop is ever in front of Loki, a transform processor can lift a log attribute onto the resource there, which is the conventional place for exactly this. Costs the exporter nothing.

Honest cost: graph2otel currently pushes straight to Grafana Cloud, so this is only real if a collector hop is wanted for other reasons. It also moves a graph2otel property into operator-side config, which is the opposite of the "closed set asserted by a test" property the issue asks for.

## Recommendation and what I have not done

**A** is the one I would build: it stays inside the SDK's model, keeps the closed-set test the issue asks for, and its cost is a tunable queue size rather than a fork rebase. **B** is faster to ship and worse to own. **C** is not a repo change at all.

This is a design fork with a real memory tradeoff on the live deployment, so I have not picked one. **`needs-rob`** — same label the tenant-side promotion step already carries, now for two reasons rather than one.

No code written, no file changed. The acceptance criteria as worded ("`graph2otel.event_domain` is on the logs resource") remain correct for option A and would need rewording for B.

## Decision received 2026-07-28 — Option A, one LoggerProvider per event domain

The maintainer chose **Option A** from the three routes recorded in the previous comment.

### What that means concretely

Build 6-8 `sdklog.LoggerProvider`s, one per event domain, each constructed `WithResource(base + graph2otel.event_domain=<domain>)`, each with its own `BatchProcessor`, all sharing the single OTLP exporter. The emitter routes a record to a provider by the domain it already derives from the event name. This stays inside the SDK's model, which is what makes the closed-set test this issue asks for possible.

**Rejected:** Option B (partitioning inside the forked `third_party/otlploghttp` exporter) — faster to ship, worse to own, and it would put graph2otel-specific behaviour inside a vendored exporter that exists to track upstream closely. Option C (splitting at a collector hop) — not a repo change and there is no collector hop today.

### The cost that must be handled in the implementation, not discovered afterwards

Each `BatchProcessor` carries its own queue (SDK default 2048 records), so worst-case buffered records multiply by the number of domains — order 16k instead of 2k. **camden runs `mem_limit: 256m` with `GOMEMLIMIT=230MiB`**, so queue sizes must come down in step with the provider count, and that sizing is part of the work rather than a follow-up. Shutdown must also flush every provider, and the delivery/degraded self-obs wrapper currently assumes one.

### Acceptance criteria stand as written

`graph2otel.event_domain` on the logs resource and absent from the metrics resource; the value set closed, code-defined and asserted against the event-name catalogue; `event_name` unchanged as structured metadata.

The final criterion — measuring that stream count is single-digit and `__stream_shard__` is gone — still requires the **tenant-side promotion**, which is a Grafana Cloud change the maintainer makes, not a repo change. The 15 promotion slots are shared across opnsense-exporter, tailscale2otel and graph2otel. So this issue can be built and shipped to the point of emitting the attribute, then waits on `needs-rob` for that last verification.

## Option A built and shipped in `3cbd879` — one item left, and it is yours

`graph2otel.event_domain` is now on the logs resource, derived from the first segment of the event name and carried by one `sdklog.LoggerProvider` per domain, all sharing the single OTLP exporter. Eight values: `defender`, `entra`, `graph2otel`, `intune`, `m365`, `mdca`, `purview`, plus an `other` fallback.

### Acceptance

- [x] `graph2otel.event_domain` on the logs resource
- [x] absent from the metrics resource — pinned by its own test, since a resource attribute participates in metric series identity and splitting it there would fork every self-obs series for no query benefit (#82)
- [x] the value set closed and code-defined, asserted against the event-name catalogue — `TestEventDomainsIsClosedAndCoversTheCatalogue` reads `spec/signal-catalog.json` and fails if a collector introduces a namespace with no provider, or if a catalogued event routes to `other`
- [x] `event_name` unchanged as structured metadata
- [ ] stream count single-digit and `__stream_shard__` gone — **needs the tenant-side promotion, which is yours to make.** Until `graph2otel.event_domain` is in the tenant's Loki structured-metadata promotion list it is queryable as an ordinary attribute and is not a stream label. The 15 slots are shared with opnsense-exporter and tailscale2otel.

### Two things found while building it that were not in the plan

**The domain derivation is deliberately identical to `internal/signalcatalog`'s `domainOf`, and that is load-bearing rather than tidiness.** The catalogue is the artifact the closed-set test checks the code against. Two separate derivations would let a record be *routed* to one domain while being *catalogued* under another — which is worse than not splitting at all, because the split would then be quietly wrong instead of absent. If either side is ever changed, change both.

**Sharing one exporter across N providers is a shutdown bug, not just a resource-saving.** `sdklog.BatchProcessor.Shutdown` flushes its queue and then shuts down the exporter it was given. With eight processors behind one exporter, the first provider to shut down closed it, and everything still queued in the other seven was handed to a closed exporter and discarded. It reproduces as an empty export on a *clean* shutdown with nothing erroring — the least visible failure there is. The exporter is now wrapped so per-provider shutdown is inert, and `Provider.Shutdown` closes it once, last, after every provider has drained.

That bug initially passed the new tests, because the fake exporter accepted exports after close. The fake now refuses them and counts them, and the sabotage check confirms it fails without the fix. A fake that cannot fail the way production fails is not a test.

### The memory cost, handled rather than deferred

Per-processor queue depth is set to **512**, not the SDK default 2048. Eight processors at the default would take the worst-case buffered set from ~2k records to ~16k, and that worst case is exactly what an OTLP outage produces — every queue filling at once while nothing drains — under camden's `mem_limit: 256m` / `GOMEMLIMIT=230MiB`. 512 x 8 is ~4k worst case, twice today's total capacity rather than eight times it; at this project's largest record (a service-health post, truncated at 8 KiB) the absolute ceiling is ~32 MiB.

The trade, stated plainly: the hottest domain can now buffer 512 rather than the 2048 it could previously claim from the shared queue. That only bites during an export stall. If camden ever shows log records dropping under stall, that constant is the first knob to raise, and it should be raised for all domains together.

## Tenant-side promotion requested — 2026-07-29, waiting on Grafana engineering

Maintainer: the promotion ticket has been raised with Grafana and is awaiting action by their engineering side. So the last acceptance box is **blocked on a third party**, not on the maintainer and not on this repo.

Nothing to do here in the meantime. The code half (`3cbd879`) is complete and inert until promotion lands — `graph2otel.event_domain` is emitted on the logs resource today and is queryable as an ordinary attribute, so there is no regression and no partial state to babysit.

**The one check worth re-running once Grafana confirms** (structured metadata cannot appear in `series` output, so this is the only test that proves promotion actually took):

```
series {service_name="graph2otel"}
```

Ticked when that returns per-domain streams carrying `graph2otel_event_domain` and `__stream_shard__` is gone. Until then, unchanged from the 2026-07-28 live check: `service_name` is the only real label and the single stream is still being auto-sharded.

## Closed 2026-08-04 by `82d0f92` — the repo half is done and the rest is not ours

Maintainer decision: close rather than hold open on a third party. The last acceptance box is **not ticked and is not being claimed** — it is recorded below with the exact command that proves it, and the re-open condition is that command's output changing.

### State, re-measured today

```
gcx --context m7kni logs series --match '{service_name="graph2otel"}' -o json
  -> {"service_name":"graph2otel"}
     {"service_name":"graph2otel","__stream_shard__":"0"}
     {"service_name":"graph2otel","__stream_shard__":"1"}
```

Unchanged from the 2026-07-28 reading. `graph2otel_event_domain` is **not** a stream label; `service_name` is the only real one and the single hot stream is still being auto-sharded. The promotion request has sat with Grafana engineering since 2026-07-29.

The attribute itself is confirmed emitting — it appears as `graph2otel_event_domain` in the structured metadata of live records, so `3cbd879` works and is simply inert until promotion. No regression, no partial state.

### Why the check does not die with the issue

Closing an issue whose last acceptance item is unverified is how a check quietly stops being run. So it was moved somewhere permanent first: `docs/signals.md` now carries the command, what promoted output looks like, and the dated negative — `82d0f92`.

**The thing worth preserving is why `series` is the only valid test.** Structured metadata can never appear in `series` output, so a `series` read is what distinguishes a promoted resource attribute from an ordinary one. A `logs query` returns `graph2otel_event_domain` whether or not promotion has happened, which makes it a test that always passes and proves nothing.

### Re-open condition

`gcx --context m7kni logs series --match '{service_name="graph2otel"}'` returns per-domain streams carrying `graph2otel_event_domain` and no `__stream_shard__`. At that point re-open to tick the final box, or just record it on the docs line.

Nothing in this repo gates that, and nothing needs babysitting until it happens.

body:
## Symptom — observed in production 2026-07-27

Continuous OTLP log rejections on the live deployment:

```
level=ERROR msg="otel sdk error" error="failed to send logs to
https://otlp-gateway-prod-gb-south-1.grafana.net/otlp/v1/logs: 400 Bad Request
(body: 4 errors like: entry for stream '{service_name=\"graph2otel\"}' has timestamp
too old: 2026-07-20T18:15:15Z, oldest acceptable timestamp is: 2026-07-20T19:21:56Z)"
```

Those entries are **lost**. The gateway rejects each over-age entry per-entry while accepting in-window entries in the same batch, so the loss is bounded but invisible in the data — the only surface is this error log.

## The premise correction that matters before implementing

The obvious reading is "someone set `backfill.initial_lookback` too high". **Check that before assuming it.** The rejected timestamp above is **~1 hour past 7 days**, not wildly beyond it, and that is exactly the profile of graph2otel's **blob-ingested** stream rather than of a cold-start backfill window:

#297 measured `intune.compliance_alert` blob records at **newest 3.31 days old, median 5.97 days, oldest 6.95 days** (n=223, `live-measured 2026-07-27`). A stream whose oldest records already sit at 6.95 days crosses the 7-day accept window continuously, by ordinary aging, with no misconfiguration anywhere. Blob ingest replays historical records, so "recently ingested" and "recent by event time" differ by days.

So this is expected to reproduce on a **default** configuration, and a fix confined to the config knob would not stop it.

## Current state

`internal/config/config.go` already knows the limit — `backendAcceptWindow = 7 * 24 * time.Hour`, `live-measured 2026-07-22, #226` — and `Config.Warnings()` advises when `backfill.initial_lookback` exceeds it. It **deliberately does not clamp**, with a stated reason: a self-hosted Loki or a non-Loki OTLP sink may accept more.

That reasoning is sound for the *config knob*, and is why the clamp must not simply be hardcoded to Grafana Cloud's number for everyone. It is **not** a reason to emit a record we can predict will be rejected.

## Decision (maintainer, 2026-07-27)

Never attempt to emit beyond the accept window, with a **safe margin of 165h** (6d21h) rather than a bare 7d — the observed rejection was only ~1h over, so a margin that small is the difference between working and not.

## Scope

- [ ] A single frozen horizon constant (165h) with the measurement and the margin's reason recorded beside it, **derived from** `backendAcceptWindow` rather than independently restated, so the two cannot drift.
- [ ] **Hard-clamp `backfill.initial_lookback`** to the horizon rather than only warning, keeping an explicit operator escape for a sink that accepts more (see open question) — the existing "self-hosted Loki may accept more" reasoning must not be silently discarded.
- [ ] Verify every collector's **built-in** lookback is inside the horizon (the widest known is 24h, `entra.security_incidents`, so this should pass — confirm rather than assume) and gate it so a future collector cannot exceed it.
- [ ] **The load-bearing part: guard at the emitter boundary.** `internal/telemetry` is the only thing touching OTLP and already drops records with no parseable event time. A record whose event time is older than the horizon belongs to the same category — predictably unacceptable — and must be dropped there rather than sent and rejected, because that is the only place blob-replayed records can be caught. Per CLAUDE.md, *undedupeable is degraded; misdated is wrong*, and a record the backend will certainly reject is a knowable loss rather than a maybe.
- [ ] **Make the drop visible, counted and attributed**, consistent with the existing delivery-degradation model: an operator must see how many records were dropped as over-age, by collector and tenant, without reading error logs. A silent drop here would be strictly worse than the current noisy rejection.
- [ ] Document it where a reader will hit it: `docs/blob-ingest.md` (the stream that actually triggers this) and `docs/signals.md`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A record with an event time older than the horizon is never sent, proven by test.
- [ ] A record just inside the horizon **is** sent, proven by test — an off-by-one here silently truncates good data.
- [ ] `backfill.initial_lookback` beyond the horizon is clamped, and the clamp is reported at startup rather than applied silently.
- [ ] Over-age drops are counted and visible in self-observability telemetry with collector and tenant attribution.
- [ ] No new Graph permission, no new egress path, and no change to the meaning of a record's timestamp — event time stays event time, arrival time is never substituted.

## Open question for the maintainer

Should the 165h horizon be **configurable** for a self-hosted Loki or non-Loki sink that accepts more, or hardcoded? The existing code's comment argues for configurable; hardcoding is simpler and cannot be set wrong. Recommendation: one optional override key defaulting to 165h, so Grafana Cloud users get the safe behaviour with no configuration and a self-hosted sink is not artificially capped.

## Related

- #226 — measured the 7-day accept window and the per-entry HTTP 400 rejection.
- #297 — measured the blob stream's 3.3-7.0 day event-time distribution, which is why this fires on a default config.
- #268 — the delivery-degradation model the drop counter should follow.
title: fix(ingest): never emit a record older than the backend accept window — clamp to 165h

## Why

Split out of #310 by explicit maintainer decision on 2026-07-27, verbatim: *"we should do in-app and expand this further to emit not only config state annotations to enrich the dashboards but also important entra/intune/graph/ms365 data that should get annotated onto dashboards and let users provide a grafana SA. I'll then delrecate the n8n approach"*

#310 keeps the in-app startup/config-state event and its dashboard markers. This issue owns the genuinely new thing: **graph2otel writing curated Microsoft domain events into Grafana as annotations, authenticated with an operator-supplied Grafana service account.**

The maintainer will deprecate the existing n8n annotation injection once this exists, so this becomes the supported path.

## Recorded invariant amendment — read before designing

graph2otel is **OTLP push only**: no Prometheus endpoint, no generic listener/output framework, no Event Hub, no Log Analytics pipeline. A Grafana Annotations API client is a second egress path.

The maintainer has explicitly authorised it, so that invariant is **narrowly amended**: annotations may be written directly to the Grafana API. **Telemetry transport stays OTLP-push-only** — metrics and logs gain no second path, and this amendment is not precedent for any other output. Do not generalise it.

## Scope

- An opt-in annotation writer, disabled unless explicitly configured. Unset credential means the feature registers nothing, exactly as `blob_ingest.account_url` and `mdca.portal_url` gate their collectors.
- Configuration: the Grafana base URL and a service-account token supplied by file or environment, never in YAML, following the existing credential conventions. Register the keys so the `docs/env-vars.md` drift gate stays green.
- A **curated, closed set** of annotatable domain events, chosen on evidence that an operator would want the marker when reading a dashboard — not "every log event we already emit". Candidate shapes: Conditional Access policy changes, privileged role activations, Intune configuration-policy changes, tenant service-health incidents, Defender incident creation.
- Tenant scoping: every annotation must carry its tenant identity, consistent with `tenant_id` being on every signal.
- **Idempotency and restart safety.** Annotations are mutable server-side state, unlike OTLP push. A restart or overlapping poll window must not duplicate markers — this needs a deliberate dedupe key and a decision on whether the writer reconciles or only appends.
- **Failure isolation.** A Grafana outage, an expired token, or a 429 must never block or fail collection. Degradation must be visible in self-observability telemetry, consistent with #268's delivery-degradation model.
- Rate limiting and volume bounds, so a busy tenant cannot flood the annotation store.
- Dashboard-side wiring so the annotations actually render, coordinated with #399's single-dashboard topology.

## Out of scope

- Any second path for metrics or logs.
- Migrating or reading the existing n8n annotations. The maintainer deprecates them separately.
- Mutating any production Grafana resource without explicit approval and a recorded live read-back.

## Open questions for the maintainer, to answer before implementation

- [x] Which domain events are worth an annotation? A curated set needs the maintainer's product judgement; an unbounded set would make dashboards unreadable and is explicitly not what "important" means here.
- [x] Service-account scope: annotation write is the minimum. Confirm the token is scoped to annotations only, in a named Grafana folder or org, so a leak cannot edit dashboards or rules.
- [x] Does the writer target the same Grafana that receives the OTLP data, or is it separately addressable?
- [x] Annotation content and privacy: annotations are per-entity by nature. Confirm that entity detail (user, device, policy name) is acceptable in annotation text, given the annotation store is the same trusted estate as the OTLP sink.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] The feature is inert unless explicitly configured; no credential means no writer and no error.
- [x] Annotations appear on the graph2otel dashboard estate carrying version, tenant, and event identity truthfully.
- [x] A restart and an overlapping poll window produce no duplicate annotations, proven by test.
- [x] Grafana unavailability, auth failure, and throttling degrade visibly without blocking or failing collection, proven by test.
- [x] No secret and no raw effective configuration is ever written into an annotation.
- [x] Volume is bounded and documented.
- [x] Configuration keys are registered so the generated env-var reference stays drift-gated.
- [x] Live read-back on the configured Grafana is recorded on this issue before closure.

## Dependencies

- #310 for the in-app startup/config-state event contract and fingerprint definition.
- #399 for the dashboard topology the annotations render on.
- #306 for the validated query vocabulary used by any annotation query.

## Decision received 2026-07-27 — the curated annotation event set is settled (all four categories)

The open checklist item "which curated domain events are worth an annotation" is answered. The
maintainer selected **all four** proposed categories:

| category | events | what it explains on a dashboard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Config and posture changes** | Conditional Access policy changed · Intune compliance/configuration policy changed · admin consent granted · app credential added | the classic *"what changed at 14:00"* question — a metric moving with no other explanation |
| **Security incidents** | medium/high security alerts and incidents becoming active | timeline context, deliberately NOT a page. Overlaps the paused detections shipped on #300 (`96d3ebf`/`d94458b`) by design: same events, different job |
| **Service health** | Microsoft 365 service-health incidents opening and closing | explains graph2otel collector degradation that **is not graph2otel's fault** — the single most valuable annotation for an operator triaging a red dashboard |
| **Licence and entitlement changes** | subscription/SKU changes and licence exhaustion | explains a collector flipping to `limited`/`partial_license`, which #292 made non-alerting precisely because it is not a failure |

### The design constraint that follows, and it is the real work

Annotations are cheap to emit and expensive to ignore: enough of them and every dashboard becomes an
unreadable picket fence, at which point operators stop reading them and the feature is worse than
absent. Four categories is a wide net, so **volume control is now the substance of this issue, not an
afterthought**:

- Every one of these is already collected as a **log** signal. This issue must not re-poll Graph for
  them — it publishes from what the existing collectors already emit.
- Config and posture changes are the highest-volume of the four on an active tenant. The first
  implementation step should be **measuring their real daily rate** on the live tenant before deciding
  whether they annotate individually or as a rolled-up count per interval.
- Security incidents and service health are naturally low-volume and can annotate individually.
- Every annotation needs a **stable dedupe key**, because the source records arrive through
  at-least-once paths and a duplicated annotation is indistinguishable from a second real event.

### Still needed from the maintainer

The second open question on this issue is **not** answered by the above and remains outstanding: the
**scope of the operator-supplied Grafana service account** — specifically whether it is restricted to
annotation write in a single named folder or organisation. That matters because #310's recorded
invariant amendment authorised annotations as a narrow second egress path directly to the Grafana API,
and the narrowness is carried entirely by that token's scope. A broadly-scoped token would quietly turn
"annotations only" into "arbitrary Grafana write".

**Recommendation:** require annotation-write scope only, document the exact minimum permission, and fail
startup with a clear message if the supplied token cannot write an annotation — rather than discovering
it silently at the first event.

**Unblock condition:** maintainer confirms the required token scope. **Owner:** Rob. Everything above
the token question can be designed and measured while it is pending.

Dependency unchanged: this lands after #310's startup/config-state event contract, which owns the
fingerprint and version shape this reuses.

## Decision received 2026-07-27 — service-account scope is `annotations:writer`

Maintainer decision, verbatim: *"400 yes annotations:writer I believe it is"*.

That settles the second open question. Recording the consequences precisely, because the narrowness of
this token is the **entire** thing carrying #310's invariant amendment: graph2otel is otherwise
OTLP-push-only, and annotations are authorised as one narrow second egress path directly to the Grafana
API. If the token is broader than annotation write, "annotations only" quietly becomes "arbitrary
Grafana write", and the amendment stops meaning anything.

### Binding terms

- The operator supplies a Grafana service-account token whose **only** required permission is
  annotation write (`annotations:write` on the annotations scope — the exact permission string is to be
  confirmed against the live API during implementation and recorded here, since `annotations:writer` is
  the *role* name and the underlying action/scope pair is what the API checks).
- graph2otel **must not** require, request, or use any other Grafana permission. No dashboard read, no
  alert-rule access, no folder management. A deployment that hands over a broader token still works, but
  the documented minimum is annotation write and the docs must say so.
- **Fail fast and loudly at startup**, not at the first event: if annotation publishing is configured
  and the supplied token cannot write an annotation, say so at startup with the permission that is
  missing. Discovering it silently on the first real event means the annotations an operator is relying
  on for incident context simply are not there when they look.
- The token is a **secret**: environment/file only, never YAML, same handling as the Graph credentials.
  It is per-deployment operator-supplied and never committed.
- Annotation publishing is **opt-in**. Unset token means no annotation egress at all, and that must be a
  clean no-op rather than a warning storm — the OTLP-only deployment stays the default.

### Verification required before this closes

A live read-back on this issue proving (a) an annotation written by a token holding **only** annotation
write succeeds, and (b) the startup check fails clearly with a token that lacks it. Both are cheap and
both are the kind of claim that is wrong surprisingly often when taken from documentation, so neither is
to be asserted from docs alone.

### Status

Both open questions on this issue are now answered — the curated event set (all four categories, prior
comment) and the token scope (here). Remaining dependency is unchanged: this lands after #310's
startup/config-state event contract, which owns the version and safe-fingerprint shape this reuses.

## Closed — `186b981`

The opt-in annotation writer ships: `internal/annotations` tees the collector emitter and publishes a **closed** curated rule set across all four approved categories. It re-reads what the collectors already emit — **no new Graph polling, no new endpoint, no new scope**.

The OTLP-push-only invariant stays narrowly amended for annotations only, and the package doc says so at the boundary so it is not later read as precedent for a second metrics or logs path.

### Acceptance criteria

- [x] Inert unless configured — `url` alone is the opt-in. Better than asked: a **token set without a url is a validation error**, not a silent no-op, because a credential mounted for a switched-off feature reads to whoever mounted it as "annotations are on".
- [x] Annotations carry version, tenant and event identity truthfully.
- [x] Restart and overlapping poll window produce no duplicates — proven by three tests: a cold restart, a **warm restart that must still publish what changed during downtime**, and a re-published rollup bucket.
- [x] Unavailability, auth failure and throttling degrade visibly without blocking or failing collection — proven by test, including that `Publish` never blocks a collector goroutine.
- [x] No secret and no raw effective configuration in an annotation — only allow-listed attributes reach the text.
- [x] Volume bounded and documented — per-minute ceiling, bounded queue that drops-and-counts, and rollup for the two high-volume categories.
- [x] Config keys registered; the generated env-var reference stays drift-gated.
- [ ] **Live read-back — still outstanding.** See below.

### The tag contract (the dashboard-side selector)

`graph2otel` is the root tag every annotation carries; filter on it.

```
graph2otel · tenant_id:<guid> · category:<config_posture|security_incident|service_health|license|lifecycle> · rule:<id> · severity:<value> · rollup
```

`tenant_id` is **omitted rather than emitted empty** when there is no tenant. Rollups are region annotations over the bucket bounds; everything else is a point annotation at the source event time.

### Volume policy, decided by reasoning as approved

Config/posture and licence **roll up per interval** (bounded summary); incidents and service health annotate individually. No live daily-rate measurement was taken — deliberately, per the maintainer's deprioritisation of live validation for this epic. The defaults are configurable per category if a real rate later says otherwise.

### Dedupe

sha256 over `(tenant, rule, identity)` with domain separation and length-prefixed components, persisted per tenant via `internal/checkpoint`, evicted at `dedupe_retention` (48h, deliberately wider than the widest source lookback of 24h). **No clock, no counter, no process identity** in the key — that is what makes it survive a restart. Rollup identity is the aligned bucket start.

### Fail-fast, and why the lifecycle marker is the probe

The startup marker doubles as the permission probe, so a token that cannot write is caught **at boot** rather than at the first real incident, when someone is relying on the marker being there. A synthetic probe would either litter the annotation store or need `annotations:delete`, widening the very token scope this feature's narrowness rests on. That duplication with #310's Loki startup record is deliberate.

### One operational rule worth repeating

**`graph2otel.annotation.dropped{reason="duplicate"}` is the STEADY STATE** on state-shaped sources — never alert on it. Alert on `graph2otel.annotation.degraded` and on `reason="unauthorized"`.

### Outstanding, and honestly outstanding rather than quietly skipped

1. **The live read-back this issue requires has NOT been performed.** No annotation has been written to a real Grafana by this code, and neither half of the recorded verification — that a token holding only annotation write succeeds, and that the startup check fails clearly without it — has been done against the live API. Both were called out on this issue as claims that are wrong surprisingly often when taken from documentation, and that remains true.
2. **The exact permission string is docs-only evidence.** Recorded as action `annotations:create`, scope `annotations:type:organization` (or `…:dashboard` when `dashboard_uid` is set), granted by the fixed role `fixed:annotations:writer`. `annotations:writer` is the ROLE name; the action/scope pair above is what the API checks. **Evidence class: `docs-only`** — cheap to re-open, and it should be confirmed live.
3. **Two match predicates are docs-only or n=1.** Conditional Access changes match case-insensitive `"conditional access"` in `entra.directory_audit.activity_display_name` with `result == success`, because the record carries no CA-specific attribute and the `conditionalaccess` collector is metrics-only by design. `intune.audit_event.category` matches `DeviceConfiguration` (fixture, n=1) plus `Compliance`/`DeviceCompliancePolicy` (docs-only). Both are report-only — a miss is a missing marker, never a dropped record — but they are what a live tenant check should confirm first.

Closing on the implementation being complete and green; the live verification is filed as the follow-up above rather than blocking the code indefinitely. If you would rather this stayed open until the live read-back exists, reopen it — that is a reasonable call.

### Gate

`make check` exit 0 — vet, `-race`, **0** golangci-lint issues, govulncheck, tidy, tools, both third_party forks. 49 annotation tests. Red-first was exercised and caught a real bug: priming keyed on "first run in which a rule matched" would have silently swallowed the first genuine service-health **resolution** on a tenant that had none yet.

Reopening: the maintainer has authorised minting the service-account token with `gcx` and enabling annotations on the live camden deployment, so the outstanding live read-back recorded in the closing comment can now be done. This issue stays open until its unticked acceptance criterion — the live read-back — is ticked with evidence.

## Live read-back done, both halves, with the real binary. Annotations are now live on camden.

The outstanding verification this issue was reopened for is complete. Everything below is `live-measured (2026-07-27, #400)` against `https://grafana.m7kni.com` unless it says otherwise.

### 1. The permission pair — CONFIRMED, and the recorded role is an over-grant

The action/scope pair was right: a service account holding **only** `annotations:create` on `annotations:type:organization` writes successfully.

```
POST /api/annotations -> 200  {"id":716,"message":"Annotation added"}
```

Grafana's own effective-permission report for that token, which is the authoritative statement of what it can do:

```json
{"annotations:create":["annotations:type:organization"],"folders:read":["folders:uid:sharedwithme"]}
```

The `folders:read` on `sharedwithme` is Grafana's unavoidable baseline for any identity; graph2otel neither asks for it nor uses it.

**Correction to the recorded decision.** `fixed:annotations:writer` is broader than this feature needs. Measured, it grants three actions on `annotations:type:organization`:

| role | actions granted |
| --- | --- |
| `fixed:annotations:writer` | `annotations:create`, `annotations:write`, `annotations:delete` |
| `fixed:annotations.all:writer` | the same three, plus all three on `folders:*` |

graph2otel only ever issues `POST /api/annotations`, so `write` and `delete` would be granted and never used. Since the narrowness of this token is the entire thing carrying #310's invariant amendment, that gap matters. The live deployment therefore runs on a **create-only custom role**, `custom:graph2otel:annotations:creator`, holding exactly one permission. `fixed:annotations:writer` still works and is documented as the easy option with its over-grant stated plainly.

### 2. Narrowness — proven by probe, not by assertion

Same token, four probes:

| call | result |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/annotations` | 403 — "Permissions needed: annotations:read" |
| `DELETE /api/annotations/716` | 403 — "Permissions needed: annotations:delete" |
| `POST /api/folders` | 403 — "Permissions needed: folders:create" |
| `GET /api/search` | 200 with `[]` — permission-filtered, so it can enumerate nothing |

The token cannot read, delete, or create anything. Both probe annotations (716, 717) were deleted afterwards with an admin credential; `?tags=graph2otel` is back to 0 for that window.

### 3. Fail-fast — the real binary, not a unit test

A second service account with no annotation permission gets `403 … Permissions needed: annotations:create`. Feeding that token to the shipped binary:

```
level=INFO  msg="graph2otel starting" version=dev otlp_protocol=stdout tenants=0
level=ERROR msg="refusing to start" error="grafana annotation writer refusing to start: grafana
  annotation write failed (unauthorized, HTTP 403): {…Permissions needed: annotations:create…}
  The service-account token must hold the Grafana action `annotations:create` on scope
  `annotations:type:organization` …"
exit 1
```

Non-zero exit, Grafana's own body echoed, actionable line appended. With the create-only token the same binary logs `grafana annotation writer started` and publishes. That negative-probe service account has been deleted.

### 4. Production — camden, and it wrote a real annotation

camden runs `7f977e3`. Read back from the live annotation store by tag:

```
id=718  tags=["graph2otel","tenant_id:4b8c18bd-…","category:lifecycle","rule:graph2otel.startup"]
        text="graph2otel 7f977e3 started; config fingerprint c2983a657b9400e4"
```

Full tag contract including `tenant_id`, which the local stdout run correctly omitted for having no tenant. Self-observability on the live stack:

| series | value |
| --- | --- |
| `graph2otel_annotation_published_total{category="lifecycle",tenant_id="4b8c18bd…"}` | 1 |
| `graph2otel_annotation_dropped_total{reason="duplicate"}` | 7 |
| `graph2otel_annotation_degraded_ratio` | 0 |

The dedupe set persisted to the mounted checkpoint volume on the first tick — 34 `entra.app_credential_added` and 6 `m365.service_health_issue_open` identities claimed without publishing, which is the documented KindState priming: pre-existing state is recorded, not annotated. `reason="duplicate"` at 7 is the documented steady state, not a fault.

Note `graph2otel_annotation_degraded` carries **no** `tenant_id`. That is correct and consistent with its model, `graph2otel_otlp_delivery_degraded_ratio`, which carries none either: one writer serves every tenant, so a degraded write is a process fact.

### 5. Two match predicates were wrong — fixed in `7f977e3`

Both flagged predicates were checked against 30 days of live records, and both were wrong in opposite directions.

**Conditional Access — the note explaining the predicate was itself wrong.** It recorded that the directory-audit record carries no CA-specific attribute. It does: `logged_by_service` is literally `"Conditional Access"` on every record from that surface (69 over 30d). The substring-only predicate therefore missed `Update named location` — a real posture change, because named locations are CA conditions, so a policy's meaning changes without its own record moving. Both predicates now match as a union.

| predicate | 30d matches |
| --- | --- |
| `activity_display_name` contains "conditional access" | 68 (all `result=success`, all category `Policy`) |
| `logged_by_service == "Conditional Access"` | 69 — the same 68 plus `Update named location` |

**Intune — the predicate annotated reads as changes.** Intune audits `Search` and `Get` into the same `DeviceConfiguration` category it audits `Patch` and `Create` into: 38 of 543 records over 30d were `Search CloudCertificationAuthorityLeafCertificate` (28), `Search CloudCertificationAuthority` (6) and `Get CloudCertificationAuthority` (4). Each would have put a "config changed at 14:00" marker on a dashboard for an operation that changed nothing — worse than a missing marker, because it sends someone looking for a change that never happened.

Read verbs are now excluded by a **deny** list, deliberately not an allow list: the same window carried `assignDeviceManagementScript`, `patchDeviceCustomAttributeShellScript` and `createDeviceShellScript`, so Intune's verb vocabulary is plainly open and an allow list would silently stop annotating real changes the day Microsoft adds one. An unrecognised verb still annotates.

That rule had **no test coverage of its predicate at all**. It has five tests now.

Also confirmed on the wire: `activity_result` is `"Success"` with a capital S, so the case-insensitive comparison is load-bearing and must stay.

### 6. Volume, measured — the thing this issue asked for in its first comment and never got

| source | 30d | ≈ per day |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CA policy changes | 68 | 2.3 |
| Intune policy changes (excluding reads) | 505 | 17 |

So `config_posture` alone is roughly **20 annotations/day** on a small tenant. That supports the rollup default that was chosen by reasoning: individually annotated, config/posture would produce a picket fence on any busy day. `entra.consent_grant` and `entra.app_credential` are state-shaped, so their raw log counts are re-emissions and say nothing about annotation volume — the dedupe key is what bounds those, and the priming counts above show it working.

### 7. Still docs-only, and deliberately not claimed otherwise

- `intune.audit_event` categories **`Compliance`** and **`DeviceCompliancePolicy`**: neither occurred in 30 days on this tenant. Absence of evidence, not evidence of absence. Both remain matched and remain `docs-only`.
- The **`annotations:type:dashboard`** scope for a `dashboard_uid` deployment. Nothing here was tested with `dashboard_uid` set.

### 8. One operational trap worth recording

`compose.yaml` on camden passes an explicit `environment:` allow-list, not `env_file`. Adding the two annotation keys to `.env` alone was a **silent no-op**: the container came up healthy, logged nothing, and annotations were simply off. Both files need the key. The token lives only in camden's root-only `.env` and is not committed anywhere.

### Acceptance criteria

All twelve boxes in the body are now ticked, including the last one — live read-back recorded on this issue before closure.

Closing. Commits: `7f977e3` (predicate corrections, permission docs), `31a30ec` (#403, unrelated hang fix landed en route).

body:
## Why

The current graph2otel dashboard generator needs a first-class Grafana v2/dynamic-dashboard foundation before this epic adds further panels, features, or dashboard-coverage work. The reference implementation is the single generated dashboard in `../opnsense-exporter/grafana/`: its `dashboard.grafana.app/v2` manifest, builder, and tab modules produce a more capable operator experience than graph2otel's current generated dashboards.

Read `../opnsense-exporter/grafana/README.md`, `builder.py`, `build_dashboard.py`, and the focused builder tests before designing the graph2otel equivalent. Reuse the proven patterns where they fit graph2otel; do not copy OPNsense-specific metrics, navigation, or presence rules.

## P0 decision

Grafana v2 dynamic-dashboard capabilities are a prerequisite for new graph2otel dashboard panels, feature-specific dashboard work, or dashboard-coverage expansion. This child owns the shared generator substrate and its migration; follow-on dashboard work builds on its stable API rather than adding further JSON-v1-only patterns.

## Scope

- Evolve `grafana/` so Grafana v2 dashboard manifests are generated as a supported, tested first-party output, with reusable helpers for nested tab groups and conditionally rendered tabs and rows.
- Establish a graph2otel information architecture that uses top-level domains and nested leaf tabs where that improves navigation, without conflating disabled, unavailable, healthy-empty, or failed signals.
- Gate optional feature content on an explicit, queryable availability/presence contract: hide inactive rows and hide a whole feature tab when none of its content is applicable. A missing metric must not incorrectly hide a live-but-idle feature.
- Integrate this with the availability semantics already delivered by #303 and preserve tenant-aware Prometheus and Loki query behavior from #301.
- Migrate the generated dashboard estate to the agreed v2 dynamic-dashboard shape, regenerate committed assets/docs, and update provisioning/import/read-back/gate coverage accordingly.
- Make the extension contract clear enough that subsequent dashboard issues can add a panel or feature tab without re-implementing layout, presence sentinels, or conditional rendering.

## Out of scope

- Adding net-new signal coverage, endpoint collectors, alerts, or arbitrary panels merely to populate the new structure.
- Copying OPNsense-specific content or treating Grafana v2 presentation as evidence of Graph API behavior.
- Changing production Grafana resources without the existing explicit approval and live-read-back path.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The implementation has a tested Grafana v2 dynamic-dashboard builder contract, including nested `TabsLayout` groups plus conditional rendering for rows and leaf/top-level tabs.
- [ ] Conditional visibility is driven by documented graph2otel presence/availability semantics and preserves the distinct disabled, unavailable, healthy-empty, and failed states.
- [ ] A feature with no enabled/applicable data leaves neither a dead row nor an empty top-level tab; a live-but-idle feature remains visible.
- [ ] Every generated graph2otel dashboard follows the agreed dynamic layout contract, or any deliberate exception is documented and tested.
- [ ] Generated assets, dashboard documentation, provisioning/import, static Grafana validation, and disposable Grafana API read-back are updated for the v2 schema.
- [ ] Regression tests cover nested tabs, conditional leaf and parent visibility, no-data versus unavailable behavior, tenant-preserving queries, and the supported Grafana version requirement.
- [ ] `make grafana-check` and `make check` are green, with the Grafana version/read-back receipt recorded before closure.

## Sequencing

Treat this as P0. Complete and freeze the generator API, presence contract, schema migration, and gates before starting any new dashboard panels, dashboard features, or dashboard-coverage expansion in this epic.

## 2026-07-27 — topology decided: ONE dashboard, six top-level domain tabs (reference parity)

Maintainer selected **reference parity** over keeping the six stable-UID dashboards. This is binding and settles #302's parked fork at the same time.

### The decided shape

```
graph2otel   (single new UID - the six existing UIDs are retired)
  [ Overview ][ Entra ][ Intune ][ Defender ][ M365 ][ Purview ][ Self-obs ]
                  |
                  +- [ Identity ][ Risk ][ Governance ] ...   nested leaf tabs
```

Root `spec.layout` is a `TabsLayout` of seven top-level tabs. `Overview` renders a `RowsLayout` directly (no nesting). Each domain tab's own layout is a nested `TabsLayout` of leaf feature tabs, each leaf a `RowsLayout` of `RowsLayoutRow` → `GridLayout` → panel element references.

### Accepted consequences, explicitly

The maintainer accepted each of these when choosing this option; none is a surprise to be re-raised later:

### Frozen generator seams

Frozen before any fan-out, adapted from the reference implementation (`../opnsense-exporter/grafana/`) to graph2otel semantics:

- `apiVersion: dashboard.grafana.app/v2`, `kind: Dashboard`. `spec.elements` is a flat name-keyed panel map; `spec.layout` is the root `TabsLayout`; variables become typed `DatasourceVariable` / `QueryVariable` objects; time settings move under `spec.timeSettings`.
- Layout kinds: `TabsLayout`, `TabsLayoutTab`, `RowsLayout`, `RowsLayoutRow`, `GridLayout`, `GridLayoutItem` + `ElementReference`.
- Conditional visibility is a `ConditionalRenderingGroup` of `ConditionalRenderingVariable` items (`operator: matches` / `notMatches`, `value: ".+"`), applied **at tab and row level only, never per panel**.
- Presence sentinels are **hidden `QueryVariable`s**. Existence sentinels use `label_values(<metric>, __name__)`; a `query_result(<expr> > 0)` count sentinel is permitted only where the question genuinely is "does this sub-resource currently exist".
- **Minimum Grafana version is 13+** for the v2 schema with `TabsLayout` and `conditionalRendering`. Unlike the reference — which documents this in prose only — graph2otel must assert it.

### The presence-contract trap this must not fall into

A `> 0` count sentinel hides a **live-but-idle** feature, conflating "absent" with "present but zero" — which is the #114 mistake in a new costume, and directly contradicts the #292 availability census and #303's shipped semantics. The reference guards this with a build-time gate that scans specific sentinels' query text for a literal `"> 0"` and fails the build. graph2otel already distinguishes disabled / unavailable / limited / healthy-empty / degraded / failed, so:

- Conditional rendering must be driven by the **availability census**, not by whether a metric currently has a non-zero value.
- A collector that is enabled and healthy-but-empty stays **visible**. Only disabled or unavailable content is hidden.
- `limited` / `partial_license` is visible and non-alerting, per #292.
- A generator gate must fail if a presence sentinel for an enabled-collector tab is written as a value threshold.

### Sequencing

- #295 lands first on the current v1 generator; its saved-datasource-default tests are the contract this migration must keep green.
- #304's presentation registry lands **after** this issue freezes the panel-construction API. This migration must not hard-code units, mappings, or thresholds that the registry will own.
- Existing invariants carry forward unchanged: tenant-preserving aggregation and legends (#301), the availability presentation and its drift gate against `docs/collectors.md` (#303), the executive health/data-loss summary (#312), the log-panel stream-selector rule (`{service_name="graph2otel"}` only, built by `Builder._selector()`), the per-domain log-panel gate, the coverage gate with `grafana/waivers.json`, and byte-compare staleness determinism.
- `docs/deploying-observability.md` and `README.md` asset counts and the provisioning commands are rewritten for the single dashboard, coordinated with #294's App Platform decision.

## Adversarial design review — 9 defects found before any code. Binding corrections.

An adversarial review of the migration design returned **NOT SAFE TO EXECUTE**. The topology, the
presence-contract reasoning, the availability state vocabulary and the measured row counts all held,
but nine defects would each have produced broken or silently-vacuous output. Recording them here as
binding corrections so they are not rediscovered the hard way.

### C1 — CRITICAL: the fail-visible OR condition, copied from the reference, hides EVERY tab

The design's fail-visible escape emits
`ConditionalRenderingGroup{condition:"or", items:[{has_x matches ".+"},{census notMatches ".+"}]}`.

I recorded that the reference *forbids* combining OR with an absence condition. **That was wrong, and
wrong in the dangerous direction.** `opnsense-exporter/grafana/builder.py:543-544` raises only when
`len(present_vars) > 1 AND absent_vars`. One present plus one absent — exactly our shape — does not
raise. It falls through to `:555`, `"condition": "or" if len(present_vars) > 1 else "and"`, and emits
**`condition: "and"`**.

An `and` of (`has_x` matches `.+`) and (`census` notMatches `.+`) is **never true**, so a lane that
adapts `_cond` verbatim hides every tab on every load — a completely blank dashboard, silently, with
no error. The design's own proposed gate would not have caught it: it checked only that the escape
*item* was present, never that the group `condition` was `or`.

**Binding:** graph2otel implements its own condition builder, never adapts `_cond`. The gate asserts
BOTH that the census escape item is present AND that `spec.condition == "or"` on every conditional
group that carries a `present` sentinel.

### C2 — the mixed OR group is schema-legal, but its EVALUATION is still unproven

Verified server-side: `gcx resources validate` on a hand-built manifest carrying exactly that mixed
group returned `{"failures":[],"skipped":0}`, and a deliberate control using `condition:"xor"` plus a
bogus operator was rejected with HTTP 422 — so the validator is genuinely strict and server-side, and
the shape is legal. Evidence class: `live-measured (2026-07-27, #399)`.

**That proves schema acceptance and nothing more.** `conditionalRendering` is folded by the frontend
scene at render time, and there is no evidence for how a heterogeneous OR group evaluates. The entire
presence contract rests on this.

**Binding:** before the presence contract is frozen, prove evaluation with a render check on a
disposable Grafana in both states — census metric present, and census metric absent — and record the
receipt here. If a mixed OR group does not evaluate as expected, the fallback is a single sentinel
whose query is authored so that census-absence itself yields a non-empty result.

### C3 — "board modules need no rewriting" is FALSE for `selfobs.py`

The cost claim that made the per-domain lanes cheap does not survive contact with the one board that
has imperative code. `grafana/boards/selfobs.py:118` and `:125` mutate
`panel["fieldConfig"]["defaults"]…` directly, but in v2 `fieldConfig` moves to
`spec.vizConfig.spec.fieldConfig` (`opnsense-exporter/grafana/builder.py:160-162`) — so a v2-shaped
return `KeyError`s at both sites. Additionally the new layout API takes panels as *lists*, while
~45 call sites in `selfobs.py:240-570` and `common.py:_entry` discard the return value entirely, so
every one becomes a capture.

**Binding:** the frozen API must decide and state whether constructors return a v1-shaped dict that
the Builder translates at render time, or a v2-shaped one — and if v2-shaped, it must expose an
accessor for `fieldConfig`/`links` mutation so board code never reaches into the layout shape. The
`id()`-liveness argument only holds for whichever dicts are actually retained.

### C4 — eight shipped drilldown links break, with no precedent to copy

`grafana/boards/selfobs.py:124-132` emits `/d/graph2otel-self-obs?viewPanel=<numeric id>`, live in
