## C2 and C4 RESOLVED — measured against real Grafana renders. Both unknowns answered.

A local two-Grafana + image-renderer harness resolved both blocking unknowns with **rendered PNGs read
visually**, not schema inspection. Every claim below is `observed` unless labelled otherwise.

Environment: `grafana/grafana:nightly` reporting `13.2.0-30227907589`, cross-checked against
`grafana/grafana:13.1.1` — **identical results everywhere**. Note for anyone reproducing this: there is
**no public Grafana 13.2.x image**; Docker Hub tops out at 13.1.1 for oss/enterprise, and production
Cloud's `13.2.0-30000045535` is a Cloud build. The nightly is the same minor with a later build number.
Dashboards were created via `POST /apis/dashboard.grafana.app/v2/namespaces/default/dashboards` → HTTP
201; `dashboard.grafana.app/v2` is the **preferredVersion** on both versions. No Prometheus or Loki was
involved — presence was driven purely by URL-settable `TextVariable`s, isolating the folding logic.

### C2 — VERDICT: the fail-visible mixed-OR encoding is SAFE. Build the presence contract on it.

Five conditions × four states. `hide` means the tab title is **absent from the tab bar entirely**.

| state | `has_x` | `census` | `and[matches has_x]` | **`or[matches has_x, notMatches census]`** | `and[notMatches census]` | `and[matches has_x, notMatches census]` | control |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 domain active, census healthy | set | set | SHOW | **SHOW** | hide | hide | SHOW |
| 2 domain genuinely absent | empty | set | hide | **hide** | hide | hide | SHOW |
| 3 census absent (fail-visible) | empty | empty | hide | **SHOW** | SHOW | hide | SHOW |
| 4 domain active, census absent | set | empty | SHOW | **SHOW** | SHOW | SHOW | SHOW |

A heterogeneous OR group folds exactly as written: each item is evaluated independently against its
variable's resolved value and the element shows if any is true. `matches ".+"` is true iff non-empty,
`notMatches ".+"` true iff empty. No special-casing, no short-circuit, no collapse.

That is precisely the required contract — visible when the domain is active, visible when the census is
entirely absent (wrong datasource / stopped exporter), hidden **only** in state 2 where a healthy census
positively reports the domain absent.

**Row-level conditions produced an identical table.** Tab-level and row-level folding are the same logic.

#### Correction to C1's stated reason (the binding correction itself still stands)

C1 claimed an `and` of (`matches has_x`) and (`notMatches census`) is "never true". **That phrasing was
wrong** — it IS true in state 4, which rendered. What is true is that it is false in **state 1, the
normal healthy operating state**, and in states 2 and 3. So adapting the reference's `_cond` verbatim
still produces the blank-dashboard outcome C1 predicts, for a narrower reason.

**Do not weaken C1 on the strength of that imprecision.** Write our own condition builder, and gate on
`spec.condition == "or"`.

#### Further measured findings that shape the contract

- **A conditioned-away tab is removed from the tab bar entirely** — not greyed, not disabled, no
  placeholder. An operator cannot distinguish a hidden tab from one that was never authored. This is
  exactly why the fail-visible escape is required rather than nice-to-have.
- **A condition naming a variable that does not exist evaluates TRUE for both `matches` and
  `notMatches`** — the element shows. So a typo'd or dropped sentinel **fails visible**, which is the
  right default. But it means rendering can never catch a misspelled sentinel: **the generator must
  assert every referenced sentinel name against the declared variable set.**
- **A 3-item mixed OR works** (`or[matches has_a, matches has_b, notMatches census]`), hiding only when
  both present vars are empty and the census is non-empty. We are not limited to the 2-item shape the
  reference's guard would have refused.
- **`hide: "hideVariable"` does not change folding** — the full four-state table was re-run with all
  variables hidden and behaved identically. This closes the substitution gap between the spike's
  settable `TextVariable`s and production's hidden `QueryVariable`s *for the folding step*.

Remaining `inferred`, deliberately labelled: that a hidden `QueryVariable` backed by `label_values(...)`
resolves to empty string when the metric is absent. That is a query-resolution property, not a
conditionalRendering one, and the reference implementation already depends on it in production.

### C4 — RESOLVED: `viewPanel` keys on `spec.id`, and tabs are addressable via `dtab`

Probed with deliberately divergent element names and ids (element `alpha` → `spec.id` 41, element
`panel-7` → id 42), which the reference builder cannot distinguish because it always makes `panel-N`
carry `spec.id == N`:

| URL form | result |
| --- | --- |
| `?viewPanel=41` | **works** — renders element `alpha` |
| `?viewPanel=panel-41` | **works** — same panel |
| `?viewPanel=alpha` | fails — "Panel not found" |
| `?viewPanel=panel-7` | fails — "Panel not found", despite being a real element **name** |

**So the v1 drilldown form survives the migration unchanged, provided `spec.id` is preserved.** The eight
`selfobs.py` drilldowns keep working, and the existing `viewPanel=(\d+)` regex in
`test_every_verdict_has_a_resolving_same_dashboard_drilldown` stays valid — **only the dashboard UID in
the link prefix changes.** This materially shrinks C4's scope.

Tab selection:

| URL form | result |
| --- | --- |
| `?dtab=Entra-ID` | **works** — slug is the tab title with spaces → `-`, case preserved |
| `?dtab=entra-id` | **works** — fully-lowercased slug also accepted |
| `?dtab=Entra-ID&Entra-ID-dtab=Risk` | **works** — nested leaf selected too; nested key is `<parent-slug>-dtab` |
| `?tab=...`, `?dtab=<index>` | no effect |

**`?dtab=<hidden-tab>` overrides conditional hiding** — the tab renders, dimmed and badged with an
eye-slash icon. That is a genuinely good escape hatch for #311's cross-tab links: a link into a
currently-absent domain lands somewhere legible rather than nowhere.

**Time range and variables survive** — `?from=now-24h&to=now` and `?var-tenant=acme` both persisted,
including combined with `viewPanel` and with nested `dtab`. A `viewPanel` link reached a panel two
layout levels deep inside a nested tab with no `dtab` params at all, so panel deep links need no tab
coordinates. This satisfies #311's absorbed "preserving time and tenant context" criterion.

### Two silent-failure traps found — both must be designed around

1. **`viewPanel=<id>` for a panel whose ancestor tab is conditioned away renders a completely blank
   body** — no message, no tab bar, nothing. A control render of the same id with the tab visible worked
   fine. This is the only silent-blank path in the whole spike and it lands **exactly on the #312
   drilldown contract**: a drilldown into a domain whose sentinel is empty gives the operator a blank
   page. Mitigation options: pair every `viewPanel` drilldown with the `dtab` of its owning tab (which
   overrides hiding), or only emit drilldowns into always-visible content.
2. **A wrong `dtab` slug is silently ignored** and the dashboard falls back to the first tab — the one
   non-fail-visible behaviour on the tab path. **The generator must gate that every emitted slug matches
   an emitted tab title.**

Minor, recorded for completeness: the very first `?dtab=` request against a freshly created dashboard did
not apply the selection, and the identical URL worked on every subsequent attempt. Likely a first-load
race between URL sync and scene construction. Irrelevant for human clicks; if a CI render check ever
asserts on `dtab`, warm the scene with one throwaway render first.

### Frozen deep-link shapes for graph2otel

- Panel drilldown: `/d/<uid>?viewPanel=<spec.id>&var-tenant=$tenant&from=$__from&to=$__to`
- Cross-tab link: `/d/<uid>?dtab=<Domain-Slug>[&<Domain-Slug>-dtab=<Leaf-Slug>]&var-tenant=$tenant&from=$__from&to=$__to`

### Consequences for the migration

- The presence contract is **proven** and can be frozen. C2 closed.
- C4 shrinks to "preserve stable numeric `spec.id` and update the UID in the link prefix" — the drilldowns
  and their test survive largely intact.
- Two new generator gates are added to the required set: **sentinel names must resolve to declared
  variables**, and **every emitted tab slug must match an emitted tab title**.
- The v2 create path and preferredVersion are confirmed on both 13.1.1 and 13.2.0, so the disposable-Grafana
  read-back step in P3 is viable, and the render check demanded by C5 is proven to work with
  `grafana/grafana-image-renderer` (Grafana refuses to start unless `GF_RENDERING_RENDERER_TOKEN` is set to
  a non-default value, and the renderer needs the matching `AUTH_TOKEN`).

Spike fixtures and the ~40 render receipts live in a session-scoped scratchpad. The findings above are the
durable artifact; the harness is reproducible in minutes from this description if the fixtures are needed
as regression assets.

## C3 RESOLVED — frozen seam decision, and the migration splits into two commits

### C3's question, answered: constructors return **v1-shaped** dicts; the Builder translates at render

C3 required the frozen API to state whether panel constructors return a v1-shaped dict translated at
render time, or a v2-shaped one with an accessor for `fieldConfig`/`links` mutation. **Decision:
v1-shaped, translated at render time.**

Rationale, in order of weight:

1. **It makes C3 mostly evaporate.** `selfobs.py:118,125` mutate `panel["fieldConfig"]["defaults"]…`
   and `builder.py:457-464` / `:509` / `:530-533` do the same inside the Builder itself. Under a
   v2-shaped return every one of those sites `KeyError`s and needs an accessor shim. Under this
   decision they are untouched, and no board module ever learns the v2 layout shape.
2. **The translation has exactly one owner.** v1→v2 is a pure function over the accumulated
   `_panels` list, testable in isolation, in one file. An accessor shim would instead spread v2
   awareness across six board modules.
3. **`_panels` already stores `{w, h, spec}`** — precisely the input a translator needs, with the
   grid dimensions already separated from the panel body.

Cost accepted: the v1 shape becomes an internal intermediate representation rather than an output
format. That is a real cost only if a v2-only feature has no v1 expression; none of the features this
migration needs (`links`, `fieldConfig`, `transformations`, `options`) is in that class.

### Consequence: two commits, with a green pause point between them

This is the substantive change to the phase plan. The migration as originally scoped is one commit —
single output file, six old files deleted, ~40 tests migrated (C9) — with no green intermediate state,
so starting it commits to finishing it. The seam decision above removes that constraint:

**Commit 1 (additive, output byte-identical).** A new `grafana/v2.py` holding the pure translation
layer, the layout primitives, the variable primitives and the new gates, with its own
`grafana/tests/test_v2.py`. `builder.py` is **not touched**; no board module is touched; no generated
dashboard changes, so the byte-compare staleness gate stays green by construction. Commits green,
closes nothing.

**Commit 2 (the switch).** `builder.py` render path, `common.py`, all six board modules,
`build_dashboard.py`, `performance_baseline.py` (C6), the ~40 test migrations (C9), single-file output,
the six deletions, docs and provisioning rewrite, render check, disposable-Grafana read-back.
`Closes #311`.

Commit 1 is where every C1–C10 gate is actually implemented and unit-tested against fixtures, so
commit 2 becomes wiring against a proven, already-green translation layer rather than a big-bang.

### Wire shapes confirmed against the reference's live committed output

Read out of `opnsense-exporter/grafana/dashboard.json` and `builder.py` rather than composed from the
schema, so these are shapes a real Grafana has accepted:

- Panel element: `{kind:"Panel", spec:{id, title, description, links, data:{kind:"QueryGroup",
  spec:{queries, queryOptions, transformations}}, vizConfig:{kind:"VizConfig", group:<viz>, version,
  spec:{options, fieldConfig}}}}` — note `vizConfig.group` carries the viz type and
  `vizConfig.spec` carries `options` + `fieldConfig`.
- Query: `{kind:"PanelQuery", spec:{refId, hidden, datasource, query:{kind:"DataQuery", version:"v0",
  group:"prometheus"|"loki", datasource, spec:{expr, refId, …}}}}`. The Loki **variable** query spec
  differs from the Loki **panel** query spec — a variable uses a bare `__legacyStringValue` string,
  not `{query, refId}`. Worth knowing before authoring the sentinels.
- Transformation: `{kind:"Transformation", group:<id>, spec:{options}}` — confirming C5's required
  conversion of both graph2otel sites.
- `DatasourceVariable.spec` uses **`pluginId`** (not `type`) and **`hide: "dontHide"`** (not `0`),
  exactly as C9 predicted. It does carry `current` and `regex` unchanged, so **#295's substance is
  preserved and only its 6 assertions move** — confirmed by reading the reference's own emitted
  variables, which carry the same `(?!grafanacloud-usage|…).+` exclusion shape #295 landed.

### Gates implemented and unit-tested in commit 1

Each maps to a recorded correction: fail-visible condition builder asserting `condition == "or"` plus
the census escape (C1, and never adapting `_cond`) · v2 transformation shape (C5) · unplaced-element
gate (C10) · every referenced sentinel name resolves to a declared variable (spike finding: a missing
variable renders TRUE, so rendering can never catch a typo) · every emitted tab slug matches an
emitted tab title (spike finding: a wrong `dtab` slug is silently ignored) · stable numeric `spec.id`
preserved so the eight existing drilldowns survive (C4) · `MIN_GRAFANA_VERSION` asserted rather than
documented in prose.

Evidence class for the wire shapes: `observed` in the reference's committed, deployed output.

## Commit 1 of 2 landed — `855acef` (additive, generated output byte-identical)

`grafana/v2.py` (the translation layer + layout primitives + gates) and
`grafana/tests/test_v2.py` (51 tests). **No other file touched.** `git status` after the change showed
exactly two new files and zero modifications, so the byte-compare staleness gate is green by
construction rather than by re-generation.

### Gates implemented, each traced to its correction

| gate | correction | what it prevents |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `condition()` emits `"or"` only, and refuses `present` with no `census` | C1 | the blank dashboard: an `and` group is false in the normal healthy state |
| `manifest_violations()` re-checks group `condition == "or"` **and** the escape item independently | C1 | a hand-built or hand-edited `and` group slipping through — the original design's gate checked only the item |
| v1 `{id, options}` → `{kind, group, spec:{options}}`, double-wrap refused | C5 | a transformation that validates clean server-side and renders wrong |
| unplaced-element and dangling-reference checks | C10 | a panel credited by the coverage gate but absent from the layout |
| every referenced sentinel resolves to a declared variable | spike finding | an undeclared variable evaluates TRUE, so rendering *cannot* catch a typo |
| duplicate sibling tab titles rejected | spike finding | a wrong `dtab` slug is silently ignored and falls back to tab 1 |
| `sentinel()` refuses `query_result(...)` / `> 0` | #114 / #303 | a value-threshold sentinel hiding a healthy-but-empty collector |
| `grid()` refuses width > 24 | — | silent overflow |
| `MIN_GRAFANA_VERSION` asserted by test | #399 body | the reference documents 13+ in prose with no assertion |

### The 5 tests that carry the most weight

46 of the 51 pin shapes and gates against fixtures. The other 5 translate **every panel the six live
boards actually build** — 405 panels — and assert the walk was not vacuous (`seen > 300`), per the
#139/#100 rule that a gate which cannot see its subject reports coverage it does not have. They prove
the translator meets text, stat, timeseries, table, bargauge, heatmap and logs panels, both
datasources, every real `fieldConfig` post-mutation, and **both** C5 transformation sites
(`labelsToFields` and `reduce` — asserted as an exact set, so a third appearing later fails loudly).
One test runs the full translate → place → gate path over the purview board end-to-end and asserts
zero violations.

This is the difference between a fixture-green translator and one proven against the real estate, and
it is what makes commit 2 wiring rather than discovery.

### Verification

- `make check` → **exit 0** (Go vet/test/lint/govulncheck/tidy + tools + both `third_party` forks + build).
- `make grafana-check` → **exit 0**: coverage `331/331` catalog metrics panelled, 0 waived, **405 panels
  across 6 dashboards** (unchanged), 134 log events over 7 log-panelled domains; 14 alert rules
  (7 enabled, 7 paused), 2 recording rules; **193 tests OK** (142 → 193).
- `uvx --from zensical==0.0.46 zensical build --clean` → **No issues found**.
- Pushed to `main` as `855acef`. Bypass-on-push output expected.

### One correction to my own earlier reading, worth recording

While re-verifying the SIEM rule set for #300 I found that `gcx`'s current-context was pointing at an
unrelated stack, which returns **221 rules and no `entra-security-g2o` group**. The correct read needs
`--context grafana.m7kni.com` → **444 rules, all 8 SIEM alerts present**. Nothing about #399 depended on
it, but any future session verifying live Grafana state must pin the context or it will conclude
resources have vanished.

### Commit 2 — remaining scope, unchanged

`builder.py` v2 render path · `boards/common.py` SECTIONS → leaf tabs · five per-domain board modules
(parallelisable, one file per lane, each with its own new `tests/test_board_<domain>.py`) ·
`build_dashboard.py` single-dashboard build · `performance_baseline.py` + fixtures (C6) · the ~40 test
migrations (C9) · the two vacuous-gate rewrites (C7) · `Overview` tab · six file deletions · docs and
provisioning rewrite · render check (C5) · disposable-Grafana v2 read-back. `Closes #311`.

C8 remains the largest unresolved authoring question: self-obs's 14 rows are one `SECTIONS` entry plus
12 `b.row()` calls inside `extra()`, and it sets `AVAILABILITY_PATTERN = None` deliberately — so the
frozen SECTIONS→leaf mapping rule does not yet say where most of that board's content goes. That is
`common.py` + `selfobs.py` work and is primary-owned, not lane work.

## C8 RESOLVED — and the resolution deletes most of commit 2's fan-out

C8 said the frozen `SECTIONS` → leaf-tab mapping rule does not cover `extra()`-produced rows, does not
say where self-obs's content goes, and collides with self-obs's deliberate `AVAILABILITY_PATTERN = None`.
All three are real. The fix is to **stop mapping from `SECTIONS` at all.**

### The rule (replaces the frozen SECTIONS→leaf rule)

**One `b.row()` call = one leaf tab.** Partition the accumulated `Builder._panels` stream at its row
markers; each `{"row": True, "title": t}` opens a leaf tab named `t`, and the panels following it are
that leaf's content.

Why this is the right rule rather than a workaround:

- **It covers every row source uniformly** — `SECTIONS`, the availability row, `extra()`, and `LOGS` all
  reach the layout through the same `b.row()` call, so there is nothing left for a mapping rule to
  special-case. C8's three complaints all dissolve rather than getting three exceptions.
- **Self-obs's `AVAILABILITY_PATTERN = None` needs no special case.** `common.py:76` simply emits no
  availability row, so that board has no `Availability` leaf. The deliberate exception is preserved by
  doing nothing, and the test guarding it keeps passing.
- **It derives instead of declaring**, which is how the rest of this generator already works —
  `titleize()` derives titles, coverage is derived by reading expressions rather than from a claim. A
  second layout declaration alongside `SECTIONS` would be a new place for a name to drift.

### Verified against the real boards, not asserted

Partitioning the live `_panels` stream of all six boards:

| board | rows → leaves | duplicate row titles | empty rows | panels before the first row |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| intune-fleet-overview | 13 | none | none | 1 |
| entra-compliance-overview | 12 | none | none | 1 |
| m365-services-overview | 7 | none | none | 1 |
| defender-security-overview | 8 | none | none | 1 |
| purview-compliance-overview | 5 | none | none | 1 |
| graph2otel-self-observability | 14 | none | none | 1 |

**59 leaves**, matching the independently recorded row count exactly. Three properties the rule depends
on all hold with no exceptions: **no board has two rows sharing a title** (so every derived `dtab` slug
is unambiguous and the duplicate-sibling-title gate passes), **no row is empty** (so no leaf renders as
a blank tab), and **exactly one panel precedes the first row on every board** — the shared `PREAMBLE`,
which the migration already replaces with one compact docs-link panel on `Overview`.

That last column is the only genuinely new rule needed: **panels emitted before the first row are
hoisted to `Overview`**. Today that is exactly the preamble on all six boards, which is being deleted
anyway, so the hoist is a safety net rather than a live code path — and it means a future board that
opens with a summary panel lands somewhere sensible instead of being silently dropped.

### Consequence: the five parallel per-domain lanes are no longer needed

This is the significant scope change. The original plan had P2 as five concurrent lanes, one per board
module, each rewriting its layout declaration. Under the row-partition rule **no board module changes at
all** — `entra_compliance.py`, `intune_fleet.py`, `m365_services.py`, `defender_security.py` and
`selfobs.py` are untouched, because their `b.row()` calls already carry the entire leaf-tab structure.

So commit 2 is a serial, primary-owned change to `builder.py`, `boards/common.py`,
`build_dashboard.py`, `performance_baseline.py`, the test suite, docs and the generated output. No
fan-out, no one-file-one-owner coordination, and no five sets of lane assertions to review.

C10's first defect also disappears with it: the #312 executive matrix stays in `selfobs.py` where it
already lives, and since no lane touches that file there is no ownership conflict to resolve.

### What this does NOT resolve

- **C3's `selfobs.py:118,125` `fieldConfig` mutations** — already handled by the v1-shaped-return seam
  decision, landed in `855acef`.
- **`selfobs.py:136-145` declares `$collector` with a v1 templating dict** via `b.variable()`. That
  still needs converting to the v2 `QueryVariable` shape. `v2.query_variable()` exists for it, but the
  call site is real work in commit 2 and the ~35 queries using `$collector` depend on it.
- **Grouping judgement.** One row per leaf is the mechanical default; whether Intune's 13 leaves read
  better as, say, 8 with some multi-row leaves is #302's substance and can be tuned afterwards without
  touching this rule.

## Commit 2 of 2 landed — `97e08b6`. The migration is complete.

`dashboards/graph2otel.json` is now the whole estate: one v2 dynamic dashboard, root `TabsLayout` of
seven tabs (Overview · Entra · Intune · Defender · M365 · Purview · Self-obs), 60 leaf tabs, 348 panels.
The six v1 files are deleted and their UIDs retired.

### C8's resolution deleted the fan-out

The row-partition rule (one `b.row()` = one leaf tab) meant **no board module needed its layout
rewritten**. The five planned parallel per-domain lanes were not needed at all; the only board-module
changes were mechanical (`UID`/`TENANT_METRIC`/`TITLE`/`TAGS` removed, `DOMAIN` added, and self-obs's
`$collector` variable converted to the v2 shape).

### Two defects caught that no local gate would have found

1. **Server-side validation rejected the manifest 422**: `sort: "alphabetical"` is not a member of the
   closed enum — the valid members are `alphabeticalAsc` and `disabled`. Every local test passed with
   the invalid value. Both members are now named constants. This is the concrete argument for keeping
   `gcx resources validate` in the loop: it is the only check that knows the server's enums.
2. **`performance_baseline.py` was measuring nothing and reporting zeros over a green suite** (C6),
   because its fixture was hand-written v1. Fixed, and it now **rejects a v1 document loudly** rather
   than silently measuring zero — that regression test is what stops the class recurring.

### Render verification — the fail-visible contract, proven on the shipped artifact

Imported the real generated manifest into a disposable Grafana **13.2.0** (`HTTP 201` via
`POST /apis/dashboard.grafana.app/v2/...`) **with no datasource configured at all** — deliberately the
worst case, since that is precisely the state that must not blank the dashboard.

- **All seven tabs rendered.** The census is entirely absent, and nothing hid. That is C1/C2's contract
  demonstrated end-to-end on the real artifact rather than on a spike fixture.
- The availability panel showed its intended *"Availability unknown … this does not mean disabled"*
  text, and metric panels their neutral no-data message.
- `?dtab=Entra&Entra-dtab=Licensing` selected the right nested leaf; the 24-column packing was correct.
- A **real shipped drilldown** (`?viewPanel=346`) resolved a panel two layout levels deep inside a
  nested tab with no tab coordinates — C4 confirmed on the shipped manifest.

Honest limit: with no datasource, this proves the manifest loads, folds and lays out correctly, and
that no panel errors. It does **not** prove a transformation renders correctly *with data*. That
residual risk is covered by pinning both transformation shapes against the reference's deployed form
and asserting the exact set `{labelsToFields, reduce}` converts.

### Two new gates from the render traps

A `viewPanel` link into a conditioned-away tab renders a **completely blank body with no message** —
the only silent-blank path found. So: every emitted `viewPanel` id must resolve to a real panel, and
its target must be unconditional **or** the link must carry a `dtab` (which overrides hiding). All 8
shipped drilldowns target Self-obs, which is unconditional, and both gates pass.

### Every migrated gate checked by sabotage, not by reading

~65 tests were migrated. A returned report is not evidence that a gate still bites, so each invariant
was broken in `builder.py` and the suite re-run:

| invariant sabotaged | tests that failed |
| --- | --- |
| tenant-preserving aggregation drops `tenant_id` | 7 |
| neutral no-data `noValue` blanked | 247 |
| LogQL stream selector reverted to the `{attr="…"}` trap (#90) | 2 |

All three fail loudly; the gates are real. Loops that skip panels now assert a non-zero floor (#139/#100
— the datasource moved into each query, so a naive port would have skipped every panel and passed
vacuously). I also restored one guard the migration had dropped: a test that
`Builder.__init__` still **raises** when the tenant dropdown metric is process-scoped. The merged test
asserted the current metric is tenant-scoped but not that the guard exists, so the `raise` could have
been deleted silently.

### Verification

- `make check` → **exit 0**; `make grafana-check` → **exit 0**, coverage **331/331** unchanged, 348
  panels across 7 tabs and 60 leaves, **203 tests** (142 → 193 → 203).
- `gcx resources validate` against live Grafana → `{"failures":[],"skipped":0}`.
- Zensical → **No issues found**.
- Re-measured baselines for **#309**: 348 panels, 7 tabs, 60 leaves, 60 rows, 376 targets, 374 unique
  expressions, 39,367 expression bytes. The old baseline (6 dashboards / 404 panels / 59 rows / 39,135
  bytes) describes an estate that no longer exists.
- Docs rewritten: `docs/deploying-observability.md` (single asset, `metadata.name` as the update key,
  the deep-link forms, and the hide-only-on-positive-evidence rule), `grafana/AUTHORING.md`,
  `README.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `Makefile`.

### Follow-ups this leaves open

- **#309** must adopt the numbers above; its recorded baseline is now stale by construction.
- **#302**'s remaining substance — whether one row per leaf is the right grouping, or whether Intune's
  13 leaves read better merged — is now a tuning question against a working topology, not a fork.
- **Live publication is still unauthorised.** Nothing was pushed to the m7kni stack; the only live
  interaction was read-only validation and a disposable local container.
- `TITLE`/`TAGS`/`UID`/`TENANT_METRIC` are gone from board modules. A board now declares `DOMAIN`,
  `DESCRIPTION`, `AVAILABILITY_PATTERN`, `SECTIONS`, and optionally `LOGS`/`extra(b)`.

Closes #311 via the commit keyword. This issue stays open only until the CI receipt below is terminal.

## Terminal CI receipt — `97e08b6`, all 8 workflows success

| workflow | conclusion |
| --- | --- |
| CI | success |
| CodeQL | success |
| Docker Security | success |
| Release | success |
| Scorecard | success |
| actionlint | success |
| zizmor | success |
| Trigger Documentation Sync | success |

Downstream: the docs-sync dispatch fired and `rknightion/m7kni-net-site`'s
`Build and Deploy Documentation` completed **success** (`repository_dispatch`, 2026-07-27T12:50:25Z).

#311 auto-closed on the `Closes` keyword, as intended.

### One consequence that needs a maintainer decision, and it is my doing

The completing commit carries a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer, so release-please has **re-titled the open
release PR #381 from `chore(main): release 1.1.0` to `chore(main): release 2.0.0`.**

That is a defensible reading — the six dashboard UIDs are retired and any existing bookmark or Grafana
link to them breaks, which is genuinely breaking for an operator. But it is worth stating what is *not*
breaking: the Go binary, every configuration key, all Graph permissions, the OTLP output, the metric and
log contracts, and the checkpoint format are **completely unchanged**. An operator who never imported a
dashboard sees no difference at all. A 2.0.0 tells everyone to expect an upgrade migration that, for the
exporter itself, does not exist.

I should have raised the version consequence before writing that footer rather than after. Options, and
history is not being rewritten either way:

1. **Accept 2.0.0.** Honest about the retired UIDs; costs a major-version signal on a compatible binary.
2. **Override to 1.1.0** with a `Release-As: 1.1.0` footer on a subsequent commit, and describe the
   dashboard change prominently in the release notes instead. Keeps semver aligned with the *software*
   contract and treats the shipped Grafana asset as a separate artifact.

**Recommendation: option 2.** graph2otel's semver should track the exporter's contract with its
operators — config, permissions, telemetry — and by that measure nothing broke. The dashboard retirement
is real but belongs in prominent release notes, not in a major bump that implies the binary needs a
migration.

Deferring to the maintainer; no further action taken on the release PR.

## Correction: this issue was closed early, by accident, and the timeline is misleading

GitHub records this issue as closed at **2026-07-27T12:21:34Z by `855acef`** — commit 1 of 2, the
additive translation layer. That is **wrong as a statement of completion**, and it was my error.

Cause: commit 1's message contains the sentence *"Resolves #399's C3 seam question"*. GitHub parses
`Resolves #399` as a closing keyword and ignores the surrounding prose entirely, so a sentence that
merely *mentions* the issue number after a keyword closed it. The intended footer on that commit was
`Refs #399`, and it was there — the accidental keyword in the body outranked it.

**The end state is nevertheless correct.** `97e08b6` completed the migration, all 8 workflows are green,
and the acceptance criteria are met, so the issue is genuinely closed now — just for the wrong reason
and roughly 90 minutes early. I am deliberately **not** reopening and re-closing it: that would add
churn without changing the outcome, and this comment is the durable record of what actually happened.

**What a future reader must not conclude:** that `855acef` completed #399. It did not. It landed the
additive first half with generated output byte-identical. The migration is `855acef` **plus** `97e08b6`.

**The trap, for anyone writing commit messages against this tracker:** a closing keyword anywhere in the
body closes the issue, including mid-sentence in explanatory prose. Write "addresses the C3 question
from #399", not "resolves #399's C3 question". The words to avoid mid-prose are `close`/`closes`/
`closed`, `fix`/`fixes`/`fixed`, `resolve`/`resolves`/`resolved` immediately preceding a `#NN`.

## The six retired v1 dashboards are now removed from production

Maintainer decision 2026-07-27: delete them. Recorded here because it is a **destructive live mutation on
production Grafana** and was explicitly excluded from the earlier publish authorisation.

### Why this was needed at all

`dashboards/graph2otel.json` was published to `grafana.m7kni.com` on 2026-07-27 (receipt on #309). The v2
dashboard's identity is `metadata.name: graph2otel`, which does not collide with any v1 UID — so publishing
*added* a seventh dashboard rather than replacing six. An operator opening the `graph2otel` folder saw seven
graph2otel dashboards, exactly one of which was current, and the six stale ones still rendered plausible
numbers from a retired layout.

### Identifying the deletion set from evidence, not from the name pattern

A substring search would have deleted the wrong set. The v1 generator was inconsistent: five boards used a
`graph2otel-` UID and the Intune one used a bare `intune-fleet-overview`, with a title carrying no prefix at
all (`Intune Fleet Overview`). So grepping live titles for "graph2otel" found **5 of 6**.

The set was instead taken from git, reading each retired file's `uid` at `97e08b6~1` — the commit before the
migration deleted them:

| repo file at `97e08b6~1` | v1 uid | live? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `defender-security-overview.json` | `graph2otel-defender-security` | yes |
| `entra-compliance-overview.json` | `graph2otel-entra-compliance` | yes |
| `m365-services-overview.json` | `graph2otel-m365-services` | yes |
| `purview-compliance-overview.json` | `graph2otel-purview-compliance` | yes |
| `graph2otel-self-observability.json` | `graph2otel-self-obs` | yes |
| `intune-fleet-overview.json` | `intune-fleet-overview` | yes |

`intune-fleet-overview` was additionally content-verified before deletion rather than trusted: tags
`["graph2otel","intune","fleet","generated"]`, the `build_dashboard.py` generator marker in its text, and 126
`intune_` metric references. It was graph2otel's own board.

### Receipt

Folder `efs83nfy641s0c` (title **graph2otel**) before: 7 dashboards. After: **1**.

```
graph2otel-defender-security   -> GONE
graph2otel-entra-compliance    -> GONE
graph2otel-m365-services       -> GONE
graph2otel-purview-compliance  -> GONE
graph2otel-self-obs            -> GONE
intune-fleet-overview          -> GONE
graph2otel                     -> PRESENT
```

The survivor is intact and unchanged: uid `<guid-1>`, generation 2, 350 elements,
7 tabs, 1 annotation, with `spec.layout` and `spec.annotations` matching the committed source exactly. Nothing
outside this folder was touched, and no alert rule, recording rule or datasource was touched.

### Two `gcx` traps this hit, both worth carrying forward

**1. `dashboards delete` is a silent no-op without `--force` in agent mode.** The first pass reported no
action; the real message was `Destructive operation requires --force in agent mode`, exit 1. Six deletions
appeared to have been issued and **nothing had been deleted**. Only re-probing each name caught it — had I
trusted the loop's output I would have recorded six deletions that never happened.

**2. A large `dashboards get` response spills to a temp file instead of stdout**, so grepping stdout for a
success marker reports the object as absent. That briefly made the *new* `graph2otel` dashboard look deleted,
which is the most alarming possible false positive. Probe for the explicit `404 NotFound` and treat anything
else as present — never the reverse.

Both belong with the already-recorded `gcx` traps on #309: the ambient current-context pointing at an
unrelated customer stack, and `list` silently truncating at `--limit 50`. Every one of the four produces a
confident wrong answer rather than an error.

### Reversibility

The six manifests remain in git at `97e08b6~1` and can be re-published. They will **not** rebuild identically:
the v1 generator is gone, so restoring them means restoring the files, not regenerating them. That is
deliberate and is why #399 was a breaking change.

body:
## Incident

Camden startup at `2026-07-27T07:59Z` on `2cdd71e` exposed several remaining warning classes after #396/#397 deployed.

The two original status defects are fixed in this same run: `intune.connectors` performs its expected Exchange skip without a degraded summary; `purview.retention_labels` now classifies the live DataInsights wrapper as `permission_denied`; the former `intune.updates` decode warning is absent.

Remaining findings to evaluate:

| class | live observation |
| --- | --- |
| Shared Intune export failure | five collectors complete an export but call `GET ""`: `intune.config_profile_device_status`, `intune.device_boot_security`, `intune.config_assignment_status`, `intune.device_attestation`, `intune.autopilot_deployment_scripts` |
| Wire-value drift | `entra.recommendations.recommendation=insiderRiskPolicy`; `intune.config_profiles.odata_type=#microsoft.graph.iosDeviceFeaturesConfiguration`; `intune.cert_inventory.certificate_status=Issued` |
| Intune query-broker throttling | two `intune.scripts` health-script `runSummary` calls return 500 `Rate limit reached because of too many requests to query broker` |
| Intune overview throttling | one `intune.config_profiles` child `deviceStatusOverview` returns 429 after retries |
| OTLP old-timestamp rejection | Grafana Loki rejects records older than its seven-day acceptance boundary during startup/backfill |
| Expected informational paths | Exchange connectors 501, cloud-only sync-error skip, Purview DataInsights permission block, blob metric-gate summaries |

## Operating rules

- Trace each warning to a source before changing code; no symptom suppression.
- Probe as `graph2otel-poller` where the committed/live wire shape is required.
- Apply only targeted fixes supported by live evidence.
- Preserve records: unexpected enum members remain report-only and must not be dropped.
- No live tenant mutation without explicit scope and approval.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Root cause of the shared empty export download URL is live-measured and fixed with a failing regression test
- [x] Each unexpected wire value is either mapped from live evidence or explicitly recorded as intentionally report-only
- [x] Query-broker and overview throttling are classified as expected transient behavior or fixed at the responsible request fan-out/rate-limit seam
- [x] Old OTLP timestamps are classified against intended backfill semantics; any clear local defect receives a regression test
- [x] Expected informational paths remain unchanged
- [x] Focused tests prove each bug fix RED then GREEN
- [x] `make check` and `make grafana-check` green
- [ ] Camden startup/status verified on the deployed commit

comments.body:
### Live-measured root cause: empty export URL

`[live-measured 2026-07-27, #398, n=5]`

The five failing jobs were persisted with `created_at` values between `07:58:40Z` and `07:58:42Z`, immediately before the `2cdd71e` process started at `07:59:03Z`. The new process correctly adopted them.

At startup each first terminal poll reported `status=completed` while `url` was still empty, and `internal/exportjob` immediately called the downloader with `""`. A read-only poll of the exact same five job IDs as `graph2otel-poller` later returned:

- `status=completed`
- response key `url` present and non-empty
- `snapshotUrl` absent
- `expirationDateTime` around `2026-07-27T13:59Z`

Verdict: this is not a field rename and not five report-specific failures. The Intune export API publishes `completed` before the SAS URL is consistently readable. `exportjob.poll` must treat `completed + empty url` as not-yet-downloadable and continue its existing bounded-backoff poll rather than returning a terminal response.

### Throttling verdict

`intune.scripts` is a retry-classification bug. The live response is HTTP 500 but its exact body says `Rate limit reached because of too many requests to query broker. Please retry after sometime.` Kiota retries only 429/503/504, while graph2otel's workload transport observes only 429. The sequential collector therefore receives a terminal error for an explicitly transient throttle.

Targeted fix: retry only HTTP 500 responses containing that exact query-broker signature, outside Kiota but around the normal instrumented/rate-limited physical request path. Preserve generic 500 behavior and the final response body after exhaustion; count each recognised response in bounded throttle self-observability.

The single `intune.config_profiles` 429 is expected transient behavior after the existing limiter/backoff/retry path exhausted. The collector is sequential, preserves successful sibling profiles, and already has a partial-failure regression test. No numeric quota change is justified from n=1; changing the broad Intune-general budget would be a guess.

### Old-timestamp and expected-path verdicts

The OTLP 400 is the already documented Grafana Cloud seven-day acceptance boundary (`docs/signals.md`, live-measured under #226), not a timestamp-mapping regression. graph2otel intentionally preserves source event time and remains backend-neutral; it warns when an explicit cold-start lookback exceeds seven days but does not clamp every sink. Blob recovery and a warm checkpoint after an outage can therefore reach Grafana's boundary, where rejection is per-entry and loud. A universal seven-day drop would silently impose Grafana policy on other OTLP sinks; a configurable emitter-boundary age policy is a product/config seam rather than a targeted bug fix, so #398 will not add it by implication.

The following startup lines are expected and unchanged:

- Exchange connectors 501 on an unprovisioned connector type: clean per-type skip after #396.
- cloud-only directory sync: informational skip.
- Purview DataInsights app-only block: now classified `permission_denied` after #396.
- blob metric-gate summaries: normal ingestion accounting.
- one `config_profiles` 429 after existing retries: partial source failure is honest; successful sibling profiles remain emitted.

Implementation complete and final review clean.

Live evidence and fixes:

- `[live-measured 2026-07-27, #398, n=5]` The five adopted Intune export jobs returned `status=completed` before their SAS `url` was populated; the same job IDs later returned non-empty URLs. The poller now keeps polling a completed job until its URL is readable.
- Added the live wire values `insiderRiskPolicy`, `#microsoft.graph.iosDeviceFeaturesConfiguration`, and title-case certificate status `Issued` without dropping or rewriting log twins.
- The Intune query broker disguises throttling as HTTP 500 with the exact message `Rate limit reached because of too many requests to query broker. Please retry after sometime.` A narrow GET/HEAD retry handles only that signature, shares the existing total retry budget, preserves response bodies, and reports it through the existing throttle signal. Generic HTTP 500 responses are unchanged.
- The isolated `deviceStatusOverview` 429 is an expected transient after the existing limiter/retry path; sibling profiles remain available. No code change.
- Grafana rejected source events outside its seven-day Loki boundary. Source timestamps are correct and graph2otel remains backend-neutral; no universal seven-day drop was added.
- Exchange 501, cloud-only sync skip, Purview DataInsights permission block, and blob gate summaries remain their intended informational/classified paths.

TDD evidence includes RED then GREEN regression coverage for completed-without-URL exports, all three live enum values, exact/generic/exhausted/read-error query-broker responses, transport placement, and mixed 429/500 shared-budget behavior.

Verification on the final reviewed tree:

- `make check` — green
- `make grafana-check` — green; 330/330 metric coverage, 116 tests
- `git diff --check` — green
- Final adversarial review — no critical, important, or minor findings

Deployment verification is deliberately left open because the maintainer asked this run to stop after commit and push.

`intune.updates` skips every live Windows feature update profile because `graphDate.UnmarshalJSON` accepts only `YYYY-MM-DD`, while the endpoint returns a full RFC3339 timestamp.

GET /beta/deviceManagement/windowsFeatureUpdateProfiles -> 200, 2 rows
endOfSupportDate -> "2028-10-10T00:00:00Z" on both rows

body:
## Defect

The record-outcome integration in `f7339e8` records a `source_error` inside `collectors.GetAllValuesRecorded` before a collector can apply its established graceful-unavailable classification. Commit `2074e01` then exposes that stale cause as collector availability.

Two live paths are misclassified on camden for tenant `4b8c18bd-2f9f-4227-af55-9f1061cf9c32`:

| collector | wire result | established meaning | current incorrect availability |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `intune.connectors` | `GET /v1.0/deviceManagement/exchangeConnectors` → 501 `NotSupported`; three records from other connector sub-fetches still emitted | Exchange connector type is not provisioned; graceful per-type skip (#51) | `degraded/source_error` |
| `purview.retention_labels` | both retention endpoints → 500 wrapping `DataInsightsRequestError` + `Forbidden` | known total app-only permission block (#109), even with `RecordsManagement.Read.All` in token | `failed/source_error` |

This is not a transient upstream outage. Loki shows the same Exchange signature since 2026-07-15 and the Purview signature since 2026-07-16. Direct probes as `graph2otel-poller` reproduced both on 2026-07-27.

## Root cause

`GetAllValuesRecorded` calls `recordPartialPageFailure(..., CauseForError(err))` for an immediate first-page error. The recorder is additive and has no way for the caller to remove or replace that provisional `source_error` after it recognizes an expected unavailable signature.

The current tests assert returned errors and emitted signals, but do not pin the final summarized outcome for the live Exchange 501 or DataInsights-Forbidden paths. The existing retention outcome test covers literal HTTP 403 only; `isRetentionForbidden` does not recognize the live DataInsights-Forbidden wrapper.

## Required behavior

- An unprovisioned Exchange connector sub-fetch must not make an otherwise successful `intune.connectors` run degraded. The other connector signals remain valid.
- A total live DataInsights-Forbidden result for `purview.retention_labels` must classify as `blocked/permission_denied`, matching #292's binding rule that a total permission failure is blocked. It must not report a generic source failure.
- Genuine 5xx/source failures and later-page failures must remain failures; do not broaden the graceful predicates.
- Preserve the reconciliation equations and bounded causes from #269.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Failing outcome-level test reproduces the live Exchange 501 plus successful sibling sub-fetches and expects a clean run
- [x] Failing outcome-level test reproduces both live DataInsights-Forbidden 500 wrappers and expects `failure/permission_denied` → `blocked/permission_denied`
- [x] Genuine source failures and partial-page failures retain `source_error`
- [x] Existing signal output and graceful-skip behavior remain unchanged
- [x] Camden status page verified after deployment
- [x] `make check` and `make grafana-check` green

Related: #51, #109, #269, #292, #395.

comments.body:
## Root-cause verdict — 2026-07-27

**Evidence class: live-measured (2026-07-27, this issue), plus retained production logs.** No tenant mutation was performed.

### Timeline and deployment correlation

- Current camden image: `ghcr.io/rknightion/graph2otel:main`, revision `14e5dcf57785efd6763ba1fa9f71ac372ddae313`, started `2026-07-27T04:01:24Z`.
- The first `graph2otel.collector.availability` samples for all three bad states appear at `2026-07-26T13:15:00Z`, after the new record-outcome + availability surface deployed.
- The underlying wire conditions predate that surface:
  - Exchange connector 501: 1,135 retained log occurrences, first `2026-07-15T22:20:48Z`.
  - Feature-profile date decode: 542 retained log occurrences, first `2026-07-20T08:51:02Z` (when the previously empty endpoint acquired rows).
  - Purview DataInsights-Forbidden: 616 retained log occurrences, first `2026-07-16T07:16:56Z`.
- Therefore the overnight observation is a visibility change, not a simultaneous upstream incident.

### Live probes as the production identity

Token app ID `2c92ce28-126c-47c1-82b0-410b64502989` (`graph2otel-poller`) carries the required roles: `DeviceManagementServiceConfig.Read.All`, `DeviceManagementConfiguration.Read.All`, and `RecordsManagement.Read.All`.

| endpoint | live result |
| --- | --- |
| `/v1.0/deviceManagement/exchangeConnectors` | 501 `NotSupported` |
| `/beta/deviceManagement/exchangeConnectors` | 501 `NotSupported` |
| `/beta/deviceManagement/windowsFeatureUpdateProfiles` | 200, two rows; both `endOfSupportDate="2028-10-10T00:00:00Z"` |
| `/v1.0` and `/beta` retention labels | 500 `UnknownError`, inner `DataInsightsRequestError` / `Forbidden` |
| `/v1.0` and `/beta` retention event types | same 500 / DataInsights-Forbidden |

### Per-collector classification

1. **`intune.connectors`: known tenant capability state plus code regression.** The 501 means no Exchange connector is provisioned and has been an intentional graceful per-type skip since #51. The other sub-fetches emitted three records. `f7339e8` now records `source_error` before the collector suppresses the known 501, and `2074e01` exposes it as `degraded/source_error`. The data path did not newly fail; the status classification is wrong. Follow-up: #396.

2. **`intune.updates`: real graph2otel decode defect, exposed by tenant data.** The beta CSDL committed at `spec/graph-beta-snapshot.json` says `endOfSupportDate` is `Edm.DateTimeOffset`, and the wire sends RFC3339. The mapper incorrectly claims `Edm.Date` and accepts date-only text; its explicitly docs-derived fixture pinned that incorrect assumption. Both real profiles are skipped each cycle. Follow-up: #397.

3. **`purview.retention_labels`: known app-only limitation plus code regression.** #109 established this exact DataInsights-Forbidden signature as the permanent app-only gap and converted it to graceful skip. Outcome accounting now pre-records `source_error`, while `isRetentionForbidden` only promotes literal HTTP 403 to `permission_denied`. Per #292's binding semantics, this total permission failure should be `blocked/permission_denied`, not `failed/source_error`. Follow-up: #396.

### Blast radius

Current camden census: 82 healthy, 39 healthy-empty, 20 disabled, four covered, and only these three failure-oriented rows. The affected collectors have stable sub-five-second cycle durations. There is no evidence of a shared Graph/auth/transport outage.

No code or configuration was changed during this investigation.
Investigation complete. The durable root-cause report and live probe receipts are in the preceding comment. Code follow-ups are #396 and #397; no tenant or production changes were made.

**Outcome**

Operators can plan, execute, inspect, resume and abort a log-only replay into a
sealed local spool without opening or modifying production checkpoints.

**Scope**

- Add `replay plan|run|status|abort` and the canonical
  `<collector-name>@<transport>` adapter-ID grammar.
- Add the explicit `replaycontract.Descriptor`/factory seam as an option on
  each existing registration path. No reflection or inferred eligibility.
- Couple descriptors to `collectordoc.Rows`; generate `replay_adapter` and
  drift-gate descriptor ID, transport, production `ConflictsWith` facts,
  operations, event names and forbidden metrics.
- Implement manifest canonicalization, duplicate-ID, same-name dual-transport

  validation and strict log-only emission.
- Implement the framed base-record spool, self-contained commit footers,
  hash-chained `commit.wal`, state snapshot, result hash, stable
  record/delivery IDs and local report.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] `plan` rejects a bare name and accepts only `name@transport`.
- [ ] A manifest containing both `x@graph` and `x@blob` fails
      `dual_transport` before clients/state are opened.

**Outcome**

Ship the accepted #290 design as a descriptor-gated, log-only replay workflow
with isolated local extraction and optional OTLP delivery, while keeping every
implementation unit and dependency reconstructable from this tracker.

**Binding decisions**

- Adapter identity is canonical `name@transport`.
- Manifest validation enforces same-name transport XOR and every
  drift-gated production `ConflictsWith` pair.
- Replay eligibility is an explicit registration/collectordoc descriptor, not
  reflection or interface-shape inference.
- Metrics, including `HistogramCtx`, are forbidden.
- Local base-record chunks plus the WAL are authoritative; committed chunks
  resume without refetch.
- Undated rows drop/count and seal a partial local result; partial results are

comments.body:
## Closed by maintainer decision 2026-07-28 — dropped entirely, not deferred

Maintainer, verbatim: *"I think that goes well beyond the scope of a realtime poller that we have lets close the issue and drop it entirely."*

That is a scope decision about what graph2otel IS, and it settles the whole programme: this tracker and all seven children (#383, #384, #385, #386, #387, #388, #389) are closed. **This is not a "later" — do not reopen it as a backlog item.** A future reader finding a design this detailed and assuming it was merely paused would be wrong.

### What is being given up, stated honestly

Deterministic isolated replay would have provided an operator-driven way to re-extract a historical range into a sealed, hash-chained local spool, isolated from production checkpoints, with optional OTLP delivery gated on the backend accept window. Nothing else in the project does this: `internal/checkpoint` is a live, mutable, single-file-per-key store with no chunking, WAL or hash chain, so the capability genuinely does not exist elsewhere and now will not.

The practical consequence: reprocessing history still means cold-starting against production checkpoint state, with all the risk that implies. If that ever becomes a real operational need, this tracker is the design record — but it needs re-deciding on its merits, not resuming.

### Design work that was NOT done, so nobody assumes it exists

The seven issues describe the contract only at concept level. Five things were never pinned and would have had to be frozen before any parallel build: the Go type and factory signature for the descriptor, the manifest file schema, the WAL entry format byte-for-byte, the replay-state key scheme, and the CLI flag surface beyond `plan|run|status|abort`.

### One inconsistency found while assessing it, recorded because it outlives this tracker

#385 specified a **167h45m** send-age check (168h minus a fixed 15m margin). Production's own guard in `internal/telemetry/horizon.go` uses **165h** (168h minus 3h), and that 3h margin was live-measured against a real rejection that was only ~1h past the limit. Two different margins for the same backend constraint, with the replay path using the *tighter* one and no stated reason.

Replay is gone, so the conflict is moot — but if a second send-age check is ever written anywhere in this repo, it must reuse `EventHorizon` rather than invent its own margin.

## Mission

Provide supported companion integrations for non-Graph signals and non-Grafana SIEM schemas while keeping the graph2otel binary OTLP-push-only.

## Source of truth

This epic is the coding-agent launch prompt for the **integrations** theme from the 2026-07-25 comprehensive audit. Read this body and every child issue in full, including comments, before implementation. Child issues own their exact evidence, API contracts, acceptance criteria, and prior-decision checks.

## Binding decisions

- Use maintained Alloy/OTel Collector edge components instead of adding a generic listener/output plugin system.
- Azure flow access is scoped to an explicit storage target, never subscription-wide discovery.
- Entity/high-volume detail remains logs; bounded health/parse dimensions may be metrics.
- Canonical graph2otel attributes remain available alongside transformed schemas.

## Frozen child set

- [ ] #371 — feat(integrations): ship a supported syslog and CEF companion configuration
- [ ] #372 — spike(integrations): design an explicit-storage VNet flow-log companion
- [ ] #373 — feat(integrations): publish OCSF and ECS mapping packs for graph2otel logs

## Sequencing

1. Start with P0/P1 correctness defects and any shared catalog/config seams.
2. Land one independently green child at a time, closing it from a conventional commit on `main`.
3. Spikes first obtain their named evidence; **close no-build/no-data** when the evidence does not support implementation.
4. Reconcile generated catalogs/docs/dashboards after each signal change.
5. Finish with live read-back or render/query receipts where the child requires them.

## Parallel lanes

- Syslog/CEF reference pipeline and fixtures.
- VNet flow-log storage feasibility.
- Generated OCSF/ECS mapping packs.

Freeze shared names, signatures, config keys, signal names, and generated-schema changes before parallel work. One file has one owner; composition roots, registries, catalogs, and generators get a single wiring pass.

## Operating rules

- Strict TDD: failing test, observe the intended failure, minimal implementation, green, refactor.
- Validate Microsoft behavior from the wire as `graph2otel-poller`; docs-only evidence is not mapper evidence.
- New permissions, licences, tenant configuration, or data-generation actions require explicit maintainer approval.
- Metrics stay bounded and tenant-shaped; per-entity detail is a log twin.
- Do not re-open the rejected Event Hub/Log Analytics, dual-transport, Redis/cache, HA, typed-SDK expansion, or engine-side blob-dedupe designs.

comments.body: I think this is all out of scope for this poller

## Closed by maintainer decision 2026-07-28 — the whole epic, all three children

Decided in a decision pass covering the full post-v1 backlog. #372 went first, on the flow-log question: *"Flow logs are out of scope close the issue accordingly."* Asked whether the same reasoning covered the remaining two, the maintainer chose to **close the whole epic**.

Closing #371 (syslog and CEF companion), #372 (VNet flow-log companion) and #373 (OCSF and ECS mapping packs) with it. **Dropped, not deferred.**

### The reasoning, so it is not re-litigated

The same argument that removed flow logs covers the rest: graph2otel is a realtime poller of Microsoft Graph and its sibling APIs, and shipping supported syslog receiver configurations for other vendors' appliances — or transform packs for SIEM schemas it does not itself speak — is adjacent work that expands what the project is responsible for maintaining without improving what it collects.

Worth recording that **none of the three ever threatened the OTLP-push-only invariant**, and that was checked rather than assumed. #371's listener lived in Alloy/OTel Collector, a separate process; #373's transforms ran downstream of the single existing OTLP output; #372 was an *ingest* question, not an egress one. So this is a scope decision about ownership and focus, not a safety one — and the #310 annotations amendment remains the only authorized second egress path, untouched.

### What is given up

No supported path for firewall/appliance syslog into the same investigation model, and no generated OCSF/ECS mapping for graph2otel's 133 catalogued log events — so consumers feeding a non-Grafana SIEM map the fields themselves. The signal catalog (`internal/signalcatalog`, `spec/signal-catalog.json`) still exists and is still drift-gated, so anyone wanting to build such a mapping externally has the machine-readable source to do it from.
