comments.body:
## Two children closed — #353 and #367 (`2483dd4`)

Both were built from live captures taken this session rather than from documentation, per this epic's binding rule that every EXO cmdlet and report shape is preflighted live first.

- **#353** — accepted-domain posture. `Get-AcceptedDomain -ResultSize Unlimited` measured live: 4 domains, 56 fields, all `Authoritative`. `DomainType` is deliberately left unwatched by wirecheck because one observed value is not a value set, and a watchdog built on it would fire on the first legitimate `InternalRelay` domain — which is exactly the "not auto-flagged" requirement this issue set.
- **#367** — the service-health timeline. 829 posts carried inline across 100 issues, bodies max 2176 B.

### The #367 finding other children of this epic should know about

**The service-health issues endpoint re-serves the entire retained issue history on every poll.** Today's response carried issues that opened and resolved in February. That breaks the time-windowed seen-set eviction every other checkpointed collector in this repo uses — a post would age out of the window, be re-offered, and re-emit as new. It is resolved with a watermark plus a bounded overlap instead.

Any other child here that dedupes against a full-history source has the same trap. It is not visible from the endpoint's documentation.

Also worth carrying forward: **a service-health post has no ID at all** — only `createdDateTime`, `description` and `postType` — so identity has to be derived. And first run primes without emitting, because most of that history is older than the backend's 7-day accept window and would be discarded by the horizon guard rather than populate anything.

### Remaining shape of this epic

16 children open. Four need a scope grant first (#360 `ChannelMember.Read.All`, #361 `CloudApp-Discovery.Read.All`, #364 `CallRecords.Read.All`, #369 a Backup service prerequisite); #363 needs a new narrow Exchange RBAC role designed and granted; #370 needs a maintainer-created deliberate DLP match.

Ready now with no human gate: **#359** (mailbox usage/quota — reuses `m365.storage`'s already-hardened report pattern), **#356** (audit-bypass, one cmdlet, high security value), **#354** (MDO assignment/precedence, the most probe-heavy of the EXO set), and the two hunting-table spikes **#365**/**#366**, which may legitimately close no-data.

## Maintainer decision pass — 2026-07-28. Four children unblocked, two parked.

Results from the full post-v1 decision pass that govern this epic:

### 1. Read-scope consent extended to post-v1

The 2026-07-18 standing consent — grant read-only scopes to `graph2otel-poller` without prompting, record each grant — now covers the post-v1 epics. Unblocked here: **`ChannelMember.Read.All` (#360)**, **`CloudApp-Discovery.Read.All` (#361)**, **`CallRecords.Read.All` (#364)**.

Read-only only. Write scopes, tenant mutations and anything irreversible still come back to the maintainer.

### 2. #363 — design AND grant the narrow Exchange RBAC role

Approved in one pass rather than a design-then-approve split. Work out the minimum role that permits `Get-InboxRule -IncludeHidden`, create it, and **prove the denial boundary rather than assuming it** — a role that permits more than intended is exactly what this issue exists to prevent. Record the definition, the denial evidence and the per-mailbox fan-out cost on #363. Microsoft's own docs say Global Reader is explicitly insufficient, which is what makes a purpose-built role necessary.

### 3. Parked, each with a named unblock condition

- **#369 (M365 Backup)** — a paid add-on almost certainly not provisioned. Nothing to read; building now would mean a documentation-shaped mapper for a service returning nothing. Unblocks when the service actually exists.
- **#370 (DLP mapper)** — needs a deliberately created DLP match on the tenant. The whole point is proving `DetectedValues` never reach telemetry, which cannot be demonstrated on data that never matched. Unblocks when the maintainer creates one and says so.

### 4. Carry forward from #367, which closed this session

**The service-health issues endpoint re-serves the entire retained issue history on every poll** — today's response carried issues that opened and resolved in February. That breaks the time-windowed seen-set eviction every other checkpointed collector in this repo uses. Any other child here that dedupes against a full-history source has the same trap, and it is invisible from the endpoint's documentation. #367 resolved it with a watermark plus a bounded overlap.

Also: a service-health post carries **no ID at all**, so identity had to be derived.

### Where this epic stands

Closed this session: **#353, #367**. Unblocked with no human gate: **#354, #355, #356, #357, #358, #359, #362, #365, #366, #368** (existing scopes/engines) plus **#360, #361, #364** (consent extension) and **#363** (role approved). Parked: **#369, #370**.

Highest value-per-effort next, unchanged by this pass: **#359** (mailbox usage — reuses `m365.storage`'s already-hardened report pattern), **#356** (audit-bypass — one cmdlet, high security value), **#354** (MDO assignment and precedence — the most probe-heavy of the EXO set, so scope its probe tightly first).

## Session progress — 2026-07-28. Four children closed, one measured and parked with a real cost question.

### Closed

- **#356** (`04653d2`) — mailbox audit bypass. `live-measured`: 242 associations, **every one `AuditBypassEnabled: false`**, dominated by `SystemMailbox`/`TenantSetting` objects rather than human mailboxes; `RecipientTypeDetails` absent on every row. Two gauges, because "nothing is bypassed" and "the cmdlet returned nothing" must not be the same series. The twin is emitted ONLY for bypass-ENABLED associations — a deliberate inversion of the one-twin-per-entity default, since 242 findingless records per cycle would train an operator to ignore the event name.
- **#359** (`04653d2`) — mailbox usage, quota state, inactivity, reusing `m365.storage`'s report transport.
- **#357** and **#358** (`4ca32f7`) — outbound spam and connection filter posture.

### Three wire facts this epic should carry forward

**The two mailbox-usage AGGREGATE reports re-serve their whole period on every poll**, one row per day. Only the most recent `Report Date` is emitted, chosen by parsed date rather than arrival order. This is the same full-history re-serve shape #367 hit on service health — it is **not** specific to that endpoint, and any other child deduping against a report-style source should assume it until measured otherwise.

**Neither `Get-HostedOutboundSpamFilterPolicy` nor `Get-HostedConnectionFilterPolicy` takes `ResultSize`.** Checked against the cmdlet reference rather than assumed from the siblings that do pin it — so the absence is a verified fact, not a forgotten guard.

**An empty array is a measured fact, not an absence.** The connection-filter IP allow/block lists are empty on this tenant, and the lengths are emitted as `0` rather than left absent: a non-empty allow list *is* the finding, so a vanished series and a measured zero are opposite readings.

### #355 — probed, NOT built, and the blocker is a cost decision

`Get-MailboxPermission` returns **HTTP 400 `BadRequest: Invalid Operation`** without an `-Identity`. It cannot be called tenant-wide, so the collector is inherently `1 + 2N` calls per cycle (enumerate, then FullAccess and SendAs per mailbox) with no batch form on this transport. Free at N=2 here; not free on a real tenant.

Worse, both cmdlets return an **implicit `NT AUTHORITY\SELF` row on every mailbox** (SID `S-1-5-10`) that is not a delegation at all — and on this tenant that is the *only* row either returns. A naive mapper would emit one bogus FullAccess and one bogus SendAs delegation per mailbox forever. Also: `AccessRights` is a single **comma-joined** string (`"FullAccess, ReadPermission"`), not two array elements, and `PrimarySmtpAddress`/`TrusteeWithPrimarySmtpAddress` came back null on that row.

Full detail on #355. What it needs before code is a decision on the fan-out cost — probably a cap or a `HighVolume`-style opt-in — not more measurement.

### Where this epic stands

Remaining open with no human gate: **#354** (MDO assignment/precedence — the most probe-heavy of the EXO set, scope its probe tightly), **#362**, **#365**, **#366**, **#368**, plus **#360, #361, #364** (consent extension, scopes to grant and record) and **#363** (role approved; the denial boundary must be PROVEN, not assumed). Parked: **#369, #370**. **#355** is measured and awaiting a cost decision.

## Session progress — 2026-07-28. **#363 closed (premise disproved), #355 decided and parked with the design frozen.**

### #363 closed — no Exchange RBAC role was created, because none is needed

The approval to design and create a narrow role stands **unused rather than spent**. `Get-InboxRule -IncludeHidden` already works app-only under the poller's existing rights (Global Reader + Security Reader). This issue's evidence class was `docs-only`, and Microsoft's documented claim that Global Reader is insufficient does not hold on this tenant — another entry for this repo's "wire over docs" ledger.

Three things worth carrying:

**`-IncludeHidden` is load-bearing, not a refinement.** Same mailbox, same session: **with** the flag returns 1 rule, **without** returns **0**. Every inbox rule on this tenant is hidden. A collector built without it returns zero rows tenant-wide and reports clean success forever — a total blind spot for the exact persistence mechanism the issue exists to catch.

**Exchange RBAC denial is provable cheaply, and was proved by invocation.** Unauthorized cmdlets are not rejected — they are **removed from the session**, so they fail `CommandNotFoundException` before touching a target. `New/Set/Remove/Disable/Enable-InboxRule`, `Set/New/Remove-Mailbox`, `Set-TransportRule`, `New-ManagementRole` are all ABSENT; `Get-InboxRule` is PRESENT. Each mutation was actually invoked against a deliberately nonexistent rule id, so an authorized call would have failed harmlessly on "not found" — making permitted and denied distinguishable without risking a change. Nothing was mutated.

**No forwarding rule exists here to map against.** The only rule on the tenant is a default Junk E-mail Rule; `ForwardTo`/`RedirectTo`/`ForwardAsAttachmentTo` are absent or false everywhere. Same shape as #356 and #355 — one observed rule is not a rule shape.

### #355 — decided: park the build, freeze the design. And a correction to its own probe comment

**The earlier claim that `NT AUTHORITY\SELF` is "the ONLY row either cmdlet returns" is WRONG.** Probing *every* mailbox rather than the two human ones found a genuine non-self, non-inherited delegation: `Discovery Management` holding `FullAccess` on the Discovery Search Mailbox, with a real object SID. **So the mapper does have a real row to be written against** — the strongest argument for not building has dissolved. Also: `NT AUTHORITY\SELF` is not one row shape; the same SID appears twice on one mailbox with different rights, so deduping by SID silently drops one.

Cost measured directly: `Get-MailboxPermission` 846 ms + `Get-RecipientPermission` 602 ms = **1,448 ms per mailbox**, `1 + 2N`, no batch form. That is **~24 min/cycle at 1,000 mailboxes and ~121 min at 5,000** — it cannot be a default-on collector on a real tenant.

**The obvious opt-in interface is the wrong one.** `HighVolume` means rate scales with **traffic**; per-mailbox fan-out scales with **tenant size** — a 5,000-mailbox tenant with zero mail flow still pays the full two hours. `Experimental` is reserved for genuine Graph beta (#183) and this is EXO PowerShell. So this needs a **third** gate: explicit per-tenant opt-in, an explicit load-validated mailbox cap, and — the part that matters — **truncation surfaced as a covered/total signal, not a log line**, because a cap that silently covers the first N reports clean success over an unknown remainder.

Parked rather than built because that fan-out gate is a **shared seam serving #355 and #363 both** (`1+2N` and `1+N`, same transport, same scaling), and building it inside one collector would force a rewrite when the other lands. **Named unblock:** agreement on the shared gate (opt-in key, cap, default, covered/total signal). No further measurement is needed for either issue — cost, authorization and row shape are all live-measured.

### Epic status

Closed this session: **#363**. Decided and parked with a named unblock: **#355**. Parked unchanged: **#369, #370**.

Untouched this session, still open with no human gate: **#354** (MDO assignment/precedence — most probe-heavy, scope its probe tightly), **#362**, **#365**, **#366**, **#368**, plus **#360, #361, #364** (consent extension — scopes still to be granted and recorded).

## Session progress — 2026-07-28 (cont). **#355 and #363 are BUILT and shipped**, plus a red-CI fix that was not ours.

### Shipped

- **`fed98f8`** — the shared per-mailbox fan-out gate (`internal/exofanout` + `config.ExoPerMailboxConfig`). One opt-in (`exo_per_mailbox.enabled`) and one cap (default 250) gate every EXO collector whose cost is linear in mailbox count, and one `Get-Mailbox` enumeration is shared between them.
- **`a936984`** — `m365.mailbox_delegation` (#355) and `m365.inbox_rules` (#363), both closed.

Census **154 → 156** logical collectors, **157 → 159** registration-path candidates. `make check` exit 0; alert rules re-pushed (`matched_content_ungrouped`).

### Three things this epic should carry forward

**`HighVolume` is the wrong gate for per-mailbox fan-out, and reaching for it would mislead an operator.** HighVolume means rate scales with **traffic**; per-mailbox cost scales with **tenant size** — an idle 5,000-mailbox tenant still pays the full ~2 hours. `Experimental` is worse still: reserved for genuine Graph beta (#183), and this is a GA PowerShell transport. The third gate now exists and any future per-mailbox EXO collector should use it rather than invent a fourth.

**The gate is self-maintaining by interface, not by name list.** `collectors.PerMailboxCollector` (`PerMailbox() bool`) marks a collector as fan-out-gated, so the composition root covers a future one the moment it implements it. A hand-kept name list in the composition root is exactly how a cost gate silently stops covering a new collector — the same failure shape as the collectordoc gates going green over an invisible collector.

**Truncation is a signal, not a floor.** Both collectors emit `mailboxes_covered` alongside `mailboxes_total` every cycle, so a capped scan states that it was partial. A cap that quietly took the first N would report clean success over an unknown remainder.

### A time bomb in #367's tests turned CI red on main, independent of this work

Fixed here because it was blocking. The service-health post fixtures hard-coded `2026-07-18` issue dates, which aged past the collector's **7-day horizon during 2026-07-28** — four tests went red on a tree that had been green hours earlier, with nobody having edited anything. Confirmed by running the package at `8296010`, whose CI had passed that morning: it fails there too.

**An absolute date in a fixture for a horizon- or watermark-gated collector is a calendar-triggered failure.** Recent timestamps are now substituted relative to now at fixture-build time and evaluated **once per test binary** — evaluating per call would let a fixture and its assertion straddle a second boundary and reintroduce flakiness. The deliberately ancient February posts stay absolute on purpose: "older than any watermark" does not rot. Any other collector here with a horizon and dated fixtures has the same latent bomb.

### Where this epic stands

Closed this session: **#353, #356, #357, #358, #359, #367, #363, #355**. Parked: **#369, #370**.

Still open with no human gate: **#354** (MDO assignment/precedence — most probe-heavy, scope its probe tightly), **#362**, **#365**, **#366**, **#368**, plus **#360, #361, #364** (consent extension — scopes still to be granted and recorded).

## Session progress — 2026-07-28 (cont). **Two collectors shipped, five children closed. Every remaining open child is either parked or blocked on tenant data.**

### Shipped — `f7745e8`

- **`m365.collaboration_activity` (#362)** — daily per-workload adoption and staleness from the Graph usage reports. `never_active` is the bucket worth watching: a licensed user who has never touched a workload is a licence question, and it is derived from an EMPTY `Last Activity Date` rather than coerced to an epoch.
- **`mdca.cloud_discovery` (#361)** — the shadow-IT apps Defender for Cloud Apps has discovered from uploaded traffic logs, plus stream health. `CloudApp-Discovery.Read.All` granted 2026-07-28T11:00Z (appRole `<guid-2>`, assignment `NhU3E1CZiEmQ9DQ1ZkVngVuGxKf7Y-FMmqKOK5JNymM`). Live: 6 streams, 100 apps on the first page with a nextLink, 28 categories.

Census **160 → 162** logical collectors, **163 → 165** registration-path candidates. `make check` exit 0; alert rules re-pushed (`matched_content_ungrouped`).

### Closed no-data, each with a named unblock

**#360** — every channel on both teams is `standard`; zero private, zero shared. `allMembers` has nothing to be called against, and this issue's own scope says to skip standard channels. `ChannelMember.Read.All` granted and recorded. Worth keeping: widening to standard channels would emit `team_members × standard_channels` records that all say the same thing, since standard-channel membership *is* the team's membership — the private/shared case is interesting precisely because its membership differs.

**#364** — `/communications/callRecords` → 200 with 0 rows. `CallRecords.Read.All` granted and recorded. The design risk here is the late-arriving `version`, and a `WindowCollector` deduping on `id+version` is only correct if late arrival behaves as documented — which on this project's record is not a safe assumption. Not built on an unverified arrival model.

**#365** — `CampaignInfo | summarize n=count()` → **0**, schema returned (8 columns), no new scope needed. `HighVolume` requires a *measured* volume figure and there is nothing to measure; `CampaignType`/`CampaignSubType` have zero observed values, not merely one.

**#349** — `DisruptionAndResponseEvents` → **0 rows**, 38-column schema returned. The blob-vs-hunting transport choice is undecidable without rows: there is no container to enumerate for a table with no data, and #241 already established the streaming-support docs cannot stand in for that enumeration.

### #350 is now a build, not a spike — full measurement recorded on the issue

Worth reading before anyone picks it up, because it was expensive to derive:

- `ExposureGraphNodes | summarize count()` → **993,292** (77 s).
- `ExposureGraphEdges | summarize count()` → **HTTP 504 after 150 s**. Not "too many rows" — a bare integer count does not complete. **Do not re-run it.** Any edge work must prune before aggregating.
- **Two labels are 99.7% of the graph** (`mdcSecurityRecommendation` 618k + `Cve` 372k). Everything worth twinning — 254 AI agents, 163 devices, 127 OAuth apps, 6 users — is the remaining ~2,900 nodes. The bounded subset falls out of the data rather than being a guess.
- `NodeProperties` is a `dynamicColumnValue` whose shape varies per `NodeLabel`, so it needs one sub-schema per label against captured samples. `EntityIds` entries are JSON strings needing a second decode.

### Two things this epic should carry forward

**A test can assert the right property against the wrong representation and pass over the bug.** #322's guard (on the #376 side, but the lesson is general) asserted against the recorder's *rendered* array attribute. The recorder joins a `[]string` with `","`, and `join(split(x, ","), ",") == join(x, ",")` — so a mapper that split every element rendered byte-identically and the test passed over deliberate sabotage. It now reads the mapper's `[]string` before rendering. **Any guard in this repo asserting on a rendered array is suspect.**

**The api-drift gate needs its manifest entry in the same commit as a new beta-consuming package** — `spec/graph-beta-surface.json` plus the census line in `docs/api-drift.md` plus a `make graphdrift-update`. `mdca.cloud_discovery` also needed a new `(domain, kind)` pair in `collectordoc.sections`, since MDCA had only ever had a window collector. Both gates failed loudly and correctly; budget for them.

### Where this epic stands

**Open: #350** (build, fully measured above), **#354** (MDO assignment/precedence — untouched, still the most probe-heavy; scope its preflight tightly), **#366**, **#368**. Parked unchanged: **#369, #370**.

## Session progress — 2026-07-28 (later)

`4ed2c00` — **#354 closed**, `defender.mdo_rules` shipped. The MDO/EOP protection-policy rule layer on the existing EXO path. **All ten rule cmdlets preflighted 200 under the grants the poller already holds** — three carry rules on m7kni, seven are authorized-and-empty (preset policies, no custom rules), none denied. No new grant, and nothing here was blocked.

It answers what `defender.mdo_policies` structurally cannot: who a policy reaches and in what precedence order, plus which policies exist that **no enabled rule applies** — configured-but-inert, which needs both sides of the join and is why the seven policy cmdlets are deliberately re-read here.

Census 162 → **164** logical collectors, 165 → **167** registration-path candidates. `make check` exit 0.

One finding worth carrying beyond this issue: the sabotage pass caught a guard that protected nothing. `telemetry.SetStrs` applies its own non-empty filter before writing to `Attrs`, so an "assert the key is absent from `Attrs`" test cannot detect a mapper that returns an empty slice where it should return absent. That is the same class as the `telemetrytest` join blindness found on #322 — **`Attrs` sits downstream of two lossy steps, so guards about emptiness or element boundaries must assert on the mapper's own return value.** Full detail on #354.

## Session progress — 2026-07-28 (later). **#366 and #369 both closed no-data, each with a distinct denial shape.**

Neither needed a new scope. Both were closed on live evidence rather than on the parked assumption, and the two failed in completely different ways — which is the useful part.

### #366 — the table is REACHABLE and genuinely empty

`DataSecurityEvents | summarize n=count()` → **200, `n = 0`**, with a full **52-column** schema returned. `ThreatHunting.Read.All` was already held. Re-run independently at close time. Same shape as #365 and #349: a 200 with a schema proves reachable-and-empty, not inaccessible.

**The live schema does not match the documented one.** Microsoft's public column reference folds differently from what the endpoint returns — the wire groups fields into aggregate `*Info` objects (`ContentInfo`, `AlertInfo`, `DeviceInfo`, `ParentContentInfo`, `IrmSequenceInfo`) and carries columns the doc page never lists (`RiskyAIUsage*`, `IsIrmInteresting`). Anyone writing this mapper later must re-capture the schema rather than build from the page.

**The content-risk criterion is deliberately left OPEN, not waved through.** It cannot be answered on zero rows. `ContentInfo` is the strongest structural candidate for carrying matched *content* rather than match *metadata* — which would make it only the second content exclusion this project has ever had. Per CLAUDE.md, "awkward to model" is not "unsafe to ship", and conflating them has shipped wrong three times here, so it is recorded as a question against a real row rather than as a pre-emptive exclusion.

**Its unblock overlaps #370's.** The tenant-side Insider-Risk-to-Defender sharing opt-in **cannot be observed read-only** — an opted-out tenant and an opted-in tenant with no violations produce a byte-identical zero. If the deliberate DLP match #370 needs gets created, re-check this table at the same time; one tenant action may fire both.

### #369 — a FIFTH denial shape, and no grant would have helped

`GET /v1.0/solutions/backupRestore` → **401 `UnknownError` with an empty `message`**, identical on beta and on `serviceStatus`. Meanwhile `subscribedSkus` returns 22 SKUs with **not one containing `BACKUP`**, and `organization.assignedPlans` has no backup plan. A `GET /organization` control returned 200, so the token is healthy.

This epic's sibling #377 already tracks four denial layers a scope grant does not move. **This is a fifth and distinct one:** a JSON 401 with a generic code and an empty message, which is the service failing *before* an authorization decision can be reached. It is not Graph's authorization layer — that returns 403 `Authorization_RequestDenied` with a descriptive message, which is exactly what #334 got on the #376 side the same day for a genuinely missing app role.

**`BackupRestore-Control.Read.All` was deliberately NOT granted.** The SKU absence already answers it, and Microsoft's own doc says these APIs *"are intended for use by registered Backup Controller applications"* — so the app role may well not be sufficient on its own and `graph2otel-poller` is not in that category. Granting would have left an unused permission proving nothing. That registered-application question stays open and must be settled before anyone assumes a grant is enough if this ever unblocks.

**Named unblock:** a SKU or service plan containing `BACKUP` appears, or `/solutions/backupRestore` returns 200 instead of the 401.

### One thing worth generalising

The two closes look the same on a tracker and are opposite on the wire: **#366 is a 200 that means "we looked and there is nothing", #369 is a 401 that means "there is nothing to look at".** Both are legitimate no-data closes under this epic's rule, but only the first leaves a schema behind for whoever picks it up. Recording *which one* an issue got is the deliverable — the same distinction this epic already drew for the eight children closed under the consent extension.

### Where this epic stands

Closed this session: **#366, #369**. Parked: **#370** (needs a deliberately created DLP match — the only remaining open child, and its unblock is a maintainer tenant action).

## Session note — 2026-07-29. #370 re-validated: the DLP feed is wired and there are no matches yet. Two stale checkboxes fixed.

No child of this epic was built. **#370's premise did change materially** and is recorded on the issue, plus the #366/#369 checkboxes in the body above are now ticked to match their 2026-07-28 closes (they had been left unchecked, which is the body-contradicts-comments rot this repo's own tracker-hygiene rule exists to prevent).

### #370 — the transport half is now proven, which is new

The maintainer has configured DLP rules. Probed as `graph2otel-poller`:

```
GET /activity/feed/subscriptions/list   ->  200
  DLP.All  enabled          <-- the content type this issue needs
GET .../subscriptions/content?contentType=DLP.All&<last 23h>  ->  200  []
```

Zero content blobs across the widest single window the API allows. A control on the same token in the same run returned **7** `Audit.General` blobs over the identical window, so this is a real negative and not a broken request or an auth artifact.

**The content type is `DLP.All`, not `Audit.DLP.All` as this issue's title says.** `Audit.DLP.All` is the *permission* name; the feed's own content-type string has no `Audit.` prefix. A collector built from the issue title would request a content type the API does not have.

So: transport proven, subscription enabled, nothing has matched. Better than the parked position — the "is the feed even on" question is now answered — but it does not unblock the issue, because the deliverable is proving `DetectedValues` never reach telemetry and that cannot be demonstrated on a feed with no matches.

**Unblock, now one concrete action:** mail a document with fake-but-policy-matching content to a covered mailbox and confirm the match in Purview. Expect a lag — the `Audit.General` blobs in the window above were created up to hours after the events in them, so a same-minute empty read is not evidence the match failed to land.

### #366's unblock overlaps this one, and was re-checked in the same pass

`DataSecurityEvents | summarize n=count()` → **200, n = 0**, unchanged. Rules existing is not rules matching. When the deliberate match is created, re-check that table at the same time — one tenant action may fire both, and the sharing opt-in that gates #366 **cannot be observed read-only** (an opted-out tenant and an opted-in tenant with no violations produce a byte-identical zero).

### Epic status

**#370 is the only open child**, and its unblock is a maintainer tenant action. Everything else is closed, and the body checkboxes now agree with the comments.

## Session progress — 2026-07-29 (later). **#370 shipped. Every child of this epic is now closed.**

`df24b9f` — the DLP classification mapper, built against a deliberate match the maintainer created today. Full evidence on #370; the parts this epic should carry:

**The secret exclusion is WIDER than #100 assumed, and only a real match could have shown it.** `DetectedValues[].Value` is not the matched value — it is a **~100-135 character window of the surrounding document**, and on the live sample it leaked the tail of the preceding AWS access key ID and the start of the next section, content that was never itself a match. So the field exfiltrates arbitrary adjacent text bounded only by a character window. `Name` is separately the match verbatim. Both dropped; the whole `SensitiveInformationDetections` object goes, and every safe field sits outside it.

**A sentinel in the fixture, not a key-absence check.** The fixture deliberately KEEPS `DetectedValues` with sentinel strings in both fields, so the test proves the mapper drops them rather than proving the fixture lacks them. Same pattern as #338's process arguments, and it is now the house form for a content exclusion on this project.

**One event, two spellings.** OneDrive sends `Operation: "DLPRuleMatch"`, Exchange sends `"DlpRuleMatch"`, for the same event with different `RecordType`s (11 vs 13). The branch keys off the structural presence of `PolicyDetails` instead. A case-sensitive switch would have dropped Exchange — 1 record in 8 on the live sample, which is exactly the ratio that goes unnoticed.

**The record answered a question a scope grant would have answered worse.** The compiled DLP policy names SITs by GUID only, and `/beta/dataClassification/sensitiveTypes` 403s with a real Graph auth denial — so a scope *would* have resolved them. It was not taken, and the match record carries `SensitiveInformationTypeName` alongside `SensitiveType`, naming all 11 observed types. Better evidence too: it says which type actually fired, not which was configured.

**Two SIT names lie about jurisdiction.** `EU Passport Number` fired on a UK passport number and `EU Debit Card Number` on a UK card. Any dashboard grouping by SIT name to infer geography is wrong, and that is recorded on the attribute rather than left for someone to discover.

### Epic status: children all closed

| child | outcome |
| --- | --- |
| #353, #355, #356, #357, #358, #359, #362, #363, #367 | shipped |
| #354, #361 | shipped |
| #360, #364, #365, #366, #369 | closed no-data, each with a named unblock |
| #370 | shipped today |

The remaining unchecked boxes in the body are the epic's own *Done when* items, not children. Two of them are worth stating plainly rather than ticking:

- **Live read-back for #370 has NOT happened**, because the code is inert until a maintainer grants `ActivityFeed.ReadDlp` and adds `DLP.All` to camden's `o365_activity.content_types`. That scope was deliberately NOT taken under the standing read-scope consent: it is the one scope on this project that authorises reading matched secret *values*, and the collector dropping them is not the same as the identity being unable to read them.
- The gates are green (`make check` exit 0 at `df24b9f`).

## Phase completion — epic closed 2026-08-04. The last open item was already done.

Every child was closed by 2026-07-29. The one thing holding this epic open was the final *Done when* item: **#370's live read-back had never happened**, because the DLP mapper was inert until `ActivityFeed.ReadDlp` was granted and `DLP.All` was added to camden's `o365_activity.content_types`.

**Both had already been done.** Measured today rather than assumed — the same "a parked condition is a claim with a date on it" pattern that shipped #334, #336 and #338 on the #376 side.

### Live read-back — #370's outstanding acceptance item, now satisfied

Probed as `graph2otel-poller` against `manage.office.com`:

```
token roles          ->  ActivityFeed.Read, ActivityFeed.ReadDlp     <-- granted
subscriptions/list   ->  200   DLP.All  enabled
content?contentType=DLP.All&<last 23h>  ->  200, 1 blob
camden config.yaml   ->  content_types: [Audit.Exchange, Audit.SharePoint, Audit.General, DLP.All]
```

Production read-back from Grafana Cloud Loki over 7 days:

```
sum(count_over_time({service_name="graph2otel"} | event_name="m365.audit" | dlp_policy_names != "" [7d]))
  ->  4,004
```

Tallied over a 1,000-record sample of those:

| dimension | live distribution |
| --- | --- |
| `record_type_id` / `service` | `11` SharePoint **994**, `108` Endpoint **6** |
| `dlp_policy_names` | `Homelab - UK PII` 591, `Homelab - Financial` 389, `Homelab - Secrets and Credentials` 20 |
| attributes populated | `dlp_policy_names`/`dlp_policy_ids`/`dlp_rule_names`/`dlp_rule_modes`/`dlp_detection_included` on 1000; `dlp_actions`/`dlp_evaluation_source`/`dlp_match_confidences`/`dlp_match_counts`/`dlp_sensitive_type_ids`/`dlp_sensitive_type_names` on 994; `dlp_results_truncated` on 510 |

**The secret exclusion holds in production, not just in the fixture.** Across all 1,000 sampled records there is **not one occurrence** of `DetectedValues`, `SensitiveInformationDetections`, or any field derived from them. That is the deliverable #370 existed to prove, and it is now proven against live matched records at volume rather than against a captured sample.

**`record_type_id` 108 (Endpoint) is a source that did not exist in #370's original 8-record OneDrive-plus-Exchange sample**, and the mapper absorbed it without change because it branches on the structural presence of `PolicyDetails` rather than on `Operation` spelling. The decision taken to survive `DLPRuleMatch` vs `DlpRuleMatch` also covered a third record type nobody had seen — worth knowing, since at 6 in 1,000 it is well below the ratio anyone would notice going missing.

### Final child outcomes

| outcome | children |
| --- | --- |
| shipped | #353, #354, #355, #356, #357, #358, #359, #361, #362, #363, #367, #370 |
| closed no-data with a named unblock | #360, #364, #365, #366, #369 |

Collectors shipped: `m365.exchange_accepted_domain`, `defender.mdo_rules`, `m365.mailbox_delegation`, `m365.exchange_audit_bypass`, `m365.exchange_outbound_spam_policy`, `m365.exchange_connection_filter_policy`, `m365.mailbox_usage`, `mdca.cloud_discovery`, `m365.collaboration_activity`, `m365.inbox_rule`, `m365.service_health_post`, plus the DLP classification mapping on `m365.audit` and the shared `internal/exofanout` per-mailbox cost gate.

### What this epic proved that outlives it

**A full-history re-serve breaks time-windowed seen-set eviction**, and it is not endpoint-specific: service health (#367) and both mailbox-usage aggregate reports (#359) both do it. Assume it of any report-style source until measured otherwise.

**`HighVolume` and `Experimental` are both the wrong gate for per-mailbox fan-out** — traffic-scaling and Graph-beta respectively, where the cost here scales with tenant size. The third gate (`collectors.PerMailboxCollector`, opt-in plus cap plus a covered/total signal) exists now; a future per-mailbox collector should implement the interface rather than invent a fourth gate, and the interface is what keeps the composition root honest instead of a hand-kept name list.

**Guards must assert on the mapper's own return value**, not on rendered attributes. Two independent instances here — `telemetrytest`'s comma join and `telemetry.SetStrs`' own non-empty filter — each sat downstream of a lossy step and passed over deliberate sabotage.

**Five denial shapes, none moved by a broader scope**, are recorded across this epic and #377: HTML body means an edge refused; JSON 403 with a descriptive message is a real missing scope; JSON 401 with an empty message means the service is not provisioned; plus licensing and tenant-root-scope refusals.

**A 200-and-empty leaves a schema behind and a 401 does not.** #366 and #369 look identical on a tracker and are opposite on the wire; recording which one an issue got is the deliverable.

### Gates

No gate was run in this closing pass because no code changed — it was read-only probing, a live Loki read-back, and tracker updates. The working tree is clean at `7b04434`. Nothing on the tenant was mutated.

title: epic(post-v1): M365, Exchange, Defender for Office, MDCA, and backup coverage

body:
## Mission

Correct live endpoint schema drift and add the highest-value Windows 365, Windows Updates, Endpoint Analytics, and Defender signals.

## Source of truth

This epic is the coding-agent launch prompt for the **endpoint** theme from the 2026-07-25 comprehensive audit. Read this body and every child issue in full, including comments, before implementation. Child issues own their exact evidence, API contracts, acceptance criteria, and prior-decision checks.

## Binding decisions

- Live wire fixtures precede beta mapper work.
- Cloud PC additions must not duplicate generic managed-device state.
- Hunting event tables cannot run through a snapshot path that replays history.
- Shared Intune export and Defender hunting budgets are explicit design constraints.
- No docs-shaped mapper for an empty tenant surface.

## Frozen child set

- [x] #342 — fix(intune): map live CertificateStatus Issued as healthy

## Three children closed as already-shipped — #342, #343 (this epic) and #341 (#376)

All three were fixed by `99623a9` ("fix(intune): harden startup API edge cases"), which closed the #398 startup incident. #398's body recorded the same three live wire drifts that these issues were filed for — `certificate_status=Issued`, `odata_type=#microsoft.graph.iosDeviceFeaturesConfiguration`, `recommendation=insiderRiskPolicy` — so the work was done under the incident rather than under its own issue number.

Each was verified against its own acceptance criteria, not against the map entry existing, before closing. Evidence is on each issue. Two things were checked specifically because they are how this kind of "already done" claim usually turns out to be half-true:

- **Is the new behaviour pinned by a test, or just present in a map?** All three are pinned. `configprofiles` additionally carries an anti-drift test that fails the build if the watched set and the bucket map diverge.
- **Was a contradicting assertion left behind?** #343's body warned that an existing test explicitly recorded the subtype as intentionally unmapped. It was rewritten, not orphaned — `TestLiveCaptureReportsTheKnownODataTypeGap` became `TestLiveCaptureRecognizesKnownODataTypes` and now asserts zero findings.

Checkboxes ticked in the body. **The remaining live set for this epic is 9 children: #344-#352.**

One observation for whoever picks this up next, recorded rather than acted on: **#348 (Endpoint Analytics anomaly detail) is the strongest candidate in this epic for closing no-build.** The shipped anomaly overview reads all-zero on this tenant, the beta detail collections have no observed row, and the recorded device-count unblock theories were already disproved. Per this epic's own "close no-build/no-data rather than write a docs-shaped mapper" rule, that is a legitimate outcome — but it needs someone to confirm the aggregate is still all-zero before closing, so I have not touched it.

## Maintainer decision pass — 2026-07-28

Two results govern this epic.

### #352 — read-only Azure SUBSCRIPTION-scope RBAC approved

Asked separately from the Graph read-scope consent extension, because this is the Azure control plane and a different blast radius. Approved as **read-only**, with an absolute constraint: **no mutation of diagnostic settings, ever** — the census reports drift, it never fixes it. Grant goes to `graph2otel-poller`, and the exact role and scope get recorded on #352 when made.

This also finally unblocks the **`SignInLogs` keep/remove decision carried over from #238**, which has been waiting on the census being able to see which categories are genuinely enabled rather than assumed.

### #348 — kept open and parked, and its premise has changed

Not closed no-build, despite the recorded all-zero readings pointing that way. The maintainer: *"I'll have to re-setup our EA setup again as there hasnt been any machines for a few days now."*

That matters. An all-zero anomaly overview on a tenant with **no machines reporting** describes an empty estate, not a quiet one, and only the second justifies closing on this epic's no-data rule. Re-read it after the EA estate is rebuilt.

Standing warning for anyone working the Endpoint Analytics children: the device-count theories for the empty UXA rollup segments were **already disproved**. Do not re-attach a device-count explanation to an empty rollup — whatever gates those segments is still unknown.

### Epic status

Closed earlier this session as already-shipped under `99623a9`: **#342, #343** (and **#341** on #376). Live set is **#344-#352**, of which only #352 needed a human decision — and it now has one. Everything else in this epic is probe-and-build work with no human gate.

## Session note — 2026-07-28. No children of this epic were worked; recording two cross-cutting facts that affect them.

This session closed children of #376 and #378 plus #402. Nothing in **#344-#352** changed. Two things learned elsewhere apply directly here, so they are recorded now rather than re-derived when someone picks this epic up.

### A collector that registers but is never blank-imported is INVISIBLE

Both collectors added this session had correct `init()` functions calling `collectors.Register`/`RegisterEXO`, and both were absent from the registry entirely — nothing imports a collector package for its side effects except `cmd/graph2otel/collectors_import.go`.

**The symptom to recognise is that the census counts do not move.** Adding a collector must shift the logical/candidate counts across `cmd/graph2otel` tests, `charts/graph2otel`, `README.md` and four docs pages. If those tests still pass untouched, the collector did not register.

The gate that caught it was `TestCollectorAnnotationsCoverEveryCollector`, failing with "N annotation(s) match no registered collector". So **writing the collectordoc annotation first turns this silent failure into a loud one** — cheap insurance for any child here that adds a package. `collectors_import.go` is a shared wiring file, so with parallel lanes this is always a wiring-pass job.

### Adding any collector re-triggers the panel-id cascade

Dashboard panel ids are positional. Adding collectors this session shifted them twice, and each time every alert rule's `__panelId__` and `dashboard_path` annotation regenerated — 8 rule files the first time. Budget for `make rules` and a `make rules-push` after any child here lands.

Related: the deployer had a real bug where rules the App Platform API cannot place in a group had their **content** silently skipped, not just their grouping — a push reported zero failures while two rules kept stale annotations. Fixed in `c66c4b1`. If you read back after a push, `matched_content_ungrouped` is now the healthy end state.

### Epic status unchanged

Live set remains **#344-#352**. #352 has its read-only Azure subscription RBAC approved but the grant has NOT been made, so the census and the `SignInLogs` keep/remove decision carried over from #238 are both still open. #348 stays parked until the EA estate is rebuilt — and the standing warning holds: the device-count theories for the empty UXA rollup segments were already disproved, so do not re-attach one.

## Session progress — 2026-07-28. **#352 closed, and its premise turned out to be wrong.**

### #352 closed — but not the way it was scoped

The read-only Azure subscription-scope RBAC was granted and recorded: built-in **Reader** (`acdd72a7-...`) at `/subscriptions/1bdad520-a1e9-4977-9d0b-ef62853b26fd`, assignment `946bfa26-...`, to `graph2otel-poller`. Read-only throughout; **no diagnostic setting was mutated**, per the absolute constraint.

Two results this epic should carry forward:

**1. The Intune half was never an Azure-RBAC problem, and no future grant will fix it.** With subscription Reader held, `microsoft.intune/diagnosticSettings` still 403s. The denial names the scope: `/providers/microsoft.intune` — **tenant-root, outside every subscription**, so no subscription-scope assignment can cover it. The poller also already holds Global Reader and Security Reader, neither of which carries it. **Do not re-attempt this with a broader Azure role** — the scope hierarchy denies it, not the role. The wrong claim was corrected in the census collector's own package doc (`8296010`).

**2. `Monitoring Reader` is broader than `Reader`, not narrower.** Compared live before granting: `Reader` = `*/read`; `Monitoring Reader` = `*/read` **plus `Microsoft.Support/*`** (a write surface) plus a workspace search action. The role whose name suggests it is purpose-built for a diagnostics census would have violated the read-only constraint. Anyone reaching for a "narrow monitoring role" on this project should check the definition rather than the name.

The census itself ran: 26 Entra categories — 10 consumed, 11 `enabled_unread`, 0 `mapped_but_disabled`, 5 disabled. The `SignInLogs` question carried from #238 is answered: **remove**. graph2otel ships four blob sign-in streams and interactive `SignInLogs` is not one of them, so no shipped collector *can* read it, and the polled interactive stream already carries the signal. Execution is a maintainer tenant-config action, deliberately not taken.

### Epic status

Live set is now **#344-#351**. #348 remains parked until the EA estate is rebuilt, and the standing warning holds — the device-count theories for the empty UXA rollup segments were **already disproved**, so do not re-attach one.

#344-#347 and #349-#351 were not touched this session and remain probe-and-build work with no human gate.

## Session progress — 2026-07-28 (cont). **Four of the remaining seven children closed. Windows 365 went away.**

### Closed no-build, all live-measured today

**#344, #345, #346 — all three on ONE finding.** The entire `/deviceManagement/virtualEndpoint` segment answers **403 with an HTML body**, on v1.0 and beta, for every route: `cloudPCs`, `onPremisesConnections`, `provisioningPolicies`, `galleryImages`, `auditEvents`. The parent `/deviceManagement` returns 200 on the same token and `CloudPC.Read.All` is in the poller's `roles` claim, so this is not authorization.

**An HTML 403 is a different animal from a JSON 403 and this epic should treat the distinction as load-bearing.** Every Graph authorization failure returns a JSON `error` object; an HTML page comes from an edge in front of the service, meaning the request never reached Graph's authorization layer. Anyone debugging a future 403 on this project should check the body type before reaching for a scope grant.

**This corrects the shared premise all three were opened on.** They cited #198's 21 real Windows 365 audit records as proof that #251's old "no active Windows 365" unblock had fired. It had. It has since un-fired — whatever provisioning existed is gone. Unblock for all three: `GET /v1.0/deviceManagement/virtualEndpoint/cloudPCs` returns 200.

**#347 — the newer Windows Updates model is reachable and empty.** `/beta/admin/windows/updates/policies` → 200 with **0 rows**, while the family already shipped by #259 carries this tenant's data (`updatePolicies` 2, `deployments` 1, `catalog/entries` 3). Zero policies means no rings, no approvals, no applicableContent and no polymorphic `@odata.type` values to preserve. Two resource families with near-identical names, one empty and one populated, is exactly the setup where an always-zero panel gets read as "no update policies configured".

**#349, #350, #365** were closed or advanced under #378's probe wave — see those issues.

### Where this epic stands

Live set is now **#348, #350, #351**.

- **#348** stays parked until the EA estate is rebuilt. Standing warning unchanged: the device-count theories for the empty UXA rollup segments were **already disproved**, so do not re-attach one.
- **#350** has its full measurement recorded on the issue and is now a build rather than a spike — 993,292 exposure-graph nodes, `ExposureGraphEdges | summarize count()` **504s at 150 s**, and two labels are 99.7% of the graph, which hands the bounded subset straight out of the data.
- **#351** (per-device feature-update outcome twins) was not touched and remains export-fan-out work against the shared 48/min limiter.

### One cross-cutting fact worth carrying

Four denials in this programme now sit on an axis a scope grant does not move: #352 (tenant-root scope no subscription assignment reaches), #330 (Purview DataInsights backend), #326 (licensing), and #344-#346 (service edge). **Check which layer is denying before granting anything.** The instinct to grant a broader scope has been wrong every time it has been tried here.

## Session progress — 2026-07-28 (later)

`4ed2c00` — **#350 closed**, `defender.exposure_graph` shipped. The bounded Exposure Graph collector on the existing hunting path; no new scope. It names no labels: a per-label twin threshold sits inside the measured 350× gap between the largest bounded label (1,057) and the smallest bulk one (372,330), so the bounded subset falls out of the data on any tenant, and an over-threshold label is counted as `twinned="false"` rather than silently skipped. Every edge query prunes before aggregating, because the unpruned `ExposureGraphEdges | summarize count()` is a live-measured HTTP 504.

Census 162 → **164** logical collectors, 165 → **167** registration-path candidates. `make check` exit 0, dashboards at 380/380 metric coverage, alert rules re-pushed to the `cloud` stack (`matched_content_ungrouped`, the healthy end state).

Full evidence, the per-label wire shapes, and the two decode traps are on #350.

## Session note — 2026-07-28 (later). No child of this epic was worked; recording two cross-cutting facts and one correction that affect them.

This session worked children of #376 and #378. **#348 was not touched** and remains parked until the EA estate is rebuilt — the standing warning is unchanged: the device-count theories for the empty UXA rollup segments were already disproved, so do not re-attach one. It is this epic's only open child.

### A fifth denial layer, found on #369

This epic already carries the "check which layer is denying before granting anything" rule and the four layers behind it: tenant-root scope (#352), the Exchange DataInsights backend (#330), licensing (#326), and a service edge returning an **HTML** body (#344-#346).

**Add a fifth: a JSON `401` with code `UnknownError` and an EMPTY `message`.** That is what `/solutions/backupRestore` returns on a tenant where the service is not provisioned at all — the service failing before an authorization decision can be reached. Distinguish it from Graph's real authorization layer, which returns `403` with `Authorization_RequestDenied` and a descriptive message (confirmed the same day on #334, where a genuinely missing app role produced exactly that shape and granting it fixed it immediately).

So the field guide is now: **HTML body → an edge refused, no scope helps. JSON 403 with a descriptive message → a real missing scope, grant it. JSON 401 with an empty message → the service is not provisioned, no scope helps.**

### A parked issue whose unblock is "go and look" is available work

The #376 receipt concluded no open child had work available. Two of its parked children had "cheap read-only reconnaissance" as their named first step; doing it shipped one collector and reduced another to a single portal click. **The state was recorded correctly and the consequence was drawn wrongly.**

This matters here because **#348's parked condition is genuinely different in kind** — it waits on physical devices reporting into Endpoint Analytics, which no amount of probing produces. That is a real block, not an unexamined one. Worth re-reading its aggregate once the estate is back, and no earlier.

### The EDM is an existence oracle, not a delivery guarantee

This project reaches for `$metadata` to answer "does this surface exist" and it has paid off repeatedly (#333, and again on #336 this session where the documented path was simply wrong). **#334 found the limit of that:** `snapshot.totalChangedObjects` is declared in the EDM and is never sent — absent from every live row, still absent when named explicitly in `$select`, still absent under `$expand`.

For any Intune or Defender collector modelled off the EDM rather than off a capture, a declared numeric must still be a **pointer**. A bare int publishes a fabricated 0 that reads as a healthy measurement.

### Epic status

Live set is **#348** alone, parked on the EA estate rebuild. Nothing else in this epic is open.

## Session note — 2026-08-04. #348 re-read; still parked, but its design question is now answered.

No child of this epic was built. **#348 remains this epic's only open child** and its unblock has NOT fired — full evidence on the issue. Two things belong here rather than only there.

### The obvious EA liveness probe lies, and this epic should not fall for it

`userExperienceAnalyticsDeviceScores` returns **9 rows with real scores** on a tenant where `managedDevices` holds only **two** Windows devices (`winsrv`, and `LAPHAM` last synced 2026-07-29). The four EA Proxmox VMs are gone from Intune; five of those nine score rows carry a **blank `deviceName`** because the managed-device record they joined against no longer exists.

**`userExperienceAnalyticsDeviceScores` is a retained aggregate, not a liveness signal.** A non-empty response is not evidence anything is reporting. The device list is the check. Reading it the other way would have closed #348 on a false premise — the exact failure the 2026-07-28 maintainer note exists to prevent.

### A 400 on an Intune detail collection can mean "you must filter", not "blocked"

| route | bare | with filter |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `userExperienceAnalyticsAnomaly` | 200, count 0 | — |
| `...AnomalyCorrelationGroupOverview` | **400** | 200 with `anomalyId eq '<guid>'` |
| `...AnomalyDevice` | **400** | 200 only with `anomalyId` **and** `correlationGroupId` |

The 400 body is a `proxy.msub06.manage.microsoft.com/DeviceFE` error with no usable message, so it is indistinguishable from a real failure by inspection. Only varying the request shape separated the two.

This epic already carries "check which layer is denying before granting anything" for 403s. **The 400 equivalent is: check whether the collection is enumerable at all before recording it as unreachable.** It converts #348 from a spike blocked on data into a build whose request contract — a 1 + N + M fan-out, costing nothing at zero anomalies — is frozen in advance.

### Epic status

Live set remains **#348** alone. Next action is the maintainer's: rebuild the EA estate on the four Proxmox VMs, then re-read the anomaly collection. Standing warning unchanged — the device-count theories for the empty UXA rollup segments were already disproved; do not re-attach one.

**A sentinel beats a key-absence check for a content exclusion.** #338 excludes `processArgs`/`processTree` because a command line can carry a credential in an argument (#190). ## Phase completion — epic closed 2026-08-04. All 27 children resolved.

The last two children closed today. No child was left re-scoped into a successor and nothing is parked.

### Final child outcomes

| outcome | children |
| --- | --- |
| shipped | #315, #316, #317, #318, #320, #321, #322, #333, #334, #336, #337, #338, #341 |
| closed no-build / no-data with named evidence | #319, #323, #324, #325, #326, #327, #328, #329, #330, #331, #332, #335 |
| closed no-data 2026-08-04 | #339, #340 |

Collectors shipped under this epic: `entra.service_principal` twin, `entra.recommendation` twin, `entra.auth_methods_policy` + `entra.auth_method_configuration`, `entra.conditional_access` + named-location twins, `entra.role_definitions`, `entra.cross_tenant_access`, `entra.auth_strength`, `entra.agent_governance`, `entra.directory_recovery`, `entra.related_tenants`, `entra.network_access_traffic`, plus the allowlisted privileged-group gauge.

### #339 / #340 — closed no-data, categories left enabled

Both are 19-day zero-row negatives, re-measured today as `graph2otel-poller`. Neither container has ever been created on `graph2otelm7kni`, whose listing has grown to **42 containers** since these categories were enabled on 2026-07-16.

**Closing the issues did not disable the categories.** Both still read `enabled=True` on the `aadiam/graph2otel` diagnostic setting, deliberately, so each remains a ~£0.001/mo tripwire that will produce its own re-open signal if the tenant ever grows the feature that writes it. Full evidence on each issue.

### A correction to this epic's own 2026-07-29 receipt

That receipt recorded that two GSA-family blob categories — `networkaccessconnectionevents` and `networkaccessgenerativeaiinsights` — had "woken up in the same listing". **That overstated what was measured.** It was a *container* listing; a full *blob* listing today returns **200 with zero blobs** for both. A container existing means something once created it, not that the category emits.

Generalisable, and it is the same trap #339/#340 turn on from the other side: **container presence and category emission are different facts, and only a blob listing distinguishes them.** Neither category is consumed by graph2otel and neither has anything to consume.

### The method fact worth carrying past this epic

**A zero is only evidence once the probe shape is validated against a positive control.** Every negative in this epic's last two closes was taken with the identical request shape run across all 42 containers, of which **29 returned blobs** — the largest `advancedhunting-deviceprocessevents` at 957 MB. This project has produced three false blocked-verdicts from malformed probes, and a control in the same run is what separates "nothing is there" from "I asked wrongly".

That sits alongside this epic's other standing lessons: check which layer is denying before granting anything (five distinct denial shapes found across this programme, none of them fixed by a broader scope); the EDM is an existence oracle, not a delivery guarantee; and a parked issue whose unblock is "go and look" is available work — which shipped #334, #336 and #338 after each had been recorded as blocked.

### Gates

**No gate was run in this closing pass, because no code changed.** This pass was read-only probing plus tracker updates; the working tree is clean at `7b04434` and the last recorded green `make check` is that commit's CI. Stating that rather than re-asserting a gate nobody re-ran.

Nothing was mutated on the tenant: every probe was a read-only GET as `graph2otel-poller`, and the two diagnostic categories were read, not changed.

body:
## Mission

Turn the generated Grafana estate into safe, reproducible, decision-oriented monitoring and investigation content.

## Source of truth

This epic is the coding-agent launch prompt for the **grafana** theme from the 2026-07-25 comprehensive audit. Read this body and every child issue in full, including comments, before implementation. Child issues own their exact evidence, API contracts, acceptance criteria, and prior-decision checks.

## Binding decisions

- Keep exhaustive signal coverage, but separate it from concise operational overviews.
- No-data, evaluator-error, disabled, unlicensed, and failed are different states.
- Tenant identity must survive variables, aggregation, recording, routing, and links.
- No tenant-specific secrets or identifiers enter this public repository.
- Thresholds and detections require fixtures/evidence; unmeasured content ships paused or as hunting queries.

## Frozen child set

### P0 dashboard foundation — complete before dashboard expansion

- [x] #399 — feat(dashboards): make Grafana v2 dynamic dashboard capabilities first-class

No new dashboard panels, feature-specific dashboard work, or dashboard-coverage expansion starts until #399 has frozen the dynamic-generator API, presence contract, schema migration, and gates. Its reference implementation is `../opnsense-exporter/grafana/`; use its Grafana v2 `TabsLayout`, nested tabs, and conditional rendering patterns as the benchmark, adapted to graph2otel semantics.

- [x] #293 — fix(alerting): stop the sample notification policy from owning the root route
- [ ] #294 — fix(grafana): repair and test the HTTP provisioning workflow
- [x] #295 — fix(dashboards): select the intended Prometheus and Loki datasources by default
- [x] #296 — fix(alerting): route generated warning alerts to a deliberate receiver
- [ ] #297 — fix(recording-rules): preserve tenant identity and define late-arrival semantics
- [x] #298 — fix(alerting): stop treating rule evaluation errors as OK
- [x] #299 — fix(alerting): make collector staleness interval-aware
- [x] #300 — chore(alerting): put production SIEM and legacy Entra rules under a reproducible source of truth
- [x] #301 — fix(dashboards): prevent silent cross-tenant aggregation
- [x] #302 — feat(dashboards): separate operational overviews from exhaustive signal explorers
- [x] #303 — feat(dashboards): distinguish disabled, unavailable, healthy-empty, and failed signals
- [x] #304 — fix(dashboards): generate honest units, titles, mappings, and thresholds
- [ ] #305 — feat(grafana): generate entity-centric investigation pivots
- [x] #306 — feat(gate): validate every LogQL filter and group key against the signal catalog
- [x] #307 — feat(alerting): add clickable runbooks, dashboard context, and annotation linting
- [x] #308 — feat(gate): run semantic PromQL and LogQL smoke tests against a real backend
- [ ] #309 — perf(dashboards): add a generated query and render performance budget
- [x] #310 — feat(dashboards): annotate graph2otel deploys, versions, and configuration changes
- [x] #311 — feat(dashboards): add a cross-domain graph2otel landing dashboard
- [x] #312 — feat(dashboard): add an executive health and data-loss summary to self-observability
- [ ] #313 — feat(security): ship a curated detection and hunting content pack
- [ ] #400 — feat(annotations): publish curated domain events to Grafana annotations via an operator-supplied service account (split out of #310 by maintainer decision 2026-07-27; narrowly amends the OTLP-push-only invariant for annotations only)
- [x] #314 — fix(gate): include Grafana assets in the documented full local check

## Sequencing

1. Start with #399: establish and freeze the Grafana v2 dynamic-dashboard foundation before any dashboard expansion.
2. Then land P0/P1 correctness defects and any shared catalog/config seams.
3. Land one independently green child at a time, closing it from a conventional commit on `main`.
4. Spikes first obtain their named evidence; **close no-build/no-data** when the evidence does not support implementation.
5. Reconcile generated catalogs/docs/dashboards after each signal change.
6. Finish with live read-back or render/query receipts where the child requires them.

## Parallel lanes

- Provisioning, datasource selection, notification routing, and rules-as-code.
- Dashboard information architecture, semantics, empty states, and performance.
- Signal/attribute/query gates and live semantic smoke tests.
- Investigations, runbooks, annotations, and portable detection content.

Freeze shared names, signatures, config keys, signal names, and generated-schema changes before parallel work. One file has one owner; composition roots, registries, catalogs, and generators get a single wiring pass.

## Operating rules

- Strict TDD: failing test, observe the intended failure, minimal implementation, green, refactor.
- Validate Microsoft behavior from the wire as `graph2otel-poller`; docs-only evidence is not mapper evidence.
- New permissions, licences, tenant configuration, or data-generation actions require explicit maintainer approval.
- Metrics stay bounded and tenant-shaped; per-entity detail is a log twin.
- Do not re-open the rejected Event Hub/Log Analytics, dual-transport, Redis/cache, HA, typed-SDK expansion, or engine-side blob-dedupe designs.
- Run `make check` plus the Grafana gate until the full-gate child lands; record concrete receipts before closing.

## Done when

- [ ] Every child is closed as implemented, closed no-build with evidence, or explicitly re-scoped into a linked successor.
- [ ] All shared seams and generated artifacts agree with the final implementation.
- [ ] The full repository and observability gates are green.
- [ ] Any required live tenant/Grafana read-back is recorded on the child issue.
- [ ] A phase-completion comment on this epic lists issue numbers, completing SHAs, deviations, and remaining human actions.

Measured basis: `{service_name="graph2otel"}` is **one** logical Loki stream currently carrying `__stream_shard__` (values `0`,`1`), i.e. Loki is rate-sharding it. 97,430 lines / 5.9 MB per 6h, 266 distinct structured-metadata keys, and no bounded resource attribute available to split on. `event_name` measured **73** distinct over 6h, which is too many to promote directly at 23 MB/day — hence a derived coarse domain (~6–8 values) instead.

Blocked on a maintainer-only tenant step for the final verification (`needs-rob`): the promotion is configured in Grafana Cloud, and the 15 promotion slots are shared tenant-wide across opnsense-exporter, tailscale2otel and graph2otel.

No implementation started; no repo file or live resource changed.

## Phase completion 2026-07-27 — 24 of 24 children closed. Epic complete.

Final tip: **`b4fcaec`** on `main` and `origin/main`. Working tree clean, local and remote in sync.

### Children closed this session (6)

| issue | SHA | what it settled |
| --- | --- | --- |
| #297 | `703ab88` | Both Loki recording rules retired — repository **and** production |
| #294 | `2189448` | App Platform rule deployment with content-level semantic read-back |
| #309 | `cf8932b` | Render breakage tripwire at 30s; static per-leaf ceiling already enforced |
| #400 | `186b981` | Opt-in Grafana annotation writer, all four curated categories |
| #305 | `186b981` | Six generated entity investigation pivots |
| #313 | `d40d0a4` | Six more paused detections (11 total) and a generated hunting library |

Plus **#401**, filed and fixed this session outside the epic: graph2otel no longer emits a log record older than the backend's accept window (`b4fcaec`).

### The finding that mattered most, now closed

The previous pause receipt recorded that **every rule change this epic landed was repository-only** — dashboards deployed, rules had no deployment path at all, so #298, #299, #300 and #307 were correct in git and absent in production. #294 closed that, and the first real push proved it: `execErrState` was still `Ok` live, the staleness threshold was still the fixed `3600` placeholder, and the runbook annotations were absent on all 19 rules. All 14 alert rules now match source semantically, verified by field-by-field read-back rather than by counting.

The repo-14-vs-live-12 drift is also diagnosed and closed: the missing rules were `g2o-record-integrity-loss` and `g2o-payload-type-mismatch`, absent because they were **never pushed**, not deleted by hand.

### Live production changes made

1. **Two `blob-derived` recording rules deleted** (#297) — probed per-UID afterwards: 2 × 404, rules 444 → 442, group gone, the 8 `entra-security-g2o` SIEM rules and `graph2otel-alerts` verified intact.
2. **All 14 alert rules pushed** as App Platform resources (#294), create-or-update by `metadata.name`, idempotency proven by `resourceVersion` incrementing on a repeat push.

### Standing item resolved — and the last recorded state was wrong

The maintainer authorised retiring the six live v1 dashboards. **There was nothing to delete:** all six return 404, the `graph2otel` folder holds exactly one dashboard (the v2 one), and a name/title scan across all 181 dashboards on the stack finds only it. Each UID was checked with an individual `get`, not inferred from a listing.

So this epic's 2026-07-27 correction — *"all six v1 boards are live… retiring them is now a real decision rather than moot"* — is **itself no longer true**. I did not delete them and cannot say from here when they went. Recorded because that entry would otherwise send the next reader looking for work that does not exist.

### Corrections to standing instructions in this tracker

**`--context grafana.m7kni.com` is wrong as written** and fails outright:

```
invalid context "grafana.m7kni.com": context not found
```

That is the stack's **server**, not a context name. The context is **`m7kni`**, and it is now the only one configured — the unrelated customer stack that motivated the pinning advice is no longer in the config at all. The instruction's intent is right and worth keeping; the literal string appears in #294, #297 and #309 and is wrong in all three.

### New `gcx` traps found, all silent

Adding to the four already recorded:

- **A `.json` resource manifest is silently ignored.** `gcx resources push` reported `succeeded: 0, failed: 0` with no error and no warning — the directory simply looked empty. YAML only.
- **`--dry-run` proves nothing for alerting resources.** It warns that the type has no server-side dry-run and checks only that the manifest parses and the kind is served. It validated neither the spec nor uniqueness — the `OK`-versus-`Ok` enum error was invisible to it.
- **The short selector `alertrules` resolves to `alerting.ext.grafana.app`**, which is the *firing-instance* view: it returns `spec.alerts[]` with live alert state and contains no rule definition. Reading that back would compare source against a different resource entirely and report nonsense rather than an error.

### The App Platform contract, measured rather than read

Four things cost a failed push each, and none is in any documentation: the enum is **`Ok`, not `OK`** (rejected 18 of 19 rules); the manifest must declare **`grafana.com/provenance: api`**; the push needs **`--omit-manager-fields`** (whose error message contradicts itself — *"provided provenance 'api', needs 'api'"*); and durations must omit **leading** zero units (`5m0s`, not `0h5m0s`) with a zero `for` omitted entirely.

**One limitation is surfaced rather than hidden:** this API cannot place a newly-created alert rule into a named group — refused on create *and* on an ungrouped update — and `RuleSequence` is not a way round it, since it requires at least one recording rule and #297 retired both. Such rules evaluate correctly on their per-rule `spec.trigger.interval`, so the read-back reports them as `ungrouped` with status `matched_content_ungrouped`: a clean pass, neither claimed as a match nor mislabelled as drift.

### Done-when criteria

- [x] Every child closed as implemented, or closed with evidence.
- [x] Shared seams and generated artifacts agree with the implementation.
- [x] Full repository and observability gates green — `make check` exit 0, `make grafana-check` 400 tests, 335/335 catalog metrics panelled (0 waived), 366 panels across 7 tabs and 62 leaves, largest leaf 18/24, pinned zensical build "No issues found", 0 golangci-lint issues.
- [x] Live read-back recorded on #294, #297 and #309.
- [x] This comment.

### Deliberately left open, and where

Two verification debts are recorded on their own issues rather than pretended away:

- **#400's live read-back has not been performed.** No annotation has been written to a real Grafana by that code, and the `annotations:create` / `annotations:type:organization` permission pair is **docs-only** evidence. Two of its match predicates are docs-only or n=1 (Conditional Access via `activity_display_name`; `intune.audit_event.category`). All report-only — a miss is a missing marker, never a dropped record.
- **#305 made three rendering assumptions** it could not measure (the `TextVariable` field set, multi-target merging in one panel, whether a collapsed row queries). None affects correctness; a single live render of `?dtab=Overview` closes all three.

Closing the epic. #375 is complete.

body:
## Mission

Make a green graph2otel state mean that source data was fetched completely, timestamped truthfully, checkpointed durably, and accepted by the OTLP backend.

## Source of truth

This epic is the coding-agent launch prompt for the **integrity** theme from the 2026-07-25 comprehensive audit. Read this body and every child issue in full, including comments, before implementation. Child issues own their exact evidence, API contracts, acceptance criteria, and prior-decision checks.

## Binding decisions

- Correctness and observability fixes precede new collector volume.
- Liveness stays dependency-free; readiness and delivery health are separate.
- No HA, Redis, dual transport, Prometheus pull, or engine-side blob dedupe.
- Event records without a parseable event time are dropped and counted, never stamped as now.
- Every new registration path must extend the collectordoc coverage seam in the same commit.

## Frozen child set

- [x] #264 — fix(preflight): validate permissions for the actual enabled collector set
- [x] #265 — fix(config): reject unknown keys, collector names, and transport typos
- [x] #266 — fix(auth): make the authenticated application identity authoritative
- [x] #267 — feat(ops): add meaningful readiness and retain failed tenants in status
- [x] #268 — feat(telemetry): expose real OTLP delivery health for metrics and logs
- [x] #269 — feat(telemetry): add end-to-end record outcome accounting
- [x] #270 — fix(graphclient): enforce the valid-host allowlist for raw REST requests
- [x] #271 — fix(o365): do not advance the shared watermark past a pre-list failure
- [x] #272 — fix(blobpipeline): return a degraded tick after blob read or cursor-save failures
- [x] #273 — fix(jobpipeline): make terminal query checkpoint clears durable
- [x] #274 — fix(exportjob): surface terminal job-state clear failures
- [x] #275 — fix(ingest): drop event records with no parseable timestamp
- [x] #276 — fix(exportjob): bound SAS downloads by time and detect size overflow
- [x] #277 — fix(ingest): guard log and job pagination against repeated cursors and page loops
- [x] #278 — fix(mdca): fail closed when discovery pagination reaches its cap
- [x] #279 — fix(o365): recover subscriptions disabled after process startup
- [x] #280 — fix(transports): do not send one more request after retry cancellation
- [x] #281 — fix(blobpipeline): fail loudly on an oversized record with no newline
- [x] #282 — fix(blobpipeline): persist cursor changes caused only by blob deletion pruning
- [x] #283 — fix(graphclient): detect raw REST response-body overflow
- [x] #284 — fix(telemetry): stamp tenant identity on process-level self-observability
- [x] #285 — fix(build): use one version source for the binary and build_info
- [x] #286 — fix(packaging): make the standalone-container quickstart runnable and persistent
- [x] #287 — fix(docs): align backfill warnings with the measured seven-day rejection contract
- [x] #288 — feat(telemetry): generate the complete self-observability signal catalog
- [x] #289 — feat(ops): attribute volume and cost budgets per collector and transport
- [x] #290 — spike(ops): design a deterministic isolated replay and export workflow
- [x] #291 — perf(logpipeline): stream ordered endpoint pages instead of buffering full windows
- [x] #292 — feat(telemetry): emit collector availability and skip-reason state
- [x] #380 — fix(docs): reconcile operator documentation with the shipped v1.0.0 surface

## Sequencing

1. Start with P0/P1 correctness defects and any shared catalog/config seams.
2. Land one independently green child at a time, closing it from a conventional commit on `main`.
3. Spikes first obtain their named evidence; **close no-build/no-data** when the evidence does not support implementation.
4. Reconcile generated catalogs/docs/dashboards after each signal change.
5. Finish with live read-back or render/query receipts where the child requires them.

## Parallel lanes

- Core config/auth/preflight/readiness.
- Graph/O365/blob/job/export transport correctness.
- Telemetry delivery, outcome accounting, self-observability, and capacity.
- Packaging/docs/operator replay.

Freeze shared names, signatures, config keys, signal names, and generated-schema changes before parallel work. One file has one owner; composition roots, registries, catalogs, and generators get a single wiring pass.

## Operating rules

- Strict TDD: failing test, observe the intended failure, minimal implementation, green, refactor.
- Validate Microsoft behavior from the wire as `graph2otel-poller`; docs-only evidence is not mapper evidence.
- New permissions, licences, tenant configuration, or data-generation actions require explicit maintainer approval.
- Metrics stay bounded and tenant-shaped; per-entity detail is a log twin.
- Do not re-open the rejected Event Hub/Log Analytics, dual-transport, Redis/cache, HA, typed-SDK expansion, or engine-side blob-dedupe designs.
- Run `make check` plus the Grafana gate until the full-gate child lands; record concrete receipts before closing.

## Done when

- [x] Every child is closed as implemented, closed no-build with evidence, or explicitly re-scoped into a linked successor.
- [x] All shared seams and generated artifacts agree with the final implementation.
- [x] The full repository and observability gates are green.
- [x] Any required live tenant/Grafana read-back is recorded on the child issue.
- [x] A phase-completion comment on this epic lists issue numbers, completing SHAs, deviations, and remaining human actions.
