body:
## Outcome

Make graph2otel events easier to consume in non-Grafana SIEMs without changing the canonical OTLP event schema or adding output protocols.

## Evidence

**Evidence class:** `architecture opportunity from the generated signal catalog (2026-07-25)`

- The generated signal catalog already inventories 133 log events and their attributes.
- OTel Collector/Alloy processors can transform and fan out records at the edge.
- There is no checked mapping from graph2otel event semantics to OCSF/ECS categories.

## Proposed scope

- Generate versioned OTel Collector/Alloy transform packs and mapping documentation from the signal catalog.
- Start with identity, authentication, device posture, email, security alert/incident, and network events.
- Preserve canonical graph2otel attributes alongside mapped fields during migration.

## Constraints and non-goals

- Do not add native Splunk/Elastic/CEF outputs to the graph2otel binary.
- Do not force lossy fields into an approximate category.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Mappings have golden source→canonical→OCSF/ECS fixtures.
- [ ] Unknown/unmapped attributes remain available rather than being dropped.
- [ ] Original event time, tenant, transport, and stable IDs survive.
- [ ] Generated mappings fail when referenced events/attributes drift.

## Prior decisions and duplicate check

- No existing issue covers portable SIEM semantic mapping; this remains a companion integration over OTLP.

## Primary sources

- [https://schema.ocsf.io/](https://schema.ocsf.io/)
- [https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/ecs/current/index.html](https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/ecs/current/index.html)

## Priority

Audit recommendation: **P3**.

comments.body: I think this is all out of scope for this poller

Closed with epic #379 by maintainer decision 2026-07-28 — syslog/CEF companions, VNet flow logs and SIEM mapping packs are all out of scope for a realtime poller. **Dropped, not deferred.** See #379's closing comment for the reasoning and for what is given up. Recorded explicitly: none of these ever threatened the OTLP-push-only invariant; that was checked, and this was a scope-and-ownership decision rather than a safety one.

## Outcome

Assess network-flow investigations for operators who already archive VNet flow logs, without widening graph2otel to subscription inventory.

## Evidence

**Evidence class:** `current Azure format/lifecycle docs-only (2026-07-25)`

- NSG flow logs cannot be newly created and retire on 2027-09-30; VNet flow logs are the replacement.
- VNet flow logs use nested block-blob update semantics unlike graph2otel's append-JSONL blob engine.
- #251 rejected subscription-wide Azure Monitor/Resource Graph/Cost access, not an explicit configured storage parser.

## Proposed scope

- Prefer a companion adapter or separate source-specific parser.
- Use Blob Data Reader on an explicitly configured account/container only.
- Measure block updates, offsets, late writes, duplicates, versions, bytes, and flow volume.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] VNet format only; no new NSG-flow implementation.
- [ ] No subscription-wide discovery permission is requested.
- [ ] Five-tuples/IPs/ports/resource IDs remain high-volume logs.
- [ ] HighVolume annotation contains real measurements before enablement.
- [ ] Cost and retention guidance precedes a build decision.

## Prior decisions and duplicate check

- Not duplicate of #89/#251: this is an explicit-storage companion for a concrete format, not a replacement Azure transport/control plane.
- Related: #89, #251.

## Primary sources

- [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/network-watcher/vnet-flow-logs-overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/network-watcher/vnet-flow-logs-overview)

## Priority

Audit recommendation: **P3**.

## Outcome

Operators should be able to ingest firewall, appliance, and legacy Microsoft-adjacent syslog/CEF into the same OTLP/Loki investigation model without turning graph2otel into a network daemon.

## Evidence

**Evidence class:** `current Alloy/OTel Collector capability (2026-07-25)`

- OpenTelemetry Collector Contrib and Grafana Alloy already provide maintained RFC3164/RFC5424 syslog receivers with TCP/TLS support.
- graph2otel is deliberately OTLP push-only and has no reason to implement a generic listener or eighth collector path.

## Proposed scope

- Publish a versioned Alloy/OTel Collector reference configuration, CEF normalization contract, golden fixtures, and Grafana investigation links.
- Use TCP with TLS/mTLS by default; make UDP an explicit lossy opt-in.
- Forward normalized OTLP logs to the same backend.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Golden RFC3164, RFC5424, and representative CEF fixtures pass.
- [ ] Original event time is preserved; malformed time has explicit reject/degraded behavior.
- [ ] Backpressure, queue, retry, oversize, parse-failure, and UDP-loss semantics are documented.
- [ ] Metrics use bounded vendor/product/severity/action/protocol/parse dimensions; entity values stay logs.

## Prior decisions and duplicate check

- This does not reopen Graph webhooks or Event Hub and does not add a generic graph2otel ingest engine.
- Related: #89, #131.

## Primary sources

- [https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/tree/main/receiver/syslogreceiver](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/tree/main/receiver/syslogreceiver)
- [https://grafana.com/docs/alloy/latest/reference/components/otelcol/otelcol.receiver.syslog/](https://grafana.com/docs/alloy/latest/reference/components/otelcol/otelcol.receiver.syslog/)

## Priority

Audit recommendation: **P2**.

body:
## Outcome

Assess whether DLP classification metadata adds value without ever emitting matched secret values.

## Evidence

**Evidence class:** `conditional residual from #100 (2026-07-25)`

- #100 leaves a dedicated `DLP.All` mapper conditional on a deliberate policy match.
- `DetectedValues[].Name/Value` can contain the matched secret and must never be emitted.
- Current raw DLP content remains intentionally excluded.

## Proposed scope

- Maintainer creates/approves one safe deliberate DLP match outside graph2otel.
- Capture the wire record and map classification/policy/rule metadata only.
- Prove secret-bearing fields are discarded before telemetry.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A deliberate real match is the named unblock.
- [ ] Tests include secret sentinel values and prove they never reach metrics, logs, errors, or fixtures.
- [ ] Every non-secret record detail remains available as a log twin where useful.
- [ ] Close no-build if metadata cannot be separated safely.

## Prior decisions and duplicate check

- This is the explicit conditional mapper residual from #100, not a proposal to re-enable raw DLP content rejected by #251.
- Related: #100, #237, #251.

## Priority

Audit recommendation: **P3**.

comments.body:
## Parked by maintainer decision 2026-07-28

Verbatim: *"Park it for another time."*

This issue cannot progress without a **deliberately created DLP match** on the tenant — a test document containing fake-but-policy-matching content. That is not something graph2otel can or should manufacture for itself, and the validation is worthless without it: the entire point is proving that `DetectedValues` never reach telemetry, which cannot be demonstrated on data that never matched.

**Unblock condition:** the maintainer creates a deliberate DLP match and says so here. Until then this is blocked on a human action, not on engineering.

Standing position unchanged from #100: DLP matched *values* are excluded — for a credential-shaped match the value IS the credential. This issue was only ever about whether the safe half (policy and rule metadata) can be separated cleanly. Untested, that separation stays unproven and unshipped.

## Validated 2026-07-29 — the DLP feed is live and wired, and there are no matches yet

Maintainer reported DLP rules are now configured and suspected there would be no hits. Probed as `graph2otel-poller` against the O365 Management Activity API to separate the two failure modes that look identical from the tracker.

### The subscription half is READY — this is new and worth recording

```
GET /api/v1.0/{tenant}/activity/feed/subscriptions/list  ->  200
  Audit.AzureActiveDirectory  enabled
  Audit.Exchange              enabled
  Audit.General               enabled
  Audit.SharePoint            enabled
  DLP.All                     enabled     <-- the one this issue needs
```

The content type is **`DLP.All`**, not `Audit.DLP.All` as this issue's title says. `Audit.DLP.All` is the *permission* name; the feed's own content-type string has no `Audit.` prefix. A collector built from the issue title would request a content type the API does not have.

### The content half is empty

```
GET .../subscriptions/content?contentType=DLP.All&startTime=<now-23h>&endTime=<now>  ->  200  []
```

Zero content blobs across the full window (the API caps a single request at 24h, so 23h is the widest single read). A control on the same token in the same run returned **7** `Audit.General` blobs over the identical window, so this is a real negative and not a broken request, a wrong tenant id, or an auth artifact.

**So the state is: transport proven, subscription enabled, nothing has matched.** That is a materially better position than when this was parked — the "is the feed even on" question is now answered — but it does not unblock the issue, because the deliverable is proving `DetectedValues` never reach telemetry and that cannot be demonstrated on a feed with no matches.

### Unblock, now narrowed to one concrete action

Trigger a match, deliberately, with fake-but-policy-matching content — e.g. mail a document containing a synthetic card number or NI number pattern to a mailbox the policy covers, and confirm the policy shows a match in Purview. Then say so here.

Two things to expect when it happens, so the next session does not misread them:

- **Content-blob arrival is not immediate.** `Audit.General` blobs in the window above were created up to hours after the events in them; budget for a lag before concluding the match did not land.
- **Re-check `DataSecurityEvents` (#366) in the same pass.** Its unblock overlaps this one and one tenant action may fire both.

Standing position unchanged from #100: matched *values* are excluded — for a credential-shaped match the value IS the credential. This issue is only about whether the policy/rule metadata separates cleanly, and untested that separation stays unproven and unshipped.

## Test data prepared 2026-07-29 — the exact policy conditions, read off the wire

The maintainer is generating a deliberate match. Rather than guess at content, the tenant's own DLP policy was read as `graph2otel-poller` so the test data matches the real conditions.

### How to read the policy without a portal (useful beyond this issue)

`GET /beta/security/dataSecurityAndGovernance/policyFiles` → 200 returns the compiled policy set. The `dlpPolicy` entry's `content` is **base64 of UTF-16LE XML** (not UTF-8 — decoding as UTF-8 yields interleaved NULs and looks like a binary blob). Decoded:

```python
xml = base64.b64decode(entry["content"]).decode("utf-16-le")
```

The poller already holds whatever this needs; no grant was made.

### The three custom policies, all `AuditAndNotify`, all `minCount=1`

| policy | id | workloads | SIT thresholds |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Homelab - Secrets and Credentials | `acaec97a-890c-469c-8e74-1841f34f22ee` | Exchange, SharePoint, OneDrive, Teams, EndpointDevices | 7 SITs: 2 at ≥85% confidence, 5 at ≥75% |
| Homelab - Financial | `<guid-4>` | same | 4 SITs: 3 at ≥85%, 1 at ≥75% |
| Homelab - UK PII | `<guid-5>` | same | 3 SITs: 1 at ≥85%, 2 at ≥75% |

**`minCount=1` on every SIT, and the conditions are content-only** — no recipient, sender or scope predicate. So a single match fires, and internal self-addressed mail is sufficient; nothing needs to leave the tenant.

Four other policies exist and are not the target here: two Adaptive Protection policies (`Enforce` mode, risk-user-scoped), a DSPM-for-AI block policy, and the default Copilot policy.

### The SIT identities are deliberately NOT resolved, and do not need to be

The conditions name SITs by GUID only (e.g. `c7bc98e8-551a-4c35-a92d-d2c8cda714a7`, `<guid-6>`, `<guid-7>`). Resolving them would need a new scope:

- `/beta/dataClassification/sensitiveTypes` → **403 JSON `InsufficientGraphPermissions`** — a real Graph authorization denial, so a scope WOULD help here.
- `/beta/security/informationProtection/sensitivityLabels` → **403 with an HTML body** — an edge refusal, so no scope helps (the denial-layer field guide from #344/#352/#369 applies unchanged).

No grant was made, because **the DLP audit record itself names the SIT that matched**, which is better evidence than a lookup: it tells us which type actually fired rather than which was configured. If a match lands and the record's type ids need naming, that is the moment to consider the read scope.

### Coverage strategy

Because the GUIDs are unresolved, each document carries **many** unambiguous exemplars for its theme with the supporting keywords high-confidence SITs require (`Card number:`, `Expiry`, `CVV`, `National Insurance Number`, `NHS Number`, `AccountKey=`, `client_secret`, …). With `minCount=1` any single hit fires the policy, so breadth beats precision.

**Every identifier is checksum-valid, computed rather than typed** — Luhn for the three card numbers, mod-97 for the IBANs, mod-11 for the NHS numbers, the weighted mod-11 for the UTRs. A failing checksum produces no match and would burn a whole round trip looking like a policy problem.

Files written to the maintainer's OneDrive (`DLP-Test-2026-07-29/`), each as `.txt` **and** `.docx` because DLP file-type coverage differs per workload, plus a `.csv` to exercise a spreadsheet extraction path. Every file opens with a SYNTHETIC-TEST-DATA header naming this issue, so nothing here is mistaken for real data later.

### What happens next

Once a match is confirmed in Purview, re-read `subscriptions/content?contentType=DLP.All` — remembering the content-type name correction above and that blobs lag their events by hours — and re-check `DataSecurityEvents` (#366) in the same pass.

## UNBLOCKED — the deliberate match fired, and the answer is unambiguous: `DetectedValues` is WORSE than "the value is the credential"

Maintainer created the matches 2026-07-29 (files into OneDrive + mail). **8 DLP records captured** via `DLP.All`: 7 OneDrive + 1 Exchange, 24 sensitive-information matches across all three Homelab policies.

### The headline finding, and it strengthens the standing exclusion rather than merely confirming it

`SensitiveInformationDetections.DetectedValues[]` has **two** fields and **both must be dropped**:

| field | what it actually contains |
| --- | --- |
| `Name` | the matched value **verbatim** — e.g. an AWS secret access key, a password, a card number |
| `Value` | **a ~100–135 character WINDOW OF SURROUNDING DOCUMENT CONTENT**, not the match |

That second one is the part nobody would predict from the field name, and it is the more dangerous of the two. Live example, redacted at the edges — a single AWS-key match returned:

```
"Name":  "wJz6XnQ2Kd8ryPmT4hLbVc1sAe9RgUf3ZoWxNiQq"
"Value": "ZK\r\n  aws_secret_access_key = wJz6XnQ2Kd8ryPmT4hLbVc1sAe9RgUf3ZoWxNiQq\r\n\r\nAzure storage (backup targ"
```

The `Value` window leaked **the tail of the preceding access key ID** and **the start of the next section** — content that was never itself a match. So emitting `Value` exfiltrates arbitrary adjacent document text, bounded only by a character window. `#100`'s framing was "for a credential match the value IS the credential"; measured, it is that **plus a slice of whatever sat next to it**.

Max observed `Value` length 135 chars; `Name` lengths 8–40. `ResultsTruncated` was `false` on all 24 matches, so a busy document could carry many more.

**Verdict: the safe half separates cleanly.** `SensitiveInformationDetections` is a single self-contained object, and dropping it whole leaves every other field intact and useful. This is a BUILD, not a close-no-build.

### The SIT GUIDs resolved themselves — the earlier decision not to grant a scope was right

The record carries both `SensitiveInformationTypeName` and `SensitiveType`, so the GUIDs from the policy XML are now named from the wire. All 11 observed:

| SIT name | GUID | hits |
| --- | --- | --- |
| User Login Credentials | `2de77d45-9d47-4ce2-990d-18e26b487194` | 3 |
| Credit Card Number | `<guid-6>` | 3 |
| International Banking Account Number (IBAN) | `<guid-8>` | 3 |
| Amazon S3 Client Secret Access Key | `881b8266-702b-4ebc-9c27-ea38c3765ab5` | 2 |
| GitHub Personal Access Token | `927cd1e7-8377-4df3-9bc3-fabdaef94787` | 2 |
| X.509 Certificate Private Key | `417b111d-1909-4457-b686-d6470b29a7ec` | 2 |
| SWIFT Code | `<guid-9>` | 2 |
| U.K. National Insurance Number (NINO) | `<guid-7>` | 2 |
| U.K. National Health Service Number | `<guid-10>` | 2 |
| EU Passport Number | `<guid-11>` | 2 |
| EU Debit Card Number | `<guid-12>` | 1 |

Note **`EU Passport Number` fired on a UK passport number** and **`EU Debit Card Number` on a UK card** — the SIT names do not describe the jurisdiction of the match, so a dashboard grouping by SIT name will mislabel geography.

### Four wire traps for the mapper

**`Operation` casing differs BY WORKLOAD.** OneDrive sends `DLPRuleMatch`; Exchange sends `DlpRuleMatch`. Same event, two spellings, and `RecordType` differs too (11 vs 13). A case-sensitive `Operation` switch silently drops one entire workload — and since OneDrive is 7 of 8 records here, the Exchange miss would be the quiet one.

**The metadata blocks are disjoint and workload-specific.** `SharePointMetaData` (18 keys: `FileName`, `FilePathUrl`, `FileOwner`, `FileSize`, `SiteCollectionUrl`, `IsViewableByExternalUsers`, `SensitivityLabelNames`, …) versus `ExchangeMetaData` (13 keys: `Subject`, `From`, `To`, `CC`, `BCC`, `RecipientCount`, `MessageID`, …). No overlap worth sharing a struct over.

**`Location` appears only on the Exchange match** (`"Message Body"`) — it says WHERE in the item the match was, and is absent on OneDrive.

**`RuleMode` on the record says `TestWithNotifyUser` while the policy XML says `mode="AuditAndNotify"`.** Two different vocabularies for the same state; the record's value is what an operator sees in Purview, so report `RuleMode` verbatim and do not reconcile it against the policy file.

### One judgment call to flag before it is built

`ExchangeMetaData.Subject` is emitted by nothing yet and **a subject line can itself contain the matched value** — someone mailing a card number in the subject is exactly the case this policy catches. It is metadata by position but content by nature. Proposal: **emit `Subject`**, because a DLP alert without the message subject is very hard to action and the SIEM feed is the point (#112) — but flag it here rather than deciding silently. Say so if it should be dropped or truncated instead.

Everything else is per-entity detail that belongs on the log twin: file name, path, owner, site, sender, recipients, sensitivity labels, `IncidentId`, policy/rule ids and names, severity, confidence, count.

### Acceptance status

- [x] A deliberate real match is the named unblock
- [x] Metadata can be separated safely — `SensitiveInformationDetections` drops whole
- [ ] Tests include secret sentinel values and prove they never reach metrics, logs, errors **or fixtures**
- [ ] Every non-secret record detail remains available as a log twin where useful

The fixture will carry **sentinel strings inside `DetectedValues`** rather than having them stripped, so the test proves the mapper drops the field instead of proving the fixture lacks it — the same reasoning as #338's process-argument sentinel.

## Shipped — `df24b9f`. Acceptance met; two maintainer actions remain before it collects anything.

The mapper is built and the exclusion is proven against a real match. `m365.activity` now maps the DLP.All classification metadata; no new collector, because DLP.All is a content type of the same engine and the same `m365.audit` event.

### Acceptance

- [x] A deliberate real match is the named unblock — 8 records, 24 matches, 11 SITs
- [x] Tests include secret sentinel values and prove they never reach metrics, logs, errors **or fixtures**
- [x] Every non-secret record detail remains available as a log twin where useful
- [x] Metadata separates safely, so this is a build rather than a no-build close

`make check` exit 0. No census change — this extends an existing collector.

### The sentinel, and why the fixture keeps the dangerous field

`testdata/dlp_records.json` **retains `DetectedValues` with sentinel strings in both `Name` and `Value`**. A fixture with those stripped would only prove the fixture lacks them; this proves the *mapper* drops them. Sabotage confirmed all four guards fire:

| sabotage | caught by |
| --- | --- |
| emit `DetectedValues[].Name` | the sentinel test, loudly |
| key the branch off `Operation == "DLPRuleMatch"` | the casing test — Exchange produced no DLP attributes |
| skip an absent numeric slot | the index-alignment test — `names=4 confidences=3` |
| drop the SIT metadata entirely | the #114 metadata test |

### What ships per match

Policy names/ids, rule names/modes, actions, severity, incident id, evaluation source, and the SIT dimensions as index-aligned parallel slices (name, GUID, confidence, count) — plus `dlp_results_truncated`, the one field read from inside the dropped object, because it says the counts are a floor rather than a total. Then the workload's own metadata: file name/path/owner/site and external-viewability for OneDrive, subject/from/to/cc/bcc/recipient-count for Exchange.

`is_viewable_by_external_users` is worth calling out as the field that turns a match into an incident: sensitive content in a private file is hygiene, the same content externally viewable is exposure.

### Two maintainer actions before this collects anything — and I have deliberately not taken either

**1. `ActivityFeed.ReadDlp` needs granting to `graph2otel-poller`.** This one is NOT being taken under the standing read-scope consent, on purpose. It is read-only, so it fits the letter of that consent — but it is the one scope on this project that authorises reading **matched secret values**, and the whole point of the work above is that graph2otel drops them. The collector dropping them is not the same as the poller being unable to read them, and expanding an identity's reach to secret content is a decision worth making explicitly rather than by standing policy.

**2. `DLP.All` needs adding to camden's `o365_activity.content_types`.** Currently `["Audit.Exchange", "Audit.SharePoint", "Audit.General"]`. Note the tenant's configured list REPLACES the default rather than extending it, so the new value must be the full list.

Until both land, the code is inert: no subscription, no records, and `RequiredPermissions` correctly declares only `ActivityFeed.Read`.

### One judgment call already flagged, restated so it is not lost

`ExchangeMetaData.Subject` **is** emitted. It is metadata by position and content by nature — a card number mailed in the subject line is exactly what these policies catch. It ships because a DLP alert without the subject is very hard to action and the per-entity SIEM feed is the point (#112). Reopen this issue if it should be dropped or truncated instead; the change is one line and one test.

### Volume note for whoever enables it

8 records from three documents and one email. The DLP.All feed carries one record per policy per item, so a real estate's rate scales with how much sensitive content moves rather than with tenant size — the `HighVolume` shape, though the gate lives on the subscription here rather than on a collector flag.

## LIVE READ-BACK — DLP.All wired on camden, and the exclusion is proven in production

The last open item on this issue is now closed with evidence rather than assertion.

### No grant was needed — a correction to my own earlier comment

I said `ActivityFeed.ReadDlp` needed granting. **It was already held.** Decoding the poller's `manage.office.com` token roles claim:

```
aud: https://manage.office.com   appid: 2c92ce28-…
roles: ["ActivityFeed.Read", "ActivityFeed.ReadDlp"]
```

So the scope question I raised for maintainer approval was moot — presumably granted alongside `ActivityFeed.Read` during #100. **Worth generalising: the O365 Management API roles live on a DIFFERENT token audience from Graph, so `g2o-probe --roles` (which decodes the Graph token) cannot see them.** Checking the Graph token for an `ActivityFeed.*` role will always come back empty and mean nothing.

### Config

`DLP.All` added to camden's `o365_activity.content_types` — full list, since the configured value REPLACES the default:

```yaml
content_types: ["Audit.Exchange", "Audit.SharePoint", "Audit.General", "DLP.All"]
```

Container recreated on `df24b9f`. `m365.activity` healthy, first run 992 fetched / 982 deduped / 10 emitted, 0 errored.

### Proof the records were actually consumed

All **8/8** of the DLP record ids captured by hand earlier appear in camden's checkpoint, alongside the content-blob id:

```
content:20260729213816983035923$…$dlp_all$DLP_All$gbr9017     SEEN
record:de884173-c847-409d-8437-71ba845600ca                   SEEN   (×8)
```

**A trap for anyone reading these checkpoints:** `seen_ids` keys are **prefixed** — `content:` for blob ids and `record:` for record ids. My first check searched bare GUIDs, got 0/8, and briefly looked like the wiring had failed. The prefix is the whole reason it read as a negative.

### Production read-back — the metadata is there

Live from `grafanacloud-logs`, 10 DLP records, 54 attributes each. A representative OneDrive match:

```
dlp_policy_names            Homelab - Financial
dlp_rule_modes              TestWithNotifyUser
dlp_actions                 NotifyUser,GenerateIncidentReport
dlp_sensitive_type_names    Credit Card Number,SWIFT Code,International Banking Account Number (IBAN)
dlp_sensitive_type_ids      50842eb7-…,cb2ab58c-…,e7dc4711-…
dlp_match_confidences       85,75,85
dlp_match_counts            3,2,2
dlp_results_truncated       false
file_path_url               https://m7knio-my.sharepoint.com/personal/…/02-supplier-payments-SYNTHETIC.txt
is_viewable_by_external_users  false
record_type                 ComplianceDLPSharePoint  (record_type_id 11)
```

and the Exchange side, confirming both spellings and the Exchange-only fields ship:

```
operation                   DlpRuleMatch            <- vs DLPRuleMatch on OneDrive
record_type                 ComplianceDLPExchange   (record_type_id 13)
dlp_match_location          Message Body            <- Exchange-only
subject                     EXTERNAL: Contractor onboarding - payroll details
mail_from / mail_to         …
dlp_sensitive_type_names    U.K. National Insurance Number (NINO),U.K. National Health Service Number,EU Passport Number
dlp_match_confidences       85,85,99
```

### Proof the secrets are NOT there

**22 secret patterns** from the planted documents — every card number, the AWS key id and secret, the storage account key, the Azure client secret, the GitHub PAT, the Google API key, the Slack token, the SQL password, the PEM header, the base64 basic-auth header, both IBANs, both NHS numbers, both NINOs, the UTR and the passport number — checked against the **full retrieved record payload**: **0 of 22 present.** Neither `DetectedValues` nor `SensitiveInformationDetections` appears as a key anywhere.

**How that was verified matters, because the obvious method is broken.** A LogQL line filter (`|= "…"`) is NOT a sound negative here: the same filter returned **0** for `U.K. National Insurance Number (NINO)`, a string that demonstrably IS in the structured metadata of a record in the window. A line filter matches the log LINE, and these bodies are one-liners like `DlpRuleMatch by … [Exchange]`. So the zeros it produced were vacuous. The check above pulls the full payload and greps client-side, with five positive controls proving the search would find a hit if there were one.

**An empty `|=` result over structured metadata is not evidence of absence** — same family as this project's existing "an empty Loki query is not evidence of a drop" rule, and worth adding to `docs/signals.md`.

### Acceptance — all four met

- [x] A deliberate real match is the named unblock
- [x] Tests include secret sentinel values and prove they never reach metrics, logs, errors or fixtures — and now proven in production, not just in tests
- [x] Every non-secret record detail remains available as a log twin where useful
- [x] Metadata separates safely (build, not no-build)

The synthetic test documents remain in the maintainer's OneDrive so a re-test needs no regeneration; delete when done. Note they will keep producing DLP matches on any re-scan, which is harmless but will show up as recurring records.

## Live read-back completed 2026-08-04 — the last outstanding acceptance item on this issue

Closing note only; no code changed. This issue closed with `df24b9f` on 2026-07-29 but recorded that **the live read-back had not happened**, because the collector was inert until `ActivityFeed.ReadDlp` was granted and `DLP.All` was added to camden's `o365_activity.content_types`. Both are now done and the read-back is recorded here.

```
poller token (manage.office.com)  ->  ActivityFeed.Read, ActivityFeed.ReadDlp
subscriptions/list                ->  200, DLP.All enabled
camden config.yaml                ->  content_types includes DLP.All
```

Loki, 7 days:

```
sum(count_over_time({service_name="graph2otel"} | event_name="m365.audit" | dlp_policy_names != "" [7d]))  ->  4,004
```

**Zero occurrences of `DetectedValues` or `SensitiveInformationDetections` across a 1,000-record sample.** The exclusion this issue existed to prove holds on live data at volume, not only against the captured fixture.

Distribution over that sample: `record_type_id` **11 (SharePoint) 994**, **108 (Endpoint) 6**. Policies: `Homelab - UK PII` 591, `Homelab - Financial` 389, `Homelab - Secrets and Credentials` 20.

**Endpoint DLP was not in this issue's original 8-record sample** and the mapper handled it unchanged, because it branches on the structural presence of `PolicyDetails` rather than on `Operation` spelling. At 6 in 1,000 it sits well below the ratio a silent drop would be noticed at.

Full epic receipt on #378.

## Outcome

Determine whether mailbox, OneDrive, and SharePoint protection policies, protected items, and failed backup/restore jobs can be exported safely.

## Evidence

**Evidence class:** `current v1 docs-only; new permission/service prerequisite (2026-07-25)`

- The v1 M365 Backup Storage API exposes protection policies/status and jobs.
- No current collector models recoverability across M365 workloads.

## Proposed scope

- Identify the least read-only permission and service prerequisite, then request approval before probing.
- Measure policy/item/job volumes and state as the poller.
- Build bounded protection/failure posture and per-policy/item/job logs if viable.

## Constraints and non-goals

- No policy, backup, restore, or protection action is created.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Exact permission/licence/prerequisite and live read receipt are recorded.
- [ ] Large protected-item populations have a bounded pagination/cadence design.
- [ ] Restore-capable endpoints are absent from runtime code.
- [ ] The spike closes no-data with a named service-enabled unblock if needed.

## Prior decisions and duplicate check

- No existing issue covers M365 Backup Storage protection health.

## Primary sources

- [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/tenants-backup-recovery-overview?view=graph-rest-1.0](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/tenants-backup-recovery-overview?view=graph-rest-1.0)

## Priority

Audit recommendation: **P1**.

comments.body:
## Parked by maintainer decision 2026-07-28

Microsoft 365 Backup is a paid add-on that is almost certainly not provisioned on this tenant, and both the exact permission and the service prerequisite are unestablished. Building against it now would mean writing a mapper from documentation for a service that returns nothing — the precise failure mode CLAUDE.md's wire-over-docs rule exists to prevent, and one this project has paid for more than once.

**Unblock condition:** M365 Backup is actually provisioned on the tenant. At that point the first step is a read-only probe to establish the real permission and response shape, not a mapper.

Recorded so nobody mistakes this for an engineering gap: there is nothing wrong with the design here, there is simply no service to read.

## Closed no-data — Microsoft 365 Backup is not provisioned on this tenant

`live-measured 2026-07-28` as `graph2otel-poller`. The parked premise ("a paid add-on almost certainly not provisioned") is **confirmed**, so this closes on evidence rather than on assumption.

### The API exists; the service does not

The type system is fully defined in **both** v1.0 and beta `$metadata` — `backupRestoreRoot`, `serviceStatus`, `exchangeProtectionPolicy`, `oneDriveForBusinessProtectionPolicy`, `sharePointProtectionPolicy`, `mailboxProtectionUnit`, `driveProtectionUnit`, `restorePoint`. Path is direct: `solutions` → `backupRestore` → the protection-policy collections. No derived-type cast needed (unlike #333). So this is **not** a "the documented shape is wrong" case.

| probe | result |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /v1.0/solutions/backupRestore` | **401** `UnknownError`, empty `message` |
| `GET /v1.0/solutions/backupRestore/serviceStatus` | **401** `UnknownError`, empty `message` |
| `GET /beta/solutions/backupRestore` | **401**, identical |
| `GET /v1.0/subscribedSkus` | 200 — **22 SKUs, not one containing `BACKUP`** |
| `organization.assignedPlans` | no backup service plan |
| `GET /v1.0/organization` (control) | 200, full tenant data — the token is healthy |

The 401 was re-run independently at close time and reproduced.

### A fifth denial shape for this project's ledger

This repo already tracks four denial layers that a scope grant does not move: tenant-root scope (#352), the Exchange DataInsights backend (#330), licensing (#326), and a service edge returning an HTML body (#344-#346). This is a **fifth and distinct shape: a JSON `401` with code `UnknownError` and an empty `message`.**

It is not Graph's authorization layer — that returns `403` with `Authorization_RequestDenied` and a descriptive message (compare #334 this same session, which returned exactly that shape for a genuinely missing app role). An empty-message 401 on a route whose service is not provisioned is the service failing before an authorization decision can be reached. **Do not read this as "needs a scope".**

### The scope was deliberately NOT granted

The documented least-privileged application permission is **`BackupRestore-Control.Read.All`** (`docs-only`; no higher-privileged alternative is listed). It was not granted, for two reasons:

1. The SKU absence is already conclusive. Granting would leave an unused permission on the poller to prove something the licence inventory has already proven.
2. Microsoft's own doc states these APIs *"are intended for use by registered Backup Controller applications"* and that an unsupported client gets a 403 — so the app role is likely **not sufficient on its own**. `graph2otel-poller` is not a registered Backup Controller application, and the grant might well not have changed the result. This is exactly the "check which layer is denying before reaching for a broader scope" rule this programme has now been bitten by four times.

### Named unblock

Either of these, checked live:

1. `GET /v1.0/subscribedSkus` returns a SKU or service plan whose part number contains `BACKUP`; **or**
2. `GET /v1.0/solutions/backupRestore` returns **200** rather than the current `401 UnknownError`.

If it unblocks, note that the registered-Backup-Controller-application question above is still open and should be settled before assuming an app-role grant is enough.

### Acceptance criteria

- [x] Exact permission/licence/prerequisite and live read receipt recorded — `BackupRestore-Control.Read.All`, SKU inventory, 401 receipts on both API versions.
- [ ] Bounded pagination/cadence design for large protected-item populations — **N/A**, no data reachable to design against. Deliberately not attempted rather than designed from documentation.
- [x] Restore-capable endpoints absent from runtime code — nothing was built, and no restore, enable, or policy-creation endpoint was called at any point.
- [x] Closes no-data with a named service-enabled unblock.

## Outcome

Assess near-real-time Teams, Exchange, M365 Apps, MFA, and GSA service quality between declared service-health incidents.

## Evidence

**Evidence class:** `beta docs-only (2026-07-25)`

- The beta M365 monitoring API exposes workload-specific short-window `serviceActivity` metrics with application permissions.
- Current service health reports advisories/incidents, not measured tenant experience.

## Proposed scope

- Select only app-only endpoints with actionable SLO semantics.
- Validate units, timestamps, aggregation windows, permissions, and empty behavior live.
- Build Experimental bounded operational metrics only for proven workloads.

## Constraints and non-goals

- Do not use delegated-only generic API usage surfaces.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Every chosen workload has a live response and unit/window receipt.
- [x] Dashboards distinguish tenant experience from Microsoft incident status.
- [x] No user-level dimension becomes a metric label.
- [x] The spike may close no-build for unavailable/unactionable workloads.

## Prior decisions and duplicate check

- Not duplicate of service health: this measures tenant service activity rather than published advisories.

## Primary sources

- [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/m365-monitoring-api-overview?view=graph-rest-beta](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/m365-monitoring-api-overview?view=graph-rest-beta)

## Priority

Audit recommendation: **P3**.

comments.body:
## Probe complete — **all 19 metric functions work.** Building, with one scope correction to the issue's premise.

Probed 2026-07-28 as `graph2otel-poller`, no new scope. The beta EDM was used as the discovery oracle first, then every declared function was called live over a 24h window at 30-minute aggregation.

### The scope correction, first, because it changes what this issue is

The issue was filed expecting **"Teams, Exchange, M365 Apps, MFA, and GSA"**. The beta EDM declares serviceActivity metric functions for **sign-in health (MFA, SAML, Conditional Access) and Global Secure Access only**. There is no Teams, no Exchange and no M365 Apps function on this surface — they do not exist to probe, so their absence is not a permission or licensing result.

Consequence: the deliverable is an **`entra.*` collector**, despite this issue's `area/m365` label. The namespace follows the data, not the filing.

### All 19 functions: 200, 48 buckets each

| group | functions | live result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| sign-in health | MFA success/failure, SAML success, CA blocked, CA compliant devices, CA managed devices (6) | all 200; `ca_compliant_devices_signin_success` carries real data in **47 of 48** buckets, the other five are measured zero |
| network access — apps | internet-app-policy allowed/blocked, private-apps allowed/blocked by connector (4) | all 200, measured zero |
| network access — users | internet-app-policy allowed/blocked users, private-app users allowed/blocked by connector (4) | all 200, measured zero |
| network access — branches | alive, BGP connected/disconnected, tunnel connected/disconnected (5) | all 200, measured zero |

**18 of 19 are measured ZERO, and that is a different fact from an empty response.** m7kni records no MFA-method sign-ins and has no GSA deployment, so the API returns 48 buckets each holding a real `0`. A collector that conflated "no data returned" with "the value is zero" would be wrong in both directions here, which is why a failed function contributes nothing rather than a zero.

### Two wire facts

**`aggregationIntervalInMinutes` accepts only 5, 10, 15 or 30.** A `60` returns `400 "aggregationIntervalInMinutes not valid. Allowed values are 5, 10, 15, 30."` — a usefully precise error that names the allowed set, rather than a denial. Recorded so nobody re-derives it.

**The response element has exactly two fields** — `{"intervalStartDateTime":"2026-07-27T12:00:00Z","value":0}` — with **no entity dimension at all**. That settles the acceptance criterion *"no user-level dimension becomes a metric label"* by construction: there is no user-level dimension on the wire. It is also why this collector carries **no log twin** — nothing per-entity is fetched, so #114 has nothing to preserve. This is the one collector shape in the tree where a gauge is the complete signal, and that is stated in the package doc so a future reader does not read the absence as a bug.

### What ships

Four gauges rather than one, because the units differ and a mixed-unit `sum by` would be meaningless: `entra.service_activity.signins` `{signin}`, `.network_access_apps` `{app}`, `.network_access_users` `{user}`, `.network_access_branches` `{branch}` — each keyed by `activity` and `aggregation_interval_minutes`. 19 series total.

The window end is truncated down to a bucket boundary so every bucket is complete and the gauge publishes the latest one: sampling a partial trailing bucket reports a half-counted interval, which on a graph is indistinguishable from a real drop — the exact failure mode this collector exists to detect.

`Experimental` and opt-in per #183 (beta-only surface). Nothing declared to `internal/wirecheck` — the activity names are graph2otel's own rendering of Microsoft's function names, not a Graph-supplied value set.

**Evidence class:** `live-measured 2026-07-28, #368`.

## Shipped in `0811619` — `entra.service_activity`

Four bounded gauges over all 19 metric functions, `Experimental` and opt-in per #183, no new grant. `make check` exit 0.

- [x] **Every chosen workload has a live response and unit/window receipt.** All 19 functions, 200, 48 buckets over 24h at 30-minute aggregation. Receipts in the comment above.
- [x] **Dashboards distinguish tenant experience from Microsoft incident status.** Its own board section, named and described against `m365.service_health` — that collector reports what Microsoft has *declared*, this reports what the tenant *experienced*.
- [x] **No user-level dimension becomes a metric label.** True by construction: the response element is `{intervalStartDateTime, value}` and carries no entity dimension at all.
- [x] **The spike may close no-build for unavailable/unactionable workloads.** Exercised — see the scope correction.

### Scope correction, restated because it changes what shipped

Filed expecting Teams, Exchange and M365 Apps. The beta EDM declares **none** of them on this surface. They were not unavailable or unlicensed; they do not exist to probe. The deliverable is therefore an `entra.*` collector despite the `area/m365` label — the namespace follows the data.

### The one that got caught by review

An earlier cut of the frozen attribute contract carried `interval_start` on the gauge, so a reader could tell which half-hour a value describes. **That is unbounded cardinality** — a new bucket start every 30 minutes is a new series every 30 minutes, forever, each with exactly one sample: the shape #112 forbids for a correlation id, reached from a different direction. `internal/signalcapture`'s per-entity denylist is an exact-match keyword list and does not contain `interval_start`, so the gate passed it clean.

**The gate not firing is not evidence of correctness.** The attribute is gone, the reasoning is recorded in `attrs_entra_serviceactivity.go` rather than quietly deleted (it is a seductive mistake — the information is genuinely useful and there is no log twin to put it on), and the package now carries an **allow-list** guard asserting the emitted key set is exactly `{activity, aggregation_interval_minutes}`. Sabotage re-adding the attribute fails it by name.

What replaces it is honesty about the sampling lag: the gauge publishes the latest **complete** bucket, so its value describes a window ending at most one aggregation interval ago.

### Two wire facts

`aggregationIntervalInMinutes` accepts only **5, 10, 15, 30** — `60` returns a 400 naming the allowed set. And 18 of 19 functions are a **measured zero** on this tenant while one carries real data in 47 of 48 buckets; a failed fetch contributes nothing rather than a zero, because the two are different facts and this collector's whole value depends on not conflating them.

No log twin, by construction — nothing per-entity is fetched, so #114 has nothing to preserve. Stated in the package doc so it is not later read as an omission and "fixed".

**Evidence class:** `live-measured 2026-07-28, #368`.

## Outcome

Capture new Microsoft service-health timeline updates once each without re-emitting large HTML on every snapshot.

## Evidence

**Evidence class:** `source-derived conditional enhancement (2026-07-25)`

- Service-health issues already return historical `posts` inline.
- Current code deliberately omits them because snapshot emission would repeat multi-kilobyte HTML every 15 minutes.

## Proposed scope

- Emit one `m365.service_health_post` per new post using checkpointed dedupe on issue/time/type.
- Measure/cap HTML body size and preserve issue linkage.

## Constraints and non-goals

- Do not ingest PIR binary file streams.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The same post emits once across repeated polls and restarts.
- [ ] New posts for an existing issue emit promptly.
- [ ] Body-size behavior is measured and bounded.
- [ ] Original event time and issue ID are preserved.

## Prior decisions and duplicate check

- Not duplicate of service-health issue/message state; this adds a checkpointed update timeline with intentionally different emission semantics.
- Related: #114.

## Primary sources

- [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/servicehealthissuepost?view=graph-rest-1.0](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/servicehealthissuepost?view=graph-rest-1.0)

## Priority

Audit recommendation: **P3**.

comments.body:
## Closed by `2483dd4`

### The measurement that shaped the design

`live-measured (2026-07-27, #367)`, as `graph2otel-poller`. `GET /v1.0/admin/serviceAnnouncement/issues?$top=100` returns posts **inline**, so this adds no request — the issue's "source-derived" framing is correct.

| fact | measured |
| --- | --- |
| issues / posts carried inline | 100 / **829** |
| post body (`description.content`, HTML) | min 42 B, median 1068 B, p95 1792 B, **max 2176 B** |
| all post bodies together | ~878 KB |
| max posts on one issue | 37 |
| `postType` | `regular` (807), `quick` (22) |
| keys on a post object | exactly `createdDateTime`, `description`, `postType` |

**A post has no ID.** That single fact decides the design: identity has to be derived, and `issueID + createdDateTime + postType` is all the wire supports.

### The trap that would have made a naive implementation wrong

The endpoint re-serves the **entire retained issue history on every poll** — today's response carried issues that opened and resolved in February. Every other checkpointed collector here evicts its seen-set on a time window, which is sound when the source offers a recent tail. Here it is not: a post would fall out of the window, be re-offered, and re-emit as new. The build lane spotted this and stopped rather than shipping it.

Resolved with the house watermark shape instead: a high-watermark over `createdDateTime` plus a seen-ID set covering only a 24h overlap behind it. A re-offered old post is below the watermark and never reconsidered, so the seen-set is bounded by time rather than by history. A post added today to a February issue carries today's timestamp, so it is above the watermark and emits promptly.

### First run primes, and that is deliberate

It records the watermark and emits nothing. Most of those 829 posts are older than the backend's 7-day accept window, so replaying history would feed the horizon guard added in `b4fcaec` rather than populate a timeline — loud rejections, no data. Same precedent as the annotation writer's state-shaped priming. Pinned by `TestFirstRunPrimesServiceHealthPostsWithoutEmitting`, because "first run emits nothing" reads as a bug without a test saying otherwise.

### Body size

Cap **8192 bytes** — 3.8x the observed max, 4.6x p95, so nothing on the wire today is touched. Over the cap it **truncates at a UTF-8 rune boundary and sets `body_truncated`**, never drops: the post's identity, issue linkage and event time are all still correct, so it is degraded, not wrong, and only wrong justifies a drop. Raw HTML is preserved verbatim rather than stripped — the transformation is lossy and the source's content is what the log is for.

A post with a missing or unparseable `createdDateTime` is dropped and counted, never stamped with arrival time.

### Verified by sabotage

Breaking the watermark persistence fails six tests including the cross-restart dedupe case, which constructs three fresh collectors over one checkpoint directory.

### For the record

`postType` is a bounded two-value set but is **not** wirecheck-watched: it is a log attribute only, never a metric label, so an unmapped value moves no series and changes no number. `make check` exit 0.

## Outcome

Test whether DataSecurityEvents provides the first collector-shaped app-only route to Insider Risk data.

## Evidence

**Evidence class:** `preview docs-only; feature sharing/data required (2026-07-25)`

- #251 found no direct Insider Risk entity API.
- The preview hunting table may expose shared data when the tenant feature/configuration is enabled.
- No real row is currently known.

## Proposed scope

- Maintainer reviews/enables the required data-sharing configuration outside graph2otel.
- Probe table availability, schema, row volume, and overlap through the existing hunting engine.
- Build only from real rows with Experimental/HighVolume decisions.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Required licence/config and approval are recorded.
- [ ] A real row is the implementation unblock.
- [ ] Content/secret risk is reviewed from the wire.
- [ ] The spike closes no-data rather than inventing a mapper.

## Prior decisions and duplicate check

- Not duplicate of #251: the possible changed fact is a new hunting-table route, gated on explicit data sharing.
- Related: #249, #251.

## Primary sources

- [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-xdr/advanced-hunting-datasecurityevents-table](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-xdr/advanced-hunting-datasecurityevents-table)

## Priority

Audit recommendation: **P2**.

comments.body:
## Closed no-data — the table is reachable and genuinely empty

`live-measured 2026-07-28`, as `graph2otel-poller` over the shipped advanced-hunting transport (#249). **No new scope was needed** — `ThreatHunting.Read.All` is already in the roles claim.

| query | result |
| --- | --- |
| `DataSecurityEvents \| summarize n=count()` | HTTP 200, **`n = 0`** |
| `DataSecurityEvents \| take 2` | HTTP 200, 0 results, full **52-column** schema returned |

The count was re-run independently at close time and returned `0` again.

This is the same shape as #365 (`CampaignInfo`) and #349 (`DisruptionAndResponseEvents`): a 200 with a schema proves the table is reachable and empty, not inaccessible. No 403, no HTML edge body, no authorization layer involved.

### The live schema does not match the documented one — treat the doc column list as directional

Microsoft's public column reference for this table is **not** what the endpoint returns. The live surface folds several documented flat fields into aggregate `*Info` objects (`ContentInfo`, `AlertInfo`, `DeviceInfo`, `ParentContentInfo`, `IrmSequenceInfo`) and carries columns the doc page does not list at all (`RiskyAIUsageAppCategory`, `RiskyAIUsageAccessedResourceInfo`, `RiskyAIUsageSensitivityLabelsInfo`, `IsIrmInteresting`). Another entry for the wire-over-docs ledger. Anyone writing the mapper later should re-capture the schema rather than build from the doc page.

Full 52 columns, `live-measured 2026-07-28`:

`Timestamp`, `EventTime`, `ApplicationNames`, `DlpPolicyMatchInfo`, `DlpPolicyEnforcementMode`, `DlpPolicyRuleMatchInfo`, `FileRenameInfo`, `AccountUpn`, `AccountObjectId`, `Department`, `SourceCodeInfo`, `CcPolicyMatchInfo`, `IPAddress`, `DeviceSourceLocationType`, `DeviceDestinationLocationType`, `IrmPolicyMatchInfo`, `UnallowedUrlDomains`, `ExternalUrlDomains`, `UrlDomainInfo`, `SourceUrlDomain`, `TargetUrlDomain`, `InternetMessageId`, `NetworkMessageId`, `EmailSubject`, `ObjectId`, `ActivityId`, `ActionType`, `SensitiveInfoTypeInfo`, `SensitivityLabelId`, `SharepointSiteSensitivityLabelId`, `PreviousSensitivityLabelId`, `Operation`, `Recipients`, `SourceRelativeUrl`, `TargetFilePath`, `PrinterName`, `Workload`, `IrmActionCategory`, `DeviceInfo`, `PhysicalAccessPointInfo`, `RemovableMediaInfo`, `TeamsChannelInfo`, `ContentInfo`, `ParentContentInfo`, `IrmSequenceInfo`, `AlertInfo`, `UserAlternateEmails`, `RiskyAIUsageAppCategory`, `RiskyAIUsageAccessedResourceInfo`, `RiskyAIUsageSensitivityLabelsInfo`, `AttachmentInfo`, `IsIrmInteresting`.

### The content-risk question is deferred, not answered — and it must be answered before any mapper

The acceptance criterion "content/secret risk is reviewed from the wire" **cannot be met on zero rows**, so it is explicitly left open rather than waved through. Structural candidates flagged from the schema, none decided:

- **`ContentInfo`** — the strongest candidate. If it carries the matched text rather than metadata about the match, it is the second content exclusion this project has ever had (the first and only being `intune/auditevents`' `modifiedProperties` values).
- **`SensitiveInfoTypeInfo`** — Microsoft documents this as *which* SIT matched, i.e. metadata. `docs-only`, unconfirmed against a real row, and this project's record on docs is poor.
- **`EmailSubject`** — user-authored content, closer to metadata than a match body.
- `TargetFilePath`, `SourceRelativeUrl`, `AttachmentInfo`, `FileRenameInfo` — paths and filenames, per-entity but not content.

Per CLAUDE.md, "awkward to model" is not "unsafe to ship" and that conflation has already shipped wrong three times (#110/#111, then `ExtendedProperties` on #100). So this is recorded as an open question against a real row, not as a pre-emptive exclusion.

### Named unblock

**A real row appears in `DataSecurityEvents`.** Check with `DataSecurityEvents | summarize n=count()` returning non-zero.

Two things gate that, and the wire cannot tell them apart:

1. The tenant must have opted in to sharing Insider Risk alerts with Microsoft Defender. Microsoft: *"If your organization hasn't opted in to share insider risk alerts with Microsoft Defender, queries that use the table aren't going to work or return any results."* `docs-only`.
2. An Insider Risk or DLP policy must actually have matched.

**The opt-in state is not observable read-only through Graph.** There is no settings endpoint for it, and an opted-out tenant and an opted-in tenant with no violations produce a byte-identical zero. Confirming it requires the Purview/Defender portal. That ambiguity is itself the finding — do not read a future zero as proof the toggle is off.

Related: #370 needs a deliberately created DLP match for the same underlying reason. If that gets created, re-check this table at the same time — one tenant action may fire both.

No mapper was written. No fixture was invented. Closing per acceptance criterion 4.

## Re-validated 2026-07-29 after DLP rules were configured — still 0 rows

The maintainer has now set up DLP rules on the tenant, so this table was re-probed as `graph2otel-poller` on the chance the no-data close had been overtaken.

```
DataSecurityEvents | summarize n=count()   ->  200, n = 0
```

Unchanged from the close. `ThreatHunting.Read.All` already held; no new scope.

**This is the expected reading and does not weaken the unblock condition.** Rules existing is not the same as rules matching — this table carries *events*, and no content has tripped a policy yet. The close stands, and the unblock is still what it was: a deliberate DLP match, which also unblocks #370. When that match is created, re-check this table at the same time; the same tenant action fires both.

Worth restating because it is the trap this table sits in: **an opted-out tenant and an opted-in tenant with no violations produce a byte-identical zero here.** So this probe confirms "still nothing to map" and specifically does *not* confirm the Insider-Risk-to-Defender sharing state either way.

## Outcome

Determine whether Defender campaign clustering adds actionable email-threat context before building a high-volume mapper.

## Evidence

**Evidence class:** `preview docs-only; existing hunting scope (2026-07-25)`

- `CampaignInfo` is a preview MDO hunting table.
- The tenant previously had no observed row/container.
- The existing hunting engine and scope can probe it, but docs alone are not mapper evidence.

## Proposed scope

- Probe count/schema/sample and query cost through the existing hunting API.
- If viable, require both Experimental and measured HighVolume gating.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A real row is the implementation unblock.
- [ ] Query partitioning respects the 100,000-row cap and shared CPU.
- [ ] No docs-shaped mapper lands.
- [ ] Overlap with Defender email signals is documented.

## Prior decisions and duplicate check

- This is a named data-gated table assessment, not a broad Defender hunting expansion.
- Related: #106, #241, #249.

## Primary sources

- [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-xdr/advanced-hunting-campaigninfo-table](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-xdr/advanced-hunting-campaigninfo-table)

## Priority

Audit recommendation: **P3**.

comments.body:
## Spike result — **no-build.** `CampaignInfo` is reachable and empty, which is what this issue asked to establish.

### The measurement — as `graph2otel-poller` through the shipped hunting API and scope, 2026-07-28

```kql
CampaignInfo | summarize n=count()   →  n = 0
CampaignInfo | take 2                →  0 results, 8-column schema returned
```

Both 200 under the existing `ThreatHunting.Read.All` — no new permission was needed, as the issue predicted. The schema comes back complete (`Timestamp`, `CampaignName`, `CampaignId`, `CampaignType`, `CampaignSubType`, `NetworkMessageId`, `RecipientEmailAddress`, `ReportId`), so the preview table is provisioned on this tenant and queryable. It has never had a row.

### Verdict

**No build**, on this issue's own terms: *"the existing hunting engine and scope can probe it, but docs alone are not mapper evidence."* The probe ran, the evidence is that there is nothing to map.

The two gates the issue set for building are both unreachable:

- **Measured `HighVolume` gating.** A `HighVolume` annotation requires a *measured* volume figure — CLAUDE.md is explicit that "high volume" with no number is not something anyone can plan capacity against. Zero rows measures nothing. And a mail campaign table is the shape where that matters: volume scales with inbound mail traffic, so a tenant with real phishing pressure could be orders of magnitude away from anything inferable here.
- **Query cost.** Also unmeasurable — a `count()` over an empty table says nothing about what the same query costs against a populated one, and this runs on the shared human hunting CPU quota.

`CampaignType` and `CampaignSubType` would be the natural bounded metric labels, and neither has a single observed value. One observed value is not a value set; zero is not even a candidate.

The earlier record ("the tenant previously had no observed row/container") is confirmed, not superseded — but it is now confirmed against the table itself rather than against a container search, which is the stronger form.

**Named unblock:** at least one row appears in `CampaignInfo` — i.e. Microsoft correlates a mail campaign against this tenant. Then: measure count and query cost, read the `CampaignType`/`CampaignSubType` value sets off real rows, and decide `HighVolume` from a real number. Both the scope and the transport are already in place, so the re-probe is one query.

### Acceptance criteria

- [x] Probe count/schema/sample and query cost through the existing hunting API — count 0, schema captured, sample empty; query cost is not measurable against an empty table and is deliberately not extrapolated.
- [ ] If viable, require both Experimental and measured HighVolume gating — not viable; no build, so no annotation to justify.

**Evidence class:** `live-measured 2026-07-28, #365`.

## Outcome

Assess meeting/call quality records with correct lag, retention, versioned dedupe, and session/segment fan-out.

## Evidence

**Evidence class:** `docs-only; new permission and HighVolume assessment (2026-07-25)`

- The v1 callRecords API is not collected and requires `CallRecords.Read.All`.
- Records can arrive late/versioned and expire after 30 days.

## Proposed scope

- After explicit scope approval, measure record count, version updates, 150+ minute lag, sessions/segments, and payload size.
- Design a WindowCollector deduping on `id+version`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Live measurements establish whether `HighVolume` is required.
- [ ] Late versions update without replaying unchanged records.
- [ ] Session/segment fan-out is bounded.
- [ ] No participant identity becomes a metric label.

## Prior decisions and duplicate check

- No existing issue covers Teams call quality records; service health and Teams inventory answer different questions.

## Primary sources

- [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/callrecords-cloudcommunications-list-callrecords?view=graph-rest-1.0](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/callrecords-cloudcommunications-list-callrecords?view=graph-rest-1.0)

## Priority

Audit recommendation: **P2**.

comments.body:
## Spike result — **no-data.** The call-record surface is reachable and empty.

### The grant (recorded per the standing consent)

`CallRecords.Read.All` — appRole `<guid-13>`, granted 2026-07-28T11:00Z as an `appRoleAssignment` on the `graph2otel-poller` SP (`13371536-9950-4988-90f4-343566456781`). Assignment id `NhU3E1CZiEmQ9DQ1ZkVngVBHAWLu1B9Hg3TugZIG118`. Read-only, application-type. Verified present in a freshly minted poller token before probing.

### The measurement

`GET /v1.0/communications/callRecords` as `graph2otel-poller` → **200, `value: []`**.

200 rather than 403, so the scope is effective and the API is provisioned. There are simply no call records: records expire after 30 days and nobody on this tenant has placed a Teams call inside that window.

### Verdict

**No build.** Every question this spike exists to answer is a property of real records and none of them survives an empty collection:

- **record count and payload size** — nothing to count or measure.
- **version updates and the 150+ minute arrival lag** — the central design risk. A `WindowCollector` deduping on `id+version` is only correct if late-arriving versions actually behave the way the documentation says, and this project's standing rule is that Microsoft's documentation has been wrong on essentially every load-bearing detail on this path. Building a checkpointed window collector on an unverified late-arrival model is how a stream silently double-counts or drops.
- **sessions and segments fan-out** — no record to expand.
- **`HighVolume` assessment** — volume here scales with call TRAFFIC, which is the textbook `HighVolume` shape (#254), and a *measured* volume figure is mandatory for that annotation. There is no traffic to measure, so the flag could not be justified even if the collector were built.

**Named unblock:** at least one Teams call has completed on the tenant within the last 30 days. Then: capture the record, measure the arrival lag against `endDateTime`, poll twice to observe whether a `version` increments on an already-seen `id`, and measure per-record payload size before designing the watermark and overlap. The scope stays granted, so the re-probe is one request.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Measure record count, version updates, 150+ minute lag, sessions/segments, and payload size — unmeasurable on an empty collection, and deliberately not inferred from documentation.
- [ ] Design a WindowCollector deduping on `id+version` — not designed, because its correctness depends on the late-version behavior above.

**Evidence class:** `live-measured 2026-07-28, #364`.
