body:
## Outcome

Determine whether forwarding, redirect, delete, and hidden inbox rules can be inventoried with command-scoped Exchange application RBAC.

## Evidence

**Evidence class:** ~~`docs-only; current Global Reader explicitly insufficient (2026-07-25)`~~ — **DISPROVED** `live-measured 2026-07-28, #363`: the cmdlet works under the poller's existing rights. See the 2026-07-28 comment.

- `Get-InboxRule -IncludeHidden` adds current-state persistence beyond audit change events.
- Microsoft states the cmdlet does not work with Global Reader or View-Only Organization Management.

## Proposed scope

- Design and request approval for the narrowest Exchange application RBAC assignment.
- Prove mutation cmdlets remain denied.
- Capture one real rule and measure N-mailbox fan-out before collector design.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Exact RBAC assignment and denial boundary are recorded. (No assignment required — existing rights suffice; denial proven by invocation.)
- [x] A real hidden/non-hidden rule shape is captured. (Junk E-mail Rule; no forwarding/redirect rule exists on this tenant to capture.)
- [x] Request cost and cadence are measured. (995 ms/mailbox avg, `1 + N`.)
- [x] No role change is made without explicit maintainer approval. (No role change was made at all.)

## Prior decisions and duplicate check

- Unified audit reports rule changes; this spike tests current-state inventory under a new least-privilege authorization model.
- Related: #250.

## Primary sources

- [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/exchangepowershell/get-inboxrule?view=exchange-ps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/exchangepowershell/get-inboxrule?view=exchange-ps)

## Priority

Audit recommendation: **P1**.

comments.body:
## Decision received 2026-07-28 — design AND grant the narrow Exchange RBAC role

The maintainer chose to have the role designed and created in one pass rather than reviewing the definition first.

Terms:
- Work out the **minimum** Exchange RBAC role that permits `Get-InboxRule -IncludeHidden`, create it, and record the exact definition here.
- **Prove the denial boundary**, do not assume it: demonstrate that mutation cmdlets are denied under the new role, and record what specifically fails. A role that turns out to permit more than intended is the failure mode this whole issue exists to avoid.
- Measure the per-mailbox fan-out cost before any mapper work — this is a per-mailbox cmdlet and the tenant's mailbox count sets the budget.
- Record everything on this issue: the role definition, the cmdlets it grants, the denial evidence, and the fan-out measurement.

Context worth keeping: Microsoft's own documentation states Global Reader is explicitly **insufficient** for this cmdlet, which is what makes a purpose-built role necessary rather than a convenience. Malicious inbox rules are a classic post-compromise persistence and exfiltration mechanism, so the coverage is worth the role.

## Spike complete — and the premise is WRONG. **No new Exchange RBAC role is needed, and none was created.**

All `live-measured 2026-07-28, #363`, app-only as `graph2otel-poller` (cert credential, `Connect-ExchangeOnline -AppId ... -Organization m7kni.io`, ExchangeOnlineManagement 3.10.0).

This issue's evidence class was `docs-only`, and the doc is wrong for this tenant. Microsoft states `Get-InboxRule` does not work with Global Reader. **It works right now, unmodified, under the poller's existing rights.**

```
OK  DiscoverySearchMailbox{...}@m7knio.onmicrosoft.com  rules=1 (1096 ms)
OK  rob@m7kni.io                                        rules=1 (1436 ms)
OK  vmuser@m7kni.io                                     rules=1  (681 ms)
```

The poller holds **Global Reader** and **Security Reader**. Which of the two carries the cmdlet was *not* isolated, deliberately — establishing it would mean revoking a standing role that three shipped collectors depend on, to answer a question that changes nothing. The capability is present; that is the operative fact.

**Consequence: acceptance item 4 is satisfied trivially — no role was designed, requested or created, because none is required.** The approval to create one stands unused rather than spent.

### `-IncludeHidden` is honoured, and it is load-bearing — not a nice-to-have

Same mailbox, same session, both shapes:

| call | rules returned |
| --- | ---: |
| `Get-InboxRule -Mailbox rob@m7kni.io -IncludeHidden` | **1** (`Junk E-mail Rule`) |
| `Get-InboxRule -Mailbox rob@m7kni.io` | **0** |

**Every inbox rule on this tenant is hidden.** A collector built without `-IncludeHidden` would return zero rows tenant-wide and report clean success forever — a total blind spot for exactly the persistence mechanism this issue exists to catch, and invisible from the endpoint's behaviour because "no rules" looks identical to "no rules found".

(An earlier probe in this session appeared to show no difference. That was an artifact of `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` capturing an error record into the result array. The clean measurement above is the real one.)

### Denial boundary — PROVEN, not assumed

Exchange RBAC does not merely reject unauthorized cmdlets; it **removes them from the session entirely**, so an unauthorized mutation fails with `CommandNotFoundException` before any target is touched.

| cmdlet | in session |
| --- | --- |
| `Get-InboxRule` | **PRESENT** |
| `New-InboxRule`, `Set-InboxRule`, `Remove-InboxRule`, `Disable-InboxRule`, `Enable-InboxRule` | **ABSENT** |
| `Set-Mailbox`, `New-Mailbox`, `Remove-Mailbox` | **ABSENT** |
| `Set-TransportRule`, `New-ManagementRole` | **ABSENT** |

Verified by invocation, not only by `Get-Command`. Each mutation was actually called — against a **deliberately nonexistent rule id**, so that an authorized call would have failed harmlessly on "not found" and an unauthorized one on permissions, making the two outcomes distinguishable without risking a real change:

```
Remove-InboxRule   -> CommandNotFoundException: The term 'Remove-InboxRule' is not recognized...
Disable-InboxRule  -> CommandNotFoundException: The term 'Disable-InboxRule' is not recognized...
Set-InboxRule      -> CommandNotFoundException: The term 'Set-InboxRule' is not recognized...
```

All three denied. **Nothing on the tenant was mutated by this spike.**

### Real rule shape captured

`Junk E-mail Rule`, `Identity=bbcfc3c5-...\721857812023476225`, `RuleIdentity=721857812023476225`, `Enabled=True`, `Priority=0`. Populated properties:

`Enabled, Identity, InError, ErrorType, Name, Priority, RuleIdentity, SupportedByTask, AnyCategory, ExceptIfAnyCategory, HasAttachment, ExceptIfHasAttachment, IsExternal, ExceptIfIsExternal, IsMentioned, ExceptIfIsMentioned, MyNameInCcBox, ExceptIfMyNameInCcBox, MyNameInToBox, ExceptIfMyNameInToBox, MyNameInToOrCcBox, ExceptIfMyNameInToOrCcBox, MyNameNotInToBox, ExceptIfMyNameNotInToBox, SentOnlyToMe, ExceptIfSentOnlyToMe, ClearCategories, ClearFlag, CompleteFlag, DeleteMessage, MarkAsRead, PermanentDelete, PinMessage, SoftDeleteMessage, StopProcessingRules, MailboxOwnerId, IsValid, ObjectState`

Caveat for whoever writes the mapper, in this repo's usual terms: **the forwarding/redirect fields this issue actually cares about — `ForwardTo`, `ForwardAsAttachmentTo`, `RedirectTo`, `DeleteMessage` set true — are absent or false on every row here, because the only rule on this tenant is a default Junk E-mail Rule.** One observed rule is not a rule shape. A real forwarding rule has to be created deliberately or constructed as a fixture, or the mapper ships never having mapped the thing it exists to detect. Same shape as #356 (242 rows, all `false`) and #355.

### Fan-out cost measured

`Get-InboxRule -Mailbox <x> -IncludeHidden`, 9 calls across 3 mailboxes:

| metric | value |
| --- | ---: |
| min | 537 ms |
| **avg** | **995 ms** |
| max | 1421 ms |

Serial, one call per mailbox, at the measured average:

| mailboxes | per-cycle cost |
| ---: | ---: |
| 3 (m7kni) | ~3 s |
| 100 | ~100 s |
| 1,000 | ~16.6 min |
| 5,000 | **~83 min** |

`Get-Mailbox -ResultSize Unlimited` enumerates in one call, so the shape is `1 + N` — the same per-mailbox fan-out problem as **#355** (`1 + 2N`), on the same transport, with no batch form.

**Note for the collector design, because the obvious answer is wrong:** `HighVolume` is *not* the right interface here. This repo defines `HighVolume` as a firehose whose rate scales with **traffic**; per-mailbox fan-out scales with **tenant size**. `Experimental` does not fit either — this is EXO PowerShell, not a Graph beta surface. So a per-mailbox collector needs an explicit fan-out budget (cap + opt-in), and #355 and #363 should share one mechanism rather than inventing two.

### Acceptance

- [x] Exact RBAC assignment and denial boundary are recorded — assignment: **none required**; denial boundary proven by invocation.
- [x] A real hidden/non-hidden rule shape is captured — with the honest caveat that no forwarding/redirect rule exists here to capture.
- [x] Request cost and cadence are measured — 995 ms/mailbox avg, `1 + N`.
- [x] No role change is made without explicit maintainer approval — **no role change was made at all.**

Closing as spike-complete: the authorization question is answered (yes, with existing rights, mutation provably denied). The collector build is not this issue and is gated on the shared per-mailbox fan-out decision tracked with #355, plus a real forwarding rule to map against.

Spike complete. Authorization question answered with no new role required; mutation denial proven by invocation; fan-out measured. Collector build is gated on the shared per-mailbox fan-out decision (with #355) and on a real forwarding rule to map against.

## Live capture against a REAL forwarding rule — plus a correction to this issue's own `-IncludeHidden` claim

The maintainer created a deliberate test rule on `vmuser@m7kni.io`. Captured read-only **as `graph2otel-poller`** (the identity the collector will actually use, not an admin session), `live-measured 2026-07-28, #363`. The artifacts are being removed immediately after this capture, so **this comment is the durable record** — the mapper should be written from here.

### CORRECTION: "every inbox rule on this tenant is hidden" was an artifact of a one-rule tenant

My earlier comment reported `-IncludeHidden` → 1 rule, without → **0**, and concluded a collector missing the flag "returns zero rows tenant-wide". **That generalisation was wrong.** With a second, user-created rule present:

| call | rules |
| --- | --- |
| `Get-InboxRule -Mailbox vmuser -IncludeHidden` | **2** — `Junk E-mail Rule`, `g2o-test-forward` |
| `Get-InboxRule -Mailbox vmuser` | **1** — `g2o-test-forward` |

So a **user-created rule is visible WITHOUT the flag**. The only thing `-IncludeHidden` added on this tenant was the *system* `Junk E-mail Rule`. The earlier zero was because the Junk rule was the sole rule, not because ordinary rules are hidden.

`-IncludeHidden` is still the right call — attacker-planted rules with a manipulated `PR_RULE_MSG_PROVIDER` are genuinely hidden, and that is the persistence case this issue exists for — but **the justification recorded above is not the reason**, and citing "without it you see nothing" would be citing an artifact. We still have **no sample of a maliciously hidden rule**; the Junk rule is not a proxy for one.

### THE TRAP: `RuleIdentity` overflows int64, and a float64 decode silently corrupts it

```
RuleIdentity = 15394007230974001153   <BigInteger>
int64  max   =  9223372036854775807   -> OVERFLOWS
uint64 max   = 18446744073709551615   -> fits
float64      -> 15394007230974001152  -> OFF BY ONE, silently
```

The type on the wire is **`BigInteger`**, not `Int64`. Decoding this into a Go `int64` overflows, and decoding a JSON number into `interface{}`/`float64` — the default path — **loses the low bits and produces a wrong id that still looks like a plausible id**. This is not theoretical: the two previously captured ids (`721857812023476225`, `5693957303879860225`) both fit int64, so a mapper built on the earlier samples alone would have looked correct and corrupted this one.

**Carry `RuleIdentity` as a string.** It is an opaque identity, never arithmetic.

### THE TRAP: `ForwardTo` is not an address

```
ForwardTo = ["Rob Knight" [EX:/o=ExchangeLabs/ou=Exchange Administrative Group (FYDIBOHF23SPDLT)/cn=Recipients/cn=8450ce8cf45b4ee88feb21c3cacff073-bbcfc3c5-0b]]
```

An `ArrayList` whose element is a **display name plus a legacyExchangeDN**, not an SMTP address. There is no SMTP address anywhere in the rule object. So "which address is mail being forwarded to" — the whole security question — **cannot be answered from the rule alone**; it needs a separate recipient resolution, or the raw value must be emitted honestly rather than half-parsed into something that looks like an address. An external forward would presumably carry an SMTP-shaped value instead, but **that shape is unobserved** and must not be assumed.

`SubjectContainsWords` is likewise an `ArrayList`, not a string.

### Full non-default property set of the forwarding rule

```
Description          = "If the message: the message includes specific words in the subject
                        'g2o-test-forward' Take the following actions: forward the message
                        to 'Rob Knight'"                                   <String>
Enabled              = True                                                <Boolean>
Identity             = 7957928c-3cd2-4bbb-98c8-cfc8466f490a\15394007230974001153  <String>
ErrorType            = None                                                <String>
Name                 = g2o-test-forward                                    <String>
Priority             = 1                                                   <Int32>
RuleIdentity         = 15394007230974001153                                <BigInteger>
SupportedByTask      = True                                                <Boolean>
SubjectContainsWords = [g2o-test-forward]                                  <ArrayList>
ForwardTo            = ["Rob Knight" [EX:/o=...]]                          <ArrayList>
MailboxOwnerId       = 7957928c-3cd2-4bbb-98c8-cfc8466f490a                <String>
IsValid              = True                                                <Boolean>
ObjectState          = Unchanged                                           <String>
```

`Identity` is `<mailbox guid>\<RuleIdentity>` — so it embeds the same oversized integer and is also string-only. `Priority` is `Int32` and distinguishes rules (Junk = 0, this = 1).

Every other property is absent or `False`. Still **unobserved and not to be invented**: `RedirectTo`, `ForwardAsAttachmentTo`, `DeleteMessage=True`, and any genuinely hidden (non-system) rule.

## The shared per-mailbox fan-out gate is built and frozen — `fed98f8`

The named unblock condition on this issue ("agreement on the shared gate: opt-in key, cap, default, and the covered/total truncation signal") has fired. It is now agreed **and** implemented, so the seam both collectors build against is stable.

**Config** (per tenant, alongside `exchange_online`):

```yaml
exo_per_mailbox:
  enabled: true         # the whole opt-in; unset registers NO per-mailbox EXO collector
  max_mailboxes: 250    # default; unset means 250, never "cap of zero"
```

`internal/config.ExoPerMailboxConfig` — `Configured()`, `Cap()`, `validate()` (rejects a negative cap; an unset cap defaults rather than erroring).

**Enumeration** — `internal/exofanout.Enumerate(ctx, client, cap) (Result, error)`:

```go
type Result struct {
    Mailboxes []Mailbox  // covered set, sorted by PrimarySmtpAddress
    Total     int        // what the tenant really has, including unaddressable rows
    Covered   int        // what this cycle will poll
    Truncated bool       // Covered < Total, for any reason
}
```

Decisions baked in, each for a stated reason:

- **`ResultSize=Unlimited` is pinned.** Without it the TOTAL is silently short and the truncation signal becomes a lie rather than a guard.
- **Deterministic sort on `PrimarySmtpAddress`**, not service order — service order is not documented as stable, and an unstable covered set would churn which mailboxes are represented between cycles, making gauges and twins uninterpretable.
- **A row with no `PrimarySmtpAddress` counts toward `Total` but not `Covered`** — it exists, but no per-mailbox cmdlet can address it, so counting it as covered would overstate coverage.
- **A zero cap means unlimited, never "collect nothing"** — the `PageSize=0` returning HTTP 200 with zero rows failure has already bitten this project once.
- **An empty tenant is not an error; a transport failure is never flattened into an empty result** — "no mailboxes" and "could not look" are opposite facts.

Both guards that carry the truncation contract (`ResultSize` and the sort) are pinned by tests that were **sabotage-verified**: each guard was broken, the intended test confirmed failing, then restored. `make check` exit 0.

**No collector consumes this yet.** What remains for this issue is the mapper alone, against the row shape already captured above — no further measurement, no further decision.

## Built and shipped — `a936984`

`m365.inbox_rules` is live, against the shared fan-out gate frozen in `fed98f8`. Mapped from the rule shape captured on this issue.

**Emitted:**
- `m365.inbox_rules.rules{enabled, has_forwarding, delete_message}` — bounded gauge.
- `m365.inbox_rules.mailboxes_covered` / `.mailboxes_total` — every cycle.
- `m365.inbox_rule` log twin per rule, Warn when it forwards or redirects.

**The int64 trap is real and is now pinned.** `RuleIdentity` is carried as a **string**. Sabotage-verified: routing it through int64 — the exact bug a normal implementation would ship — fails `TestRuleIdentityPreservesFullPrecisionViaJSONNumber`. Worth restating why this was invisible: both rule ids captured *before* this issue's forwarding rule (`721857812023476225`, `5693957303879860225`) fit int64 comfortably, so a mapper built on those samples would have looked correct and silently corrupted `15394007230974001153` into `...152`.

**`ForwardTo` is emitted verbatim.** It carries a display name plus a legacyExchangeDN and no SMTP address, so the collector does not synthesize one — a half-parsed value reads as complete and would be wrong. The display-name portion is emitted separately under a name that says it is a display name. **External-vs-internal forwarding is not determinable from this cmdlet**, and the package doc says so rather than implying the collector knows.

**`-IncludeHidden` is pinned** by a test asserting the parameter, with the measurement on this issue as its justification.

**Cardinality:** verified independently from the generated signal capture — metric `AttrKeys` are the three booleans only; the 16 per-entity attributes (mailbox, rule name, identity, forwarding targets) live on the twin. No series grows with tenant size.

**Unobserved and deliberately not invented:** `RedirectTo`, `ForwardAsAttachmentTo`, `DeleteMessage=true`, and any genuinely maliciously-hidden (non-system) rule. The fields are mapped; nothing is wirecheck-watched on a value set that has not been seen.

**One correction carried into the code.** My earlier comment justified `-IncludeHidden` with "without it you see zero rows tenant-wide". That was an artifact of a one-rule tenant — a user-created rule is visible *without* the flag. The flag is still correct, because attacker-planted rules are hidden by construction, but the package doc records the real reason rather than the artifact.

**Gating:** off unless BOTH `exchange_online.enabled` and `exo_per_mailbox.enabled` are set. Default cap 250 mailboxes (~4 min/cycle at the measured 1.0 s/mailbox). No new Exchange RBAC role was ever needed or created.

`make check` exit 0. Census 154 → 156 logical collectors. Alert rules re-pushed after the panel-id shift.

The test forwarding rule was removed afterwards and the tenant verified back to its pre-test state — only the system `Junk E-mail Rule` remains, visible with `-IncludeHidden` and not without.

## Outcome

Show who can access private/shared channels, including external tenants that do not appear as team guests.

## Evidence

**Evidence class:** `docs-only; new permission and fan-out (2026-07-25)`

- Current Teams coverage identifies channel type but not membership.
- `allMembers` is available for private/shared channels under `ChannelMember.Read.All`.

## Proposed scope

- After explicit scope approval, measure private/shared channel count, paging, and fan-out.
- Skip standard channels.
- Emit bounded membership-type/directness/externality/role counts and per-member logs.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Externality compares member tenant ID to configured tenant ID, not guest heuristics.
- [ ] No user/tenant/team/channel identity becomes a metric label.
- [ ] Page and request budgets are measured before implementation.
- [ ] Per-channel RSC is not used for tenant-wide polling.

## Prior decisions and duplicate check

- Not duplicate of #247: installed apps/channels ship, but membership and external tenant access do not.
- Related: #121, #247.

## Primary sources

- [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/channel-list-allmembers?view=graph-rest-1.0](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/channel-list-allmembers?view=graph-rest-1.0)

## Priority

Audit recommendation: **P2**.

comments.body:
## Spike result — **no-data.** Every channel on this tenant is standard, and standard channels are explicitly out of this issue's scope.

### The grant (recorded per the standing consent)

`ChannelMember.Read.All` — appRole `<guid-14>`, granted 2026-07-28T11:00Z as an `appRoleAssignment` on the `graph2otel-poller` SP (`13371536-9950-4988-90f4-343566456781`). Assignment id `NhU3E1CZiEmQ9DQ1ZkVngQFBpsvRlXxAmnk-1AkuDdg`. Read-only, application-type.

### The measurement — as `graph2otel-poller`, 2026-07-28

Two teams, ten channels, **every one `membershipType: "standard"`**:

| team | channels |
| --- | --- |
| `907e7f1e…` | alerts-security, alerts-infra, irm, alerts-observability, alerts-apps, General — all standard |
| `8ad28759…` | General, approvals, github-notify, n8n-notify — all standard |

**Zero private channels. Zero shared channels.** So `allMembers` — the relationship this whole issue is built on, and the reason the scope was needed — has nothing to be called against.

### Verdict

**No build**, and this is the issue's own scope boundary rather than a judgment call: the proposed scope says *"Skip standard channels."* Ten out of ten channels are standard. Applying the stated design to this tenant yields an empty collector.

There is a real reason not to widen it to standard channels to get data. Standard-channel membership is the TEAM's membership — every team member is in every standard channel — so a per-channel membership collector over standard channels would emit `team_member_count × standard_channel_count` records that all say the same thing, and `m365.teams.membership.total` already reports it once. The private/shared case is the interesting one precisely because its membership *differs* from the team's, which is what makes an external or unexpected member a finding.

**Named unblock:** at least one private or shared channel exists. `GET /v1.0/teams/{id}/channels` then returns a non-standard `membershipType`, and the `allMembers` shape, the paging behavior and the fan-out cost can all be measured before any mapper is written. The scope stays granted, so the re-probe is two requests.

### Acceptance criteria

- [x] After explicit scope approval, measure private/shared channel count, paging, and fan-out — **count is zero**, measured across both teams; fan-out cost is therefore unmeasurable and not guessed.
- [x] Skip standard channels — the design constraint held, and it is what makes this a no-data close.
- [ ] Emit bounded membership-type/directness/externality/role counts and per-member logs — no build; the shape carries to the unblocked one.

**Evidence class:** `live-measured 2026-07-28, #360`.

## Outcome

Add actual mailbox storage, quota status, active counts, and last activity to configured mailbox posture.

## Evidence

**Evidence class:** `docs-only over an existing live report engine/scope (2026-07-25)`

- `m365.exchange_mailboxes` knows configured quotas but not actual storage/quota status/activity.
- Graph reports provide aggregate and detail CSV functions under existing `Reports.Read.All`.
- `m365.storage` already implements the relevant 302 CSV/report-settings pattern.

## Proposed scope

- Fetch mailbox storage, quota-status counts, active counts, and detail reports with shared partial-outcome handling.
- Emit bounded storage/count/quota metrics and one mailbox-usage twin per detail row.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Report concealment state is read and surfaced.
- [ ] Partial report success remains usable; all-report failure is not green.
- [ ] UPN/mailbox identity stays log-only.
- [ ] Report throttling and 302/SAS safety reuse existing hardened machinery.

## Prior decisions and duplicate check

- Not duplicate of mailbox configuration posture or SharePoint/OneDrive storage; this is actual Exchange usage.
- Related: #120, #240, #250.

## Primary sources

- [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/reportroot-getmailboxusagedetail?view=graph-rest-1.0](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/reportroot-getmailboxusagedetail?view=graph-rest-1.0)

## Priority

Audit recommendation: **P1**.

comments.body:
Built in `04653d2`, reusing `m365.storage`'s already-hardened report transport rather than reinventing it. Three reports captured live as `graph2otel-poller` on 2026-07-28, all HTTP 200 — `getMailboxUsageDetail`, `getMailboxUsageStorage`, `getMailboxUsageQuotaStatusMailboxCounts`, all `period='D7'`.

Bounded gauges: `m365.mailbox_usage.storage_used_bytes` (tenant-wide, one series) and `m365.mailbox_usage.quota_status.mailboxes{quota_state}` over Microsoft's own fixed five-bucket vocabulary, zero-filled every cycle so a bucket emptying reads as an explicit `0` rather than a vanished series. Per-mailbox detail — UPN, item count, storage used, all three quota thresholds, deleted-item counters, last activity, archive presence, derived `days_inactive` — rides the `m365.mailbox_usage` twin, never a metric label.

### Two wire behaviours worth carrying forward

**The two aggregate reports return one row PER DAY and re-serve the whole period on every poll.** Emitting every row would restate the same days forever, so only the row with the most recent `Report Date` is used — selected by parsed date, with tests that put the newest row in the middle and at the end of the fixture, because arrival order is not guaranteed. This is the same full-history re-serve shape #367 hit on service health; it is not specific to that endpoint.

`getMailboxUsageDetail` has **no `Report Date` column** — it is one row per mailbox, not per day — so the latest-day logic applies only to the two aggregates.

**An empty CSV cell is omitted, never coerced.** `Deleted Date` is blank on a live mailbox and `Last Activity Date` is blank on one never used; a fabricated `0`, `false` or epoch would assert a deletion or an activity that never happened. `days_inactive` is omitted entirely when the date is blank or unparseable rather than read as inactive-forever.

### Two corrections made during review, recorded because they were not in the plan

**`ReportSettings.Read.All` is now declared.** The collector reads `/admin/reportSettings` to decide whether report names are concealed — a separate resource with its own scope — but declared only `Reports.Read.All`. The poller already holds both (live-verified 2026-07-28: `displayConcealedNames: false`), so nothing was broken, but the generated scope documentation is built from that list, and a scope the code calls but the list omits sends an operator to grant an incomplete set. Declaring it is not the same as requiring it: a failure there degrades to unknown-concealment rather than erroring.

**`names_concealed` is omitted, not defaulted, when the setting is unreadable.** `m365.storage` can fall back to a data heuristic because Microsoft zeroes `Site Id` under concealment; no analogous sentinel has been observed on this report's name columns, and a heuristic with no evidence behind it is worse than none — the same reasoning that leaves fields unwatched in `internal/wirecheck`.

The collector key is `m365.mailbox_usage`, matching its event name and the underscore convention the majority of the m365 collectors use. It was renamed from `m365.mailboxusage` before landing, since it is a config key and would have been a breaking change later.

## Outcome

Expose IP allow lists that can bypass normal inbound filtering, separately from the Tenant Allow/Block List.

## Evidence

**Evidence class:** `docs-only; current authorization unmeasured (2026-07-25)`

- `Get-HostedConnectionFilterPolicy` is not collected.
- This control acts at a different mail-flow stage than the shipped allow/block list.

## Proposed scope

- Capture the live policy shape under current EXO roles.
- Emit bounded entry counts/booleans and one policy twin with IP/range lists and safe-list state.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] IPv4, IPv6, and range forms are preserved verbatim in logs.
- [ ] IPs never become metric labels.
- [ ] Alerts require evidence-backed dangerous state, not merely a non-empty block list.
- [ ] No overlap claim with Tenant Allow/Block remains implicit.

## Prior decisions and duplicate check

- Not duplicate of existing Defender allow/block coverage; the enforcement stage and data are different.
- Related: #250.

## Primary sources

- [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/exchangepowershell/get-hostedconnectionfilterpolicy?view=exchange-ps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/exchangepowershell/get-hostedconnectionfilterpolicy?view=exchange-ps)

## Priority

Audit recommendation: **P2**.

comments.body:
Built in `4ca32f7` from a live capture taken as `graph2otel-poller` on 2026-07-28 (`live-measured 2026-07-28, #358`).

One policy on this tenant, the `Default` one, with `IPAllowList` and `IPBlockList` both **empty**, `EnableSafeList: false`, `DirectoryBasedEdgeBlockMode: "Default"`.

### The measured zero is the whole point, and it is pinned

A non-empty allow list *is* the finding — an allow-listed sender bypasses spam filtering entirely, which is why this is worth a metric at all. So `ip_allow_list_length` and `ip_block_list_length` are emitted as a measured `0` on a healthy tenant rather than left absent. A vanished series and a measured zero are opposite facts here: one means nothing is allow-listed, the other means the collector did not run.

Sabotage-verified rather than read: making the emission conditional on a non-empty list fails `TestCollect_DefaultPolicyEmptyListsReadAsMeasuredZero` with `ip_allow_list_length points = 0, want 1 (measured, not absent)`.

The entries themselves ride the twin, capped at 100 — **with the true uncapped count alongside**, so a capped list still states its real size rather than silently reporting the cap. IPv4, IPv6 and CIDR forms are preserved verbatim. An IP is never a metric label.

### Two decisions worth stating

**The length gauges come from the DEFAULT policy only**, for the same reason as #357: several policies can exist, per-policy numeric labels breach the cardinality rule, and aggregating list sizes across policies is meaningless. Custom policies keep full detail on their own twins.

**`DirectoryBasedEdgeBlockMode` is NOT wirecheck-watched.** Only `"Default"` was observed. One observed value is not a value set.

The cmdlet takes no `ResultSize` — checked against the cmdlet reference, not assumed from the sibling collectors that do pin it.

Expose automatic forwarding, outbound recipient limits, threshold actions, and effective rule assignment.

## Evidence

**Evidence class:** `docs-only; current authorization unmeasured (2026-07-25)`

- Current MDO coverage is predominantly inbound-focused.
- Hosted outbound spam policy/rule cmdlets are not collected.

## Proposed scope

- Probe policy/rule cmdlets under current EXO registration.
- Emit bounded effective-forwarding/action counts and per-policy/rule state logs.
- Preserve raw and derived effective forwarding state separately.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Default/custom/disabled/exclusion cases are captured and tested.
- [ ] Any effective-state derivation is tied to current live-confirmed behavior.
- [ ] Recipient/notification lists remain log-only.
- [ ] No policy mutation cmdlet is available.

## Prior decisions and duplicate check

- No existing issue covers outbound spam/forwarding policy posture.
- Related: #233, #250.

## Primary sources

- [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/exchangepowershell/get-hostedoutboundspamfilterpolicy?view=exchange-ps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/exchangepowershell/get-hostedoutboundspamfilterpolicy?view=exchange-ps)

## Priority

Audit recommendation: **P1**.

comments.body:
Built in `4ca32f7` from a live capture taken as `graph2otel-poller` on 2026-07-28 (`live-measured 2026-07-28, #357`).

Bounded gauge `m365.exchange.outbound_spam.policies{is_default, enabled}` plus `m365.exchange.outbound_spam.recipient_limit{limit}` over the three thresholds. One `m365.exchange_outbound_spam_policy` twin per policy carries the rest — auto-forwarding mode, threshold action, BCC/notify flags and their recipient lists (capped, with `arrays_truncated` set when they were).

### Three things worth recording

**The cmdlet takes no `ResultSize`.** Checked against the cmdlet reference rather than assumed from `Get-AcceptedDomain`, which does pin it — so the usual silent-truncation guard genuinely does not apply here, rather than having been forgotten.

**The numeric limit gauges are sourced from the DEFAULT policy only.** A tenant can hold custom policies alongside the default. Labeling a numeric gauge by policy identity breaches the cardinality rule, and summing or averaging a recipient limit across policies produces a number that means nothing. Every custom policy still gets its full detail on its own twin, so nothing is dropped — a LogQL query answers the per-policy question, which is exactly the split CLAUDE.md's rule prescribes. Flagging it because it is a judgment call, not something the issue specified.

**`AutoForwardingMode` and `ActionWhenThresholdReached` are deliberately NOT wirecheck-watched.** Each was observed with exactly one live value (`Automatic`, `BlockUserForToday`). One observed value is not a value set, and a watchdog built on one would fire on the first legitimate second value — training the reader to ignore the signal.

## Outcome

Detect accounts whose owner, delegate, and admin mailbox actions bypass audit logging.

## Evidence

**Evidence class:** `docs-only; current authorization unmeasured (2026-07-25)`

- Organization/mailbox audit flags can look healthy while an account-wide bypass remains enabled.
- `Get-MailboxAuditBypassAssociation` is not collected and defaults to a 1,000-row limit.

## Proposed scope

- Probe app-only authorization and both boolean outcomes.
- Use `ResultSize=Unlimited` and measure volume.
- Emit one bounded enabled count and one state twin per association; enabled is Error severity.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Live authorization/shape precedes mapping.
- [ ] An enabled association cannot disappear into an aggregate.
- [ ] Identity remains log-only.
- [ ] Large-tenant cadence is justified by measured row/byte cost.

## Prior decisions and duplicate check

- No existing issue covers mailbox audit-bypass current state.
- Related: #250.

## Primary sources

- [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/exchangepowershell/get-mailboxauditbypassassociation?view=exchange-ps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/exchangepowershell/get-mailboxauditbypassassociation?view=exchange-ps)

## Priority

Audit recommendation: **P1**.

comments.body:
Built in `04653d2` from a live capture taken as `graph2otel-poller` on 2026-07-28.

### What the wire actually holds — `live-measured 2026-07-28, #356`

`Get-MailboxAuditBypassAssociation` returned **242 associations, every one `AuditBypassEnabled: false`**. The population is dominated by system objects (`SystemMailbox{...}`, `TenantSetting_...`, `Asc-2X1-...`), not one row per human mailbox. `RecipientTypeDetails` is **absent on every row**, so nothing is built on it. The response also carries an `@adminapi.warnings` array complaining that two objects are "corrupted or isn't compatible with Microsoft support requirements" — that is about unrelated quota properties, not about audit bypass, and is not treated as a collection failure.

### Shape, and the two places it departs from the house default

Two bounded gauges, no per-mailbox label: `m365.exchange.audit_bypass.enabled_count` and `m365.exchange.audit_bypass.examined`. **The second one is not redundant.** Without it, "nothing is bypassed" and "the cmdlet returned nothing" are the same series — one is healthy and the other is a source outage or a scope regression.

The log twin is emitted **only** for associations with bypass ENABLED. That inverts this project's usual one-twin-per-entity rule, deliberately: 242 records per cycle carrying no finding would train an operator to ignore the event name entirely. Here the twin *is* the finding, and its population is bounded by "someone deliberately turned this on" rather than by tenant size — which is the property that makes the inversion safe.

### The pointer, and why it is the whole point

`AuditBypassEnabled` decodes as `*bool`. A row missing the key is INDETERMINATE — excluded from both gauges, given no twin — because defaulting an absent key to `false` would report a mailbox this project could not classify as healthy, which is the exact inversion the collector exists to catch.

Sabotage-verified: making the decoder return a real `false` for an absent key fails `TestCollect_IndeterminateKeyAbsent` with `examined = 2, want 1`. Live data never exercises this branch (all 242 rows carry the key), so it is covered by a constructed fixture.

The healthy tenant now reads `enabled_count=0, examined=242`. That is the steady state, and it is stated rather than inferred from silence.

## Outcome

Expose standing FullAccess and SendAs paths that are invisible in the current mailbox twin.

## Evidence

**Evidence class:** `docs-only; current authorization and fan-out unmeasured (2026-07-25)`

- The mailbox collector carries `GrantSendOnBehalfTo` only.
- `Get-MailboxPermission` and `Get-RecipientPermission` cover separate delegation paths.

## Proposed scope

- Preflight current app-only authorization and N-mailbox request cost before any role discussion.
- Reuse the mailbox census for per-mailbox FullAccess calls.
- Emit bounded permission-kind/inherited/deny counts and one log per assignment.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Authorization and live row shape are captured first.
- [ ] Direct/inherited, allow/deny, and self/non-self are distinguishable.
- [ ] Inherited defaults and `NT AUTHORITY\SELF` are retained but not elevated as findings.
- [ ] Mailbox/trustee identities remain log-only.

## Prior decisions and duplicate check

- No current collector or issue covers FullAccess/SendAs current-state inventory.
- Related: #250.

## Primary sources

- [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/exchangepowershell/get-mailboxpermission?view=exchange-ps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/exchangepowershell/get-mailboxpermission?view=exchange-ps)
- [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/exchangepowershell/get-recipientpermission?view=exchange-ps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/exchangepowershell/get-recipientpermission?view=exchange-ps)

Audit recommendation: **P1**.

comments.body:
## Probe results — the fan-out question is now measured, and it decides the design

Probed app-only as `graph2otel-poller` on 2026-07-28. Everything below is `live-measured 2026-07-28, #355`.

### Both cmdlets work, and both are PER-MAILBOX

| cmdlet | covers | without `-Identity` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Get-MailboxPermission` | FullAccess | **HTTP 400 `BadRequest: Invalid Operation`** |
| `Get-RecipientPermission` | SendAs | returns, but scoped per recipient in practice |

`Get-MailboxPermission` **cannot be called tenant-wide**. It requires an `Identity`, so this collector is inherently `1 + N` calls per cycle: one to enumerate mailboxes, then one per mailbox — and the same again for SendAs if both are wanted, so realistically `1 + 2N`.

That is the whole design question for this issue, and it is not a detail to settle during implementation. On the m7kni tenant N=2 and it is free. On any real tenant it is not, and the EXO InvokeCommand transport has no batch form. Whatever gets built needs an explicit answer to "what does this cost on a 5,000-mailbox tenant", and probably a cap or an opt-in, in the way `m365.message_trace` is `HighVolume` and opt-in.

### The signal-to-noise problem, which is worse than it looks

Both cmdlets return an **implicit self-permission on every mailbox** that is not a delegation at all:

- `Get-MailboxPermission` → `User: NT AUTHORITY\SELF`, `AccessRights: ["FullAccess, ReadPermission"]`, `UserSid: S-1-5-10`
- `Get-RecipientPermission` → `Trustee: NT AUTHORITY\SELF`, `AccessRights: ["SendAs"]`, `TrusteeSidString: S-1-5-10`

On this tenant that is the ONLY row either cmdlet returns — there are no real delegations here. So a naive mapper emits one "FullAccess delegation" and one "SendAs delegation" per mailbox, tenant-wide, forever, and every one of them is noise. `NT AUTHORITY\SELF` / SID `S-1-5-10` must be filtered, and so must `IsInherited: true`.

Note the consequence for testing: **the live tenant currently exercises only the filtered-out branch.** A real delegation has to be constructed as a fixture, or created deliberately on the tenant, or the mapper ships never having mapped anything. Same shape as #356, where all 242 rows read false.

### Two more wire facts

`AccessRights` is a `#Collection(String)` whose single element is the **comma-joined** string `"FullAccess, ReadPermission"` — not two array elements. Splitting on the wire array alone gives one right, not two.

`PrimarySmtpAddress` and `TrusteeWithPrimarySmtpAddress` came back **null** on the SELF row, so the human-readable trustee address is not guaranteed present. `Identity` is a bare GUID, not an address — resolving it to something an operator recognises is another lookup.

### Status

Not started. The probe is done and no permission was needed beyond what the poller already holds. What this needs before code is a decision on the fan-out cost, not more measurement.

## Decision: **park the build, freeze the design.** Plus a correction — this issue's own probe comment is wrong on the load-bearing point.

`live-measured 2026-07-28, #355`, app-only as `graph2otel-poller`, both cmdlets `PRESENT` in the RBAC session.

### Correction: a REAL non-self delegation exists on this tenant

The earlier probe comment states that `NT AUTHORITY\SELF` is *"the ONLY row either returns"*. **That is wrong**, and it matters, because it was the strongest argument for not building.

Probing every mailbox (`Get-Mailbox -ResultSize Unlimited`, then per-identity) rather than only the two human ones:

```
DiscoverySearchMailbox{D919BA05-...}   MbxPerm=3  RcptPerm=1
   MP user=[NT AUTHORITY\SELF]      rights=[FullAccess, ReadPermission]                 deny=False inherited=False sid=[S-1-5-10]
   MP user=[NT AUTHORITY\SELF]      rights=[FullAccess, ExternalAccount, ReadPermission] deny=False inherited=False sid=[S-1-5-10]
   MP user=[Discovery Management]   rights=[FullAccess]                                 deny=False inherited=False sid=[S-1-5-21-1196097974-1292650839-4244031858-1272443]
   RP trustee=[NT AUTHORITY\SELF]   rights=[SendAs] type=[Allow] sid=[S-1-5-10]
rob@m7kni.io                          MbxPerm=1  RcptPerm=1   (SELF only)
vmuser@m7kni.io                       MbxPerm=1  RcptPerm=1   (SELF only)
```

`Discovery Management` holding `FullAccess` on the Discovery Search Mailbox is a genuine non-self, non-inherited delegation with a real object SID. **So the mapper has a real row to be written against, and does not have to ship never having mapped one.** The earlier conclusion presumably came from probing only the two user mailboxes.

Second new fact: `NT AUTHORITY\SELF` is **not one row shape**. The same SID appears twice on one mailbox with different rights (`FullAccess, ReadPermission` and `FullAccess, ExternalAccount, ReadPermission`). Deduping SELF by SID alone silently drops one.

Confirmed unchanged from the earlier probe: `AccessRights` is a collection whose **single element is a comma-joined string** — `[FullAccess, ExternalAccount, ReadPermission]` is one element carrying three rights, so splitting on the array alone yields one right, not three.

### Still unobserved, and must not be invented

`Deny=True` and `IsInherited=True` do not occur anywhere on this tenant; every row reads `False`. Both fields are **present and populated**, so they are mappable — a bool that reads `False` is an observed value, unlike an unobserved enum member. But acceptance criterion 2 ("allow/deny and direct/inherited are distinguishable") can only be proven one-sided here, and that limit should be stated in the collector rather than papered over.

### Cost, measured directly rather than inferred

| cmdlet | avg (n=6) |
| --- | ---: |
| `Get-MailboxPermission` | 846 ms |
| `Get-RecipientPermission` | 602 ms |
| **combined per mailbox** | **1,448 ms** |

`1 + 2N`, no batch form on the EXO `InvokeCommand` transport.

| mailboxes | per-cycle serial cost |
| ---: | ---: |
| 3 (m7kni) | ~4 s |
| 1,000 | ~24 min |
| 5,000 | **~121 min** |

At 5,000 mailboxes a single cycle exceeds two hours, so on a real tenant this cannot be a default-on collector at any normal interval.

### The design, frozen — and why the obvious opt-in interface is the WRONG one

**`HighVolume` does not fit, and using it would actively mislead.** This repo defines `HighVolume` as a firehose whose rate scales with **traffic** (`m365.message_trace`: one record per message per recipient). Per-mailbox fan-out scales with **tenant size** — a 5,000-mailbox tenant with zero mail flow still pays the full 121 minutes. `Experimental` fits even worse: this is EXO PowerShell, not a Graph beta surface, and #183 reserved that flag for genuine Graph beta.

So this needs a **third** gate rather than a reuse of either:

- explicit per-tenant opt-in (unset ⇒ the collector does not register at all, same shape as `blob_ingest.account_url` and `mdca.portal_url`);
- an explicit **mailbox cap** with a documented default, validated at load, in the manner of the #337 privileged-group allowlist (capped at 50, load-validated);
- **truncation must be visible as a signal, not a log line** — a cap that silently covers the first N mailboxes reports clean success over an unknown remainder, which is the failure mode this repo treats as worse than not collecting. Two gauges, as with #356: covered vs total.
- interval measured in hours, not minutes.
- `NT AUTHORITY\SELF` (`S-1-5-10`) and `IsInherited=True` are **retained and counted, never elevated to a finding** (criterion 3) — not filtered away, which is what a naive reading of the earlier comment would have produced.
- mailbox and trustee identities stay **log-only**, never metric labels (criterion 4).

**#363 shares this exact problem** (`1 + N`, 995 ms/mailbox, same transport, same tenant-size scaling) and should use the same mechanism rather than a second one invented alongside it.

### Why parked rather than built

The cost question this issue was blocked on is now answered, and the data blocker is gone. What remains is that the fan-out budget is a **shared, cross-cutting config seam** serving at least two collectors (#355, #363), and freezing a shared seam is not something to bolt onto one collector's build. Building #355's mechanism in isolation would almost certainly force a rewrite when #363 lands on top of it.

**Named unblock:** agreement on the shared per-mailbox fan-out gate above (opt-in key, cap, default, and the covered/total truncation signal), after which #355 and #363 are both mechanical builds against a real captured row. No further measurement is required for either — cost, authorization, and row shape are all now live-measured.

Acceptance criteria stay unticked: this is a design decision plus a data correction, not the build.

## Live capture of a REAL non-self delegation — both cmdlets, as the poller

The maintainer created a deliberate `FullAccess` + `SendAs` delegation on `vmuser@m7kni.io` for `rob@m7kni.io`. Captured read-only **as `graph2otel-poller`**, `live-measured 2026-07-28, #355`. The artifacts are being removed straight after this capture, so **this comment is the durable record** — the mapper should be written from here.

### `Get-MailboxPermission -Identity vmuser@m7kni.io`

```
user=[NT AUTHORITY\SELF] rights=[FullAccess, ReadPermission] deny=False inherited=False sid=[S-1-5-10]                                          smtp=[]
user=[rob@m7kni.io]      rights=[FullAccess]                 deny=False inherited=False sid=[S-1-5-21-1196097974-1292650839-4244031858-1272489] smtp=[]
```

### `Get-RecipientPermission -Identity vmuser@m7kni.io`

```
trustee=[NT AUTHORITY\SELF] rights=[SendAs] type=Allow sid=[S-1-5-10]                                          smtp=[]
trustee=[rob@m7kni.io]      rights=[SendAs] type=Allow sid=[S-1-5-21-1196097974-1292650839-4244031858-1272489] smtp=[]
```

This closes the **non-self `SendAs`** gap — previously only the `Discovery Management` FullAccess row existed, and `SendAs` had no non-self sample at all.

### What the real row confirms, and what it corrects

**`User`/`Trustee` carries a usable identity for a real delegation** — `rob@m7kni.io`, an actual UPN — where the implicit row carries the literal string `NT AUTHORITY\SELF`. So the self row is distinguishable by **either** the `S-1-5-10` SID **or** the `NT AUTHORITY\` prefix; the SID is the more reliable key of the two, since the display string is localisable.

**`PrimarySmtpAddress` / `TrusteeWithPrimarySmtpAddress` are EMPTY even on the real delegation.** The earlier probe recorded these as null "on the SELF row", which read as a property of the self row specifically. It is not — they are empty on a genuine non-self delegation too, so **the mapper must take the identity from `User`/`Trustee` and must not depend on the SMTP field being populated on any row.**

**The real row is the single-element case**: `AccessRights = [FullAccess]`, one element, no comma. The comma-joined multi-right form (`"FullAccess, ReadPermission"`, and the three-right `"FullAccess, ExternalAccount, ReadPermission"`) occurs on the SELF rows. So a mapper must split on `", "` *within* each element **and** iterate elements — a single real delegation would not have revealed the comma case, and the SELF rows alone would not have revealed the single case.

### Still unobserved — do not invent

`Deny=True` and `IsInherited=True` do not occur anywhere on this tenant; every row of both cmdlets reads `False`. Both fields are present and typed, so they are safe to map, but acceptance criterion 2 ("allow/deny and direct/inherited are distinguishable") remains proven **one-sided only**, and the collector should say so rather than imply it has seen both.

`AccessControlType` on `Get-RecipientPermission` reads `Allow` on every row; `Deny` is unobserved.

### Status unchanged

The data gap is now closed for the common case, but this issue stays **parked on the shared per-mailbox fan-out gate** (opt-in key, cap, default, covered/total truncation signal) described in the previous comment — that seam serves both this issue and #363 and should be frozen once, not invented twice. No further measurement is needed: cost, authorization and row shape are all live-measured.

## The shared per-mailbox fan-out gate is built and frozen — `fed98f8`

The named unblock condition on this issue ("agreement on the shared gate: opt-in key, cap, default, and the covered/total truncation signal") has fired. It is now agreed **and** implemented, so the seam both collectors build against is stable.

**Config** (per tenant, alongside `exchange_online`):

```yaml
exo_per_mailbox:
  enabled: true         # the whole opt-in; unset registers NO per-mailbox EXO collector
  max_mailboxes: 250    # default; unset means 250, never "cap of zero"
```

`internal/config.ExoPerMailboxConfig` — `Configured()`, `Cap()`, `validate()` (rejects a negative cap; an unset cap defaults rather than erroring).

**Enumeration** — `internal/exofanout.Enumerate(ctx, client, cap) (Result, error)`:

```go
type Result struct {
    Mailboxes []Mailbox  // covered set, sorted by PrimarySmtpAddress
    Total     int        // what the tenant really has, including unaddressable rows
    Covered   int        // what this cycle will poll
    Truncated bool       // Covered < Total, for any reason
}
```

Decisions baked in, each for a stated reason:

- **`ResultSize=Unlimited` is pinned.** Without it the TOTAL is silently short and the truncation signal becomes a lie rather than a guard.
- **Deterministic sort on `PrimarySmtpAddress`**, not service order — service order is not documented as stable, and an unstable covered set would churn which mailboxes are represented between cycles, making gauges and twins uninterpretable.
- **A row with no `PrimarySmtpAddress` counts toward `Total` but not `Covered`** — it exists, but no per-mailbox cmdlet can address it, so counting it as covered would overstate coverage.
- **A zero cap means unlimited, never "collect nothing"** — the `PageSize=0` returning HTTP 200 with zero rows failure has already bitten this project once.
- **An empty tenant is not an error; a transport failure is never flattened into an empty result** — "no mailboxes" and "could not look" are opposite facts.

Both guards that carry the truncation contract (`ResultSize` and the sort) are pinned by tests that were **sabotage-verified**: each guard was broken, the intended test confirmed failing, then restored. `make check` exit 0.

**No collector consumes this yet.** What remains for this issue is the mapper alone, against the row shape already captured above — no further measurement, no further decision.

## Built and shipped — `a936984`

`m365.mailbox_delegation` is live, against the shared fan-out gate frozen in `fed98f8`. Mapped from the row shape captured on this issue, not from documentation.

**Emitted:**
- `m365.mailbox.delegation.assignments{kind, trustee_kind, is_inherited}` — bounded gauge. `kind` splits `full_access`/`send_as`, `trustee_kind` splits `self`/`delegated`.
- `m365.mailbox.delegation.mailboxes_covered` / `.mailboxes_total` — every cycle, so a capped scan states it was partial.
- `m365.mailbox_delegation` log twin per NON-SELF, NON-INHERITED assignment, carrying mailbox, trustee, trustee SID, rights, deny.

**Acceptance:**
- [x] Authorization and live row shape captured first — both cmdlets `PRESENT`, shapes recorded above.
- [x] Direct/inherited, allow/deny, self/non-self distinguishable — with the honest limit that `Deny=true` and `IsInherited=true` are **unobserved** on this tenant. Both are mapped, neither is wirecheck-watched, and the package doc says why: a watchdog built on one observed value fires on the first legitimate second one.
- [x] Inherited defaults and `NT AUTHORITY\SELF` retained but not elevated — the metric bucket is incremented **before** the twin is suppressed, so SELF is counted as inventory and never emitted as a finding. Filtering it away entirely would have lost the inventory; twinning it would have buried the real findings under one bogus row per mailbox per cycle.
- [x] Mailbox/trustee identities log-only — verified independently from the generated signal capture: metric `AttrKeys` are `is_inherited`, `kind`, `trustee_kind` only. No series grows with tenant size.

**The three wire traps are each pinned by a test**, and I verified that by sabotage rather than by reading the diff — breaking the guard and confirming the test goes red:
- removing the within-element `", "` split (so `"FullAccess, ReadPermission"` stays one right) → 2 tests fail;
- removing the SELF twin suppression → 4 tests fail;
- `PrimarySmtpAddress` is never trusted — it is empty even on the real `rob@m7kni.io` delegation, so identity comes from `User`/`Trustee`.

**Gating:** off unless BOTH `exchange_online.enabled` and the new `exo_per_mailbox.enabled` are set. Not `HighVolume` and not `Experimental` — see `fed98f8` for why both labels would have been false here. Default cap 250 mailboxes (~6 min/cycle at the measured 1.45 s/mailbox).

`make check` exit 0. Census 154 → 156 logical collectors. Alert rules re-pushed after the panel-id shift (`matched_content_ungrouped`, the healthy end state).

The test artifacts the maintainer created for this capture were removed afterwards and the tenant verified back to its pre-test state — `Get-MailboxPermission`/`Get-RecipientPermission` return `NT AUTHORITY\SELF` only.

body:
## Outcome

Show which recipients actually receive MDO/EOP policies, in what priority, and whether preset protections are active.

## Evidence

**Evidence class:** `source/doc inventory; cmdlets require live preflight (2026-07-25)`

- `defender.mdo_policies` exports policy definitions but not their rule assignment/exclusion layer.
- Rule partners exist for ATP/EOP/built-in/hosted content/malware/anti-phish/Safe Links/Safe Attachments/Teams.
- Only Teams protection rule behavior has been measured under current roles.

## Proposed scope

- Preflight each read-only rule cmdlet as the poller and record empty versus denied.
- Join definitions to rules without dropping orphaned definitions/rules.
- Emit bounded rule-family/enabled/assignment counts and per-rule state logs.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Every proposed cmdlet has an authorization and wire-shape receipt.
- [x] Custom, preset, disabled, exclusion, absent-rule, and orphan cases are tested.
- [x] Recipient lists and rule names remain log-only.
- [x] Licence-specific surfaces degrade explicitly.

## Prior decisions and duplicate check

- Not duplicate of #233/#250: current MDO policy definitions cannot answer effective assignment.
- Related: #233, #250.

## Primary sources

- [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/exchangepowershell/get-atpprotectionpolicyrule?view=exchange-ps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/exchangepowershell/get-atpprotectionpolicyrule?view=exchange-ps)
- [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/exchangepowershell/get-eopprotectionpolicyrule?view=exchange-ps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/exchangepowershell/get-eopprotectionpolicyrule?view=exchange-ps)

## Priority

Audit recommendation: **P1**.

comments.body:
## Preflight complete — **every rule cmdlet is authorized. Nothing is blocked; this is a build.**

Probed live 2026-07-28 as `graph2otel-poller` over the Exchange Online admin API (`POST outlook.office365.com/adminapi/beta/{tid}/InvokeCommand`), under the grants the poller already holds (`Exchange.ManageAsApp` + Security Reader). No new scope, no new role.

### Authorization and wire-shape receipt, per cmdlet

| cmdlet | HTTP | rows | verdict |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Get-ATPProtectionPolicyRule` | 200 | 1 | authorized, wire shape captured |
| `Get-EOPProtectionPolicyRule` | 200 | 1 | authorized, wire shape captured |
| `Get-ATPBuiltInProtectionRule` | 200 | 1 | authorized, wire shape captured |
| `Get-HostedContentFilterRule` | 200 | 0 | authorized, **empty** |
| `Get-MalwareFilterRule` | 200 | 0 | authorized, **empty** |
| `Get-AntiPhishRule` | 200 | 0 | authorized, **empty** |
| `Get-SafeLinksRule` | 200 | 0 | authorized, **empty** |
| `Get-SafeAttachmentRule` | 200 | 0 | authorized, **empty** |
| `Get-TeamsProtectionPolicyRule` | 200 | 0 | authorized, **empty** |
| `Get-HostedOutboundSpamFilterRule` | 200 | 0 | authorized, **empty** |

**Empty is not denied, and the distinction is structural here rather than a matter of interpretation.** An unauthorized Exchange cmdlet is *deleted from the app-only session* and comes back `CommandNotFoundException` before it ever touches a target; a 403 EXO body is a run of NUL bytes, not JSON. Ten 200s with a `value` array means ten authorized reads. The seven zeros are a m7kni configuration fact — the tenant runs preset security policies and has created no custom rules — not a permission gap, and the collector must report them as measured-zero rather than unavailable.

### Wire shape — uniform across families

`Get-EOPProtectionPolicyRule`, verbatim:

```json
{
  "HostedContentFilterPolicy": "Standard Preset Security Policy1784144691483",
  "AntiPhishPolicy": "Standard Preset Security Policy1784144689723",
  "MalwareFilterPolicy": "Standard Preset Security Policy1784144693315",
  "State": "Enabled",
  "Priority@data.type": "System.Int32",
  "Priority": 0,
  "Comments": null,
  "Description": "Take the following actions:\r\n\tApply hosted content filter policy \"...\"....",
  "RuleVersion": "14.0.0.0",
  "SentTo": null, "SentToMemberOf": null, "RecipientDomainIs": null,
  "ExceptIfSentTo": null, "ExceptIfSentToMemberOf": null, "ExceptIfRecipientDomainIs": null,
  "Conditions": null, "Exceptions": null,
  "Identity": "Standard Preset Security Policy",
  "Guid": "0c13168e-3b97-4e6c-b108-0ddd32197339",
  "Name": "Standard Preset Security Policy",
  "IsValid": true,
  "WhenChanged": "2026-07-15T19:45:06.0000000+00:00"
}
```

The ATP rules carry `SafeAttachmentPolicy` + `SafeLinksPolicy` in place of the three EOP policy fields; every other field is identical. Three traps worth recording:

- **The wire interleaves OData sidecars** (`Priority@data.type`, `Guid@odata.type`, `WhenChanged@data.type`) next to the real keys. Any mapper that walks the map must skip keys containing `@`.
- **`Priority` is a real `0`** on the highest-priority rule. A falsy check drops exactly the rule that matters most.
- **All six recipient-scoping fields are NULL on this tenant, and null means UNSCOPED, not empty.** The rule applies to everyone. Rendering a null as an empty list reads "applies to everyone" as "applies to nobody" — backwards in the most dangerous direction — so the mapper omits the attribute instead.

### Decisions taken for the build

- **`rule_family` and `condition` are the bounded metric dimensions**; recipient addresses, group names and domains are twin-only, per #112 and this issue's own acceptance criterion.
- **The seven `Get-*Policy` cmdlets are re-read here**, overlapping `defender.mdo_policies` on purpose. An orphaned policy — one that exists and that no enabled rule applies — is visible only from both sides at once, and re-reading a cheap cmdlet costs less than coupling two collectors. Seventeen read-only Invokes per hourly cycle.
- **`State` is NOT declared to `internal/wirecheck`.** One observed value is not a value set (#234).
- **A disabled rule rates Warn; an enabled unscoped rule rates Info.** A preset security policy covering the whole tenant is the recommended configuration, not a finding — rating it Warn would fire on every correctly configured tenant.

**Evidence class:** `live-measured 2026-07-28, #354`.

## Shipped in `4ed2c00` — `defender.mdo_rules`

The MDO/EOP protection-policy rule layer, on the existing EXO path, off unless `exchange_online.enabled` is set. `make check` exit 0. No new grant — the ten rule cmdlets and the seven policy cmdlets all run under `Exchange.ManageAsApp` + Security Reader, already held.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [x] **Every proposed cmdlet has an authorization and wire-shape receipt.** All ten preflighted live and recorded in the comment above: three returning rules, seven authorized-and-empty, none denied. The three non-empty shapes are committed verbatim as `testdata/`.
- [x] **Custom, preset, disabled, exclusion, absent-rule and orphan cases are tested.** All six, plus a present-but-empty recipient array, an unrecognized `State`, a failed rule fetch and a failed policy fetch. m7kni has no custom/disabled/exclusion rules, so those fixtures are hand-built and each is commented as synthetic rather than passed off as captured.
- [x] **Recipient lists and rule names remain log-only.** The only metric labels are `rule_family`, `state`, `condition` and `policy_type` — bounded sets fixed by Exchange's rule model or derived here. `signalgate_test.go` enforces it.
- [x] **License-specific surfaces degrade explicitly.** Every cmdlet degrades independently through `errors.Join`, and a family whose fetch failed emits **no series at all** rather than a seeded zero.

**Ships**

- Gauges `defender.mdo.rules{rule_family, state}` (all 20 family × state pairs seeded), `.rules.conditions{rule_family, condition}`, `.rules.unscoped{rule_family}` (all 10 seeded), `.unreferenced_policies{policy_type}`.
- Log twins `defender.mdo_rule` and `defender.mdo_unreferenced_policy`.
- The seven `Get-*Policy` cmdlets are re-read here on purpose: an orphaned policy — one that exists and that no enabled rule applies — is visible only from both sides at once, and re-reading a cheap cmdlet costs less than coupling two collectors. Seventeen read-only Invokes per hourly cycle. Policy names are matched case-insensitively, as Exchange identities are.

**Three decisions worth recording**

**A NULL condition is unscoped, not empty.** The attribute is omitted rather than emitted as an empty list. Rendering NULL as `[]` would read "applies to everyone" as "applies to nobody" — backwards in the most dangerous direction — and on this tenant every one of the six conditions is NULL on every rule, so it is the normal case, not an edge case.

**A failed fetch is a gap, not a zero.** Seeding is right for a family that was read and had no rules; it is wrong for one whose cmdlet errored, because a confident `0` is indistinguishable from a measurement. On error the family's seeded entries are deleted and it emits nothing, per the #240 rule. An empty or unrecognized `State` buckets under `unknown` rather than minting a `state=""` series.

**A disabled rule Warns; an enabled unscoped rule does not.** A preset security policy covering the whole tenant is the recommended configuration. Rating it Warn would fire on every correctly configured tenant, which is how a severity level stops meaning anything.

Nothing is declared to `internal/wirecheck`: `State` was observed at exactly one value and one observed value is not a value set (#234); `rule_family` and `condition` are graph2otel-derived names, not Graph-supplied.

**Verification — the sabotage pass found a guard that protected nothing.** Flipping `stringList` so a NULL condition renders as a present empty list — the exact inversion above — did **not** fail the test written to catch it. Root cause: `telemetry.SetStrs` applies its own non-empty filter before writing to `Attrs`, so an "assert the key is absent from `Attrs`" check silently absorbs a broken mapper. Separately, a present-but-empty array (`"SentTo": []`) was uncovered entirely and its sabotage went undetected. Both are now pinned at the mapper's own return value and at the consumers that read it directly, and both sabotages were re-run independently after the fix: the first now fails four tests, the second two, and restoring the seeded-zero-on-failure fails `TestRuleFetchFailureAggregatesAndOthersStillEmit` by name.

**Evidence class:** `live-measured 2026-07-28, #354`.

Expose whether Exchange domains are authoritative or relay recipients elsewhere, alongside DKIM and connector posture.

## Evidence

**Evidence class:** `live-measured in #250; refresh before mapping (2026-07-25)`

- `Get-AcceptedDomain -ResultSize Unlimited` returned four authoritative domains under the existing EXO registration.
- No current collector models accepted-domain type/default state.

## Proposed scope

- Refresh a verbatim record as the poller.
- Emit bounded counts by domain type/default and one domain twin with initial/default/MatchSubDomains state.
- Keep domain names log-only.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `ResultSize=Unlimited` is pinned in a transport test.
- [ ] All returned domains receive twins.
- [ ] InternalRelay is not automatically treated as a finding.
- [ ] Goldens, annotations, docs, and full gate are green.

## Prior decisions and duplicate check

- Not duplicate of Exchange connector or DKIM collectors; accepted domains define a separate mail-routing boundary.
- Related: #250, #253.

## Primary sources

- [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/exchangepowershell/get-accepteddomain?view=exchange-ps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/exchangepowershell/get-accepteddomain?view=exchange-ps)

## Priority

Audit recommendation: **P1**.

comments.body:
## Closed by `2483dd4`

### Live evidence this was built from

`live-measured (2026-07-27, #353)`, probed read-only as `graph2otel-poller` via the Exchange Online admin API. `Get-AcceptedDomain -ResultSize Unlimited` → HTTP 200, 9300 bytes, **4 domains, 56 fields per row**. All 4 `Authoritative`; `Default` true on exactly one; `InitialDomain` true on the `.onmicrosoft.com` one; `SmtpDaneStatus` `Disabled` and `AuthenticationType` `Managed` across the board. `ResultSize=Unlimited` is pinned by test, per the recorded EXO truncation trap.

### `DomainType` is deliberately NOT wirecheck-watched

Only `Authoritative` was observed — 4 of 4. **One observed value is not a value set.** A watchdog built on it would fire on the first legitimate `InternalRelay` domain a tenant adds, which is correct data, and CLAUDE.md is explicit that a watchdog firing on correct data is worse than none because it trains the reader to ignore the signal. `InternalRelay` and `Mixed` stay `docs-only` and are used only as a labelled fixture proving the twin never flags them.

That also satisfies this issue's own requirement that `InternalRelay` not be auto-flagged: the mapper has no good/bad branch on `DomainType` at all, and `TestCollect_InternalRelayNotFlaggedAsFinding` pins the twin at Info regardless of type.

### Shape

Bounded gauge `m365.exchange.accepted_domains{domain_type, is_default_domain}`; one `m365.exchange_accepted_domain` twin per domain carrying the name and the posture flags. The domain **name is never a metric label** — it is per-entity and grows with how many domains a tenant owns, so it lives on the twin where a LogQL `count by` answers the same question free.

### Verified by sabotage

Adding a domain name to the gauge labels fails `TestCollect_DomainNameNeverOnMetric`. The cardinality guard is enforced, not just intended.

`make check` exit 0.
