## Outcome

Determine whether Intune diagnostic categories are enabled, read, redundant, or wasting storage, including the unresolved `SignInLogs` disposition.

## Evidence

**Evidence class:** `explicit blocked residual from #238 (2026-07-25)`

- #238 shipped the Entra ARM census.
- The `microsoft.intune/diagnosticSettings` GET remains unmeasured because the poller lacks subscription RBAC.
- The same issue leaves `SignInLogs` enabled-but-unread without a durable keep/remove decision.

## Proposed scope

- After explicit approval, grant the narrow read-only subscription RBAC needed for this one census.
- Read back Intune diagnostic settings and compare enabled categories with collector/transport coverage.
- Record a keep/remove recommendation; do not mutate settings in graph2otel.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] The exact RBAC role/scope and read receipt are recorded.
- [x] Every enabled category is classified as consumed, other-transport, data-gated, intentionally retained, or waste. (Entra half complete; the Intune half is structurally unreadable — see the 2026-07-28 comment.)
- [x] `SignInLogs` receives an explicit decision. (Remove; execution is a maintainer tenant-config action.)
- [x] No diagnostic setting is changed by the collector.

## Prior decisions and duplicate check

- This is the uncompleted Intune half of #238, not a repeat of the shipped Entra census.
- Related: #134, #238.

## Priority

Audit recommendation: **P3**.

comments.body:
## Decision received 2026-07-28 — read-only subscription-scope RBAC approved

The maintainer approved granting graph2otel-poller a **read-only role at Azure subscription scope**. This was asked separately from the Graph read-scope consent extension because it is the Azure control plane, not Graph, and therefore a different blast radius.

Terms:
- Read-only. **No mutation of diagnostic settings** under any circumstance — the census reads what exists and reports drift; it never fixes it.
- The grant is to the `graph2otel-poller` identity, never another app identity.
- Record the exact role and scope on this issue when made.

This also unblocks the outstanding **`SignInLogs` keep/remove call from #238**, which has been waiting on the census being able to see which categories are actually enabled rather than assumed.

## Done — grant made, census run, `SignInLogs` decided. One core premise of this issue is WRONG.

All `live-measured 2026-07-28, #352`, probed app-only as `graph2otel-poller` (appId `2c92ce28-126c-47c1-82b0-410b64502989`). Read-only throughout: every call was a GET. **No diagnostic setting was created, modified or deleted.**

### 1. The grant, exactly as made

| field | value |
| --- | --- |
| role | **Reader** (built-in, `<guid-15>`) |
| scope | `/subscriptions/1bdad520-a1e9-4977-9d0b-ef62853b26fd` |
| principal | `13371536-9950-4988-90f4-343566456781` (`graph2otel-poller`, ServicePrincipal) |
| assignment id | `<guid-16>` |
| created | `2026-07-28T08:02:08Z` |

**`Reader`, not `Monitoring Reader` — and that is the opposite of the intuitive pick.** The role definitions were compared live rather than assumed:

- `Reader` → actions `*/read`. Nothing else.
- `Monitoring Reader` → actions `*/read` **plus `Microsoft.Support/*`** plus `Microsoft.OperationalInsights/workspaces/search/action`.

`Microsoft.Support/*` is a **write** surface (it can open support tickets). So despite the name suggesting it is the purpose-built narrow role for a diagnostics census, `Monitoring Reader` is strictly **broader** than `Reader` and is **not read-only** — it would have violated this issue's own constraint. `Reader` is both narrower and strictly read-only.

### 2. The Intune half is NOT an Azure-RBAC problem — this issue's premise is disproved

This issue exists because "the poller lacks subscription RBAC". It now has it, and **`microsoft.intune` still 403s**:

```
403 AuthorizationFailed
The client '2c92ce28-...' with object id '13371536-...' does not have authorization
to perform action 'microsoft.intune/diagnosticSettings/read' over scope
'/providers/microsoft.intune' or the scope is invalid.
```

The scope in the denial is `/providers/microsoft.intune` — **tenant-root, not under any subscription**. No subscription-scope assignment can ever cover it, so no amount of Azure RBAC at subscription scope was ever going to close this. The poller additionally already holds **Global Reader** and **Security Reader**, and neither carries it either.

**Do not re-attempt this by granting a broader Azure role.** The scope hierarchy denies it, not the role. Named unblock: an identity authorized at the `microsoft.intune` tenant-root provider (Intune-side RBAC / Intune Administrator), which is a different mechanism entirely and a different blast radius.

Corrected in the code that carried the wrong claim: `8296010`.

The grant was not wasted — it **did** flip the storage-account resource read from 403 to 200, and it enabled the per-resource census in §3.

### 3. Census results

**Per-resource (subscription scope — newly readable):** 10 resources. Two support diagnostic settings (`Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts`, `Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults`) and **both have none configured**. The other 8 return `400 ResourceTypeNotSupported` — `Microsoft.Insights/actiongroups`, `Microsoft.Syntex/accounts`, and 6 × `Microsoft.HybridCompute/machines`. That 400 is a **capability** fact, not a permission failure; anything automating this must not conflate the two.

**Entra tenant (`microsoft.aadiam`, one setting named `graph2otel` → storage account `graph2otelm7kni`):** 26 categories, classified against the 37 containers the registered blob collectors actually read (`collectors.BlobContainers`).

| state | n | categories |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| **consumed** | 10 | AuditLogs, GraphNotificationsActivityLogs, ManagedIdentitySignInLogs, MicrosoftGraphActivityLogs, MicrosoftServicePrincipalSignInLogs, NonInteractiveUserSignInLogs, ProvisioningLogs, RiskyUsers, ServicePrincipalSignInLogs, UserRiskEvents |
| **enabled_unread** (billed, read by nothing) | 11 | AgentRiskEvents, MicrosoftGraphPolicyLogs, NetworkAccessAlerts, NetworkAccessConnectionEvents, NetworkAccessGenerativeAIInsights, PreAuthenticationDiscoveryLogs, RemoteNetworkHealthLogs, RiskyAgents, RiskyServicePrincipals, ServicePrincipalRiskEvents, **SignInLogs** |
| **mapped_but_disabled** | 0 | — |
| **disabled** | 5 | ADFSSignInLogs, AzureADGraphActivityLogs, B2CRequestLogs, EnrichedOffice365AuditLogs, NetworkAccessTrafficLogs |

`mapped_but_disabled` being 0 is the healthy reading: no collector is polling a container that will never be written.

### 4. `SignInLogs` — explicit decision: **REMOVE**

Recommendation is removal, and the reason is stronger than "nothing reads it today".

`graph2otel` ships exactly **four** blob sign-in streams (`internal/collectors/entra/signins/blob.go`): `microsoftserviceprincipalsigninlogs`, `serviceprincipalsigninlogs`, `noninteractiveusersigninlogs`, `managedidentitysigninlogs`. **Interactive `SignInLogs` is not among them and has no container registered anywhere in the project.** Interactive sign-ins reach graph2otel over Graph, not blob. So this is not "unread pending a collector" — there is no shipped collector that *can* read it, and the polled interactive stream already covers the signal.

The stated reason for retention has also expired: #137's note held `SignInLogs` open "until the latency instrument has served", and #137 is closed.

So the category is writing and being billed to deliver a signal graph2otel already has by another transport.

**Execution is a maintainer action, deliberately not taken here** — this issue forbids mutating diagnostic settings, and I did not. Unblock: remove the `SignInLogs` category from the `graph2otel` diagnostic setting in the tenant, after which the census drops it from `enabled_unread` automatically.

**If it is retained instead, it needs to be retained explicitly**, because the census raises `enabled_unread` as a **Warn** — a permanent warning on a deliberate configuration trains an operator to ignore the census, which is the failure mode this repo treats as worse than having no watchdog. Retention would therefore need an acknowledged-category allowance in the census rather than a silent standing Warn. I have not built that, because it is only worth building if the answer is "keep".

### Acceptance

- [x] The exact RBAC role/scope and read receipt are recorded — §1.
- [x] Every enabled category is classified — §3. The **Intune** categories remain unclassifiable, and §2 shows that is structural, not a missing grant.
- [x] `SignInLogs` receives an explicit decision — §4, remove.
- [x] No diagnostic setting is changed by the collector — nothing was mutated by anything, collector or human.

Closing: the subscription-RBAC question this issue was opened to answer is now settled, including the negative result that it does not unlock the Intune half. The two follow-on actions are both maintainer tenant-config actions with named unblocks above, not engineering work.
Closed by the census + decision recorded above. The engineering half is done and the two residuals are maintainer tenant-config actions with named unblocks, not code.

## Read-back — `SignInLogs` removed by the maintainer, confirmed live

The maintainer disabled `SignInLogs` on the `graph2otel` diagnostic setting. Re-ran the census against `providers/microsoft.aadiam/diagnosticSettings` (read-only GET, as `graph2otel-poller`), `live-measured 2026-07-28, #352`:

| state | before | after |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| consumed | 10 | 10 |
| enabled_unread | 11 | **10** |
| mapped_but_disabled | 0 | 0 |
| disabled | 5 | **6** |

`SignInLogs` now classifies as `disabled` — the benign state (disabled, and no collector maps it). The standing `enabled_unread` **Warn** is gone.

Consequence: the acknowledged-category allowance floated as the alternative is **not needed** and was not built. Nothing to carry forward from that branch of the decision.

The remaining 10 `enabled_unread` categories are unchanged and out of scope for this issue: AgentRiskEvents, MicrosoftGraphPolicyLogs, NetworkAccessAlerts, NetworkAccessConnectionEvents, NetworkAccessGenerativeAIInsights, PreAuthenticationDiscoveryLogs, RemoteNetworkHealthLogs, RiskyAgents, RiskyServicePrincipals, ServicePrincipalRiskEvents.

## Outcome

Feature update reporting should answer which device failed and why, not only per-policy summary counts.

## Evidence

**Evidence class:** `explicit residual from #38/#193 (2026-07-25)`

- Per-policy summary shipped via #193.
- `FeatureUpdateDeviceState` and failure detail remain unimplemented because they require per-policy export fan-out sharing the 48/min budget.

## Proposed scope

- Measure per-policy report volume and schedule within the shared export-job limiter.
- Emit bounded outcome counts and one per-device result/failure twin.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Fan-out and rate-budget math is documented for the live policy count.
- [x] Every fetched device outcome gets a log twin.
- [x] No device identity becomes a metric label.
- [x] Partial policy failure is visible and does not discard healthy policies.

## Prior decisions and duplicate check

- Not duplicate of #38/#193: summary coverage exists; this is the named per-device residual.
- Related: #38, #193.

## Priority

Audit recommendation: **P2**.

comments.body:
## Unblocked — the export report exists and returns per-device rows. Building.

Probed 2026-07-28 as `graph2otel-poller`. Two feature-update profiles on the tenant, and the export completes:

```
POST /beta/deviceManagement/reports/exportJobs
     {"reportName":"FeatureUpdateDeviceState","filter":"(PolicyId eq '<profileId>')","format":"csv"}
  -> 201 -> inProgress x3 -> completed  (~8 s)
  -> 811-byte zip, one CSV member, 9 device rows
```

**The job id does not echo the report name** — it comes back as `WindowsUpdatePerPolicyPerDeviceStatus_<guid>`. Worth knowing before something keys off it.

### The trap: every status column ships twice, and only one of the two may be a metric label

```
"PolicyId","DeviceId","DeviceName","UPN","AggregateState","AggregateState_loc",
"CurrentDeviceUpdateStatus","CurrentDeviceUpdateStatus_loc","LatestAlertMessage","LatestAlertMessage_loc"
"29851ca2-…","dc910cbf-…","DESKTOP-ROTDNUB","vmuser@m7kni.io","Success","Success","8","Installed","0","Not applicable"
```

The bare column is the stable machine value; the `_loc` suffix is a **localized display string** — `CurrentDeviceUpdateStatus` is the code `8` while `_loc` is the English `Installed`. Which language that is depends on the tenant, so a `_loc` value keyed as a metric label changes series identity when the tenant's display language changes and silently splits one signal into two.

So the bare column keys the gauge and the localized one rides the twin. The twin carries **both**, because `8` alone is unreadable and `Installed` alone is unstable — this is a case where emitting one of the pair would be worse than emitting neither.

### Fan-out and budget, per the acceptance criterion

`1 + N`, N = feature-update profile count, bounded by tenant CONFIGURATION rather than tenant size. Live: 2 profiles, ~8 s per job, against the shared 48/min export-job limiter. At a 6h default interval even a hundred-profile tenant fits inside one cycle, so the per-collector enable/interval keys are the cost gate and **no new config surface is added**. A failed policy is logged and skipped, contributing no points rather than zeros — a failed read is a gap, not a measured zero.

**Evidence class:** `live-measured 2026-07-28, #351`.

## Shipped in `0811619` — `intune.feature_update_devices`

`make check` exit 0.

- [x] **Fan-out and rate-budget math is documented for the live policy count.** `1+N`, N = feature-update profile count (2 live), one export job each, ~8 s per job against the shared 48/min limiter, 6h default interval. Bounded by tenant *configuration*, not tenant size; the per-collector enable/interval keys are the cost gate and no new config surface was added.
- [x] **Every fetched device outcome gets a log twin.** One `intune.feature_update_device` per row, all 9 live rows covered by a full-mapping test.
- [x] **No device identity becomes a metric label.** `device_id`, `device_name` and `upn` are twin-only; the gauges key on `policy_name` plus the machine status columns.
- [x] **Partial policy failure is visible and does not discard healthy policies.** `errors.Join`; a failed profile contributes no points rather than zeros (#240), and a 403 on either the profile list or export-job creation is a graceful `Info` skip, matching `intune.feature_update_summary`.

### The trap, and a correction to my own earlier evidence

I originally recorded "only `Success` observed" from the first three rows. **That was wrong** — the 9-row export carries two states, and the second one is what makes this collector's central rule concrete rather than theoretical:

```
AggregateState "Success"    ->  AggregateState_loc "Success"      identical
AggregateState "InProgress" ->  AggregateState_loc "In progress"  DIFFERENT
```

So the bare and `_loc` columns are byte-identical on every healthy row. **A mapper verified only against healthy devices cannot tell the two columns apart at all**, and would key the gauge off a localized display string — which changes series identity when the tenant's display language changes, silently splitting one signal into two. Same for `CurrentDeviceUpdateStatus` (`2`/`8` vs `Offering`/`Installed`) and `LatestAlertMessage` (`0` vs `Not applicable`).

The bare column keys every gauge; the localized one rides the twin. The twin carries **both**, because `8` alone is unreadable and `Installed` alone is unstable.

### The guard written for that trap did not work, first time

`TestNoLocalizedValueReachesAnyMetricAttribute` asserted the localized *keys* were absent from metric attrs. Its name said value; it checked keys. Swapping the mapper to `row["AggregateState_loc"]` leaves the key `aggregate_state` untouched, so **it passed clean** — only an unrelated hardcoded-expectation test failed, incidentally.

It is now a value-level guard: `aggregate_state` must be `Success` or `InProgress` and never `In progress`, and likewise for the other two pairs. Re-sabotaged independently across all three columns after the fix; each one now fails it, and it is the only failing test.

That is the third guard in this tree in a week asserting one layer above where the bug lives — after `telemetrytest`'s join erasing element boundaries and `SetStrs`' empty-filter erasing absent-vs-empty. Worth stating as a rule: work out what a broken mapper would actually produce, then check the assertion is not sitting above a step that erases it.

Nothing is declared to `internal/wirecheck` — two observed values across one tenant's nine devices is not a value set (#234).

**Evidence class:** `live-measured 2026-07-28, #351`.

## Outcome

Assess risky Exposure Graph nodes/edges for critical identity/device/resource investigations without exporting an unbounded whole graph.

## Evidence

**Evidence class:** `preview docs-only; existing hunting transport (2026-07-25)`

- Preview `ExposureGraphNodes` and `ExposureGraphEdges` tables are available through the shipped hunting API.
- #251 rejected a nonexistent general Exposure Management REST surface, not these hunting tables.
- The 100,000-row/64 MB cap and shared human hunting CPU make a full graph unsafe.

## Proposed scope

- Measure schema, counts by label, licence availability, dynamic properties, and useful server-side predicates.
- Design a deliberately bounded risky subset and preserve selected node/edge twins.

## Constraints and non-goals

- Do not fabricate attack paths, choke points, or centrality from raw nodes/edges.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Real nodes/edges and property shapes precede mapping.
- [x] Queries stay below row/byte/CPU limits by proof.
- [x] Unknown labels/properties do not drop rows.
- [x] Any derived criticality metric has explicit semantics and evidence.

## Prior decisions and duplicate check

- Not duplicate of #251; the changed fact is a collector-shaped hunting-table route on an existing engine.
- Related: #249, #251.

## Primary sources

- [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-xdr/advanced-hunting-exposuregraphnodes-table](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-xdr/advanced-hunting-exposuregraphnodes-table)
- [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-xdr/advanced-hunting-exposuregraphedges-table](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-xdr/advanced-hunting-exposuregraphedges-table)

## Priority

Audit recommendation: **P2**.

comments.body:
## Probe result — **the bounded design is now measurable, and the unbounded one is measurably impossible.** Leaving open with the evidence.

Probed live 2026-07-28 as `graph2otel-poller` through the shipped hunting API under the existing `ThreatHunting.Read.All`. No new scope was needed, as this issue predicted.

### The size problem is real, and worse than "large"

```kql
ExposureGraphNodes | summarize n=count()   →  993,292   (77.3 s)
ExposureGraphEdges | summarize n=count()   →  HTTP 504  (150.1 s, gateway timeout)
```

**A bare `count()` over the edges table does not complete.** Not "returns too many rows" — the request times out at the gateway before returning a single integer. That is the strongest possible confirmation of this issue's premise: the 100,000-row / 64 MB cap is not the binding constraint, the query itself is, and any design that touches the full graph is dead before it reaches a row limit.

Note the asymmetry, because it shapes everything: nodes are countable in 77 s, edges are not countable at all. **Any edge work must carry a `where` predicate that prunes before the aggregation** — a design constraint, not a tuning detail.

### The bounded route works, and the label census is the useful signal

```kql
ExposureGraphNodes | summarize n=count() by tostring(NodeLabel) | order by n desc | take 20   →  20 rows, 27.3 s
```

| NodeLabel | count |
| --- | --- |
| `mdcSecurityRecommendation` | 618,032 |
| `Cve` | 372,330 |
| `baseModel` | 1,055 |
| `serviceprincipal` | 895 |
| `ai-agent` | 254 |
| `mdcManagementRecommendation` | 195 |
| `device` | 163 |
| `Microsoft Entra OAuth App` | 127 |
| `mdcAuditingRecommendation` | 96 |
| `group` | 74 |
| `IP address` | 16 |
| `SaaS Application` | 13 |
| `microsoft.compute/virtualmachines` | 12 |
| `mde-healthFinding` | 12 |
| `user` | 6 |
| `managedidentity` | 4 |
| `entra-userCookie` | 3 |
| `subscriptions` | 2 |
| `aadSecurityRecommendation` | 1 |
| `mdcSoftwareScanningTool` | 1 |

**Two labels are 99.7% of the graph.** `mdcSecurityRecommendation` + `Cve` = 990,362 of 993,292. Everything an operator would actually want a twin for — 254 AI agents, 163 devices, 127 OAuth apps, 6 users, 4 managed identities — is in the remaining 0.3%, about 2,900 nodes total.

That is the bounded subset, and it falls straight out of the data rather than being a guess: **exclude the two bulk recommendation/CVE labels and the rest of the graph is small enough to twin in full.** No sampling, no arbitrary top-N, no centrality heuristic.

### Node shape, captured

`ExposureGraphNodes` returns 6 columns: `NodeId`, `NodeLabel`, `NodeName`, `Categories` (string collection), `EntityIds` (string collection of JSON-encoded `{"type":…,"id":…}` blobs), and `NodeProperties`.

**`NodeProperties` is the trap.** It is a `dynamicColumnValue` — an arbitrarily deep, per-label-shaped object. A real `baseModel` node returned a nested `rawData.aiModelMetadata` carrying `modelName`, `modelVersion`, `createdBy`, `collectionType`, `depricationDate` (Microsoft's typo, on the wire), `isExpired`, `taskCapabilities` and more. Every label has a different shape. Emitting it raw would ship an unbounded, unreviewed object; mapping it typed means one sub-schema per label. **`NodeLabel` is the discriminator and any build must decide this per label, against captured samples, not generically.**

`EntityIds` entries are JSON strings, not objects — they need a second decode, and a mapper that treats them as plain identifiers will emit `{"type":"AiModelNameAndVersion","id":"name=phi-4;version=7"}` as if it were an id.

### Why this stays open rather than closing

Everything this spike was asked to measure is measured — schema, counts by label, availability, dynamic properties, and a useful server-side predicate. The remaining work is a build, not a spike, and it is a real one: per-label `NodeProperties` sub-schemas against captured samples, plus an edge query that prunes before aggregating.

Recording it now because it was **expensive to derive** — the edges timeout alone cost 150 s against a shared human hunting CPU quota, and re-running these three queries to rediscover the same facts would cost that again.

**Do not re-run `ExposureGraphEdges | summarize count()`.** It is now a known 504.

**Constraint restated, unchanged:** do not fabricate attack paths, choke points or centrality from raw nodes and edges. The label census above is a census; it is not a graph analysis and must not be presented as one.

**Evidence class:** `live-measured 2026-07-28, #350`.

## The bounded design, measured end to end — and the threshold now falls out of the data instead of naming labels

Follow-on probe 2026-07-28 as `graph2otel-poller`, same `ThreatHunting.Read.All`, no new scope. This completes the schema/limits work and fixes the design; the previous comment's counts stand unchanged.

### Three more queries, all completing

| query | result | elapsed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ExposureGraphNodes \| where NodeLabel !in ("mdcSecurityRecommendation","Cve") \| summarize count()` | **2,932** | 25.8 s |
| `ExposureGraphNodes \| where NodeLabel !in (…) \| summarize … by NodeLabel` (one real row per label) | 19 labels | 25.1 s |
| `ExposureGraphEdges \| where SourceNodeLabel !in (…) and TargetNodeLabel !in (…) \| summarize count() by EdgeLabel` | **337 edges, 13 labels** | 71.7 s |

`ExposureGraphEdges | summarize count()` unpruned remains a known HTTP 504 and was not re-run. The pruned form completing in 72 s is the proof the previous comment asked for: **a `where` predicate that prunes before the aggregation turns an uncountable table into a 337-row one.**

Edge labels, pruned: `can authenticate as` 122, `has permissions to` 120, `has credentials of` 20, `member of` 17, `routes traffic to` 16, `can impersonate as` 15, `can authenticate to` 14, `runs on` 3, `contains` 3, `affecting` 2, `frequently logged in by` 2, `has role on` 2, `used by` 1.

### The bounding rule is data-driven — no hardcoded label names

The previous comment proposed excluding `mdcSecurityRecommendation` and `Cve` by name. **That is the wrong shape and the collector does not do it.** The numbers say why: those two labels hold 618,032 and 372,330 nodes, and the next-largest label holds **1,057**. That is a 350× gap with nothing in it.

So the collector applies a **per-label twin threshold** sitting inside that empty band. A label whose population exceeds it is bulk inventory: **counted, and reported as `twinned="false"`, never silently truncated.** Everything else is twinned in full. On m7kni that reproduces the exact two-label exclusion, and on a tenant whose bulk labels are different it still separates inventory from investigable entities — with no label names in the source, no sampling, no top-N, and no centrality heuristic. The bounded subset genuinely falls out of the data.

### Node property shapes, one live sample per label

All 19 captured. `NodeProperties` is a `dynamicColumnValue` whose real payload sits under `rawData`, and the shapes cluster into roughly seven families — identity (`serviceprincipal`, `managedidentity`, `user`, `group`, `Microsoft Entra OAuth App`), device (`device`, `microsoft.compute/virtualmachines`), finding (`mdc*Recommendation`, `mde-healthFinding`, `aadSecurityRecommendation`), AI model (`baseModel`), AI agent (`ai-agent`), SaaS (`SaaS Application`), cloud account (`subscriptions`) — plus five labels whose `rawData` is entirely empty (`IP address`, `mdcSoftwareScanningTool`, `dataSensitivityScan`, `aadSecurityRecommendation`, and the empty case generally).

The twin therefore carries the **observed field union**, attempting every mapped field on every node and omitting what the wire did not send, with `NodeLabel` as the discriminator — the same one-builder-many-shapes pattern `defender.mdo_policies` uses for its seven policy types. That is what makes this issue's acceptance criterion *"unknown labels/properties do not drop rows"* true by construction rather than by vigilance: a label nobody has seen yet still produces a record.

Four mapping facts, all live:

- **`EntityIds` entries are JSON strings needing a second decode.** They become two index-aligned lists, ids and type names; an element that fails to decode keeps its raw text with the type `unparsed`, so alignment holds and the failure is visible rather than dropped.
- **`depricationDate` is Microsoft's spelling, on the wire** (label `baseModel`). Read theirs, publish `deprecation_date`.
- **`description` is not emitted.** On the finding labels it is multi-paragraph HTML — one `mdcAuditingRecommendation` sample runs past 600 characters of markup about a PostgreSQL setting. It is remediation prose, identical on every tenant, and not a fact about this tenant's graph.
- **`NodeProperties` itself is never emitted raw**, in any form.

### Edge shape, captured

`ExposureGraphEdges` returns `EdgeId`, `EdgeLabel`, `SourceNodeId/Name/Label/Categories`, `TargetNodeId/Name/Label/Categories`, `EdgeProperties`. `EdgeProperties` is empty for most labels — with one exception that is the best thing in the whole table: a **`can authenticate to`** edge carries `userRightsOnDevice`, holding `userRights` (`SeDebugPrivilege`, `SeImpersonatePrivilege`, `SeBackupPrivilege`, …), `logonMethods`, and **`isLocalAdmin: true`**. That is a per-edge statement of what an identity can actually do on a device, and it is mapped.

### What ships

`defender.exposure_graph`, on the existing hunting path, off unless `hunting.enabled` is set.

- Gauges `defender.exposure_graph.nodes{node_label, twinned}`, `.edges{edge_label, twinned}`, `.excluded_labels` — every dimension is Microsoft's own ontology (19 node labels, 13 edge labels), bounded by the ontology rather than by tenant size.
- Log twins `defender.exposure_graph_node` and `defender.exposure_graph_edge` carry every per-entity fact. `NodeId`, `NodeName` and `EntityIds` are never metric labels (#112).
- Four queries per cycle at a 6 h interval, with a per-label fallback if the combined twin fetch would approach the hard 100,000-row cap. Since every twinned label is under the threshold by construction, a per-label query can never hit that cap — which is why this collector needs no hash-sharding, unlike `defender.vulnerabilities`.
- **NOT `Experimental`:** the transport is Graph v1.0 `runHuntingQuery`, and #183 reserves that gate for genuine Graph *beta* surfaces. Nothing is declared to `internal/wirecheck` either — `NodeLabel` and `EdgeLabel` pass through verbatim with no map bucketing them to `"unknown"`, so there is no mapped set to derive an enum from, and #234 forbids inventing one.
- **Still not a graph analysis.** No attack paths, no choke points, no centrality. The constraint is unchanged and the collector honors it.

**Evidence class:** `live-measured 2026-07-28, #350`.

## Shipped in `4ed2c00` — `defender.exposure_graph`

Bounded exposure-graph collector on the existing hunting path, off unless `hunting.enabled` is set. `make check` exit 0, census 162 → **164** logical collectors / 165 → **167** registration-path candidates. No new scope: `ThreatHunting.Read.All` was already held.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [x] **Real nodes/edges and property shapes precede mapping.** Every field is mapped off a verbatim live capture taken as `graph2otel-poller` on 2026-07-28 — one real node per label for all 19 bounded labels, one real edge per label for all 13, committed as `testdata/`. Nothing is mapped from documentation.
- [x] **Queries stay below row/byte/CPU limits by proof.** Four queries per cycle at a 6 h interval, each one measured: node census 25.8 s, node twins 25.1 s, pruned edge census 71.7 s, edge samples 100.2 s. Every edge query carries a `where` predicate that prunes before aggregating; the unpruned form is the known 504 and a test asserts the predicate is present on every edge query the client receives.
- [x] **Unknown labels/properties do not drop rows.** The twin carries the observed field union with `node_label` as discriminator and attempts every mapped field on every node, so a label nobody has seen still produces a record. A table-driven test walks all 19 live labels.
- [x] **Any derived criticality metric has explicit semantics and evidence.** None is derived — no attack paths, no choke points, no centrality. The only aggregates are counts of Microsoft's own label ontology.

**The bounding rule, restated because it changed during the build.** It names no labels. A per-label twin threshold sits inside the measured 350× empty band between the largest bounded label (1,057) and the smallest bulk one (372,330); anything above it is counted and reported as `twinned="false"`. That reproduces the two-label exclusion on m7kni and still works on a tenant whose bulk labels differ. Because every twinned label is under the threshold by construction, a per-label fallback query can never reach the hard 100,000-row cap — which is why this collector needs no hash-sharding, unlike `defender.vulnerabilities`.

**Ships**

- Gauges `defender.exposure_graph.nodes{node_label, twinned}`, `.edges{edge_label, twinned}`, `.excluded_labels{entity_type}` (node/edge, both seeded).
- Log twins `defender.exposure_graph_node` and `defender.exposure_graph_edge`. `node_id`, `node_name`, `entity_ids` and every mapped property are twin-only (#112).
- Not `Experimental` (Graph v1.0 transport, #183). Nothing declared to `internal/wirecheck` — both labels pass through verbatim with no map bucketing them to `"unknown"`, so there is no mapped set to derive an enum from and #234 forbids inventing one.

**Two wire traps that turned out to be one trap in two places.** `EntityIds` elements are JSON strings needing a second decode — and so are the edge table's `delegatedPermissions.permissions`, `applicationPermissions.permissions` and `roles.rolePermissions`, which wrap their values as `{"permissionValue":…}` / `{"roleValue":…}`. Both are decoded to values; an element that fails to decode keeps its raw text rather than being dropped. `has permissions to` is the second-largest edge label (120 of 337), so leaving it unmapped would have shipped the label with nothing but its endpoints.

Also mapped: `userRightsOnDevice` on `can authenticate to` (privileges, logon methods, `is_local_admin`) and `primaryRefreshToken` on `has credentials of`. `depricationDate` is read at Microsoft's spelling and published as `deprecation_date`. Finding `description` is multi-paragraph HTML and is not emitted, guarded by a test that fails if `AttrDescription` ever appears.

**Verification.** Two guards were sabotage-tested rather than read: removing the edge prune predicate failed `TestEdgeQueries_AlwaysCarryNodeLabelPredicate` naming the exact 504 query shape, and shipping `EntityIds` un-decoded failed `TestEntityIds_DoubleDecode`. A third sabotage — shipping the permission wrappers un-decoded — failed three tests. Both were restored and the suite is green.

**Evidence class:** `live-measured 2026-07-28, #350`.

body:
## Outcome

Capture automatic attack-disruption, predictive-shielding, affected entities, policy, and action outcomes as a real event stream.

## Evidence

**Evidence class:** `docs-only; transport choice requires live evidence (2026-07-25)`

- The advanced-hunting table is event-shaped and accessible through the existing hunting API/scope.
- The current Hunt path is snapshot-only with no checkpoint; using it directly would replay history every interval.
- #241 proved Microsoft's streaming support page cannot be trusted without container enumeration.

## Proposed scope

- Enumerate real storage containers first.
- Prefer blobpipeline when a container exists; otherwise design a windowed hunting path with watermark, overlap, dedupe, and shared CPU controls.
- Build only with real rows or a maintainer-approved generated Defender event.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Transport choice is live-measured.
- [ ] Stable event identity is established despite no obvious published ID.
- [ ] No snapshot replay path can emit the same history every six hours.
- [ ] An eighth registration path extends collectordoc in the same commit.

## Prior decisions and duplicate check

- Not duplicate of #249: that issue reserves hunting for posture tables; this first proves a safe event-stream transport.
- Related: #106, #241, #249.

## Primary sources

- [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-xdr/advanced-hunting-disruptionandresponseevents-table](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-xdr/advanced-hunting-disruptionandresponseevents-table)

## Priority

Audit recommendation: **P1**.

comments.body:
## Probe result — **no-data.** The table exists, the transport works, and the tenant has never produced a row.

### The measurement — as `graph2otel-poller` through the shipped hunting API, 2026-07-28

```kql
DisruptionAndResponseEvents | summarize n=count()   →  n = 0
DisruptionAndResponseEvents | take 2                →  0 results, 38-column schema returned
```

Both 200 under the existing `ThreatHunting.Read.All`. The schema comes back fully populated (`Timestamp`, `ActionType`, `DeviceId`, `SourceDeviceId`, `TargetDeviceId`, `CompromisedAccountCount`, `PolicyId`, `PolicyName`, `IsPolicyOn`, `ReportId`, …), so the table is provisioned and queryable — it has simply never had an automatic-attack-disruption event written to it. That is the expected steady state for a tenant that has not been attacked.

### Verdict

**No build.** The transport question this spike exists to settle cannot be settled without rows:

- **The blob-vs-hunting choice is undecidable.** The proposed scope says to enumerate real storage containers first and prefer `blobpipeline` when one exists. There is no container to find for a table with no data, and #241 already established that Microsoft's streaming-support documentation cannot be trusted without live container enumeration — so the docs cannot stand in.
- **The windowed-hunting fallback needs a measured event time.** `Timestamp` is in the schema, but a watermark, an overlap and a dedupe key have to be validated against real arrival behavior. Building a checkpointed window collector on an unverified arrival model is how a stream silently double-counts or drops, and this project has no delta query on any log endpoint to fall back on.
- The issue's own constraint already says **build only with real rows or a maintainer-approved generated Defender event**. Neither exists.

Using the current snapshot-only Hunt path directly remains wrong for the reason the issue states — it would replay all history every interval — and nothing here changes that.

**Named unblock, either one:** (a) a real automatic-attack-disruption event lands in the table, or (b) the maintainer approves generating one, the way #129 exists to synthesize a risk event. Then the transport decision can be made on a measured arrival lag rather than on documentation.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Enumerate real storage containers first — not performed; with zero rows the enumeration cannot distinguish "no container" from "container with no data", so it would produce a misleading negative rather than an answer.
- [ ] Prefer blobpipeline when a container exists; otherwise design a windowed hunting path — undecidable, see above.
- [x] Build only with real rows or a maintainer-approved generated Defender event — the constraint held; nothing was built.

**Evidence class:** `live-measured 2026-07-28, #349`.

body:
## Outcome

Identify which anomaly occurred, its correlation groups, and affected devices rather than four tenant-wide zero/nonzero severity counts.

## Evidence

**Evidence class:** `live empty aggregate plus docs/CSDL detail routes (2026-07-25)`

- The shipped anomaly overview returns all four counts at zero on the current tenant.
- Beta anomaly, correlation-group, and affected-device collections now exist but have no observed row.
- Prior fleet-size unblock theories were disproved.

## Proposed scope

- Probe bare/select/top/count variants as the poller.
- Build only from a real nonempty sample.
- Emit bounded anomaly counts and one twin per anomaly/group/device.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A first observed anomaly row is the named unblock, not a guessed device-count threshold.
- [ ] Every fetched entity receives a twin.
- [ ] Device identities and correlation features remain log-only.
- [ ] Double-counting impacted devices across anomalies is documented/avoided.

## Prior decisions and duplicate check

- Not duplicate of #194: that issue shipped the aggregate overview and explicitly lacks these detailed collections.
- Related: #194, #225.

## Primary sources

- [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/intune-devices-userexperienceanalyticsanomaly-list?view=graph-rest-beta](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/intune-devices-userexperienceanalyticsanomaly-list?view=graph-rest-beta)

## Priority

Audit recommendation: **P2**.

comments.body:
## Kept open and parked — maintainer decision 2026-07-28, with new context

Verbatim: *"keep open parked for now I'll have to re-setup our EA setup again as there hasnt been any machines for a few days now."*

That is a **material change to this issue's premise** and is the reason it is not being closed no-build.

The recorded evidence said the shipped Endpoint Analytics anomaly overview reads all-zero and the beta detail collections have no observed row — which, on this epic's own "close no-data rather than write a docs-shaped mapper" rule, pointed at closing it. It now turns out the tenant's Endpoint Analytics estate has had **no machines reporting for several days**, so the all-zero reading may be describing an empty estate rather than a genuinely quiet one. Those are different facts and only one of them justifies closing.

**Unblock condition:** the maintainer rebuilds the EA setup and devices report again. Only then is a fresh all-zero reading evidence of anything.

Related and worth knowing for anyone picking up this epic: the recorded device-count unblock theories for the UXA rollup segments were **already disproved** — do not re-attach a device-count explanation to an empty rollup. Whatever gates those segments is still unknown.

## Re-read 2026-08-04 — the unblock has NOT fired, and the API contract is now known anyway

Two separable results. The parked condition is still parked, but the design question this spike was going to answer from a sample turned out to be answerable from the API's own request contract, with no rows at all.

Kept open by maintainer decision: **the EA estate gets rebuilt first**, then this is re-read.

### 1. The EA estate has not come back — and the obvious probe says it has

This is worth stating carefully because the first reading was wrong.

`GET /v1.0/deviceManagement/userExperienceAnalyticsDeviceScores` returns **9 rows** with real scores, which looks exactly like a healthy reporting estate. It is not one. `GET /v1.0/deviceManagement/managedDevices` returns 12 devices of which only **two run Windows**:

| device | last sync |
| --- | --- |
| `winsrv` | 2026-08-04T09:01:54Z |
| `LAPHAM` | 2026-07-29T17:12:26Z |

The four EA Proxmox VMs (`DESKTOP-88S17PG`, `DESKTOP-ROTDNUB`, `DESKTOP-N3FH69O`, `DESKTOP-HMG7DH5`) are **absent from Intune entirely**. Five of the nine score rows carry a **blank `deviceName`** with `model: "Standard PC (Q35 + ICH9, 2009)"` / `manufacturer: "QEMU"` — retained historical scores for devices whose managed-device record no longer exists, so the name has nothing to join against. Two more blank rows are Parallels ARM VMs and one is a Cloud PC, none of them in `managedDevices` either.

**`userExperienceAnalyticsDeviceScores` is a retained aggregate, not a liveness signal.** A non-empty response from it is not evidence that anything is reporting, and reading it that way is how this issue would get closed on a false premise. The device list is the check.

So the unblock recorded on 2026-07-28 — *"I'll have to re-setup our EA setup again"* — has not happened, and the all-zero anomaly reading below still describes an empty estate rather than a quiet one.

### 2. The detail collections are NOT enumerable — this is new, and it hands over the collector shape

Probed as `graph2otel-poller`. A bare GET on two of the three detail collections returns 400, which reads as "blocked" and is not:

| route | bare | with filter |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `userExperienceAnalyticsAnomaly` | **200**, `@odata.count: 0` | — |
| `userExperienceAnalyticsAnomalySeverityOverview` | **200**, all four counts 0 | — |
| `userExperienceAnalyticsAnomalyCorrelationGroupOverview` | **400** | **200** with `$filter=anomalyId eq '<guid>'` |
| `userExperienceAnalyticsAnomalyDevice` | **400** | **200** only with `$filter=anomalyId eq '<guid>' and correlationGroupId eq '<guid>'` |

`anomalyId` alone is **not** sufficient on `AnomalyDevice` — it 400s, as does `correlationGroupId` alone and `deviceId` alone. Both keys are required together.

The 400 body is a `proxy.msub06.manage.microsoft.com/DeviceFE/StatelessDeviceFE` error with no usable message, so it is indistinguishable from a genuine failure by inspection. **Only varying the request shape separated "requires a filter" from "broken".** Same lesson as the disproved theories this issue already carries: three false blocked-verdicts on this project have come from a single probe shape.

**What that settles, without a single row:** the collector is necessarily a **1 + N + M fan-out** — list anomalies, then per anomaly fetch its correlation groups, then per (anomaly, group) pair fetch devices. There is no tenant-wide enumeration of anomalous devices to be had, so the "avoid double-counting impacted devices across anomalies" acceptance item is a real design constraint rather than a nicety: the same device legitimately appears under multiple (anomaly, group) pairs and the fan-out is what surfaces it.

Cost is zero while `userExperienceAnalyticsAnomaly` is empty, and scales with anomaly count rather than device count — so this does **not** need the per-mailbox-style fan-out gate that #355/#363 needed.

### Where this leaves the issue

Unchanged: **a first observed anomaly row is the unblock**, and no mapper gets written from docs or an invented fixture. What has changed is that the shape question is answered in advance, so when a row does appear the work is mapping fields, not rediscovering the request contract.

Standing warning, unchanged and worth repeating because it keeps getting re-derived: **the device-count theories for the empty UXA rollup segments were already disproved.** Do not attach a device-count explanation to an empty rollup. Whatever gates those segments is still unknown, and an unexplained empty recorded as unexplained is better than a confident wrong story.

Next action is the maintainer's: rebuild the EA estate on the four Proxmox VMs, let Endpoint Analytics accumulate, then re-read `userExperienceAnalyticsAnomaly` and the severity overview. All probes here were read-only GETs; nothing was mutated.

## Outcome

Add staged quality-update rings, pause/hotpatch posture, explicit approvals, applicable content, and compliance-change state.

## Evidence

**Evidence class:** `existing live Windows Updates plus docs/CSDL additions (2026-07-25)`

- #259 proved the existing `updatePolicies` and `deployments` families are populated.
- The newer beta `policies/rings/approvals/applicableContent` model is distinct and unprobed.
- `WindowsUpdates.Read.All` is already held.

## Proposed scope

- Probe every relationship for every returned policy and establish its relationship to the shipped `updatePolicy` model.
- Read and preserve each polymorphic `@odata.type`.
- Keep audience members and matched devices out of initial scope.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Live payloads prove which policy families are populated.
- [ ] Overlap with current collectors is documented rather than guessed.
- [ ] Policy/ring/approval/compliance-change twins preserve entity detail.
- [ ] `/products` remains excluded per #259.

## Prior decisions and duplicate check

- Not duplicate of #259: this adds the separate newer policy/ring/approval model while retaining the shipped update-policy/deployment collectors.
- Related: #259.

## Primary sources

- [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/windowsupdates-adminwindowsupdates-list-policies?view=graph-rest-beta](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/windowsupdates-adminwindowsupdates-list-policies?view=graph-rest-beta)

## Priority

Audit recommendation: **P2**.

comments.body:
## Probe result — **no-build.** The newer model is reachable and empty; the model already shipped is the one carrying this tenant's data.

### The measurement — as `graph2otel-poller` under the existing `WindowsUpdates.Read.All`, 2026-07-28

| request | rows |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /beta/admin/windows/updates/policies` | **0** — the newer policies/rings/approvals model this issue exists to probe |
| `GET /beta/admin/windows/updates/updatePolicies` | **2** — the family #259 already ships |
| `GET /beta/admin/windows/updates/deployments` | **1** — also already shipped |
| `GET /beta/admin/windows/updates/catalog/entries?$top=3` | **3** — Microsoft's catalog, identical on every tenant |

All 200. The scope is effective and the newer surface is reachable — it simply has nothing in it.

### Verdict

**No build.** This issue's premise was that *"the newer beta `policies/rings/approvals/applicableContent` model is distinct and unprobed"*. It is now probed: distinct, yes; populated, no. With zero policies there are no rings, no approvals and no applicable content hanging off them, so the relationship fan-out this issue asked to measure has nothing to fan out over, and the polymorphic `@odata.type` handling it asked to preserve has no polymorphic values to preserve.

The specific thing being avoided is shipping a collector whose gauges read zero forever while `updatePolicies` — a different resource family, already collected — carries the tenant's actual update posture. Two families with near-identical names, one empty and one populated, is exactly the setup where an always-zero panel gets read as "no update policies configured".

**Named unblock:** at least one policy exists under `/beta/admin/windows/updates/policies`. Then the relationship walk (rings, approvals, applicableContent), the `@odata.type` set and the join back to the shipped `updatePolicy` model can all be measured against real rows. Re-probe is one request; the scope is already held.

### Acceptance criteria

- [x] Probe every relationship for every returned policy and establish its relationship to the shipped `updatePolicy` model — **zero policies returned**, so there is no relationship to walk. The shipped model is separately confirmed populated (2 policies, 1 deployment), which is the useful half of the answer.
- [ ] Read and preserve each polymorphic `@odata.type` — no polymorphic values exist to read.
- [x] Keep audience members and matched devices out of initial scope — unchanged; nothing was fetched beyond the four requests above.

**Evidence class:** `live-measured 2026-07-28, #347`.

## Outcome

Expose the inaccessible Cloud PC worklist plus RTT, bandwidth, UDP, and dropped-connection trends by region.

## Evidence

**Evidence class:** `docs/CSDL only; Windows 365 data now exists (2026-07-25)`

- Beta read-only report POSTs exist under `CloudPC.Read.All` and are not Intune export-job creation.
- They return schema/value streams that require live column validation.

## Proposed scope

- Capture every selected report and page as the poller.
- Build a schema-indexed decoder rather than fixed column order.
- Emit current daily/weekly non-additive quality gauges and per-device/region logs.

## Constraints and non-goals

- Do not backfill the seven-day tenant metrics report into current-state Prometheus metrics.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Live schema, paging, number encoding, and empty behavior are measured.
- [ ] Per-device identity remains log-only.
- [ ] Quality units/trends are not combined into a fabricated score.
- [ ] Experimental gate, docs, and goldens are complete if built.

## Prior decisions and duplicate check

- Distinct from Cloud PC lifecycle and connectivity history: this owns report-shaped accessibility and regional quality.

- [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/cloudpcreports-getinaccessiblecloudpcreports?view=graph-rest-beta](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/cloudpcreports-getinaccessiblecloudpcreports?view=graph-rest-beta)

## Probe result — **the entire `virtualEndpoint` segment is refused, and not by Graph.** Closing all three Cloud PC children on one finding.

This comment covers **#344, #345 and #346** — all three route through `/deviceManagement/virtualEndpoint`, and none of them can start.

### The measurement — as `graph2otel-poller`, 2026-07-28

| request | result |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /v1.0/deviceManagement` | **200** |
| `GET /v1.0/deviceManagement/virtualEndpoint` | **403** |
| `GET /v1.0/deviceManagement/virtualEndpoint/cloudPCs` | **403** |
| `GET /beta/deviceManagement/virtualEndpoint/cloudPCs` | **403** |
| `GET /v1.0/deviceManagement/virtualEndpoint/onPremisesConnections` | **403** |
| `GET /v1.0/deviceManagement/virtualEndpoint/provisioningPolicies` | **403** |
| `GET /v1.0/deviceManagement/virtualEndpoint/galleryImages` | **403** |
| `GET /v1.0/deviceManagement/virtualEndpoint/auditEvents` | **403** |

**The 403 body is HTML, not JSON** — a bare `<html><head><title>403 Forbidden</title></head>…` page. That is the load-bearing detail. Every Graph authorization failure this project has ever seen returns a JSON `error` object with a `code` and a `message`; an HTML 403 comes from an edge in front of the service, so the request never reached Graph's authorization layer at all. **This is a service-availability refusal, not a permission problem**, and the parent `/deviceManagement` returning 200 in the same token proves the token itself is fine.

`CloudPC.Read.All` is in the poller's token — verified by decoding the `roles` claim, it is there. So the usual next move is already spent.

### Correcting these issues' shared premise

All three were opened on the strength of *"#198 consumed 21 real Windows 365 audit records after Cloud PCs were provisioned, so #251's old `no active Windows 365` unblock has fired."* That was true when written. **It is no longer true**: whatever Windows 365 provisioning existed then is gone, and the segment now refuses at the edge. The unblock fired and then un-fired.

### Verdict

**No build** for all three, on a shared blocker rather than three separate ones:

- **#344** (Cloud PC lifecycle and network-connection health) — no inventory route responds.
- **#345** (connectivity and health-check events) — needs per-Cloud-PC fan-out over a device list that cannot be fetched.
- **#346** (inaccessible-device and regional quality reports) — the report POSTs live under the same refused segment.

Nothing about any of the three designs was disproved. They are unreachable, not wrong.

**Named unblock, one condition for all three:** `GET /v1.0/deviceManagement/virtualEndpoint/cloudPCs` returns 200 — i.e. Windows 365 is licensed and provisioned on the tenant again. Re-probe is a single request. **Check the response body type before concluding anything from a future 403 here**: HTML means the service is refusing, JSON means authorization, and they need completely different responses.

**Do not re-attempt any of these by granting a broader Graph scope.** That is now the fourth denial in this programme sitting on an axis a scope grant does not move (#352 tenant-root scope, #330 Purview DataInsights backend, #326 licensing, now this).

**Evidence class:** `live-measured 2026-07-28, #344`.

## Outcome

A live Intune configuration subtype should have an evidence-backed bounded bucket rather than inflating `odata_type="other"`.

## Evidence

**Evidence class:** `live-measured (2026-07-25)`

- Live wirecheck reports `#microsoft.graph.iosDeviceFeaturesConfiguration`.
- Three current profiles land in the generic `other` bucket.
- The existing test explicitly records the subtype as intentionally unmapped before this evidence existed.

## Proposed scope

- Capture/sanitize the live object and add a bounded mapper category derived from the type map.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A live-shaped fixture fails before the new mapping.
- [ ] Current rows move out of `other`.
- [ ] Wirecheck remains report-only for future subtypes.
- [ ] No profile identity becomes a metric label.

## Prior decisions and duplicate check

- No existing issue covers this exact live subtype.
- Related: #234.

## Priority

Audit recommendation: **P1**.

comments.body:
## Already shipped in `99623a9` — closing as done

Landed with `99623a9` ("fix(intune): harden startup API edge cases", closing the #398 startup incident), alongside #341 and #342.

Verified against this issue's acceptance criteria:

- [x] **Current rows move out of `other`.** `configprofiles.go:91` maps `#microsoft.graph.iosDeviceFeaturesConfiguration` to the `ios_device_features` bucket, and `TestCollectEmitsLiveSnapshotEndToEnd` pins the resulting counts (`ios_device_features: 1`, `ios_custom: 1`) against the live fixture. The lookup is exact-match with an `other` fallback, so those pinned counts fail without the entry.
- [x] **Wirecheck remains report-only for future subtypes.** `knownODataTypes` is derived from `odataTypeBuckets` (`configprofiles.go:120-130`), and there is a dedicated anti-drift test — `TestWatchedODataTypesAreDerivedFromTheBucketMap` (`configprofiles_test.go:547`) — that fails the build if the two diverge. This is the strongest form of CLAUDE.md's derive-don't-restate rule anywhere in the three issues.
- [x] **No profile identity becomes a metric label.** The gauge is keyed only on the bounded `odata_type` bucket; `TestNoPerEntityAttribute` covers it.

### The specific trap this issue set up was avoided

The body noted that "the existing test explicitly records the subtype as intentionally unmapped before this evidence existed" — exactly the kind of stale assertion that would now contradict the fix and quietly reassert the old belief. It was not left behind: `TestLiveCaptureReportsTheKnownODataTypeGap` was renamed to `TestLiveCaptureRecognizesKnownODataTypes` (`configprofiles_test.go:527`) and rewritten to assert **zero** findings. The only surviving `other`-bucket assertions use a synthetic genuinely-unmapped type, which is correct and unrelated.

Tests green: `ok internal/collectors/intune/configprofiles 0.354s`.

## Outcome

Issued fleet certificates must not be counted as `unknown`.

## Evidence

**Evidence class:** `live-measured (2026-07-25)`

- Live wirecheck repeatedly reports `intune.cert_inventory certificate_status=Issued`.
- The mapper recognizes lowercase `issued` only.
- All eight current certificate rows therefore land in `state="unknown"`.

## Proposed scope

- Add an exact-case live fixture and map the observed wire value through the existing bounded state model.
- Retain the raw status on the log twin.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The failing live-shaped test is observed before the fix.
- [ ] `Issued` maps to healthy.
- [ ] No wirecheck increment occurs after a full export cadence.
- [ ] Unknown future values remain report-only and never drop rows.

## Prior decisions and duplicate check

- No existing issue covers this exact post-#234 wire value.
- Related: #234.

## Priority

Audit recommendation: **P0**.

comments.body:
## Already shipped in `99623a9` — closing as done

Landed with `99623a9` ("fix(intune): harden startup API edge cases", closing the #398 startup incident). #398 recorded the same three live wire drifts filed as #341/#342/#343.

Verified against this issue's acceptance criteria, not merely against the map entry existing:

- [x] **`Issued` maps to healthy.** `certinventoryreport.go:153` — `"Issued": "healthy"` in `certificateStatusBuckets`.
- [x] **The failing live-shaped test is pinned.** `TestLiveIssuedCertificateStatusIsHealthyAndMapped` (`certinventoryreport_test.go:443`) asserts `state == "healthy"` for wire value `Issued`. `certificateStatusBucketFor` is an exact-match lookup falling back to `other`, and only lowercase `issued` existed before, so the test fails deterministically without the entry — it is a real pin, not a decorative one.
- [x] **No wirecheck increment after a full export cadence.** `knownCertificateStatuses` is **derived from `certificateStatusBuckets`' own keys** (`certinventoryreport.go:191-197`, with the reason stated in the comment above it), so the watched set is exactly the mapped set and cannot drift. The test asserts zero `wirecheck.MetricUnexpected` points for the `Issued` fixture.
- [x] **Unknown future values remain report-only and never drop rows.** `TestUnmappedCertificateStatusIsAnnounced` feeds an unmapped value, asserts the diagnostic fires **and** that the row still reaches the log twin carrying the raw status.

That last pair is the property that matters most here: the whole reason this was a P0 is that all eight live certificate rows were landing in `state="unknown"`, so the gauge said nothing true about the fleet. The derived watched set is what stops the next casing change from doing it again silently.

Tests green: `ok internal/collectors/intune/certinventoryreport 0.345s`.

A current recommendation label value should not fire schema drift and remain outside the declared watched set.

## Evidence

- Live logs and Prometheus contain `recommendation="insiderRiskPolicy"`.
- The mapper emits it as a metric label, but the declared recommendation enum omits it.

## Proposed scope

- Capture a sanitized live fixture and derive the watched set from the mapper's keyed values.
- Do not accept `unknownFutureValue` generically.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The live value is covered by fixture and enum derivation.
- [ ] No watchdog increment occurs after a complete poll.
- [ ] A future unmapped value still reports without dropping the record.

Audit recommendation: **P1**.

comments.body:
## Already shipped in `99623a9` — closing as done, not as won't-do

This landed as part of `99623a9` ("fix(intune): harden startup API edge cases", which closed the #398 startup incident). All three live wire values #398 recorded — `recommendation=insiderRiskPolicy`, `odata_type=#microsoft.graph.iosDeviceFeaturesConfiguration`, `certificate_status=Issued` — are the same three drifts filed here and on #342/#343.

Verified against this issue's acceptance criteria rather than against the existence of a map entry:

- [x] **The live value is covered by fixture and enum derivation.** The value is in `knownTypes` (`internal/collectors/entra/recommendations/recommendations.go:53`) and in the live fixture (`recommendations_test.go:87,96`, captured `live-measured 2026-07-17, #165`).
- [x] **No watchdog increment after a complete poll.** `TestCollectEmitsStatusPriorityAndImpactedCounts` now asserts `len(rec.MetricPoints(wirecheck.MetricUnexpected)) == 0` against that fixture (`recommendations_test.go:320-322`).
- [x] **A future unmapped value still reports without dropping the record.** `TestCollectReportsUnmappedEnums` feeds an invented type, asserts the watchdog fires **and** that the gauge still emits (`recommendations_test.go:391-411`).

### One nuance worth recording, because the acceptance wording does not fit this collector

The proposed scope said "derive the watched set from the mapper's keyed values". **This collector has no bucket map to derive from** — `status`, `priority` and `recommendationType` are passed through RAW as metric labels, which is exactly why #234 wanted them watched. The package says so at `recommendations.go:37-40`: the sets are declared from the Graph beta CSDL EnumType definitions because there is no in-repo map.

So the drift risk that CLAUDE.md's derive-don't-restate rule guards against — a watched set diverging from a mapped set — structurally cannot occur here: `knownTypes` is the single declaration point and its only consumer is the `watch.Value` call at line 136. The rule applies to collectors that DO have a bucket map; `certinventoryreport` and `configprofiles` (#342/#343) both derive correctly, and `configprofiles` even has an explicit anti-drift test.

`unknownFutureValue` is excluded from every set, as this issue required.

Tests green: `ok internal/collectors/entra/recommendations 0.342s`, `ok internal/wirecheck 0.309s`.

Assess the remaining pre-authentication discovery category only after the tenant emits a real event.

## Evidence

**Evidence class:** `data-gated residual from #134 (2026-07-25)`

- #134 found the category enabled but empty and therefore unmappable.
- It remains visible in the live unread-category inventory.

## Proposed scope

- Capture a legitimate row when the corresponding tenant feature produces one.
- Measure content, volume, identifiers, and overlap with sign-in/risk/GSA signals.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A real row is the explicit unblock condition.
- [ ] No docs-shaped mapper lands.
- [ ] Secrets/content risk and volume are reviewed from the wire.

comments.body:
## Re-validated 2026-07-29 — still no container, 13 days after enablement

Same probe as #339, same listing (`graph2otelm7kni`, as `graph2otel-poller`, 200, **41 containers**):

```
insights-logs-preauthenticationdiscoverylogs   ->  ABSENT
```

Enabled 2026-07-16, so a ~13-day negative. The account has grown 9 → 41 containers over that period, so the destination is demonstrably healthy and receiving — the absence is the category, not the plumbing.

**Finding: `PreAuthenticationDiscoveryLogs` emits zero rows on m7kni over 13 days, live-measured 2026-07-29.**

### One thing that changed and does NOT unblock this

#134 speculated this category might need Global Secure Access / Entra Private Access. **GSA is now genuinely in use on this tenant** — all three forwarding profiles read `state: enabled` and `/beta/networkAccess/logs/traffic` returns real rows today (see #338). Two GSA-family blob categories that were previously container-less have also woken up in the same listing: `insights-logs-networkaccessconnectionevents` and `insights-logs-networkaccessgenerativeaiinsights`.

So the most obvious "it needs GSA" theory has been **partially tested and did not fire** — GSA traffic is flowing and this category is still silent. That is worth recording rather than leaving the theory standing unexamined, but it is not a disproof either: Private Access specifically (as opposed to internet/M365 forwarding) may be the actual trigger, and pre-authentication discovery may need app-proxy-style published applications that do not exist here.

**Do not attach a confident explanation to this absence.** Same discipline as the disproved device-count theories on the UXA rollup segments (#348) — an unexplained empty is better recorded as unexplained.

### Unblock unchanged

A real row. No docs-shaped mapper, no invented fixture. Keeping it enabled costs ~£0.001/mo and preserves the tripwire; the disable option from #134's acceptance criteria stays available and is a maintainer tenant-config action, not repo work.

## Closed no-data 2026-08-04 — 19-day zero-row negative. The category stays enabled.

Maintainer decision: close the issue, **keep the diagnostic category on**. Separable actions; both recorded here so nobody later assumes the close turned the tripwire off.

### Measured today, as `graph2otel-poller`

Same listing as #339 (`graph2otelm7kni`, `GET /?comp=list`, 200, **42 containers**):

```
insights-logs-preauthenticationdiscoverylogs   ->  ABSENT
```

Enabled **2026-07-16**, so a **19-day** negative, up from 13 days on 2026-07-29. Still enabled on the setting (`GET /providers/microsoft.aadiam/diagnosticSettings`, 200):

```
setting "graph2otel":  PreAuthenticationDiscoveryLogs  enabled=True
```

Probe shape validated the same way: every container enumerated with the identical request, **29 of 42 hold blobs**. The absence is the category.

### The GSA theory is now more thoroughly dead than it was

#134 speculated this category might need Global Secure Access. The 2026-07-29 comment recorded that GSA is genuinely in use — traffic flowing, `entra.network_access_traffic` shipped under #338 — and the category was still silent, and noted that two GSA-family blob categories had "woken up" in the same listing.

**That last observation is now corrected.** `insights-logs-networkaccessconnectionevents` and `insights-logs-networkaccessgenerativeaiinsights` were re-probed today with a full blob listing rather than a container listing: both return **200 with zero blobs**. A container existing is not the same as a category emitting, and reading container presence as "woken up" overstated it. Those two are in exactly the same state as this one.

**Do not attach a confident explanation to this absence.** Private Access specifically, or app-proxy-style published applications, remain untested candidates rather than answers. Same discipline as the disproved device-count theories on #348.

### Why this closes

Nothing left to measure, no action available to any reader, and a strong negative against a demonstrably healthy destination. `live-measured 2026-08-04`.

**Re-open condition:** `insights-logs-preauthenticationdiscoverylogs` appears in the container listing. The category stays enabled as a free tripwire, so that will happen on its own if the tenant grows the feature.

No docs-shaped mapper, no invented fixture.

- Related: #134.

## Priority

Audit recommendation: **P3**.

comments.body:
## Re-validated 2026-07-29 — still no container, 13 days after enablement

Full container listing on `graph2otelm7kni` as `graph2otel-poller` (`GET /?comp=list`, 200, **41 containers**):

```
insights-logs-microsoftgraphpolicylogs   ->  ABSENT
```

Azure creates a container on first write, so absent = nothing has ever been written. The category was enabled on the `aadiam/graph2otel` diagnostic setting **2026-07-16**, so this is a ~13-day negative, well past the 24h documented bar and well past the 19.6h first-write latency that #134 recorded as its worst observed case.

### Why this is now strong evidence where the earlier reading was weak

#134's negative was explicitly untrustworthy: `GraphNotificationsActivityLogs` was absent at 19.6h and started emitting **6 minutes later**, which is why no verdict was taken then. That failure mode is now excluded by elapsed time — the account has had 13 days and 32 further containers have appeared in the interim (the account went 9 → 41 containers, including the whole `advancedhunting-*` family, `riskyusers`, `userriskevents`, `managedidentitysigninlogs`, `operationallogs`, `windows365auditlogs`). The storage destination is demonstrably healthy and receiving.

**So the finding is: `MicrosoftGraphPolicyLogs` emits zero rows on m7kni over 13 days, live-measured 2026-07-29.**

Per #134's framing this reads as *needs a tenant feature this tenant lacks* rather than *not valuable* — on a tenant with whatever writes it, it may well emit. The shape, overlap and volume criteria remain **unanswerable rather than unanswered**: with no rows there is nothing to document, and the "does it duplicate `entra.conditional_access` or `SignInLogs`' CA detail" question cannot be settled from a category name.

### Kept open, and a maintainer option worth naming

Unblock condition unchanged: **the first real row**. No mapper from docs, no synthetic fixture.

The alternative is #134's own acceptance criterion — *categories that do not earn their place are turned off*. My recommendation is **keep it enabled**: the cost is ~£0.001/mo with a 7-day lifecycle, and the entire point of this residual is to catch a first row whenever the tenant grows whatever feature writes it. Disabling would trade a free tripwire for nothing. That is a maintainer tenant-config call either way, and neither option involves repo work.

## Closed no-data 2026-08-04 — 19-day zero-row negative. The category stays enabled.

Maintainer decision: close the issue, **keep the diagnostic category on**. Those are separable actions and this comment records both halves so a future reader does not assume the close disabled the tripwire.

### Measured today, as `graph2otel-poller`

Full container listing on `graph2otelm7kni` (`GET /?comp=list`, 200, **42 containers**):

```
insights-logs-microsoftgraphpolicylogs   ->  ABSENT
```

Azure creates a container on first write, so absent = nothing has ever been written. Enabled on the `aadiam/graph2otel` diagnostic setting **2026-07-16**, so this is a **19-day** negative — up from the 13-day reading on 2026-07-29, and far past the 19.6h worst-observed first-write latency #134 recorded.

The category is still live on the setting (`GET /providers/microsoft.aadiam/diagnosticSettings`, 200):

```
setting "graph2otel":  MicrosoftGraphPolicyLogs  enabled=True
```

### The probe shape was validated rather than assumed

A zero from one request shape is how three false blocked-verdicts have been produced on this project. Every container on the account was enumerated with the identical request: **29 of 42 hold blobs**, the largest being `advancedhunting-deviceprocessevents` at 957 MB across 40 blobs. So the listing works and the absence is the category, not the probe and not the destination.

### Why this closes rather than stays open

The unblock condition — a first real row — is unchanged and remains correct. What changed is that it is no longer worth an open issue: there is no action any reader can take to advance it, no measurement left to make, and 19 days of a demonstrably healthy destination is a strong negative. `live-measured 2026-08-04`.

**The tripwire survives the close.** `MicrosoftGraphPolicyLogs` stays enabled at ~£0.001/mo with the 7-day lifecycle, so if the tenant ever grows whatever feature writes this category, the container appears on its own.

**Re-open condition:** `insights-logs-microsoftgraphpolicylogs` appears in the container listing. At that point the shape, overlap and volume criteria in the body become answerable for the first time — they are currently unanswerable rather than unanswered, since the "does it duplicate `entra.conditional_access` or the sign-in CA detail" question cannot be settled from a category name.

No mapper was written from docs and no synthetic fixture was created, per the acceptance criteria.
