body:
## Outcome

After forwarding is enabled, assess allowed/blocked traffic, connection health, application posture, and aggregate reports as an Experimental HighVolume feed.

## Evidence

**Evidence class:** `data-blocked residual from #239 (2026-07-25)`

- #239 proved the traffic endpoint returns 200/empty because forwarding profiles are disabled, not because the route is absent.
- Current Microsoft docs name `NetworkAccess-Reports.Read.All`; historical configuration records a different held scope and must be revalidated.

## Proposed scope

- Maintainer enables a forwarding profile and routes deliberate test traffic outside graph2otel.
- Then validate exact permission, wire shape, paging, event time, dedupe, and measured volume as the poller.
- Separate window traffic logs from bounded health/report snapshots.

## Constraints and non-goals

- Do not fetch or emit Generative AI prompt/content data in this issue.
- Do not reopen Event Hub, Log Analytics, or dual transport.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Forwarding/test traffic is the named unblock condition.
- [ ] A real nonempty payload and permission receipt precede mapper work.
- [ ] Both `Experimental` and `HighVolume` gates are applied if built.
- [ ] User/device/IP/FQDN/URL/session detail stays log-only.

## Prior decisions and duplicate check

- Not duplicate of #239: that closed issue established reachability and the exact external data unblock; this residual begins only when that condition is deliberately exercised.
- Related: #130, #239, #251.

## Primary sources

- [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/networkaccess-logs-list-traffic?view=graph-rest-beta](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/networkaccess-logs-list-traffic?view=graph-rest-beta)

## Priority

Audit recommendation: **P2**.

comments.body:
## Parked by maintainer decision 2026-07-28

Verbatim: *"Park it until GSA is in use."*

Restating why, because this is a **data** block and not a permission block, and the two are easy to confuse: #239 recorded that Global Secure Access forwarding profiles are disabled on this tenant. With no forwarding profile there is no traffic, so a probe returns empty **regardless of what scope is granted** — and an empty result here would look identical to a mapping failure.

That is exactly the trap this project has hit before: an empty response is not evidence of a broken collector, and a green tick on an empty collection is not evidence of data.

**Unblock condition:** the maintainer enables a forwarding profile and routes some test traffic through it. Only then is probing meaningful. Do not grant a scope or write a mapper before that — a mapper written against no rows is a docs-shaped mapper by another name.

## UNBLOCKED — GSA is forwarding traffic and the logs are returning real rows (live-measured 2026-07-29)

The named unblock condition has fired. Maintainer confirmed GSA is set up with traffic flowing; probed as `graph2otel-poller`.

### The premise correction, first

This issue was parked because **all three forwarding profiles were `state: disabled`**, so a probe returned 200-and-empty regardless of scope. That is no longer true:

```
GET /beta/networkAccess/forwardingProfiles   -> 200
  Microsoft 365 traffic forwarding profile   m365      enabled   priority 100
  Internet traffic forwarding profile        internet  enabled   priority 300
  Private access traffic forwarding profile  private   enabled   priority 200
GET /beta/networkAccess/tenantStatus         -> 200  onboarded
GET /beta/networkAccess/logs/traffic         -> 200  REAL ROWS + @odata.nextLink
```

`NetworkAccess.Read.All` was already held (live-verified 2026-07-23) — **no new grant is needed and none was made.**

### Measured volume — the figure the `HighVolume` annotation requires

| measurement | result |
| --- | --- |
| one clock hour, server-side filtered (18:00–19:00Z) | **3,695 rows**, 4 pages, 6.0 s, not truncated |
| implied daily rate | **~88,700 rows/day** |
| generating estate | essentially **one** Windows 11 client |

That is the number that decides the gate. ~89k records/day from a single device means the rate scales with **traffic**, not tenant size — the `HighVolume` definition exactly (#254), and it must carry this measured figure in its `collectordoc` annotation rather than the words "high volume". It is also beta-only, so it takes `Experimental` as well (#183); both gates register only when config explicitly enables them, so it ships **off by default**.

Worth stating plainly: on a real estate this is the largest single stream this project would ship. It must not be default-on, and the `event_domain` stream split (#402) is still awaiting tenant-side promotion, so the log stream it lands in is already auto-sharding.

### Query surface — measured, not assumed

| capability | result |
| --- | --- |
| `$top` ceiling | **exactly 1000**. `$top=1001` → 400 naming the limit verbatim |
| `$filter` on `createdDateTime` | **works**, including a two-sided `ge`/`lt` window |
| `$filter` on `trafficType` | works |
| `$orderby=createdDateTime` | works; **default order is DESCENDING** (newest first) |
| `$count=true` | **400** — `Query option 'Count' is not allowed` |

Server-side windowing plus ascending order is what makes this a well-behaved `WindowCollector`: the watermark can bound the fetch on the wire instead of paging the firehose and discarding. Note the default descending order — a collector that pages with the default and stops early gets the newest rows, not the oldest, which is the wrong end for watermark advancement.

### Wire shape — ~70 fields, and most of them are empty strings

One verbatim row captured. The identity/detail fields are all present and all log-only per #112: `userPrincipalName`, `userId`, `deviceId`, `sourceIp`, `destinationIp`, `destinationFQDN`, `destinationUrl`, `destinationPort`, `transportProtocol`, `deviceOperatingSystem`, `agentVersion`, `initiatingProcessName`, `sentBytes`/`receivedBytes`, `policyId`/`policyRuleId`.

Two shape facts that must drive the mapper:

**Microsoft uses empty string, not absent, for "no value".** On the captured row `userId`, `userPrincipalName`, `sessionId`, `destinationIp`, `destinationUrl`, `policyRuleId`, `threatType`, `remoteNetworkId` and ~15 others are all `""` while being structurally present. So `SetStr`-style absence handling is correct and a required-field check on presence would pass over a row carrying nothing. Distinct from the `null` fields (`httpMethod`, `responseCode`, `operationStatus`, `policyType`, `isAgentic`, `tlsDetails`, `privateAccessDetails`, `dnsRequestMetadata`, `aiAgentDetails`, `kerberosAuthenticationInfo`) — two different "no value" encodings in one row.

**The schema now carries an agentic-AI block** (`isAgentic`, `isTokenAgentic`, `agenticSessionId`, `agentVirtualId`, `agentTypeId`, `agentTypeName`, `mcpPrimitiveName`, `mcpProtocolVersion`, `aiAgentDetails`, `aiAgentDetectionDetails`, `processTree`, `processArgs`) that is null/empty on every observed row. Per this project's wirecheck rule, **no value set is derivable from zero observations** — those fields stay unwatched and are recorded as such rather than mapped speculatively. `processArgs`/`processTree` also need a content-risk look against a real populated row before being emitted; a command line can carry a credential.

This issue's own non-goal stands: **no Generative AI prompt/content data is fetched or emitted here.**

Building now as a `WindowCollector`: own watermark + bounded overlap + seen-id dedupe on `transactionId`, server-side `createdDateTime` filter, ascending order, `$top=1000`, bounded counter `entra.network_access.transactions{traffic_type, action}` only, everything per-connection in the log twin.

## Shipped and closed — `4fce107`

`entra.network_access_traffic` is live, built against the wire and not the docs. Every acceptance criterion is met: forwarding/test traffic was the named unblock and it fired, a real non-empty payload preceded the mapper, both gates are applied, and every per-connection field is log-only.

Census 169 → 170 logical / 172 → 173 candidates. `make check` exit 0, dashboard panels placed, beta manifest and drift snapshot updated.

### The gates, with the measured number the annotation requires

`HighVolume` **and** `Experimental`, and both are load-bearing rather than belt-and-braces — an operator needs the two facts independently. HighVolume carries the figure per #254: **3,695 records in one clock hour**, from essentially one Windows 11 client, ≈88,700/day. Experimental carries the beta dependency per #183. It ships **off**.

No new grant. `NetworkAccess.Read.All` was already held; the ReadWrite variants the endpoint's own 403 message lists are explicitly not taken, and a test fails if a declared scope ever contains `ReadWrite`.

### The query decisions, all measured

`$top` ceiling exactly 1000 · `$count=true` → 400 · `$filter` on `createdDateTime` works two-sided · **default order is DESCENDING**.

`$orderby=createdDateTime asc` is accepted and is deliberately **not** used. Accepting an `$orderby` is not evidence that page order is stable across a paged, throttled, multi-region firehose, and that is not a property this project assumes from one successful request. So the window drains under strict `gt`/`lt` and sorts client-side. Cost is bounded — at the measured rate a 5-minute window is ~300 records, inside one page. `initialLookback` is one hour and `maxWindow` six, because a day-scale cold start on a busy tenant would drain tens of thousands of rows before the first watermark is written.

### No bounded counter, and that is the decision rather than an omission

#239 sketched `entra.network_access.transactions{traffic_type, action}`. Not built: a LogQL `count by (traffic_type, action)` over these records answers the identical question at no series cost, the logpipeline engine emits logs only, and every other dimension anyone would actually slice by (destination FQDN, user, device, policy rule) is unbounded and could never be a label (#112). The rate panel on the dashboard *is* that count-by, and its description says so.

### Three wire facts this surface should be known for

**Two different encodings of absence in one record.** ~20 fields are structurally present and set to the **empty string** (`sessionId`, `destinationIp`, `destinationUrl`, `threatType`, `userId`/`userPrincipalName` on service traffic) while `httpMethod`, `responseCode`, `operationStatus`, `policyType`, `isAgentic` and every nested object use **null**. So a presence check finds a row carrying nothing. A bare int on `responseCode` publishes a fabricated HTTP 0; a false `isAgentic` claims GSA evaluated a connection it never looked at.

**`operationStatus` is GSA's own processing status, NOT the connection's.** 2,941 of 3,000 rows are `action=block` with `operationStatus=success`. Reading it as connection success is the obvious and wrong interpretation, and it is called out on the dashboard panel because that is where someone will hit it.

**`threatType` has two spellings of nothing** — `""` and `"NoneFound"` — and only the second survives into the record, so a query filtering on absence must handle both.

The byte counters are the deliberate exception to the pointer rule and always emit including zero: a blocked connection transferred nothing, and that measured zero is the evidence the block took effect.

### Content exclusions, held down by a sentinel rather than a key check

`processArgs`/`processTree` are not emitted — a command line can carry a credential in an argument (#190) — and neither is the agentic block beyond `isAgentic` (`agenticSessionId`, `agentVirtualId`, `agentTypeId`/`Name`, `mcpPrimitiveName`, `mcpProtocolVersion`, `aiAgentDetails`, `aiAgentDetectionDetails`), which is null or empty on every one of the 3,000 observed rows. No GenAI prompt/content data is fetched or mapped, per this issue's non-goal.

The guard is a **sentinel injected into those fields**, asserting the value reaches no attribute and no body by any path. A key-absence check only proves the mapper skips the names it was told about; it would pass over a future generic passthrough. Sabotage confirmed it fires.

### Wirecheck: nothing watched, recorded as a decision

wirecheck guards values that key a metric label, where an unmapped member moves series membership. This collector emits no metrics, so nothing it reads can move a series. Observed sets are two values each (`trafficType` internet/microsoft365, `action` allow/block) and a watchdog built on them **would fire on the first legitimate `private` row from Private Access** — a correct row, which is the failure mode this project refuses to ship.

### Recorded gaps in the fixture

No populated `destinationUrl` (9 of 3,000 live rows have one — it needs TLS inspection to resolve) and no Private Access row: m7kni's private profile is enabled but carried no traffic in the sample. Both are noted as gaps rather than filled with invented rows.

Every guard was sabotage-verified — broken, and the test confirmed to fail — rather than verified by reading the diff. Five sabotages, five catches, one of which (`setInt` on the sibling #336 collector) exposed a genuinely unguarded path.

## Outcome

Operators should optionally track population changes for a small configured set of high-value groups without unbounded group labels.

## Evidence

**Evidence class:** `explicit residual from #43 (2026-07-25)`

- #43 deferred a config-driven allowlist for member-count gauges.
- The project now has central cardinality controls, but the allowlist remains required because entity labels are still prohibited.

## Proposed scope

- Add an explicit per-tenant group-ID allowlist with a strict configured maximum.
- Emit member counts only for those groups and preserve membership detail in logs where already available.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] No group outside the allowlist creates a series.
- [ ] The allowlist has a validated small maximum.
- [ ] Missing/inaccessible groups are distinguishable from zero members.
- [ ] Group display names are not metric labels unless the bounded contract explicitly chooses and gates them.

## Prior decisions and duplicate check

- This is the surviving narrow residual from #43, not a generic per-group metric proposal.
- Related: #43, #112, #235.

## Priority

Audit recommendation: **P3**.

comments.body:
## Closed by `2483dd4`

### The cardinality exception, and why it holds

`group_id` reaches a metric label here and nowhere else in the project. It is safe for exactly one reason: the label set is a per-tenant config allowlist, capped at **50** and validated at load, so cardinality is decided by a human editing YAML and cannot grow with tenant size at runtime. The allowlist IS the bound. 50 was chosen as the point where an operator can still read and vouch for the whole list in one sitting — generous over the built-in privileged roles plus break-glass groups, far short of where an allowlist stops being a reviewable control.

### Two gauges, because one cannot say "I could not look"

- `entra.privileged_groups.members.total{group_id}` — emitted **only** for a group read successfully this cycle. A `0` here is a measured empty group.
- `entra.privileged_groups.accessible{group_id}` — emitted for **every** configured group, **every** cycle, `1` or `0`.

A gauge value cannot express "unknown", so the second gauge carries that fact explicitly. Without it, a deleted or forbidden group would be silence on the first gauge, indistinguishable from an empty one — and for a privileged group those are opposite facts. The log twin carries the bounded reason a gauge cannot (`not_found` / `forbidden` / `error`) and Warns.

### Live-verified the wire, which upgraded a docs-only assumption

`live-measured (2026-07-27, #337)`, probed read-only as `graph2otel-poller`:

| probe | result |
| --- | --- |
| `/groups/{id}/members/$count`, `Accept: application/json` | **HTTP 415** |
| same, no `ConsistencyLevel` | HTTP 400 `Request_UnsupportedQuery` |
| same, `ConsistencyLevel: eventual` + `Accept: text/plain` | **200**, body is the bare integer `2` |
| `/transitiveMembers/$count`, same headers | 200, also `2` |
| nonexistent group | **404 `Request_ResourceNotFound`** — so the inaccessible classification is real, not assumed |

The shared `collectors.Count` helper already sends both headers and already records the 415 fact, so the implementation was correct on the wire; this measurement independently re-confirms it.

### One decision left open on purpose

It counts **direct** members. A member nested inside another group is not counted, so on a tenant that nests groups this is a floor rather than a total — which for a privileged group is arguably the wrong number, since nesting is a real escalation path. Both endpoints were live-verified to work identically, so switching is a one-line change, but it changes what the metric MEANS and is not mine to decide silently. Recorded here rather than made. The package doc says the same.

## Follow-up decision 2026-07-28 — switch to TRANSITIVE membership

The open question recorded in this issue's closing comment is answered: the maintainer chose **transitive** membership.

Reasoning, so it stays settled: for a *privileged* group the security-relevant number is everyone who effectively holds the privilege, however they got it. A direct count silently misses a member added via a nested group — and nested groups are a real privilege-escalation path. That is a false negative on a security signal, the same class of error as the fabricated zero this session fixed on #315.

**The change:** `/groups/{id}/members/$count` becomes `/groups/{id}/transitiveMembers/$count`. Both shapes were live-verified working with identical headers on 2026-07-27, so this is the one-line change described in the closing comment, plus the package doc and the collector-doc annotation updated to say the count is now a total rather than a floor.

Not yet executed — carried into the next work session with the rest of the decided-but-unshipped items.

Switched to transitive membership in `099ba59`, per the 2026-07-28 decision.

`/groups/{id}/transitiveMembers/$count` replaces `/members/$count`. Both were live-verified during this issue's original build to work identically — same `ConsistencyLevel: eventual` + `Accept: text/plain` headers, same response shape — so this is a change of endpoint, not of transport.

**The metric's meaning changes with it**, and both the package doc and `docs/collectors.md` now say so: the count is a TOTAL rather than a floor, and it spans every transitive member type (users, nested groups, service principals), not users only.

The reasoning, restated so it is not re-litigated: a direct count omits a principal nested inside another group, and for a *privileged* group that is not a rounding error — a nested member is a full member for every authorization decision Entra makes. The direct count therefore reads LOW exactly when someone has widened the blast radius by nesting. An over-count is a question an operator can investigate; an under-count is a missed escalation.

The test pins the wire path **literally**, not through `memberCountURL`. Every other test in the package builds its fake's keys from that helper and would have stayed green through this change.

## Outcome

Determine whether related-tenant signals reveal unmanaged partner, billing, or cross-tenant exposure without overstating approximate relationships.

## Evidence

**Evidence class:** `preview docs-only; irreversible external prerequisite (2026-07-25)`

- The beta Tenant Governance API exposes related tenants.
- Microsoft requires tenant discovery to be enabled and states that enablement cannot be reverted.

## Proposed scope

- Never implement or call the enable POST.
- Only probe after the maintainer independently enables discovery and approves the read scope.
- If viable, emit bounded relationship/signal counts and per-tenant logs.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The codebase contains no discovery-enable mutation.
- [ ] Disabled state has an explicit skip reason.
- [ ] A real payload precedes mapper work.
- [ ] Documentation states relationships are signals, not proof of ownership/control.

## Prior decisions and duplicate check

- No existing collector covers related-tenant discovery; it is distinct from cross-tenant access policy.

## Primary sources

- [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/tenantgovernanceservices-list-relatedtenants?view=graph-rest-beta](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/tenantgovernanceservices-list-relatedtenants?view=graph-rest-beta)
- [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-governance/tenant-governance/how-to-enable-tenant-discovery](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-governance/tenant-governance/how-to-enable-tenant-discovery)

## Priority

Audit recommendation: **P3**.

comments.body:
## Parked by maintainer decision 2026-07-28

Verbatim: *"park it (I will enable it just not today)."*

So this is parked with a **stated intent to unblock**, not an indefinite hold — the distinction matters for whoever reads this next.

The constraint is unchanged and is the whole reason this needs a human: Microsoft's related-tenant discovery **enable action is IRREVERSIBLE**. graph2otel must never call that POST under any circumstance, and no probe is meaningful until discovery is on.

**Unblock condition:** the maintainer enables related-tenant discovery himself and says so here. The read scope is then covered by the standing consent recorded on #376. Until both, nothing to do.

## Read scopes granted and the disabled state is now live-measured. One maintainer action remains.

`live-measured 2026-07-28` as `graph2otel-poller`.

### Scopes granted (read-only, standing consent)

| appRole | GUID | assignment id |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TenantGovernance-RelatedTenant.Read.All` | `<guid-17>` | `NhU3E1CZiEmQ9DQ1ZkVngSEatG60-CJLj5eZo66eAMw` |
| `TenantGovernance-Setting.Read.All` | `<guid-18>` | `NhU3E1CZiEmQ9DQ1ZkVngbFhh4d-WV1AlIVu1j_yKcs` |

Both read-only, both stay granted. **No enable action was called** — the constraint that this codebase never contains the discovery-enable mutation is intact, and nothing was mutated on the tenant.

### The path was not what the docs imply — the EDM found it

`/beta/tenantRelationships/tenantGovernance` → **400 `Resource not found for the segment 'tenantGovernance'`**. The `tenantRelationship` singleton carries only `multiTenantOrganization`, `managedTenants`, `delegatedAdminCustomers`, `delegatedAdminRelationships`.

Grepping `$metadata` for the type resolved it in one step: the `tenantGovernance` navigation property hangs off **`directory`**, not `tenantRelationships`. Correct paths:

- `/beta/directory/tenantGovernance/settings`
- `/beta/directory/tenantGovernance/relatedTenants`

Same lesson as #333 — the EDM is the cheap oracle and it beat guessing at documented paths.

### Acceptance criterion 2 is already satisfiable, and cheaply

`GET /beta/directory/tenantGovernance/settings` → **200**:

```json
{ "isRelatedTenantsEnabled": false, "canReceiveInvitations": false }
```

So the disabled state is **directly observable as data** rather than having to be inferred from an error. The collector reads `settings` first and skips with an explicit reason when `isRelatedTenantsEnabled` is false — it never needs to eat a 403 to find out. That is the right design and it falls straight out of the wire.

For completeness, the denial when disabled is also explicit and self-describing rather than generic:

```
HTTP 403 forbidden
"Tenant <id> Related tenant discovery has not been enabled for tenant <id>."
```

Notably this is a *different* 403 from a missing-scope 403 (`Insufficient permissions to perform this operation.`, seen on #334 the same day) — the message distinguishes "not enabled" from "not permitted", so the two are separable in code rather than collapsing into one bucket.

### What remains — maintainer action, and it is irreversible

`isRelatedTenantsEnabled` is `false`. Enabling related-tenant discovery is a tenant action **Microsoft states cannot be reverted**, which is why this issue forbids graph2otel from ever calling the enable POST and why it was parked in the first place.

Where: **Entra admin center → Identity Governance → Tenant Governance → enable tenant discovery** (`https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-governance/tenant-governance/how-to-enable-tenant-discovery`).

**Named unblock:** `GET /beta/directory/tenantGovernance/settings` returns `"isRelatedTenantsEnabled": true`, at which point `relatedTenants` returns a real payload.

Mapper work stays blocked until then, per acceptance criterion 3 — a real payload precedes the mapper, and the `relatedTenant` field set will not be characterised from documentation. The enum values in the EDM (`relationshipStatus`, `relationshipCreationType`, `permissionType`, `requestStatus`) are recorded but **one observed value is not a value set**, so nothing gets a `wirecheck` watch until real rows exist.

Also to carry into the mapper when it happens: the EDM declares `relatedTenant.isMicrosoftInfrastructure`, so some discovered relationships will be Microsoft's own infrastructure rather than partner or billing exposure. Documentation must state relationships are **signals, not proof of ownership or control** (acceptance criterion 4) — and that flag is the concrete case that makes the point.

## UNBLOCKED — tenant governance is enabled and returning real data (live-measured 2026-07-29)

The irreversible maintainer enable has been done. Probed as `graph2otel-poller` on the paths this issue established (`/beta/directory/tenantGovernance/...`, **not** the documented `/beta/tenantRelationships/...`):

### Acceptance criterion 2 → criterion 3

```
GET /beta/directory/tenantGovernance/settings   -> 200
{"isRelatedTenantsEnabled": true, "canReceiveInvitations": true}
```

Both flags were `false` when this was measured on 2026-07-28. The disabled-state read still works exactly as designed — the collector reads `settings` first, so a disabled tenant skips with an explicit reason instead of eating a 403.

```
GET /beta/directory/tenantGovernance/relatedTenants   -> 200, 16 rows, single page
```

### Wire shape (n=16, full census, no sampling)

| field | present | non-null | note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | 16 | 16 | the related tenant's tenant id |
| `createdDateTime` | 16 | 16 | 16 distinct values, all 2026-07-29T00:38:59Z — **discovery-record creation, not relationship age** |
| `isMicrosoftInfrastructure` | 16 | 16 | **13 false, 3 true** |
| `multiTenantApplicationMetrics` | 16 | 16 | the only metric populated tenant-wide |
| `b2BRegistrationMetrics` | 16 | **1** | |
| `b2BSignInActivityMetrics` | 16 | **1** | |
| `appB2BSignInActivityMetrics` | 16 | **1** | |
| `billingMetrics` | 16 | **0** | never populated on this tenant |

Each metric object is `{initial: {...}, recent: {...}}` — a first-observation snapshot and a current one, each carrying its own `createdDateTime`/`updateDateTime` plus a `watermarkDateTime`, and counters split inbound/outbound (`inboundMonthlyTotalUsers`, `outboundMonthlyTotalUsers`, `inboundMonthlyTotalApplications`, `outboundMonthlyTotalApplications`, and on `b2BRegistrationMetrics` an un-suffixed `inboundTotalUsers`).

### Three traps this collector has to handle, all visible in the census above

**Four of the five metric objects are null on almost every row, and null is not zero.** 15 of 16 rows have no B2B metrics at all and no row has billing metrics. A bare numeric field would publish a fabricated `0` reading as "no inbound B2B users from this tenant" when the truth is "Microsoft sent no measurement". Every metric leaf must be a **pointer** — the #334 lesson, and this surface is a worse offender than that one because the absence is the common case rather than the exception.

**`isMicrosoftInfrastructure` splits the population and must bucket the gauge.** 3 of 16 are Microsoft's own infrastructure tenants; a count that folds them in tells an operator they have 16 external tenant relationships when they have 13. This is the bounded, tenant-shaped axis — the tenant *ids* are per-entity and belong in the twin, never in a metric label.

**`createdDateTime` is the discovery record's own creation, not an event time.** All 16 are within one second of each other, at the moment discovery was enabled — so it dates the *feature being turned on*, not the relationship. It must not be used as a log record's event timestamp; per CLAUDE.md a snapshot twin leaves the timestamp at poll time. The genuinely time-bearing fields are the `watermarkDateTime`/`updateDateTime` inside each metric block.

### Scopes

Already granted and recorded on this issue 2026-07-28: `TenantGovernance-RelatedTenant.Read.All`, `TenantGovernance-Setting.Read.All`. Both used above; no new grant needed.

Building now: bounded gauges (discovery-enabled and invitations flags, related-tenant count by `is_microsoft_infrastructure`, and bounded aggregates of the metric blocks) plus one `entra.related_tenant` twin per row carrying the per-tenant detail. Beta-only, so `Experimental` per #183 and registered in `spec/graph-beta-surface.json`.

## Shipped and closed — `e627e02`

`entra.related_tenants` is live. Acceptance criterion 3 is satisfied against a real payload, not a docs shape: 16 discovered tenants, 13 external and 3 Microsoft infrastructure.

**Emitted.** Bounded gauges `entra.related_tenants.discovery_enabled`, `.can_receive_invitations`, `.total{is_microsoft_infrastructure}`, `.with_metrics{kind}`, and the cross-row sums `.b2b_registered_users{direction}` / `.b2b_signin_users{direction}` / `.multi_tenant_applications{direction}`. One `entra.related_tenant` twin per row. Beta manifest registered, dashboard panels placed on the Entra compliance board, `make check` exit 0, census 168 → 169 logical / 171 → 172 candidates.

### Four decisions worth reading before touching this collector

**The disabled path emits NO POINTS, not zeros.** `settings` is read first, so a tenant without discovery never has to eat a 403 — and on that path the count gauges are absent rather than zero, because "discovery is off" and "discovery ran and found nothing" are opposite facts. `discovery_enabled` carries which one it was. Sabotage-verified by routing the disabled path through the populated emitter; the test caught it.

**`with_metrics{kind}` exists to keep the pointer discipline legible.** Four of five metric blocks are null on almost every row, so a flat zero on the counters means *Microsoft supplied no measurement* — not *no B2B activity*. Without a coverage series that distinction is only visible as missing attributes on individual twins, which nobody reads that way. The dashboard section puts this panel above the counters for the same reason.

**One leaf struct decodes four blocks that do not share a field set**, and no live row exercises the dangerous case. `b2BRegistrationMetrics` carries lifetime `inboundTotalUsers`/`outboundTotalUsers`; the two sign-in blocks carry monthly user *and* application counters; `multiTenantApplicationMetrics` carries application counters only. Every block that is present on this tenant sends every counter it defines — so the block-level nil checks kept passing while a sabotaged `setInt` fabricated zeros, and the first sabotage pass found nothing. A constructed test for "present block, absent leaf" now covers it. **That gap is the #334 shape** (a field declared and simply not sent) and it is the failure mode this surface is most exposed to, because Microsoft populates these blocks incrementally.

**`createdDateTime` is not an event time.** All 16 rows carry one within a second of each other, because it dates the moment discovery was *enabled*, not the relationship. The twins are state twins at poll time; backdating would date every relationship to that instant and re-stamp them all on a re-enable. The genuinely time-bearing fields are each block's `watermarkDateTime`/`updateDateTime`, which are emitted as attributes.

### Two things deliberately not built

**`billingMetrics` leaves are unmodeled.** Null on all 16 rows, so there is no observed shape to map and this project does not write mappers from documentation (#142/#165). The twin carries `has_billing_metrics` so the day one appears is visible. Note the trap: a JSON `null` decodes into a **non-nil** `json.RawMessage` holding the four bytes `"null"`, so a bare nil check reports every live row as carrying billing metrics.

**Only the `recent` snapshot's counters are emitted**, plus the earliest `initial.createdDateTime` as `metrics_first_observed_date_time`. Emitting both sides would double the attribute count for a growth delta nobody has asked for yet; the first-observed timestamp is the part of `initial` that carries information the row does not otherwise have.

### Fixture

Related-tenant GUIDs are substituted with realistic values — they identify real partner organizations. Every other byte, including the null blocks that are most of the payload, is verbatim.

### Note for the operator

It is `Experimental` (both paths are beta-only per #183), so it registers only when explicitly enabled. **It is not enabled on camden.** Enabling it is a one-line config change and a maintainer decision, not a code change.

body:
## Outcome

Evaluate whether Microsoft's Tenant Configuration Management API can report configuration drift across Entra, Defender, Exchange, Intune, Purview, and Teams.

## Evidence

**Evidence class:** `current v1 documentation; new cross-workload prerequisite (2026-07-25)`

- The GA TCM API exposes monitors, drifts, results, and snapshots across workloads.
- It requires service setup and permissions not present in graph2otel.
- This may expose cross-workload posture that previously had no direct entity API.

## Proposed scope

- Document the service-principal/configuration prerequisite and least read-only scope.
- After approval, probe monitors/drifts/results/snapshots as the poller.
- Compare its signals with current collectors before proposing an engine or mapper.

## Constraints and non-goals

- No configuration application, remediation, or tenant mutation.
- Do not treat TCM as a replacement for source-exact collectors without measured equivalence.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A live feasibility/overlap matrix covers each supported workload.
- [ ] Polling, paging, retention, and drift identifiers are measured.
- [ ] A build/no-build verdict names the architecture seam.
- [ ] Any new registration path extends collectordoc in the same commit.

## Prior decisions and duplicate check

- No existing issue covers the GA TCM surface; this is not Graph Data Connect or Power Platform admin.

## Primary sources

- [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/unified-tenant-configuration-management-api-overview?view=graph-rest-1.0](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/unified-tenant-configuration-management-api-overview?view=graph-rest-1.0)

## Priority

Audit recommendation: **P1**.

comments.body:
## Parked by maintainer decision 2026-07-28

Parked together with #334, for the same reason and on the same terms: the cross-workload service-principal and configuration prerequisite for Tenant Configuration Management drift monitoring is **unidentified**, and sits outside the scopes currently held. It cannot be probed until someone establishes what it needs.

**Unblock condition / first step when resumed:** cheap read-only reconnaissance to establish the real prerequisite and whether the capability exists on this tenant, reported here before any build.

As on #334: this issue looks actionable in the epic list and is not. The unknown prerequisite is the blocker, and discovering it is a task in its own right.

## Reconnaissance complete — the prerequisite is now IDENTIFIED, and it is bigger than a scope grant

`live-measured 2026-07-28`. This issue was parked because nobody knew what it needed. That is now answered, and it moves from "parked-unknown" to a concrete go/no-go for the maintainer.

### The API is real and reachable in principle

`configurationManagement` types are present in **both** v1.0 and beta `$metadata`: `configurationMonitor`, `configurationDrift`, `configurationMonitoringResult`, `configurationSnapshotJob`, `configurationBaseline`. Path: `admin` → `configurationManagement` → the five collections. No version skew.

Every collection returns **403** with a JSON error (`UnknownError`, empty message) on both v1.0 and beta — Graph's authorization layer, not an edge, not licensing.

### The prerequisite is a two-part tenant setup, and part of it is a WRITE grant to a Microsoft-owned identity

**Part 1 — a first-party service principal that does not exist here.** Microsoft's overview page, verbatim: *"The tenant configuration APIs need admins to first add TCM service principal to their tenant and then grant permissions to it. This is a pre-requisite step."*

The SP is Microsoft's own app, fixed appId `<guid-3>`. Live-checked: `GET /v1.0/servicePrincipals?$filter=appId eq '03b07b79-...'` → **200 `{"value": []}`**. It is not provisioned. (Control: the companion `6b91db1b-...` M365 Admin Services SP **is** present, so the filter works.)

**Part 2 — that SP must then be granted app roles against every workload it monitors**, including write-shaped ones (`User.ReadWrite.All`, `Policy.Read.All`, an EXO application access policy), because a monitor impersonates calls into each workload when it runs.

**Part 3 — separately**, `graph2otel-poller` would need `ConfigurationMonitoring.Read.All` for the read path. Confirmed absent from the roles claim. That part alone is trivially within the standing read-only consent; the other two are not.

### Why I stopped rather than proceeding

Part 1 creates a new Microsoft-owned service principal in the tenant. Part 2 grants it **write** scopes over user and policy objects, to an identity graph2otel does not control after the grant. Both are live-tenant mutations well outside the read-only standing consent, and Part 2 is the kind of blast radius that comes back to the maintainer every time.

### What it would actually buy — the overlap matrix

TCM reports **drift from a declared baseline**, which is a different axis from graph2otel's source-exact entity state. It would not replace a single existing collector.

| workload | graph2otel today | verdict |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Entra | source-exact policy/config collectors | complementary — "did it change from what we declared" vs "what is it now" |
| Intune | source-exact device/config/policy | complementary |
| Defender | XDR hunting + blob signals | complementary |
| Purview | label / eDiscovery collectors | complementary |
| **Exchange** | transport-rule config **not** collected | **new coverage** |
| **Teams** | **not** collected | **new coverage** |

So the honest value is two workloads of genuinely new coverage, plus a drift axis that duplicates nothing.

### Costs that would land on the tenant, not just on graph2otel

Documented tenant-wide limits (`docs-only`): 30 monitors per tenant, fixed 6h monitor interval, 800 resources/day across all monitors, 20,000 resources/month snapshot quota, 12 visible snapshot jobs, 7-day snapshot retention, 30-day drift retention. These are **shared with any human admin using TCM in the same tenant** — graph2otel would occupy part of a finite tenant budget, which no other collector in this project does.

The SP-provisioning step is also framed by Microsoft as a public-preview onboarding requirement, implying it gets simpler at GA.

### Decision needed — three options

1. **Close no-build.** The prerequisite is a write-scoped grant to a Microsoft identity plus consumption of a shared tenant quota, for two workloads of new coverage. Reconnaissance done, blocker fully named. **This is my recommendation** — the cost is tenant-shaped and permanent, the benefit is an axis nothing currently depends on.
2. **Provision and build.** Maintainer creates the SP, grants it its workload scopes, and `ConfigurationMonitoring.Read.All` goes to the poller. Then re-probe and design.
3. **Keep parked with the prerequisite now recorded**, and revisit at TCM GA when the SP-provisioning step may no longer be required.

No tenant mutation was made. No SP was created. No scope was granted for this issue.

## Closed won't-do — maintainer decision 2026-07-29

Verbatim: *"TCM we can close as wont'do."*

This closes on the recommendation already recorded here. Restating the cost that decided it, so nobody re-opens it on coverage grounds:

- Microsoft's first-party TCM service principal (appId `<guid-3>`) is **not provisioned** on this tenant — live-verified `{"value": []}` against a control lookup that does return its companion SP.
- Provisioning it is not the cost. The cost is that it then needs **write** app roles (`User.ReadWrite.All`, `Policy.Read.All`, an EXO application access policy) so its monitors can impersonate into each workload. That is a permanent write grant to a Microsoft-owned identity, well outside the read-only standing consent, and it is not something a read-only telemetry exporter should be the reason for.
- It also consumes a share of a finite tenant-wide quota (30 monitors, 800 resources/day) shared with any human admin doing the same thing by hand.

What is being given up, stated honestly rather than minimised: **two workloads of genuinely new coverage** (Exchange transport config, Teams) plus a config-drift axis that duplicates nothing graph2otel ships. That is a real gap and it stays a gap.

**Re-open condition, if it ever changes:** Microsoft ships TCM in a shape that does not require write app roles on a first-party SP to read drift — e.g. a read-only Graph surface the poller can query directly. The discovery is complete and recorded above; a future reader does not need to redo it.

No scope was granted, nothing was provisioned, and no tenant state was changed for this issue.

body:
## Outcome

Determine whether directory backup policy, snapshot freshness, and failed recovery jobs can be exported as security posture.

## Evidence

**Evidence class:** `current beta documentation; new permission/service prerequisite (2026-07-25)`

- The Entra Backup and Recovery beta API now exposes backup/recovery configuration, snapshots, and jobs.
- No existing collector covers directory recoverability.

## Proposed scope

- Identify the least read-only application permission and service prerequisite, then request approval before a probe.
- Measure snapshot retention/freshness and job state as the poller.
- Build Experimental bounded posture plus per-snapshot/job logs if available.

## Constraints and non-goals

- No backup, restore, or recovery job creation.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Exact permission, licence, and prerequisite are recorded from a live read.
- [ ] Automatic snapshot cadence and retention are measured, not inferred.
- [ ] Restore-capable endpoints never appear in runtime code.
- [ ] The spike closes no-data with a named service-enabled unblock if needed.

## Prior decisions and duplicate check

- No existing issue covers Entra recovery services.

## Primary sources

- [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/entrarecoveryservices-backup-recovery-overview?view=graph-rest-beta](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/entrarecoveryservices-backup-recovery-overview?view=graph-rest-beta)

## Priority

Audit recommendation: **P1**.

comments.body:
## Parked by maintainer decision 2026-07-28

Parked together with #335. Both have a prerequisite **nobody has identified yet** — neither the exact permission nor whether the underlying service is provisioned on this tenant is known, so neither can even be probed without discovery work first.

The maintainer chose not to spend that discovery effort now.

**Unblock condition / first step when resumed:** cheap read-only reconnaissance to establish (a) what permission the surface actually requires and (b) whether the service exists on this tenant. That reconnaissance is the work — it converts this from an unknown into either a real plan or a clean no-build. Do not skip it and write a mapper from documentation.

Flagged deliberately: an issue with an unidentified prerequisite **looks actionable in an epic list when it is not**. That is why this note exists rather than leaving it silently open.

## Reconnaissance complete — this is a BUILD, not a no-data close. Scope granted, live data present.

`live-measured 2026-07-28` as `graph2otel-poller`. The parked reason ("prerequisite never identified") is resolved: the prerequisite was a single read-only app role, and with it the surface returns real data.

### Scope granted

**`EntraBackup.Read.All`** — appRole `<guid-19>` ("Read Preview jobs and snapshots"), assignment id `NhU3E1CZiEmQ9DQ1ZkVngYO1lCVMYqFLkfqMDHgqX3Y`, granted to `graph2otel-poller` 2026-07-28 under the standing read-only consent extension. Read-only; it stays granted.

Before the grant, both collections returned a JSON `403 Forbidden` / `Insufficient permissions to perform this operation.` — Graph's own authorization layer, not an edge and not licensing. That is the shape a genuinely missing app role produces, and it is worth contrasting with #369's empty-message `401 UnknownError`, closed the same day, where no grant would have helped.

### The path

`/directory/recovery` → `snapshots` and `jobs`. Reached from the `directory` entity, same as `administrativeUnits`.

### Four measured facts that change the issue's premise

**1. This is NOT beta-only. The `beta-api` label is wrong and it must NOT be `Experimental`.**

`GET /v1.0/directory/recovery/snapshots` returns **200 with identical data** to beta. The `entraRecoveryServices` schema block is byte-identical in both `$metadata` documents. Per #183, `Experimental` is reserved for genuine Graph *beta* surfaces — this is GA, so the collector ships on v1.0 with no opt-in gate.

**2. Retention is 7 days, live-measured — and the docs contradict themselves on this.**

The Graph API overview page says **5 days**; the Entra admin-center page says **7**. The wire says 7:

- 7 snapshots, no `nextLink`.
- Newest `2026-07-27T22:00:00Z`, oldest `2026-07-21T22:00:00Z`.
- Exactly daily at `22:00:00Z`, no drift across all 7.

Another wire-over-docs entry. The cadence is *measured*, not inferred, which is acceptance criterion 2.

**3. `totalChangedObjects` is declared in the EDM and NEVER returned on the wire.**

`snapshot` declares `createdDateTime`, `totalChangedObjects`, and nav properties `recoveryJobs`/`recoveryPreviewJobs`. The live response carries **only `id` and `createdDateTime`** — and it is still absent when explicitly `$select`ed by name, and still absent under `$expand=recoveryJobs`.

This is the absent-field trap head-on: a bare `int32` in the Go struct would publish a fabricated `0` for "objects changed since the last snapshot", which reads as a healthy quiet directory. **It must be a pointer, and an absent value must emit no series** — the same correction #315 made for `impactedResources` earlier in this epic.

**4. A snapshot id is not addressable, and it decodes to a timestamp.**

`GET /directory/recovery/snapshots/{id}` returns **404 `Snapshot with identifier ... not found`** for an id the list call returned one second earlier — with the `==` both raw and percent-encoded. So the collection is the only route; do not design a per-snapshot fetch.

The id is base64 of a unix epoch: `MTc4NTE4OTYwMA==` → `1785189600` → `2026-07-27T22:00:00Z`, matching its own `createdDateTime`. Derivable, not opaque — so it is a stable dedupe key, but it carries no information the record does not already have.

### Current state of the two collections

- **`snapshots`**: 7 rows (above).
- **`jobs`**: **200 with `value: []`** on both v1.0 and beta. Empty is the healthy steady state — a recovery job only exists after someone runs a restore. This is a "green tick is not evidence of data" collector: the mapper for job status has no live sample and must be written from the EDM enum plus the first real row, not invented richly now.

Job shape from the EDM (`recoveryJobBase`): `status` (`initialized`/`running`/`successful`/`failed`/`abandoned`/`calculating`/`loadingData`/`unknownFutureValue`), `jobStartDateTime`, `jobCompletionDateTime`, `targetStateDateTime`, `totalChangedObjectsCalculated`, `totalChangedLinksCalculated`; `recoveryJob` adds `totalObjectsModified`, `totalLinksModified`, `totalFailedChanges`.

### Restore-capable surface — named here so it is never called

The EDM binds a `cancel` **action** and `getChanges` / `getFailedChanges` functions to the job types, and `recoveryAction` includes `softDelete`/`update`/`restore`. **None of these may appear in runtime code** (acceptance criterion 3). The collector calls exactly two GETs: the two collections above.

### Build plan

- `entra.directory_recovery`, GA (not `Experimental`), on the existing snapshot-collector path.
- Bounded gauges: snapshot count, age of the newest snapshot in seconds (the actual posture signal — a stale newest snapshot is the finding), job counts bucketed by `status`.
- Log twins: one per snapshot, one per job. `totalChangedObjects` omitted when absent, never zeroed.
- `wirecheck`: watch `recoveryStatus`, derived from the map the collector keys on rather than restated.

## Closed by `a467c3e` — `entra.directory_recovery` shipped

Built from this issue's own live measurement; nothing was re-probed and nothing was written from documentation.

### Acceptance criteria

- [x] **Exact permission, licence and prerequisite recorded from a live read** — `EntraBackup.Read.All` (appRole `<guid-19>`, assignment `NhU3E1CZiEmQ9DQ1ZkVngYO1lCVMYqFLkfqMDHgqX3Y`). It is the whole prerequisite: with it granted, both collections return 200 immediately. No licence gate, no service-enable step, no registered-application category. That is the opposite of #369, closed the same day.
- [x] **Automatic snapshot cadence and retention measured, not inferred** — 7 snapshots, daily at 22:00:00Z with no drift, spanning 7 days. Retention is 7 days, against a Graph doc page saying 5 and an admin-center page saying 7.
- [x] **Restore-capable endpoints never appear in runtime code** — pinned by `TestCollectorNeverConstructsARestoreCapableURL`, which asserts on the recorded request log rather than on a reading of the source. Exactly two URLs may be requested.
- [x] **Closes no-data with a named unblock if needed** — not needed; there was data.

### What shipped

Four bounded gauges and two log twins. The design decisions worth keeping:

**Age is the signal, the count is not.** Retention holds the count flat at 7 on any healthy tenant, so it says nothing on a dashboard. `newest_snapshot_age` is what climbs when the backup service quietly stops. It is **omitted entirely** when no snapshot carries a parseable timestamp — a 0-second age would claim a snapshot had just been taken on a tenant that has none, which is the most dangerous reading this collector could produce.

**The jobs gauge is split in two** because the collection is empty in the healthy steady state. Without an always-emitted total, "no restore has ever run" and "the collector is disabled" would be the same absent series. Same reasoning as #337's two gauges and #356's.

**Every numeric on both resources is a pointer.** `totalChangedObjects` is the case that forced it, but the same trap sits on `totalFailedChanges`, where a fabricated 0 asserts a clean restore that Graph never reported.

**Both twins are state-stamped, not backdated.** The oldest retained snapshot sits exactly at the 7-day retention edge, which is also the backend's accept horizon — backdating would push it against that boundary every single cycle.

### Wirecheck, and a deliberate departure worth flagging

Job `status` **is** watched, derived from the bucket map the collector keys on. The watched members come from the EDM's `recoveryStatus` enum rather than from observed rows, because the jobs collection is empty — **zero observed values**.

This project normally refuses to watch on a single observed value, on the grounds that one value is not a value set. Watching a *declared Microsoft enum* is a different and stronger basis than watching an inference from one sample, so this is a considered departure rather than an oversight. Nothing on the snapshot resource is watched: it carries no enum at all.

### Verification

`make check` exit 0. Census 167 → **168** logical collectors, 170 → **171** registration-path candidates. Dashboards at 400/400 metric coverage; alert rules regenerated for the panel-id cascade and re-pushed (`matched_content_ungrouped`, the healthy end state).

Three guards were verified by **sabotage**, each broken and confirmed to fail before being restored:

| sabotage | guard that caught it |
| --- | --- |
| `totalChangedObjects` renders `nil` as a real 0 | `TestAbsentTotalChangedObjectsEmitsNoKey`, `TestLiveCaptureEmitsOneTwinPerSnapshot` |
| newest-age reads element 0 instead of scanning | `TestNewestAgeScansEveryRowNotJustTheFirst` |
| an empty collection emits a 0-second age | `TestNoSnapshotsEmitsNoAgeSeries`, `TestUnparseableCreatedDateTimeEmitsNoAgeSeries` |

The absence guards deliberately assert on the **mapper's own `telemetry.Attrs`**, not on the recorder's rendered `map[string]string`. This repo has twice shipped a guard that asserted one layer above the bug (#322's rendered-array join, #354's `SetStrs` empty filter), and "this numeric key is absent" is exactly that class of claim.

body:
## Outcome

Determine whether user/admin threat-submission workflow status and verdicts add a distinct SIEM signal.

## Evidence

**Evidence class:** `docs-only; new permission required (2026-07-25)`

- The beta email-threat submissions surface is separate from delivery events, quarantine state, and unified audit history.
- It requires new `ThreatSubmission.Read.All` consent.

## Proposed scope

- After explicit grant approval, establish data, timestamp/filter/paging semantics, and dedupe boundaries.
- Compare rows against Defender email, quarantine, and audit signals.

## Spike result — **no-data**, with one adjacent surface worth its own issue.

### The grant (recorded per the standing consent)

`ThreatSubmission.Read.All` — appRole `<guid-20>`, granted 2026-07-28T10:53Z as an `appRoleAssignment` on the `graph2otel-poller` SP (`13371536-9950-4988-90f4-343566456781`). Assignment id `NhU3E1CZiEmQ9DQ1ZkVngQiSG76nggBDou0dxIQW9XM`. Read-only, application-type. Verified present in a freshly minted poller token before probing.

### The measurement — as `graph2otel-poller`

| request | result |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /beta/security/threatSubmission/emailThreats` | **200, 0 rows** |
| `GET /beta/security/threatSubmission/urlThreats` | **200, 0 rows** |
| `GET /beta/security/threatSubmission/fileThreats` | **200, 0 rows** |
| `GET /v1.0/security/threatSubmission/emailThreats` | **400** `Resource not found for the segment 'threatSubmission'` |
| `GET /beta/security/threatSubmission/emailThreatSubmissionPolicies` | **200, 1 row** |

Two facts to carry beyond this issue.

**The surface is beta-only, confirmed rather than assumed.** The v1.0 segment does not exist — a 400 on the path segment itself, not a 404 on a resource. So any future build here is `Experimental` under #183's definition (a genuine Graph beta surface), which is the correct use of that flag rather than the "expensive" misuse #254 warns against.

**Nobody on this tenant has reported an email.** Three submission collections, all 200, all empty. The scope works; there is simply no submission history.

**No build.** Every question this issue asks — event time, immutable id, paging semantics, dedupe boundaries, and the overlap analysis against Defender email/quarantine/audit signals — is a property of real rows. Without the overlap analysis in particular there is no evidence the source adds a *distinct* signal, which was the whole question.

```json
{"id":"DefaultReportSubmissionPolicy","isReportToMicrosoftEnabled":true,

Thirteen boolean switches governing whether users can report phishing at all and where those reports go — bounded, tenant-shaped, exactly the 0/1 posture-gauge shape `entra.tenant_policy` already uses, and readable **today** under the scope just granted. It is a different question from this issue's (are reports flowing?) so it is not folded in here, but it is the one genuinely buildable thing this probe found and it does not wait on the unblock above.

Determine whether phishing simulation campaign, action, and training outcomes are available and useful as bounded posture plus per-user logs.

## Evidence

**Evidence class:** `prior probe inconclusive; new permission required (2026-07-25)`

- #251's 200/empty probe lacked `AttackSimulation.Read.All`, so it did not establish a genuine no-data condition.
- The v1 APIs support simulation and user result listing for appropriately licensed tenants.

## Proposed scope

- Request explicit approval for `AttackSimulation.Read.All`.
- Acquire a fresh token, validate simulation/user-result shapes and volume, then build or record a real blocker.
- Treat per-user results as log detail and consider HighVolume from measurement.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The prior inconclusive premise is corrected in the issue record.
- [ ] A licensed/non-licensed or populated/empty result is measured as the poller.
- [ ] No campaign action or training mutation is implemented.
- [ ] Any build preserves one log per user outcome.

## Prior decisions and duplicate check

- Not duplicate of #251: this retries only after naming the missing scope that made its probe inconclusive.
- Related: #251.

## Primary sources

- [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/attacksimulationroot-list-simulations?view=graph-rest-1.0](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/attacksimulationroot-list-simulations?view=graph-rest-1.0)
- [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/usersimulationdetails-list?view=graph-rest-1.0](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/usersimulationdetails-list?view=graph-rest-1.0)

comments.body:
## Spike result — **no-data**, and #251's inconclusive premise is now corrected.

### The grant (recorded per the standing consent)

`AttackSimulation.Read.All` — appRole `<guid-21>`, granted 2026-07-28T10:53Z as an `appRoleAssignment` on the `graph2otel-poller` SP (`13371536-9950-4988-90f4-343566456781`). Assignment id `NhU3E1CZiEmQ9DQ1ZkVngfVeTnw5L_1AkSmCEZVnZHk`. Read-only, application-type. Confirmed present in a freshly minted poller token before probing — the whole point of this issue was that the previous probe ran without it.

### Correcting the prior record

**#251's 200/empty result did not establish a no-data condition, and this issue was right to say so.** That probe ran without `AttackSimulation.Read.All`, so its empty response proved nothing either way. That premise is now spent: the scope is granted, verified in the token, and the result is measured again below.

### The measurement — as `graph2otel-poller`, all v1.0, all 200

| request | rows |
| --- | --- |
| `/security/attackSimulation/simulations` | **0** |
| `/security/attackSimulation/simulationAutomations` | **0** |
| `/security/attackSimulation/trainings` | **50, with `@odata.nextLink`** |

**The trainings collection is a decoy and must not be read as data.** Every row carries `"source": "global"` — it is Microsoft's own built-in training catalog, identical on every licensed tenant, not a record of anyone completing anything. Sample row: `{"displayName": "Business Email Compromise", "type": "unknown", "source": "global", "durationInMinutes": 7, "availabilityStatus": "available"}`. A collector counting trainings would emit an impressive non-zero number that says nothing about this tenant, and would keep saying it forever. Training *completion* is a per-user result attached to a simulation — and there are no simulations.

Also worth carrying: those catalog rows have `"createdDateTime": "0001-01-01T00:00:00Z"`, the **.NET `DateTime.MinValue` sentinel**. It parses cleanly as a date, so it would sail into `internal/telemetry` as a real event time and publish a record dated year 1. Same sentinel found on the eDiscovery case surface (#323) the same day. Any future build here must recognize and drop it rather than stamp it.

### Verdict

**No build.** This issue's outcome is simulation campaign, action and training *outcomes*. Zero simulations means zero campaigns, zero user actions and zero completion results — nothing to bucket into bounded posture and nothing to write a per-user log twin against. The `HighVolume` question the issue raises cannot be answered either: volume scales with users-per-simulation, and there is no simulation to measure one.

The scope stays granted — read-only, no cost, and the re-probe on unblock is one request.

**Named unblock:** one attack simulation has been run to completion on the tenant. `/simulations` then returns rows, per-user results become reachable, and the volume measurement `HighVolume` would need becomes possible. Until then this is a genuine measured no-data condition rather than an inconclusive one — which is the difference between this close and #251's.

### Acceptance criteria

- [x] The prior inconclusive premise is corrected in the issue record — above.
- [x] A licensed/non-licensed or populated/empty result is measured as the poller — 200/empty on simulations, with the scope verified in the token.
- [x] No campaign action or training mutation is implemented — three GETs, nothing else.
- [ ] Any build preserves one log per user outcome — no build; the constraint carries to the unblocked one.

**Evidence class:** `live-measured 2026-07-28, #331`.

Determine whether stuck or failed event-driven retention propagation can be observed at a scalable cadence.

## Evidence

**Evidence class:** `docs-only; existing scope (2026-07-25)`

- The retention-events list surface is not collected.
- Official query support is limited and permits potentially large populations.
- Existing `RecordsManagement.Read.All` is sufficient to probe.

## Proposed scope

- Measure count, paging, timestamps, result/status fields, and incremental options as the poller.
- Build bounded status metrics and per-event failure logs only if a scalable shape exists.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Live volume and page behavior are recorded.
- [ ] The spike closes no-build unless a bounded incremental strategy is proven.
- [ ] Event identities/details remain log-only.
- [ ] No retention trigger mutation is introduced.

## Prior decisions and duplicate check

- No existing issue covers retention-event propagation; label/policy inventory is different.
- Related: #101, #111, #237.

## Primary sources

- [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/security-retentionevent-list?view=graph-rest-1.0](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/security-retentionevent-list?view=graph-rest-1.0)

## Priority

Audit recommendation: **P2**.

comments.body:
## Spike result — closing **no-build**. The surface is unreadable by the poller, and it is not a Graph scope gap.

Probed live 2026-07-28 as `graph2otel-poller`. Every call below was read-only.

### The collection cannot be read at all

| request | result |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /v1.0/security/triggers/retentionEvents` | **500** `UnknownError` wrapping `{"ErrorCode":"DataInsightsRequestError","Message":"DataInsights command(GET) FAILED - Forbidden. TargetServer = <exchange-server-1>"}` |
| `GET /beta/security/triggers/retentionEvents` | **500**, identical `DataInsightsRequestError ... Forbidden` |
| `GET /v1.0/security/triggerTypes/retentionEventTypes` | **500**, identical |

The spike's acceptance criterion is *"closes no-build unless a bounded incremental strategy is proven"*. Volume, paging, timestamps and incremental options are all unmeasurable when the list call never returns a page. Nothing to bound, so: **no build**.

### It is NOT a missing Graph scope, and that is the part worth carrying

`RecordsManagement.Read.All` **is** in the poller's token — confirmed by decoding the `roles` claim, 52 roles, it is there. So the usual next move (grant a scope and retry) is already spent.

The failure is also **partial across sibling routes under that same scope**, which is what rules out "the scope is not really effective":

| route | result |
| --- | --- |
| `/v1.0/security/labels/authorities` | **200**, 3 rows |
| `/v1.0/security/labels/categories` | **200**, 13 rows |
| `/v1.0/security/labels/retentionLabels` | **500** `DataInsightsRequestError ... Forbidden` |
| `/v1.0/security/labels/departments` | **500** `DataInsightsRequestError ... Forbidden` |

Same scope, same tenant, same token, same minute — two routes serve and two refuse. The refusal is raised by the **Exchange DataInsights backend the Purview routes proxy to**, named in the error body, not by Graph's own authorization layer. Graph reports it as a 500 rather than a 403, so it does not look like an authorization failure and will be misread as a transient server error by anyone who sees it once.

**Do not re-attempt this by granting a broader Graph scope.** Same shape as #352's Intune result: the denial is not on the axis the obvious fix moves.

### Unblock condition, if this is ever reopened

A probe establishing what authorization the Purview/DataInsights backend actually wants for the retention-event and retention-label routes — most likely a Purview-side role assignment rather than a Graph application permission, in the same family as the Exchange directory-role requirement recorded on #363. Reopen only with that evidence in hand; re-running the three requests above will just reproduce this table.

### Also measured, and free

`/v1.0/security/labels/authorities` (3) and `/categories` (13) **are** readable under the scope already held and are not collected today. Bounded, tenant-shaped, cheap. Not in this spike's scope, so not built here — worth its own issue if file-plan reference data is wanted.

**Evidence class:** `live-measured 2026-07-28, #330`.

## Outcome

Assess group-level privileged active/eligible membership without an unbounded two-calls-per-group crawl.

## Evidence

**Evidence class:** `docs-only; new permissions and bounded-discovery problem (2026-07-25)`

- Directory-role PIM feeds do not include PIM for Groups.
- Assignment/eligibility endpoints require a group or principal filter.

## Proposed scope

- Request approval for the two narrow privileged-group schedule read scopes.
- Find and measure a bounded discovery route before proposing a collector.
- If viable, emit assignment-type counts and per-assignment logs.

## Constraints and non-goals

- Enumerating every group and issuing two calls each is a no-go.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The spike produces a bounded discovery design or closes no-build.
- [ ] Any grant is explicitly approved and read-only.
- [ ] Group/principal identities stay log-only.
- [ ] P2/ID Governance availability is recorded from the live tenant.

## Prior decisions and duplicate check

- Not duplicate of #66/#242: those cover directory-role PIM, not privileged group schedules.
- Related: #66, #242.

## Primary sources

- [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/privilegedaccessgroup-list-assignmentscheduleinstances?view=graph-rest-1.0](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/privilegedaccessgroup-list-assignmentscheduleinstances?view=graph-rest-1.0)
- [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/privilegedaccessgroup-list-eligibilityscheduleinstances?view=graph-rest-1.0](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/privilegedaccessgroup-list-eligibilityscheduleinstances?view=graph-rest-1.0)

## Priority

Audit recommendation: **P2**.

comments.body:
## Spike result — **no-build.** The unbounded-crawl problem is confirmed real, and no bounded discovery route was proven.

### The grants (recorded per the standing consent)

Both narrow schedule scopes, granted 2026-07-28T10:53Z as `appRoleAssignment`s on the `graph2otel-poller` SP (`13371536-9950-4988-90f4-343566456781`), read-only, application-type:

| scope | appRole id | assignment id |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `PrivilegedAssignmentSchedule.Read.AzureADGroup` | `<guid-22>` | `NhU3E1CZiEmQ9DQ1ZkVngQSFue-NAxBLsKn9vQHN-3I` |
| `PrivilegedEligibilitySchedule.Read.AzureADGroup` | `<guid-23>` | `NhU3E1CZiEmQ9DQ1ZkVngRXZo6SYL19IiyM72R8jQdA` |

Both confirmed in a freshly minted poller token before probing.

### The filter requirement is real — measured, not read

An unfiltered list is refused on every one of the three schedule surfaces:

| request | result |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /v1.0/identityGovernance/privilegedAccess/group/assignmentScheduleInstances` | **400** `The required parameters GroupId or PrincipalId is missing.` |
| `.../eligibilityScheduleInstances` | **400**, same message |
| `.../eligibilitySchedules` | **400**, same message |

So the issue's central premise holds and is now live-measured rather than docs-only: there is no way to ask "what PIM-for-Groups assignments exist on this tenant". Every read must name a group or a principal up front, which is what makes discovery, not authorization, the hard part.

### The one candidate bound was tested and does not close the question

PIM for Groups is most often described as governing role-assignable groups, which would give a bounded discovery set — role-assignable groups are capped by tenant governance, not tenant population, and they are filterable in one request.

`GET /v1.0/groups?$filter=isAssignableToRole eq true&$count=true` (with `ConsistencyLevel: eventual`) → **200, `@odata.count: 0`**.

Zero role-assignable groups on this tenant, so the candidate route is untestable here. **And it would not be sufficient even if it had returned rows:** PIM for Groups also covers ordinary security and Microsoft 365 groups, so `isAssignableToRole eq true` is a strict subset of the governed population. A collector built on that filter would look correct and silently miss every PIM-governed non-role-assignable group — an under-count on a privileged-access signal, which is the failure direction that matters. The same reasoning closed #337 in favor of transitive membership: an over-count is a question, an under-count is a missed escalation.

The other candidate, filtering by `principalId` over a set of privileged principals, has the same defect in a different place — it needs a bounded list of principals, which is the same discovery problem moved one step.

### Verdict

**No build.** The acceptance criterion is *"The spike produces a bounded discovery design or closes no-build."* No bounded design survives scrutiny: the only filterable candidate is provably incomplete, and enumerating every group with two calls each is the explicit non-goal in this issue's own constraints.

Both scopes stay granted — read-only, no cost, and they make the re-probe a single request if a bounded route ever appears.

**Named unblock, two conditions, either one:** (a) Microsoft ships a tenant-wide list route or a discovery filter for PIM-for-Groups schedules, making bounded enumeration possible; or (b) the operator names a small allowlist of groups to watch — the shape `entra.privileged_groups` already uses, where cardinality is decided by a human editing YAML and can never grow with tenant size at runtime. **(b) is the more likely route and it is a design this repo has already validated**, but it is a different issue from "find a bounded discovery route", so it is not smuggled in here.

### Acceptance criteria

- [x] The spike produces a bounded discovery design or closes no-build — closes no-build, with the candidate design tested and rejected on completeness rather than untested.
- [x] Any grant is explicitly approved and read-only — both, recorded above.
- [x] Group/principal identities stay log-only — no implementation; constraint carries forward.
- [x] P2/ID Governance availability is recorded from the live tenant — the schedule endpoints answer 400 (a query-shape error) rather than 403, so the feature is provisioned and reachable; there is nothing to enumerate.

**Evidence class:** `live-measured 2026-07-28, #329`.

comments.body:
## Spike result — **no-data**. The request surface is reachable and empty, downstream of #327's empty package inventory.

### The grant

Covered by the single `EntitlementManagement.Read.All` grant recorded on #327 — appRole `<guid-24>`, assignment `NhU3E1CZiEmQ9DQ1ZkVngc-io-0qqOBKowzeHR1fLIg` on the `graph2otel-poller` SP, 2026-07-28T10:53Z, read-only, application-type. No separate grant was needed for this issue.

This is a consequence, not an independent finding: #327 measured zero access packages on this tenant, and an assignment request is a request *for a package*. With no packages there is nothing anyone could have requested, so a populated request stream here was never possible. The two issues share one blocker.

### Verdict

**No build**, and specifically no window collector. This issue's design — a checkpointed window feed over time-ordered requests — depends on three things it cannot get from an empty collection: proof that incremental filtering works on the timestamp field, a measured event-time semantic, and an immutable id to dedupe on. All three are structural properties of real rows. Inventing them from documentation and shipping a checkpointing window collector is how a stream silently double-counts or skips, and this project has no delta query on any log endpoint to fall back on.

The free-text handling question the issue raises deliberately stays open. Its own wording is *"assess free-text fields from real samples rather than applying a blanket PII rule"* — which is right, and it is precisely why nothing is decided here. Requestor justifications and approver answers are the fields in question; guessing at their treatment without seeing one would be the blanket rule the issue exists to avoid. This project has already paid for the "awkward to model" reflex three times (#110/#111, then `ExtendedProperties` on #100).

**Named unblock:** an access package exists AND at least one assignment request has been submitted against it — approved, denied or expired, any outcome. Then: capture the row, measure incremental filter support and event-time semantics, and decide the free-text question against the real fields. **#327 unblocks first; this issue cannot move before it.**

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Approved, denied, expired, and delivery-failed behavior is validated or named as a data blocker — **named as a data blocker**, which the criterion allows.
- [x] Request identities and free text remain log-only — no implementation; the constraint carries forward and the field-level decision stays deliberately open.
- [ ] Incremental dedupe and event time are proven — unprovable on an empty collection, and not assumed from documentation.
- [x] No submit/update API is called — nothing beyond the single GET above was issued.

**Evidence class:** `live-measured 2026-07-28, #328`.

 "createdDateTime":"2025-09-10T19:00:50.027Z"}
```

`catalogType: "serviceDefault"` is the tell. Every tenant with the feature turned on has this row whether or not anyone uses entitlement management, so it is not evidence of use and a collector counting catalogs would report `1` on a tenant that has never created an access package.

### Verdict

**No build.** The outcome asked for is package/assignment/expiration/orphaned-external-access state. Zero packages, zero assignments and zero policies means every one of those is unmappable, and the only non-empty collection is a row Microsoft creates for everyone.

The specific failure being avoided: shipping four gauges that read `0, 0, 0, 1` forever. That looks like a healthy tenant with no entitlement risk, and it is indistinguishable from a mapper that never worked. This project has a rule for exactly this — mappers are written against live samples, never documentation — and #142 (`"platform": "windows"`, never on the wire) is what it cost when the rule was skipped.

The scope stays granted: read-only, no cost, and the re-probe on unblock is one request rather than another grant cycle.

**Named unblock:** at least one access package exists with at least one assignment. `accessPackages` and `assignments` then return rows, and package/assignment/policy shapes plus the expansion fan-out cost can be measured before any mapper is written.

### Acceptance criteria

- [x] Real package and assignment shapes are captured before mapping — none exist to capture; no mapping written. The rule held rather than being worked around.
- [ ] Expired/failed/current states remain identifiable without entity metric labels — not reached; the constraint carries to the unblocked build.
- [ ] Expansion/fan-out cost is bounded — not measurable with zero packages.
- [x] The spike may close no-data with an explicit package-created unblock — that is this close.

**Evidence class:** `live-measured 2026-07-28, #327`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A real read-only sample precedes mapper work.
- [ ] Every failed user/task remains identifiable in logs.
- [ ] One failed child request produces partial/degraded telemetry, not false clean success.
- [ ] Checkpoints/dedupe use stable run/result IDs.
