comments.body:
## Spike result — **blocked on LICENSING, not on permission.** The grant was made and is provably not the obstacle.

### The grants (recorded per the standing consent)

Both scopes this issue asked for, granted 2026-07-28T10:53Z as `appRoleAssignment`s on the `graph2otel-poller` SP (`13371536-9950-4988-90f4-343566456781`):

| scope | appRole id | assignment id |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `LifecycleWorkflows-Workflow.ReadBasic.All` | `<guid-25>` | `NhU3E1CZiEmQ9DQ1ZkVngTlghWBwKi5PhQ5rC10Y5_4` |
| `LifecycleWorkflows-Reports.Read.All` | `<guid-26>` | `NhU3E1CZiEmQ9DQ1ZkVngTYZLnQh8GRAtxTRVPo5k_k` |

Read-only, application-type. Both confirmed present in a freshly minted poller token immediately before the probe — so the result below is not a stale-token artifact.

### The measurement

Every Lifecycle Workflows route answers **403**, with the same body:

```
Insufficient license to complete this operation. User workflows require an Entra ID
Governance license. Agent-related workflows require a Microsoft Agent 365 or
Microsoft 365 E7 license. See https://aka.ms/LCWLicenseInfo.
```

| request | result |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /v1.0/identityGovernance/lifecycleWorkflows/workflows` | 403, licence |
| `GET /v1.0/identityGovernance/lifecycleWorkflows/workflowTemplates` | 403, licence |
| `GET /v1.0/identityGovernance/lifecycleWorkflows/deletedItems/workflows` | 403, licence |

`workflowTemplates` is the informative one: it is Microsoft's own static template catalog, identical on every tenant and carrying no customer data. That it 403s too means the licence gate sits in front of the entire `lifecycleWorkflows` segment, not in front of tenant-specific content. There is no partial read to build on and no cheaper corner to probe.

### Verdict

**Closing with a licensing unblock**, not a no-build. The distinction matters: nothing about the design was disproved. The API exists, the permission model is satisfied, and the spike's real questions — retention, paging, nested run/task/user fan-out — are simply unanswerable without a licence.

**Do not re-attempt this by granting a broader Graph scope.** The scopes are already held and the denial is on a different axis. This is the third instance of that pattern in this programme (#352's `/providers/microsoft.intune` tenant-root scope, #330's Purview DataInsights backend, now this) and it keeps costing a probe cycle: the obvious next move — grant more permission — is the wrong one every time.

**Named unblock:** the tenant holds a Microsoft Entra ID Governance licence. Re-run `GET /v1.0/identityGovernance/lifecycleWorkflows/workflows`; a 200 reopens this with real shapes to map. The two scopes stay granted so that re-probe is one request.

### Acceptance criteria

- [x] A real read-only sample precedes mapper work — no sample obtainable, and no mapper written. The rule held.
- [ ] Every failed user/task remains identifiable in logs — not reached.
- [ ] One failed child request produces partial/degraded telemetry — not reached.
- [ ] Checkpoints/dedupe use stable run/result IDs — not reached.
- [x] The spike may close no-data with an explicit workflow-created unblock condition — closing on the stronger licence condition above.

**Evidence class:** `live-measured 2026-07-28, #326`.

## Outcome

Case inventory should expose disabled/erroring holds, custodian hold status, and failed long-running operations.

## Evidence

**Evidence class:** `docs-only child routes over a live case surface (2026-07-25)`

- The current collector proves cases exist but does not inspect legal holds, custodians, or operations.
- The existing eDiscovery data-plane registration and read scope can reach these v1 child resources.

## Proposed scope

- Probe per-case legal holds, custodians, and operations through the existing registration.
- Emit bounded counts by enabled/status/error/action and one state log per child resource.

## Constraints and non-goals

- Do not ingest review-set content, search results, exports, or binary case material.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Live shapes and case/page fan-out are measured.
- [ ] Each child route degrades independently.
- [ ] Zero/.NET sentinel dates are handled consistently.
- [ ] Content-bearing fields remain out of scope.

## Prior decisions and duplicate check

- Not duplicate of #102/#149: those establish case inventory/registration, not child-resource operational health.
- Related: #102, #149.

## Primary sources

- [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/security-ediscoverycase-list-legalholds?view=graph-rest-1.0](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/security-ediscoverycase-list-legalholds?view=graph-rest-1.0)
- [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/security-ediscoverycase-list-custodians?view=graph-rest-1.0](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/security-ediscoverycase-list-custodians?view=graph-rest-1.0)
- [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/security-ediscoverycase-list-operations?view=graph-rest-1.0](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/security-ediscoverycase-list-operations?view=graph-rest-1.0)

## Priority

Audit recommendation: **P1**.

comments.body:
## Probe result — **parking the build**, with the fan-out cost measured and one live trap that changes how this must be written.

Probed live 2026-07-28 as `graph2otel-poller`, read-only, through the existing eDiscovery registration and `eDiscovery.Read.All`. Every child route the issue names is reachable. None of them has a row.

### All six child routes are reachable; all six are empty

One case exists on this tenant (`ed1518bd…`, the default `Content Search` case).

| route | result | latency |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `…/ediscoveryCases/{id}/legalHolds` | 200, **0 rows** (see the trap below — it 500s first) | 11.4 s |
| `…/custodians` | 200, 0 rows | 7.4 s |
| `…/operations` | 200, 0 rows | 2.0 s |
| `…/noncustodialDataSources` | 200, 0 rows | 10.4 s |
| `…/searches` | 200, 0 rows | 2.0 s |
| `…/tags` | 200, 0 rows | 3.1 s |

**Fan-out cost, measured:** ~36 s of wall clock for one case across six routes, `1 + 6N` requests with no batch form and no `$expand`. These are among the slowest endpoints this project touches — a single empty `legalHolds` list took 11.4 s. On a tenant with 50 cases that is roughly 30 minutes per cycle, so this needs the same shape of explicit cost gate `exo_per_mailbox` got in `fed98f8` rather than being default-on. Recording it here so it is not re-measured.

### Why the build is parked rather than shipped

Every route returns `value: []`. There is no live shape for a hold, a custodian or an operation, so a status/error mapper would be written against documentation — which this repo forbids, and for a reason it has already paid for (`"platform": "windows"` was never on the wire, #142). Precedent is `entra/tenantpolicy` and #355 before its row was found: emit a count, write no field mapper against unseen data.

Emitting counts alone would not satisfy this issue either. The outcome asked for is *"disabled/erroring holds, custodian hold status, and failed long-running operations"* — every one of those is a `status`/`error` field bucket, and none can be mapped from an empty list. A collector that shipped six always-zero gauges would report clean success over a surface nobody has ever seen return data: the "a green tick is not evidence of data" trap, in its purest form.

**Named unblock:** one real legal hold OR one custodian OR one completed operation exists on a case, so the status field set can be captured. Creating one is a tenant mutation and is a maintainer decision, not something to force with a synthetic fixture.

### The trap that must be handled when this is built — a live `.NET DateTime.MinValue` sentinel

The issue's own acceptance criterion says *"Zero/.NET sentinel dates are handled consistently"*. It is live, it is on the **case** object itself, and here is the exact sequence:

1. First `GET /v1.0/security/cases/ediscoveryCases` returned the case with
   `"createdDateTime": "0001-01-01T00:00:00Z"` and the same value for `lastModifiedDateTime` — **`DateTime.MinValue`, not a real timestamp.**
2. While in that state, every child route 500s with `"The compliance case \"ed1518bd-…\" doesn't exist. Please create the case."` — a **500 whose text is really a 404**, on a case the collection had just listed.
3. A `GET` on the single case materialized it. Both timestamps became `2026-07-28T10:41:06.776Z` with `lastModifiedBy.user.displayName: "graph2otel-poller"`, and the child routes started returning 200/empty.
4. Re-listed three times over the following minute: the timestamps are now **stable**. This is a one-time materialization of the tenant's default `Content Search` case, not a per-read mutation — checked specifically, because a read that mutates state would be a much bigger problem than this issue.

Two things follow, both binding on whoever builds this:

**The sentinel must be dropped, not stamped.** `internal/telemetry` only sets non-zero timestamps and a record with no parseable event time is dropped rather than stamped on arrival. `0001-01-01T00:00:00Z` *parses* — that is the danger. It would sail through as a real event time and publish a case as having been created in year 1. It has to be recognized and treated as absent.

**A 500 from a child route can mean "the parent is a stub", not "the service is broken".** The independent-degradation requirement already in the acceptance criteria covers it, but the retry behavior matters: backing off hard on that 500 is wrong, and so is treating it as fatal for the whole collection.

### Acceptance criteria status

- [x] Live shapes and case/page fan-out are measured — fan-out and cost measured; **child-resource shapes do not exist to measure**, which is the parking reason.
- [x] Each child route degrades independently — requirement confirmed necessary by the 500-on-stub case above.
- [x] Zero/.NET sentinel dates are handled consistently — sentinel located live, disposition decided (drop, never stamp).
- [x] Content-bearing fields remain out of scope — unchanged; review sets, search results and exports were not requested and are not in scope.

**Evidence class:** `live-measured 2026-07-28, #323`.

## Recheck 2026-07-28 (later) — **the unblock has not fired. Still parked, and the parking reason is unchanged.**

Re-probed all six child routes as `graph2otel-poller`. Every one is still `200` with zero rows:

| route | result | latency |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `…/legalHolds` | 200, 0 rows | 7.1 s |
| `…/custodians` | 200, 0 rows | 1.2 s |
| `…/operations` | 200, 0 rows | 5.8 s |
| `…/noncustodialDataSources` | 200, 0 rows | 1.2 s |
| `…/searches` | 200, 0 rows | 2.1 s |
| `…/tags` | 200, 0 rows | 1.3 s |

Two things confirmed while re-probing, both worth having:

**The case materialization from this morning held.** `createdDateTime` is now `2026-07-28T10:41:06.776Z` and stable across this fourth read, and the child routes answer `200` rather than the `500 "the compliance case doesn't exist"` they returned while the case was a `DateTime.MinValue` stub. So that was a genuine one-time materialization, not a read that mutates state on every poll — which is the reassuring answer, and it is now confirmed over a multi-hour gap rather than a one-minute one.

**The latencies reproduced.** 18.7 s across six routes for a single case, against 36 s this morning — same order, still among the slowest endpoints this project touches, still `1 + 6N` with no batch form.

### The named unblock, and what would fire it

The unblock condition on the comment above stands verbatim: **one real legal hold OR one custodian OR one completed operation must exist on a case**, so the status/error field set can be captured from the wire. Nothing has changed on the tenant, so nothing new can be mapped.

Building anyway would mean writing a status/error mapper from documentation — which this repo forbids, and has already paid for (`"platform": "windows"` was never on the wire, #142). Six always-zero gauges would report clean success over a surface nobody has ever seen return data.

**This needs a maintainer decision, not more probing.** Creating a legal hold or adding a custodian to the `Content Search` case is a tenant mutation, and per the standing rule live-tenant mutations need explicit approval with the exact operation named. The cheapest option that would unblock it is adding a single custodian to the existing case (`POST …/ediscoveryCases/{id}/custodians` with one user), which is reversible and would capture the custodian `status`/`holdStatus` field set. **I am not doing that unprompted.**

**Evidence class:** `live-measured 2026-07-28, #323`.

## Unblocked 2026-07-28 — holds/operations/sources are on the wire. **`custodians` is a dead collection in the new product, and that is now measured, not assumed.**

The maintainer created two eDiscovery Premium cases (`custod`, `case2`) with hold policies and People/data sources. Re-probed as `graph2otel-poller`, read-only. The named unblock from the comment above has fired for holds and operations; the custodian half resolves the opposite way, with evidence.

### Live counts, 3 cases

| case | legalHolds | custodians | noncustodialDataSources | operations | searches | tags |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ed1518bd` Content Search | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| `28ce2eda` custod | 2 | **0** | 0 | 5 | 1 | 0 |
| `26179e8a` case2 | 2 | **0** | 0 | 2 | 0 | 0 |

### `custodians` cannot be populated from the current product — do not wait for it

The new unified eDiscovery experience (classic retired 2025-08-31) demoted custodians from the primary organizing unit to cases, and **renamed them "People"** in the UI — which is why no "custodian" string appears anywhere in the portal any more. The maintainer added two People data sources to `case2` and attached them to hold policies. They do **not** materialize as `ediscoveryCustodian`. They land as:

`GET /security/cases/ediscoveryCases/{case}/legalHolds/{hold}/userSources` and `/siteSources`

Three separate attempts across two cases, each confirmed by `operations` gaining a `holdPolicySync` while `custodians` stayed at zero. `custodians` is a legacy Graph collection the current UI has no path into.

**Disposition:** emit the custodian count (honest — it is genuinely zero), write **no custodian field mapper**. Same shape as `entra/tenantpolicy`. This is a closed question, not a deferral: there is no tenant action that would populate it. The custodian's own sub-collections are declared in the v1.0 EDM as `Collection(self.userSource)` / `Collection(self.siteSource)` — the *same types* now sampled live from a hold — so if Microsoft ever repopulates it, the source mapper already covers it.

### Live field sets now captured

`legalHold`, `caseOperation`, `userSource`, `siteSource`, `ediscoverySearch`, `ediscoveryReviewSet`. Captures in the probe scratch.

### Wire traps found — each one breaks the design the issue body proposed

**1. `legalHold.status` is `null` on every healthy hold.** The issue proposed bucketing "disabled/erroring holds" on it. Populated fields are `isEnabled: true` and `errors: []`. Keying the gauge on `status` would bucket a healthy tenant entirely into `unknown` — a green tick over nothing. **The gauge must key on `isEnabled` + `len(errors)`.**

**2. `userSource.id` is not always a GUID.** An inactive mailbox on `case2` carries
`"id": "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000.vmuser@m7kni.io"` — a zero-GUID prefix concatenated with the email — beside a normal-GUID active row in the same collection on the same hold. It is also unbounded-ish and identity-bearing: log twin only, never a metric label.

**3. `createdBy.user` uses three different conventions across sibling routes on one case.**

| route | shape |
| --- | --- |
| `legalHolds` | `{"id": "Rob Knight", "displayName": null}` — **the human name is in the `id` field** |
| `operations`, `searches` | `{"id": "<guid>", "displayName": "Rob Knight", "userPrincipalName": "rob@m7kni.io"}` |
| case object, sources | `{"id": null, "displayName": "Rob Knight"}` |

A mapper trusting `user.id` to be a GUID publishes a person's name into an id attribute.

**4. The `.NET DateTime.MinValue` sentinel is live again, on a new field:** `siteSource.site.createdDateTime` is `0001-01-01T00:00:00Z`. Same trap the case object had this morning — it *parses*, so it passes the emitter's non-zero check and would publish a site as created in year 1. `realDateTime` already handles this and must be applied to every date on every child route.

**5. `operations.createdBy` is `null`** for system-generated actions (`holdPolicySync`) and populated for user-initiated ones (`estimateStatistics`, `addToReviewSet`). Needs nil-safety, not a required field.

**6. `unifiedGroupSources` 400s on a legal hold.** The EDM declares it only on `ediscoveryCustodian`. Must not be fetched per-hold.

**7. `search.dataSourceScopes` is a comma-joined string**, not an array: `"allTenantMailboxes,allTenantSites"`.

**8. `search.contentQuery` carries real participant email addresses.** Log twin only; never a metric label (#112).

**9. `caseMembers` returns 401** for the poller — `eDiscovery.Read.All` plus the S&C data-plane registration does not cover it. Out of scope for this issue, but it is a real scope boundary worth not re-discovering.

### Enums for `internal/wirecheck`, read from the v1.0 `$metadata` EDM

| enum | members | observed live |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `caseAction` | contentExport, applyTags, convertToPdf, index, estimateStatistics, addToReviewSet, holdUpdate, purgeData, exportReport, exportResult, holdPolicySync, unknownFutureValue | holdPolicySync, addToReviewSet, estimateStatistics |
| `caseOperationStatus` | notStarted, submissionFailed, running, succeeded, partiallySucceeded, failed, unknownFutureValue | succeeded |
| `dataSourceHoldStatus` | notApplied, applied, applying, removing, partial, unknownFutureValue | applied |
| `sourceType` | mailbox, site, unknownFutureValue | mailbox |

Per #234 the watched set is derived from the map the collector keys on, not restated here.

### Fan-out cost, re-measured at 3 cases

4 case-level routes + 2 source routes per hold = 20 requests for 3 cases / 4 holds, ~60 s wall clock. Still `1 + kN`, no batch form, no `$expand`. Confirms the earlier finding that this needs an explicit cost gate rather than being default-on.

**Evidence class:** `live-measured 2026-07-28, #323`.

## Built and shipped — `purview.ediscovery_case_health`

The unblock fired: two eDiscovery Premium cases with real hold policies gave live field sets for legal holds, hold data sources and case operations. The collector is written against verbatim captures of those, never against documentation.

### What ships

New collector `purview.ediscovery_case_health` (`internal/collectors/purview/ediscoveryhealth`), a `SnapshotCollector` on the `Deps`/`All` path, hourly, `Experimental` and `eDiscovery.Read.All` — opt-in for the same reason as `purview.ediscovery_cases`, i.e. the Security & Compliance data-plane registration, not a beta surface.

Fetches per covered case: `legalHolds` → per hold `userSources` + `siteSources`, plus `custodians`, `noncustodialDataSources`, `operations`.

**Metrics — all bounded, no `case_id` label anywhere (#112):**

| metric | labels |
| --- | --- |
| `purview.ediscovery.legal_holds` | `enabled`, `has_errors` |
| `purview.ediscovery.hold_sources` | `source_type`, `hold_status` |
| `purview.ediscovery.case_operations` | `action`, `status` |
| `purview.ediscovery.custodians` | none (aggregate count) |
| `purview.ediscovery.noncustodial_data_sources` | none (aggregate count) |
| `purview.ediscovery.case_health.cases_covered` / `…cases_total` | none |

**Log twins (#114):** `purview.ediscovery_legal_hold`, `purview.ediscovery_hold_source`, `purview.ediscovery_case_operation` — carrying case id, hold id, source id, mail address, site URL and the per-entity detail no metric may key on.

### The issue's own proposed design was wrong, and this is the correction

The body asked for holds bucketed by their `status` field. **`legalHold.status` is `null` on every healthy hold on the wire.** A gauge keyed on it collapses a healthy tenant entirely into `unknown` and reports clean success over nothing — the exact "green tick is not evidence of data" trap the parking comment warned about. The gauge keys on `isEnabled` and `len(errors) > 0`, both of which are populated. The raw `status` is carried to the log twin as `hold_state` so a future non-null value is visible without any metric depending on it.

### Wire traps handled, each with a dedicated test

All nine traps from the probe comment above. The load-bearing ones: the non-GUID source id (`00000000-…-000000000000.vmuser@m7kni.io`) is preserved verbatim on the log twin and kept off every metric; `createdBy.user` is resolved across its three inconsistent shapes by a helper that falls back to `id` only when `displayName` is empty *and* `id` does not parse as a GUID (there is deliberately no `created_by_id` — on `legalHolds` it would publish a person's name into an id key); the `0001-01-01T00:00:00Z` sentinel on `siteSource.site.createdDateTime` is dropped, not stamped; `unifiedGroupSources` is never fetched.

`wirecheck` watchdogs on the three fields that key a metric label (`hold_status`, `action`, `status`), each `Enum` **derived from the bucket map the collector already keys on** rather than restated, per #234. Report-only.

### Cost gate

`1 + 4C + 2H` GETs, no batch form, no `$expand`, re-measured at ~60 s for 3 cases / 4 holds. Capped at `DefaultMaxCases = 50` per cycle with `cases_covered` / `cases_total` emitted every cycle so a shortfall is visible rather than silent. No new config key — the collector is already opt-in twice over.

### Two defects found in review, both fixed, both now guarded

Neither was caught by the build lane's own tests; both were found by reading the diff and proven by a test that fails when the fix is reverted.

**1. A total read failure published a confident zero (#240).** `custodians` and `noncustodial_data_sources` are aggregate-only counts accumulated from zero, so if *every* case's fetch on one of those routes failed, the counter was still `0` and the gauge published it — a GAP asserted as a measured zero. Fixed with a `countingRoute` that tracks whether any case's fetch actually succeeded; the gauge is now absent entirely when none did. The honest zero (a case answering 200 with an empty collection, which is this tenant's steady state) is still published — both halves are asserted, so an implementation that just stopped publishing would fail the test.

**2. An absent `percentProgress` published a fabricated `0%`.** The v1.0 EDM declares it with no `Nullable="false"`, so Graph may omit it, and `0` is a *meaningful* value for this field rather than an obviously-wrong sentinel — decoded into a bare `float64` the two are indistinguishable downstream. Now a pointer; absent stays absent, with a positive control asserting a real `100` still lands.

### Acceptance criteria

- [x] Live shapes and case/page fan-out are measured — shapes captured verbatim from three real cases; fan-out re-measured and capped.
- [x] Each child route degrades independently — only the top-level case list is fatal; every child route emits nothing rather than a zero on failure, guarded by `TestChildRouteFailureDegradesIndependently` and `TestTotalRouteFailurePublishesNoCount`.
- [x] Zero/.NET sentinel dates are handled consistently — `realDateTime` on every date on every route, guarded by `TestZeroDateSentinelIsDropped` with a positive control.
- [x] Content-bearing fields remain out of scope — `searches`, `tags`, `reviewSets` and review-set content are never fetched, guarded by `TestUnifiedGroupSourcesIsNeverFetched`.

**Evidence class:** `live-measured 2026-07-28, #323`.

## Outcome

Access-review telemetry should show whether scheduled reviews are actually being completed and what decisions are pending.

## Evidence

**Evidence class:** `live-measured residual plus docs-only fan-out (2026-07-25)`

- The shipped collector inventories definitions only.
- A live `InProgress` definition returned an empty inline `instances` array on v1 and beta.
- Real progress requires per-definition instances and per-instance decisions.

## Proposed scope

- Measure instance/decision counts, paging, and request budget as the poller.
- Emit bounded counts by instance status and decision outcome plus per-instance/per-decision logs.
- Use actual decision timestamps where present.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] A live non-inline instance/decision payload is captured before mapper work.
- [x] Fan-out has a bounded concurrency/request budget.
- [x] Every fetched decision remains identifiable in logs.
- [x] Inaccessible or empty reviews degrade explicitly rather than claiming completion.

## Prior decisions and duplicate check

- Not duplicate of #260: that issue explicitly left completion/staleness out after proving inline instances empty.
- Related: #251, #260.

## Primary sources

- [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/accessreviewscheduledefinition-list-instances?view=graph-rest-1.0](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/accessreviewscheduledefinition-list-instances?view=graph-rest-1.0)
- [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/accessreviewinstance-list-decisions?view=graph-rest-1.0](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/accessreviewinstance-list-decisions?view=graph-rest-1.0)

## Priority

Audit recommendation: **P1**.

comments.body:
## Unblocked — **the non-inline route works.** Building.

#260 closed this as a residual because the inline `instances` array came back EMPTY under `$expand` on both v1.0 and beta. That measurement was correct and it was about `$expand`, not about the data. Probed the **child routes directly** 2026-07-28 as `graph2otel-poller`, read-only, no new scope:

| route | result | latency |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/v1.0/identityGovernance/accessReviews/definitions` | 200, 1 definition | 0.2 s |
| `…/definitions/{did}/instances` | 200, **1 instance** | 0.2 s |
| `…/instances/{iid}/decisions` | 200, **3 decisions** | 0.2 s |
| `…/instances/{iid}/contactedReviewers` | 200, 1 reviewer | 0.2 s |

Fan-out is `1 + N + 2M` and these are **fast** — 0.2 s each, unlike the eDiscovery child routes on #323. This is the third time on this project that varying the probe shape turned a "blocked" verdict into live data.

### Three sentinels on one record, spelled three different ways

The live decision is `NotReviewed`, and its "nobody has acted" state arrives as:

- **A zero-GUID object.** `reviewedBy` is fully populated with `id: "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"` and empty-string `displayName`/`userPrincipalName` — not null, not absent. Mapping it through would publish a reviewer that does not exist, and a `count by (reviewed_by_id)` would show a phantom holding every pending decision on the tenant. Same for `appliedBy`. Treated as ABSENT.
- **JSON `null`** on `reviewedDateTime` and `appliedDateTime`.
- **An empty STRING** on `principal.lastUserSignInDateTime` — so a presence check is not enough.

The zero GUID is the same class as the `0001-01-01T00:00:00Z` DateTime.MinValue sentinel already recorded on #323 and #350. Three of these have now turned up on this project in one day, in three different shapes.

### What ships

Two gauges on the existing collector — `entra.access_reviews.instances{status}` and `.decisions{decision, applied_result}` — plus `entra.access_review_instance` and `entra.access_review_decision` twins. `decision` and `applied_result` are deliberately separate labels: a decision can be `Deny` and still never have been applied, which is precisely the "the review ran and changed nothing" case this issue exists to surface. `recommendation` rides the twin rather than becoming a third label.

Warn when an instance is past its `endDateTime` and a decision is still `NotReviewed` — a review that expired without being done.

**Evidence class:** `live-measured 2026-07-28, #319`.

## Shipped in `0811619`

`entra.access_reviews` now answers whether reviews are being **completed**, not just whether they exist. `make check` exit 0.

- [x] **A live non-inline instance/decision payload is captured before mapper work.** All fixtures are verbatim from the 2026-07-28 capture; nothing was mapped from documentation.
- [x] **Fan-out has a bounded concurrency/request budget.** `1+N+M` with `maxDefinitions=200`, `maxInstancesPerDefinition=50`, `maxDecisionsPerInstance=5000`, each justified in code against the measured ~0.2 s per request. A cap that bites marks `arrays_truncated` on the affected twin — a silent cap reads as "covered everything".
- [x] **Every fetched decision remains identifiable in logs.** One `entra.access_review_decision` twin per decision; ids, UPNs, display names and links are twin-only (#112).
- [x] **Inaccessible or empty reviews degrade explicitly rather than claiming completion.** A failed child fetch omits its parent from the gauge instead of emitting a confident zero (#240), and does not abort siblings. Verified by sabotage: reinstating the seeded zero fails `TestInstancesFetchFailureOmitsDefinitionAndDoesNotAbortRest`.

### The correction this issue rests on

**#260's measurement was right and its conclusion was wrong.** The inline `instances` array really is empty under `$expand` on both v1.0 and beta — but that is a fact about `$expand`, not about the data. The child routes serve it directly. Recording the shape of the error because it is the third time this month a "blocked" verdict on this project came from one probe shape rather than from the API.

### Three sentinels, one record, three spellings

`reviewedBy` and `appliedBy` arrive as **fully populated objects whose id is the zero GUID** with empty-string names — not null, not absent. Mapping one through would put a phantom reviewer on every pending decision, and a `count by (reviewed_by_id)` would show it holding the lot. `reviewedDateTime` and `appliedDateTime` are JSON `null`. `principal.lastUserSignInDateTime` is an **empty string**. Each has a guard at both the mapper's own return value and through the full pipeline's `Attrs` — asserting only at `Attrs` is how two guards in this tree shipped protecting nothing this week. Sabotaging the zero-GUID check fails two tests.

`decision` and `applied_result` are separate labels because a decision can be `Deny` and still never have been applied — the "the review ran and changed nothing" case. `recommendation` rides the twin rather than tripling the series.

### One documented omission

`contactedReviewers` is reachable and is **not** fetched. It appeared in the fan-out math but no metric or twin was ever specified for it, and fetching data with nowhere to put it is wasted request budget. Called out in the package doc rather than left as an accident.

**Evidence class:** `live-measured 2026-07-28, #319`.

## Evidence

**Evidence class:** `source-derived; mapper requires a fresh live capture (2026-07-25)`

## Primary sources

- [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/conditionalaccessroot-list-namedlocations?view=graph-rest-1.0](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/conditionalaccessroot-list-namedlocations?view=graph-rest-1.0)

comments.body:
## Evidence inventory and decision gate — clean pause

Read-only reconciliation completed on 2026-07-26; no files, permissions, captures, or live tenant state were changed.

Current source already fetches v1.0 Conditional Access policies and named locations with the existing `Policy.Read.All` scope. It emits bounded gauges but discards policy configuration and named-location entity detail. Historical `live-measured 2026-07-17, #165` captures cover five enabled policies and both named-location subtypes, but the residential CIDRs in the IP-location fixture were deliberately replaced with documentation ranges. That fixture cannot be represented as both wire-verbatim and suitable evidence for emitting the ranges.

The historical wire also proves absence/null/empty traps that a twin must preserve: country locations omit `isTrusted`; IP locations carry it; nested policy objects may be null; arrays may be empty; false booleans are distinct from omission. The existing aggregate may continue collapsing absent `isTrusted` to false, but a state twin must not claim the wire returned false when the key was absent.

### Decisions required before fresh capture or implementation

1. **Public fixture handling**
   - **Recommended:** capture as `graph2otel-poller`, retain a private evidence receipt, and commit a deterministically redacted fixture explicitly labelled `captured-and-redacted`; tests preserve shape, types, omission/null distinctions, and both IP-range discriminators without publishing tenant CIDRs.
   - Alternative: establish an approved protected fixture store and keep only a synthetic structural fixture publicly. This adds private infrastructure ownership.
2. **Twin schema**
   - **Recommended:** one `entra.conditional_access_policy` state event and one `entra.named_location` state event per returned entity, using typed fixed attributes and arrays; preserve omission/null distinctions and do not create per-target child records.
   - Alternative: normalized per-condition/per-target events, which materially expands record volume and the issue's contract.

Unblock condition: Rob approves the fixture privacy route and event/schema option. Required human action and owner: Rob. After approval, obtain fresh read-only poller captures of policies and both named-location subtypes, then start strict TDD. No new permission is required for the recommended path.

## Decisions received 2026-07-28 — both answered, with one amendment. Unblocked.

### 1. Fixture privacy — approved WITH a change to what redaction means

The recommended route was accepted, but the maintainer amended how the redaction is done, verbatim:

> *"redacted committed fixture but rather than it being completely redacted just change the cidrs so theyre still realistic just not mine"*

So: capture as `graph2otel-poller`, keep a private evidence receipt, commit a fixture labelled `captured-and-redacted` — and **substitute realistic public CIDRs, not documentation ranges**.

This matters more than it sounds. The existing fixture's residential ranges were replaced with documentation ranges (`192.0.2.0/24` and friends), which are structurally unlike real input: they are a fixed size, obviously synthetic, and exercise none of the variety the mapper will actually meet. A substituted CIDR must look like something a tenant would really configure — plausible public space, realistic prefix lengths, a mix of sizes — so the mapper is tested against realistic shape while publishing nothing of the tenant's. Deterministic substitution, so re-capturing produces a stable diff.

### 2. Twin schema — one twin per entity, approved as recommended

One `entra.conditional_access_policy` state event and one `entra.named_location` state event per returned entity. Typed fixed attributes and arrays. **No per-target or per-condition child records** — the normalised alternative is rejected.

### The wire trap this must preserve, restated because it is easy to lose

Country locations **omit** `isTrusted`; IP locations **carry** it. Nested policy objects may be null; arrays may be empty; a `false` boolean is a different fact from an absent key. The existing aggregate may keep collapsing an absent `isTrusted` to false, but **a state twin must never claim the wire returned false when the key was not there** — that is the absent-field-is-not-a-sentinel rule, and it is the single most likely way this implementation goes quietly wrong.

Both IP-range discriminators must survive redaction, since telling the two apart is part of what the twin reports.

No new permission is required; `Policy.Read.All` is already held. Take fresh read-only captures of policies and both named-location subtypes, then strict TDD.

Built in `04653d2` to both decisions as recorded: one twin per entity, no per-condition or per-target children, and a capture-and-redact fixture with realistic substituted CIDRs.

Fresh read-only captures were taken as `graph2otel-poller` on 2026-07-28: 16 CA policies covering all three `state` values, one with null `grantControls` and twelve with null `sessionControls`, plus both named-location subtypes. Seven policies went into the twin fixture, chosen to cover those shapes; the existing five-policy fixture is untouched so the gauge tests keep their original evidence.

### The `isTrusted` trap, and how it is actually held down

Live-confirmed on this tenant: the `countryNamedLocation` carries no `isTrusted` key at all, while the `ipNamedLocation` carries it as `true`. `IsTrusted` decodes as `*bool` and the twin sets the attribute only when non-nil.

Three tests hold the three cases apart — absent must be **omitted**, a wire `false` must be **emitted as false**, and the full `Collect` path must preserve both. Sabotage-verified: collapsing the guard to `l.IsTrusted != nil && *l.IsTrusted` fails with `attrs[is_trusted] = false present, want ABSENT`. The existing aggregate gauge still collapses absent to false, deliberately, and that is unchanged — the two are different questions.

Both IP-range discriminators survive: IPv4 and IPv6 ranges land in separate arrays rather than one merged list, so telling them apart does not depend on re-parsing the string.

### Fixtures

The named-location fixture is labelled `captured-and-redacted (2026-07-28, #318)`. Only `cidrAddress` values were substituted, 1:1 preserving each range's IP version and prefix length; everything else is verbatim wire. The **existing** fixture's RFC 5737/3849 documentation ranges were replaced with the same realistic values and its comment rewritten to say why — a fixed-size, obviously-synthetic range exercises none of the shape the mapper meets.

### One judgment call worth flagging

An entity whose `state` or `@odata.type` is unrecognized **still gets its twin**, using the raw wire value; only the gauge bucket skips it. The decision comment said "one state event per *returned* policy", and dropping a record because a future enum member appeared is the failure mode this project's log twins exist to prevent. Reopen if the twin was meant to be gated on recognition.

comments.body:
## Evidence inventory and decision gate — clean pause

Read-only reconciliation completed on 2026-07-26; no files, GitHub state beyond this comment, permissions, or live tenant state were changed.

Current source already fetches the v1.0 singleton `/policies/authenticationMethodsPolicy` with the existing `Policy.Read.AuthenticationMethod` scope, but decodes only configuration `id` and `state` and emits two bounded gauges. The `live-measured 2026-07-17, #165` fixture contains seven returned configurations (FIDO2, Authenticator, SMS, Voice, X.509, Verifiable Credentials, QR Code PIN) and top-level policy/campaign fields. Temporary Access Pass, hardware/software OATH, email, and custom/external configurations remain unobserved.

Secrets review: the observed fields contain policy metadata and target identifiers, not passwords, private keys, actual PINs, or credential values. Arbitrary raw configuration JSON must not be emitted: an unseen provider subtype could introduce an unreviewed sensitive field. Unknown subtypes should emit only generic `id`, `state`, and `@odata.type` until captured evidence supports more.

### Decision required before implementation

Affected contract: the new event names and targeting representation define a public telemetry/data-model contract.

- **Option A — recommended:** `entra.auth_methods_policy` for the singleton and one `entra.auth_method_configuration` event per returned method. Use a fixed typed attribute schema and bounded arrays for include/exclude target identifiers. Preserve subtype-specific observed fields on that one configuration event; unknown subtypes remain generic only.
- **Option B:** add normalized per-target child events. This improves target-level filtering but expands record cardinality and goes beyond the issue's one-event-per-configuration acceptance shape.

Recommendation consequences: Option A keeps one source row to one configuration twin, avoids raw JSON, preserves entity detail in logs, and adds no metric labels or permissions.

Unblock condition: Rob approves Option A or names the alternative event/schema contract. Required human action and owner: Rob, telemetry-contract decision. All implementation for this child is gated; no independent code change remains within #317.

## Decision received 2026-07-28 — Option A approved. Unblocked.

Maintainer approved **Option A** as written in the decision-gate comment. Restating the binding terms so implementation needs no further interpretation:

- One `entra.auth_methods_policy` event for the singleton.
- One `entra.auth_method_configuration` event per returned configuration.
- **Fixed typed attribute schema**, bounded arrays for include/exclude target identifiers. No raw configuration JSON anywhere.
- Subtype-specific observed fields are preserved on the configuration event.
- **An unknown subtype emits only `id`, `state` and `@odata.type`.** This is the load-bearing part of the choice, not a detail: an unseen provider subtype could carry a field nobody has reviewed, and emitting arbitrary JSON would ship it. A new subtype therefore arrives deliberately under-described until someone captures it.
- No new metric labels, no new permission — `Policy.Read.AuthenticationMethod` is already held.

Option B (normalised per-target child events) is **rejected**; do not reintroduce per-target records.

### Evidence position at unblock

The `live-measured 2026-07-17, #165` fixture carries seven configurations — FIDO2, Authenticator, SMS, Voice, X.509, Verifiable Credentials, QR Code PIN — plus the top-level policy and campaign fields. Temporary Access Pass, hardware/software OATH, email and custom/external configurations are **unobserved** and must stay that way in the mapper: docs-derived subtype handling is exactly what the generic-until-captured rule above is for.

No new capture is required to start. Strict TDD from the existing fixture.

Built to Option A in `04653d2`, from the existing `live-measured 2026-07-17, #165` fixture — no new capture was needed and none was taken beyond a confirmation read of the singleton.

The gauges are unchanged. Two events added: `entra.auth_methods_policy` for the singleton (policy version, migration state, and the registration campaign's state, snooze duration and bounded include/exclude target ids) and `entra.auth_method_configuration` per returned configuration, carrying that subtype's observed fields — FIDO2 attestation and key restrictions, Authenticator's software-OATH flag, Voice's office-phone flag, QR-code PIN length and lifetime. Fixed typed attributes, arrays capped, no raw JSON anywhere.

**The unknown-subtype restriction is pinned by a test that asserts an exact attribute count**, not merely the absence of a few keys — `TestCollectUnknownSubtypeEmitsOnlyGenericFields` fails if the twin carries anything beyond `id`, `state` and `odata_type`. Sabotage-verified: moving the target-array population above the early return makes it fail with 6 attributes instead of 3. That matters because the restriction is the whole reason Option A was chosen, and a test that only checked for named forbidden keys would pass over a field nobody had thought to forbid.

Every optional scalar decodes as a pointer, so an absent key emits no attribute rather than a fabricated `false`/`0`.

### One deliberate deferral, recorded rather than left implicit

`X509Certificate`'s nested policy configuration (`authenticationModeConfiguration`, `certificateUserBindings`, `crlValidationConfiguration`, `issuerHintsConfiguration`) and `MicrosoftAuthenticator`'s `featureSettings` are **not modeled**. Each needs its own multi-field typed sub-schema, and "fixed typed schema, no raw JSON" means they cannot be shipped as a blob in the meantime. They are omitted, not partially rendered — a half-mapped nested object would read as complete.

This is a scope call, not a blocker: everything at the top level of those subtypes is emitted. Worth its own issue if the X.509 configuration turns out to matter for posture reporting.

comments.body:
## Clean-pause status — actionable, no implementation started

Reconciled against `main` at `04bb0582364738d71813132ce7767ef802910f05` on 2026-07-26.

- The current false-zero premise remains valid: the collector's bare `/beta/directory/recommendations` list decodes an optional inline `impactedResources` array and emits impact series from it even when the relationship is omitted.
- The existing m7kni fixture is `live-measured 2026-07-17, #165`: five recommendations, rich top-level fields, and no inline `impactedResources` property. It proves the current zero is fabricated, but it does not prove which complete request shape is cheapest.
- No Graph probe was executed in this pause wave. A local scratch probe was drafted, then removed rather than leaving half-finished work.
- No source, fixture, test, generated artifact, permission, tenant configuration, or live resource was changed for #315.

Resume with a read-only `graph2otel-poller` comparison of: the bare list; the list with `$expand=impactedResources`; each returned recommendation's `/impactedResources` relationship; and `/impactedResources/$count`. Record status, request count, response size, and relationship cardinality without recording recommendation or tenant identifiers. Then freeze the cheapest complete request shape and start the strict failing-test cycle.

This child is actionable and is paused only because the maintainer requested a clean programme stop. It has no human unblock requirement at this point.

## Live request-shape decision — `live-measured 2026-07-26, #315`

Probed read-only as the production `graph2otel-poller` identity on Camden using the existing `DirectoryRecommendations.Read.All` grant. No tenant data, permission, configuration, or service was changed. Output was sanitized to counts/status/bytes; no tenant or recommendation identifier was recorded.

| Shape | HTTP requests | Bytes | Recommendations / impacted rows | Result |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Bare `/beta/directory/recommendations` | 1 | 36,734 | 15 recommendations; `impactedResources` present on 0 | 200; proves the current zero series are fabricated from omission |
| List with `$expand=impactedResources` | 1 | 46,832 | 15 recommendations; property present on all 15; 14 impacted rows | 200; no nested continuation links |
| Per-recommendation `/impactedResources` | 15 | 9,657 | 14 impacted rows | all 200 |
| Per-recommendation `/impactedResources/$count` | 15 | 15 | total 14 | all 200 |

The expanded list matched the relationship row count for every recommendation (`0` mismatches), and every relationship matched its `$count` (`0` mismatches). It remained one list page/request and added 10,098 response bytes, while either fan-out added 15 requests.

### Frozen implementation contract

Use one paged list request with `$expand=impactedResources`. It is the cheapest complete shape measured on this tenant and preserves terminal pagination through the existing `GetAllValuesRecorded` path. Emit the impact gauge only when the navigation property is present on a decoded record; an omitted relationship emits no impact series. Emit one `entra.recommendation` state twin from the already-returned recommendation fields. No per-entity field becomes a metric label.

The acceptance checkbox for live request/page-cost measurement is now checked. The temporary probe binary/source was removed from Camden and the local ignored scratch tree after capture.

## Clean safe-pause receipt — evidence boundary

Paused deliberately at the boundary between live evidence and implementation. The read-only request-shape measurement is complete in the [live evidence receipt](https://github.com/rknightion/graph2otel/issues/315#issuecomment-5085322876), and the acceptance checkbox for that measurement is checked.

No production TDD, mapper, collector, generated-artifact, or documentation change has started for #315. There is therefore no partial implementation to preserve or commit. The temporary ignored probe source and local binary were removed, and read-back on Camden confirms both copied probe paths are absent.

Repository state at pause: `HEAD == origin/main == 04bb0582364738d71813132ce7767ef802910f05`; no staged files and no programme diff. The only local status entries are the pre-existing unrelated `T AGENTS.md` and untracked `.superpowers/`, both untouched. Every exact-SHA workflow remains terminal success.

#315 remains actionable and is paused by maintainer request, not blocked on a human decision. Resume by re-reading the body and comments, writing the ignored local implementation plan, then strict TDD for: omitted relationship emits no impact series; the collector requests the frozen expanded URL; one `entra.recommendation` state twin is emitted per recommendation; generated signal/catalog/collector artifacts reconcile. Run #341 only after #315 releases the shared recommendations package.

## Closed by `2483dd4`

Built to the frozen contract from the live request-shape comparison; nothing was re-derived or re-probed.

- **One list request with `$expand=impactedResources`**, pinned by `TestCollectRequestsExpandedURL`.
- **`ImpactedResources` decodes as a POINTER** (`*[]json.RawMessage`). That is the whole fix: a plain slice cannot tell "Graph omitted the navigation property" from "the relationship is genuinely empty", and `len(nil) == 0` is exactly how the fabricated zero got published. Omitted → no series at all; present-but-empty → a real measured zero.
- **One `entra.recommendation` state twin per recommendation**, built from fields that were already being fetched and thrown away — name, scores, benefits, remediation impact, licences, action steps, dates. No per-entity field is a metric label.

### Verified by sabotage, not by reading

Reintroducing the old behaviour — accumulating `0` for a type whose relationship was absent — fails `TestCollectOmittedImpactedResourcesEmitsNoImpactSeries`. The guard is real, not decorative.

### Honest note on fixtures

The no-series case runs against the existing `live-measured 2026-07-17, #165` capture, which omits the property on every record. The does-emit case runs against a **constructed** fixture: the first two live records with an inline `impactedResources` array added, shaped per the beta `$metadata` EDM. It is labelled as constructed in the source rather than presented as a capture, because no expanded response body was retained from the probe — only its counts and byte sizes.

Acceptance criteria all ticked. `make check` exit 0.

The self-observability dashboard should answer `is the poller delivering complete data?` before exposing subsystem charts.

## Evidence

**Evidence class:** `live render-verified (2026-07-25)`

- The current self-observability board has 34 panels but no single readiness/delivery/data-loss verdict.
- It can show successful collectors while OTLP delivery is rejected, or blank process-level panels because of tenant scoping.
- Recent `graph2otel.api.unexpected` bursts were visible only after manual inspection.

## Proposed scope

- Build a first-screen summary from readiness, exporter delivery, record reconciliation, checkpoint, lag, throttling, cardinality clipping, and schema-drift signals.
- Link each degraded state to its detailed row/runbook.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] The summary distinguishes source collection, internal processing, and backend delivery.
- [x] Known loss/degradation paths cannot render green.
- [x] Healthy-empty domains do not degrade exporter health.
- [x] Every verdict has a drilldown and documented calculation.

comments.body:
Implementation classification (`gpt-5.6-sol`, high reasoning, primary-owned): this is an operator-visible cross-signal verdict seam in `grafana/boards/selfobs.py`, with shared ordering/link tests in `grafana/boards/common.py` and `grafana/tests/test_build_dashboard.py`. No subagent or concurrent writer owns those files.

Frozen design:
- The first screen is a matrix, not one synthetic score. Source collection, source-to-emitter loss, exporter callbacks, checkpoint persistence, clipping, throttling, and API drift stay separate so one healthy dimension cannot erase another degraded one.
- `healthy_empty` is neutral. Disabled, covered, and `limited/partial_license` do not enter the source-failure calculation.
- `dropped|errored` outcomes are known source-to-emitter loss.
- Exporter callback success means exporter accepted, not backend retention or exactly-once delivery.
- Grafana cannot reproduce dependency-free local liveness or latched readiness when metrics are unavailable; the summary will state the `/readyz` and admin-status fallback rather than invent a readiness metric or private URL.
- Every summary dimension gets a same-dashboard drilldown preserving time and variables through Grafana-supported URL variables.

The TDD boundary pins each PromQL calculation, exclusion set, delivery/readiness wording, link target, and first-screen ordering. No new recording rule, private identifier, or production Grafana mutation is in this source wave.

Implemented and pushed in `b6efee6d8c667042dd402363f620f13465b2a08a` (`feat(dashboards): add executive health summary`).

Delivered:
- The first query row is an eight-dimension matrix rather than a synthetic score: current source failures, source-to-emitter record loss, exporter callback degradation, checkpoint persistence failures, source-event emission lag, cardinality clipping, Microsoft API assumption violations, and reported throttle consumption.
- `healthy_empty`, disabled, covered, `limited/partial_license`, and licence-unavailable states do not enter the source-failure expression. Missing series render as unknown and explicitly not a green verdict.
- Delivery wording is bounded to exporter callback acceptance; it does not claim backend retention or exactly-once delivery. A first-screen boundary panel points operators to `/readyz` and admin status when the metrics path is unavailable rather than fabricating a Grafana readiness verdict.
- Every verdict has one same-dashboard drilldown whose target panel exists and whose link preserves `from`, `to`, and all dashboard variables.
- Adversarial acceptance review caught the initially omitted event-lag dimension before commit; the TDD contract was extended RED then GREEN before regeneration.
