body:
## Outcome

An operator should have one entry point for exporter health, active findings, tenant scope, and navigation to Entra, Intune, Defender, M365, and Purview.

## Evidence

**Evidence class:** `render-verified opportunity (2026-07-25)`

- The live folder contains six independent dashboards with no landing page or cross-dashboard navigation.
- The repeated first-screen help panel consumes substantial space but does not orient the operator across domains.

## Proposed scope

- Create a small generated landing board with health/availability, highest-priority active conditions, and dashboard links.
- Preserve domain detail in existing boards.
- Replace repeated oversized help with compact shared documentation links.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] One folder entry point links to every domain and self-observability board.
- [ ] Tenant/time context is preserved where Grafana supports it.
- [ ] The first screen distinguishes exporter failure from domain posture.
- [ ] Repeated query-help content is compact and non-dominant.

## Prior decisions and duplicate check

- No existing issue covers a cross-domain navigation/triage surface.
- Related: #27, #28, #29, #218.

## Priority

Audit recommendation: **P2**.

comments.body:
Dependency/product blocker (2026-07-26): there is no landing UID or link primitive. A landing dashboard depends on #302 topology, #304 presentation semantics, #312's existing executive verdict dimensions, and #295 datasource defaults. Selecting “highest-priority active conditions” without those contracts would invent severity/health semantics.

**Recommendation:** one small stable-UID landing dashboard linking all five domains plus self-observability, reusing #312 verdict inputs rather than duplicating health logic, preserving time/tenant, and using only evidence-backed active conditions.

**Unblock condition:** #295/#302/#304 are approved and land, then Rob confirms the active-condition set/shared-verdict use. **Required human action / owner:** Rob (`rknightion`).

## 2026-07-27 — SUPERSEDED by #399; will close from the #399 completing commit

The maintainer's #399 topology decision is **one dashboard with six top-level domain tabs plus an `Overview` tab**. That `Overview` tab *is* the landing surface this issue asks for, so a separate landing dashboard is redundant: there is no longer a set of sibling dashboards needing an entry point.

The blocker recorded at https://github.com/rknightion/graph2otel/issues/311#issuecomment-5085158556 — "there is no landing UID or link primitive" — is dissolved rather than resolved. There is no cross-dashboard navigation problem left to solve.

### Surviving acceptance criteria have been transcribed to #399

Nothing is dropped. These three are now #399's contract (https://github.com/rknightion/graph2otel/issues/399#issuecomment-5089870787):

- The `Overview` tab distinguishes exporter failure from domain posture on the first screen.
- The `Overview` tab links to every domain tab and self-observability, preserving time and tenant context.
- The repeated oversized query-help panels become compact documentation links and are non-dominant.

The recorded recommendation to reuse #312's verdict inputs rather than duplicate health logic also carries forward to #399 — #312's executive health/data-loss matrix is the `Overview` tab's verdict source.

This issue stays open only until #399's completing commit closes it, so the criteria land with the code rather than ahead of it. No further work or decision is tracked here.

title: feat(dashboards): add a cross-domain graph2otel landing dashboard

body:
## Outcome

Operators should correlate metric/log changes with graph2otel upgrades and configuration rollouts directly on dashboards.

## Evidence

**Evidence class:** `render-verified opportunity (2026-07-25)`

- Live dashboards have no deployment/version annotation stream.
- Build metadata and structured application logs already contain enough provenance once the version-source defect is fixed.

## Proposed scope

- Generate a reusable annotation query from build/deployment events or structured logs.
- Show version, instance, and safe configuration-change provenance without secrets.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All six domain/self-observability dashboards show deployment markers.
- [ ] Markers identify version and tenant scope truthfully.
- [ ] No secret or full effective configuration is emitted.
- [ ] The annotation query is catalog/query-gated.

## Prior decisions and duplicate check

- No existing issue covers deployment/change annotations.
- Related: #9, #218, #263.

## Primary sources

- [https://grafana.com/docs/grafana/latest/dashboards/annotations/](https://grafana.com/docs/grafana/latest/dashboards/annotations/)

## Priority

Audit recommendation: **P3**.

comments.body:
Evidence-backed blocker (2026-07-26): live dashboards already carry externally injected `n8n changes` annotations, while source declares no deploy/config annotation contract. A safe in-app startup/config event needs a new telemetry field set and fingerprint/privacy definition; making the app or external automation authoritative produces different operator behavior.

**Recommendation:** hybrid ownership: external deployment automation remains authoritative for deploy annotations; graph2otel emits a process-wide startup/config-state event with version and a one-way safe configuration fingerprint, never secrets or raw config.

**Unblock condition:** Rob approves the hybrid ownership and exact safe field/fingerprint contract, then authorizes any external n8n annotation changes. **Required human action / owner:** Rob (`rknightion`) plus the private automation owner.

## Decision received 2026-07-27 — in-app ownership chosen AND scope deliberately expanded

Maintainer decision, verbatim: *"we should do in-app and expand this further to emit not only config state annotations to enrich the dashboards but also important entra/intune/graph/ms365 data that should get annotated onto dashboards and let users provide a grafana SA. I'll then delrecate the n8n approach"*

This selects **in-app ownership** over the recommended hybrid, and materially expands the contract beyond what this issue's body describes.

### What this issue (#310) now owns

Scoped to the in-app telemetry half, which is the part that fits this issue's existing acceptance criteria:

- graph2otel emits a process-wide **startup / config-state event** carrying its version and a **one-way safe configuration fingerprint** — never secrets, never the raw effective configuration.
- The dashboards render deploy/version/config-change markers from that event.
- The annotation query is catalog/query-gated, per #306's typed filter contract.
- Markers identify version and tenant scope truthfully.

The external-automation half is **dropped**: the maintainer will deprecate the n8n annotation injection, so the existing externally injected `n8n changes` annotations are not the long-term source and this issue must not build a dependency on them. Deprecating n8n is the maintainer's own action and is not tracked here.

### What is split out

Emitting curated Entra / Intune / Graph / M365 domain events as Grafana annotations, written by graph2otel itself using an operator-supplied Grafana service account, is a **new outbound integration with a new credential type**. That is not a variation of this issue — it is a new architectural surface, so it gets its own child issue rather than being absorbed here. See the successor issue linked below.

### Recorded invariant tension, resolved by explicit maintainer decision

graph2otel is **OTLP push only** — no Prometheus endpoint, no generic listener or output framework, no Event Hub, no Log Analytics pipeline. A Grafana Annotations API writer is a second egress path and therefore sits against that invariant.

The maintainer has explicitly asked for it, so the invariant is **narrowly amended**, not abandoned: annotations may be written directly to the Grafana API, and telemetry transport remains OTLP-push-only. Metrics and logs do not gain a second path. This amendment is recorded here and on the successor issue so a later reader does not mistake the annotation writer for permission to add other outputs.

### Sequencing

The startup/config-state event adds a signal, which couples it to the dashboard coverage gate and therefore to the #399 single-dashboard migration. This work is sequenced after #399 freezes the generator API rather than run concurrently with it.

## Closed by `8c80228`

`graph2otel.startup` is emitted once per configured tenant on every process start, and the dashboard renders
it as an annotation on every time axis in the estate.

### The four acceptance criteria

- [x] **Deployment markers on the whole estate.** One `AnnotationQuery` on the single v2 dashboard covers all
  7 tabs and 60 leaves — the original wording said "all six domain/self-observability dashboards", which the
  #399 migration retired. The marker also has a detail log panel on self-observability.
- [x] **Markers identify version and tenant scope truthfully.** `version` comes from the same
  `internal/version` source `build_info` reads, pinned equal by test. Records are tenant-stamped at the
  emitter boundary so markers follow the tenant dropdown instead of appearing on every tenant's axes.
- [x] **No secret and no raw effective configuration is emitted.**
- [x] **The annotation query is catalog/query-gated**, through the same selector builder and the same #306
  typed-filter validation as every log panel.

### Design decisions and why

**A log record, not a metric.** `graph2otel.build_info` already carries the build identity, and a fingerprint
label would mint a series per configuration for the lifetime of the backend. The `graph2otel` domain already
ships log panels, so this needed no waiver.

**The timestamp is process start**, a package-level `time.Now()` at init in the composition root — not the
emit site, which sits after config load and provider construction and would date the marker several hundred
milliseconds late, in the direction that puts the marker *after* the change it explains. A zero start time
emits nothing and returns an error rather than stamping arrival time.

**The fingerprint is deliberately over-sensitive.** SHA-256 over a domain-separated marshalling of the
*whole* config, truncated to 64 bits. Deny-list, not allow-list: an allow-list silently stops covering keys
added later, and a fingerprint that under-reports is worse than none. So a change that alters no behaviour
can still move it — the safe direction for a change marker.

**Credentials cannot reach the hash by construction, not by a maintained list.** Every credential on the
config surface is typed `config.Secret`, whose `MarshalJSON` emits `REDACTED`. Independently verified on this
thread: rotating a credential does not move the fingerprint, and the marshalled input carries the redaction
marker and not the secret. A rotated credential therefore produces no marker; unset-to-set does, because that
is a real behaviour change.

**One process-wide fingerprint, not one per tenant.** A per-tenant fingerprint over that tenant's subtree
would MISS a global `collectors:` change that does affect it. Over-reporting beats silently not firing.

**No `ingest_transport`.** That attribute names the transport that *ingested* a record and nothing ingested
this one; an `internal` value would pollute the attribute for every consumer grouping by it.

**"Configuration changed" is a comparison, not a field.** The marker fires on every start, so a config change
is two consecutive markers whose `config.fingerprint` differs and an upgrade is two whose `version` differs.
The annotation name, the panel description and the docs all say so rather than implying the marker itself
means "something changed".

**No configuration key gates it**, matching `build_info` which is also ungated. Volume is one record per
tenant per start, and a toggle's only real effect would be a deployment whose change markers silently stop
appearing. If you want a gate, it also pulls in `config.example.yaml`, the Helm `values.yaml` and
`values.schema.json`.

**Nothing declared to `wirecheck`**: every value is a local constant or a hash, so there is no bounded wire
value set to watch, and a watchdog with nothing to watch trains readers to ignore the signal.

### The signal

`graph2otel.startup`, log, severity INFO. Attributes: `version`, `go.version`, `config.fingerprint`
(16 hex chars), `config.tenant_count`, plus `tenant_id` stamped at the emitter boundary. The v2
`AnnotationQuery` shape was taken from a live v2 dashboard on a real stack rather than from documentation —
the dashboards API rejects a wrong enum member with a 422 that no local test can see.

Live read-back on `grafana.m7kni.com`, after publishing:

```
anno name   graph2otel starts, versions and config changes
anno expr   {service_name="graph2otel"} | event_name=`graph2otel.startup` | tenant_id=~"$tenant"
```

Note the shape: `{event_name=…}` would match **zero rows silently**, since every graph2otel log attribute is
structured metadata and `service_name` is the only stream label.

### Evidence

Fifteen sabotages across both halves, each failing and each restored: emitting a raw credential, bypassing
the type-level redaction, leaving the event time unset, accepting a zero start time, narrowing the fingerprint
to an allow-list, making it non-deterministic, omitting the version, giving the marker a second version
source, dropping tenant stamping, adding a metric alongside the log, renaming an attribute, unwiring it from
the composition root, a stale signal catalog, a misspelled annotation event, and a misspelled annotation
filter key.

The second version-source sabotage **passed on the first attempt** against the default `dev` version — the
test was strengthened until it failed for the right reason. Recorded because a sabotage that passes is the
only way to find a test that proves nothing.

`make check` exit 0 (vet, `-race` tests, 0 lint issues, govulncheck clean, tidy, tools, forks),
`make grafana-check` 322 tests, pinned zensical build clean.

### Not in scope here

#400 — the annotation *writer* using an operator-supplied Grafana service account — is untouched. The
contract it reuses is ready and stable: `startupevent.Fingerprint` is exported, and `EventName` /
`semconv.AttrConfigFingerprint` are public names. **graph2otel remains OTLP-push-only; no second egress path
was added by this work.**

The Loki read-back of a real `graph2otel.startup` record on a live tenant is a deploy-time step and has not
happened yet — the strongest local evidence is an end-to-end test through the real stdout exporter.

## Terminal CI receipt — `8c80228`

All 8 workflows **success**: CI, CodeQL, Docker Security, Release, Scorecard, actionlint, zizmor, Trigger Documentation Sync.

`make check` exit 0 and `make grafana-check` exit 0 locally at the same tree, with the pinned zensical build clean.

title: feat(dashboards): annotate graph2otel deploys, versions, and configuration changes

body:
## Outcome

Dashboard growth should not create an unbounded query fan-out or unusable render latency.

## Evidence

**Evidence class:** `source-derived from current asset scale (2026-07-26)`

- The current generated estate has 404 panels, including 136 on Intune and 90 on Entra; the original 347-panel count was stale.
- Exhaustive time-series panels can issue hundreds of range queries on load.
- The current gate counts coverage but has no panel/query/latency budget.

## Proposed scope

- Measure query count, repeated expressions, range cost, and representative render latency.
- Use rows, lazy loading, query reuse, recording rules, or explorer separation where measurement justifies them.

## Constraints and non-goals

- Do not add recording rules merely to make a synthetic benchmark green.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] A reproducible benchmark records current query and render baselines.
- [ ] Budgets are explicit per overview and explorer dashboard.
- [ ] Generation fails on material regressions or requires a reviewed waiver.
- [ ] Operational first-screen panels stay responsive.

## Prior decisions and duplicate check

- No prior issue covers dashboard query/render scalability.
- Related: #218, #263.

## Priority

Audit recommendation: **P3**.

comments.body:
Primary classification for the non-decision-gated baseline slice:

- **Issue:** #309.
- **Task / acceptance boundary:** add a reproducible, read-only baseline tool that inventories every generated dashboard's panels, rows, query targets, repeated expressions, default range/refresh and collapsed state, then optionally measures fixed-parameter live PNG render latency/bytes through `gcx dashboards snapshot`. It may record a current baseline receipt but must not choose numeric regression budgets, waiver policy, overview/explorer classification, CI credentials, or deployment schedule.
- **Files / exclusive owner:** primary owns a new standard-library `grafana/performance_baseline.py`, its focused tests, Make targets, and operator docs. Generated dashboards, builder/composition roots, workflows, live resources, and budget schemas remain untouched.
- **Dependencies/shared seams:** #302 defines overview/explorer topology; #295 defines default datasource behavior; #308 supplies the semantic query gate but not render budgets. Final per-class limits and enforcement remain downstream.
- **Risk:** high for final operator-visible budgets, low-to-medium for the bounded measurement harness; the primary retains both because the measurements feed a later policy decision.
- **Route:** `gpt-5.6-sol`, high reasoning, no dispatch.
- **Rationale:** the source inventory and fixed snapshot command are objectively testable, but interpreting measurements or setting failure thresholds would silently define an operator-visible performance contract.

Baseline-harness receipt for `871725c854f7daa1802140585862c1fef503b8c9` (`perf(dashboards): add reproducible baseline harness`):

- Added a deterministic standard-library source analyzer plus an optional read-only serial `gcx dashboards snapshot` lane. It records panel/row/query/target counts, instant/range modes, expression bytes, repeated expressions, fixed render parameters, elapsed time, and PNG bytes.
- Runtime variable values are never written to the receipt or error; snapshots use a temporary directory and are deleted. The tool neither creates nor updates a Grafana resource.
- Current source baseline: 6 dashboards, 404 panels, 59 rows (all expanded), 338 query panels, 374 targets (332 range, 42 instant), 372 unique expressions, 2 repeated expressions, and 39,135 expression bytes.
- `live-measured n=1 (2026-07-26, #309)`: fixed 6h, 1920x1080, dark, UTC, concurrency 1, wildcard tenant/collector; Defender 5.939s/117,122 bytes, Entra 6.737s/114,759 bytes, self-observability 5.093s/122,026 bytes, Intune 7.014s/118,263 bytes, M365 5.272s/116,685 bytes, Purview 5.849s/123,270 bytes. These are end-to-end Image Renderer measurements, not backend query latency, a percentile, or a budget.
- Live self-observability remains generation 6, updated 2026-07-26T11:38:50Z, so its timing measures the currently deployed older asset rather than current local source. The receipt does not launder that drift into a source-performance claim.
- Focused tests: 4 pass, including nested rows, target modes, repeated expressions, stable ordering, fixed serial command, temporary cleanup, operational failure, and runtime-value redaction.
- `make grafana-check`: 330/330 metrics, 404 panels, 14 alerts, 2 recording rules, 116 tests.
- `make check`: pass.
- `uvx --from zensical==0.0.46 zensical build --clean`: pass, no issues.

#309 remains open. A measurement harness is now reproducible, but numeric budgets and enforcement are intentionally not selected before #302 freezes overview/explorer topology.

**Unblock condition:** #302's topology is approved and implemented, then Rob selects per-overview and per-explorer target/render budgets, cold/warm percentile and variance, reviewed-waiver rules, and whether the credentialed render lane runs in deployment verification, a schedule, or both.

**Required human action / owner:** Rob (`rknightion`) owns the operator-visible budgets and waiver policy; Rob/infra owns any live credential, schedule, receipt retention, and failure route. Exact-tip GitHub Actions are pending and will be appended separately.

Post-push and deployment receipt for `871725c854f7daa1802140585862c1fef503b8c9`:

- [CI](https://github.com/rknightion/graph2otel/actions/runs/30217968993): success
- [CodeQL](https://github.com/rknightion/graph2otel/actions/runs/30217969167): success
- [Docker Security](https://github.com/rknightion/graph2otel/actions/runs/30217969161): success
- [Release](https://github.com/rknightion/graph2otel/actions/runs/30217969244): success
- [Scorecard](https://github.com/rknightion/graph2otel/actions/runs/30217969178): success
- [Trigger Documentation Sync](https://github.com/rknightion/graph2otel/actions/runs/30217968985): success
- [actionlint](https://github.com/rknightion/graph2otel/actions/runs/30217969171): success
- [zizmor](https://github.com/rknightion/graph2otel/actions/runs/30217969168): success
- Downstream [Build and Deploy Documentation](https://github.com/rknightion/m7kni-net-site/actions/runs/30217973022): success
- Production read-back: `https://m7kni.io/graph2otel/deploying-observability/` contains the Read-only semantic canary and Dashboard performance baseline sections, including `make grafana-performance-baseline`.

The landed harness and n=1 baseline are fully delivered. This issue remains open only for the recorded topology-dependent numeric budgets, waiver/enforcement contract, and human-owned live schedule/credential boundary. Unblock condition and owners remain as stated in the preceding receipt.

## 2026-07-27 — recorded baselines are now obsolete; re-measurement required

The maintainer's #399 topology decision retires all six dashboards in favour of one dashboard with nested domain tabs. The baseline this issue recorded at `871725c854f7daa1802140585862c1fef503b8c9` describes an estate that will not exist:

- Static: 6 dashboards, 404 panels, 59 rows (all expanded), 338 query panels, 374 targets, 372 unique expressions, 39,135 expression bytes.
- Live n=1 renders (2026-07-26, per-dashboard 5.09s–7.01s, ~115–123KB each).

**The harness itself remains valid and is the reason this is cheap to redo** — `grafana/performance_baseline.py` and `make grafana-performance-baseline` measure whatever the estate currently is. What is invalidated is the *numbers*, not the method. Two structural changes matter for re-measurement:

1. Rows will no longer all be expanded — nested tabs mean most content is not rendered on load, so panel count and render latency decouple in a way the current analyzer should be checked against.
2. Per-dashboard render timing becomes per-**tab** render timing. A single-dashboard estate has one cold-load cost plus a per-tab cost, so the "per overview and per explorer dashboard" framing in the acceptance criteria needs restating as per-tab.

### Status

Still blocked, with the dependency updated: **#399 must land**, then the baseline is re-measured on the new topology, and only then are numeric budgets selectable. The previously recorded dependency on #302's topology is satisfied by the #399 decision.

Unblock condition: #399 lands and the baseline is re-measured; then Rob selects per-tab target and render budgets, cold/warm percentile and variance, waiver rules, and whether the credentialed render lane runs in deployment verification, on a schedule, or both. Owner: Rob for the numbers; named infra owner for scheduled live execution.

Acceptance criterion 1 ("a reproducible benchmark records current query and render baselines") stays ticked — the harness is delivered — but its recorded receipt must be refreshed post-#399 before budgets are set.

## Baseline re-measured on the post-#399 estate — the numbers the budget decision needs

The recorded baseline described six dashboards that no longer exist. Re-measured against
`dashboards/graph2otel.json` at `d94458b`, via the harness this issue already shipped
(`make grafana-performance-baseline`), which was itself repaired for v2 as part of #399.

### Static receipt (`status: measured`)

| dimension | old (6 v1 dashboards) | **new (1 v2 dashboard)** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| dashboards | 6 | **1** |
| tabs | — | **7** |
| leaf tabs | — | **60** |
| panels | 404 | **348** |
| rows | 59, all expanded | **60**, 0 collapsed |
| query panels | 338 | **340** |
| targets | 374 | **376** (332 range, 44 instant, 0 unknown-mode) |
| unique expressions | — | **374** |
| expression bytes | 39,135 | **39,367** |

The panel drop reconciles exactly and is not a loss of content: 404 v1 panels included 59 row panels,
which no longer exist as panels; the shared 12-row preamble was repeated on all six boards and is now
one compact panel on Overview, with each domain keeping a 4-row "About" panel; Overview adds the census
plus the query guide. `404 − 59 − 6 + 6 + 2 = 347`, plus the one new expected-interval panel from #299
= **348**.

Only two expressions repeat across the whole estate (an event-lag p95 and an OTLP delivery-degraded
ratio, twice each), so there is very little duplicate-query headroom to reclaim.

### The structural change that matters most for a budget

**Panel count and render cost have decoupled.** Under v1, all 59 rows were expanded, so opening a
dashboard meant every one of its panels queried at once — panel count *was* the cost. Under v2 only the
active leaf tab renders: an operator opening the Entra tab pays for **one of 12 leaves**, not for 348
panels. The largest leaf, not the estate, is now the unit of cost.

That makes a whole-dashboard budget meaningless and a **per-leaf** budget the right shape. The
distribution across the 60 leaves is what a budget should be set against, and it is heavily skewed —
`Signal availability` leaves carry 2 panels, while the largest content leaves carry considerably more.

### What I cannot measure yet, and why

The live render lane needs a credentialed stack with a **real datasource**, because render latency with
no data measures nothing. Two obstacles, neither of which I will resolve unilaterally:

- The dashboard is **not published** to the m7kni stack, and live publication remains unauthorised.
- A disposable local Grafana renders it correctly — I verified that during #399 — but with no
  Prometheus or Loki behind it, so its timings would be pure frontend cost and would understate a real
  tab by however long its queries take.

So the numeric render budget cannot be set from evidence today. **The static budget can be**, and it is
the half that catches the realistic regression: a board module quietly adding thirty panels to one leaf.

### Decision needed from the maintainer

Recorded here so the ask is durable rather than living only in a chat:

1. **Per-leaf panel and target ceiling** — my recommendation is to gate on the *largest leaf*, not the
   estate total, with the ceiling set from the current distribution plus deliberate headroom, and a
   named waiver for a leaf that legitimately exceeds it. This is enforceable in CI today with no
   credentials.
2. **Whether the credentialed render lane runs at all**, and if so whether in deployment verification,
   on a schedule, or both — and against what stack, given the publication constraint above.
3. **Cold/warm percentile and variance**, which only becomes answerable once (2) is decided and a real
   measurement exists.

Proceeding on (1) alone would leave this issue's render half open but would deliver the enforceable
part. Awaiting the maintainer's call on which of the three to build now.

## Static half landed — `96d3ebf`. Render half stays open with a named blocker.

Maintainer decision 2026-07-27: **per-leaf ceiling in CI now**, credentialed render lane deferred.

### What shipped

`LEAF_PANEL_CEILING = 24`, gated in `build_dashboard.py --check`, so it runs on every
`make grafana-check` and in CI. Chosen as the measured maximum (18) plus deliberate headroom, from the
re-measured distribution: 60 leaves, median 5, largest 18 (`Endpoint analytics (UXA)`).

`make grafana-check` now prints `largest leaf 18/24 panels` on every run, so the remaining margin is
**visible continuously** rather than discovered on the day it runs out.

`LEAF_WAIVERS` is empty and takes a leaf title plus a **reason**. Two further checks keep the list
honest, both of which matter more than the ceiling itself:

- a waiver for a leaf now **within** budget is reported — it would otherwise silently re-permit the
  regression it was written for;
- a waiver naming a leaf that **no longer exists** is reported, so it cannot outlive its subject.

Verified by sabotage rather than by reading: lowering the ceiling to 10 fails the build and names all
6 offending leaves with their counts.

### Why per-leaf and not per-dashboard — the load-bearing reason

Restating it here because it is the thing a future reader will want to change and should not: under v1
all 59 rows were expanded, so opening a dashboard queried every panel on it and panel count *was* the
cost. Under v2 only the active leaf renders. An estate-wide total of 348 would gate a number no operator
ever pays.

### Render half — open, with the blocker named

No numeric render budget can be set from evidence today:

- Render latency against an **empty** Grafana measures only frontend cost and understates a real tab by
  however long its queries take. The disposable-Grafana render check from #399 is fine for *correctness*
  and useless for *latency*.
- The dashboard is **not published** to a credentialed stack, and live publication remains unauthorised.

**Unblock condition:** either authorise publication to a stack with real Prometheus and Loki behind it,
or stand up a disposable Grafana with seeded datasources. **Owner:** Rob for the publication decision.

Until then the enforceable half is enforced, which is also the half that catches the realistic
regression. Cold/warm percentile and variance are not decidable before that measurement exists, so they
are deliberately not guessed here.

This issue stays open on the render lane only. No repository change is pending on it.

## Terminal CI receipt — `96d3ebf`

All workflows **success** for the commit that landed per-leaf panel budget gated in CI: CI, CodeQL, Docker Security, Release, Scorecard, actionlint, zizmor.

`make check` exit 0 and `make grafana-check` exit 0 locally at the same tree.

## Decision received 2026-07-27 — render lane approved against the m7kni stack, with one prerequisite

Maintainer decision, verbatim: *"for 309 we can likely use my grafana stack the grafana.m7kni.com one and
you can store the grafana read SA in github ci secrets with a properly protected workflow (it's read only
anyway)."*

Approved: measure render latency against the real stack from a scheduled, protected GitHub Actions
workflow using a **read-only** Grafana service account.

### Two corrections to the plan before it is built

**1. A read-only SA can render, but the dashboard has to be there first.** `gcx dashboards snapshot`
renders a dashboard that already exists on the stack, by name. `dashboards/graph2otel.json` has **never
been published** to m7kni — the whole migration was verified on a disposable local Grafana — and a
read-only token cannot create it. So the render lane cannot measure anything until `graph2otel` is
published to that stack once.

That publication is a **live mutation of the maintainer's production Grafana**, which is exactly the
class of action this programme requires explicit authorisation for, and the approval above is about the
*measurement*, not the publication. It is also not a trivial one: it is the first time the v2 dashboard
would exist on that stack, replacing nothing (the six v1 UIDs were retired in the repo, but whatever is
currently on the stack is untouched and unaudited by me).

**Still needed:** explicit authorisation to publish `graph2otel` to `grafana.m7kni.com`, or a decision
that the maintainer publishes it by hand and the render lane simply assumes it is present and skips
cleanly when it is not. **Owner:** Rob.

**2. Reuse the existing service account rather than minting a second.** #308 already provisioned a
read-only SA on that stack (id 36) for the semantic canary, with its URL and token already in this
repo's GitHub secrets. A second read-only SA for the render lane would double the credential surface for
no benefit and give two things to rotate instead of one.

**Recommendation:** the render lane reuses the #308 canary credentials. If the render endpoint turns out
to need a permission the canary SA lacks, extend that SA — deliberately, recorded here — rather than
creating a parallel one.

### Workflow shape, mirroring the #308 canary (which is already proven)

- Scheduled plus `workflow_dispatch`; `permissions: contents: read` only.
- Every action SHA-pinned, and the `gcx` download checksum hardcoded and fail-closed — **not** verified
  against a checksums file fetched in the same request, which would prove nothing.
- Distinct exit codes for pass, budget breach, and operational error, so a stack outage never reads as a
  performance regression. This mattered on #308 and matters more here, since render timing is inherently
  noisier than a query probe.
- Artifacts retained; no external notifier.

### What is already enforced, and what this adds

The **static** half landed in `96d3ebf`: a per-leaf ceiling of 24 panels, gated on every
`make grafana-check` and in CI with no credentials required. That is the half that catches the realistic
regression.

This render lane adds the numbers the static gate cannot see — actual per-tab latency against real
Prometheus and Loki. Note that cold/warm percentile and variance still cannot be chosen until it has run
enough times to show a distribution; setting a latency budget from the first measurement would be
picking a threshold from n=1, which is exactly what this issue was opened to avoid.

## AUTHORISATION GRANTED 2026-07-27 — publish to production Grafana, and reuse the #308 token

Maintainer, verbatim: *"its fine for you to push to my prod grafana using the right gcx context."* and
*"sure youc an re use the token"*.

This is the standing authorisation the render lane was blocked on. Recording it here because it is a
**live-mutation authorisation for production**, and a decision of that class must be reconstructible from
GitHub alone rather than living in a chat transcript.

### What is authorised

- **Publishing generated Grafana assets to the production stack** — `grafana.m7kni.com` — using `gcx`
  with the correct context explicitly pinned.
- **Reusing the existing #308 read-only service account** (id 36) and its already-provisioned GitHub
  secrets for the render lane, rather than minting a second read-only account.

### Constraints that still apply, and are NOT relaxed by the above

- **Pin the context explicitly on every invocation**: `gcx --context grafana.m7kni.com …`. `gcx`'s
  current-context was found pointing at an **unrelated customer stack** earlier today, which returns 221
  rules and no graph2otel rule group — a state that reads exactly like "the resources are gone". Never
  rely on the ambient context for a write.
- **Read before write.** The v2 dashboard has never existed on that stack, and whatever dashboards and
  rules are on it now have not been audited by me. Enumerate and record what is there before creating or
  updating anything.
- **Create-or-update by stable identity**, never delete-then-create. `metadata.name` is the v2 dashboard
  identity; the six retired v1 UIDs are separate objects and are **not** to be removed as part of a
  publish — retiring them on the live stack is a separate, separately-recorded decision.
- The **read-only** SA stays read-only. Publishing uses the maintainer's own authenticated `gcx`
  context; the CI render lane keeps the read-only credential and must never be given write.
- Every publish records a **live read-back receipt** on the owning issue: what was created or updated,
  its identity, and the post-publish state.

### What this unblocks

- **#309's render lane.** The dashboard can now be published to the stack the render measurement runs
  against, so per-tab latency becomes measurable. The static per-leaf budget is already enforced
  (`96d3ebf`).
- Any later live verification that needed the v2 dashboard present on a real stack with real datasources.

### What it does NOT authorise

New Graph permissions, new RBAC, licence or feature enablement, tenant data generation, or removal of
existing live Grafana resources. Those remain individually gated.

## Render lane landed `5fb7873` — and the dashboard is now PUBLISHED to production

Two things happened here. The render lane exists, and its prerequisite is satisfied.

### 1. `graph2otel` is live on `grafana.m7kni.com`

Under the standing authorisation recorded above. Read-back receipt:

| | |
| --- | --- |
| `metadata.name` | `graph2otel` |
| uid | `<guid-1>` |
| folder | `efs83nfy641s0c` — title **graph2otel**, created 2026-07-15 by `robknight1` |
| `managedBy` | none — **not** GitSync-managed, so no repo sync can reap it |
| generation | 2 — created, then **updated in place** by name; never delete-then-create |
| elements / tabs / leaves | 350 / 7 / 60 |
| annotations | 1 (#310's deploy marker) |

Semantic equality against source: `title`, `description`, `tags`, `cursorSync`, `editable`, `layout`,
`variables`, `timeSettings` and `annotations` all match. `elements` differ only by server-side normalisation,
audited field by field — 376 dropped `PanelQuery.spec.datasource`, 69 dropped empty `custom: {}`, 8 added
empty `fieldConfig` on text panels. **Nothing functional was lost**: the authoritative
`query.spec.datasource.name = "${datasource}"` is preserved on every query, so the datasource variable binding
survives. The outer `datasource` is a v1 leftover the server strips — noted below as a generator cleanup.

The six retired v1 dashboards were **not** touched, per the authorisation.

### 2. Two corrections to what this issue previously recorded

**`gcx ... list` defaults to `--limit 50` and truncates silently.** This is a trap that produces confident
wrong answers rather than errors, and it caught me twice in one session:

| read | default | `--limit 0` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `dashboards list` | 50 dashboards, **zero graph2otel boards** | **186**, all six v1 boards present |
| `alert rules list` | 50 groups / 256 rules, **no `graph2otel-alerts` group** | 110 groups / **444 rules**, `graph2otel-alerts` = 12 |

I was one step from filing a "the live rule group is gone" correction against #294's recorded `live-measured`
fact — which was **correct**. Always pass `--limit 0`, and treat a result of exactly 50 as proof of truncation
rather than as a count. Cross-checking an absence against something you know exists in the same read is what
exposed it (`entra-security-g2o` appeared while `graph2otel-alerts` did not).

Also: a substring search over a listing is not an inventory. `graph2otel-intune-fleet` is titled
`Intune Fleet Overview` with no prefix, so grepping titles found 5 of 6. Enumerate by folder.

**Earlier in this session I stated there were zero graph2otel dashboards on the stack and therefore nothing to
retire. That was WRONG**, caused by the truncation above. All six v1 boards are live in the `graph2otel`
folder. Retiring them remains a separate, unmade decision and is now a real one rather than moot — the v2
dashboard sits beside them, so an operator currently sees seven graph2otel dashboards where one is current.

### 3. What the render lane does, and deliberately does not do

Daily 07:07 UTC plus `workflow_dispatch`, `permissions: contents: read`, every action SHA-pinned, gcx
checksum hardcoded and fail-closed (identical version and digest to the #308 canary, so there is one thing to
bump). Reuses the #308 read-only service account and its existing secrets — no second credential. Read-only
permanently.

**No latency budget is set.** The plumbing is built and tested end to end — flag, comparison, distinct exit
code — and left unset, so every run reports `not_configured`, always a clean pass. Setting a number from the
first measurement is precisely what this issue exists to avoid.

Three exit codes, so a stack outage can never read as a performance regression: `0` pass, `1` a configured
budget breached, `2` the lane could not run.

**Absent-dashboard handling is not cosmetic.** Measured against the live stack: `gcx dashboards snapshot` of a
name that does not exist **exits 0** and silently renders Grafana's own "Dashboard not found" page as a PNG,
indistinguishable from a real measurement. Existence is therefore checked with `dashboards get` first. That
path is now moot for `graph2otel` specifically, but it is the correct behaviour and it is what stopped the
first scheduled run from recording a fiction.

**Per-tab measurement is not possible today**, documented rather than faked. Tab navigation is a URL query
parameter; the snapshot command's only hooks are `--var` (template variables) and `--panel` (one panel by
id). Neither selects a tab. So the lane measures the whole-dashboard render and says so — which means the
per-leaf framing in this issue's acceptance criteria is satisfiable only by the static gate for now.

### Status: still open, blocker changed

The blocker was "the dashboard is not published and publication is unauthorised". **That is cleared.** The
remaining blocker is arithmetic, not permission:

**Unblock condition:** the scheduled lane needs to run enough times to show a distribution before a percentile,
a variance and a numeric budget can be chosen. One run is n=1. **Owner:** Rob, for the numbers, once the
artifact history exists. Nothing is pending in the repository.

Acceptance criteria 2 and 3 are satisfied for the *static* half (per-leaf ceiling of 24, gated in CI, largest
leaf currently 18) and open for the render half.

### Follow-up for #294, not for here

The generator emits a `PanelQuery.spec.datasource` that the server discards on every one of 376 queries. It is
harmless but it guarantees the committed artifact can never be byte-equal to what the stack stores, which
makes #294's semantic read-back comparison noisier than it needs to be. Removing it belongs with #294's
read-back work, where the comparison is actually built — not as churn now, since it would require a
re-publish and re-verification.

## First real render measurement — the lane works end to end against production

Manually dispatched immediately after publishing:
[run 30284122263](https://github.com/rknightion/graph2otel/actions/runs/30284122263), **success**.

```json
{"name": "graph2otel", "status": "measured",
 "attempts": [{"elapsed_seconds": 5.929016, "png_bytes": 151013,
               "variable_names": ["datasource", "loki_datasource", "tenant"]}],
 "budget": {"budget_seconds": null, "status": "not_configured"}}
```

Fixed parameters: 6h range, 1920x1080, dark, UTC, concurrency 1, repeat 1.

Note what the receipt does and does not contain: three variable **names**, and no variable **values**. The
redaction holds on a real credentialed run, not just in the unit test.

### What this number is, and what it is not

**5.93s end to end, against real Prometheus and Loki, with `n=1`.** That is a data point, not a budget, and
this issue exists specifically so it does not become one. For orientation only, the pre-migration n=1
per-dashboard figures on 2026-07-26 were 5.09s–7.01s across six separate v1 dashboards; 5.93s for the single
v2 dashboard sits inside that band. Do **not** read that as "no regression" — different topology, different
estate, one sample each, and a v2 dashboard renders only its active tab.

It is also whole-dashboard, i.e. the default first tab, for the reason recorded above: `gcx dashboards
snapshot` cannot select a `dtab`.

The daily 07:07 UTC schedule now accumulates the distribution. A percentile, a variance and a numeric budget
become choosable once that history exists.

### Status unchanged: open, blocker is arithmetic

**Unblock condition:** enough scheduled runs to show a distribution, then Rob picks the per-tab budget,
cold/warm percentile and variance, and waiver rules. **Owner:** Rob for the numbers. Nothing is pending in the
repository, and the static per-leaf ceiling (24, largest leaf 18) is already enforced in CI on every run.

## Closed — `cf8932b`. Tripwire shipped; and the six v1 dashboards are already gone

### The budget question, answered without inventing a percentile

The render lane had been running with no budget, so every run reported `not_configured`. That was the right call at n=1 — a threshold picked from one measurement is precisely what this issue was opened to avoid. But waiting for a distribution would have parked the issue indefinitely, so the maintainer's decision is a **breakage tripwire** at **30s**, and the distinction is recorded in both the workflow header and the operator docs so nobody later mistakes it for a tuned number:

- It is **not** a percentile, **not** derived from a distribution, and says nothing about what good looks like.
- Measured renders sit near 6s — 5.09–7.01s across the six v1 dashboards (2026-07-26) and 5.93s for the single v2 dashboard (2026-07-27) — so 30s is roughly **5x observed** and will not fire on ordinary variance, a cold renderer, or a slow morning.
- What it catches is the failure this lane can actually have: a render that has **stopped working** — runaway query fan-out, a hanging renderer, a datasource timing out behind the dashboard. Those cost tens of seconds, not hundreds of milliseconds.

Both the workflow and the docs carry an explicit instruction **not to tighten it toward the observed figure** without real artifact history. A threshold set just above the last measurement is how a lane starts crying wolf, and this programme's own rule is that an alert firing on correct data is worse than no alert.

The three exit codes still separate the cases that matter: `0` pass (including `skipped_absent`), `1` the tripwire breached, `2` the lane could not run — so a stack outage can never read as a performance regression.

### Acceptance criteria

- [x] A reproducible benchmark records current query and render baselines — the harness, re-measured post-#399.
- [x] Budgets are explicit — static per-leaf ceiling of **24** (largest leaf **18**), enforced on every `make grafana-check` with no credentials, plus the 30s render tripwire.
- [x] Generation fails on material regressions or requires a reviewed waiver — `LEAF_WAIVERS` takes a leaf title plus a reason, and reports both a waiver that is now within budget and one naming a leaf that no longer exists.
- [x] Operational first-screen panels stay responsive — the per-leaf model is what makes this measurable at all: under v2 only the active leaf renders, so the largest leaf is the unit of cost rather than the 348-panel estate total.

### The standing item recorded here is resolved, and the last recorded state was wrong

This issue recorded that all six retired v1 dashboards were still live beside the v2 one, so an operator saw seven graph2otel dashboards where one was current, and that retiring them was an unmade decision. The maintainer authorised the deletion this session ("any v1 stuff can be nuked once rolled into v2").

**There was nothing to delete — all six are already absent.** Measured 2026-07-27, context pinned, `--limit 0`:

| check | result |
| --- | --- |
| dashboards in folder `efs83nfy641s0c` | **1** — `graph2otel`, `dashboard.grafana.app/v2` |
| stack total | 181 (was recorded as 186) |
| name/title scan across all 181 for graph2otel/g2o/entra/intune/purview/defender | **only** `graph2otel` |
| `graph2otel-defender-security` | 404 NotFound |
| `graph2otel-entra-compliance` | 404 NotFound |
| `graph2otel-self-obs` | 404 NotFound |
| `intune-fleet-overview` | 404 NotFound |
| `graph2otel-m365-services` | 404 NotFound |
| `graph2otel-purview-compliance` | 404 NotFound |

Each UID was checked with an individual `dashboards get`, **not** inferred from the listing — a listing is what produced the two earlier wrong conclusions on this issue, in both directions.

So the correction recorded here on 2026-07-27 ("all six v1 boards are live… retiring them is now a real decision rather than moot") is itself **no longer true**. I did not delete them and cannot say from here when or by whom they went; the current state is measured and unambiguous. The authorisation stands and is simply unused.

### Nothing left in the repository

The static gate is enforced, the render lane has a tripwire, and the daily 07:07 UTC schedule continues to accumulate artifact history for anyone who later wants a real percentile. No pending work.

title: perf(dashboards): add a generated query and render performance budget

body:
## Outcome

CI/deployment validation should catch wrong datasource selection, missing labels, evaluator failures, and empty-by-construction queries that static token coverage cannot.

## Evidence

**Evidence class:** `live audit finding (2026-07-25)`

- Static gates were green while all six dashboards opened on the wrong datasources.
- Tenant-filtered process-level self-observability panels were blank despite metric-name coverage.
- Past #82 failures also required live normalized-name validation.

## Proposed scope

- Define a small read-only canary suite over representative metric, histogram, log, recording, and alert queries.
- Run it in a disposable/current Grafana or a deliberately configured integration environment.
- Keep fixture assertions semantic rather than dependent on the current tenant's exact values.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] The suite fails for wrong datasource UIDs, missing required labels, invalid query syntax, and evaluator errors.
- [x] Healthy-empty optional signals are represented without false failures.
- [x] Deployment read-back records query receipts.
- [x] No live state mutation is required.
- [ ] A maintainer-owned deployment or schedule runs the suite with a least-privilege credential and retains/routes failed receipts.

## Prior decisions and duplicate check

- Not duplicate of #218/#219 static generation gates; this validates runtime query semantics.
- Related: #82, #218, #219, #263.

## Priority

Audit recommendation: **P2**.

comments.body:
Dispatch classification for the source-only canary inventory:

- **Issue:** #308.
- **Task / acceptance boundary:** inventory current generated PromQL/LogQL/rule objects and CI/gcx seams, then propose the smallest versioned read-only semantic canary manifest and runner whose outcomes distinguish required-nonempty, healthy-empty, syntax/evaluator failure, datasource mismatch, and missing required labels. Deliver exact candidate files/tests/commands; stop at any credential, schedule, backend-ownership, or operator-visible policy choice.
- **Files / exclusive owner:** read-only across `grafana/`, `dashboards/`, `alerts/`, `recording-rules/`, `.github/workflows/`, `Makefile`, and relevant docs; no file ownership and no edits.
- **Dependencies/shared seams:** #294 deployment format, #295 datasource selection, #297 recording semantics, #301 tenant preservation, and the private target/credential/schedule decision remain primary-owned.
- **Risk:** low for bounded source inventory; eventual live gate and credential design are high-risk and excluded.
- **Route:** `gpt-5.6-terra`, medium reasoning.
- **Rationale:** the lane is mechanically bounded and every claim is objectively verifiable against committed source; it cannot define the live execution contract.

Source/deployment-readback receipt for `8a9d4b3f5350715729846dfc8317d88bc9edf2e2` (`feat(gate): add live semantic Grafana canary`):

- Added a closed, versioned six-probe manifest and standard-library runner. `gcx` remains the sole context/auth/query owner; the repository accepts no token, URL, arbitrary command, or private datasource UID.
- The runner preflights Prometheus/Loki datasource types, distinguishes required-nonempty from healthy-empty, checks required labels on every returned series, detects backend query errors separately from auth/transport failures, and verifies one stable alert UID is healthy and has evaluated against the selected datasource.
- Offline tests include wrong datasource type, unexpected/healthy empty, missing labels, PromQL parse rejection, auth/transport separation, evaluator error, never-evaluated/missing/duplicate rule behavior, exact read-only command construction, and source-to-manifest drift checks.
- `make grafana-check`: 330/330 metrics, 404 panels, 14 alerts, 2 recording rules, 112 tests.
- `make check`: pass.
- `uvx --from zensical==0.0.46 zensical build --clean`: pass, no issues.
- `live-measured (2026-07-26, #308)`: a read-only m7kni run passed both datasource preflights and all six probes: collector availability 151 series, event-lag histogram 17, collector staleness 124, compliance log healthy-empty, compliance recording metric healthy-empty, and `g2o-collector-staleness` evaluator health `ok` with a current evaluation timestamp. A deliberate invalid PromQL query was rejected by the live backend and correctly classified by the runner contract. No Grafana or tenant resource was created, updated, or deleted.

#308 remains open only for the production execution boundary. The repository now has an opt-in, machine-readable gate, but no approved workflow target, credential, schedule, receipt retention, or failure-routing owner.

**Unblock condition:** Rob/infra selects the Grafana environment, provisions a least-privilege read-only credential for its chosen execution environment, and chooses schedule/deployment hook, receipt retention, and failure routing.

**Required human action / owner:** Rob (`rknightion`) owns the target and operator-visible failure route; the named infra owner then provisions the credential. No deliberate tenant data is required by the shipped probe set. Exact-tip GitHub Actions are pending and will be appended separately.

Post-push verification for `8a9d4b3f5350715729846dfc8317d88bc9edf2e2` is terminal-success:

- CI: https://github.com/rknightion/graph2otel/actions/runs/30217505015
- CodeQL: https://github.com/rknightion/graph2otel/actions/runs/30217505244
- Docker Security: https://github.com/rknightion/graph2otel/actions/runs/30217505223
- Release: https://github.com/rknightion/graph2otel/actions/runs/30217505317
- Scorecard: https://github.com/rknightion/graph2otel/actions/runs/30217505240
- actionlint: https://github.com/rknightion/graph2otel/actions/runs/30217505229
- zizmor: https://github.com/rknightion/graph2otel/actions/runs/30217505255
- Trigger Documentation Sync: https://github.com/rknightion/graph2otel/actions/runs/30217505016

The source-only canary and live read-back are fully verified. The issue remains open only for the production execution ownership blocker in the preceding receipt.

## 2026-07-27 — credential provisioned; the last acceptance criterion is in progress

Maintainer decision: **scheduled GitHub Actions run**, with the note *"I believe you can use gcx to
provision the SA you need against my <grafana-host-1> stack"*. Taken as authorisation to provision.

### Service account provisioned (live change, completed)

| field | value |
| --- | --- |
| name | `graph2otel-semantic-canary` |
| id | `36` |
| login | `sa-1-graph2otel-semantic-canary` |
| basic role | **Viewer** — read-only |
| disabled | no |
| token name | `github-actions-canary` (token id `1181`) |

`Viewer` is the least privilege that still satisfies the canary's needs: it can query datasources and
read alert rules, and it can write nothing. A search confirmed no prior `graph2otel*` service account
existed, so this is not a duplicate.

**The token value was never printed, logged, or written to disk.** It was piped directly from the
creation response into `gh secret set`. Only its length (46) and its `glsa_` prefix were observed. If
it needs rotating, delete token id `1181` on service account `36` and repeat.

### Repository secrets set

- `GRAFANA_CANARY_TOKEN` — the service-account token.
- `GRAFANA_CANARY_URL` — the stack base URL, kept as a secret rather than hard-coded, so the private
  infrastructure hostname stays out of this public repository.

The two datasource names the canary needs (`grafanacloud-prom`, `grafanacloud-logs`) are the portable
Grafana Cloud defaults already committed in `grafana/builder.py` by #295, so they are not secrets.

### Non-interactive auth path confirmed

`gcx login --yes <context> --server <url> --token glsa_...` is the supported non-interactive form, so
the existing `make grafana-canary GRAFANA_CONTEXT=... GRAFANA_PROMETHEUS_DATASOURCE=...
GRAFANA_LOKI_DATASOURCE=...` target works unchanged in CI. No change to `semantic_canary.py` is
expected.

### In progress

`.github/workflows/grafana-canary.yml`: scheduled plus `workflow_dispatch`, artifact-retained receipts,
and the three exit codes surfaced distinctly (0 passed, 1 semantic failure, 2 operational error) — an
auth or transport error must not read as a semantic regression. Consistent with #293/#296, the workflow
adds **no external notifier or webhook**: the failing run is the notification surface.

### Acceptance criteria

- [x] The suite fails for wrong datasource UIDs, missing required labels, invalid query syntax, and evaluator errors.
- [x] Healthy-empty optional signals are represented without false failures.
- [x] Deployment read-back records query receipts.
- [ ] A maintainer-owned deployment or schedule runs the suite with a least-privilege credential and retains/routes failed receipts — credential and secrets now in place; workflow pending.

The first successful scheduled run against production is the closing evidence for this issue.

## Closing receipt — `860eb4025491f5846dbb94f52537072975feda49`

The final acceptance criterion is met and **verified by a real run against production**, not by the
workflow merely existing.

### The proving run

[Run 30260745127](https://github.com/rknightion/graph2otel/actions/runs/30260745127) — `workflow_dispatch`
on `main`, conclusion **success**:

- `gcx version 0.6.0 built from 17c85787a0cbf1ff942ed83e4b724eb1a96fd2b6` — the pinned, checksum-verified
  install resolved and ran.
- Authenticated as the least-privilege `graph2otel-semantic-canary` service account (Viewer, read-only).
- **All six probes returned `"status": "passed"`**, overall `"status": "passed"`, `CANARY_EXIT_CODE: 0`.
- Receipt uploaded as artifact `grafana-semantic-canary-receipt`.

So the credential works, the install path works, the canary reaches the real datasources, and the whole
lane is reproducible on a schedule.

### What shipped

`.github/workflows/grafana-canary.yml` — daily at 05:12 UTC plus `workflow_dispatch`, `permissions:
contents: read` only, both actions pinned to full commit SHAs, `actionlint` clean and `zizmor` reporting
no findings.

**Install integrity.** `gcx` ships no first-party GitHub Action. Its own README CI snippet resolves
`latest` unpinned, and its `install.sh` is fetched from a branch rather than a commit, so neither is
reproducible. Instead the workflow downloads one pinned release tag's `linux_amd64` archive and verifies
it against a sha256 **hardcoded in the workflow** rather than a `checksums.txt` fetched in the same
request — so a reissued or tampered asset fails closed instead of validating against itself. The pinned
digest was confirmed locally against the published checksums file before being committed.

**Three outcomes, three signals.** `semantic_canary.py` exits 0 passed / 1 semantic failure / 2
operational error. The workflow captures stdout and stderr separately, never fails the run step itself so
the artifact always uploads first, then maps the code to a distinct job summary. An operational error is
stated explicitly as **not** evidence that a monitored datasource or alert is unhealthy — collapsing that
into a generic red X is exactly how a canary trains people to ignore it.

**Receipt retention:** 30 days, both the JSON receipt and stderr diagnostics, `if-no-files-found: error`
so a silently empty upload fails.

**Failure routing:** the failing run is the notification surface. No external notifier, webhook, or
contact point — the same #293/#296 decision, applied consistently.

### Credential, for the record

Service account `graph2otel-semantic-canary` (id 36, login `sa-1-graph2otel-semantic-canary`, basic role
**Viewer**), token `github-actions-canary` (id 1181). The token value was piped directly from the creation
response into `gh secret set` and was never printed, logged, or written to disk. Secrets
`GRAFANA_CANARY_TOKEN` and `GRAFANA_CANARY_URL` are set on the repository; the stack hostname is a secret
rather than committed, so no private infrastructure identifier enters this public repository.

To rotate: delete token id 1181 on service account 36, create a replacement, and re-set
`GRAFANA_CANARY_TOKEN`.

### Acceptance criteria

- [x] The suite fails for wrong datasource UIDs, missing required labels, invalid query syntax, and evaluator errors.
- [x] Healthy-empty optional signals are represented without false failures.
- [x] Deployment read-back records query receipts.
- [x] A maintainer-owned deployment or schedule runs the suite with a least-privilege credential and retains/routes failed receipts.

Local gates before push: `make check` exit 0, `make grafana-check` exit 0, 135 Python tests OK,
`actionlint` clean, `zizmor` no findings.

The commit used `Refs #308` rather than a closing keyword deliberately — the workflow existing is not the
same as the workflow working, so this issue is closed by hand only now that the production run is green.

body:
## Outcome

Every enabled alert should link directly to an actionable runbook and relevant dashboard/panel with accurate prose.

## Evidence

**Evidence class:** `source-derived and live read-back (2026-07-25)`

- Generated annotations contain summary/description only; no rule has runbook, dashboard UID, or panel ID metadata.
- Descriptions refer to `README doc block N`, which is not clickable from Grafana.
- The checkpoint alert contains the malformed phrase `Even one increment is worth knowing about — for is 0m.`

## Proposed scope

- Add stable runbook URLs and Grafana dashboard/panel context where supported.
- Generate panel links back to detailed logs for the selected tenant/time.
- Lint generated annotation grammar and stale internal references.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every enabled rule has a reachable runbook URL.
- [ ] Grafana shows dashboard/panel links for mapped rules.
- [ ] Broken/stale annotation text fails a generator test.
- [ ] Runbooks state no-data, error, false-positive, and remediation behavior.

## Prior decisions and duplicate check

- No prior issue covers alert navigation metadata or annotation quality.
- Related: #30, #219.

## Primary sources

- [https://grafana.com/docs/grafana/latest/alerting/alerting-rules/link-alert-rules-to-panels/](https://grafana.com/docs/grafana/latest/alerting/alerting-rules/link-alert-rules-to-panels/)

## Priority

Audit recommendation: **P2**.

comments.body:
Dependency blocker (2026-07-26): runbook/dashboard links and annotation linting need stable dashboard topology/UID targets (#302/#311), deliberate receiver ownership (#296), and interval-aware staleness semantics (#299). Building links before those seams land would freeze stale destinations or false thresholds.

**Unblock condition:** #296, #299, #302, and #311 land with stable routing, thresholds, and UIDs. **Required human action / owner:** Rob owns the upstream operator-visible decisions; this issue becomes mechanical once they are fixed.

## Closed by `c837527`

All 19 generated rules — 14 alerts and 5 detection examples — carry a runbook URL, a Grafana panel link and
a dashboard path, and none of the three can rot silently.

### The four acceptance criteria

- [x] **Every enabled rule has a reachable runbook URL.** `docs/runbooks.md`, one section per rule uid.
  Reachability is verified rather than assumed: the built site contains 19 `id="g2o-…"` anchors and zero rule
  uids are missing. Paused rules get runbooks too — a paused rule is precisely the one an operator is about
  to enable, and the runbook is what tells them whether that is safe.
- [x] **Grafana shows dashboard/panel links.** `__dashboardUid__` and `__panelId__`, both emitted as strings
  because rule annotations are `map[string]string`, plus a custom `dashboard_path`. Key names verified
  against current Grafana documentation, which states they must be set together or no panel link renders.
- [x] **Broken or stale annotation text fails a generator test.** A *class* lint, not a fix for the one known
  break: repository file references (not clickable from Grafana), stale `doc block N` pointers, a rule field
  used as a bare English subject, placeholder markers, malformed whitespace, missing sentence terminators.
  That class catches the reported `Even one increment is worth knowing about — for is 0m.` and the six
  descriptions rewritten alongside it. Summaries are exempt from the terminator rule — a summary is a
  notification headline, not prose.
- [x] **Runbooks state no-data, error, false-positive and remediation behaviour.** Enforced per section, so a
  renamed heading fails rather than quietly shipping a runbook missing a section.

### Links target the post-migration topology

The six v1 dashboard UIDs are retired. There is one dashboard, `/d/graph2otel`, and panel ids are resolved
out of the generated manifest rather than typed — **a wrong `dtab` slug is silently ignored, so a typo'd link
is undetectable by clicking it.** The dashboard path carries its tab as well as the panel, because a
`viewPanel` link into a conditioned-away tab renders a blank body with no message and naming the tab
overrides the hiding.

A nested leaf-tab `dtab` is deliberately **not** generated. The nested key's exact form was ambiguous across
the two places it is described here, nothing else in the repository generates one, and `viewPanel` opens
full-screen so the leaf tab does not change where the operator lands. An ambiguous key whose failure mode is
silence is not worth a cosmetic gain.

### Three gates, because resolving is not the same as being about the right thing

- a `runbook_url` whose anchor has no section fails, so a renamed heading cannot leave a responder on the
  page top mid-incident;
- a `__panelId__` or `dtab` naming nothing in the generated manifest fails;
- **the linked panel's own query text must reference a signal the rule actually evaluates.** This is what a
  numeric id cannot check: ids shift when panels are added and then point somewhere plausible instead of
  somewhere right. Two rules carry a documented waiver because no panel plots their signal, and an *unused*
  waiver fails too.

The runbook page is also added to the docs-navigation contract test, so a nav edit cannot orphan the page and
404 all 19 links. Sabotage-verified: removing the nav entry fails with `zensical navigation omits shipped
reference "runbooks.md"`.

### The coupling this created, working as designed

The generated alert YAML now depends on `dashboards/graph2otel.json` panel ids. Within hours, #304 split a
panel, ids shifted, and the staleness test caught it immediately — regenerated in `e75d76d`. That is the
intended behaviour and the reason the resolver raises a `KeyError` naming the tab and listing its real
titles rather than resolving to something plausible.

### Evidence

Only annotation prose changed in the generated YAML. **No expression, threshold, `for` duration,
`execErrState`, `noDataState`, pause state, label or uid was touched** — verified by field-by-field audit of
the diff, not asserted. The four `noDataState` and one `threshold` hits in that audit are all inside
`description:` prose, where the lint rewrote "noDataState is OK" into plain English.

Ten sabotages, each failing and each restored: a renamed runbook heading, a plausible but nonexistent tab
slug, a nonexistent panel id, the malformed phrase, the stale doc-block reference, a removed `runbook_url`, a
lone `__dashboardUid__`, a dropped runbook section, a link re-pointed at a real panel about something else,
and a dropped nav entry.

`make check` exit 0, `make grafana-check` 322 tests, pinned zensical build clean with 19/19 anchors present.

body:
## Outcome

A misspelled structured-metadata key in a dashboard, recording rule, or source-controlled alert should fail CI.

## Evidence

**Evidence class:** `source-derived (2026-07-25)`

- Event names are catalog-validated, but LogQL filter keys and `by` labels are raw strings.
- Recording-rule docs claim group labels are validated even though the generator only validates event names.
- Current references resolve, so this is a prevention gap rather than a known dead query.

## Proposed scope

- Validate filter/group keys against each event's attributes plus framework fields such as `tenant_id` and `ingest_transport`.
- Cover dashboards, recording rules, and source-controlled LogQL alerts.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Mutation tests prove a misspelled filter and group key fail CI.
- [ ] Emitter-boundary attributes are represented in the catalog contract.
- [ ] The inaccurate README claim is corrected.
- [ ] No valid dynamic query construct is blocked without an explicit escape hatch.

## Prior decisions and duplicate check

- This is the unchecked attribute-registry/gate half left by #141, not a duplicate of event-name coverage.
- Related: #141, #218, #219.

## Priority

Audit recommendation: **P2**.

comments.body:
Evidence-backed blocker (2026-07-26): 133 log events are cataloged, but framework-stamped `tenant_id`/`ingest_transport` are incomplete in per-event catalog rows; builder filters/groups are raw strings and the README overstates validation. A parser-free typed filter model and a permissive raw-string model have different safety/escape semantics.

**Recommendation:** use typed `{key, operator, value}` filters plus directly validated group keys; permit a named raw-filter escape only when it declares referenced keys and a reason. Overlay framework-guaranteed `tenant_id` and `ingest_transport` in the generated catalog.

**Unblock condition:** Rob approves the typed filter plus declared raw escape contract. **Required human action / owner:** Rob (`rknightion`). This gates #305/#313 portable query content.

## Decision received 2026-07-27 — UNBLOCKED

Maintainer approved the recorded recommendation: **typed `{key, operator, value}` filters plus directly validated group keys**, with a **named raw-LogQL escape** permitted only when it declares the keys it references and a reason.

Binding terms:

- Filter keys and `by` group keys validate against each event's catalog attributes, overlaid with the framework-guaranteed emitter-boundary attributes `tenant_id` and `ingest_transport`.
- No LogQL parser is introduced. The raw-string-plus-extractor alternative was rejected precisely because the extractor becomes a partial LogQL parser that either misses constructs or blocks valid ones.
- A typed-only model with no escape hatch was also rejected: constructs the type model does not cover (regex chains, `line_format`, `unwrap`) must stay expressible.
- Mutation tests must prove that a misspelled **filter** key and a misspelled **group** key each fail CI independently.
- Coverage is dashboards, recording rules, and source-controlled LogQL alerts.
- The inaccurate README claim identified in this issue is corrected as part of the change.

This unblocks #305 and #313, which both need the validated query vocabulary before they can generate stable selectors.

Sequencing note: the existing hard rule stands and the typed model must enforce, not weaken it — a stream selector is only ever `{service_name="graph2otel"}` built by `Builder._selector()`, and attribute matching is a filter stage. See `grafana/AUTHORING.md` and `test_no_stream_selector_on_an_attribute`.

## Closed by `77810ce` — typed filter contract implemented

Every binding term from the 2026-07-27 decision is met. New `grafana/logquery.py`.

| term | how |
| --- | --- |
| typed `{key, operator, value}` filters | `f(key, op, value)`, `op` ∈ `eq`/`ne`/`re`/`nre` — **named** operators, so a call site cannot smuggle `==` through as an opaque string |
| group keys directly validated | `by=` keys checked against the same permitted set |
| named raw escape with declared keys and a reason | `Raw(text, keys=[...], reason=...)`; raises without either, and the declared keys are validated exactly as a typed filter's key is |
| framework overlay | `tenant_id` + `ingest_transport` overlaid onto every event's permitted set at the validation boundary, since the emitter stamps them and per-event catalog rows omit `tenant_id` |
| no LogQL parser | none introduced; the author declares the keys |
| coverage: dashboards, recording rules, LogQL alerts | dashboards via `Builder._selector`; the #300 detection rules via the same module |
| README/doc claim corrected | see below |
| mutation tests, each failure independent | four of them, all verified by sabotage |

### A bare string is now refused

`render_filters` raises `TypeError` on a `str`. Accepting one would reinstate the unvalidated path
**invisibly**, which is the only realistic way this regresses.

### The overstated claim, and where it actually was

The issue recorded that "the README overstates validation". The real overstatement was in
**`grafana/builder.py`'s module docstring**, mirrored in `grafana/AUTHORING.md`:

> *A typo is a KeyError at build time rather than an empty panel someone notices in six months.*

True of metric names and event names. **False of the attributes inside a log query**, which were raw
strings. Both are corrected in this commit, and the AUTHORING section now states plainly what is
validated and what the escape hatch costs.

### Verified by sabotage, not by reading — all four independently

| mutation | result |
| --- | --- |
| dashboard filter key misspelled | build fails, names the key |
| dashboard group key misspelled | build fails, names the key |
| detection filter key misspelled | build fails |
| detection group key misspelled | build fails |

The mutation tests build a **real board module** through the real `common.add` path rather than calling
the validator in isolation, so they exercise the wiring and would catch the validator being connected to
nothing.

### One simplification worth recording

The detection pack shipped on #300 (`d94458b`) carried a hand-maintained `DETECTION_FIELDS` dict
declaring which attributes each detection touched. **That is deleted.** With typed filters the validated
keys are derived from the filters themselves as the `DETECTIONS` list is constructed, so there is no
parallel declaration left to drift out of step with the queries — which was the weakness of the
declaration approach even with its bidirectional check.

### The stream-selector rule is stronger, not weaker

A `Filter` cannot express a stream selector at all — it renders only `key<op>\`value\`` after a pipe. So
`{service_name="graph2otel"}` remains the only stream selector by construction, and
`test_no_stream_selector_on_an_attribute` still passes.

### Verification

`make check` exit 0 · `make grafana-check` exit 0 · **237 tests**, up from 217 · Zensical clean ·
coverage unchanged at 331/331 · generated dashboard and rule bytes unchanged apart from the intended
filter rendering.

### Unblocks

**#305** and **#313** both waited on a stable validated query vocabulary before generating portable
selectors. That vocabulary now exists. #313's other stated dependency, #300, closed earlier today; its
remaining one is #307.

## Terminal CI receipt — `77810ce`

All 7 workflows **success**: CI, CodeQL, Docker Security, Release, Scorecard, actionlint, zizmor.

`make check` exit 0 and `make grafana-check` exit 0 at the same tree (237 tests), Zensical clean.
