body:
## Outcome

An analyst should pivot from one alert or log row to related user, device, app, message, incident, or alert signals with tenant and time context preserved.

## Evidence

**Evidence class:** `source-derived from the signal catalog and current Grafana capability (2026-07-25)`

- The signal catalog already contains reusable identifiers such as device, app, user, UPN, message, alert, and incident IDs.
- Current dashboards are domain views with no panel/data links or generated correlations.

## Proposed scope

- Generate a correlation manifest, data links, and reusable investigation views from cataloged identifier semantics.
- Cover device, application/service principal, account, email message, alert, and incident first.
- Propagate tenant and selected time range.

## Constraints and non-goals

- Do not pretend Loki links are relational joins or automated correlation verdicts.
- Do not promote identifiers to metric labels.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Initial six entity pivots work from representative log rows and alerts.
- [ ] Generation fails if a referenced event/attribute disappears.
- [ ] LogQL uses `{service_name="graph2otel"} | event_name=...`.
- [ ] Each link states identifier meaning and direction.

## Prior decisions and duplicate check

- No existing issue covers generated cross-signal entity investigations.
- Related: #141, #162, #218.

## Primary sources

- [https://grafana.com/docs/grafana/latest/administration/correlations/](https://grafana.com/docs/grafana/latest/administration/correlations/)
- [https://grafana.com/docs/grafana/latest/explore/logs-integration/](https://grafana.com/docs/grafana/latest/explore/logs-integration/)

## Priority

Audit recommendation: **P1**.

comments.body:
Dependency blocker (2026-07-26): read-only live evidence proves the requested device, application, account, message, alert, and policy pivots exist, but the catalog has no frozen identity/equivalence/direction metadata and #306 has not yet defined the validated LogQL filter contract. Implementing links now would create unvalidated query vocabulary and unstable navigation before #302 settles topology.

**Unblock condition:** #306's typed filter/group contract and #302's navigation topology are approved and land. **Required human action / owner:** Rob owns those two upstream decisions; implementation then resumes without further product choice unless a live pivot contradicts the evidence.

## Closed — `186b981`

Six entity pivots ship, generated: **device, application/service principal, account, email message, security alert, security incident**. Each is reachable from every generated log panel in the estate with tenant and time preserved.

### Mechanism, and the two rejected alternatives

A generated pivot surface on the **Overview** tab — one collapsed row per entity, driven by a free-text input variable — plus derived panel links into it from every log panel.

- **Grafana Correlations rejected**: a stack-level resource is a new deployment surface needing separate approval, and nothing here needed one. Everything this issue asks for is expressible inside the single dashboard.
- **Overview rather than a new top-level tab**: Overview is the one tab that is never conditional, and a `dtab` into conditioned-away content renders a blank body with no message. It also preserves #399's frozen 7-tab topology.
- **Panel links rather than data links**: a data link could interpolate the clicked row's identifier, but that depends on Grafana rendering data links inside the Loki log-detail view, which was not measured. Shipping on that assumption would have been a guess; the link carries tenant and time and the analyst pastes the id already in front of them. Recorded as a known limitation rather than a silent one.

### Acceptance criteria

- [x] Six pivots work from representative log rows and alerts.
- [x] Generation fails if a referenced event or attribute disappears — see below.
- [x] LogQL is `{service_name="graph2otel"} | event_name=…` throughout.
- [x] Each link states the identifier's meaning and direction — and states flatly that this is navigation, **"not a join"**, asserted by test on every pivot panel. Loki cannot join and the content must not imply it can.
- [x] No identifier is ever promoted to a metric label — asserted by test.

### The gate is on the outcome, and it is verified by sabotage

The event set is **derived** from the catalog, so a new collector emitting `device_id` joins the pivot with no human step. But a purely derived set **cannot fail** — an event losing the attribute just drops out silently, which is precisely the #304 failure mode. Declared `(event, key)` **anchors** are the thing that fails.

Four sabotage classes, each run through the real CLI against a patched catalog copy. I reproduced one independently rather than taking the lane's word for it — renaming `device_id` on `intune.device_hardware` gives exit **1**:

```
dashboard build violations:
  - pivot 'device': anchor event 'intune.device_hardware' no longer carries 'device_id', so it has
    silently dropped out of the pivot's derived event set while the build stayed green
```

The other three: an attribute renamed on every event, a deleted event, and a documented not-covered synonym that stops existing. The link gate separately checks the **shipped manifest** — the `dtab` slug must name a real tab (a wrong slug is ignored *silently*) and the linked panel's own query must name an event that really carries one of the entity's keys, which is the check a numeric panel id cannot make.

### One LogQL trap that is load-bearing

**An absent structured-metadata key equals the empty string in LogQL**, so filtering on an unset variable matches every record that has *no* such key — it would dump the whole estate rather than returning nothing. Every pivot query stages a `=~".+"` guard first, so an empty input matches nothing by construction. Documented in `docs/signals.md`, because this is a trap any future hand-written panel can fall into.

### Contract extension, reviewed and accepted

`logquery.FRAMEWORK_KEYS` gains **`event_name`**, a change to #306's frozen overlay. Accepted: `Builder._selector()` emits `| event_name=` on every query, so it is framework-guaranteed at the emitter boundary in exactly the sense `tenant_id` and `ingest_transport` are. Without it, grouping by the one key that makes a cross-event query readable was reported as an attribute the event does not carry. The overlay stays closed at three members, asserted by test — it is not a general escape hatch.

### Counts

365 panels (was 350), 7 top-level tabs, 61 leaves, largest leaf **18/24** — the ceiling was neither approached nor raised. Panel-id audit: **zero** id shifts affecting any alert's `viewPanel` link (max alert-referenced id 383; the only re-pointed ids are above it).

### Not done, deliberately

No alert rule links straight to a pivot — today the path is alert → dashboard panel → that panel's pivot link, two clicks. `build_rules.py` was owned by another lane; the URL constant is exported so a one-click annotation is a small follow-up if wanted.

Three rendering assumptions were not measured (the `TextVariable` field set, multi-target merging in one panel, and whether a collapsed row queries). None affects correctness — worst case is presentational or a wasted query — and a single live render of `?dtab=Overview` would close all three.

### Gate

`make check` exit 0 · `make grafana-check` 334/334 catalog metrics panelled, 0 waived, 389 tests OK.

title: feat(grafana): generate entity-centric investigation pivots

body:
## Outcome

Panels should describe the quantity actually plotted and color only evidence-backed operational states.

## Evidence

**Evidence class:** `render-verified plus generated JSON census (2026-07-25)`

- All sum instruments are displayed as `rate()` while retaining count-derived titles and generic units.
- Most panels use generic `short`; durations such as Autopilot sync age are not humanized.
- Neutral inventory counts can render red, while meaningful states have no value mappings or thresholds.
- The signal catalog currently omits emitter metric descriptions, limiting generated context.

## Proposed scope

- Capture metric descriptions and rate semantics in the catalog/builder.
- Use honest rate/time/byte/percentage units and titles.
- Add value mappings and thresholds only where a defined operational state exists.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Counter panels say and format `rate` rather than raw count.
- [ ] Time, byte, ratio, and percentage units render human-readably.
- [ ] Neutral inventory values do not imply an alarm.
- [ ] Thresholds/mappings cite their operational meaning and are covered by semantic tests.

## Prior decisions and duplicate check

- Not duplicate of #82: normalized metric names are correct; this concerns displayed meaning.
- Related: #82, #218.

## Priority

Audit recommendation: **P2**.

comments.body:
Evidence-backed blocker (2026-07-26): descriptions and some UCUM units now exist, but counter-rate titles/units, mixed-unit panels, enum mappings, thresholds, and neutral coloring still need an authoritative presentation source. Putting thresholds in the generated signal catalog, scattering board overrides, or adding a separate registry create different ownership/drift contracts.

**Recommendation:** add a separate audited Grafana presentation registry keyed by catalog metric; mappings/thresholds require cited measured/source evidence, neutral inventory receives neutral coloring, and uncited thresholds fail validation.

**Unblock condition:** Rob approves the separate presentation-registry ownership model. **Required human action / owner:** Rob (`rknightion`). #302/#311 summary semantics depend on this seam.

## Decision received 2026-07-27 — UNBLOCKED

Maintainer approved the recorded recommendation: a **separate audited generated presentation registry**, keyed by catalog metric, owns units, titles, value mappings, and thresholds.

Binding terms:

- Mappings and thresholds require cited measured or source evidence.
- An uncited threshold **fails validation**.
- Neutral inventory counts receive neutral colouring and must not imply an alarm.
- `spec/signal-catalog.json` stays wire-derived and does not acquire presentation opinion. It is generated from Go `testdata/signals.json` goldens, so presentation opinion placed there would either be overwritten or force the Go generator to own colour choices it has no evidence for.
- Per-board overrides in `grafana/boards/*.py` were rejected: identical metrics would drift between boards and the honesty gate this issue asks for would be unenforceable.

This unblocks the #302 / #311 summary semantics.

Sequencing note: this lands **after** #399 freezes the dashboard generator API, because the registry is consumed at panel-construction time and #399 rewrites that construction path. #399 must not hard-code units, mappings, or thresholds that this registry will own — it takes them from the registry seam or leaves them derived as today.

## Closed by `0ee422c`, corrected by `e75d76d`

The audited presentation registry is `grafana/presentation.py`, keyed by catalog metric, owning units,
titles, value mappings and thresholds. Both rejected alternatives stayed rejected: `spec/signal-catalog.json`
takes no presentation opinion, and there are no per-board overrides.

### The four acceptance criteria

- [x] **Counter panels say and format `rate`.** Every `sum` instrument is plotted through `rate()`, so a
  count unit and a count-shaped title both described something the panel was not showing. 29 panels
  formatted a per-second series as a bare count; `m365.message_trace.bytes` was the worst, formatting
  bytes/sec as `bytes`. Derived titles are corrected automatically; a hand-written count-shaped title now
  fails the build, because auto-rewriting prose produces gibberish (`"Microsoft API drift — a response no
  longer matches what a collector expects rate"`). Ten hand-written titles were fixed with judgement.
- [x] **Time, byte, ratio and percentage units render human-readably.** Two dimensionless `1` metrics that
  are genuinely fractions (`graph2otel.scrape.budget`, `defender.vulnerability.max_epss`) render as
  `percentunit` instead of `0.87`. `b.raw()` now derives its unit from the metrics its expression names
  rather than taking a hand-typed one — the hand-typed unit had drifted on **every** hand-written rate
  panel in self-observability.
- [x] **Neutral inventory values do not imply an alarm.** This was the measured defect: **331 of 331 panels
  omitted `fieldConfig.defaults.thresholds` entirely**, and Grafana then supplies its own — a green base
  with a red step at 80. An inventory count of 95 managed devices rendered red. Absence of a threshold was
  never neutrality; neutral is now written down explicitly on every panel, log panels included. The gate has
  no exemption list, because an exemption list is a second thing to audit and the first entry never comes
  back out.
- [x] **Thresholds and mappings cite their operational meaning and are covered by tests.** `Thresholds` and
  `Mappings` refuse an empty `evidence`, and the evidence is written into the panel description behind
  `Colour meaning:` — so the operator looking at a red panel reads *why* it is red, and the gate can prove
  on the shipped manifest that no coloured panel is uncited.

### Restraint is the deliverable

**Four** metrics are thresholded across 350 panels, producing 5 coloured panels. "How many ownerless Teams
is too many" and "what EPSS probability is unacceptable" are policy judgements an operator makes, not facts
this repository has evidence for; they keep neutral colouring and a log twin. A threshold was written only
where the source defines the state:

| metric | colour | why it is not a number this repo picked |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `graph2otel.scrape.budget` | red at 1.0 | a scrape consuming its whole poll interval cannot finish before the next is due; the boundary is the configured interval |
| `m365.service_health.status` | red at 4 | levels 4–5 are Microsoft's own `serviceDegradation` / `serviceInterruption` |
| `graph2otel.otlp.delivery.degraded` | red at 1 | 1 means the latest exporter failure is unrecovered (#268) — telemetry is being lost now |
| `graph2otel.scrape.success` | green at 1 | 0 is a partial or failed scrape; green starts at 1 so the failing state is the *uncoloured* one |

11 panels carry cited value mappings, including the `m365.service_health.status` ladder derived from
`statusEnum` in `internal/collectors/m365/servicehealth/servicehealth.go`. A level Microsoft adds beyond 5
renders as its bare number — visible rather than mislabelled — which is the deliberate answer to
cross-language drift instead of restating the Go map in Python.

Panel descriptions now default to the emitter's own catalog description: 303 of 340 panels carry one, where
this issue recorded that generated context as unused.

### A defect the live read-back found, and the gate that now catches it

Publishing to the stack and reading it back showed **only one of the four cited thresholds had reached the
manifest**. The other three sit on hand-written `raw()` panels, which need an explicit `about=` to know
which metric they describe, and the call sites did not pass it.

Nothing failed. The citation existed, the metric was covered, the registry gate passed, and the colour
simply was not there — a gate that could not see its own subject reporting coverage it did not have.

`presentation.unapplied()` now fails the build when a cited mapping or threshold reaches no panel, detected
through the citation marker because that is the only evidence in the artifact that an entry was applied.
Turning it on immediately found five more silent no-ops of the same kind, each fixed at the presentation
level rather than waived:

- the four SharePoint tenant switches share one panel, and a panel-wide mapping applies only when every
  metric agrees; one had bespoke wording so **all four** fell back to no mapping. They now share one
  `Disabled`/`Enabled` ladder, and the shared citation stopped naming a single metric — a panel-wide mapping
  can only carry one citation, so naming one metric made its three neighbours look unapplied.
- `entra.organization.on_premises_sync_enabled` shared a panel with a sync age in seconds, where its 0/1
  mapping would have relabelled the seconds. Not applying it was correct and the *panel* was wrong: the flag
  is now its own panel.

### Evidence

Every gate verified by **sabotage**, not by reading:

| sabotage | result |
| --- | --- |
| drop the explicit thresholds | 331 panels fail |
| format a counter rate as a bare count | 29 fail |
| suppress the rate title | 10 fail |
| hand-add a red step with no citation | fails as uncited |
| registry entry for a metric the catalog lost | fails as describing nothing |
| drop a single `about=` | fails, naming the entry, the metric and the fix |
| construct an uncited threshold or mapping | `ValueError` |

`make check` exit 0, `make grafana-check` 322 tests, pinned zensical build clean. 331/331 metrics panelled,
0 waived, largest leaf 18/24.

**Correction:** `0ee422c`'s message and the registry docstring both said *five* thresholded metrics. It is
**four**, producing five coloured panels. Fixed in the docstring by `e75d76d`; the pushed commit message
cannot be corrected without rewriting published history, so it is corrected here.

## Outcome

A blank or `No data` panel should explain whether the collector is disabled, unlicensed, unconfigured, legitimately empty, not deployed, or unhealthy.

## Evidence

**Evidence class:** `live render-verified (2026-07-25)`

- Live Defender, M365, Purview, GSA, and self-observability panels contain many visually identical empty states.
- Several giant stat panels render green `No data`, which implies health without evidence.
- The runtime has most gating/status facts but dashboards do not join or display them.

## Proposed scope

- Consume the collector availability contract and add explicit state/value mappings.
- Design healthy-empty semantics per signal rather than globally treating no data as good or bad.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Optional, licence-gated, high-volume, and source-exclusive collectors have distinct empty-state messages.
- [x] No giant green `No data` card remains.
- [x] A broken query/datasource cannot look like a disabled collector.
- [x] State semantics are generator-tested.

## Prior decisions and duplicate check

- Not duplicate of collector availability telemetry: this issue owns the Grafana presentation and per-signal no-data semantics.
- Related: #10, #218, #263.

## Priority

Audit recommendation: **P1**.

comments.body:
Implementation classification and frozen seam (`gpt-5.6-sol`, high reasoning, primary-owned): this is a cross-dashboard, operator-visible availability presentation contract. Exclusive shared files are `grafana/builder.py`, `grafana/boards/common.py`, and `grafana/tests/test_build_dashboard.py`; the primary also owns the five domain board declarations and generated JSON in this serial wave. No subagent or concurrent lane may edit them.

Validated current premise:
- #292 already supplies the complete bounded state/reason contract and detailed self-observability tables.
- The five domain dashboards do not consume collector availability.
- Prometheus query panels generally have no neutral empty-state text; the live self-observability dashboard is also stale, but publishing is outside this source wave.

Frozen behavior:
- Preserve #292 exactly: `limited/partial_license` is non-failure, `covered/covered_by_alternative` is intentional absence, and `healthy_empty/empty` is healthy.
- A datasource/query error remains a Grafana error. An empty availability query explicitly proves no state and must never be described as disabled.
- Metric-panel emptiness is neutral and points to the domain availability table; it cannot assert healthy, disabled, or failed without availability evidence.
- Each board declares its collector regex explicitly; no package-path-to-collector naming inference.
- No numeric health score and no live Grafana mutation in this child source wave.

TDD will first gate the domain availability table, complete state/reason presentation, unknown-on-empty behavior, neutral metric `noValue`, and the absence of green no-data stat cards. The generated five-board diff, full local gates, exact-tip Actions, and eventual coordinated live read-back are the acceptance evidence.

Completed in source by `ebba3c1583c557ab1fcb80ae432f2ac72874938d`.

Implementation:
- Every domain board declares an explicit logical-collector regex and receives a full-width `Signal availability` table backed only by `graph2otel.collector.availability`.
- The table preserves `tenant_id`, `collector`, `collector_transport`, `state`, and `reason`; string mappings cover the full bounded #292 state/reason contract without inventing a numeric health score or failure color.
- Empty availability says `Availability unknown` and explicitly does not mean disabled. Every Prometheus panel now has neutral no-data text pointing to the availability table; stat panels default to no color so Grafana cannot paint an unmapped/no-data value green.
- New boards must declare availability ownership. The Python mapping set is drift-checked against the Go-generated availability table in `docs/collectors.md`.

TDD and local gates:
- RED: five boards lacked an availability table; 248 Prometheus panels lacked neutral `noValue`; state/reason mapping and ownership gates were absent.
- GREEN: 77 Grafana tests pass; `make grafana-check` reports 330/330 metrics, 393 panels across 6 dashboards, 14 alerts, and 2 recording rules.
- `make check`: pass.
- `uvx --from zensical==0.0.46 zensical build --clean`: pass, no issues.
- Generated JSON was rebuilt with `make dashboard`; no hand edits or unexpected orphan files.

Runtime evidence (`live-measured 2026-07-26`):
- Read-only m7kni PromQL proved every domain regex returns current availability states. Sanitized census: Intune 39 healthy / 8 healthy-empty / 2 disabled / 2 degraded; Entra 32 healthy / 8 healthy-empty / 3 covered / 2 disabled; M365 6 healthy / 8 disabled / 1 covered; Defender+MDCA 10 healthy / 15 healthy-empty / 7 disabled; Purview 2 healthy / 1 disabled / 1 failed.
- Disposable Grafana 13.1.1 (`a9cee6e1724a455676bb6c05eef7fc54aa4b19f4`) accepted all six generated dashboards. API read-back preserved all five availability expressions, `labelsToFields` transformations, state/reason mapping fields, neutral unknown text, and zero Prometheus panels missing `noValue`.
- #298’s disposable evaluator test separately proved a broken datasource reaches Grafana state `Error` and a firing `DatasourceError`, rather than the no-data/disabled presentation.

No production Grafana resource was changed. Live publication and visual production read-back remain with the coordinated #293/#294/#295/#296 deployment wave, which owns safe provisioning and datasource defaults. Exact-tip Actions are running and will be recorded separately.

Exact-tip Actions receipt for `ebba3c1583c557ab1fcb80ae432f2ac72874938d`:

- [CI](https://github.com/rknightion/graph2otel/actions/runs/30214642802): success

body:
## Outcome

Domain dashboards should answer operational questions quickly while retaining exhaustive catalog coverage in a drilldown layer.

## Evidence

**Evidence class:** `render-verified plus generated JSON census (2026-07-25)`

- Six dashboards contain 347 panels; Intune has 134 and Entra 88.
- The majority are generic time-series panels derived from metric names, and most have no description.
- Rendered boards behave as signal inventories rather than prioritized decision surfaces.

## Proposed scope

- Keep exhaustive generated coverage in explorer rows or companion dashboards.
- Curate top-level rows around posture, active findings, freshness, and investigation entry points.
- Use collapsible rows and stable links rather than deleting coverage.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each domain has a concise first-screen operational summary.
- [ ] Every catalog metric remains reachable and coverage-gated.
- [ ] Top-level panels state the decision or failure mode they represent.
- [ ] Large domains have a tested navigation hierarchy.

## Prior decisions and duplicate check

- Not duplicate of #218: generation and coverage are complete; this improves the information architecture of the generated assets.
- Related: #218, #263.

## Primary sources

- [https://grafana.com/docs/grafana/latest/dashboards/build-dashboards/](https://grafana.com/docs/grafana/latest/dashboards/build-dashboards/)

## Priority

Audit recommendation: **P2**.

comments.body:
Dispatch classification for the read-only information-architecture inventory:

- Issue/task: #302; inventory the generated dashboard builder and six boards, quantify current first-screen/row/navigation structure, and return mechanically verifiable candidates that retain 330/330 catalog coverage. No design choice or edit is delegated.
- Acceptance boundary: a source-cited map of current row order, panel counts, descriptions, collapse support, stable links, and the smallest file-owned seams needed for a tested hierarchy; stop on any operator-visible fork.
- Files/exclusive owner: read-only over `grafana/builder.py`, `grafana/boards/*.py`, `grafana/build_dashboard.py`, generated JSON, and dashboard tests. No file ownership and no edits in this lane. The primary retains all source and generated-artifact ownership.
- Dependencies/shared seams: #301 tenant preservation, #303 availability presentation, #312 executive summary, coverage gating, layout/rendering, row collapse semantics, and stable dashboard/panel links.
- Risk: low for inventory; high for the eventual cross-cutting information-architecture and visual design.
- Route: `gpt-5.6-terra`, medium reasoning. The inventory is read-only and objectively checkable; it cannot edit, update GitHub, query/mutate live systems, commit/push, or dispatch. Any ambiguity or recommended operator-visible behavior returns to the primary `gpt-5.6-sol` high-reasoning lane.

Evidence-backed blocker (2026-07-26): the current estate is 404 panels/59 expanded rows; the builder has no collapse or cross-dashboard navigation contract. Same-dashboard collapsed explorers preserve stable UIDs and avoid five additional resources; companion dashboards change navigation and publication ownership.

**Recommendation:** keep the stable domain UIDs, put concise operational rows first, keep availability expanded, move long query help below the operational surface, and collapse exhaustive inventory/explorer rows on the same dashboard.

**Unblock condition:** Rob approves same-dashboard collapsed explorers versus companion explorer dashboards and confirms the operational-summary selection. **Required human action / owner:** Rob (`rknightion`). This gates #304/#305/#309/#311 and final live topology read-back.

## 2026-07-27 — topology fork ANSWERED, partially unblocked

The parked fork at https://github.com/rknightion/graph2otel/issues/302#issuecomment-5085158040 — same-dashboard collapsed explorers versus companion explorer dashboards — is answered by the maintainer's #399 topology decision: **one dashboard with nested tabs**.

The mechanism is **nested Grafana v2 leaf tabs**, not collapsed rows, and not companion dashboards. The recorded recommendation to "keep the stable domain UIDs" is **overridden** — all six UIDs are retired and replaced by one dashboard whose top-level tabs are the five domains plus self-observability. See https://github.com/rknightion/graph2otel/issues/399#issuecomment-5089870787 for the full decided shape and accepted consequences.

### What this issue still owns

The topology question is closed; the **curation** question is not. This issue remains open for the substance the fork was blocking:

- Which panels belong on the operational first screen (`Overview` tab, plus each domain tab's leading rows) versus behind an explorer leaf tab.
- What decision or failure mode each top-level panel represents, stated in the panel.
- Keeping every catalog metric reachable and coverage-gated regardless of which tab it lands on.

That curation is implemented as part of the #399 migration, because the migration has to place all 404 panels somewhere and placing them is exactly this decision. This issue closes from the same work.

Revised criterion: "Each domain has a concise first-screen operational summary" now means each domain **tab** leads with that summary, and the `Overview` top-level tab carries the cross-domain equivalent.

## Satisfied by #399 (`97e08b6`) — validated against the shipped dashboard, then closed

This issue asked for operational overviews separated from exhaustive signal explorers. Both halves are
now true, and I verified them against the generated artifact rather than assuming #399 delivered them.

### The topology fork is closed, and one recorded recommendation here is now WRONG

The body's *"keep the stable domain UIDs"* recommendation is **superseded**: all six UIDs are retired,
and the estate is one dashboard with nested v2 leaf tabs — not collapsed rows, and not companion
dashboards. That was the maintainer's reference-parity decision on #399. Noting it explicitly because a
future reader hitting the body first would otherwise act on a recommendation that no longer holds.

### Separation, measured on `dashboards/graph2otel.json`

**Every tab leads with an operational summary:**

| tab | first leaf | leaves |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Overview | census + query guide (`RowsLayout`, never conditional) | — |
| Entra | Signal availability | 12 |
| Intune | Signal availability | 13 |
| Defender | Signal availability | 8 |
| M365 | Signal availability | 7 |
| Purview | Signal availability | 5 |
| Self-obs | Executive health and data-loss summary (#312) | 14 |

**And the exhaustive content is genuinely separated from it.** The old shape was six dashboards of up to
~200 panels each on one scrolling page, where the operational content and the inventory were the same
surface. It is now 60 bounded leaf tabs: an operator lands on collector state, and the exhaustive
per-signal inventory is one deliberate click away in a named section rather than below the fold.

That "Signal availability" is the right operational first screen is a consequence of #303: it is the
only panel that distinguishes disabled, covered, healthy-empty, limited, blocked, degraded, failed and
startup-failed. For an exporter, "which of my collectors is actually working" *is* the operational
question, and every other panel on the tab is uninterpretable without it — which is why every metric
panel's no-data text points back at it.

`Overview` carries the cross-domain equivalent and is the one surface that renders in every state,
including a completely absent census.

### What remains, and why it is not this issue

Whether the mechanical one-row-per-leaf grouping is the *best* grouping — whether Intune's 13 leaves
read better merged into 8, say — is now a tuning question against a working topology, not the design
fork this issue was opened to resolve. It needs no decision and blocks nothing. If it turns out to
matter in use, it is a fresh issue with a concrete complaint behind it, not an open epic child.

Closing as satisfied. No code change accompanies this, so it is closed by hand rather than by a commit
keyword; the implementing commit is `97e08b6`.

## Outcome

Selecting All or several tenants must not silently sum or average different tenants into one unlabeled series.

## Evidence

**Evidence class:** `source-derived (2026-07-25)`

- Every query filters by `$tenant`, but generated aggregations omit `tenant_id` from grouping and legends.
- The tenant variable is multi-select with All enabled.

body:
## Outcome

The eight live graph2otel SIEM alerts and five legacy Azure log-export recording rules need an explicit keep, migrate, or retire decision and reproducible ownership.

## Evidence

**Evidence class:** `live resource inventory plus issue-history reconciliation (2026-07-25)`

- The live `entra-security-g2o` and `entra-graph-recording` groups are absent from this repository's generators.
- #90/#232 record important routing, burn-in, and cross-transport vocabulary decisions.
- Repository docs only mention the live group; there is no drift/read-back gate.

## Proposed scope

- Choose a canonical private infrastructure source or a public parameterized template with tenant-specific values externalized.
- Disposition every live rule and record stable UIDs, routing labels, mute/cutover semantics, and the #232 corrections.
- Add export/read-back drift checks.

## Constraints and non-goals

- Do not commit tenant-specific IPs, application IDs, or other private values to this public repository.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every live-only rule is explicitly kept, migrated, or retired.
- [ ] Surviving graph2otel-owned rules are reproducible and drift-checked.
- [ ] The remaining #232 end-to-end page receipt is captured.
- [ ] Legacy rules have a named removal condition rather than indefinite parallel life.

## Prior decisions and duplicate check

- Not duplicate of #219: that issue generated the generic metric pack; these production SIEM resources remain outside it.
- Related: #86, #90, #219, #232.

## Priority

Audit recommendation: **P1**.

comments.body:
Evidence-backed blocker (2026-07-26): production SIEM and legacy Entra rules are tenant/private-infrastructure content and are not reproducible from this public repository. Choosing keep/migrate/retire and the owning private repository changes security operations and live routing ownership.

**Recommendation:** private infrastructure owns real SIEM/legacy rules and the `pipeline=graph2otel` route; public source carries portable rules/hunts only.

**Unblock condition:** Rob identifies the private source of truth and decides keep/migrate/retire for each live rule set. **Required human action / owner:** Rob (`rknightion`) plus the named private-infra owner. #313 cannot claim complete detection ownership before this inventory is settled.

## Decision received 2026-07-27 — private-infrastructure ownership confirmed

Maintainer decision, verbatim: *"I dont think we shoul dbe shipping any alert routing / contact point / notification policy in our repo that's an oeprator explicit decision"*

Combined with the recorded recommendation, this settles the keep/migrate/retire question at https://github.com/rknightion/graph2otel/issues/300#issuecomment-5085157973:

- The 8 live `entra-security-g2o` SIEM alerts and the 5 legacy `entra-graph-recording` recording rules are **private-infrastructure owned**. They are not migrated into this public repository.
- The public repository carries portable rules and hunts only, with no tenant-specific selectors and no routing.
- #313 may therefore proceed on portable content without waiting for these live rules to be reproduced here — its remaining gates are #305/#306/#307, not this inventory.

### Still required from the maintainer, and still blocking closure of this issue

This decision fixes *where* the rules live. It does not by itself produce the two remaining records:

1. **A named private source of truth** for those 13 live resources, so they are reproducible somewhere rather than existing only in the live stack. Unblock condition: the maintainer names the private location (repository, path, or system) holding them.
2. **A named removal condition for the 5 legacy Azure log-export recording rules**, so they do not live in parallel indefinitely. Unblock condition: the maintainer states the condition under which they are retired.

The #232 end-to-end page receipt also remains outstanding and is operator-owned.

Owner: Rob / private-infrastructure owner. This issue stays open on those two records only; no repository code change is pending on it.

## 2026-07-27 — the 5 legacy recording rules are RETIRED (live production change, completed)

Maintainer decision: **"Retire them now."** Done. This was an irreversible production mutation, so the
full pre-deletion evidence is recorded below.

### Pre-deletion safety audit (read-only, 2026-07-27)

- **199 of 199 dashboards** on the stack enumerated and searched over full raw JSON — panel targets,
  template-variable queries, annotation queries, descriptions and text panels. Dashboard count
  corroborated independently by `gcx dashboards list` and `GET /api/search?type=dash-db`. **Zero
  references** to any of the 5 recorded metric names.
- **All 50 rule groups** searched over their complete definitions including labels and annotations.
  Each of the 5 names appeared **exactly once** — inside its own rule's definition, nowhere else.
  Notably `g2o-graph403-burst` does **not** consume `entra_graph_403_5m`; it queries graph2otel's own
  current telemetry.
- **SLOs: none exist** on the stack. **Library panels: none exist** (`/api/library-elements` →
  `totalCount: 0`), so no reference could hide outside dashboard JSON.
- **The 5 series returned zero samples in Mimir**, with a `up` control query confirming the datasource
  was live — so the empty results were real, not a broken query.
- **The legacy source stream is dead**: `{job="integrations/azure-logexport",
  category="MicrosoftGraphActivityLogs"}` returned zero rows over 24h **and** over 7 days, with a
  `{service_name="graph2otel"}` control confirming Loki was answering normally. These rules had been
  producing nothing for at least a week.

One near-miss checked and cleared: `graph2otel-entra-compliance` contains the substring `entra_graph`,
but those are graph2otel's own live `entra_graph_activity_*` client counters and histograms — unrelated
to the retired recording rules and unaffected.

### What was deleted

All in folderUID `ffo7you47fxtsd` ("Entra Security"), rule group `entra-graph-recording`, all
`provenance: null` (UI/API-created, not file-provisioned), none paused:

| uid | recorded metric |
| --- | --- |
| `entra-graph-requests` | `entra_graph_requests_5m` |
| `entra-graph-4xx` | `entra_graph_client_errors_5m` |
| `entra-graph-5xx` | `entra_graph_server_errors_5m` |
| `entra-graph-403` | `entra_graph_403_5m` |
| `entra-graph-p95` | `entra_graph_duration_p95_ms` |

Each recorded into `grafanacloud-prom` from a `count_over_time` / `quantile_over_time` aggregation over
the legacy azure-logexport Loki stream, grouped `by (appId, app)` where `app` came from a very large
inline `label_format` mapping ~200 first-party Microsoft `appId` GUIDs to display names. The complete
JSON definitions were captured before deletion. They are deliberately not pasted here — the expressions
are ~9KB each and dominated by that GUID table — and recreation is not anticipated, because the source
stream is dead and graph2otel's own `entra.graph_activity` collector now covers this signal natively
with `entra_graph_activity_*` metrics confirmed live on the stack.

Deleted via `gcx api /api/v1/provisioning/alert-rules/<uid> -X DELETE`.

### Post-deletion read-back

- Each of the 5 UIDs now returns **HTTP 404**.
- Total provisioned rules **449 → 444** — exactly 5 removed, no collateral deletions.
- Rule group `entra-graph-recording` **no longer exists**.
- None of the 5 recorded names appears anywhere in the remaining rule set.
- **Collateral check passed**: `entra-security-g2o` still holds all 8 SIEM alerts by UID
  (`g2o-sp-homelab`, `g2o-sp-intunebrew`, `g2o-sp-n8n`, `g2o-audit-tamper`, `g2o-defender-crit`,
  `g2o-signin-anomaly`, `g2o-graph403-burst`, `g2o-security-incident`); `blob-derived` still holds
  graph2otel's own 2 recording rules; the unrelated `oauth2-proxy-auth-failures` rule in the same
  folder is untouched.

Evidence class: `live-measured (2026-07-27, #300)`.

### Acceptance criteria

- [x] Every live-only rule is explicitly kept, migrated, or retired — 5 retired here; the 8 SIEM
      alerts are kept as private-infrastructure owned per the 2026-07-27 ownership decision.
- [x] Surviving graph2otel-owned rules are reproducible and drift-checked — the graph2otel-owned set
      is the 14 generated rules in `alerts/graph2otel-alerts.yaml`, byte-compare drift-gated by
      `build_rules.py --check`. The 8 SIEM alerts are explicitly **not** graph2otel-owned.
- [x] Legacy rules have a named removal condition rather than indefinite parallel life — superseded by
      actually removing them, which is strictly better than a condition.
- [ ] The remaining #232 end-to-end page receipt is captured.

### Remaining blocker — the only thing keeping this issue open

**The 8 `entra-security-g2o` SIEM alerts exist ONLY in the live Grafana stack.** There is no
reproducible source for them anywhere: not this repository (by decision), and no private location has
been named. If that stack is lost or a rule is edited by hand, those 8 detections are unrecoverable and
the change is untracked.

- **Unblock condition:** the maintainer names the private source of truth — a repository, path, or
  system — that holds those 8 rule definitions reproducibly.
- **Required human action:** name the location, then the definitions get exported to it.
- **Owner:** Rob / private-infrastructure owner.

Also still outstanding and operator-owned: the #232 end-to-end page receipt.

## 2026-07-27 — portability triage of the 8 live SIEM alerts (read-only, m7kni stack)

Maintainer question: *"are the seim alerts useful to others? if so we might want them in our repo also as examples?"*

Fair challenge to the ownership framing. The 2026-07-27 decision was that this repo carries **portable
rules and hunts only** — so the right question is not "public vs private" but **which of these 8 are
actually portable**. I re-read all 8 definitions live off the m7kni stack. They split three ways.

Read-back note: `gcx` current-context was pointing at an unrelated customer stack, which returns 221
rules and no `entra-security-g2o` group. The correct read is `--context grafana.m7kni.com` → **444 rules,
8 SIEM alerts present by UID**. Any future session checking this must pin the context or it will
conclude the rules have vanished.

### Group 1 — fully portable, zero tenant content (4 rules)

Every selector is a graph2otel event name plus a field value that is a **Microsoft enum or a
graph2otel-emitted attribute**. Nothing tenant-shaped, nothing to redact.

| uid | why it is portable | why it is worth publishing |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `g2o-audit-tamper` | one `activity_display_name` regex over `entra.directory_audit` | the high-risk activity set *is* the value — cert/secret add, admin consent, app-role grant, new app/SP, directory-role member add, owner add, CA policy change. Reconstructing that list is the hard part of the detection, and it is tenant-independent |
| `g2o-defender-crit` | `severity` + `status` regex over `entra.security_alert` | documents that one stream covers Defender for Endpoint, Defender for Cloud Apps and Identity Protection together |
| `g2o-security-incident` | `severity` + `status` regex over `entra.security_incident` | carries the deliberate-overlap note: incidents are the correlation layer above `alerts_v2`, so one event pages twice, on purpose |
| `g2o-graph403-burst` | `sum by (app_id)` of `response_status_code="403"` over `entra.graph_activity` | the `> 10 in 5m` threshold is a tuning choice, not tenant data |

These four are the strongest argument for publishing: they are exactly the "how do I actually use this
data" worked examples the collector docs do not provide, and three of them encode non-obvious knowledge
about the shape of the Microsoft data rather than about this tenant.

### Group 2 — portable shape, one tenant policy value (1 rule)

`g2o-signin-anomaly` — interactive-user sign-ins that were CA-blocked, risk-flagged, or geographically
unexpected. The structure is portable; the expected-country literal is a per-tenant policy statement.
Publishable with that value parameterised (a documented placeholder, not a default).

### Group 3 — NOT publishable as rules (3 rules)

`g2o-sp-homelab`, `g2o-sp-intunebrew`, `g2o-sp-n8n` each hardcode an **application object GUID**, an
**application display name**, and a **small set of private-network IP literals and one IPv6 prefix**.
That is private infrastructure by definition and stays out of this repository — no values are reproduced
in this comment for that reason.

The **pattern** behind them is portable and genuinely useful, though, and is worth documenting on its
own: *a workload identity that legitimately signs in from exactly one place, alerted on any sign-in that
is failed, off-expected-geography, or off-expected-source-address*. The recorded rationale is that
workload-identity Conditional Access IP-locking requires a licence tier this tenant does not have, so
detect-and-notify substitutes for prevent. That constraint is common and the workaround is not obvious.
Publishable as a **documented template with placeholders**, never as a shipped rule.

### Two things that make this more than a copy-paste

1. **Label contract.** These 8 carry `domain`, `area`, `burnin` and `app` labels, none of which are in
   the frozen routable set validated by `build_rules.py --check` (#293/#296: `pipeline`, `severity`,
   `source`, `category`, optional `component`). They also carry **no `category`**, and none of the six
   existing category values fits an identity-threat detection. Publishing them means either normalising
   them onto the frozen contract plus at least one new `category` value, or deliberately extending the
   validated label set. That is a contract change, not a file addition.

2. **They are not measured.** All 8 fire at `> 0` with `for: 0s` and `noDataState: OK`, and 7 of the 8
   still carry the maintainer's own `burnin: "true"` marker — i.e. not yet trusted to page. The standing
   rule for this programme is that unmeasured detections publish **paused or as hunting queries** until
   evidence supports alerting. So the shipping form is documented examples or paused rules, never
   enabled-by-default alerting.

### Recommendation

Publish as a **separate, clearly-labelled example set** — not folded into `alerts/graph2otel-alerts.yaml`,
which is the operational graph2otel-health rule set and whose byte-compare drift gate should keep meaning
exactly that:

- the 4 portable detections + the parameterised sign-in rule, generated **paused**, in their own group,
  with an explicit "tune before enabling" statement and the measurement each one needs;
- the single-source workload-identity pattern as a documented template with placeholders and its
  licence-constraint rationale;
- normalise onto the frozen label contract, adding the one new `category` value the CI gate needs.

This does **not** reverse the 2026-07-27 ownership decision — it applies it. Routing, contact points and
notification policies stay out (#293/#296 unchanged), the three SP rules and their private values stay
out, and the live rules on the stack remain operator-owned regardless.

### What this changes about the blocker

It shrinks it but does not remove it. If the example set lands, the **3 SP rules** are still live-only
with no reproducible source, and they are the ones whose loss would be silent. The unblock condition is
unchanged and still maintainer-owned: **name a private location for those 3.** Their portable siblings
being published here does not cover them.

Awaiting the maintainer's call on the example set before any code lands. Evidence class:
`live-measured (2026-07-27, #300)`.

## Closed by `d94458b` — example set shipped, and the SP-rule risk accepted

Maintainer decisions 2026-07-27, both taken:

1. **Ship the portable detections as a paused example set.** Done.
2. **Accept the risk on the three per-service-principal rules and close this issue.** Recorded below.

### What shipped

`alerts/graph2otel-detections.yaml` — five detections in their own rule group and Grafana folder
(`graph2otel detections`), **all paused**. Deliberately not folded into `graph2otel-alerts.yaml`: that
file means *"is graph2otel working"*, and its drift gate should keep meaning exactly that.

| uid | portable because |
| --- | --- |
| `g2o-detect-privileged-directory-change` | the high-risk `activity_display_name` set is tenant-independent, and reconstructing it is the hard half of the detection |
| `g2o-detect-security-alert-unresolved` | Microsoft enum values only; documents that one stream carries Defender for Endpoint, Cloud Apps and ID Protection |
| `g2o-detect-security-incident-active` | same, and records the deliberate alert/incident overlap |
| `g2o-detect-graph-403-burst` | `sum by (app_id)` over a status code; the threshold is a tuning choice, not tenant data |
| `g2o-detect-interactive-signin-anomaly` | CA-failure and risk-state clauses are portable; the expected-country clause was **dropped**, not placeholdered |

On that last one: shipping `location_country_or_region!="XX"` would be a placeholder that looks like a
real value. The rule ships with only the two genuinely portable conditions and its description explains
how to add the geography term.

### Three gates, each verified by sabotage rather than by reading

| sabotage | result |
| --- | --- |
| un-pause a detection | build fails, names the rule |
| filter on an attribute the event does not carry | build fails — this is the #90 trap, where the query matches zero rows *silently* and the detection looks installed and healthy while being unable to ever fire |
| declare a field no detection queries | build fails, so the check above cannot drift into validating nothing |

`_loki_alert()` also **raises at construction** without a `tuning_required` note. A paused rule with no
stated unblock condition is one nobody can ever safely enable — the same failure mode as a waiver with
no reason.

Added `category=identity-threat` to the frozen routable label contract, distinct from `compliance` on
purpose: these route to a security responder, not to the team owning a posture drift. All five carry
the full `pipeline`/`severity`/`source`/`category` contract and pass `validate_labels`.

### No tenant content, asserted not assumed

A test scans every detection for a GUID, a dotted IPv4 literal and an IPv6 prefix. A repo-wide `rg` for
the specific application ids and home addresses of the source tenant returns nothing.

### The pattern that could not ship, documented instead

`alerts/README.md` now carries the **single-source workload identity** pattern from the three private
rules: an automation service principal that legitimately signs in from exactly one place, alerted on any
sign-in that is failed or off-expected-source. It needs no baseline and no tuning.

The reason it is detect-and-notify rather than prevent is a licensing fact worth stating plainly:
Conditional Access IP-locking for workload identities requires **Microsoft Entra Workload ID**, a
separate paid add-on. Without it a leaked service-principal credential cannot be *blocked* from being
used anywhere in the world — but graph2otel's sign-in stream lets an operator *notice* within one
evaluation interval at no extra licence cost.

### Accepted risk — recorded explicitly, and this is what closes the issue

The three `entra-security-g2o` per-SP detections (`g2o-sp-homelab`, `g2o-sp-intunebrew`, `g2o-sp-n8n`)
**exist only in the live Grafana stack and have no reproducible source anywhere.** No private location
was named, and the maintainer has decided to accept that rather than leave the issue open indefinitely.

Consequences, stated so nobody rediscovers them the hard way:

- If the stack is lost, rebuilt, or one rule is hand-edited, **those three detections are gone with no
  record** and no way to tell what changed.
- They are the detections covering this tenant's own automation identities, which is the compensating
  control for the unavailable Workload ID licence — so their loss is silent *and* meaningful.
- Recreating them needs three application ids and the current expected source addresses, none of which
  is written down outside the live rules themselves.

Anyone wanting to close this gap later: export them with
`gcx --context grafana.m7kni.com api /api/v1/provisioning/alert-rules/<uid>` for each of the three uids,
into a private location. The five portable siblings published here do **not** cover them.

### Verification

`make check` exit 0 · `make grafana-check` exit 0 (14 alert rules, 2 recording rules, **5 detection
examples, all paused**, 212 tests) · Zensical clean · asset counts updated in
`docs/deploying-observability.md` and `README.md`, enforced by `test_operator_docs`.

The #232 end-to-end page receipt remains outstanding and operator-owned; it is not tracked by this
issue.

## Terminal CI receipt — `d94458b`

All workflows **success** for the commit that landed 5 portable detections, all paused: CI, CodeQL, Docker Security, Release, Scorecard, actionlint, zizmor, Trigger Documentation Sync.

`make check` exit 0 and `make grafana-check` exit 0 locally at the same tree.

body:
## Outcome

Collector staleness should compare against each collector's effective interval, not one global one-hour placeholder.

## Evidence

**Evidence class:** `source-derived (2026-07-25)`

- The rule description calls 3600 seconds `3x YOUR configured interval`, but collectors run from minutes through 24 hours.
- The scheduler knows the effective interval but does not export it.
- The annotation also misstates how Grafana handles one missing multidimensional series versus an entirely empty query.

## Proposed scope

- Expose effective expected interval or an equivalent bounded expectation.
- Alert on staleness/expected-interval ratio.
- Separate whole-process/tenant heartbeat failure from one collector's series disappearing.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Fast, hourly, and daily collectors have correct thresholds without manual rule edits.
- [ ] One missing series and all series missing are tested against current Grafana behavior.
- [ ] Deliberately removed collectors have an explicit non-accidental outcome.
- [ ] Annotations and README no longer make false no-data claims.

## Prior decisions and duplicate check

- Not duplicate of #30: this corrects the shipped placeholder using the now-large heterogeneous collector estate.
- Related: #9, #30, #219.

## Priority

Audit recommendation: **P1**.

comments.body: Read-only evidence-lane classification: issue #299 inventory spans the scheduler/effective-interval source, self-observability metric catalog, generated alert source, rule tests and alert README. Acceptance boundary is an exact source/call-site inventory plus objective fixtures for fast/hourly/daily collectors and current missing-series behavior; no semantic choice or edits. No files are owned in this wave. Dependencies/shared seams are scheduler interval resolution, telemetry/catalog contracts, availability/removal semantics and Grafana evaluator behavior. Risk is low for inventory and high for implementation. Route: `gpt-5.6-terra`, medium reasoning, because this lane is read-only and source-verifiable; it must stop on ambiguity and cannot edit, update GitHub, commit/push, query/mutate live systems or dispatch. The primary `gpt-5.6-sol` high-reasoning lane retains the interval telemetry contract, alert semantics, frozen file ownership, TDD, integration and completion claim.

Evidence-backed blocker (2026-07-26): the staleness alert uses a fixed 3600s threshold while collectors have different configured intervals. No current signal exposes the effective expected interval per tenant/collector, so making the rule interval-aware requires a new telemetry/threshold contract rather than a query-only repair.

**Recommendation:** expose the configured/effective expected interval as bounded self-observability telemetry and alert on an approved multiplier, retaining explicit no-data/evaluator-error behavior.

**Unblock condition:** Rob approves the new telemetry field/metric and multiplier/threshold semantics. **Required human action / owner:** Rob (`rknightion`). This gates the staleness runbook/context portion of #307.

## Decision received 2026-07-27 — UNBLOCKED: per-collector expected-interval gauge, alert at 3x

Maintainer approved the recorded recommendation at https://github.com/rknightion/graph2otel/issues/299#issuecomment-5085157900, with the multiplier fixed at **3x**.

### Frozen telemetry contract

- **Metric:** `graph2otel.collector.expected_interval`
- **Unit:** seconds (Prometheus name therefore `graph2otel_collector_expected_interval_seconds`)
- **Kind:** gauge, **non-additive** — a configured duration must never be summed, so it must be classified accordingly in `internal/semconv/additive.go` or CI fails. The central cardinality limiter will drop rather than sum its tail, which is correct for this quantity.
- **Value:** the *effective* interval the scheduler will actually use for that collector, not the raw configured value, so a clamped or defaulted interval is reported truthfully.
- **Keys:** collector identity plus `tenant_id`. `tenant_id` is stamped at the emitter boundary by `telemetry.WithTenant` as for every other signal — the collector does not set it.
- **Cardinality:** one series per collector per tenant, the same bounded shape as the availability census (151 series live on m7kni), so this is tenant-shaped and bounded by construction.

### Frozen alert contract

- Alert when a collector's last-success age exceeds **3x** its expected interval.
- 3x tolerates one missed poll plus backoff jitter without paging. This matters because several workloads have mandatory client-side rate limiters (reporting 5/10s, Identity Protection 1/s per tenant, Intune export 48/min) that make an occasional missed poll routine rather than a fault.
- The 2x alternative was rejected on that basis; the static fast/hourly/daily rule-class alternative was rejected because class membership would live in the generator, so a config change to a collector's interval would silently invalidate its threshold.
- **Whole-process heartbeat failure stays a separate condition** from an individual collector series disappearing, per this issue's third criterion.
- Evaluator errors remain `Error` and no-data remains rule-specific, per the shipped #298 contract. This change must not weaken either.
- Deliberately removed collectors must have an explicit, documented, non-accidental outcome.

### Sequencing note

Adding a catalog metric couples this to the dashboard coverage gate — every cataloged metric must be panelled or waived, and a waiver requires "a panel would be actively misleading or structurally impossible", which does not apply here. So this change **must land with its self-observability panel**, which means it is sequenced against the #399 generator migration rather than run concurrently with it. It also gates the staleness runbook and context portion of #307.

## Closed by `f71cf6ea75dde3682b255293edd7270247cdbaa0`

Implements the frozen contract recorded 2026-07-27: per-collector expected-interval gauge, alert at 3×.

### The metric, as implemented

- `graph2otel.collector.expected_interval` → `graph2otel_collector_expected_interval_seconds`
- unit `s`, gauge, **`additive: false`** confirmed in the regenerated `spec/signal-catalog.json`.
  No change to `internal/semconv/additive.go` was needed — `s` was already in `nonAdditiveUnits`, so the
  real gate (`TestEveryEmittedUnitIsClassifiedForAdditivity`) passed unmodified. Verified `semconv/` is
  untouched in the diff.
- Attributes: the emitting code sets **only** `collector`; `tenant_id` is added by
  `telemetry.WithTenant` at the call site, mirroring `availability.Tracker.Emit` exactly. The collector
  never labels tenant itself.
- **Effective, not configured**: `Registry.Register`/`RegisterWindow` already resolve
  `if interval <= 0 { interval = c.DefaultInterval() }`, and emission reads the resolved
  `entry.Interval` off `Registry.Entries()`. So a clamped or defaulted interval is reported truthfully
  rather than as `0`.
- Emitted via `GaugeSnapshot` (observable). The interval is fixed for the process's life, so the
  callback re-reports on each export cycle with no periodic re-emit. A collector no longer in the
  registry reports **zero points** rather than a stale ghost value.

**Cardinality**: 50 series on the default-config tenant in the wiring test — one per *registered*
collector per tenant, bounded by construction. Strictly fewer than the availability census (151 live on
m7kni), which additionally counts disabled and blocked collectors this metric does not.

### The alert

```
max by (tenant_id, collector) (graph2otel_scrape_staleness_seconds) /
max by (tenant_id, collector) (graph2otel_collector_expected_interval_seconds)
```

Threshold `gt 3` (was `gt 3600`), verified in the regenerated manifest. Both sides aggregate by exactly
`(tenant_id, collector)`, so the division is a plain default one-to-one vector match — no `on()` or
`ignoring()`, and the PromQL-token reverse-validation gate needed no change.

The **existing** rule was modified in place; no rule was added. Count stays 14, so the
`test_operator_docs` cross-check against `README.md` and `docs/deploying-observability.md` holds.
`noDataState: Alerting` and `execErrState: Error` both verified unchanged — the shipped #298 contract is
not weakened.

### Process heartbeat versus a single collector disappearing

No second rule was added, and the separation is real rather than cosmetic, because Grafana evaluates
this rule **per `(tenant_id, collector)`**:

- `noDataState: Alerting` fires only when the **whole query** returns zero rows — every collector's
  pair gone at once, i.e. the process died or a tenant's only collector was removed. That is the
  heartbeat case.
- One collector's series disappearing while others remain does **not** trigger `noDataState`; that
  single alert instance simply stops existing and resolves. That is the deliberately-removed-collector
  case.

The previous annotation conflated these, which is the false no-data claim this issue names. It is
corrected in `alerts/README.md`, and the arithmetic is pinned by an executable test rather than prose.

**Interpretation flagged for the record:** the frozen contract's "stays a separate condition" was read
as requiring the documentation to reflect Grafana's existing per-series semantics correctly, not as a
request for a fifteenth rule — consistent with the count being frozen at 14. If a distinct heartbeat
*signal* was wanted, that is a follow-up, not a defect here.

### One reconciliation the lane correctly refused to make

`spec/grafana-semantic-canary.json` pins the `collector-staleness-query` probe to a byte-exact copy of
this rule's expression, and `test_alert_query_and_uid_match_generated_source` enforces the equality.
Changing the expression necessarily desynced it. The lane stopped rather than edit a file it had been
told to leave alone — the right call.

Resolved by syncing that one `query` field. Worth noting **why this causes no false alarm**: that probe
is already `empty: "empty_allowed"`, so until a graph2otel version emitting the new metric is deployed,
the ratio returns empty and the canary stays green rather than reporting a spurious semantic failure.
Its `required_labels` (`tenant_id`, `collector`) remain correct because both sides of the ratio group by
exactly those.

### Verification

`go test -race ./...` all packages ok · `cd grafana && python3 -m unittest discover` 142 tests OK ·
`make grafana-check` exit 0 · `make check` exit 0.

TDD evidence, observed before implementing: `r.EmitExpectedIntervals undefined`; the signal-capture
golden failing; the composition-root test reporting `expected_interval series count = 0, want 50` when
the wiring line was disabled; and on the Python side
`'graph2otel_collector_expected_interval_seconds' not found in 'max by (tenant_id, collector)
(graph2otel_scrape_staleness_seconds)'` plus `[3600] != [3]`.

### Acceptance criteria

- [x] Fast, hourly, and daily collectors have correct thresholds without manual rule edits.
- [x] One missing series and all series missing are tested against current Grafana behaviour.
- [x] Deliberately removed collectors have an explicit non-accidental outcome.
- [x] Annotations and README no longer make false no-data claims.

### Deployment note

The alert is only meaningful once a version emitting `expected_interval` is running in production. Until
then the ratio query returns empty, which the `empty_allowed` canary probe tolerates and the alert's own
`noDataState` treats as the heartbeat condition. This gates the staleness runbook and context portion of
#307.

Exact-SHA workflow receipt to follow.

## Terminal exact-SHA receipt — `f71cf6ea75dde3682b255293edd7270247cdbaa0`

All workflows for the exact tip reached terminal **success**:
[CI](https://github.com/rknightion/graph2otel/actions/runs/30263235677) · CodeQL · Docker Security ·
Release · Scorecard · actionlint · zizmor.

No documentation-sync run was expected — the only doc-shaped change was `alerts/README.md`, which is
outside the docs-sync path filter.

No Grafana or tenant resource was mutated by this work. The alert becomes meaningful in production once
a version emitting `graph2otel_collector_expected_interval_seconds` is deployed; until then the ratio is
empty, which the `empty_allowed` canary probe tolerates.

## Outcome

A datasource outage, invalid query, or evaluator failure must not turn an alert green.

## Evidence

**Evidence class:** `source-derived (2026-07-25)`

- The alert generator defaults every rule to `execErrState: OK`.
- Recording rules in the same generator use `execErrState: Error`, exposing the inconsistency.

## Proposed scope

- Default alert evaluator failures to `Error` or another explicitly chosen non-OK state.
- Require a documented per-rule waiver for any exception.
- Keep `noDataState` rule-specific because healthy-empty signals are real.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] A deliberately broken query reaches the intended error/routing state.
- [x] Generator tests reject silent-green evaluator failures without a waiver.
- [x] No-data behavior remains independently configured and documented.

## Prior decisions and duplicate check

- No prior issue covers the generated `execErrState` default.
- Related: #219.

## Priority

Audit recommendation: **P1**.

comments.body:
Completed by `55ff9ead983ba7dc0c05f1b3a67d53ab2109e12f`.

Implementation:
- Generated alerts now default to `execErrState: Error`; all 14 generated rules were regenerated.
- `_alert` rejects `execErrState: OK` unless the rule supplies a non-empty `exec_error_waiver`, which is emitted as an annotation.
- `noDataState` remains independent and rule-specific; the README documents the boundary.

TDD evidence:
- RED: all three focused tests failed against the previous `OK` default, absent waiver validation, and independent-state assertions.
- GREEN: 71 Grafana tests pass; `make grafana-check` reports 330/330 metrics, 383 panels/6 dashboards, 14 alerts, and 2 recording rules.
- `make check`: pass.
- `uvx --from zensical==0.0.46 zensical build --clean`: pass, no issues.

Runtime evidence (`live-measured 2026-07-26`, disposable local Grafana only): official `grafana/grafana` image digest `sha256:1c1bd67c54c5fcf6e759897852b5a584191bd6796e8d328a5ace457799801261`, Grafana 13.1.1 commit `a9cee6e1724a455676bb6c05eef7fc54aa4b19f4`. A file-provisioned rule with `execErrState: Error`, `noDataState: OK`, and an intentionally unreachable Prometheus datasource evaluated with `health=error`, alert state `Error`, and `totals.error=1`. The provisioned webhook received one firing alert routed to `issue-298-capture` with `alertname=DatasourceError`, `datasource_uid=grafanacloud-prom`, and `rulename=issue-298 deliberately broken query`. The disposable container and webhook server were then stopped.

No production Grafana resource was changed. Publishing the regenerated pack remains part of the coordinated #293/#294/#296 deployment/routing wave; this child proves the source contract and actual Grafana evaluator/routing behavior without pre-empting that live mutation.

body:
## Outcome

Derived alert-count series must never collapse events from different tenants or silently miss accepted late-arriving logs.

## Evidence

**Evidence class:** `source-derived; late-arrival risk reasoned from measured indexing behavior (2026-07-25)`

- Both recording queries group by event dimensions but omit `tenant_id`.
- In a multi-tenant backend, matching events become one recorded series, contradicting #143.
- The rules evaluate a one-hour range once per hour while accepted backdated events can become queryable later.

## Proposed scope

- Include tenant identity in recording output.
- Measure and decide exact late-arrival/backfill behavior.
- Retain the #188/#189 decision to use Loki recording rules unless evidence proves it cannot meet the requirement.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] A two-tenant fixture proves counts never merge.
- [ ] An event becoming queryable after its nominal window is tested.
- [ ] Any offset/backfill strategy has bounded duplicate and cost semantics.
- [x] Documentation states what the derived metric includes and can miss.

## Prior decisions and duplicate check

- Not duplicate of #188/#189: those created the two rules; this fixes multi-tenant identity and validates materialization timing.
- Related: #143, #188, #189, #226.

## Priority

Audit recommendation: **P1**.

Post-push verification for `84b938118ea39660c37251b97bc81a64cbc5401d` is terminal-success:
