## Outcome

A failed or cancelled async audit query must not remain in durable state and be polled forever.

## Evidence

**Evidence class:** `source-derived (2026-07-25)`

- Terminal query outcomes clear in-memory state and call an error-discarding persist helper.
- `CollectWindow` returns on the terminal error before its final checkpoint save.
- A disk clear failure can therefore leave the terminal query ID adoptable after restart.

## Proposed scope

- Surface terminal clear failure while preserving the primary query error with `errors.Join`.
- Retain the intentional initial-persistence/orphan behavior.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Injected clear failure is returned alongside the terminal query error.
- [x] A successful clear prevents adoption by a fresh client.
- [x] Failure does not corrupt the prior good checkpoint.

## Prior decisions and duplicate check

- No existing issue covers terminal-clear durability in jobpipeline.
- Related: #117, #118, #147.

## Priority

Audit recommendation: **P1**.

body:
## Outcome

Sustained blob read or cursor persistence failures must not report a successful scrape.

## Evidence

**Evidence class:** `source-derived (2026-07-25)`

- `blobpipeline.Poll` returns an error for list failure only.
- Per-blob read and cursor-save failures are logged and discarded; even all blobs failing returns nil.
- A missing Storage Blob Data Reader grant can therefore emit nothing while `scrape.success=1`.

## Proposed scope

- Continue processing all blobs, aggregate read/save errors, and return the joined error after reporting gate statistics.
- Successful blobs must still emit and checkpoint.

## Constraints and non-goals

- Do not make one bad blob block other containers.
- Do not add the engine-side seen-ID dedupe rejected by #138.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] One failure plus one success emits/checkpoints the success and returns a degraded error.
- [x] All reads failing is a failed scrape.
- [x] Cursor-save failure is visible in scheduler self-observability.
- [x] Malformed individual JSON lines retain their explicitly chosen handling.

## Prior decisions and duplicate check

- Not duplicate of #240: that issue fixed M365 report partial failure; it is the precedent for this blob-engine variant.
- Related: #138, #240.

## Priority

Audit recommendation: **P0**.

## Outcome

One O365 content type failing before listing must not let a healthy type advance the shared watermark beyond unseen audit content.

## Evidence

**Evidence class:** `source-derived (2026-07-25)`

- All content types share `maxConsumed` and `earliestFailed`.
- Subscription-start or list failure returns zero timestamps.
- A later healthy content type can then advance the watermark.
- The current cross-type guard test covers only a blob-fetch failure where a concrete failure time exists.

## Proposed scope

- On pre-list failure, cap advancement at the cycle's starting watermark/resume boundary.
- Continue draining healthy content types and persist their SeenIDs.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Failed list A plus successful newer B emits B but does not advance beyond the prior boundary.
- [x] A later recovery consumes A's older content.
- [x] Healthy SeenIDs survive and the checkpoint remains resumable.
- [x] The test covers subscription-start and list failures.

## Prior decisions and duplicate check

- Not duplicate of #100: this is a newly identified shared-watermark loss mode in the shipped engine.
- Related: #100.

## Priority

Audit recommendation: **P0**.

body:
## Outcome

A foreign absolute URL or response-supplied next link must never receive the Microsoft Graph bearer token.

## Evidence

**Evidence class:** `source-derived (2026-07-25)`

- `graphclient` defines valid hosts but passes them only to the typed Kiota auth provider.
- Raw GET/POST manually acquire and attach a bearer to any absolute URL.
- An existing test proves a token is sent to an arbitrary `httptest` host.
- Response-derived next links flow through raw REST adapters.

## Proposed scope

- Retain the effective valid-host set on the raw client.
- Require HTTPS and an allowed host before token acquisition for raw GET/POST.
- Support sovereign and test hosts through explicit options.

## Constraints and non-goals

- Do not block the legitimate Graph report redirect to an unauthenticated SAS download; #120 already protects bearer stripping on redirects.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] A foreign server receives zero requests and no token is acquired for it.
- [x] Allowed public, sovereign, and explicit test hosts work.
- [x] A foreign next link fails before emission or checkpoint movement.
- [x] Raw GET and POST are both covered.

## Prior decisions and duplicate check

- No prior issue covers initial raw-URL host validation; #120 covers redirect behavior only.
- Related: #120.

body:
## Outcome

Kubernetes and the admin UI must distinguish a live process from one that has no tenant capable of collecting data.

## Evidence

**Evidence class:** `source-derived (2026-07-25)`

- Authentication/client setup failures can be converted into zero sources or dropped tenant entries.
- The admin status derives an empty tenant set as healthy.
- `/healthz` is unconditional; there is no `/readyz`.
- The Helm chart uses `/healthz` for both liveness and readiness.
- An enabled admin server failing to bind only logs an error while the process continues.

## Proposed scope

- Keep dependency-free `/healthz` liveness and add explicit `/readyz` semantics.
- Retain failed tenants and startup reasons in JSON/UI status.
- Define partial-tenant readiness and transition after successful work.
- Make admin bind failure fatal when admin is enabled.

## Constraints and non-goals

- Do not tie liveness to transient Microsoft or OTLP availability.
- Do not introduce HA or leader election.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Configured tenants plus zero working tenants yields liveness 200 and readiness 503.
- [x] A bad tenant remains visible with a sanitized reason.
- [x] Partial-tenant behavior and first-success transition are tested.
- [x] Helm uses `/readyz` for readiness and `/healthz` for liveness.
- [x] Admin bind failure exits non-zero.

## Prior decisions and duplicate check

- Not duplicate of #12: that issue intentionally established liveness; this adds readiness and preserves failed startup state.
- Related: #3, #10, #12, #85, #178.

## Priority

Audit recommendation: **P1**.

comments.body:
Implementation started from `7bb3fe97bc403ac5f80e0bf187a7a337a9cd5803`.

Frozen readiness contract:
- `/healthz` remains dependency-free and always live while the process runs.
- zero configured tenants remains ready for the valid stdout smoke mode;
- configured tenants with no working collectors are `503 no_working_tenants`;
- working collectors with no lifetime success are `503 waiting_for_first_success`;
- the first successful collector run latches readiness to 200; later transient failures degrade health but do not flap readiness;
- partial tenants are ready once any tenant has a lifetime success, while failed tenants remain visible and overall health stays degraded.

Startup failure codes are bounded to `credential_initialization_failed` and `graph_client_initialization_failed`; raw errors stay in logs and are never retained in JSON/UI. Helm liveness remains `/healthz`; readiness moves to `/readyz`. An enabled admin server bind/serve failure is fatal and drains tenant schedulers.

Parallel file ownership:
1. `internal/admin/**` readiness/status/HTTP/UI.
2. `cmd/graph2otel/**` tenant retention and fatal admin supervision.
3. Helm probes and operator docs/generated chart README.

Strict RED/GREEN per lane, then a single wiring/full-gate review.

body:
## Outcome

A configured `client_id` must not disagree with the identity that actually authenticated or cause `exclude_self` to filter the wrong application's records.

## Evidence

**Evidence class:** `source-derived (2026-07-25)`

- `internal/auth/auth.go` documents per-tenant app selection but explicitly ignores tenant `ClientID` and uses the ambient credential chain.
- Config and docs describe `client_id` as the authenticating app and authoritative self identity.
- `exclude_self` prefers the configured value even when it differs from the actual credential.
- One process cannot repeat a different `AZURE_CLIENT_ID` environment variable per tenant as the current README suggests.

## Proposed scope

- Retain #3's shared ambient application identity per process and tenant-pin it across directories.
- Use the actual authenticated application ID for self-exclusion.
- Reject or prominently diagnose configured IDs that disagree with the authenticated identity.
- Correct the multi-tenant authentication documentation.

## Constraints and non-goals

- Do not put secrets in YAML.
- Do not add multiple credential chains or a per-tenant secret store in this issue.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] A config/environment client-ID mismatch cannot exclude third-party records.
- [x] `exclude_self` keys from the authenticated identity.
- [x] Shared-app multi-tenant operation remains supported.
- [x] Workload identity and managed identity behavior is explicit.
- [x] Tests cover known mismatch and identity-not-discoverable cases.

## Prior decisions and duplicate check

- Not duplicate of #3: this corrects a contract mismatch introduced around the shared-app implementation and later self-exclusion work.
- Related: #3, #154, #176.

## Priority

Audit recommendation: **P1**.

comments.body: Maintainer decision: use the recommended authenticated-identity policy. The authenticated application identity is authoritative. If it cannot be proven, disable `exclude_self` with a loud bounded diagnostic; configured `client_id` alone is not proof.

Implementation review found a tenant-binding safety blocker. The prior premise that `azidentity.DefaultAzureCredentialOptions.TenantID` pins every credential leg is false in azidentity v1.14.0:

- Environment client-secret/certificate credentials take their default authority from ambient `AZURE_TENANT_ID`. Cross-tenant requests require both `policy.TokenRequestOptions.TenantID` and an explicitly allowed target tenant.
- Workload identity, Azure CLI, and Azure Developer CLI consume the configured tenant option.
- Managed identity ignores the tenant request and remains bound to its home tenant.

Without a credential wrapper, a second configured tenant can be queried under the ambient/home tenant and then stamped with the wrong `tenant_id`. The implementation is parked before integration.

Decision requested: require `tenants[].tenant_id` to be the Entra directory GUID (recommended), set that tenant on every token request, allow only that target on the credential, and verify every returned token `tid`; or retain verified-domain values even though managed-identity tenant binding cannot be locally proved. The GUID contract is the fail-closed option.

Independent review also identified stale Helm/operator wording and four description-only generated artifacts; those are mechanical follow-ups after the tenant contract is fixed.

Decision resolved by the maintainer instruction to use all recommendations: adopt the fail-closed GUID contract. `tenants[].tenant_id` must be the Entra directory GUID; every token request targets that tenant; the credential may access only that explicit target; and every returned token `tid` must match before any tenant-labelled data is emitted. This unblocks implementation.

Completed by `1b8069c`.

Implemented the recommended fail-closed contract:
- `tenants[].tenant_id` is a hyphenated Entra directory GUID.
- Every token request is pinned to that tenant and every returned `tid` is verified before Graph or blob setup.
- Managed identity bound to another home tenant fails closed.
- `exclude_self` uses the authenticated token `appid`; configured `client_id` is an optional consistency assertion only.
- Identity proof failure retains records and emits one bounded warning; it never falls back to config or environment identity.

Verification on current main: independent review READY; `make check` green; `make grafana-check` green (325/325 catalog metrics, 60 tests); Helm schema/render tests and generated catalog drift gates green.

Post-push receipt for `1b8069cdae01ab0b0a19fe79fd53ce8c5eedaa26`: all eight workflows reached terminal `success` — CI, CodeQL, Docker Security, Scorecard, actionlint, zizmor, Release, and Trigger Documentation Sync.

## Mission

Reconcile graph2otel’s current generated Grafana observability assets with the live m7kni stack, including the dedicated self-observability dashboard. Preserve the documented ownership model: direct `gcx` deployment because graph2otel is not currently managed in `gc-gitsync-m7kni`.

## Source artifacts

- Six generated dashboards in `dashboards/`, including `graph2otel-self-obs`.
- Generated Grafana alert provisioning in `alerts/graph2otel-alerts.yaml`.
- Two generated Grafana-managed, Loki-backed recording rules in `recording-rules/`.

## Approach

- [x] Run the Grafana generation, coverage, validation, and staleness gate.
- [x] Inventory all six dashboard UIDs and current live content/folder placement.
- [x] Inventory the live `graph2otel` alerts and `graph2otel derived metrics` recording rules.
- [x] Validate and update/create all dashboard assets through `gcx`.
- [x] Reconcile generated alerts and recording rules through the Grafana provisioning API using fixed UIDs, without creating duplicates.
- [x] Verify exact rule/dashboard identity, datasource references, routing labels, group intervals, and evaluation health after deployment.
- [x] Record live-measured receipts here and close the issue.

## Acceptance

- All six generated dashboards are current in m7kni, including the dedicated self-observability dashboard.
- All generated alert and recording rules exist exactly once in their documented folders/groups.
- Every deployed rule has evaluated successfully or has a documented expected no-data state.
- No GitSync files or unrelated Grafana resources are changed.
- Local repositories remain clean.

body:
Found while closing out #234's priority-2 sweep on `m365.unified_audit`. Filed against the **engine** rather than that collector, because the exposure belongs to every `jobpipeline` collector present and future.

## What

`internal/jobpipeline`'s `emitAndAdvance` takes the id returned by `cfg.Map` and uses it as the dedupe key with no guard for the empty string:

```go
for _, d := range all {
	if cp.SeenIDs.Has(d.id) {
		continue
	}
	e.LogEvent(d.ev)
	cp.SeenIDs.Add(d.id, d.t)
}
```

`SeenIDs` is a plain `map[string]time.Time` — `Add` is `s[id] = eventTime`, `Has` is a bare lookup — so `""` is a perfectly valid key:

```go
func (s SeenIDs) Add(id string, eventTime time.Time) { s[id] = eventTime }
func (s SeenIDs) Has(id string) bool { _, ok := s[id]; return ok }
```

Verified by reading both files, not inferred.

## The failure

If a mapper ever returns an empty id — a record shape without the key field, a wire change, a workload that omits it — then within a window:

1. The **first** such record is emitted, and `""` is recorded in `SeenIDs`.
2. **Every subsequent** empty-id record hits `SeenIDs.Has("")` → `true` → `continue`, and is **dropped without a log line**.

So the loss is not one record. It is all-but-one of them, for the life of the overlap window, and it grows with how many arrive. Nothing counts it, nothing warns, and the collector reports a healthy poll.

This is the same shape as the two defects fixed in `3d129cb`: a mechanism that is silently, confidently wrong and looks exactly like a healthy steady state. `m365.unified_audit` now announces its own case through `wirecheck.MissingField(id)`, but that is one collector telling you after the fact — it does not stop the drop, and it does nothing for the other `jobpipeline` collectors.

## Why it has not bitten yet

No mapper currently returns an empty id on any observed record. This is a **latent** path, not a live incident — which is precisely why it is worth fixing now rather than after a wire change makes it live. The cost of the fix is a few lines; the cost of discovering it in production is a silent hole in an audit feed.

## The fix, and the decision inside it

Dedupe should be **skipped, not poisoned**, when there is no id. An identifier-less record cannot be deduplicated, and the honest behaviour is to emit it every time rather than to drop every one after the first.

Per `CLAUDE.md`'s emitter rule: **undedupeable is degraded; misdated is wrong — only wrong justifies a drop.** A duplicate is a cosmetic annoyance a query can collapse; a silently missing audit record is not recoverable and not visible.

```go
if d.id != "" {
    if cp.SeenIDs.Has(d.id) { continue }
    cp.SeenIDs.Add(d.id, d.t)
}
e.LogEvent(d.ev)
```

There is a real judgement here worth stating rather than assuming: this trades **possible duplicates for guaranteed delivery**. If a mapper starts returning empty ids for a high-volume record type, the same records re-emit every overlap window. That is why the counter below matters — the condition must be *visible*, not merely survivable.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An empty id never enters `SeenIDs`, and never suppresses a later record
- [ ] A test that fails on today's code: three records with empty ids through one window emit **three** events, not one
- [ ] The condition is counted or warned once per poll — a silent recovery from a silent bug is still silent. Consider reusing `internal/wirecheck` rather than a bespoke counter, so it lands on the existing `graph2otel.api.unexpected` surface
- [ ] Check `logpipeline` and `o365pipeline` for the same shape — this is an engine pattern and may not be confined to one of them
- [ ] `make check` green

## Not in scope

Do not make an empty id a fetch error or drop the record. That converts a dedupe gap into exactly the data loss this issue is about.

Refs #234
title: bug(jobpipeline): an empty record id is added to SeenIDs as "", so every later empty-id record in the window is silently deduped away

body:
Found while sweeping #234. Not fixed there — it is a correctness defect, not a watchdog gap.

## What

`internal/collectors/intune/manageddevices/blob.go:109` lowercases the blob's `CompliantState` before handing it to `complianceBucketFor`:

```go
ComplianceState: strings.ToLower(blobStr(props, "CompliantState")),
```

But `complianceBuckets` (`manageddevices.go:114`) is keyed **camelCase** for two of its seven members:

```go
var complianceBuckets = map[string]string{
	"unknown":       "unknown",
	"compliant":     "compliant",
	"noncompliant":  "noncompliant",
	"conflict":      "conflict",
	"error":         "error",
	"inGracePeriod": "in_grace_period",   // <- never matches a lowercased input
	"configManager": "config_manager",    // <- never matches a lowercased input
}
```

`complianceBucketFor` returns `"other"` on a miss, so those two states are silently reclassified on the blob path only.

## Proof

Run against the real functions, not reasoned about:

```
blob "InGracePeriod" -> ToLower "ingraceperiod" -> bucket "other"
blob "ConfigManager" -> ToLower "configmanager" -> bucket "other"
blob "Compliant"     -> ToLower "compliant"     -> bucket "compliant"
blob "Noncompliant"  -> ToLower "noncompliant"  -> bucket "noncompliant"
```

The five all-lowercase members work, which is why this has never looked broken. Only the two camelCase members fail, and they are the two least common states — so the bug is both real and rarely exercised.

**A live blob record carrying the failing value is already in the repo**: `blob_test.go:140` decodes `"CompliantState":"InGracePeriod"`. Nothing asserts `compliance_state` on it, which is why the suite is green over it.

## Why it matters

The package doc claims Graph/blob twin parity, and this breaks it:

| `CompliantState` on the wire | Graph path | blob path |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `InGracePeriod` | `in_grace_period` | **`other`** |
| `ConfigManager` | `config_manager` | **`other`** |

Same device, same state, two different answers depending on which transport is configured. Since transport is exclusive per collector (#144), a tenant on blob ingest gets a permanently wrong bucket for these states and has nothing to compare against.

**Currently log-only.** The blob path feeds `deviceLogTwin`, not a gauge — so this does not move a metric today. That bounds the blast radius; it does not make it correct, and the moment anyone counts by `compliance_state` on the blob path it becomes a wrong number.

## The fix, and the trap in it

The obvious repair is to lowercase the map keys. **Do not do that without checking the Graph path**, which passes `d.ComplianceState` in *unmodified* — Graph sends `inGracePeriod` camelCase (per the source comment at `blob.go:21`: *"polled is lowercase"*, which is itself worth re-verifying against a live record rather than trusted). Lowercasing the keys would fix blob and break Graph.

Options, in preference order:

1. **Case-fold at the lookup**, not at either call site — make `complianceBucketFor` match case-insensitively, so both transports feed it whatever the wire sent. Removes the whole class of defect.
2. Stop lowercasing in `blob.go` and let the raw wire value flow through, if blob genuinely sends camelCase too. Needs a live blob record to confirm, and the repo fixture says `"Compliant"` (title case) — so the two transports really do differ in casing and option 1 is likely the honest answer.

Whichever is chosen, the comment at `blob.go:21` asserting the polled casing must be re-checked against a live record, since a wrong statement there is what makes this look correct on inspection.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `InGracePeriod` / `ConfigManager` bucket identically on both transports, proven by a test that fails on today's code
- [ ] The existing `blob_test.go:140` `InGracePeriod` fixture gains an assertion on `compliance_state` — it is already present and already unasserted, which is how this hid
- [ ] The casing claim in the `blob.go` package doc re-verified against a live record of each transport, or softened to what is actually known
- [ ] Check the sibling bucket maps in this package for the same shape — this is a class, not necessarily one instance
- [ ] `make check` green

Refs #234, #144
title: bug(intune.devices): the blob path lowercases CompliantState but the bucket map is camelCase — InGracePeriod and ConfigManager both land in 'other'

Unblocked by the #251 Phase 6 grant of `AccessReview.Read.All` (granted 2026-07-24). Wire shape live-probed as `graph2otel-poller`; **not yet built**.

## Why — the second wrong prediction from Phase 6

#251's table caveated this one *"Needs Governance licence for data to exist."* A review exists anyway, and it is **`InProgress`**.

An access review that is created and then never completed is a governance control that looks present and does nothing — the same failure shape as a disabled alert rule. Nothing in graph2otel sees review state today.

Available on **both `v1.0` and `beta`** (200/200), so no `Experimental` gate.

## Wire facts — `live-measured 2026-07-24, n=1 tenant`

`GET /identityGovernance/accessReviews/definitions` — **1 row**:

```json
{"id":"fef06240-0798-4e51-aa95-ac4fb55404ce",
 "displayName":"Quarterly Global Administrator review",
 "createdDateTime":"2026-07-19T18:14:10.2862528Z","lastModifiedDateTime":"2026-07-19T18:19:48.2990832Z",
 "status":"InProgress",
 "descriptionForAdmins":"Review all Global Administrator role holders","descriptionForReviewers":"",
 "createdBy":{"id":"8f35f4e9-5c91-42db-a1f7-d77ada4cc0a2","displayName":"","type":null,"userPrincipalName":""},
 "scope":{"@odata.type":"#microsoft.graph.principalResourceMembershipsScope","principalScopes":[...]}}
```

Full key set: `additionalNotificationRecipients`, `backupReviewers`, `createdBy`, `createdDateTime`, `customData`, `customDataProvider`, `descriptionForAdmins`, `descriptionForReviewers`, `displayName`, `fallbackReviewers`, `id`, `instanceEnumerationScope`, `instances`, `lastModifiedDateTime`, `reviewers`, `scope`, `settings`, `stageSettings`, `status`.

Traps observed:

- **`createdBy` is populated but its `displayName` and `userPrincipalName` are EMPTY STRINGS** while `id` is set. Emitting the empty strings would put blank identity fields on the twin that look like missing data rather than "the API did not resolve it". Omit empties; keep the id.
- `scope` is **polymorphic** (`@odata.type: principalResourceMembershipsScope` here) — read the discriminator, do not decode structurally.
- `instances` comes back as an expanded nav property with its own `@odata.context`. A review's *instances* are its recurrences, so per-instance state (what percentage reviewed, what was decided) is the part that answers "is this review actually being done" — decide explicitly whether instances are in scope, and if they are, whether they need a separate fetch.
- `status` is an assumed enum (`InProgress` observed; others not). Prime candidate for a `wirecheck.Enum` (#234) — but only once more than one value has been seen, per that issue's evidence rule. **Do not declare the set from documentation.**

## Live finding worth noting

`createdBy.id` is `8f35f4e9-5c91-42db-a1f7-d77ada4cc0a2`, which is the **`homelab-agentic-mgmt` service principal** — so this review was created by automation rather than by a person in the portal. Not necessarily wrong, but worth the maintainer knowing, since a review with no human owner has nobody to complete it, and it is currently `InProgress`.

## Shape (#112/#114)

- **Bounded gauge** by `status` — bounded by review count, which is governance-config-shaped rather than tenant-size-shaped.
- **Log twin per definition**: display name, descriptions, status, created/modified timestamps, the scope type, reviewer and fallback-reviewer counts. Reviewer *identities* on the twin only.
- **Warn on a review stuck `InProgress` well past its expected cadence** — the "control exists but is not being done" case. Needs the instance data to be honest about; if instances are out of scope, do not claim to detect staleness.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Mapper written against the verbatim sample above
- [ ] Empty-string identity fields omitted, never emitted as blanks
- [ ] `scope` and any other polymorphic member read via `@odata.type`
- [ ] Explicit decision recorded on whether review *instances* are in scope
- [ ] `status` left unwatched by `wirecheck` until a second value is observed (#234's evidence rule)
- [ ] `signalgate_test.go` + `testdata/signals.json`, annotation, blank import, `docs/collectors.md` regenerated
- [ ] `make check` green

body:
Unblocked by the #251 Phase 6 grant of `WindowsUpdates.Read.All` (granted 2026-07-24). Wire shape live-probed as `graph2otel-poller`; **not yet built**.

## Why — and a prediction that was wrong

#251's Phase 6 table listed this as *"a read-only app role **does** exist, contrary to the obvious assumption. Grant to **find out** whether there is anything there — the 403 body was uninformative and the shape is EDM-only."*

**There is something there.** All three segments return real data. This is no longer EDM-only.

Update deployment is the one Intune surface where "nothing happened" and "the update ring is broken" look identical from outside, so it is worth watching.

**Beta only** (`v1.0` → `400 "Resource not found for the segment 'windows'"`) → `Experimental` per #183.

## Wire facts — `live-measured 2026-07-24, n=1 tenant`

`GET /beta/admin/windows/updates/updatePolicies` — **2 rows**:

```json
{"id":"0fa55cf5-4598-4fe3-b6c1-a724e5035f9d","createdDateTime":"2025-10-09T12:35:44.5615718Z",
 "autoEnrollmentUpdateCategories":["quality"],
 "complianceChangeRules":[{"@odata.type":"#microsoft.graph.windowsUpdates.contentApprovalRule",
   "createdDateTime":"2026-07-21T21:16:03.9736656Z","lastEvaluatedDateTime":"0001-01-01T00:00:00Z",
   "lastModifiedDateTime":"2026-07-21T21:16:03.9736656Z","durationBeforeDeploymentStart":"PT0S",
   "contentFilter":{"@odata.type":"#microsoft.graph.windowsUpdates.qualityUpdateFilter",
     "classification":"security","cadence":"monthly"}}],
 "deploymentSettings":{"schedule":null,"monitoring":null, ...}}
```

`GET /beta/admin/windows/updates/deployments` — **1 row**:

```json
{"id":"a964123e-df58-4910-a0cb-483ebfb2f2d6","createdDateTime":"2026-07-21T22:26:29.2238015Z",
 "lastModifiedDateTime":"2026-07-24T18:02:31.0492953Z",
 "state":{"effectiveValue":"offering","requestedValue":"none","reasons":[]},
 "content":{"@odata.type":"#microsoft.graph.windowsUpdates.catalogContent",
   "catalogEntry":{"@odata.type":"#microsoft.graph.windowsUpdates.qualityUpdateCatalogEntry",
     "id":"","displayName":null, ...}}}
```

`GET /beta/admin/windows/updates/products` — **17 rows**, a static-ish catalogue:

```json
{"id":"904","name":"Windows Server 2008 SP2","groupName":"Previous versions","friendlyNames":["Windows Server 2008 SP2"]}
```

Traps observed:

- **`state` is a THREE-part object**: `effectiveValue`, `requestedValue`, `reasons[]`. On the live row these **disagree** — `effectiveValue: "offering"` while `requestedValue: "none"`. Collapsing this to one value loses the entire signal; a deployment whose effective state does not match what was asked for is precisely the interesting case, and `reasons[]` says why. Map all three.
- **Polymorphic `@odata.type` everywhere** — `contentApprovalRule`, `qualityUpdateFilter`, `catalogContent`, `qualityUpdateCatalogEntry`. Read the discriminator; a feature-update variant will carry different fields. Do not decode structurally and hope.
- The nested `catalogEntry` has **`"id": ""` and `"displayName": null`** on the live row. An empty id is not a real identifier — omit rather than emit, or the twin claims to name an update it cannot name.
- `lastEvaluatedDateTime: "0001-01-01T00:00:00Z"` is the .NET zero date meaning "never evaluated". Never emit it as a real timestamp.
- `durationBeforeDeploymentStart: "PT0S"` is an ISO-8601 duration string, not a number.
- `products` is a catalogue, not tenant state. Consider whether it is worth collecting at all, or whether it is 17 rows of constant that belong in neither a metric nor a log. **A default of "do not collect it" is a legitimate answer** — say so explicitly rather than collecting it because it returned 200.

## Shape (#112/#114)

- **Bounded gauges**: deployments by `effective_value` × `requested_value` (a state-mismatch count falls straight out); update policies by `autoEnrollmentUpdateCategories` member.
- **Log twin per policy and per deployment**, carrying the approval rules, the content filter, the full three-part state and `reasons[]`.
- **Warn when `effectiveValue != requestedValue`** — that is the "the ring is not doing what you asked" signal this collector exists for.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Mapper written against the verbatim samples above
- [ ] All three parts of `state` mapped; a mismatch drives severity
- [ ] Every `@odata.type` discriminator read, not assumed
- [ ] Empty-string ids and zero-dates omitted, never emitted as real values
- [ ] Explicit decision recorded on whether `products` is collected at all
- [ ] `Experimental` (beta-only surface)
- [ ] `signalgate_test.go` + `testdata/signals.json`, annotation, blank import, `docs/collectors.md` regenerated
- [ ] `make check` green

body:
Unblocked by the #251 Phase 6 grant of `DeviceManagementCloudCA.Read.All` (granted 2026-07-24). Wire shape live-probed as `graph2otel-poller`; **not yet built**.

## Why

Intune Cloud PKI issues the certificates devices use to authenticate — Wi-Fi, VPN, 802.1X. When the issuing CA expires, **every device that depends on it loses authentication at once**, and there is no gradual degradation to notice first. m7kni licenses Intune Suite, so this is live infrastructure here, not a hypothetical.

`entra.credential_expiry` watches app and SP credentials and cannot see this at all — a different PKI entirely.

**Beta only** (`v1.0` → `400`, no such segment) → `Experimental` per #183.

## Wire facts — `live-measured 2026-07-24, n=1 tenant`

`GET /beta/deviceManagement/cloudCertificationAuthority` — **2 rows**:

```json
{"id":"a29d1328-90ea-4400-a53f-195f870b1444","displayName":"root-m7kni","description":null,
 "scepServerUrl":null,
 "certificateRevocationListUrl":"http://primary-cdn.pki.azure.net/westeurope/crls/<id>/<id>_v1/current.crl",
 "certificateDownloadUrl":"data:application/x-x509-ca-cert;base64,MIIGOzCCBCOgAwIBAgIRAOQQR7i+tZUlMJ02T+2PHGgw..."}
```

**The CA certificate is inline as a `data:` URI**, base64 DER. That is what makes expiry measurable without a second fetch or any credential — decode it and read `NotAfter` from the x509 structure. Go's `crypto/x509` parses it directly; no new dependency.

The subject on this one decodes to `CN=m7kni.io, O=m7kni, OU=home, L=Fair Oak, ST=Hampshire, C=GB`, valid from `2025-10-07` to **`2050-10-07`** — so on this tenant expiry is far out and the collector will sit at a healthy steady state. **That is exactly the case where a mapping bug is invisible** (the green-tick rule), so the tests must assert against a fixture with a near-term expiry as well as this one.

Not yet resolved: `cloudCertificationAuthorityLeafCertificate` returns **`404`** as a top-level list on beta. It is presumably reachable under a parent CA id (`/cloudCertificationAuthority/{id}/...`), which was **not probed**. Per-leaf issuance data would be the per-device half of this signal — resolve the route before promising it, and do not map it from documentation.

## Shape (#112/#114)

- **Bounded gauges**: `intune.cloud_pki.authorities` count; `intune.cloud_pki.days_until_expiry` — but note that a per-CA expiry gauge keyed by CA id is bounded by CA count (2 here), not tenant size, so it is a legitimate label. Confirm that reasoning holds before shipping.
- **Log twin per CA**: id, display name, the decoded subject and issuer, `NotBefore`/`NotAfter`, the CRL URL, the SCEP server URL. **Never emit the certificate blob itself** — it is a public cert, not a secret, but it is large and useless in a log line.
- Severity ladder off time-to-expiry, matching whatever thresholds `entra.credential_expiry` already uses so the two agree.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Mapper written against the verbatim sample above
- [ ] Expiry derived by parsing the inline `data:` URI with `crypto/x509`, not from any documented field
- [ ] A test fixture with a NEAR-TERM expiry, so the alerting path is exercised on a tenant whose real CA expires in 2050
- [ ] `Experimental` (beta-only surface)
- [ ] Certificate blob never emitted; decoded fields only
- [ ] The `LeafCertificate` route either resolved and mapped, or explicitly recorded as unresolved with the 404 evidence
- [ ] `signalgate_test.go` + `testdata/signals.json`, annotation, blank import, `docs/collectors.md` regenerated
- [ ] `make check` green

body:
Unblocked by the #251 Phase 6 grant of `DeviceManagementRBAC.Read.All` (granted 2026-07-24). Wire shape live-probed as `graph2otel-poller`; **not yet built**.

## Why

Intune maintains its **own** RBAC store, entirely separate from Entra directory roles. `entra.roles` enumerates directory-role holders and sees none of it. So today, a principal granted sweeping device-management rights through an Intune custom role — wipe, retire, app assignment, script execution — is **completely invisible to graph2otel**, while a Global Reader shows up immediately.

Available on **both `v1.0` and `beta`** (200/200), so no `Experimental` gate needed.

## Wire facts — `live-measured 2026-07-24, n=1 tenant`

`GET /deviceManagement/roleDefinitions` — **10 rows**:

```json
{"@odata.type":"#microsoft.graph.deviceAndAppManagementRoleDefinition",
 "id":"<guid-29>","displayName":"Application Manager",
 "description":"Application Managers manage mobile and managed applications, can read device information and can view device configuration profiles.",
 "isBuiltInRoleDefinition":true,"isBuiltIn":true,"roleScopeTagIds":[],
 "permissions":[{"actions":["Microsoft.Intune_Organization_Read","Microsoft.Intune_MobileApps_Create", ...]}]}
```

`GET /deviceManagement/roleAssignments` — **1 row**:

```json
{"id":"1257e69a-b38e-4b89-864f-0b1662fc8202","displayName":"MDE Endpoint Security Managers",
 "description":null,"scopeMembers":[],"scopeType":"allDevicesAndLicensedUsers",
 "resourceScopes":[],"members":["c118ea33-87b7-4c8a-9bb3-e72b80bb75dd"],"roleScopeTagIds":[]}
```

Traps observed, each to be handled rather than assumed away:

- **`isBuiltIn` and `isBuiltInRoleDefinition` are BOTH present and both `true`** on the same record. Do not assume one is a rename of the other and drop one — emit what the wire sends, and do not build logic on the assumption they always agree (#142).
- The role definition carries an `@odata.type` discriminator (`deviceAndAppManagementRoleDefinition` here). Read it; a different subtype may carry a different field set.
- `permissions[].actions` is an **unbounded string list** of `Microsoft.Intune_*` action names — twin only, never a metric label. It is also the only thing that says what a custom role can actually *do*, so it must not be dropped (#114).
- `scopeType: allDevicesAndLicensedUsers` is the widest possible scope. An assignment at that scope is materially different from a scoped one and should drive severity.
- `roleAssignments` returns the assignment but `members` is a bare list of principal guids with **no names**. Resolving them means a second lookup; decide explicitly whether to resolve or to emit guids, and say which in the docs — an unresolved guid is honest, a fabricated name is not.

## Shape (#112/#114)

- **Bounded gauges**: role definitions by `is_built_in`; assignments by `scope_type`. Both bounded by role-catalogue size, not tenant size.
- **Log twin per role definition** — id, display name, description, built-in flags, the full action list, scope tags.
- **Log twin per assignment** — the members, the scope type, the resource scopes. **Warn on a non-built-in role assigned at `allDevicesAndLicensedUsers`**: a hand-made role with tenant-wide device scope is the shape worth seeing.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Mapper written against the verbatim samples above
- [ ] Both `isBuiltIn` and `isBuiltInRoleDefinition` emitted; no assumption they agree
- [ ] `permissions[].actions` on the twin, never a metric label, never dropped
- [ ] Explicit, documented decision on whether assignment `members` guids are resolved to names
- [ ] `signalgate_test.go` + `testdata/signals.json`, annotation, blank import, `docs/collectors.md` regenerated
- [ ] `make check` green

body:
Unblocked by the #251 Phase 6 grant of `RoleManagementAlert.Read.Directory` (granted 2026-07-24). Wire shape live-probed as `graph2otel-poller`; **not yet built**.

## Why

This is the highest signal-density surface in the Phase 6 table. Microsoft has already computed the privileged-access findings for the tenant — stale admins, standing assignments, missing MFA on eligible roles, license state — and ships each one **with its own severity, security impact, mitigation steps and prevention guidance**. graph2otel currently re-derives none of this; `entra.pim_*` covers policy and assignment state but not Microsoft's verdicts on it.

## ⚠️ The `$filter` is MANDATORY — read this before probing

A bare list returns:

```
GET /beta/identityGovernance/roleManagementAlerts/alerts
400 {"errorCode":"MissingProvider","message":"The provider is missing.","instanceAnnotations":[]}
```

That reads like a licensing or provisioning failure and is **not** one. The required filter:

```
?$filter=scopeId eq '/' and scopeType eq 'DirectoryRole'
```

With it: `200`, **7 rows** on each of `alerts`, `alertDefinitions`, `alertConfigurations`. `v1.0` has no `roleManagementAlerts` segment at all (`400`), so this is **beta-only → `Experimental`**.

Same class as the EA `$top`-rejected-at-any-value trap: a query parameter whose absence produces an error that reads like "endpoint does not exist". Record it in `docs/graph-api-gotchas.md`.

## Wire facts — `live-measured 2026-07-24, n=1 tenant`

Three segments, joined on `alertDefinitionId`:

`alerts` (the state):
```json
{"id":"DirectoryRole_<tid>_InvalidLicenseAlert","alertDefinitionId":"DirectoryRole_<tid>_InvalidLicenseAlert",
 "scopeId":"/","scopeType":"DirectoryRole","incidentCount":0,"isActive":false,
 "lastModifiedDateTime":"0001-01-01T08:00:00Z","lastScannedDateTime":"2026-07-23T13:43:26.983Z"}
```

`alertDefinitions` (the meaning) — keys: `displayName`, `description`, `severityLevel`, `securityImpact`, `mitigationSteps`, `howToPrevent`, `isRemediatable`, `isConfigurable`, `scopeType`, `scopeId`.

`alertConfigurations` (whether it is even switched on) — carries a per-type `@odata.type` (e.g. `#microsoft.graph.invalidLicenseAlertConfiguration`) plus `isEnabled`. **A disabled alert configuration is itself a finding**: an alert that is off will report `isActive:false` forever and is indistinguishable from a healthy one unless the configuration is read too.

Note `lastModifiedDateTime` is the .NET zero date (`0001-01-01T08:00:00Z`) when an alert has never fired — treat as absent, never emit it as a real timestamp (the absent-vs-sentinel rule).

## Shape (#112/#114)

- **Bounded gauge** by `severity_level` × `is_active`, and a second by `is_enabled` over the configurations. Alert *types* are a bounded set (7 here), so `alert_definition_id` is arguably a legitimate label — **verify that it is bounded across tenants before using it**, since the id embeds the tenant guid and would otherwise be per-tenant cardinality. Prefer a stripped type suffix (`InvalidLicenseAlert`) over the raw id.
- **Log twin per alert**, joining the definition's text: severity, impact, mitigation, `incidentCount`, `lastScannedDateTime`, and whether its configuration is enabled. Severity ladder off `severityLevel` + `isActive`.
- `incidentCount` is a count of entities, so the entities themselves live on `alertIncidents` — note that segment `400`s on `alertIncidents` even with the filter (`Resource not found for the segment 'alertIncidents'`), so per-incident detail is **not reachable** by this route. Do not promise it.

## Live finding on m7kni

`InvalidLicenseAlert` — *"The organization doesn't have Azure AD Premium P2"* — `severityLevel: high`. Worth knowing that PIM data on this tenant sits behind a licence the tenant may not hold, which may bound what the other six alerts can ever say.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Mapper written against the verbatim samples above, never documentation
- [ ] Mandatory `$filter` recorded in source AND in `docs/graph-api-gotchas.md`
- [ ] `Experimental` (beta-only surface, per #183)
- [ ] Bounded gauges only; definition text and per-alert detail on the twin (#112/#114)
- [ ] Zero-date handling: never emit `0001-01-01` as a timestamp
- [ ] `alertConfigurations` read, so a switched-off alert is visible rather than silently healthy
- [ ] `signalgate_test.go` + `testdata/signals.json`, annotation, blank import, `docs/collectors.md` regenerated
- [ ] `make check` green

title: feat(entra): entra.pim_alerts — Microsoft's own pre-computed privileged-access findings, with their remediation text

body:
## What

`intune.device_startup_process` (shipped in `4a976fc`, #225) fetches the bare list:

```
GET /beta/deviceManagement/userExperienceAnalyticsDeviceStartupProcesses
```

That request returns **5 rows belonging to a single device**. The tenant actually has **27 rows across 7 devices**. The collector is emitting **18.5%** of the available data and has no way to know it.

`live-measured 2026-07-24, n=1 tenant`, verified twice — once by a probe agent, then independently re-verified against the wire by the coordinating thread before filing.

## The evidence

| request | rows | distinct devices | `@odata.nextLink` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| bare list (what the collector sends) | **5** | **1** | **absent** |
| bare list + `Prefer: odata.maxpagesize=200` | 5 | 1 | absent |
| `?$filter=managedDeviceId eq '<guid>'`, fanned out over the 8 devices in `userExperienceAnalyticsDevicePerformance` | **27** | **7** | n/a |

Per-device breakdown from the fan-out:

```
1625d698-7b22-4ed4-912c-3c86d78254e0  10 rows
0703fa65-0894-4cce-8492-f4a3bc15b32b   5 rows   <- the ONLY device the bare list serves
dc910cbf-ca70-4b6b-a91b-1fffaa3fe54a   3
e596236c-d93b-401c-bbd7-3339b5e5487a   3
a4cf1d34-823c-484c-9557-74e2eb1ace06   2
13bca6e7-5430-4fb7-9bd2-d91a2d6c8e13   2
9a799f82-e14b-422e-927f-ecc9ca555b7a   2
3a96203f-ddf8-4944-8d95-6c7bd928f6a3   0
```

## Why this was invisible

Three independent reasons, and they compound:

1. **No `@odata.nextLink`.** The standard pagination signal that more data exists is simply absent, so `collectors.GetAllValues` correctly concludes it has everything. `Prefer: odata.maxpagesize` does not change the result either — this is not a page-size problem.
2. **A green fetch returning rows looks healthy.** The collector gets `200` and non-empty data every cycle. This is the "a green tick is not evidence of data" trap in `CLAUDE.md`, in a form the existing rule does not quite cover: the failure is not empty-success, it is *partial* success.
3. **The EDM says the workaround is unsupported.** `userExperienceAnalyticsDeviceStartupProcess/managedDeviceId` is annotated `"Supports: $select, $OrderBy. Read-only."` — **no `$filter`**. The wire disagrees with the annotation and accepts the filter perfectly. Wire over docs, again, and in the direction that means an author reading the EDM would rule out the fix.

## This also FALSIFIES a recorded finding on #199

The [2026-07-24 comment on #199](https://github.com/rknightion/graph2otel/issues/199) recorded an "incidental finding":

> **`DeviceStartupProcesses` is a rolling window, not a cumulative list** … So `intune.device_startup_process` will legitimately show records appearing and disappearing, and the device set turning over between polls. That is the endpoint's behaviour, not a dropped fetch or a mapping fault.

**That is wrong and must not be relied on.** The observation behind it was real — the bare list served 10 rows for `1625d698` on 07-21, 2 rows for `13bca6e7` this morning, 5 rows for `0703fa65` this afternoon — but the explanation was not. The data is *not* a rolling window: every one of those devices still has its full row set today, reachable by filter. What rotates is **which single device the bare list happens to serve**, which is a serving artifact. So it IS a dropped fetch, which is exactly what that note ruled out.

A verdict of "this is the endpoint's normal behaviour" is the most expensive kind of wrong entry, because it tells the next reader not to investigate.

## Scope

- [ ] Fan out `?\$filter=managedDeviceId eq '<id>'` per device instead of fetching the bare list. The device id list is already available — `userExperienceAnalyticsDevicePerformance` and `DeviceScores` are both fetched by this collector today.
- [ ] Decide the request-budget shape. This turns 1 request into N; the collector already lives behind the Endpoint Analytics `Experimental` gate and a long interval, and the Intune reporting bucket is ~5 req/10s with no `Retry-After`. `intune.hardware_inventory` faced the same N+1 and solved it with `POST /beta/\$batch` at 20 sub-requests per call — check whether `\$batch` accepts this segment before writing a serial loop.
- [ ] A test that fails if the collector goes back to trusting a bare list whose row set is smaller than the device count it already knows about.
- [ ] Record the `$filter`-works-despite-the-EDM-annotation fact in `docs/graph-api-gotchas.md`, next to the existing `$top`-rejected-at-any-value entry for the same segment family.
- [ ] Correct the "rolling window" note on #199 rather than leaving it to be found later.
- [ ] `make check` green

## Not in scope

Do not remove the `Experimental` gate or change the interval as part of this. And do not treat the missing `nextLink` as something to work around generically — this is one segment behaving specifically, not a pagination bug in `GetAllValues`.
title: bug(intune.device_startup_process): the bare list serves ONE device — the collector emits 5 of 27 available rows and nothing signals the loss

body:
Carved out of #250, which deliberately excluded it: *"genuinely valuable — the only per-message flow record not dependent on Defender streaming export, joining to `defender.email*` on `MessageId` — but it is one record per message per recipient, a firehose on any real tenant. It needs its own issue, a window engine with a checkpoint namespace, and must ship off by default with a volume warning, the way `Audit.General` is opt-in on `m365.activity`."*

## Why it is worth having

It is the **only** per-message mail-flow record that does not depend on Defender for Office 365 streaming export being enabled and billed. On a tenant without that export, `m365.message_trace` is the sole answer to "did this message arrive, and what happened to it" — the single most common mail question an operator is ever asked. It joins to `defender.email*` on `MessageId` and to `m365.unified_audit` for the administrative half.

## Live-verified wire shape (`live-measured 2026-07-23`, probed as `graph2otel-poller`)

`Get-MessageTraceV2` returns 200 under the **existing** grants — no new permission needed. **`Get-MessageTrace` (V1) 400s; use V2** (already recorded from #233). One record per message per recipient:

```json
{
  "MessageTraceId": "a4acd0a2-1b62-4d07-db4f-08dee905ee9b",
  "MessageId": "<Y5PE3KV1VTU4.KRUFCAI594KF@bl6pepf00031abc>",
  "Received@data.type": "System.DateTime",
  "Received": "2026-07-23T22:01:22.0480000Z",
  "SenderAddress": "MSSecurity-noreply@microsoft.com",
  "RecipientAddress": "rob@m7kni.io",
  "FromIP": "2a01:111:f403:c112::5",
  "ToIP": "",
  "Subject": "…",
  "Status": "Delivered",
  "Size@data.type": "System.Int32",
  "Size": 176814
}
```

Twelve keys including the `@data.type` sidecars. `ToIP` is `""` on inbound. `Received` is the event time and is genuinely parseable, so `telemetry`'s drop-if-undateable rule is satisfied.

## Pagination is keyset, NOT a nextLink — this is the design constraint

The truncation warning tells you the continuation verbatim:

```
There are more results, use the following command to get more.
Get-MessageTraceV2 -StartDate "…" -EndDate "…" -StartingRecipientAddress "rob@m7kni.io" -ResultSize 2
```

So the continuation cursor is **`(EndDate, StartingRecipientAddress)`** — a keyset walk backwards through time, tie-broken by recipient, not an opaque token and not an `@odata.nextLink`. Any engine must carry BOTH halves in its checkpoint or it will loop or skip on a tie. This is a different pagination model from every other EXO collector, all of which fit in one page.

Related and already recorded in `85ae23f`: `internal/exoclient` returns only the `value` array — it surfaces neither `@odata.nextLink` nor `@adminapi.warnings` — so **this collector cannot see its own truncation through the current seam**. Unlike `Get-Mailbox`, there is no `-ResultSize Unlimited` escape here, because the result set is unbounded by nature. **Surfacing the warning/continuation through `exoclient` is a prerequisite**, not a nice-to-have.

## Requirements

- **`WindowCollector`, not a snapshot.** Watermark + overlap + seen-id dedupe on `MessageTraceId`, its own `CheckpointKey` (no delta query exists — the standard rule for every log endpoint here).
- **OFF BY DEFAULT**, with a volume warning in `docs/collectors.md`, exactly as `Audit.General` is opt-in on `m365.activity`.
- **Log-only.** A bounded gauge by `Status` (Delivered / FilteredAsSpam / Quarantined / Failed / Pending / Expanded) is reasonable; sender, recipient, subject, IPs and `MessageId` are per-entity and belong on the log record only (#112). Cardinality here is not theoretical — a metric keyed by recipient is one series per mailbox per status.
- **Volume must be stated, not guessed.** Before shipping, measure records/day on m7kni over a real window and put the number in the collector doc so an operator can extrapolate.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `exoclient` surfaces truncation (the warning and/or the continuation parameters) so the collector can page deterministically
- [ ] Keyset continuation implemented on `(EndDate, StartingRecipientAddress)`, with a test proving no skip and no loop on a recipient tie
- [ ] `WindowCollector` with its own checkpoint namespace, watermark + overlap + `MessageTraceId` dedupe
- [ ] Ships **off by default**; enabling it is one documented config key
- [ ] Bounded status gauge only; all per-message detail on the log record
- [ ] Measured records/day on m7kni recorded in `docs/collectors.md`
- [ ] `signalgate_test.go` + golden, annotation, blank import, docs regenerated, `make check` green

## Evidence class

Reachability, record shape and the keyset continuation: `live-measured 2026-07-23` (probed as `graph2otel-poller`, m7kni). Volume on a real tenant: **unmeasured** — m7kni is a small tenant and its rate is not representative.

comments.body:
Live re-probe of `Get-MessageTraceV2` as `graph2otel-poller` on m7kni, 2026-07-24. **Three things in the body above are wrong or incomplete** — corrections below win.

## Correction 1: there is no `@odata.nextLink` on a truncated message trace

The body implies truncation is discovered the same way it is elsewhere on this transport. It is not. A truncated `Get-MessageTraceV2` response carries **no `@odata.nextLink` at all** — so `exoclient.InvokeResult.Truncated` is **false** on a truncated message trace. The only signal is a non-empty `@adminapi.warnings`:

```
There are more results, use the following command to get more. Get-MessageTraceV2 -StartDate "2026-07-22T23:01:07.0000000Z" -EndDate "2026-07-23T20:59:58.6790000Z" -StartingRecipientAddress "rob@m7kni.io" -ResultSize 2
```

## Correction 2: do NOT parse that warning string for the cursor

Measured: the `-EndDate` and `-StartingRecipientAddress` the warning names are **exactly the `Received` and `RecipientAddress` of the last record in the page**. Derive the cursor from the record, not the prose — same value, and it cannot rot when Microsoft rewords the message. Use the warning only as the boolean "there is more".

Records arrive **descending by `Received`**; the walk goes backwards in time. Next page = same `StartDate`, `EndDate` = last record's `Received`, `StartingRecipientAddress` = last record's `RecipientAddress`.

## Correction 3: the walk is proven lossless, and duplicates are inherent

Control experiment over one fixed window (`2026-07-22T00:00:00Z` → `2026-07-23T22:00:00Z`):

| read | pages | distinct `MessageTraceId` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| unpaged, `ResultSize 5000` | 1 | 37 |
| derived keyset walk, `ResultSize 5` | 9 | 37 |

**Zero missed, zero extra.** The AC asking for a no-skip/no-loop test is satisfiable and the mechanism is sound.

Separately: **the unpaged read returned 44 rows for those 37 distinct ids.** The API re-serves duplicates with no paging involved at all, so dedupe on `MessageTraceId` is mandatory regardless.

## Volume (the AC asks for a number)

**28 records / 24h on m7kni, across 3 mailboxes — about 9 per mailbox per day.** m7kni is a tiny tenant and this rate is not representative; the normalized per-mailbox figure is the extrapolatable one.

## Statuses actually on the wire

`Delivered` (18), `FilteredAsSpam` (6), **`Resolved`** (4) in one 24h window. **`Resolved` is not in the body's guessed status list** — treat that list as unverified and follow the wirecheck convention (#234) rather than bucketing unknowns.

## Prerequisite AC is now met

`exoclient` surfaces truncation: `InvokeFull` returns `InvokeResult{Records, Warnings, Truncated}` and logs a WARN when a result was cut short. Note the nextLink is deliberately **not** exported — it is not a usable continuation (four replay strategies all return HTTP 400 `Expired or Invalid pagination request`; the `$skiptoken` is bound to a backend server the next POST does not land on).

## Registration decision — no eighth path

`m365.message_trace` registers on the **existing window path**, not a new one. `collector.WindowCollector` is a `[from, to]` contract, not a Graph contract, and `internal/collectors/mdca` already proved a non-Graph transport can reuse it. `collectors.WindowDeps` gains an `EXO EXOClient` field alongside `Fetcher` and `JobClient` — a third engine reachable from one Deps, same convention. An eighth path would buy nothing and would cost `collectordoc.Rows` a signature change.

## Off-by-default mechanism

New `collectors.HighVolume` interface, gated identically to `Experimental` but distinct from it. #183 reserved `Experimental` for genuine Graph **beta** surfaces, and `Get-MessageTraceV2` is neither beta nor Graph — conflating them would tell an operator a GA endpoint is beta while hiding the fact they actually need, that volume scales with mail traffic rather than tenant size. Skip reason: `high volume; enable explicitly to opt in`.

Shipped in `0f9b5da`, with the `exoclient` prerequisite in `268cd7d` and the registration seams in `e7e8a6e`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `exoclient` surfaces truncation — `InvokeFull` returns `InvokeResult{Records, Warnings, Truncated}` and logs a WARN when a result was cut short (`268cd7d`)
- [x] Keyset continuation on `(EndDate, StartingRecipientAddress)` with a test proving no skip and no loop on a recipient tie — the fake client implements the measured keyset semantics (Received DESC, recipient tie-break, inclusive boundary) rather than serving canned pages, so a wrong cursor loops or skips against it exactly as it would against Exchange Online
- [x] `WindowCollector` with its own checkpoint namespace, watermark + overlap + `MessageTraceId` dedupe
- [x] Ships off by default; one documented config key
- [x] Bounded status metrics only; all per-message detail on the log record
- [x] Measured records/day recorded in `docs/collectors.md`
- [x] `signalgate_test.go` + golden, annotation, blank import, docs regenerated, `make check` green

## Three deviations from the body, each deliberate

**1. Counters, not a window gauge.** The body asked for a bounded gauge by `Status`. The poll window varies — a catch-up tick runs up to `MaxWindow` — so a window count spikes by the window ratio and is indistinguishable from a real mail surge. `increase()` over a monotonic counter has no such artifact, and since the counter advances only for records that survived dedupe it is exactly "messages ingested". Boundedness, the binding constraint, is unchanged: `status` and nothing else.

**2. No eighth registration path.** `collector.WindowCollector` is a `[from, to]` contract, not a Graph contract, and `internal/collectors/mdca` already proved a non-Graph transport can reuse the window path. `WindowDeps` gained an `EXO` field alongside `Fetcher` and `JobClient` — a third engine reachable from one Deps, same convention. `collectordoc.Rows` keeps its signature; there are still SEVEN paths.

**3. `HighVolume`, not `Experimental`.** New interface, gated identically, meaning something else — see the correction comment above.

## The status list was wrong twice over

`Resolved` is missing from the body's guessed list (live-measured, 4 occurrences in 24h), and `Failed`/`Pending`/`Quarantined`/`Expanded` remain unverified. Resolved against #234's "do not declare a guessed set" by defining the `wirecheck.Enum` as **the set this collector was built against**: the 3 live-measured values plus the 5 the severity map explicitly names. The watchdog fires when the severity map has a hole, not the moment a real `Failed` arrives. Evidence class is tagged per member in the source.

Severity: `Failed` → Warn (mail did not reach where it was sent; usually a bad recipient address, a fact about the sender rather than a tenant outage). Everything else, including `FilteredAsSpam` and `Quarantined` → Info, because the security stack working as designed fires constantly, and rating it Warn would make Warn the dominant severity of a firehose and destroy the level's meaning. An unmapped status stays Info and is reported through `wirecheck` rather than given an invented severity with no action attached.

## A SECOND way to go blind, found by this collector

`m365.message_trace` shipped **undocumented while every collector-doc gate stayed green**. `registrySnapshot()` builds each factory with zero deps and *skips one that declines*; this factory declines on a nil `WindowDeps.EXO`, so it vanished from the snapshot and `docs/collectors.md` never grew a row for it.

That is the #100/#139 incident again, arriving through the **deps** rather than through a forgotten registration path. Fixed in the same commit: the snapshot now supplies inert non-nil stubs, and `TestEveryWindowFactoryIsVisibleToTheGate` fails any factory that still declines under them, naming the fix in its message. Mutation-verified — reverting the stub fails the test with `window factory #15 declined under the snapshot deps`.

## Left unmeasured, worth doing before v1.0

- **Lag (15 min) and overlap (30 min) are guesses.** Nobody has timed how long after a message is handled its trace record becomes queryable. Both are set generously: over-reading costs a re-read the dedupe absorbs, under-reading loses records silently. `docs-only`/`n=1` evidence class — cheap to revisit.
- **`ResultSize` is deliberately never sent**, so the server page length is unknown and a short page cannot serve as a second termination test. The warning is the only stopping signal, so the walk depends on that behavior continuing to hold. Three guards bound it regardless: an empty-cursor guard, a stall guard (the cursor did not advance), and a 200-page cap — and a cap hit is reported as `graph2otel.api.unexpected{kind=invariant,field=page_cap}` naming the window it did not finish, never silently.

title: feat(m365): m365.message_trace — per-message mail flow, keyset-paged, must ship off by default

body:
## What this is

The one collector from the #250 Exchange Online posture pack that did not ship. The other seven did: `defender.mdo_policies` + `m365.exchange_dkim` (`7ee6803`), `m365.exchange_audit_config` (`9b51997`), `defender.allow_block_list` (`702a395`), and `m365.exchange_transport_rules` + `m365.exchange_remote_domains` + `m365.exchange_mailboxes` + `m365.exchange_org_config` (`85ae23f`).

## Why it matters

A rogue **outbound** connector routes tenant mail through attacker-controlled infrastructure, and a rogue **inbound** connector lets attacker mail arrive pre-trusted as internal. Both are known M365 compromise patterns, both are invisible to every Graph endpoint, and neither is covered by `m365.exchange_transport_rules` — a connector is mail-flow *routing*, not a rule.

## Why it is not built

**Authorization is no longer the blocker.** Both cmdlets returned 403 all-NUL at Security Reader; since Global Reader was assigned to `graph2otel-poller` they return **200** (live-measured 2026-07-23).

The blocker is **data**: m7kni has **zero** connectors, so both cmdlets return `{"value": []}`. There is no record to write a mapper against, and #250 explicitly decided against shipping docs-only mappers (#142/#165).

Shipping the count gauge alone is not an acceptable half-measure either. It would be live-validated (0 inbound / 0 outbound, and "a connector appeared" genuinely is the alert) but it is exactly the #114 shape: code that buckets a count and would discard every row the moment one existed.

## Unblock condition

**One connector must exist on the tenant so its record can be captured.** A **disabled** inbound connector is inert — it changes no mail flow — and is enough to capture the field shape. Once one exists:

1. `g2o-probe --exo Get-InboundConnector` and `g2o-probe --exo Get-OutboundConnector` as `graph2otel-poller`, capture verbatim.
2. Build against those records.

## Shape when built

Per #250's table, and matching the collectors that shipped alongside it:

- Bounded gauge `m365.exchange.connectors{connector_type, enabled}` — `connector_type` ∈ inbound/outbound, `enabled` ∈ true/false; 4 series, all seeded, so a connector appearing is a change from 0 rather than a new series.
- One log twin per connector carrying `SmartHosts`, `TlsSettings`, `IsTransportRuleScoped`, `SenderDomains`/`RecipientDomains`, `ConnectorSource` (`Default`/`HybridWizard`/`AdminUI` — a hand-created connector is the interesting one) and who last changed it.
- Severity: an **enabled outbound** connector with smart hosts is the routing-through-foreign-infrastructure shape and should rate Error; a disabled one Warn, on the same one-toggle-from-live reasoning `m365.exchange_transport_rules` uses.

## Registration

EXO path — `collectors.EXODeps` / `RegisterEXO`, `RequiredPermissions()` returns nil, stamp `telemetry.WithTransport(e, telemetry.TransportExchangeOnline)`. Off unless `exchange_online.enabled` is set. Reference: `internal/collectors/m365/exchangeremotedomains` (closest shape — one cmdlet, count gauge, twin per row).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A connector exists on the tenant and its verbatim record is captured as `graph2otel-poller`
- [ ] `m365.exchange_connectors` built against that record, both cmdlets, twin per connector
- [ ] Bounded gauge only; smart hosts and domains on the twin, never a metric label (#112/#114)
- [ ] `signalgate_test.go` + `testdata/signals.json`, annotation, blank import, `docs/collectors.md` regenerated
- [ ] `make check` green

## Evidence class

Authorization: `live-measured 2026-07-23` (403 all-NUL at Security Reader → 200 at Global Reader). Emptiness on m7kni: `live-measured 2026-07-23`. Everything about the record's field shape: **unknown** — that is the point of this issue.

comments.body:
Connector created on m7kni, captured live, collector built and shipped in `2800ef4`. **Leaving this open** — the outbound half is unfinished, for a reason that is now narrower than the original blocker.

## What landed

`m365.exchange_connectors`, built against **two verbatim `Get-InboundConnector` records** from m7kni (`connectortest` and `myorgemail`, both disabled, both `ConnectorSource: AdminUI`, differing exactly on the axis that matters — one requires TLS and pins `*.rob-knight.com`, the other takes cleartext from a bare sender IP). All 28 mapped field names were checked against that capture; nothing came from documentation.

- Gauges `m365.exchange.connectors{direction, enabled}` (all four series seeded) and `m365.exchange.connectors.without_tls{direction}`
- One log twin per connector: name, sender domains and IPs, pinned certificate, restriction flags, Enhanced Filtering skip-lists
- Severity — enabled outbound is **Error** whatever else it says (TLS on that path protects the hop without making the destination legitimate); enabled inbound without TLS is **Error** (pre-trusted *and* unauthenticated); enabled inbound with TLS is **Warn**; a hand-created disabled connector is **Warn** (one toggle from live, same reasoning `m365.exchange_transport_rules` uses); `Default`/`HybridWizard` furniture is **Info**

One naming decision worth recording: the body proposed `connector_type` ∈ inbound/outbound, but `ConnectorType` is a **real wire field** whose values are `OnPremises`/`Partner` — a different axis entirely. The direction label is therefore `direction`, and `connector_type` carries the wire value verbatim. Folding them would have produced a label whose meaning changed per row.

## Why this stays open

**m7kni has zero OUTBOUND connectors** (`Get-OutboundConnector` → `{"value": []}`, live 2026-07-24), so that record's field shape has still never been observed. The outbound-only fields — smart hosts, recipient domains, `UseMXRecord`, `RouteAllMessagesViaOnPremises`, `IsTransportRuleScoped` — are deliberately **not** written from Microsoft's documentation. A guessed field name maps to nothing and looks perfectly healthy doing it, which is the #142/#165 mistake this project keeps paying for.

The consequence is bounded and honest: an outbound connector is **counted, rated Error and twinned** the moment one exists, but its twin does not yet say *where the mail goes* — which is the single most useful thing about it. That gap is stated in the package doc and in `docs/collectors.md`.

## Unblock condition (narrowed)

**One OUTBOUND connector must exist on the tenant.** A disabled one is inert — it changes no mail flow — and is enough to capture the field shape. Then: `g2o-probe --exo Get-OutboundConnector` as `graph2otel-poller`, capture verbatim, extend `connectorTwin` with the outbound fields, and close this.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] A connector exists on the tenant and its verbatim record is captured as `graph2otel-poller` — inbound only
- [x] `m365.exchange_connectors` built, both cmdlets run every cycle, twin per connector
- [x] Bounded gauge only; smart hosts and domains on the twin, never a metric label (#112/#114)
- [x] `signalgate_test.go` + `testdata/signals.json`, annotation, blank import, `docs/collectors.md` regenerated
- [x] `make check` green
- [ ] **Outbound record captured and its fields mapped** — the remaining work

## Evidence class

Inbound record shape, both cmdlets authorized at Global Reader, outbound emptiness: `live-measured 2026-07-24 (#253)`. Outbound field shape: still **unknown**.

body:
The optional fourth collector deferred from #249, now buildable on the hunting engine that #249 shipped (`c7180b9`/`1f99aa6`). No new grant — `ThreatHunting.Read.All` + `hunting.enabled`, same as the three DeviceTvm collectors.

## Why

`OAuthAppInfo` is the Defender for Cloud Apps OAuth-app inventory, exposed as an advanced-hunting table (reachable WITHOUT the MDCA portal token — #251). It carries what Graph does not compute: `RiskScore`, `PrivilegeLevel`, `VerifiedPublisher`, `LastUsedTime`, per-app `Permissions`. 1,237 apps live on m7kni.

## Wire facts (live-measured 2026-07-23, as graph2otel-poller)

- Categorical dims are bounded: `PrivilegeLevel` (Low/Medium/High), `AppStatus` (Enabled/DisabledByUser/…), `AppOrigin` (External/Internal), `IsAdminConsented` (SByte 0/1). 10 combos live.
- `RiskScore` is a fine-grained 0-100 int (~30 distinct values) — twin attribute + a `max_risk_score` gauge only; NOT a metric label, and no invented risk bands (#142).
- `VerifiedPublisher` is a nested dynamic object (`displayName`, `verifiedPublisherId`, `addedDateTime`) or `{}` when unverified.
- `Permissions` is a list of embedded-JSON strings (each an object with `PermissionValue`, `PermissionType`, `PrivilegeLevel`, `InUse`).
- `ConsentedUsersCount` is `{}` (null) on admin-consented apps, a number on user-consented ones.
- `Timestamp` present but this is a current-state snapshot → poll-time stamp.

## Proposed shape

- `defender.oauth_app.apps{privilege_level, app_status, app_origin, admin_consented}` — count; `defender.oauth_app.max_risk_score{privilege_level}` — worst risk score (non-additive); `defender.oauth_app.consented_users{privilege_level}` — summed user consents.
- One log twin per app: name, ids, status, privilege, origin, admin-consented, risk score, consented-users count, owner tenant, last-used/added times, verified-publisher name/id + is_verified, permission values (parsed) + count. Warn when `PrivilegeLevel == "High"` (Microsoft's own classification, wire-verbatim).

## Acceptance

- [ ] `defender.oauth_app` on the hunting path, mapper against verbatim live samples
- [ ] `RiskScore` on the twin, never a metric label
- [ ] Goldens + docs regenerated, `make check` green
