body:
Tracker for the coverage-gap research run on 2026-07-23. Six parallel research lanes probed the live m7kni tenant read-only as `graph2otel-poller`, covering Entra identity, Intune/W365, Defender XDR, Purview, M365 workloads, and non-Graph first-party surfaces.

**Every load-bearing claim in the child issues was independently re-verified against the wire by the coordinating thread**, not taken from an agent brief. Claims that survived only as agent assertions are tagged `docs-only` or `EDM-only` in the child issues.

## Operating rules for this program

- **Tier 1 first.** Everything in tier 1 needs no grant, no new engine and no new auth. Several are already-billed data being deleted unread.
- **Wire over docs, without exception.** This run found Microsoft's own streaming-event-types page wrong on ≥5 rows and the beta EDM disagreeing with the wire on an enum. Mappers are written against live samples or they are not written.
- **A 403 naming a read scope is a grantable candidate, not a dead end.** A 403 with no scope named, a 500 `DataInsightsRequestError`, an HTML 403 from Application Gateway, and a 401 `ServiceFabricGraphAuthenticationMiddleware` all mean different things — see #237 for the table.
- **Empty is not a verdict.** Several candidates are `blocked-on-data` on this tenant. Do not write a mapper against docs to fill the gap (#142/#165).

## Phase 1 — tracker corrections (recorded facts that actively mislead)

- [x] #237 — "DLP policy enumeration" is not a permanent gap; the endpoint returns the full policy set on held scopes. Also narrows the `security/labels` entry to per-collection blocking
- [x] #238 — #134's "reading diagnostic settings needs a different identity" is wrong; poller gets 200. Carries the diagnostic-settings census gate
- [x] #239 — #130's GSA deferral condition ("until a GSA tenant exists") has fired; tenant reports `onboarded`
- [x] `CLAUDE.md` describes four collector registration paths and warns a fifth would need `Rows`' signature changed. ~~There are **six**~~ — corrected to six in `850e932`, then to **seven** in `9721555` after #249 added the hunt path (`snapshot, window, blob, o365, mdca, exo, hunt`) and duly changed `Rows`' signature in the same commit. `collectordoc` **does** walk all seven — verified, not a gate hole. The count recurred as documentation lag one path later, so the note now says to correct it the moment a path lands

## Phase 2 — production defect found incidentally

- [x] #240 — `m365.storage` reports 100% success while emitting zero data when all four reports fail. Source-verified: `Collect` has one return path, `return nil`

## Phase 3 — tier 1: free (no grant, no new engine, no new auth)

- [x] #241 — 4 unread blob containers: Defender behaviour layer + Teams message security. Enabled, written, billed, deleted unread on a 7-day lifecycle
- [x] #243 — `entra.secure_score` discards 234 per-control rows every hour. #114 violation on a shipped collector; highest value-per-effort in the sweep
- [x] #242 — PIM role-activation policy settings (145 policies). Nothing answers "what does it take to activate this role"
- [x] #244 — ownerless apps (21 of 27 live) + federated identity credentials, the trust edge `entra.credential_expiry` structurally cannot see
- [x] #245 — tenant policy posture: 11 bounded CIS-shaped switches
- [x] #246 — DLP policy inventory + enforcement mode (**blocked on #237**)
- [x] #247 — Teams installed apps (sideloaded + RSC grants) + channel census (shared channels)
- [x] #248 — Managed Google Play bind health + Autopilot sync staleness, folded into existing collectors

## Phase 4 — tier 2: new engine, scope already granted

- [x] #249 — hunting-query engine + `DeviceTvm*`. 24,912 live vulnerability instances, 7,893 config assessments, 1,542 software rows. `ThreatHunting.Read.All` is granted and referenced nowhere in the tree. **No TVM blob container exists**, so blob cannot reach it

## Phase 5 — tier 3: existing EXO engine, no new grant

- [x] #250 — Exchange Online posture pack. **7 of 8 shipped**, issue CLOSED: MDO policies + DKIM (`7ee6803`), audit config (`9b51997`), allow/block list (`702a395`), transport rules + remote domains + mailboxes + org config (`85ae23f`). Connectors carved out to **#253** — authorized now, but m7kni has zero connectors so there is no record to map
- [x] `m365.message_trace` — issue filed as **#254**, with the record shape and the keyset `(EndDate, StartingRecipientAddress)` continuation live-probed. Still to build; must ship off by default, and needs `exoclient` to surface truncation first

## Phase 6 — tier 4: read-only grants worth requesting

~~Each 403 below named its scope verbatim unless marked otherwise. **No grant has been made; each needs explicit approval.**~~

> **RESOLVED 2026-07-24 — this table is superseded.** All nine were approved by the maintainer; **eight were granted** and `NetworkAccess.Read.All` needed no grant because the poller ALREADY HELD IT (live-verified 2026-07-23) — the row below was stale from the day it was written. **Six of the eight carry real data**; `CustomDetection` and `TeamworkDevice` returned 0 rows exactly as predicted. Two predictions below were WRONG: `WindowsUpdates.Read.All` is not EDM-only (2 policies, 1 deployment, 17 products) and `AccessReview.Read.All` has data despite the licence caveat (1 definition). `ReportSettings` answered: `displayConcealedNames: false`. The scope handback (`SecurityAnalyzedMessage.Read.All`) was NOT done — the maintainer chose grant-all over handback. Full results, verbatim samples and a new mandatory-`$filter` gotcha: [Phase 6 comment](https://github.com/rknightion/graph2otel/issues/251#issuecomment-5073630626).

| candidate | scope to grant | notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PIM alerts | `RoleManagementAlert.Read.Directory` | Microsoft's own pre-computed privileged-access findings, entity-named. Highest signal density of anything needing a grant |
| ~~GSA traffic logs~~ | ~~`NetworkAccess.Read.All`~~ | **ALREADY GRANTED — no action was ever needed.** #239 piece 2 is data-blocked (traffic forwarding off), not grant-blocked |
| Intune Cloud PKI | `DeviceManagementCloudCA.Read.All` | Intune Suite **is** licensed here, so evaluable immediately. A silently-expiring private CA is a fleet-wide auth outage |
| Intune RBAC | `DeviceManagementRBAC.Read.All` | Intune's own RBAC store is separate from Entra directory roles; an Intune-custom-role admin is invisible today |
| Custom detection rules | `CustomDetection.Read.All` | Monitors the detection layer itself. Zero on this tenant, so unverifiable until one exists |
| WUfB deployment service / Autopatch | `WindowsUpdates.Read.All` | A read-only app role **does** exist, contrary to the obvious assumption. Grant to *find out* whether there is anything there — the 403 body was uninformative and the shape is EDM-only |
| Access reviews | `AccessReview.Read.All` | Needs Governance licence for data to exist |
| Teams devices | `TeamworkDevice.Read.All` | Teams Rooms firmware drift. v1.0 route does not exist; beta only. m7kni almost certainly has no devices |
| Report settings | `ReportSettings.Read.All` | One call. **Prerequisite** for any usage-report log twin — when name concealment is on, every UPN in those reports is an opaque hash |

**Scope to hand back:** `SecurityAnalyzedMessage.Read.All` — granted, referenced nowhere, gates exactly one endpoint (`security/collaboration/analyzedEmails`) that #233 already measured as unbuildable. Blast radius with no upside.

## Explicitly NOT worth doing — do not re-litigate

- **Windows 365 / `virtualEndpoint`** — every path 403s `accessDenied` including the tenant-independent catalogs. All three W365 SKUs are **Suspended at zero units**: a licence gate, not an app-only gap. `CloudPC.Read.All` is granted but **unspendable** without a maintainer reactivating a trial. Do not build blind. `intune.alert_records`/`alertRules` (9 system rules) is the one W365 signal reachable without that, and has no records here
- **Intune Data Warehouse** — app-only works (#196), but its differentiated value is 30–60 days of history and a TSDB rejects backfilled samples. Closed won't-do; reason unchanged
- **Graph Data Connect** — an Azure Synapse/Data Factory pipeline with per-run PAM approval, billed per GB. Not collector-shaped
- **Power Platform admin API** — app-only requires `New-PowerAppManagementApp`, which grants the SP *tenant-admin-equivalent* permissions. Rejected on the privilege model, independent of data value
- **Graph change notifications / webhooks** — would need an inbound public TLS endpoint, subscription renewal on a ≤3-day clock, and an encryption cert for resource data. No signal in graph2otel's domain is notification-only
- **Event Hub / Log Analytics transports** — #89 settled it; blob is cheapest and Event Hub's entire measured advantage was 12 seconds against an upstream ~4-minute delay
- **Azure Monitor metrics / Cost Management / Resource Graph** — each needs a *new Azure RBAC grant*, widening the poller from "read blobs in one account" to "read the subscription", to replace `scripts/storage-report.py` which already works on Rob's own identity. Recommend not doing it
- **MDCA beyond discovery** — its alerts already arrive via `entra.security_alerts` / `defender.alert_info` (6 of 15 alerts carry `ServiceSource: Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps`), activities via `defender.cloud_app_event`, and the OAuth app inventory is reachable as `OAuthAppInfo` **without** the portal token
- **`m365.activity` `DLP.All` content type** — already an accepted config value, and its payload carries raw matched secrets (`DetectedValues[].Value`; a live sample contains a full credit-card number). The classification-metadata-only version is better served by #246 and by `ComplianceDLP*` record types on the audit-query API, neither of which carries content

## No API anywhere — confirmed this run

Insider Risk Management, Communication Compliance, Information Barriers, Compliance Manager: **zero** matching entity sets in the beta EDM and **zero** matching Application roles across all 707 app roles enumerated on the Graph SP. Their only trace is audit *record types*, reachable via the audit-query API. Microsoft Security Exposure Management (exposure score, initiatives, attack paths) likewise has no `/security` navigation property — only the exposure *graph*, via advanced hunting.

## Untestable on m7kni — not gaps, do not record as such

`subjectRightsRequests` (500 `HostNotFound` — Priva not provisioned), Exact Data Match (404 `TenantDeploymentNotFound`), Defender Threat Intelligence (403 naming a *licence*, not consent), MDI health/sensors (cloud-only tenant, no DC sensors), attack simulation (200-empty, but the poller lacks `AttackSimulation.Read.All` so the 200 proves nothing).

## Method note worth keeping

Two false conclusions were produced and caught during this run, both from n=1 inference:

1. An intermittent **Azure Application Gateway HTML 403 wrapped in `{"code":"UnknownError"}`** was attributed to a missing `User-Agent` header. Twelve identical bare requests then returned the real RP answer. **The rule is: on `UnknownError` with an HTML body, retry — never record a verdict from one observation.**
2. `/reports/*` returned sustained `429 ServiceThrottleThresholdExceeded`. Six agents were probing concurrently against a 5-req/10s budget, so **"chronically degraded" and "we saturated it ourselves" are not separable** from this run's evidence. #240 states this rather than asserting a cause.

### A NEW API gotcha, found the hard way

`identityGovernance/roleManagementAlerts/*` **`400`s on a bare list** with an unusual body:

```json
{"errorCode":"MissingProvider","message":"The provider is missing.","instanceAnnotations":[]}
```

The `$filter` is **MANDATORY, not optional**:

```
?$filter=scopeId eq '/' and scopeType eq 'DirectoryRole'
```

With it, all three segments return 7 rows each. This is the same class as the EA `$top`-rejected-at-any-value trap: a query parameter whose absence produces an error that reads like the endpoint does not exist. `MissingProvider` in particular looks like a licensing or provisioning failure, which is exactly the wrong conclusion — and would have been recorded as a permanent gap under the old habit of taking one probe at face value. Worth an entry in `docs/graph-api-gotchas.md` when the collector lands.

Verbatim first alert and its definition:

```json
{"id":"DirectoryRole_<tid>_InvalidLicenseAlert","alertDefinitionId":"DirectoryRole_<tid>_InvalidLicenseAlert",
 "scopeId":"/","scopeType":"DirectoryRole","incidentCount":0,"isActive":false,
 "lastModifiedDateTime":"0001-01-01T08:00:00Z","lastScannedDateTime":"2026-07-23T13:43:26.983Z"}
```

The definition side carries `displayName`, `description`, `severityLevel` (`high`), `securityImpact`, `mitigationSteps`, `howToPrevent`, `isRemediatable`, `isConfigurable` — i.e. Microsoft's own pre-computed finding *with its remediation text*, which is the signal density the table claimed for it.

### `ReportSettings` answered — the prerequisite is CLEAR

```json
{"displayConcealedNames": false}
```

Name concealment is **off** on m7kni, so UPNs in usage reports are real rather than opaque hashes. Any usage-report log twin is therefore viable here. Note this is a per-tenant switch, so a collector reading concealable reports must read this setting and say so rather than assuming — on a tenant with it on, every UPN it emits would be a hash that looks like data.

### CloudCA — two real certification authorities

```json
{"id":"a29d1328-90ea-4400-a53f-195f870b1444","displayName":"root-m7kni",
 "certificateRevocationListUrl":"http://primary-cdn.pki.azure.net/westeurope/crls/…/current.crl",
 "certificateDownloadUrl":"data:application/x-x509-ca-cert;base64,MIIGOzCCBCOg…"}
```

The CA certificate is inline as a data URI, so validity dates are parseable without a second fetch — which is what makes "a silently-expiring private CA is a fleet-wide auth outage" actually measurable.

It remains referenced nowhere in the tree and gates exactly one endpoint (`security/collaboration/analyzedEmails`) that #233 measured as unbuildable. Still worth revoking; needs its own call.

| issue | surface | notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| #256 | `entra.pim_alerts` | beta-only; **mandatory `$filter`** or the endpoint 400s with `MissingProvider` |
| #257 | `intune.rbac` | v1.0 + beta; the role store `entra.roles` structurally cannot see |
| #258 | `intune.cloud_pki` | beta-only; CA cert is inline as a `data:` URI, so expiry is parseable with `crypto/x509` |
| #259 | `intune.windows_updates` | beta-only; `state` is a three-part object whose parts **disagree** on the live row |
| #260 | `entra.access_reviews` | v1.0 + beta; one review `InProgress`, created by the `homelab-agentic-mgmt` SP |

`ReportSettings.Read.All` did not need its own issue — it is one field (`displayConcealedNames: false`), recorded in the Phase 6 comment above as the prerequisite fact for any future usage-report twin.

**Phase 6 is complete.** The remaining item on this epic is the `SecurityAnalyzedMessage.Read.All` handback, which was deliberately not done (grant-all was chosen over handback) and needs its own maintainer call.

## All five Phase 6 collectors shipped — `3d129cb` (2026-07-24)

Every buildable surface the Phase 6 grants unlocked is now built, merged and gated. Seven parallel lanes over disjoint file sets; each diff reviewed and `make check` re-run on `main` rather than taken from a returned brief.

| issue | collector | shape |
| --- | --- | --- |
| #256 | `entra.pim_alerts` | 3 gauges + twin joining definition text; beta, `Experimental` |
| #257 | `intune.rbac` | 2 gauges + definition/assignment twins; v1.0, not `Experimental` |
| #258 | `intune.cloud_pki` | 3 gauges + CA/leaf twins; beta, `Experimental` |
| #259 | `intune.windows_updates` | 2 gauges + policy/deployment twins; beta, `Experimental` |
| #260 | `entra.access_reviews` | 1 gauge + definition twin; v1.0, not `Experimental` |

Plus two production defects the work exposed: **#255** and **#261**, both fixed in the same commit.

### Four of my own issue bodies were wrong on the wire, and the lanes caught it

Worth recording, because these were written from verbatim captures and still contained errors:

- **#258 said the record had 5 fields.** It has ~35, including `validityStartDateTime`/`validityEndDateTime`. Resolved by keeping the certificate as the source of truth and making the wire dates a *labelled fallback*, with disagreement raising a WARN.
- **#257 missed that a role assignment carries no link to its role.** Both candidate joins were measured and both silently lose data: `$expand=roleDefinition` returns `null` **and drops `scopeType`/`scopeMembers`/`roleScopeTagIds`**; the per-definition nav truncates `members` to `[]`.
- **#260's key set was beta's.** `v1.0` omits `backupReviewers`, `customData`, `customDataProvider`. Mapping `backupReviewers` from my issue as written would have shipped a permanent fabricated `0`.
- **#259 listed four `@odata.type` discriminators.** There is a fifth: `driverUpdateFilter` carries neither `classification` nor `cadence`, so a structural decode maps the driver policy as a quality filter with two empty strings.

### Routes and facts resolved that this epic had left open

- **`cloudCertificationAuthorityLeafCertificate` is reachable** — `GET /beta/deviceManagement/cloudCertificationAuthority/{caId}/cloudCertificationAuthorityLeafCertificate` → **200, 69 rows** (8 active / 43 expired / 18 revoked) with device and user identity per row. The top-level list still `404`s despite the beta EDM declaring it as a `ContainsTarget` nav prop. Both recorded.
- **`issuedStagedLeafCertificateCount: 0`** on a CA that has issued 69 leaves — it counts *staged*, not issued. A near-miss for a fabricated metric.
- **Leaf `keyUsages`/`extendedKeyUsages` are doubly encoded** — typed `Collection(Edm.String)`, returned as a one-element collection whose element is a JSON-encoded array. And `extendedKeyUsages` is one name with two shapes: objects on a CA, encoded strings on a leaf.
- **The `roleManagementAlerts` `$filter` is mandatory**, recorded in `docs/graph-api-gotchas.md`. Its `MissingProvider` error reads like a licensing failure; under the old habit of taking one probe at face value it would have been filed as a permanent gap.

### A collision the merge caught that neither lane could have

Two lanes independently coined `AttrScopeType = "scope_type"` in separate files — and meant **different things**: `intune.rbac`'s is the wire's `scopeType` enum (`allDevicesAndLicensedUsers`), `entra.access_reviews`' is a stripped `@odata.type` discriminator. That is the `tpm_version` collision from #199 exactly: one attribute key, two meanings, a query silently matching the wrong shape.

Renamed to `scope_odata_type` with the reasoning in-source. The Go compiler caught it only because both chose the same *symbol*; had they differed by a letter it would have shipped silently. **Per-collector `semconv` files prevent file conflicts, not semantic ones** — worth knowing before the next parallel build.

### A claim that did NOT survive verification

One lane reported a second defect — that WFA `metricDevices` uses a different id space, citing LAPHAM as `d5900d67-…` — and wrote it into a source comment as a live fact. **Re-measured: false.** All 7 metricDevices ids are byte-identical to their DeviceScores counterparts, LAPHAM included, and no `d5900d67-…` id exists in either collection. The original struct doc was right. An issue was nearly filed on it; the comment now records the measurement and the retraction.

### Remaining on this epic

- **The `SecurityAnalyzedMessage.Read.All` handback** — still granted, still referenced nowhere, still gating one endpoint #233 measured as unbuildable. The maintainer chose grant-all over handback, so this was deliberate, not overlooked. Needs its own call.
- Everything else in Phase 6 is closed.

## Epic complete — the last item (the SecurityAnalyzedMessage handback) is done (2026-07-25)

The maintainer chose **revoke** over the previously-chosen grant-all. Executed as \`homelab-agentic-mgmt\`:

\`\`\`
DELETE /servicePrincipals/{pollerSP}/appRoleAssignments/{id}   -> HTTP 204
GET    /servicePrincipals/{pollerSP}/appRoleAssignments/{id}   -> HTTP 404 (Request_ResourceNotFound)
\`\`\`

- appRole GUID: \`<guid-38>\` (SecurityAnalyzedMessage.Read.All), assignment id \`NhU3E1CZiEmQ9DQ1ZkVngR0_EPHlGC9LhPFu9xGSZEI\`.
- App-role delete only — **no directory-role escalation** was used (mgmt holds \`AppRoleAssignment.ReadWrite.All\`).
- The scope was referenced nowhere in the tree and gated one endpoint (\`security/collaboration/analyzedEmails\`) that #233 measured as unbuildable, so revoking it removes blast radius and costs no coverage. Poller drops one Graph app role (53 → 52).
- **Note on verification:** the immediate re-LIST of the poller's assignments still showed the role (Graph directory-replication lag on the list replica); the authoritative confirmation is the 204 on DELETE plus the 404 on a direct GET of the assignment id.

### Every child of this epic is closed
Phases 1–6 all landed in prior sessions (see the phase comments above): the tracker corrections, the tier-1/2/3 collector builds (#237–#250, #252–#254, #256–#260), the hunting engine (#249), the EXO pack, and the five Phase-6-grant collectors (\`3d129cb\`). The only outstanding item was this deliberate scope handback.

Closing the epic.

title: epic: coverage-gap program — 6-lane live-tenant research, 3 tracker corrections, 1 production defect, 4 tiers of new coverage

body:
## The engine already exists

`internal/exoclient` shipped with #233 and is live. It is **pure REST** — one `POST https://outlook.office365.com/adminapi/beta/{tenantID}/InvokeCommand` carrying `{"CmdletInput":{"CmdletName":...,"Parameters":{...}}}`, results in a flat `value` array. **No PowerShell runtime, no module, no shell-out.** `internal/collectors/exo.go` defines the full registration path (`EXOClient`, `EXODeps`, `EXOFactory`, `RegisterEXO`, `EXOAll`) and `internal/collectordoc.Rows` already walks it. Config gate `exchange_online.enabled` exists at `internal/config/config.go:285`, default false.

Both grants are already made and live-measured working: app role `Exchange.ManageAsApp` **plus** the Entra directory role **Security Reader**. Neither alone does anything (401 → 403 → 200).

**Exactly one consumer today: `defender.quarantine`.** Every candidate below is one more collector on a working engine — no new transport, no new grant.

## Candidates, highest value first

| collector | cmdlet(s) | signal | bounded metric |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `m365.exchange_transport_rules` | `Get-TransportRule` | A rule that BCCs or forwards all mail externally is textbook BEC persistence. Invisible today | count by `state` × `mode` (Audit/AuditAndNotify/Enforce); twin per rule with name, priority, actions |
| `m365.exchange_connectors` | `Get-InboundConnector`, `Get-OutboundConnector` | A rogue outbound connector routing mail through attacker infrastructure is a known M365 compromise pattern | count by type × enabled; twin with `SmartHosts`, `TlsSettings`, `IsTransportRuleScoped` |
| `defender.allow_block_list` | `Get-TenantAllowBlockListItems -ListType Sender\|Url\|FileHash\|IP`, `Get-TenantAllowBlockListSpoofItems` | An allow-list entry is a standing, expiring hole past mail security, and a documented attacker persistence technique. No other API, no other transport | `{list_type, action, list_subtype}` — bounded 4×2×2 — plus `expiring_soon{list_type, action}`, the `entra.credential_expiry` pattern. Twin per entry; **Error on a non-expiring allow entry** |
| `m365.exchange_org_config` | `Get-OrganizationConfig`, `Get-AdminAuditLogConfig` | Modern auth, `AuditDisabled`, and **`UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled`** | boolean posture gauges + one config twin |
| `m365.exchange_remote_domains` | `Get-RemoteDomain` | `AutoForwardEnabled` per remote domain — is external auto-forwarding permitted at all | count by `auto_forward_enabled`; twin per domain |
| `defender.mdo_policies` | `Get-HostedContentFilterPolicy`, `Get-MalwareFilterPolicy`, `Get-AntiPhishPolicy`, `Get-SafeLinksPolicy`, `Get-SafeAttachmentPolicy`, `Get-AtpPolicyForO365`, `Get-TeamsProtectionPolicy` | What each verdict class actually *does* (`SpamAction`, `HighConfidencePhishAction`, ZAP toggles). **No Graph API exists for any of it** | count by policy type × action per verdict class; twin per policy |
| `m365.exchange_mailboxes` | `Get-Mailbox` | Census by `RecipientTypeDetails` (UserMailbox / **SharedMailbox** / Room / …), plus per-mailbox `ForwardingSmtpAddress`, `DeliverToMailboxAndForward`, `LitigationHoldEnabled`, `AuditEnabled` | count by recipient type × forwarding-configured × audit-enabled; twin per mailbox |
| `m365.exchange_dkim` | `Get-DkimSigningConfig` | DKIM signing + selector rotation per accepted domain — pairs with the SPF/DMARC story `entra.domains` cannot tell | count by enabled; twin per domain |

## `Get-AdminAuditLogConfig` corrects a tracker claim

#99 recorded that turning on the unified audit log is *"outside every API surface graph2otel touches"*. Since #233 that is no longer true for the **read** half — `Get-AdminAuditLogConfig` runs on the transport graph2otel now owns.

This matters operationally: when the unified audit log is off, `m365.activity` and `m365.unified_audit` silently return nothing, and that is **indistinguishable from a quiet tenant**. graph2otel still cannot and should not *set* it, but it can now report that it is off.

## Verify this first, before scoping the whole pack

Every cmdlet above is **assumed** authorized by **Security Reader**, the directory role currently assigned. Only `Get-QuarantineMessage` is verified at that level. `Get-TransportRule`, `Get-Mailbox`, `Get-OrganizationConfig` are **not**.

If they 403, the fix is a **second read-only directory role** (Global Reader, or Exchange's View-Only Configuration) — **not** a Graph scope. That is a maintainer tenant action needing explicit approval.

**Trap:** a 403 body from this API is a run of **NUL bytes, not JSON** (`docs/graph-api-gotchas.md:163-166`). Test one cmdlet and read the raw bytes before concluding anything.

## Evidence class

Transport, auth model and error contract: `live-measured 2026-07-23, #233`. Seven cmdlets verified reachable during #233: `Get-QuarantineMessage`, `Get-TeamsProtectionPolicy`, `Get-TeamsProtectionPolicyRule`, `Get-AtpPolicyForO365`, `Get-HostedContentFilterPolicy`, `Get-MalwareFilterPolicy`, `Get-MessageTraceV2` (V1 `Get-MessageTrace` 400s — use V2).

**Every other cmdlet here is `docs-only`.** None was probed in this sweep — the transport is POST and the research pass was GET-only.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Probe one config cmdlet under Security Reader and record the result before building the pack
- [ ] `defender.allow_block_list` first — smallest surface, least role uncertainty, no other API
- [ ] Then transport rules, connectors, remote domains, org config
- [ ] `defender.mdo_policies` last (largest cmdlet set)
- [ ] Each collector's doc states which cmdlets are `live-measured` vs `docs-only`
- [ ] Goldens + `docs/collectors.md` regenerated

## Deliberately excluded here

`m365.message_trace` (`Get-MessageTraceV2`) is genuinely valuable — the only per-message flow record not dependent on Defender streaming export, joining to `defender.email*` on `MessageId` — but it is **one record per message per recipient**, a firehose on any real tenant. It needs its own issue, a window engine with a checkpoint namespace, and must ship **off by default** with a volume warning, the way `Audit.General` is opt-in on `m365.activity`.

comments.body:
Probed every cmdlet in the pack under the CURRENT grant (Security Reader) as `graph2otel-poller`, 2026-07-23 — the acceptance-criteria gate. A 403 here is an all-NUL body (the `docs/graph-api-gotchas.md:163` trap), confirmed by reading raw bytes. The boundary is not "config vs data" — Security Reader authorizes the security-relevant read cmdlets and denies general Exchange config:

**Authorized under Security Reader (200, buildable now):**

| cmdlet | data on m7kni |
| --- | --- |
| Get-HostedContentFilterPolicy, Get-MalwareFilterPolicy, Get-AntiPhishPolicy, Get-SafeLinksPolicy, Get-SafeAttachmentPolicy, Get-AtpPolicyForO365, Get-TeamsProtectionPolicy | rich |
| Get-DkimSigningConfig | rich |
| Get-AdminAuditLogConfig | rich (carries `UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled` — the #99 correction) |
| Get-TransportRule | 200, **empty** (no rules configured) |
| Get-TenantAllowBlockListItems, Get-TenantAllowBlockListSpoofItems | 200, **empty** |

**NOT authorized under Security Reader (403 all-NUL — need a second read-only directory role):**

`Get-InboundConnector`, `Get-OutboundConnector`, `Get-RemoteDomain`, `Get-AcceptedDomain`, `Get-Mailbox`, `Get-OrganizationConfig`.

**Shipped so far (`7ee6803`):** `defender.mdo_policies` (all 7 MDO cmdlets, rich) + `m365.exchange_dkim`. Both mappers written against verbatim live samples.

**Buildable next with no grant:** `m365.exchange_audit_config` (Get-AdminAuditLogConfig — rich, the UAL-ingestion signal), and `defender.allow_block_list` + `m365.exchange_transport_rules` (authorized but empty on m7kni → count gauge is the validated signal, twin mapper is docs-only until an entry appears, the appownership precedent).

**⛔ Grant decision for @rknightion — the connectors / remote-domains / mailboxes / org-config half:** these need a **second read-only Entra directory role** on the poller SP — **Global Reader** (covers all of them) or Exchange **View-Only Configuration** (transport/config only, not mailboxes). This is a maintainer tenant action; nothing self-granted. I will build those four collectors the moment the role is added and I can capture live samples. Until then they are parked, not written from docs.

Status + plan for the remainder (2026-07-23).

**Live-verified this session:** the poller already holds every read scope these collectors need on the Graph side; the EXO boundary is the only gate. `Get-TransportRule` and `Get-TenantAllowBlockListItems`/`...SpoofItems` are **authorized (200) but empty** on m7kni (no transport rules configured, empty allow/block list). The connectors / remote-domains / accepted-domains / mailboxes / OrganizationConfig cmdlets are **403 (all-NUL)** — need a second read-only directory role.

**Decision — build against live samples, not docs.** Rather than ship docs-only mappers for the empty/403 endpoints (which the project rule forbids, #142/#165), the remaining #250 collectors will be built in a follow-up **after two maintainer tenant actions**, so every mapper is written against real wire data:

1. **Generate data** for the empty endpoints (so a real twin sample exists): create one Exchange **transport rule**, and add one **Tenant Allow/Block List** entry (a blocked sender and, ideally, one *allow* entry with an expiry and one without — to exercise the Error-on-non-expiring-allow path).
2. **Assign a second read-only directory role** to the `graph2otel-poller` service principal — **Global Reader** (covers connectors, remote/accepted domains, mailboxes, OrganizationConfig) — in the Entra portal. This is the clean path (no management-app privilege escalation); alternatively I can self-grant it transiently via the mgmt credential at build time and revoke it after.

The follow-up session then probes each newly-populated/unblocked cmdlet as the poller, captures verbatim samples, and builds: `defender.allow_block_list`, `m365.exchange_transport_rules`, `m365.exchange_connectors`, `m365.exchange_remote_domains`, `m365.exchange_mailboxes`, and the `Get-OrganizationConfig` half of `m365.exchange_org_config` (the `Get-AdminAuditLogConfig` half already shipped in `9b51997`).

**UNBLOCKED — both maintainer tenant actions landed; re-probed as `graph2otel-poller` 2026-07-23.**

The authorization boundary recorded in the [earlier comment](https://github.com/rknightion/graph2otel/issues/250#issuecomment-5062967770) has moved. **Global Reader is assigned to the poller SP**, and the previously 403-all-NUL cmdlets now return 200:

| cmdlet | before | now | data on m7kni |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Get-Mailbox` | 403 all-NUL | **200** | 3 mailboxes, 336 keys each (2 `UserMailbox` + 1 `DiscoveryMailbox`) |
| `Get-OrganizationConfig` | 403 all-NUL | **200** | 1 object, 336 keys |
| `Get-RemoteDomain` | 403 all-NUL | **200** | 1 (`Default`, `*`) — `AutoForwardEnabled: true` |
| `Get-AcceptedDomain` | 403 all-NUL | **200** | 4 domains, all `Authoritative` |
| `Get-InboundConnector` | 403 all-NUL | **200** | **empty** |
| `Get-OutboundConnector` | 403 all-NUL | **200** | **empty** |

And the two authorized-but-empty cmdlets now carry data:

| cmdlet | now |
| --- | --- |
| `Get-TransportRule` | **2 rules** — `g2o-test` (Enabled/Enforce, `FromScope: NotInOrganization`, prepends `EXTERNAL: `) and `encrypt` (**Disabled**/Enforce, no conditions, RMS `Encrypt`) |
| `Get-TenantAllowBlockListItems -ListType Sender` | 4 entries — 2 `Allow` + 2 `Block` |
| `... -ListType IP` | 1 `Allow` |
| `... -ListType Url` / `-ListType FileHash` | empty |
| `Get-TenantAllowBlockListSpoofItems` | 1 entry |

**The Error-on-a-standing-hole case exists on the wire.** Three distinct expiry shapes were captured, which is exactly what `defender.allow_block_list` needs to be built honestly:

- `Block` entries: `ExpirationDate` set, `RemoveAfter: null`
- `Sender` `Allow` entries: `ExpirationDate: null`, `RemoveAfter: 45` — bounded (auto-removes 45d after last use)
- `IP` `Allow` entry: `ExpirationDate: null` **and** `RemoveAfter: null` — a **permanent standing allow**, the Error condition

**Wire facts (`live-measured 2026-07-23`), for the mappers:**

- Booleans on this transport are real JSON `true`/`false` — **not** the SByte `0`/`1` encoding the advanced-hunting API uses (#249). Do not carry that helper over.
- `@data.type` sidecar keys (`System.Int32`, `System.Guid`, `System.DateTime`) sit next to their columns, as on `Get-AdminAuditLogConfig`; exact-name reads ignore them.
- `Get-TenantAllowBlockListItems` emits a **malformed duplicate key**, `"LastUsedDate(DateTime])"`, alongside the real `LastUsedDate`. Read `LastUsedDate` by exact name.
- `Get-TransportRule` `Conditions`/`Actions`/`Exceptions` are `#Collection(String)` of fully-qualified .NET predicate class names (e.g. `Microsoft.Exchange.MessagingPolicies.Rules.Tasks.FromScopePredicate`), or `null` when none — not a friendly rule DSL.
- `Get-Mailbox` quotas are **formatted strings**, not numbers: `"99 GB (106,300,440,576 bytes)"`. `LitigationHoldDuration` is the string `"Unlimited"`; `RetainDeletedItemsFor`/`AuditLogAgeLimit` are .NET TimeSpan strings (`"14.00:00:00"`).
- `Get-Mailbox` needs `ResultSize`; the default page emits an `@adminapi.warnings` string telling you results were truncated, plus an `@odata.nextLink`.

**Plan for this session.** Building the five collectors that now have live samples, in the issue's stated order: `defender.allow_block_list`, `m365.exchange_transport_rules`, `m365.exchange_remote_domains`, `m365.exchange_mailboxes`, and the `Get-OrganizationConfig` half (`m365.exchange_org_config`).

**`m365.exchange_connectors` stays parked**, and this is the one gap. Both connector cmdlets are now authorized but m7kni has **zero** connectors, so there is no twin sample and a mapper for it would be exactly the docs-only guess this issue already decided against (#142/#165). The count gauge alone is live-validated (0 inbound / 0 outbound — and "a connector appeared" is the actual alert), but shipping a count-only collector is the #114 shape: code that buckets a count and would discard every row if one appeared. It builds the moment a connector exists — a **disabled** inbound connector is inert and would be enough to capture the shape.

**Closed by `85ae23f`. Seven of the pack's eight collectors are shipped; the eighth is #253.**

| collector | cmdlet(s) | commit | role needed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `defender.mdo_policies` | 7 MDO cmdlets | `7ee6803` | Security Reader |
| `m365.exchange_dkim` | Get-DkimSigningConfig | `7ee6803` | Security Reader |
| `m365.exchange_audit_config` | Get-AdminAuditLogConfig | `9b51997` | Security Reader |
| `defender.allow_block_list` | Get-TenantAllowBlockListItems x4 + ...SpoofItems | `702a395` | Security Reader |
| `m365.exchange_transport_rules` | Get-TransportRule | `85ae23f` | Security Reader |
| `m365.exchange_remote_domains` | Get-RemoteDomain | `85ae23f` | **Global Reader** |
| `m365.exchange_mailboxes` | Get-Mailbox -ResultSize Unlimited | `85ae23f` | **Global Reader** |
| `m365.exchange_org_config` | Get-OrganizationConfig | `85ae23f` | **Global Reader** |
| `m365.exchange_connectors` | Get-In/OutboundConnector | — | **#253** |

`make check` green at each commit. Every mapper written against verbatim live records captured as `graph2otel-poller`, per this issue's own decision not to ship docs-only mappers.

**#253 is the honest close on connectors.** Authorization is no longer the blocker — both cmdlets are 200 under Global Reader. The blocker is that m7kni has **zero** connectors, so there is no record to map. The count gauge alone would be live-validated but is the #114 shape (code that buckets a count and would discard every row if one appeared), so it is parked with a named unblock condition rather than half-shipped: **one connector must exist**, and a *disabled* inbound connector is inert and enough.

**Wire facts recorded this session (`live-measured 2026-07-23`), all encoded in the collectors:**

- **`ResultSize=Unlimited` is load-bearing on `Get-Mailbox`, not a tuning knob.** The default page is **ONE row** plus an `@odata.nextLink` and an `@adminapi.warnings` truncation string, and `internal/exoclient` neither follows the link nor surfaces the warning — it returns only the `value` array. A collector that did not ask for everything would report a tenant of one **and look perfectly healthy**. The `exoclient` package doc asserted this transport has no `@odata.nextLink`; that was **WRONG** and is corrected in `85ae23f`, along with a note that surfacing truncation through that seam is unbuilt.
- **Three expiry shapes on the allow/block list, and null ≠ permanent.** `ExpirationDate` set → bounded; `ExpirationDate` null **with** `RemoveAfter` → still bounded (removes N days after last use); `ExpirationDate` null **and** `RemoveAfter` null → nothing ever removes it. Only the third is the standing hole, so only it is Error. Reading a null `ExpirationDate` as "permanent" would have over-fired on m7kni's two Sender allows.
- **Coercion traps in `Get-OrganizationConfig`.** `PublicFoldersEnabled` is the **string** `"Local"`, not a boolean; `MessageRecallEnabled` / `FocusedInboxOn` / `DefaultAuthenticationPolicy` arrive **null**, meaning "not configured", not false. Both are omitted from the 0/1 gauge rather than coerced — a 0 would assert a decision the tenant never made. Same for `TNEFEnabled` on remote domains.
- **Formatted strings stay verbatim.** Mailbox quotas are `"99 GB (106,300,440,576 bytes)"`, `LitigationHoldDuration` is `"Unlimited"`, and `RetainDeletedItemsFor`/`AuditLogAgeLimit` are .NET TimeSpans. Re-deriving a byte count would emit a number the API never sent (#142).
- **Booleans on this transport are real JSON bools**, NOT the SByte `0`/`1` the advanced-hunting API uses (#249). The `internal/tvm` helper does not carry over.
- **`Get-TenantAllowBlockListItems` emits a malformed duplicate key**, `"LastUsedDate(DateTime])"`, alongside the real `LastUsedDate`. Every read is by exact name, which also skips the `"<Name>@data.type"` sidecars.
- **Transport-rule `Conditions`/`Actions`/`Exceptions`** are `#Collection(String)` of fully-qualified .NET class names under one constant namespace (stripped for readability; anything outside it passes through verbatim), or `null` when the rule has none.
- **The multi-recipient rule properties** (`BlindCopyTo`, `CopyTo`, `RedirectMessageTo`, `AddToRecipients`) are null on m7kni, so their NAMES are live-verified and their **populated shape is not**. `recipientsOf` accepts both the array and bare-string shapes rather than betting on one.

**Two real findings on m7kni**, surfaced by the new collectors rather than hypothesized:

- The wildcard (`*`) remote domain has **`AutoForwardEnabled: true`** — automatic external forwarding is permitted to anywhere. `m365.exchange_remote_domain` rates that **Error**.
- The tenant has a **never-expiring IP Allow entry** (`ExpirationDate` and `RemoveAfter` both null) — a permanent bypass of mail security. `defender.allow_block_list` rates that **Error**.

Neither is a bug in graph2otel; both are the collectors doing their job on the first poll.

**Not done here, deliberately:** `m365.message_trace` stays excluded per this issue's own scoping (firehose, needs its own window engine and must ship off by default) and still needs its own issue. `Get-AcceptedDomain` is now authorized and returns 4 domains on m7kni but was never a named collector in this pack — a possible follow-up (`DomainType: InternalRelay` is the interesting posture value), not a gap in it.

## Correction to this issue's closing comment: "the default page is ONE row" is WRONG

Re-measured live as `graph2otel-poller` on m7kni, 2026-07-24.

The closing comment above (and the matching note on #251) states that `Get-Mailbox`'s default page is **ONE row**. **It is not.** That conclusion came from a probe that had itself passed `-ResultSize 1` and then read its own input back as the service's default. Unparameterized, `Get-Mailbox` returns **all 3** m7kni mailboxes, with `@adminapi.warnings` present-and-empty and no `@odata.nextLink`.

**The true default page size is UNKNOWN** and is not measurable on this tenant — 3 mailboxes exist, so all that can be said is that it is at least 3. It is now recorded as unknown rather than replaced with another guess.

**What survives unchanged:** `-ResultSize Unlimited` is still load-bearing, and for a *better* reason than the one originally given. A truncated page's `@odata.nextLink` **cannot be followed at all** — four replay strategies (same body, empty parameters, `%24` percent-decoded, cookie jar plus `X-AnchorMailbox`) each return HTTP 400 `Expired or Invalid pagination request. Default Expiry time is 00:30:00`, immediately. The `$skiptoken` embeds a backend mailbox-server name and each POST lands on a different backend, so the cursor's affinity is unreproducible by this client. The cmdlet's own parameter is therefore the **only** way to defeat a page, and a tenant larger than one page would silently report a fraction of its mailboxes.

Also measured: `@adminapi.warnings` is an **array of strings** (`#Collection(String)`), not a single string — a client decoding it as a string fails on precisely the response that matters. And `Prefer: odata.maxpagesize=N` **is** honored by the service, which is recorded only so it is not rediscovered and mistaken for a paging solution; a smaller page is worthless when the cursor cannot be followed.

Corrected in: the `internal/exoclient` package doc, `internal/collectors/m365/exchangemailboxes`, its `TestCollect_AsksForEveryMailbox` guard comment, and the `docs/collectors.md` annotation. The truncation-surfacing seam that this comment recorded as "unbuilt" is now built — `exoclient.InvokeFull` returns `InvokeResult{Records, Warnings, Truncated}` and logs a WARN on truncation.

Evidence class: `live-measured 2026-07-24 (#253/#254)`.

title: feat(m365/defender): Exchange Online posture pack — 8 collectors on the shipped EXO engine, no new transport, no new grant

body:
## The gap

`ThreatHunting.Read.All` is **granted, in the poller's token, and referenced nowhere in the source tree** (`rg 'runHuntingQuery|ThreatHunting' --glob '*.go'` → zero hits outside `internal/preflight`). All 21 `defender.*` collectors are `collectors.BlobDeps`.

The API is bought and unspent, and it is the only route to the `DeviceTvm*` family — which answers **"what is unpatched / exposed"**, a question nothing in graph2otel's 58 collectors can answer.

## It is hunting-only. Blob physically cannot reach it.

The Defender streaming export writes 24 `insights-logs-advancedhunting-*` containers on this tenant. **Not one is a `DeviceTvm*` table** — verified against the live container list (39 containers total).

## Live data on m7kni (`live-measured 2026-07-23`, independently reproduced)

`DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities`:

```
High      17144 instances   55 devices   1581 CVEs
Medium     6433             49           1015
Critical    772             44            147
Low         563             49             78
TOTAL     24912
```

The KB join (`DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilitiesKB` on `CveId`) works server-side and adds `CvssScore`, `EpssScore`, `IsExploitAvailable`, `CvssVector`, `PublishedDate`: **270 exploit-available instances** (High 145 / Medium 125), max EPSS 0.99506, max CVSS 10.0.

`DeviceTvmSecureConfigurationAssessment`: **7,893 rows / 87 devices / 170 configurations.** Applicable split — Security controls 1,085 ok / 953 failing (46 devices), OS 961 / 316, Network 550 / 468 (52 devices), Accounts 187 / 135, Application 47 / 144 (37 devices).

`DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory`: **1,542 rows / 73 devices / 277 products.** `EndOfSupportStatus`: 20 `Upcoming EOS Version`, 18 `EOS Version`, 5 `EOS Software`.

## Why this does not contradict #106

#106 chose blob over the hunting API deliberately, because streaming export consumes **no advanced-hunting CPU quota** and that quota is shared with humans querying in the Defender portal. **That reasoning is still correct for the EDR event tables and must not be overridden for them.**

It does not transfer to TVM, for two measured reasons:

1. **These are current-state snapshots, not event streams.** `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` has **no `Timestamp` column at all**. There is nothing to tail. A daily or 6-hourly poll is a handful of queries per day.
2. Every bounded metric is a single server-side `summarize`. Only the log twin needs row-level output.

**Do not poll TVM at collector-default intervals** — that is exactly the failure mode #106 warned about.

## The real constraint is the row cap, not the quota

**100,000 rows per query, hard.** m7kni returns 24,912 vulnerability rows today; a 5,000-device tenant will exceed it. A twin fetch must partition (by severity, then `hash(DeviceId, N)`) or the collector silently truncates. Design for it up front.

## Proposed collectors

**`defender.vulnerabilities`** — `defender.vulnerability.instances{severity, exploit_available}` (8 series), `.affected_devices{severity, exploit_available}`, `.cves{severity}`, `.max_cvss{severity}`, `.max_epss{severity}`. Twin per (device, CVE, software) with device, OS, CVE, severity, CVSS, EPSS, exploit-available, vendor/product/version, `recommended_security_update`, `cve_mitigation_status`. **Error** on Critical or exploit-available.

**`defender.secure_config`** — `defender.secure_config.assessments{configuration_category, is_compliant}` (10 series measured), `.noncompliant_devices{configuration_category}`, `.impact_at_risk{configuration_category}`. Twin per (device, configuration).

**`defender.software_inventory`** — `defender.software.installs{end_of_support_status}` (4 series), `.eos_devices{...}`, `.products{...}`. Twin per (device, product, version).

## Mapper traps (`live-measured`)

- The KB table is **321,736 rows** — join server-side, never ship it
- Emit `severity` **verbatim** from the wire (`Critical`/`High`/`Medium`/`Low`); do not invent a scale (#142)
- `CveMitigationStatus` is **empty string, not null**, on 24,905 of 24,912 rows. Do not treat empty as missing
- No `Timestamp` on the vulnerability table ⇒ stamp twins at poll time and keep wire values on attributes, as `defender.quarantine` and `entra.risk` already do

## Architecture

This is a **new construction path** — `HuntDeps` alongside `Deps`, `WindowDeps`, `BlobDeps`, `O365Deps`, `MDCADeps`, `EXODeps`.

**CLAUDE.md's #139/#100 warning applies with full force:** `internal/collectordoc.Rows` must be taught to walk it **in the same commit**, or the doc and coverage gates pass over a set of collectors they cannot see. That is precisely the incident those gates exist to prevent.

## Value ordering vs existing coverage

`intune.updates` and the three `*_update_summary` export collectors say whether a **policy deployed**. None says whether a **CVE is still present**, and none covers third-party software at all — 277 distinct products here. `exploit_available` + EPSS turns 24,912 rows into a ranked worklist.

`DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory` overlaps `intune.detected_apps` on the catalogue but adds version-level rows, **CPE** (the join key onto vulnerability data), EOS status/date, and coverage of Defender-onboarded devices that Intune does not manage (73 here vs the Intune fleet). Keep both.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Hunting engine + `HuntDeps` registration path, with `collectordoc.Rows` extended in the same commit
- [ ] Client-side rate limiting and a **long** default interval (6h or daily), with the #106 reasoning recorded in the collector doc so it is not "fixed" to a short one later
- [ ] Row-cap partitioning for twin fetches, with a test that proves it does not silently truncate
- [ ] The three collectors above, mappers written against live query output
- [ ] `defender.oauth_app` (`OAuthAppInfo`, 1,129 rows — Defender's `RiskScore`, `PrivilegeLevel`, `VerifiedPublisher`, `LastUsedTime`, none of which Graph computes) is a reasonable fourth, after the three
- [ ] Goldens + `docs/collectors.md` regenerated

## Absent from this tenant's schema, recorded so nobody re-probes

`DeviceTvmBrowserExtensions(+KB)`, `DeviceTvmCertificateInfo`, `DeviceTvmHardwareFirmware`, `CloudAuditEvents` — dropped by an `isfuzzy` union, i.e. not in the schema. The first three are the **Defender Vulnerability Management add-on** tables; the three core TVM tables above are present **without** the add-on, which is the useful half of that finding.

Method note worth reusing: `union isfuzzy=true (T | getschema | summarize cols=count() | extend T="T"), ...` separates *absent* from *empty* in one request, because `isfuzzy` silently drops non-existent tables while `getschema` returns rows even for an empty one.

Two singleton GETs, no grant, both fold into **existing** collectors with no new metric names and no new cardinality axes. Each closes a silent-failure mode.

47 Intune collector packages ship and the domain is close to saturated — these are the two things a full sweep of `/deviceManagement/*` and `/deviceAppManagement/*` found that are both uncovered and cheap.

## 1. Android Managed Google Play connector health → fold into `intune.connectors`

`GET /beta/deviceManagement/androidManagedStoreAccountEnterpriseSettings` → **200**, singleton, `live-measured 2026-07-23`. Already authorized by held scopes.

Fields: `bindStatus`, `lastAppSyncDateTime`, `lastAppSyncStatus`, `deviceOwnerManagementEnabled`, `androidDeviceOwnerFullyManagedEnrollmentEnabled`, `enrollmentTarget`, `managedGooglePlayEnterpriseType`, `ownerOrganizationName`, `ownerUserPrincipalName`, `lastModifiedDateTime`.

`intune.connectors` today covers exactly three connector types — Exchange, MTD, NDES (`internal/collectors/intune/connectors/connectors.go:1-17`). Add a fourth bounded `connector_type="android_managed_store"` value to the existing `intune.connector.state` and `intune.connector.heartbeat_age_seconds` (age from `lastAppSyncDateTime`). Twin carries `bindStatus`, `lastAppSyncStatus`, `enrollmentTarget`, `ownerUserPrincipalName`.

**Zero new metric names.** A broken Android Enterprise bind stops all Android app delivery silently.

## 2. Autopilot device-sync staleness → fold into `intune.autopilot`

`GET /beta/deviceManagement/windowsAutopilotSettings` → **200**, singleton. Fields: `syncStatus`, `lastSyncDateTime`, `lastManualSyncTriggerDateTime`, `id`.

`intune.autopilot` reads `windowsAutopilotDeviceIdentities` + `windowsAutopilotDeploymentProfiles` and **never the sync singleton** — so "Autopilot registrations stopped arriving from the OEM/partner" is currently undetectable.

Add `intune.autopilot.sync_age_seconds` (gauge, no attributes) + `intune.autopilot.sync_status{sync_status}` (bounded enum). Twin only when not healthy.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Managed Google Play folded into `intune.connectors` as a fourth connector type — no new metric names
- [ ] Autopilot sync folded into `intune.autopilot` — two bounded series
- [ ] Both ride the existing collectors' fetch cycles; no new collector, no new interval
- [ ] Beta endpoints registered in `spec/graph-beta-surface.json`
- [ ] Goldens + `docs/collectors.md` regenerated

## Note on values vs fields

m7kni looks Android-free, so the Managed Google Play **values** are uninteresting here — but the fields are populated and mappable, which is what the mapper needs. State that in the collector doc.

body:
## Two gaps, one per-team fan-out

`m365.teams` ships inventory governance — teams by visibility, ownerless count, with-guests count, membership by role. It stops at the team boundary.

### 1. Installed apps — sideloaded binaries and RSC grants

`GET /beta/teams/{id}/installedApps?$expand=teamsApp` → **200, count=63** on the tenant's single team, `live-measured 2026-07-23`. **No grant needed** — satisfied by roles already held.

Keys: `id`, `teamsApp{id, externalId, displayName, distributionMethod}`, `grantedResourceSpecificApplicationPermissions[]`, `consentedPermissionSet`, `scopeInfo{scope, teamId}`.

Two signals here, and the second is the important one:

- `distributionMethod` is a closed 3-value enum — `store` / `organization` / **`sideloaded`**. A sideloaded app is an unreviewed third-party binary running inside a team.
- **Resource-specific consent (RSC) is a real blind spot.** An RSC grant such as `ChannelMessage.Read.Group` or `TeamMember.Read.Group` lets an app read every message in that team **without any tenant-wide Graph scope**. `entra.consent` sees `oauth2PermissionGrants` and app-role assignments — it cannot see RSC at all. This is not a duplicate of existing consent coverage.

### 2. Channels — including shared channels

`GET /beta/teams/{id}/channels` → 200, count=1. Keys: `membershipType` (`standard`/`private`/`shared`), `isArchived`, `email`, `filesFolderWebUrl`, `webUrl`, `createdDateTime`, `moderationSettings`, `tenantId`.

A **shared** channel exposes content to an *external tenant* via Entra B2B direct connect, governed by a different policy from guest access — so no guest appears in the tenant and `m365.teams`' existing with-guests gauge cannot see it.

`filesFolderWebUrl` is the join key into the SharePoint storage/sharing story.

## Proposed shape

- `m365.teams.installed_apps.total{distribution_method, has_rsc_permissions}` — bounded, `distributionMethod` is a fixed 3-value enum
- `m365.teams.channels.total{membership_type}` and `{is_archived}` — bounded

Twins: `m365.teams_app` per (team, app) with the RSC permission list joined, **Warn** on `sideloaded` or any non-empty RSC grant. `m365.team_channel` per channel with `membershipType`, `filesFolderWebUrl`.

## Cost — this is the part to get right

`m365.teams` already issues one `GET /teams/{id}?$select=summary,isArchived` per team (`teams.go:206-210`), because the list form nulls those fields. Adding channels and installedApps makes it **three requests per team per cycle**. On a 500-team tenant that is 1500 requests through the directory throttle bucket per cycle, against 1-per-team today.

Build them as **one collector sharing the existing fan-out**, or as separate collectors with their own long intervals — not as two more independent full sweeps at `m365.teams`' interval.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Installed-apps and channel coverage, sharing the existing per-team fan-out
- [ ] Bounded gauges only; nothing keyed by team id or app id
- [ ] Twins with Warn on sideloaded / RSC-granted apps
- [ ] Explicitly measure and document the per-cycle request cost at N teams
- [ ] Beta endpoints registered in `spec/graph-beta-surface.json`; both have v1.0 equivalents, so prefer v1.0 if the fields are present there
- [ ] Goldens + `docs/collectors.md` regenerated

## Sampling caveat

**m7kni is a one-team tenant**: 1 team, 1 channel, 63 installed apps. The mappers are shaped from n=1. The *distributions* — how many private vs shared channels, how many sideloaded apps — are not observable here. Say so in the collector doc.

## Dead ends recorded

- `GET /beta/teamwork/teamsAppSettings` (tenant-wide Teams app policy) → **412 `PreconditionFailed: Requested API is not supported in application-only context`**. The crispest possible refusal — the service names the restriction itself. Do not retry, do not grant anything.
- `GET /v1.0/appCatalogs/teamsApps` (tenant app catalogue) → 403, needs `AppCatalog.Read.All`. Not held; lower value than the per-team install view.

body:
Blocked on the ledger correction in #237, which establishes the endpoint exists and is readable app-only.

## Signal

Which DLP policies exist, what mode each is in (audit vs enforce), which workloads and locations each covers, what actions each rule takes, and when any of it last changed. Specifically: **did someone quietly downgrade a policy from Enforce to audit-only.**

Covered by nothing today. `entra.security_alerts` carries DLP *alerts* (`serviceSource: dataLossPrevention` — the collector polls `/security/alerts_v2` unfiltered, so those already arrive); nothing carries DLP *policy state*.

## Endpoint

`GET /beta/security/dataSecurityAndGovernance/policyFiles` — 200 on scopes already held, no grant, no data-plane registration. v1.0 400s; beta only.

Live on m7kni (`live-measured 2026-07-23`): 6 policies / 8 rules, modes `AuditAndNotify` and `Enforce`, bindings across `Exchange`, `SharePoint`, `OneDriveForBusiness`, `Teams`, `EndpointDevices`, rule actions `NotifyUser`, `GenerateIncidentReport`, `GenerateAlert`, `BlockAccess`, `EndpointRestrictAccess`.

## Build notes — read these before writing the parser

- `content` is `Edm.Binary` holding **base64 of UTF-16LE XML**, root `<Content xmlns="http://schemas.protection.outlook.com/hygienews/">`. Not JSON, not UTF-8. Decode `base64 → utf-16-le`.
- The row carries `version` (a 128-hex-char hash) and `status` ∈ `modified` / `notModified` / `noContent`. **Store `version` in the checkpoint and skip the 76 KB parse when unchanged** — that is what makes a short interval affordable.
- **The wire disagrees with the EDM on `fileType`.** The beta metadata declares `policyFileType` as `dlpPolicy`, `dlpSensitiveInformationType`, `dataCollectionPolicy`, `unknownFutureValue`. The wire returned id `CustomClassifications` with `fileType: customClassifications` — a member not in the enum. **Do not switch exhaustively on the declared enum.**
- Bindings sit at **policy** level, not rule level. A rule's `workload=` attribute is a comma-joined string; the `<bindings>` block is the location scoping.

## Secrets boundary — this one is safe, and it is worth saying why

This is **policy definition**, not matched content. It carries rule names and sensitive-info-type GUIDs, no detected values. It is **not** the hazard documented on `m365.activity`'s `RequiredPermissions`, where `PolicyDetails[].Rules[].ConditionsMatched.SensitiveInformation[].SensitiveInformationDetections.DetectedValues[].Value` carries the matched secret itself (a live sample on this tenant contains a full credit-card number).

Safe to emit in full. Do not generalise the `m365.activity` exclusion to this endpoint by feel — CLAUDE.md is explicit that "awkward to model" is not "unsafe to ship", and that mistake has shipped three times.

## Proposed shape

Metrics, bounded by policy count rather than tenant size:

- `purview.dlp.policies{mode}`
- `purview.dlp.rules{workload, action}`
- `purview.dlp.policy_bindings{workload, binding_type}`
- `purview.dlp.policy.last_changed.age`

Twins: `purview.dlp_policy` per policy (`policy_id`, `policy_name`, `mode`, `when_changed_utc`, `when_rules_changed_utc`, bound workloads) and `purview.dlp_rule` per rule (`rule_id`, `management_rule_id`, `rule_name`, `policy_id`, `workload`, `actions` joined, `last_modified_utc`, sensitive-info-type ids + min/max count/confidence).

Snapshot engine, long interval — policy config changes rarely.

## Licence

DLP requires E5 / M365 E5 Compliance. Endpoint returned 200 on m7kni. Adaptive Protection policy rows in the sample imply Insider Risk Management is licensed here too.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] #237 landed first (ledger corrected)
- [ ] `purview.dlp_policies` collector with the UTF-16LE parser and the `version`-checkpoint skip
- [ ] Bounded metrics + both twins
- [ ] Explicit test that no rule condition value is emitted (guard the secrets boundary by test, not by comment)
- [ ] Beta endpoint registered in `spec/graph-beta-surface.json`
- [ ] Goldens + `docs/collectors.md` regenerated

body:
## The gap

The CIS/benchmark tenant switches — can ordinary users register applications, create groups, read other users, invite guests; is legacy MSOL PowerShell blocked; is user consent for risky apps allowed; is the admin consent workflow on; does the default app-management policy restrict long-lived secrets — are invisible in graph2otel today.

This is the class of setting that gets changed once during an incident and never changed back.

## Evidence — all 200 on `Policy.Read.All`, already held (`live-measured 2026-07-23`)

| endpoint | body |
| --- | --- |
| `policies/authorizationPolicy` | `{allowInvitesFrom, allowedToSignUpEmailBasedSubscriptions, allowedToUseSSPR, allowEmailVerifiedUsersToJoinOrganization, blockMsolPowerShell, allowUserConsentForRiskyApps, defaultUserRolePermissions, guestUserRoleId}` |
| `policies/adminConsentRequestPolicy` | `{isEnabled, notifyReviewers, remindersEnabled, requestDurationInDays, reviewers, version}` |
| `policies/defaultAppManagementPolicy` | `{isEnabled: true, applicationRestrictions:{passwordCredentials:[], keyCredentials:[], identifierUris:{...}}, servicePrincipalRestrictions}` |
| `policies/appManagementPolicies` | 200, empty |
| `groupLifecyclePolicies` | 200, empty |
| `policies/featureRolloutPolicies` | 200, empty |

## Proposed shape

**One** gauge `entra.tenant_policy.setting`, valued 0/1, with attribute `setting` drawn from a fixed enumerated list:

`users_can_create_apps`, `users_can_create_security_groups`, `users_can_read_other_users`, `guest_invite_scope`, `msol_powershell_blocked`, `user_consent_for_risky_apps_allowed`, `sspr_allowed`, `email_verified_join_allowed`, `admin_consent_workflow_enabled`, `app_management_policy_enabled`, `app_password_credentials_restricted`

Fully bounded, ~12 series, independent of tenant size.

Log twin carrying the raw policy objects, including `guestUserRoleId` (the GUID that distinguishes Guest from Restricted Guest — the difference matters and is not otherwise expressible) and the credential-restriction arrays, whose shape is unbounded and therefore twin-only.

Snapshot engine, long interval.

## Why one collector and not six

Four of the six endpoints are empty on this tenant and are single small objects everywhere. Six separate collectors for eleven booleans would be worse than one. This is also the natural home for `groupLifecyclePolicies` and `featureRolloutPolicies` if they ever carry data, and for the `multiTenantOrganization` state (`{state: "inactive"}`, one field) rather than giving that its own collector.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `entra.tenant_policy_posture` collector over the six endpoints, degrading gracefully where empty
- [ ] Single bounded gauge as specified; verify series count is fixed
- [ ] Twin carries `guestUserRoleId` and the credential-restriction arrays
- [ ] Goldens + `docs/collectors.md` regenerated

## Adjacent, deliberately excluded

- `directory/administrativeUnits` → 200 empty. The interesting field is restricted-management AUs (`isMemberManagementRestricted`), unverifiable with zero AUs
- `policies/permissionGrantPolicies` → 403, needs `Policy.Read.PermissionGrant`. This is the *definition* of consent policies; `entra.consent` already emits the actual grants, which is the question operators ask
- `directory/attributeSets`, `directory/customSecurityAttributeDefinitions` → 403, needs `CustomSecAttributeDefinition.Read.All`. Tiny surface, empty on most tenants
- `identityProviders` → 403, needs `IdentityProvider.Read.All`. m7kni has none

body:
## Two distinct gaps, one fetch

### 1. Ownerless applications and service principals

`live-measured 2026-07-23`: `GET /v1.0/applications?$select=id,displayName&$expand=owners&$top=999` → 200, **27 applications, 21 of them ownerless (78%)**. `servicePrincipals?$expand=owners` likewise 200.

An ownerless app registration is one nobody can be asked "is this still needed?" — it is the entry point to credential sprawl and it accumulates silently. `Application.Read.All` is already held.

### 2. Federated identity credentials — the gap `entra.credential_expiry` structurally cannot see

`GET /beta/applications?$select=id,appId,displayName,createdDateTime,signInAudience&$expand=federatedIdentityCredentials,owners` → 200, 27 apps, `federatedIdentityCredentials` inline on every one. (**Zero on m7kni** — empty here proves nothing about other tenants. The `$expand` is beta-only.)

`entra.credential_expiry` buckets secret and certificate expiry. **A federated identity credential has no expiry**, so an application whose trust is a GitHub OIDC subject reports perfectly clean while anyone with write access to that repo can authenticate as it. The subject string is the whole signal:

```
issuer:  https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com
subject: repo:org/repo:ref:refs/heads/main
```

This is a supply-chain trust edge with no representation anywhere in graph2otel.

## Proposed shape

- `entra.application.ownership{has_owner, sign_in_audience}`
- `entra.service_principal.ownership{has_owner, service_principal_type}`
- `entra.application.federated_credentials{issuer_host}` — bounded in practice (`token.actions.githubusercontent.com`, `sts.windows.net`, a k8s OIDC host); the central limiter (#235) folds any tail

Log twins:

- `entra.application` — app id, display name, created, sign-in audience, owner count, owner UPNs. **Warn** on zero owners
- `entra.federated_identity_credential` — app id/name, credential name, `issuer`, `subject`, `audiences`

Snapshot engine, rides an already-cheap fetch. No grant. No licence requirement.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Ownership gauges + twins for applications and service principals

body:
## The gap

`entra.secure_score` already fetches everything below, every hour, and decodes **two fields**.

`internal/collectors/entra/securescore/securescore.go:107-127` decodes only `currentScore` and `maxScore` from `GET /v1.0/security/secureScores?$top=1`. The same response carries `controlScores` — **234 entries**, `live-measured 2026-07-23` — each:

```
{controlCategory, controlName, description, score, scoreInPercentage,
 implementationStatus, lastSynced, on, count, total}
```

plus `averageComparativeScores` (peer benchmarks by `AllTenants` / seat band / industry), `activeUserCount`, `licensedUserCount`, `enabledServices`.

And `GET /v1.0/security/secureScoreControlProfiles` is *also* already fetched, then collapsed at `securescore.go:146-180` into two counts with **no log twin**, discarding `maxScore`, `rank`, `tier`, `threats[]`, `service`, `actionType`, `actionUrl`, `deprecated`, `implementationCost`, `userImpact`, `remediation`, `remediationImpact`.

This is a **#114 log-twin violation on a shipped collector**: the collector can answer "what is my score" but never "which control is failing and what do I do about it". No new fetch, no new scope, no new engine — a mapper.

## Proposed shape

Metrics (bounded by Microsoft's control catalogue, not tenant size):

- `entra.secure_score.by_category{control_category}` and `.max_by_category{control_category}` from `controlScores`
- `entra.secure_score.peer_average{basis}` from `averageComparativeScores`

Log twin `entra.secure_score_control` per control: `control_name`, `control_category`, `score`, `max_score`, `score_in_percentage`, `implementation_status`, `tier`, `rank`, `threats`, `service`, `action_type`, `action_url`, `deprecated`, `last_synced`.

**Warn** at `scoreInPercentage < 100` on a non-deprecated control.

## Why this is worth doing before any new collector

It is the highest value-per-unit-of-work item found in the whole coverage sweep: the data is already on the wire, already paid for in request budget, and thrown away 234 rows at a time every hour. `actionUrl` in particular turns the twin into a worklist rather than a report.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Decode `controlScores` and emit the per-control log twin
- [ ] Category gauges + peer-average gauge
- [ ] Twin the control profiles rather than collapsing to two counts
- [ ] Verify no metric series is keyed by anything that grows with tenant size
- [ ] Goldens updated; `docs/collectors.md` regenerated

## Caveat

Strictly this is "data we already fetch and drop" rather than a new surface. It is filed with the new-coverage batch because `controlScores` is a nav property the code has never read and the peer-benchmark array is genuinely new — but weight it as a fix, not a feature.

Closed by `fd8cb41` (pushed to main).

Emits from the two existing fetches, no new scope/engine:
- gauges `entra.secure_score.by_category{category}`, `.max_by_category{category}`, `.peer_average{basis}` — all bounded, none per-entity
- log twins `entra.secure_score_control` (Warn below 100%) and `entra.secure_score_control_profile` (actionUrl/tier/threats worklist)

Mappers written against the `controlScores` + full-profile live fixtures already committed for this collector (`live-measured #165`). Golden regrown (5→8 metrics + 2 log twins), `docs/collectors.md` regenerated, `make check` green.

Design note: the two endpoints stay independent (a failure in one still emits the other — the existing resilience tests require it), so the twins are deliberately NOT joined across endpoints. The Warn condition uses `scoreInPercentage < 100` alone; the `deprecated` flag lives only on the profile twin. `scoreInPercentage` is decoded as a pointer so an absent field stays Info rather than false-warning as 0%.

body:
## The gap

`entra.roles` answers **who holds what** — standing directory-role membership plus PIM active/eligible/permanent counts. Nothing answers **what it takes to get it**.

A Global Administrator eligible-assignment that activates on justification alone, with no MFA and no approval, is the single most consequential misconfiguration in an Entra tenant, and it is invisible in every signal graph2otel ships.

## Evidence (`live-measured 2026-07-23`, no grant needed)

```
GET /v1.0/policies/roleManagementPolicies?$filter=scopeId eq '/' and scopeType eq 'Directory'&$expand=rules
200, 145 policies, rules expanded inline (17 rules on the sample)
```

`Policy.Read.All` and `RoleManagement.Read.Directory` are both already in the poller's token. One request, all policies, rules inline.

Live rule bodies captured:

```
Enablement_EndUser_Assignment.enabledRules = ["MultiFactorAuthentication","Justification"]
Approval_EndUser_Assignment.setting = {isApprovalRequired:false, isApprovalRequiredForExtension:false,
                                       isRequestorJustificationRequired:true, approvalMode:"SingleStage",
                                       approvalStages:[{approvalStageTimeOutInDays:1, ...}]}
Expiration_EndUser_Assignment  = {isExpirationRequired:true,  maximumDuration:"PT8H"}
Expiration_Admin_Assignment    = {isExpirationRequired:false, maximumDuration:"P180D"}
AuthenticationContext_EndUser_Assignment = {isEnabled:false, claimValue:null}
```

**Per-role variance is real and is the signal**: a `$top=1` fetch returned a policy whose activation `enabledRules` was `["Justification"]` only — no MFA — while the full fetch's first policy required MFA.

`GET /v1.0/policies/roleManagementPolicyAssignments?$filter=...` maps `roleDefinitionId` → `policyId`, returning `{id, policyId, roleDefinitionId, scopeId, scopeType}`.

## Proposed shape

Bounded gauge `entra.pim.role_policy.requirement`, counting role policies by:

- `requirement` ∈ `mfa_on_activation` / `approval_required` / `justification_required` / `auth_context_required` / `activation_expiry_required` / `eligibility_expiry_required`
- × `enabled` ∈ true/false
- × `caller` ∈ `EndUser` / `Admin`

≈ 24 series, fixed, independent of tenant size.

**Do not** key a duration gauge by role — that is 145 series and grows with the role catalogue. Durations go on the twin.

Log twin `entra.pim_role_policy` per policy: `role_definition_id`, `policy_id`, `is_organization_default`, `activation_max_duration`, `activation_enabled_rules` (comma-joined), `approval_required`, `approval_stage_timeout_days`, `assignment_expiry_required`, `assignment_max_duration`, `auth_context_enabled`, `auth_context_claim`, `last_modified_date_time`.

**Warn** when a policy allows activation with neither MFA nor approval.

Snapshot engine, long interval (6–24h — this is configuration, not events).

## Licence

Entra ID P2 (PIM). Tenant has it; the PIM half of `entra.roles` is already live.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `entra.pim_role_policies` collector, mapper written against the live wire above
- [ ] Bounded gauge as specified — verify the series count does not scale with role count
- [ ] Log twin per policy, Warn on the no-MFA-no-approval combination
- [ ] `roleDefinitionId` → role display name resolution (or state explicitly why the twin carries the GUID only)
- [ ] Registered, `docs/collectors.md` regenerated, goldens updated

## Related dead end, recorded so it is not re-probed

`roleManagement/directory/roleAssignmentScheduleRequests` and `roleEligibilityScheduleRequests` → **403**, and the error names **only ReadWrite scopes** (`RoleAssignmentSchedule.ReadWrite.Directory`, `RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Directory`, `RoleAssignmentSchedule.Remove.Directory`). There is no read-only application permission for PIM *request* history. It is also largely redundant — PIM activations already land in `entra.directory_audits`. `live-measured 2026-07-23`.

body:
Four blob containers on the tenant's storage account are **enabled, written, billed, and read by no collector**. They ride the existing `blobpipeline` + `BlobDeps` path — no new engine, no new scope, no new auth, no new layout. They are on a 7-day lifecycle, so today graph2otel pays to delete them unread.

Building them or turning them off are the only two defensible states.

## 1. `defender.behavior` + `defender.behavior_entity`

Containers `insights-logs-advancedhunting-behaviorinfo` and `insights-logs-advancedhunting-behaviorentities`, both live.

Defender's **behaviour** layer: the sub-alert "suspicious pattern observed and scored" records that sit between raw EDR telemetry and a fired alert. Everything graph2otel ships today starts at the alert (`entra.security_alerts`, `defender.alert_info`). A SIEM wants both tiers.

`live-measured 2026-07-23`, one record read verbatim from the container: a real `ImpossibleTravelActivity` for a named UPN, `ServiceSource: "Microsoft Cloud App Security"`, `Categories: ["InitialAccess"]`, `AttackTechniques: ["Valid Accounts (T1078)", "Cloud Accounts (T1078.004)"]`, with `StartTime`/`EndTime` and a prose `Description`. `BehaviorEntities` returned 5 rows against that one `BehaviorId`, one per entity, with the same ~37-column shape as `AlertEvidence`.

Volume: 5 / 20 rows per 30 days on this tenant. Trivial.

Proposed: exactly the shipped `defender.alert_info` / `defender.alert_evidence` pair, one tier down. Log-only, joined on `behavior_id`. A bounded counter by `action_type` × `service_source` is possible later; log-only matches the sibling pair and is the safer first cut.

## 2. `defender.teams_message` + `defender.teams_message_url`

Containers `insights-logs-advancedhunting-messageevents` and `insights-logs-advancedhunting-messageurlinfo`. **Both created 2026-07-23 09:10Z**, each holding one blob.

Defender for Office 365 protection of **Teams messages**. graph2otel has zero Teams *security* coverage — `m365.teams` is inventory governance only.

`MessageEvents` is 29 columns: `TeamsMessageId`, `SenderEmailAddress`/`DisplayName`/`ObjectId`/`SenderType`, `RecipientDetails`, `ThreadId`/`ThreadName`/`ThreadType`, `GroupId`/`GroupName`, `IsExternalThread`, `MessageType`/`Subtype`, `Subject`, `ThreatTypes`, `DetectionMethods`, `ConfidenceLevel`, `DeliveryAction`, `DeliveryLocation`, `ReportId`, `SafetyTip`. Volume 3 / 9 rows per 30 days.

Proposed: mirror `defender.email` / `defender.email_url`, joined on `MessageId`. `IsExternalThread` + `SenderType` is the external-collaboration attack surface.

**This clears a #233 blocker.** #233 records `MessageEvents` as having *"never held a single row"*, with the stated reproduction step "post an internal Teams message containing a URL, then re-probe". That happened; the containers now exist.

## Important: Microsoft's own doc is wrong here

The [supported streaming event types](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-xdr/supported-event-types) page lists **`BehaviorInfo` and `BehaviorEntities` as "Not available"** in every cloud. They are streaming to this tenant's storage account right now. The same table omits `IdentityInfo`, `MessageEvents` and `MessageUrlInfo` entirely, all three of which are also streaming.

That page is wrong on at least five rows. Anyone who checks it before proposing a table will reject buildable ones. Worth an entry in `docs/graph-api-gotchas.md` — this is the wire-over-docs rule landing on a page nobody had checked against the account.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `defender.behavior` + `defender.behavior_entity` collectors, mappers written against the live container samples (not docs)
- [ ] `defender.teams_message` + `defender.teams_message_url` collectors, same
- [ ] All four registered so `internal/collectordoc` sees them; `docs/collectors.md` regenerated
- [ ] Signal goldens updated
- [ ] Record the streaming-event-types doc error in `docs/graph-api-gotchas.md`
- [ ] Volume on this tenant is tiny (n=5/20/3/9 per 30d) — enough to write mappers against, **not** enough to characterise volume. State that in the collector docs

## Note

`MessagePostDeliveryEvents` is in the hunting schema but returns 0 rows and has no container. Ship it alongside `MessageEvents` only if it ever produces data.
