body:
## The bug

`internal/collectors/m365/storage/storage.go` — `Collect` has exactly **one** return statement, `return nil`. Every fetch failure is swallowed:

```go
// fetch GETs a report (RawGet follows the 302 to the CSV) and parses it. A
// fetch/parse failure logs a warning and returns nil — the report is skipped,
// never fatal.
func (c *Collector) fetch(ctx context.Context, r report) []map[string]string {
	raw, err := c.g.RawGet(ctx, c.baseURL+"/reports/"+r.fn)
	if err != nil {
		c.logger.Warn("m365.storage: report unavailable, skipping", ...)
		return nil
	}
	...
}
```

So when all four reports fail, the collector emits **zero** metrics and **zero** twins, and the scheduler records a successful scrape. The status page reports `last_success: true, failures: 0, success_rate_pct: 100`.

This is CLAUDE.md's "a green tick is not evidence of data" as a live production condition, not a hypothetical.

## Observed

Production, camden, 2026-07-23 16:01–16:08: `"m365.storage: report unavailable, skipping"` for **all four** reports, each `context deadline exceeded` after ~100s (`last_duration_ms: 400030` = 4 × the client timeout). Collector reported success.

Independently, probing `/reports/*` as the poller in the same window and again hours later:

```
getSharePointSiteUsageStorage(period='D7')        -> HTTP 429 ServiceThrottleThresholdExceeded
getMailboxUsageQuotaStatusMailboxCounts(period='D7') -> HTTP 429 ServiceThrottleThresholdExceeded
```

`Content-Type: text/plain`, **no `Retry-After`**, no JSON error envelope on some responses.

## Important caveat on the API-health half

A six-agent research sweep was probing this tenant concurrently, and `/reports/*` throttles at 5 req/10s. **I cannot separate "the reports API is chronically degraded" from "we saturated it ourselves."** The 429s are real; their cause is not established. Do not record "reports API degraded" as a fact.

The **code** defect is independent of that and verifiable from source alone.

## Why the current behaviour is defensible-looking but wrong

Skipping an unavailable report rather than failing the whole collector is the right instinct — one report being down should not lose the other three. The defect is that a run which fetched *nothing* is indistinguishable from a healthy one.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A run where **every** report failed must not report success. Partial success (some reports fetched) should still succeed
- [ ] Emit a self-obs signal for per-report fetch outcome so the failure is visible without reading logs — this is the same gap `graph2otel.api.unexpected` fills for wire drift
- [ ] `ServiceThrottleThresholdExceeded` is a **different, service-side** throttle from the documented 5 req/10s ceiling in `docs/graph-api-gotchas.md` — it survives minutes of backoff and sends no `Retry-After`. Add it to the throttle table with that distinction stated
- [ ] Re-measure `/reports/*` health when nothing else is probing the tenant, and record the result with an evidence tag either way
- [ ] Audit the other report-backed collectors for the same swallow-and-succeed shape

## Related

`GET /v1.0/admin/reportSettings` → **403 `S2SUnauthorized`**; `ReportSettings.Read.All` is not held. `m365.storage` falls back to an all-zeros-GUID heuristic to detect name concealment (`storage.go:242-254`) — but in this incident that heuristic had no rows to inspect either, so the tenant's actual `displayConcealedNames` value is unknown. Granting `ReportSettings.Read.All` is one scope and is a prerequisite for any usage-report **log twin**: when concealment is on, every UPN and site name in those reports is an opaque per-tenant hash, which silently destroys the twin's join key.
title: fix(m365.storage): all four reports can fail and the collector still reports 100% success — zero data, green tick

## The unblock condition has fired

`docs/graph-api-gotchas.md` records `NetworkAccessTrafficLogs` as a corrected non-gap with a deferral: *"has a beta endpoint that names its own scope (#130 — out of scope until a GSA tenant exists)"*.

**A GSA tenant now exists.** `live-measured 2026-07-23`, as `graph2otel-poller`:

```
GET /beta/networkAccess/tenantStatus
200 {"onboardingStatus": "onboarded", "onboardingErrorMessage": null}
```

CLAUDE.md's tracker-hygiene rule requires that any "do not X yet" name its unblock condition so a later reader can check whether it has fired. This one did, and nothing checked. Filing so it is checkable.

## Two separable pieces of work

### 1. GSA posture — free, no grant, buildable today

All six of these returned **200** on `Policy.Read.All`, which the poller already holds (`live-measured 2026-07-23`):

| endpoint | result |
| --- | --- |
| `beta/networkAccess/tenantStatus` | `{onboardingStatus, onboardingErrorMessage}` |
| `beta/networkAccess/forwardingProfiles` | **n=3**, `{state, trafficForwardingType, priority, isCustomProfile, associations, assignmentRules, clientFallbackAction, localNetworkSettings, servicePrincipal, version, lastModifiedDateTime}` |
| `beta/networkAccess/filteringPolicies` | n=1, `{action, name, version}` |
| `beta/networkAccess/settings/conditionalAccess` | `{signalingStatus, dataPlaneSignalingOptions}` |
| `beta/networkAccess/settings/crossTenantAccess` | `{networkPacketTaggingStatus, dataPlaneTaggingOptions}` |
| `beta/networkAccess/connectivity/remoteNetworks` | empty |

Proposed: `entra.gsa.onboarding_status` (enum gauge, mapped in `docs/signals.md` like `m365.servicehealth`), `entra.gsa.forwarding_profiles{traffic_forwarding_type, state}`, `entra.gsa.filtering_policies{action}`, `entra.gsa.signaling_enabled`, `entra.gsa.packet_tagging_enabled`. Twins per profile and per policy. Snapshot engine.

Beta-only, so it must be registered in `spec/graph-beta-surface.json` per `docs/api-drift.md`.

### 2. GSA traffic logs — needs one read-only grant

`GET /beta/networkAccess/logs/traffic` → **403**, body names the scopes verbatim:

```
Authentication_MSGraphPermissionMissing: The principal does not have required
Microsoft Graph permission(s): Directory.ReadWrite.All, NetworkAccess.Read.All,
NetworkAccess.ReadWrite.All, NetworkAccess-Reports.Read.All to call this API.
```

**Grant `NetworkAccess.Read.All` (or `NetworkAccess-Reports.Read.All`) — read-only.** Do NOT take `NetworkAccess.ReadWrite.All` or `Directory.ReadWrite.All`, which the same error also lists.

Window engine (no delta query on any Graph log endpoint; own watermark + overlap + seen-id). Log-only: per-connection `user_principal_name`, `device_id`, `destination_fqdn`, `destination_ip`, `destination_port`, `transport_protocol`, `traffic_type`, `action`, `policy_id`/`policy_rule_id`, `source_ip`, `agent_version`, byte counts. Bounded counter `entra.network_access.transactions{traffic_type, action}` only.

Response shape is **unmeasured** — blocked on the grant. Do not write the mapper from docs.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Update the `docs/graph-api-gotchas.md` deferral note: the condition has fired, with the `live-measured` evidence above
- [ ] Build GSA posture (piece 1) — no grant needed
- [ ] Decide on the `NetworkAccess.Read.All` grant; if granted, probe first and write the traffic mapper against the wire
- [ ] Measure traffic-log volume on this tenant before enabling by default
- [ ] Four GSA-family blob diagnostic categories (`RemoteNetworkHealthLogs`, `NetworkAccessAlerts`, `NetworkAccessConnectionEvents`, `NetworkAccessGenerativeAIInsights`) are enabled and container-less — see #238

## Dead end recorded

`beta/networkAccess/reports/getDeviceUsageSummary(...)` → **400** `Resource not found for the segment 'getDeviceUsageSummary'`. Function name wrong or absent on this tenant's beta; not chased.

comments.body:
**Correction item landed** (`861d339`): `docs/graph-api-gotchas.md` now records that #130's "until a GSA tenant exists" deferral has fired (`tenantStatus` → onboarded), with the split between free posture (piece 1) and grant-gated traffic logs (piece 2).

**Remaining (the feature builds):**
- Piece 1 (GSA posture — no grant): buildable today, but needs verbatim wire samples re-captured as the poller before writing the mapper (wire-over-docs — the issue lists fields, not full JSON). Not built this session.
- Piece 2 (traffic logs): blocked on a `NetworkAccess.Read.All` grant decision; response shape unmeasured. Do NOT write the mapper from docs.

Left open for both builds.

Piece 1 (GSA posture) shipped in 27c2258 (`Closes #239`). A pure-beta Experimental snapshot collector `entra.gsa` reading six `/beta/networkAccess` resources on `Policy.Read.All` (already held; all live-verified 200 as `graph2otel-poller` 2026-07-23).

**Emitted:** bounded gauges `entra.gsa.onboarding_status` (numeric enum, mapped in `docs/signals.md`), `.forwarding_profiles{traffic_forwarding_type,state}`, `.filtering_policies{action}`, `.remote_networks`, `.signaling_enabled`, `.packet_tagging_enabled`; log twins `entra.gsa_forwarding_profile` + `entra.gsa_filtering_policy`. The per-remote-network twin is deliberately **not** emitted — m7kni has none, so there is no live shape to map (#142/#165). Beta surface registered, snapshot regenerated, `make check` green.

**Wire-vs-issue note:** `filteringPolicies` returns a bare `#filteringPolicies` odata context (not `#networkAccess/filteringPolicies`); the resource path is still under `networkAccess`. Recorded in the beta manifest.

**Piece 2 (traffic logs)** — `GET /beta/networkAccess/logs/traffic` → 403 naming `NetworkAccess.Read.All` (read-only; do NOT take the ReadWrite/`Directory.ReadWrite.All` variants the same error lists). Its wire shape is unmeasured so no mapper is written from docs. This grant decision is tracked in the #251 Phase 6 table — closing here does not drop it.

Correction to piece 2 (live-measured 2026-07-23 as `graph2otel-poller`): traffic logs are **not grant-blocked**. The poller **already holds `NetworkAccess.Read.All`**, and `GET /beta/networkAccess/logs/traffic` returns **200 with an empty `value`** — not 403. So piece 2 is **data-blocked, not scope-blocked**: no traffic flows because all three GSA forwarding profiles are `state: disabled` on m7kni (see the `entra.gsa` posture data). To generate traffic-log data, a forwarding profile must be enabled and client/branch traffic actually routed through GSA. The mapper stays unwritten until then (wire-over-docs, #142/#165) — the endpoint shape is confirmed reachable, the payload is unmeasured because there is none.

body:
## What is wrong

A probe comment on #134 states:

> I did not verify the diagnostic setting's own configuration — that is an ARM control-plane read and the poller holds only `Storage Blob Data Reader` on this account plus Graph scopes. Reading it would require a different identity, which the identity split (#109) forbids.

The premise is wrong. The poller reads it as itself.

## Evidence (`live-measured 2026-07-23`, as `graph2otel-poller`)

`GET https://management.azure.com/providers/microsoft.aadiam/diagnosticSettings?api-version=2017-04-01` (ARM audience token, client-assertion JWT, same cert) → **200**, setting name `graph2otel`, sink `graph2otelm7kni`, **26 categories, 21 enabled**.

The boundary is real but much narrower than recorded — two ARM reads in the same session, same identity:

| read | result |
| --- | --- |
| `providers/microsoft.aadiam/diagnosticSettings` | **200** |
| `providers/microsoft.intune/diagnosticSettings` | 403 `AuthorizationFailed` |
| the storage account resource itself | 403 `AuthorizationFailed` |

So it is specifically the **tenant-level `microsoft.aadiam` provider** that reads, authorized by the poller's Entra roles rather than by Azure RBAC. Not "ARM generally".

`providers/microsoft.aadiam/diagnosticSettingsCategories` 400s — the settings object's own `logs[]` array is the only enumerable list.

## Why this matters beyond the correction

It makes a structural gate available. Six containers on the storage account are enabled, written, billed and **read by nothing** — found by hand in this sweep:

```
insights-logs-advancedhunting-behaviorentities
insights-logs-advancedhunting-behaviorinfo
insights-logs-advancedhunting-messageevents
insights-logs-advancedhunting-messageurlinfo
insights-logs-devicecomplianceorg
insights-logs-signinlogs
```

A collector diffing the ARM category list against the registered blob collectors finds the seventh automatically, and catches the **opposite and more dangerous direction**: a collector polling a container that will never be written reports clean success forever. `docs/blob-ingest.md` already warns that an empty container is not evidence of a fault; nothing detects it.

## Proposed shape

`graph2otel.blob.categories` gauge by `state` ∈ `consumed` / `enabled_unread` / `mapped_but_disabled` / `disabled`, computed by diffing the ARM response against registered blob collectors' `Container` values. Log twin per category naming it and its state. **Warn on `enabled_unread`, Error on `mapped_but_disabled`.**

Snapshot engine, one fetch, no cursor, no pagination. `DefaultAzureCredential` already mints per-audience tokens (it does exactly this for the storage data plane), so the ARM audience is not new machinery.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Correct the #134 comment's claim (post a correcting comment; do not rewrite history)
- [ ] Record in `docs/blob-ingest.md` that the poller can read `microsoft.aadiam` diagnostic settings, with the `microsoft.intune` 403 as the stated boundary
- [ ] Build the `graph2otel.blob.categories` self-obs gauge + twin
- [ ] Categories new since #135's 19-category sweep, all currently enabled and zero-row on m7kni: `RiskyAgents`, `AgentRiskEvents`, `RemoteNetworkHealthLogs`, `NetworkAccessAlerts`, `NetworkAccessConnectionEvents`, `NetworkAccessGenerativeAIInsights`, `B2CRequestLogs`. `CustomSecurityAttributeAuditLogs` is configured in a *separate* diagnostic-settings section and does not appear in this list at all
- [ ] Someone with ARM access should read `providers/microsoft.intune/diagnosticSettings` once and record the category list — one GET, closes the Intune half of the census this gate closes for Entra

## Related

- `SignInLogs` is enabled, writing, and deliberately unread — #135 says it "gets removed from the diagnostic setting after #137's latency measurement runs". **#137 has closed and the removal has not happened.** 1.97 MB over 33 blobs, under 1% of the account against MGAL's 325.5 MB, so this is tracker hygiene rather than cost. It should be either removed or explicitly documented as retained; what it should not be is accidentally on.

## What is wrong

`docs/graph-api-gotchas.md`, "Permanent gaps and the fallback path", lists **DLP policy enumeration** among signals with *no API anywhere*, re-audited `[live 2026-07-16, #130 audit]`. That is false.

`GET /beta/security/dataSecurityAndGovernance/policyFiles` returns the tenant's complete DLP policy definition **on scopes the poller already holds**, no grant and no data-plane registration.

## Evidence (`live-measured 2026-07-23`, as `graph2otel-poller`)

```
status 200
  id=DataCollectionPolicy   fileType=dataCollectionPolicy   status=noContent    b64len=0
  id=DlpPolicy              fileType=dlpPolicy              status=modified     b64len=204224
  id=CustomClassifications  fileType=customClassifications  status=noContent    b64len=0
```

`DlpPolicy.content` decodes (base64 → **UTF-16LE**, not UTF-8) to 76,583 chars of XML carrying 6 policies / 8 rules with:

- per-policy `mode` — observed `AuditAndNotify` and `Enforce`
- per-policy `<bindings><binding workload="..." >` — observed `Exchange`, `SharePoint`, `OneDriveForBusiness`, `Teams`, `EndpointDevices`
- per-rule actions — `NotifyUser`, `GenerateIncidentReport`, `GenerateAlert`, `BlockAccess`, `EndpointRestrictAccess`
- per-rule conditions with sensitive-info-type GUIDs and `minCount`/`maxCount`/`minConfidence`/`maxConfidence`

v1.0 400s (`Resource not found for the segment 'policyFiles'`); beta only.

## Why it was missed

#99 probed `security/dataLossPreventionPolicies`, `dataLossPrevention/policies` and `protectionScopes` — three plausible route names. `dataSecurityAndGovernance/policyFiles` is not shaped like a policy collection at all; it is a file-blob delivery endpoint for the client-side Purview SDK. This is the repo's own "vary the probe shape before calling it blocked" rule, missed.

**Retention policy bindings, listed in the same sentence, remain a genuine gap.** Only one of the pair falls. Do not delete the whole entry.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Remove "DLP policy enumeration" from the permanent-gap ledger in `docs/graph-api-gotchas.md`; leave "retention policy bindings"
- [ ] Correct `docs/data-plane-registration.md` → "What this does not fix" → the line *"DLP policy enumeration — the Purview APIs evaluate content against policy; they never enumerate policy."* That generalisation was true of the Purview Ecosystem roles #99 enumerated and is false of Graph
- [ ] Narrow the Purview/labels entry: `security/labels` blocking is **per-collection**, not per-root. On `RecordsManagement.Read.All`, `authorities` (3 rows), `categories` (13), `citations` (5), `filePlanReferences` (0) all return 200; only `retentionLabels` and `departments` 500 with `DataInsightsRequestError`
- [ ] Record the collector candidate as a follow-up issue (do not build here)

## Note for whoever writes the doc entry

Record the four distinct app-only refusal signatures observed on this surface in one session, because they mean different things and were being conflated:

| signature | meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `500 DataInsightsRequestError` / "FAILED - Forbidden" | Purview DataInsights backend refuses app-only for that collection. No scope or shape moves it |
| `403 InsufficientGraphPermissions` (JSON) | Graph gateway; normally grantable — but check the app role actually exists first |
| `403` HTML from `Microsoft-Azure-Application-Gateway/v2` | not a Graph error; the delegated-only signature. A JSON-only client fails to decode it |
| `401 ServiceFabricGraphAuthenticationMiddleware.ValidateToken` | data-plane registration missing (#102) — can appear on a sub-resource of a case whose parent is served fine |

And two that are **not** refusals: `500 HostNotFound` and `404 TenantDeploymentNotFound` mean the backend service is not provisioned for the tenant. Do not record those as gaps.

body:
## What

`otelEmitter.GaugeSnapshot` stores its observable state in `e.observables[name]`, keyed by **metric name alone**, and replaces `og.points` wholesale on every call:

```go
og, ok := e.observables[name]      // internal/telemetry/emitter.go:147
...
og.points = resolved               // full replace, internal/telemetry/emitter.go:173
```

There is exactly **one** `otelEmitter` for the process — `cmd/graph2otel/tenants.go:100` takes `provider.Emitter()` once and `telemetry.WithTenant` wraps that same instance per tenant (`tenants.go:291`). `WithTenant` stamps `tenant_id` onto the points but does nothing to the instrument key.

So with two configured tenants, both call `GaugeSnapshot("intune.devices.count", ...)` against the same `observableGauge`, and **the second call erases the first tenant's series**. Whichever tenant polls last wins until the other polls again. This applies to all **321** `GaugeSnapshot` call sites, which is the majority of the metric surface.

## Why it has never shown

m7kni is a single-tenant deploy. With one tenant the replace is correct — it is exactly the "a series absent from a later snapshot drops out" behaviour the `GaugeSnapshot` doc comment describes and which #104 wanted.

## Why it matters

`README.md` and `CLAUDE.md` advertise multi-tenant from day one, and #143 went to real trouble to make `tenant_id` a metric label so two tenants' domain metrics stop being the same series. This defeats that for every observable gauge: the label is correct on the points that survive, but most points do not survive.

The failure is silent and looks like flapping data, not like a bug.

## Fix sketch

Key the observable state by (metric name, tenant) rather than name alone, and have the registered callback range every tenant's point set for that instrument. The instrument itself must still be registered exactly once per name — registering `Float64ObservableGauge` twice for one name is its own problem — so the split belongs *inside* `observableGauge`: one instrument, a `map[tenant][]obsPoint`, and a callback that ranges all of them.

The tenant has to reach the emitter for that. `WithTenant` already knows it; the cleanest seam is for the tenant decorator to pass it through rather than for the base emitter to re-read `tenant_id` out of every point's attrs.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Failing test first: two `WithTenant`-wrapped emitters over one provider, both snapshotting the same metric; both tenants' series present after collection
- [ ] Instrument still registered once per metric name
- [ ] Single-tenant behaviour byte-identical — a series dropped from a later snapshot still drops out of the export
- [ ] Empty tenant (`WithTenant` passthrough) still works
- [ ] `make check` green

Found while reading the emitter for #235, whose limiter has to key its per-metric state the same way. Refs #235, #143, #104

body:
## What & why

graph2otel currently bounds metric cardinality in **three unrelated ways**, two of which are hand-maintained and one of which is arbitrary:

1. **Per-collector allow-lists.** `intune.detected_apps` and `intune.uxa.app_crash_count` each carry a fixed `defaultAllowedApps` list (outlook/excel/winword/…). Anything unlisted is **dropped entirely** — which on m7kni today means 100% of the app-health data is discarded, because the one live row is `LogonUI.exe`. Every such list is a maintenance burden and a guess about what matters.
2. **The SDK cardinality limit.** `cardinality.metric_limit` (default 2000) sets the OTEL SDK's per-instrument cap; excess attribute sets collapse into `otel.metric.overflow`. This is **arrival-ordered, not significance-ordered** — the series that survive are whichever showed up first, which is effectively random. `graph2otel.series.active/.limit/.overflowing` report where each metric sits.
3. **One hand-rolled meaningful bucket.** `internal/collectors/entra/graphactivity/endpoints.go` already buckets to "a MEANINGFUL bucket rather than the opaque overflow series" — the pattern this epic generalises.

**The goal:** one central, automatic, per-metric cardinality policy applied at the emitter boundary, so no collector maintains an allow-list and no significant series is lost to arrival order. Keep the top N series per metric ranked by significance; fold the remainder into an explicit `other` bucket. Self-hosted Prometheus/Mimir users who do not care about active-series cost set the limit to `0` and get everything.

**Proposed config** (names to be confirmed):
- `cardinality.per_metric_limit` — default **5000**, `0` = unlimited.
- `cardinality.global_limit` — default **100000**, `0` = unlimited.
- The existing `cardinality.metric_limit` (SDK-level, default 2000) needs reconciling with these — three overlapping caps would be worse than one. Likely outcome: this mechanism replaces it as the primary control and the SDK limit stays as a dumb backstop set above it.

## The design forks — these need answering before implementation

None of these is a blocker on the idea; all of them change the code.

### 1. What does "most popular" mean? (the load-bearing one)

The proposal is to "sort by how many series have each label". For a `GaugeSnapshot` every series is emitted **exactly once per cycle**, so occurrence-frequency is uniform and ranks nothing. The ranking has to come from somewhere real. Candidates:

- **By the metric's own value** — top 5000 apps by crash count, top 5000 policies by device count. Meaningful for count-shaped metrics, and probably the right default.
- **By persistence** — how many consecutive cycles the series has appeared. Favours stable series over one-offs.
- **Hybrid** — value, tie-broken by persistence.

### 2. "Fold into other" is only valid for ADDITIVE metrics

Summing the tail is correct for counts (crashes, devices, elevations). It is **meaningless or wrong** for a score, ratio, or percentage gauge — `intune.uxa.app_health.os_version_score` folded into an `other` bucket would emit an invented number. The emitter must know each instrument's aggregation semantics and either sum the tail (additive), or drop it while emitting a **count of dropped series** (non-additive). Emitting a fabricated aggregate would be a worse failure than the current drop.

### 3. Cumulative counters cannot be folded retroactively

A counter series that has been reported independently and later migrates into `other` breaks monotonicity — `other` jumps by the counter's accumulated value and the original series goes stale. Either fold from first observation only, or scope v1 to `GaugeSnapshot` and handle counters separately.

### 4. Flapping / hysteresis

If top-N membership changes each cycle, series appear and disappear repeatedly — staleness in Prometheus, broken `rate()`, and a noisy graph. Needs hysteresis: evict only after K consecutive cycles outside the top N, and admit only after K inside.

### 5. Global cap arbitration

A per-metric cap is local and easy. A global cap needs to decide **which metric gives up series** when the total is exceeded — proportional shrink, worst-offender-first, or a per-metric weight. Needs a deterministic, documented rule, or the global cap becomes unpredictable.

### 6. Observability of the clipping itself

Clipping is data loss and must not be silent. Extend the existing `graph2otel.series.*` self-obs with per-metric folded-series counts, in the spirit of `graph2otel.api.unexpected` (#234): a bounded counter saying *that* it happened, with the detail elsewhere.

## What this explicitly does NOT change

**This is not a licence to put per-entity identity into metric labels.** With a 5000 cap and a 50k-user tenant, labelling a metric by UPN yields an arbitrary 5000 series plus a meaningless `other` bucket, at real cost, when the log twin already answers "which one" better and for free. The rule from #112/#114 stands unchanged: **metrics carry bounded aggregates, logs carry entities, and "not a metric label" still means LOG TWIN, never dropped.**

This mechanism is for dimensions that are *moderately* unbounded and genuinely aggregate-shaped — application names, OS versions, policy names, endpoints — where the tail is long but the head is meaningful. The epic should encode that as written policy, not just a knob, or it will be read as permission to label by device id.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Design forks 1–6 decided and recorded on this issue before implementation
- [ ] Central per-metric limiter at the `internal/telemetry` emitter boundary (the only thing touching OTLP), so no collector implements its own
- [ ] `cardinality.per_metric_limit` (default 5000, 0 = unlimited) + `cardinality.global_limit` (default 100000, 0 = unlimited), registered in the config drift gate so `docs/env-vars.md` regenerates
- [ ] Relationship to the existing `cardinality.metric_limit` resolved and documented
- [ ] Non-additive instruments never receive a fabricated `other` aggregate
- [ ] Hysteresis so top-N membership does not flap cycle to cycle
- [ ] Per-metric folded-series counts in the `graph2otel.series.*` self-obs surface
- [ ] `intune.detected_apps` and `intune.uxa.app_crash_count` allow-lists **removed** and their collectors relying on the central limiter — the proof the mechanism works
- [ ] `docs/signals.md` + `docs/collectors.md` updated; `make check` green

Refs #112, #114, #194, #234, #82

comments.body:
## Fork decisions — decided, implementation starting

Evidence gathered first, so these are not guesses.

| fact | evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Instrument mix across collectors: **321 `GaugeSnapshot`**, 93 `Gauge`, 23 `Counter`, 16 `Histogram`, 1 `UpDownCounter` | grep over `internal/collectors` |
| Live max per-metric series on m7kni is **175** (`intune.compliance.setting.devices`). Nothing is remotely near the 2000 SDK cap. | `topk(25, max_over_time(graph2otel_series_active[24h]))`, `live-measured 2026-07-23, #235` |
| The metrics that already hand-roll a bound are **exactly** the ones with a genuinely unbounded key: `intune.detected_apps.device_count`, `intune.uxa.app_crash_count` (both GaugeSnapshot + allow-list), `entra.graph_activity.endpoint_requests` (Counter + sticky `other` at 200 paths) | source read |
| `sdkmetric.WithCardinalityLimit(0)` **fully disables** the SDK cap | `go doc`. The comment in `provider.go:91-97` claiming "the SDK's own default of 2000 still applies" is **wrong** and gets fixed. |
| `telemetrytest.MetricPoint` already carries `Unit` and `Kind` | `internal/telemetrytest` — `signalcapture` simply never read them |

### 1. "Most popular" = the metric's own value, descending

Occurrence-frequency ranks nothing for a `GaugeSnapshot` (every series is emitted exactly once per cycle), so the ranking comes from the value. Tie-break on the rendered attribute set lexicographically, so the outcome does not depend on Go map iteration order.

### 2. Additivity is decided by UNIT, not by instrument kind — and unclassified is a build failure

Kind is insufficient precisely where it matters: `intune.detected_apps.device_count` is a non-additive-by-kind observable gauge holding a very additive device count. The unit already in every emit call is the discriminator.

- **additive:** any `{annotation}` unit outside the deny-set, plus `By`/`Bi`; and Counter/UpDownCounter/Histogram whatever their unit
- **non-additive:** `1`, `%`, `s`, `min`, `h`, `d`, and the annotation deny-set `{score}` `{version}` `{ratio}` `{percent}`
- **unknown unit:** treated non-additive (fail safe) *and* fails the gate

Additive tail → summed into one `other` point. Non-additive tail → dropped, with the dropped count emitted. A fabricated aggregate is never emitted.

### 3. Sticky admission, so nothing is folded retroactively

For synchronous instruments a series, once admitted, stays admitted for the process lifetime, and a never-admitted series' adds go to `other` from its first observation. `other` is monotonic and no series ever migrates, so the monotonicity break this fork worried about cannot occur. This is not new — `graphactivity`'s `cappedPath` has done exactly this in production since #185.

### 4. Hysteresis is a band with one cycle of memory

Admit at rank < `limit`; evict only at rank >= `limit + band`, band = 10% of limit (min 1). Needed only for `GaugeSnapshot`, whose membership is recomputed per cycle. State is one previously-admitted set per (metric, tenant).

### 5. Global cap arbitrates by max-min fairness (water-filling)

Metrics under their fair share (`global_limit / metric_count`) keep everything; the surplus redistributes among over-share metrics, repeating until stable. Computed once per export cycle from the previous cycle's counts, so the hot path reads a precomputed effective limit. That means a one-cycle lag on a sudden burst — correct and documented; a synchronous global count would need a lock across every metric on every data point.

### 6. Clipping is loud

`graph2otel.series.clipped{metric_name, mode}` where mode is `folded`/`dropped`, plus `graph2otel.series.total`. `graph2otel.series.limit` is reused; `graph2otel.series.overflowing` is **repurposed** to "this metric is clipping", since the SDK overflow it currently means will no longer exist. A WARN on the transition *into* clipping for a metric and an INFO on the transition out — not once per cycle.

### 7. NEW FORK the issue missed: which attribute becomes `other`?

Folding `{app_name, platform}` by setting both to `other` would destroy the bounded `platform` breakdown. So the limiter picks a **clip key** — the attribute with the most distinct values for that metric — and groups the tail by the remaining attributes with only the clip key set to `other`. The choice is **sticky per metric** (decided on first clip, retained) so it cannot churn cycle to cycle. If the fold still yields more than `limit/10` groups, the next-highest-cardinality key is also folded, repeating until bounded.

This is the mechanism `graphactivity` hand-codes today: it sets only `normalized_path` to `other` and keeps `request_method` and `response_status_class` intact.

### 8. Self-observability is never clipped

`graph2otel.*` is bounded by collector count and tenant count by construction, and silently dropping our own health signals under load is the worst available failure mode. Self-obs series still **count toward** the reported global total; they are just never candidates for clipping.

### 9. Config: rename, do not redefine

`cardinality.metric_limit` is removed, replaced by:

- `cardinality.per_metric_limit` — default **5000**, `0` = unlimited
- `cardinality.global_limit` — default **100000**, `0` = unlimited

A rename rather than a redefinition because the semantics change fundamentally — arrival-ordered SDK drop becomes significance-ranked fold. An operator who set the old key to 50000 to neuter it should be told, not silently re-pointed. Setting the old key is a fail-fast config error naming the replacement. The SDK cap is disabled outright per maintainer decision: our limiter supersedes it for both per-series and total cardinality.

## Build order — four commits, green between each

1. **signalcapture records Unit + Kind.** Mechanical; regenerates all ~110 goldens once. Also closes the metric-catalogue gap #218 needs.
2. **Additivity classification + tree-walking gate** over every golden, so a new unit fails CI until classified. Sits alongside `TestEveryCollectorPackageEnforcesCardinality`.
3. **The limiter itself** — `internal/telemetry/limit.go`, applied innermost (inside the Provider, wrapping `otelEmitter`) so it sees tenant/transport-stamped attrs. Plus config, provider wiring, self-obs.
4. **Retire the allow-lists** — `detectedapps` and `endpointanalytics` — which is the proof the mechanism works. `signalcapture.perEntityKeys`' long comment excluding `app_name` rests on those allow-lists existing and must be rewritten.

## Adjacent bug found while reading the emitter — filed as #236

`otelEmitter.GaugeSnapshot` keys `e.observables[name]` by metric name only, so with two configured tenants one tenant's snapshot erases the other's. Not caused by this work and not fixed by it, but it decides how the limiter keys its state (per metric AND tenant), so it is on the critical path for design correctness.

## Shipped — `aedd01b`, `1e03ff3`, `86c2cf7`, `40d9e43`

All six forks decided (plus a seventh the issue had not surfaced), implemented, and `make check` green at each commit. The OTEL SDK's per-instrument cap is disabled outright per maintainer decision — graph2otel's limiter is now the only thing bounding series count, on both axes.

### What landed

| commit | what |
| --- | --- |
| `aedd01b` | `signalcapture` records each metric's unit + aggregation kind; all 74 goldens regenerate once. Also closes the metric-catalogue gap #218 needs. |
| `1e03ff3` | `internal/semconv/additive.go` + two tree-walking gates over every golden |
| `86c2cf7` | the limiter itself, config, provider wiring, self-obs |
| `40d9e43` | both allow-lists retired — the proof |

### Deviations from the plan in the comment above, and why

**`graph2otel.series.overflowing` is RETIRED, not repurposed.** The plan said repurpose it to "this metric is clipping". It reported the SDK overflow, which no longer exists, and repointing the name at the nearest surviving condition would have made a live dashboard signal quietly mean something else. `graph2otel.series.clipped{metric.name, mode=folded|dropped}` replaces it with strictly more information, and the dashboard panel moved with it.

**The tracker's memory guard is now separate from the reported limit.** They used to be one number, correctly: the SDK dropped everything past the limit, so the true distinct count WAS the limit. The limiter emits up to `limit + band + other`, and the tracker sits INSIDE it — so a guard pinned at the limit would have under-reported by exactly the amount that only appears once a metric goes over, which is the one moment anyone reads it. `NewCardinalityTrackerForLimit` splits them.

**`PerMetric` bounds the ADMITTED series; `other` is emitted in addition.** Making the limit an exact ceiling on emitted series would require shrinking the ranked set by however many fold groups it produced — a second pass — or collapsing the fold to exactly one series, which destroys the bounded breakdown that fork 7 exists to preserve. Documented honest ceiling: `limit + band(10%) + foldGroups`.

**An intra-package unit-conflict check was dropped as unbuildable.** The emitter caches each instrument by name on first use, so a second call site's unit never reaches the Recorder — the check would have been structurally incapable of firing, which is #139/#100's shape exactly (a gate reporting coverage it does not have). Cross-package conflicts ARE visible, since the goldens are separate files, and `TestNoMetricNameIsEmittedWithTwoShapes` covers that.

### Both new gates were verified to FIRE, not just to pass

Dropping `By` from the additivity table flags 4 metrics; a planted duplicate metric name flags the shape conflict. Both pass again on revert.

### Retiring the allow-lists surfaced one real behaviour they were providing incidentally

They canonicalized to their own casing, which folded Intune's casing variants of one application together. Removing them naively doubled the series for `Google Chrome` / `google chrome`. Bucketing is now keyed on the lowercased name with the emitted label taken from the first spelling in **catalog** order — not map order, which would flip the label between runs and churn series for nothing.

### Config migration

`cardinality.metric_limit` is **removed**. `per_metric_limit` (5000) and `global_limit` (100000) replace it, 0 = unlimited on either. Setting the old key now **refuses to start** and names the replacement: koanf silently ignores unknown keys, and this is not a pure rename — the old key drove an arrival-ordered SDK cap that no longer exists, so an operator who had set it to 50000 to neuter it would have silently inherited the new mechanism at its default.

### Acceptance criteria

- [x] Design forks 1–6 decided and recorded before implementation (plus fork 7: which attribute becomes `other`)
- [x] Central limiter at the `internal/telemetry` emitter boundary, applied innermost so tenant/transport stamps are already on
- [x] `per_metric_limit` + `global_limit`, registered in the config drift gate
- [x] Relationship to `cardinality.metric_limit` resolved — removed, with a fail-fast migration error
- [x] Non-additive instruments never receive a fabricated `other` aggregate
- [x] Hysteresis so top-N membership does not flap
- [x] Per-metric clip counts in `graph2otel.series.*`
- [x] Both allow-lists removed
- [x] `docs/signals.md` + `docs/collectors.md` + CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md updated; `make check` green

### Not verified yet

Everything above is unit-verified. It has not run against the live tenant — nothing on m7kni is near a 5000 limit (largest metric: 175 series), so the clipping paths will not exercise themselves in production. Worth a deliberate low-limit soak on camden before treating the fold as live-proven.

Also filed while reading the emitter: **#236** — `GaugeSnapshot` keys its observable state by metric name alone, so with two configured tenants one tenant's snapshot erases the other's, across all 321 call sites. Single-tenant deploys are unaffected, which is why it has never shown.

body:
## Why

Almost every load-bearing fact on this project's path was established by **measuring a live tenant**, because Microsoft's documentation was wrong about it (CLAUDE.md, "wire over docs"). A measurement is true of one tenant at one moment. When Microsoft adds an enum member, renames a field, or changes what a filter does, the change is **silent**: the API keeps answering HTTP 200 and the collector keeps emitting numbers that are quietly wrong.

`internal/wirecheck` (`f08f994`, #233) is the mechanism that breaks that silence — a bounded counter `graph2otel.api.unexpected{collector,field,kind}` plus a once-per-process WARN carrying the offending value. It is currently wired into **`defender.quarantine` only**.

This issue is the sweep.

## The specific problem this fixes

**38 collectors bucket an unrecognized value to the literal string `"unknown"`.** A new Microsoft enum member therefore disappears into a bucket nobody inspects, and where the field is a **metric label** it silently changes series membership — the count moves and nothing says why.

`m365.service_health` already does the right thing the hard way: it maps an unmapped status to `-1` specifically so it is visible rather than silently counted as healthy (#119). That per-field sentinel is what `wirecheck` generalizes.

## Scope

For each collector below: identify the fields whose value set is **assumed**, declare the known set as a `wirecheck.Enum`, and report deviations. Priority order, because not all bucketing is equal:

1. **Fields used as METRIC LABELS** — an unmapped value creates or moves a series, so the number itself becomes wrong. Highest value, do these first.
2. **Fields carrying a documented invariant** — a server-side filter, a parseable composite id, a guaranteed-present key. These are the assumptions most likely to have been measured exactly once.
3. **Log-only attributes** — lowest value; an odd string in a log is visible to anyone querying it, so the watchdog adds least here. Consider skipping rather than adding noise.

### Collectors with `"unknown"` bucketing or an `orUnknown` helper

<details><summary>38 files</summary>

```
entra/credentialexpiry  entra/deleteditems      entra/domains
entra/mfaregistration   entra/organization      entra/recommendations
entra/risk              entra/riskyagents       entra/roles
entra/securescore       entra/signinactivity
intune/appinstallreport intune/appletokens      intune/autopilot
intune/autopilotevents  intune/certificates     intune/certinventoryreport
intune/compliance       intune/configprofiles   intune/connectors
intune/detectedapps     intune/deviceencryption intune/endpointanalytics
intune/enrollment       intune/gpoanalytics     intune/hardwareinventory
intune/malware          intune/manageddevices   intune/mobileapps
intune/noncompliantsettings                     intune/remediationrunstates
intune/scripts          intune/settingscatalog
m365/sharepointsettings m365/storage
purview/ediscoverycases purview/retentionlabels purview/sensitivitylabels
```

</details>

Also in scope, and arguably ahead of the log-only work: the collectors landed in this session that carry fresh single-measurement assumptions — `defender.email_post_delivery` (`ActionType` / `ActionTrigger` / `ActionResult` value sets, none of them enumerated from anything but one live record) and `m365.unified_audit`'s quarantine additions (the undocumented `RequestType` integer enum).

## Deliberately NOT in scope

- **Turning findings into errors.** An unexpected value must never drop a record — that converts a cosmetic surprise into a hole in the data. `wirecheck` is report-only by design.
- **Whole-payload schema diffing.** `wirecheck` reports assumptions a collector chose to declare, which is what keeps the signal worth reading. A generic unknown-field differ over every Microsoft response would emit constantly and be ignored within a week.
- **Removing the `"unknown"` buckets.** The bucket is often correct behaviour — a value genuinely absent on the wire has to go somewhere. The bug is that it is *indistinguishable* from a value we failed to anticipate. Report first; only then consider whether the bucket should split.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A rule recorded in `CLAUDE.md` (or `docs/signals.md`): a new collector that assumes a value set declares it to `wirecheck`, and the reason it is an assumption
- [ ] Every metric-label field whose value set is assumed is declared and watched (priority 1 above)
- [ ] Every documented invariant taken from a single measurement is declared and watched (priority 2)
- [ ] `defender.email_post_delivery` and `m365.unified_audit`'s quarantine fields covered
- [ ] A decision recorded on whether log-only attributes are in or out, with the reasoning — not left ambiguous
- [ ] `docs/signals.md`'s `graph2otel.api.unexpected` section updated to drop "currently wired into `defender.quarantine` only"
- [ ] An alert rule proposed for `increase(graph2otel_api_unexpected_total[1h]) > 0` (see `alerts/README.md`), or an explicit note that it is dashboard-only
- [ ] `make check` green

## Note on sequencing

This is deliberately incremental — it does not need doing in one pass, and doing all 38 at once would be a large diff of low-confidence guesses about value sets. A collector's enum should be declared from **evidence** (a live sample, or an API error body that enumerates the members, which is how `defender.quarantine`'s eleven `QuarantineTypes` were obtained), not from documentation. Where neither exists, prefer leaving the field unwatched over declaring a guessed set — a watchdog that fires on correct data is worse than none.

**14 enum declarations across 9 collectors**, every one a metric-label field. `make check` green on `main` (vet, race tests, golangci-lint 0 issues, govulncheck, tidy, build). Built by a worktree-isolated subagent; diff reviewed and the gate re-run on `main` by the coordinating thread rather than taken from the brief.

**The pattern worth keeping:** where the collector already keys on a bucket map, the `Enum` is **derived from that map's keys** rather than restated. Eleven collectors bucket to `"unknown"` but their legitimate value set **cannot be established from anything in the repo** — only from Microsoft's documentation. Per this issue's own rule (*"a watchdog that fires on correct data is worse than none"*), they stay unwatched:

Most share one shape: an `orUnknown` helper passes the raw value straight through with **no bucket map at all**, so there is nothing to derive a set from and no fixture variety to infer one.

- **`m365.sharepoint_settings` is the highest-value gap.** Exactly one value of each field exists anywhere in the repo. One live probe of `/admin/sharepoint/settings` closes it.
- **`entra.risk` passes `riskLevel`/`riskState` RAW to `GaugeSnapshot`** — no bucketing whatsoever. `riskState`'s set is nowhere in the repo (fixtures show only `atRisk`, `confirmedCompromised`, `remediated`). Declaring `riskLevel` alone would half-cover a pair that is always queried together, so both wait for a pass that can establish both.

**`intune.devices`' `operating_system` is excluded on different grounds** and should not be revisited: it is free text with no Graph-side enum, so no set exists to declare. Recorded in the source so nobody adds it later.

## Two defects found while reading, filed rather than folded in

- **#261** — `intune.devices`' blob path lowercases `CompliantState` while `complianceBuckets` is camelCase, so `InGracePeriod` and `ConfigManager` both land in `"other"` on blob and in `in_grace_period` / `config_manager` on Graph. Verified empirically against the real functions. A live blob record carrying the failing value is already in the repo at `blob_test.go:140` with **no assertion on `compliance_state`**, which is exactly why the suite is green over it.

The new counter now distinguishes them, which is the prerequisite for the bucket split this issue anticipates.

## Two observations for the remaining acceptance criteria

- **`intune.malware`'s `status` is not actually bounded.** It emits `unknown_<flag>`, creating one series per unrecognized flag name Microsoft invents. Self-naming is deliberate (#150), but the label set is unbounded in principle, contrary to the bounded-metric rule. #235's central limiter backstops it, so this is a note rather than a defect.
- **Two collectors already had an ad-hoc per-row `logger.Warn` for this exact purpose** (`intune.app_install_status`, `intune.cert_inventory`). Both left in place: `cert_inventory`'s is pinned by a test, and both carry per-row context (`issuer_name`, `Platform_loc`) that the bounded counter deliberately must not. If the resulting two-lines-per-surprise reads as noise, the ad-hoc Warn is the one to drop.

## Next, and the sharpest remaining candidate

**`entra.conditional_access`'s `namedLocationType`** is priority 1 and worse than anything declared above: when `@odata.type` is neither `ipNamedLocation` nor `countryNamedLocation` it **skips the location entirely**, so a new subtype does not move a series — it *silently reduces the count*. The evidence exists (two constants the collector defines). It needs `namedLocationPoints`' signature widened to take the reporter and emitter, which is why this pass stopped short of it.

Remaining on this issue: that one, priority 2 (documented invariants from a single measurement), the `defender.email_post_delivery` / `m365.unified_audit` fields named in the body, the `CLAUDE.md` rule, the `docs/signals.md` correction, and the alert-rule decision. Note the body's *"currently wired into `defender.quarantine` only"* was already stale before this commit — `m365.message_trace` declares enums too (`0f9b5da`).

## Progress — 7 of 8 acceptance criteria done; criterion (b) advanced to 20 watched collectors (2026-07-25)

Audited the whole issue against live code (the earlier "sharpest remaining candidate" note was stale — `entra.conditional_access`'s `namedLocationType` had already landed in `3d129cb`). Current state:

| criterion | status | evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| (a) rule in CLAUDE.md/signals.md | DONE | `CLAUDE.md` wirecheck paragraph; `docs/signals.md` "The rule for a new collector" |
| (b) every metric-label field watched | **ADVANCED, not complete** | see below |

| (g) alert rule or dashboard-only note | DONE | `docs/signals.md` records it as dashboard/log territory, not paging |
| make check | DONE | green at every commit |

### Criterion (b) — landed this session

- **`67f7fb9`** — the two raw-passthrough pairs #234 had left unwatched because a single live read shows one value each: `entra.risk` (`riskLevel`/`riskState`) and `m365.sharepoint_settings` (`sharingCapability`/`sharingDomainRestrictionMode`). Resolved by **generating the value range on the live tenant** (maintainer-approved) and declaring each `wirecheck.Enum` from the Graph v1.0 CSDL `$metadata` (the API's own schema), cross-checked against those live values. All four `sharingCapability` members were observed by cycling the tenant setting through them and restoring; `unknownFutureValue` excluded from every set so its appearance fires the watchdog. Grants used: `SharePointTenantSettings.ReadWrite.All` (granted to the mgmt app, cycle run, **revoked** — 404 confirmed) and the pre-existing `IdentityRiskyUser.ReadWrite.All` (left in place, not mine to revoke). No poller write scope; poller stays read-only.
- **`f30e296`** — four collectors that already keyed a metric label on a bucket map but never reported: `intune.gpo_analytics` (`readiness`, `ingestion_type`), `intune.config_profiles` (`odata_type`), `intune.enrollment` (`config_type`), `intune.noncompliant_settings` (`setting_status`, ad-hoc Warn replaced by the counter). Each `Enum` derived from the map, never restated.
- **`f1bc0db`** — `entra.risky_agents`, reusing `entra.risk`'s exported `KnownRiskLevels`/`KnownRiskStates` (the identical Identity Protection enums) so the two cannot drift.

`docs/signals.md` now lists **20 collectors** declaring watched value sets.

Five collectors still pass a metric-label value raw with no watched set, listed in `docs/signals.md` as recorded gaps: `entra.recommendations` (`status`/`priority`/`recommendationType`), `intune.device_encryption` (`EncryptionState` et al.), `intune.mobile_apps` (`appType`/`publishingState`), `intune.remediation_run_states` (`DetectionState`/`RemediationState`), and `intune.hardware_inventory`'s DeviceGuard states (`Manufacturer`/`TPMSpecificationVersion` are free text — no set to declare). Closing (b) means declaring those from the beta `$metadata` (or documenting any that are genuinely free-text). Per this issue's own "incremental" note, they are the last pass.

## Closed — criterion (b) complete (`c703629`)

The final five metric-label collectors now declare a `wirecheck.Enum` from the Graph beta CSDL `$metadata` (fetched live as `graph2otel-poller`, read-only, 2026-07-25), or document their field as enum-less where no bounded set exists:

title: Extend wirecheck across the collectors: stop silently bucketing unrecognized Microsoft values

body:
graph2otel today exposes **no quarantine signal at all**: no metric, no audit history, nothing for Teams or files. The only incidental coverage is `defender.email`'s `delivery_location` log attribute (blob `EmailEvents`), which answers "how many *arrived* in quarantine" via LogQL and nothing else — no release tracking, no expiry, no admin action trail.

This issue covers the whole quarantine surface. **Everything below was live-measured against m7kni as `graph2otel-poller` on 2026-07-23** — no claim here comes from Microsoft's documentation.

## Live baseline (m7kni, 2026-07-23)

`POST /v1.0/security/runHuntingQuery`, `EmailEvents | where Timestamp > ago(30d) | summarize n=count() by DeliveryLocation, DeliveryAction`:

| DeliveryLocation | DeliveryAction | n |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Inbox/folder | Delivered | 109 |
| On-premises/external | Delivered | 15 |
| Failed | Blocked | 13 |
| Dropped | Blocked | 10 |
| **Quarantine** | **Blocked** | **2** |

Both quarantined messages were subsequently released (system release, see the audit record below). A small tenant — the mapping work must not be validated on volume alone (CLAUDE.md: a green tick is not evidence of data).

## What is reachable, and what it costs

### 1. `EmailPostDeliveryEvents` — exported, ingested by nothing `[live-measured 2026-07-23]`

`insights-logs-advancedhunting-emailpostdeliveryevents` **exists in the storage account and holds live records**. It was simply never in #106's table list — not a rejection, an omission. The envelope is byte-identical in shape to every other Defender table (`properties` + `Timestamp` event-time binding), so `internal/collectors/defender` plumbing applies unchanged.

Full wire field set observed (13 columns, all strings, no `InitiatingProcess`, no device block):

```
Timestamp NetworkMessageId InternetMessageId Action ActionType ActionTrigger
ActionResult RecipientEmailAddress DeliveryLocation ThreatTypes DetectionMethods
ReportId SenderFromAddress EmailDirection
```

`SourceLocation` is in the hunting schema but was **not on the wire** — map against the live sample, not the schema (#142 precedent: `"platform": "windows"` was never on the wire).

Live sample:

```json
{"time":"2026-07-22T10:44:33.4250955Z","category":"AdvancedHunting-EmailPostDeliveryEvents",
 "properties":{"Timestamp":"2026-07-22T10:43:05Z","NetworkMessageId":"80aa9dda-...","Action":"Reprocessed",
 "ActionType":"Redelivery","ActionTrigger":"SpecialAction","ActionResult":"Success",
 "RecipientEmailAddress":"rob@m7kni.io","DeliveryLocation":"Inbox","ReportId":"80aa9dda-...","EmailDirection":null}}
```

`ReportId` is a composite string, as on `EmailEvents` — a `StrField`, not a `NumField`. Joins to `defender.email` on `network_message_id`.

**Cost: one mapper + one golden. No tenant change, no new scope, no new engine.**

### 2. Quarantine audit record types — the API is already running `[live-measured 2026-07-23]`

`POST /beta/security/auditLog/queries` **accepted all four** quarantine record-type filters (HTTP 201, echoed back PascalCase):

| filter string | RecordType | covers |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `quarantine` | 65 | release / preview / export / delete, email |
| `quarantineMetadata` | 201 | quarantine item metadata |
| `teamsQuarantineMetadata` | 204 | **Teams message quarantine** |
| `updateQuarantineMetadata` | 225 | metadata updates |

The query **succeeded** and returned a real record:

```json
{"auditLogRecordType":"Quarantine","operation":"QuarantineReleaseMessage","service":"Quarantine",
 "userType":"System","userPrincipalName":"System release","createdDateTime":"2026-07-22T10:43:06Z",
 "auditData":{"@odata.type":"#microsoft.graph.security.defaultAuditData","RecordType":65,
  "Workload":"Quarantine","ResultStatus":"Successful","NetworkMessageId":"80aa9dda-c565-45a0-6133-08dee7cf4a7a",
  "ReleaseTo":"rob@m7kni.io","RequestType":2}}
```

Two things this proves:

- `NetworkMessageId` is on the audit record, so the audit trail **joins directly to `defender.email` and `defender.email_post_delivery`** on `network_message_id`. One quarantine story across three transports.
- `auditData` deserializes as `defaultAuditData`, **not** the `quarantineAuditRecord` subtype the beta `$metadata` declares. It is an OpenType so every field is present, but a mapper must not key off `@odata.type`.

`m365.unified_audit` already runs exactly this API with `AuditLogsQuery.Read.All` (already granted). Its `recordTypeFilters` is a deliberately curated include-list (`internal/collectors/m365/unifiedaudit/unifiedaudit.go:102`) — these four just need adding to it.

**Cost: four strings in an include-list + a mapper branch. No new scope.**

### 3. `security/collaboration/analyzedEmails` — the release-aware per-message view `[live-measured 2026-07-23]`

`GET /beta/security/collaboration/analyzedEmails` returns **HTTP 200 as the poller** — `SecurityAnalyzedMessage.Read.All` is already in the token (44 roles). This is the Threat Explorer surface and it is the only Graph endpoint that distinguishes *still held* from *released*:

```
originalDelivery.location: {inbox_folder: 12, quarantine: 2, onprem_external: 1}
latestDelivery.location:   {inbox_folder: 14,               onprem_external: 1}
```

Both quarantined messages show `originalDelivery.location=quarantine`, `latestDelivery.location=inbox_folder` — released. That is the signal `EmailEvents` alone cannot give.

Per-message payload is rich: `threatTypes`, `detectionMethods`, `threatDetectionDetails`, `attachments[]` with `detonationDetails`, `urls[]`, `authenticationDetails`, `policy`/`policyAction`/`policyType`, `primaryOverrideSource`, `exchangeTransportRules[]`, `dlpRules[]`, `timelineEvents[]`, `directionality`, `spamConfidenceLevel`/`phishConfidenceLevel`/`bulkComplaintLevel`.

**Traps — record these in `docs/graph-api-gotchas.md`:**

- **`startDateTime` / `endDateTime` are accepted and silently ignored.** Windows of 1d, 7d, 30d and 31d all returned the *identical* 15 rows spanning ~20h (oldest `2026-07-22T11:25:54Z`, newest `2026-07-23T07:02:33Z`, `now` ≈ `08:05Z`). A caller trusting the window would believe it had 30 days of data.
- **`$filter` is rejected outright.** `loggedDateTime ge X` → `Invalid filter with operator`; `X and Y` on the same property → `Invalid filter with propNames = loggedDateTime, loggedDateTime`; any enum comparison on `latestDelivery/location` → `not a valid enumeration type constant` (the service mangles the qualified form). There is **no server-side quarantine filter** — the collector must fetch the window and filter client-side.
- **`$count` and `$orderby` are rejected** (`Query option 'Count' is not allowed`).
- `$top` works and produces `@odata.nextLink`; without `$top` the whole set arrives in one page.

Consequence: this is a **poller-with-dedupe** surface (dedupe on `networkMessageId` + `recipientEmailAddress`, which is exactly the `id` field's composition), never a backfill one. Rolling window ≈20h means a poll interval well under that, and a checkpoint that tolerates re-seeing everything.

**Cost: new `WindowCollector`-shaped collector. Experimental (genuine Graph beta, per #183). No new scope.**

### 4. Teams message quarantine

> **SUPERSEDED 2026-07-23** — the inference below ("the streaming export is not enabled for them") was ~~wrong~~. The tables are empty because `MessageEvents` only records **external** conversations plus **internal messages containing a URL**; Teams protection itself is on (`ZapEnabled: true`). See the correction comment.

~~`MessageEvents`, `MessagePostDeliveryEvents` and `MessageUrlInfo` are present in the tenant's advanced-hunting schema (`GET /beta/security/getHuntingSchema`, 51 tables) but have no container in the storage account — the streaming export is not enabled for them.~~ Container listing (37 containers, none matching `message*`) is accurate; the *explanation* was not — containers are created on first write, and no row has ever been produced.

Two independent routes to Teams quarantine, and they are complementary rather than alternatives:

- `teamsQuarantineMetadata` (204) via the audit query — **available right now**, no tenant change (item 2 above).
- The three `Message*` tables via blob — needs the export switched on in the Defender portal, then three mappers.

### 5. Queue depth — the one genuine architectural break `[live-measured 2026-07-23]`

The security console's Quarantine page has three tabs (Email, Teams messages, Files) and **all three are served by `Get-QuarantineMessage`, which has no Graph equivalent.** The beta `$metadata` has no quarantine entity set of any kind — the only quarantine types in it are `identityGovernance` (workflow quarantine), Intune Exchange-access states, and the audit record types above.

Measured, not assumed:

- The poller **can** acquire an `https://outlook.office365.com/.default` token (any app can).
- ~~`POST https://outlook.office365.com/adminapi/beta/{tid}/InvokeCommand` with `Get-QuarantineMessage` → **HTTP 401, empty body.**~~ **RESOLVED 2026-07-23** — `Exchange.ManageAsApp` + the **Security Reader** directory role were granted; the same call now returns **HTTP 200** and true queue depth is reachable. Measured progression 401 → 403 → 200. See the unblocked comment for the live record shape, the join key, and the `QuarantineTypes` enum traps.

So a true queue-depth gauge requires a fifth ingest transport with a **non-Graph auth path** and a **write-capable app role** (`Exchange.ManageAsApp` is not read-only) plus a directory-role assignment — a third documented scope break alongside Intune report-export and O365 `POST /subscriptions/start`.

**Everything reachable without that break is a *flow* view — arrivals and releases, not queue depth.** A gauge derived from `analyzedEmails` (`originalDelivery.location=quarantine AND latestDelivery.location=quarantine`) means "quarantined in the last ~20h and not yet released". That is a legitimate bounded aggregate and it is **not** queue depth; naming or documenting it as queue depth would be a lie.

## Telemetry model

Per #112/#114 — metrics carry bounded tenant-shaped aggregates, logs carry the entities, and "not a metric label" means **log twin, never dropped**:

- **Metrics** (bounded, cardinality independent of tenant size): counts by `delivery_location` × `delivery_action`, by `threat_type`, by `directionality`, by post-delivery `action_type` × `action_result`, by audit `operation`.
- **Logs**: one record per message / per post-delivery action / per audit record, carrying `network_message_id`, `internet_message_id`, recipient, sender, subject, threat detail. UPNs and subjects ship by design — the backend is a trusted sink.
- **`network_message_id` is the join key** across `defender.email`, `defender.email_post_delivery`, `m365.audit` and the analyzedEmails collector. It must be spelled identically everywhere.
- `ingest_transport` distinguishes the four paths (`blob` / `graph` / `audit_query`), stamped at the emitter boundary as always (#141).
- Namespace: `defender.*` for the blob tables (peer domain, on when blob ingest is configured, NOT `Experimental` per #183); the `analyzedEmails` collector is a genuine Graph beta surface so it **is** `Experimental`.

## Container inventory gaps found while probing

The 37-container listing also surfaced two exported-but-unread containers unrelated to quarantine, worth their own issue rather than scope creep here:

- `insights-logs-advancedhunting-behaviorentities`
- `insights-logs-advancedhunting-behaviorinfo`

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `defender.email_post_delivery` collector — mapper against the captured live sample, golden test, registered via `RegisterBlob`, `docs/collectors.md` regenerated
- [x] `m365.unified_audit` `recordTypeFilters` extended with the four quarantine record types; mapper handles `defaultAuditData` (not `quarantineAuditRecord`); `NetworkMessageId` / `ReleaseTo` / `RequestType` surfaced as attributes
- [x] ~~`analyzedEmails` collector~~ **DROPPED** — superseded by `defender.email_post_delivery`; its date params are silently ignored (~20h rolling window) so it cannot back a metric. See the 2026-07-23 design comment. Original scope: — client-side windowing, dedupe on `networkMessageId`+`recipientEmailAddress`, bounded gauges + per-message log twin, `Experimental()`
- [x] `docs/graph-api-gotchas.md`: the ignored-date-params trap, the `$filter`/`$count`/`$orderby` rejections, the 20h rolling window, the EXO 401, the `defaultAuditData` type mismatch — each with its evidence tag
- [x] `docs/signals.md`: the quarantine story across all transports, joined on `network_message_id`, with worked LogQL
- [x] Queue-depth position stated explicitly wherever a quarantine metric is documented: this is flow, not queue depth
- [ ] Live-verified against m7kni before close (a quarantined message synthesized if none arrives naturally — 2 in 30d is not a test corpus)
- [x] `make check` green

## Decisions needed

1. **Enable Defender streaming export for `MessageEvents` / `MessagePostDeliveryEvents` / `MessageUrlInfo`?** Tenant mutation. Default if unanswered: ship `teamsQuarantineMetadata` audit coverage only, and leave the blob tables as a follow-up.

## Design settled + EXO parameter surface measured 2026-07-23

Build started on the two self-contained lanes (below). Before dispatching them the EXO transport was probed properly, and the results change the shape of the quarantine work: the three signals split cleanly across three transports, and each one is now the *right* transport for what it carries rather than a compromise.

### The model: state / movement / history are three different questions

The earlier framing treated "quarantine coverage" as one collector to be built somewhere. It is three, and conflating them is what made the metric contract look impossible:

| question | signal | transport | shape |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **State** — how many messages are held *right now* | `defender.quarantine` | EXO `Get-QuarantineMessage` | bounded gauges + per-held-message log twin |
| **Movement** — a message entering or leaving quarantine | `defender.email_post_delivery` | Defender blob (`EmailPostDeliveryEvents`) | log per action |
| **History** — held / released / deleted / previewed, and policy changes | `m365.unified_audit` | Purview audit query API | log per audit record |

All three key on `network_message_id`, so they join. That is the whole point: a single id threads the state gauge, the movement event, and the audit trail.

This also resolves the metric-contract problem noted earlier. True queue depth is a **gauge** and only EXO can produce it. Everything else about quarantine is an **event**, and events belong in logs where LogQL `count by` answers the aggregate for free — CLAUDE.md's cardinality rule, applied rather than worked around. No collector needs to invent a windowed pseudo-gauge.

### `analyzedEmails` is NOT being built — superseded

The Graph beta `security/collaboration/analyzedEmails` surface was the earlier candidate for the metric half. It is dropped, for three reasons that compound:

1. Its `startDateTime`/`endDateTime` parameters are **silently ignored** (`live-measured 2026-07-23`) — it returns a ~20h rolling window regardless, and rejects `$filter`, `$count` and `$orderby`. A gauge over an uncontrollable window is not a metric contract.
2. Its per-message content overlaps `defender.email` almost entirely, and its one distinctive field pair (`originalDelivery.location` vs `latestDelivery.location`) is exactly what `EmailPostDeliveryEvents` carries as a proper event with an action, a trigger and a result.
3. It is a beta Graph surface, so it would cost a `spec/graph-beta-surface.json` registration and the associated drift gate, to duplicate data already arriving over a stable transport.

Re-open only if Microsoft ships server-side filtering on it. `[docs-only + live-measured 2026-07-23]`

### EXO `Get-QuarantineMessage` parameter surface `[live-measured 2026-07-23, #233]`

Probed as `graph2otel-poller` over `POST https://outlook.office365.com/adminapi/beta/{tid}/InvokeCommand`. Every row below is a measurement, not a doc reading.

| probe | result | consequence for the collector |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ReleaseStatus=NOTRELEASED` | **0 rows** (vs 2 for `RELEASED`) | **This is the true queue-depth query.** Held-only, no client-side filtering needed |
| `StartReceivedDate=2030-01-01` | 0 rows | the date window **genuinely filters** server-side |
| `EndReceivedDate=2000-01-01` | 0 rows | ditto, both ends |
| `StartReceivedDate=2026-07-22T09:30Z` (messages at 08:58) | 0 rows | boundary respected to the minute |
| `StartReceivedDate=2026-07-01` | 2 rows | control — the filter is not just always-empty |
| `Page=2` | 0 rows | paging is `Page`/`PageSize`, 1-indexed |
| `PageSize=1001` | 200 | over-limit **accepted, not rejected**; ceiling unverifiable at n=2 |
| `PageSize=0` | **200, 0 rows** | a zero PageSize returns silence rather than erroring — must be guarded |
| `BogusParameter=1` | **400** `AmbiguousParameterSetException` | unknown parameter names fail loudly |
| `QuarantineTypes=Nonsense` | **400** | invalid enum *values* fail loudly |
| `QuarantineTypes=Spam` / `=Malware` | 2 / 0 rows | valid values filter correctly |
| `Direction=Inbound` / `=Outbound` | 2 / 0 rows | direction filters |
| `EntityType=Email` | **403** | still denied at Security Reader — see the open question below |

Contrast with `analyzedEmails` above: **this API rejects what it does not understand.** That is a materially better contract, and it is the strongest argument for EXO over the Graph beta surface.

**The prefix-match trap survives all of this and is the one to remember.** `QuarantineTypes=Nonsense` 400s, but `QuarantineTypes=File` returns **200 with 0 rows** — because PowerShell prefix-matched it onto `FileTypeBlock`. A wrong-but-prefix-valid enum value is therefore indistinguishable from "no matching messages" forever. Validate against the enum list, never against a 200. The authoritative list, from the 400 body: `Spam, TransportRule, Bulk, Phish, HighConfPhish, Malware, SPOMalware, DataLossPrevention, FileTypeBlock, AdminTriggered, PPI`.

### Full live record shape

One live record, complete (m7kni, 2026-07-23). `EntityType` is present in the **response** even though it cannot be used as a **filter** — and `TeamsConversationType` exists on the same record, which is how a Teams-quarantined item would surface if one existed:

`Identity` is `<NetworkMessageId>\<recipient-guid>` — split on `\` for the join key.

### `internal/exoclient` — the transport, deferred to its own pass on purpose

The EXO client is a sibling of `internal/o365activityclient`, not a fork of `internal/graphclient`, for the same reason that one is: same `azidentity` credential and the same `auth.TenantAuth` seam, different audience (`https://outlook.office365.com/.default`), different delivery model (a POSTed cmdlet envelope, not a paged GET), different failure vocabulary (the useful text is buried in `internalexception.message`; `error.message` is always the useless `"Invalid Operation"`).

It needs **no fifth registration path** — it is a plain `SnapshotCollector` taking a new `Deps.EXO` field, so `collectordoc.Rows`' signature is untouched and the #139/#100 coverage-gate hazard does not apply.

It is **deliberately not being built in parallel** with the two lanes below. It is predominantly a wiring change — `internal/collectors/registry.go` (`Deps`), `internal/config/config.go`, `cmd/graph2otel/tenants.go`, `config.example.yaml` — and the operating rule is that integration files get a dedicated pass, never concurrent lanes. ### In flight now

Teams **queue depth** still needs `-EntityType Teams` → 403 at Security Reader. Recommendation stands: cover Teams quarantine via the `teamsQuarantineMetadata` audit record type (read-only, no new privilege, shipping in the lane above) and do **not** escalate the service principal to a write-capable role (Quarantine Administrator / Security Administrator) for a queue-depth number on a surface that is admin-only by design. Default if unanswered: that.

## Landed 2026-07-23 — movement + history, `5bb442c`

Two of the three quarantine signals are in `main`. `make check` green over the merged whole (not per-lane), pushed.

### `defender.email_post_delivery`

New Defender advanced-hunting blob collector over `EmailPostDeliveryEvents` — ZAP, manual and automated remediation, redelivery. The only signal that shows a message **moving** into or out of quarantine, joined to `defender.email` on `network_message_id`.

- 13 columns, all strings — the table carries no numeric or boolean columns, and its `ReportId` is a composite string, not the numeric per-device sequence the `Device*` tables use.
- Event time bound to `properties.Timestamp`, no fallback.
- `ActionResult` other than `Success` emits at WARN — a remediation that did not succeed is the interesting case.
- Not `Experimental`; `blob_ingest.account_url` is the whole opt-in, per #183.
- Golden confirms the omit-on-null contract independently of the unit test: `threat_types`, `detection_methods` and `email_direction` were null on the pinned live record and are absent from `testdata/signals.json`.

**One correction to the brief that drove this**, worth recording because it contradicts the sibling table. The plan called for asserting the event time differs from **both** envelope clocks. On this table's live record `_TimeReceivedBySvc` (`2026-07-22T10:43:05.0000000`) is the *same instant* as `properties.Timestamp` (`2026-07-22T10:43:05Z`), so that arm of the assertion could only ever fail. Only the envelope `time` (`10:44:33.4250955Z`, 88s later) genuinely differs, and that is what the test pins. On `defender.email`'s live record all three clocks differ. So **the three-clock spread is per-table, not a Defender-wide invariant** — do not write a shared assertion that assumes it. `[live-measured 2026-07-23, #233]`

**A near-miss found while writing the tests, now gated.** An ordinary AAD sign-in record's `auditData.ExtendedProperties` contains an entry whose `Name` is literally `"RequestType"` (value `OAuth2:Authorize`). It is a list entry, not a top-level `auditData` key, so reading the field is correct — but any implementation that searched `ExtendedProperties` **by name** would stamp `request_type` on every sign-in in the tenant. `TestQuarantineAttrsAbsentOnNonQuarantineRecords` drives that exact record to pin it. `[live-measured, #233]`

Also confirmed on the wire: `request_type` crosses the mapper as `float64` and reaches the emitter flattened to the string `"2"`. Both layers are asserted, so a change to either trips a test.
