## Landed — the state signal, `5b50d7d` + `073eb8e`

The three-part model is now complete in code. `make check` green over the whole tree, pushed.

| part | signal | transport | commit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| state | `defender.quarantine` | Exchange Online admin API | `073eb8e` |
| movement | `defender.email_post_delivery` | Defender blob | `5bb442c` |
| history | `m365.unified_audit` quarantine record types | Purview audit query | `5bb442c` |

`internal/exoclient` (the transport) landed separately as `5b50d7d` so it was reviewable on its own.

### `defender.quarantine`

One gauge, `defender.quarantine.held_messages.total{quarantine_type,direction,entity_type}` — bounded by Microsoft's enums, never by tenant size — plus one log twin per held message with sender, recipients, subject, quarantine policy and tag, expiry, and the eight permission flags. The flags are emitted even when false: `permission_to_release=false` (the recipient cannot self-release) is the interesting case, not an absence.

Queue **depth**, not flow, and `ReleaseStatus=NOTRELEASED` is what makes that true. Released messages stay visible to the API for the rest of their 30-day retention, so counting them would leave the number elevated for a month after an incident instead of returning to zero.

STATE feed, so records are stamped at poll time with `ReceivedTime` kept as an attribute — the `entra/risk` reasoning: stamping arrival time would pile every repeat of a still-held message onto one instant and make "what was held at 14:00" unanswerable.

### Three silent-failure traps, encoded as tests rather than comments

All three return HTTP 200 or otherwise look fine, which is why none of them is a comment:

- **`PageSize=0` returns 200 with zero rows** instead of erroring. A zero would be permanent silence indistinguishable from an empty quarantine.
- **`EntityType` 403s at Security Reader**, so sending it breaks the collector for the least-privileged identity that can read quarantine at all.
- **A record with an unparseable `Identity` still occupies quarantine**, so it must count toward the gauge even though its join key is lost.

### A bug caught before it shipped, worth recording

The collector declared `IngestTransport()` and I assumed that stamped the attribute. It does not. `collector.TransportOf` feeds the **admin status page** only; `telemetry.WithTransport` is what stamps `ingest_transport` onto records, and it is applied by the ingest ENGINES. There is no engine on the EXO path and the Scheduler's baseline is `TransportGraph` — so every record from the Exchange Online admin API would have been labeled `graph`, on a collector whose whole point is that Graph cannot see this data.

`mdca.discovery_parse` and the 15 Intune report-export collectors are in exactly the same position and all call `WithTransport` inside their own `Collect`. That is now done here too, with a test asserting the declared value and the stamped value are the same constant. **Generalizable rule: any engineless collector declaring a non-Graph transport must stamp it in `Collect`; declaring it is not stamping it.**

### Wiring decisions

**`EXODeps` is a SIXTH registration path**, mirroring `MDCADeps` — which corrects what the previous comment said. That comment claimed EXO needed no new path because it could take a `Deps` field. It could, and it would be wrong: `collectors.All()` registers for every tenant, so the collector would exist everywhere and 403 forever on the majority that lack the grants. A distinct path lets the composition root construct it only for tenants that opted in, and record an explicit absent-with-a-reason skip for the rest.

The #139/#100 gate-blindness trap was handled in the same commit: `registrySnapshot()` walks `EXOAll()` and `collectordoc.Rows` takes the slice. A registration path the doc gates cannot SEE makes them pass over an undocumented collector, which is worse than no gate.

Defender also gains its first non-blob doc section — queue depth is metric-shaped and its endpoint is not a container, so the blob columns would have been three blanks and a lie.

**Opt-in is `exchange_online.enabled`**, not the presence of a URL or token, because unlike MDCA this carries no secret of its own — the tenant's existing credential just requests a different audience. What it needs is the two grants, which cannot be inferred: a token mints fine without either and the failure only surfaces when a cmdlet runs.

`RequiredPermissions()` is empty and deliberately so: the declaration surface models GRAPH scopes, and neither grant is one. Both are documented in the collector reference and in `config.ExchangeOnlineConfig`, which is what an operator actually reads.

### Remaining

- [ ] `docs/graph-api-gotchas.md` + `docs/signals.md` — the quarantine story across all four transports with worked LogQL, and the trap ledger
- [ ] **Live verification, and it needs a synthesized message.** `ReleaseStatus=NOTRELEASED` returns **0** on m7kni right now: 2 quarantined messages in 30 days, both auto-released. The collector has never seen a non-empty queue, and a green tick over a permanently empty list proves nothing (CLAUDE.md). A deliberately quarantined test message is required before this can be called verified — flagging rather than assuming, since it means putting a message into quarantine on a production tenant.
- [ ] Teams queue depth — **not** being pursued. `-EntityType Teams` is denied to Security Reader and reading it would mean escalating the service principal to a write-capable role (Quarantine Admin / Security Admin) for one number on a surface that is admin-only by design. Teams quarantine is covered through `teamsQuarantineMetadata` in the audit trail instead. Recommendation stands unless overridden.

## Docs landed, `dfb51b6` — everything but live verification is done

Four of the remaining acceptance items are ticked. The only open one is live verification, and it needs a decision (below).

### `docs/signals.md` — the quarantine dataset

New section: the four-transport table, worked LogQL for the queries an operator actually wants (everything held; held-but-unreleasable; release events joined to their message; the full history of one `network_message_id` across all four transports; quarantine rate by policy), and the statement this issue asked for explicitly — **`held_messages.total` is queue DEPTH, not flow**. The two answer opposite questions and only one of them is a gauge; flow is a `count_over_time` over the log twins, deliberately not a metric, because a rate keyed by sender or policy would be a series per entity.

It also documents that **an empty quarantine emits no series at all, not a zero**. That is correct behaviour for an observable snapshot — a combination that stops appearing drops out rather than ghosting under forced cumulative temporality, same as `entra.risky_users.total` — but it is exactly the shape someone builds an "alert if no data" rule on, so it now says to alert on the series exceeding a threshold and to use the `graph2otel.*` staleness signals for liveness instead.

**Two corrections in the same file**, both now wrong rather than merely incomplete:

- The `defender.*` namespace was described as "advanced-hunting tables", "log-only", and gated by `blob_ingest.account_url`. `defender.quarantine` is none of those three. It is now documented as two transports with two independent switches.
- The `ingest_transport` value set was listed as six. It is seven.

### `docs/graph-api-gotchas.md` — the Exchange Online section

The entries that earn their place are the ones where **the API returns success and is lying**:

- PowerShell **prefix-matches enum values**, so a wrong value returns 200 with zero rows forever (`QuarantineTypes=File` silently resolved to `FileTypeBlock`). Validate against the enum list, never against a 200. The authoritative member list is recorded.
- **`PageSize=0` returns 200 with zero rows** instead of erroring.
- **A 403 body may not be JSON at all** — a run of NUL bytes. That is what a missing directory role looks like, i.e. the most likely production failure.
- The **two-grant model**, because no amount of app-role work moves a 403 that wants a directory role.
- The error-unwrapping precedence, since `error.message` is always `"Invalid Operation"`.

`analyzedEmails` is written up as a **rejected** surface rather than omitted, with the measurement that disqualified it. Recording why something was not built is what stops it being re-proposed — and the contrast (that API silently ignores what it does not understand; the EXO API rejects it) is the actual argument for the transport that was chosen.

The M365 audit-query section gains the `defaultAuditData`-not-`quarantineAuditRecord` type mismatch, the four accepted record-type filters, and the `ExtendedProperties`-named-`RequestType` near-miss.

### `docs/blob-ingest.md` — one entry

Within the Defender advanced-hunting family the three clocks **do not spread consistently per table**. On `EmailPostDeliveryEvents`' live record `_TimeReceivedBySvc` is the same instant as `properties.Timestamp`; on `EmailEvents` all three differ. So "the event time differs from both envelope clocks" passes on one table and can only fail on the other — a shared assertion across the family is unsafe. The binding rule itself (bind to `properties.Timestamp`, no fallback) is unchanged and still correct. `[live-measured 2026-07-23, #233]`

Also fixed a broken anchor in `signals.md`: the `configuration.md` link dropped a hyphen, and a heading containing `" / "` renders two.

---

## The one open item: live verification needs a decision

`ReleaseStatus=NOTRELEASED` returns **0** on m7kni. Two quarantined messages in thirty days, both auto-released. So `defender.quarantine` has **never been observed against a non-empty queue** — every code path past "the list was empty" is untested against the live API.

Per CLAUDE.md, a green tick over a permanently empty list is not evidence: "a mapping bug is invisible when the list is always empty" is the exact failure mode #129 exists for. Unit tests pin the mapping against a real captured record, so this is not unverified in the ordinary sense — what is unverified is the **live round trip**: paging, the request shape as the API actually parses it, and the gauge under a real non-zero count.

Closing this honestly needs a message deliberately put into quarantine. That is a mutation on a production tenant, so it is the maintainer's call, not something to do unprompted. Options:

1. **Send a GTUBE test message** to a monitored mailbox — the anti-spam equivalent of EICAR, designed for exactly this, and it lands in quarantine as `Spam` under the existing Standard Preset policy. Cleanest option; no policy change, no real threat, and it is what the preset is already configured to catch.
2. **Temporarily tighten a policy** so an ordinary bulk message quarantines. More disruptive and needs reverting.
3. **Ship it unverified against a non-empty queue**, with this stated as the known gap and re-verified the first time something quarantines naturally.

Recommendation: **(1)**. Default if unanswered: leave the issue open with this as the sole blocker rather than closing on an empty-list green tick — the thing this project has repeatedly been bitten by.

Everything else on the acceptance list is done and pushed.

## CORRECTION: GTUBE does NOT quarantine on this tenant `[live-measured 2026-07-23]`

The previous comment recommended a GTUBE test message and said it "lands in quarantine as `Spam` under the existing Standard Preset policy". **That is wrong.** A GTUBE message was sent and did not quarantine.

What actually happened — message trace, via `Get-MessageTraceV2`:

```
2026-07-23T11:20:31 | rob@rob-knight.com -> rob@m7kni.io | FilteredAsSpam | XJS*C4JDBQADN1.NSBN3*2IDNEN*GTUBE-STANDARD-AN...
```

The message arrived and was filtered correctly. It went to the **Junk folder**, not quarantine. Quarantine stayed at the same 2 released messages across 20 one-minute polls (11:18Z → 11:38Z).

### Why — the live policy actions

`Get-HostedContentFilterPolicy`, both policies on the tenant:

| action | Default | Standard Preset |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `SpamAction` | `MoveToJmf` | **`MoveToJmf`** |
| `HighConfidenceSpamAction` | `MoveToJmf` | `Quarantine` |
| `PhishSpamAction` | `MoveToJmf` | `Quarantine` |
| `HighConfidencePhishAction` | `Quarantine` | `Quarantine` |
| `BulkSpamAction` / `BulkThreshold` | `MoveToJmf` / 7 | `MoveToJmf` / 6 |

**GTUBE scores as ordinary spam, not HIGH-CONFIDENCE spam.** Under the Standard Preset `SpamAction` is `MoveToJmf`, so it is structurally incapable of quarantining. The error was assuming "GTUBE is the anti-spam EICAR" implies "GTUBE quarantines" — it triggers the *verdict*, but the *action* is policy, and on a Standard Preset tenant only high-confidence spam, phish and malware quarantine.

Generalizable: **a test artifact proves a detection verdict, never a disposition.** Read the policy's action for that verdict class before choosing the artifact.

### What does quarantine here

- **EICAR attachment → malware.** `Get-MalwareFilterPolicy` exposes no configurable `Action` — malware quarantine is unconditional — with `QuarantineTag: AdminOnlyAccessPolicy`. This is the reliable trigger.
- **Banned file type → `FileTypeBlock`.** `EnableFileFilter: True` on both policies; matches on extension, not content, so a harmless file with a blocked extension quarantines with no malware involved. The fallback if outbound scanning strips EICAR before it leaves the sending provider.
- Temporarily setting `SpamAction: Quarantine` would also work but mutates live filtering for real mail and needs reverting — not recommended.

Either of the first two is **better coverage than GTUBE would have given**: they exercise a different `quarantine_type` (`Malware` / `FileTypeBlock` rather than `Spam`) and the `AdminOnlyAccessPolicy` tag, so the per-message permission flags come back mostly `false` — the branch that has never been observed live.

### Status

`defender.quarantine` remains **unverified against a non-empty queue**. Nothing about the collector is implicated: the transport answered HTTP 200 on all 20 polls and correctly reported an empty held-set. What has not been exercised is paging and the gauge under a real non-zero count.

`Get-MessageTraceV2` is also newly confirmed as reachable at this privilege level — `Get-MessageTrace` (v1) returns 400 `DirectInvokeCmdletExecutionException`, the V2 form returns 200. Useful for any future "did the mail actually arrive" question; not currently a collector.

## Live end-to-end verification `[live-measured 2026-07-23]` — done without a synthesized message

Waiting for a quarantined message turned out to be the wrong way to close this. The shipped collector was run **against the live tenant**, unmodified, with only the client beneath it swapped to drop the held-only filter so it saw the two rows the tenant actually has. Throwaway harness, not committed; the working tree is unchanged and the golden untouched.

### Results

```
HELD-ONLY (the shipped query):  gauge points=0  logs=0   err=nil
ALL ROWS  (filter stripped):    gauge points=1  logs=2

  gauge  2  {direction:Inbound  entity_type:Email  quarantine_type:Spam}

  log  event=defender.quarantine  ts_zero=true  transport="exchange_online"
       nmid="86bab6ca-b175-4b84-d76c-08dee7cf55a8"  type="Spam"
       status="RELEASED"  tag="DefaultFullAccessWithNotificationPolicy"
       permission_to_release="true"
  log  event=defender.quarantine  ts_zero=true  transport="exchange_online"
       nmid="80aa9dda-c565-45a0-6133-08dee7cf4a7a"  ...
```

### What this closes

- **The request shape is parsed as intended by the live API.** The collector's exact parameter set (`PageSize`, `Page`, `ReleaseStatus`) returned HTTP 200 — not a hand-written probe, the shipped code path.
- **The empty path is correct end to end**: 0 held rows produces 0 gauge points, 0 logs and a **nil error**, rather than an error or a phantom zero series.
- **Real wire records map correctly** — the gauge counted 2 under the right bounded labels, and both log twins carried the right values.
- **`ingest_transport="exchange_online"` is stamped on the records.** This is the bug that nearly shipped (declaring a transport is not stamping it), now confirmed against live output rather than only in a unit test.
- **`Timestamp` is zero — poll time**, confirming the STATE-feed rule live.
- **`network_message_id` is correctly split from the composite `Identity`** on real data.

### What is still NOT verified, stated plainly

- **A genuinely HELD record has never been mapped.** Both live rows are `RELEASED`. The shape is presumed identical and only field values differ, which is a small risk but not zero.
- **Paging beyond one page** is untestable on this tenant — it needs >1000 held messages and always will.
- **A non-`Spam` `quarantine_type`**, the `AdminOnlyAccessPolicy` tag, and the mostly-`false` permission-flag branch remain unobserved.

### Incidental finding

A **released** record emits two attributes a held record does not: `released_by` and `released_count` (the held fixture has `ReleasedBy: []` / `ReleasedCount: 0`, which `SetStrs`/`SetNum` correctly omit). This surfaced as a signals-golden drift while the live harness was in the tree. The committed golden reflects a **held** record's attribute set, which is right — held is the only thing the shipped query ever returns.

### Why no test message was sent

Recorded so the next attempt does not repeat it:

- **GTUBE cannot work here** — `SpamAction: MoveToJmf` on the Standard Preset (see the correction comment above).
- **A blocked file extension cannot work either.** `Get-MalwareFilterPolicy` shows `FileTypeAction: **Reject**` on both policies, so a banned attachment gets an NDR — it never reaches quarantine. This was the recommended fallback in the previous comment and it is **wrong**; `.docm`/`.exe`/etc. would have bounced. `[live-measured 2026-07-23]`
- **EICAR remains the only mail-based trigger** (malware quarantine is unconditional; the policy exposes no `Action` for it, `QuarantineTag: AdminOnlyAccessPolicy`). Gmail and most providers block EICAR on send, so it needs a sending path that does not scan outbound.
- A **transport rule** with a `Quarantine` action would also do it, but creating one is a write the read-only poller identity cannot make.

### Recommendation

Close #233 on the coverage work. The remaining gap — one held record, one non-Spam type — is genuinely small, is documented above rather than hidden, and will close itself the first time the tenant quarantines anything naturally (2 in the last 30 days, so weeks not months). Re-verifying then costs one command.

Holding the issue open indefinitely for a synthesized message is worse than closing it with the gap stated: an open issue with everything done reads as unfinished work, which is the failure mode CLAUDE.md's "milestone deferral" rule warns about.

## Closing — quarantine coverage shipped, with the residual assumptions instrumented rather than hidden

Closed by `f08f994` (the completing commit carries `Refs`, not a closing keyword, so this is a manual close — history not rewritten, per CLAUDE.md).

### What shipped

| part | signal | transport | commit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| state — held right now | `defender.quarantine` | Exchange Online admin API | `073eb8e` |
| movement — entering / leaving | `defender.email_post_delivery` | Defender blob | `5bb442c` |
| history — held/released/deleted | `m365.unified_audit` quarantine record types | Purview audit query | `5bb442c` |
| transport | `internal/exoclient` | — | `5b50d7d` |
| docs | signals / gotchas / blob-ingest | — | `dfb51b6` |
| assumption watchdog | `internal/wirecheck` | — | `f08f994` |

All four transports key on `network_message_id`, so quarantine is one joinable dataset. The original question — "does the app expose the number of emails in quarantine" — is now yes, and it is genuine queue depth rather than flow.

### Why this closes without a synthesized held message

The maintainer's call, and the right one: **ship on the measured assumptions, but instrument them so a deviation announces itself.**

The end-to-end live run (comment above) already proved the request shape against the live API, the empty path, real-record mapping, the `exchange_online` transport stamp, and the `Identity` split. What could not be proven was a genuinely HELD record, a non-`Spam` type, and paging — the last of which is untestable on this tenant at any point in the future, since it needs >1000 held messages.

Those residuals are now **watched at runtime** rather than assumed silently. `defender.quarantine` declares its assumptions to `wirecheck` and emits `graph2otel.api.unexpected{collector,field,kind}` plus a one-shot WARN naming the offending value if any of them stops holding:

- the `quarantine_type` / `entity_type` / `direction` enums — all three are **metric labels**, so a member Microsoft adds later would otherwise silently create a series;
- `held_only_filter` — the serious one. If `ReleaseStatus=NOTRELEASED` ever stops filtering server-side, `held_messages.total` quietly becomes "everything still in retention": a number that stays elevated for a month after an incident and looks entirely plausible while doing so;
- `page_cap` — hitting it means the gauge **undercounts**, a wrong number rather than a missing one;
- `network_message_id` recoverable from the composite `Identity` — the join key that makes the four signals one dataset.

A finding is never an error and never drops a record: losing data because a field grew a new enum member would turn a cosmetic surprise into a hole.

### Known gaps, stated rather than closed over

- **No held record has ever been mapped.** Both live rows are `RELEASED`. Shape presumed identical, values differ. The watchdog covers the ways this could go wrong.
- **Paging is untestable here** and always will be.
- **`AdminOnlyAccessPolicy` and the mostly-`false` permission-flag branch are unobserved.**
- **Teams queue depth is not covered** — `-EntityType Teams` is 403 at `Security Reader`, and escalating to a write-capable role for one number on an admin-only-by-design surface was rejected. Teams quarantine is covered through the `teamsQuarantineMetadata` audit record type instead. If a Teams row ever does appear in the unfiltered result set, `entity_type` is watched and will say so.

All four will close themselves the first time the tenant quarantines something naturally (2 in the last 30 days), and re-verifying costs one command.

### Corrections made during this work, recorded so they are not repeated

1. **GTUBE cannot force a quarantine here** — `SpamAction: MoveToJmf` on the Standard Preset. The test message arrived and went to Junk. A test artifact proves a detection **verdict**, never a **disposition**.
2. **A blocked file extension cannot either** — `FileTypeAction: Reject`, so it NDRs rather than quarantining. This was recommended as the fallback and was wrong.
3. **`analyzedEmails` was dropped**, not forgotten — its date parameters are accepted, return 200, and change nothing.
4. **EXO needed a sixth registration path**, not a `Deps` field as first claimed — `collectors.All()` registers for every tenant, so the collector would have existed everywhere and 403'd forever.
5. **Declaring a transport is not stamping it.** `IngestTransport()` feeds the admin page only; without `telemetry.WithTransport` in `Collect`, every record would have been labeled `graph`.

### Follow-up

**#234** — extend `wirecheck` across the other collectors. 38 of them currently bucket unrecognized values to the literal `"unknown"`, which is the same silent-failure class this issue hit, at scale.

title: feat(collectors): Defender quarantine coverage — email + Teams, audit history + flow metrics

body:
## What happened

A live Defender for Cloud Apps alert — "Unusual addition of credentials to an OAuth app",
`2026-07-22T16:34:45.39Z`, alert id `ca6a60f1005deef347017038cc` — was ingested correctly by
graph2otel on **both** transports and reached Loki, but produced **no IRM page**.

graph2otel was not at fault. The Grafana alert rule `g2o-defender-crit` filtered
``| service_source=~`(?i).*defender.*endpoint.*` ``, and the alert's `service_source` is
`microsoftDefenderForCloudApps`. The rule has been fixed live (see "Live changes already made").

The reason this is a repo issue: the near-miss was caused by an **undocumented property of
graph2otel's own output**, and `docs/signals.md` says nothing about it.

## Finding 1 — the two transports emit different value vocabularies for identically-named attributes

The same alert arrives on two paths, with the same attribute *names* and incompatible attribute
*values*. Measured over the full 7d window on m7kni (all records on both streams, not a sample):

| source | Graph `entra.security_alert` | blob `defender.alert_info` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Defender for Endpoint | `microsoftDefenderForEndpoint` | `Microsoft Defender for Endpoint` |
| Defender for Cloud Apps | `microsoftDefenderForCloudApps` | `Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps` |
| Entra ID Protection | `azureAdIdentityProtection` | `AAD Identity Protection` |
| `severity` | `medium` / `high` / `informational` | `Medium` / `High` / `Informational` |

Both collectors emit the wire verbatim, which is correct per the project's wire-over-docs rule —
Graph `alerts_v2` uses camelCase enums, the Defender `AlertInfo` advanced-hunting table uses display
strings. The consequence is the part that needs writing down: **a LogQL filter written against one
transport's vocabulary matches exactly zero rows on the other.**

The Identity Protection row is the sharp edge. `azureAdIdentityProtection` and
`AAD Identity Protection` share no substring, so a `(?i)` regex does not rescue it — unlike the
`severity` row, where case-insensitive matching is sufficient.

Same-alert evidence (alert id `ca6a60f1005deef347017038cc` on both streams):

| | `entra.security_alert` | `defender.alert_info` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| event time | `16:34:45.39Z` | `16:27:19Z` |
| emitted | `16:52:09Z` | `16:37:11Z` |
| latency | ~17.5 min | ~10 min |
| `service_source` | `microsoftDefenderForCloudApps` | `Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps` |
| `severity` | `medium` | `Medium` |
| `detection_source` | `cloudAppSecurity` | `Cloud App Security` |

The latency difference is structural, not incidental: `entra.security_alerts` runs a 10m interval
with a 15m safety lag (`securityalerts.go:52-57`), so ~20 min from alert creation to a page is the
design, not a fault. Worth stating so nobody debugs it as one.

`[live-measured 2026-07-22]`

## Finding 2 — `docs/signals.md` and the defender package doc still carry pre-#183 Experimental claims

#183 made the `defender.*` advanced-hunting collectors non-`Experimental` and on-by-default whenever
`blob_ingest` is configured. Two places never caught up and now state the opposite:

- `docs/signals.md:13-14` — "Log-only, Experimental, off by default (#106)."
- `internal/collectors/defender/defender.go:19-21` — "EXPERIMENTAL + off by default — this is the
  highest-volume surface graph2otel touches, so each table is opted in explicitly per #106 (the
  subpackage's wrapper returns `Experimental() == true`)."

Both are false as shipped. Verified two ways:

1. `rg -n "func .*Experimental\(\) bool" internal/collectors/defender/` returns **nothing** — no
   subpackage implements the interface the comment describes.
2. On camden, every `defender.*` collector reports `enabled: true` in `status.json` while the
   deployed `config.yaml` lists none of them under `collectors:` — they register purely off
   `blob_ingest.account_url`.

This is the exact rot pattern `CLAUDE.md`'s tracker-hygiene section calls out: a later decision
reversed an earlier claim and the prose was left asserting the reversed-away state.

## Scope

Documentation only. No collector behaviour changes — the emitted values are correct and stay
verbatim.

1. Add a cross-transport vocabulary section to `docs/signals.md`, alongside the existing
   "Attributes that mean the same thing on both M365 transports" and "Risk signals: the two
   transports are NOT interchangeable" sections, which this sits directly beside as a third
   instance of the same class of trap.
2. Include the alerting guidance the incident produced: do not scope a rule to a single
   `service_source`, and expect ~20 min alert-to-page on the Graph path.
3. Correct the two stale Experimental claims in Finding 2.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `docs/signals.md` documents the `service_source` / `severity` vocabulary split between
      `entra.security_alert` and `defender.alert_info`, with the live-measured table and an evidence tag
- [ ] It states explicitly that `azureAdIdentityProtection` vs `AAD Identity Protection` defeats a
      `(?i)` regex, so case-insensitive matching is not a sufficient fix
- [ ] It records the ~20 min Graph alert-to-page latency and its cause (10m interval + 15m lag)
- [ ] `docs/signals.md:13-14` no longer claims `defender.*` is Experimental / off by default
- [ ] `internal/collectors/defender/defender.go` package doc no longer claims
      `Experimental() == true` wrappers exist
- [ ] `make check` green

## Live changes already made (Grafana, outside this repo)

Recorded here so they are reconstructible from GitHub alone:

- `g2o-defender-crit` retitled to "G2O — Security alert (Medium/High, unresolved)"; `service_source`
  filter dropped; now
  ``| severity=~`(?i)(high|medium)` | status=~`(?i)(new|inProgress)` ``. Validated at 7 matches/7d
  across all three sources. Stale annotation claiming "0 rows/30d" replaced.
- `g2o-security-incident` created — `entra.security_incident`, `severity` medium/high,
  `status=~(?i)(active|inProgress)`. 6 matches/7d. `resolved` and `redirected` excluded
  (`redirected` = merged into another incident, a duplicate by construction).
- Both in folder `ffo7you47fxtsd`, group `entra-security-g2o` (60s interval), labels
  `severity=critical` + `source=entra`, which match the existing notification-policy route to the
  `irm-security` receiver. Routing was never the fault.
- Not yet done: no page has actually traversed IRM end to end. Query-match and route-matcher
  alignment are verified; delivery is not.

comments.body:
Done in f22d647 (pushed to `main`).

**`docs/signals.md`** — new section *"Security alerts: the two transports emit different VALUES for the same attributes"*, placed alongside the existing M365-twin-transport and risk-transport sections as the third instance of the same class of trap. Carries the live-measured vocabulary table with its evidence tag, the explicit note that `(?i)` does not rescue `azureAdIdentityProtection` vs `AAD Identity Protection`, the recommended source-agnostic rule query, why excluding already-`resolved` alerts is lossless (dedupe is on alert id, so status is poll-time and never re-emitted), the ~20 min Graph alert-to-page latency with its cause, the faster-but-narrower ~10 min blob twin, and the separate `active`/`resolved`/`redirected` status vocabulary on `entra.security_incidents`.

**Stale Experimental claims** — corrected in three places, one more than the issue listed:

| location | was |
| --- | --- |
| `docs/signals.md:13-14` | "Log-only, Experimental, off by default (#106)" |
| `internal/collectors/defender/defender.go:19-21` | "EXPERIMENTAL + off by default … wrapper returns `Experimental() == true`" |
| `internal/collectors/defender/defender.go:70` | "…and adds `Experimental()`" (on the `New` doc comment — not spotted when the issue was filed) |

`make check` green: 0 lint issues, all tests pass, no vulnerabilities, both modules tidy, build OK.

Docs only — no collector behavior changed, values stay verbatim on both paths.

**Still outstanding, deliberately not done:** no page has actually traversed IRM end to end. The rule queries are validated against real data (7 matches/7d for alerts, 6 for incidents) and the rule labels match the notification-policy route to the `irm-security` receiver, but delivery itself is unproven — confirming it needs either a synthesized tenant alert or a temporary lookback widen, both of which fire a real page.

body:
## What

graph2otel never called `otel.SetErrorHandler`, so every error the OpenTelemetry SDK raises went to the global default handler — which writes via Go's standard `log` package. Unstructured, unlevelled, and outside every filter an operator has configured for graph2otel's `slog` output.

```console
$ grep -rn "SetErrorHandler" --include='*.go' .
(no matches — only otel.Handle CALL SITES, in internal/telemetry/emitter.go)
```

## Why it matters

This is the channel that carries **OTLP export rejections**, which is what makes it more than a tidiness issue. Found while investigating #226: the Grafana Cloud gateway refuses a log record timestamped beyond its 7-day accept window with a genuinely actionable 400:

```text
400 Bad Request: entry for stream '{service_name="graph2otel"}' has timestamp too old:
2026-07-08T13:05:10Z, oldest acceptable timestamp is: 2026-07-15T13:05:10Z
```

A rejected record is **data loss** in a SIEM feed. That message names both the offending timestamp and the exact limit, so it is the single most useful line the process can emit when a backfill overshoots — and it was arriving in a different format from every other line, at no level, invisible to a log pipeline keyed on graph2otel's own output.

Worth stating precisely, because #226 got this wrong in the other direction: wiring this would **not** have prevented #226. That issue's records were never rejected at all. The two are related only in that both live in the blind spot around export failures.

## Fix

`otelErrorHandler(logger)` in `cmd/graph2otel/main.go`, wired immediately after the logger is built and before the telemetry provider (so provider-construction errors are already covered). Logged at **ERROR** — a dropped record is not a note.

Extracted as a named function rather than an inline closure so it is testable: `TestOtelErrorHandlerLogsThroughTheAppLogger` asserts the level and that the underlying error text survives, using a real rejection string as the fixture.

## Acceptance

- [x] SDK errors route to graph2otel's structured logger
- [x] Logged at ERROR
- [x] Wired before the provider is constructed
- [x] Test pins level + message preservation
- [x] `make check` green
title: fix(obs): OTEL SDK errors bypassed the app logger — OTLP export rejections landed unstructured on stderr

body:
## What

`telemetrytest.Recorder` captured the value of every non-string log attribute as the empty string. Found while building #226's clamp, whose marker attribute is a bool and read back as `""`.

`flattenLogRecord` stringified with `log.Value.AsString()`:

```go
rec.WalkAttributes(func(kv log.KeyValue) bool {
    attrs[kv.Key] = kv.Value.AsString()   // asserts a kind; does not convert
    return true
})
```

`AsString()` on the OTel log API **asserts** `KindString` rather than converting — for any other kind it returns `""` and emits an internal "invalid Kind" diagnostic that no test reads. Measured across the supported `telemetry.Attrs` types:

| emitted | captured |
| --- | --- |
| `"str"` (string) | `"str"` ✅ |
| `[]string{"a","b"}` | `"a,b"` ✅ (joined before it reaches the log API) |
| `true` (bool) | `""` ❌ |
| `int64(42)` | `""` ❌ |
| `1.5` (float64) | `""` ❌ |

## Why it matters

Numeric attributes are a large share of the log-twin surface — `startup_impact_ms`, `battery_age_days`, `max_capacity_percentage`, `app_crash_count`, every score and count added across #179/#194/#199/#225. **No test in the project could assert any of their values.** A test that tried would have compared `""` against `""` and passed vacuously; in practice authors wrote presence-only checks instead, which is the shape the existing tests have.

This is the #139/#164 pattern one level down — a gate reporting coverage it does not have — but with a narrower blast radius than either of those, and the limit is worth stating precisely rather than overselling the find:

- **Goldens are NOT affected.** `internal/signalcapture` iterates `for k := range l.Attrs` and records attribute **keys** only, never values. So `docs/collectors.md` and the signal captures were never wrong because of this.
- **Production was never affected.** `internal/telemetry/emitter.go`'s `toLogKV` builds correctly-typed `log.KeyValue`s, so the wire carried the right values throughout. This is a test-observability defect, not a data defect.

So nothing shipped wrong. What was missing is the ability to *prove* it had not.

## Fix

`logValueString` in `internal/telemetrytest/recorder.go` renders every kind (`KindString`, `KindBool`, `KindInt64`, `KindFloat64`, `KindBytes`, `KindSlice` recursively, with a `v.String()` default), and `flattenLogRecord` uses it.

Pinned by `TestEmitterLogEventCapturesEveryAttributeKind`, which asserts a string, bool, int64, float64 and `[]string` attribute all survive with their values intact — chosen from the real `intune.device_startup` attribute set rather than invented names.

Full suite re-run after the change: green, no test depended on the empty-string behaviour.

## Acceptance

- [x] Recorder renders every log attribute kind
- [x] Regression test pins all five types
- [x] `make check` green
- [x] Confirmed goldens/signalcapture unaffected (keys only)
- [x] Confirmed production emit path unaffected (`toLogKV` was always correct)

body:
## Symptom

`scripts/storage-report.py` reports **£59.39/month** for `graph2otelm7kni`. Azure Cost Management
reports **£1.53 month-to-date**, with a last-full-day run-rate of **£12.91/month**. The script is
**~4.7x** high.

## Root cause: `AVG_APPEND_BYTES = 7300` is 4.9x too low

The script never measures write operations — it back-solves them:

```
rate = bytes / (avg_append * actual_retention)
```

Two inputs. One is right, one is badly wrong:

- **Retention anchor is correct.** Lifecycle policy is `delete-after-1d`
  (`daysAfterModificationGreaterThan: 1.0`, `blobTypes: [blockBlob, appendBlob]`) and auto-detect
  reads it correctly. Resident 3.0 GB matches one day of ingress (2.99 GB on 2026-07-21). ✅
- **`AVG_APPEND_BYTES = 7300` is wrong.** Measured from Azure Monitor on 2026-07-21:
  `2,994.5 MB Ingress / 84,139 AppendBlock = 35,590 B/append` — **4.9x** the constant.

That single error explains essentially the whole gap: script 13.3M appends/mo vs actual
84,139 x 30.44 = **2.56M/mo**, ratio 5.2x.

The docstring already predicted this: *"the 7300 B/append mean was measured on the Entra categories
(MGAL / sign-ins); the Defender tables may batch differently."* They batch far larger. The blended
figure is also a **moving target** as Defender streams came online:

| day | Ingress | AppendBlock | blended B/append |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2026-07-16 | 212.2 MB | 20,144 | 10,534 |
| 2026-07-17 | 907.0 MB | 49,787 | 18,218 |
| 2026-07-18 | 991.0 MB | 38,874 | 25,493 |
| 2026-07-19 | 1,456.3 MB | 61,317 | 23,750 |
| 2026-07-20 | 1,823.4 MB | 75,822 | 24,048 |
| 2026-07-21 | 2,994.5 MB | 84,139 | **35,590** |

A hardcoded constant cannot track that. `[live-measured 2026-07-22, #NNN]`

## Second defect: list operations are excluded

`cost_row()` drops reads and listing as "small, not implied by size". ListBlobs runs at
**9,381/day** -> ~285K/mo -> **~£1.28/month**, about 10% of the real bill, and it is billed at the
same £0.0447/10K rate as writes (meter `LRS List and Create Container Operations`).

## Actual billing evidence

Cost Management, resource `graph2otelm7kni`, July MTD (billing starts 2026-07-16 — the account is new):

| meter | quantity | cost |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Hot LRS Write Operations | 32.7743 (10K) | £1.4650 |
| LRS List and Create Container Operations | 1.3435 (10K) | £0.0601 |
| Intra Continent Data Transfer Out | 0.0758 GB | £0.0011 |
| All Other Operations | 0.086 | £0.0003 |
| Hot LRS Data Stored | 0.2638 GB-mo | **£0.00 (free tier)** |
| **total** | | **£1.53** |

The script's price constants are **correct** — 32.7743 x £0.0447 = £1.4650 exactly. Only the
op-count model is wrong.

Daily billed: 07-16 £0.033, 07-17 £0.232, 07-18 £0.176, 07-19 £0.275, 07-20 £0.346,
**07-21 £0.424** (last full day) -> x30.44 = **£12.91/mo**.

Whole-subscription MTD is £1.58, so nothing else material is in play.

### Corrected picture

| | script today | actual |
| --- | --- | --- |
| appends/mo | 13.3M | 2.56M |
| write-ops £/mo | £59.35 | £11.45 |
| list-ops £/mo | excluded | ~£1.28 |
| storage £/mo | £0.04 | £0.00 (free tier) |
| **total** | **£59.39** | **~£12.8** |

Volume is still ramping — 07-21 was the highest day yet — so steady state may land above £13.

## Free-account grant: immaterial, do not model it

The 12-month free grant expires 2026-09-11 and every meter that matters is already exceeded
(write ops at 3,377% of allowance). Total value at current volume: Hot LRS Write Ops 10K/mo
£0.045 + List/Create 20K/mo £0.089 + Hot Read 20K/mo £0.007 + Data Stored 5 GB/mo £0.044 +
Data Transfer Out 15 GB ~£0.16 = **~£0.35/month**, under 3% of the bill. Expiry moves the
number by pennies. Noted in the docstring; not modelled. `[live-measured 2026-07-22]`

## Fix

Stop estimating the append count. It is directly measurable, exactly as `docs/blob-ingest.md`
already says (*"Don't guess at the batching; read the counter"*) — the script just never did it.

- [ ] Query Azure Monitor `Transactions` filtered `ApiName eq 'AppendBlock'` on
      `<account>/blobServices/default` -> hard write-op count, no assumption
- [ ] Query `Ingress` over the same window -> auto-calibrate `avg_append = Ingress / AppendBlock`
      per run, replacing the 7300 constant for the per-container split and all what-if scenarios
- [ ] Bill `ListBlobs` (+ `CreateContainer`) at the write rate; keep reads/egress itemised but noted as minor
- [ ] Per-container attribution stays byte-share allocated (the `Transactions` metric has **no
      container dimension**) — state that in the output rather than implying it is exact. It
      under-attributes Entra (small appends) and over-attributes Defender (large ones).
- [ ] Graceful fallback to the documented constant when the metrics call is denied or empty,
      with a visible warning that the number is modelled not measured
- [ ] Preserve `--volume-scale` / `--scale NAME=X` / `--model-retention-days` semantics, now
      anchored on the measured rate
- [ ] Update `docs/blob-ingest.md`: the **£3.07/month** figure is Entra-only, measured
      2026-07-17 before the Defender advanced-hunting streams were enabled, and the
      "~7.3 KB per append" anchor is superseded by the measured blended 35.6 KB
- [ ] Tests for the calibration and fallback paths

## Acceptance

Run with no flags reproduces the Cost Management last-full-day run-rate within ~10%, and with
no metrics access degrades to the old modelled number carrying an explicit warning.

comments.body:
Fixed in fd1531e (pushed to `main`).

## What changed

`scripts/storage-report.py` now reads the billable op count off Azure Monitor instead of
back-solving it from resident bytes:

- **`Transactions` filtered `ApiName eq 'AppendBlock'`** — an exact count of billable appends
  (an append blob supports no other write). Averaged over whole UTC days only, today excluded,
  because `az monitor metrics list` reports a part-day as a full bucket and would drag the rate
  down in proportion to how early you run it.
- **`Ingress / AppendBlock` calibrates the mean append size every run.** `AVG_APPEND_BYTES = 7300`
  is now fallback-only and labelled as such; `--avg-append-bytes` still overrides both.
- **Byte-share allocation across containers, stated openly in the report.** The `Transactions`
  metric has no container dimension, so account totals are exact and per-row splits are
  indicative — under-stating small-record Entra streams, over-stating large-batch Defender ones.
  The report prints that caveat rather than implying the rows are measured.
- **Listing is now billed** at the write rate (`LRS List and Create Container Operations`).
  ~9,400 ListBlobs/day is ~£1.30/mo, ~10% of the bill, and `cost_row()` dropped it as "small".
  Reads priced separately at £0.0036/10K. `DeleteBlob` is excluded from every bucket — blob
  deletes are not billable.
- **Fallback preserved and made loud.** `--no-metrics`, or a denied Monitor call (needs
  `Monitoring Reader`), runs the old model and renders `MODELLED` in red naming the 4.9x history.
- **Ramp detector.** When the last full day diverges >25% from the averaged window the report
  says `RAMPING UP` / `FALLING` and points at `--metrics-days 1`. This account is at 1.14x, so
  it stays quiet — but a 3-day average during a ramp is a trailing figure and shouldn't pass
  itself off as current.
- Measured rates + calibrated append size are recorded in the history snapshot, so the op rate
  is trackable separately from the bytes.

`--volume-scale` / `--scale NAME=X` / `--model-retention-days` semantics are unchanged, now
anchored on the measured rate. Doubling volume prices to exactly 2x.

## Verification against the bill

| run | result |
| --- | --- |
| `--metrics-days 1` (matches the last billed full day) | **£12.87** |
| Cost Management, 2026-07-21 actual x 30.44 | **£12.91** |
| delta | **0.3%** |
| `--metrics-days 3` (default) | £11.39 — 12% low, correctly, because the window averages a ramp |
| `--no-metrics` (fallback) | £59.42, rendered `MODELLED` in red |

Acceptance bar was ~10% on the default run. The default lands 12% low **because the account is
still ramping**, not because the model is wrong: the 3-day window averages 73.8K appends/day
against 84.1K on the last full day. The measured line prints its own window and rates so this
is visible rather than hidden, and `--metrics-days 1` is exact.

Live calibration on this account: **28,354 B/append** over the 3-day window, **35,590 B** over
the last full day — against the 7,300 B constant that caused the bug.

## Docs

`docs/blob-ingest.md`: the £3.07/month headline (Entra-only scope) and the "~7.3 KB per append"
anchor are replaced with the billed meter split and the measured blend. The #89
blob-vs-LA-vs-EventHub ranking is **re-framed, not re-quoted** — LA prices per GB ingested so
higher volume widens blob's margin — and explicitly tagged as scaled-from-#89's-prices rather
than re-measured, so nobody cites a specific LA number as live. The free-account grant is
documented as deliberately not modelled, with the arithmetic.

## Tests

`scripts/storage_report_test.py` — 26 cases over the pure cost model: measured vs modelled
paths, calibration, byte-share allocation summing to the measured total, the 7300 constant
being unable to move a measured op count, metric-envelope parsing (including gap buckets that
must not be read as zeroes), and the whole-day window. Stdlib `unittest`, no `az` round-trip.

    python3 scripts/storage_report_test.py

## Out of scope, flagged

`make check` currently fails at `govulncheck` on a pre-existing `golang.org/x/text@v0.38.0`
issue (GO-2026-5970, fixed in v0.39.0), reached via `internal/o365activityclient/transport.go:174`.
Unrelated to this change — this diff is Python and Markdown only. `go vet`, `go test -race` and
`golangci-lint` are all green. Needs its own dep-bump issue.

body:
## Why

`opnsense-exporter` and `tailscale2otel` both ship a **"Runtime trend (~10 min)"** block on their admin/console status page — Goroutines / Heap-in-use / GC-rate stat cards plus live line charts fed by a background `runtime.ReadMemStats` sampler. graph2otel's admin page has none of it: the only chart primitive is the per-collector duration sparkline (`drawSpark`), and there is no `registerChart`/`drawChart` framework, no runtime sampler, and no in-process history beyond `collector.StatusTracker`'s per-collector rings.

Reference implementations:

| repo | sampler | render |
| --- | --- | --- |
| opnsense-exporter | `internal/webui/runtime.go` (`runtimeSampler`) | `internal/webui/templates/page.html.tmpl` |
| tailscale2otel | `internal/app/sampler.go` (`runtimeHistory`) | `internal/app/statushtml/page.html.tmpl` |

Both sample every 10s and retain 60 samples (~10 min). graph2otel already has `internal/ringbuf` (the same generic ring both siblings sample into), so the plumbing exists.

This is admin-page introspection only — none of it is emitted as OTLP, and it is independent of self-observability.

## Scope

Add a background sampler to `internal/admin` and render six trend groups on the Overview tab.

**Runtime trend (~10 min)** — parity with both siblings:
- `chGoroutines` — goroutine count
- `chHeap` — heap in use (MiB)
- `chGC` — GC cycles/sec (differenced `MemStats.NumGC` over elapsed wall time)

**Throughput & fleet trend (~10 min)** — new, graph2otel-first:
- `chEmit` — two series: metric data points/sec and log records/sec, measured with `atomic.Uint64` counters at the innermost `otelEmitter` (so every `WithTenant`/`WithTransport` decorator is counted exactly once) and differenced over elapsed wall time
- `chCard` — total active series from `telemetry.CardinalityTracker.Snapshot()` (0 when self-obs is off)
- `chFailing` — collectors whose last run failed, summed across tenants
- `chDuration` — mean collector run duration (ms) across all tenants

**Throttle headroom trend** — graph2otel-only (no sibling analogue): a headroom sparkline column per `(tenant, workload)` row on the existing rate-limit panel, sampled from `WorkloadLimiter.Snapshot`.

Also port the zero-dependency `registerChart`/`drawChart` line-chart framework (value axis, gridlines, area fill, hover crosshair + tooltip) from `tailscale2otel/internal/app/statushtml/page.html.tmpl`, redrawing on refresh, tab-show and theme toggle.

## Design constraints

- **Sampler cadence 10s, 60 samples retained**, matching both siblings. Rings are `internal/ringbuf`.
- **Rate series start at the second sample.** A rate needs a prior observation; emitting `0` for the first sample would draw a value that never happened. Rate series are therefore one shorter than the value series — the charts are independent, so this is fine.
- **Emit counters must be free on the hot path**: atomics only, no lock, no allocation. `GaugeSnapshot` counts `len(points)`, every other metric call counts 1, `LogEvent` counts 1.
- **Nothing here is emitted as OTLP.** In-process introspection only.
- A monotonic total that appears to go backwards clamps its delta to 0 rather than drawing a negative rate.
- `runtime.ReadMemStats` stops the world briefly — it runs only on the 10s sampler tick, never per HTTP request.
- Sampler state must be nil-safe and empty-safe: a `Server` built but never `Start`ed renders "collecting…" rather than panicking.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `internal/telemetry`: `atomic.Uint64` emit counters on `otelEmitter` + `Throughput()` accessor on the emitter and on `*Provider`
- [ ] `internal/admin/sampler.go`: sampler with rings for goroutines, heap, GC rate, active series, emit rates, failing count, mean duration, and per-(tenant, workload) headroom
- [ ] Sampler launched from `Server.Start`, immediate first sample then 10s ticker, stops with ctx
- [ ] `Status` JSON gains `runtime`, `throughput`, `fleet`, `cardinality` blocks; `RateLimitStatus` gains `headroom_series`
- [ ] `registerChart`/`drawChart` framework + chart CSS ported into `page.html.tmpl`
- [ ] Overview renders both trend sections with all seven chart ids and their stat cards
- [ ] Throttle panel renders a headroom sparkline per workload row
- [ ] Tests: rate differencing (first sample, unmoved counter, backwards counter), fleet aggregation, ring truncation, JSON field presence, HTML render assertions for the new chart ids and headings
- [ ] `make check` green

## Out of scope

- Emitting any of these as OTLP metrics — `graph2otel.*` self-obs already covers what belongs on the wire.
- Persisting history across restarts. These rings are deliberately in-process and bounded.

comments.body:
Landed in `e4a7439`, `make check` green (0 lint issues, no vulnerabilities).

**What shipped**

| chart id | series | source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `chGoroutines` | goroutines | `runtime.NumGoroutine()` |
| `chHeap` | heap in use (MiB) | `MemStats.HeapAlloc` |
| `chGC` | GC cycles/sec | `MemStats.NumGC` differenced over elapsed wall time |
| `chEmit` | metric points/sec + log records/sec | `atomic.Uint64` counters on `*otelEmitter`, differenced |
| `chCard` | total active series | `telemetry.CardinalityTracker.Snapshot()` |
| `chFailing` | collectors failing | `collector.StatusTracker` summed across tenants |
| `chDuration` | mean run duration (ms) | same, mean of `LastDuration` over collectors that have run |

Plus a headroom sparkline column per `(tenant, workload)` row on the throttle panel, from `WorkloadLimiter.Snapshot`.

**Design points worth keeping**

- Counting sits on the innermost `otelEmitter`, not the decorators, so a record passing through `WithTenant` → `WithTransport` → emitter is counted exactly once. `Histogram` delegates to `HistogramCtx`, so only `HistogramCtx` counts — counting both would double every histogram.
- Rate series start at the **second** sample and are one shorter than the value series. A 0 for the first sample would draw a throughput dip that never happened.
- Zero elapsed records no rate at all (not +Inf); a backwards total clamps to 0 (not a negative rate).
- A registered collector with no run record is **pending**, never failing — a starting process must not read as a broken one.
- `Status.SeriesTrend` is deliberately not named `Cardinality`: `pageModel` already has a `Cardinality` field (the tab view), and an embedded `Status.Cardinality` would be silently shadowed in every template expression.
- `sparkline` is now generic over `~int64 | ~float64` with two named entry points (`sparkline`/`sparklineF`) because `html/template` cannot call a generic function.
- `admin.New` gained a 7th parameter (`ThroughputSource`); `*telemetry.Provider` satisfies it, nil is safe.

**Not done, deliberately**

- None of these are emitted as OTLP. The `graph2otel.*` self-obs metrics already carry what belongs on the wire.
- No persistence across restarts. The rings are in-process and bounded on purpose.

The matching ports to opnsense-exporter and tailscale2otel (everything except throttle headroom, which has no sibling analogue) are tracked separately in those repos.

body:
## What

`intune.device_startup` (the per-boot twin added in `4a976fc`, #225) emits records that **never appear in Loki**, and nothing anywhere reports a failure. Every other twin added in the same commit landed on the first poll.

It is the only one of the five stamped with a **backdated event time** rather than poll time, which makes the timestamp the prime suspect — and makes this a problem for any future event-stamped collector, not just this one.

## Evidence — camden `version=8a131c0`, 2026-07-21

The sub-fetch demonstrably ran and processed all three rows. Live wire at the time of the poll:

```
2026-07-19T21:23:25Z  update   totalBootTimeInMs=36135   totalLoginTimeInMs=-1
2026-07-20T03:45:25Z  update   totalBootTimeInMs=24031
2026-07-19T20:53:06Z  unknown  totalBootTimeInMs=-1      totalLoginTimeInMs=160761
```

The histograms from that same loop iteration are in Grafana Cloud and are exactly right:

```
sum(intune_uxa_boot_time_ms_milliseconds_count)  = 2       (36135 + 24031, the -1 excluded)
sum(intune_uxa_boot_time_ms_milliseconds_sum)    = 60166
sum(intune_uxa_login_time_ms_milliseconds_count) = 1
sum(intune_uxa_login_time_ms_milliseconds_sum)   = 160761
```

`e.LogEvent` is called unconditionally immediately after those `e.Histogram` calls in the same loop body (`endpointanalytics.go`, `collectStartupHistories`), so three log records were emitted. In Loki, over every window tried:

```
{service_name="graph2otel"} | event_name="intune.device_startup"        --since 30m   -> 0
                                                                        --since 96h   -> 0
                                          --from 2026-07-19 --to 2026-07-21           -> 0
{service_name="graph2otel"} |= "device startup:"                        --since 168h  -> 0
```

Contrast, same collector, same poll, same emitter — all present:

| twin | records | timestamp |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `intune.device_startup_process` | 10 | poll time |
| `intune.device_battery_health` | 1 | poll time |
| `intune.device_app_health` | 1 | poll time |
| `intune.device_resource_performance` | 0 | n/a — segment genuinely empty |
| **`intune.device_startup`** | **0** | **backdated 1–2 days** |

`intune.hardware_inventory`'s twin (poll time) also landed on the same push, 9 of 9 devices.

## Ruled out

- **Not an emitter gate.** `otelEmitter.LogEvent` sets the timestamp when non-zero and emits; there is no freshness/age check anywhere in `internal/telemetry` or `internal/collector/scheduler.go`.
- **Not twin suppression.** `internal/collectors/twinsuppress.go` covers the #135-C blob-vs-polled pairs only; this event is not in it.
- **Not an export error.** No OTLP/export error in the camden container logs; the only WARNs are unrelated `cert_inventory` enum warnings.
- **Not "Loki rejects all backdated records."** `intune.epm_elevation_events` holds 43 records timestamped 2026-07-14 → 2026-07-19, so old timestamps do land — though note those may have been backdated only by hours *at the moment of ingestion*, which is the distinction that matters and which this evidence does not settle.

## Leading hypothesis

Grafana Cloud's OTLP log ingestion silently drops records whose timestamp is further in the past than some accepted window, with no error propagated back to the SDK. If true, the practical limit is somewhere under ~40h.

The distinction to test is **backdate-at-ingestion-time**, not absolute record age: `epm_elevation_events` accumulated its old-looking records gradually, so it may never have pushed a record more than a few hours behind wall clock.

## Proposed controlled test

Emit two records differing only in timestamp — one at poll time, one backdated by N hours — and binary-search N. Do this against a **scratch `service_name`**, not the production stream, so the corpus is not polluted. If the drop is confirmed and the threshold found, the options are:

1. Accept it and document the horizon in `docs/signals.md` — event-stamped collectors lose anything older than the window.
2. Clamp: emit at poll time when the event time is older than the horizon, carrying the true time as an attribute (`event_time`) so nothing is lost or misdated. This keeps CLAUDE.md's rule intact — the record is not *claimed* to have happened now, the real time is right there on the record.
3. Drop deliberately and count it, so the loss is visible in `graph2otel.*` self-observability rather than silent.

Option 2 is probably right, but the measurement comes first.

## Why this matters beyond one twin

CLAUDE.md's rule is that a record with no parseable event time must be dropped, never stamped on arrival, because stamping on arrival silently claims it happened now. This issue is the mirror image: stamping with the true event time silently **loses** the record. Both failure modes are invisible at the collector — `last_success=true`, no error, no metric — which is the property that makes it worth a gate rather than a comment.

Every currently event-stamped collector should be checked against this once the horizon is known, starting with `intune.epm_elevation_events`, `intune.autopilot_events` and `m365.activity`.

Found during deploy-verification of #225.
