## Measured: the drop is real, silent, absolute, and the horizon is ~4h20m — not ~40h

Ran the controlled test this issue proposed, against scratch `service_name`s so the production corpus stays clean. `[live-measured 2026-07-22, #226, n=3 runs]`

**Method.** A standalone Go program using the same exporter and SDK versions graph2otel ships (`otlploghttp` v0.20.0, `sdk/log` v0.20.0), pushing to the same Grafana Cloud OTLP gateway (`prod-gb-south-1`, instance <grafana-stack-id>) with the same basic-auth header construction. Each record differs only in `SetTimestamp`, carrying its intended backdate as an attribute. Two stream shapes per run:

- **Run A** — faithful to production: emit one record at wall-clock now, flush, wait, *then* push the backdated records into that established stream.
- **Run B** — a virgin stream, backdated records pushed oldest-first, no fresh record to set the head.

### Result 1 — the horizon is absolute, not relative to the stream head

Runs A and B dropped and kept **exactly the same records**. A virgin stream whose first entry is 72h old behaves identically to a stream whose head is at now.

| backdate | 0 | 15m | 45m | 75m | 90m | 3h | 6h | 12h | 24h | 48h | 72h |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| landed | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ |

This **refutes the leading hypothesis in the body**. The suspicion was Loki out-of-order rejection relative to the stream head (`max_chunk_age/2`), which would have made the single-stream design — `service_name` as the only stream label — the root cause. It is not. Stream head is irrelevant; the cutoff is measured against wall clock.

It also revises the estimate: the body guessed "somewhere under ~40h". The real horizon is **an order of magnitude tighter**.

### Result 2 — the boundary, to 2-minute resolution

Two further sweeps narrowed it:

| sweep | landed | dropped |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 3h → 6h, 15m steps | 180, 210, 225, 240, 255 | 270, 285, 300, 330, 360 |
| 255 → 275, 2m steps | 255, 257, 259 | 261, 263, 265, 267, 269, 271, 275 |

**Practical horizon ≈ 260 minutes (4h20m).**

One caveat stated honestly rather than smoothed over: those two sweeps ran 39 seconds apart, so they **cannot distinguish a fixed age (~260 min) from a fixed wall-clock instant (~09:00Z that day)**. Both fit the data exactly. A repeat sweep separated by ≥30 minutes discriminates them — if the boundary in minutes grows by the elapsed time it is an instant, if it holds at ~260 it is an age. Doing that before anything is written into `docs/signals.md`; an unverified horizon in a reference doc is precisely the rot this project keeps paying for.

### Result 3 — the SDK reports success for records that are discarded

`otel.SetErrorHandler` was wired to print in the probe. Across all three runs and every dropped record: **zero errors**. `ForceFlush` returned nil each time. The OTLP gateway accepts the push and the records are discarded downstream with nothing propagated back.

So "no error in the camden container logs" is not evidence the push worked — it is the expected observation either way. Worth noting separately: **graph2otel never calls `otel.SetErrorHandler`** (`grep` across the tree finds only `otel.Handle` call sites in `internal/telemetry/emitter.go`), so export errors land on the OTel default handler and stderr rather than the app's structured logger. That is a second, independent gap in the same blind spot.

### What this means for the fix

The body's option 2 (clamp, carry the true time as an attribute) is the right call and the measurement does not change it — but it does change the parameter. A horizon of ~4h20m means the affected set is much wider than one twin: **any collector emitting an event more than ~4 hours old is losing records silently today**, including on a normal poll cycle where an API returns a record from earlier in the day.

Building: a clamp at the emitter boundary with the true time preserved on the record, a counter so the loss stops being invisible, and a configurable horizon (self-managed Loki will have a different limit). Details to follow on the completing commit.

## RETRACTION — my previous comment on this issue is WRONG, and so was this issue's premise

Both the "~4h20m horizon" I reported above and the original report are refuted. Recording this in full because the same mistake was made twice on the same issue, by two different investigations, and it is cheap to make a third time.

### The headline: `intune.device_startup` IS in production Loki

Queried live today:

```logql
{service_name="graph2otel"} | event_name=`intune.device_startup`   --from now-7d
-> "device startup: category=update total_boot=24031ms"  (records present)
```

The records were never dropped. **This issue describes a defect that does not exist.**

### What my "~4h20m horizon" actually was: querying too early

Every sweep in the comment above was queried within seconds of the push. Backdated records are indexed through a **late-data path** — they carry a `__time_shard__` label — and are not queryable for some minutes after being accepted. I read "not yet visible" as "dropped" and then built a boundary, a step-function hypothesis and a wall-clock instant on top of it.

Re-queried hours later, **every record I recorded as dropped was present**:

| run | I reported dropped | actually landed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 15m…72h sweep | 6h, 12h, 24h, 48h, 72h | 0, 15m, 45m, 75m, 90m, 3h, 6h, 12h, 24h, 48h, 72h |
| 3h→6h sweep | 270, 285, 300, 330, 360 | all of 180…360 |
| 255→275 sweep | 261, 263, 265, 267, 269, 271, 275 | all of 255…275 |
| virgin-stream, old-only | everything | 360, 720, 1440, 2880, 4320 |

A second, independent error compounded it: one of my rechecks used `count_over_time({…}[24h])`, whose 24h range excludes 2–3 day old records **by the query**, which is what briefly made it look like there was a cutoff between 12h and 24h.

Two conclusions from that comment survive and two do not:

- ✅ **Absolute, not relative to the stream head** — a virgin stream and the production-shaped stream behaved identically. Still true.
- ✅ **`otel.SetErrorHandler` is never called** in graph2otel. Still true, still a real gap.
- ❌ **"~4h20m horizon"** — does not exist. Withdrawn entirely.
- ❌ **"the SDK reports success for every discarded record"** — false. See below.

### The real behaviour, measured properly

Pushing records at 7d and 14d produced an immediate, explicit rejection naming the limit:

```text
400 Bad Request: entry for stream '{service_name="g2o-tsprobe-b-deep1"}' has timestamp
too old: 2026-07-08T13:05:10Z, oldest acceptable timestamp is: 2026-07-15T13:05:10Z
```

`[live-measured 2026-07-22, #226]`

- **The accept window is exactly 7 days** (`now - 168h`), stated by the gateway itself.
- **Rejection is loud**, reaching the OTel error handler and stderr. It is not silent.
- **Rejection is per-ENTRY, not per-batch.** That same push had 12h/1d/2d/3d accepted while only the 7d and 14d entries were refused — so one over-old record cannot poison a batch of good ones.

### What shipped, and what was reverted

`9a3efc0` added a clamp relocating records older than 3h. **Reverted in `65ce1ff`.** With a real 7-day window, a 3h default would have relocated every record aged 3h–7d that the backend accepts perfectly well — `m365.activity`, `intune.epm_elevation_events`, every backfilling window collector — destroying the true event time of records that were never at risk, invisibly. That is a worse defect than the one it was built to fix, and it would have looked like it was working.

Two things from that commit were independently verified and are kept:

- **`backendAcceptWindow` 13d → 7d.** It was a maintainer estimate (#118) and is now pinned to the wire with the rejection body quoted in the source. Right order of magnitude, wrong number — and while it was 13d the warning it drives could only fire past 13 days.
- **#230**, the `telemetrytest` recorder bug (every non-string log attribute value captured as `""`), found while testing the now-reverted code. Real, unrelated, fixed.

### The durable lesson

**An empty Loki query is not evidence of a drop.** The explicit 400 is. Nothing distinguishes "accepted but not yet indexed" from "discarded" at the moment you look, and both this issue's premise and my investigation of it died on exactly that. Written into `docs/signals.md` and CLAUDE.md rather than left on the issue, because the next person to deploy-verify an event-stamped collector will hit it within minutes of a poll.

Closing stays correct — there is no defect here — but the reasoning on `9a3efc0`'s "Closes #226" was wrong, and this comment is the record of why.

title: intune.device_startup twin never lands in Loki — event-time-stamped log records may be silently dropped when backdated

body:
> **CORRECTED 2026-07-21 — read [this comment](https://github.com/rknightion/graph2otel/issues/225#issuecomment-5034836074) before the body below.**
> The body asserts a #114 hard-rule violation. **That is wrong and is retracted.** `intune.endpoint_analytics` is one of only two collectors #114 audited as a *deliberate* no-twin exception, recorded in `docs/pii-cardinality-audit.md` specifically so a later sweep would not re-litigate it — which is what this issue did.
> The field-count evidence below is accurate; the conclusion drawn from it is not. What survives: (1) the audit doc was factually stale and is now fixed, (2) `AppHealthDevicePerformance` is genuinely uncollected and is new coverage, (3) where the exception line now sits is an open maintainer decision, since #179 and #194 already overrode it for two sub-fetches without recording why.

## What & why

`intune.endpoint_analytics` fetches per-device rows in four sub-fetches, buckets them into a histogram or a count, and **discards every other field**. That is the exact shape #114 declares a bug: *"A collector that fetches per-entity rows, buckets a count, and discards the rest is a bug: it can answer 'how many' but never 'which one'."*

Concretely, on a tenant with one battery-reporting device, graph2otel today can tell you *that* one device is at battery-health score 63 — but not that it is `LAPHAM`, not that the battery is `179` days old, and not that it holds `100%` max capacity with an `80` minute estimated runtime. All of that is on the wire, in the same response, already paid for.

This is the fifth instance of the lineage the #110–#115 sweep was meant to end, so the framing matters: **"already aggregated into a metric" was never a reason to drop the entity.**

## Evidence — what is fetched vs what survives

`GET beta/deviceManagement/userExperienceAnalyticsBatteryHealthDevicePerformance`, verbatim live row `[live-measured 2026-07-21, n=1 tenant]`:

```json
{"id":"b740c02b-…","deviceId":"d5900d67-…","deviceName":"LAPHAM","model":"Standard",
 "manufacturer":"PCSpecialist","deviceModelName":"Standard","deviceManufacturerName":"PCSpecialist",
 "maxCapacityPercentage":100,"estimatedRuntimeInMinutes":80,"batteryAgeInDays":179,
 "fullBatteryDrainCount":-1,"deviceBatteryCount":1,"deviceBatteryTags":[],
 "deviceBatteryHealthScore":63,"healthStatus":"meetingGoals",
 "deviceBatteriesDetails":[{"batteryId":"LiON;52245;OEM;0","maxCapacityPercentage":100,"fullBatteryDrainCount":0}]}
```

`batteryHealthPerformance` decodes **2 of 15 fields** (`deviceBatteryHealthScore`, `healthStatus`). **13 are dropped**, including every field that identifies the device or explains the score.

| sub-fetch | per-entity rows | twin today | verdict |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `collectDeviceScores` | per device | **yes** (`endpointanalytics.go:484`) | correct — the reference shape |
| `collectWorkFromAnywhere` | per device | **yes** (line 720) | correct |
| `collectBatteryHealth` | per device | **no** | 13 of 15 fields dropped |
| `collectStartupHistories` | per boot event | **no** | drops `deviceId`, `startTime`, `restartStopCode`, `restartFaultBucket`, `operatingSystemVersion`, `isFirstLogin`, `isFeatureUpdate`, and the boot-phase breakdown |
| `collectResourcePerformance` | per device | **no** | 0 rows today, same shape as battery |
| `collectAppHealth` | per app | **no** | additionally silently drops every app outside a hardcoded allow-list |
| `collectBaselines` / `collectAnomalySeverityOverview` / `collectAppHealthOSVersion` | bounded aggregates | n/a | correct by design |

`restartStopCode` / `restartFaultBucket` are the sharpest loss: those are Windows crash-bucket identifiers, the field you would actually alert on, and they are fetched and thrown away every cycle.

## Related: a live surface that is not collected at all

`GET beta/deviceManagement/userExperienceAnalyticsAppHealthDevicePerformance` returns a live row today and appears in no sub-fetch:

```json
{"deviceId":"d5900d67-…","deviceDisplayName":"LAPHAM","deviceModel":"Standard",
 "deviceManufacturer":"PCSpecialist","appCrashCount":0,"crashedAppCount":0,"appHangCount":0,
 "meanTimeToFailureInMinutes":2147483647,"deviceAppHealthScore":100.0,
 "deviceAppHealthStatus":"TBD","healthStatus":"meetingGoals","processedDateTime":"2026-07-20T03:05:36Z"}
```

This carries `appHangCount` and `meanTimeToFailureInMinutes` — **literally #194's 4th scope checkbox**, which is parked there because the *application*-level segment (`AppHealthApplicationPerformance`) is empty under the 5-device floor. The **device**-level equivalent has data now. That checkbox is partially unblockable without waiting on the fleet.

(`deviceAppHealthStatus: "TBD"` is the same undocumented wire status already bucketed to `other` by `collectAppHealthOSVersion`; the int32-max MTTF sentinel is already handled there too.)

## The bit that changes #194's battery verdict

#194 parks `BatteryHealthModelPerformance` and `BatteryHealthOsPerformance` as blocked on "≥5 battery-bearing devices", and I proposed moving them to the permanent-gap ledger since m7kni will not reach five laptops.

That proposal is **withdrawn**. Those endpoints are *Microsoft's* rollup of per-device data **we already hold** — `BatteryHealthDevicePerformance` carries `model` and `manufacturer` on every row. The 5-device floor is Microsoft's statistical-significance threshold for publishing *their* aggregate; it is not a limit on data availability. graph2otel can compute a model-keyed or OS-keyed battery rollup itself, from one device or a thousand, with no floor.

**Caveat to respect if this is built:** a locally-computed rollup will not necessarily match Microsoft's numbers — the statistic they use (mean vs median), their sentinel handling, and their inclusion rules are all unknown. So it must not be named or documented as parity with `BatteryHealthModelPerformance`. Emit it under a distinct name as graph2otel's own aggregation, and say so in the description.

## Scope

- [ ] Log twin on `collectBatteryHealth` — one record per device carrying identity, `batteryAgeInDays`, `maxCapacityPercentage`, `estimatedRuntimeInMinutes`, `deviceBatteryCount`, and the per-battery `deviceBatteriesDetails`. WARN when the score is below goal.
- [ ] Log twin on `collectStartupHistories` — one record per boot event, carrying `restartCategory`, `restartStopCode`, `restartFaultBucket`, the boot-phase breakdown, and `startTime` as the event timestamp.
- [ ] Log twin on `collectResourcePerformance` (0 rows today — build only when a live row exists, per the map-against-live-samples rule).
- [ ] `collectAppHealth`: stop silently discarding non-allow-listed apps — the allow-list may bound the *metric*, it must not bound the twin.
- [ ] Add `userExperienceAnalyticsAppHealthDevicePerformance` as a sub-fetch (live row available); tick #194's app-health checkbox to the extent this covers it.
- [ ] Optional, decide separately: graph2otel-computed battery rollup by model / OS version, under its own name, with the non-parity caveat documented.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Every per-entity field fetched either reaches a metric as a bounded label or reaches the twin — nothing fetched is dropped (#114). Guard tests pin it per sub-fetch.
- [ ] No device identity, model, serial or battery id becomes a metric label (#112).
- [ ] Mapped against the verbatim live rows above, not docs (#142).
- [ ] `-1` and int32-max sentinels excluded from both metrics and twins — coordinate with #224, which fixes the histogram half.
- [ ] `docs/collectors.md` + goldens regenerated; `make check` green; deploy-verified on camden with real rows in Loki, not empty-success.

Refs #194, #199, #114, #112, #224.

comments.body:
## Correction: this issue's central claim was wrong. `intune.endpoint_analytics` is an AUDITED no-twin exception, not an oversight.

I filed this asserting a #114 hard-rule violation. That framing is **retracted**. #114 audited this exact collector and put it in its LOW / recommend-closing-as-won't-do section:

> **`intune.gpoanalytics`** / **`intune.endpointanalytics`** — migration readiness / device perf-UX scoring; not SIEM-shaped.

and `docs/pii-cardinality-audit.md` records it as one of only two deliberate exceptions, with the rationale, explicitly so that a later sweep would not re-litigate it:

> **Two are audited, deliberate exceptions with no twin** — recorded here so a future sweep does not re-litigate them […]
> - `intune.endpointanalytics` — boot/startup performance is an ops question; the Intune console answers it better.

The package source says the same: `startupHistory` rows are described as "a per-BOOT firehose that keeps its #114-audited no-twin exception". I read that comment only after filing. **I was the future sweep re-litigating a settled decision** — precisely the failure mode #114 wrote that paragraph to prevent. The bare field-count evidence in the body (13 of 15 dropped) is accurate; the conclusion drawn from it was not.

## What IS a real finding: the audit doc is now factually stale

`docs/pii-cardinality-audit.md` states `intune.endpointanalytics` has **no twin**. That is no longer true, and has not been since #179:

| twin | EventName | added by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| per-device Endpoint Analytics scores | `intune.device_endpoint_analytics` | #179 |
| per-device Win11 upgrade readiness | `intune.device_work_from_anywhere` | #194 |

So two later maintainer decisions already overrode the audited exception for two sub-fetches, and the audit doc was never updated. That matters more than the original claim, because the same doc warns about exactly this:

> **A wrong claim in an audit doc does not just fail to catch a bug — it actively hides it from the next audit.** Check the source, not this file.

This is the second recorded rot in that document (the export-collector scope list rotted twice, corrected on #201 in `bfbe749`). It is a doc that is load-bearing for future audits and is not gated by anything.

## The genuine open question

The exception is no longer applied consistently, and no decision record says where the line now sits. Inside one collector:

| sub-fetch | per-entity rows | twin | status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `collectDeviceScores` | per device | yes | exception overridden (#179) |
| `collectWorkFromAnywhere` | per device | yes | exception overridden (#194) |
| `collectBatteryHealth` | per device | no | exception still applied |
| `collectStartupHistories` | per boot | no | exception still applied, explicitly |
| `collectResourcePerformance` | per device | no | moot — 0 rows on this tenant |

Nothing documents why device *scores* earned a twin but device *battery* did not. It is not a principled line, it is the order the issues happened to land in.

## Revised scope

The rule-violation framing is gone. What remains is one documentation fix (uncontested) and one maintainer decision.

- [ ] **Uncontested:** correct `docs/pii-cardinality-audit.md` — `intune.endpointanalytics` emits two twins; the "no twin" claim is stale. Record which sub-fetches are twinned and which remain excepted, so the line is written down rather than inferred.
- [ ] **Uncontested:** add `userExperienceAnalyticsAppHealthDevicePerformance` as a sub-fetch. It is **not collected at all today**, has a live row, and is new coverage rather than a twin decision. Bounded metric aggregates only, unless the decision below says otherwise. Partially unblocks #194's app-health checkbox, which is parked behind the empty *application*-level segment.
- [ ] **Needs a maintainer call:** does the audited exception stand for the remaining sub-fetches? Options, with the case for each:
  - **Keep the exception.** Battery/boot data is ops, the Intune console shows it, and #114's reasoning is undisturbed. Cost: graph2otel can say "one device scores 63" but never "LAPHAM's battery is 179 days old", and cannot chart per-device battery decay over time — which the console genuinely does not do, since it shows current state, not history.
  - **Twin battery only.** Low volume (one record per battery-bearing device per cycle), and the fields that explain the score (`batteryAgeInDays`, `maxCapacityPercentage`, `estimatedRuntimeInMinutes`) are the actionable half. Leaves the per-boot firehose excepted, which is the part #114's volume argument actually targets.
  - **Twin battery, and startup histories only for abnormal restarts.** Scope the boot twin to rows with a non-empty `restartFaultBucket` or an abnormal `restartCategory`, so the crash-diagnostic value is captured without the firehose. This is the pattern #114 itself endorsed for `entra.consent` ("emit the twin only for high-privilege classified grants"), so it is consistent with the audit rather than a carve-out from it.

My recommendation is the third: it respects the volume argument that motivated the exception while not discarding `restartStopCode` / `restartFaultBucket`, which are the only genuinely diagnostic fields in the set. But this is a data-model decision on an audited exception, so it should be an explicit call rather than something a build pass assumes.

Related: #224 (the sentinel half of this, now fixed in `1577068`), #114, #112, #194, #199.

## Shipped — exception withdrawn, every per-entity sub-fetch now twins (`4a976fc`)

Maintainer decision: override the #114 exception wholesale rather than scope it. Built and on `main`.

### New twins

| EventName | shape | carries |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `intune.device_battery_health` | per device, state | `battery_age_days`, `max_capacity_percentage`, `estimated_runtime_minutes`, `battery_count`, `battery_ids` (per-cell), score, health state |
| `intune.device_startup` | per BOOT, **event** | `restart_stop_code`, `restart_fault_bucket`, the full boot/login phase breakdown, `os_version`, `is_first_login`, `is_feature_update` |
| `intune.device_startup_process` | per (device, process) | `process_name`, `product_name`, `publisher`, `startup_impact_ms` |
| `intune.device_app_health` | per device, state | `app_crash_count`, `crashed_app_count`, `app_hang_count`, `device_app_health_score`, MTTF |
| `intune.device_resource_performance` | per device, state | CPU/RAM spike percentages, `total_ram_mb`, `cpu_display_name`, `disk_type`, `machine_type`, core count |

Three decisions worth recording, because they are not obvious from the diff:

**The boot twin is stamped with the row's own `startTime`, not poll time.** Every other twin in this collector is a state feed re-emitted each cycle and deliberately carries a zero timestamp. A boot is an event that happened at a specific instant; stamping it on arrival would pile every historical restart onto one moment and make "which device rebooted at 03:00" unanswerable. An unparseable `startTime` leaves the timestamp zero rather than defaulting to now — per CLAUDE.md, a record must never be stamped on arrival.

**`intune.device_startup_process` emits no metric at all.** The (device, process) pair is unbounded, so every aggregation shape would either grow with fleet size or need an arbitrary allow-list. A LogQL `topk` over `startup_impact_ms` answers the same question without a series per process.

**Boot twins raise to WARN only on crash evidence** — a non-empty `restart_fault_bucket`, or a stop code that is not `"0"`. A routine reboot stays INFO, so the WARN stream is the blue screens.

### Two sub-fetches were new

`userExperienceAnalyticsDeviceStartupProcesses` — recorded on #199 as route-blocked. It was not: the probe carried `$top`, which that segment rejects at any value. The bare list returns rows.

`userExperienceAnalyticsAppHealthDevicePerformance` — was not collected at all. It is the only live source of `appHangCount` and `meanTimeToFailureInMinutes` on a tenant under the 5-device Endpoint Analytics floor, which is exactly why #194 could not build them from the application-level segment. Also adds a bounded `intune.uxa.app_health.device_count{health_state}` gauge.

### Evidence classes, stated honestly

Battery, startup-history, startup-process and app-health mappings are pinned to **verbatim live rows** (m7kni, graph2otel-poller, 2026-07-21) held as test fixtures.

`resourcePerformance` is the exception: that segment returns 0 rows on m7kni, so its field names are **EDM-derived from the beta `$metadata`, not live-verified**. That is a weaker evidence class and it is marked as such in the source rather than dressed up. The exposure is bounded by construction — every field is emitted only when present, so a wrong name yields an absent attribute, never a wrong value.

### Doc

`docs/pii-cardinality-audit.md` no longer claims this collector has no twin. It now records the withdrawal, the full per-sub-fetch table, and why the original rationale did not survive. `entra.agreements` is now the only audited no-twin exception in the codebase.

The lesson kept in that file is about the document, not about endpoint analytics: a "do not re-open this" note with no mechanism to detect that it has gone stale is a trap for the next reader. It was reversed twice by later issues and stayed on the page unchanged both times.

Remaining on this issue: nothing. Closing once deploy-verified on camden.

## Deploy-verified on camden (`version=8a131c0`, 2026-07-21) — real data, with one exception

`intune.endpoint_analytics` and `intune.hardware_inventory` both `runs=1, last_success=true, last_error=none`.

### `intune.hardware_inventory` — 9 of 9 devices

```

```

All three device rollups sum to exactly **9**, which is the current live `managedDevices` count — **re-probed to confirm rather than assumed**. The tenant went 10 → 9 between this morning's probe and the deploy (`DESKTOP-MHTMHH4` and `DESKTOP-2F6PPF2` gone, `<device-1>` new — the Windows VMs are being rebuilt, see #194). The initial 9-vs-10 discrepancy was the fleet moving, not a dropped device: no skip warnings in the container log, and the twin carries 9 distinct `device_name`s matching the live list exactly.

Twin `intune.device_hardware`, 9 records, e.g. `MBP16` — `total_storage_bytes=2142114938880`, `free_storage_bytes=1611686477824`, `product_name=MacBookPro18,2`, `vbs_state=running`; `TampooniPad` — `battery_level_percentage=69`, `imei`, `esim_identifier`, `cellular_technology=GSM`. `tenant_id` stamped, `ingest_transport=graph`.

Note the Windows storage total (382 GiB across 2 devices) is smaller than macOS — the Linux host contributes **no** storage series at all, which is the deliberate zero-is-absent handling working: it reports `totalStorageSpace=0` on a machine that plainly has a disk.

### #224 sentinel fix — verified in production, precisely

```
sum(intune_uxa_boot_time_ms_milliseconds_count)  = 2       sum = 60166   (36135 + 24031)
sum(intune_uxa_login_time_ms_milliseconds_count) = 1       sum = 160761
```

Live wire at poll time was three boot rows: one with a real boot and a `-1` login, one with a real boot, one with a `-1` boot and a real login. The histograms took **exactly** the three real measurements and none of the three sentinels. Before the fix these would have read count=3/sum=60165 and count=3/sum=160759.

Note for anyone querying these: the normalized names are `intune_uxa_boot_time_ms_milliseconds_*` — #82 appends the unit, so the `_ms` in the metric name gets `_milliseconds` on top of it. Mildly ugly and pre-existing; not changed here.

### #225 twins

| twin | records | note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `intune.device_startup_process` | 10 | `MsMpEng` 8038ms, `MsSense` 4822ms, … |
| `intune.device_battery_health` | 1 | LAPHAM, age 179d, 100% max capacity, per-cell battery id |
| `intune.device_app_health` | 1 | LAPHAM, 0 crashes / 0 hangs, MTTF sentinel correctly omitted |
| `intune.device_resource_performance` | 0 | expected — segment is empty on this tenant |
| **`intune.device_startup`** | **0** | **NOT verified — see #226** |

### One thing is NOT working: `intune.device_startup`

Three records were emitted (the histograms from the same loop iteration prove the loop ran over all three rows) and **none reached Loki**, over every query window tried, with no error at the collector, the emitter, or the OTLP exporter. It is the only twin here stamped with a **backdated event time** rather than poll time.

Filed as **#226** with the full evidence and a proposed controlled test. Not closing #225 on a twin that cannot be shown to work — the other four are verified, that one is not.

The reason it is its own issue rather than a fix here: if backdated log records are being dropped, that is a pipeline-wide property affecting every event-stamped collector (`intune.epm_elevation_events`, `intune.autopilot_events`, `m365.activity`), and the horizon needs measuring before anything is changed.

## `intune.device_startup` verified in production — the last unverified twin. Closing.

This issue was held open on one thing: *"Not closing #225 on a twin that cannot be shown to work."* It can now be shown to work. `[live-measured 2026-07-22, #225]`

```logql
sum by (event_name) (count_over_time({service_name="graph2otel"} | event_name=~`intune.device_.*` [7d]))
```

| twin | records (7d) |
| --- | --- |
| `intune.device_startup_process` | 240 |
| `intune.device_app_health` | 24 |
| `intune.device_battery_health` | 24 |
| **`intune.device_startup`** | **13** |
| `intune.device_resource_performance` | 0 — expected, segment genuinely empty on this tenant |

The startup twin is not merely present, it is **correctly stamped**. A sampled record sits in Loki at `2026-07-20T03:45:25Z`, which is byte-for-byte the `startTime` of the boot row on the wire (`2026-07-20T03:45:25Z, update, totalBootTimeInMs=24031`) and matches its body `device startup: category=update total_boot=24031ms`. So the deliberate design decision recorded on the shipping comment — that a boot is an event stamped with its own `startTime` rather than poll time, unlike the four state twins — is doing exactly what it was meant to do. A record ~2.3 days old landed and kept its true position on the time axis.

### Why it looked broken

It was never broken. **#226 is refuted** (see [the retraction there](https://github.com/rknightion/graph2otel/issues/226#issuecomment-5046293337)): backdated records are indexed through a late-data path and are not queryable for some minutes after being accepted, so the deploy-verification query in the comment above ran before they were visible and returned zero rows. Nothing distinguishes that from a drop at the moment you look.

The real accept window is **7 days**, stated by the gateway in its rejection body, and rejection is a loud per-entry HTTP 400 — not silent. A boot record 1–2 days old was never at risk.

The trap is now written into `docs/signals.md` and CLAUDE.md, because it cost this issue a false blocker and then cost #226's investigation a fabricated "4h horizon" on top of it: **an empty Loki query is not evidence of a drop; the 400 is.**

### Issue state

All five twins from `4a976fc` are accounted for — four carrying live data, one legitimately empty. The doc correction and the `AppHealthDevicePerformance` sub-fetch both landed in that commit. Nothing remains open here.

body:
## What

`intune.endpoint_analytics`' `collectStartupHistories` feeds Endpoint Analytics' **`-1` "not enough data" sentinel** straight into two live histograms as if it were a real measurement:

- `intune.uxa.boot_time_ms` (`intune_uxa_boot_time_ms` after #82 normalization)
- `intune.uxa.login_time_ms`

`internal/collectors/intune/endpointanalytics/endpointanalytics.go:499-516` records both histograms unconditionally:

```go
e.Histogram(bootTimeMetric,  "ms", "...", h.TotalBootTimeInMs,  bootTimeBounds, attrs)
e.Histogram(loginTimeMetric, "ms", "...", h.TotalLoginTimeInMs, bootTimeBounds, attrs)
```

`telemetry.otelEmitter.HistogramCtx` (`internal/telemetry/emitter.go:165`) records whatever it is handed — there is no negative guard at the emitter boundary, by design.

## Evidence — live, and it is firing on every poll

`GET beta/deviceManagement/userExperienceAnalyticsDeviceStartupHistory` on m7kni returns exactly two rows, and **both carry a `-1`** `[live-measured 2026-07-21]`:

```json
{"deviceId":"1625d698-…","startTime":"2026-07-19T21:23:25Z","coreBootTimeInMs":2989,
 "groupPolicyBootTimeInMs":0,"featureUpdateBootTimeInMs":33146,"totalBootTimeInMs":36135,
 "groupPolicyLoginTimeInMs":-1,"coreLoginTimeInMs":-1,"responsiveDesktopTimeInMs":-1,
 "totalLoginTimeInMs":-1,"restartCategory":"update","operatingSystemVersion":"10.0.26200.8037"}

{"deviceId":"1625d698-…","startTime":"2026-07-19T20:53:06Z","coreBootTimeInMs":-1,
 "groupPolicyBootTimeInMs":-1,"featureUpdateBootTimeInMs":-1,"totalBootTimeInMs":-1,
 "groupPolicyLoginTimeInMs":-1,"coreLoginTimeInMs":160762,"responsiveDesktopTimeInMs":160760,
 "totalLoginTimeInMs":160761,"restartCategory":"unknown","operatingSystemVersion":""}
```

Row 1 has a valid boot time and a sentinel login time. Row 2 is the mirror image. So on the current tenant **each of the two histograms receives one real sample and one `-1` sample per cycle** — a 50% poisoning rate, recurring every poll, currently live on camden.

Effect: `_sum` is dragged down by 1ms per bad sample, `_count` overstates how many boots/logins were actually measured, and every derived average is wrong. A `-1` also lands in the lowest explicit bucket, so the distribution claims sub-millisecond boots that never happened. The failure is quiet — the numbers stay plausible.

## The collector already knows about this sentinel

`collectDeviceScores` handles it correctly, 30 lines above (`endpointanalytics.go:470`):

```go
if cs.score < 0 {
    continue // -1 = "not enough data" sentinel: excluded from the histogram AND omitted from the twin
}
```

`collectAppHealthOSVersion` similarly excludes the int32-max MTTF sentinel (`mttfNoFailuresSentinel`, line 87). `collectStartupHistories` is the one sub-fetch that was never given the guard. This is not an unknown-wire-shape problem — it is an inconsistently applied rule inside a single file.

## Fix

Skip the sentinel per-field, not per-row: row 1 has a genuine `totalBootTimeInMs` worth keeping and a sentinel `totalLoginTimeInMs` worth dropping, so dropping the whole row would discard real data. Follow `collectDeviceScores`' precedent — omit the observation, do not clamp to zero (a clamped `0ms` boot is as wrong as `-1`, just harder to notice).

## Acceptance

- [ ] TDD: a failing test first, fed both live rows verbatim as fixtures, asserting `intune.uxa.boot_time_ms` receives exactly ONE observation (36135) and `intune.uxa.login_time_ms` exactly ONE (160761).
- [ ] Guard applied per-field in `collectStartupHistories`; a row with sentinels in both fields emits nothing.
- [ ] Sweep the remaining sub-fetches for the same omission and fix or explicitly clear each: `collectBatteryHealth` (`deviceBatteryHealthScore`), `collectResourcePerformance` (`deviceResourcePerformanceScore`), `collectAppHealth` (`appCrashCount`). Note `fullBatteryDrainCount: -1` is live on the battery row today.
- [ ] `make check` green; deploy to camden and confirm the histograms no longer take a negative sample.

## Notes

Same family as #142 ("never invent wire values") inverted: here a value that IS on the wire is being taken literally when it is a control code. Worth an entry in `docs/graph-api-gotchas.md` — Endpoint Analytics uses `-1` for "not enough data" across `deviceScores`, `startupHistory` and `batteryHealthDevicePerformance`, and int32-max for "no failures observed" on MTTF fields. Two sentinels, two meanings, both look like measurements.

Found while re-probing #194/#199 parked surfaces.

body:
## What & why

`intune.settings_catalog` lists security baselines with:

```
GET beta/deviceManagement/templates?$filter=templateType eq 'securityBaseline'
```

That matches **one of the three** security-baseline templates on m7kni. Live, as `graph2otel-poller`, 2026-07-21:

| template | `templateType` | matched by the filter? | `deviceStateSummary` on the cast path |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| MDM Security Baseline for Windows 10 and later for November 2021 | `securityBaseline` | yes | 200 |
| Microsoft Defender for Endpoint baseline | `advancedThreatProtectionSecurityBaseline` | **no** | **200** |
| Microsoft Edge baseline | `microsoftEdgeSecurityBaseline` | **no** | **200** |

Both unmatched templates answer 200 on `.../templates/{id}/microsoft.graph.securityBaselineTemplate/deviceStateSummary` with the same six-field `securityBaselineStateSummary` shape the collector now decodes correctly (#222) — all counts 0 on this tenant, since nothing is assigned. So this is pure under-coverage, not a shape problem: two thirds of the tenant's security baselines have no compliance series at all, and nothing says so.

Discovered while verifying #222. `templateType` is an enum with several baseline-flavoured members rather than one, and the filter treats it as if there were only one.

## The decision to make

Deliberately left open rather than guessed at:

- **Filter by `@odata.type`** (`#microsoft.graph.securityBaselineTemplate`) instead of `templateType`. That is precisely the set for which the cast path is valid, so it is the definition that matches the request being made. Needs checking that Graph accepts an `isof`/type filter here, or that client-side filtering of the full templates list is acceptable (16 templates on this tenant).
- **Enumerate the baseline `templateType` members** explicitly. Straightforward, but it re-freezes a list that will rot the next time Microsoft adds a baseline flavour — the same failure mode as the export-collector doc lists (see #201).

Recommendation: the first, with the wire behaviour verified before implementing.

## Acceptance

- [ ] All three m7kni baselines emit `intune.security_baseline.devices` series.
- [ ] The selection rule cannot silently miss a future baseline type, or fails loudly if it does.
- [ ] `make check` green; deployed and verified on camden.

Refs #222, #220.

body:
## What & why

`intune.settings_catalog`'s security-baseline sub-signal has **two defects that stack**, so it has never emitted a single correct data point. Both are live-measured as `graph2otel-poller` against m7kni, 2026-07-21, and both were surfaced by the new beta drift canary (#220) while slicing the EDM.

### 1. The URL 400s on every run — the sub-signal emits nothing at all

`settingscatalog.go` requests `GET beta/deviceManagement/templates/{id}/deviceStateSummary`. On the wire that is:

```
400 BadRequest — Resource not found for the segment 'deviceStateSummary'.
```

`deviceStateSummary` is bound on the **derived** type, so it needs a cast segment. Live-verified working path:

```
GET beta/deviceManagement/templates/{id}/microsoft.graph.securityBaselineTemplate/deviceStateSummary
→ 200 {"id":"2209e067-…","secureCount":0,"notSecureCount":0,"unknownCount":0,"errorCount":0,"conflictCount":0,"notApplicableCount":0}
```

This is visible in production right now — camden logs the graceful skip on **every** cycle:

```
level=INFO msg="settingscatalog: security baseline deviceStateSummary unavailable; skipping"
  collector=intune.settings_catalog baseline_name="MDM Security Baseline for Windows 10 and later for November 2021"
  error="… status 400 … Resource not found for the segment 'deviceStateSummary'."
```

The graceful skip is why this never looked like a failure: it degrades to silence, and silence is indistinguishable from a healthy tenant with nothing to report.

### 2. Every field name in the decode struct is wrong — so even a fixed URL yields all zeros

`baselineDeviceStateSummary` (settingscatalog.go:414-421) decodes `secureDeviceCount` / `notSecureDeviceCount` / `unknownDeviceCount` / `notApplicableDeviceCount` / `errorDeviceCount` / `conflictDeviceCount`. The wire — and the beta EDM — say **`secureCount` / `notSecureCount` / `unknownCount` / `notApplicableCount` / `errorCount` / `conflictCount`**, with no `Device` infix on any of them.

The code comment cites Microsoft's documentation for the `*DeviceCount` names. The EDM has no `securityBaselineDeviceStateSummary` type at all: `deviceStateSummary` on `securityBaselineTemplate` binds to `microsoft.graph.securityBaselineStateSummary`, whose six properties are the names above. **Wire over docs, again.**

Had the URL been correct, this would have been the worse bug of the two: six gauges reporting a confident, permanent zero for the security posture of every baseline.

## Scope

- [ ] Fix the request path to use the `microsoft.graph.securityBaselineTemplate` cast segment.
- [ ] Fix the six JSON field names to the live wire names.
- [ ] Test against the **verbatim live 200 response body** above, so the mapping is pinned to the wire and not re-derived from docs.
- [ ] Keep the graceful skip for genuinely unavailable templates — but make sure a 400 on the *primary* path can no longer masquerade as "this tenant has no baselines".

## Acceptance

- [ ] `make check` green.
- [ ] Deployed to camden and the 400 is gone from the logs, with the gauge emitting real (possibly zero-valued) series.

Note the counts are genuinely 0 on m7kni — no devices are assigned to those three baselines — so post-fix the values stay 0, but for the honest reason, and the request stops erroring. Found via #220.

comments.body:
## Fixed, deployed, verified (camden `version=15d2f16`, 2026-07-21)

**The 400 is gone.** It previously logged on every cycle for every baseline; the running container now reports **zero** occurrences of `security baseline deviceStateSummary unavailable`, and `intune.settings_catalog` logs nothing at all — no warnings, no skips.

**The gauge emits for the first time.** Six series in Grafana Cloud where there were none:

```
intune_security_baseline_devices{baseline_name="MDM Security Baseline for Windows 10 and later for November 2021", state="secure"}          0
                                                                                                                  state="not_secure"      0
                                                                                                                  state="error"           0
                                                                                                                  state="conflict"        0
                                                                                                                  state="not_applicable"  0
                                                                                                                  state="unknown"         0
```

The values are genuinely 0 — nothing is assigned to that baseline on m7kni — but they are now an *honest* zero from correctly-decoded wire fields, rather than the two-layer silence they were before. That distinction is the whole bug: the old test asserted zero emitted points and passed happily.

**A related gap this surfaced, filed separately as #223:** the collector lists baselines with `$filter=templateType eq 'securityBaseline'`, which matches **1 of the 3** security-baseline templates on this tenant. The other two (`advancedThreatProtectionSecurityBaseline`, `microsoftEdgeSecurityBaseline`) both return 200 on the same cast path and are silently uncovered.

body:
## What & why

Both fleet siblings run **daily upstream-API canaries** that catch API changes before they silently
break collectors (opnsense `cmd/apidrift` + `live-canary.yml` + 172 reflected golden schemas, and
`cmd/apicontract` + `api-contract.yml`; tailscale `tools/apidrift` + `api-drift.yml` spec-diff +
`live-contract.yml`). graph2otel has **no upstream drift testing at all** — its `internal/signalcapture`
goldens (#140) gate *emitted* signals, not the *upstream* Graph surface.

## Scope decision — beta-only

Graph **`v1.0` is contractually stable** (Microsoft rarely breaks it), so drift value concentrates on
the **beta** endpoints graph2otel consumes (sign-ins non-interactive/SP/MI, several Intune reports,
recommendations, etc. — all the `Experimental()` / `BaseURLOverride` collectors). Scope the canary to
the consumed beta operations, mirroring tailscale2otel's "consumed operations" scoping.

## Approach — spec-diff, not live-payload golden

- Commit a snapshot of the consumed Graph surface. Microsoft publishes OpenAPI + CSDL `$metadata` for
  v1.0 and beta, so a tailscale-style spec-diff is directly portable.
- A `tools/graphdrift`-equivalent scoped to the consumed beta operations; non-zero exit on drift →
  file/resolve a tracking issue (the t2o pattern).
- A scheduled workflow (daily).

## Explicitly NOT in scope

- The opnsense **live-payload-structure** canary (a test tenant + app credentials in CI secrets,
  validating real payloads against structs daily) is heavier and needs standing CI credentials. Do the
  spec-diff first; only consider live-payload if the spec-diff proves insufficient.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Committed Microsoft Graph **beta** spec snapshot (OpenAPI/CSDL) for the consumed operations
- [ ] `tools/graphdrift`-equivalent diffs the live spec vs the snapshot, non-zero exit on drift
- [ ] A scheduled workflow runs daily and files/updates a tracking issue on drift
- [ ] Docs state which endpoints the canary covers and why v1.0 is excluded

---
_Filed 2026-07-20 from a three-way fleet-parity audit of graph2otel vs `opnsense-exporter` and `tailscale2otel`. **v1.0 gate** (per #79's standing rule that every open issue gates the release). Parent tracker #79; release checklist #35._

comments.body:
## Shipped — `f6a957a`

All four acceptance boxes met. Detail on the decisions that mattered:

**Snapshot source: the live CSDL, not the OpenAPI mirror.** `GET https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/$metadata` returns 200 **anonymously** (no tenant credentials — verified, which is what makes a daily unattended job possible), 7,235,035 bytes of XML. Chosen over `microsoftgraph/msgraph-metadata` because it is what the service serves about itself rather than a downstream conversion on a lag, and because the EDM is *walkable*: entity sets and singletons bind to types and navigation properties chain, so a consumed path resolves to a type by construction instead of by string-matching a synthesized operation id.

**Slicing.** `spec/graph-beta-surface.json` declares only paths; the tool resolves each through the EDM (entity set/singleton → key segments → derived-type casts → navigation properties up the base chain → bound functions) and captures the resolved type, its base chain, and the complex/enum types its own properties reference. Navigation targets are deliberately **not** followed — that pulls in most of the 5,801-type document. Result: **60 operations, 145 types, a 97 KB committed snapshot** instead of 7.2 MB. The snapshot records no schema version and no timestamp, so nothing churns unless the contract actually moves.

**Noise control** is what decides whether a canary gets read or muted. Breaking (exit 3, files/updates one tracking issue, fails the run): type or property removed, property retyped, base type or kind changed, enum member removed, a path that stops resolving or resolves elsewhere. Info (exit 0, reported, never fires): anything **added**. Additive movement is the normal shape of beta churn and cannot break a decoder.

**Two gates keep the manifest honest, and both were verified to bite** rather than assumed to:
- `TestBetaSurfaceManifestCoversEveryBetaConsumer` scans non-test Go via `go/ast` **string literals** (not grep — `internal/logpipeline` mentions the beta root in a comment, and `intune/remediationrunstates` names its beta root `defaultBaseURL`, so neither a comment scan nor an identifier scan would work). It failed in both directions on demand — and it caught a genuine gap immediately: `intune.device_encryption`, shipped hours earlier in this same session, was consuming a beta URL the manifest did not know about.
- A second gate fails when a watched collector is missing from `docs/api-drift.md`'s coverage table. It caught the same collector.

**Verified end-to-end, not just "it compiles".** Clean run against live metadata exits 0. Perturbing the snapshot to claim `advancedBitLockerStates` was `Edm.String` and to drop `fileVaultStates` produced exactly the right verdicts:

```
| breaking | microsoft.graph.managedDeviceEncryptionState | property_type_changed | advancedBitLockerStates: Edm.String -> microsoft.graph.advancedBitLockerState |
| info     | microsoft.graph.managedDeviceEncryptionState | property_added        | fileVaultStates (microsoft.graph.fileVaultState) |
EXIT=3
```

**`go run` would have silently broken the signal.** Live-measured on go1.26.5: `go run` collapses any non-zero exit to 1 and prints `exit status N` to stderr, so drift (3) and tool failure (2) become indistinguishable. The workflow builds the binary first. Worth noting the sibling `tailscale2otel/.github/workflows/api-drift.yml` does use `go run` and captures `$?` — its `code == '3'` drift branch can therefore never fire. That is a bug on that repo, not this one.

**Also wired:** a nested `tools/` module is invisible to a root `./...`, so it would have rotted uncaught — `make tools-check` runs its vet+test and is wired into `make check` and CI. The tool is standard-library-only (no `go.sum`), so the daily job needs no module cache. `actionlint` clean; `zizmor --persona=auditor` reports no findings.

**Deliberately not covered**, stated in the doc so it reads as scope rather than omission: `mdca.discovery_parse` (legacy portal API, no machine-readable schema) and the blob/`defender.*` collectors (Azure Storage envelopes, covered by `docs/blob-ingest.md` + the signalcapture goldens).

### It found a real defect on its first look

Slicing the EDM surfaced a live bug in the shipped `intune.settings_catalog` collector's security-baseline sub-signal. Filed separately.

body:
## What & why

graph2otel maintains **12 alert rules** (`alerts/graph2otel-alerts.yaml`, 4 enabled + 8 `isPaused:true`
companions) and **2 recording rules** (`recording-rules/*.json`) **by hand**, with no CI validation.
Both siblings generate rules from a single Python source, which is what lets them regen-gate in CI.

At 12 rules the hand-written cost is low and the alert docs (`alerts/README.md`, ~16KB, per-rule
threshold rationale + false-positive notes) are genuinely strong — so this is about **CI-regen-gating**,
not rule quality. Lower priority than the dashboard builder.

Fleet reference: opnsense-exporter `grafana/alerts/build_rules.py` (single `RULES`/`RECORDING` lists →
grafana-managed manifests) + `validate_manifests.py`; tailscale2otel `deploy/alerts/gen/build_rules.py`.

## Scope

- Single-source generator producing the grafana-managed alert + recording-rule manifests.
- A `validate_manifests.py`-equivalent + regen-staleness check wired into `make grafana-check`.
- Preserve the existing per-rule doc content.

## Keep the log-derived recording rules

graph2otel's recording rules run `count_over_time({service_name="graph2otel"} | event_name=… [1h])`
against **Loki** and record a Prometheus metric — a pattern neither sibling has and the right one here.
The generator must support **Loki-datasource** recording rules, not just PromQL.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Generator emits the alert + recording-rule manifests
- [ ] Loki-datasource recording rules supported
- [ ] Manifest validation + regen-staleness in `make grafana-check`
- [ ] Existing rule coverage + docs preserved
- [ ] `make check` + grafana-check green

---
_Filed 2026-07-20 from a three-way fleet-parity audit of graph2otel vs `opnsense-exporter` and `tailscale2otel`. **v1.0 gate** (per #79's standing rule that every open issue gates the release). Parent tracker #79; release checklist #35._

comments.body:
## Unblocked by #218 — and #218 found a live naming bug in `alerts/`

`6ddaaf4` landed the dashboards-as-code tier and left two things this issue can consume directly.

### 1. The catalogue exists, so the hard part of this issue is already done

`spec/signal-catalog.json` carries all **274** emitted metrics with `name`, `prometheus_name`, `unit`, `kind`, `additive` and `attr_keys`, aggregated from the 139 `testdata/signals.json` goldens and regenerated by `./scripts/regen-generated.sh`. It is **self-updating** — a new collector's golden feeds it with no human step.

`grafana/promname.py` (mirrored by `internal/signalcatalog.PrometheusName`, and pinned to it by a test over all 274 metrics) already reproduces the OTLP→Prometheus translation this issue's rules need. A rule generator should read the catalogue rather than hand-writing normalized names, which is exactly the class of bug below.

### 2. A shipped alert rule queries a metric name that cannot exist

`alerts/graph2otel-alerts.yaml:688` queries:

```
graph2otel_throttle_limit_percentage
```

The metric is emitted with unit `"%"` at `internal/graphclient/ratelimit_transport.go:101`, so OTLP normalization appends `_percent` — the correct name is **`graph2otel_throttle_limit_percentage_percent`**. The same rule produces `entra_secure_score_percentage_percent` elsewhere in the shipped dashboard, so the convention is not in doubt.

**The rule is `isPaused: true`**, which is why nobody noticed: it has never evaluated, so `alerts/README.md`'s live-verification claim does not cover it. A paused rule with a wrong metric name is the alert-side twin of the dead dashboard panels #218 found — invisible precisely because it never runs.

Not fixed here: `alerts/` is this issue's scope, and #218 was explicitly bounded away from it.

### 3. Two other unfixed naming facts worth folding into the generator's acceptance

From #218's regeneration of the committed dashboards, for symmetry when this issue audits the rules:

- `graph2otel_series_overflowing` is emitted **nowhere** (it was removed in #235; `series.clipped` and `series.active` are the live ones).
- `graph2otel_checkpoint_persist_errors` is a Counter, so `rate()` needs `_total`.

### Suggested addition to this issue's acceptance criteria

- [ ] Rules are generated from `spec/signal-catalog.json`, so a metric name in a rule cannot be one that is never emitted
- [ ] A gate that fails when a rule references a metric absent from the catalogue — the alert-side equivalent of #218's coverage gate, and what would have caught the `_percent` bug
- [ ] `graph2otel_throttle_limit_percentage` corrected to `graph2otel_throttle_limit_percentage_percent`

**Caveat on that first one:** ~20 self-observability metrics are emitted outside collector packages (scheduler, transport, telemetry) and therefore are **not** in the catalogue — see #218's closing note. A gate that fails on any uncatalogued metric would false-positive on those until `internal/signalcapture` is extended beyond collector packages. Either extend it first, or allow-list the hand-declared set the way `grafana/boards/selfobs.py` does.

body:
## What & why

graph2otel ships **3 hand-written JSON dashboards** (`dashboards/intune-fleet-overview` ~56KB,
`entra-compliance-overview` ~31KB, `graph2otel-self-observability` ~20KB) with **no builder, no
metric-coverage gate, and no CI validation**. Nothing forces a newly-emitted metric onto a panel —
the exact drift the fleet coverage gate exists to prevent. This is the single widest divergence from
both siblings on the observability-as-code axis.

Fleet reference:
- opnsense-exporter `grafana/build_dashboard.py` — `coverage()` fails the build (write **and**
  `--check`) if any catalogue metric is off a panel; per-tab modules under `grafana/tabs/`
  (`grafana/tabs/AUTHORING.md`); wired via `make grafana-check` as a required `ci-success` leg.
- tailscale2otel `deploy/grafana/gen/build.py` (generator shape) + `tools/metricscatalog`
  (machine-readable emitted-metric catalogue).

## Scope — two steps; the catalogue is a prerequisite

1. ~~**Metric catalogue.** Extract a machine-readable list of every metric graph2otel emits
   (name + type + labels), analogous to tailscale2otel's `tools/metricscatalog`. graph2otel has no
   catalogue today.~~ **CORRECTED 2026-07-24 — graph2otel DOES have a catalogue, in distributed
   form.** 134 per-package `internal/collectors/*/*/testdata/signals.json` goldens already carry
   263 metric names and 125 log event names with `Name`/`Unit`/`Kind`/`AttrKeys`, **derived from
   what the tests actually emit** (`signalcapture.Main -update`) and already drift-gated by #140.
   So step 1 is an **aggregation of existing goldens**, not new extraction machinery — and the
   catalogue is then **self-updating**: a new collector's golden is written by
   `./scripts/regen-generated.sh` and the aggregate picks it up with no human step. See the
   [correction comment](https://github.com/rknightion/graph2otel/issues/218#issuecomment-5073875544)
   for the two design decisions this forces (hard gate + explicit waiver list; log coverage gated
   per DOMAIN, not per event).
2. **Builder + coverage gate.** A Python builder emitting the dashboard JSON; `coverage()` fails when
   any catalogue metric is unpanelled; `make dashboard` (write) + `make grafana-check` (`--check` +
   regen-staleness), wired into `ci-success`.

## Folds in #162

The generated dashboards must include **log panels** (#162 — today zero log panels ship, so the
SIEM value has no surface). Build them into the generator using the correct
`{service_name="graph2otel"} | attr=…` LogQL form (never a stream selector on an attribute, per #90).
Close #162 as part of this, or keep it as the log-panel sub-task.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Machine-readable metric catalogue generated from the emitted-metric surface
- [ ] Python builder emits all 3 dashboards; `make dashboard` regenerates
- [ ] Coverage gate fails (write + `--check`) when a catalogue metric is unpanelled
- [ ] `make grafana-check` wired into `ci-success`
- [ ] At least one log panel per log-shaped domain (#162), using the correct LogQL form
- [ ] `make check` + grafana-check green

Refs #162, #90, #112

---
_Filed 2026-07-20 from a three-way fleet-parity audit of graph2otel vs `opnsense-exporter` and `tailscale2otel`. **v1.0 gate** (per #79's standing rule that every open issue gates the release). Parent tracker #79; release checklist #35._

comments.body:
## CORRECTION — the metric catalogue already exists, and it already self-updates

The body's step 1 says *"Extract a machine-readable list of every metric graph2otel emits (name + type + labels), analogous to tailscale2otel's `tools/metricscatalog`. **graph2otel has no catalogue today.**"*

**That is wrong**, and acting on it would build extraction machinery that duplicates something already in the tree — and something strictly better than the tool it proposes copying. Verified 2026-07-24 against the repo.

### What actually exists

**134 per-package `internal/collectors/*/*/testdata/signals.json` goldens**, carrying **263 distinct metric names** and **125 distinct log event names**. Each entry is exactly the shape a dashboard builder needs:

```json
{
  "Metrics": [
    { "Name": "intune.device_encryption.devices", "Unit": "{device}", "Kind": "gauge",
      "AttrKeys": ["device_type", "encryption_readiness_state", "encryption_state"] }
  ],
  "Logs": [
    { "EventName": "intune.device_encryption",
      "AttrKeys": ["advanced_bitlocker_states", "device_id", "user_principal_name", ...] }
  ]
}
```

Three properties that matter here, none of which tailscale2otel's `metricscatalog` has:

1. **Derived from what the tests actually EMIT** (`signalcapture.Main -update`), not parsed out of source. A metric that exists in code but is never emitted does not appear; one emitted under a branch does. That is the honest surface for a coverage gate.
2. **Already drift-gated (#140).** A package whose emitted signals change fails CI until its golden is regenerated. The catalogue therefore cannot silently rot.
3. **Already coverage-gated at the package level.** `scripts/regen-generated.sh` fails a collector whose package has **no** `signals.json` golden at all — so a new collector cannot skip the mechanism.

### What this changes about the work

Step 1 is not "extract a catalogue". It is **"aggregate 134 existing goldens into one file"** — a small deterministic merge, regenerated by the existing `./scripts/regen-generated.sh` alongside everything else it already regenerates.

**The self-updating property comes free.** New collector lands → `regen-generated.sh` writes its golden → the aggregate picks it up with no human step and no separate catalogue to maintain. This was the maintainer's explicit requirement: the catalogue must update itself from the code as new metrics land, not be a hand-maintained list that a gate merely checks.

Step 2 (builder + coverage gate + CI) stands unchanged.

### Two design decisions this forces, recorded up front

**1. An auto-updating catalogue + a hard coverage gate means every future collector must ship a panel or CI goes red.** That is the gate working as intended — this issue exists precisely because "nothing forces a newly-emitted metric onto a panel" — but it is a standing workflow cost, so it should be a decision rather than a surprise.

Resolution: **the gate fails, with an explicit waiver list.** A deliberately-unpanelled metric is then a visible, commented entry someone chose to write, not a silent gap. A gate with no escape hatch gets disabled the first time it blocks something urgent; a gate with an *undocumented* escape hatch is not a gate. The waiver list is the middle path, and it must carry a reason per entry.

**2. Log-panel coverage (#162) is gated per DOMAIN, not per event.** There are 125 distinct log event names. One panel each would be an unusable dashboard and a gate nobody could ever satisfy, so it would be waived wholesale within a week. #162's actual ask is *"at least one shipped log panel per domain that has a log-shaped signal"* — that is the gateable unit.

### Unchanged and still true

The rest of the body stands: 3 hand-written JSON dashboards with no builder and no CI validation, the `coverage()` model from opnsense-exporter's `grafana/build_dashboard.py`, `make dashboard` + `make grafana-check` wired into `ci-success`, and #162's log panels folded in using the correct `{service_name="graph2otel"} | attr=…` LogQL form (never a stream selector on an attribute — #90).

**Scope note:** the maintainer has scoped this pass to **#218 only**. #219 (alert/recording-rule generator) is explicitly NOT in scope and stays open.

## What & why

graph2otel supports file-based secrets for exactly one field (`mdca.token_file`, added in #145). Its
own **egress** secrets — the OTLP push token (`otlp.grafana_cloud.token`) and the Pyroscope
`basic_auth_password` — have no `_file` sibling, so they can only be supplied inline (env/YAML), which
is worse for Kubernetes secret mounts. Both fleet siblings support file-based secrets broadly.

Fleet reference: tailscale2otel `internal/config/secretfile.go` — `resolveSecretFiles` resolves
value-XOR-file for ~9 secret fields at config Load.

## Scope

- Add `*_file` resolution (value XOR file; error if both set) for:
  - `otlp.grafana_cloud.token` → `otlp.grafana_cloud.token_file`
  - Pyroscope `basic_auth_password` → `..._file`
- Mirror the existing `mdca.token_file` pattern; feed resolved values through `config.Secret`.

## Explicitly out of scope

- **Tenant auth secrets.** graph2otel delegates tenant credential resolution to
  `azidentity.DefaultAzureCredential`, whose own env/file/managed-identity chain is the correct
  multi-tenant Azure idiom. Do **not** hand-roll `_file` for tenant auth — that would be a regression,
  not parity.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `otlp.grafana_cloud.token_file` and the Pyroscope password `_file` resolve at Load
- [ ] value-XOR-file conflict errors clearly
- [ ] resolved values are `config.Secret` (redacted in logs/status/config tab)
- [ ] `make check` green

## What & why

THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md and the SBOM are produced today, but **inline in CI** rather than as
extracted, locally-runnable scripts with Makefile targets. This is the one release-tooling item
where graph2otel sits below both fleet siblings, and the repo already flags it as a follow-up in code.

Current state:
- `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` generated inline via `go-licenses` in `.github/workflows/publish.yml:49-79`.
- SBOMs via goreleaser + syft in `.github/workflows/release-please.yml`.
- In-repo comments (`publish.yml:46-48`, `release-please.yml:91-93`) explicitly say "no scripts/notices.sh yet (tracked follow-up)".
- No `make notices` / `make sbom`; the container image does not bake `/licenses`.

Fleet reference:
- opnsense-exporter: `scripts/notices.sh` (+ `notices.tsv.tmpl`), `scripts/sbom.sh`, `make notices` / `make sbom`, licenses baked into the image at `/licenses`.
- tailscale2otel: identical `scripts/{notices,sbom}.sh` trio.

## Scope / approach

- Extract the go-licenses invocation into `scripts/notices.sh` producing `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` (port opnsense's template).
- Extract the syft invocation into `scripts/sbom.sh` (SPDX + CycloneDX).
- Add `make notices` and `make sbom` calling the scripts.
- Have `publish.yml` / `release-please.yml` call the scripts instead of the inline blocks (single source of truth).
- Bake `/licenses` into the container image (Dockerfile `COPY` of the notices output).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `scripts/notices.sh` exists, runs locally, regenerates `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`
- [ ] `scripts/sbom.sh` exists, runs locally, emits SPDX + CycloneDX
- [ ] `make notices` and `make sbom` wired

Follow-up to the #202/#204 export-catalog sweep: the 4 reports that 400 without a restriction filter, investigated live (probed as graph2otel-poller 2026-07-20). Outcome — **only one is worth building, and via a read-only path, not the export.**

## Live findings on the 4 filter-required reports

| report | finding | decision |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DeviceEnrollmentFailures` | `PostExportJobAsync not supported for reportType DeviceEnrollmentFailures` — **not exportable at all**. Enrollment failures are already covered by the existing `intune.enrollment_events` window collector (enrollmentTroubleshootingEvents). | **Nothing to build** |
| `FeatureUpdateDeviceState` | needs a `(PolicyId eq …)` restriction filter (a feature-update profile). m7kni has **0 `windowsFeatureUpdateProfiles`** (the throwaway profile from #193 was deleted), so there is no source data and nothing to verify. The per-policy summary (`intune.feature_update_summary`, #193) already covers the rollup. | **Defer** — no data + low incremental value; revisit if a real feature-update profile is created |
| `AppInvByDevice` | needs a `(DeviceId eq …)` restriction filter — one export **per device**, a fleet-sized fan-out. High cardinality, high cost, and app inventory is already partly covered by `intune.detected_apps`. | **Skip** — cost/value fails |
| `DeviceRunStatesByProactiveRemediation` | needs a `(PolicyId eq …)` restriction filter (one export per proactive-remediation script). **Valuable** — m7kni has 11 real remediations with live per-device run states. BUT the same data is available **read-only** via `GET /deviceManagement/deviceHealthScripts/{id}/deviceRunStates`, no write scope, no export-job fan-out. | **Build read-only** (this issue) |

## What to build: `intune.remediation_run_states`

Per-device proactive-remediation health — which devices pass/fail each remediation detection, the detection script's own output message, and whether remediation ran. A strong operational + SIEM signal (a failing health detection is exactly what an admin/analyst wants surfaced).

- **Source (beta-only — `deviceHealthScripts` 400s on v1.0, "Resource not found for the segment"):**
  - `GET /beta/deviceManagement/deviceHealthScripts?$select=id,displayName,publisher` — the remediations (11 on m7kni).
  - per remediation: `GET /beta/deviceManagement/deviceHealthScripts/{id}/deviceRunStates?$expand=managedDevice($select=deviceName,operatingSystem,osVersion,managedDeviceOwnerType)` — per-device run states.
- **Read-only, least privilege:** `DeviceManagementConfiguration.Read.All` (deviceHealthScripts) + `DeviceManagementManagedDevices.Read.All` (managedDevice expand). Both already granted to the poller. **No write-scope break** (unlike the export path).
- **`Experimental`** (beta Graph surface, per the #183 rule — beta = Experimental).
- **State snapshot, not an event stream:** each `(policy, device)` row updates in place, so this is the straight snapshot pattern (like `intune.config_setting_status`, #204) — no watermark/dedup/checkpoint. Twins stamp now.
- **Live record shape (verified):** `detectionState` (success/fail/…), `remediationState` (skipped/remediated/failed/…), `preRemediationDetectionScriptOutput` (the message, e.g. `PENDING (PendingFileRename): unrebooted 3.9d (>= 3d)`), `preRemediationDetectionScriptError`, `remediationScriptError`, `postRemediation*`, `lastStateUpdateDateTime`, `lastSyncDateTime`, `assignmentFilterIds`, `managedDevice{deviceName, operatingSystem, osVersion, managedDeviceOwnerType}`.

## Cardinality (#112/#114)

- **Metric** — bounded gauge (`GaugeSnapshot`) keyed only by `(script_name, detection_state, remediation_state)`. `script_name` is tenant-shaped (bounded by number of remediations, ~11), states are small enums — series count is bounded by tenant shape, not tenant size (the project explicitly allows per-policy/state aggregates).
- **Twin** — one log per `(remediation, device)` carrying the per-entity detail (device name/OS, detection message, errors, timestamps). Scales with fleet×remediations, exactly like `intune.devices` twins; never dropped (#114). Severity WARN on `detectionState == fail` or a non-empty script error; INFO otherwise.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `intune.remediation_run_states` collector: list remediations → page each one's deviceRunStates → bounded gauge + per-(remediation,device) twin. TDD, live-shaped fixture.
- [ ] Registered (`collectors_import.go`) + annotated (`collectordoc`) + `docs/collectors.md` regenerated + signalcapture golden.
- [ ] `make check` green.
- [ ] Deployed to camden (Experimental → explicitly enabled) + verified in Grafana Cloud: the LAPHAM "Pending Reboot Age" fail is present in the metric and the twin.
- [ ] Close the loop on the other 3 reports here (nothing-to-build / defer / skip, as above).

Tracker #79. Precedes: nothing. Depends on: nothing.

Part of the fleet-wide operator-console alignment tracked in **rknightion/opnsense-exporter#337**. The three exporters (opnsense-exporter, graph2otel, tailscale2otel) are converging their operator consoles on **tailscale2otel's tabbed single-page layout + theme** (chosen as the reference look). This issue covers graph2otel's share.

## Current state (`internal/admin`)

Single server-rendered `page.html.tmpl`, inline CSS, **zero JS**. Read-only. body:
`EpmElevationReportElevationEvent` (43 live rows on m7kni) is the per-elevation event detail behind the EPM aggregate we already ship (`intune.epm_elevations`). Strong SIEM signal: each row is one privilege elevation with `Id, DeviceId, DeviceName, EventDateTime, ElevationType, FilePath, Upn, ProductName, Hash, Justification, Result, ParentProcessName, PolicyId, IsSystemInitiated, ...`.

**Why this is NOT a clean snapshot clone (blocks a trivial build):** it is an EVENT stream — unique `Id` + real `EventDateTime`. Re-exporting every 6h re-emits all rows → duplicate log lines in Loki, and old events get rejected at Grafana ingest (stale event time). It needs a **watermark + seen-Id dedup**, exactly like `internal/logpipeline` does for Graph log endpoints — but over the export transport, which has no checkpoint plumbing today (`collectors.Deps` has no CheckpointStore for export collectors).

## Plan
- [ ] Add optional checkpoint access to the export collector path (Deps or a small store handle), or a thin event-over-export helper.
- [ ] Collector: emit each new elevation as a log event with `EventDateTime` as event time; checkpoint max EventDateTime + a seen-Id set for overlap dedup (mirror logpipeline's watermark+overlap+seen-id design).
- [ ] Metric: count by `elevation_type` / `result` (bounded); per-event detail on the twin.
- [ ] `make check` green; deploy + verify on camden (43 rows present).

Deferred from the #202 sweep so it can be built carefully rather than as a dup-storm. Depends on #203. Tracker #79.

comments.body:
Shipped + deployed + verified. SHA `9883cfd`, live on camden `version=9883cfd`.

**What landed**
- New collector `intune.epm_elevation_events` (`EpmElevationReportElevationEvent`, export transport, Experimental, `DeviceManagementManagedDevices.ReadWrite.All`).
- Snapshot `collectors.Deps` gained an optional `*checkpoint.Store` (the same store the window/blob/job engines use). **No new registration path** — it stays on the existing snapshot `All()` path, so the `collectordoc` coverage gate keeps seeing it. Its checkpoint namespace (`export/EpmElevationReportElevationEvent`) cannot collide with exportjob's in-flight `JobRecord` for the same report — `jobFileKey` prefixes those with `jobrecord\x00` (separate file).
- Watermark + `SeenIDs` dedup over the export transport (overlap window 30d, well beyond the report's retained set so `SeenIDs` alone dedupes exactly; the "older than overlap" skip is a backstop). Each elevation emits once, stamped with its own `EventDateTime`.

**Wire traps handled (live-probed as graph2otel-poller 2026-07-20, 43 rows)**
- `EventDateTime` is **not** RFC3339 — the export CSV renders `2026-07-19 19:10:54.0000000` (space separator, 7 fractional digits, no zone, UTC). Parsing as RFC3339 would drop every row. Custom layout tried first, RFC3339 as fallback; an unparseable time (or a missing `Id`) drops the row rather than emit it misdated/undedupeable.
- `<Null>`/`""` are absent-column sentinels (`RuleId`/`PolicyId` on an unmanaged elevation) → omitted, never emitted verbatim.
- Explicit `select` of the 22 columns does **not** 400 — no localized `_loc` column is named (the #203 trap).

**Cardinality (#112/#114):** metric is a bounded monotonic counter keyed only by `(elevation_type, result)`; every per-event field (event id, upn, device, file path, hash, parent process, policy) rides the log twin. Unmanaged elevations → WARN.

**Verification (Grafana Cloud, `gcx`)**
- `intune_epm_elevation_events_count_total{elevation_type="UnmanagedElevation",result="0"} = 43` — exactly the 43 live rows, one bounded series, tenant-stamped. Counter = 43 (not >43) proves all rows parsed (correct `EventDateTime`), deduped, and emitted with **zero drops** — no parse-drop warnings on camden.
- Log twins are emitted with their true `EventDateTime` (1–5 days old on m7kni), so they are **age-rejected at Grafana's OTLP-log ingest** and not visible in Loki — the designed tradeoff (never misdate to now), identical to the accepted #135/#200 stale-sample precedent. Confirmed it is age, not a query/pipeline fault: a now-stamped sibling twin (`intune.config_setting_status`) queries back fine through the same path. Fresh elevations (near-real-time) would ingest cleanly.
- Cross-poll dedup is unit-verified (`TestSecondPollDeduplicates`: second poll of the same rows through a fresh emitter but the persisted checkpoint emits zero twins and adds zero to the counter).

`make check` green (vet + test + golangci-lint + govulncheck + build). Depended on #203 (done).

body:
## Symptom (live)

On camden, two shipped export collectors emit nothing — every run 400s:
- `intune.noncompliant_settings` (`NoncompliantDevicesAndSettings`)
- `intune.config_assignment_status` (`DeviceAssignmentStatusByConfigurationPolicy`)

```
POST /deviceManagement/reports/exportJobs: status 400: BadRequest
```

## Root cause (wire-verified 2026-07-20, probed as graph2otel-poller)

Not a filter and not a data problem. The `select` these collectors pin names a **localized `_loc` column**, and the export API 400s when a `_loc` column is named in `select` — even though that column appears in the report's default (no-select) output. Binary-searched the first breaking column:

- `NoncompliantDevicesAndSettings`: breaks at `SettingNm_loc` (col 8/12). No-select → 201.
- `DeviceAssignmentStatusByConfigurationPolicy`: breaks at `UnifiedPolicyPlatformType_loc` (col 10/14). No-select → 201.

The pinned columns were never wire-validated against an explicit select (the "live-measured" probe used no-select). Both collectors genuinely need the `_loc` friendlies for their log twins, and those columns exist ONLY in the default output.

## Fix

`internal/exportjob`: make `select` optional. When `Request.Select` is empty, OMIT the `select` key from the POST body (an empty array is not the same as an absent key) so the report returns its default columns. Was previously a hard "programming error" guard.
- `exportJobBody.Select` → `json:"select,omitempty"`.
- Drop the non-empty guard in `Export`.
- `Request.Select` doc updated: empty = take default columns; pin explicitly where the report supports it.

Both collectors now pass `Select` empty (documented why inline). Columns are read by name from the default output; a missing column degrades to empty rather than 400ing.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `internal/exportjob` supports empty Select (key omitted); unit test pins that the `select` key is absent from the body.
- [ ] Both collectors omit select; their tests assert `Select` empty.
- [ ] `make check` green.
- [ ] Deployed to camden; both collectors run `ok` and emit (verified in Grafana Cloud).

Found during the #202 export-catalog sweep. Same `_loc`-in-select trap will apply to the new config-policy collectors, so this unblocks those too.

comments.body:
Deployed + verified on camden (`version=9fc685e`, 2026-07-20). Both previously-dead export collectors now emit — **zero 400s** in the logs:
- `intune_noncompliant_settings_count` — 2 series in Grafana Cloud (was emitting nothing).
- `intune_config_assignment_status_assignments` — 17 series (was emitting nothing).

Fix confirmed end-to-end: empty `select` → `select` key omitted from the POST body → report returns default columns (incl. the `_loc` friendlies) → data flows.

Follow-up (a436064): once rows flowed, `noncompliant_settings` measured a live `SettingStatus=5` / `_loc="Error"` on WINSRV that its decode map lacked (bucketed to "unknown"). Now seeded `5 → error` (live-measured, the map grows only on evidence).
