The **Apps** and **Scripts** tabs of the per-device deployment-details pane are not collected. Add two sibling collectors so admins can track per-app / per-script install status and failures during device prep.

## Live evidence (wire, probed as graph2otel-poller 2026-07-20, m7kni)

Both reports go through the same `POST /beta/deviceManagement/reports/exportJobs` subsystem we already use.

- `AutopilotV2DeploymentStatusDetailedAppInfo` — **2 rows** returned. Columns (verbatim header): `DeviceId, ApplicationId, PolicyInstallStatus, IsAdminSelected, ApplicationName, AppType`. Sample: `Microsoft 365 Apps for Windows 10 and later`, `OfficeSuiteApp`, status `2`, `IsAdminSelected=True`.

- [ ] `make check` green; signalcapture golden gate per collector.
- [ ] Deploy to camden, enable both (Experimental), verify export runs ok against live WINSRV deployment.

## Acceptance

- Both collectors ship, `make check` green, cardinality guard tests pass (per-entity data on twin only).
- Raw `PolicyInstallStatus` emitted verbatim, no invented severity.

comments.body:
## Live export probe of both halves, 2026-07-21 — one is buildable now, one is not a report at all

Probed as `graph2otel-poller` against m7kni: created a real export job per candidate `reportName`, polled to completion, downloaded and read the CSV. `[live-measured 2026-07-21, #201, n=1 tenant]`

### `EpmAggregationReportByDevice` — **does not exist**. Closing that item won't-do.

`POST /deviceManagement/reports/exportJobs` returns `400 BadRequest — PostExportJobAsync not supported for reportType Unknown.` for all three plausible spellings:

| reportName | result |
| --- | --- |
| `EpmAggregationReportByDevice` | 400 `reportType Unknown` |
| `EpmAggregationReportByDevices` | 400 `reportType Unknown` |
| `EpmAggregationReportDevice` | 400 `reportType Unknown` |
| `EpmElevationReportElevationEvent` (control, already shipped) | **201 created** |

The control proves the request shape and the write scope are fine — the name is what Graph cannot resolve. `reportType Unknown` is the same failure mode as `DeviceEnrollmentFailures` on #207, and it means Graph has no such report, not that the tenant has no rows. There is no per-device EPM aggregation report to wire; per-device elevation attribution is already available from `intune.epm_elevation_events` (#205), which carries the device on every elevation record. **Not blocked-on-data — genuinely absent.**

### `EpmAggregationReportByUser` + `...ByPublisher` — **live rows, building now**

Both export cleanly, and both accept an **explicit `select`** naming exactly their columns (no `_loc` column is involved, so the #203 trap does not apply — the select is pinned):

```
EpmAggregationReportByUser      "ManagedCount","UnmanagedCount","TotalCount","Upn"
                                "0","40","40","AzureAD\RobKnight"
                                "0","3","3","rob@m7kni.io"

EpmAggregationReportByPublisher "CompanyName","ElevationType","ElevationCount"
                                "Microsoft Windows","UnmanagedElevation","43"
```

Wire trap worth recording: the `Upn` column is **not always a UPN** — one live row carries the down-level logon name `AzureAD\RobKnight`. It is emitted verbatim; no parsing or normalisation.

### `AutopilotV1DeploymentStatus` — re-confirmed blocked-on-data (third confirmation)

Export job completes, the 27-column header is valid (`DeviceId,UserId,UPN,EnrollmentMethod,…,EspUserSetupFailureDetails`), **0 rows**. Same as 2026-07-19 and 2026-07-20. m7kni is an Autopilot-V2 / device-preparation tenant. Unblock condition unchanged: a tenant with legacy Autopilot V1 deployment data to map against.

## Both buildable variants shipped — `bfbe749`

`intune.epm_elevations_by_user` (`EpmAggregationReportByUser`) and `intune.epm_elevations_by_publisher` (`EpmAggregationReportByPublisher`) are on `main`. Both mapped against the live CSV rows in the comment above, both `Experimental` (the export write scope), both 6h, both riding the existing `internal/exportjob` engine — no new transport.

| collector | metric | twin |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `intune.epm_elevations_by_user` | `intune.epm_elevations_by_user.count{elevation_governance}` — exactly two series (`managed`, `unmanaged`), both always emitted even at zero | per user: `upn`, `managed_count`, `unmanaged_count`, `total_count`; WARN when the user holds any unmanaged elevation |
| `intune.epm_elevations_by_publisher` | `intune.epm_elevations_by_publisher.count{elevation_type}` — wire enum verbatim | per publisher: `company_name`, `elevation_type`, `elevation_count`; WARN on `UnmanagedElevation` |

Cardinality: the UPN and the publisher name never become metric labels (both unbounded in principle) — they ride the twins, per #114 they are never dropped. Guard tests pin both.

One naming call worth recording: the by-user governance label is `elevation_governance`, **not** `epm.elevation_governance`. A dotted key would survive to the wire but reach PromQL normalized to an underscore (#82), leaving the golden, the docs and the query surface disagreeing about the label's own name. Every other domain attribute in the repo is bare snake_case.

Docs fixed in the same commit: `permissions.md` §4 and `pii-cardinality-audit.md` both hand-listed the export-report collectors that need `DeviceManagementManagedDevices.ReadWrite.All`. That list had gone stale **twice** (three → six) and the real count is now **22**. Both now carry the count plus a pointer to the generated `collectors.md` table, which cannot rot. There is still no gate tying "declares the write scope" to "named in prose" — pointing at generated output is the cheaper fix than building one.

### This issue's remaining scope

- ~~`EpmAggregationReportByDevice`~~ — **closed won't-do**: no such report exists (evidence in the comment above). Per-device elevation attribution already ships via `intune.epm_elevation_events` (#205).
- `AutopilotV1DeploymentStatus` — the only thing left here. Blocked-on-data, re-confirmed 2026-07-21 (job completes, header valid, 0 rows). **Unblock: a tenant with legacy Autopilot V1 deployment data.**

## Deployed + verified in Grafana Cloud (camden `version=bfbe749`, 2026-07-21)

Both collectors enabled in camden `config.yaml` and confirmed emitting real data — not empty-success.

**Metrics** (`grafanacloud-prom`):

```
intune_epm_elevations_by_user_count{elevation_governance="unmanaged"}       43
intune_epm_elevations_by_user_count{elevation_governance="managed"}          0
intune_epm_elevations_by_publisher_count{elevation_type="UnmanagedElevation"} 43
```

43 on both cuts, and the already-shipped `intune.epm_elevations` application rollup also totals 43 — three independent report aggregations agreeing is the cross-check that the sums are right. The `managed=0` series is present rather than absent, which is the point of seeding both series.

**Log twins** (`{service_name="graph2otel"} | event_name="intune.epm_elevations_by_user"`) — both users present, and the wire trap survives the whole pipeline intact:

```
upn="AzureAD\RobKnight"  managed_count=0  unmanaged_count=40  total_count=40  severity=WARN
upn="rob@m7kni.io"       managed_count=0  unmanaged_count=3   total_count=3   severity=WARN
```

`ingest_transport=report_export` and `tenant_id` are stamped on every record (#141/#143). WARN fired correctly on both — every elevation on this tenant is unmanaged.

## AutopilotV1 re-probe 2026-07-21 (later) — 4th confirmation of 0 rows, and the root cause is now exact

Re-ran the export end to end as `graph2otel-poller`, then probed the Autopilot configuration itself — which had never been checked. `[live-measured 2026-07-21, #201, n=1 tenant]`

**Export, unchanged:** `POST /beta/deviceManagement/reports/exportJobs {"reportName":"AutopilotV1DeploymentStatus","format":"csv"}` → `201`, job `completed`, CSV downloaded, 27-column header valid, **0 data rows**.

```
"DeviceId","UserId","UPN","EnrollmentMethod","EnrollmentDateTime","EnrollmentStatus","FailureReason",
"FailureDetails","OS","OSVersion","DeviceName","AutopilotProfileName","DeviceSerialNumber",
"DeviceRegisteredDateTime","ESPPolicyName","ESPPolicyId","DeploymentState","DeploymentStartDateTime", …
```

**Root cause, new:** the tenant has no Autopilot objects of any kind.

| endpoint | rows |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /beta/deviceManagement/windowsAutopilotDeviceIdentities` | **0** |
| `GET /beta/deviceManagement/windowsAutopilotDeploymentProfiles` | **0** |

This supersedes the previous framing ("m7kni is an Autopilot-V2 / device-preparation tenant"). It is not that V2 was chosen over V1 — **no Autopilot device has ever been registered and no deployment profile of either generation exists**. The report is empty because nothing has ever been deployed through Autopilot, which is a stronger and more actionable statement than "wrong Autopilot generation".

**Consequence: this is synthesizable, and entirely within maintainer control.** Unlike #194's EA segments (which wait on device count and telemetry accumulation) and unlike a genuinely absent report (`EpmAggregationReportByDevice`, closed won't-do above), the only thing standing between this tenant and a populated `AutopilotV1DeploymentStatus` report is a configuration that has never been created. Sketch:

1. Create a **Windows Autopilot deployment profile** (V1 — user-driven, Entra-joined). This is `windowsAutopilotDeploymentProfiles`, distinct from a device-preparation policy.
2. Register one VM's hardware hash into `importedWindowsAutopilotDeviceIdentities` (hash via `Get-WindowsAutopilotInfo` on the VM).
3. Assign the profile to a group containing that device.
4. Reset the VM and run it through OOBE so a deployment actually executes.

Each of steps 1–3 is a **tenant write**, so it needs explicit maintainer approval and is not covered by the read-only standing consent; step 4 is manual work on the VM. Once one deployment completes, the report gains a row and the mapper can be built against it per the map-against-live-samples rule.

**Status:** still blocked-on-data, but reclassified from *"waiting for a tenant that happens to have legacy Autopilot data"* (open-ended, may never fire) to *"waiting on a ~1h deliberate setup on m7kni"* (a decision, not a wait). Recording it that way so a later reader does not treat it as unreachable.

**Cross-reference:** #199 notes `userExperienceAnalyticsNotAutopilotReadyDevice` returns 0 rows and assumed a device-count gate. Given zero Autopilot identities tenant-wide, that segment's emptiness may be definitional rather than gated — and note the tension: performing the synthesis above would make devices Autopilot-ready and keep that segment empty for a different reason.

## Closing — Autopilot V1 is a maintainer won't-do (2026-07-21)

Maintainer decision: **graph2otel will not support Autopilot V1.** The remaining scope item is withdrawn.

The previous comment established that this was synthesizable — the tenant has zero Autopilot device identities and zero deployment profiles, so a V1 profile plus a hardware-hash import plus one OOBE run would have produced report rows. That path is declined deliberately: it would mean standing up a legacy deployment mechanism on a tenant that does not use it, purely to generate sample data for a mapper, and Autopilot V1 is not a surface this exporter will carry.

`intune.autopilot_deployment` continues to ship the **V2 / device-preparation** variant, which is what this tenant and current Intune guidance actually use.

### Final state of this issue

| item | outcome |
| --- | --- |
| `EpmAggregationReportByUser` → `intune.epm_elevations_by_user` | **shipped** `bfbe749` |
| `EpmAggregationReportByPublisher` → `intune.epm_elevations_by_publisher` | **shipped** `bfbe749` |
| `EpmAggregationReportByDevice` | **won't-do** — report does not exist (`400 reportType Unknown` on all spellings, against a 201 control) |
| `AutopilotV1DeploymentStatus` | **won't-do** — maintainer decision, this comment |

Nothing here is left blocked-on-data. Closing.

body:
The Defender XDR advanced-hunting ingest (#106) shipped 17 per-table blob mappers, one per `insights-logs-advancedhunting-*` container. Two tables in the storage account had **no collector**, so their data landed billed and unread: `AlertInfo` and `UrlClickEvents`. Both now carry live data on m7kni (captured as `graph2otel-poller` 2026-07-20), so both are buildable against real samples. This closes the 19/19 advanced-hunting coverage gap.

## Built (this commit)

- **`defender.alert_info`** ← `AdvancedHunting-AlertInfo`. One log per Defender XDR alert header: `alert_id`, `title`, `category` (MITRE tactic), `severity`, `detection_source`, `service_source`, `attack_techniques`. The alert-level companion to `defender.alert_evidence`'s per-entity rows — join on `alert_id`. Severity string → log severity via the `alertevidence` convention (High→Error, Medium/Low→Warn). Live sample: `Severity=High`, `Category=InitialAccess`, `Title="Malicious IP address"`, `DetectionSource="AAD Identity Protection"`.
- **`defender.url_click_event`** ← `AdvancedHunting-UrlClickEvents`. One log per Safe Links URL-click verdict: `url`, `url_chain`, `action_type` (ClickAllowed/…), `is_clicked_through`, `threat_types`, `detection_methods`, `account_upn`, `network_message_id`, `workload`, app name/version. Zero MDO Safe-Links coverage existed before.

Wire note: `UrlChain` arrives on the wire as a pre-serialized JSON **string** (not a native array), carried through unmodified via `StampStrings`; `DetectionMethods`/`ThreatTypes` are JSON null in the sample and mapped via `jsonStr` (null → omitted). `AlertInfo.MachineGroup` is JSON null → omitted.

## Acceptance

- [x] Both mappers written against verbatim live m7kni samples (not docs)
- [x] Per-entity detail as log attributes only (#112); log-only, no metrics
- [x] On when `blob_ingest` is configured (peer to the other 17 `defender.*`; not Experimental, per #183)
- [x] `docs/collectors.md` regenerated; `internal/collectordoc` annotations added; coverage gate green
- [x] `make check` green

body:
> **Status 2026-07-21 (corrected):** `intune.device_encryption` shipped (`bfbe749`). Two items previously parked here as *blocked-on-data* were **NOT** blocked — both verdicts were probe-shape errors and are retracted in [this comment](https://github.com/rknightion/graph2otel/issues/199#issuecomment-5034387201):
> - ~~`hardwareInformation` is null on every row~~ → **wrong**, that was a LIST GET; the single-entity GET returns 16–21 populated fields, and `$batch` makes the per-device fetch cheap. **Buildable now.**
> - ~~`DeviceStartupProcesses` 400s on a plain list, route unresolved~~ → **wrong**, the probe carried `$top`; the bare list returns real rows. `$top`/`$count` are rejected outright on that segment (400) and on `DeviceStartupHistory` (500). **Buildable now.**
>
> ~~Genuinely still blocked-on-data: `DeviceStartupProcessPerformance` (new, 0 rows), `DevicesWithoutCloudIdentity`, `NotAutopilotReadyDevice`.~~
>
> **Status 2026-07-24 (`45f0fe0`):** `DevicesWithoutCloudIdentity` and `NotAutopilotReadyDevice` are **closed out of scope** and recorded in the permanent-gap ledger in `docs/graph-api-gotchas.md` as *reachable but never populated* — both are exception lists on a tenant with zero Autopilot identities (#201), re-probed across three days and a 10 → 17 device fleet. **This issue is now scoped to `DeviceStartupProcessPerformance` alone, with NO unblock condition** — the "boot telemetry from more than one device" condition recorded on 2026-07-23 fired (3 records/2 devices → 11/6) and the segment did not move, so what gates a UXA rollup being published is unknown and is explicitly not device count. See [this comment](https://github.com/rknightion/graph2otel/issues/199#issuecomment-5070446326).

Filed at maintainer request (2026-07-20), out of the #194 discussion. Sub-area of the Intune reporting/analytics tracker #192.

## What & why

Advanced Analytics (Intune Suite) has **two distinct surfaces**, and graph2otel only touches one:
1. **Endpoint Analytics *scores*** (startup / app-reliability / battery / resource / WFA) — aggregate, **Windows-only**, and gated behind a hard **5-device "insufficient data" floor** (Microsoft docs, confirmed live 2026-07-20: m7kni has 1 EA-scored device). This is #194s territory.
2. **Device inventory / device query** — per-device hardware/software properties. graph2otel does **not** tap this at all.

This issue covers surface #2 (the inventory bits) for the **non-Apple fleet (Windows + Linux)**.

## Live findings (2026-07-20, probed as `graph2otel-poller`)

App-only reachable (HTTP 200) inventory surfaces, most **empty on m7kni** (same device-count gate as EA — will fill with the Windows desktop VMs being stood up):
- `managedDeviceEncryptionStates` — **8 rows** (has data now)
- `managedDevices.hardwareInformation` — per-device HW inventory (200)
- `userExperienceAnalyticsDeviceStartupProcesses`, `userExperienceAnalyticsResourcePerformance`, `userExperienceAnalyticsDevicesWithoutCloudIdentity`, `userExperienceAnalyticsNotAutopilotReadyDevice` — 200, 0 rows (device-count gated)

**Linux caveat (important):** the one Linux device on m7kni (`oli`) is **Defender-managed (`managementAgent=msSense`), NOT Intune MDM** — so its Intune inventory is thin (4 populated `hardwareInformation` keys) and it is **not EA-eligible**. The real Linux device-inventory/software source is almost certainly the **Defender advanced-hunting tables (`DeviceInfo`, `DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory`) already flowing via the #106 blob path**, not Intune. Research this before assuming an Intune route exists for Linux.

**Device Query (on-demand KQL)** is a separate *action*-based surface, not a poll endpoint — app-only pollability for a scheduled collector is TBD.

## Scope (research-first, wire-over-docs)

- [ ] Enumerate the app-only-pollable advanced-analytics inventory surfaces; pick the operationally-useful ones (encryption state, HW inventory, startup processes, resource perf).
- [ ] Shape per the cardinality rule (#112/#114): per-device rows -> **log twins**; bounded rollups -> gauges. No per-device metric labels.
- [ ] **Windows:** the surfaces above — device-count gated; unblocks when the Windows VM fleet pushes reporting devices past the EA floor.
- [ ] **Linux:** determine the real source. Intune `managedDevices` inventory is thin for a Defender-managed Linux box; check whether Defender advanced-hunting `DeviceInfo` / `DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory` (#106 blob) is the correct Linux inventory feed instead.
- [ ] **Apple (macOS/iOS):** Device Query supports them ("collect automatically") — noted as a follow-on, out of this Windows+Linux issues scope unless folded in.

## Acceptance

- [ ] App-only reachability verified per surface (live, as the poller).
- [ ] Mappers built against **live samples** — surfaces empty on m7kni recorded as awaiting-data, never mapped blind (empty-collection hides mapping bugs, #142/#129).
- [ ] `docs/collectors.md` regenerated; coverage gate green (`internal/collectordoc` walks the path).

## Not a v1.0 gate

New enhancement, **post-v1** — does not block the v1.0 cut (#35 Gate 0) unless re-prioritized. Most of its data is device-count-gated on m7kni anyway.

Refs #192, #194, #106.

comments.body:
## Full surface probe 2026-07-21 — one buildable surface, and the Linux question answered

Probed every surface this issue lists, as `graph2otel-poller` against m7kni. `[live-measured 2026-07-21, #199, n=1 tenant]`

| surface | v1.0 | beta | rows | verdict |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `managedDeviceEncryptionStates` | 400 (no such segment) | 200 | **5** | **BUILD** — real, actionable data |
| `managedDevices` `hardwareInformation` | 400 (property absent on the v1.0 type) | 200 | 3/3 | park — see below |
| `userExperienceAnalyticsDeviceStartupProcesses` | 400 | 400 | — | needs a device-scoped route; not a plain list |
| `userExperienceAnalyticsDevicesWithoutCloudIdentity` | 400 (no such segment) | 200 | 0 | park (nothing to map) |
| `userExperienceAnalyticsNotAutopilotReadyDevice` | 400 (no such segment) | 200 | 0 | park (nothing to map) |

### Encryption state — building now

Beta-only, 5 live rows, and the data is the "why is this device not encrypted" detail that `intune.devices`' boolean `isEncrypted` gauge cannot answer. Two Windows devices are genuinely unencrypted with named blockers:

```json
{"deviceName":"DESKTOP-MHTMHH4","deviceType":"windowsRT","encryptionState":"notEncrypted","encryptionReadinessState":"ready","encryptionPolicySettingState":"notAssigned","advancedBitLockerStates":"osVolumeUnprotected,tpmNotReady","tpmSpecificationVersion":"2.0"}
{"deviceName":"wintest","encryptionState":"notEncrypted","advancedBitLockerStates":"osVolumeUnprotected,osVolumeTpmRequired,osVolumeTpmOnlyRequired,osVolumeEncryptionMethodMismatch,tpmNotReady"}
{"deviceName":"mbp14","deviceType":"macMDM","encryptionState":"encrypted","encryptionReadinessState":"notReady","fileVaultStates":null}
```

Wire facts recorded: `advancedBitLockerStates` is a **comma-joined flag list** with unbounded combinations (twin only, never a metric label); macOS reports `deviceType=macMDM` and modern Windows reports `deviceType=windowsRT` — both emitted verbatim (#142: never "correct" a wire value); `fileVaultStates` is null tenant-wide; `policyDetails` is an empty array on every row and is not mapped blind.

### Hardware inventory — parked, with the reason

`hardwareInformation` is reachable app-only on beta but is **almost entirely null on this tenant, including on the Windows devices**. Live sample from the Windows box `DESKTOP-2F6PPF2`: `totalStorageSpace=0, freeStorageSpace=0, manufacturer=null, model=null, tpmSpecificationVersion=null, tpmManufacturer=null, tpmVersion=null, osBuildNumber=null, operatingSystemEdition=null, systemManagementBIOSVersion=null, productName=null`. Populated: `serialNumber` (a Parallels VM id), the three `deviceGuard*` states, and `deviceLicensingStatus=unknown`. Mapping ~30 fields that are null on every available row is exactly the blind-mapping the project forbids. The identity fields that *are* useful (model, manufacturer, serial) already ride the `intune.devices` twin. **Unblock condition: a fleet of real (non-VM) Windows hardware reporting inventory.**

### Linux — answered: the source is Defender, not Intune

The issue asked whether Intune `managedDevices` inventory or the Defender advanced-hunting blob path is the real Linux inventory feed. It is Defender. The one Linux device (`oli`) is `managementAgent=msSense` and its Intune `hardwareInformation` is empty except `deviceGuard*` — while **`defender.device_info` already ships** (one of the 19 advanced-hunting tables now collected over the #106 blob path) and carries OS, version, and device posture for exactly that class of device. No Intune-side Linux inventory work is warranted.

Caveat recorded honestly: `DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory` (per-device *software* inventory) is **not** among the 19 advanced-hunting tables currently streamed to the storage account, and whether Defender XDR's streaming API can export it at all was not tested in this pass. That is a diagnostic-settings question, not a graph2otel code gap.

## `intune.device_encryption` shipped — `bfbe749`

The one surface in this issue with live data is built and on `main`.

- **Source:** `GET beta/deviceManagement/managedDeviceEncryptionStates` (beta-only; v1.0 has no such segment → `Experimental`, read-only `DeviceManagementManagedDevices.Read.All`, 1h).
- **Metrics (bounded wire enums only):** `intune.device_encryption.devices{encryption_state, encryption_readiness_state, device_type}` and `intune.device_encryption.policy_state{encryption_policy_setting_state}` — two metric names rather than one four-dimensional gauge, so a naive `sum()` over either is the true device count.
- **Twin** `intune.device_encryption`, one record per device: device id/name, UPN, device type, OS version, TPM version, the three states, the raw `advancedBitLockerStates` blocker list and `fileVaultStates`. **WARN whenever the disk is not encrypted** — the actionable case, and on this tenant that is two real Windows devices.
- **Cardinality (#112/#114):** device identity, UPN, OS/TPM version and the blocker list never become metric labels; they ride the twin and are never dropped. Guard test pins it.

Two implementation notes worth keeping:

`deviceType` is emitted verbatim, so macOS shows as `macMDM` and modern Windows as `windowsRT`. Those look wrong and are not — "correcting" them would invent values that were never on the wire (#142).

Both flag-list fields (`advancedBitLockerStates`, `fileVaultStates`) decode **tolerantly** — a JSON string passes through, a JSON array is comma-joined, anything else omits the attribute rather than failing the row. `advancedBitLockerStates` is live-verified as a comma-joined string, but that is n=1: one tenant, one day. `fileVaultStates` is null on every row here, so its populated shape is genuinely unknown. ### CORRECTION 1 — `managedDevices.hardwareInformation` is NOT null. The earlier probe used a LIST GET.

Recorded earlier on this issue: *"almost entirely null on this tenant, including on the Windows devices… `totalStorageSpace=0, freeStorageSpace=0, manufacturer=null, model=null, tpmSpecificationVersion=null`… Mapping ~30 fields that are null on every available row is exactly the blind-mapping the project forbids."*

| `GET managedDevices/{id}?$select=hardwareInformation` | 200 | **16–21** |
| `GET managedDevices?$expand=hardwareInformation` | 400 | `Property 'hardwareInformation' on type … ` — not expandable |
| `GET managedDevices?$filter=id eq '{id}'&$select=hardwareInformation` | 400 | filter on `id` unsupported here |

### CORRECTION 2 — `DeviceStartupProcesses` is NOT route-blocked. `$top` is the trigger.

Recorded earlier: *"`400` on a plain list on both versions; needs a device-scoped route that has not been resolved."* The request was not a plain list — it carried `$top`. Isolated cleanly:

| segment | bare | `$top=5` | `$top=50` | `$top=200` | `$count=true` | `$orderby=id` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `userExperienceAnalyticsDeviceStartupProcesses` | **200, rows** | 400 | 400 | 400 | 400 | 200 |
| `userExperienceAnalyticsDeviceStartupHistory` | **200, rows** | 500 | 500 | 500 | 500 | 500 |
| `userExperienceAnalyticsDeviceStartupProcessPerformance` | 200, 0 | 200 | 200 | 200 | 200 | 200 |

This is a **new API gotcha, and a nastier variant of the known `$top`-ceiling trap** (`docs/graph-api-gotchas.md`): these two segments reject `$top` *at any value* rather than above a ceiling, and `$count` with it, while `$orderby` is fine. The two segments also fail with **different status codes for the same cause** — 400 vs 500 — so a 500 here is not a transient Graph fault.

The EDM confirms the route was never in doubt: `userExperienceAnalyticsDeviceStartupProcesses` is a plain `ContainsTarget="true"` collection nav on the `deviceManagement` singleton, type `Collection(graph.userExperienceAnalyticsDeviceStartupProcess)`.

Verbatim live rows (the Parallels Windows VM):

```json
{"id":"1625d698-…","managedDeviceId":"1625d698-…","processName":"MsMpEng",
 "productName":"Windows Defender Antivirus","publisher":"Microsoft Corporation","startupImpactInMs":8038}
{"…","processName":"MsSense","productName":"Windows Defender Advanced Threat Protection","startupImpactInMs":4822}
{"…","processName":"WmiPrvSE","productName":"WMI Provider Host","startupImpactInMs":4822}
```

Corroborating evidence that the bare route is sound: **`intune.endpoint_analytics` already polls `userExperienceAnalyticsDeviceStartupHistory` in production and is green** (`internal/collectors/intune/endpointanalytics/endpointanalytics.go:500`). It survives because `collectors.GetAllValues` paginates with the `Prefer: odata.maxpagesize` header and never emits `$top` (`internal/collectors/graph.go:113`). No shipped collector is at risk from this gotcha — but any new one that reaches for `$top` on an EA segment would be.

**Verdict: unparked. Buildable now.** Shape per #112/#114: `startupImpactInMs` per (device, process) is per-entity → **log twin**; the bounded rollup belongs on the sibling below.

Named in the EDM next to the two above; **200 on both v1.0 and beta, 0 rows** today. ### Method note

The general lesson, now three for three (#222, and both corrections above): **an empty or errored result from a request whose shape was never validated is not evidence about the tenant.** All three were recorded as tenant-data facts with confident rationale attached. Before parking anything as blocked-on-data, vary the request shape first — bare vs `$select` vs `$top` vs single-entity vs cast segment — and only then attribute the emptiness to the tenant.

## Both unparked items shipped (`b85fc1b`, `4a976fc`)

The two verdicts retracted earlier today are now built.

### `intune.hardware_inventory` — new collector (`b85fc1b`)

Beta-only, Experimental, read-only `DeviceManagementManagedDevices.Read.All`, **24h**.

The interval is the mitigation for the fetch shape. `hardwareInformation` only materializes on a single-entity GET, `$expand` is rejected and `$filter` on `id` is rejected, so the collector pages `managedDevices` for ids then fetches hardware **20 devices per `POST /beta/$batch`** — `1 + ceil(N/20)` requests per cycle, the most expensive shape in the repo. Intune itself only refreshes device hardware inventory on a multi-day cycle, so a shorter interval would burn quota re-fetching identical data.

**Metrics** (bounded aggregates only): `intune.hardware_inventory.devices{operating_system,manufacturer}`, `.tpm_devices{tpm_specification_version}`, `.device_guard_devices{vbs_state,credential_guard_state}`, `.storage_bytes{operating_system,storage_state}`.

**Twin** `intune.device_hardware` — 27 attributes: storage, the full TPM triple, Device Guard/VBS/Credential Guard, BIOS version, OS edition/language/product type, licensing status, supervision/shared flags, wired IPs, and mobile identity (IMEI, eSIM, carrier, cellular technology). Fields `intune.devices` already twins — serial, model, wifi MAC, `isEncrypted` — are deliberately not duplicated.

Wire traps handled, each live-observed and each pinned by a test:

- `batteryHealthPercentage` and `batteryChargeCycles` read **0 on every device including a working MacBook Pro**. Zero battery health on a functioning laptop is not a measurement, it is "not reported" — omitted rather than emitted as a real zero. Same treatment extended to `totalStorageSpace`, which reads 0 on a Linux host that plainly has a disk; such a device contributes no storage series rather than a series claiming zero bytes.
- `deviceGuard*` reports Windows-only values on macOS (`mbp14` returns `meetHardwareRequirements` / `running`). Emitted **verbatim**, not filtered by OS — with a comment that it is not trustworthy on non-Windows and must not be read as a macOS security posture. Correcting it would invent values that were never on the wire (#142).
- `deviceLicensingStatus` is a **string carrying `"25"`** on one device — Graph stringifying an enum member it has no name for. Decodes tolerantly (string or bare number); a strict decode would fail the whole row on a tenant sending the other shape.
- `operatingSystemProductType` 0 is emitted verbatim and deliberately NOT given the zero-is-absent treatment: 0 on a Mac is "not applicable", not a self-contradictory reading.

Fields deliberately left unmapped, on the `policyDetails` precedent — never map what nobody has seen populated: `sharedDeviceCachedUsers` (`[]` fleet-wide), `deviceLicensingLastErrorCode`/`Description`, `meid`, `batterySerialNumber`, `osBuildNumber`, `ipAddressV4`, `subnetAddress`, `residentUsersCount`, `deviceFullQualifiedDomainName`.

**Caveat recorded honestly:** the `$batch` chunk size of 20 is **docs-only, not live-measured**. The probe ran all ten devices in one call, so `$batch` itself is live-verified but the 20 boundary was never driven to its edge on m7kni. It is the safe direction — a wrong ceiling costs requests, not correctness.

**Cross-collector conflict this exposed and fixed:** `intune.device_encryption` was emitting `tpmSpecificationVersion` under the attribute key `tpm_version`, while this collector uses `tpm_version` for the chip's own firmware version. One key, two meanings depending on which collector wrote the record — a query filtering on it silently matched the wrong shape on one of them. `device_encryption` now emits `tpm_specification_version`, which is what it actually reads. Breaking rename on a week-old attribute; correct to do now rather than bake in.

### `DeviceStartupProcesses` — shipped as `intune.device_startup_process` (`4a976fc`)

Built into `intune.endpoint_analytics` as a 10th sub-fetch (it is a `userExperienceAnalytics*` signal and reuses that collector's Experimental gate), twin-only with no metric — the (device, process) pair is unbounded. See #225.

The `$top` gotcha is now recorded in the source: that segment rejects `$top` at **any** value with a 400 and `$count` with it, while `$orderby` is accepted; the sibling `DeviceStartupHistory` has the same trigger but answers **500**. No shipped collector is exposed, because `collectors.GetAllValues` paginates with `Prefer: odata.maxpagesize` and never emits `$top` — which is also why the already-shipped `DeviceStartupHistory` fetch has been green all along. Worth adding to `docs/graph-api-gotchas.md` as a distinct trap from the usual per-endpoint `$top` ceiling: there is no ceiling to stay under, the parameter is simply unsupported.

## Related work landed on the sibling issue

`45f0fe0` closed #194 — `ModelScores`, the previously-unmapped sixth score category (`meanResourceSpikeTimeScore`, which the shipped `DeviceScores` fetch had been silently discarding), and the `ResourcePerformance` widening including a zero-is-absent bug where `totalRamInMB=0` was emitted as a real reading on a VM that plainly has RAM. Two new query-mechanics gotchas went in with it: `$count=true` empties `value` on `ModelScores`, and `$orderby=id` returns 500 on `AppHealthDeviceModelPerformance`. None of it changes anything shipped from this issue — `intune.device_encryption`, `intune.hardware_inventory` and `intune.device_startup_process` are unaffected.

## Re-probe 2026-07-24 (later) — a FOURTH theory falsified, and the census that should have been run first

Full `userExperienceAnalytics*` family census as `graph2otel-poller`, every segment enumerated from the beta EDM (44 nav properties) and GET'd bare, plus 14 request shapes against the target. `[live-measured 2026-07-24, #199, n=1 tenant]`

`userExperienceAnalyticsDeviceStartupProcessPerformance` is still `200` / `"@odata.count": 0` on both versions under every shape tried: bare, three numeric `$filter`s, two `$orderby`s, `$select` of real columns, `Prefer: odata.maxpagesize=25`, single-entity, `/$count`.

### Theory 4 — "the per-process input only exists on one device" — REFUTED

This was the obvious remaining explanation, since the bare per-device list serves 5 rows for one device. It is wrong. The rollup's raw input exists on **7 devices / 27 (device, process) rows** right now:

```
WmiPrvSE     on 6 devices
MsSense      on 6 devices
omadmclient  on 5 devices
```

A rollup over that would trivially produce rows with `deviceCount` 5–6. It produces none. So the input is not the constraint, and this joins device count, boot-telemetry volume and request shape on the falsified list. **Four theories, four refutations — the "no unblock condition attached" position recorded in `45f0fe0` is holding up and should stay.**

### The handler is real and model-faithful, so this is not a routing or shape problem

Worth recording so nobody re-opens that line of enquiry:

- `$select=bogusProperty` → `400 "Could not find a property named 'bogusProperty' on type 'microsoft.graph.userExperienceAnalyticsDeviceStartupProcessPerformance'."` — it knows its own type.
- `$filter` is accepted on exactly the three properties the EDM annotates as filterable (`deviceCount`, `medianImpactInMs`, `totalImpactInMs`) and rejected on the three it does not (`processName`, `productName`, `publisher`).
- The binding is a plain `ContainsTarget="true"` collection nav, **identical in kind** to the populated siblings — it is not secretly a function.
- There is **no** `summarize`-style function for startup processes anywhere in the family, and none of the **77** `deviceManagementReports` actions mentions startup, process or user-experience-analytics. The async report/export API is not an alternate route to this aggregate.

### The one real pattern in the census — model-keyed rollups

| populated (application-keyed) | empty (model-keyed) |
| --- | --- |
| `AppHealthApplicationPerformance` 3 | `AppHealthDeviceModelPerformance` 0 |
| `AppHealthApplicationPerformanceByOSVersion` 12 | `BatteryHealthModelPerformance` 0 |
| `BatteryHealthAppImpact` 7 | `WorkFromAnywhereModelPerformance` 0 |
| `AppHealthOSVersionPerformance` 2 | |

Corroborated twice over: all 8 `DevicePerformance` rows carry `"modelStartupPerformanceScore": -1.0`, and `summarizeDevicePerformanceDevices(summarizeBy='model')` returns `200` with 0 rows.

**This is a correlation, not a mechanism, and `ModelScores` already breaks it** by publishing one row. It is recorded as an observation only. The target is process-keyed and is the only fleet rollup in its family, so it has no populated peer to compare against — its nearest structural analogue, `ImpactingProcess`, returns `500`.

### Untestable today, stated rather than assumed

- **Enablement state could not be read.** `?$select=userExperienceAnalyticsSettings` returns `401 UnknownInConvertApiError` despite `DeviceManagementServiceConfig.Read.All` + `DeviceManagementConfiguration.Read.All` on the token. The bare singleton reports `"settings": null`, which is indistinguishable from "not projected for this caller". It also reports `lastReportAggregationDateTime: "0001-01-01T00:00:00Z"` — the .NET zero date — but whether that field governs UXA rollups or only the compliance summarization beside it is **unknown**, and is not being turned into theory five.
- **Device scope could not be read at all** — `DeviceScopes` `500`, `DeviceScope` `404`, `SummarizedDeviceScopes()` `500`. Scope filtering therefore cannot be ruled out.
- Five segments return a stable (not transient) `500`: `Categories`, `DeviceScopes`, `ImpactingProcess`, `RemoteConnection`, `SummarizedDeviceScopes`. With one tenant there is no way to tell tenant-specific from Graph-wide.

**No new unblock condition is attached, deliberately.** Nothing found here is a mechanism, and attaching a fifth predicted trigger would repeat the mistake this issue has already made four times.

### ⚠️ The census found a PRODUCTION DEFECT — filed as #255

The important outcome of this probe is not about the rollup. The bare `userExperienceAnalyticsDeviceStartupProcesses` list serves **5 rows for ONE device** while the tenant has **27 rows across 7**, with **no `@odata.nextLink`** to signal the loss. The shipped `intune.device_startup_process` collector emits 18.5% of the available data and looks healthy doing it. Re-verified independently against the wire before filing. See **#255**.

### CORRECTION — the "rolling window" finding recorded on this issue earlier today is WRONG

The 2026-07-24 comment above recorded:

> **`DeviceStartupProcesses` is a rolling window, not a cumulative list** … records appearing and disappearing … **is the endpoint's behaviour, not a dropped fetch or a mapping fault.**

The observation was real (10 rows for `1625d698` on 07-21, 2 for `13bca6e7` this morning, 5 for `0703fa65` this afternoon) but the explanation was not. Every one of those devices still holds its full row set today, reachable via `?$filter=managedDeviceId eq '<guid>'`. What rotates is **which single device the bare list happens to serve** — a serving artifact. So it **is** a dropped fetch, which is precisely what that note ruled out.

Recorded prominently because "this is the endpoint's normal behaviour" is the most expensive class of wrong entry: it instructs the next reader not to look.

Note also that the `$filter` which reaches the data is annotated in the EDM as **unsupported** on `managedDeviceId` (`"Supports: $select, $OrderBy"`). Wire over docs, in the direction where trusting the EDM would have ruled out the fix.

## Escalation attempt complete — H2 settled, and the summarize path is broadly non-functional

Following the maintainer's "one more escalation attempt first" call, the untested hypothesis H2 from this morning's census was run. It needed correcting before it could be run at all, and the answer is more decisive than expected. `[live-measured 2026-07-24, #199, n=1 tenant]`

### H2 as posed was untestable — the parameter values did not exist

The proposed test was `summarizeDevicePerformanceDevices(summarizeBy='manufacturer')` and `(summarizeBy='operatingSystemVersion')`. Both return:

```
400 BadRequest: The string 'manufacturer' is not a valid enumeration type constant.
```

The real member set, from the beta EDM:

```xml
<EnumType Name="userExperienceAnalyticsSummarizedBy">
  <Member Name="none" Value="0" /><Member Name="model" Value="1" />
  <Member Name="allRegressions" Value="3" /><Member Name="modelRegression" Value="4" />
  <Member Name="manufacturerRegression" Value="5" />
  <Member Name="operatingSystemVersionRegression" Value="6" />
  <Member Name="unknownFutureValue" Value="7" />
</EnumType>
```

(Note `Value="2"` is absent — a removed member, not a gap worth chasing.)

Worth recording as method: **a hypothesis whose test uses invented parameter values is not a test.** Those two strings came from reasoning about what the axis "should" be rather than from the EDM, and they would have produced a `400` that read like "the function is broken" — a fifth false verdict on this issue. The EDM is the cheap oracle and should have been read first.

### Run against the members that actually exist

| `summarizeBy` | result |
| --- | --- |
| `model` | **200**, 0 rows |
| `none` | **400** backend error |
| `allRegressions` | **400** backend error |
| `modelRegression` | **400** backend error |
| `manufacturerRegression` | **400** backend error |
| `operatingSystemVersionRegression` | **400** backend error |

All five failures carry the same `DeviceFE/StatelessDeviceFEService` backend error body seen on the five `500`-ing UXA segments in the census.

**So H2 resolves, but not to the model-keyed-specifically answer it proposed.** `model` is the only member the tenant answers at all, and it answers empty. The summarize/aggregation function is **broadly non-functional here**, which sits alongside the five UXA segments returning stable `500`s and every model-keyed rollup returning 0.

### Where that leaves this issue

Five theories have now been tested and none survived: device count, boot-telemetry volume, request shape, per-process input availability, and now the summarize-axis hypothesis. The census also established that the target's OData handler is real and model-faithful, its binding is an ordinary contained collection nav identical to the populated siblings, no `summarize` function exists for startup processes, and none of the 77 `deviceManagementReports` actions touches this data.

**There is no mechanism reachable from here, and no tenant action available that has not already been tried.** Continuing to probe is not converging — each round costs real calls and returns the same zeroes.

Recommendation, and it is the same disposition the two posture lists already received in `45f0fe0`: **record `userExperienceAnalyticsDeviceStartupProcessPerformance` in the permanent-gap ledger in `docs/graph-api-gotchas.md` under the existing "reachable but never populated" class, with the five falsified theories attached so nobody re-derives them, and close this issue.** The per-device sibling ships and works; the fleet rollup is opportunistic and this tenant never gets it.

That will be done in the same commit as the other work currently in flight, so the ledger entry and the close land together rather than the issue closing on a promise.

### Unaffected

`intune.device_encryption`, `intune.hardware_inventory` and `intune.device_startup_process` all remain live. Note the last of those is being fixed under **#255** — the fetch defect found by this census, which is the genuinely valuable outcome of the whole exercise.

## Closed — ledgered in `docs/graph-api-gotchas.md`

**Correction on the SHA, so `git show` does not mislead a later reader.** The closing commit `2ce5a77` is **empty** — it carries only the `Closes #199` keyword. The actual ledger edit landed one commit earlier in **`3d129cb`**, swept in with the seven-lane merge. History is not being rewritten to tidy that up (the repo rule is explicit about published history); this comment is the record instead. **Read `3d129cb` for the change, not `2ce5a77`.**

`userExperienceAnalyticsDeviceStartupProcessPerformance` is now in the permanent-gap ledger under the existing **reachable but never populated** class, alongside the two posture lists from `45f0fe0`.

The entry carries all five refuted theories, which is the point of its length — four of them were recorded at the time as confident, reasoned verdicts, and each cost a probing round to undo:

1. Device count / the documented five-device EA floor — refuted by `ModelScores` publishing a `modelDeviceCount: 1` bucket while ignoring a five-device one.
2. Boot-telemetry volume — the condition **fired** (3 records/2 devices → 11/6; scored devices 4 → 10) and nothing moved.
3. Request shape — 14 shapes across both versions.
4. Per-process input availability — the input exists on **7 devices / 27 rows**.
5. The summarize axis — only `model` answers `200` (empty); every other valid member `400`s with the same backend error as the five UXA segments that `500`.

The ledger says explicitly **not to attach an unblock condition** to this segment. An unconditioned "do not start" caused real damage on #106; an unfulfillable predicted trigger is the same failure wearing a rationale.

### The valuable outcome was not about the rollup

**#255** — the fetch defect this investigation exposed in a *shipped* collector — is fixed in `3d129cb`. `intune.device_startup_process` was emitting **5 of 27** available rows and looking healthy doing it. That, and the correction to the "rolling window" note, are what the probing actually bought.

### Also closed from this issue's lineage

`intune.device_encryption`, `intune.hardware_inventory` and `intune.device_startup_process` all remain live; the last now fans out per device over `$batch`.

body:
## What

`insights-logs-windows365auditlogs` is landing on `graph2otelm7kni` and **no issue catalogues it** — it is not in #135's 20-category map nor #134's three unknowns. It is a Windows 365 / Cloud PC **admin audit** stream (config changes to Cloud PC user settings, provisioning policies, etc.). Following the #134 discipline: an enabled-and-writing category must not sit unexamined — assess it, then decide build / already-covered / turn off.

## Live sample (probed as graph2otel-poller, 2026-07-19, m7kni)

Tiny volume (1 blob, 36 KB). One real record, `operationName: "Create CloudPcUserSetting"`:

```json
{
  "time": "2026-07-19T15:07:16.0166130Z",
  "operationName": "Create CloudPcUserSetting",
  "resultType": "Success",
  "category": "Windows365AuditLogs",
  "tenantId": "4b8c18bd-...",
  "identity": { "UPN": [{"Identity":"rob@m7kni.io"}], "ObjectID": [], "ApplicationID": [{"Identity":"69cc3193-..."}] },
  "properties": {
    "ComponentName": "UserSettingControllerV1", "ServiceName": "CloudPC Service",
    "OtherExtendedProperties": "operationType:Create,category:CloudPC,activityDateTime:7/19/2026 3:07:15 PM,correlationId:...,resources:[{DisplayName:user, Type:CloudPcUserSetting, ResourceId:..., ModifiedProperty:[{Name:Id,...},{Name:SelfServiceEnabled,NewValue:False},{Name:LocalAdminEnabled,NewValue:True},...]}],"
  }
}
```

## Traps observed (wire, not docs)

- **The actionable detail is a semi-structured STRING, not JSON.** `properties.OtherExtendedProperties` packs `operationType`, `category`, `correlationId`, and `resources[].ModifiedProperty[]` into one delimited string with **US-format datetimes** (`7/19/2026 3:07:15 PM`). Parsing it is bespoke; there is no clean nested object.
- **Event time:** top-level `time` vs the `activityDateTime` inside the string — must be checked for the same envelope-vs-event-time skew every other category has shown (#135). Do not bind to `time` without verifying.
- **`identity` is an array-of-objects shape** (`UPN: [{Identity: ...}]`), not a scalar.

## Assess before building (per #134)

1. **Overlap — likely the deciding question.** `m365.activity` (O365 Management API) already declares a `Windows365CustomerLockbox` record type (`internal/collectors/m365/activity/recordtypes.go:220`). Check whether Cloud PC admin audits ALSO flow through the O365 Management Activity API and/or `m365.unified_audit` — if so this is already covered and the category should be turned off, not built.
2. **Volume** on a real Cloud PC tenant (m7kni barely uses it).
3. **Verdict:** build a collector (parsing `OtherExtendedProperties`) / already-covered by m365.activity or unified_audit / not worth it → turn off.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Overlap assessed vs `m365.activity` + `m365.unified_audit` (does CloudPC audit flow there already?)
- [ ] Event-time binding verified against a live sample (not `time` blindly)
- [ ] Volume measured
- [ ] Verdict recorded: build / already-covered / turn off — and if turn off, the category is removed from the diagnostic setting, not left enabled

Refs #134, #135, #100

comments.body:
## Spike verdict (2026-07-19): assessed → keep the category ENABLED, defer building a collector

Assessed the three ACs live (as graph2otel-poller from camden). Verdict: **do not build a bespoke collector now, do not turn the category off — keep it enabled and revisit only on a real Cloud PC tenant.**

### Overlap — NOT covered by a shipped collector (as far as can be shown), and NOT confirmed covered by unified audit

Probed `/deviceManagement/auditEvents` (the source of `intune.audit_events`) and `/auditLogs/directoryAudits` (`entra.directory_audits`), most-recent 200 each.

**Trap worth recording so a later session doesn't misread it:** a naive substring scan reported "14 CloudPC matches" in the Intune audit and "16" in directory audits — **all false positives.** They matched the string `CloudPC.Read.All` sitting inside each event's `actor.userPermissions` blob (the app's granted scopes), NOT a CloudPC *operation*. Filtering that out: **no `CloudPcUserSetting` / `virtualEndpoint` operation appears in the recent 200 Intune audit events** (the display names are all standard deviceManagement actions — device config, Autopilot, apps). So `intune.audit_events` does **not** capture the CloudPC admin-config stream that `Windows365AuditLogs` carries.

The O365 unified-audit overlap (`m365.unified_audit` via `auditLogQuery`) is **not confirmed either way** — that path is an async query that runs >10min (#100) and m7kni's CloudPC volume is one record, so a probe there is low-value and was not run.

### Volume — negligible on m7kni

One blob, 36 KB, one record (`Create CloudPcUserSetting`) since the category was enabled. m7kni barely uses Cloud PC. A mapper for the semi-structured `OtherExtendedProperties` string (delimited, nested `resources[].ModifiedProperty[]`, US-format dates) cannot be validated against one record without risking the #142 "map from imagination" trap.

### Event-time binding (AC)

Not bound — deferred with the build. Note for whoever builds it: the record has both top-level `time` (envelope) and an `activityDateTime` inside the `OtherExtendedProperties` string; they must be checked for the same envelope-vs-event skew every other category showed (#135), so do not bind to `time` blindly.

### Verdict

- **Do not build now** — one live record is not enough to write a bespoke parser against (wire over docs), and the value on this tenant is nil.
- **Do not turn the category off** — turning off a blob diagnostic category is a one-way door for ad-hoc IR lookups (#96's lesson), and coverage elsewhere is unconfirmed, so removing it would risk a silent audit gap. It is 36 KB; leave it landing.
- **Unblock / revisit condition:** a tenant that actually uses Cloud PC at volume. Then (1) confirm overlap vs `m365.unified_audit`/`m365.activity` with a real query, and (2) if uncovered, build a collector parsing `OtherExtendedProperties` against real multi-record samples.

Closing the spike with this verdict; category stays enabled.

Assessed (verdict above): Windows365AuditLogs is NOT covered by intune.audit_events (the apparent matches were CloudPC.Read.All permission-string noise), O365-unified-audit overlap unconfirmed, and m7kni CloudPC volume is one record. Keep the category enabled (don't turn off — one-way door for IR), defer building a bespoke OtherExtendedProperties parser until a real Cloud PC tenant provides volume.

## Reopening — real Windows 365 data is now flowing (2026-07-19, later)

Rob provisioned a couple of W365 machines. Re-probed the blob as graph2otel-poller: **`insights-logs-windows365auditlogs` now has 4 hourly blobs (~58 KB)** with genuine multi-record admin-audit content — no longer the single-record trap that made it unbuildable earlier today.

Distinct `operationName`s observed so far: `Create CloudPcUserSetting`, `Patch CloudPcProvisioningPolicy`, `Reprovision CloudPcProvisioningPolicy`. Enough real samples to write the `OtherExtendedProperties` parser against the wire (not imagination).

**The unblock condition fired → this is now a BUILD.** Wire facts re-confirmed for the mapper:
- Log-only blob `WindowCollector` over `insights-logs-windows365auditlogs` (blobpipeline), transport `blob`.
- Top-level: `operationName`, `resultType`, `time` (RFC3339 Z envelope).
- `identity` is array-of-objects: `UPN:[{Identity}]`, `ObjectID:[{Identity}]` (actor object id), `ApplicationID:[{Identity}]`, `TenantId:[{Identity}]` — extract `[0].Identity`.
- **`properties.OtherExtendedProperties` is the semi-structured STRING** carrying `operationType`, `category`, `activityDateTime` (US format e.g. `7/19/2026 9:00:29 PM`), `correlationId`, `shoeboxCategory`, and `resources:[{DisplayName, Type, ResourceId, ModifiedProperty:[{Name,OldValue,NewValue}]}]`. Parse the target Type/ResourceId/DisplayName + modified-property NAMES (secret boundary #112: names only, never values).
- **Event time:** verify `time` (envelope) vs the inner `activityDateTime` for skew before binding — do NOT bind to `time` blindly (#135 lesson). Same envelope-vs-event question every category has.
- Overlap vs `m365.unified_audit` still unconfirmed but now moot — build it; if a later unified-audit probe shows dupes, dedupe downstream.

Still keep the category enabled (it is). Buildable next session.

Shipped + deployed + live-verified.

- Collector `intune.cloud_pc_audit` — commit 4608e59, live on camden `version=5059d84`.
- Log-only blob `SnapshotCollector` over `insights-logs-windows365auditlogs` (blobpipeline), transport `blob`. Default-enabled read-only ingest, **not** Experimental (#183) — setting `blob_ingest.account_url` + streaming the category is the whole opt-in, so it auto-ran on deploy with no config change.

**Live verification (camden status.json, 2026-07-19):** `runs=1, last_success=true, failures=0`, `byte_offset=58326, blobs_tracked=4, newest_blob=…/d=19/h=21/…` — consumed all 4 blobs / 21 records across the 8 observed operation types, genuine ingest not empty-success.

**Mapper (built against 21 verbatim live records, #142):**
- Parses the semi-structured `properties.OtherExtendedProperties` STRING with anchored regexes (scalar values are comma-free; resource fields anchor on the following key). Modified-property **NAMES only**, never Old/New values (#112) — which also sidesteps the one hard case, an `assignments` NewValue that is itself nested JSON.
- Event time binds to the inner `activityDateTime` (US-format, UTC), not the envelope `time` (~1s-later export clock, #135). Unparseable → dropped, no fallback.
- It is the `intune.audit_events` peer for Cloud PC: reuses that collector's vocabulary field-for-field (`activity`, `activity_operation_type`, `activity_result`, `category`, `component_name`, `correlation_id`, `id`, `actor_*`, `resource_types`/`resource_display_names`/`modified_property_names`) + one new attr `resource_ids` (which CloudPC policy/setting was touched).
- `identity.Other` (the actor app's granted-scope list + the constant "Windows 365 Ibiza Extension" proxy app) is deliberately ignored — the permission-string noise this spike flagged; the real initiator is the UPN.

Closed by 4608e59.

body:
## The question

Can `intune.devices` run **graph for its metric aggregates and blob for its per-device log twins simultaneously**, so the hourly full-fleet page-walk (graph2otel's single most expensive poll) is retired on a large tenant without losing per-entity detail or metric accuracy?

This is the genuinely-dual-capable case CLAUDE.md flags explicitly ("the one genuinely dual-capable signal (`intune.devices`) is #132's question"; "the 'graph for metrics, blob for logs' split only bites on a collector that emits both"). It is **not** resolved by #131 (which closed "dual mode" for the **log-only** WindowCollectors, where dual ≡ blob because they emit zero metrics — reasoning that does not transfer to a collector emitting both).

## Why this supersedes #132's "redundant → turn off" recommendation

#132 (closed) sampled the `Devices` / `DeviceComplianceOrg` blob categories, found per-device rows, and recommended treating them as **redundant** with the polled walk's twin and **turning them off**. That verdict is correct only if you keep the full walk. It is small-tenant-biased: it under-weights the at-scale case where the *point* is to stop running the walk and serve the per-device twins from blob instead.

**Do NOT turn off the `Devices` / `DeviceComplianceOrg` blob categories.** Keep them enabled; they are the candidate log transport for this design.

## Constraints this design must solve (live-verified)

1. **Transport is `source: graph XOR blob` per collector, enforced by #144 `ConflictsWith`.** A single collector being graph-for-metrics AND blob-for-logs at once is machinery that does not exist. It needs `intune.devices` split so the metric path and the log-twin path can carry different sources — the dual-transport capability #131 declined for the log-only case but which genuinely applies here.
2. **The cheap graph metrics path is currently lossy.** `managedDeviceOverview`'s OS summary summed to **9 against a real fleet of 10** (#132/#130 — no Linux bucket). "graph for metrics" via the overview endpoint needs that gap closed, or metrics still require the full walk.
3. **Blob is NOT a latency win — it is a cost/throttle win at scale.** Measured (#89/#135): blob ran ~73 min behind on a low-volume signal while polling was far ahead. Blob latency improves as volume rises and Graph's reporting/throttle ceiling worsens as volume rises; the curves cross somewhere. Justify this design by the hourly full-fleet walk's throttle cost on a large fleet, **not** by freshness.
4. **Cardinality rule unchanged (#112/#114):** per-device rows are log twins, never metric labels; whichever transport carries them, no per-device id becomes a series label.

## Live-verified facts (probed as graph2otel-poller, 2026-07-18/19)

- `insights-logs-devices` and `insights-logs-devicecomplianceorg` are landing on `graph2otelm7kni` with per-device rows (`DeviceName`, `UPN`, `ComplianceState`, `OS`, `OwnerType`, `DeviceHealthThreatLevel`, `Model`/`Manufacturer`/`Ownership`/`StorageTotal/Free`/`WifiMacAddress`/`IMEI`/`JoinType`, ...). Full field lists on #132.
- The polled `managedDevice` resource carries a wider (~60-field) superset; a field-by-field diff (polled vs blob) is required before the log twin can be switched to `source: blob` without losing signal (recorded on #132, unresolved).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Decide: build the metrics-source/logs-source split for `intune.devices`, or record precisely why not (with the scale threshold where it would pay off)
- [ ] If build: design how a collector declares two transports (metrics=graph, logs=blob) without violating #144's per-collector `ConflictsWith`
- [ ] Resolve the lossy-overview metric path (the 9-vs-10 Linux gap) or state that metrics stay on the walk
- [ ] Field-by-field diff: polled `managedDevice` twin vs blob `Devices`+`DeviceComplianceOrg` rows — what is lost if logs move to blob
- [ ] Until decided: `Devices`/`DeviceComplianceOrg` blob categories stay ENABLED (reverse #132's turn-off recommendation)

Refs #130, #131, #132, #135, #144

comments.body:
## Spike verdict (2026-07-19): the split is already SHIPPED; retiring the walk is deferred, blocked on cheap-accurate metrics

Resolved against the live tenant (as graph2otel-poller from camden) **and** the current code. The issue's framing predates the mechanism that already solves half of it.

### The "graph-for-metrics + blob-for-logs" split is ALREADY BUILT — via two collectors, not #144

This AC — *"design how a collector declares two transports (metrics=graph, logs=blob) without violating #144"* — is moot. That decomposition (one collector, two transports) is the wrong shape and doesn't need building. **#135-F already ships the split as a keep-gauges/suppress-twin pair** (`internal/collectors/intune/manageddevices/blob.go`):
- `intune.devices` (polled SnapshotCollector) — keeps emitting its bounded fleet **gauges** from the page-walk.
- `intune.devices_blob` (blob log-only collector) — emits the per-device **twin** (`intune.managed_device`) from the `Devices` blob category.
- The composition root registers `RegisterBlobTwinOwner(eventManagedDevice, intune.devices_blob)`: when the blob twin runs, the **polled twin is suppressed** so the two transports don't double-emit.

So metrics already come from graph and logs already come from blob, simultaneously, with **zero** #144 change — #144's per-collector `source: graph XOR blob` is satisfied because these are two collectors, each single-transport. The blob twin is normalized byte-identical to the polled twin (verified 2026-07-18, #135), **except `partnerReportedThreatState`** — absent from the `Devices` category, it comes from `DeviceComplianceOrg` (the field-diff AC: that one field is what "moves to blob" would lose, and it's covered by keeping the second category).

### What is NOT solved — and why the full-fleet walk can't be retired yet

The point of this issue is to **stop running the hourly page-walk**. Keep-gauges/suppress-twin still runs it — for the **gauges**. Retiring it needs the metric aggregates from somewhere cheaper than the walk, and neither candidate works today:

1. **`managedDeviceOverview` (the cheap graph summary) is LIVE-CONFIRMED LOSSY.** `[live-measured 2026-07-19, #197, n=1 tenant]` Its `deviceOperatingSystemSummary` = iOS 4 + macOS 2 + Windows 5 = **11**; `enrolledDeviceCount` = **12**; the true `managedDevices` fleet = **13**. It has **no Linux bucket and no empty-OS bucket**, so it silently undercounts by 1-2 devices on a 13-device tenant. It cannot back an accurate OS/compliance gauge. (Same class as #130/#132's 9-vs-10.)
2. **Counting the blob rows can't reproduce the gauges either** — `blob.go`'s own doc states it: the `Devices` blob is a *periodic inventory dump*, not a guaranteed complete per-window census, so counting a window's rows double-counts a device that appears in multiple snapshots and under-counts one that hasn't been re-dumped. Deriving accurate counts would need a verified full-inventory-cycle dedupe (latest-row-per-device over one complete cycle), and the cycle's completeness/cadence is unverified.

### Verdict

- **Defer retiring the walk.** The split is shipped; the walk stays because it is the only source of *accurate* fleet gauges today. `managedDeviceOverview` is unusable (lossy, out of our control to fix); blob-derived counts need a full-census dedupe that isn't proven.
- **`Devices` / `DeviceComplianceOrg` blob categories stay ENABLED** — they power the shipped blob twin (reaffirmed; #132's turn-off recommendation stays reversed).
- **Scale threshold to revisit:** when the hourly page-walk's IntuneDevices-tier throttle cost genuinely dominates (order thousands of devices), the payoff is a blob-census-dedupe collector that produces accurate counts from the blob so the walk can be dropped. Below that (m7kni: 13 devices) the walk is free and this is not worth building.

Closing this spike: **the split asked for is already live (#135-F); the walk-retirement it was really after is deferred with the two blocking reasons above and a scale threshold.** No code change this pass.

Spike resolved (verdict above): the graph-metrics/blob-logs split is already shipped via #135-F keep-gauges/suppress-twin; retiring the full-fleet walk is deferred — managedDeviceOverview is live-confirmed lossy and blob rows can't be counted without a full-census dedupe. Blob categories stay enabled. Revisit at ~thousands of devices.

body:
Part of the Intune reporting/analytics spike (tracker: #192). **Spike first — do NOT build the engine until the live probe is green and Rob signs off on the fifth-transport lift.**

## Why this is different

The Intune Data Warehouse is the **only app-only source of historical / trend data** — it samples daily and keeps a 30/60-day star-schema. Everything else graph2otel reads is current-state; nothing in Graph gives time-series. That is the entire payoff. But it does not fit the `graphclient` transport — it is effectively a **fifth ingest engine** alongside logpipeline / jobpipeline / blobpipeline / o365pipeline:

- **Host:** `https://fef.{region}.manage.microsoft.com/ReportingService/DataWarehouseFEService/{collection}?api-version=v1.0` — `{region}` (e.g. `msua06`) is tenant-specific and **discovered from the Data Warehouse blade** in the Intune admin center; not a fixed host.
- **Audience:** `https://api.manage.microsoft.com/` (NOT `graph.microsoft.com`, NOT the Graph SDK).
- **App role:** `get_data_warehouse` under the **Intune** API (an application permission), NOT a Graph scope.
- **Query model:** GET-only OData v4, `$filter` restricted to `DateKey` / `RowLastModifiedDateTimeUTC`, plus a custom `maxhistorydays=N`. Star schema — fact rows carry surrogate `*Key` FKs; join the dimension collections client-side. Win32 apps excluded.

Docs: [configure app-only auth](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/developer/data-warehouse/configure-app-only-auth) · [endpoints](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/developer/data-warehouse/ref-api-endpoints) · [collections](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/developer/data-warehouse/ref-collections) · [data model](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/developer/data-warehouse/ref-data-model)

## What the spike must prove (live, as the poller, before any build)

App-only is **docs-supported but unverified end-to-end**. Live-measured 2026-07-19: a client-credentials token for `https://api.manage.microsoft.com/.default` **issues** (aud correct) but carries `roles=[]` — the `get_data_warehouse` role is ungranted, so a DW read would 401/403 today.

- [ ] Grant `get_data_warehouse` (Intune API app role) to `graph2otel-poller` via `homelab-agentic-mgmt`; record the appRole GUID + grant here (standing read-scope consent covers it, but this is a non-Graph API so name it explicitly).
- [ ] Discover the tenant's DW region base URL from the admin-center blade (needs Rob, or a discovery probe).
- [ ] Mint a fresh token (roles embed at issue time) and **GET one date-keyed collection end-to-end** (e.g. `enrollmentActivities` or `compliancePolicyStatusDeviceActivities`) — prove app-only actually returns rows, not just a token.
- [ ] Record the verdict on this issue with an evidence tag. **Go/no-go on the fifth engine depends on this probe, not the docs.**

## Candidate collections (if the probe is green)

Highest value = the daily-history tables with no Graph equivalent:
- `enrollmentActivities`, `compliancePolicyStatusDeviceActivities`, `deviceConfigurationProfileDeviceActivities`, `policyDeviceActivities`, `mobileAppInstallStatusCounts` — per-day count-by-state → **directly metric-shaped daily gauges/counters**.
- `devicePropertyHistories` — per-device daily snapshot, 60 days (log-shaped trend).
- `intuneManagementExtensions` — IME health per Windows device per day, 60 days.

## Build decision (only after a green probe)

- [ ] Decide: a new `internal/dwpipeline` engine + `dw.*` namespace peer domain, or defer. Weigh the fifth-transport maintenance cost against the trend-data payoff. Note `internal/collectordoc` must walk any new registration path (the #139/#100 coverage-gate trap) — a fifth path changes `Rows`' signature.
- [ ] If deferred, park this issue with the probe result recorded so a future session doesn't re-derive it.

## Acceptance (of the SPIKE)
- [ ] The end-to-end app-only probe result is recorded here with a `live-measured (date)` tag — green or red.
- [ ] A go/no-go on the DW engine build is stated, with reasoning. (A green probe does not obligate the build; a red probe closes app-only DW.)

comments.body:
GO on feasibility — app-only Data Warehouse access is **live-verified working** (2026-07-19, as graph2otel-poller).

## Grant (done)
`get_data_warehouse` (appRole `<guid-39>`) assigned to the poller SP `13371536-9950-4988-90f4-343566456781` on the **Microsoft Intune API** SP `<guid-40>` (appId `<guid-41>`). Assignment id `NhU3E1CZiEmQ9DQ1ZkVngZsT_08s8MtBgb76vEhidDQ`. Granted via homelab-agentic-mgmt. **Read-only.** Note: this is a granted-but-unused scope until a DW collector ships — revoke if the build is a no-go.

## Region URL
`https://fef.msub06.manage.microsoft.com/ReportingService/DataWarehouseFEService` (api-version=v1.0). `{region}` for m7kni = **msub06**.

## End-to-end probe (fresh token after grant)
- `api.manage.microsoft.com` token roles = `["get_data_warehouse"]` ✅
- **Service root** `?api-version=v1.0` → `200`, lists all **42 collections**: `devices, users, userDeviceAssociations, devicePropertyHistories, enrollmentActivities, compliancePolicyStatusDeviceActivities(+PerPolicy), deviceConfigurationProfileDeviceActivities/UserActivities, policyDeviceActivities/UserActivities/policyTypeActivities, mobileAppInstallStatusCounts, intuneManagementExtensions(+HealthStates/Versions), mamApplications/mamApplicationInstances/mamCheckins/mamDeviceHealths, termsAndConditions, appRevisions/appTypes, policies/policyTypes/policyPlatformTypes` + all the dimension tables (`dates, deviceCategories, deviceTypes, ownerTypes, complianceStates, managementStates, managementAgentTypes, deviceRegistrationStates, enrollmentFailureCategories/Reasons, ...`).
- `dates` → `200`, real row (`dateKey:20160101, fullDate, dayOfWeek, ...`).
- `devices` → `200`, real row — confirms the **star-schema surrogate keys** (`deviceTypeKey, ownerTypeKey, complianceStateKey, ...` + `rowLastModifiedDateTimeUTC`); dimensions must be joined client-side.
- `enrollmentActivities` → `200` but **0 rows** on m7kni.

## Verdict
**App-only DW is FEASIBLE** (`live-measured 2026-07-19, #196`). The fifth-engine feasibility blocker is cleared.

## Caveat that shapes the BUILD go/no-go
The DW's unique value is *historical/trend* data — the daily `*Activities` tables and `devicePropertyHistories`. On this 6-device tenant several of those are **empty right now** (`enrollmentActivities`=0). Current-state collections (`devices`, `users`) have data but overlap what Graph already gives. So the fifth-engine build is de-risked technically, but its **immediate payoff on m7kni is limited** until the daily tables accumulate. Build-vs-defer is the remaining decision (a fifth `internal/dwpipeline` engine + `dw.*` namespace, distinct host/audience/auth).

Closing as **won't-do** (decision by Rob, 2026-07-19).

**Rationale:** the DW's only differentiated value is *historical/trend* data, and that does not translate into the Grafana model — a TSDB rejects backfilled old samples (Prometheus drops samples older than ~1h; graph2otel's emitter would stamp the historical `dateKey`/`rowLastModifiedDateTimeUTC`, which the backend rejects), so the 30–60-day server-side history cannot be ingested usefully. Everything else the DW exposes (current-state devices/users/compliance/config/apps) is already collected via the Graph API. So a fifth ingest engine buys nothing we can actually use.

**Feasibility is still banked** (above): app-only works via `get_data_warehouse`, region `msub06`, all 42 collections reachable — if the Grafana-side constraint ever changes, this is a solved problem to reopen from.

**Cleanup done:** the `get_data_warehouse` app-role grant on graph2otel-poller was **revoked** (appRoleAssignment `NhU3E1…` deleted, `204`; verified the poller is back to its prior 46 assignments). No unused scope left on the poller — read-only least-privilege posture restored.

body:
Part of the Intune reporting/analytics spike (tracker: #192). Build regardless of the Data Warehouse outcome.

## What & why

The portal "Device attestation status (preview)" and "Device encryption status" (Monitor) surfaces expose per-device boot-security state — BitLocker, Secure Boot, TPM version, code integrity, virtualization-based security, memory integrity, firmware protection, secured-core. This is real security posture beyond the coarse compliance flag graph2otel already emits, and it is reachable app-only with a scope already held (`DeviceManagementManagedDevices.Read.All`) — **no new engine, no new grant**.

## API surface (app-only confirmed by scope; the poller already holds `DeviceManagementManagedDevices.Read.All`)

Three overlapping routes — pick the cheapest that carries the fields:

1. **`deviceHealthAttestationState`** — a complex property on `managedDevice`, v1.0 + beta. Reachable via `GET /deviceManagement/managedDevices?$select=id,deviceName,deviceHealthAttestationState` (or `$expand`). Rich per-device fields: `bitLockerStatus`, `secureBoot`, `codeIntegrity`, `tpmVersion`, `virtualizationBasedSecurity`, `memoryIntegrityProtection`, `firmwareProtection`, `securedCorePC`, `systemManagementMode`. **Preferred** — folds into the existing `intune.devices` fleet fetch (`FleetFetcher`) rather than a new poll. [docs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/intune-devices-devicehealthattestationstate)
2. `TpmAttestationStatus` / `WindowsDeviceHealthAttestationReport` — export-job reportNames backing the portal grids. Use only if the `$select` route omits a needed column; otherwise avoid the export write-scope path.
3. `deviceIdentityAttestationDetail` (**beta only**) — newer "Windows enrollment attestation" per-device state. [docs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/intune-devices-deviceidentityattestationdetail?view=graph-rest-beta)

## Data-model decision

Per-device boot-security is **log-shaped** (cardinality grows with the fleet) → emit a per-device log twin (event e.g. `intune.device_attestation`) carrying the attestation fields. Add **bounded gauges** for the tenant-shaped rollups only: device count by `bitLockerStatus`, by `secureBoot` state, by `tpmVersion`, by attestation health — a `count by` the twin answers the same for free, so keep the gauge set small.

## Scope
- [ ] Extend the `intune.devices` fleet `$select` (or a dedicated collector) to pull `deviceHealthAttestationState`; live-verify the field set is populated on m7kni Windows devices.
- [ ] Emit a per-device attestation log twin.
- [ ] Bounded gauges: device count by BitLocker / SecureBoot / TPM-version / attestation-health buckets.
- [ ] If a needed column is absent from the `$select` route, fall back to `TpmAttestationStatus` export (reuse `internal/exportjob`) — decide on live evidence, not docs.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Fields validated against a **live** m7kni Windows device (attestation state is null on non-Windows / non-attested devices — an all-null sample must not be read as "field unsupported").
- [ ] No secret/credential-shaped field emitted (there are none here, but confirm — this stays read-only posture).
- [ ] `docs/collectors.md` regenerated; gate green.

comments.body:
First wave landed in `35c4afa` (pushed to main).

**Shipped:** `intune.device_attestation` ← `TpmAttestationStatus` export report (5 live rows on m7kni). Gauge `intune.device_attestation.devices` by `attestation_status` × `os`; per-device log twin (AttestationStatus, TpmManufacturer/Version, Model, Ownership, LastCheckin); WARN when status != Completed. Experimental/default-off, `DeviceManagementManagedDevices.ReadWrite.All` (already held).

**Live-measured pivot (important):** the `deviceHealthAttestationState` **property on `managedDevices` is null on every device tenant-wide** (all 5 sampled, incl. Windows), so the `$select`/`$expand` approach in the original issue body yields nothing here. The **export report is the working path** — same property-vs-export lesson as `intune.app_install_status`. Recorded in the collector package doc.

**Follow-up (not yet built):** `WindowsDeviceHealthAttestationReport` export — returns the full boot-security field set (BitLocker/SecureBoot/CodeIntegrity/VSM/FirmwareProtection/SecuredCorePC/MemoryIntegrity/SystemManagementMode, all with `_loc` siblings); **1 row live** (only 1 attesting device on m7kni). Higher-value posture detail; worth a second collector when useful.

## Boot-security posture shipped + deployed + verified — closing #195

`intune.device_boot_security` ← `WindowsDeviceHealthAttestationReport` shipped in `96b0591`, deployed to camden `:main` (version=77af941), live-verified: `enabled=true, has_run=true, runs=1, last_success=true, last_error=none`. Mapped against 2 verbatim m7kni rows (LAPHAM + DESKTOP-Q8HBBJ4).

- Faceted bounded gauge `intune.device_boot_security.devices{posture,status,os}` (bitlocker/secure_boot/code_integrity/vsm/firmware_protection/memory_integrity/secured_core_pc).
- Full-posture per-device twin `intune.device_boot_security` (+ boot_debugging/os_kernel_debugging/safe_mode/winpe/elam/aik/dep + tpm_version + attestation_error). WARN on a non-Success attestation.

This was the last named item on this issue (the follow-up to the earlier `TpmAttestationStatus` `intune.device_attestation`, which is also live on camden). Both device-attestation and boot-security posture now ship. **Closing.** `WindowsDeviceHealthAttestationReport`'s `_loc` display columns are deliberately not emitted (the collector carries Microsoft's canonical enum values).
