body:
Part of the Intune reporting/analytics spike (tracker: #192). Build regardless of the Data Warehouse outcome.

## What & why

`intune.endpoint_analytics` (Experimental) already polls 6 UXA segments and emits bounded gauges + a per-device log twin. Endpoint analytics exposes more "advanced analytics" surfaces that are genuinely absent from the device/compliance endpoints. This issue adds the ones that are live-reachable app-only and have a clean OTel shape. Same collector, same `DeviceManagementManagedDevices.Read.All` scope, same Experimental gate.

Docs: [userExperienceAnalytics resources](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/intune-devices-userexperienceanalyticsoverview) (per-segment pages under the same path).

## Live-measured segment triage (2026-07-19, poller vs m7kni)

| segment | result | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `userExperienceAnalyticsModelScores` (v1.0) | `200 value=0` | **add** — bounded by device model; empty on m7kni (few models), real data on a larger fleet. Metric-shaped (per-model score gauges). |
| `userExperienceAnalyticsAnomalySeverityOverview` (beta) | `200` — `low/medium/high/informationalSeverityAnomalyCount` | **add** — bounded counts by severity. Metric-shaped gauge. |
| `userExperienceAnalyticsOverview` (v1.0 + beta) | `400 ResourceNotFound` | **skip — dead** (re-confirms #179). |
| `userExperienceAnalyticsScoreHistory` (v1.0) | `400 ResourceNotFound` | **skip — dead.** |
| `userExperienceAnalyticsWorkFromAnywhereMetrics` (v1.0) | `400 No OData route` on the plain path — needs `/{id}` or a `.../workFromAnywhereModelPerformance` navigation | **investigate the correct route**, then add model-level WFA scores (bounded). |

## Scope
- [x] `userExperienceAnalyticsModelScores` — per-model score gauges (bounded cardinality = # device models).
- [x] `userExperienceAnalyticsAnomalySeverityOverview` (beta) — gauge of anomaly counts by severity.
- [x] Work-from-anywhere model performance / hardware-readiness (bounded, model-level) — resolve the correct route first (plain `WorkFromAnywhereMetrics` list 400s).
- [x] Per-app app-health detail beyond the current crash count: `appHangCount`, `meanTimeToFailureInMinutes`, `activeDeviceCount` from `userExperienceAnalyticsAppHealthApplicationPerformance` (already polled — widen the mapping).
- [x] ~~(Optional, beta) model/OS-level battery + resource performance rollups~~ **not built, deliberately** — Microsoft's battery rollups are an aggregate of data graph2otel already collects per device, so a local rollup has no floor at all; tracked as optional on #225. Original text: (Optional, beta) model/OS-level battery + resource performance rollups (`...BatteryHealthModelPerformance`, `...BatteryHealthOsPerformance`) — metric-shaped, complement the existing device-level battery twin.

## Acceptance
- [x] Model/OS/tenant-level scores → bounded gauges; any per-device/per-app additions → the existing log twin (never dropped, #114).
- [x] Beta segments stay under the existing `Experimental()` gate.
- [x] Mappings validated against a **live** UXA response (ModelScores + anomalies are empty/small on m7kni — an empty list must not mask a mapping bug; #142/#129 lesson).
- [x] No per-device-per-boot series emitted as metrics — startup histories stay log-only.
- [x] `docs/collectors.md` regenerated; gate green.



---

> **CLOSED by `45f0fe0` (2026-07-24).** All five scope items shipped or dispositioned — see [the closing comment](https://github.com/rknightion/graph2otel/issues/194#issuecomment-5070440427).
>
> **The triage table above is superseded on one point.** It says `ModelScores` is "empty on m7kni (few models), real data on a larger fleet", and later comments hardened that into "needs ≥5 EA-scored devices sharing one model string". That is **WRONG** — the first published row has `modelDeviceCount: 1`, while a five-device model bucket on the same tenant the same day was absent. What gates a UXA rollup being published is unknown and is not device count; recorded in `docs/graph-api-gotchas.md`.

comments.body:
First wave landed in `35c4afa` (pushed to main).

**Shipped:** added `intune.uxa.anomaly_count` to `intune.endpoint_analytics` — the beta `userExperienceAnalyticsAnomalySeverityOverview` singleton, emitted as a bounded gauge by `anomaly_severity` (low/medium/high/informational). Live-verified `200` with those four int fields on m7kni (all zero — a valid steady state).

**Blocked-on-data (not built, recorded so a later session does not re-derive):**
- `userExperienceAnalyticsModelScores` — `200` but **`@odata.count=0`** on m7kni (too few device models scored). Cannot build the mapper against live samples per the "never map against empty/docs" rule; revisit when the tenant has model scores.
- `userExperienceAnalyticsAppHealthApplicationPerformance` widening — also `count=0` live.
- `userExperienceAnalyticsWorkFromAnywhereMetrics` — the plain list path returns `400 No OData route` (needs a `/{id}` or `.../workFromAnywhereModelPerformance` navigation); route to be resolved before building.
- Confirmed dead (do not build): `Overview`, `ScoreHistory` — `400 ResourceNotFound` on both v1.0 and beta.

## WFA shipped — route resolved live; ModelScores/AppHealth stay parked (2026-07-19)

Commit `77af941`. The Work-From-Anywhere piece of this issue is done; the two blocked-on-data pieces are re-confirmed parked.

### WFA — route resolved, built
The blocker on the last comment was "`userExperienceAnalyticsWorkFromAnywhereMetrics` plain-list returns `400 No OData route` — route TBD". Resolved live (as graph2otel-poller, 2026-07-19):
- `.../userExperienceAnalyticsWorkFromAnywhereMetrics` → **400** `No OData route ... ~/singleton/navigation`
- `.../userExperienceAnalyticsWorkFromAnywhereMetrics/allDevices` → **400** `~/singleton/navigation/key`
- `.../userExperienceAnalyticsWorkFromAnywhereMetrics/allDevices/metricDevices` → **200, 1 row** ✅

Built as an 8th sub-fetch on `intune.endpoint_analytics` (it is a `userExperienceAnalytics*` signal and reuses the collector's Experimental gate + per-fetch skip-and-log). Mapped against the one verbatim device row (LAPHAM: `upgradeEligibility: "upgraded"`, every hardware check `false`, all scores `null` — device not yet assessed):
- Bounded gauge `intune.uxa.work_from_anywhere.device_count{upgrade_eligibility, health_state}`.
- Per-device twin `intune.device_work_from_anywhere`: a hardware readiness check rides the twin **only when it FAILED** (the actionable Win11-blocker signal; a capable device carries none), plus cloud/windows posture scores (null omitted). WARN on `notCapable`.

This is the Windows 11 upgrade-readiness detail behind the tenant WFA score — genuinely useful for Win10-EOL migration tracking.

### Still parked — blocked-on-data (re-confirmed live 2026-07-19)
- `userExperienceAnalyticsModelScores` — `@odata.count=0` (too few device models scored). Cannot map against empty; wire over docs.
- `userExperienceAnalyticsAppHealthApplicationPerformance` widening — `count=0`.

`AnomalySeverityOverview` shipped in the first wave. So this issue is now **2 of 4 shipped (anomaly, WFA), 2 parked-on-data (ModelScores, AppHealth)** — staying open scoped to the two parked items. **Unblock:** the tenant accumulating model scores / app-health rows; revisit then. Deploy-verify on camden to follow.

Deploy-verified: the WFA Win11-readiness sub-fetch is live on camden (`intune.endpoint_analytics` version=77af941, runs=1, last_success=true, no error); the metricDevices navigation returns 1 device row on m7kni.

Research: the empty segments are device-count-gated, not misconfigured (2026-07-20)

Live-probed as `graph2otel-poller` + checked current MS docs (Endpoint Analytics support/configure/scores/troubleshoot).

**Root cause = the 5-device EA floor.** MS docs, verbatim: *"a status of insufficient data means there arent enough devices reporting… at least five devices currently required."* m7kni has **1** EA-scored device (LAPHAM). `ModelScores` / `AppHealthApplicationPerformance` / `BatteryHealthModelPerformance` / `BatteryHealthOsPerformance` / `ResourcePerformance` / `AppHealthDeviceModelPerformance` all sit under that floor -> empty by design, not a mapping or config fault.

**These EA scores are Windows-only** (the score is a weighted avg of Startup + Application reliability + Work-from-anywhere). The tenants 2 macOS + 4 iOS + 1 Linux devices cannot contribute — so the lever is *more Windows devices*, not Apple coverage.

**The EA data-collection policy is already correct — no new profile needed.** `windowsHealthMonitoringConfiguration` "Intune data collection policy": `allowDeviceHealthMonitoring=enabled`, scope `bootPerformance`, assigned to **All Devices**. New Windows devices inherit it automatically.

**Unblock path (maintainer action in progress):** Windows desktop VMs are being stood up and kept on. Once >=5 Windows devices report EA telemetry (restart + ~25h each), these segments populate and get built against live rows. So they are **data-gated on device count, not deferred** — #194 stays open scoped to them.

**Buildable NOW:** `userExperienceAnalyticsAppHealthOSVersionPerformance` returns **1 live row** (`osVersion`/`osBuildNumber`/`activeDeviceCount`/`meanTimeToFailureInMinutes`/`osVersionAppHealthScore`) — OS-version aggregation survives the floor. Will build this segment now (bounded gauge by `os_version`), independent of the VM fleet.

**Also filed #199** — the device-inventory / device-query advanced-analytics surface (distinct from these scores) as a new post-v1 collector (Windows + Linux). `[live-measured 2026-07-20, #194]`

`AppHealthOSVersionPerformance` shipped + deployed (`770aaaa`)

The one #194 segment with live data on m7kni is built and live on camden.

- Added `userExperienceAnalyticsAppHealthOSVersionPerformance` (v1.0) to `intune.endpoint_analytics` as three bounded gauges keyed by `os_version` (bounded by the fleet OS-version count): `intune.uxa.app_health.os_version_score{os_version,health_state}`, `intune.uxa.app_health.active_device_count{os_version}`, `intune.uxa.app_health.mean_time_to_failure_minutes{os_version}`. OS-version aggregate -> metric-shaped, **no log twin** (#192).
- Mapped against the **verbatim live m7kni row** (probed as graph2otel-poller 2026-07-20): `osVersion=10.0.26120.3281, activeDeviceCount=1, osVersionAppHealthScore=100, osVersionAppHealthStatus="TBD"`. The int32-max (`2147483647`) MTTF "no failures" sentinel is excluded; the undocumented wire status `"TBD"` buckets to `other` (bounded, wire-over-docs-safe).
- TDD (`TestCollectEmitsAppHealthOSVersionAsBoundedAggregates` pins the bounded keys + sentinel exclusion + no-twin), `make check` green, golden + `docs/collectors.md` regenerated.
- **Deployed + verified on camden** (`version=770aaaa`): `intune.endpoint_analytics` `runs=1, last_success=true, last_error=none`, 1730ms.
- **Why this one and not the rest:** it survives the 5-device EA "insufficient data" floor because it aggregates by **OS build, not device model**.

**#194 stays open**, scoped to the 5 per-model segments (`ModelScores`, `AppHealthApplicationPerformance`, `BatteryHealthModelPerformance`, `BatteryHealthOsPerformance`, `ResourcePerformance`) — all data-gated on the Windows fleet crossing 5 EA-reporting devices. ## Correction: withdrawing the "permanent gap" proposal for the two battery segments

In the comment above I proposed moving `BatteryHealthModelPerformance` and `BatteryHealthOsPerformance` to the permanent-gap ledger, on the grounds that m7kni will never have five battery-bearing devices. **Withdrawn — that reasoning was wrong**, and worth stating plainly rather than quietly dropping.

Those two endpoints are Microsoft's *rollup* of data graph2otel **already collects per device**. `userExperienceAnalyticsBatteryHealthDevicePerformance` returns `model` and `manufacturer` on every row alongside the score. The 5-device floor is Microsoft's statistical-significance threshold for publishing their own aggregate — it is not a statement about data availability. A model-keyed or OS-keyed battery rollup can be computed locally from one device or a thousand, with no floor at all.

So the correct disposition is neither "blocked-on-data" nor "permanent gap" — it is **"do not need Microsoft's endpoint for this"**. Tracked as an optional item on #225 rather than here, with the caveat that a locally-computed rollup must not be presented as parity with Microsoft's (their statistic, sentinel handling and inclusion rules are all unknown, so the numbers will not necessarily agree).

The general lesson, and the reason this is being recorded rather than edited away: *"Microsoft's aggregate endpoint is empty"* and *"the underlying data is unavailable"* are different claims, and this issue conflated them. Worth checking the same distinction before parking any other rollup endpoint.

## `collectAppHealth` drops rows instead of twinning them — a #114 violation, and the fix is this issue's open checkbox

Raised while reviewing why the one live `AppHealthApplicationPerformance` row produces nothing.

`collectAppHealth` (`internal/collectors/intune/endpointanalytics/endpointanalytics.go:833`) filters every row through `allowedApp()` against a fixed 8-entry `defaultAllowedApps` list (outlook/excel/winword/powerpnt/onenote/teams/chrome/msedge). Non-matching rows hit `continue` and are **discarded entirely** — the function emits exactly one thing, `e.GaugeSnapshot(appCrashCountMetric, …)`, and no `LogEvent`.

**The allow-list itself is correct** and should stay. `intune.uxa.app_crash_count{app_name}` keyed by an unfiltered `appName` would grow one series per distinct application in the tenant — cardinality that scales with fleet size, which is exactly what #112 forbids.

**Dropping the other rows is the bug.** CLAUDE.md's hard rule, from #114: *"'not a metric label' means LOG TWIN, never dropped. A collector that fetches per-entity rows, buckets a count, and discards the rest is a bug: it can answer 'how many' but never 'which one'."* That is precisely the current shape — the collector pays for the fetch and throws the data away. Today's live row is `LogonUI.exe`, so on this tenant **100% of the fetched app-health data is discarded** and the metric is empty.

The fix is already scoped on this issue as the checkbox *"Per-app app-health detail beyond the current crash count: `appHangCount`, `meanTimeToFailureInMinutes`, `activeDeviceCount`"*, which is now unblocked (the segment returned its first row today). Shape: keep the allow-list gating the **metric**, add a log twin for **every** row carrying `appName`, `appDisplayName`, `appPublisher`, `appHealthScore`, `appHealthStatus`, `appCrashCount`, `appHangCount`, `activeDeviceCount`, `appUsageDuration`, with the int32-max `meanTimeToFailureInMinutes` sentinel excluded and `appHealthStatus="TBD"` bucketed as it already is on the OS-version segment.

Worth checking the same shape on the other sub-fetches in this collector before closing — the "bucket a count, drop the rows" pattern is easy to repeat.

## Re-probe 2026-07-24 — the EA floor broke: 4 → 10 scored devices, `ModelScores` has a row, `AppHealthApplicationPerformance` has three. And the recorded unblock condition was WRONG.

Ran every parked segment as `graph2otel-poller` against m7kni, on the recheck date set on 2026-07-23. `[live-measured 2026-07-24, #194, n=1 tenant]`

| segment | v1.0 | beta | rows | change since 2026-07-23 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `userExperienceAnalyticsDeviceScores` | 200 | 200 | **10** | 4 → 10 |
| `userExperienceAnalyticsModelScores` | 200 | 200 | **1** | **0 → 1 — UNBLOCKED** |
| `userExperienceAnalyticsAppHealthApplicationPerformance` | 200 | 200 | **3** | 1 → 3 |
| `userExperienceAnalyticsAppHealthDevicePerformance` | 200 | 200 | **6** | 1 → 6 |
| `userExperienceAnalyticsResourcePerformance` | 400 | 200 | 1 | unchanged |
| `userExperienceAnalyticsAppHealthOSVersionPerformance` | 200 | 200 | 2 | unchanged (shipped) |
| `userExperienceAnalyticsAppHealthDeviceModelPerformance` | 200 | 200 | 0 | unchanged |
| `userExperienceAnalyticsBatteryHealthModelPerformance` | 400 | 200 | 0 | unchanged |
| `userExperienceAnalyticsBatteryHealthOsPerformance` | 400 | 200 | 0 | unchanged |
| `userExperienceAnalyticsDeviceStartupHistory` | 200 | 200 | **11** | 3 → 11, across 6 devices |

**The test-data loop worked.** All five `Standard PC (Q35 + ICH9, 2009)` QEMU VMs are now in the EA-scored set with real `startupPerformanceScore` (50.0 each) and, on four of them, real `meanResourceSpikeTimeScore` (64.33 / 64.81 / 91.73 / 92.62) — the CPU/RAM loop is driving past the tenant's own `cpuSpikeTimePercentageThreshold 15.0` / `ramSpikeTimePercentageThreshold 30.0`. Startup history went 3 records across 2 devices to **11 across 6**, with the staggered reboots visible at `2026-07-22T14:42–14:44Z`.

### CORRECTION — the "≥5 EA-scored devices sharing one model string" unblock condition is refuted

Recorded on this issue 2026-07-21 and repeated since: *"`ModelScores` / `AppHealthDeviceModelPerformance`: ≥5 EA-reporting devices **sharing one model string**"*, with the reasoning that "five devices of five different models produce five buckets of one and stay under the floor in every bucket".

The live row says otherwise, verbatim:

```json
{"id":"Virtual Machine_Microsoft Corporation","model":"Virtual Machine",
 "manufacturer":"Microsoft Corporation","modelDeviceCount":1,
 "endpointAnalyticsScore":100.0,"startupPerformanceScore":-1.0,"appReliabilityScore":-1.0,
 "workFromAnywhereScore":-1.0,"batteryHealthScore":-1.0,"meanResourceSpikeTimeScore":100.0,
 "healthStatus":"meetingGoals"}
```

`modelDeviceCount: 1`. A single-device model bucket is published. And the inversion is exact: the **five**-device `Standard PC (Q35 + ICH9, 2009)` / QEMU bucket is **absent** from `ModelScores`, while the **one**-device `Virtual Machine` / Microsoft Corporation bucket is present. Whatever gates this segment, it is not a per-bucket device count — the prediction on this issue was not merely imprecise, it was backwards for today's data.

The most likely remaining explanation is daily rollup lag: `AppHealthDevicePerformance.processedDateTime` is `2026-07-23T03:05:37Z` tenant-wide, and the QEMU devices entered the scored set after that. **That is a hypothesis, not a measurement** — recorded as such, not as the new unblock condition. The honest statement is that the gate is unknown and the 5-device-per-bucket claim should not be repeated.

### `ModelScores` — buildable now

One live row, every EDM field present on the wire. Notes for the build:

- `-1` is the per-field insufficient-data sentinel here exactly as on `DeviceScores` (four of the six score fields carry it). Must be excluded, never emitted as a negative score.
- `modelDeviceCount` is the bucket size and is metric-shaped — it makes the model bucket self-describing.
- `id` is `"<model>_<manufacturer>"`, so model and manufacturer are the natural bounded label pair (bounded by distinct fleet models, per #112).
- `healthStatus` is `meetingGoals` on a bucket with four unscored fields — as on `DeviceScores`, the status is not derivable from the numbers.

### `AppHealthApplicationPerformance` — 3 rows, and one of them clears the allow-list

```json
{"appName":"LogonUI.exe","appDisplayName":"","appPublisher":"","activeDeviceCount":8,
 "appUsageDuration":230,"appCrashCount":0,"appHangCount":0,"appHealthScore":100.0,
 "appHealthStatus":"TBD","allOrgsHealthScore":0.0,"meanTimeToFailureInMinutes":2147483647}
{"appName":"SearchHost.exe","appDisplayName":"Microsoft® Windows® Operating System",
 "appPublisher":"Microsoft Corporation","activeDeviceCount":6,"appUsageDuration":90, …}
{"appName":"msedge.exe","appDisplayName":"Microsoft Edge","appPublisher":"Microsoft Corporation",
 "activeDeviceCount":5,"appUsageDuration":772, …}
```

`msedge.exe` **is** in `defaultAllowedApps`. That matters for the #114 fix scoped on this issue: for the first time both halves are verifiable against live rows — the allow-listed metric path (msedge) and the twin-for-everything-else path (LogonUI, SearchHost). Two of the three rows carry populated `appDisplayName`/`appPublisher` while `LogonUI.exe` has **empty strings** for both, so the "empty string, not absent" case is exercised by real data rather than assumed.

`meanTimeToFailureInMinutes` is int32-max on all three (the known no-failures sentinel) and `appHealthStatus` is `"TBD"` on all three (the known undocumented status already bucketed to `other`).

### Two new API gotchas, both of the "malformed probe reads as no data" family

- **`$count=true` empties `value` on `ModelScores`.** `?$count=true` returns `200` with `@odata.count: 1` and `"value": []` — the count is right and the rows are gone. A probe reaching for `$count` to check emptiness gets a zero-length collection from a segment that has data. Given this issue's history of parking surfaces on "count=0", worth recording explicitly.
- **`$orderby=id` → 500 on `AppHealthDeviceModelPerformance`** (bare list is `200`). Same family as the `$top` trap already recorded for the startup segments on #199: an accepted-looking OData parameter that the segment rejects outright, and with a 5xx rather than a 4xx.

### Status

- **Buildable now:** `ModelScores` (new sub-fetch), the `AppHealthApplicationPerformance` widening + #114 twin fix, and the `ResourcePerformance` items already unblocked yesterday (`totalRamInMB` zero bug, six unmapped fields).
- **Still empty:** `AppHealthDeviceModelPerformance` (0 rows, gate unknown — do not restate the refuted device-count condition).
- **Battery rollups:** unchanged; disposition remains the 2026-07-21 correction — locally computable from `BatteryHealthDevicePerformance`, tracked on #225.
- `AppHealthDevicePerformance` 1 → 6 rows is #225's territory, noted here because it moved in the same pass.

## Closed by `45f0fe0` — all five scope items are now either shipped or dispositioned

### What shipped in this commit

**`ModelScores` — new sub-fetch (v1.0).** Two bounded gauges keyed by `(model, manufacturer)`: `intune.uxa.model_score{model,manufacturer,category,health_state}` across the six score categories, and `intune.uxa.model_device_count{model,manufacturer,health_state}` for the bucket size. No log twin — a model bucket is an aggregate, not an entity (#192, and this issue's own acceptance criterion). The `-1` sentinel is excluded per field, which on the live row removes four of the six categories. Mapped against the verbatim m7kni row, pinned in the test as `modelScoresLiveRow`.

**`meanResourceSpikeTimeScore` — the sixth score category, now mapped on `DeviceScores` too.** Found while building the above. It is on the `userExperienceAnalyticsDeviceScores` wire and always has been; the `deviceScore` struct simply predates it, so the already-shipped sub-fetch was **discarding a real, populated score** — 100 on `wintest`, 64.33 / 64.81 / 91.73 / 92.62 on the four load-generating VMs. It now feeds both the score histogram (a sixth `category`) and the per-device twin. Not in this issue's scope as written, but it is the same field this issue's `ModelScores` work required, and leaving it unmapped on the sibling would have been the "bucket a count, drop the rows" shape #114 forbids.

**`ResourcePerformance` — evidence upgrade, six new fields, and a live-evidenced bug fix.**

- The EDM-derived caveat on the struct and on the `semconv` block is **withdrawn**: every originally-mapped field name matched the wire once the segment returned a row, so the block is now `[live-measured 2026-07-24]`. Leaving a "not live-verified" note in place after verification is the rot the #146 post-mortem is about.
- Six wire fields that were never mapped now ride the twin: `averageSpikeTimeScore`, `cpuSpikeTimeScore`, `ramSpikeTimeScore`, `cpuClockSpeedInMHz`, and the two `*PercentageThreshold` values. The thresholds are the **tenant's own policy** (15% CPU / 30% RAM on m7kni), not device readings — they are what turn a bare `cpu_spike_time_percentage=12` into a judgement.
- **Zero-is-absent bug fixed.** `totalRamInMB` and `cpuClockSpeedInMHz` read `0` on a VM that demonstrably has RAM and a clock, and the blanket `if value >= 0` guard emitted that as a real reading — a twin claiming the machine has no memory. They now require `> 0`. `cpuSpikeTimePercentage` keeps `>= 0`, because 0% spike time genuinely is a measurement of zero. The guard has to be **per field**; a blanket fix in either direction is wrong. Same trap `intune.hardware_inventory` already handles for `totalStorageSpace`.
- `deviceCount` is deliberately left unmapped: it is the only aggregate-shaped field on a per-device row and has only ever been observed as the `-1` sentinel.

### The scope checkboxes

| scope item | disposition |
| --- | --- |
| `userExperienceAnalyticsModelScores` | **shipped**, `45f0fe0` |
| `userExperienceAnalyticsAnomalySeverityOverview` | shipped, `35c4afa` |
| Work-from-anywhere readiness | shipped, `77af941` (route resolved live: only the `.../allDevices/metricDevices` leaf returns 200) |
| Per-app app-health detail (`appHangCount`, `meanTimeToFailureInMinutes`, `activeDeviceCount`) | **shipped**, `b9c594c` + `40d9e43`. The widening landed as part of the #114 twin fix: every application row is twinned as `intune.app_health` carrying all three fields, and the eight-entry allow-list that had been discarding 100% of m7kni's data was retired entirely in #235 in favour of the central cardinality limiter |
| (Optional) model/OS-level battery rollups | **not built, deliberately** — see below |

`BatteryHealthModelPerformance` / `BatteryHealthOsPerformance` are still 0 rows, and the disposition recorded on 2026-07-21 stands: these are Microsoft's *rollup* of data graph2otel already collects per device, so the correct answer is "do not need Microsoft's endpoint for this" rather than "blocked-on-data". A locally-computed model- or OS-keyed rollup has no floor at all. Tracked as an optional item on #225, with the caveat that it must not be presented as parity with Microsoft's — their statistic, sentinel handling and inclusion rules are unknown, so the numbers will not necessarily agree.

`AppHealthDeviceModelPerformance` is 0 rows and was never a scope item on this issue. Its gate is unknown (see below); it is not carried forward behind a fabricated unblock condition.

### What went into `docs/graph-api-gotchas.md`

The durable half of this issue's investigation, all `[live-measured 2026-07-24]`:

- **What gates a UXA rollup being published is UNKNOWN, and it is not device count.** This issue spent a week reading Microsoft's documented five-device floor onto the empty rollup segments. The floor is real for the *score Microsoft computes* and does not explain which rollup rows get published. Both device-count theories are refuted by the same day's wire — `ModelScores` published a one-device bucket while ignoring a five-device one, and #199's `DeviceStartupProcessPerformance` stayed empty after boot telemetry went from 3 records across 2 devices to 11 across 6. The rule recorded: do not attach a device-count unblock condition to an empty UXA rollup, because it reads as testable, passes, and changes nothing. The per-device siblings return rows on a tiny tenant and are the reliable source; the rollups are opportunistic.
- **`$count=true` on `ModelScores` returns the count and drops the rows** — `@odata.count: 1` with `"value": []`. Read the rows, not the count.
- **`$orderby=id` → 500 on `AppHealthDeviceModelPerformance`** while the bare list is 200. Not transient.

### Gate

`make check` green (vet + test -race + lint + govulncheck + tidy + build). Signal goldens and `docs/collectors.md` regenerated. New tests: `TestCollectEmitsModelScoresAsBoundedAggregates`, `TestResourcePerformanceTwinDistinguishesUnreportedZeroFromRealZero`, `TestDeviceScoresMapTheSixthScoreCategory`.

Deploy-verification on camden to follow.

## Deployed, and deploy-verification caught a bug the tests could not — fixed in `9e2dc45`

`45f0fe0` went out on camden (`version=45f0fe0`, `intune.endpoint_analytics` green, 2437ms) and the new metrics landed in Grafana Cloud. Then reading the actual values — rather than the green tick — surfaced this:

```
intune_uxa_model_score{model="Virtual Machine", category="mean_resource_spike_time"}  0
```

A model published as scoring **zero** on a category it was never assessed on.

### Endpoint Analytics has TWO ways of saying "no score" and the collector handled one

Alongside the `-1` sentinel, it simply **omits** a score field it has nothing to say about. Same row, same tenant, same day:

```
09:2x  {"id":"Virtual Machine_Microsoft Corporation", … "meanResourceSpikeTimeScore":100.0, "healthStatus":"meetingGoals"}
14:0x  {"id":"Virtual Machine_Microsoft Corporation", …                                      "healthStatus":"meetingGoals"}
```

Nothing else changed; the field is just gone. In Go a plain `float64` unmarshals that omission to `0`, which passes the `>= 0` sentinel guard and gets published as a real score. **That is worse than the `-1` the guard exists to catch:** `-1` is filterable, an absent field leaves nothing on the wire to filter on, and on a 0–100 score a fabricated zero reads as the worst possible result rather than as missing data.

**Fix:** every score field on both `deviceScore` and `modelScore` is now `*float64` — `nil` means never mentioned, and is skipped for the histogram, the gauge and the twin alike. The `-1` handling is unchanged and still applies to fields that ARE present. This also closes the same latent hole on the five pre-existing categories, which have simply never been observed absent. `wfaMetricDevice` already used pointers for exactly this reason and was the right precedent to have followed.

### Why no test caught it, which is the part worth keeping

The fixture had the field — because the fixture was written from a wire sample that had it. Every test passed, `make check` was green, and the mapping was verified against a live sample per this issue's own acceptance criterion. **The only thing that caught it was querying the backend for the emitted series and reading the value.** A green collector run and a correct-looking mapping are both compatible with publishing a fabricated number.

Recorded in `docs/graph-api-gotchas.md` as a trap distinct from the `-1` sentinel.

### Live verification after the fix (camden `version=9e2dc45`)

`time() - timestamp(intune_uxa_model_score)` per series, which is the way to read true sample age — an instant query's `value[0]` is the evaluation time and looks fresh for a series that stopped being written:

| series | sample age at T | at T+2min |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `category="endpoint_analytics"` | 40s | **21s** — still being written |
| `category="mean_resource_spike_time"` | 102s | **143s** — stopped, ageing out |

The fabricated series is no longer produced. And where the field IS on the wire, the new mapping works — the per-device histogram now carries all six categories:

```
group by(category)(intune_uxa_device_score_bucket)
→ app_reliability, battery_health, endpoint_analytics, mean_resource_spike_time,
  startup_performance, work_from_anywhere
```

`intune_uxa_model_device_count{model="Virtual Machine", health_state="meeting_goals"} 1` — the real bucket size, and a direct standing refutation of this issue's retracted five-device theory.

title: feat(intune.endpoint_analytics): add ModelScores + AnomalySeverityOverview + WFA + per-app app-health detail

body:
Part of the Intune reporting/analytics spike (tracker: #192). Build regardless of the Data Warehouse outcome.

## What & why

The Intune "Reports" and per-device "Monitor" blades are backed by the async export-job API `POST /deviceManagement/reports/exportJobs`. graph2otel already has the generic create→poll→download→parse engine (`internal/exportjob`, #17) and three collectors on it (`intune.app_install_status`=`AppInstallStatusAggregate`, `intune.cert_inventory`=`AllDeviceCertificates`, `intune.defender_agents`=`DefenderAgents`). That is **3 of ~100+** valid `reportName`s. This issue wires the high-value remainder — each new collector is a thin adapter over the existing engine (a `reportName`, a `$select`, a parse+emit mapping), not new transport.

App-only confirmed: the export API meters app callers explicitly (48 req/app/min, 100/tenant/min). The poller already holds `DeviceManagementManagedDevices.ReadWrite.All` (job creation) plus the `Apps`/`Configuration` read scopes.

Docs: [export Intune reports via Graph](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/device-management/reports/export-graph-apis) · [full reportName reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/device-management/reports/ref-graph-available-reports)

## Scope — prioritized reportNames

**Aggregate/metric-shaped (pre-bucketed counts — cheapest OTel fit, do first):**
- [ ] `PolicyComplianceAggReport(V3)` / `SettingComplianceAggReport(V3)` — compliance rollups by policy/setting
- [ ] `ConfigurationPolicyAggregate(V3)` — config-policy device rollup
- [ ] `FeatureUpdatePolicyStatusSummary` / `QualityUpdatePolicyStatusSummary` — the "Deployment status per update ring" / "Security update status" Monitor reports
- [ ] EPM insights: `EpmAggregationReportByApplication(V2)` / `...ByPublisher(V2)` / `...ByUser(V2)` — no direct Graph resource exists for these

**Per-entity (log-shaped twins — `count by` in LogQL for aggregates):**
- [ ] `DeviceNonCompliance` / `NonCompliantDevicesByCompliancePolicy(V3)` — the "Noncompliant devices" report
- [ ] `DeviceAssignmentStatusByConfigurationPolicy*` — the "Configuration policy assignment failures" Monitor report
- [ ] `DeviceEnrollmentFailures` — the "Enrollment failures" Monitor report
- [ ] `AutopilotV1DeploymentStatus` / `AutopilotV2DeploymentStatus` — "Windows Autopilot deployment status"
- [ ] `FeatureUpdateDeviceState` / `DeviceFailuresByFeatureUpdatePolicy` (needs `PolicyId`) — per-device update state

(Device attestation reports `TpmAttestationStatus` / `WindowsDeviceHealthAttestationReport` are covered by the attestation child issue, not here.)

## Acceptance
- [ ] Each new collector reuses `internal/exportjob`; no new transport engine.
- [ ] Aggregates → bounded gauges; per-entity → log twins (never a dropped count, #114).
- [ ] `reportName`s that ship **raw enum codes** (e.g. `platform=2`, compliance-state ints) are mapped to names — the #142 trap; verified against a live export, not docs.
- [ ] Each collector `Experimental()` if it uses a beta-only reportName or column set; scope declared per report.
- [ ] `docs/collectors.md` regenerated; coverage gate green (`internal/collectordoc` walks the export path).
- [ ] Mappers validated against a live export from m7kni (several reports are empty on a small tenant — an empty export must not mask a mapping bug).

comments.body:
First wave landed in `35c4afa` (pushed to main).

**Shipped** (both Experimental/default-off, on the existing `internal/exportjob` engine, mappers built against live m7kni exports captured as the poller 2026-07-19):
- `intune.config_assignment_status` ← `DeviceAssignmentStatusByConfigurationPolicy` (310 live rows). Gauge `intune.config_assignment_status.assignments` by `report_status` × `policy_platform` (bounded, non-localized enums); per device×policy log twin; WARN on Error/Conflict/Noncompliant. Covers the "Configuration policy assignment failures" Monitor report.
- `intune.noncompliant_settings` ← `NoncompliantDevicesAndSettings`. Gauge by `os` × `setting_status`; per-device-per-setting twin (which setting is noncompliant) — the detail the summary-only `intune.compliance` gauges cannot answer.

**Live-measured notes for the remaining waves:**
- `FeatureUpdatePolicyStatusSummary` / `QualityUpdatePolicyStatusSummary` — schema captured & valid, but **0 rows on m7kni** (no update policies). Buildable but cannot validate the mapper against live rows here; deferred until there is data or built with the schema explicitly flagged.
- `DeviceEnrollmentFailures` — **NOT export-capable**: `POST /exportJobs` returns `400 PostExportJobAsync not supported for reportType DeviceEnrollmentFailures`. Docs were wrong; dropped from the export path.
- Still open: EPM insights (`EpmAggregationReportBy*`, no direct Graph resource), `AutopilotV1/V2DeploymentStatus`, `DeviceNonCompliance` per-device variant.

Decision (reaffirmed 2026-07-19): the reports-export collectors stay **Experimental / opt-in**, and this is by the **write-scope** rationale, NOT beta. `POST /deviceManagement/reports/exportJobs` is a v1.0 endpoint, but creating a job requires `DeviceManagementManagedDevices.ReadWrite.All` — the single break from graph2otel's read-only-by-default posture. Keeping them opt-in preserves that guarantee (a default deployment needs no write scope). This is the same basis on which #183 left the export collectors Experimental while narrowing the flag elsewhere; `Experimental` therefore keeps its dual meaning here (beta **or** write-scoped export). Do not flip export collectors to default-on without re-deciding the read-only-by-default posture.

## Second wave shipped + remaining report types triaged (2026-07-19)

Continuing from the first-wave comment. Live probe (as graph2otel-poller from camden, 2026-07-19) drove every remaining candidate export to completion and captured verbatim rows; buildable ones are now shipped.

### Shipped this wave (commit `96b0591`, Experimental/default-off, mapped against verbatim m7kni rows)
- **`intune.autopilot_deployment`** ← `AutopilotV2DeploymentStatus` (2 live rows). Bounded gauge by raw `DeploymentStatus` code + per-device twin (provisioning phase, duration, result code); WARN on non-zero `ResultCode`. **`AutopilotV1DeploymentStatus` returns 0 rows** on m7kni (device-prep tenant) — parked, blocked-on-data.
- **`intune.epm_elevations`** ← `EpmAggregationReportByApplication` (7 live rows). Endpoint Privilege Management: bounded elevation-count gauge summed by `elevation_type` + per-application twin (file/hash/version/count/is-background); WARN on `UnmanagedElevation` (a user elevating outside any EPM policy — the security signal).

### `DeviceNonCompliance` — assessed, NOT built (redundant)
5 live rows. Its fields overlap `intune.devices` (manageddevices), which **already** emits a per-device twin carrying `complianceState` (with the `in_grace_period` bucket), `partnerReportedThreatState`/DeviceHealthThreatLevel, device identity, serial, and last-sync (`manageddevices.go:105` $select). The **only** field `DeviceNonCompliance` adds that nothing else surfaces is **`InGracePeriodUntil`** (the exact grace-expiry timestamp — `intune.devices` has the *state* `in_grace_period` but not the *date* it expires).

A whole new export collector (its own 6h job + the ReadWrite write-scope break) for one delta field is not worth it. **Cheaper path recommended instead:** add the managedDevice property **`complianceGracePeriodExpirationDateTime`** to `intune.devices`' existing `$select` + twin (docs-level; verify it's on the polled resource before wiring). Deferred to a small `intune.devices` follow-up rather than a new collector — and it interacts with #197 (which is reconsidering `intune.devices`' transport), so it should land there.

### Blocked-on-data, parked (recorded so a later session doesn't re-derive)
- `AutopilotV1DeploymentStatus` — 0 rows (V2-only tenant).
- `FeatureUpdatePolicyStatusSummary` / `QualityUpdatePolicyStatusSummary` — 0 rows (no update policies), re-confirmed.
- EPM `EpmAggregationReportBy{Device,User,Publisher}` and per-elevation detail — not built this pass; the by-application aggregate is the highest-value cut and is shipped. The others are follow-ups if per-device/per-user elevation attribution is wanted.

### State of #193
Shipped: `config_assignment_status`, `noncompliant_settings` (first wave) + `autopilot_deployment`, `epm_elevations` (this wave). Parked blocked-on-data: AutopilotV1, FeatureUpdate/QualityUpdate. Assessed-redundant: DeviceNonCompliance. Remaining genuinely-open: EPM by-device/user/publisher variants (follow-ups, not gates). Deploy-verify on camden to follow.
Deploy-verified: `intune.autopilot_deployment` + `intune.epm_elevations` live on camden (version=77af941, runs=1, last_success=true, no error) against non-empty reports (2 Autopilot-V2 / 7 EPM rows).

**Grace-expiry decision (Rob approved 2026-07-19):** don't build a DeviceNonCompliance collector; instead add the managedDevice property `complianceGracePeriodExpirationDateTime` to `intune.devices`' existing `$select` + twin (the one non-redundant field DeviceNonCompliance offered). Verify the property is on the polled managedDevice resource, add it to the graph twin, and check blob-twin parity (the `Devices`/`DeviceComplianceOrg` blob may or may not carry a grace-expiry field — if not, the blob twin omits it via SetStr like it does for partnerReportedThreatState). Small follow-up, tracked here.

## Grace-expiry shipped + deployed + verified (2026-07-19)

Added `complianceGracePeriodExpirationDateTime` to `intune.devices` — commit 5059d84, live on camden `version=5059d84` (`intune.devices` + `intune.devices_blob` both `runs=1, last_success=true`).

- Added to the fleet `$select` + the per-device twin (`manageddevices.go`), carried through the shared `deviceLogTwin`, so both the graph and blob transports emit the identical `compliance_grace_period_expiration` attribute.
- **Two sentinels dropped, live-measured 2026-07-19** (`graceExpiry`): the max date `9999-12-31` (compliant, no deadline — 7/14 devices) and the zero date `0001-01-01` (state unknown — 3/14). Only a real deadline emits. m7kni currently has 3 devices with genuine deadlines (one expired → noncompliant, two active).
- **Blob-twin parity confirmed:** the `Devices` category carries the same value as `InGracePeriodUntil` (no-tz, variable-fraction, identical sentinels) — parsed into the same `managedDevice` field, so parity holds rather than the blob twin omitting it.

### #193 state after this
- **Shipped:** `config_assignment_status`, `noncompliant_settings`, `autopilot_deployment`, `epm_elevations` (earlier waves) + this grace-expiry add. This was the last buildable-with-data, non-EPM item.
- **Blocked-on-data, parked** (unblock = a tenant with the data; not fired on m7kni): `AutopilotV1DeploymentStatus` (0 rows), `FeatureUpdatePolicyStatusSummary` / `QualityUpdatePolicyStatusSummary` (0 rows — no update policies).
- **Genuinely-open follow-ups (not gates per prior comment):** EPM `EpmAggregationReportBy{Device,User,Publisher}` variants — the by-application aggregate is shipped; these add per-device/user/publisher attribution if wanted.

Nothing buildable-with-data remains under #193. Remaining items are either blocked-on-data (parked) or non-gate follow-ups — a maintainer call on whether either should hold v1 (#35 Gate 0).

Data-gen for the blocked `FeatureUpdatePolicyStatusSummary` — 2026-07-20.

The summary was 0-rows because m7kni had no update policies. Created one (via `homelab-agentic-mgmt`, which already holds `DeviceManagementConfiguration.ReadWrite.All`):
- `windowsFeatureUpdateProfile` **`g2o-193-featureupdate-DELETE-ME`** (id `dae032f0-7c03-4a69-95b0-9e4b3abc82e7`), `featureUpdateVersion="Windows 11, version 24H2"`.
- **Chosen to be inert:** every m7kni Windows device is on build 26100–26300 (24H2/25H2), i.e. at or above the 24H2 target. Feature update profiles never downgrade and take no action on a device at/above target, so this triggers zero upgrades — it exists only to make the report return rows.
- Assigned to `All Windows Client Devices` (dynamic, actively-reporting) so the summary populates. Status rows appear as devices report against the policy (hours–day).

Once rows land, I build the `FeatureUpdatePolicyStatusSummary` export collector against the live export.

**Still not generated: `QualityUpdatePolicyStatusSummary`** — its `windowsQualityUpdateProfile` is an *expedite* policy that force-installs a patch, so it is a blast-radius decision (assign to `Windows-Test-VMs` only / target an already-installed KB / defer to post-v1), not something to push at the fleet. Parked pending that call.

**Cleanup pending:** delete profile `dae032f0…` after the collector is built + verified. `[live-measured 2026-07-20]`

`intune.feature_update_summary` + `intune.quality_update_summary` shipped in 2ac12bb — the last data-gated reportNames (`FeatureUpdatePolicyStatusSummary` / `QualityUpdatePolicyStatusSummary`), unblocked by the inert update policies created on m7kni (comment above). Both mapped against live exports captured 2026-07-20 as graph2otel-poller: pre-aggregated per-policy counts → bounded gauge keyed by policy × `update_deployment_state` (in_progress/error/success), no per-device twin. Experimental (the ReadWrite export-job scope). `make check` green.

**Closing #193.** The genuinely-remaining items were split to **#201**: `AutopilotV1DeploymentStatus` (blocked-on-data — 0 rows on this V2/device-prep tenant) and the EPM by-device/user/publisher variants (non-gate follow-ups; the by-application cut ships as `intune.epm_elevations`). Neither holds v1.

**Cleanup pending:** delete the two throwaway profiles (`g2o-193-featureupdate-DELETE-ME` `dae032f0…`, `g2o-193-qualityupdate-DELETE-ME` `5b0eba92…`) after camden deploy-verify.

body:
## Mission

Research spike + build-out tracker for the **Intune reporting / analytics / service surfaces** — the "Reports" and "Monitor" blades, endpoint/advanced analytics, tenant messages, service health, and the Intune Data Warehouse. Goal: emit the operationally-useful slices as OTel metrics or logs, without rebuilding what already ships. This issue is the durable record of the spike; the build work is split into the child issues below.

Sub-tracker of the v1.0 launch tracker #79 — its operating rules apply (app-only least-privilege, live-measure before implementing, metrics carry aggregates / logs carry entities).

## Spike findings (live-measured 2026-07-19, as `graph2otel-poller` cert on camden vs the m7kni tenant)

### Already shipped — no work needed
Two of the four original asks (Intune messages, service health) and the endpoint-analytics core are already covered:

| Ask | Covered by | Live proof (2026-07-19) |
|---|---|---|
| Intune **messages** (incl. Autopatch/MC posts) | `m365.servicemessages` → `GET /admin/serviceAnnouncement/messages` (`ServiceMessage.Read.All`); log twin carries the affected `services[]` array | `value=50+` tenant-wide |
| **Service health dashboard** | `m365.servicehealth` → `GET /admin/serviceAnnouncement/healthOverviews?$expand=issues` (`ServiceHealth.Read.All`) | `healthOverviews value=29` (incl. `Microsoft Intune=serviceDegradation`), `issues value=5` |
| **Endpoint analytics** (core) | `intune.endpoint_analytics` (Experimental) — 6 UXA segments (DeviceScores, DeviceStartupHistory, AppHealthApplicationPerformance v1.0; BatteryHealthDevicePerformance, ResourcePerformance, Baselines beta); bounded gauges + per-device log twin | `DeviceScores value=1`, `BatteryHealthDevicePerformance value=1` |

The Intune-portal "Messages" and "Service health and message center" blades are **service-filtered views of the same tenant-wide `serviceAnnouncement` surface** — no Intune-specific API behind them.

### Confirmed dead ends — do not build
- **`userExperienceAnalyticsOverview` and `userExperienceAnalyticsScoreHistory`** — `400 ResourceNotFound` on **both** v1.0 and beta (live-measured 2026-07-19, re-confirming #179). The tenant-wide score singleton was removed from Graph; the per-device `DeviceScores` collection is the replacement (already collected). Microsoft docs still describe `Overview` as current — it is not. `wire over docs`.
- **Windows Autopatch "Messages" blade** (planned-maintenance posts under Tenant admin → Windows Autopatch) — backed by the undocumented `services.autopatch.microsoft.com` store; **no supported app-only Graph API**. The same service-comms surface via `serviceAnnouncement/messages` (already collected). Park unless a documented API appears.

### Genuine gaps → child issues (ranked by net-new value)
- [ ] **Data Warehouse spike** — the *only* app-only source of 30/60-day historical/trend data, but a **fifth ingest engine** (host `fef.{region}.manage.microsoft.com`, audience `api.manage.microsoft.com`, app role `get_data_warehouse`, tenant-specific base URL discovered from the portal). App-only is **docs-supported but NOT yet verified end-to-end** — a token for `https://api.manage.microsoft.com/.default` issues but carries `roles=[]` (the role is ungranted). Spike first, build only on a green live probe. → #196
- [ ] **Reports export-job expansion** — rides the *existing* `internal/exportjob` engine; only **3 of ~100+** `reportName`s are wired (`AppInstallStatusAggregate`, `AllDeviceCertificates`, `DefenderAgents`). High-value unwired: compliance aggregates, config assignment-failure reports, feature/quality-update summaries, `TpmAttestationStatus`, Autopilot deployment status, EPM insights. → #193
- [ ] **Endpoint-analytics expansion** — add net-new segments to `intune.endpoint_analytics`: `ModelScores` (v1.0, `200` live), `AnomalySeverityOverview` (beta, `200` live — bounded low/med/high/info counts), work-from-anywhere, per-app app-health detail, model-level battery/resource. → #194
- [ ] **Device attestation / boot security** — `deviceHealthAttestationState` (BitLocker/SecureBoot/TPM/code-integrity per device) via a `managedDevices` `$select`; no new engine. → #195

## Poller scope posture (live 2026-07-19)
Already holds every Graph scope the reports/analytics/attestation children need: `DeviceManagementManagedDevices.Read.All` **+ `.ReadWrite.All`** (export-job creation), `DeviceManagementConfiguration.Read.All`, `DeviceManagementApps.Read.All`, `DeviceManagementScripts.Read.All`, `Reports.Read.All`, `ServiceHealth.Read.All`, `ServiceMessage.Read.All`, `CloudPC.Read.All`. The **only** new grant this whole program needs is `get_data_warehouse` (Intune API, not Graph) — gated behind the DW spike.

## Operating rules
- Metrics carry bounded aggregates; per-entity detail is a **log twin, never a dropped count** (#114). Model/OS-level scores are metric-shaped; per-device/per-app rows are log-shaped.
- Beta-only segments gate behind the whole-collector `Experimental()` opt-in.
- Mappers written against **live samples**, never docs (empty-collection success hides mapping bugs — several of these segments are empty on m7kni).
- Every export-report collector needs the one `...ReadWrite.All` write scope to POST a job — the documented least-privilege wrinkle (#17), already held.

comments.body:
First build wave landed in `35c4afa` (main): 3 new export collectors + 1 endpoint-analytics signal, all mapped against live m7kni samples. Progress on the three build children:
- #193 — 2 report collectors shipped (`config_assignment_status`, `noncompliant_settings`); update-summary/EPM/Autopilot reports remain; `DeviceEnrollmentFailures` dropped (not export-capable).
- #194 — `AnomalySeverityOverview` shipped; `ModelScores`/`AppHealth`/`WFA` blocked-on-data or route-TBD (details on the issue).
- #195 — `TpmAttestationStatus` shipped; the `deviceHealthAttestationState` property is null tenant-wide so export is the path; `WindowsDeviceHealthAttestationReport` (full boot-security) is the follow-up.

All shipped collectors are Experimental/default-off — no change to the running camden deployment until enabled. DW spike (#196) unstarted (needs the `get_data_warehouse` grant + region URL).

DW spike (#196) **closed won't-do** (2026-07-19). App-only feasibility was proven live (grant + `msub06` URL + 42 collections reachable, recorded on #196), but the DW's only differentiated value is historical/trend data that cannot be backfilled into the Grafana TSDB model, and everything current-state is already covered via Graph. The `get_data_warehouse` grant was revoked (poller back to least-privilege). Feasibility is banked on #196 if the constraint ever changes.

Tracker status: #193 (reports-export, first wave shipped, more report types remain), #194 (anomaly shipped; ModelScores/WFA blocked-on-data), #195 (TpmAttestationStatus shipped; WindowsDeviceHealthAttestationReport follow-up) remain open; #196 closed won't-do.

First wave is **live on camden** (verified 2026-07-19). Enabled `intune.config_assignment_status`, `intune.device_attestation`, `intune.noncompliant_settings` in `config.yaml` (endpoint_analytics was already on, so its new `anomaly_count` went live on restart). All four ran a full export/collect cycle: `has_run=true`, `runs=1`, `last_success=true`, `last_error=none` — against a tenant with real rows (310 assignment / 5 attestation / 3 noncompliant), so genuine ingest.

Also fixed (8625539): the hand-written write-scope docs (permissions.md §4, collectors.md note, SECURITY.md write-break inventory, pii-cardinality-audit.md) all said "three export collectors" and named only the original three — updated to six. There is no drift gate tying "declares DeviceManagementManagedDevices.ReadWrite.All" to "named in those docs", which is why it went stale silently; a follow-up could add one.

## Live probe of the whole reporting cluster (2026-07-19, as graph2otel-poller from camden)

One export-job + Graph pass over every open item in this cluster, to sort buildable-now from blocked-on-data before writing any mapper (wire-over-docs). `[live-measured 2026-07-19, #192, n=1 tenant]`

### Export reports — POST `/deviceManagement/reports/exportJobs`, polled to completion, CSV header+rows captured

| report | rows on m7kni | verdict |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `WindowsDeviceHealthAttestationReport` (#195 follow-up) | **2** | **BUILD** — full boot-security schema live (Bitlocker/CodeIntegrity/SecureBoot/VSM/FirmwareProtection/MemoryIntegrity/MemoryAccess/SecuredCorePC/SMM/TpmVersion/AttestationError, each + a `_loc` sibling) |
| `AutopilotV2DeploymentStatus` (#193) | **2** | **BUILD** — DeviceId/EnrollmentTimeInUtc/CurrentProvisioningPhase/DeploymentStatus/DeploymentDurationTimeInSeconds/Phase/ResultCode/DeviceName/SerialNumber/UPN |
| `EpmAggregationReportByApplication` (#193) | **7** | **BUILD** — EPM elevation-by-app: CompanyName/ElevationType/FileVersion/Hash/InternalName/ElevationCount/FileName/IsBackgroundProcess |
| `DeviceNonCompliance` (#193) | **5** | assess overlap first — per-device noncompliance w/ `InGracePeriodUntil` + `DeviceHealthThreatLevel` + `LastContact` (grace-period is the non-redundant bit vs `intune.compliance` / `intune.noncompliant_settings`) |
| `AutopilotV1DeploymentStatus` (#193) | **0** | PARK — schema valid, no rows (m7kni is Autopilot V2). Blocked-on-data |
| `FeatureUpdatePolicyStatusSummary` (#193) | **0** | PARK — confirmed again, no update policies |

### Endpoint-analytics beta (#194)

- **WFA route RESOLVED:** the singleton `.../userExperienceAnalyticsWorkFromAnywhereMetrics` 400s (`No OData route`), and so does `/allDevices`; the working path is **`.../userExperienceAnalyticsWorkFromAnywhereMetrics/allDevices/metricDevices`** → **200, 1 row**, per-device Win11 upgrade-eligibility + cloud-management posture (`upgradeEligibility`, `workFromAnywhereScore`, `windowsScore`, `cloudManagementScore`, `cloudIdentityScore`, `cloudProvisioningScore`, `ramCheckFailed`/`tpmCheckFailed`/… , `healthStatus`). **BUILD.**
- `userExperienceAnalyticsModelScores` — still `@odata.count=0`. PARK.
- `userExperienceAnalyticsAppHealthApplicationPerformance` — still `count=0`. PARK.

### #197 lossy-overview — reproduced with fresh numbers

`managedDeviceOverview.deviceOperatingSystemSummary` = iOS 4 + macOS 2 + Windows 5 = **11**; `enrolledDeviceCount` = **12**; true `managedDevices` fleet = **13** (adds Linux ×1 + one empty-OS device — neither has a summary bucket). The "overview is lossy, no Linux bucket" claim on #197 holds live.

### Verdict for the cluster

Buildable this pass: **#195 boot-security**, **#193 AutopilotV2 + EPM-by-app** (+ maybe DeviceNonCompliance), **#194 WFA**. The rest (#193 AutopilotV1 + FeatureUpdate, #194 ModelScores + AppHealth) are blocked-on-data on m7kni and stay parked with that recorded reason.

## Second wave deployed + live-verified on camden (2026-07-19)

All four new collectors from this session are live on camden `:main` (version=77af941), each `enabled=true, has_run=true, runs=1, last_success=true, last_error=none, skip_reason=none` — and the source reports are non-empty on m7kni (2 boot-security / 2 Autopilot-V2 / 7 EPM / 1 WFA rows), so this is genuine ingest, not empty-success.

| collector | issue | commit | status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `intune.device_boot_security` | #195 (**closed**) | `96b0591` | live, verified |
| `intune.autopilot_deployment` | #193 | `96b0591` | live, verified |
| `intune.epm_elevations` | #193 | `96b0591` | live, verified |
| `intune.endpoint_analytics` WFA readiness | #194 | `77af941` | live, verified (already-enabled collector) |

### Cluster state after this session
- **#195 CLOSED** — device attestation + boot-security posture both ship.
- **#193** open, scoped to residuals: EPM by-device/user/publisher variants (follow-ups). Blocked-on-data (parked): AutopilotV1, FeatureUpdate/QualityUpdate summaries. Assessed-redundant: DeviceNonCompliance (grace-expiry better added to `intune.devices` via `complianceGracePeriodExpirationDateTime`).
- **#194** open, scoped to ModelScores + AppHealthApplicationPerformance (both `@odata.count=0` on m7kni — blocked-on-data).
- **#196** closed won't-do (DW).

The buildable-with-data reporting surface is now shipped; what remains under #193/#194 is blocked-on-data on m7kni, not blocked on design.

## Closing this tracker — the spike is complete and every buildable child has shipped

This issue's job was to (a) find out what the Intune reporting / analytics / service surfaces actually expose app-only, and (b) split the buildable parts into children. Both are done, so the tracker closes and the residue lives on the two issues named at the bottom.

### Where each spike finding landed

| finding | outcome |
| --- | --- |
| Intune **messages** + **service health** — already covered by `m365.servicemessages` / `m365.servicehealth` | no work needed; confirmed live |
| **Data Warehouse** (fifth ingest engine) | **#196 closed won't-do** — app-only feasibility proven live (grant + `msub06` URL + 42 collections), but its only differentiated value is historical/trend data that cannot be backfilled into the TSDB model. `get_data_warehouse` grant revoked; feasibility banked on #196 if the constraint ever changes |
| **Reports export-job expansion** | **#193 closed.** The wave shipped `intune.config_assignment_status`, `intune.noncompliant_settings`, `intune.autopilot_deployment`, `intune.epm_elevations`, `intune.feature_update_summary`, `intune.quality_update_summary` — and the catalogue sweep it triggered went well past this issue's original list (#202 autopilot apps/scripts, #203 the `_loc` select defect, #204 six more report collectors, #205 the per-elevation event stream, #207 remediation run states) |
| **Endpoint-analytics expansion** | **#194 open, blocked-on-data.** Shipped: `AnomalySeverityOverview`, Work-From-Anywhere Win11 readiness, `AppHealthOSVersionPerformance`. Parked: five per-model segments, all empty behind Microsoft's documented 5-device EA floor (m7kni is at 3 EA-scored devices as of 2026-07-21) |
| **Device attestation / boot security** | **#195 closed** — `intune.device_attestation` + `intune.device_boot_security` both ship |

Two confirmed dead ends from the spike still hold and should not be re-derived: `userExperienceAnalyticsOverview` and `userExperienceAnalyticsScoreHistory` are `400 ResourceNotFound` on both v1.0 and beta (the tenant-wide score singleton is gone; per-device `DeviceScores` is the replacement), and the Windows Autopatch "Messages" blade has no supported app-only Graph API — the same service-comms content arrives via `serviceAnnouncement/messages`, which is already collected. `[live-measured 2026-07-19, #192]`

### What this pass added before closing

Probed the last two open questions live on 2026-07-21 and built what had data:

- `EpmAggregationReportByUser` + `EpmAggregationReportByPublisher` → shipped as `intune.epm_elevations_by_user` + `intune.epm_elevations_by_publisher` (#201).
- `managedDeviceEncryptionStates` (beta) → shipped as `intune.device_encryption` (#199) — the BitLocker/FileVault blocker detail behind `intune.devices`' boolean `isEncrypted`.
- `EpmAggregationReportByDevice` → **no such report** (`400 reportType Unknown` for every spelling, against a control that returns 201). Not blocked-on-data; absent. Recorded on #201.

### Residue, and where it lives

Nothing here is design-blocked; both remaining items are waiting on tenant data that does not exist yet on m7kni:

- **#194** — five per-model endpoint-analytics segments. Unblock: ≥5 Windows devices reporting EA telemetry.
- **#201** — `AutopilotV1DeploymentStatus`. Unblock: a tenant with legacy Autopilot V1 deployment data.

Scope posture is unchanged from the spike: no new Graph grant was needed for anything built under this tracker, and the only write scope in play remains the documented export-job one (`DeviceManagementManagedDevices.ReadWrite.All`).

body:
## Why

#155 taught us that Entra's directory recycle bin (`/directory/deletedItems`) is a real signal source and that the `isDeleted` field on live objects lies — the tombstone list is the source of truth. #155 used it narrowly, to reconcile the `entra.risk` gauge against deleted-but-still-listed risky USERS. But the recycle bin is broader than that, and graph2otel currently has no general view of it.

## What the recycle bin holds (30-day soft-delete window)

`/directory/deletedItems/microsoft.graph.{user,group,application,servicePrincipal,device}` — deleted directory objects recoverable for 30 days. This is governance + security signal:
- **Deleted apps / service principals** sitting in the bin = supply-chain / persistence surface (a deleted-then-restored SP is a known attacker technique).
- **Deleted groups** with recoverable membership = access that can be silently restored.
- **Accumulation** (many objects near their 30-day purge, or a spike in deletions) = mass-deletion incident signal.

## What's already covered (don't rebuild)

- **Delete EVENTS** ship today via `entra.directory_audits` (verified live #184/#190): "Delete user", "Delete application", "Delete group", etc. flow as `entra.directory_audit` logs with `category`/`activityDisplayName`. That is the *event* ("X was deleted at T by Y").
- **Risky-user reconciliation** (`entra.risk`, #155) uses the user tombstones for its gauge.

The gap is the **current-state inventory** of the bin — "how many deleted objects of each type are recoverable right now, and which ones" — which no collector answers. An event stream and a recycle-bin census are different questions (the event can age out of the audit window while the object still sits in the bin).

## Scope to assess then build

- [ ] Confirm live (as `graph2otel-poller`) which `deletedItems` object types the poller can list and their `$count`/paging behavior (`docs/graph-api-gotchas.md` rules; `$count` needs `ConsistencyLevel: eventual`).
- [ ] A snapshot collector (proposed `entra.deleted_items`) emitting **bounded metrics** — count of recoverable deleted objects by type (`user`/`group`/`application`/`servicePrincipal`/`device`), and a "near-purge" bucket (deletedDateTime within N days of the 30-day purge) — plus a **log twin per deleted object** (id, type, displayName, deletedDateTime) per the #112/#114 metrics-carry-aggregates / logs-carry-entities rule.
- [ ] Least-privilege scopes: `Directory.Read.All` likely covers deletedItems reads — verify per type.
- [ ] Fold in the **#155 blob-twin `is_deleted` gap**: on a tenant where the risky-user twin is blob-owned (`entra.risky_users`, camden), the twin does NOT carry `is_deleted` (`blob.go:104` passes nil, by design — the append stream is not reconciled). So on the production tenant, a SIEM query over `entra.risky_user` twins cannot tell which risky user is deleted. Decide whether an `entra.deleted_items` census makes that acceptable (cross-reference by id) or whether the blob twin should also be reconciled.

## Out of scope

Delete *events* (already covered by `entra.directory_audits`). Non-directory recycle bins (SharePoint/OneDrive/M365 group mailbox soft-delete are separate surfaces — note them but do not scope here).

comments.body:
Shipped in `3647b21` (Closes #191). Mapped against verbatim live tombstones probed as `graph2otel-poller`, 2026-07-19.

## What landed
`entra.deleted_items` SnapshotCollector over the five casts `/directory/deletedItems/microsoft.graph.{user,group,application,servicePrincipal,device}`. From one paged fetch per type:
- **gauge** `entra.deleted_items.count{object_type, near_purge}` — bounded 5×2 series.
- **log twin** `entra.deleted_item` per object: `id`, `display_name`, `deleted_date_time`, `near_purge`, plus the type's own identifier (`user_principal_name` / `app_id` / `device_id`) — per-entity detail on the log, never a metric label (#112/#114).

Scope: `Directory.Read.All` (one grant covers all five casts; the poller listed every type with it). Per-type fetch error is logged + joined, never fatal to the rest. `DefaultInterval` 30m. `make check` green.

## Live-verified wire facts `[live-measured 2026-07-19, #191, n=1 tenant]`
- All 5 casts return **200** with real tombstones (user 4, group 5, application 5, servicePrincipal 3, device 3) and `$count=true`+`ConsistencyLevel: eventual` works.
- **`deletedItems/user` does NOT return `deletedDateTime`** in its default projection — an explicit `$select` is required (every other type returns it unprompted). The collector `$select`s it uniformly.
- An application (`IntuneManager`) sat **recoverable 44 days after deletion**, past the nominal 30-day purge. So `near_purge` flags "≥25 days deleted (approaching OR past purge)" rather than trusting a hard 30-day ceiling.

## #155 blob-twin `is_deleted` gap (raised in this issue)
Out of scope for this collector and left as-is: on the production tenant the risky-user twin is blob-owned (`entra.risky_users`) and does not carry `is_deleted`. A SIEM query can now cross-reference by `id` against the `entra.deleted_item` census instead, which is the acceptable resolution the issue asked to decide.

body:
## What

`entra.directory_audits` already emits every consent (`ApplicationManagement`) and role-change (`RoleManagement`) event as an `entra.directory_audit` log (verified source + live, see #184 close comment). But its mapper (`internal/collectors/entra/directoryaudits/directoryaudits.go:80-133`) only extracts `targetResources[].displayName` + a count — it does **not** read `targetResources[].modifiedProperties[]`, where the actually-actionable detail lives: *which role* was added, *which scope* was consented. So a SIEM sees "a role was changed" but not "the Global Administrator role was granted to X".

## Live sample (probed as graph2otel-poller, 2026-07-19, m7kni)

- `RoleManagement` / `Add member to role`: `modifiedProperties` displayNames = `Role.ObjectID`, `Role.DisplayName`, `Role.TemplateId`, `Role.WellKnownObjectName`, `TargetId.ServicePrincipalNames`, `ActorId.ServicePrincipalNames`.
- `ApplicationManagement` / `Add service principal`: `AccountEnabled`, `AppPrincipalId`, `DisplayName`, `ServicePrincipalName`, `Credential`, `ServicePrincipalTag`.

`modifiedProperties[]` entries are `{displayName, oldValue, newValue}`.

## Scope

Enrich the **existing** mapper (no new collector, no new registration path):

- [ ] For the consent/role categories, extract selected `modifiedProperties` into bounded, first-class attributes — e.g. `role_name` (from `Role.DisplayName`), `granted_scope` (consent), and the `modified_property_names` list. New `semconv.Attr*` consts.
- [ ] TDD against the live sample above (map against wire, never docs — CLAUDE.md hard rule).
- [ ] **Secret boundary:** emit modifiedProperty NAMES always; for VALUES, follow CLAUDE.md's one exclusion — a `Credential` / password / cert modifiedProperty value can BE the credential, so never emit those values. Role names and consented scopes are NOT secrets and are safe to emit. Do not over-generalize the exclusion (the #110/#111 lesson).
- [ ] Regenerate the signal golden + `docs/collectors.md` (annotation `Collects` prose if attributes change) + `docs/signals.md`.
- [ ] `make check` green.

## Out of scope

New collectors of any kind (the events already ship). Everything else in #184's audit (which resolved to "already covered").

comments.body:
## Done — 1d73fe7

Enriched the existing `entra.directory_audits` mapper (no new collector/registration path) to walk `targetResources[].modifiedProperties[]` and emit three attributes:

| attribute | source | notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `modified_property_names` | union of all changed property `displayName`s | sorted, deduped, bounded — NAMES only |
| `role_name` | `Role.DisplayName` change | directory-role assignments |
| `granted_scope` | `AppRole.Value` change | app-role consent grants (the exact permission string, e.g. `TeamSettings.Read.All`) |

**Secret boundary held.** NAMES always; VALUES only for the two safe fields above. A `Credential` `newValue` (which can BE the credential) is never emitted — proved by `TestMapDirectoryAuditNeverEmitsCredentialValue`. Did not over-generalise the exclusion (the #110/#111 lesson).

**Wire, not docs.** `newValue` is JSON-in-JSON on the wire (`"\"Purview Workload Content Writer\""`); `unquoteAuditValue` unwraps it and leaves non-string values (`[true]`) untouched. TDD against two **verbatim live m7kni records** probed as `graph2otel-poller` [live-measured 2026-07-19]:
- a `RoleManagement` / "Add member to role" granting the poller the *Purview Workload Content Writer* role → `role_name`;
- an `ApplicationManagement` / "Add app role assignment to service principal" granting `TeamSettings.Read.All` (this session's own #121 grant — the `additionalDetails` User-Agent proves provenance) → `granted_scope`.

Also confirmed the PIM "outside of PIM" variant carries **no** `Role.DisplayName`, so `role_name` is correctly conditional (absent, not empty).

**Free win:** the enrichment flows to the `AuditLogs` blob twin automatically — `blob.go` reuses `mapDirectoryAudit`, so blob-sourced directory audits gain the same three attributes.

Regenerated the signals golden (drove `role_name`/`granted_scope` through the emitter end-to-end so the golden — and #140's doc columns — reflect the real surface, per the #164 discipline) + `docs/collectors.md` annotation prose. `make check` green.

## Deployed + verified on camden

Raw `requestUri` contains GUIDs, UPNs/emails, `$count` segments, opaque ids — unbounded. Ships with defence in depth:

2. **Hard distinct-path cap** in the deriver (default 200): beyond the cap, collapse to `normalized_path="other"`. Fails safe *before* the SDK's 10k `otel.metric.overflow` backstop (`internal/telemetry/cardinality.go`).
