body:
## What & why

Follow-up from #135-C's coverage audit. graph2otel has 23 collectors that emit BOTH a metric and a per-entity log twin from Graph polls; only 2 (`entra.risk`, `intune.devices`) have an Azure Monitor diagnostic-settings blob equivalent. This issue audits whether the OTHER 21 "graph-only" metric+twin collectors could ever be sourced from a diagnostic-settings category (enabled or not), so we either build blob support where it's real or record — once, definitively — that it isn't, rather than re-asking per collector.

**Answer: near-total no.** 19 of the 21 are inventory / current-state data with no event-log analog. A diagnostic log is an append-only event stream; it fundamentally cannot reproduce a snapshot of "what exists right now" (current SKU consumption, current domain posture, current label catalog). Only **`entra.consent`** and **`entra.roles`** touch a real diagnostic category — `AuditLogs` — and there the category carries *change events*, not the current inventory the collector emits. So they are candidates for an **additive change-event collector**, NOT a re-source of the existing polled twin.

## Ground truth (live, 2026-07-18)

The storage account has 31 containers today; every one already maps to a known collector (done/building/deliberately-skipped). `insights-logs-auditlogs` (Entra `AuditLogs`) is already flowing — so the two candidates below need **no new diagnostic category enabled on the tenant**, only a parser over blobs already arriving. Method: probe as `graph2otel-poller` against `https://graph2otelm7kni.blob.core.windows.net`.

## Diagnostic-settings category catalogs (Microsoft Learn — verify envelope live before building)

**Entra ID** ([diagnostic settings logs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/monitoring-health/concept-diagnostic-settings-logs-options)): `AuditLogs`, `SignInLogs`, `NonInteractiveUserSignInLogs`, `ServicePrincipalSignInLogs`, `ManagedIdentitySignInLogs`, `ProvisioningLogs` (cloud-app provisioning — NOT Entra Connect hybrid sync), `ADFSSignInLogs`, `RiskyUsers`, `UserRiskEvents`, `RiskyServicePrincipals`, `ServicePrincipalRiskEvents`, `RiskyAgents`, `AgentRiskEvents`, `NetworkAccessTrafficLogs`, `RemoteNetworkHealthLogs`, `EnrichedOffice365AuditLogs`, `MicrosoftGraphActivityLogs`, `MicrosoftServicePrincipalSignInLogs`, `CustomSecurityAttributeAuditLogs`, `GraphNotificationsActivityLogs`.

**Intune** ([route logs to Azure Monitor](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/governance/integrate-azure-monitor)) — the entire catalog is four categories: `AuditLogs`, `OperationalLogs`, `DeviceComplianceOrg`, `IntuneDevices` (category id `Devices`). There is NO Intune category for app-install status, app-protection/MAM, cert connectors, cert inventory, Defender-agent state, endpoint-analytics, or malware — all report/current-state surfaces reachable only via Graph.

## Per-collector classification

| collector | data shape | candidate category | confidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| entra.consent | inventory (metrics) + event-derivable twin | `AuditLogs` — consent/grant events | med — consent *actions* are in AuditLogs (already blob); current grant inventory ≠ change events, so this is a NEW event collector, not a re-source |
| entra.roles | inventory (metrics) + event-derivable twin | `AuditLogs` — role-assignment/PIM change events | med-high — role add/remove + PIM activate/eligible are in AuditLogs; membership counts stay a Graph poll, only a change-event twin is blob-able |
| entra.credential_expiry | inventory | none | high — future-expiry projection has no event stream |
| entra.domains | inventory | none | high — posture snapshot |
| entra.licensing | inventory | none | high — consumption totals aren't derivable from assignment events |
| entra.mfa_registration | inventory | none | high — registration state, no category |
| entra.signin_activity | inventory (computed staleness) | none (raw events in SP/SignInLogs) | low — absence-of-event; a log can't prove a non-sign-in without the full population from Graph |
| entra.syncerrors | inventory | none | high — `onPremisesProvisioningErrors` is hybrid-sync state; do NOT map to `ProvisioningLogs` (that's cloud-app provisioning, a different surface) |
| intune.app_install_status | inventory | none | high — not in the 4 Intune categories |
| intune.app_protection | inventory | none | high |
| intune.certificates | inventory | none | high |
| intune.cert_inventory | inventory | none | high |
| intune.defender_agents | inventory | none | high |
| intune.endpoint_analytics | inventory | none | high |
| intune.malware | inventory (event-like twin) | none in Intune | med — detection is event-*like* but no Intune category; adjacent events may be in the Defender XDR advanced-hunting tables already ingested as `defender.*` (separate surface) |
| m365.servicehealth | inventory | none | high |
| m365.servicemessages | event-like | none | high — message-center posts via Graph serviceAnnouncement; no diagnostic category |
| m365.sharepoint_settings | inventory | none | high |
| m365.storage | inventory | none | high |
| purview.retention_labels | inventory | none | high |
| purview.sensitivity_labels | inventory | none | high |

## Recommended scope

Build blob support for **only** these two, and only as **additive audit-event collectors** fed from the already-flowing `insights-logs-auditlogs` container (no new diagnostic category to enable):

1. **entra.consent → AuditLogs** — consent / permission-grant change events (`Consent to application`, `Add app role assignment grant`, `Add delegated permission grant`). Complements, does not replace, the polled current-grant inventory.
2. **entra.roles → AuditLogs** — role-assignment + PIM activate/eligible change events. Complements the polled standing-membership counts.

**Out of scope / never blob-able (do not re-open per collector):** the other 19 are inventory/current-state with no event-log form — `credential_expiry`, `domains`, `licensing`, `mfa_registration`, `signin_activity`, `syncerrors`, all 7 `intune.*`, both `m365.service*`, `m365.sharepoint_settings`, `m365.storage`, both `purview.*`.

## Dual-emit guard (required)

Both candidates also emit metrics, so both are subject to the #135-C composition-root auto-suppress: when a blob-sourced twin for a category is enabled, the polled collector KEEPS its gauges but SUPPRESSES its own per-entity log twin (blob twin XOR polled twin).

**Subtlety specific to these two:** the blob `AuditLogs` twin is *change events*, whereas the current polled twin is *current inventory* — different record shapes, potentially both worth keeping. So this is NOT the clean "same record, two transports" case of #135-D. Resolve as an explicit design decision before wiring: does enabling the AuditLogs event stream suppress the polled inventory twin (they're different data), or do both coexist (metric-emitting collector emitting two DISTINCT log streams)? Likely the latter, which means these are really NEW collectors (`entra.consent_events` / `entra.role_change_events`) rather than a source toggle on the existing ones — decide before building.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Decide the consent/roles model: additive change-event collector vs. source toggle (see the subtlety above).
- [ ] If building: live-verify the `AuditLogs` blob envelope carries consent-grant and role-assignment `activityDisplayName`/`category` values on the tenant (probe as `graph2otel-poller`).
- [ ] Map against a real sample, never docs.
- [ ] Apply the #135-C guard appropriately per the model decision.
- [ ] `make check` green.

_Audit performed 2026-07-18; catalogs are Microsoft-Learn-sourced (docs-only) and cross-checked against the live 31-container set. The 19 inventory verdicts are structural (inventory has no event form) and high-confidence; the 2 candidates are docs-only until the AuditLogs envelope is live-verified._

comments.body:
## Premise re-validated against source + live tenant — already covered by `entra.directory_audits`, closing

Per the validate-premise-before-building rule, I checked this against both the code and the live m7kni tenant before writing anything. The result: **consent and role change events already ship** — building `entra.consent_events` / `entra.role_change_events` would duplicate records already on the wire.

**Source (confirmed):** `entra.directory_audits`' mapper (`internal/collectors/entra/directoryaudits/directoryaudits.go:80-87`) reads `category` + `activityDisplayName` and emits them **unconditionally — there is no category filter**, so every directory-audit record flows through, including `RoleManagement` (role changes) and `ApplicationManagement` (consent / app-role grants). The tests already pin this: `directoryaudits_test.go:269-297` asserts a `RoleManagement` / "Add member to role" record maps to `entra.directory_audit` with body `RoleManagement: Add member to role (success)`, and `:343` covers `ApplicationManagement`. It ships over BOTH transports (graph poll of `/auditLogs/directoryAudits` and the `insights-logs-auditlogs` blob, per the #135-D source toggle).

**Live (confirmed, probed as `graph2otel-poller`, 2026-07-19):** real records exist right now on m7kni —
- `RoleManagement`: `Add member to role`, `Add member to role outside of PIM (permanent)` (result=success), with `modifiedProperties` = `Role.ObjectID`, `Role.DisplayName`, `Role.TemplateId`, `TargetId.ServicePrincipalNames`, …
- `ApplicationManagement`: `Add service principal` (result=success), `modifiedProperties` = `AccountEnabled`, `AppPrincipalId`, `DisplayName`, `ServicePrincipalName`, `Credential`, …

Query them today: `{service_name="graph2otel"} | event_name="entra.directory_audit" | category="RoleManagement"` (or `category="ApplicationManagement"`).

**Verdict:** the issue's core ask is already satisfied. The `entra.consent` / `entra.roles` collectors are a separate thing — *inventory state feeds* (current membership / grant surface, re-emitted each cycle), not change events — so there is no suppression conflict and nothing to toggle.

**The one genuine residual** — `directoryaudits.go` maps only `targetResources[].displayName` + a count, not `targetResources[].modifiedProperties[]`, so the granted scope (consent) and the role name (role change) are IN the record but not first-class attributes. That is a small, contained **enrichment of the existing mapper**, not a new collector, and it needs a live modifiedProperties sample to map against (which I've now captured above). Filing it as its own scoped issue rather than reopening this one.

Closing #184 as already-covered.

title: Audit: which graph-only metric+twin collectors could be blob-sourced (near-total no; 2 additive AuditLogs candidates)

body:
## Decision

`collectors.Experimental` (the composition-root opt-in gate — off unless a config layer explicitly enables the collector) is to mean **exactly one thing: the collector is backed by a Graph _beta_ API**. It must NOT be used as a generic "new / higher-volume / opt-in" flag.

Rob, 2026-07-18: *"I want the edr default on when blob configured please. The only things truly experimental are the graph beta APIs."*

## Scope of this change

**Flip to non-experimental (default-on):**

- The **17 `defender.*` advanced-hunting blob collectors** (#106). They are read-only Azure Storage blob ingest, not a Graph API at all, and are fully live-verified. They run whenever `blob_ingest.account_url` is set — "default on when blob is configured."
- **`m365.servicemessages`** (#182). It polls v1.0 `/admin/serviceAnnouncement/messages` with a read-only scope (`ServiceMessage.Read.All`, already granted on the tenant). Neither beta nor write-scoped.

Both fail even the *existing* `beta`-column definition in `docs/collectors.md` line 30 ("backed by a Graph beta endpoint **or** a write-scoped export") — they are neither — so this is a correctness fix, not just a policy change.

**Left Experimental (correctly beta or write-scoped, out of scope):**

- Genuinely beta-endpoint: `entra.recommendations`, `entra.signin_activity`, `intune.autopilot`, `intune.autopilot_events`, `intune.certificates`, `intune.updates`, `intune.scripts`, `intune.gpo_analytics`, `intune.settings_catalog`, `intune.endpoint_analytics`.
- Write-scoped export-job (violate default read-only, must stay opt-in): `intune.app_install_report`, `intune.cert_inventory_report`, `intune.defender_agents`.
- `m365.unified_audit` / `m365.activity` — licensing-gated / async query surface.

> Note: the `Experimental` flag currently conflates "beta API" with "write-scoped / cost / unverified." This issue only fixes the mislabelled read-only-non-beta collectors. A later cleanup could split those two meanings into separate interfaces; not doing that now.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Remove `Experimental()` + the `collectors.Experimental` compile-assert from the 17 defender collectors and `m365.servicemessages`
- [ ] Update `internal/collectordoc/annotations.go` summaries (drop "Experimental + off by default")
- [ ] Regenerate `docs/collectors.md` + `docs/signals.md`; `beta` column clears for the 18
- [ ] Update `CLAUDE.md` defender-namespace line (no longer "Experimental + off by default")
- [ ] `config.example.yaml`: note that setting `blob_ingest.account_url` turns the Defender collectors on
- [ ] `make check` green
- [ ] Live: enable `blob_ingest` on the camden deployment so the Defender data flows (ops step)

body:
## What

Decide the fate of the `insights-logs-advancedhunting-cloudappevents` Defender XDR streaming container: build a collector, or turn the table off. Split out of #106 because it is the one Defender table that is **not** a straightforward build — it needs a filtering decision first.

## Findings (live sample 2026-07-18, `graph2otel-poller`)

- **Second-largest container in the whole account: ~168 MB** (40 hourly blobs) — behind only `deviceprocessevents`. Correcting an earlier internal estimate: this is **~100 MB/day**, not ~4 GB/day (40 blobs are 40 hourly partitions, not per-hour); `deviceprocessevents` (~326 MB/day) actually grows faster. Still a top-two volume driver.
- **100% noise in the sampled hour:** all 20 sampled records are one macOS endpoint (MBP16) deleting its own Spotlight index cache — `ActionType=FileDeleted`, `RawEventData.Application=spotlightknowledged.updater`, `~/Library/Metadata/CoreSpotlight/…` paths — surfaced through Defender's Endpoint→MCAS connector. Zero security signal.
- The table's **real** value (OAuth app grants, Exchange/SharePoint/OneDrive file ops, MCAS alerts) is genuinely useful but **unexercised** in this one-hour endpoint-noise window.

## The problem

CloudAppEvents is a firehose whose signal-to-noise depends entirely on which `Workload`/`ActionType` rows land. Unlike the Device* tables (curated EDR telemetry), this one carries a lot of endpoint-housekeeping noise via the Endpoint connector. Building it as-is ships ~100 MB/day of mostly-Spotlight-cache churn.

## What to decide

- [ ] Capture a **wider, multi-hour / multi-day sample** to characterise the real `Workload` + `ActionType` distribution (the one-hour sample is not enough to write it off or map it)
- [ ] Determine whether an **`ActionType`/`Workload` allow-list** (mirroring `intune.detected_apps`' allow-list and `m365.unified_audit`'s `recordTypeFilters`) can keep the OAuth/Exchange/SharePoint signal while dropping the endpoint-file-op noise — and whether the streaming export itself can be scoped, or it must be filtered consumer-side
- [ ] Redo the cost-benefit at the measured post-filter volume (`scripts/storage-report.py` gives per-container size + growth; a cost estimate is being added to it)
- [ ] Verdict: build with a filter / turn the table off / defer

## Interim recommendation

Leave it **HOLD** (do not build) and consider turning the `cloudAppEvents` table off in the Defender streaming export until the filter question is answered — it is a top-two storage cost with no demonstrated signal yet on this tenant.

Child of #106.

comments.body:
## Resolved: build kept, no filter needed — the "100% noise" was a one-hour sampling artifact

`defender.cloud_app_event` was built in #106 (package `internal/collectors/defender/cloudapp`, live on camden). Re-probed a **wide** sample as `graph2otel-poller` (2026-07-18): **11,580 records across 8 hourly blobs**.

ActionType distribution:
```
activity            7582
edit                1029
add_to_folder        530
change_acl_editors   528
change_user_access   528
access_item_content  521
create               519
FileDeleted          167   <- the Spotlight-cache noise
Search / Validate / trash / upload / login_success / AuditSearchCompleted  <200 combined
```
Application field: empty on 11,413/11,580 (SharePoint/Exchange ops); `spotlightknowledged.updater` only **166/11,580 ≈ 1.4%**.

So the original one-hour sample that read as "100% Spotlight noise" was an artifact of sampling a single quiet endpoint-heavy hour. The real distribution is dominated by SharePoint/Exchange **file ops, ACL changes, and access-permission changes** — exactly the OAuth/file-op/MCAS signal this table exists for. `[live-measured 2026-07-18]`

**Verdict: no ActionType/Workload allow-list.** At ~1.4% housekeeping noise, a filter would add config surface and a maintenance burden to drop a rounding error, against the project's "Loki is free here, per-entity SIEM detail is the deliverable" stance (#112). Storage cost is a separate lever (the Defender streaming export scope), not a collector concern.

Closing — cloud_app_event ships as built.

## What

Widen `managedDevicesSelect` and the `intune.managed_device` log twin to carry four hardware/threat fields the current `$select` omits. These come from the **same** `/deviceManagement/managedDevices` page-walk at zero extra Graph cost (the walk already runs hourly) — no new endpoint, no new scope.

Fields (live-verified against m7kni 2026-07-18 as `graph2otel-poller`):

- `model` — populated (`MacBook Pro`, `iPad Pro (12.9")`, `Standard PC (Q35 + ICH9, 2009)`, …)
- `manufacturer` — populated (`Apple`, `PCSpecialist`, `QEMU`, `Parallels International GmbH.`)
- `wiFiMacAddress` — populated on Apple/laptops; **empty string `""`** on some Windows/Linux (WINSRV, oli) — emit only when non-empty
- `partnerReportedThreatState` — the MTD/Defender-reported device threat state (bounded enum: unknown/secured/lowSeverity/…/compromised). `"unknown"` on all m7kni devices today (no active MTD connector), but it is the field the Intune `DeviceComplianceOrg` blob surfaces as `DeviceHealthThreatLevel` — bounded, always present, emit always.

**Not added:** `ethernetMacAddress` — **null on every m7kni device**, so it would ship pure nulls (#142 lesson: do not map a field that is never on the wire).

## Why

Closes the field-parity gap identified on #132: the Intune `Devices` / `DeviceComplianceOrg` blob categories carry these fields, but so does the polled resource — so capturing them here lets those two blob diagnostic categories be turned off with no loss (one transport per signal, not two).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `managedDevicesSelect` extended with `model,manufacturer,wiFiMacAddress,partnerReportedThreatState`
- [ ] `managedDevice` struct + `deviceLogTwin` carry the four fields; model/manufacturer/mac emitted only when non-empty, threat state always
- [ ] Each new attribute key is a `semconv.Attr*` constant (Gate B — no bare literals)
- [ ] Golden `testdata/signals.json` regenerated; fixture includes a device exercising all four fields
- [ ] `docs/collectors.md` regenerated (twin attr list is generated from the golden)
- [ ] `make check` green
- [ ] Cardinality rule respected: these are log-twin attributes, never metric labels (#112)

Child of #132.

body:
## What

`intune.endpoint_analytics` (Experimental, enabled on camden) logs two sub-endpoints as `endpoint analytics sub-endpoint not available on this tenant; skipping` and skips them. **The tenant is not missing the feature — the collector is calling the wrong URLs**, and its error handling turns a wrong-endpoint 400 into a silent "tenant gap". This is the #142 lesson again: a green tick / a graceful skip is not evidence the API usage is right.

## Live-measured (2026-07-18, as `graph2otel-poller` — cert on camden — against m7kni)

Probed every UXA segment on **both** v1.0 and beta:

| segment the collector calls | v1.0 | beta | verdict |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `userExperienceAnalyticsOverview` (`endpointanalytics.go:318`, v1.0) | **400 ResourceNotFound** | **400 ResourceNotFound** | dead segment — does not exist on either version |
| `userExperienceAnalyticsDeviceStartupHistories` (`:331`, v1.0) | **400 BadRequest** | **400 BadRequest** | wrong name — it is **singular** |

Correct/available segments (same probe):

| segment | v1.0 | beta | note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `userExperienceAnalyticsDeviceStartupHistory` (singular) | 200 | 200 | the real startup-history collection |
| `userExperienceAnalyticsDeviceScores` | 200 **value=1** | 200 **value=1** | per-device Endpoint Analytics scores — **has data on m7kni** |
| `userExperienceAnalyticsAppHealthOverview` | 200 (singleton, `insights`) | 200 | the app-health overview singleton |
| `userExperienceAnalyticsAppHealthApplicationPerformance` (`:350`, v1.0) | 200 (empty) | 200 | fine |
| `userExperienceAnalyticsBatteryHealthDevicePerformance` (`:376`, beta) | **400** | 200 **value=1** | correctly beta-only in the code; **has data** |
| `userExperienceAnalyticsResourcePerformance` | **400** | 200 (empty) | **beta-only** — confirm the code calls it on beta, not v1.0 |
| `userExperienceAnalyticsBaselines` | 200 (empty) | 200 | fine either version |

So the tenant genuinely **has** Endpoint Analytics (device scores + battery health both return a device); the collector just asks for two segments that don't exist as written.

## The two bugs

1. **Wrong/dead endpoints.**
   - `userExperienceAnalyticsOverview` does not exist on Graph anymore (400 on both versions). There is no tenant-wide overview singleton. The equivalent live data is `userExperienceAnalyticsDeviceScores` (per-device scores — map as a bounded aggregate + a per-device log twin, #112) and/or `userExperienceAnalyticsAppHealthOverview` (a real singleton). Decide the replacement against the live shape; do not reinstate a segment that 400s.
   - `userExperienceAnalyticsDeviceStartupHistories` → use the singular `userExperienceAnalyticsDeviceStartupHistory`.
   - Audit EVERY sub-endpoint's version while here: `resourcePerformance` is beta-only (400 on v1.0) like battery health — confirm it is fetched from beta, not v1.0.

2. **Error handling masks the bug (the deeper one).** The collector treats any failure on a sub-endpoint as `not available on this tenant; skipping`. That conflates two different things: **"the tenant lacks this feature/license"** (a legitimate quiet skip) and **"graph2otel asked for a segment that does not exist"** (a graph2otel bug that must be loud). A `400 ResourceNotFound`/`BadRequest` naming a route segment is the latter — it should surface as an error, not a silent skip, or a genuinely-wrong endpoint hides for the life of the collector (as these two did).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Fix the two endpoints (singular startup history; replace the dead overview with a live-verified segment — map against a real sample, not docs).
- [ ] Audit each sub-endpoint's v1.0-vs-beta correctness against the live probe; call beta-only families from beta.
- [ ] Distinguish "wrong/dead endpoint" (loud — our bug) from "tenant lacks the feature" (quiet skip) in the error handling, so a future wrong URL cannot masquerade as a tenant gap.
- [ ] Mappers written against the live samples (`userExperienceAnalyticsDeviceScores` has a device on m7kni to pin against).
- [ ] `docs/graph-api-gotchas.md` records the UXA surface reality (overview singleton removed; startup history is singular; battery/resource are beta-only) with a `live-measured (2026-07-18)` tag.
- [ ] `make check` green.

Refs #142 (green-tick-is-not-data), the endpoint_analytics package doc.

comments.body:
## Fixed in `e64f5a4` — both endpoints corrected, error taxonomy reversed, `make check` green

### The two endpoint bugs
- **`userExperienceAnalyticsOverview` (dead)** → replaced with **`userExperienceAnalyticsDeviceScores`** (v1.0, returns a real device on m7kni). Mapped against the live LAPHAM sample as bounded aggregates: `intune.uxa.device_score` (histogram, by `category` ∈ endpoint_analytics/startup_performance/app_reliability/work_from_anywhere/battery_health) + `intune.uxa.device_count` (gauge, by `health_state`). The old `intune.uxa.score{category,health_state}` gauge is retired — there is no tenant-wide overview singleton to feed it anymore.
- **`userExperienceAnalyticsDeviceStartupHistories` → singular `…DeviceStartupHistory`** (the plural 400s; the singular is 200).

### The `-1` sentinel
Device scores use `-1` for "not enough data yet" (LAPHAM's `startupPerformanceScore` was -1 while its other scores were populated). It's excluded from the score histogram so it can't drag the distribution toward zero; the device still counts in `device_count` under its `healthStatus`. Pinned in a test.

### Version audit (AC2) — all correct
`deviceScores` / `startupHistory` (singular) / `appHealthApplicationPerformance` are v1.0; `batteryHealthDevicePerformance` and `resourcePerformance` are **beta-only** (400 on v1.0, 200 on beta) and the code already calls both on beta. No change needed there. `baselines` fine either version.

### The deeper bug — error taxonomy (AC3)
A `400/404 "not found for segment"` now surfaces **loudly** (logged distinctly as "graph2otel bug, not a tenant gap", joined into the returned error) instead of being swallowed. Only a genuine **403** (not licensed) is a quiet skip. The old `isFeatureNotProvisioned` "gap" reading was the dead overview misdiagnosed: a valid UXA segment returns 200 with `insufficientData` even on an immature tenant, so a segment-404 can only ever be our wrong URL. The test-file provenance comment (which had recorded the same misdiagnosis) is corrected, and `TestCollectSkipsResourceNotFound400Gracefully` is inverted to `TestCollectSurfacesWrongEndpoint400AsBug`.

### One design call worth flagging — no log twin
I mapped `deviceScores` as **bounded aggregates only, no per-device log twin**, on purpose: this collector already carries a #114-audited exception for its per-device rows (startup histories), reasoning that UXA is an *ops* question — Intune's own Endpoint Analytics console answers "which device scores low" better than a log stream, and there is no security signal. Device scores fit that exact exception, so a twin would break the collector's consistent philosophy and mint several new score-attribute keys for no security gain. The issue body suggested a twin (#112); I diverged to stay consistent with the audited exception rather than silently. **If you'd rather have the per-device twin, say so and I'll add it** (device_name + the 5 scores + health_status).

### AC status
- [x] Two endpoints fixed (singular startup; dead overview → deviceScores mapped against a live sample)
- [x] v1.0-vs-beta audited; beta-only families called on beta
- [x] Wrong/dead endpoint (loud) vs tenant-lacks-feature (403 quiet skip) distinguished
- [x] Mappers written against the live sample (LAPHAM); `-1` sentinel handled
- [x] `docs/graph-api-gotchas.md` records the UXA surface reality with a `live-measured (2026-07-18)` tag
- [x] `make check` green

`[live-measured 2026-07-18, #179]`

## Follow-up: per-device log twin added (`5b770e9`)

Per the maintainer's call, `deviceScores` now also emits a per-device log twin (`intune.device_endpoint_analytics`) alongside the bounded histogram + gauge — the #112/#114 shape (metrics = "how many / distribution", twin = "which device"). It carries `id` (managed-device id), `device_name`, `model`, `manufacturer`, `health_state`, and each score the device actually reported. Scores are string-valued structured metadata; the `-1` sentinel is omitted from the twin (absence = not reported), matching the histogram exclusion. Timestamp left at poll time (state feed, like `entra/risk`'s twin). The per-boot `startupHistory` firehose keeps its #114 no-twin ops exception — these device-state rows are the right shape for a twin. `make check` green.

title: bug(intune): endpoint_analytics calls dead/wrong UXA endpoints and mis-skips them as 'not available on this tenant'

body:
## Why

**A disabled collector is usually not a gap — its signal is still collected, just over another transport.** The admin status page (`/`, `/api/status.json`) shows each collector's run state but not *how* it ingests or *whether a disabled collector is covered by a sibling*. So a row that reads `disabled — disabled by config` looks like missing data when the data is actually flowing over a different transport. On camden today, three rows read that way and all three are covered:

- `entra.signins.non_interactive` / `entra.signins.service_principal` — the **polled** (beta) forms, off because their GA `.blob` twins carry the identical records (18/18, 1375/1375 id overlap; #144 refuses both).
- `m365.unified_audit` — the beta audit-query form, off because `m365.activity` (O365 Management Activity API) covers the same signal.

And with the `source: graph|blob` toggle (#135 group D), `entra.directory_audits` / `entra.provisioning` now run over **blob** on camden with the polled side skipped — the page should say which source is live, not hide half of it.

The fix is both a **data** gap (the model carries no transport/coverage) and a **wording** gap (the copy states the mechanism — "disabled by config" — instead of the meaning — "collected over another transport").

## The wording (concrete copy)

Replace the bare mechanism text with meaning-first copy. A collector that is off **but covered** must not read as a gap:

- covered by a twin → **`collected via entra.signins.non_interactive.blob (blob)`**, with a secondary/muted note `polled form off by design` — NOT `disabled — disabled by config`.
- source-switchable, blob active → **`ingesting via blob`** (and `graph polling off`), not two rows or a bare "disabled".
- genuinely off, no twin covering it → keep an honest **`disabled`** (this is the only case that is really a gap), and reserve the plain "disabled by config" wording for it.

The principle: **state what is happening to the signal, not which switch was flipped.** "Disabled" should mean "this signal is not being collected anywhere", and nothing else should say it.

## Part A — transport + coverage (registry/config-derived, cheap)

- [x] Add `Transport` to `CollectorStatus` ∈ `graph` / `blob` / `o365_activity` / `audit_query` / `report_export` (same taxonomy as `ingest_transport`, #141). The composition root already knows each collector's path + `source` at registration — populate it there.
- [x] For a source-switchable collector (directory_audits/provisioning), show the **active** source (graph|blob), not both.
- [x] Add `CoveredBy` to `CollectorStatus`: for a collector that is off whose records are shipped by a registered twin, name the twin + its transport (derive the pairing from `ConflictsWith()` — the blob/o365 twin already names its polled peer — crossed with which side is actually registered). Drive the meaning-first copy above off this.
- [x] HTML + JSON both carry the new fields; a covered collector never renders as a gap.
- [x] Tests: a covered collector renders `collected via … (transport)`; a genuinely-off collector (no covering twin) still reads `disabled`; a source-switchable collector shows the active transport.

## Part B — cursor / checkpoint state (checkpoint-derived, more work)

- [x] Surface per-collector state from the `CheckpointStore` so the page answers "is it keeping up", not just "is it registered":
  - blob collectors → total byte offset + blobs tracked + newest consumed hour (from `blobcursor_*`);
  - window collectors → watermark / last window end;
  - job collectors → in-flight job id, if any.
- [x] Add a `State` sub-object to `CollectorStatus`; the StatusTracker or admin snapshot reads the store (read-only) at render time.
- [x] Tests with a faked store.

## Notes

- Part A is the high-value, low-risk half and directly fixes the misleading view — do it first.
- Read-only: the admin page must never mutate the checkpoint store or config.
- The transport taxonomy must match `ingest_transport` (#141) so the UI and the log attribute agree.

comments.body:
## Part A shipped — `1f4dcb8` (on main)

Transport + twin coverage now on the status page and `/api/status.json`. `make check` green.

### What landed
- **`CollectorStatus.Transport`** ∈ `graph`/`blob`/`o365_activity`/`audit_query`/`report_export`, via a new single-source `collector.TransportOf`. Each engine exposes `IngestTransport()` returning the **same `telemetry.Transport` constant it already stamps** onto records with `WithTransport` (#141) — so the UI value and the log-record value cannot drift. Pinned per engine by test (`logpipeline`→graph, `jobpipeline`→audit_query, `blobpipeline`→blob, `o365pipeline`→o365_activity, the 3 exportjob collectors→report_export). A source-switchable collector (#135 group D) reports its **active** source with no extra logic: `entra.directory_audits` on `source: blob` shows `blob`, because the collector registered under that name is the blob one.
- **`CollectorStatus.CoveredBy`** `{collector, transport}`, set on an off collector whose records a registered twin ships. Derived from the **live registry** via `ConflictsWith()` (the blob/o365 twin already names its polled peer) — no hand-maintained list, so a new twin is picked up the day it lands (same robustness as `checkRegistryConflicts`, avoiding the #139 gate-blindness trap).
- **Meaning-first copy:** a covered collector renders `collected via <twin> (<transport>) · polled form off by design` with a `covered` badge — never a bare `skipped`. A genuinely-off collector with no covering twin still reads `disabled`. Enabled rows carry a `via <transport>` chip.
- **Header roll-up honesty:** covered rows are counted in a new `CoveredCount`, split out of `SkippedCount`, so the per-tenant summary never tallies a collected signal as a gap (`… · N covered · M skipped`).

### Design note
The body said "the composition root already knows each collector's path … populate it there." I did it in **admin instead** — it derives everything from data it already receives (`Registry.Entries()` + `skips`), so `cmd/graph2otel/tenants.go` (the high-blast-radius composition root) is **untouched**. Same fields, same correctness, lower blast radius, and the transport value stays single-source with what the engines stamp.

### camden effect (once the edge image ships this)
The three rows that read `disabled — disabled by config` — the beta `entra.signins.non_interactive`/`entra.signins.service_principal` (covered by their `.blob` twins) and `m365.unified_audit` (covered by `m365.activity`) — will render `collected via …` instead of looking like gaps. `entra.directory_audits`/`entra.provisioning` (running `source: blob` on camden) show `via blob`.

### Part B — remaining (unticked in the body)
Cursor/checkpoint state (blob byte-offset + newest consumed hour; window watermark; in-flight job id) via a read-only `State` sub-object reading the `CheckpointStore` at render time. Left as the follow-up half; the issue stays open for it.

Part B shipped in 5f75ac9 (auto-closed via the commit). Per-collector checkpoint cursor state now renders on the admin status page, read read-only from the checkpoint store at render time:

- **window collectors** (logpipeline/jobpipeline/o365pipeline + `mdca.discovery_parse`): watermark + staleness (now−watermark, guarded against an NTP backward jump) + overlap-dedupe set size + any adopted in-flight job id; cold start omits the watermark rather than showing a 1970 date.
- **blob collectors** (blobpipeline): total byte offset + blobs tracked + newest consumed hour, from the `BlobCursor`.

Design: a `CheckpointReporter` seam mirroring #178 Part A's `TransportOf` — the engine that OWNS the checkpoint key implements `CheckpointState()` and reads its own store (the key is not derivable from `Name()`), and `admin` just calls `collector.CheckpointStateOf`. Read-only, render-time, non-mutating.

**Known gap (deliberate, low-value):** the three report-export collectors (`intune/appinstallreport`, `defenderreport`, `certinventoryreport`) don't surface their in-flight job id — the store is encapsulated inside `exportjob.Client` and the collector never exposes its report key. They are snapshot-shaped (no watermark), so the only missing state is a transient id; not worth threading a new accessor through `Runner`→`Client` for. All high-value states (window watermark+staleness, blob byte-offset/newest-hour) are covered. `make check` green.

body:
The five-collector posture batch shipped in b2dfa9d (closing #122/#123/#124/#125/#173), fully unit-tested against fixtures + green `make check`. Four carry a **live-tenant confirmation** step that needs a probe as `graph2otel-poller` on m7kni — deferred out of the build (no live tenant in the build context) and collected here so they run in one sitting rather than getting lost in closed-issue comments. None blocks the code; each is a "confirm it behaves in prod" check with a defined fallback.

- [ ] **#124 — `intune.devices.os_version.count` cardinality.** Measure the distinct `os_version` count on the live fleet. Ships the **full** build string as the label today. If the count is large, fallback = bucket the metric to minor version (`major.minor`), keep the full build on the `intune.managed_device` twin only (config-free code tweak).
- [ ] **#125 — `entra.users.population` correctness.** Confirm the four joint `{user_type, account_enabled}` counts sum to the tenant total, and each combination's sum over the other dimension matches the corresponding existing marginal on `entra.users.total`. A mismatch = a compound `$filter` is wrong.
- [ ] **#122 — license group filter auth.** Confirm `GET /groups?$filter=hasMembersWithLicenseErrors eq true&$select=id,displayName` returns **200** under app-only cert auth. The Graph docs' permission table for this endpoint was flagged untrustworthy, so this needs a live check, not a docs assertion. (Requires `Group.Read.All`, added to the collector.)
- [ ] **#123 — sync-errors sweep cost.** On a hybrid-synced tenant, record the page count + duration of a full `/users` sweep so the opt-in cost is documented rather than assumed.

Each probe's result should be recorded back on its originating issue with a `live-measured (date, #issue)` tag. #173 needs no probe (its fields were already live-captured 4/4 on #165).

body:
Follow-up to #154, which shipped the **blob-path** self-exhaust exclusion (`blob_ingest.exclude_self`, `ad92d56`). This owns the two items that were out of scope there — both need a live `graph2otel-poller` probe or a transport decision, neither is a blocker.

## Background (measured)

graph2otel is **59.9% of its own `MicrosoftGraphActivityLogs` volume** (#152, live 2026-07-17). The blob-path filter (#154) drops the poller's own records on the blob categories that carry an `appId` (MGAL + the SP-sign-in blob categories). But the poller's exhaust plausibly lands in other transports too, and those are unmeasured and uncovered.

## 1. Measure the self-share on the other candidate signals

Probe as `graph2otel-poller` (read-only), the way #137/#152 did:
- **`entra.signins.service_principal`** (Graph-polled, `logpipeline`) — the poller acquires a token per poll; each is an SP sign-in. What fraction of this stream is the poller itself?
- **`MicrosoftServicePrincipalSignInLogs` / `ServicePrincipalSignInLogs`** (blob) — already *covered* by #154's filter; quantify the saving so the two levers aren't double-counted.
- **`m365.activity` / UAL** (`o365pipeline`) — unknown whether Graph calls even surface here. Measure before designing.

Related concentration already found (#137): one Defender TVM scan-agent SP is **96.4%** of `ServicePrincipalSignInLogs`, so that category is robot-dominated regardless.

## 2. Decide coverage

If the measured self-share on a transport is material, extend the opt-in exclusion to it — reusing #154's design verbatim: **self-only by appId == that tenant's own client_id** (never a third party), **default off**, and a **loud per-collector drop counter** (`graph2otel.*`, never a silent drop). Do NOT reuse `ingest_transport` (#141) or name anything `source`.

- `logpipeline` (Graph-polled SP sign-ins): the record carries the SP appId; the filter injects the same way `blobpipeline.emitLines` does.
- `o365pipeline` (`m365.activity`): only if the poller's calls surface in UAL at all — measure first.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Self-share measured per transport above, recorded with a `live-measured` tag
- [ ] For each transport, a decision (extend / skip) with reasoning
- [ ] Any extension reuses #154's self-only + default-off + loud-counter design; guard test that a third-party appId is never filtered
- [ ] `make check` green

Refs #154, #152, #137, #141

comments.body:
Shipped in `66d55eb` (Closes #176). All measurements probed live as `graph2otel-poller` from camden, 2026-07-19.

## Config change (no backward compat, pre-1.0)
`blob_ingest.exclude_self` → **tenant-level `tenants[].exclude_self`**, old key deleted. The same "self" spans transports, so one flag now covers both the blob consumer and the Graph-polled SP sign-in stream. `config.example.yaml` + `docs/blob-ingest.md` updated; camden's config sets no `exclude_self`, so nothing was lost by the rename.

## Self-share per transport — `[live-measured 2026-07-19, #176, n=1 tenant]`

| transport | self-share | decision |
| --- | --- | --- |
| blob `MicrosoftGraphActivityLogs` | **59.9%** (already #154) | the material saving; unchanged |
| Graph `entra.signins.service_principal` | **168 / 14,763 = 1.1%** (poller appId `2c92ce28…`; dominant app `32d104a5…` is 95%) | mechanism **built + wired, default off** — the one tenant flag covers it, but no reason to enable by volume |
| `m365.activity` default subscription | **0/131 SharePoint, 0/119 Exchange**; only non-default `Audit.AzureActiveDirectory` had 3/258 (~1.2%) | **skip** — poller does no Exchange/SharePoint ops, so no self-exhaust to filter |

## Mechanism

Reuses #154's self-only + default-off + loud-counter design verbatim. Guard tests: a third-party appId is never filtered; nil `SelfAppID` / empty `SelfClientID` no-op; non-SP streams ignore the flag. `make check` green.

## Summary

`purview/sensitivitylabels` emits its `purview.sensitivity_label` log twin's `description` attribute from the wire field `description`, but on the live wire that field is empty on every label — the human-readable text lives in `toolTip`, which the mapper does not read. So the twin ships **no description from real data**.

## Wire evidence (live-measured 2026-07-17, #165, as graph2otel-poller against m7kni)

`GET /security/dataSecurityAndGovernance/sensitivityLabels` (v1.0, 200 app-only), all 5 labels:

| name | description | toolTip |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Personal | `""` | "Non-business data, for personal use only" |
| Public | `""` | "Organization data that's specifically pr…" |
| General | `""` | "Organization data that is not intended f…" |

`description` is `""` on 5/5; `toolTip` carries the text on 5/5. `displayName` is also `null` on every row — the mapper correctly reads `name` for the label name; only the description source is wrong.

## Why it stayed green

The pre-#165 docs fixture populated `description`, so the twin's `description` attribute looked sourced. The fixture is now the verbatim live capture and the new `TestSensitivityCollectFromLiveCapture` asserts `description` is absent from real data.

## Fix

Read `toolTip` (falling back to `description` if a future tenant populates it) for the twin's description attribute. Confirm the attribute name/semantics against #112 (per-entity text belongs on the log twin, not a metric label — it already is).

## Acceptance
- [ ] the `purview.sensitivity_label` twin carries the label's human text from `toolTip`
- [ ] live-capture test asserts the real tooltip text reaches the emitter

body:
## Summary

`intune/scripts` decodes the three per-script/tenant summary singletons through a `{"value":{…}}` envelope, but the live wire returns those bodies with the counts at the **top level** (OData `$entity` shape). Result: in production **every runSummary and remediation-overview count decodes to 0** — the metrics silently under-report on a real tenant.

## Wire evidence (live-measured 2026-07-17, #165, as graph2otel-poller against m7kni)

`GET /beta/deviceManagement/deviceHealthScripts/{id}/runSummary` and `GET /beta/deviceManagement/deviceHealthScripts/getRemediationSummary` both return top-level fields, no `value` key:

- runSummary top-level keys: `id, issueDetectedDeviceCount, noIssueDetectedDeviceCount (=3), detectionScriptPendingDeviceCount, …` — **no `value`**
- getRemediationSummary top-level keys: `scriptCount (=12), remediatedDeviceCount` — **no `value`**

Decoding through the `.Value` envelope yields `noIssueDetectedDeviceCount → 0` (true 3) and `scriptCount → 0` (true 12). Direct top-level decode yields the real values. n=2/2 captured singletons.

## Affected sites

| envelope type (decl) | consumed |
| --- | --- |
| `scriptRunSummaryEnvelope` — `scripts.go:144-146` | `scripts.go:314-321` |
| `healthScriptRunSummaryEnvelope` — `scripts.go:166-168` | `scripts.go:361-368` |
| `remediationOverviewEnvelope` — `scripts.go:180-182` | `scripts.go:395-401` |

## Why it stayed green

The pre-#165 docs-derived fixture used the enveloped `{"value":{…}}` shape — the same wrong shape the decoder assumes — so the fixture confirmed the bug instead of catching it. This is the exact #165 thesis. The fixture is now pinned to the real top-level capture, and `TestCollectAgainstLiveCapturesExposesRunSummaryEnvelopeDefect` asserts the current (wrong) zeros with the true wire values in comments — it flips to green when the decode is fixed.

Contrast: `intune/mobileapps` reads `Value` when non-nil else the bare fields, so it tolerates both shapes; `intune/settingscatalog` decodes its singletons directly. `scripts` is the only one that reads `.Value` unconditionally.

## Fix

Decode each of the three singletons at the top level (like settingscatalog does), or make the envelope tolerant (`Value` if present, else the bare object) as mobileapps does. Then flip the regression assertion in the test to the real values.

## Acceptance
- [ ] runSummary / healthScript runSummary / remediationOverview decode the real top-level counts
- [ ] the pinned regression test asserts the true values (3, 12, …), not 0

comments.body: Fixed in `54489d6` (on main). The three summary singletons (scriptRunSummary, healthScriptRunSummary, remediationOverview) now decode at the top level (OData $entity), matching the wire — the `{value:{...}}` envelope structs are deleted. Previously every runSummary/remediation count silently decoded to 0 in production. The regression test flipped to assert the true values (3, 12); `make check` green.

title: intune/scripts: runSummary + remediation counts decode to 0 — wire is top-level, decoder assumes {"value":{…}} envelope

body:
Surfaced during #165's live capture of `entra/mfaregistration`.

## What

`GET /reports/authenticationMethods/userRegistrationDetails` returns four fields the collector's
`$select` does not request, and the mapper therefore never sees. Confirmed live 2026-07-17 (an
unfiltered probe vs the collector's `$select` response, as `graph2otel-poller`) — all four
populate on all 4/4 rows on m7kni:

| field | live value(s) | signal value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `userType` | `member` / `guest` | **highest** — lets every existing MFA/SSPR posture gauge slice member vs guest. Guests with weak MFA are a distinct risk class. Viable as a bounded metric label (2 values) AND a log-twin attribute |
| `isSystemPreferredAuthenticationMethodEnabled` | `true` (4/4) | tenant-posture KPI — Microsoft's system-preferred-MFA rollout state, same family as the existing mfa/sspr gauges |
| `systemPreferredAuthenticationMethods` | `["PhoneAppNotification"]` / `["Fido2"]` | which method the system prefers per user; log-twin attribute + count-by distribution |
| `userPreferredMethodForSecondaryAuthentication` | `"push"` (4/4) | the user-chosen default second factor; natural log-twin attribute alongside `methods_registered` |

## This is not a bug

The current `$select` (`mfaregistration.go`, `requestPath`) is a deliberate least-fetch. Nothing
is broken — the fixture (#165) faithfully represents the current 12-field response. This issue is
purely "these four are available and worth adding", not "the mapper drops them wrongly".

## Why it matters

`userType` in particular changes what the collector can answer. Today "how many guests are not
MFA-registered" is unanswerable from this signal — the bounded gauges don't carry a member/guest
dimension and the log twins don't carry `user_type`. A guest with weak MFA is exactly the kind of
entity a SIEM feed exists to surface.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Decide which of the four to add and at which layer. `userType`: both a bounded metric label
      (respects #112 — 2 values, does not grow with tenant size) and a log-twin attribute. The
      other three: log-twin attributes (per-user, not aggregate). Follow the cardinality rule —
      metrics carry the bounded `user_type` breakdown, logs carry the per-user method detail
- [ ] Add the chosen fields to `requestPath`'s `$select` and to the `userRegistrationDetail`
      struct
- [ ] Extend the fixture (it already pins the 12-field $select response; the capture with these
      fields exists) and regenerate the golden
- [ ] `make check` green

## Reference

The four fields, live-captured 2026-07-17, are recorded in the `entra/mfaregistration` fixture doc
comment (`liveUsers` in `mfaregistration_test.go`), which points here.

comments.body:
Shipped in b2dfa9d (on `main`).

All four dropped fields added to the `$select` + struct. Telemetry placement:
- `user_type` → a new **bounded metric label** on `entra.mfa.registration.users.total` (now `{status, user_type}`, lowercased member/guest) **and** a log-twin attribute.
- `system_preferred_auth_enabled`, `system_preferred_auth_methods`, `user_preferred_secondary_method` → **log-twin attributes only** (per-user posture detail) on `entra.user_registration`.
- Fixture extended with the four live-captured fields; golden regenerated.

**Scoping decision (recorded):** `user_type` rides **only** on `users.total`, not on `methods.total` or `admin_mfa_capable.total` — the status gauge is where the "members vs guests posture" question lives, and crossing the other two adds golden/label churn for marginal value. If you later want `user_type` on those two as well, that's a clean follow-up, not something this change did implicitly.

No live probe needed — the fields were already live-captured on 4/4 rows (#165), and the change is `$select`-only against the pinned fixture.

title: feat(entra): mfaregistration could surface userType (member/guest) + system-preferred-method posture - the endpoint sends them, the $select drops them

body:
Found by a live capture during #165.

## The wire

`GET /deviceManagement/auditEvents` on m7kni, read as `graph2otel-poller`, **`activity`
(top-level) is null on 5/5 rows** `[live-measured 2026-07-17, #165]`. The friendly action name
lives in `displayName` and `activityType`, both populated on every row:

| activity | displayName | activityType |
| --- | --- | --- |
| null | `Create device configuration 2.0 (beta)` | `Create DeviceManagementConfigurationPolicy` |
| null | `Syncing Multi Token DEP Devices, Profiles and Account Details` | `SyncMultiTokenDEPDevicesProfilesAndAccountDetails DepOnboardingSetting` |
| null | `Search CloudCertificationAuthority` | `Search CloudCertificationAuthority` |

## The mapper

`internal/collectors/intune/auditevents/auditevents.go:201`:

```go
Body: fmt.Sprintf("%s: %s (%s)", category, activity, activityResult),
```

`activity` is the null field. On live data every log record's Body renders with an empty middle:

```
"DeviceConfiguration:  (Success)"
                     ^^ two spaces, nothing between the colon and the parens
```

The `activity` attribute itself is fine — `setStr` omits it when empty, so it's simply absent
(not emitted as `""`). The defect is confined to the Body: the human-readable summary of every
Intune audit event names nothing about what the event actually was, because it interpolates the
one field that's structurally empty instead of the two that carry the action.

## Why it tested green

The hand-written fixtures set `"activity": "Create"` / `"Update"` — a plausible-looking value
that isn't on the wire — so the Body assertion passed against fiction. Same class as #142/#153
and the four other dead/wrong mapper lines this #165 wave surfaced (#167, #168, #169, #170).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Body uses a populated field. `displayName` is the friendly one-line summary
      (`"Create device configuration 2.0 (beta)"`); `activityType` is the schema-ish action
      (`"Create DeviceManagementConfigurationPolicy"`). `displayName` reads best for a SIEM Body;
      pick against how the other collectors' Bodies read.
- [ ] Decide whether to keep mapping top-level `activity` to the `activity` attribute at all — it
      has no wire witness on this tenant. Either drop it, or keep it with a comment that it is
      empty in practice (do not let a future fixture re-introduce a fake value for it — that's the
      exact regression this issue documents).
- [ ] Update `TestMapAuditEventAgainstLiveRecord` / the end-to-end test's Body assertion
      (`internal/collectors/intune/auditevents/auditevents_test.go`) to the real, non-empty Body
- [ ] `make check` green

## Note

`actor.ipAddress` is also null on all 5 rows (the `actor_ip_address` attribute was dropped from
the golden in the #165 fixture commit for exactly this reason) and `actor.userPermissions`
(`["*"]`) + `actor.servicePrincipalName` are unmapped — the latter two are potential SIEM signal,
out of scope here, noted so they aren't lost.

comments.body: Fixed in `a1cf204` (on main). Log `Body` now renders `displayName` instead of the top-level `activity` field, which is null on every live record (Body was rendering `"DeviceConfiguration:  (Success)"`). The `activity` attribute mapping is unchanged (setStr omits it when empty) and carries a comment warning against re-introducing a fake fixture value. `make check` green.

title: bug(intune): auditevents Body renders an empty action - it interpolates activity, which is null on the wire; displayName carries the name

body:
Found during #165's live-capture inventory sweep of the blob account, not by directly investigating this claim — a byproduct of checking blob container contents broadly.

## What #94 and `docs/blob-ingest.md` say today

#94 (closed) established Intune `OperationalLogs` (the compliance-alert **fired-event** stream) as a permanent gap on the **Graph** side: Graph exposes only the notification templates, and the dedicated Intune API (`0000000a-…`) has zero app-only roles. **That half is still true and not being disputed here.**

`docs/blob-ingest.md`'s "What it is for" table adds a *separate* claim about the **blob** escape hatch specifically for this category:

> Intune `OperationalLogs` — **No Graph endpoint** (#94). The compliance-alert *fired-event* stream; Graph exposes only the notification templates. — and, in the row for `ManagedIdentitySignInLogs` (a different category, same sentence pattern applied by analogy) — "**not built**: the container does not exist on the verification tenant, so there is no live sample to map against and this project does not map from documentation."

CLAUDE.md's "Permanent gaps and the fallback path" section lists the same signal among things with "no API anywhere."

## What's actually there now

Live-measured 2026-07-17, `graph2otelm7kni` storage account, as `graph2otel-poller` (confirmed via `az account show`, not a cached admin session): container `insights-logs-operationallogs` **exists and holds real content** — a genuine fired-alert record:

```json
{
  "time": "2026-07-17T11:50:38.5951000Z",
  "tenantId": "4b8c18bd-2f9f-4227-af55-9f1061cf9c32",
  "category": "OperationalLogs",
  "operationName": "Compliance",
  "properties": {
    "AlertDisplayName": "Managed Device THRWX5256T_14_... is not Compliant",
    "AlertType": "Managed Device Not Compliant",
    "Description": "MacOSCompliancePolicy.StorageRequireEncryption_...||Device_Encryption_FileVault2Encrypted||Equals True||False||SecurityInfo/FDE_Enabled",
    "IntuneDeviceId": "33dcca32-d6ea-478b-88d9-e2a891f9d83a",
    "DeviceName": "THRWX5256T_14_...",
    "DeviceOperatingSystem": "MacMDM 26.5.2 (25F84)",
    "UserName": "rob", "UPNSuffix": "m7kni.io", "UserDisplayName": "Rob Knight",
    "ScenarioName": "Microsoft.Management.Services.Diagnostics.SLAEvents.DeviceNotInComplianceSecurityAlert",
    "OperationalLogCategory": "DeviceCompliance"
  }
}
```

This is exactly the shape the "permanent gap" framing said would never exist: a real compliance-alert fired-event, on this tenant, in the diagnostic-settings blob output, with a device id, UPN, and the actual policy check that failed.

## What this corrects, precisely

Not #94's core claim (Graph still cannot see this). What's wrong is the **narrower** claim that the blob escape hatch specifically was unbuildable for lack of a sample: `docs/blob-ingest.md`'s framing implies no verification tenant has ever produced this category, which is no longer true — it may have been true when #94/blob-ingest.md were written and the diagnostic setting simply wasn't enabled yet.

## Scope

Filed as a correction, not a build request. **Building a collector for this is out of scope here** — #165 is fixture-provenance work on existing collectors; this is a new-signal opportunity that belongs with #135 (which already owns "map the remaining blob diagnostic categories") or a dedicated issue. This one exists so the "permanent, no sample" framing in CLAUDE.md and `docs/blob-ingest.md` gets corrected before it hardens further, per the project's own body-freshness rule.

## Suggested acceptance criteria (for whoever picks this up)

- [ ] `docs/blob-ingest.md`'s `OperationalLogs` row updated: still no Graph path, but now has a live blob sample and could be built via the same escape hatch as `entra.graph_activity`
- [ ] CLAUDE.md's "Permanent gaps" list either drops this entry or adds a footnote pointing here
- [ ] Decide whether to fold the actual collector build into #135's worklist or spin out its own `kind/feature` issue — `OperationalLogCategory` in the sample suggests there may be more than one alert type under this category, worth a wider sample before mapping
title: docs: Intune OperationalLogs blob path is buildable now - corrects blob-ingest.md's 'no live sample' framing (Graph gap in #94 unaffected)

Found by a live capture during #165.

## The wire

`POST /security/auditLog/queries` result set on m7kni, read as `graph2otel-poller`, **500/500
rows** `[live-measured 2026-07-17, #165]`:

- Envelope `clientIp` is **null on all 500 rows**.
- `auditData.ClientIP` (nested inside the classic-schema payload) holds a real address on
  **474/500 rows**.

## The mapper

`internal/collectors/m365/unifiedaudit/unifiedaudit.go:194`:

```go
setStr(attrs, "client_ip", str(rec, "clientIp"))
```

Reads the envelope field, which is structurally null. `client_ip` has never been emitted from a
real record.

## Why it tested green for the package's whole life

The old hand-written fixture supplied `"clientIp": "203.0.113.7"` (Microsoft's own TEST-NET-3
documentation example) at the top level and asserted it mapped through. Same class as #142's
`"platform": "windows"`, #153's invented `riskType`, #167's `servicePrincipal` shape, and #169's
`tags` — the fifth instance of this exact bug class found this session.

## Scope note

The 500-row capture was an unfiltered query window; none of the rows happen to be a record type
this collector's `recordTypeFilters` include-list would actually return (the window held
DLPEndpoint/DataInsights/AuditSearch/AADStsLogon/AAD types). The `clientIp`/`auditData.ClientIP`
relationship is a property of the query API's **envelope**, which `mapRecord` reads uniformly
across record types — so the finding is not scoped to a record type this collector excludes, but
worth naming so nobody assumes the 500 rows are a filtered sample of what this collector polls.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Decide: map `auditData.ClientIP` (fixing the dead line so a real IP reaches `client_ip`),
      or drop the mapper line + attribute entirely if the envelope field is never going to carry
      anything. `auditData` is JSON-encoded per record — same "decode a nested field" shape as
      riskdetections' `additionalInfo` (#153/#159), so that package's `additionalInfoPairs`
      pattern is a reasonable model if `auditData` needs more than this one field pulled out of it.
- [ ] Update `TestTopLevelClientIPIsNull` (in `unifiedaudit_test.go`, currently pins the absence)
      once the decision lands
- [ ] Golden regenerated if the fix adds the attribute back
- [ ] `make check` green

## Related

`m365.unified_audit` and `m365.activity` are twins over the same underlying audit data
(`docs/signals.md`) — worth checking whether `m365/activity`'s mapper has the same envelope-vs-
nested-payload assumption for its own client-IP-shaped field before assuming this is isolated to
the query API transport.

comments.body: Fixed in `2fe6b2c` (on main). `client_ip` now reads `auditData.ClientIP` (the envelope `clientIp` was null on 500/500 records); the dead envelope read is gone. `auditData` is already a decoded map on this transport, so no second JSON decode is needed (unlike riskdetections' additionalInfo) — noted in-code. A synthetic in-scope fixture (SharePointFileOperation, RFC-5737 IP) exercises the fixed path since no live in-scope capture carried a ClientIP. Golden +`client_ip`; `make check` green.

Found by a live capture during #165.

## The wire

`GET /security/incidents` on m7kni, read as `graph2otel-poller`, **0/5 rows carry a `tags` key**
`[live-measured 2026-07-17, #165]`. All 5 carry `customTags` and `systemTags` instead:

```
row id=16  customTags=[]  systemTags=[]
row id=15  customTags=[]  systemTags=[]
row id=14  customTags=[]  systemTags=["Security Testing"]
row id=13  customTags=[]  systemTags=[]
row id=12  customTags=[]  systemTags=[]
```

## The mapper

`internal/collectors/entra/securityincidents/securityincidents.go:158-159`:

```go
if tags := strSlice(rec, "tags"); len(tags) > 0 {
    attrs["tags"] = tags
}
```

`tags` is not a field this endpoint sends. This line is **dead on every real poll**.

## Why it tested green for the package's whole life

The old hand-written fixture asserted `tags: ["Priority","Ransomware"]` and asserted it mapped
through. Same class as #142's `"platform": "windows"`, #153's invented `riskType`, and #167's
`servicePrincipal` shape — a fixture written from documentation confirming the belief that wrote
it. This is the third instance found in this wave alone.

## Why it matters now specifically

**The golden still carries `tags`**, sustained only by a synthetic fixture in `TestEmitsNoMetrics`
— it survived the #165 fixture swap because nothing forced its removal. #140 wants to generate
`docs/collectors.md`'s signal columns from these goldens. Left as-is, that publishes `tags` as a
*measured* attribute of `entra.security_incident` that no live poll can ever produce — exactly
#140's own stated failure mode, "wrong in the confident direction."

## The decision this issue exists to make

Two real, distinct fields carry the data `tags` was presumably meant to summarize:
`customTags` (operator-set) and `systemTags` (Defender-set). Collapsing them into one `tags`
attribute is a data-modeling choice, not a typo fix — decide whether to:
- emit two attributes (`custom_tags`, `system_tags`), or
- emit one combined `tags` reading the real fields, or
- drop the attribute entirely if nothing downstream needs it

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Decide the shape (see above) and implement it reading the real wire fields
- [ ] Update `TestLiveRecordCarriesNoWireTagsKey` (currently pins the absence — it should start
      failing once the fix lands, which is the point) and `TestMapIncidentAgainstLiveRecord`'s

body:
Found by a live capture during #165.

## The wire

`GET /auditLogs/directoryAudits` on m7kni, read as `graph2otel-poller`, **5/5 rows, no exceptions,
across 2 distinct apps** `[live-measured 2026-07-17, #165]`:

```json
"initiatedBy": {
  "app": {
    "appId": null,
    "displayName": "Intune Compliance Client Prod",
    "servicePrincipalId": "8ab73e2f-f11f-4bf3-a693-7a9d37bd5b49",
    "servicePrincipalName": null
  },
  "user": null
}
```

`appId` is null on every app-initiated record this project has ever captured. The only real
identifier present is `servicePrincipalId`.

## The mapper

`internal/collectors/entra/directoryaudits/directoryaudits.go:99`:

```go
setStr(attrs, "initiator_app_id", str(app, "appId"))
```

Maps a field that is structurally null on the wire. `servicePrincipalId` is unmapped.

## Impact

Every app-initiated directory audit ships with **no initiator identifier at all** — only a
display name (`initiator_app_display_name`), which is not unique and not a stable pivot key. A
SIEM query correlating a directory audit back to the calling service principal by id has nothing
to join on.

## Evidence this is not a one-off

Confirmed independently against the raw capture (not just the test fixture) — 5/5 rows, 2 apps
(`Azure AD Cloud Sync`, `Intune Compliance Client Prod`), `appId` null on all, `servicePrincipalId`
populated on the one row where the app is a first-party service principal rather than an
app-with-no-SP-record.

## Where this is recorded today

`internal/collectors/entra/directoryaudits/directoryaudits_test.go`:
`TestLiveDirectoryAuditAppInitiatorHasNoAppID` pins the wire fact independent of mapper behavior.
`TestMapDirectoryAuditAgainstLiveRecord`'s exact-key-set assertion documents `initiator_app_id`
as absent from the real record. Neither test fixes the mapper.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Map `servicePrincipalId` as a fallback identifier when `appId` is null — decide the
      attribute name (`initiator_app_id` reused for whichever is present, vs a distinct
      `initiator_service_principal_id`) against how #161's attribute registry wants to handle
      dual-identifier fields, since this shape (a null primary id + a populated SP id) may recur
      elsewhere in the tree
- [ ] Update `TestLiveDirectoryAuditAppInitiatorHasNoAppID` and
      `TestMapDirectoryAuditAgainstLiveRecord` to assert the new attribute is present
- [ ] Golden regenerated
- [ ] `make check` green

## Related, lower priority — also unmapped on this record, not filed as bugs here

`additionalDetails` (DeviceId/DeviceOSType/DeviceTrustType — same shape class as riskdetections'
additionalInfo, #153/#159's precedent), `operationType`, and `targetResources[].type/.id/
.userPrincipalName/.modifiedProperties`. These read as scope for a mapper-enrichment issue rather
than defects — flagging here so they aren't lost, not proposing them as this issue's scope.

New distinct attribute `initiator_service_principal_id` from `initiatedBy.app.servicePrincipalId`; `initiator_app_id` (appId, null on app-initiated records) left as-is per the maintainer decision — no overload.
