title: bug(entra): directoryaudits initiator_app_id maps a field that's always null on app-initiated records - servicePrincipalId is the real identifier

body:
Found by a live capture during #165. **Two stacked defects on one mapper block. Their combined effect: `entra.provisioning` has never emitted service-principal attribution from a real record, and never could.**

## The wire

`GET /auditLogs/provisioning` on m7kni, read as `graph2otel-poller`, **5/5 rows, no exceptions** `[live-measured 2026-07-17, #165]`:

```json
"servicePrincipal": {"displayName": "Grafana PS", "id": "e7e9d06f-8673-4759-bfed-67d499095d2f"}
```

Two apps across the sample (`Cloudflare`, `Grafana PS`), same shape both.

## Defect 1 — it is an object, not a collection

`internal/collectors/entra/provisioning/provisioning.go:114-118` states the assumption outright, and sources it to the docs:

```go
// servicePrincipal is a COLLECTION on provisioningObjectSummary (per the
// Graph resource doc), unlike the single-object sourceIdentity/
// targetIdentity; a provisioning job runs through exactly one service
// principal in practice, so the first entry is used.
if sp := firstNested(rec, "servicePrincipal"); sp != nil {
```

`firstNested` (`provisioning.go:147`) type-asserts `m[key].([]any)`. That assertion **fails on an object**, so `firstNested` returns `nil`, so the `if` never enters. Both attributes are skipped.

## Defect 2 — the name field is `displayName`, not `name`

```go
setStr(attrs, "service_principal_name", str(sp, "name"))
```

The object has no `name` key. So **fixing only the shape yields one attribute, not two** — `str(sp, "name")` returns `""` and `setStr` drops it. This is the trap worth naming: an obvious-looking shape-only fix looks like it works and silently still loses `service_principal_name`.

## Impact

`service_principal_id` and `service_principal_name` are **never emitted from any real record**. A SIEM query pivoting provisioning events by target app returns nothing, silently — the collector's own log twin cannot answer "which app did this sync run through".

## Why it tested green for the package's whole life

The old hand-written fixture encoded **both mistakes and asserted they mapped**:

```go
"servicePrincipal": []any{map[string]any{"id": "sp-guid", "name": "ServiceNow"}},
```

A fixture written from the docs cannot fail: it encodes the author's belief of the wire and then confirms it. This is #142's `"platform": "windows"` and #153's invented `riskType` — the **third** instance of the same class, which is exactly the argument of #165.

## Current state

`provisioning.go` is **untouched** — the defect is recorded, not fixed, so the fix gets its own reviewable change. The live capture landed in `provisioning_test.go` as `liveProvisioning` `[live-measured 2026-07-17, #165]`, and three tests now pin the wire facts mapper-independently:

- `TestLiveProvisioningServicePrincipalIsSingleObject` — asserts the wire shape, independent of mapper behavior
- `TestMapProvisioningAgainstLiveRecord` — exact attribute-set equality; its `wantKeys` documents the two absent attributes as a **recorded defect, not blessed behavior**
- `TestCollectorEmitsLiveRecordEndToEnd` — asserts both attributes absent at the emitter, with instructions to update all three sites when fixing

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `servicePrincipal` read as a single object (`nested`, not `firstNested`)
- [ ] bind `displayName`, not `name`
- [ ] `provisioning.go:114-118`'s docs-sourced comment replaced with the live-measured truth
- [ ] the three test sites above updated to assert the attributes are now PRESENT with the real values (`Grafana PS` / `e7e9d06f-…`)
- [ ] golden regenerated — expect 10 → 12 keys
- [ ] consider whether `firstNested` has any remaining caller; if not, remove it rather than leave a helper whose only use encoded a docs error
- [ ] `make check` green

## Note

`targetSystem.details.ServicePrincipalId` / `ServicePrincipalDisplayName` carry the same values as a fallback, if the top-level object ever proves inconsistent across tenants.

comments.body: Fixed in `b3f38e5` (on main). `servicePrincipal` is read as a single object via `nested` (was `firstNested`, which returned nil on an object) and bound to `displayName` (was `name`) — both defects, so service_principal_id/name had never emitted from a real record. `firstNested` removed (no remaining caller). Golden 10→12; `make check` green.

title: bug(entra): provisioning service-principal attribution has never emitted - servicePrincipal is an object, not a collection, and the name field is displayName

body:
Surfaced by #164's honest-golden pass (`c29ffb3`). The golden made it visible for the first time; it was invisible while the golden showed 2 of 9 attribute keys.

## What

`intune/enrollmentevents` parses each record's `id` and uses it **purely as the logpipeline dedupe key**. It never emits it. Verified:

```
$ rg -n 'setStr\(attrs, "id"' internal/collectors/intune/enrollmentevents/enrollmentevents.go
  (no emit site)
```

Every sibling window collector does emit it:

| collector | emits `id` |
| --- | --- |
| `intune/auditevents` | yes |
| `intune/autopilotevents` | yes |
| `entra/riskdetections` | yes |
| `entra/securityalerts` | yes |
| **`intune/enrollmentevents`** | **no** |

## Why it matters

graph2otel is a SIEM feed — CLAUDE.md's framing is that per-entity detail in logs is the whole point, and #112's rule is "metrics answer how many, logs answer which one". An enrollment-failure log that carries no record id cannot be pivoted back to its source record in Intune. An analyst reading the alert has the failure category and the device, and no handle on the underlying `troubleshootingEvent` to go and read.

It is also the cheapest possible fix: the value is **already parsed and in hand** for dedupe. This is one `setStr`.

## Not a cardinality problem

To pre-empt the reflex: this collector emits **logs only, no metrics**, so #112 is satisfied by construction. `id` on a log attribute is the design, not a violation — the rule is about which pipeline carries what, not about withholding data (#112/#114; the "PII guidance" misreading of it caused #110/#111 and a third recurrence on #100).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `intune.enrollment_failure` emits `id`
- [ ] Its golden (`testdata/signals.json`) covers it
- [ ] The existing pin added in `c29ffb3` — which asserts the CURRENT id-less behavior with a pointer here — is inverted rather than deleted, so the gap cannot silently return
- [ ] `make check` green

## Note on provenance

This package has **no live fixture** (#165) — its richest record is synthetic. That does not block this fix: `id` is a top-level field on `deviceManagementTroubleshootingEvent` that the collector already reads successfully for dedupe, so its presence on the wire is proven by the dedupe path working live. But do not treat the rest of that fixture as measured.

comments.body: Fixed in `00e8e6f` (on main). `intune.enrollment_failure` now emits `id` (one setStr; the value was already parsed for dedupe). The c29ffb3 pin was inverted, not deleted, so the id-less gap cannot silently return. Golden gained `id`; `make check` green.

title: bug(intune): intune.enrollment_failure logs carry no id - the one window collector that cannot be pivoted back to its source record

body:
Found by two independent lanes while fixing #164, then measured. **This is a different problem from #164 and cannot be fixed the same way.**

## The distinction that matters

- **#164** — the golden understates what the **mapper emits**. The mapper is fine; the test never drove the rich fixture into the emitter. Fixed by test wiring. `entra/graphactivity` 0 → 24, `entra/riskdetections` 4 → 23.
- **This issue** — the **fixture itself was never measured against the wire**. The mapper was written from Microsoft's documentation. No amount of test wiring fixes it: driving a docs-derived fixture end-to-end just goldens fiction more thoroughly.

A golden can be perfectly honest about what the mapper emits and still describe a shape Microsoft never sends.

## Evidence

`entra/provisioning` and `entra/directoryaudits`:
- Fixture values are Microsoft's own documentation placeholders: **`alice@contoso.com`** (`contoso.com` is literally the example domain in Microsoft's docs), `Bob User`, `corr-1`, `audit-1`, `src-guid`, `sp-guid`, `Alice Source`.
- `git log --all -S'provisioningObjectSummary'` returns exactly one commit — `d7814ce`, which created both packages. Nothing since added a live record.
- Neither carries the house `verbatim` / `pulled from the live` marker.
- `provisioning.go:115` says it outright: *"servicePrincipal is a COLLECTION on provisioningObjectSummary (**per the Graph resource doc**)"*.

`entra/securityalerts`, `entra/securityincidents`, `m365/unifiedaudit` — all hand-written (`tenant-guid-1`, `alert-1`, `inc-1`, `analyst@contoso.com`, `203.0.113.7` (TEST-NET-3), `priorityScore: 87`). `m365/unifiedaudit` is the interesting case: its **field names and crossed user-field semantics ARE live-verified** (500/500 on m7kni, #100/#151) — only the values are invented. So provenance is per-fact, not per-fixture.

Coarse tree-wide count (regex over each package's tests for live markers vs docs-shaped values — indicative, not exact):

| | packages |
| --- | ---: |
| claim a live fixture | 12 |
| only docs-shaped values | 16 |
| neither marker | 24 |
| **total with tests** | **52** |

The 12 is generous: it flags `entra/securityalerts`, which a lane then proved hand-written. So the real number is lower.

## Why this is the project's own rule being broken

CLAUDE.md, top-level:

> **Wire over docs.** Microsoft's documentation has been wrong on essentially every load-bearing detail on this project's path. Never assert API behavior from docs alone; measure, then record with a `live-measured` tag.

> mappers are written against live samples, never docs or hand-written fixtures (`"platform": "windows"` was never on the wire — #142).

#142 is precisely this bug, caught once. The ledger of times docs were wrong here is long: `additionalInfo` is a JSON-encoded string not an object; Graph v1.0 `riskDetection` has no `riskType`; the query API's `userId` field holds the classic UserKey; `tenantId` on an alert is ours not Microsoft's (#143). Every one was found by measuring.

**A hand-written fixture cannot fail.** It encodes the author's belief and then confirms it. `entra/riskdetections`'s test invented a `riskType` key that does not exist on v1.0, which kept a dead mapper line looking tested for the project's entire life (#153). That is not an anecdote — it is what this class of fixture does by construction.

## Why it matters now specifically

**#140 wants to generate `docs/collectors.md`'s signal columns from these goldens.** Publishing docs-derived attribute keys as a collector's *measured* signal surface would launder Microsoft's documentation into our own reference as if we had verified it — `"platform": "windows"` one level up, and wrong in the confident direction. #164 already says a doc wrong that way is worse than the prose it replaces.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Establish per-package fixture provenance and record it **in the fixture's doc comment**, not in an issue: `live-captured (date, #issue)` / `docs-derived` / `shape live-verified, values invented`
- [ ] Capture live records for the packages whose endpoints return data on m7kni — probe as `graph2otel-poller` only
- [x] ~~For endpoints that return nothing on this tenant (`entra/provisioning` needs SCIM app-provisioning configured; likely empty here)~~ **WRONG — corrected 2026-07-17.** `GET /auditLogs/provisioning` returned 66 rows on this tenant; SCIM provisioning is configured and active (Cloudflare, Grafana PS). `entra/provisioning` was fixed with a real live capture, not marked docs-derived — see the wave-1 comment below. The general principle ("empty on this tenant is a finding, not a failure") still holds for whichever packages turn out to actually be empty; it just didn't apply here.
- [ ] For endpoints that ARE genuinely empty on this tenant, say so explicitly and mark the package docs-derived rather than pretending. **"Empty on this tenant" is a finding, not a failure** — this is CLAUDE.md's "a green tick is not evidence of data" trap, and #129's synthesize-an-event workaround is the precedent. Candidates identified in the capture-inventory comment: `deviceManagementScripts`, `intents`, `ndesConnectors`, `userPfxCertificates`, `androidManagedAppProtections`, `iosManagedAppProtections`, `mdmWindowsInformationProtectionPolicies`, `targetedManagedAppConfigurations`, `identityGovernance/termsOfUse/agreements` — not yet tagged
- [x] `entra/directoryaudits` is the cheapest win — the tenant almost certainly has audit records. **Confirmed and done 2026-07-17**: 1045 live rows, fixture replaced, golden 5→10 keys (`e1c126b`)
- [ ] #140's doc generation must distinguish measured from docs-derived, or not claim measurement at all
- [ ] `make check` green

## Do not

Do not delete or "fix" a docs-derived fixture by inventing a better one. If no live record can be obtained, the honest outcome is a **tagged** docs-derived fixture and a collector whose mapper is known-unverified — not a fixture that looks measured.

## Related

- #164 — golden understates the mapper (test wiring). Different problem, already in progress.
- #142 — the same bug caught once, in one collector.
- #153 — the invented `riskType` key.
- #129 — synthesize a real event when the tenant will not produce one.

compliance-alert fired-event stream; Graph exposes only the notification templates; the

   (28KB/hour) have real content. Capture via Graph (no shape-equivalence question) and replace
   the docs-derived fixture. This was explicitly called out in #165 as "likely empty" — that
   premise is disproved.
2. **entra/directoryaudits** — Graph has 1045 rows, confirmed cheapest win as #165 predicted.
3. **entra/securityalerts, entra/securityincidents** — the live records were already pulled this
   session (5 rows each, 37/20 keys) but never applied to the fixtures. Highest-leverage,
   lowest-effort lane: the capture step is done, only the fixture-swap + provenance tag + golden
   regen remains.
4. **m365/unifiedaudit** — field names live-verified already; only values need real capture. Lower
   priority than the above since it's partially done.
5. **A wide swath of "empty" Intune endpoints are genuine tenant-shape findings**, not failures —
   record provenance as "docs-derived, endpoint confirmed empty on this tenant (2026-07-17)"
   rather than leaving them unmarked.
6. **Blob is the right source only for `graphactivity`** (no Graph equivalent, already done) and
   as a **cross-check**, not primary source, for directoryaudits/provisioning/signins where Graph
   itself has rich data with no shape-equivalence risk.

   collectors with nothing live on the wire *right now* (0 rows) — their goldens already reflect
   this session's ThinReasons-driven fixtures; leave as-is unless a fresher live event appears.

## Wave 1 landed — 5 packages, all `make check` green tree-wide, 4 real bugs found

## Wave 2 landed — 5 more packages, all `make check` green tree-wide

**Two process notes worth recording:**

title: test: most collector fixtures were written from Microsoft docs, not the wire - the project rule they violate is its own hardest-won one

body:
Found independently by two lanes during the 2026-07-17 parallel run, then measured across the tree. This is a defect in the #140 gate itself (`2bf2b37`), i.e. in the thing built to stop exactly this class of problem.

## What

`internal/signalcapture` goldens **the union of what a package's tests emit**. Its package doc is honest that this is a lower bound:

> The union is a LOWER BOUND on a collector's true signal surface: a code path no test exercises emits nothing here, so it cannot be judged.

The gap is far bigger than "lower bound" implies. Most collectors have a **rich live fixture that only ever reaches the mapper directly**, plus a **minimal synthetic fixture** that is the only thing driven through the engine into a Recorder. The golden captures the synthetic one.

Measured 2026-07-17 (attribute keys set by each package's non-test source vs keys present in its golden):

| missed | package | golden/source |
| ---: | --- | --- |
| 22 | `entra/graphactivity` | **0/22** |
| 15 | `intune/auditevents` | 4/18 |
| 12 | `intune/certificates` | 14/22 |
| 12 | `entra/provisioning` | 3/14 |
| 9 | `intune/malware` | 17/22 |
| 9 | `entra/directoryaudits` | 5/13 |
| 7 | `m365/unifiedaudit` | 5/11 |
| 7 | `intune/enrollmentevents` | 2/8 |
| 7 | `entra/securityalerts` | 6/12 |
| 6 | `intune/autopilotevents` | 3/8 |
| 6 | `entra/securityincidents` | 8/13 |

**12 of 51 packages understate.** `entra/graphactivity`'s golden is `"Logs": null` — it records **nothing at all** for a collector that sets 22 attributes.

(The counts are a `setStr|setBool|setNum|attrs[...]` regex over each package's source, so treat them as indicative ±1. The shape is not in doubt: `entra/riskdetections` was independently confirmed at 4 keys goldened vs 22 emitted, and driving its live record end-to-end took the golden to 23.)

## Why it matters

**1. It blocks #140's remaining acceptance criterion.** #140 still wants:

> - [ ] Signals columns in `docs/collectors.md` are generated from real emissions, not hand-maintained

Generating the doc from these goldens today would ship a reference that **understates `graph2otel`'s own signal surface by 18–22 attributes on a third of its collectors** — a doc that is wrong in the confident direction, which is worse than the hand-written prose it replaces. **#140 cannot close on the goldens as they stand.**

**2. It is the exact bug class the gate exists to prevent.** CLAUDE.md records #139/#100 as "a fourth registration path landed and the coverage test stayed green over a missing collector" — a gate reporting coverage it did not have. `2bf2b37` reproduced that shape one level down: the gate is green, and the artifact it produces is 18 attributes short of the truth.

**3. The drift half is weakened in proportion.** A golden that never saw an attribute cannot detect that attribute changing. `m365/unifiedaudit`'s golden covers `[id, ingest_transport, operation, record_type, service]` and **no user attribute** — so the `user_principal_name` → `user_id` rename (#163) would not have tripped its drift gate at all. Its twin `m365/activity` caught it. Same signal, same event name, opposite coverage.

## The fix, and the one already proven

`entra/riskdetections` (`c7864d6`) has the shape: `TestCollectorEmitsLiveRecordEndToEnd` drives the **live** record through `CollectWindow` into a Recorder. That both proves the fields survive the engine and makes the golden honest — 4 keys → 23.

Per package: drive the existing live fixture end-to-end. The fixtures are already in the tree; they are just not reaching the emitter.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every collector package drives its richest live fixture end-to-end into a Recorder, so its golden reflects its real surface
- [ ] `entra/graphactivity` (`"Logs": null`) is non-empty
- [ ] `m365/unifiedaudit`'s golden covers `user_key` and `user_id`
- [ ] A mechanical check that a golden is not trivially thin — e.g. fail when a package's golden has zero signals while its source sets attributes. Without this, the next collector regresses silently and the table above regrows
- [ ] `internal/signalcapture`'s package doc stops implying the lower bound is narrow, and states the real failure mode: a synthetic fixture, not an unexercised code path, is what usually truncates the golden
- [ ] Only then: #140's doc-generation AC
- [ ] `make check` green

## Do not

Do **not** "fix" this by having `signalcapture` read the mapper's source or reflect over the collector. The golden's one real guarantee is that it is produced FROM actual emissions, so it cannot describe a signal that does not exist. A static-analysis version would inherit exactly the credibility problem it exists to solve.

comments.body:
## My premise in the body above is WRONG for most packages. Correcting it before it hardens.

The body says:

> Most collectors have a **rich live fixture that only ever reaches the mapper directly**, plus a **minimal synthetic fixture** that is the only thing driven through the engine into a Recorder.

Two lanes independently found that false, then I measured it. For most of these packages **there is no live fixture at all** — the "rich" fixture is hand-written from Microsoft's documentation. `alice@contoso.com`, `Bob User`, `tenant-guid-1`, `203.0.113.7` (TEST-NET-3). `contoso.com` is Microsoft's own example domain.

That splits this issue in two, and only the first half is mine:

| class | problem | fixable by test wiring? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **A** | golden understates what the **mapper emits** — the live fixture never reached the emitter | **yes** — this issue |
| **B** | the **fixture was never measured against the wire**; the mapper encodes Microsoft's docs | **no** — needs a live capture → **#165** |

Class B is the more serious one and is now **#165**. Driving a docs-derived fixture end-to-end does not make it true; it goldens fiction more thoroughly. This issue stays scoped to class A.

## Landed so far

| package | golden before → after | class |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `entra/graphactivity` | **0 → 24** (`"Logs": null`!) | A — genuinely live blob record |
| `m365/unifiedaudit` | 5 → 12 | A (field names live-verified; values invented — #165) |
| `entra/securityalerts` | 6 → 13 | A (fixture hand-written — #165) |
| `entra/securityincidents` | 8 → 12 | A (fixture hand-written — #165) |
| `entra/riskdetections` | 4 → 23 (`c7864d6`) | A — live #129 Tor record |

**`m365/unifiedaudit`'s golden now covers `user_key` and `user_id`.** The #163 rename that would have slipped past its drift gate would now trip it.

## Deliberately NOT done — and this is the right call

`entra/provisioning` (3/14) and `entra/directoryaudits` (5/13) are **left understated**. Driving their synthetic fixtures end-to-end was mechanically trivial — ~20 minutes, would have taken them to ~15 and ~14 keys — and would have been **actively harmful**: it would publish 12 documentation-derived attribute keys as a collector's *measured* signal surface, straight into #140's doc generation. That is `"platform": "windows"` (#142) one level up.

An understated golden is a known gap. A confidently wrong one is #140's stated failure mode: *"wrong in the confident direction, which is worse than the hand-written prose it replaces."* **Leaving these two visibly thin is the honest state until #165 gives them real records.**

Same reasoning excluded `securityincidents`' `alert_ids`/`alert_count` (11 of 13 source keys, not 13): they only populate under `$expand=alerts`, which the collector never sends. Goldening them would make the golden **overstate** — the same credibility problem inverted.

## Two harness limits worth recording

1. **`telemetrytest.Recorder` cannot represent non-string log attributes.** It flattens via `log.Value.AsString()`, which returns `""` for any non-string Kind and logs `"AsString" "error"="invalid Kind"`. So `evidence_count` (int), `priority_score` (int), `tags` ([]string), `duration_ms`, and the geo floats are asserted for **presence** at the emitter and for **value** at the mapper. Production is correct (`telemetry.toLogKV` maps these properly); this is the test harness, and the `invalid Kind` noise in test output is that gap talking. Attribute KEYS still reach the golden correctly, which is what the golden records.
2. **`entra/graphactivity` remains 2 keys short by choice**: `user_id` and `scopes` are absent because the live record is an **app-only** call, which carries neither. The delegated shape is live-verified in aggregate (45 of 335 sampled records) but the only delegated *record* in the tree has an invented `userId`. Goldening it would buy 2 keys with a fabricated value.

## Corrected AC

- [x] `entra/graphactivity` (`"Logs": null`) is non-empty — **0 → 24**
- [x] `m365/unifiedaudit`'s golden covers `user_key` and `user_id`
- [ ] ~~Every collector package drives its richest live fixture end-to-end~~ → **only packages that HAVE a live fixture.** The rest are #165.
- [ ] A mechanical check that a golden is not trivially thin (in progress)
- [ ] `internal/signalcapture`'s package doc states the real failure mode
- [ ] Then #140's doc-generation AC — gated on **both** this and #165

## Class A is done — `1eb5124`, `c29ffb3`, `53fc618`. `make check` green.

### Goldens

| package | before → after |
| --- | --- |
| `entra/graphactivity` | **0 → 24** (was `"Logs": null`) |
| `intune/auditevents` | 4 → 19 |
| `entra/securityalerts` | 6 → 13 |
| `intune/autopilotevents` | 3 → 12 |
| `m365/unifiedaudit` | 5 → 12 |
| `entra/securityincidents` | 8 → 12 |
| `intune/enrollmentevents` | 2 → 9 |
| `entra/riskdetections` | 4 → 23 (`c7864d6`, earlier) |

### The mechanical check (`53fc618`)

`signalcapture.ThinReasons`, called from `Main` **before `Golden`** — so `-update` **refuses to write** a thin golden. That ordering is the substance: a thin golden is born in an `-update` run, and a check that flagged it afterwards would be arguing with a file that already looks like an accepted baseline.

Two rules: (1) zero signals captured; (2) a log carrying only framework-stamped keys (`ingest_transport`, `tenant_id`) — which closes rule 1's cheapest escape, since driving an *empty* record through an engine still gets it stamped, making the golden non-empty and still worthless.

**Two things deliberately not built.** This issue's AC suggested *"fail when a package's golden has zero signals **while its source sets attributes**"*. The source-regex half is dropped: a regex over the mapper is an **exemption mechanism** — a package whose emit style it fails to match is silently excused — which is #139/#100 verbatim. It is also unnecessary: the existing tree-walk already proves every collector package installs `Main`, so *`Main` running is itself* the "ought this to emit" signal.

The stronger rule "every signal must carry an attribute" was **measured before being generalized, and rejected**: 11 of 52 packages legitimately emit unlabeled metrics (`entra.secure_score.current`, `entra.organization.age_days`, `intune.devices.overview.enrolled_device_count`) — a tenant-wide total has nothing to break down by. It would have cried wolf on a fifth of the tree on day one. That is the `app_name` lesson: a false positive trains people to add exemptions, and an exempted gate is worse than none. Pinned by `TestBareMetricWithNoAttrKeysIsNotThin`.

**Honest limit, in the code:** it is a floor. It catches "nothing" and "nothing but stamps". It **cannot** catch 4-of-22 truncation — that needs to know what the mapper *could* emit, i.e. the static analysis this issue forbids. Above the floor, honesty stays a review duty.

### Package doc

The old "known limit" section blamed unexercised code paths and called the gap benign — *"fails in the safe direction… a coverage problem worth having anyway"*. **Both claims were wrong.** The cause is a rich fixture reaching only the mapper while a thin synthetic one is the only thing driven into a Recorder — the norm, not an exotic branch. And the two halves fail **differently**: the #112 cardinality half does fail safe; the #140 **drift half does not**. `m365/unifiedaudit` covered no user attribute, so #163's rename never tripped its gate while its twin caught it. A thin golden looks like a passing gate and is not one. That asymmetry is now the doc's headline.

### AC status

- [x] `entra/graphactivity` non-empty
- [x] `m365/unifiedaudit` covers `user_key` + `user_id`
- [x] A mechanical check that a golden is not trivially thin
- [x] `internal/signalcapture`'s package doc states the real failure mode
- [x] `make check` green
- [ ] ~~Every collector package drives its richest **live** fixture end-to-end~~ → **impossible as written; most packages have no live fixture. That is #165.**
- [ ] #140's doc-generation AC — gated on **#165**, not on this issue

### Left thin on purpose

`entra/provisioning` (3/14) and `entra/directoryaudits` (5/13). Driving their synthetic fixtures end-to-end was ~20 minutes and would have published 12 documentation-derived keys as a *measured* signal surface, straight into #140's doc generation. An understated golden is a known gap; a confidently wrong one is #140's stated failure mode. They stay visibly thin until #165 gives them real records. They pass `ThinReasons` because they are truncated, not empty — which is exactly the floor's documented limit, not a gap in it.

### Bug surfaced by the honest goldens

**#166** — `intune/enrollmentevents` emits no `id`; it parses one purely as a dedupe key. It is the only window collector missing it, so its logs cannot be pivoted back to their source record. Invisible while its golden showed 2 of 9 keys. Pinned, not silently fixed.

**Not** a bug, verified three ways: `intune/auditevents` still emits no `modifiedProperties` VALUES. The honest golden is now itself the evidence (19 keys, `modified_property_names`, nothing value-shaped), plus a new emitter-boundary guard that drives a secret-bearing certificate change through the whole engine and scans every attribute and body for the secret — strictly stronger than the old mapper-level test, which could not have seen a leak downstream — plus structurally: `oldValue`/`newValue` appear in `auditevents.go` only in comments, never in code.

This issue can close on class A. #165 carries the rest.

title: build: the signal goldens understate what 12 collectors emit - graphactivity records 0 of its 22 attributes

body:
Retroactive tracking issue: the work landed in the commit that closes this. Filing it so the tracker records the decision and its reasoning (#79 operating rule: nothing untracked).

## What

Both M365 audit signals (`m365.activity`, `m365.unified_audit` — both emit event name `m365.audit`) carried an attribute called `user_principal_name`. It holds the **classic O365 UserId** field, and live measurement shows only **~91% of values are UPN-shaped**. The rest are bare GUIDs, the literal `Not Available`, `ServicePrincipal_<guid>`, or a display name.

The name asserts a shape the value does not have. Anyone treating it as an email address is wrong ~9% of the time, silently.

## Decision (maintainer, 2026-07-17)

**Rename it to `user_id` on both signals.** End state per signal, exactly two user attributes:

| attribute | meaning | `m365.unified_audit` wire field | `m365.activity` wire field |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `user_key` | classic **UserKey** — opaque id | `userId` | `UserKey` |
| `user_id` | classic **UserId** | `userPrincipalName` | `UserId` |

## The trap this must not re-create

#151 (closed, 5ea620e) removed a **duplicate** `user_id` from `m365.activity`: `userID := str(rec,"UserId")` was setStrd to BOTH `user_id` and `user_principal_name` with no branch, so they were identical by construction on every tenant. This is **not** a revert of that — it renames the survivor. Three user attributes on a signal means the #151 mistake has been made again.

## The crossover that reads as a bug and is not

On `m365.unified_audit` the mapping looks inverted, deliberately: wire `userId` → attr `user_key`, wire `userPrincipalName` → attr `user_id`. The query APIs top-level `userId` field is a Microsoft misnomer whose content is the classic UserKey (live-verified 500/500 over one tenant and window, 2026-07-17). Both collectors map each field to what it **contains**, not to what it is **called**.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `user_principal_name` is gone from both signals; `user_id` present on both
- [ ] Exactly two user attributes per signal, pinned by a set-equality test (not a key-presence check)
- [ ] Per-package `testdata/signals.json` goldens regenerated
- [ ] `docs/signals.md`s M365 table states the truth, including the ~9% non-UPN shapes
- [ ] Breaking, pre-1.0 — noted for the #35 release checklist

## Scope note

`user_principal_name` legitimately still exists on other signals (`entra.signin`, `intune.managed_devices`, `entra.risk`, …) where the value genuinely is a UPN. This is about the two M365 audit signals only.
title: fix(m365)!: user_principal_name holds the classic UserId, which is only ~91% UPN-shaped - the name lies

body:
## What

graph2otel ships three dashboards. **None contains a single log panel.** Found while sweeping #143/#158.

The two domain dashboards are entirely PromQL. So the pipeline that carries the product's stated value — *"Used as a **SIEM feed**: per-entity detail in logs is the point"* (CLAUDE.md) — has no shipped surface, while the metrics that can only answer *"how many"* get two whole dashboards.

`docs/signals.md` states the split plainly:

> **Metrics answer "how many"; logs answer "which one".**

Today we ship the "how many" and leave "which one" as an exercise.

## Why this is worth more than a nice-to-have

**#90 makes the user's first attempt fail silently.** Log attributes are Loki **structured metadata**, not stream labels. Only `service_name` is a stream label, so the intuitive query:

```logql
{event_name="entra.signin"}     # matches ZERO rows, silently. Not an error.
```

…returns nothing, forever, with no indication anything is wrong. The correct form is:

```logql
{service_name="graph2otel"} | event_name=`entra.signin` | status_error_code!=`0`
```

`docs/signals.md` calls the wrong form *"the single most common way to get a rule that silently never fires"*. A shipped, correct log panel is worth more than the doc paragraph, because it is copy-pasteable and cannot be misread — and the doc has not been enough: the shipped **alert rules** and **74 dashboard queries** were both built on a false belief about labels (#143, #160).

## Candidates, in rough value order

Each pairs with an existing metric panel — the metric says how many, the panel below says which:

- **`entra.signin`** — failed sign-ins by `status_error_code`, with `user_principal_name` / `ip_address` / `location_country_or_region`. The `53004` case is what #129 used to prove Tor detection fires.
- **`entra.risk_detection`** — now carries `mitre_techniques` (#153). An ATT&CK-filtered panel (`mitre_techniques=~"T1090.*"`) is the highest-signal thing this project emits.
- **`intune.audit_event`** — who changed what, with `modifiedProperties` names.
- **`m365.audit`** — note `user_key` vs `user_principal_name` semantics (#151) and that the latter is only ~91% UPN-shaped.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] At least one shipped log panel per domain that has a log-shaped signal
- [ ] Every LogQL query uses the `{service_name="graph2otel"} | attr=…` form — a stream selector on an attribute is the bug this is partly meant to inoculate against (#90)
- [ ] Panels state which datasource they need (Loki), and degrade honestly when it is absent rather than looking broken
- [ ] Consider a text panel stating the metrics-vs-logs split and the structured-metadata trap in the dashboard itself, where someone writing their own query will actually read it

## ⚠️ Sequence after #143

**#143 has been decided: `tenant_id` is being added to domain signals.** Whether domain **logs** get it is explicitly called out there as a decision not to be made by accident. Build these panels after that lands, or they will need re-instrumenting exactly like the 74 PromQL queries did (#158).

## Do not

- Do not use `{event_name="…"}` as a stream selector. It matches nothing, silently (#90).
- Do not put per-entity data on a metric to make a panel easier — that is #112, and it is now gated (`internal/signalcapture`). The log twin already carries it.

Refs #90, #112, #143, #153, #158
title: feat(dashboards): zero log panels ship - the signal that answers 'which one' has no surface

body:
## What

Split out of **#141**, whose provenance half landed (`62c3850`) and is closed. This is the other half of that issue: the attribute-name registry. It is a different shape of change — mechanical, wide, low-risk — and it pairs with #140's capture work rather than with provenance.

## Verified (re-measured 2026-07-17; they had already drifted from #141's original counts, which is itself the argument)

| measure | #141 claimed | today |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `setStr(attrs, "literal", …)` call sites | 310 | **312** |
| distinct attribute-key literals | 198 | **199** |
| duplicate `func setStr` definitions (one per package) | 27 | **27** |
| attribute constants in `internal/semconv` | 3 | **4** (`AttrIngestTransport` landed with #141) |
| collectors using a shared constant for a **data** attribute | **0** | **0** |

## The drift this has already produced, all live in `main`

- **Aliased keys**: `m365/activity/activity.go` emits both `workload` and `service` from the same variable. Discoverable only by reading the file.
- **One key, two meanings**: `tenant_id` is *our* tenant on self-obs metrics (`semconv.AttrTenantID`) and *Microsoft's* tenant parsed from the payload at `entra/securityalerts/securityalerts.go:104` and `entra/securityincidents/securityincidents.go:147`.
- **`source` is overloaded three ways**: `intune/certificates/certificates.go:507` (`managed_device`), `:566` (`user_pfx`), and `entra/riskdetections/riskdetections.go:120` (Microsoft's own `source` field passed through). This is why #141's provenance attribute is `ingest_transport` and not `source`.

## ⚠️ This now collides with #143's decision — read that first

#143 has been decided: **`tenant_id` is being added to every domain metric**. That makes the `tenant_id` double-meaning above *worse*, not better: `securityalerts` / `securityincidents` already emit a `tenant_id` **log** attribute meaning Microsoft's tenant, and if domain signals gain our `tenant_id`, that key means two different things on those two signals.

**Sequence this with #143 deliberately.** Whichever lands second must not silently inherit the collision. Renaming the Microsoft one (e.g. `ms_tenant_id`, `alert_tenant_id`) is the obvious move and is cheap pre-1.0.

## What to build

1. **A registry of attribute-name constants** in `internal/semconv`, covering data attributes rather than only the 4 infrastructure ones.
2. **One `setStr` helper**, not 27.
3. **A gate on attribute-name drift** — at minimum: no duplicate/aliased keys, no key with two meanings. Pairs with #140, which gates *signal* names from the same captured data. Note #140's `internal/signalcapture` already captures **attribute keys per signal** (`testdata/signals.json`), so the raw material for this gate exists — asserting on attribute keys and on signal names are two assertions over one capture.
4. Resolve `workload`/`service` aliasing — or document it as intentional.
5. Disambiguate the two `tenant_id` meanings (see the #143 note above).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Data attribute names come from a registry of constants, not bare literals at 312 call sites
- [ ] The 27 duplicated `setStr` helpers are one helper
- [ ] `workload`/`service` aliasing at `activity.go` resolved or documented as intentional
- [ ] The two meanings of `tenant_id` are disambiguated, and the resolution is consistent with #143
- [ ] A test gates attribute-name drift (pairs with #140)
- [ ] `make check` green

## Do not

- Do not rename an attribute purely for tidiness. Every rename is a breaking change to someone's LogQL; pre-1.0 makes it cheap but not free, and the goldens (#140) make each one visible — use them as the review surface.
- Do not name anything `source` (three live meanings) and do not reuse `ingest_transport` (#141 owns it, log-only by decision).

Refs #141, #140, #143, #112

comments.body:
Done in `edf715d` (on main). Full migration landed.

**Registry:** `internal/semconv/attrs_{entra,intune,m365,purview,shared}.go` — one `Attr<PascalCase>` constant per attribute key (VALUE = the exact wire string), covering ~440 literal sites across 52 collector packages. The 27 byte-identical `func setStr` copies are gone, replaced by one exported `telemetry.SetStr` (+ `SetBool`/`SetNum`/`SetList`/`SetStrs`/`SetDurationSeconds`). Scope was larger than the plan's 377 — it also covered the 175 `telemetry.Attrs{}` metric-label literals + 42 direct `attrs[k]=` writes + a few keys passed indirectly through a helper param (`devices.boolSnapshot`) or an axis-struct field (`users`) that the seed extraction missed (`is_compliant`, `is_managed`, `account_enabled`, `on_premises_sync_enabled` — added).

**Pure symbol rename:** attribute VALUES unchanged, so every `testdata/signals.json` golden is byte-identical tree-wide (verified) — zero LogQL/dashboard/alert impact.

**Both gates, mutation-verified:**
- Gate A (`internal/semconv/attrs_registry_test.go`) — no two constants share a value, except the intentional `AttrWorkload`/`AttrService` alias.
- Gate B (`internal/semconv/attrs_bareliteral_gate_test.go`) — AST walk over the collectors; fails on any bare string attribute key in a `telemetry.SetX` call, a `telemetry.Attrs{}` literal, or an `attrs[...]` write. Confirmed it catches a reverted key and passes clean on the current tree. (Known limit: keys passed through a bespoke helper param aren't AST-detectable; the migration handled the few that exist.)

**Line items:** `workload`/`service` aliasing preserved + documented on the constants (`AttrWorkload`/`AttrService`, m365/activity sets both from one `Workload` value by design). The `tenant_id` double-meaning #141 flagged was already removed by #143 — grep confirms no payload-derived `tenant_id` line survives in securityalerts.go/securityincidents.go; `AttrTenantID` documents it is our tenant only. gosec G101 false-positives on the credential/token-named constants are excluded for `attrs_*.go` only.

`make check` green. Built via one seam-freeze pass + 6 disjoint per-domain migration lanes; every diff reviewed against the golden invariant.

title: refactor(telemetry): 199 attribute-name literals, 27 duplicate setStr helpers, and tenant_id means two things - build the registry

body:
## What

Found while sweeping #158. The dashboards were the symptom; **this is almost certainly the source.**

`alerts/README.md:37` states, flatly:

> Every metric carries a `tenant_id` label. Every rule groups `by (tenant_id, …)` … so a rule fires **per tenant**

**This is false.** `tenant_id` is on `graph2otel.*` self-obs signals ONLY — nothing injects it into domain metrics or domain logs. That is live-verified and #143 owns the decision. `docs/signals.md` and `CLAUDE.md` both say the opposite of this README.

A doc asserting a label that does not exist is how #158 happened: 74 dashboard queries were built against exactly this claim, and every one of them returned zero rows forever.

## The alert rules fail DIFFERENTLY from the dashboards — and worse

Six rules group domain metrics by a label they do not have: `graph2otel-alerts.yaml` lines **46, 117, 188, 259, 331, 402**. (Lines 474, 545, 617, 688 are self-obs rules and are correct.)

`sum by (tenant_id) (metric)` on a label-less metric does **not** return nothing. It collapses to a single group with `tenant_id` unset. So unlike the dashboards, **these rules still fire** — they just lie:

- `{{ $labels.tenant_id }}` renders **empty** in every summary and description (lines 99, 100, 170, 241, 242, 312, …), so every alert names a tenant it cannot name.
- `group_by: ["alertname","tenant_id"]` (`contactpoints.yaml:27`) separates nothing.
- **Worst — the ratio rules at 331 and 402 compute a wrong number, not a missing one:**

```promql
(sum by (tenant_id) (intune_compliance_devices{state="compliant"})
 / sum by (tenant_id) (intune_compliance_devices)) and sum by (tenant_id) (intune_compliance_devices) >= 5
```

On more than one tenant this **blends every tenant into one fleet-wide ratio** while claiming to be per-tenant. A missing panel is obvious; a plausible-looking compliance percentage that is silently an average across tenants is not. Harmless on a single tenant; wrong the moment a second one lands.

## The deeper question this exposes — do NOT fix it by adding the label

There is a real design consequence here that #143 should answer explicitly, and it is bigger than the alerts:

**Without `tenant_id`, two tenants' domain metrics are the same series.** Identical name, identical labels, no distinguishing dimension. They do not sum — they collide. So "multi-tenant from day one" (CLAUDE.md) is true of collection and *not* true of the domain metric data model as it stands.

That may be entirely intentional: per-tenant slicing lives in the logs, which carry the entity detail, and metrics are per-deployment aggregates. But the alerts and dashboards were both written believing otherwise, so the belief is load-bearing and undocumented. **Adding `tenant_id` to domain metrics is NOT the fix** — it reopens #143, changes every series in the project, and is a cardinality/cost decision, not an alert bug.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `alerts/README.md` states the truth: domain metrics carry no `tenant_id`; only `graph2otel.*` does
- [ ] The six domain rules no longer group by `tenant_id`, and their summaries/descriptions stop interpolating a label that is always empty
- [ ] The two ratio rules (331, 402) are correct — or explicitly documented as per-deployment, not per-tenant
- [ ] `contactpoints.yaml`'s `group_by` reviewed for the same assumption
- [ ] The multi-tenant domain-metric question above is answered on #143 (a sentence in `docs/signals.md` is enough if the answer is "metrics are per-deployment; slice tenants in the logs")
- [ ] `make check` green

## Do not

- Do not add `tenant_id` to domain metrics (#143, live-verified, deliberate).
- Do not assume the self-obs rules are broken too — they are correct and must keep their `tenant_id` grouping.

Refs #143, #158, #112

comments.body:
## CLOSED by `b0293c4` — but by the opposite of this issue's acceptance criteria. Recording why.

This issue's analysis was **correct on the facts and wrong on the fix**. Preserving both, because the facts are worth keeping and the fix would have caused damage.

### What this issue got right

- `alerts/README.md:37` was false. ✅
- The six domain rules (46, 117, 188, 259, 331, 402) grouped by a label their metrics did not have. ✅
- `sum by (tenant_id)` on a label-less metric **collapses to one unlabeled group and keeps firing** rather than returning nothing — so these failed differently, and worse, than the dashboards. ✅
- The ratio rules (331, 402) therefore computed a **wrong number, not a missing one**, silently blending tenants. ✅ This was the single strongest argument in the whole #143 decision.
- Lines 474/545/617/688 are self-obs and were always correct. ✅

### What it got wrong — its ACs are now REVERSED

> **Adding `tenant_id` to domain metrics is NOT the fix** — it reopens #143, changes every series in the project, and is a cardinality/cost decision, not an alert bug.

The maintainer decision on #143 (2026-07-17) chose exactly that. It is the fix. The reasoning: without the label, two tenants' domain metrics are not merely unsliceable — they are **the same series** (one MeterProvider, one resource, identical labels), so a multi-tenant deploy gets a meaningless number rather than a coarse one, while the project advertises multi-tenancy. And `tenant_id` grows with tenant COUNT (bounded, operator-chosen), not tenant SIZE, so #112 does not disqualify it.

So, explicitly, these three ACs are **struck** — doing them would have been the bug:

- ~~The six domain rules no longer group by `tenant_id`~~ → they **keep** grouping. They are now correct.
- ~~their summaries/descriptions stop interpolating a label that is always empty~~ → `{{ $labels.tenant_id }}` now renders. Kept.
- ~~The two ratio rules are correct — or explicitly documented as per-deployment~~ → they are now genuinely per-tenant. Kept.

**`graph2otel-alerts.yaml` and `graph2otel-contactpoints.yaml` are unchanged by the fix.** They were written for the post-#143 world and simply became true. `contactpoints.yaml:27`'s `group_by: ["alertname","tenant_id"]` now separates correctly.

### What actually changed

`alerts/README.md` only — it now states the truth, and records the "collapses to one unlabeled group and keeps firing" trap as history, since that is the non-obvious part worth keeping.

One precision the original claim lacked: a deployment that configures **no tenant id** stamps no label, and every `by (tenant_id)` rule collapses to a single unnamed group. That is correct for single-tenant (the group *is* the deployment) but means `{{ $labels.tenant_id }}` renders empty. Documented rather than left to be rediscovered.

### The lesson worth keeping

This issue and #158 were both filed against the *symptom* while #143 — open, with the same analysis in more detail — owned the *decision*. #158 was closed as a duplicate; this one reached the right diagnosis and prescribed the wrong treatment because it did not know a decision was pending. **Check for an owning decision issue before prescribing a fix to its symptom.**

title: bug(alerts): README claims every metric carries tenant_id (it does not) - and the compliance-ratio rules silently blend tenants into one wrong number

body:
## What

The live `riskDetection` record carries per-entity fields that the mapper reads past. Found while landing #153's MITRE work against a verbatim live record. `[live-measured 2026-07-17, #129/#153]`

| field | live value | why it matters |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `additionalInfo.userAgent` | `Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh…) … Firefox/140.0` | **strongest candidate.** The client string behind a risk detection is a first-order SIEM pivot, and `#153`'s parser already extracts `additionalInfo` pairs — this is roughly one line now |
| `tokenIssuerType` | `AzureAD` | distinguishes cloud vs federated issuance on a risk event |
| `userDisplayName` | (present) | the human-readable identity; every other entity signal carries one |
| `location.state` | `Noord-Holland` | `location_country_or_region` is already mapped; state is the next resolution down |
| `location.geoCoordinates` | lat/long | impossible-travel and geofencing rules want it |

## Why this is a bug, not a wishlist

#114's HARD rule: *"not a metric label" means LOG TWIN, never dropped.* A collector that fetches per-entity rows and keeps only some of them can answer "how many" and a bit of "which one", but not the question the operator actually has. These fields are already fetched — the records are on the wire and parsed — and then discarded at the mapper. That is the #110/#111/#114 shape, which this project has now paid for three times.

There is no cardinality argument against any of them: `entra/riskdetections` **emits no metrics at all**, so every field here is log-only by construction and #112 holds trivially.

## Why it was invisible

Same reason as everything else on #153: the risk collection is empty on a healthy tenant, so nobody had ever looked at a real record. It took #129 synthesizing a Tor sign-in to produce one. A green tick is not evidence of data.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `userAgent` emitted on `entra.risk_detection` (reuse `#153`'s `mitreTechniques` `additionalInfo` parser — it is the same `[{"Key","Value"}]` payload)
- [ ] Decide each of `tokenIssuerType`, `userDisplayName`, `location.state`, `location.geoCoordinates` — emit, or record why not. A field left out needs a reason that is not "awkward to model"
- [ ] Guard tests built from the archived live record, not hand-written fixtures
- [ ] `docs/signals.md` updated with any new attribute
- [ ] `make check` green

## Do not

- Do not assume `additionalInfo` is a JSON object. It is a JSON-encoded **string** holding `[{"Key","Value"}]` pairs — a mapper written to the intuitive shape parses nothing and reports success forever (#153).
- Do not put any of these on a metric label (#112). This collector has no metrics; keep it that way.
- Do not invent field shapes from Microsoft's docs. Every field above is quoted from a live record; anything else needs a live read first (#142).

Refs #153, #129, #114, #112
title: feat(entra): entra.risk_detections drops userAgent, tokenIssuerType, geo and display name - all on the wire, all high SIEM value

body:
## What

`dashboards/intune-fleet-overview.json:1778` queries:

```
intune_defender_product_status{tenant_id=~"$tenant"}
```

**`tenant_id` is never on a domain metric.** It is on `graph2otel.*` self-obs signals ONLY — live-verified, and #143 owns that design decision. Nothing injects it into domain metrics or domain logs; their labels are exactly what the collector passed.

So this panel matches zero series and renders empty, permanently. Not intermittently, not on some tenants — always.

## Why it matters more than one panel

CLAUDE.md names this exact mistake as a standing trap ("Do not filter domain-signal dashboards by `tenant_id` (returns no data, always)"), which means the shipped dashboard is currently demonstrating the trap it warns about. A user's first encounter with graph2otel's dashboards includes a panel that silently shows nothing, and the natural conclusion is "the collector is broken", not "the query has a label that does not exist".

An empty panel and a broken collector look identical from the dashboard. That is the failure mode this project keeps paying for.

## Found how

Noticed while fixing #150 (`intune.defender.product_status` is the metric in question). Outside that change's file boundary, so recorded rather than fixed.

## Scope — check the rest before fixing this one

This is unlikely to be the only instance. **Sweep every dashboard for `tenant_id` on a non-`graph2otel_*` metric** before closing, rather than fixing line 1778 and moving on.

## The real question this raises

If per-tenant dashboard filtering is a thing users will reasonably want, an empty panel is the symptom, not the disease — #143 decided domain signals carry no `tenant_id`, and that decision is live-verified and deliberate. Either:

- the dashboards drop the tenant filter (single-tenant deployments lose nothing; multi-tenant ones lose the ability to slice), or
- multi-tenant slicing needs a different mechanism, which is a #143 conversation and NOT something to reopen here without evidence.

Prefer the first unless someone brings a real multi-tenant need.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] No dashboard filters a domain metric by `tenant_id`
- [ ] Every dashboard swept, not just line 1778 — report the count found
- [ ] If a dashboard variable `$tenant` is now unused, remove it rather than leaving a control that does nothing
- [ ] `make check` green

## Do not

- Do not add `tenant_id` to domain metrics to make the query work. That reopens #143, whose decision is live-verified, and it would add a label to every series in the project — a cardinality and cost change, not a dashboard fix.

Refs #143, #150, #112
