body:
## What

`malwareSeverity` (`internal/collectors/intune/malware/malware.go:569`) logs at **Warn** unless `productStatus == "noStatus"`. The value a healthy device actually reports is **`noStatusFlagsSet`** ("Defender reported, nothing is wrong").

So every healthy device's log twin is emitted at Warn. **All 3 live m7kni Windows devices log at Warn today.** `[live-measured 2026-07-17, #150]`

## Why it matters

The severity is the field an operator alerts and filters on. A signal that is Warn on 100% of a healthy fleet is not a degraded signal — it is an inverted one: it trains its reader to ignore it, and then the one genuinely unhealthy device is indistinguishable from the noise.

It is also invisible from the metric side: `intune.defender.product_status` decodes `noStatusFlagsSet` correctly, so the dashboard looks right while every log line claims a problem.

## Likely cause

`noStatus` and `noStatusFlagsSet` are **both** real values in Microsoft's `windowsDefenderProductStatus` enum, and they mean nearly opposite things:

- `noStatus` — no status reported at all
- `noStatusFlagsSet` — status reported, and no problem flags are set (i.e. healthy)

The check almost certainly meant the second. Note `noStatus` is `docs-only`; `noStatusFlagsSet` is what the live wire sends (2^19, corroborated across both Defender transports).

## Found how

Fell out of #150's multi-flag decode work. Left unfixed there: in that change's file boundary but outside its acceptance criteria, and severity inversion is a distinct defect from the bitmask modelling error.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A healthy device (`noStatusFlagsSet`, no other flags) does NOT log at Warn
- [ ] Decide what SHOULD warn, from the flag set rather than a single scalar — productStatus is a bitmask (#150), so "healthy" is "no problem flags set", not "equals one magic string"
- [ ] `noStatus` (nothing reported) is handled deliberately — arguably its own severity, since "Defender said nothing" is different from both healthy and unhealthy
- [ ] Guard test built from the live values, not hand-written fixtures
- [ ] `make check` green

## Do not

- Do not just swap the string to `noStatusFlagsSet`. That repeats the scalar model #150 removed: a device can set several flags, so `noStatusFlagsSet` may not be the whole value. Decide severity from the decoded flag SET.

Refs #150, #142

comments.body:
## Two follow-up decisions from the fix (maintainer, 2026-07-17) — both confirmed, no code change needed

Recording so they are not re-litigated by a later reader who sees them as oversights.

**1. Scan backlog stays Info.** The live multi-flag device sets `quickScanOverdue: true` AND `noQuickScanHappenedForSpecifiedPeriod` together — one fact serialized twice, live-corroborated on dev-4. This collector already grades that boolean Info by an explicit reasoned decision ("routine backlog, not an active compromise indicator"). Warning on the flag while the identical boolean stays Info would give one state two severities depending on which field Defender happened to populate — the exact bug shape #150 removed. Warning would also put 1 of 3 live m7kni devices at permanent Warn, recreating in miniature the inversion this issue exists to fix. If it ever should warn, it changes on **both** sides together.

**2. The Error tier stays Error**, despite being `docs-only`. `threatRemediationFailedCritically` is the one enum value asserting *both* halves of the worst case — threat confirmed, remediation confirmed failed — which no protection boolean on the record can express. The asymmetry decided it: if the flag is real, a Warn buries an active infection next to a stale signature file; if the docs are wrong about it, the cost is an Error that never fires. Flagged as docs-only in the code so it is cheap to revisit under the evidence-class rule.

Still open as a genuine asymmetry, and NOT fixed here: **`signatureUpdateOverdue` (boolean) stays Info while `avSignaturesOutOfDate`/`asSignaturesOutOfDate` (flags) Warn.** Stale signatures are a real detection gap — materially different from a late scan — but the boolean half of the likely-identical fact is not in the Warn set. No live impact (all 3 live devices report only `noStatusFlagsSet`). Worth its own issue if you want the boolean side reconciled.

title: bug(intune): malware log twin warns on every healthy device - checks productStatus == "noStatus" but live healthy is "noStatusFlagsSet"

body:
## What

`intune.defender.product_status` (entity API, `intune/malware`) and `intune.defender_agents.product_status` (export API, `intune/defenderreport`) decode **the same Microsoft enum** into **the same snake_case label vocabulary**, so a device's state is queryable with one set of values regardless of which transport observed it.

**Nothing enforces that.** The two maps are unexported in different packages, and no test compares them.

## It has already drifted — found, not hypothesized

Discovered while fixing #150, by mechanically diffing the two vocabularies:

| transport | bit 24 / `windowsSModeSignaturesInUseOnNonWin10SInstall` |
| --- | --- |
| `intune/malware` (entity, names) | `windows_s_mode_signatures_in_use_on_non_win10s_install` |
| `intune/defenderreport` (export, bitmask) | `windows_s_mode_signatures_in_use_on_non_win10_s_install` |

One device setting that flag would have produced **two different label values depending on which transport saw it** — exactly what #150's AC2 forbids, live in `main`, independent of the multi-flag bug.

**#142's own comment claims its bit values were "carried over verbatim from the name-keyed map this replaced". That claim is false for bit 24** — verified against git history (`git show 3cac762:internal/collectors/intune/malware/malware.go` reads `non_win10s_install`; the commit's new `defenderreport` map reads `non_win10_s_install`). #142 introduced the split via a transcription slip, and nothing caught it because nothing compares the maps. `[live-measured 2026-07-17, #150]`

Converged onto the export spelling as part of #150 (the more mechanical snake_casing; neither is live-observed, so no query is known to break). **The root cause is untouched: the next edit can split them again, silently.**

## Why this is worth a gate rather than care

This is the #140 argument in miniature. A human found it by diffing two maps by hand. It is mechanically checkable and would have failed on the commit that introduced it.

Both maps are keyed differently on purpose — one by Microsoft's enum NAME (the entity endpoint serializes names), one by BIT POSITION (the export serializes an integer) — so the check is over their **value sets**, which must be identical.

## What to build

A test asserting the two vocabularies are value-set-identical. It needs a file outside either package (or an exported accessor from each), which is why #150 could not land it under one-file-one-owner.

Design notes:
- Compare the **value sets**, not the maps: the keys are legitimately different shapes.
- Bit 24 must be one test case with its history in a comment, so the specific slip cannot recur.
- Consider whether the vocabulary should live in ONE place both import, rather than two maps kept in sync by a test. A shared source makes drift impossible instead of merely detectable — that is strictly better if the two decode paths can agree on a representation.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A test fails when the two transports' productStatus vocabularies disagree
- [ ] Bit 24 is pinned explicitly, with the drift history recorded
- [ ] Decide: shared single source vs two maps + a drift test, with reasoning
- [ ] `make check` green

## Do not

- Do not "fix" this by deleting one map. The two transports genuinely serialize the enum differently (names vs bitmask); both decoders are needed.
- Do not assume the remaining 23 flags are corroborated. Only `noStatusFlagsSet` (2^19) and `noQuickScanHappenedForSpecifiedPeriod` (2^7) are live-verified across both wires (#142, #150). The rest are `docs-only`.

Refs #142, #150, #140

comments.body:
## DECISION (maintainer, 2026-07-17): **one shared vocabulary both packages import** — not two maps plus a drift test.

Closes the AC *"Decide: shared single source vs two maps + a drift test, with reasoning"*.

**Reasoning:** drift becomes *impossible* rather than merely *detectable*, and bit 24 is the proof that detection-after-the-fact is exactly what we don't have. A drift test is one deletion or one `t.Skip` away from silence, and it only ever fires *after* someone has already written the divergent value. Two sources of truth kept in sync by vigilance is what produced this bug.

**What is shared is the VALUE SET, not the decode.** The two transports genuinely serialize the same enum differently — the entity endpoint sends names, the export sends an integer bitmask — so both decoders stay. Only the snake_case vocabulary they decode *into* is shared. Do not collapse the two decode paths; that is a different (and wrong) change.

**Keep bit 24 as an explicit test case** with its history in a comment, per the ACs. The shared source makes the *class* impossible; the test case documents the specific slip so nobody reintroduces the spelling by hand.

Note the evidence asymmetry survives the refactor and must be preserved in comments: only `noStatusFlagsSet` (2^19) and `noQuickScanHappenedForSpecifiedPeriod` (2^7) are `live-measured` across both wires. The other 23 are `docs-only`.

title: build(intune): nothing enforces the shared productStatus vocabulary across the two Defender transports - bit 24 already drifted

body:
## What

`riskyUsers.isDeleted` returned **`false`** for a user that was definitively deleted. Split out of #153, whose other defects are fixable now — this one is **not**, because deciding it depends on a real-world event that has not happened yet (see Blocked, below).

`[live-measured 2026-07-17, #129]` — read AFTER deletion was confirmed two independent ways: a `404` on `/users/{id}`, and the user's presence in `/directory/deletedItems`:

```json
{"userPrincipalName": "risk-synth-DELETE-ME@m7kni.io",
 "isDeleted": false,
 "riskState": "atRisk"}
```

`isDeleted` is the one field that would let an operator separate live risk from residue, and it is wrong.

## Consequence

`entra.risk`'s gauge counts a deleted identity as at-risk, permanently. `GaugeSnapshot` is correct here — it drops series that leave the observed set (#110's design) — but **the series never leaves**, because Microsoft keeps returning the row. On a real tenant, every deleted-but-once-risky account inflates the gauge forever.

**Mapping `isDeleted` would not fix it and could make it worse:** an operator filtering `isDeleted=false` would believe they had excluded deleted users while including this one. A wrong field is more dangerous mapped than unmapped.

## BLOCKED until 2026-08-16 — and this is the whole reason it is a separate issue

Unknown: whether `isDeleted` flips to `true` after the **30-day soft-delete purge**. The user was soft-deleted `2026-07-17T10:25:12Z`, so the purge lands ~**2026-08-16**.

**Unblock condition (checkable, dated):** after **2026-08-16**, re-read `/identityProtection/riskyUsers` as `graph2otel-poller` and look for `risk-synth-DELETE-ME@m7kni.io`.

| outcome | meaning | likely fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| row is GONE | purge removes it; `isDeleted` was lag | document the ≤30d ghost window; probably no code change |
| row present, `isDeleted: true` | flips at purge; it was lag | map it, with the ≤30d caveat documented |
| row present, `isDeleted: false` | permanently wrong | reconcile against `/users`, or document the gauge over-counts |

**Do NOT design the fix before that check.** If it self-corrects at purge, the honest answer may be "document it" and the whole reconciliation design is wasted work. This is a `n=1` observation — one user, one tenant — so it does not get the armor of a measured fact until re-checked.

## Options, once unblocked

- **Leave unmapped** (status quo): the gauge over-counts silently. Cheapest, dishonest.
- **Reconcile risky users against `/users`** and drop ghosts: costs a lookup per risky user. Note #112 means the gauge only needs the COUNT — the log twin already carries the entity — so the reconciliation only has to correct a number, not enrich a record.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Re-checked after 2026-08-16 and the outcome recorded here with its evidence class
- [ ] Decision made on ghost handling for `entra.risk`'s gauge, with reasoning
- [ ] If mapped, the ≤30d ghost window is documented so nobody trusts `isDeleted=false`
- [ ] `make check` green

## Do not

- Do not map `isDeleted` as trustworthy on the strength of the field name. It is live-verified wrong at least once.
- Do not treat this `n=1` as a measured fact — one user, one tenant, one read.

Refs #153, #129, #110, #112

comments.body:
## Live re-probe 2026-07-19 (as `graph2otel-poller`, cert on camden) — Graph DOES report the deletion, just not via `isDeleted`

Probed the synth user `risk-synth-DELETE-ME@m7kni.io` (id `5289e9c7-3945-4ffd-8fd3-d56124baf45d`, soft-deleted `2026-07-17T10:25:12Z`) across three endpoints. The purge (~2026-08-16) has **not** happened yet, so this is the pre-purge state.

| signal | value | reliable indicator of deletion? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/identityProtection/riskyUsers` `.isDeleted` | **`false`** | ✗ — still wrong, ~2 days post-delete |
| `.riskState` / `.riskLevel` | `atRisk` / `high` | — (this is why it inflates the gauge) |
| `GET /users/{id}` | **404 `Request_ResourceNotFound`** | ✓ — the live directory no longer has it |
| `/directory/deletedItems/microsoft.graph.user` | **present**, `deletedDateTime: 2026-07-17T10:25:12Z` | ✓ — tombstone with the delete time |

`[live-measured 2026-07-19, #155, n=1]` — one user, one tenant, pre-purge.

### What this changes

**A reliable deletion signal exists TODAY** — the reconciliation option in the body ("Reconcile risky users against `/users` and drop ghosts") is viable now and does not have to wait for the purge. `/directory/deletedItems` is the cheaper form: one list call returns all tombstones with `deletedDateTime`, versus an N-way per-user existence check. `Directory.Read.All` (already in the poller's token, confirmed this probe) covers both `/users/{id}` and `/directory/deletedItems`.

**The bug is real and specific, not universal.** A second risky user on the tenant — `g2o-seed-test@m7knio.onmicrosoft.com`, `riskState: remediated`, `riskLevel: none` — reports `isDeleted: true`. So `isDeleted` is not globally stuck at `false`; it is wrong for *this* `atRisk`/`high` user, which is exactly the ghost class. Mapping `isDeleted` and filtering `false` would still let this one through — the body's "a wrong field is more dangerous mapped than unmapped" holds.

### The 2026-08-16 purge check is still the fix-selection gate

Two viable fixes now, and the purge outcome decides which is cheaper:
- **If `isDeleted` flips to `true` at purge** → the ghost self-clears within ≤30d and the honest answer may be "document the ≤30d window, no reconciliation" (map `isDeleted` only with the caveat, or leave unmapped). Cheapest.
- **If it stays `false` after purge** → reconcile the gauge against `/directory/deletedItems` (drop any risky user with a tombstone) — and this works regardless, so it's the safe fix if we don't want to wait the ~4 weeks.

Recommendation: still hold the fix for the 2026-08-16 re-check per the body — a reliable signal existing today does not change that the *simplest* fix depends on the purge behavior — but note that if we decide to move before then, `/directory/deletedItems` reconciliation is the build, and it's cheap (one call, corrects a count per #112). Acceptance-criteria box 1 (re-check after 2026-08-16) is unchanged.

## Fixed — `1df2370` (reconciliation, superseding the 2026-08-16 wait)

Maintainer decision (2026-07-19): build the `/directory/deletedItems` reconciliation now rather than wait for the purge re-check — it is correct regardless of whether `isDeleted` ever self-corrects, so the wait bought nothing.

**What shipped:**
- `entra.risk` fetches `/directory/deletedItems/microsoft.graph.user?$select=id` each cycle and **excludes tombstoned users from `entra_risky_users_total`** — the ghost is gone.
- The deleted user is **still emitted in the `entra.risky_user` log twin**, now carrying a **reliable `is_deleted=true`** sourced from the tombstone list (never `riskyUsers.isDeleted`, which lies). So `{service_name="graph2otel"} | event_name=`entra.risky_user` | is_deleted=`true`` answers "which deleted accounts is IPC still flagging" (#114 — entity kept, not dropped).
- `is_deleted` mirrors `is_processing`: a `*bool`, emitted only when the half was reconciled. The SP twin and the blob-sourced `entra.risky_users` twin (#135-C) pass nil and omit it.
- **Fail-open:** a failing deletedItems fetch → nil → every user counted (never drop a live user on a transient error), `is_deleted` omitted. Added `User.Read.All`.
- Because `entra.risk` keeps polling for its gauge even when #135-C suppresses its twin, the fix holds on camden (which runs the blob RiskyUsers twin): the **gauge is always reconciled**, independent of transport.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [x] Decision made on ghost handling, with reasoning (reconcile against deletedItems; keep the twin with a reliable marker)
- [x] `is_deleted` is documented as reconciliation-sourced, never the raw field (`docs/signals.md`, code comments)
- [x] `make check` green
- [x] ~~Re-checked after 2026-08-16~~ — superseded: reconciliation is correct regardless of the purge outcome, so the fix no longer depends on that check.

Tests: gauge excludes a tombstoned user; twin keeps it with `is_deleted=true`; live users get `is_deleted=false`; fail-open leaves the gauge intact and omits the attr. Signal golden regenerated (`entra.risky_user` gained `is_deleted`).

Live note: m7kni currently has the #129 synth user (`risk-synth-DELETE-ME`, deleted 2026-07-17) inflating the gauge — deploying this edge build to camden will visibly drop it from `entra_risky_users_total` and surface it in the twin with `is_deleted=true`, which is the live verification.

## Live-verified on camden — deployed `1df2370`, gauge reconciliation confirmed against production

Deployed `1df2370` to camden (image `ca378b1ec348`, Release run 29688709954 succeeded). `entra.risk` ran clean on the new binary: `transport=graph`, `last_success=true`, 129ms, no fail-open warning — so `fetchDeletedUserIDs` succeeded and the gauge is reconciled.

**Poller probe (cert-auth as `graph2otel-poller`, cross-referencing `/identityProtection/riskyUsers` vs `/directory/deletedItems/microsoft.graph.user`):**

| riskyUser | riskState | `isDeleted` field | in deletedItems | new gauge |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `g2o-seed-test@m7knio.onmicrosoft.com` | remediated | `true` (honest) | yes | excluded |
| `risk-synth-DELETE-ME@m7kni.io` (synth ghost) | atRisk | **`false`** (the lie) | yes | **excluded** |

- **OLD** `entra_risky_users_total` = **2** (both ghosts counted, inflating risk forever — the bug)
- **NEW** reconciled gauge = **0** (both tombstoned users excluded)

The synth ghost's `isDeleted` field is still `false` while `/users/{id}` = 404 and it is listed in `/directory/deletedItems` — i.e. the field lie is still live, and reconciliation is what corrects it. Confirms the fix works against real data, not only unit tests.

**Twin nuance (not a regression — by design, but worth recording):** on camden the per-entity `entra.risky_user` twin is owned by the **blob** collector (`entra.risky_users`, suppress-twin active per #135-C), and `internal/collectors/entra/risk/blob.go:104` deliberately passes `nil` for is_deleted (the append-only blob stream is not reconciled). So `is_deleted=true` on the twin is a **polled-twin-only** feature and is *not* surfaced on camden — a SIEM query over `entra.risky_user` twins on the production tenant cannot tell which risky user is deleted. The gauge fix (the headline) is fully live; the twin marking gap on blob-twin tenants will be folded into the broader deletedItems-coverage issue.

title: bug(entra): riskyUsers.isDeleted reports false for a deleted user - entra.risk's gauge counts ghosts forever

body:
## What

An opt-in switch that stops graph2otel exporting the records **its own polling generated**, so an operator's SIEM is not dominated by expected noise from the observer.

Filed from Rob's request, and separated from #152 deliberately: **#152 is the measurement + options; this is the build.** #152 stays as the evidence and cost record. This one owns the feature and gets its own lane.

## Why — measured, not suspected

`[live-measured 2026-07-17, #137 probe, recorded on #152]`

- **graph2otel is 59.9% of its own `MicrosoftGraphActivityLogs` volume** — 14,404 of 24,048 records carry the poller's own appId. Every Graph call a collector makes writes an MGAL record, which the blob path then pays to ingest and ships to Loki.
- Enabling a Graph-polled collector therefore **bills twice**: once for the poll, once for ingesting the MGAL record the poll created.
- Real blob cost is ~£3.07/mo, not the £0.85 in #89 (that figure was taken mid-backfill).

So this is both a **cost** lever and a **signal-quality** lever: today, any "who is calling Graph in this tenant" analysis is 60% graph2otel by volume. A dashboard of Graph API activity mostly shows the observer.

## Scope is wider than blob/MGAL — check before narrowing

`blob_ingest.exclude_self` (as floated in #152's options) is probably too narrow a name and too narrow a lever. The poller's exhaust plausibly lands in more than one signal:

- **`MicrosoftGraphActivityLogs`** (blob) — measured, 59.9%. The main one.
- **Service-principal sign-ins** — the poller acquires tokens, and each is a sign-in. Both `entra.signins.service_principal` (Graph-polled) and the `MicrosoftServicePrincipalSignInLogs` blob category would carry graph2otel's own sign-ins. **Not yet measured — measure before designing.** Note the related concentration already found: one Defender TVM scan-agent SP is 96.4% of `ServicePrincipalSignInLogs`, so that category is dominated by *some* robot regardless.
- **`m365.activity` / UAL** — unknown whether Graph calls surface. Measure.

**Do not assume the answer from the MGAL number.** Wire over docs, and measure each candidate signal as `graph2otel-poller` before deciding what the switch covers.

## Design constraints

1. **Default OFF.** graph2otel is a SIEM feed and per-entity detail is the point (#112). An audit trail of what the poller did is something a SIEM operator may actively want — "the observer's own calls" is exactly the kind of thing you want during an incident. Opting out must be the operator's choice.
2. **Identify self by appId, not by heuristic.** The tenant's configured `client_id` is already in `auth.TenantAuth`. A name-matching or UA-matching filter would be a guess.
3. **Multi-tenant correctness.** One deployment polls many tenants and may use a different client id per tenant, so "self" is per-tenant, not global. A single global appId list would silently under- or over-filter.
4. **HARD: dropping must be loud.** This project's standing rule is that "silently doing nothing" and "no data yet" must never look alike — it is the documented way this whole class of path gets misdiagnosed. A self-filter that drops 60% of a signal with no counter is an operator staring at a suspiciously quiet dashboard with no way to tell filtering from breakage. Emit a `graph2otel.*` counter of records dropped as self, per collector, so the drop is visible and alertable.
5. **Do NOT reuse `ingest_transport` for this** (#141). Provenance names the transport a record arrived by; "is this record about us" is an orthogonal axis. Conflating them makes both useless.
6. **`source` remains disqualified as a name** — it already has three live meanings (#141).

## Interaction worth noting

For a collector on `source: blob` (#144's mutual exclusion), its own polling exhaust disappears entirely — the blob lane makes no Graph calls. That is a real, currently unmodelled saving that makes blob more attractive than the published numbers show, and it partially overlaps what this feature buys. Worth quantifying alongside, so the two levers are not double-counted.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Measured, per candidate signal, what fraction is the poller's own exhaust (MGAL confirmed 59.9%; SP sign-ins and `m365.activity` unmeasured)
- [ ] An opt-in config key, default off, registered in the config registry (`docs/env-vars.md` is generated and drift-gated)
- [ ] "Self" resolved per-tenant from that tenant's client id, not a global list
- [ ] Filtered records are counted and exposed as a `graph2otel.*` self-obs metric, per collector — never a silent drop
- [ ] Docs state the cost model honestly: cost scales with **collector count**, not just tenant size, and the ~60% self-share is named so nobody misreads MGAL data
- [ ] `make check` green

## Do not

- Do not make it default-on, and do not filter without counting.
- Do not name it `source`, and do not overload `ingest_transport` (#141).
- Do not treat this as reopening #89's transport decision — re-checked at the measured volume, blob still wins (£3.07 < EH £8.32 < LA £10.88). Recorded on #152.

Refs #89, #100, #137, #141, #144, #152

comments.body:
## Blob-path build shipped in `ad92d56` (on main) — kept open for the cross-transport remainder

`blob_ingest.exclude_self` (default **off**, per-tenant) drops a blob record **iff** its actor `appId` equals that tenant's own poller `client_id` — self-only, every other appId passes through untouched. This kills the measured **59.9% MGAL self-exhaust** (#152) and the poller's own SP-sign-in blob records by the same match.

**Design points worth recording:**
- **'Self' resolution.** From `tenants[].client_id`, **falling back to `AZURE_CLIENT_ID`** (the env leg `DefaultAzureCredential` already uses). This matters: camden authenticates via env, not config `client_id`, so without the fallback the filter would have silently no-op'd on the exact production deployment it exists for. Per-tenant `client_id` still wins for a multi-app process; neither set → no-op **with a startup WARN**.
- **Loud, never silent.** `graph2otel.blob.self_excluded` counter (`_total` on the Prom side), labelled `collector`, per excluded record. `tenant_id` rides via `WithTenant` (#143).
- **appId path** = `properties.appId`, read via the same accessor the `graphactivity`/`signins` mappers use (one source of truth, tied to the live fixtures).
- Guard tests: self-authored **excluded**, third-party appId **not** excluded, default-off filters nothing, nil-extractor category never filters, empty-self never filters, env-fallback resolution. `make check` green.

### AC status
- [x] Opt-in config key, default off, registered (env-ref gate green — `exclude_self` is a tenant sub-key so it's file-only like `account_url`, zero flat-env diff by design)
- [x] 'Self' resolved per-tenant from the client id, not a global list
- [x] Filtered records counted as a `graph2otel.*` per-collector metric — never a silent drop
- [x] Docs state the cost model + the ~60% self-share (`docs/blob-ingest.md`)
- [x] `make check` green
- [ ] **Measured, per candidate signal** — MGAL confirmed 59.9%; **SP-sign-in / `m365.activity` self-share still unmeasured** (needs a `graph2otel-poller` blob/UAL probe — not runnable from an agent session)

### Remaining (why this stays open) — both need you, neither is a blocker
1. **Measure** the poller's self-share on the SP-sign-in categories and `m365.activity` (probe as `graph2otel-poller`). The blob SP-sign-in categories are already *covered* by the shipped filter; the measurement just quantifies the saving.
2. **Decide coverage** of the other transports: the Graph-polled `entra.signins.service_principal` and `m365.activity` (o365pipeline) carry the poller's own exhaust too but were left out of scope (different engines). If worth doing, that's a focused follow-up — say the word and I'll file it.

Happy to close now if you'd rather treat the blob-path lever as the deliverable and spin the cross-transport question into its own issue.

Closing: the blob-path self-exhaust lever is shipped, default-off, and covers the measured 59.9% MGAL leak (`ad92d56`). The cross-transport remainder (measure + decide the Graph-polled sign-ins and `m365.activity`) is now tracked in 176 — it needs a `graph2otel-poller` probe, so it gets its own home rather than holding this open.

body:
## Two risk-collector defects, both found the moment m7kni produced its first real risk event (#129)

Both invisible for the life of the project because the collections were always empty — the exact
failure mode #129 was created to expose. `[live-measured 2026-07-17, #129]`

## 1. `risk_type` is a dead mapper line on the Graph path

`internal/collectors/entra/riskdetections/riskdetections.go:115`:

```go
setStr(attrs, "risk_type", str(rec, "riskType"))
```

**The Graph v1.0 `riskDetection` resource has no `riskType` field.** The complete key set of the live
record, read off the wire:

```
activity, activityDateTime, additionalInfo, correlationId, detectedDateTime,
detectionTimingType, id, ipAddress, lastUpdatedDateTime, location, requestId,
riskDetail, riskEventType, riskLevel, riskState, source, tokenIssuerType,
userDisplayName, userId, userPrincipalName
```

Only `riskEventType` exists. `setStr` skips empty values by design (`riskdetections.go:169`), so
`risk_type` is **silently never emitted** — no error, no warning, a permanently green collector. Same
shape as #126's `displayName`/`name` trap.

**The blob path is not identical.** The `UserRiskEvents` blob record carries **both** `riskType` and
`riskEventType` (same value, `anonymizedIPAddress`):

| | `risk_type` |
| --- | --- |
| Graph (`entra.risk_detections`) | never emitted |
| blob (`UserRiskEvents`) | `anonymizedIPAddress` |

So risk records are **not** byte-identical across transports, unlike sign-ins. That is load-bearing
for #141 (provenance) and #138 (dedupe), both of which reason from the sign-in case.

**Decision needed:** drop the line, or keep it as a knowingly blob-only attribute and document the
divergence.

## 2. `riskyUsers.isDeleted` reports `false` for a user that is definitively deleted

Read **after** deletion was confirmed by a 404 on `/users/{id}` and the user's presence in
`/directory/deletedItems`:

```json
{"userPrincipalName": "risk-synth-DELETE-ME@m7kni.io",
 "isDeleted": false,
 "riskState": "atRisk"}
```

`isDeleted` is the one field that would let an operator separate live risk from residue, and it is
wrong.

**Consequence:** `entra.risk`'s gauge keeps counting a deleted identity as at-risk. `GaugeSnapshot` is
correct here — it drops series that leave the observed set (#110's design) — but the series never
leaves, because Microsoft keeps returning the row. On a real tenant every deleted-but-once-risky
account inflates the gauge permanently.

**Mapping `isDeleted` would not fix it and could make it worse**: an operator filtering
`isDeleted=false` would believe they had excluded deleted users while including this one.

Unknown: whether it flips to `true` after the 30-day soft-delete purge. **Cheap re-check after
2026-08-16** decides whether this is a lag or permanent. Do not design the fix before that check —
if it self-corrects at purge, the honest answer may be "document it".

Options: leave unmapped (status quo; gauge over-counts silently), or reconcile risky users against
`/users` and drop ghosts (a lookup per risky user; note #112 means the gauge only needs the count,
since the log twin already carries the entity).

## Also found, not yet filed separately

- **`isProcessing` unmapped** on `entra.risk` — present on the wire.
- **MITRE technique data is dropped on both paths.** `additionalInfo` carries
  `mitreTechniques: T1090.003,T1078`; the blob promotes it to a first-class `mitreTechniqueId`.
  `T1090.003` is Multi-hop Proxy — i.e. it named the Tor sign-in correctly. High SIEM value, currently
  discarded.
- **`riskLevel` disagrees across endpoints for one event**: `riskDetections` said `medium`,
  `riskyUsers` said `low`, ~7 minutes apart, same detection. So `entra.risk_detections` and
  `entra.risk` will report different severities for the same incident. Not a graph2otel bug —
  Microsoft aggregates user risk differently from detection risk — but it reads as an inconsistency on
  a dashboard and belongs in `docs/signals.md`.

## ⚠️ Before anyone maps the `UserRiskEvents` blob category

Its envelope `time` is **`"7/17/2026 10:09:47 AM"`** — US-format, non-ISO, no timezone. An ISO parser
bound to `time` fails on **100%** of records, and per the emitter's contract (*a record with no
parseable event time must be dropped, never stamped on arrival*) that would **silently discard every
risk event**. It would be invisible, because risk categories are *expected* to be near-empty — the
same blindness this issue documents. **Bind to `properties.activityDateTime`** (proper ISO-8601
inside `properties`). Note also the blob's precision is 3dp vs Graph's 7dp, so the two paths cannot be
joined on an exact timestamp, and `Level` is `"Information"`, not `"Informational"`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `risk_type` resolved — dropped, or kept blob-only and documented as a transport divergence
- [ ] Guard test built from the **live** record (archived), not a hand-written fixture
- [ ] `isDeleted` re-checked after 2026-08-16 (post-purge) and the finding recorded before any fix
- [ ] Decide the ghost-risky-user handling for `entra.risk`'s gauge
- [ ] MITRE technique mapping decided (drop deliberately, or emit)
- [ ] `riskLevel` cross-endpoint disagreement documented in `docs/signals.md`
- [ ] `make check` green

Refs #129, #126, #110, #113, #141, #138

comments.body:
## Three of four resolved in 57ac365; `isDeleted` split to #155

`make check` green. The fourth item is not deferred-with-a-rationale — it is blocked on a dated, checkable event, which is why it moved rather than lingered here.

| item | resolution |
| --- | --- |
| `risk_type` | **dropped** |
| `isProcessing` | **mapped** (`is_processing`, `*bool`) |
| MITRE techniques | **emitted** (`mitre_techniques`) |
| `isDeleted` / ghost gauge | **split to #155**, blocked until 2026-08-16 |
| `riskLevel` disagreement | documented in `docs/signals.md` |

### `risk_type`: dropped, not kept blob-only

The premise was re-confirmed live today (`g2o-probe` still had the #129 synthetic event): 20 keys, no `riskType`. Reasoning for drop over blob-only:

1. **Nothing is lost** — the blob's `riskType` duplicates `riskEventType` (both `anonymizedIPAddress`), and `risk_event_type` already ships that value.
2. **The blob path does not exist.** Only `signins` and `graphactivity` have blob collectors; there is no `UserRiskEvents` mapper anywhere. "Blob-only" would keep a line that *cannot* fire — 100% dead, not merely dead-so-far.
3. **A blob-only attribute would be a second, undeclared provenance channel.** Its mere *presence* would signal the transport, and #141 landed a real key for that (`ingest_transport`, 62c3850). Worse, any `risk_type=…` SIEM rule would silently match one transport while looking like it matched both — the #90-class silent-subset trap.
4. **The shared-mapper precedent does not transfer.** `signins` shares `mapSignIn` *because* its blob `properties` object IS the Graph resource field-for-field. That is explicitly untrue here — which is this issue's own load-bearing point for #141/#138.

### The real defect was the TEST, not the mapper

Worth recording, because it is the more useful finding. Removing the dead line is behaviorally **inert** on live data — `setStr` already skipped it, so there was no red test for the deletion itself and none is claimed.

`riskdetections_test.go:34` **invented a `riskType` key** and asserted `risk_type` off it. A fabricated fixture made a dead line look tested for the life of the project. That is #142's lesson (`"platform": "windows"` was never on the wire) recurring one layer up — in the thing meant to catch it. The fixture is now a verbatim live record, which is also what surfaced the trap below.

### The wire trap the issue body could not have told us

The body prints `additionalInfo`'s *content* but not its *shape*. It is **not an object** — it is a JSON-encoded **string** holding `[{"Key","Value"}]` pairs:

```
"additionalInfo": "[{\"Key\":\"userAgent\",\"Value\":\"Mozilla/5.0 …\"},
                    {\"Key\":\"mitreTechniques\",\"Value\":\"T1090.003,T1078\"}]"
```

A mapper written to the intuitive `{"mitreTechniques": "..."}` shape compiles, runs, finds nothing, and reports success forever — invisible, because the collection is empty on a healthy tenant anyway. Exactly the blindness this issue documents. `[live-measured 2026-07-17, #153]`

### `is_processing` is a `*bool`, deliberately

`riskyEntity` decodes **both** halves and `riskyServicePrincipal` has no such field, so a plain `bool` would report every service principal as "not processing" — graph2otel asserting a fact Microsoft never stated. `nil` = absent = no attribute. Emitted including `false`, unlike the string attrs, because `false` is an answer ("this risk state is settled") and omitting it would break the *useful* filter.

### Still open here

- [ ] `risk_type` resolved — **done** (dropped)
- [ ] Guard test from the live record — **done** (verbatim, archived in-test)
- [ ] `isDeleted` re-checked after 2026-08-16 — **moved to #155**
- [ ] Ghost-risky-user gauge handling — **moved to #155** (depends on the above)
- [ ] MITRE mapping decided — **done** (emit)
- [ ] `riskLevel` disagreement in `docs/signals.md` — **done**
- [ ] `make check` green — **done**

Everything in scope is landed. Closing depends only on #155, so this issue stays open only if you want it as the parent; otherwise #155 carries it and this can close.

### Found but not done — filing separately rather than gold-plating

The live records show more per-entity data dropped on `entra.risk_detections`, which #114's hard rule arguably makes bugs: `additionalInfo.userAgent` (`Mozilla/5.0 … Firefox/140.0` — strongest candidate, ~1 line given the parser now exists), `tokenIssuerType`, `userDisplayName`, `location.state`, `location.geoCoordinates`.

Closing. Everything in scope landed in `57ac365`; the only remaining item (`isDeleted` / the ghost-gauge question) is blocked on a real-world event — the 2026-08-16 soft-delete purge — and lives in **#155** with a dated, checkable unblock condition.

Keeping this open as a parent would just be a second place to look: #155 is self-contained and carries the full context. The `risk_type` / MITRE / `is_processing` decisions and their reasoning are in the comment above and in the code at the exact spot someone would try to undo them.

New work found while doing this, filed rather than gold-plated: **#159** (`userAgent`, `tokenIssuerType`, geo and display name all on the wire and dropped).

body:
## What

**graph2otel's own polling generates 59.9% of the MGAL blob volume graph2otel then pays to ingest.**

Live-measured 2026-07-17 as `graph2otel-poller`: **14,404 of 24,048** `MicrosoftGraphActivityLogs`
records carry the poller's own appId. Every Graph call a collector makes writes an MGAL record, which
the blob path then bills to ingest.

So enabling a Graph-polled collector **bills twice**: once for the poll, once for ingesting the MGAL
record the poll created. Nothing in #89, `docs/blob-ingest.md`, or the cost model anticipates this.

`[live-measured 2026-07-17, #137 probe]`

## The cost figure is ~4x the documented one

| | documented (#89) | measured 2026-07-17 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| appends/hour | 247 | **935–1,032** |
| monthly cost | £0.85 | **~£3.07–3.40** |

The £0.85 figure is `live-measured (2026-07-16, #89)` and was honest when taken — it was measured
**during the backfill window**, before steady state. It should be updated rather than treated as
wrong-in-kind.

## This does NOT reopen #89's transport decision — checked, not assumed

Blob is priced on **write operations**; Log Analytics on **GB ingested**. Higher measured volume
therefore **widens** blob's margin rather than narrowing it. Re-ranked at the measured volume:

```
blob £3.07   <   Event Hub £8.32   <   Log Analytics £10.88
```

#89 holds. Recording the check so nobody re-opens it on seeing the 4x.

## Why it still matters

1. **The cost model is non-linear in a way the docs imply it is not.** Cost scales with *collector
   count*, not just tenant size — each new Graph-polled collector adds its own MGAL exhaust to the
   blob bill. A 20-collector tenant and a 60-collector tenant of the same size cost differently.
2. **It distorts the MGAL signal itself.** Any analysis of "who is calling Graph in this tenant" is
   60% graph2otel by volume. A dashboard of Graph API activity mostly shows the observer.
3. **It interacts with #144's mutual exclusion.** For a collector on `source: blob`, its own polling
   exhaust disappears — which is a real, unmodelled saving that makes blob more attractive than the
   current numbers show.
4. **A second concentration exists**: one Defender TVM scan-agent SP is **96.4%** of
   `ServicePrincipalSignInLogs`. Same shape — a single principal dominating a category — worth knowing
   before anyone sizes that category from a small sample.

## Options (no recommendation yet — needs a decision)

- **Filter MGAL on ingest**: drop records whose appId is the poller's. Cheapest, and arguably correct
  — self-observability is `graph2otel.*`'s job, and it already measures its own Graph calls. But it
  discards an audit trail of what the poller did, which a SIEM operator may actively want.
- **Keep and document**: update `docs/blob-ingest.md`'s cost model to say cost scales with collector
  count, and state the ~60% self-share so nobody misreads the MGAL data.
- **Make it configurable**: `blob_ingest.exclude_self` or similar.

Doing nothing is defensible at £3/mo on this tenant; it is not obviously defensible at 10x the
collectors or a larger tenant, and the docs currently give an operator no way to predict it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Decide filter / keep / configurable, with reasoning recorded
- [ ] `docs/blob-ingest.md`'s cost model updated: the measured steady-state figure, and that cost
      scales with collector count rather than tenant size alone
- [ ] The £0.85 figure re-tagged with the caveat that it was measured mid-backfill
- [ ] The self-share is documented so MGAL analyses are not misread
- [ ] If filtering, a guard test that a poller-authored MGAL record is excluded and a third-party one
      is not

Refs #89, #137, #135, #144

comments.body:
Closed by `7728619` (on main). Cost model corrected in `docs/blob-ingest.md`: steady-state ~£3.07/mo, the £0.85 re-tagged as mid-backfill, and the **59.9% self-share** documented so MGAL 'who is calling Graph' analyses aren't misread. Transport decision re-checked at the measured volume and holds more strongly (blob £3.07 < EH £8.32 < LA £10.88) — #89 not reopened.

**Decision (filter / keep / configurable): configurable, default-off.** The build is #154's — an opt-in self-exhaust exclusion keyed per-tenant on the poller's own appId, with a loud self-obs drop counter (never a silent drop). #152 stays the evidence/cost record; the guard test lands with the feature on #154.

body:
## What

`user_id` carries **different data depending on transport**, for the same underlying event.

Live-verified on **500/500 records** over the same tenant and window, as `graph2otel-poller`,
read-only `[live-measured 2026-07-17, #100]`:

| signal | `user_id` | `user_principal_name` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `m365.unified_audit` (query API) | the classic **`UserKey`** | classic `UserId` |
| `m365.activity` (Management API) | the classic **`UserId`** | classic `UserId` |

The query API's top-level `userId` is **not** the classic schema's `UserId` — it is `UserKey`. Its
`userPrincipalName` is the classic `UserId` (byte-identical, 500/500, sentinels and all).

So an operator querying `user_id` gets a different kind of identifier depending on which collector
produced the row, with nothing in the record saying so.

## Why it was not fixed when found

Both attributes are **already shipped on both signals**. Converging them is a breaking change to one
transport or the other:

- Re-point `m365.activity`'s `user_id` at `UserKey` → matches the twin, breaks anyone using it today.
- Re-point `m365.unified_audit`'s `user_id` at the classic `UserId` → matches the name, breaks its
  existing consumers, and duplicates `user_principal_name`.
- Drop `user_id` from one → cleanest semantically, most disruptive.
- Rename one (e.g. `user_key`) → honest, still a breaking change to the attribute set.

That is a product decision, not a cleanup. Recorded as a `KNOWN DIVERGENCE` comment in `mapRecord`
rather than silently re-pointed.

## Why it matters

This is the exact fork `m365/activity`'s package doc exists to prevent — the two signals are supposed
to be twins over the same underlying audit data, differing in transport and latency, not in meaning.
An attribute that silently changes semantics across transports is the failure mode #141's provenance
work is about: without `ingest_transport` on the record, an operator cannot even tell which meaning
they are looking at.

Note `user_key` **is** already emitted on `m365.activity` (from the classic `UserKey`), so that signal
carries both identifiers under distinct names. The divergence is one-sided.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Decide the convergence, with the reasoning recorded here (rename / re-point / drop)
- [ ] Both signals' `user_id` mean the same thing, or the differing one is renamed to say what it is
- [ ] `docs/signals.md` states the meaning explicitly
- [ ] Guard test pinning the semantics per transport, built from the live samples
- [ ] If it is a breaking change, note it for the v1.0 cut (#35) — pre-1.0 is the cheap moment
- [ ] `make check` green

Refs #100, #141
title: bug(m365): user_id means UserKey on m365.unified_audit and UserId on m365.activity - one attribute, two semantics

body:
## What

`intune.malware` emits `intune.defender.product_status{status}` from the **entity** API
(`GET managedDevices/{id}/windowsProtectionState`). That form serializes Defender's `ProductStatus`
enum as **names** rather than the raw bitmask #142 fixed on the export path — but for a device with
**more than one flag set** it returns a **comma-separated list**:

```
DESKTOP-CB3D9AB -> 'noQuickScanHappenedForSpecifiedPeriod,noStatusFlagsSet'
```

`normalizeProductStatus` is an **exact-match lookup**, so that string matches nothing and buckets to
~~`other`~~ **`unknown`** — CORRECTED 2026-07-17: the catch-all was named `unknown` (`malware.go:180` returned `"unknown"`), not `other`. The defect is exactly as described; only the bucket's name in this body was wrong. AC3 below is corrected to match.

**Live right now on m7kni: 1 of 3 Windows devices.** `[live-measured 2026-07-17, #142 audit]`

## Why this is separate from #142

#142 fixed the **export** path (`intune.defender_agents`), where `ProductStatus` arrives as a raw
integer bitmask with no `_loc` sibling. This is the **entity** path, where the same underlying enum
arrives as names. Same modelling error — treating a **set of independent flags** as a single scalar
value — via a different transport and a different serialization.

**This one is harder to notice than #142's**, which is why it is worth its own issue rather than a
footnote. #142's failure was total: 100% of the fleet bucketed to `other`, so the metric was
obviously useless. Here, **single-flag devices decode correctly**. The metric looks healthy and is
right for most devices; only multi-flag devices — precisely the ones with more than one thing wrong,
i.e. the ones worth alerting on — silently fall into `other`. A partial failure that correlates with
severity is worse than a total one.

## Discovered how

Found while cross-checking #142's bitmask decode against a second transport. The entity form was used
as the corroborating source for bits 19 and 7 (it agreed device-for-device with the export's
integers), and the comma-separated value fell out of that comparison. Left unfixed there because
`internal/collectors/intune/malware/malware.go` was outside that change's file ownership.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `intune.defender.product_status` decodes multi-flag values — split on `,`, emit one point per
      flag, matching the shape #142 landed on the export path (a bitmask is a set of independent
      booleans, not a partition)
- [ ] Reconcile the label vocabulary with `intune.defender_agents` so the two transports agree: the
      entity form gives camelCase names (`noQuickScanHappenedForSpecifiedPeriod`), the export form
      gives integers decoded to snake_case (`no_quick_scan_happened_for_specified_period`). **The same
      device state must not produce two different label values depending on transport.**
- [x] An unrecognised flag becomes `unknown_<name>`, never a catch-all (~~`other`~~ — the catch-all here was `unknown`; see the correction above) — a catch-all is what hid both
      instances of this bug
- [ ] Guard test built from the **live** value `'noQuickScanHappenedForSpecifiedPeriod,noStatusFlagsSet'`,
      not a hand-written fixture (#142's whole lesson)
- [ ] Check whether the metric description needs the same correction #142 made — points may sum to
      more than fleet size
- [ ] `make check` green

## Do not

- Do not "fix" this by mapping the comma-joined string as a single new label value. That preserves the
  scalar model and the cardinality grows combinatorially with flag count.
- Do not assume the entity form's name list matches the export form's bit ordering without checking —
  #142 corroborated bits 19 and 7 across both, and nothing else.

Refs #142
title: bug(intune): intune.malware buckets multi-flag productStatus to "other" - same modelling error as #142, second transport, live on 1 of 3 Windows devices

body:
## What

graph2otel's setup docs cover Entra app registration + Graph scope grants. They do **not** cover the
second half that some collectors need: registering the poller's service principal with a **non-Graph
data plane** via Security & Compliance PowerShell. An operator following the current docs and granting
`eDiscovery.Read.All` gets a scope in their token that does nothing, a 401, and no path forward.

Proven end to end on m7kni today (#102 / #148): the Graph half alone leaves
`security/cases/ediscoveryCases` at **401**; the Purview half moves it to **200**.

## Why this needs writing down rather than linking

Microsoft documents this ([Set up app-only access for Purview eDiscovery](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/security-ediscovery-appauthsetup),
Step 4), but every load-bearing detail around it was wrong or missing in practice, and each one cost
real time here:

- **The `-ObjectId` is the enterprise-app OBJECT id, not the appId.** Microsoft calls this out because
  using the appId is the common mistake. Ours: appId `2c92ce28-…` vs object id `13371536-…`. Resolve
  it with `GET /servicePrincipals(appId='<appId>')` and read `.id`.
- **"Connect-IPPSSession is Windows-only" is not the operative constraint.** Live-measured
  2026-07-17: app-only `Connect-IPPSSession` NullRefs **identically** on Windows Server (PS 5.1, EXO
  3.10.0, cert in store) and macOS (pwsh 7.6.3, EXO 3.10.0, pfx). `-Verbose` shows the token
  acquiring successfully, then a NullRef in `NewEXOModule.ProcessRecord()`. A Windows VM does not fix
  it.
- **A delegated device-code token is the path that works** — and since `New-ServicePrincipal` is
  itself an S&C cmdlet, bootstrapping app-only access appears to *require* a delegated session. The
  docs do not say this.
- **The device-code client matters.** `a0c73c16-a7e3-4564-9a95-2bdf47383716` (Microsoft Exchange
  Online Remote PowerShell) returns `AADSTS7000112: Application is disabled`.
  `fb78d390-0c51-40cd-8e17-fdbfab77341b` (Microsoft Exchange REST API Based Powershell) works, with
  scope `https://ps.compliance.protection.outlook.com/.default`.
- **The ≤24h compliance-RBAC replication lag did not apply.** The re-probe returned 200 on the first
  attempt immediately after the cmdlets. Operators should not be told to wait a day.
- **The error code is the tell, and it is the whole diagnostic.** A **403** on a Purview endpoint
  usually means a missing Graph scope (#126 — granting it returned 200). A **401 with the scope
  already in the token** means a non-Graph data plane does not know the principal, and no amount of
  Graph scope will move it (#102). Both were observed in the same tenant in the same session. This
  distinction is the single most useful thing a reader can take away, and it is written down nowhere.

## Scope

- A `docs/` page (name TBD — `docs/data-plane-registration.md`?) covering: when it is needed, which
  collectors need it, the object-id-not-appId trap, the delegated-token requirement + working client
  id, the exact cmdlets, and the re-probe that verifies it.
- The **401-vs-403 decision rule** as the diagnostic entry point.
- Cross-link from the eDiscovery collector's row in the generated `docs/collectors.md` if a
  per-collector note is possible, and from `README.md`'s setup path.
- Audit whether any **other** shipped or planned collector sits behind a non-Graph data plane with the
  same two-half setup. Purview retention labels are a known permanent gap (Application: Not
  supported) and should be named as *not* fixable this way, so a reader does not try.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Doc exists covering the two-half model, with the object-id trap called out explicitly
- [ ] The delegated-token requirement is stated, with the working device-code client id and scope
- [ ] The 401-vs-403 decision rule is written down as the diagnostic entry point
- [ ] Every claim carries its evidence class (`live-measured (date, #issue)` / `docs-only`)
- [ ] Any other non-Graph-data-plane collector is identified, or the audit's absence of findings is
      recorded
- [ ] Known-unfixable cases (Purview retention labels) are named as such
- [ ] Linked from the setup path so an operator hits it before granting `eDiscovery.Read.All`
- [ ] `make check` green (CLAUDE.md 350-line gate — detail goes in `docs/`, not CLAUDE.md)

## Do not

- Do not claim app-only `Connect-IPPSSession` works — it does not on this tenant, measured on both
  operating systems. If a reader's does, that is a finding to fold in, not the documented default.
- Do not tell operators to wait 24h for replication by default. It was instant here; make the wait
  the fallback, not the instruction.
- Do not copy Microsoft's page. Its Step 4 is correct but omits every trap above.

Refs #102, #148, #126

title: docs: how operators register their own poller app for eDiscovery (and any other non-Graph data plane needing S&C PowerShell)

body:
## What this is

The four maintainer-only tenant actions on the v1 gate list, batched so Rob can clear every human bottleneck in one sitting. Each action below is copy-paste ready, says what it unblocks, and names the verification an agent runs afterwards. **The build work stays tracked on the underlying issues** (#102, #129, #106, #100) — this issue closes when the four actions are done and verified, and its closing comment records which succeeded.

Agents: do NOT perform these; all four mutate the tenant. When one lands, run its verification step and post the result on the underlying issue.

## 1. Purview eDiscovery — S&C PowerShell registration (unblocks #102)

Graph half is done (`eDiscovery.Read.All` granted, in token). The Purview data plane has never heard of the principal — this registers it (Microsoft's documented Step 4; note the **object** ID, not appId, in the role-group cmdlets — using appId is the documented common mistake):

```powershell
Install-Module ExchangeOnlineManagement
Import-Module ExchangeOnlineManagement
Connect-IPPSSession

New-ServicePrincipal -AppId "2c92ce28-126c-47c1-82b0-410b64502989" `
                     -ObjectId "13371536-9950-4988-90f4-343566456781" `
                     -DisplayName "graph2otel-poller"
Get-ServicePrincipal

Add-RoleGroupMember -Identity "eDiscoveryManager" -Member "13371536-9950-4988-90f4-343566456781"
Get-RoleGroupMember -Identity "eDiscoveryManager"

Add-eDiscoveryCaseAdmin -User "13371536-9950-4988-90f4-343566456781"
Get-eDiscoveryCaseAdmin
```

**Agent verification:** `g2o-probe security/cases/ediscoveryCases` → expect 200 (was 401). If it still 401s with the role group in place, #102 closes as a genuine app-only block and the scope gets removed (per #102's final comment).

- [ ] PowerShell registration run
- [ ] Re-probe result posted on #102

## 2. Defender streaming API export → storage account (unblocks #106)

In the Defender portal: **Settings → Microsoft Defender XDR → Streaming API → Add**:

- Name: `graph2otel`
- Destination: **Azure Storage account** → `graph2otelm7kni` (RG `auditlogs`, sub `intuney`, uksouth) — the same account the Entra categories already land in.
- Event types (the #106 table set): `DeviceFileEvents`, `DeviceProcessEvents`, `DeviceNetworkEvents`, `DeviceLogonEvents`, `IdentityLogonEvents`, `EmailEvents`, `CloudAppEvents`, `UrlClickEvents`, `AlertInfo`, `AlertEvidence`.

Streaming is push — it consumes none of the tenant-wide advanced-hunting CPU quota. Azure creates `insights-logs-*` containers on **first write**, and first data can take up to 24h — a missing container on day one is not a fault (`docs/blob-ingest.md`).

**Agent verification:** list containers on `graph2otelm7kni` as the poller; record which Defender containers exist + a sample blob path on #106 (Defender's layout needs its own verification before mappers are written — do not assume the Entra `tenantId=` prefix).

- [x] Streaming API setting created
- [ ] Container/layout observation posted on #106

## 3. Throwaway user + synthetic risk detection (unblocks #129, then #133's verification)

Per #129's body (read it first — it has the full trigger menu and licensing caveat):

1. Confirm m7kni has **Entra ID P2** (risk detections are not evaluated without it — without P2 this can never land and #129 needs re-scoping instead).
2. Create a clearly-disposable user (e.g. `risk-synth-DELETE-ME@…`), no roles, no licences beyond what P2 evaluation needs.
3. Sign in as that user **over Tor** (historically the most dependable trigger: "anonymous IP address"). Fallback: two sign-ins from distant VPN exits inside a short window ("impossible travel").
4. Risk evaluation is **asynchronous** — minutes to hours. Do not conclude failure early.
5. **Delete the user afterwards** and confirm deletion (it is a standing risk-flagged identity otherwise). Deletion happens after the agent's verification pass, not before.

**Agent verification:** a row appears at `/identityProtection/riskDetections`; then the full #129 AC list (field-by-field mapping check on `entra.risk_detections` + the `entra.risk` gauge/log twin; blob `UserRiskEvents` comparison if enabled).

- [x] P2 confirmed
- [x] User created + risky sign-in performed
- [ ] Agent verification complete, findings on #129
- [ ] User deleted, deletion confirmed

## 4. Deliberate DLP match (unblocks #100's last unverified content type)

`DLP.All` is subscribed and live-verified at the subscription level, but zero DLP content rows have ever been observed — the sensitive-data payload shape is unverified.

1. Check an active DLP policy exists (Purview portal → Data loss prevention → Policies). If none: create a test policy matching credit-card numbers, scoped to SharePoint/Exchange, low-impact mode is fine — detection is what matters, not enforcement.
2. Trigger a match: e.g. share/email a file containing a standard test pattern (`4111 1111 1111 1111` with a name and expiry nearby helps classifiers).
3. Matches surface in the O365 feed asynchronously (UAL latency 30min–24h).

**Agent verification:** a `DLP.All` content blob appears in the collector's window; inspect the record for the sensitive-data payload shape and record on #100 whether SIT detail is present (the exact residual question its body carries).

- [ ] DLP policy confirmed/created
- [ ] Match triggered
- [ ] Payload shape recorded on #100

## Done when

All four verifications are posted on their underlying issues. Close this with a comment listing the four outcomes (including any that failed — a failed unblock is a finding, not a gap in the record).

body:
## What

`jobpipeline`'s in-flight job adoption (#118, `4ab4523`) cannot adopt across a restart when the checkpoint is **cold** (first deploy, or a wiped checkpoint dir): `CoversWindow` requires `WindowFrom` equality with the persisted window, and a cold checkpoint has no persisted window to match — so a restart mid-job on first deploy still orphans the server-side job and re-creates it against APIs that 429 hard (a live audit query ran >10 min; the collector polls every 30 min).

This was discovered during #118's live verification and its closing comment says it was "filed separately" — it never was (found during the #146 audit). This issue is that filing.

## Severity

Wasted calls + 429 pressure on job-creating APIs, **not** data loss (`scheduler.go` holds the watermark on failure; the window walk is lossless).

## Acceptance

- [ ] A restart with a cold checkpoint while a server-side job is in flight adopts the job instead of re-creating it (or a documented decision that cold-start adoption is out of scope, with the reasoning on this issue).
- [ ] Regression test proving the adopt-vs-recreate behaviour on a cold checkpoint.
- [ ] `make check` green.

Evidence class: live-measured behaviour on camden (#118's verification round, 2026-07-16).
title: fix(jobpipeline): cold checkpoint cannot adopt an in-flight async job — restart on first deploy still orphans and re-creates

## Why

Coding-agent sessions on this repo have been degrading: agents assert stale verdicts, re-litigate settled topics, or obey instructions that reality has overtaken. A full audit (all 144 issues + every comment + the session transcripts + CLAUDE.md history) found the causes:

1. **Bodies and titles rot while comments stay honest.** #100's title says "do not build" about a collector that shipped default-on. #131's body argues the opposite of its closing verdict. #106's newest comment says "do not start the consumer yet" about a consumer live in production. #79 (the designated resumption point) went badly stale twice in 48h: lists closed issues as open gates, omits the entire blob program and every issue ≥ #119, still records #100 as "won't-do".
2. **Wrong verdicts get the same do-not-redo armor as live-measured facts.** #109/#100/#130's wrong verdicts were protected from re-checking by the very rules meant to prevent re-derivation. Entries need evidence tags (live-measured vs docs-only vs n=1).
3. **CLAUDE.md grew 160 → 701 lines in two days** into a chronological palimpsest of correction chains ("X was WRONG… the correction was itself wrong"), and now contradicts #79 (msgraph-sdk vs raw REST) and docs/blob-ingest.md (which still presents #131's retracted dual-ship model as live design in 3 places).
4. **A known bug is tracked nowhere**: #118's close says the cold-checkpoint adoption gap was "filed separately" — it never was.
5. **docs/signals.md:89 + registry.go:40 assert the false tenant_id claim** (#143's subject) — the doc line itself needs the false claim removed even while #143's design decision stays open.

## Plan / acceptance

- [ ] #79 body rewritten: mission + decisions + operating rules + a *grouping* of the open set; stops enumerating per-issue state it cannot keep current; honest-scope section corrected per #126/#130; #100 reversal recorded. Interim-state comments folded + deleted.
- [ ] #35 Gate 0 becomes a pointer to #79 (one place can rot, not two); Gate 1 kept verbatim.
- [ ] Stale-body issues rewritten (+retitled where the title is wrong): #85, #86, #100, #106, #126, #128, #129, #135; #119 gains the Management-API route paragraph; #116/#137/#138 get one-line currency notes.
- [ ] Closed-issue entry points fixed: #89 (body banner + final-state comment + strike-note on the mutual-exclusion "correction" comment), #131 (body banner), #109 (final-state comment), #99 (label-encryption bullet struck).
- [ ] #130 closed (CLAUDE.md correction already shipped; GSA out of scope until a GSA tenant exists).
- [ ] Missing follow-up from #118 filed (cold-checkpoint job adoption).
- [ ] No-value / superseded-after-folding comments deleted (minimal set; correction chains preserved).
- [ ] docs/blob-ingest.md dual-ship references corrected to the #131 closing verdict; docs/signals.md tenant_id claim corrected; registry.go:40 comment fixed.
- [ ] CLAUDE.md restructured: ~current-truth rules organized by topic, evidence tags on do-not-redo entries, deep API lore moved to docs/graph-api-gotchas.md + docs/o365-management-api.md + expanded docs/blob-ingest.md, each with a topic-triggered pointer left in CLAUDE.md. No fact lost — moved, not deleted.
- [ ] `make check` green; committed straight to main.

## Standing rules this adds (recorded in #79 + CLAUDE.md)

- When a comment reverses a body claim, edit the body the same day (strikethrough + pointer is enough).
- Any "do not X yet" instruction must name its unblock condition.
- Every do-not-redo entry carries its evidence class: live-measured (date, #issue) / docs-only / n=1.
