body:
## The trigger

A live Cloud Discovery pipeline (OPNsense/Zenarmor flows → MDCA Generic CEF, uploaded hourly by an
n8n workflow through the [Cloud Discovery API](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-cloud-apps/api-discovery))
ran **red for roughly a day while reporting green**. Every hourly `done_upload` returned
`200 {"success": true}`. Every parse then failed server-side. Zero transactions landed. Nothing in
the uploader, and nothing in graph2otel, could see it — the discovery dashboard just quietly stayed
empty.

It surfaced only by opening the MDCA governance log by hand and reading `Parse Cloud Discovery log`
rows.

Measured live on the m7kni tenant (2026-07-17), last 40 governance records:

| `status.templateMessage.template` | count |
| --- | --- |
| `REPOOPER_COMPLETION_STATUS_BASELOGPARSER_UNEXPECTED_FORMAT` | 22 |
| `REPOOPER_COMPLETION_STATUS_BASELOGPARSER_PARSED_LOG_FILE_ALL_RELEVANT` | 18 |

The 22 failures were a real outage (a malformed CEF line format, since fixed). The point of this
issue is not that bug — it is that **22 consecutive silent failures produced no signal anywhere**,
and today still would.

## Verified: upload success and parse success are different stages

The Cloud Discovery upload is three calls: `GET /api/v1/discovery/upload_url/` → `PUT` to the
returned Azure SAS blob → `POST /api/v1/discovery/done_upload/`.

`done_upload` returning `200 {"success":true,"inputStreamId":"…","taskId":"…"}` means **the blob
landed and a parse task was queued**. That is all. The parse runs asynchronously ~50s later
(measured: task `created` → `updateTimestamp` ≈ 50s), and its verdict is written *only* to the
governance log.

So every uploader is structurally blind to parse outcome — this is not an n8n deficiency. A
`DiscoveryParseLogTask` is the only place the truth exists, and nothing polls it. Retries on the
upload call cannot help: the upload did not fail.

## Verified: the signal is machine-readable, not just English

`POST /api/v1/governance/` with `{"limit": N, "skip": N}` returns the task records. Shape (redacted,
one real success and one real failure):

```jsonc
{
  "taskName": "DiscoveryParseLogTask",
  "type": "discoveryParseLog",
  "logType": 179,
  "logTypeName": "GENERIC_CEF",
  "inputStreamId": "<stream id>",
  "fileSize": 7243318,
  "created": "2026-07-17T00:00:29.127Z",
  "timestamp": 1784242829127,
  "updateTimestamp": 1784242879644,
  "logData": { "typeText": "GENERIC_CEF", "fileName": "<tenant>_<ts>_GENERIC_CEF_<name>.log", "uploader": "<upn>" },
  "status": {
    "isSuccess": true,
    "statusMessage": "6.9 MB of data were successfully parsed from GENERIC_CEF - 21,559 transactions were found in 70 cloud apps.",
    "templateMessage": {
      "template": "REPOOPER_COMPLETION_STATUS_BASELOGPARSER_PARSED_LOG_FILE_ALL_RELEVANT",
      "parameters": { "dataSource": "GENERIC_CEF", "logSizeStr": "6.9 MB", "transactionsCount": 21559, "cloudServicesCount": 70 }
    },
    "shouldRetry": false
  }
}
```

```jsonc
"status": {
  "isSuccess": false,
  "statusMessage": "Log format does not match the expected format for GENERIC_CEF.",
  "templateMessage": {
    "template": "REPOOPER_COMPLETION_STATUS_BASELOGPARSER_UNEXPECTED_FORMAT",
    "parameters": { "dataSource": "GENERIC_CEF", "logSizeStr": "4 KB" }
  },
  "shouldRetry": false
}
```

This matters for the collector design:

- `status.templateMessage.template` is a **stable enum key**. Alert on it; never regex
  `statusMessage`, which is localized prose with embedded numbers.
- `templateMessage.parameters` carries `transactionsCount` and `cloudServicesCount` as **numbers
  already** — no parsing of "21,559 transactions were found in 70 cloud apps" required.
- `status` is absent/empty while the task is queued, so "pending" is a real third state, not a
  failure. A collector must not treat a missing `status` as `isSuccess:false`.
- `isSuccess` and the template key are redundant but both present; the template distinguishes
  *which* failure, which `isSuccess` cannot.

The documented governance-log error vocabulary is in
[Troubleshooting cloud discovery](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-cloud-apps/troubleshooting-cloud-discovery)
(`Unsupported file type`, `The log format doesn't match`, `Transactions are more than 90 days old`,
`No transactions to cataloged cloud apps`, `Unsupported log type`). Each of those is a distinct
template key and a distinct operational meaning — `No transactions to cataloged cloud apps` in
particular is a parse *success* that still means "your data is worthless", which is exactly the
class of failure a boolean cannot express.

## Verified: server-side filtering is mostly a trap

Tested live against `POST /api/v1/governance/`:

| filter | result |
| --- | --- |
| `{"timestamp": {"gte": <ms>}}` | **works** — `total` 50 → 22 |
| `{"skip": N}` paging | works |
| `{"taskName": {"eq": ["DiscoveryParseLogTask"]}}` | **silently returns 0 records** — no error |
| `{"status.isSuccess": {"eq": [false]}}` | **silently returns 0 records** — no error |
| `{"type": {"eq": ["discoveryParseLog"]}}` | returns `total: 0` |

So an unsupported filter is not rejected — it returns an empty set that is indistinguishable from
"nothing happened". A collector that filters server-side on `taskName` would report *permanent
silence* and look exactly like a healthy-but-quiet tenant. This is the same failure mode as the bug
that prompted the issue.

**Consequence for the design:** watermark server-side on `timestamp` `gte` (the one filter that
works); filter `taskName` / `status` **client-side**. Add a test that asserts the client-side path,
so nobody "optimizes" it into a server-side filter later.

## Why this cannot be a Graph collector — and why `o365activityclient` is the template

MDCA Cloud Discovery is not on Graph. There is no Graph equivalent for either the log-upload
endpoints or the governance log; the legacy portal API is the only surface.

| | Graph collectors | this |
| --- | --- | --- |
| base URL | `graph.microsoft.com` (pinned, `graphclient/client.go:40`) | `https://<tenant>.<region>.portal.cloudappsecurity.com` |
| auth | `DefaultAzureCredential` → `Bearer` (`auth/auth.go:88`) | **static** `Authorization: Token <secret>` |
| client | `msgraph-sdk-go` + Kiota middlewares | plain HTTP |

**The non-Graph part is already precedented and should not be re-litigated.**
`internal/o365activityclient/` (~2.3k lines) talks to `manage.office.com` with its own base-URL
constant (`o365activityclient.go:92-101`), its own instrumented transport and rate limiter
(`transport.go`), its own bounded `Operation` classifier, a `checkHost` guard that refuses to attach
credentials to a foreign host (`o365activityclient.go:291`), and a body cap. Its auth is injected at
exactly one line — `req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+tok.Token)`,
`o365activityclient.go:318`. An MDCA client is that package's shape with a static token at that one
line, and `tokenCredential` (`:169`) dropped entirely.

**The genuinely new thing is the static secret**, and it needs an explicit decision:
`config.TenantConfig` documents itself as "intentionally carries no secret material"
(`config.go:164-167`). A `config.Secret` field here is a deliberate, reviewable break with that
contract. In-repo precedent for an env-supplied `config.Secret` is
`ProfilingPyroscope.BasicAuthPassword` (`config.go:158`). **The token must come from env, never
committed YAML.**

Also note the framework itself is agnostic and needs no changes: `collector.WindowCollector`,
`collector.Registry`, `telemetry.Emitter`, `checkpoint.Store` and `config.CollectorSettings` assume
nothing about Graph (`checkpoint.Checkpoint.Endpoint` is an arbitrary string namespace; its "Graph
endpoint" doc comment is cosmetic).

## Proposed shape

A new domain, `mdca.*`, and one collector: **`mdca.discovery_parse`**.

- **`internal/mdcaclient/`** — modeled on `o365activityclient`: base URL from config, `Options{Emitter,
  BaseURL, Token, Limiter, MaxRetries, baseTransport}`, `NewClient` doing no network I/O, one `do()`
  setting `Authorization: Token <secret>`, `checkHost` pin, `maxBodyBytes` cap, and its own
  `transport.go` with **its own** `graph2otel.mdca.http.*` metric names. Per `transport.go:14-23`,
  reusing `graph2otel.o365activity.*` names would silently take the first-registered description —
  do not.
  - Throttle: MDCA documents **30 requests/min/tenant** across the whole API
    ([REST API](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-cloud-apps/api-introduction)) and
    responses are capped at 100 items. Size the limiter for that, and note the budget is shared with
    anything else hitting this tenant's MDCA API.
- **`internal/collectors/mdca.go`** — `MDCADeps` / `MDCAFactory` / `RegisterMDCA` / `MDCAAll`,
  mirroring `blobs.go` (60 lines).
- **`internal/collectors/mdca/discoveryparse/`** — `WindowCollector`. The governance log is an event
  stream with a timestamp and a stable ID, which is exactly the `WindowCollector` contract.
  - watermark: `timestamp` (ms epoch), server-side `gte`
  - dedupe: `_id`, via `checkpoint.SeenIDs` with an overlap window — a task's `status` **mutates
    after creation** (queued → success/failure ~50s later), so the record must be re-read after the
    watermark passes it. Either lag the window past the parse latency, or key dedupe on
    `_id + updateTimestamp` so the terminal state is not dropped as a duplicate. **This is the
    subtle bit of the whole issue** — a naive `_id` dedupe ships only the `PENDING` state and
    permanently hides every verdict.
  - `Lag()`: parse latency measured ~50s; needs a margin.

**Logs** (per-entity detail): one event per `DiscoveryParseLogTask` — `mdca.discovery_parse` —
attributes `template`, `is_success`, `data_source` (`GENERIC_CEF`), `log_type`, `input_stream_id`,
`file_size`, `transactions_count`, `cloud_services_count`. Severity `Error` on `isSuccess:false`,
`Info` otherwise. Note `telemetrytest` cannot render `log.Int64` — emit numeric attrs as strings if
they must be asserted in tests (`internal/telemetrytest/recorder.go`).

**Metrics** (bounded aggregates only): `GaugeSnapshot`, not `Gauge` — the attribute set churns and
cumulative temporality would ghost dead series. Attributes bounded to `input_stream_id` × `template`
(streams are single-digit per tenant; templates are a small closed enum). Candidates:

- `mdca.discovery.parse.last_success.age_seconds` — **the one that would have caught this.** Alerts
  on silence, which a failure counter cannot: a dead uploader emits no failures either.
- `mdca.discovery.parse.transactions` / `mdca.discovery.parse.cloud_services` — straight from
  `templateMessage.parameters`; a collapse to zero is the "parsed fine, discovered nothing" case.
- `mdca.discovery.parse.tasks` by `template` — failure-mode breakdown.

**Config** — new `TenantConfig` sub-block, mirroring `blob_ingest` / `o365_activity`, where setting
it IS the opt-in (no block → collector never registers):

```yaml
tenants:
  - tenant_id: "..."
    client_id: "..."
    mdca:
      portal_url: "https://<tenant>.<region>.portal.cloudappsecurity.com"
      # token: via env only (G2O_...), config.Secret, never YAML
```

Mark the collector `Experimental()` — the legacy MDCA API has no Graph successor and a real
deprecation risk; opt-in is the honest default.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `internal/mdcaclient/` — client + `transport.go`, own `graph2otel.mdca.http.*` metrics, bounded `Operation` classifier, `checkHost` pin, body cap, limiter sized to 30 req/min/tenant, `NewClient` does no I/O
- [ ] Static token via `config.Secret`, sourced from env; **never** read from YAML; redacted in dumps/admin
- [ ] `internal/collectors/mdca.go` — Deps/Factory/`RegisterMDCA`/`MDCAAll`
- [ ] `mdca.discovery_parse` `WindowCollector`, `Experimental() bool` = true
- [ ] Watermark server-side on `timestamp gte`; `taskName`/`status` filtered **client-side**, with a test pinning that (an unsupported server-side filter returns an empty set, not an error)
- [ ] Pending tasks (absent `status`) are not emitted as failures, and are re-read once terminal — dedupe keyed so the verdict is not dropped as a duplicate of the pending record
- [ ] Logs: one `mdca.discovery_parse` event per task, `Error` severity on failure
- [ ] Metrics: `GaugeSnapshot` only; `last_success.age_seconds` present; attributes bounded to `input_stream_id` × `template`
- [ ] `cmd/graph2otel/collectors_import.go` — blank import
- [ ] `cmd/graph2otel/tenants.go` — `registerMDCACollectors` + `recordMDCASkips`, called **before** `checkRegistryConflicts` (`tenants.go:199`)
- [ ] **`cmd/graph2otel/collectordoc_test.go:42` `registrySnapshot()` extended to walk the new path** — otherwise all three doc gates pass blind (the file says so at `:36-41`)
- [ ] `internal/collectordoc/collectordoc.go:121` — `mdca` added to `domains` (unknown prefix is a hard error)
- [ ] `internal/collectordoc/annotations.go` — `Annotation` entry
- [ ] CLAUDE.md "Metric namespaces" — `mdca.*` added
- [ ] `config.example.yaml` **and** `charts/graph2otel/values.yaml` updated (`TestExampleConfigCoversEveryKey`, `TestHelmValuesConfigCoversEveryKey`), then `scripts/regen-generated.sh`
- [ ] Tests: stdlib only, `httptest`/`baseTransport` seam, `telemetrytest.Recorder`, injected clock; cover success, failure, **pending→terminal transition**, and the empty-set-filter trap
- [ ] `alerts/graph2otel-alerts.yaml` rule + `alerts/README.md` doc block (see below)
- [ ] `docs/collectors.md` regenerated; `docs/signals.md` / `docs/permissions.md` prose for the non-Graph auth path
- [ ] `make check` green

## Alerting intent (the actual deliverable)

Two rules, because they catch different failures and one cannot cover the other:

1. **Parse failing** — any `isSuccess:false` (i.e. any `template` other than
   `..._PARSED_LOG_FILE_ALL_RELEVANT`) in the last hour. This is the 22-failure outage above.
2. **Uploads stopped** — `mdca.discovery.parse.last_success.age_seconds` > ~3h. Silence is the
   failure a failure-counter structurally cannot see: if the uploader dies, MDCA generates no
   failed tasks, and rule 1 stays green forever.

Rule 1 default-enabled; rule 2 is the one that would actually have caught a dead pipeline. Per
`alerts/README.md`, both need the 3-node A→B→C pipeline shape and a doc block, and metric names
follow OTLP→Prometheus normalization (dots→underscores, `_total` on counters).

## Out of scope

Everything else in the MDCA API (discovered apps, block scripts, alerts, activities). This issue is
the governance/parse-health signal only. `98: "MCASAlerts"` in
`internal/collectors/m365/activity/recordtypes.go` is an O365 audit record-type decoder constant and
is unrelated — nothing polls MDCA today.

## Parked (Rob, 2026-07-18) — build-ready, blocked on the portal token

Assessed 2026-07-18. The data is real and current (the live capture in the body above, 2026-07-17: 40 `DiscoveryParseLogTask` records — 22 `UNEXPECTED_FORMAT` failures + 18 successes), and the collector is fully buildable against that sample. Parking per Rob's call until the token is provisioned.

**The one hard unblock — a static portal token, NOT the poller cert.** MDCA Cloud Discovery is the legacy portal API (`https://<tenant>.<region>.portal.cloudappsecurity.com`), authenticated with `Authorization: Token <secret>` — it does NOT use `graph2otel-poller`/`DefaultAzureCredential`, so there is no app-registration scope to grant. Confirmed 2026-07-18: no MDCA token is in camden's `/opt/graph2otel/.env` (only the OTLP token); the static token currently lives in the separate n8n uploader's credentials. **To unblock:** provision it as a `config.Secret` from env on camden (precedent: `ProfilingPyroscope.BasicAuthPassword`, `config.go:158`). Until then the collector can be built + unit-tested but NOT live-verified — and the repo rule is a green tick over an unexercised mapper proves nothing.

**Build spec (all live-captured 2026-07-17, in the body; template = `o365activityclient`/`o365pipeline`, the other non-Graph first-party client):**
- **Endpoint:** `POST /api/v1/governance/` body `{"limit":N,"skip":N,"filters":{"timestamp":{"gte":<ms>}}}`. Watermark server-side on `timestamp gte` ONLY — filter `taskName == "DiscoveryParseLogTask"` and `status` **client-side** (unsupported server-side filters return empty, not error — pin with a test).
- **Auth:** static `Authorization: Token <secret>`.
- **Event time:** `timestamp` (ms epoch). **Dedupe on `_id + updateTimestamp`, not `_id` alone** — the task's `status` mutates ~50s after creation (queued→verdict), so `_id` dedupe ships only the PENDING record and hides every verdict. `Lag()` past the ~50s parse latency.
- **Log twin `mdca.discovery_parse` (#112):** one per task — `template`, `is_success`, `data_source`, `log_type`, `input_stream_id`, `file_size`, `transactions_count`, `cloud_services_count`; `Error` severity on `isSuccess:false`.
- **Metrics (bounded, GaugeSnapshot):** `mdca.discovery.parse.last_success.age_seconds` (the alert-on-silence one), `.transactions`, `.cloud_services`, `.tasks` by template; attrs bounded to `input_stream_id × template`.
- **New `mdca.*` domain**, `Experimental()` (legacy API, no Graph successor), opt-in via an `mdca` `TenantConfig` sub-block. **Must extend `collectordoc` `domains` map + `registrySnapshot()` walk** — a new registration path silently passes the doc gates unless the walker is extended (#139/#100 fourth-path gate-blindness trap).
- Traps (live-verified 2026-07-17): 30 req/min/tenant cap, 100-item response cap; `status` absent while queued (a real third 'pending' state).

Resume: provision the token, then build + live-verify against the live governance records.

## Unblocked + starting build — one design change: `token_file`, not env `Secret`

Token provisioned (portal `https://m7knio.eu2.portal.cloudappsecurity.com`, region eu2). Validated live 2026-07-19 as the poller-independent static token: `POST /api/v1/governance/ {"limit":5,"skip":0}` → HTTP 200, `{"total":100,"data":[...]}`, records carrying `_id` / `timestamp` (ms) / `updateTimestamp` (ms) / `status.isSuccess` / `status.templateMessage.template` / `taskName` / `inputStreamId` / `fileSize` / `logType`. Parse latency `timestamp`→`updateTimestamp` observed up to ~980s (16 min) — the dedupe-on-`_id+updateTimestamp` requirement is confirmed real.

### Correction to the parked build spec (wire-over-docs)

The parked comment and the body's config note say the token is a `config.Secret` sourced from env (`G2O_TENANTS__0__MDCA__TOKEN`, precedent `ProfilingPyroscope.BasicAuthPassword`). **That is impossible and I've measured it:**

- `env.go:26-29` already documents that this config has *no* `[]TenantConfig` env binding.
- Empirically (throwaway probe, 2026-07-19): setting `G2O_TENANTS__0__CLIENT_ID` did not just fail to bind — it **destructively wiped the entire tenants slice** (`tenant_id` and `client_id` both went empty), because the env key `tenants.0.client_id` clobbers the YAML-loaded slice with a map-shaped value.

`ProfilingPyroscope.BasicAuthPassword` works only because it is **top-level**, not inside a slice. A per-tenant secret has no env path here.

**Decision — `token_file` instead of an env `Secret`:**

```yaml
tenants:
  - tenant_id: "..."
    mdca:
      portal_url: "https://<tenant>.<region>.portal.cloudappsecurity.com"
      token_file: "/path/to/mdca_token"   # non-secret PATH; the token file is mounted, never in YAML/env
```

- `MDCAConfig{ PortalURL string; TokenFile string }` — both fields are non-secret (a URL and a filesystem path), so they live safely in YAML.
- The composition root reads the token from `TokenFile` at client construction, fail-fast if unreadable/empty.
- Per-tenant safe, multi-tenant safe, secret stays out of YAML/env, standard k8s secret-mount pattern.
- Acceptance criterion "Static token via `config.Secret`, sourced from env" is superseded by "static token read from a per-tenant `token_file`; never in YAML/env; redacted in dumps/admin (nothing to redact — only a path is stored)".

Everything else in the acceptance list stands. Building now with TDD; will live-verify against the m7kni governance log and wire camden's token file on deploy.

## Live-verified on camden against the production Cloud Discovery governance log — closing

Shipped in e8ee309 (deployed to camden on image bea2f46443de, the 5f75ac9 `:main` build). Wired the static token into camden as a mounted secret file:

- `/opt/graph2otel/secrets/mdca_token` (uid 65532, mode 400), mounted read-only at `/etc/graph2otel/secrets/mdca_token`;
- `tenants[].mdca.{portal_url: https://m7knio.eu2.portal.cloudappsecurity.com, token_file}` in config.yaml;
- `collectors["mdca.discovery_parse"].enabled: true` — it is Experimental, so the `mdca` block registers it but it still needs the explicit opt-in (as designed).

**Live status.json (poller-independent, static-token path):**

```json
{ "name": "mdca.discovery_parse", "enabled": true, "transport": "mdca",
  "has_run": true, "runs": 1, "failures": 0, "last_success": true, "last_duration_ms": 1453,
  "state": { "kind": "window", "watermark": "2026-07-19T14:00:28Z", "staleness": "34m50s", "seen_ids": 1 } }
```

- `transport: "mdca"` — the sixth `ingest_transport` value (#141) is live.
- The collector polled the real m7kni governance log, mapped a real `DiscoveryParseLogTask`, and advanced its **watermark to 14:00:28** (a real task timestamp). `seen_ids: 1` is exactly correct — every task in the 4h cold-start window was emitted, and the bounded dedupe set retains only the one inside the 30m overlap. `last_success=true`, zero failures against production data — not a green-tick-over-empty.
- The `state` block also live-verifies #178 Part B (the checkpoint cursor UI) end-to-end for a self-contained WindowCollector.

**One design note confirmed live:** setting `mdca.portal_url` registers the collector but, because it is `Experimental` (legacy portal API, no Graph successor), it is gated OFF until explicitly enabled under `collectors:` — it logged `skipping experimental collector (opt-in)` until I added the enable line. That double opt-in (mdca block + experimental enable) is intentional and matches every other beta/experimental surface on this tenant.

Every acceptance-criteria box is met: client + transport, token_file (superseding the impossible env-Secret — see the earlier comment), watermark/client-side-filter/pending→terminal dedupe, log twin + gauges + counter, collectordoc fifth-path walk, alerts (doc block 5), docs, `make check` green, and now live-verified. Closing.

body:
## Measured live on camden 2026-07-16, `55e3999`

Two collector pairs are running simultaneously and shipping the same records into one stream:

```
entra.signins.non_interactive          runs=3   ← polled (beta, Experimental, explicitly enabled)
entra.signins.non_interactive.blob     runs=3   ← blob   (NOT Experimental, registers with blob_ingest)
entra.signins.service_principal        runs=3   ← polled
entra.signins.service_principal.blob   runs=3   ← blob
```

Intersecting each polled collector's own checkpoint `seen_ids` against the ids in its blob container:

```
non_interactive:    polled seen_ids: 18    -> ids present in BOTH: 18     (100%)
service_principal:  polled seen_ids: 1375  -> ids present in BOTH: 1375   (100%)
```

**Total overlap, not partial.** Every id the polled collector has ever seen is also in the blob. Both emit event name `entra.signin` with the same `id` (CLAUDE.md: "`properties.id` == the polled `signIn.id`"), so every one of those records ships twice.

Worse: per #141 there is no provenance attribute, so the two copies are **byte-identical** — an operator cannot tell them apart, cannot attribute the duplication to a transport, and cannot drop one lane at query time. This is exactly the failure #141 predicts, arriving before #141 is fixed.

## Nothing enforces the rule, and the rule is written down

CLAUDE.md already states it:

> **`source: graph|blob` must be mutually exclusive per collector — both enabled = duplicate records** (#89/#128)

and the collector reference already says of `m365.unified_audit`:

> Superseded by `m365.activity` ... **leave only one of the two enabled**

Both are sentences in documentation. Verified: there is **no** startup check, no config validation, no conflict declaration anywhere in `cmd/`, `internal/config/`, or `internal/collectors/registry.go`. The only non-comment references to `m365.unified_audit` outside its own package are documentation strings in `collectordoc/annotations.go`.

## Why this survived until now

CLAUDE.md records the reason, and it is exactly right — it just stopped being true on camden:

> The sign-in streams escaped this only because their polled beta twins are **Experimental** (off by default), so blob-on + polled-off = each event once.

camden explicitly enables all three beta sign-in streams **and** sets `blob_ingest.account_url`. Off-by-default is not enforcement; it is luck, and it runs out the moment an operator opts in to both — which is the documented way to use this product.

`entra.signins.interactive` is safe only because no `.interactive.blob` collector exists. That is an accident of coverage, not a design.

## The three conflicting pairs today

| polled | blob / alternate transport | conflicting now? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `entra.signins.non_interactive` | `entra.signins.non_interactive.blob` | **YES — live on camden** |
| `entra.signins.service_principal` | `entra.signins.service_principal.blob` | **YES — live on camden** |
| `m365.unified_audit` | `m365.activity` | no — only because `m365.unified_audit` was disabled on camden by hand an hour ago |

## Design

**A collector declares its conflicts; the composition root enforces them; a test proves the enforcement is not blind.**

1. **`ConflictsWith() []string`** — a small optional interface next to `Experimental`, implemented by the collector that knows it is a second transport for records another collector already emits. The blob twins declare their polled twin; `m365.activity` declares `m365.unified_audit`.

2. **Enforce at startup, fail fast.** After registration, for each registered collector implementing the interface, if a named peer is also registered, return an error naming both collectors and how to resolve it. Fail-fast, not warn: a config in this state was never working, it was silently wrong, and #117 already set the precedent (an unwritable checkpoint dir fails the process rather than degrading silently).

   **This is a deliberate breaking change for anyone in the conflicting state** — including camden, which will refuse to boot until its config is fixed. That is the point. Shipping every record twice while reporting 100% healthy is worse than not booting.

3. **Do NOT derive conflicts from the event name.** `entra.signins.interactive` and `entra.signins.non_interactive` both emit `entra.signin` and do **not** conflict — they are disjoint slices of one endpoint. Event-name equality is not the rule; "same records over a different transport" is, and only the author knows that.

4. **A central list would go blind** — the #139/#100 lesson (`collectordoc.Rows` walked three of four registration paths and its gate passed because it could not see the fourth). A declaration on the collector itself travels with the collector. Pair it with a test that walks **every** registration path (`All`, `WindowAll`, `BlobAll`, `O365All`) so a new transport twin cannot register without being seen.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `ConflictsWith` declared on the two blob sign-in twins and on `m365.activity`
- [ ] Startup fails, with an error naming both collectors and the fix, when a conflicting pair is registered for a tenant
- [ ] A test proves the check fires — watch it fail for the right reason before the fix
- [ ] A test proves the check does NOT fire for `entra.signins.interactive` + `entra.signins.non_interactive` (same event name, disjoint records, legitimate)
- [ ] The conflict walk covers every registration path, so a future twin cannot be invisible to it (#139)
- [ ] camden's config resolved: pick blob or polled per sign-in stream, and record which and why
- [ ] `m365.unified_audit`'s docs re-scoped: it is NOT "superseded" (see below)
- [ ] `make check` green

## Also: "superseded" is over-claimed and should be corrected

`m365.activity` beats `m365.unified_audit` on transport — stable v1.0 vs beta-only (the v1.0 form 404s live), 2,000 req/min vs 429-on-rapid-create (#98), ~2 min to content vs a >10-minute async query. That is real and it is why `m365.activity` exists.

It does **not** beat it on volume control, and the reference currently claims a clean supersede that does not hold:

- `m365.unified_audit` sends server-side `recordTypeFilters` — a curated Exchange/SharePoint/OneDrive/Teams include-list that **deliberately excludes `DLPEndpoint`** (3,003 of #98's 3,837 records were endpoint-DLP `FileDeleted` from one host).
- `m365.activity` has **no server-side filtering at all**. Its only volume knob is the content-type subscription, five buckets. Teams lives only in `Audit.General`, which was **3,865 of 4,035 records (95.8%) endpoint-DLP noise** on a six-device tenant — and #112 forbids fetch-and-discard, so enabling it ships all of it.

So the precise residual is: **`m365.unified_audit` can fetch Teams while excluding the endpoint-DLP firehose; `m365.activity` cannot.** Worth nothing on a tenant where Loki is free; decisive for the per-GB operators the default-content-types comment was written for ("graph2otel is public OSS and other operators pay per GB; Loki being free on the verification tenant is not a reason to ship everyone a firehose").

The uncomfortable part, which the docs should say rather than hide: **that cheaper path is beta-only.**

Re-scope the reference row from "Superseded by `m365.activity`" to what is actually true: the same signal over two transports that trade against each other — stable/fast/all-or-nothing vs beta/slow/record-type-filtered — and exactly one may be enabled.

## Do not

- Do not delete `m365.unified_audit` under this issue. It is the **only** `jobpipeline` collector, so deleting it makes `internal/jobpipeline` dead code and moots half of #118 — that is a separate decision with a real cost (the only affordable Teams path), not a cleanup.
- Do not derive conflicts from event-name equality. It produces a false positive on the interactive/non-interactive sign-in pair immediately.
- Do not "solve" this by making the blob twins Experimental. Off-by-default is what let this ship; it is not enforcement.
- Do not warn-and-continue. The whole failure mode is that it looks healthy while double-shipping.

Refs #89, #98, #112, #128, #139, #141

## camden resolved — the live double-shipping is stopped

Fixed **before** pushing, deliberately: watchtower auto-deploys `:main`, so shipping a fail-fast check against a config that trips it would have taken camden down.

| stream | resolution |
| --- | --- |
| `entra.signins.non_interactive` | polled **disabled**, `.blob` kept |
| `entra.signins.service_principal` | polled **disabled**, `.blob` kept |
| `entra.signins.interactive` | polled kept — no `.blob` twin exists |
| `entra.signins.managed_identity` | polled kept — no `.blob` twin exists |
| `m365.unified_audit` | disabled, `m365.activity` kept |

**Why blob won on the two contested pairs:** the polled form of those two streams is **beta-only** (the `signInEventTypes` filter 400s on v1.0), so dropping it removes a beta dependency — the blob path is GA. Blob ingest is also the direction #89/#135/#137 want exercised. The cost is #138: `blobpipeline` does not dedupe, so these ship ~2.3% duplicates until that lands. Tracked, and strictly better than the 100% duplicates measured here.

Verified after: 58 registered, 0 failing, 0 ERROR lines, no conflicting pair.

## The pair list is exhaustive, not just the three that were obvious

Four blob collectors exist. `entra.graph_activity` has no polled twin (MicrosoftGraphActivityLogs has no Graph endpoint at all) and `entra.signins.microsoft_service_principal` has none either — so two blob pairs plus the m365 pair is the complete set today.

## Where the design in this issue was WRONG

The plan said the check "must walk EVERY registration path". **That was wrong**, and implementing it as specified would have rebuilt the exact shape that went blind in #139/#100. All four paths funnel into one `collector.Registry`, so the check walks `reg.Entries()` and sees every path **by construction** — a fifth path is covered the day it lands, for free. Re-walking `All`/`WindowAll`/`BlobAll`/`O365All` would have been a list to keep in sync, which is the disease, not the cure.

## Residual risk — stated because nothing tests it

Walking the registry moves the risk to the **call site**: `checkRegistryConflicts` must run after all registration, never between two paths. That ordering is documented at the call and gated by **nothing**. `setupTenant` needs credentials and a network, so if someone moves the check above `registerBlobCollectors`, no test fails.

The structural fix would be to validate inside the registry or the scheduler, where ordering cannot be got wrong — but the import direction forbids it today (`collectors` → `collector`, and `ConflictsWith` lives in `collectors`). Worth revisiting if a fifth transport lands.

## Mutation-tested, not assumed

Six mutations, each caught by name. The load-bearing one: making `registrySnapshot` stop walking the blob path still left the gate reporting the m365 pair — so a weaker "did it error at all?" assertion would have gone **green while blind**. Only asserting every measured pair by name catches it. Independently re-run before commit: dropping `m365.activity`'s declaration fails `TestEveryKnownConflictPairFires` + `TestConflictCheckSeesEveryRegistrationPath`; reverting goes green.

## Docs re-scoped

`m365.unified_audit` no longer claims to be "superseded". It is a trade: `m365.activity` wins on transport, `unified_audit` wins on volume control (server-side `recordTypeFilters` excluding `DLPEndpoint`; `m365.activity` has no server-side filtering and reaches Teams only via `Audit.General` = 95.8% endpoint-DLP noise, all shipped per #112). The docs now state plainly that the cheaper path is beta-only rather than hiding it.

Not deleted, per this issue's "Do not" — it remains the only `jobpipeline` collector, and that decision has a real cost.

title: fix(collectors): nothing enforces transport mutual-exclusion — camden ships every non-interactive + service-principal sign-in TWICE, measured

body:
## The false claim, and what it cost

`docs/signals.md:89`:

> Every metric carries a `tenant_id` label so one process's telemetry for several tenants stays distinguishable in a shared backend. Dashboards built against these signals should add a `$tenant` template variable and filter every panel query by it — see the shipped dashboards under `dashboards/` for the pattern.

**No `entra_*` or `intune_*` metric carries `tenant_id`.** Only `graph2otel.*` self-obs metrics do. Both shipped domain dashboards followed the doc's instruction and filter on a label that is not there.

`internal/collectors/registry.go:40-41` repeats the same misconception in code, where a collector author will read it:

```go
// TenantID is the tenant this collector instance serves (for logging; the
// scheduler already labels emitted telemetry with the tenant).
```

The scheduler labels **its own** `scrape.*` metrics with the tenant. It does not touch collector-emitted telemetry. `docs/pii-cardinality-audit.md:133` gets it right ("The framework self-obs metrics carry `tenant_id`"), so the docs already contradict each other.

## Verified: there is no code path that could add it

- **Not a resource attribute.** `buildResource` (`internal/telemetry/provider.go:211-241`) sets `service.name`, optionally `service.version`, plus SDK/OS/host/narrow-process detectors. It takes `(ctx, opts, bool)` and never sees a tenant.
- **No per-tenant provider.** One MeterProvider and one LoggerProvider for the process (`provider.go:165-176`); every tenant shares one emitter (`cmd/graph2otel/tenants.go:79`, `emitter := provider.Emitter()`). `setupTenant` never constructs a provider or resource.
- **The emitter injects nothing.** `buildAttrs` (`internal/telemetry/emitter.go:244-253`) is a pure map→KV conversion; `GaugeSnapshot` (`:103-110`) adds nothing. A metric's labels are exactly what the collector passed.
- **No collector passes it.** e.g. `intune/compliance/compliance.go:391`: `Attrs: telemetry.Attrs{"setting_name": …, "platform": …, "state": …}`.

`tenant_id` reaches a metric from exactly four places, all self-obs: `internal/collector/selfobs.go:76-82`, `internal/license/emit.go:34`, `internal/graphclient/ratelimit_transport.go:93`, `internal/graphclient/transport.go:93`.

(The hits at `securityalerts.go:104` / `securityincidents.go:147` are **log** attributes parsed from the Graph payload - Microsoft's tenant, not ours. Red herring, and separately a name collision worth resolving alongside the attribute-registry issue.)

## Impact differs per dashboard

### `entra-compliance-overview.json` - hard broken, ~24 panels return no data, always

Variable (`:31-49`): `"query": "label_values(tenant_id)"`, `includeAll: true`, `multi: true`, **no `allValue`**.

`label_values(tenant_id)` is the bare-label form, so it resolves across the whole TSDB and finds real tenant GUIDs on `graph2otel_scrape_*` / `graph2otel_tenant_license_tier_ratio`. Those always exist. `cmd/graph2otel/main.go:102` hardcodes `SelfObsEnabled: true`. So the dropdown **populates with plausible GUIDs**, and the dashboard looks correctly configured.

With `includeAll` and no `allValue`, "All" interpolates to the alternation of the real options → `entra_users_total{tenant_id=~"guid-a|guid-b"}`. The series carry no `tenant_id`; a missing label reads as `""`; `""` does not match the fully-anchored alternation. **No match - including when a specific tenant is picked.** 26 `tenant_id` references.

### `intune-fleet-overview.json` - inert, not visibly broken

Variable (`:2358-2379`): `"query": "label_values(intune_devices_count, tenant_id)"`, `includeAll: true`, no `allValue`.

`intune_devices_count` carries no `tenant_id`, so `label_values` returns empty → the dropdown offers only "All" → the interpolated matcher permits the empty string → `intune_compliance_setting_devices{tenant_id=~""}` matches the label-less series → **panels render**. So `:565` is not user-visibly broken; it is silently inert. There is no reachable state in which it filters anything, and per-tenant scoping is impossible on a multi-tenant deploy. 52 `tenant_id` references.

### `graph2otel-self-observability.json` - correct, leave alone

`label_values(graph2otel_scrape_success_ratio, tenant_id)` with `"allValue": ".*"` (`:33-44`): scoped to a metric that carries the label, with an explicit all-value. All 37 references are on `graph2otel_*` metrics.

## The actual decision (state it, do not let it be implicit)

Two ways to make the code & docs agree, and they are not equivalent:

1. **Add `tenant_id` to every domain metric.** Makes `docs/signals.md:89` true and makes per-tenant scoping work on a multi-tenant deploy - the product's day-one claim. Cost: multiplies active series by tenant count. Grafana Cloud bills on active series (#105), and this is exactly the axis #112 says must not grow with tenant size. Though note: #112's rule is about growth with **tenant size** (per-user/per-device), not with **tenant count**, which is bounded and operator-chosen. Not obviously disqualified; needs a decision, not a reflex.
2. **Strip the filter from both dashboards and fix the docs.** Cheap, honest, and leaves a multi-tenant operator unable to scope a domain panel by tenant.

Single-tenant deploys are unaffected either way, which is why this survived.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `docs/signals.md:89` says something true
- [ ] `registry.go:40-41`'s "the scheduler already labels emitted telemetry with the tenant" corrected
- [ ] `entra-compliance-overview.json` returns data
- [ ] `intune-fleet-overview.json`'s `tenant_id` filter either works or is gone - not inert
- [ ] The add-label vs strip-filter decision recorded with its reasoning
- [ ] Something gates it, so a dashboard cannot filter on a label no metric emits (pairs with #140 / the attribute-registry issue)
- [ ] `make check` green

## Do not

- Do not touch `graph2otel-self-observability.json`. It is the one that is right, and it is the reference for what correct looks like.
- Do not "fix" this by adding `allValue: ".*"` to the entra dashboard. That hides the empty result behind a matcher that matches everything; the label still is not there and per-tenant scoping still cannot work.
- Do not add `tenant_id` to domain metrics without recording the active-series decision above.

Refs #105, #112, #140

comments.body: Scope note (2026-07-17, #146): verified while fixing `docs/signals.md:89` — domain **logs** lack `tenant_id` too, not just metrics. The scheduler's `WithTenant` adds `semconv.AttrTenantID` to its own self-obs metrics and namespaces checkpoint keys, and nothing wraps the emitter handed to `Collect`/`CollectWindow`, so a domain log record's attributes are exactly what the collector passed. The doc line and the `registry.go` Deps comment are corrected to say so (no false claim remains), but the design decision this issue owns — how multi-tenant separation should work on domain signals — now covers logs as well as metrics.

## DECISION (maintainer, 2026-07-17): **option 1 — add `tenant_id` to every domain metric.**

This closes the AC *"The add-label vs strip-filter decision recorded with its reasoning"*. Recording it here so it is never implicit again.

### The reasoning

Per-tenant scoping of domain signals is the product's day-one claim, and option 2 permanently forecloses it. The cost objection does not survive this issue's own analysis:

> #112's rule is about growth with **tenant size** (per-user/per-device), not with **tenant count**, which is bounded and operator-chosen. Not obviously disqualified; needs a decision, not a reflex.

`tenant_id` multiplies series by the number of tenants an operator has **deliberately configured**. That is bounded, small, and the growth is *correct* — those genuinely are different measurements. A single-tenant deploy (the common case) sees no series-count change at all, only one extra label.

### The argument that decided it, and which this issue does not yet state

**Without `tenant_id`, two tenants' domain metrics are not merely unsliceable — they are the same series.** Same metric name, same labels, one shared MeterProvider, one shared resource (`buildResource` never sees a tenant, per this issue's own verification). So `intune_compliance_devices{state="compliant"}` from tenant A and tenant B collide and interleave. A two-tenant deploy does not get a coarse number; it gets a **meaningless** one.

That reframes the choice. Option 2 is not "cheap and honest, loses tenant scoping" — it is "cheap, and silently produces wrong numbers on any multi-tenant deployment", while `README`/`CLAUDE.md` advertise multi-tenancy. Option 1 is the only one where the shipped claim is true.

⚠️ **Evidence class: `reasoned`, NOT `live-measured`.** The collision is deduced from the code paths this issue verified (one provider, one resource, labels are exactly what the collector passed) — it has not been observed, because the verification tenant is single-tenant. It is near-certain but it is not measured. **If a second tenant ever lands, measure it before trusting this paragraph.**

### Consequence: #158's dashboard fix pre-empted this decision and must be partly reversed

`59489eb` (#158) stripped all 74 `tenant_id` filters from both domain dashboards. That was **option 2, applied unilaterally, while this issue was open** — my error: I filed #158 without finding #143, which already documented the same breakage in more detail. #158 should be treated as a duplicate of this issue's dashboard half.

The commit is not wasted — the dashboards were broken *at that moment* and now render — but once the label exists, tenant filtering should be **re-added deliberately**, with the label actually present and the `$tenant` variables restored. Sequencing is therefore: land the label, then re-instrument the dashboards, then the alerts.

### Scope this decision now touches

- `#160` — `alerts/README.md:37` ("Every metric carries a `tenant_id` label") becomes TRUE once this lands, and the six domain rules grouping `by (tenant_id)` become correct rather than silently blending tenants. **Do not fix #160 by removing the grouping — this decision makes it right.** #160's ratio rules (331, 402) are the strongest independent argument for option 1: they silently average across tenants today.
- `registry.go:40-41`'s comment is still wrong today and must be corrected *as* the label lands, not before.
- Every collector package's `testdata/signals.json` golden (2bf2b37) will gain `tenant_id` on its metrics — that diff IS the review surface for this change, and is the cheapest way to see exactly which series are affected. Regenerate with `scripts/regen-generated.sh signals`.
- The `#112` gate (`internal/signalcapture`) does **not** flag `tenant_id` — correctly, since it is bounded by tenant count. No exemption needed.

### Implementation notes for whoever takes it

- The seam is almost certainly **not** per-collector. Every collector receives its emitter from the Scheduler, which already knows its tenant (`WithTenant`) — the same chokepoint #141's `WithTransport` decorator uses (`62c3850`). A `WithTenant`-style emitter decorator stamping metrics is the shape; **do not thread a tenant through 58 collectors.**
- Note the asymmetry with #141: provenance is **log-only** because a metric label changes series identity (#82). This is the opposite — it is deliberately a **metric** label, and it WILL change series identity for every domain metric. That is the point, and it is a breaking change to every existing dashboard/alert query. Pre-1.0 is the moment.
- **Decide explicitly whether domain LOGS also get it.** This issue and CLAUDE.md both say `tenant_id` is absent from domain logs too. Logs are Loki structured metadata (#90), so adding it there is additive and cheap — and a SIEM feed almost certainly wants to know which tenant a sign-in came from. Do not let this ride on the metric decision by accident.
- There is a live name collision: `securityalerts.go:104` / `securityincidents.go:147` already emit a `tenant_id` **log** attribute parsed from Microsoft's payload — *their* tenant, not ours. If domain logs gain our `tenant_id`, that key means two things on those two signals. Resolve before, not after.

## LANDED — `b0293c4`. And this issue's "name collision" was wrong.

### The collision does not exist. Correcting it here so nobody re-derives it.

This issue's implementation note said:

> There is a live name collision: `securityalerts.go:104` / `securityincidents.go:147` already emit a `tenant_id` **log** attribute parsed from Microsoft's payload — *their* tenant, not ours. If domain logs gain our `tenant_id`, that key means two things on those two signals. Resolve before, not after.

**That is false.** The planned fix (rename Microsoft's to `ms_tenant_id`) would have invented an attribute for a meaning that does not exist.

The belief rested on a **hand-written fixture** — `"tenantId": "tenant-guid-1"` — which says nothing about what the field contains. Probed live as `graph2otel-poller`, 2026-07-17:

```
our AZURE_TENANT_ID: 4b8c18bd-2f9f-4227-af55-9f1061cf9c32

=== /security/alerts_v2?$top=5 -> 200
   id=ca69cc1cc22dc45a23ee30d46a                tenantId=4b8c18bd-…-9f1061cf9c32  == OURS
   id=da7d9031bd-68b8-4a8b-9a0a-e3789eba907d_1  tenantId=4b8c18bd-…-9f1061cf9c32  == OURS
   (5/5 == OURS)
=== /security/incidents?$top=5 -> 200
   (5/5 == OURS)
```

**10/10 rows, both endpoints, byte-equal to the poller's own tenant.** Microsoft's `tenantId` on an alert is "the tenant the alert was created in" — which, since we poll our own tenant with our own app, is us.

So those two lines were never a conflicting meaning. They were a **hand-rolled, per-collector preview of exactly what this issue adds globally**. Both are DELETED rather than renamed: the value is redundant with the emitter's stamp, so the delete loses no information (explicitly **not** a #114 "bucketed the count, discarded the entity" drop), and a second writer for a key the emitter owns is how the two eventually disagree. Both fixtures still supply `tenantId`, so `TestWireTenantIDIsNotEmitted` proves the mapper ignores it rather than that the test forgot to set it.

`[live-measured 2026-07-17, #143 — n=10, single tenant. Strong, not proven: a cross-tenant MSSP/B2B alert was not observable here.]`

### What shipped

- `telemetry.WithTenant` stamps `semconv.AttrTenantID` at the **emitter boundary**, wired at the composition root (`cmd/graph2otel/tenants.go`) outside `WithTransport`. Exactly the seam this issue predicted; no tenant threaded through 58 collectors.
- **Logs get it too** — decided explicitly, per this issue's instruction not to let it ride in by accident. Log attributes are Loki structured metadata (#90), so it is additive and cannot break a stream selector; a SIEM feed wants to know which tenant a sign-in came from; and it is what makes the two deletes above lossless.
- **Empty tenant is a passthrough**, matching `collector.WithTenant`'s existing "" semantics. Single-tenant deploys and every collector unit test are byte-identical to before.
- `#160` needed **no rule change** — its six domain rules already grouped `by (tenant_id)` and are now correct. `alerts/README.md:37` is now true. Closed by the same commit.
- Dashboards: `59489eb` reverted. The 74 filters and both `$tenant` variables are back. `graph2otel-self-observability.json` untouched.

### The gate worth knowing about

`tenantEmitter` embeds `Emitter`, so any method it does not override is **promoted** — it compiles perfectly and emits unstamped, merging two tenants' series on exactly the metric nobody checked. That is #141's failure shape.

`TestEveryEmitterMethodStampsTheTenant` parses the `Emitter` interface with `go/ast` and fails until every method is handled. **Mutation-proven**: built with only `LogEvent` overridden first, it named all six missing methods. Add an 8th method to `Emitter` and it fails until stamped.

### Correction to this issue's golden prediction

> Every collector package's `testdata/signals.json` golden (2bf2b37) will gain `tenant_id` on its metrics — that diff IS the review surface for this change.

**It does not, and that is correct.** Collector tests build their emitter from `telemetrytest.New()` directly and never pass through the composition root, so no golden changed. The golden documents what the **collector** emits; `tenant_id` is an infrastructure stamp applied above it. (`ingest_transport` appears in ~10 goldens only because those tests drive the real `logpipeline`, which is genuinely part of the record's production.)

The review surface is instead `internal/telemetry/tenant_test.go` + the AST gate. Noting it because "the goldens are the review surface" would otherwise read as a promise the next reader would find unmet.

### Still `reasoned`, not measured

The same-series collision that justified option 1 remains **deduced**, not observed — the verification tenant is single-tenant. Unchanged by this commit. If a second tenant ever lands, measure it.

title: fix(dashboards/docs): `docs/signals.md` claims every metric carries `tenant_id` - it does not, and the entra dashboard filters on it

body:
## Measured live 2026-07-16 (probed as `graph2otel-poller`, exact collector select lists)

Three collectors consume `internal/exportjob`. **None sets `LocalizationType`**, so Intune returns raw numeric codes in the primary column. Verified against the wire, not inferred:

```
AppInstallStatusAggregate: 371 rows, headers=['DisplayName','Platform','Platform_loc']
    Platform:      NUMERIC CODES -> ['1','2','3','5']
DefenderAgents: 3 rows, headers=['DeviceName','DeviceState','DeviceState_loc','ProductStatus']
    DeviceState:   NUMERIC CODES -> ['0']
    ProductStatus: NUMERIC CODES -> ['524288','524416']
AllDeviceCertificates: 0 rows (header only, no _loc sibling)
```

`exportjob.Request.LocalizationType` exists (`exportjob.go:89-92`, json tag `localizationType,omitempty` at `:232`) and is already threaded into the request body (`:416`) and the in-flight dedupe key (`:405`). **The only place in the repo that sets it is a test** (`inflight_test.go:255`). All three collectors build their `Request` with `ReportName`/`Select`/`Format` only: `appinstallreport.go:192-196`, `defenderreport.go:296-300`, `certinventoryreport.go:308-312`.

`Row` is `map[string]string` of raw cell text (`exportjob.go:96`) and `parseCSVRows` (`:523-548`) does header-keying and nothing else. Nothing decodes.

## Three different failure shapes - do not treat them as one bug

### 1. `intune.app_install_status` - visibly wrong, and the fix is already on the wire

`appinstallreport.go:242` (log) and `:220` (**metric label**) pass `row["Platform"]` straight through. Live result: `platform="2"`.

**`Platform_loc` is returned by default and is already sitting unread in the `Row` map.** The probe selected only `["DisplayName","Platform"]` and Microsoft returned `Platform_loc` anyway. `Select` does not suppress it. So the decoded name is already being fetched, parsed, header-keyed & thrown away.

The package doc names the hazard without noticing it landed: `appinstallreport.go:29-31` bounds the metric by "five columns x **the platform enum**".

**The test fixture is fiction and is why this shipped**: `appinstallreport_test.go:214` asserts `"platform": "windows"`. That's a hand-written localized string the live API never sends.

### 2. `intune.defender_agents` - silently wrong, and worse than #1

`ProductStatus` has **no `_loc` sibling**, because it is not an enum. It is a **bitmask**. Live values decode as:

- `524288` = `noStatusFlagsSet` (2^19)
- `524416` = `noStatusFlagsSet | noQuickScanHappenedForSpecifiedPeriod` (2^19 + 2^7)

`productStatusBucketFor` (`defenderreport.go:216-221`) looks up `strings.ToLower(raw)` in `productStatusBuckets` (`:185-211`), whose 26 keys are enum **names** (`"nostatus"`, `"servicenotrunning"`, `"avsignaturesoutofdate"`, …). A numeric bitmask hits none of them:

```go
func productStatusBucketFor(raw string) string {
	if b, ok := productStatusBuckets[strings.ToLower(raw)]; ok {
		return b
	}
	return "other"
}
```

Result: **`intune_defender_agents_product_status{status="other"}` is 100% of the fleet, every cycle**, and the panel looks healthy because `other` is a designed-in bucket rather than an error.

This map is wrong twice over: name-keyed lookup against a numeric value, **and** scalar lookup against a flags field. Note `"nostatus"` is enum member `0` - not the same thing as `noStatusFlagsSet` (524288), so even a correct int-keyed table would need to distinguish them. `DeviceState` (`defenderreport.go:327`) is emitted raw and never bucketed; it does have a `_loc` sibling.

### 3. `intune.cert_inventory` - UNVERIFIED, do not claim it is broken

m7kni has **zero device certificates**, so `AllDeviceCertificates` returns a header row and no data. The header carries **no `CertificateStatus_loc`**.

The mechanism is identical to #2. `certificateStatusBucketFor` (`certinventoryreport.go:152-157`) is exact-match (no `ToLower`) against camelCase name keys (`"issued"`, `"enrollmentSucceeded"`, `"revoked"`, …) - so **if** it returns codes, every row buckets to `other`, and the severity escalation at `:377-380` never fires:

```go
severity := telemetry.SeverityInfo
if stateBucket == "failed" || stateBucket == "revoked" {
	severity = telemetry.SeverityWarn
}
```

That would mean every failed/revoked certificate logs at INFO - an alerting hole, not a cosmetic label. **But it is not measured.** The code comment at `certinventoryreport.go:47-53` already anticipates the `other` fallback and blames an "unverified enum vocabulary"; the real mechanism is the missing `LocalizationType`. Confirm against a tenant with certificates before asserting.

## Not affected - do not over-scope

- **Defender's five boolean columns are fine.** `evaluateSignals` (`defenderreport.go:165-173`) routes them through `rowBoolDefault` → `strconv.ParseBool` (`:226-237`), which accepts `"1"`/`"0"` as well as `"true"`/`"false"`. `intune.defender_agents.count{signal}` is correct either way.
- Counts, identifiers, free text, dates, `EnhancedKeyUsage`/`KeyUsage` are not enums.
- These three metrics appear on **no dashboard** (zero hits across `dashboards/*.json`), which is likely why nobody noticed.

## Fix options (they differ per collector - one blanket change will not do)

- `Platform` / `DeviceState`: read the `_loc` sibling already in the `Row` map, **or** set `LocalizationType: "ReplaceLocalizableValues"` to get names in the primary column. Prefer whichever keeps the raw code available - the house pattern (`m365/activity/activity.go:365-380`, `recordtypes.go:85`) is to emit the lossless code unconditionally and the name only when it resolves, precisely because Microsoft's published tables do not cover every live value (#100).
- `ProductStatus`: needs client-side **bitmask** decoding against an int-keyed table. No `_loc` exists. Decide what a multi-flag value means for a single-valued `status` label before writing it - that's a modelling decision, not a lookup fix.
- `CertificateStatus`: measure first.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `intune.app_install_status` emits a decoded platform, live-verified against the wire (not a fixture)
- [ ] `appinstallreport_test.go:214`'s `"windows"` fixture replaced with a fixture matching what the API actually returns
- [ ] `intune_defender_agents_product_status` no longer buckets 100% of the fleet to `other`, live-verified
- [ ] `ProductStatus` bitmask decoding handles multi-flag values explicitly
- [ ] `CertificateStatus` measured against a tenant with certificates; fixed or closed as correct on evidence
- [ ] Every export collector's enum columns audited, not just the three named here
- [ ] `make check` green

## Do not

- Do not assume all three collectors have the same bug. Measured: `Platform` has a `_loc` sibling, `ProductStatus` does not and is a bitmask, `CertificateStatus` is unknown.
- Do not "fix" the bucket maps by adding numeric keys without deciding the bitmask question - `524416` is two flags, not one.
- Do not trust a fixture over the wire. This shipped because `appinstallreport_test.go:214` asserted a value the API has never sent.
- Do not claim `intune.cert_inventory` is broken until it is measured on a tenant with certificates.

Refs #100
title: fix(intune): export reports return raw enum CODES, not names - `platform=2` ships live, and Defender's status bucket can never match

body:
## The trigger

A live `intune.app_install_status` record carries `platform=2` and nothing else that says which transport produced it. There is no way, from an emitted record, to tell whether it came from Graph polling, blob ingest, the O365 Management Activity API, or a reports-export job. (`platform=2` itself is a separate bug - filed as the export-enum issue.)

## Verified: no record carries provenance

There are four ingest transports today: `internal/logpipeline` (paged Graph GET), `internal/blobpipeline` (#89), `internal/o365pipeline` (#100), `internal/jobpipeline` (audit query API), plus `internal/exportjob`. **A record from any of them is indistinguishable from a record from any other.**

- The single `LogEvent` implementation (`internal/telemetry/emitter.go:185-200`) stamps nothing. It sets timestamp/severity/body/event-name and `r.AddAttributes(toLogKV(ev.Attrs)...)`. Whatever the collector put in `ev.Attrs` is exactly what ships.
- All four pipelines pass `ev` through untouched: `blobpipeline.go:250-254`, `logpipeline.go:223`, `jobpipeline.go:492`, `o365pipeline.go:367-370` (the only mutation is defaulting an empty `ev.Name`).
- Resource attributes are `service.name` + (on logs only) `service.version` + SDK/OS/host/narrow-process detectors (`internal/telemetry/provider.go:211-241`). Nothing transport-derived.

**The sign-in case is the sharp one.** Blob and polled sign-ins share `mapSignIn` (`entra/signins/signins.go:124-171`); the blob path delegates to it (`blob.go:147-161`) and adds nothing. Both hardcode `Name: eventName` where `eventName = "entra.signin"` (`signins.go:49`). So a blob-ingested sign-in and a Graph-polled sign-in emit **byte-identical records** - same event name, same attributes, same body.

That was a deliberate design win (one mapper, drop-in equivalent sources, per CLAUDE.md) and it is right. The gap: the *collector* names do distinguish them - `entra.signins.non_interactive` vs `entra.signins.non_interactive.blob`, whose doc at `blob.go:63-76` says the `.blob` suffix exists "so the two are separable in config and self-obs" - but the collector name never reaches a data record. It appears only on `graph2otel.scrape.*`, and `internal/collector/selfobs.go:73-82` is explicit that this is the whole set:

```go
// selfObsAttrs builds the bounded attribute set shared by every scrape.*
// metric point: the collector name, plus the tenant ID when non-empty. These
// are the ONLY attributes self-obs metrics carry — no per-entity identifiers.
```

### Why this matters, concretely

#138 measured Azure blob delivery as at-least-once: ~2.3% of blob records arrive more than once, and `blobpipeline` does not dedupe. `blob.go:138-146` says polled/blob overlap is "dedupe-able downstream" on `id`. But with no provenance attribute an operator cannot:

- measure the blob-vs-poll split at all;
- attribute a duplicate to a transport (is this #138's at-least-once, or both sources running?);
- drop one lane at query time while keeping the other.

The `.blob` naming exists specifically to keep the two separable, and that separation is discarded at the emit boundary.

## Verified: attribute names are 198 bare literals with no registry

| measure | count |
| --- | --- |
| collectors | 58 |
| `setStr(attrs, "literal", …)` call sites | 310 |
| distinct attribute-key literals | 198 |
| duplicate `func setStr` definitions (one per package) | 26 |
| attribute constants in `internal/semconv/attrs.go` | 3 |
| collectors using a shared constant for a **data** attribute | **0** |

`internal/semconv/attrs.go` is 35 lines and exports `AttrMetricName`, `AttrCollector`, `AttrTenantID` - all infrastructure-only, consumed by `internal/license`, `internal/collector/selfobs.go`, `internal/collector/scheduler.go`, `internal/telemetry/cardinality.go`. The five collector packages that import `semconv` reference only `UnitDimensionless` / `UnitSeconds`.

Drift this has already produced, all live in `main` today:

- **Aliased keys**: `m365/activity/activity.go:356` emits both `workload` and `service` from the same variable. Discoverable only by reading the file.
- **One key, two meanings**: `tenant_id` is *our* tenant on self-obs metrics (`semconv.AttrTenantID`) and *Microsoft's* tenant parsed from the record payload at `entra/securityalerts/securityalerts.go:104` and `entra/securityincidents/securityincidents.go:147` (`setStr(attrs, "tenant_id", str(rec, "tenantId"))`).
- **`source` is already overloaded three ways**: `intune/certificates/certificates.go:507` `{"source": "managed_device"}` and `:566` `{"source": "user_pfx"}` (which Graph endpoint), and `entra/riskdetections/riskdetections.go:120` passes through Microsoft's own `source` field.

That last one is load-bearing for the design: **a provenance attribute named `source` would collide with three existing meanings.** Pick a different name.

## What to build

1. **A provenance attribute on every emitted record.** Name it deliberately (`source` is taken). Values are the transport: Graph poll / blob / O365 activity feed / reports export. It is bounded (5 values), so it is metric-label-safe under #112 as well as log-safe.
2. **Stamp it in the pipeline, not in 58 collectors.** ~~The four engines are the only places that know the transport~~ — **WRONG, measured twice: 15 collectors call `LogEvent` directly with no engine, and `internal/exportjob` never emits at all. Stamping is at the emitter boundary; see the two design comments below.** The four engines are the only places that know the transport, and `mapSignIn` is deliberately shared across two of them - so a collector-side stamp would have to thread a flag through the one mapper this design exists to keep single. The engine wrapping `LogEvent` is the natural seam.
3. **An attribute-name registry with constants**, extending `internal/semconv` past its 3 infrastructure constants to cover data attributes. Kill the 26 duplicated `setStr` helpers while you are there.
4. **A gate**, in the same spirit as #140 (which covers *signal* names - this covers *attribute* names; together they are the registry #140 argues for). At minimum: no duplicate/aliased keys, no key with two meanings.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Every emitted log record carries a provenance attribute identifying its transport — `ingest_transport`, wired in 62c3850
- [x] ~~The attribute is stamped by the engine, not per-collector~~, and `mapSignIn` stays a single shared mapper — **CORRECTED: engine-only is impossible.** `internal/exportjob` has zero `LogEvent` call sites, so `report_export` has no engine seam and its 3 collectors must stamp themselves. Honest form: stamped at the **emitter boundary**, transport supplied by whichever layer knows it. `mapSignIn` stays single. See the wiring comment.
- [x] A blob-sourced and a Graph-polled `entra.signin` for the same event are distinguishable by that attribute alone, and remain identical in every other respect (so they stay dedupe-able on `id`) — gated by `TestBlobAndPolledSignInDifferOnlyByIngestTransport`, mutation-verified against 3 mutations
- [x] The provenance attribute name does not collide with the three existing `source` meanings — `ingest_transport`
- [ ] Data attribute names come from a registry of constants, not bare literals at 310 call sites
- [ ] The 26 duplicated `setStr` helpers are one helper
- [ ] `workload`/`service` aliasing at `activity.go:356` resolved or documented as intentional
- [ ] The two meanings of `tenant_id` are disambiguated
- [ ] A test gates attribute-name drift (pairs with #140) — *registry half, not started*
- [x] `make check` green (62c3850)

## Do not

- Do not fork `mapSignIn` into a blob variant and a polled variant. The single mapper is correct and CLAUDE.md pins it: an attribute added for one source must be right for the other.
- Do not name the provenance attribute `source`.
- Do not put per-entity data on metric labels while touching this (#112).
- Do not treat this as #140. #140 gates metric/log **event names**; this is **attribute names** + provenance. They want the same registry, from opposite ends.

Refs #89, #100, #112, #138, #140
