## Design premise is incomplete: there is a **fifth** emit path, and engine-only stamping would silently miss 15 collectors

The body's item 2 says: *"Stamp it in the pipeline, not in 58 collectors. The four engines are the
only places that know the transport."* **The four engines are not the only places that emit.**
Measured against the tree today:

```
$ grep -rln "LogEvent(" internal/collectors/ --include="*.go" | grep -v _test | wc -l
15
```

Fifteen collectors call `telemetry.LogEvent` **directly**, bypassing all four pipelines:

```
purview/labels                  intune/manageddevices        intune/malware
intune/certificates             intune/appprotection         intune/appinstallreport
intune/defenderreport           intune/certinventoryreport   entra/credentialexpiry
entra/domains                   entra/mfaregistration        entra/roles
entra/consent                   entra/signinactivity         entra/risk
```

These are the `SnapshotCollector` log twins — the #114/#110 shape (bounded gauge + one log per
entity, one fetch), of which `entra/risk` is the reference. They poll Graph directly and emit inline;
no pipeline is involved. The four engines each have exactly one `LogEvent` call site
(`logpipeline.go:223`, `blobpipeline.go:254`, `jobpipeline.go:537`, `o365pipeline.go:370`), and none
of them is on these collectors' path.

`[live-measured 2026-07-17, #141]`

### Why this matters more than a missed count

Stamping only in the four engines satisfies the letter of AC1 for pipeline-sourced records and
**silently fails it for 15 collectors**. The failure mode is the bad one: an operator filtering
`ingest_transport="graph"` would get logpipeline's records and silently miss `entra/risk`,
`entra/roles`, `intune/manageddevices` and twelve others. A provenance attribute that is *absent on a
quarter of the collectors* is worse than no provenance attribute, because absence reads as "not that
transport" rather than "not stamped".

This is structurally **the same bug as the #139/#100 incident** recorded in CLAUDE.md: *"a fourth
registration path landed and the coverage test stayed green over a missing collector"* — a design
enumerated the paths it knew about, a path outside the enumeration existed, and the gate could not
see it. Enumerating "the four engines" repeats that mistake one layer down.

### The chokepoint is the emitter, not the engines

CLAUDE.md already names the real seam: *"**Telemetry emitter facade** (`internal/telemetry`) — the
only thing touching OTLP."* There is exactly **one** `LogEvent` implementation
(`emitter.go:185`). Everything — all four engines and all 15 direct callers — funnels through it.
That is the only boundary with no fifth path behind it, because it is the boundary by construction.

Proposed: stamp at the emitter boundary via a per-transport decorator, e.g.
`telemetry.WithTransport(e, TransportBlob)`, so each engine wraps its own emitter and the composition
root hands snapshot collectors a `TransportGraph`-stamped one. The property worth buying is that an
**unstamped emit should be impossible or loud, never silently defaulted**. A default of "graph" in the
base emitter would reintroduce exactly the silent-lie failure this issue exists to remove.

### Consequence for the value set

The body says "bounded (5 values)" in one place and lists four transports in another. With the fifth
path visible the honest set is five engines but the transports are:

| value | source |
| --- | --- |
| `graph` | `logpipeline` **and** the 15 direct-emitting snapshot collectors |
| `blob` | `blobpipeline` |
| `o365_activity` | `o365pipeline` |
| `audit_query` | `jobpipeline` |
| `report_export` | `exportjob` |

Note `graph` covers two code paths, which is correct — it is the *transport* that is being named, not
the engine. Still bounded, so still metric-label-safe under #112.

### Naming — candidates checked for collision

All free as of today (`grep` over `internal/`, non-test): `ingest_transport`, `transport`,
`ingest_path`, `ingest_source`, `provenance` — 0 hits each. `source` remains disqualified (three live
meanings, re-confirmed on #140). Recommending **`ingest_transport`**: "transport" is already the
house term (CLAUDE.md: *"Four ingest engines, one per transport shape"*, *"Transport is exclusive per
collector"*), and the `ingest_` prefix keeps it from being read as the OTLP transport (gRPC/HTTP),
which is a different thing this project also has.

### Does not touch #143

`tenant_id` stays self-obs-only. This adds a new bounded key; it does not inject anything into domain
signals beyond that key, so #143's live-verified design decision is unaffected and is not being
reopened here.

## Second hole, found while wiring: `exportjob` never emits at all — so a "graph" default mislabels 3 collectors **today**

The previous comment established that 15 collectors bypass the engines. Wiring the decorator surfaced
a sharper version of the same problem, and it changes the design rather than just widening it.

**`internal/exportjob` has zero `LogEvent` call sites.** The four engines with one each are
`logpipeline.go:223`, `blobpipeline.go:254`, `jobpipeline.go:537`, `o365pipeline.go:370`. `exportjob`
is not an emitting engine — it creates/polls/downloads a job and hands the parsed rows back, and its
**collectors** emit directly:

```
intune/appinstallreport    intune/defenderreport    intune/certinventoryreport
```

All three are in the 15 direct emitters. So `report_export` — one of the five transport values this
issue asks for — **has no engine seam to stamp from**. It can only be stamped by those three
collectors.

### Why this kills the tempting shortcut

The natural wiring is two layers: the Scheduler wraps its emitter `TransportGraph` (the truthful
default for the snapshot collectors that poll Graph and emit inline), and each engine re-wraps with
its own transport. Given `transportEmitter` precedence where the **outermost stamp wins**, that works
for blob / o365 / audit_query — the engine's wrapper is outermost and the Scheduler's inner `graph`
correctly does not clobber it.

**It silently mislabels the three export collectors as `graph`.** They never pass through an engine
that could override, so the Scheduler's default is the only stamp they get, and it is wrong. This is
not a hypothetical future-engine risk — it is three shipped collectors, today, and the failure is
exactly the one this issue exists to remove: an attribute that confidently states the wrong
provenance is worse than no attribute.

`[live-measured 2026-07-17, #141]` — `grep -rn "LogEvent(" internal/exportjob/` returns nothing;
the three collectors' own `LogEvent` calls are in their `Collect`.

### Consequence for the AC list

AC2 as written — *"The attribute is stamped by the engine, not per-collector"* — **cannot hold for
`report_export`**, because no engine emits it. The honest form is: stamped at the **emitter
boundary**, with the transport supplied by whichever layer knows it — the engine where one exists,
and the three export collectors themselves where none does. That is three `WithTransport` call sites
that are unavoidable, not a shortcut being taken.

The `mapSignIn` constraint AC2 was really protecting is unaffected: it stays a single shared mapper,
because the stamp never enters the mapper.

### Status of the build

`telemetry.WithTransport` + `semconv.AttrIngestTransport` are built and tested (5 transports, copy
semantics under `-race`, outermost-stamp precedence, metrics-untouched). Mutation-verified rather
than trusted: the naive in-place stamp fails the mutation test and trips the race detector by
crossing values between two transports sharing one mapper's map; removing the precedence guard fails
`TestWithTransportOutermostStampWins` with `"graph", want "blob"`.

Provenance is **log-only** by decision: adding a label to an existing metric changes its series
identity and would break dashboards/alerts on the current normalized names (#82). Log attributes are
Loki structured metadata (#90), so adding one is additive. Pinned by
`TestWithTransportLeavesMetricsUnstamped`.

**Not yet wired** into the Scheduler / engines / the three export collectors — the export collectors'
files are held by the concurrent #142 work. Wiring + the blob-vs-graph `entra.signin` equivalence
gate is the remaining work.

## Wired. Provenance half is done; the attribute-registry half is not.

`62c3850`, `make check` green. Every emitted log record now names its transport. The decorator from `603cd69` is no longer dead code.

### What landed

| layer | transport | where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `logpipeline` | `graph` | `Poll` entry, once per cycle |
| `blobpipeline` | `blob` | `Poll` entry |
| `jobpipeline` | `audit_query` | `Run` entry |
| `o365pipeline` | `o365_activity` | `Collect` entry |
| `intune/appinstallreport`, `intune/defenderreport`, `intune/certinventoryreport` | `report_export` | each collector's `Collect` — no engine seam exists |
| the 12 remaining direct emitters | `graph` | composition root wraps the Scheduler's emitter (`tenants.go:204`) |

All 19 non-test `LogEvent` call sites are accounted for. Stamping is once per collection cycle, not per record.

**Self-obs is untouched, verified rather than assumed:** `emitScrapeMetrics`, `emitCheckpointPersistError` and `exportjob`'s `graph2otel.export.*` emit **metrics only** — zero `LogEvent` calls between them. So the Scheduler's log-only decorator cannot stamp a self-obs record with a transport it doesn't have. `[live-measured 2026-07-17, #141]` (grep over `internal/collector/selfobs.go`, `internal/license`, `internal/graphclient`, `internal/exportjob`).

### The gates, each mutation-verified

A passing gate proves nothing until it is shown to fail, so each was broken on purpose:

**The key AC** — `TestBlobAndPolledSignInDifferOnlyByIngestTransport`. It drives **both real engines from one live-pinned record**: the blob side gets the diagnostic-settings envelope, the polled side gets that envelope's inner `properties` object (which IS the Graph signIn resource). Not two fixtures asserted to agree — one record arriving two ways, which is the production case.

| mutation | result |
| --- | --- |
| blob stamp removed | FAIL — `blob record ingest_transport = "", want "blob"` |
| blob mislabelled `graph` | FAIL — `"graph", want "blob"` + `the two transports are indistinguishable` |
| `mapSignIn` forked per-transport | FAIL — `attr "blob_only_extra" present on the blob record but absent on the polled one` |

The third matters most: it is the mutation that **satisfies "distinguishable" while silently destroying dedupe-ability on `id`**. That is the failure the AC pair exists to catch, and the reason the single shared mapper is pinned.

**`TestEveryEngineStampsItsOwnTransport` now exists.** The doc comment in `transport.go` referenced it while it did not exist — a false claim, now made true. It deliberately **does not trust its own list**: it reads the tree, so a fifth `*pipeline` package fails the build until registered. A hand-maintained enumeration of engines would repeat the #139/#100 incident exactly ("a fourth registration path landed and the coverage test stayed green over a missing collector"). Mutation-verified: `internal/fakepipeline` → FAIL; logpipeline stamp removed → FAIL.

**`TestExportJobStillHasNoEmitSeam`** pins the fact that forced the three-collector stamping, so it gets revisited if `exportjob` ever grows an emit path.

### AC corrections

**AC2 as written is impossible and the body is now edited to say so.** *"The attribute is stamped by the engine, not per-collector"* cannot hold for `report_export`: `internal/exportjob` has zero `LogEvent` call sites. The honest form, now in the body: **stamped at the emitter boundary, transport supplied by whichever layer knows it**. The constraint AC2 was really protecting is intact — `mapSignIn` stays one shared mapper, because the stamp never enters it.

### Weakest link, stated plainly

The composition-root baseline (`tenants.go`) is the one link with no behavioral test — `setupTenant` needs a live credential to reach a Scheduler. It is guarded by a source-level assertion (`cmd/graph2otel/transport_test.go`, mutation-verified), which proves the line is **present**, not that it works. The decorator's own tests cover the latter. Flagging it rather than implying full coverage.

Related: the known limit of the baseline shape is that a future non-Graph engine which forgets to wrap inherits `graph` rather than failing loudly. `TestNoUnregisteredIngestEngineExists` is what closes that for `*pipeline` packages.

### Still open on this issue — the registry half

Deliberately not attempted here; this was the provenance unit. Remaining ACs: the 198 bare attribute literals → a `semconv` registry, the 26 duplicated `setStr` helpers → one, `workload`/`service` aliasing at `activity.go:356`, the two meanings of `tenant_id`, and the attribute-name drift gate. Recommend splitting those into their own issue so this one can close on the provenance work — they are a different shape of change (mechanical, 310 call sites, high diff / low risk) and pair with #140.

## Closing — provenance is done. The registry half is split out.

Maintainer decision (2026-07-17): split, rather than let a large mechanical job block a finished piece of work from closing.

**Landed and live:** `ingest_transport` on every emitted log record — `603cd69` (decorator) + `62c3850` (wiring). All 19 non-test emit sites accounted for, stamped at the emitter boundary, with the blob-vs-Graph `entra.signin` equivalence gate mutation-verified against three mutations including the subtle one (forking `mapSignIn`, which satisfies "distinguishable" while silently destroying dedupe on `id`).

Two premises in this issue's body were measured false along the way and are corrected in place: *"the four engines are the only places that know the transport"* (15 collectors emit with no engine; `exportjob` never emits at all), and AC2's *"stamped by the engine, not per-collector"* (impossible for `report_export`).

**The registry half — 199 bare literals, 27 duplicate `setStr` helpers, the `workload`/`service` alias, and `tenant_id`'s two meanings — is now its own issue.** It is a different shape of change and pairs with #140's capture, which already records attribute keys per signal.

⚠️ One thing changed under it: **#143 has been decided in favour of adding `tenant_id` to every domain metric.** That makes the `tenant_id` double-meaning *worse* — `securityalerts`/`securityincidents` emit a `tenant_id` log attribute meaning **Microsoft's** tenant. The registry issue carries that warning; sequence the two deliberately.

body:
## What

Nothing in this repo gates the signals graph2otel actually emits. Every gauge, counter, log event name and attribute set in `docs/collectors.md`'s signals columns is hand-maintained & referenced by **zero tests**. `make check` will never notice when they drift.

#139 fixes half of it. It generates the registry-knowable facts (name, kind, interval, experimental/license gating, required permissions, blob container/cursor/role) and gates those. It **cannot** cover the signals columns, and that limit is structural rather than laziness: metric names and event names are string literals inside each collector's `Collect()`. The registry never sees them.

So even after #139 lands, the more valuable half of that reference is still unguarded.

## Verified, 2026-07-16

Walked the code rather than assuming:

- No signals registry, no declared-signals interface, no test anywhere gating a metric name or an event name.
- `docs/collectors.md` is referenced by no test at all.
- The **only** generated artifact in the repo is `docs/env-vars.md`, from `config.example.yaml` via `TestEnvReferenceDocInSync` + `-update`. The machinery exists. It covers config keys & nothing else.

**Metrics are not gated either.** This is not "logs are missing the treatment metrics get". Neither has it.

## Why this is more than a docs chore

The cardinality rule (#112) is enforced by convention & per-collector guard tests. Nothing enforces it globally. A collector that emits a per-entity metric label, or that buckets a count & emits no log twin, is invisible to CI.

Not hypothetical - that is #83, found today. `intune.app_install_status` shipped `app_name` as a metric label (1,870 series on a 6-device tenant) **and** emitted no log twin at all, while both its sibling export collectors have twins. The #114 sweep missed it and nothing has caught it since. #83's own body claims the collector "already emits per-row logs". It does not. A gate catches both halves on the first commit.

## Three mechanisms - pick deliberately, do not default

**a) A declared-signals interface:** collectors declare their emitted metric names/units, event names & attribute keys; the generator reads them. Cheap and simple, but it creates a second source of truth that can itself drift from what `Collect()` actually calls. Only honest if something cross-checks the declaration against real emissions.

**b) Static analysis / AST walk** of the emit call sites. No second source of truth, but brittle the moment a name is computed, passed through a helper, or built in a loop. Several collectors already do exactly that.

**c) Recorder-capture harness:** run each collector against a faked Graph client + the in-memory `Recorder`, capture what it actually emitted, golden it with `-update` (the `TestEnvReferenceDocInSync` pattern). Truth by construction - the doc reflects real emissions, not a claim about them. Cost is a fixture per collector across 57 collectors, but **most collectors already have precisely this test setup**, so the marginal cost is far lower than it looks.

(c) is the right answer. Confirm the "most collectors already have this setup" claim against the real test files before building on it - that came from walking the code, not from running anything.

## The strongest version of this

A Recorder-capture gate doesn't have to stop at documentation. Once you have captured what every collector actually emits, you can assert on it:

- No metric attribute key appears in a per-entity denylist (UPN, object id, IP, correlation id, serial, device id).
- Any collector fetching per-entity rows emits a log twin.

That turns #112's hard rule from a convention people remember into a gate that fails the build. #110/#111/#114 exist because twelve collectors quietly broke that rule, and #83 is a thirteenth that survived the sweep. That is where the value is. The generated doc is almost a side effect.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Decide the mechanism (a/b/c), with the reasoning recorded here
- [ ] Signals columns in `docs/collectors.md` are generated from real emissions, not hand-maintained
- [ ] A drift gate fails a plain `go test` when a collector's emitted signals do not match the doc
- [ ] Wired into `scripts/regen-generated.sh` and its header comment, alongside `docs/env-vars.md` and #139's collector reference
- [ ] Covers metrics **and** log events - both are ungated today
- [ ] Decide whether to extend it into a mechanical #112 cardinality gate (per-entity denylist on metric attrs; twin required), or file that separately
- [ ] Hand-written prose that no generator can know survives - same constraint as #139
- [ ] `make check` green

## Do not

- Do not hand-fix the signals columns and close this. Same failure as #139: it drifts again by next month, and the gate is the deliverable.
- Do not duplicate #139's registry gate. That one covers registry facts; this one covers emissions. Different sources, same doc.
- Do not build (a) without a cross-check. An undetected lie in a declaration is worse than an obviously stale table.

Refs #139, #112, #114, #83

## Mechanism decision: **(c) recorder-capture**, and the claim it rests on is confirmed

The body asks for the mechanism to be chosen with reasoning recorded, and explicitly says to confirm
the "most collectors already have this setup" claim **against the real test files** before building
on it, since it came from reading code rather than running anything. Confirmed:

```
$ find internal/collectors -name "*_test.go" | wc -l
57
$ grep -rl "Recorder\|telemetrytest" internal/collectors/ --include="*_test.go" | wc -l
52
```

**52 of 57 collector test files (91%) already drive a faked client into the in-memory Recorder.**
The claim holds, and it is the deciding fact: (c)'s "a fixture per collector across 57 collectors"
cost is largely already paid. The marginal work is capturing what the Recorder already sees and
goldening it, not building 57 harnesses.

`[live-measured 2026-07-17, #140]` — grep counts against the tree at that date, not an estimate.

### Why not (a) or (b)

- **(a) declared-signals interface** — rejected on the body's own terms: it creates a second source
  of truth, and an undetected lie in a declaration is worse than a visibly stale table. It would only
  be honest with a cross-check, and that cross-check *is* (c) — so (a) is strictly (c) plus a
  redundant declaration to keep in sync.
- **(b) AST walk** — rejected: brittle exactly where this repo already lives. Names are computed and
  passed through helpers today (`entra/signins` hardcodes `Name: eventName` from a package-level
  `eventName` const, and `mapSignIn` is shared across two transports by design). A static walk would
  need to constant-fold across packages to see them.

(c) is truth-by-construction: the doc reflects real emissions because it is produced from them.

### Sequencing note — this and #141 are the same registry

#141 covers **attribute** names; this covers **signal** names. Its counts re-verified today against
the tree (they have drifted slightly since filing, which is itself the argument for a gate):

| measure | #141 claimed | today |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `setStr(attrs, "literal", …)` call sites | 310 | **312** |
| distinct attribute-key literals | 198 | **199** |
| duplicate `func setStr` definitions | 26 | **27** |

The `source` three-way overload is confirmed live in `main`: `intune/certificates/certificates.go:507`
(`"source": "managed_device"`), `:566` (`"source": "user_pfx"`), and
`entra/riskdetections/riskdetections.go:120` (passes through Microsoft's own `source` field). A
provenance attribute named `source` would be a fourth meaning — #141's conclusion stands.

Recorder-capture is the natural substrate for **both**: once each collector's real emissions are
captured, asserting on attribute keys (denylist, no aliasing) and on signal names are two assertions
over the same captured data. Building #141's registry first and #140's capture second would mean
writing the cross-check twice.

## The #112 gate is built and live (94f6ca9). The doc-generation half is not — and exploration found a real blocker for it.

`make check` green. Taking the issue's own framing seriously — *"That turns #112's hard rule from a convention people remember into a gate that fails the build. ... That is where the value is. The generated doc is almost a side effect."* — the gate is done and the side effect is not.

### What landed

`internal/signalcapture`, plus one `TestMain` per collector package (51) and a completeness gate in `cmd/graph2otel`.

**The shape is the interesting part.** `telemetrytest.New` self-registers, so a package's `TestMain` sees the union of everything its tests emitted **without any test opting in**. That was forced by measurement, not taste: there are **364 `telemetrytest.New()` call sites across 51 packages**, so a per-call-site design is a huge diff and — far worse — silently incomplete the first time someone forgets. Self-registration means every test written from now on is judged by a gate its author has never heard of. `[live-measured 2026-07-17, #140]`

The completeness half (`TestEveryCollectorPackageEnforcesCardinality`) **walks the tree rather than trusting a list**, so a new collector package fails until it installs the gate. A hand-kept list would have repeated the #139/#100 incident verbatim.

Both halves mutation-verified: removing a package's `TestMain` fails the completeness gate; each denylisted key fails on a metric label; per-entity keys on a **log** do not fire.

### The finding that shaped the denylist — a key name cannot see boundedness

**The first draft flagged two collectors, and both were CORRECT code.**

`app_name` was on the list, citing #83 (1,870 series on a six-device tenant). Run against the tree it immediately failed `intune.detected_apps.device_count` and `intune.uxa.app_crash_count`. Reading them: **both bound `app_name` with a fixed, package-level allow-list** (`defaultAllowedApps`) and filter at the emit site, so their series count is a **compile-time constant** — precisely the bounded aggregate #112 asks for.

#83's `app_name` was the whole detected-app **catalog** (unbounded); theirs is an **allow-list** (bounded). Same key, opposite cardinality, decided by collector logic a key-name check cannot observe. **The gate was wrong, not the collectors** — I was one step from filing two bogus bug reports and "fixing" working code.

So the bar for an entry is stricter than "is often per-entity": a key belongs only where a **bounded use is implausible** — nobody allow-lists UPNs or serial numbers. Keys a collector could legitimately bound (`app_name`, `issuer_name` — a tenant has a handful of issuing CAs) are excluded. A false positive trains people to add exemptions, and an exempted gate is worse than none. Pinned by `TestAllowListBoundedAppNameIsNotAViolation` so nobody re-adds it. `[live-measured 2026-07-17, #140]`

**Consequence for this issue's premise:** the gate found **zero** existing violations after correction. #83 is closed and its collector is genuinely fixed. The gate's value is preventing the *next* one, not finding a current one — and "the tree is clean on these keys" is now a verified fact rather than a hope.

### Also caught: my own leak

Unconditional retention of Recorders made `logpipeline`'s `TestScalePollMemoryBoundedByWindowNotBacklog` fail on the first run — correctly; a Recorder holds every record it saw. Retention is now opt-in (`telemetrytest.StartCapture`, called only by `signalcapture.Main`), so only packages running the gate pay for it. The existing suite caught a real defect in the new gate, which is a decent advert for both.

### Known limit, stated rather than implied

The union is a **lower bound**: a code path no test exercises emits nothing, so it cannot be judged. This proves *"nothing a test exercises breaks the rule"*, not *"nothing breaks the rule"*. It fails safe — it never green-lights an emission it has seen — and it is in the package doc, not just here.

### The doc-generation half: blocked on attribution, and AC1 needs rethinking

Not attempted, and I do not think it should be attempted as written.

**The blocker.** The capture is **per package**, but `docs/collectors.md` is per **collector row**, and a package can host several collectors (`entra/signins` has 4 polled streams + 3 blob). Emitted records carry no collector name — only self-obs does — so a package capture **cannot be attributed to a collector name**. Generating per-collector signal columns from it would be approximate, and an approximate generated doc is a lie with a machine's authority behind it. Options: reflect the factory's package path (hacky), drive each collector individually from the registry through a fake `GraphClient` (feasible — it is a 2-method interface — but needs ~57 URL→JSON fixtures, duplicating fixtures the tests already have), or accept package granularity.

**AC1 is worth amending.** It says the signals columns should be *"generated from real emissions"*. But the doc's compressed prose (``intune.malware.overview.detected_devices`/`.total`/`.by_severity{severity}``) is hand-written **for readability**, and a generator would replace it with a flat list — a real regression for the reader. AC3 (*"a drift gate fails when a collector's emitted signals do not match the doc"*) is the AC that carries the value, and it is satisfiable **without** generating anything: keep `annotations.go`'s prose as the declaration and cross-check it against the capture at package granularity (set equality of metric names). That is mechanism (a) made honest by (c) — which this issue explicitly allows: *"(a) ... Only honest if something cross-checks the declaration against real emissions."* No attribution needed, readability preserved, doc cannot lie.

Recommend: amend AC1 to the cross-check, or split the doc half into its own issue. Happy to build the cross-check next; wanted the design fork recorded before spending the cycle on it.

### AC status

- [x] Decide the mechanism (a/b/c), reasoning recorded — (c), earlier comment
- [ ] Signals columns generated from real emissions — **blocked on attribution; recommend amending to a cross-check (above)**
- [ ] A drift gate fails when emitted signals do not match the doc — **not built; tractable at package granularity**
- [ ] Wired into `scripts/regen-generated.sh` — not built (nothing generated yet)
- [x] Covers metrics **and** log events — the capture does both; the #112 gate is metrics-only *by design*
- [x] Decide whether to extend into a mechanical #112 cardinality gate — **decided: built it**
- [ ] Hand-written prose survives — N/A until something generates
- [x] `make check` green

## AC1 update: the cross-check I proposed is ALSO wrong. Here is the proof, and what landed instead (2bf2b37).

I proposed keeping `annotations.go`'s prose as the declaration and cross-checking it against the capture. Implementing it killed it — recording that before anyone tries it again.

### Why the prose cannot be the declaration

The signal column's shorthand is **contextual, and inconsistent within a single entry**:

```
`entra.organization.directory.sync.last_sync_age_seconds`, `.age_days`, `.verified_domains.total`
```

`.age_days` continues the full name (`…directory.sync.age_days`). `.verified_domains.total` plainly does **not** hang off `directory.sync` — a human reader silently re-bases it to `entra.organization`. The base is inferred from meaning, not from grammar. Any parser would have to guess, and **a gate that guesses is worse than none** — which is the exact brittleness objection this issue used to reject mechanism (b).

That ambiguity is also the deeper point: **the prose is not a reliable declaration at all.** If a parser can misread it, so can a person. Cross-checking against it would have gated the doc against a source that is itself imprecise.

### What landed instead

Each collector package goldens the union of its real emissions to `testdata/signals.json` — metric names, log event names, and attribute keys — with a drift gate in `signalcapture.Main` and `-update` wired into `scripts/regen-generated.sh signals`.

Mutation-verified, not assumed: renaming an emitted metric fails with `signal drift (#140): emitted signals changed`.

This is **truth by construction**: produced FROM the emissions, it cannot describe a signal that does not exist. It is the substrate the generated doc needs, and it is already a drift gate on its own terms — a collector's emissions can no longer change silently, which is how the doc drifted from reality in the first place.

A golden diff is a **review prompt, not an error**: you changed what a collector emits, which is often correct — accept it with `-update`.

### The remaining blocker for the doc, stated precisely

**Attribution.** Captures are per **package**; `docs/collectors.md` rows are per **collector**. Emitted records carry no collector name (only self-obs does). Measured today: only **2 of 51** packages host more than one collector — `entra/signins` (7) and `purview/labels` (2). So it is nearly 1:1, and `entra/signins` is harmless because all 7 emit the same `entra.signin`. **`purview/labels` is the one real case**: sensitivity and retention emit different metrics, and a package-level capture would attribute both rows the union — a doc that is wrong with a machine's authority behind it.

Three ways out, none free:
1. **Reflect the factory's package path** (`runtime.FuncForPC`) to map package → collector names. Works; hacky; couples the doc gate to Go internals.
2. **Drive each collector individually from the registry** through a fake `GraphClient` (it is a 2-method interface, so this is feasible) — exact attribution, but needs ~57 URL→JSON fixtures duplicating what the tests already have.
3. **Accept package granularity** and split `purview/labels`, or label the doc honestly as per-package.

Recommend (1) or (3); (2) rebuilds fixtures that already exist. Wanted this recorded before spending a cycle on it.

### AC status

- [x] Decide the mechanism (a/b/c) — (c), recorded earlier
- [ ] Signals columns generated from real emissions — **captures exist and are gated; rendering blocked on attribution above**
- [x] A drift gate fails a plain `go test` when a collector's emitted signals change — **landed** (against the golden, not the doc; the doc is not a parseable source, see above)
- [x] Wired into `scripts/regen-generated.sh` (`signals` target) and its header comment
- [x] Covers metrics **and** log events — names + attribute keys for both
- [x] Decide whether to extend into a mechanical #112 cardinality gate — **built** (94f6ca9)
- [ ] Hand-written prose survives — N/A until something renders
- [x] `make check` green

## Progress — attribution unblocked (`504d83b`), doc generation now blocked on #164

### Landed

**`504d83b` — `purview/labels` split into `purview/sensitivitylabels` + `purview/retentionlabels`.** This was the attribution blocker: the golden is a union over a PACKAGE's tests, so a package hosting two collectors that emit different signals could say what the package emitted but never which collector emitted it.

Measured before splitting anything: **exactly 2 of 51 collector packages host >1 collector**, and only one is a problem.

| package | collectors | verdict |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `entra/signins` | 7 | **not split** — all seven emit `entra.signin`, so the union is already attributable |
| `purview/labels` | 2 | **split** — sensitivity and retention emit different signals; the only real blocker in the tree |

Proven a pure refactor: the union of the two new goldens is byte-identical to the old package's golden. Attribution now holds — sensitivity's golden owns `purview.sensitivity_label` + `purview.labels.count`; retention's owns the other four.

So `package == collector` is now true tree-wide, and this AC is met:

- [x] Decide the mechanism (a/b/c), with the reasoning recorded here
- [x] A drift gate fails a plain `go test` when a collector's emitted signals do not match the doc
- [x] Covers metrics **and** log events
- [x] Wired into `scripts/regen-generated.sh`
- [x] Extended into a mechanical #112 cardinality gate

### The remaining AC is BLOCKED — do not attempt it yet

> - [ ] Signals columns in `docs/collectors.md` are generated from real emissions, not hand-maintained

**#164** — the goldens understate what 12 of 51 collectors emit. `entra/graphactivity`'s golden is `"Logs": null` against a mapper that sets 22 attributes; `intune/auditevents` shows 4 of 18; `entra/provisioning` 3 of 14.

Cause: each package's rich live fixture only ever reaches the **mapper**, while a minimal synthetic fixture is what gets driven through the engine into a Recorder — and the golden captures emissions, so it captures the synthetic one.

**Generating the doc from these goldens would ship a reference understating graph2otel's own signal surface by up to 22 attributes on a third of its collectors** — wrong in the confident direction, which is worse than the hand-written prose it replaces. #164 is a hard prerequisite for this AC. `entra/riskdetections` (`c7864d6`) already demonstrates the fix (drive the live record end-to-end; its golden went 4 → 23).

### Correction to this issue's own framing

This issue reasoned that the doc's prose could not be cross-checked because `annotations.go`'s `Emits` shorthand re-bases contextually within one entry. That still holds. But the conclusion drawn from it — that a golden produced FROM emissions is "truth by construction" — is only half right. **It cannot describe a signal that does not exist; it can and does omit signals that do.** The gate's package doc calls this a lower bound and implies the gap is narrow. It is not. Fixed framing is part of #164.

### Scripts gotcha found while splitting

`scripts/regen-generated.sh signals` globs via `git ls-files`, which reads the **index**, not the working tree. A rename is invisible to it until staged — it will list the deleted package and neither new one. Self-heals on `git add`; worth knowing before someone debugs it.

## Fixture-honesty precondition cleared (#165)

The recorder-capture goldens this issue relies on (`testdata/signals.json`, approach **(c)**) are only trustworthy if the fixtures driving each collector's `Collect()` reflect the real wire. Until now most were hand-written from Microsoft's docs, so a golden could faithfully capture a *fictional* emission — the exact failure #165 was opened to fix.

As of #165's wave-3 completion (see rknightion/graph2otel#165), **every one of the 52 collector packages is provenance-labeled**: verbatim live capture, live-verified partial, or an explicit empty/blocked/count-only tag. So the signals goldens now reflect emissions driven by real captured wire records rather than docs-shaped placeholders. Two dead/mis-decoded mapper lines a docs fixture had kept green surfaced and were filed (#174 scripts runSummary→0, #175 sensitivitylabels description/toolTip) — the kind of drift a signals gate exists to catch, now visible because the fixtures are honest.

**One caveat this gate must respect:** where the m7kni tenant cannot reach a branch (no high-privilege consent grant, no device certificates, empty risk collections, hybrid-sync on a cloud-only tenant, etc.), that branch's fixture is *still synthetic by necessity* and is labeled in-fixture. A denylist/twin-presence assertion built on the goldens is trustworthy for the live-captured surface; the synthetic branches are documented where they live so they are not mistaken for measured.

No code change here — this is a status note that the (c) harness now rests on live fixtures tree-wide.

Done in `dc49fc1` (on main). The Metric-namespace / Log-event columns of `docs/collectors.md` are now generated from each collector package's `testdata/signals.json` golden, not hand-written. `collectordoc` resolves each collector to its package via `reflect` PkgPath (never a name→folder transform — `entra.signin_activity` lives in `entra/signinactivity`), with a named exception for the one bare `*blobpipeline.BlobCollector` (`entra.graph_activity`). Rendering is flat and fully-qualified: metric names carry their attr keys (`name{k1,k2}`), log events are bare (per-entity attr sets run 15-22 deep = noise).

**Gate:** `TestCollectorReferenceDocInSync` is now the signal drift gate for free (it diffs `Render(rows)` vs the committed doc); `Rows` additionally hard-errors on a registered collector with no golden. `scripts/regen-generated.sh` reordered to envref → signals → collectordoc (the doc now reads committed goldens).

Generation immediately paid: it fixed the `entra.organization` drift (doc said `entra.organization.directory.sync.last_sync_age_seconds`; the real metric has no `organization.` infix) and surfaced ~12 collectors' log twins + several `.*`-abbreviated metric sets the hand-written prose had silently understated. Also fixed a latent `flag redefined: update` panic (signalcapture registered its `-update` flag at package init, which collided with cmd/graph2otel's own once collectordoc imported it for types — moved into `Main`). `make check` green.

title: build(docs): nothing gates the signals we actually emit - metric AND log event names drift unguarded

body:
## What

`docs/collectors.md` is hand-maintained and has drifted. **57 collectors are registered; 49 are documented.** Nothing in `make check` notices, so it drifts silently and will keep drifting.

Generate it from the registry instead, and gate the drift in `go test` — the pattern `docs/env-vars.md` already uses (golden test + `-update`, drift gate under a plain `go test`, `make regen` for convenience). Extend the same treatment to **blob collectors**, which have no doc home in that table at all today.

## The drift, measured

Enumerated by walking the real registry (`collectors.All()` + `WindowAll()` + `BlobAll()`), not by grepping:

| collector | kind | why it is missing |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `entra.graph_activity` | blob | table is keyed on Graph endpoints; blob collectors poll none |
| `entra.signins.microsoft_service_principal` | blob | same |
| `entra.signins.service_principal.blob` | blob | same |
| `entra.signins.non_interactive.blob` | blob | same |
| `entra.security_incidents` | window | plain drift (#109) |
| `m365.unified_audit` | window | plain drift |
| `purview.sensitivity_labels` | snapshot | plain drift (#126) |
| `purview.retention_labels` | snapshot | plain drift (#126) |

Good news: **zero stale rows** — nothing documented that no longer exists. The drift is one-directional (new collectors don't get added), which is exactly the shape a generator fixes.

Note `purview.labels` does not exist — it is **two** collectors, `purview.sensitivity_labels` and `purview.retention_labels`. That is the kind of error a hand-maintained table produces and a generated one cannot.

## Why a generator rather than "just add the 8 rows"

Adding the rows fixes today and rots again by next month — it already has, twice (#109 and #126 both shipped collectors without touching this doc). The gate is the deliverable; the rows are a side effect.

There is also a self-demonstrating argument: producing the table above by grep gave the **wrong answer in both directions** — it caught metric/event names (`purview.sensitivity_label`, `purview.labels.count`) as if they were collectors, and missed collectors whose names come from spec structs (`entra.directory_audits`, `entra.provisioning`). Only walking the registry gave truth. If a careful hand-diff is unreliable, the doc cannot be maintained by hand.

## Blob collectors need a column set of their own

The current table's columns are Graph-shaped: *"the Graph API endpoint(s) it polls, the Graph application permission scope(s) it declares via `RequiredPermissions()`"*. A blob collector polls no endpoint and declares no Graph scope — it reads a container and needs the **`Storage Blob Data Reader`** data-plane role instead. Today they are documented in [`docs/blob-ingest.md`](docs/blob-ingest.md), which is right for the *narrative* but leaves them out of the reference.

Per-blob-collector, the generated reference wants:

- **container** (`insights-logs-<category>`) and the diagnostic-settings **category** it comes from
- **cursor key** (defaults to the container) — surfacing this makes a #135-style collision visible
- **interval**, **license/experimental gating** — same as every other collector
- **required role** — `Storage Blob Data Reader`, not a Graph scope
- **event name** emitted, and the fact that blob collectors emit **no metrics** (#128)
- that they only register when `blob_ingest.account_url` is set

## What already exists to build on

- `scripts/regen-generated.sh` + `TestEnvReferenceDocInSync` (golden `-update` mode; drift gate is the same test under `go test`) — the pattern to copy.
- `TestExampleConfigCoversEveryKey` / `TestHelmValuesConfigCoversEveryKey` in `internal/config/completeness_test.go` — the "nothing is missing" gate shape.
- The registry itself already exposes everything needed: `Name()`, `DefaultInterval()`, and the `Experimental` / `license.CapabilityRequirer` / `RequiredPermissions` interfaces the composition root already type-asserts on.

The awkward part: a factory needs `Deps` to construct, and the interfaces are only visible on the constructed value. `newCollector(collectors.Deps{})` works (the compile-time checks at the bottom of each collector file already do exactly this), but the generator must not accidentally require a live Graph client.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `docs/collectors.md` (or a successor) is generated from the registry, covering **all 57** collectors including blob
- [ ] A drift gate fails `go test` when a registered collector is missing from the doc — the actual deliverable
- [ ] Wired into `scripts/regen-generated.sh` and documented in its header comment alongside `docs/env-vars.md`
- [ ] Blob collectors get their own columns (container / cursor key / `Storage Blob Data Reader` / no-metrics), not forced into Graph-shaped ones
- [ ] Hand-written prose that the registry cannot know (why a collector exists, its traps) survives — this must not flatten the doc into a machine-readable table nobody reads
- [ ] `purview.labels` is not resurrected — it is two collectors
- [ ] `make check` green

## Do not

- Do not just add the 8 rows and close this. Without the gate it drifts again, and that is the whole point.
- Do not delete `docs/blob-ingest.md`'s narrative. The reference table and the "why this path exists at all" doc are different jobs.

Refs #89, #109, #126, #135

comments.body:
## Shipped: the reference is generated and the drift is gated - `5ced2e7`

`docs/collectors.md` is generated from the real registry. All **57** collectors covered; the 8 missing ones are in. `make check` green.

### The gates, proven by mutation

Both were made to fail, not just to pass. A gate that only ever passes is decoration.

Deleting a row from the doc:
```
--- FAIL: TestCollectorReferenceDocInSync
    docs/collectors.md is out of date with the collector registry — regenerate with
    `scripts/regen-generated.sh collectordoc` ... and commit the result
```

Dropping a collector's annotation, which simulates the drift that actually happens (a new collector ships undocumented):
```
--- FAIL: TestCollectorAnnotationsCoverEveryCollector
    1 registered collector(s) have no annotation in internal/collectordoc/annotations.go —
    add one (what it collects, its endpoint(s), what it emits) so the reference documents it:
      intune.app_install_status
```

### The split

`internal/collectordoc` walks `All()`/`WindowAll()`/`BlobAll()`, constructing each with a zero-value `Deps` so no live Graph client is needed. It generates only what the registry genuinely knows: name, kind, interval, experimental/license gating, permissions. Blob collectors get their own columns - container, cursor key, `Storage Blob Data Reader`, the `account_url` opt-in, and that they emit no metrics - rather than being forced into Graph-shaped ones they cannot fill.

Prose the registry cannot know lives in `annotations.go` and is spliced around the generated block, so the reference does not flatten into a machine-readable table nobody reads.

`purview.labels` is not resurrected. It is two collectors.

### Scope narrowed, and this is the useful part

**The signals columns cannot be generated, and that limit is structural.** Metric names and event names are string literals inside each collector's `Collect()`. The registry never sees them. Verified while scoping this: there is no signals registry, no declared-signals interface, and **no test anywhere gating a metric or event name** - `docs/collectors.md` was referenced by zero tests, and `docs/env-vars.md` is the repo's only generated artifact.

Worth stating flat: **metrics are not gated either.** This was never "logs lack what metrics have."

Filed as **#140**, with the argument for a Recorder-capture harness and the case for extending it into a mechanical #112 gate.

title: build(docs): generate the collector reference from the registry — 8 of 57 collectors are undocumented and nothing catches it

body:
## What

Azure Monitor's diagnostic-settings pipeline is **at-least-once**. It writes the same logical event into the blob more than once, and `blobpipeline` has no dedupe, so every blob-sourced collector ships those duplicates straight through to the backend.

Found while mapping the sign-in categories (#135). **This is not a #135 bug and not a cursor bug** — it affects `entra.graph_activity` too, which has been shipping ~2.7% duplicates since #89.

## The measurement (live, 2026-07-16)

Consistent across every category that has data. One event was observed delivered **three** times.

| category | records | re-delivered |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `MicrosoftGraphActivityLogs` | 11,134 | **302 (2.71%)** |
| `ServicePrincipalSignInLogs` | 771 | 18 (2.33%) |
| `MicrosoftServicePrincipalSignInLogs` | 216 | 6 (2.78%) |
| `NonInteractiveUserSignInLogs` | 40 | 1 (2.50%) |
| `SignInLogs` | 3 | 0 |

Overall: **25 of 1,091** sign-in records (2.29%) were written more than once.

## What a duplicate looks like

A separate line, usually in the **same** hour blob (20 of 22 cases; 2 landed in a different hour), with a **byte-identical `properties` payload** and a **fresh envelope `time`**. From `insights-logs-microsoftserviceprincipalsigninlogs/…/h=04/…/PT1H.json`:

```
line 15: envelope time 2026-07-16T04:09:50.8283497Z
line 20: envelope time 2026-07-16T04:16:16.9097253Z

both:    id              = <guid-42>
         createdDateTime = 2026-07-16T04:07:15.0223935+00:00
         correlationId   = <guid-43>
         uniqueTokenId   = _PozksnN8UuL45gN63omAA
         line length     = 3546 bytes (both)
```

6.4 minutes apart. Same event, re-delivered.

## Why the cursor cannot fix this

Both copies are real, distinct bytes. A byte-offset cursor consuming each exactly once **is behaving correctly**. Verified decisively across a cold start plus a restart: for all **1,035** emitted ids, the number of times graph2otel emitted a record **exactly equalled** the number of times Azure wrote it — zero over-emission, zero loss. The engine is faithful; the source is duplicated.

This is also why the ~3.4% cross-run overlap seen on restart is **not** a checkpoint bug: those were events Azure re-delivered into bytes appended after the first run's cursor.

## Why the polled path doesn't have this

`logpipeline` carries a **seen-id set** in its checkpoint (`{watermark, overlap_window, seen_ids}`) precisely because Graph's log endpoints have no reliable ordering and it re-fetches an overlap window. `blobpipeline` has no equivalent — it never needed one for *its own* correctness, and Azure's re-delivery was not known when #89 shipped.

So today the two sources differ materially: **polled sign-ins are deduped, blob sign-ins are not.** That belongs in #131's dual-ship reasoning.

## Design questions (not yet decided)

- **Where does the id come from?** `ContainerConfig.Map` returns `(Event, bool)`. Dedupe needs a per-category identity — `id` for sign-ins, `requestId` for Graph activity. Probably `Map` returns an id like `logpipeline`'s mapper does, or a separate `ID func(rec)`.
- **What bounds the memory?** A seen-id set over a 7-day retained window is large (MGAL alone is ~150k rows/7d). `logpipeline` bounds it by the overlap window; blob has no equivalent natural bound. Per-blob is **not** sufficient — 2 of 22 duplicates crossed hour blobs.
- **Does it persist?** It must survive restart, or a restart re-emits whatever it re-reads. (Today a restart re-reads nothing, so this is only a question once dedupe exists.)
- **Is a bounded, imperfect dedupe worth it?** Catching the same-blob 90% cheaply may beat a perfect-but-expensive one. Duplicates are byte-identical, so a content hash is viable and needs no per-category id extractor.
- **Or is downstream dedupe the honest answer?** Every collector already emits its identifying attribute. A Loki/backend-side dedupe costs graph2otel nothing and cannot go stale.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Decide: engine-side dedupe vs documented downstream dedupe, with the reasoning recorded
- [ ] If engine-side: bounded memory, persisted across restart, and correct across hour blobs
- [x] `entra.graph_activity` benefits too — it is the largest source of duplicates by volume
- [x] Re-measure the re-delivery rate **after** m7kni finishes backfilling (#137) — this rate was measured during enablement backfill and may not be steady-state
- [x] `docs/blob-ingest.md` updated with whatever is decided

## Do not

- Do not "fix" this by making the cursor re-read less. The cursor is provably exact.
- Do not assume the 2.3% is steady-state — see #137.

Refs #89, #131, #135, #137

comments.body: Currency note (2026-07-17, #146): two referenced decisions have since settled — #131 closed (no dual mode) and #144 landed (`ConflictsWith` transport mutual exclusion), so both-sources duplicates are structurally impossible now; the only duplicate source left is Azure's at-least-once delivery, which slightly strengthens the documented-downstream-dedupe option. Note also #141: downstream dedupe guidance is hampered until records carry a provenance attribute — decide these two together.

Closed by 5776acb (docs on `main`).

**Decision: dedupe downstream, not in the engine.** Reasoning recorded in `docs/blob-ingest.md` and the recipe in `docs/signals.md`; the short version:

Engine-side dedupe is the wrong trade. It would need a seen-id set that is (a) **unbounded** — Azure re-delivers across the full 7-day retention with no natural window to bound it by (MGAL alone is ~150k rows/7d), unlike `logpipeline`'s overlap window; (b) **persisted across restart**, growing the byte-offset checkpoint without limit; and (c) **correct across hour blobs** (re-deliveries cross blob boundaries, so per-blob dedup is insufficient). Against that, the byte-offset cursor is *provably exact* today, and a bounded/lossy set risks dropping genuinely distinct events to catch a 2.7–4% duplication that the backend deduplicates for free and exactly.

Every blob-sourced record already carries its identity key as **structured metadata** (`id` for sign-ins, `request_id` for `entra.graph_activity`) and the duplicates are byte-identical, so downstream dedupe is exact, costs graph2otel nothing, and cannot go stale.

**The recipe** (now in `docs/signals.md` → *Deduplicating blob-sourced records*):
- **Counts/alerts** — count distinct identity keys, not raw lines: `count(sum by (id) (count_over_time({service_name="graph2otel"} | event_name=`entra.signin` [1h])))`. Counting `count_over_time` lines directly over-counts by the duplication rate.
- **Raw SIEM export** — dedupe in the ingesting store on `id`/`request_id`, keeping any one copy. **Never assume at-most-two** — multiplicity reaches ×4.

**Acceptance criteria:** decision recorded ✅; `entra.graph_activity` covered (`request_id`) ✅; re-delivery rate re-measured at steady state (#137, in the docs) ✅; `docs/blob-ingest.md` updated ✅. The "if engine-side" line is intentionally left unchecked — that path was not taken.

The `blobpipeline` / `logpipeline` dedupe asymmetry this raised for #131's dual-ship reasoning is moot: #131 closed (no dual mode) and #144 landed transport mutual exclusion, so a record only ever travels one transport.

title: fix(blobpipeline): Azure delivers at-least-once — ~2.3% of blob-sourced records are duplicates

body:
Two questions #89 left open. Both were unanswerable while the tenant was still backfilling from enablement (2026-07-16), and #89 is now closed, so they need a home rather than living only in CLAUDE.md.

**Neither is a blocker.** The shipped design (`internal/blobpipeline`) is correct under either answer — this is about replacing a measured-but-contaminated number with a clean one, and about knowing whether a future optimisation is available.

## 1. Can a frozen hour EVER grow again once enablement backfill is done?

Measured 2026-07-16: Azure's backfill walks history oldest-first, and an hour freezes once backfill passes it (`h=00`/`01`/`11`/`12`/`13` all stopped at a fixed size **and** append-block count while `h=02` was still filling and `h=03` had only just appeared).

What is unknown is the **steady state**: with backfill finished, does a genuinely closed hour ever receive a late record?

- **If no** — a future optimisation exists: stop re-reading blobs older than some settle horizon, shrinking the per-tick working set. Worth having on a large tenant.
- **If yes** — the current design is not merely safe but necessary, and that should be recorded so nobody "optimises" it away later.

Today the consumer re-checks every listed blob, which is correct either way and cheap (only 1–2 blobs actually grow per tick; the rest cost a size comparison). **Do not build the optimisation without the answer** — this is exactly the kind of "obviously safe" assumption that #89 already caught being wrong once.

**How:** snapshot every blob's size + `append_blob_committed_block_count`, wait a day, diff. A blob whose block count moves after a long-frozen period is the answer.

## 2. Clean post-backfill latency + append-op numbers

Both current figures are contaminated by backfill competing for throughput:

| measure | current value | why it is dirty |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MGAL envelope → blob write | 4.6m newest-record age, 4.4m min, 8.6m median | sampled during active backfill (biases **against** blob, so the true gap is likely smaller) |
| append ops | 247/hour → ~£0.80/mo | the settled-hours sample still spans backfilled hours |

The append-op figure matters most: #89's Phase 1 predicted £0.05–0.24/mo and the measured value is **~£0.85/mo total** — 4x low. It does not flip the transport decision (Event Hub is £8.34, Log Analytics £1.54) but the number is quoted in docs and should be right.

**How:** `append_blob_committed_block_count` is a direct count of billable AppendBlock ops (append blobs support no other write), so cost is measurable exactly, without guessing at Azure's batching. Take five settled hours from a day with no backfill running.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Answer to (1) with evidence, recorded in `docs/blob-ingest.md` + CLAUDE.md — and the settle-horizon optimisation either filed as its own issue or explicitly ruled out
- [ ] Clean append-op count; `docs/blob-ingest.md`'s cost figure updated if it moves
- [ ] Clean MGAL latency figures on a backfill-free window
- [ ] CLAUDE.md's "STILL OPEN" note on the backfill entry resolved rather than left standing

Refs #89, #135

comments.body: Gate note (2026-07-17, #146): three things hang off this measurement — #128 (blob→metrics spike: unblocks when `g2o-arrival` shows steady state), #138 (duplicate-rate re-measure: the 2.3% figure is backfill-contaminated), and the #135 `SignInLogs` diagnostic-setting removal (it stays until the latency instrument has served). When this closes, note the unblocks on those three.

## Backfill has settled — measured. Both questions answered, and one premise of this issue is WRONG

Probed 2026-07-17 09:44–10:17Z as **`graph2otel-poller`** (appId `2c92ce28-126c-47c1-82b0-410b64502989`, cert credential, storage audience). Method: snapshot every blob's `size` + `append_blob_committed_block_count` across all 9 containers (174 blobs), diff over time, and compute each hour bucket's **settle lag** = `last_modified − hour_end`.

**Evidence class: live-measured (2026-07-17, #137).**

### Backfill ended at ~2026-07-16T17:00Z — the crossover is visible to the hour

`insights-logs-microsoftgraphactivitylogs`, settle lag per hour bucket:

| hour bucket | hour_end | last_modified | settle lag | reading |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: | --- |
| `07-16T00` | `07-16T01` | `07-16T13:06` | **12.11h** | backfill |
| `07-16T01` | `07-16T02` | `07-16T14:07` | **12.13h** | backfill |
| `07-16T02` | `07-16T03` | `07-16T15:08` | **12.15h** | backfill |
| … 07-16T03…13 … | | | **12.16–12.31h** | backfill |
| `07-16T14` | `07-16T15` | `07-17T03:05` | **12.09h** | backfill (last pre-enablement hour) |
| `07-16T15` | `07-16T16` | `07-16T17:02` | **1.04h** | ⟵ **crossover** |
| `07-16T16` | `07-16T17` | `07-16T17:19` | **0.32h** | live |
| `07-16T17` | `07-16T18` | `07-16T18:04` | **0.08h** | live |
| `07-16T18` … `07-17T08` (15 consecutive) | | | **0.03–0.37h** | live |
| `07-17T09` | `07-17T10` | (open) | — | CURRENT HOUR |

Two distinct delivery streams, cleanly separated:

- **Backfill** filled the pre-enablement hours (`07-16T00`…`14`), walking **oldest-first at ~1 hour of history per hour of wallclock** (13:06 → 14:07 → 15:08 → 16:10 …), each bucket freezing **~12.1h after its hour closed**. It finished at `07-17T03:05` when it caught up to the enablement point.
- **Live** took over from `07-16T15`, and every hour since settles **~2–8 minutes after the hour closes** — which matches the known ~4-minute Entra-side propagation delay, independently corroborating it.

Same pattern across all six categories with data (median settle lag over closed hours: MGAL 0.37h, SPSignIn 11.88h, MSPSignIn 11.85h, NonInteractive 11.87h, SignIn 11.29h, Provisioning 11.93h — the sign-in medians sit high only because half their buckets are the backfilled ones).

### 1. Can a frozen hour grow again? — no observed case in steady state

| window | result |
| --- | --- |
| 09:44:48Z → 09:47:06Z (138s) | 171/174 blobs byte-identical. **3 grew — all `h=09`, the current hour.** 0 new blobs. |
| **09:44:48Z → 10:17:25Z (1,957s = 33 min)** | **169/174 byte-identical. 5 grew — ALL `h=09`, the then-current hour. 12 new blobs — all `h=10` (the new hour) or first-write-of-`h=09`.** **Zero closed buckets grew.** |
| `07-16T17` → `07-17T08` — **16 consecutive settled hours, 6 categories** | **zero** closed buckets have received an append beyond ~8 min past close |

The 33-minute diff is the load-bearing one. Every byte of growth across the whole account landed in the **open hour**:

```
GREW (all h=09, open at snapshot A):
  microsoftgraphactivitylogs          1,877,730 -> 4,059,071  blocks 188 -> 549
  serviceprincipalsigninlogs             83,539 ->   984,557  blocks  21 -> 178
  microsoftserviceprincipalsigninlogs   331,978 ->   864,048  blocks  93 -> 237
  noninteractiveusersigninlogs           21,622 -> 1,385,393  blocks   3 -> 161
  auditlogs                               5,706 ->    19,228  blocks   3 ->   6
UNCHANGED: 169  (every d=16 bucket and every closed d=17 bucket)
```

**Answer, as far as this can be answered in one session: in steady state a bucket freezes ~4 min after its hour closes and has not been observed to grow again.** The 12h-lagged buckets were backfill, not late-arrival — that distinction is the thing this issue needed and it is now measured.

**This is NOT sufficient to build the settle-horizon optimisation on.** What is proven is "no late append in a ~19h observation window on one tenant". The issue asks whether a frozen hour can **EVER** grow — a genuinely rare late record (a lagging region, a delayed Entra-side flush) would not necessarily appear in 19h on a 10-device tenant. The optimisation trades correctness for a size-comparison saving that is already cheap (an unchanged blob costs one HEAD-equivalent; only 1–2 blobs grow per tick). **Recommend: keep re-checking every listed blob, and record that the settle horizon is measured at ~8 min but not guaranteed.** If the optimisation is ever built, a settle horizon below **13h** would have silently dropped real backfill data on this very tenant on 2026-07-16 — that is the number to remember.

Evidence class on the "never grows" half: **live-measured, n=1 tenant, 19h window** — cheap to reopen, not armored.

### 2. ⛔ The duplicate re-measure is done — and this issue's premise about it is WRONG

This issue and the #146 gate note both state the 2.3% figure is *"backfill-contaminated"*. **It is not.** Measured both windows side by side, same method, identifying attribute per category (`requestId` for MGAL, `id` for sign-ins/audit):

| category | clean 16h (`07-16T17`→`07-17T08`) | backfill 15h (`07-16T00`→`14`) | docs/blob-ingest.md |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `MicrosoftGraphActivityLogs` | 24,048 recs, 654 dupes, **2.72%** | 25,550 recs, 710 dupes, 2.78% | 2.71% |
| `ServicePrincipalSignInLogs` | 9,578 recs, 389 dupes, **4.06%** | 6,765 recs, 302 dupes, 4.46% | 2.33% |
| `MicrosoftServicePrincipalSignInLogs` | 2,927 recs, 120 dupes, **4.10%** | 1,989 recs, 82 dupes, 4.12% | 2.78% |
| `NonInteractiveUserSignInLogs` | 908 recs, 27 dupes, **2.97%** | 714 recs, 30 dupes, 4.20% | 2.50% |
| `SignInLogs` | 18 recs, 1 dupe, 5.56% *(n too small)* | 15 recs, 2 dupes, 13.33% *(n too small)* | — |
| `AuditLogs` | 73 recs, 0 dupes, **0.00%** | 84 recs, 0 dupes, 0.00% | — |

**The clean and contaminated windows agree to within noise.** At-least-once re-delivery is a **steady-state property of Azure's diagnostic-settings delivery**, not a backfill artifact. The re-measure was worth doing and its result is "the number was never dirty".

Two corrections to `docs/blob-ingest.md` fall out:

1. **The rate is higher than recorded, on the sign-in categories.** The doc says *"a consistent 2.3%–2.8%"*. On a clean window with 4–12× the sample size it is **2.7%–4.1%**, and the sign-in family clusters near **4%**, not 2.3%. The doc's `ServicePrincipalSignInLogs` 2.33% (n=771) is superseded by 4.06% (n=9,578).
2. **Multiplicity reaches 4, not 3.** The doc says *"one event observed delivered three times"*. Clean-window histograms:

   | category | ×1 | ×2 | ×3 | ×4 |
   | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
   | MGAL | 22,808 | 519 | 66 | **1** |
   | `ServicePrincipalSignInLogs` | 8,846 | 302 | 36 | **5** |
   | `MicrosoftServicePrincipalSignInLogs` | 2,706 | 88 | 7 | **6** |
   | `NonInteractiveUserSignInLogs` | 859 | 19 | 1 | **2** |

   A downstream dedupe (or #138's engine-side fix) must not assume at-most-two copies.

`AuditLogs` at **0/73 across both windows** is the interesting outlier — either genuinely exactly-once, or n is too small to show a ~3% rate (expected ~2 dupes at 73 records, so absence is weak evidence). **Do not record AuditLogs as exactly-once** — n=73, evidence class n-too-small.

### 3. ⛔ Clean append-op count: ~4× the documented figure — and the cost is a feedback loop

Backfill's last write anywhere was `07-17T03:05`, so the only hours with **zero backfill running anywhere on the account** are `07-17T04`…`08`. That is exactly this issue's prescribed method (*"take five settled hours from a day with no backfill running"*), so it is the headline. The wider 16h live-stream window is given as corroboration — the two agree within 10%, so the conclusion is not sensitive to window choice.

| measure | docs/blob-ingest.md | **STRICT: 07-17T04…08 (5h, zero backfill)** | WIDE: 07-16T17→07-17T08 (16h) | ratio (strict) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | ---: |
| appends/hour | 247 | **935** | 1,032 | **3.8×** |
| bytes per append | ~10.6 KB | **7.3 KB** | 7.4 KB | 0.7× |
| appends/month (×730h) | ~180,000 | **~682,800** | ~753,700 | 3.8× |
| write cost @ £0.0447/10K | ~£0.81/mo | **~£3.05/mo** | £3.37/mo | 3.8× |
| data volume | ~0.7 GB/mo | **~4.99 GB/mo** | 5.56 GB/mo | ~7× |
| **total** | **~£0.85/mo** | **~£3.07/mo** | £3.39/mo | **3.6×** |

Per-container appends/hour (wide window): `serviceprincipalsigninlogs` 408 · `microsoftgraphactivitylogs` 386 · `microsoftserviceprincipalsigninlogs` 177 · `noninteractiveusersigninlogs` 54 · `auditlogs` 4.3 · `signinlogs` 1.1 · `devices` 0.6 · `devicecomplianceorg` 0.6.

**Backfill was not the cause of the discrepancy** — the backfill window ran at 897 appends/h, *lower* than the clean window's 935–1,032. The doc's 247/h was measured on 2026-07-16 before the volume drivers below were fully in play.

**The two drivers, live-measured:**

1. **graph2otel is 59.9% of its own MGAL volume.** Of 24,048 MGAL records in the clean window, **14,404 carry `appId = 2c92ce28-…` = `graph2otel-poller`**. MGAL is Graph API-call telemetry, so graph2otel polling Graph *generates* the records it then pays to ingest. Its top URIs: `/groups/$count` 2,410 · `/devices/$count` 1,235 · `/servicePrincipals` 773 · `/users/$count` 624 · `/beta/auditLogs/signIns` 431. **Blob-ingest cost therefore scales with graph2otel's own poll rate** — enabling a collector raises the bill twice (once for the poll, once for ingesting the MGAL record it creates). Nothing in #89 or `docs/blob-ingest.md` anticipates this feedback loop and it is worth stating explicitly there.
2. **One noisy tenant SP is 96.4% of `ServicePrincipalSignInLogs`** — `Application to manage WDATP TVM Network scan agent` (appId `32d104a5-…`), 9,234 of 9,578 sign-ins in 16h (~577/h). That single app costs more in blob appends than every Intune and audit category combined. Not graph2otel's doing; worth knowing before anyone reads the bill as "graph2otel costs £3.39/mo".

### 4. Does the 4× correction disturb #89? No — it strengthens blob

`docs/blob-ingest.md` says #89 *"pre-registered that the decision was not close enough for a 4× cost error to flip it"*. Re-ran the ranking with the **live-measured volume** against **#89's live-queried uksouth GBP prices** (Azure Retail Prices API, 2026-07-16):

| transport | cost at measured 4.99 GB/mo (strict window) | basis |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| **Storage (current)** | **£3.07/mo** | 682,800 writes @ £0.0447/10K + 1.15 GB resident @ £0.0145/GB |
| Event Hub Basic | £8.32/mo | standing TU charge; ingress negligible |
| Log Analytics | **£10.88/mo** | 4.99 GB @ £2.1819/GB |

**The margin widened rather than narrowed.** Blob is priced on *write operations*, Log Analytics on *GB ingested* — so a volume underestimate hurts LA harder than blob. At #89's assumed ~1 GB/mo, LA was £1.54 and blob £0.85 (1.8× apart); at the measured volume they are £10.88 vs £3.07 (3.5× apart). **#89's decision holds, for the same reasons, more strongly.** No reopen warranted.

⚠️ Caveat on the comparison: #89's ~1 GB/mo baseline was measured in the *existing Log Analytics workspace* fed by the old 19-category `entralogs` setting; the `aadiam/graph2otel` setting has a different category set enabled (notably both service-principal sign-in categories). So the 5.6× is **not** purely growth — part is a different category mix. The re-rank above is sound because it prices *the volume graph2otel actually ingests today*, but do not read "5.6× growth" as a time series. Evidence class: **live-measured volume × docs-priced meters** = derived, not a live bill.

### 5. ⛔ Clean MGAL latency — measured, and it is NOT smaller than the backfill-era figure

This issue predicted the 4.6m figure was *"sampled during active backfill (biases **against** blob, so the true gap is likely smaller)"*. **Measured clean: it is not smaller.**

Method: newest-record age = `now − max(record event time)` over the current hour's blob, sampled 6× between 09:58Z and 10:07Z (backfill-free by §1). For MGAL the envelope `time` **is** the event time (per `docs/blob-ingest.md`), so this is a true event→blob-write propagation measure.

| category | samples | result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `MicrosoftGraphActivityLogs` | 3.22 / 4.52 / 4.76 / 4.90 / 5.04 / 5.13 min | **median ~4.8 min, range 3.2–5.1 min** |
| prior figure (backfill-era, #89) | — | 4.6 min newest-record age |

**Clean ≈ 4.8 min vs dirty 4.6 min — the same, marginally *larger*.** The predicted bias did not exist. This is consistent with the §1 finding that steady-state buckets freeze ~2–8 min after close, and it independently corroborates the ~4-minute Entra-side propagation delay that #89 identified as upstream of the transport fork. **The "blob is floored at ~4 minutes" claim in `docs/blob-ingest.md` is confirmed on clean data.**

⚠️ **Do not compare the sign-in categories on this measure.** Sampled alongside: `ServicePrincipalSignInLogs` newest-record age 1.32–2.68 min — *apparently* fresher than MGAL, but that is an artifact. For sign-in categories the envelope `time` is the **ingestion** time (28s–1077s later than `properties.createdDateTime`), so this measures ingestion→write, not event→write. The comparable number would need binding to `createdDateTime`. Not measured here.

**Incidental finding:** the current hour's blob **does not exist for the first few minutes of the hour** — sampling at 10:00–10:04Z returned `BlobNotFound` for `h=10` while `h=09` was still receiving records with event times up to 09:59. Azure creates the hour's blob on first write, ~4 min in. Benign for the byte-offset design (a missing blob is simply not listed), but a consumer that assumes "the current hour always has a blob" would log a spurious error every hour.

### Acceptance criteria status

- [x] **Answer to (1)** — backfill settled `07-16T17:00Z`; steady-state buckets freeze ~2–8 min after close; **no closed bucket observed growing** across 16 settled hours / 6 categories / a ~19h window. **Settle-horizon optimisation: recommend explicitly ruling it out** (rationale + the 13h number above), not filing it.
- [x] **Clean append-op count** — 935/h (strict 5h zero-backfill window), ~£3.07/mo total. `docs/blob-ingest.md`'s cost figure **moves ~3.6×** and needs updating, along with the 247/h, 10.6 KB/append, 180,000/mo and £0.85/mo figures.
- [x] **Clean MGAL latency** — ~4.8 min median (range 3.2–5.1), vs 4.6 min during backfill. **The re-measure changes nothing** — record that the original figure was sound and that the predicted backfill bias was not real.
- [ ] CLAUDE.md "STILL OPEN" note on the backfill entry — resolvable from §1 once someone edits it. (Not edited here: this probe was read-only, no code or doc changes.)

### Unblocks (per the #146 gate note)

- **#138** — the duplicate-rate re-measure is **done**, and its premise was wrong: the 2.3% was never backfill-contaminated. The real steady-state figure is **2.7% (MGAL) / ~4% (sign-ins), multiplicity up to ×4**. #138 can proceed on these numbers; it does not need to wait for anything further.
- **#128** — steady state is confirmed reached (`07-16T17:00Z`), so the recency gate can be designed against real settled data. Note the ~12.1h backfill lag as the historical worst case a recency gate must tolerate on *enablement*, not steady state.
- **#135 `SignInLogs` diagnostic-setting removal** — **unblocked**. The gate was *"it stays until the latency instrument has served"*; the clean latency measure is taken (§5) and returned ~4.8 min, confirming the backfill-era figure rather than revising it. The instrument has served. Note `SignInLogs` is also the emptiest category on this account (18 records / 16h, 1.1 appends/h), so removing it changes essentially nothing about cost — the case for removal is tidiness, not spend.

**This issue can close** once someone edits `docs/blob-ingest.md` + CLAUDE.md with §1's steady-state answer and §3's corrected cost figures. Nothing further needs measuring on the tenant.

### ⛔ Incidental, and more urgent than anything above: `UserRiskEvents` / `RiskyUsers` envelope `time` is NOT ISO 8601

Two containers appeared mid-probe — `insights-logs-userriskevents` (10:12:18Z) and `insights-logs-riskyusers` (10:16:53Z) — carrying **#129's synthesized risk event** (`risk-synth-DELETE-ME@m7kni.io`, `riskEventType: anonymizedIPAddress`, `riskLevel: medium`). #129's synthesis worked, and the blob side now has live risk data to map against.

**Their envelope breaks every timestamp rule in `docs/blob-ingest.md`:**

```json
{"time": "7/17/2026 10:09:47 AM",           // <-- US M/D/YYYY h:mm:ss AM/PM. NOT ISO. NO TIMEZONE.
 "resourceId": "/tenants/…/providers/microsoft.aadiam",
 "operationName": "User Risk Detection",
 "Level": "Information",                     // <-- CAPITAL L. Every other category uses "level".
 "resultSignature": "None",
 "identity": "risk synth - delete me (graph2otel #129)",
 "properties": {"activityDateTime": "2026-07-17T10:07:37.536Z",   // <-- ISO, 3-digit fraction
                "detectedDateTime": "2026-07-17T10:07:37.536Z",
                "lastUpdatedDateTime": "2026-07-17T10:09:47.256Z",
                "source": "IdentityProtection", "riskState": "atRisk", …}}
```

Three traps, all live-measured (2026-07-17):

1. **`time` is `"7/17/2026 10:09:47 AM"`** — US-format, no timezone designator. The doc's rule *"MGAL and AuditLogs bind to `time` and are correct to"* plus the emitter rule *"a record with no parseable event time must be dropped"* combine into a live hazard: an ISO parser bound to `time` fails on **100%** of risk records, and the emitter then **silently drops every one**. A collector would look green and ship nothing — exactly the "green tick is not evidence of data" failure mode, made worse because the risk categories are *expected* to be near-empty, so the drop would never look wrong. **Bind to `properties.activityDateTime` / `detectedDateTime` (ISO). Never to `time`.**
2. **`Level` is capitalised** (`"Level": "Information"`), against `"level"` everywhere else — and the value is `Information`, not `Informational`. A severity mapper keyed on `level` reads nothing and defaults, on every record.
3. **`properties.source` = `"IdentityProtection"`** — a **fourth** overload of `source`. CLAUDE.md already forbids naming a provenance attribute `source` because the key is "overloaded three ways"; this is the fourth, and it is on the wire.

This is a **fifth distinct envelope family** (after MGAL, the sign-in family, AuditLogs, and Intune `Devices` per #132). The doc's timestamp-binding table needs a `UserRiskEvents`/`RiskyUsers` column, and its *"verify per category before sharing a mapper"* rule is vindicated again. **#129 should see this before it maps anything** — its synthesized event is the sample to map against, and the `time` field is a trap laid directly in its path.

### Summary of corrections this probe makes to `docs/blob-ingest.md`

| current text | corrected |
| --- | --- |
| "Measured live at **247 appends/hour**" | **935/h** (strict zero-backfill window) |
| "~10.6 KB per append" | **~7.3 KB** |
| "~180,000 appends/month" | **~683,000** |
| "**~£0.85/month**" total | **~£3.07/month** |
| "0.7 GB/month of data" | **~5.0 GB/month** |
| "a consistent **2.3%–2.8%**" duplicate rate | **2.7% (MGAL) / ~4.0–4.1% (sign-ins)** |
| "one event observed delivered **three** times" | **four** times observed (14 ids across 4 categories) |
| "**Still open** (#137): whether a frozen hour can EVER grow again" | steady state reached `07-16T17:00Z`; buckets freeze ~2–8 min after close; no closed bucket observed growing in ~19h. Not proven "never" — n=1 tenant. |
| "The ~2.3% duplicate rate below was also measured DURING backfill and **needs the same re-measure**" | re-measured; **backfill was never a contaminant** — clean and dirty windows agree within noise |

Done in `7728619` (on main). The post-backfill re-measure was fully captured in the probe comment above; this applies its corrections to `docs/blob-ingest.md`: cost £0.85→**£3.07/mo** (935 appends/h, ~5.0 GB/mo), duplicate rate **2.7% (MGAL) / ~4% (sign-ins)** with multiplicity **×4**, steady-state answer (buckets freeze ~2–8 min after close; settle-horizon optimisation explicitly ruled out with the 13h number), and the **59.9% self-exhaust feedback loop**. CLAUDE.md carried no 'STILL OPEN' note (it lived only in the doc), so nothing to resolve there.

Unblocks per the gate note: **#138** (duplicate re-measure done — steady-state, never backfill-contaminated; proceed on 2.7%/~4%, ×4), **#128** (steady state confirmed), **#135 SignInLogs removal** (latency instrument has served).

One incidental finding from the probe belongs to **#129**, not here: the `UserRiskEvents`/`RiskyUsers` blob envelope `time` is US-format (`"7/17/2026 10:09:47 AM"`, no TZ) — an ISO parser bound to `time` silently drops 100% of risk records. Bind to `properties.activityDateTime`/`detectedDateTime`. Flagging on #129 so it maps against the right field.
