> **Status update 2026-07-19 (see the [live census comment](https://github.com/rknightion/graph2otel/issues/135#issuecomment-5016452618)):** this issue's own scope is **complete except `ManagedIdentitySignInLogs`** (container still absent — data-gated, unblocks when it appears). Groups A, B (2/3), D (both) shipped; the two risk blob twins (RiskyUsers/UserRiskEvents) now carry live data → verification is #129's. The newly-populated containers below are NOT this issue's work: `graphnotifications`→#134 (observe, don't build), `devices`/`devicecomplianceorg`→**#197** (NOT redundant — keep enabled), `windows365auditlogs`→**#198**. Everything else is correctly awaiting data or owned by #132/#133/#134. The group checkboxes below are the historical tracker; only ManagedIdentity remains open here.

---

> Body updated 2026-07-17 (#146): the acceptance block below previously showed every box ticked (they were per-shipped-category ticks) while most of the worklist was unbuilt — misread as "issue complete" at a glance; now unticked and reworded to cover the whole worklist. Group D's gate is restated: **#131 has closed** (verdict: dual-ship is empty for WindowCollectors; mutual exclusion right, enforced by #144), so group D is unblocked as a `source: graph|blob` toggle question. The `SignInLogs` removal in "Do not" is **deferred until #137's latency measurement runs** (comment of 2026-07-16 18:53Z), not immediate.

## What

The blob-ingest engine shipped with #89 (`internal/blobpipeline`, live-verified), but only **one** of the 20 enabled diagnostic categories has a collector: `entra.graph_activity` (`MicrosoftGraphActivityLogs`).

The other 19 are landing in `graph2otelm7kni` right now, billed, deleted by the 7-day lifecycle rule, and **read by nothing**. Each is a `ContainerConfig` + a `Map` function — no transport work, no new infra, no new scopes.

## Why this is not one big issue

The engine is done, so each category is an independent, small, testable unit. They differ only in their mapping, and the mappings are **not** derivable from documentation — #89 found three type traps in `MicrosoftGraphActivityLogs` alone that produce a silently-wrong collector rather than an error. Each category needs its own live sample checked before its mapper is written.

**Read [`docs/blob-ingest.md`](../blob/main/docs/blob-ingest.md) first.** It carries the layout, the traps, and the reasons.

## The categories, grouped by what they buy

### A. No Graph route at all — blob is the ONLY source

- [x] **`MicrosoftServicePrincipalSignInLogs`** — Microsoft first-party service-to-service auth. Live-verified (#89) that our polled `entra.signins.service_principal` returns **zero** first-party appIds, so this is a genuinely different dataset, not a duplicate. 21,554 rows/7d. Microsoft: *"offered as an opt-in through diagnostic settings only"* — there is no API.
- [x] **Intune `OperationalLogs`** — BUILT `intune.compliance_alerts` (60d7571). the compliance-alert *fired-event* stream (#94). Graph exposes only the notification templates. **May emit zero rows on m7kni** (a tenant with compliant devices legitimately fires nothing) — if so it stays a legitimate gap for other tenants but cannot be verified end-to-end here.

### B. Retires a beta dependency

These three are `Experimental`/opt-in today **only** because the `signInEventTypes` filter is beta-only (v1.0 returns HTTP 400). Diagnostic settings emit them as first-class categories: no filter, no beta.

- [x] **`NonInteractiveUserSignInLogs`**
- [x] **`ServicePrincipalSignInLogs`**
- [ ] **`ManagedIdentitySignInLogs`** — **NOT built**: the container does not exist on m7kni (zero records), so there is no live sample to map against. Its shape is very probably identical to the two siblings above — and "very probably" against imagination is exactly the reasoning that produced #109/#100/#130's wrong verdicts. It lands when a tenant emits one.

Worth deciding as part of this: does a blob-sourced version become **default-on**, given it is v1.0-stable? (#131 closed after this was written: there is no `dual` mode — a collector's source is `graph` XOR `blob`, enforced by #144's `ConflictsWith`. So the question is purely which source is the default.)

### C. Identity Protection — three have NO collector at all

- [ ] **`ServicePrincipalRiskEvents`**, **`RiskyAgents`**, **`AgentRiskEvents`** — see #133; blob may be the cheaper route than polling, since the IPC workload is capped at **1 req/s per tenant across all apps** with no `Retry-After` (graph2otel's tightest constraint).
- [ ] **`RiskyUsers`**, **`UserRiskEvents`**, **`RiskyServicePrincipals`** — polled today; blob dodges that same ceiling.

⚠️ **All of these emit ~zero rows on m7kni** — no mapping here is verifiable until #129 synthesises a real risk event. Do not write a mapper for them against imagination; #109/#100/#130 are three separate cases of a confident wrong verdict reached without live data.

### D. Default-on collision — needs the `source` toggle, then mappable today

- [x] **`AuditLogs`**, **`ProvisioningLogs`** — `entra.directory_audits` / `entra.provisioning` are **default-on v1.0 polled collectors emitting the same events with the same ids**, so a blob twin both-enabled ships every record twice (the exact duplication #144 exists to prevent). ~~Gated on #131~~ **#131 closed**: the gate is now just wiring the `source: graph|blob` toggle for these collectors (mutual exclusion, `ConflictsWith`). `AuditLogs` is verified mappable today — the blob `properties` object IS the Graph `directoryAudit` resource (28/28 field check), **reuse `mapDirectoryAudit`, do not write a second mapper** (correction comment below + CLAUDE.md).

### E. Unknown shape

- [ ] **`GraphNotificationsActivityLogs`**, **`MicrosoftGraphPolicyLogs`**, **`PreAuthenticationDiscoveryLogs`** — #134 owns the decision to build or disable. Not this issue's work; listed so the 20 reconcile.

### F. Intune inventory

- [ ] **`Devices`**, **`DeviceComplianceOrg`** — #132 owns the shape question first (if `Devices` carries per-device inventory it could retire the hourly full-fleet page-walk). Blocked on blobs landing.

## Acceptance criteria

These apply to **every** category as it lands (the group checkboxes above are the completion tracker):

- [ ] Every mapper written **against a real live sample**, not documentation
- [ ] Per-entity detail as log attributes, never metric labels (#112); no category emits metrics without #128 landing first
- [ ] Distinct `CursorKey` where two collectors share a container
- [ ] Each category's `level`/type quirks checked individually — a shared severity mapper is **already known to be wrong** across MGAL and SignInLogs
- [ ] Categories that turn out to carry nothing on m7kni are recorded as such, not silently left half-built
- [ ] `docs/blob-ingest.md` "what it is for" table updated as each lands
- [ ] `make check` green

## Do not

- **Do not give `SignInLogs` a collector.** It is a deliberate duplicate of `entra.signins.interactive`, kept only as the latency measurement instrument (#89). It gets **removed from the diagnostic setting after #137's latency measurement runs** — not before, and never mapped.
- Do not add `AzureADGraphActivityLogs` (deprecated API) or the GSA/ADFS/EnrichedO365 family (zero rows here, and `EnrichedOffice365AuditLogs` is synthesised downstream by Sentinel — it has no source anywhere).

Refs #89, #94, #128, #129, #131, #132, #133, #134

comments.body:
## ⚠️ Mapping trap for the sign-in categories: the envelope `time` is NOT the event time

Found while auditing what the `SignInLogs` latency instrument actually produced (#89). This applies to **every** sign-in category in group B, and to `SignInLogs` if anyone ever maps it.

The one real `SignInLogs` record on the tenant, decomposed:

```
properties.createdDateTime : 11:27:34Z   <- the ACTUAL sign-in
envelope   time            : 11:58:35Z   <- 31 MINUTES LATER
blob       last_modified   : 13:11:46Z
```

**`MicrosoftGraphActivityLogs` gets away with binding the OTLP timestamp to the top-level `time`** — on MGAL, `time` and `properties.timeGenerated` are byte-identical, so `entra.graph_activity` is correct as written.

**Sign-in categories must bind to `properties.createdDateTime` instead.** Copying MGAL's mapper shape would silently backdate every sign-in by ~31 minutes — no error, no warning, just every sign-in landing in the wrong half-hour on every dashboard and alert.

This is the third instance of the same lesson, so it is worth stating as a rule rather than a list: **the diagnostic-settings envelope is not consistent across categories.** So far:

| field | MGAL | SignInLogs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `time` vs real event time | identical | **31m late** |
| `level` | `"Informational"` (always, even on 500s) | `"4"` (numeric string) |
| `resourceId` casing | `/TENANTS/…/MICROSOFT.AADIAM` | `/tenants/…/Microsoft.aadiam` |
| `durationMs` (top level) | string `"497815"` | int `0` |

**Check each category's own sample. Do not generalise from a shipped mapper**, and do not build a shared envelope helper on the assumption these agree — they demonstrably do not.

One more, unrelated to timing but relevant to whoever maps the sign-in streams: that record carried `deviceDetail.deviceId` and `.displayName` as literal **`"{PII Removed}"`** strings. It was a B2B guest sign-in (`rob.knight@grafana.com` into m7kni), so the home tenant's device PII is scrubbed in the resource tenant's logs. A mapper must not emit `device_id="{PII Removed}"` as though it were an identifier — treat it as absent.

## Bonus finding: blob latency scales with volume

Relevant to the group B decision ("does a blob-sourced sign-in stream become default-on?") and to #131.

| | records/hour | envelope → blob write |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `MicrosoftGraphActivityLogs` | ~2,650 | **4–8 min** |
| `SignInLogs` | ~1.4 | **73 min** |

The 73 minutes is destination-side batching on a stream with nothing to batch. Cross-checked live at 15:22Z: Graph's newest sign-in was **14:09** (72m old), blob's was **11:27** (235m old) — for a low-volume signal, polling is far ahead.

**This is not an argument against blob for sign-ins**, because the blob case for group B was never freshness — it was retiring the `/beta` dependency so those three streams can stop being `Experimental`. But it does mean a blob-sourced sign-in stream is **not** a freshness upgrade on a small tenant, and it should not be sold as one.

It also **supports the large-tenant intent** recorded on #89: blob's latency improves as volume rises, which is exactly where Graph's reporting ceiling (5 req/10s per app per tenant, no `Retry-After`) gets worse. The two curves move in opposite directions. Worth a real number on a large tenant before #131 commits to anything.

Caveat, stated plainly: **n=1**, during enablement backfill. Do not quote 73 minutes as a steady-state figure. The volume-dependence is the durable claim; the number is not.

## Shipped: the three categories with live data — `180caf8`

`entra.signins.microsoft_service_principal` (group A), `entra.signins.service_principal.blob` and `entra.signins.non_interactive.blob` (group B). `make check` green; live-verified end to end.

### The mapping trap: confirmed, and worse than this issue recorded

The comment above put it at 31 minutes, from n=1. Against ~700 live records across all three categories, the real shape is **variable ingestion lag**, not a constant:

| category | n | `time` == `createdDateTime` | delta range |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| `MicrosoftServicePrincipalSignInLogs` | 155 | **0** | 37s – 655s |
| `ServicePrincipalSignInLogs` | 518 | **0** | 28s – 1077s |
| `NonInteractiveUserSignInLogs` | 27 | **0** | 57s – 1050s |

Never equal, not once. And because the gap is variable you **cannot** recover the event time by subtracting a constant — which makes binding to `time` more clearly wrong, not less. Bound to `properties.createdDateTime` with **no fallback** (a fallback silently reintroduces the bug). Pinned by a test that fails if anyone rebinds it — **verified by mutating the implementation and watching it fail**, not assumed.

`level` is `"4"` on 100% of records in all three, including the failures (7000113, 70043). Severity comes from `properties.status.errorCode`.

### The rule refined: the envelope is consistent WITHIN a family, not ACROSS

This issue says don't generalise from a shipped mapper. Correct — but I checked rather than assumed, and the three sign-in categories diff to **zero type conflicts** (differences are additive optional fields only). So they legitimately share one mapper. MGAL vs sign-ins agree on nothing. The rule is: verify agreement against live samples; don't assume it either way.

### Bigger finding: the blob `properties` object IS the Graph `signIn` resource

Every field the polled `mapSignIn` reads is present in **all four** categories. So these reuse that mapper rather than duplicating it — same `entra.signin` event name, same attributes, same `id`. The two sources are **drop-in equivalents**, and an attribute added for one is automatically right for the other. That is why they live in `entra/signins` rather than a new package: not a second signal, a second source.

`{PII Removed}` needs no guard: it lands only in `deviceDetail.deviceId`/`.displayName`, which `mapSignIn` does not read. Noted in the code, because it goes live the moment someone maps `deviceDetail`.

### Group A confirmed on blob data directly

The "different dataset" claim was inferred from the polled API in #89. Now confirmed at source:

```
microsoftserviceprincipalsigninlogs : 160/160 records owned by MICROSOFT's tenant (f8cdef31)
serviceprincipalsigninlogs          : 541/541 records owned by m7kni
overlap of sign-in ids              : ZERO
```

A clean partition by app ownership. Top first-party callers: Defender for Cloud Apps APIs, Defender for Identity, AAD Terms Of Use, SyncFabric. The polled collector can never surface any of them.

### The decision this issue asked for: do the blob versions become default-on?

**Yes — and they are, because `blob_ingest.account_url` is already the opt-in.** Standing up a storage account, creating the diagnostic settings and granting a data-plane role is an explicit, effortful act; a second opt-in buys nothing, and marking a v1.0-stable source "beta" would contradict the entire reason group B exists. They declare Entra P1, so a Free tenant gets a stated skip rather than a silent empty container.

**No duplication by default:** the polled twins are `Experimental` → off by default. Blob ingest configured ⇒ blob versions on, polled beta versions off ⇒ each sign-in once. Duplicating needs the deliberate act of enabling a beta stream *and* configuring blob ingest; `id` is identical across sources, so downstream dedupe works. No machinery added for it — that is #131's call.

**But freshness is not the sell, and I have not sold it as one** (README + docs both say so). Blob latency scales with volume; on a small tenant polling is far ahead.

### ⚠️ Found while verifying: Azure delivers at-least-once → #138

Not a #135 bug — it affects `entra.graph_activity` too, shipped yesterday. **~2.3% of blob records arrive more than once**, byte-identical payload, fresh envelope `time`, usually in the same blob. `blobpipeline` has no dedupe (`logpipeline` does), so blob-sourced collectors pass those duplicates through. The cursor provably cannot fix it. Filed as **#138** with the measurements.

The same test proved the engine exact: across a cold start plus a restart, **for all 1,035 emitted ids the emitted count equalled the number of times Azure wrote the record** — zero over-emission, zero loss.

### Live verification

```
cold start : 942 sign-in records, cursors persisted per blob
restart    : 120 records (only newly-appended bytes re-read)
timestamps : every record carries its own event time; none stamped at ingest
severity   : 17 WARN from status.errorCode, level ignored
```

### Container state, 16:04Z (re-check with `g2o-arrival`)

`managedidentitysigninlogs`, `auditlogs`, `provisioninglogs`, all six IPC categories, the three unknowns (#134) and all three Intune categories (#132) are **still absent** — nothing written yet, not misconfigured.

**Unrelated docs gap noticed:** `docs/collectors.md` lists none of `purview.labels`, `m365.unified_audit`, or any blob collector. Blob collectors are documented in `docs/blob-ingest.md` by design (they poll no Graph endpoint, which is what that table is keyed on), but the first two look like genuine drift.

## Arrival check 18:32Z: only 6 of 20 containers exist. `AuditLogs` is new; 14 categories have still written NOTHING.

Probed read-only **as the poller** (cert on camden, per CLAUDE.md's "probe as `graph2otel-poller`, never as another app").

```
container                                             blobs         bytes  newest
insights-logs-auditlogs                                   4        13,312  18:00:40Z   <- NEW since 16:04Z
insights-logs-microsoftgraphactivitylogs                 15    48,149,878  18:32:23Z   <- shipped
insights-logs-microsoftserviceprincipalsigninlogs         9     2,587,871  18:32:02Z   <- shipped
insights-logs-noninteractiveusersigninlogs                9     1,072,107  18:31:55Z   <- shipped
insights-logs-serviceprincipalsigninlogs                  9    12,277,703  18:32:29Z   <- shipped
insights-logs-signinlogs                                  4        39,378  17:48:06Z   <- the dead instrument; still to be REMOVED
TOTAL                                                          64,140,249
```

### What this changes

**Only ONE new category became mappable: `AuditLogs`.** Everything else on this issue's list is still unwritable against real data, and this issue is explicit that a mapper must not be written against imagination.

Still absent, 4.5h after enablement (~14:15Z):

- `ManagedIdentitySignInLogs` - group B's last member
- `ProvisioningLogs` - group D
- **All six Identity Protection categories** - expected; m7kni emits ~zero risk rows until #129
- **All three #134 unknowns** (`GraphNotificationsActivityLogs`, `MicrosoftGraphPolicyLogs`, `PreAuthenticationDiscoveryLogs`) - 4.5h of silence is now itself weak evidence toward "emits nothing here", though #134's own 24h bar has not elapsed
- **All three Intune categories** (#132: `Devices`, `DeviceComplianceOrg`, `OperationalLogs`) - worth noting these come from a **separate diagnostic setting** (`microsoft.intune/graph2otel`) than the 17 Entra ones (`aadiam/graph2otel`). Zero containers from that setting after 4.5h is a different signal from a slow category: it is consistent with the Intune setting not delivering at all. #132 should check the setting itself before concluding anything about row shape.

Azure creates a container on **first write**, so absence still means "nothing written yet", not "misconfigured" - but 14 of 20 silent while 6 are actively growing narrows what that can mean.

### `AuditLogs` is gated

It is group D (dual-ship log side), which this issue gates on **#131** settling what `dual` means as a mode. `entra.directory_audits` already polls the same signal, so shipping a blob twin without that decision is exactly the duplicate-into-one-pipeline case #131 exists to prevent. Not blocked on data any more - blocked on a decision.

### 🔴 Separate finding: the blob collectors have never run in production

**camden's `config.yaml` has no `blob_ingest.account_url`**, so `entra.graph_activity` and the three sign-in blob collectors register on **no** deployment. The engine and its collectors shipped (#89, #135 `180caf8`) and were verified ad-hoc, but the production deployment has never exercised them, and the 7-day lifecycle rule is deleting the data unread in the meantime.

That is a deployment gap, not a code gap, and it is worth closing before more categories are mapped - otherwise each new mapper is shipped into a path nothing runs.

## Deployment gap CLOSED: blob ingest is running in production for the first time

The gap reported above is fixed. `blob_ingest.account_url` added to camden's `config.yaml`; container recreated 18:50Z. All four blob collectors registered and consumed the backlog that the 7-day lifecycle was deleting unread:

```
container                              blobs   bytes consumed
microsoftgraphactivitylogs                16      50,045,145
serviceprincipalsigninlogs                 9      13,554,399
microsoftserviceprincipalsigninlogs        9       2,978,905
noninteractiveusersigninlogs               9       1,114,426
                                          --      ----------
                                          43      67,692,875
```

Byte-offset cursors persisted per blob, exactly as designed. Verified the data-plane role FIRST with a ranged GET (`HTTP 206`, real bytes) rather than enabling and hoping - per CLAUDE.md, `Owner` lists containers but cannot read content, and that failure is indistinguishable from "no data yet".

Two honest notes on the change:

- **It moved two variables, not one.** `compose.yaml` carries `pull_policy: always`, so the recreate also pulled `main` and jumped the deployment from the 16:36Z image to `version=4ab4523`. That incidentally deploys #83, #139 and #118 as well. Not what I intended to test, but nothing regressed and the blob cursors prove the config change is what registered the collectors.
- **`SignInLogs` stays in the diagnostic setting for now.** This issue's "Do not" section says it should be removed. Not yet: it is #137's latency-measurement instrument, and #137's clean post-backfill re-measure has not run. Removing it now destroys the instrument before it has been read. Worth removing after #137, not before.

## `AuditLogs` characterised against live data - and it is a THIRD envelope pattern

Sampled all 6 blobs. The headline: **a string-equality test on the timestamp gives a FALSE POSITIVE here**, and that test is exactly the one the sign-in work used.

```
=== time vs properties.activityDateTime ===
  byte-identical strings : 0/9          <- looks like the sign-in bug
  delta seconds          : min=0.000  max=0.000  nonzero=0/9   <- but it is the SAME INSTANT
```

They are never equal as strings and always equal as instants. The difference is pure serialisation:

```
time                        = "2026-07-16T18:30:36.6431870Z"      7-digit fraction, Z
properties.activityDateTime = "2026-07-16T18:30:36.643187+00:00"  6-digit fraction, +00:00
```

So `AuditLogs` behaves like MGAL (envelope `time` IS the event time), **not** like the sign-in categories - but a naive `time == properties.X` check reports `0/9` and would send the next person straight to "bind to `activityDateTime`, no fallback, it is late like the sign-ins". That conclusion would be wrong, reached from a correct-looking measurement.

**Rule, worth adding to CLAUDE.md: compare timestamps as PARSED INSTANTS, never as strings.** The sign-in finding survives this unharmed (0/700 equal with deltas of 28-1077s is a real gap, not a formatting artefact), but it survives by luck of magnitude, not by method.

### The envelope is a MIX of the two known patterns

This kills any remaining case for a shared envelope helper, and confirms "map per category" for a third time:

| field | MGAL | SignInLogs | **AuditLogs** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `time` vs event time | identical | ~31m late | **identical (as instant)** |
| `level` | `"Informational"` | `"4"` | **`"Informational"`** |
| `durationMs` (top level) | string `"497815"` | int `0` | **int `0`** |
| `resourceId` casing | `/TENANTS/…/MICROSOFT.AADIAM` | `/tenants/…/Microsoft.aadiam` | **`/tenants/…/Microsoft.aadiam`** |

It follows MGAL on timestamps and `level`, and SignInLogs on `durationMs` and casing. No category predicts another.

### 🔴 The sample is NOT representative, and this issue's own rule says that matters

**9 records across 6 blobs, and all 9 are the same event:**

```
properties.category        1 distinct -> {'ProvisioningManagement': 9}
properties.loggedByService 1 distinct -> {'Account Provisioning': 9}
properties.operationType   1 distinct -> {'Read': 9}
properties.result          1 distinct -> {'success': 9}
operationName              1 distinct -> {'Execution': 9}
```

That is the Entra Cloud Sync heartbeat, not directory audit activity. **Zero `targetResources[].modifiedProperties` in the sample** - which does NOT mean the category lacks them; it means these 9 records are the wrong 9 records. A real audit event (user created, role assigned) carries `modifiedProperties` with old/new values, and CLAUDE.md's one genuine content exclusion applies to them: emit the property **names**, never the **values**.

So `AuditLogs` is **not yet safely mappable**, and the blocker is no longer only #131. It is also that this issue's own bar - *"a mapper written against a real live sample, not documentation"* - is unmet. Nine heartbeats is closer to documentation than to a sample.

`properties.id` shows 9 distinct over 9 records, so **0% re-delivery** here versus #138's 2.3-2.7% elsewhere. Do not read that as "AuditLogs is exempt". n=9 cannot measure a 2.3% rate.

## Live evidence that bears on #131 and #100

I granted two app roles at 18:40Z, which generates real directory audit events (`Add app role assignment to service principal.`). Where they landed:

- **O365 Management Activity API (#100): present within ~2 minutes.** The 18:42Z content blob carried them, alongside `UserLoggedIn` x8.
- **`AuditLogs` blob category: still absent ~10 minutes later.** The container's newest record is an 18:30Z provisioning heartbeat.

Consistent with this issue's earlier finding that blob latency is volume-dependent and bad for low-volume streams. It is a data point for #131's dual-ship split, not a verdict - the blob may still catch up, and I have not waited it out.

## Where this leaves the issue

Unchanged from the 18:33Z check: only 6 of 20 containers exist. `ManagedIdentitySignInLogs`, `ProvisioningLogs`, all six Identity Protection categories, the three #134 unknowns and all three Intune categories have still written nothing. `AuditLogs` is the only new one, and it now needs **both** #131's decision **and** a representative sample before a mapper is honest.

## ⚠️ Correction: `AuditLogs` is NOT blocked on data. It is mappable today, blocked only on #131.

My comment above said `AuditLogs` was *"not yet safely mappable"* because the container held 9 records that were all the same Cloud Sync heartbeat, and that this issue's own bar (*"a mapper written against a real live sample"*) was unmet. **Wrong on both counts.** Retracting it.

### The reasoning error

I judged the sample by its **variety**. But `mapDirectoryAudit` is **field-driven, not event-type-driven** - and more to the point, **no new mapper is being written**. This issue's own `180caf8` established the pattern: the blob `properties` object IS the Graph resource, so the polled mapper is reused. The "write it against a live sample, not documentation" bar exists to stop someone *inventing* a mapper from docs. It does not apply when the mapper already exists and is already exercised live against the full variety by `entra.directory_audits`.

Checked against **28 live records**, every field `mapDirectoryAudit` reads:

```
  id                     28/28      correlationId          28/28
  category               28/28      initiatedBy            28/28
  activityDisplayName    28/28      targetResources        28/28
  result                 28/28
  resultReason           28/28      initiatedBy.app.displayName  : "Azure AD Cloud Sync"
  loggedByService        28/28      targetResources[].displayName: ["Grafana PS"]
```

### Clarification on the "turn off" verdicts above — one transport per signal, not "blob is useless"

The `SignInLogs` / `RiskyUsers` / `UserRiskEvents` "turn off" recommendations assume the **polled** collector stays enabled. Event time = envelope `time`; skip the trailing `{properties:{Stats:{RecordCount}}}` batch-summary record (`resultType:Completed` vs per-device `resultType:None`).

**DeviceComplianceOrg (second container) — decision needed.** It carries compliance-focused per-device rows (`ComplianceState_loc`, `DeviceHealthThreatLevel` = the polled `partnerReportedThreatState`, `ManagementAgents`, `OwnerType`). Options: (a) fold into the same `intune.managed_device` twin as an enrichment (risk: two blob sources for one twin → dedupe/merge complexity); (b) its own twin/collector; (c) leave for #132. Recommend (c)/(b): keep #135-F to the `Devices` inventory twin; treat DeviceComplianceOrg separately. Full page-walk RETIREMENT stays #132's field-diff — #135-F only moves the twin, keeps the polled gauges.

Samples captured live 2026-07-18 (`insights-logs-devices`: 11 devices + 1 Stats; `insights-logs-devicecomplianceorg`: 11). Mechanism + samples ready; the enum map is the one thing that must be live-verified against both shapes before coding.

## #135-C piece 2 + #135-F live-verified on camden (2026-07-18)

Deployed 635421d (`version=635421d` in the startup log). The keep-gauges/suppress-twin stack is live end-to-end:

| collector | role | state | proof |
|---|---|---|---|
| `entra.risky_users` | blob twin (RiskyUsers) | enabled, runs=1, failures=0, last_success=true | `blobcursor_insights-logs-riskyusers` created 22:15 — consumed real data |
| `intune.devices_blob` | blob twin (Devices) | enabled, runs=1, failures=0, last_success=true | `blobcursor_insights-logs-devices` created 22:15 — consumed real data |
| `entra.risk` | polled (gauges) | enabled, runs=1, failures=0, last_success=true | keeps its gauge; risky_user twin suppressed (blob owns it) |
| `intune.devices` | polled (gauges) | enabled, runs=1, failures=0, last_success=true | keeps its fleet gauges; managed_device twin suppressed |
| `entra.risk_detections` | blob source (UserRiskEvents) | enabled, runs=1, failures=0, last_success=true | (piece 1) |

Both blob twins are default-on (blob configured), so the composition root auto-populated `SuppressedTwins` = {entra.risky_user, intune.managed_device} and the two polled collectors dropped exactly those twins while keeping their gauges — no config change needed, exactly as designed.

**#135-C: complete** (UserRiskEvents source toggle + RiskyUsers keep-gauges/suppress-twin; RiskyServicePrincipals deferred — no container on this tenant). **#135-F: complete** (Devices twin; DeviceComplianceOrg + full page-walk retirement remain #132). The general `SuppressedTwins` mechanism now covers both metric-emitting collectors that have a blob twin — audited (#184) to be the complete set.

## Container inventory + diagnostic-category status — 2026-07-19 (as `graph2otel-poller`)

Re-probed the storage account (31 containers) and cross-checked the two still-absent categories against the diagnostic settings.

**Rob confirmed both `ManagedIdentitySignInLogs` and `RiskyServicePrincipals` are ENABLED in the `aadiam/graph2otel` diagnostic setting.** Yet neither container exists (`insights-logs-managedidentitysigninlogs`, `insights-logs-riskyserviceprincipals` both absent). This is NOT a category-name→container-name mismatch — the naming convention (`insights-logs-<category-lowercased>`) lines up fine. The gap is upstream: **no events have been generated.**

- **`ManagedIdentitySignInLogs` (group B)** — no container = no managed-identity sign-ins have occurred. m7kni has no MI-using Azure resource, so nothing authenticates as an MI. Enabling the category is necessary but not sufficient; it fills only when an MI signs in. `[live-measured 2026-07-19, n=1]` Still unbuildable (no sample) until an MI resource exists — Rob is considering deploying one.
- **`RiskyServicePrincipals` (group C remainder)** — no container = no risky-SP detections. Requires Workload Identities Premium, which m7kni lacks (Rob confirmed). Stays deferred-unverifiable; not worth blocking on.

Present risk containers unchanged: `insights-logs-riskyusers` + `insights-logs-userriskevents` (both hold the #129 synth event, already built as #135-C). The four SP/agent IPC categories (`riskyserviceprincipals`, `serviceprincipalriskevents`, `riskyagents`, `agentriskevents`) all lack containers — gated on WIP / no events, → #133.

## Live census 2026-07-19 16:10Z (probed as graph2otel-poller, storage.azure.com scope, cert on camden)

`graph2otelm7kni` now holds **32 containers**. Cross-referenced against the built collectors, this issue's own scope is **effectively complete** — every category #135 directly owns has shipped, and two that were empty when their mappers were written now finally carry live data:

| category | container (blobs / bytes) | collector | group |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| MicrosoftGraphActivityLogs | 74 / 347 MB | `entra.graph_activity` | shipped |
| MicrosoftServicePrincipalSignInLogs | 77 / 56 MB | `entra.signins.microsoft_service_principal` | A ✓ |
| ServicePrincipalSignInLogs | 77 / 192 MB | `entra.signins` blob twin | B ✓ |
| NonInteractiveUserSignInLogs | 77 / 34 MB | `entra.signins` blob twin | B ✓ |
| OperationalLogs | 3 / 7 KB | `intune.compliance_alerts` | A ✓ |
| AuditLogs | 77 / 2.6 MB | `entra.directory_audits` blob twin | D ✓ |
| ProvisioningLogs | 11 / 270 KB | `entra.provisioning` blob twin | D ✓ |
| RiskyUsers | 4 / 3.8 KB — **now has data** | `entra.risk` blob twin | C ✓ (built) |
| UserRiskEvents | 3 / 8.9 KB — **now has data** | `entra.risk_detections` blob twin | C ✓ (built) |
| Devices | 3 / 46 KB | `intune.managed_devices` blob twin | F (see #197) |
| SignInLogs | 31 / 1.4 MB | deliberately unmapped (latency instrument, #89) | do-not |

### The one item this issue still owns: `ManagedIdentitySignInLogs`

Container **still absent** on m7kni (no managed-identity sign-ins to emit). Correctly deferred — its shape is very probably identical to the two sibling sign-in categories, but "very probably against imagination" is the #109/#100/#130 mistake. **Unblock condition: the `insights-logs-managedidentitysigninlogs` container appears** (a tenant emits an MI sign-in); then it reuses `mapSignIn` like the other two blob sign-in twins. Nothing else in this issue's own scope is open.

### RiskyUsers / UserRiskEvents now carry live data — relevant to #129

Both risk blob twins were built and shipped against the polled-API shape while their containers were empty (this issue and #129 both warned the mappings were unverified end-to-end). They now have real blob records. This is the live sample #129 was waiting for to verify the risk-signal mappings against a real event — see #129.

### Newly-populated containers that are NOT this issue's work — handed to owners

- `graphnotificationsactivitylogs` (12 / 239 KB) — **#134 (closed) already ruled: do not build yet**, pending a 7-day observation (~2026-07-24) to decide if it carries anything but Microsoft-internal notification traffic. Leave enabled, do not map.
- `devicecomplianceorg` (5 / 35 KB) + `devices` — **NOT redundant; do NOT turn off.** #132's "redundant → turn off" recommendation is reversed: these are the candidate log transport for the metrics-via-graph + logs-via-blob split for `intune.devices` at scale. Tracked as **#197**.
- `windows365auditlogs` (1 / 36 KB) — brand-new, uncatalogued Cloud PC admin-audit category. Triage filed as **#198** (assess overlap with `m365.activity`'s `Windows365CustomerLockbox` before building).

### Still genuinely absent (correctly, not misconfigured)

`managedidentitysigninlogs`, `riskyserviceprincipals`, `serviceprincipalriskevents`, `riskyagents`, `agentriskevents` (the last four → #133), `microsoftgraphpolicylogs`, `preauthenticationdiscoverylogs` (→ #134). Container absence is a weak signal until well past 24h (this account has shown first-write latency up to 19.6h — #134), so these are recorded as awaiting-data, not gaps.

**Verdict: #135's own worklist is complete except `ManagedIdentitySignInLogs` (data-gated).** Re-scoping the body accordingly.

## `ManagedIdentitySignInLogs` re-checked — still absent (2026-07-19)

Re-listed the storage containers live as graph2otel-poller (storage data-plane). **33 containers present; `managedidentity` is NOT among them** (the account has `serviceprincipalsigninlogs`, `microsoftserviceprincipalsigninlogs`, `noninteractiveusersigninlogs`, `signinlogs`, but no managed-identity sign-in container). The category still isn't writing to the account.

**Unblock condition (unchanged, not fired):** the `insights-logs-managedidentitysigninlogs` container appearing on the account. When it does, the collector reuses `mapSignIn` (the transport-identical sign-in mapper) — a small addition, no new mapper. Every other category #135 owns is shipped; this is the only remaining item, staying parked.

Data-gen executed for the one remaining item (`ManagedIdentitySignInLogs`) — 2026-07-20.

A managed identity had never signed in on m7kni, so the container never existed. Synthesized one:
- Throwaway **user-assigned MI** `g2o-misynth-DELETE-ME` created in `intuney/auditlogs` (clientId `2f39d8ec-e2c9-4e60-b9ac-3aa56f1a3637`, principalId `fa179562-7d53-49bc-b38a-c52915cf554c`). Registered `Microsoft.ManagedIdentity` + `Microsoft.ContainerInstance` providers on the `intuney` sub as a side effect.
- One-shot ACI `g2o-misynth-delete-me` (`restart-policy Never`) ran `az login --identity --client-id 2f39d8ec…` 6× — container logs confirm `signed-in-1..6` as `MSIClient-2f39d8ec…`. This generates `managedIdentity` sign-in events, which the `aadiam/graph2otel` diagnostic setting routes to `insights-logs-managedidentitysigninlogs`.

**Unblock condition (this issue’s sole remaining item) is now firing.** Awaiting the `insights-logs-managedidentitysigninlogs` blob container to appear (first-write latency on this account has been up to ~19.6h). When it lands, the collector reuses `mapSignIn` verbatim like the other two blob sign-in twins — no new mapper.

**Cleanup pending (do at the end):** delete the ACI + the throwaway MI once the blob lands and the collector is verified. `[live-measured 2026-07-20]`

Closed by 2ac12bb. `entra.signins.managed_identity.blob` — the last unmapped blob diagnostic category (the status note above: "only ManagedIdentity remains open here"). The container appeared on m7kni 2026-07-20 (synthetic MI sign-ins, #135 data-gen), mapped verbatim: properties IS the same signIn resource, so `mapSignIn`/`deriveSignin` map it unchanged. It's a `.blob` twin of the polled beta `entra.signins.managed_identity` stream — live-measured 1/1 id overlap, so the pair `ConflictsWith` (#144). `make check` green. Deploy-verify on camden to follow.

Deploy-verified on camden (`version=2ac12bb`): `entra.signins.managed_identity.blob` run=1, ok=True, cursor advanced (read the full MI blob, 3250 bytes). The polled beta twin `entra.signins.managed_identity` was enabled on camden (opted-in when no blob existed) → conflicted at startup (#144 working as designed), so I disabled it in camden config; the blob is now the sole managed-identity transport, matching how `service_principal`/`non_interactive` already work.

title: feat(collectors): map the remaining 19 blob diagnostic categories (engine shipped; they land unread today)

body:
## Mission

Three Entra diagnostic categories exist that **nobody has assessed**, that **no collector maps to**, and whose **contents are unknown**:

- `GraphNotificationsActivityLogs`
- `MicrosoftGraphPolicyLogs`
- `PreAuthenticationDiscoveryLogs`

All three were **enabled on the `aadiam/graph2otel` diagnostic setting on 2026-07-16** specifically so their shape can be observed. **This issue is to assess them and then decide: build, or turn off.** They must not sit enabled-and-unexamined.

## Why we know nothing about them

- **Absent from Microsoft's published category doc** — [concept-diagnostic-settings-logs-options](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/monitoring-health/concept-diagnostic-settings-logs-options) documents ~15 categories. These are not among them.
- **The API returns no `categoryDisplayName`** — `GET /providers/microsoft.aadiam/diagnosticSettingsCategories` lists the names and nothing else.
- **No graph2otel collector maps to any of them.**
- They were **absent from the tenant's original 19-category diagnostic settings** (created 2025-10-02), so they are **new** — the category list grew from 19 to 26 in the interim.

**This is the honest position: we do not know if these are valuable, redundant, or noise.** Nobody should guess from the names.

## Why they were enabled rather than dismissed

The bar for every other category was *"no Graph route, or blob removes a beta dep, or blob supplies a dual-ship log side"* — and **nine categories were excluded** on it. These three are the deliberate exception, justified as **discovery**:

**Guessing from names would be reckless here, and today proves it.** On this exact tenant, in this session, the documented blob prefix was **wrong** (`resourceId=` vs the actual `tenantId=`), the sensitivity-label `displayName` is **always null** with the value in `name`, and two "confirmed permanent" gaps turned out to be **missing scopes**. Observation has beaten documentation four times today. Enabling costs ~£0.001/mo and the 7-day lifecycle caps the worst case.

**But "enable to find out" is only defensible if someone actually looks.** That is this issue.

## What to determine, per category

1. **Does it emit anything at all on m7kni?** Several enabled categories emit **zero rows** here (`ADFSSignInLogs`, `EnrichedOffice365AuditLogs`, the GSA family). These may be the same — in which case turn them off and record that they need a feature this tenant lacks.
2. **What is the row shape?** Read the raw JSON Lines. Field list, not a doc quote.
3. **Is it already covered by Graph?** Specifically:
   - `MicrosoftGraphPolicyLogs` — is this Conditional Access / policy *evaluation* telemetry? `entra.conditional_access` already polls CA **policy config**; evaluation *events* would be a genuinely different and valuable signal (which policy fired, on which sign-in). **Or it may just duplicate `SignInLogs`' CA detail — check before assuming.**
   - `GraphNotificationsActivityLogs` — Graph change-notification/subscription activity? Possibly related to `MicrosoftGraphActivityLogs` (already captured) but for the webhook surface.
   - `PreAuthenticationDiscoveryLogs` — pre-auth/app-proxy/Entra Private Access? If it needs GSA, expect zero rows like the rest of that family.
4. **Is it metric-shaped, log-shaped, or both?** Per #112: bounded aggregates → metrics; per-entity detail → log attributes, never labels; too-high-cardinality-for-a-label → **log twin, never dropped**.
5. **Volume.** If one is chatty it could cost more than everything else combined. Measure before keeping.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Raw rows captured for each (or **"emits zero rows on this tenant"** recorded, with how long we waited)
- [ ] Real field shape documented per category — observed, not inferred
- [ ] Overlap assessed against existing collectors (esp. `MicrosoftGraphPolicyLogs` vs `entra.conditional_access` and vs `SignInLogs`' CA detail)
- [ ] Volume measured per category
- [ ] **Verdict per category: build a collector / already covered / zero rows / not worth it**
- [ ] **Categories that do not earn their place are TURNED OFF** — do not leave them enabled by default
- [ ] Anything worth building gets its own issue with the shape and scope
- [ ] CLAUDE.md records what each actually is, so nobody re-investigates

## ⏳ Blocked on time

Azure documents **up to 24h** before data lands in a new storage destination (#89 saw Entra data in ~15 min, but these are different categories and may differ). **An empty container is expected, not broken.** Check with `g2o-arrival`.

## Out of scope

- Building collectors — that is a follow-up per category, if any earn it.
- Keeping them enabled indefinitely without a verdict. **The point is to decide.**

Related: #89 (categories enabled + the selection bar), #132 (same shape-verification pattern for Intune `Devices`/`DeviceComplianceOrg`), #112 (cardinality rule).

comments.body: Ripeness note (2026-07-17): the 24-hour observation bar (from enablement ~2026-07-16 14:15Z) has passed. The decision is actionable now — check whether any of the three containers exist as `graph2otel-poller`; #135's 18:32Z check already recorded 4.5h of silence.

## Zero containers for all three at 19.6h — but ⚠️ the 24h bar has NOT actually passed yet

Probed 2026-07-17 **09:47Z** as **`graph2otel-poller`** (appId `2c92ce28-126c-47c1-82b0-410b64502989`, cert credential). Container listing and blob content read both succeeded on this account, so this is a real negative, not an RBAC artifact.

**Evidence class: live-measured (2026-07-17, #134).**

### ⚠️ Correction to the ripeness comment above

The ripeness comment states the 24h bar "has passed". **By its own stated enablement time it has not.** Arithmetic:

| | |
| --- | --- |
| enablement (per the ripeness comment) | `2026-07-16T14:15Z` |
| probe time | `2026-07-17T09:47Z` |
| **elapsed** | **19.6h** |
| 24h bar fires at | `2026-07-17T14:15Z` |
| **remaining** | **4.4h** |

19.6h ≠ 24h. This does not change the *direction* of the evidence, but the acceptance criterion on this issue is explicit — *"Raw rows captured for each (or 'emits zero rows on this tenant' recorded, **with how long we waited**)"* — and "we waited 19.6h against a documented 24h bar" is not the same record as "we waited out the bar". **Turning them off now would be a verdict taken 4.4h early**, on an issue whose whole premise is that guessing ahead of observation has already been wrong four times on this tenant.

### The observation

Full container list on `graph2otelm7kni` — **9 containers, unchanged from the 2026-07-17 baseline**:

```
insights-logs-auditlogs
insights-logs-devicecomplianceorg
insights-logs-devices
insights-logs-microsoftgraphactivitylogs
insights-logs-microsoftserviceprincipalsigninlogs
insights-logs-noninteractiveusersigninlogs
insights-logs-provisioninglogs
insights-logs-serviceprincipalsigninlogs
insights-logs-signinlogs
```

| category | expected container | status at 19.6h |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GraphNotificationsActivityLogs` | `insights-logs-graphnotificationsactivitylogs` | **absent** |
| `MicrosoftGraphPolicyLogs` | `insights-logs-microsoftgraphpolicylogs` | **absent** |
| `PreAuthenticationDiscoveryLogs` | `insights-logs-preauthenticationdiscoverylogs` | **absent** |

Azure creates the container on first write, so absent = **nothing written yet**.

### What makes the negative meaningful — and what weakens it

**Strengthening it:** the Intune diagnostic setting (a *separate* setting, enabled at roughly the same time) **did** deliver inside this window — `insights-logs-devices` and `insights-logs-devicecomplianceorg` both appeared, first record `2026-07-17T00:14:37Z` = **10.0h after enablement** (see #132). So a category on this account that has data has demonstrably had time to prove it. The Entra live stream has been writing continuously throughout (see #137).

**Weakening it:** Intune `OperationalLogs` is *also* still container-less at 19.6h from the same setting — and nobody has concluded that one emits zero rows. First-write latency on this account has been observed anywhere from ~15 min (#89) to 10.0h (Intune, today). A 19.6h negative is consistent with "zero rows" **and** with "slow category", and the 10.0h datapoint is the reason the 24h bar exists rather than a 6h one.

### Recommendation

**Do not issue the verdict yet.** Re-list containers **after `2026-07-17T14:15Z`** (the actual bar). That is a one-command check:

```sh
# as graph2otel-poller, not az CLI / not homelab-agentic-mgmt
<probe> containers   # expect the same 9; a 10th = one of these three woke up
```

If all three are still absent at ≥24h, that satisfies this issue's acceptance criterion — record **"emits zero rows on this tenant, waited 24h+"** (evidence class: live-measured, negative) and turn them off per the acceptance criteria, noting that the shape/overlap/volume criteria are **unanswerable rather than unanswered**: with no rows there is nothing to document a field shape from, and `MicrosoftGraphPolicyLogs` vs `entra.conditional_access` overlap cannot be assessed from a name.

The zero-row outcome would put all three alongside `ADFSSignInLogs` / `EnrichedOffice365AuditLogs` / the GSA family — enabled, delivering nothing on m7kni, needing a tenant feature this tenant lacks. Worth recording *that* as the finding rather than "not valuable": on a tenant with the relevant feature they may well emit.

**I did not verify the diagnostic setting's own configuration** — that is an ARM control-plane read and the poller holds only `Storage Blob Data Reader` on this account plus Graph scopes. Reading it would require a different identity, which the identity split (#109) forbids for questions about what graph2otel can see. If the three categories were disabled or removed after 2026-07-16, container absence would prove nothing — **someone with ARM access should confirm the setting still lists all three** before the negative is recorded as final.

## ⛔ CORRECTION to my comment 30 minutes ago: `GraphNotificationsActivityLogs` is NOT zero-rows — it started emitting mid-probe

**Retract the "all three absent" framing above.** It was true at 09:47Z and false by 10:17Z.

`insights-logs-graphnotificationsactivitylogs` **now exists** and has data. First records:

```
insights-logs-graphnotificationsactivitylogs/tenantId=4b8c18bd-…/y=2026/m=07/d=17/h=09/m=00/PT1H.json
  5,624 bytes, 2 records, blob written 09:54:36Z
  record event times: 09:50:51.1268375Z, 09:51:04.8930910Z
```

| | |
| --- | --- |
| container absent at | **09:47:06Z** (snapshot A + B, both confirmed) |
| container present at | **10:17:25Z** (snapshot C) |
| first record event time | **2026-07-17T09:50:51Z** |
| first blob write | **09:54:36Z** (≈3.7 min propagation — consistent with the ~4 min Entra-side delay) |
| **elapsed since enablement** (~2026-07-16T14:15Z) | **19.6h** |

**This is the whole reason the 24h bar exists.** My previous comment declined to issue the zero-rows verdict at 19.6h on the grounds that the bar had not actually passed. It hadn't, and the category woke up **6 minutes later**. Had the verdict been taken at the 19.6h mark — as the ripeness comment's "the decision is actionable now" invited — this category would have been **turned off 6 minutes before it first emitted**, and the issue closed with a permanently wrong finding.

Recording the mechanism, since "the container was absent for 19.6h" is genuinely misleading evidence: **first-write latency on this account now spans ~15 min (#89) → 10.0h (Intune, #132) → 19.6h (this category)**. Container absence is a **very weak** signal until well past 24h. Do not treat it as a countdown that gets more meaningful in a smooth curve — it does not.

### What it actually is: Graph change-notification publisher telemetry

#134's hypothesis — *"Graph change-notification/subscription activity? Possibly related to `MicrosoftGraphActivityLogs` but for the webhook surface"* — is **confirmed**. It logs Graph's own notification-publisher worker delivering change notifications to subscribers.

Observed envelope (n=2, live-measured 2026-07-17):

| envelope | type | sample |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `time` | str | `2026-07-17T09:51:04.8930910Z` (ISO, 7-digit fraction) |
| `resourceId` | str | `d0428537-bde0-416e-9bcf-ebb922bac393\|` — **a request id with a trailing pipe, NOT an ARM resource path** |
| `operationName` | str | `Graph Notifications Activity` |
| `category` | str | `GraphNotificationsActivityLogs` |
| `resultSignature` | str | `7/17/2026 9:51:04 AM +00:00` — **US-format datetime in a "signature" field** |
| `durationMs` | str | `"17"` (string at top level, **int inside `properties`** — the same top-level-string/nested-int split MGAL has) |
| `level` | str | `Informational` |
| `location` | str | `North Europe` |
| `tenantId` | str | |

`properties` (25 keys): `message`, `timeGenerated`, `correlationId`, `contextId`, `resourceId`, `resultDescription`, `resultSignature`, `resultStatusCode` (int), `subscriptionId`, `publicationIds`, `applicationId`, `workloadNamespace`, `workloadResource`, `webHeaders`, `accountType`, `containerLocation`, `operationType`, `loggingLevel`, `durationMs` (int), `isReplay`, `location`, `tenantId`, + the four `__UDI_RequiredFields_*` keys to drop.

The payload is **prose in `message`**, not structured fields:

```
Publishing 1 notifications to aadgroups-dq-prodweu.vault.azure.net
Message.Id: d0428537-…|
 Basic notification for TenantId: 4b8c18bd-…, appId: 65d91a3d-…
Publication time: 7/17/2026 9:51:04 AM +00:00
Request-Id: d0428537-…
Duration: 17
Response:
 200 OK: Successfully published notifications to the event hub.
Connection info:
 Use singleton http-client: True …
```

`workloadResource` is a **JSON string** (not an object) carrying the actual change:

```json
{"changeType":"updated","clientState":"<scrubbed>","resource":"Groups/dc8c1de9-…",
 "[IsResourceTransformed]":true,"subscriptionExpirationDateTime":"…","subscriptionId":"…","tenantId":"…"}
```

### Assessment against this issue's criteria

1. **Emits on m7kni?** **Yes** — but barely: 2 records in the first hour. Volume is negligible next to MGAL (386 appends/h). Needs a longer window to characterise; **do not extrapolate a rate from n=2**.
2. **Row shape?** Documented above. **Prose-in-`message`, not structured** — the useful fields (`changeType`, `resource`) are buried in a JSON *string* inside `workloadResource`, and `resource` is the only per-entity handle.
3. **Already covered by Graph?** **No** — this is the notification/webhook publishing surface. `MicrosoftGraphActivityLogs` covers Graph *API calls*; this covers Graph *pushing notifications outward*. Genuinely different, and no Graph read endpoint exposes it.
4. **Metric- or log-shaped?** **Log-shaped.** Per-notification rows with per-entity `resource` handles. A bounded gauge could count by `resultStatusCode`/`workloadNamespace`/`changeType`; the rows themselves are twin material (#112/#114).
5. **Whose notifications?** ⚠️ **Both observed records are Microsoft's own first-party subscriptions**, not the tenant's: appIds `65d91a3d-…` and `65c8bd9e-…`, publishing to `aadgroups-dq-prodweu.vault.azure.net` and `peopleprofileeventprodwesteuropealias.servicebus.windows.net` — Microsoft-internal endpoints. **n=2, so this is a hint, not a finding.** If it holds, the category's value is low for a tenant that runs no Graph subscriptions of its own — it would mostly log Microsoft talking to itself. **This is the question that decides build-vs-disable, and it needs a real observation window, not two rows.**

### The other two

Still **absent** at 10:17Z (19.6h+ — bar fires 14:15Z):

| category | container | status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `MicrosoftGraphPolicyLogs` | `insights-logs-microsoftgraphpolicylogs` | **absent** |
| `PreAuthenticationDiscoveryLogs` | `insights-logs-preauthenticationdiscoverylogs` | **absent** |

Given one of the three surfaced at 19.6h, **absence for these two now carries even less weight than my previous comment allowed.** Re-check after 14:15Z, and honestly, given the observed 19.6h datapoint, a 48h re-check would be better evidence than a 24h one before either is disabled.

### Revised recommendation

- **`GraphNotificationsActivityLogs`** — **do not disable.** It emits, it is not covered by Graph, and it is log-shaped. **But do not build a collector yet either**: decide first whether it carries anything but Microsoft-internal notification traffic (criterion 5). Suggest a **7-day observation** against `applicationId` distribution — the same "is this our data or Microsoft's?" question that `MicrosoftServicePrincipalSignInLogs` had to answer, and which `docs/blob-ingest.md` resolved in that category's favour. Cost of waiting is ~£0.001/mo.
- **`MicrosoftGraphPolicyLogs` / `PreAuthenticationDiscoveryLogs`** — verdict still not takeable. Re-check ≥14:15Z, preferably 2026-07-18.

### Unrelated but observed on the same account, worth knowing

Two containers **not on this issue's list** also appeared during the probe window: `insights-logs-riskyusers` (10:16:53Z) and `insights-logs-userriskevents` (10:12:18Z). Contents are #129's synthesized risk event (`risk-synth-DELETE-ME@m7kni.io`, `riskEventType: anonymizedIPAddress`) — i.e. **#129's synthesis worked and the blob side now has live risk data.** Flagged on #137; not touched here.

## 1 of 3 has emitted: `GraphNotificationsActivityLogs` — first rows, real shape

`insights-logs-graphnotificationsactivitylogs` **now exists** (container created 09:54:02Z,
2026-07-17). It did not exist during this morning's sweep, so this is new within the last hour.

Listed and read as **`graph2otel-poller`** (SP `2c92ce28-…`, cert auth — verified via
`az account show` that the session was the poller and not a cached user login, which it initially was;
the first listing attempt silently ran as `rob@m7kni.io` because `az login -p` no longer accepts a
certificate and fell through to a cached session. Worth knowing: `az` fails that one **open**, not
closed).

`[live-measured 2026-07-17, #134]`

| category | container | verdict |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GraphNotificationsActivityLogs` | **exists**, 2 rows in the first hourly blob | **emits — assessed below** |
| `MicrosoftGraphPolicyLogs` | absent | still no data |
| `PreAuthenticationDiscoveryLogs` | absent | still no data |

Blob path `tenantId=…/y=2026/m=07/d=17/h=09/m=00/PT1H.json` — **the `tenantId=` prefix layout holds**
for this category too.

### What it actually is

**Graph change-notification (webhook subscription) delivery telemetry** — one record per notification
publish attempt. Not a guess; the payload says so:

```json
{
  "time": "2026-07-17T09:51:04.8930910Z",
  "operationName": "Graph Notifications Activity",
  "category": "GraphNotificationsActivityLogs",
  "resultSignature": "7/17/2026 9:51:04 AM +00:00",
  "durationMs": "17",
  "properties": {
    "resultDescription": "200 OK: Successfully published notifications to the event hub.",
    "resultStatusCode": 200,
    "subscriptionId": "86ffb427-d53c-4f15-b609-2d8b4005eab5",
    "workloadNamespace": "Microsoft.DirectoryServices",
    "workloadResource": "{ \"changeType\": \"updated\", \"clientState\": \"<scrubbed>\",
                           \"resource\": \"Groups/dc8c1de9-…\", … }",
    "applicationId": "65d91a3d-ab74-42e6-8a2f-0add61688c74",
    "timeGenerated": "2026-07-17T09:51:04.893091Z",
    "correlationId": "252b75ec-…",
    "durationMs": 17
  }
}
```

**Assessment against this issue's three questions:**

1. **Does it emit on m7kni?** Yes — but only because *some other app* holds a Graph change-notification
   subscription (appId `65d91a3d-…`, on `Groups/…`, publishing to an event hub). **graph2otel uses no
   change notifications**, so this category describes third-party subscription traffic in the tenant,
   never graph2otel's own.
2. **Row shape:** field list above, read off the wire.
3. **Already covered by Graph?** No — there is no Graph endpoint for notification *delivery* outcomes.
   It is genuinely new information. Whether it is *useful* is the open question: it is
   delivery-plumbing telemetry (did a webhook publish succeed, how long did it take), not identity or
   security signal.

### Traps found in the shape

- **`resultSignature` is a US-format timestamp** (`"7/17/2026 9:51:04 AM +00:00"`), not a signature.
  Same class as O365's `CreationTime` and `UserRiskEvents`' `time`. The envelope's own `time` field is
  proper ISO-8601 — a mapper must not reach for `resultSignature`.
- **`durationMs` is a STRING at envelope level (`"17"`) and an INT inside `properties` (`17`).** Same
  name, two types, one record.
- **`resourceId` is not a resource id** — it is `"d0428537-bde0-416e-9bcf-ebb922bac393|"`, a message id
  with a trailing pipe. It does not match the ARM-style `resourceId` every other category uses.
- **Microsoft's internal plumbing leaks into the schema**: `__UDI_RequiredFields_TenantId`,
  `__UDI_RequiredFields_UniqueId`, `__UDI_RequiredFields_EventTime` (a .NET tick count,
  `639198786648930910`, not a timestamp any parser will recognise), `__UDI_RequiredFields_RegionScope`.
  These are undocumented and could vanish without notice — do not bind to them.
- **`message` is a multi-line human-readable blob** carrying connection-pool internals
  (`Connections limit: 48`, `Use singleton http-client: True`). It duplicates the structured fields.

### Recommendation (not yet a decision)

**Lean disable for `GraphNotificationsActivityLogs`**, on the issue's own bar — *"no Graph route, or
blob removes a beta dep, or blob supplies a dual-ship log side"*. It clears the first clause (no Graph
route) but the signal is third-party webhook-delivery plumbing with no identity/security value for a
SIEM feed, and its schema is visibly unstable (undocumented `__UDI_` internals, a type-inconsistent
field, a misnamed `resourceId`). Cost of leaving it enabled is trivial, but this issue's whole point is
that enabled-and-unexamined is the thing to avoid — it is now examined, and the answer is "not for us".

**The other two remain unanswerable.** Their containers do not exist, and per the "created on first
write" behaviour that means **no data has been generated**, not that the categories are broken — the
same lesson `UserRiskEvents` just taught on this tenant (see below). Do not conclude "dead" from
absence.

### Related, and it is the reason to be patient here

`insights-logs-userriskevents` and `insights-logs-riskyusers` **both appeared today at 10:12Z and
10:16Z** — created by the synthetic risk event in #129, minutes after being absent for the entire life
of this tenant. They were missing because **there was nothing to write**, not because the categories
did not work. `MicrosoftGraphPolicyLogs` and `PreAuthenticationDiscoveryLogs` may be in exactly that
state: functional, waiting for a triggering activity this tenant has not performed. Absence is not
evidence here, and this tenant has now demonstrated that twice in one day.

## Verdict: `GraphNotificationsActivityLogs` → **NOISE, turn off**

Sampled live 2026-07-18 as `graph2otel-poller` (cert on camden). 65 KB / 7 blobs on `graph2otelm7kni`. Real row shape (one record):

```json
{ "operationName": "Graph Notifications Activity", "category": "GraphNotificationsActivityLogs",
  "resultDescription": "200 OK: Successfully published notifications to the event hub.",
  "properties": { "message": "Publishing 1 notifications to aadgroups-dq-prodweu.vault.azure.net ...
    Basic notification for TenantId: 4b8c18bd-..., appId: 65d91a3d-ab74-42e6-8a2f-0add61688c74 ...
    Response: 200 OK: Successfully published notifications to the event hub.",
    "resultStatusCode": 200, "subscriptionId": "fb1d7486-...", "durationMs": 21 } }
```

This is **change-notification delivery telemetry** for a Graph subscription — the "we published N notifications to an event hub / 200 OK" plumbing log. Two things settle it as noise:

- **It is not graph2otel's own signal.** The emitting `appId` (`65d91a3d-…`) is not the poller's app registration, and graph2otel has no change-notification/webhook subscriber anywhere in the codebase (`grep` for `changeNotification` / `/subscriptions` only hits the unrelated O365 Management Activity API machinery in `internal/o365pipeline`). This is a third-party/first-party-Microsoft subscription's delivery health, riding this tenant.
- **No actionable security or inventory content.** The payload is a success/failure delivery message (`200 OK`, `durationMs`), not an audited action. There is no anomaly framing, no per-entity subject worth a log twin. `MicrosoftGraphActivityLogs` (already ingested by `entra.graph_activity`) is the *API-call* telemetry that matters; this is only the webhook-fanout side, and for subscriptions graph2otel does not own.

**Recommendation: turn off the `GraphNotificationsActivityLogs` category on the `aadiam/graph2otel` diagnostic setting.** No collector, no build. `MicrosoftGraphPolicyLogs` and `PreAuthenticationDiscoveryLogs` (this issue's other two) were not among the enabled containers in the 2026-07-18 inventory — they emit zero rows here and are still pending their own sample.

`[live-measured 2026-07-18, #134, n=1]`

Closed by `60d7571`.

**`GraphNotificationsActivityLogs` → built** as `entra.graph_notifications` (blob collector, on by default when blob ingest is configured). Mapped against a live sample as `graph2otel-poller` (2026-07-17): change-notification delivery telemetry — `application_id` (subscription owner, the persistence/supply-chain signal), `subscription_id`, `workload_namespace`, `operation_type`, `result_status_code`, `result_description`. Severity from `result_status_code` (the record `level` is `"Informational"` on everything — same trap as MGAL). `[live-measured 2026-07-18]`

**The other two unknowns: verdict `leave enabled, documented gap`.** `MicrosoftGraphPolicyLogs` and `PreAuthenticationDiscoveryLogs` write **zero** on m7kni — both still absent from the storage account 24h+ after diagnostic-settings enablement (31-container inventory, 2026-07-18). No live sample ⇒ no mapper (the project rule: never map against imagination). They stay enabled in the diagnostic setting so a sample can land later; if either ever emits, file a build issue then. Not disabled — the streaming cost of two empty categories is nil, and disabling would forfeit the free chance to catch a first sample.

**Correction (`live-measured 2026-07-23`, #238):** an earlier comment on this issue stated that reading the diagnostic setting's own configuration "would require a different identity, which the identity split (#109) forbids." That premise is **wrong**. `graph2otel-poller`, using its own cert with an ARM-audience token, reads `GET https://management.azure.com/providers/microsoft.aadiam/diagnosticSettings?api-version=2017-04-01` → **200** (setting `graph2otel`, 26 categories / 21 enabled). It is authorized by the poller's Entra roles, not Azure RBAC. The boundary is narrow: `microsoft.intune/diagnosticSettings` and the storage account resource itself both 403 for the same identity — so it is specifically the tenant-level `microsoft.aadiam` provider that reads, not ARM generally. Recorded in `docs/blob-ingest.md`; the census-gate collector this enables is tracked on #238.

Correction (#238, live-measured 2026-07-23 as `graph2otel-poller`): the earlier note here — "reading the diagnostic settings own configuration would require a different identity, which the identity split (#109) forbids" — is **wrong**. The poller reads the tenant-level `microsoft.aadiam` diagnostic settings as *itself*, authorized by its Entra roles rather than by Azure RBAC:

- `GET https://management.azure.com/providers/microsoft.aadiam/diagnosticSettings?api-version=2017-04-01` → **200** (26 categories, 21 enabled)
- `GET .../providers/microsoft.intune/diagnosticSettings` → **403** `AuthorizationFailed`
- the storage account resource itself → **403** `AuthorizationFailed`

So the boundary is real but much narrower than recorded: the `microsoft.aadiam` provider reads; general ARM (Intune provider, the storage account) does not. This unblocked the blob-category census in #238 (shipped `0018b32`). The Intune half of the census still needs an Azure-RBAC identity and stays out of scope.
