body:
> **Status (2026-07-19):** the **service-principal** signal is DONE — `entra.service_principal_risk_detections` shipped (`90b3708`/`66ae6d4`/`3e0a7b8`) and live-verified against a synthesized detection; `entra.risk`'s risky-SP gauge false-negative WIP gate was fixed too (`9d50c0b`). This issue stays OPEN scoped ONLY to **`riskyAgents` + `agentRiskDetections`**, which are BLOCKED (no Entra Agent ID identity exists on m7kni to map against — unblock = stand up one agent identity). See the latest comment for the full record.

---

## Mission

Three Identity Protection signals have **no graph2otel collector at all** — we capture them nowhere, via neither Graph nor blob. All three are **verified reachable** and their diagnostic categories are now enabled, so the data will be waiting.

| signal | Graph endpoint | reachable? | blob category | collector |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Service principal risk detections** | `identityProtection/servicePrincipalRiskDetections` | ✅ **200 on v1.0 AND beta** | `ServicePrincipalRiskEvents` ✅ enabled | ❌ **none** |
| **Risky agents** | `identityProtection/riskyAgents` | ✅ **200 on beta** (403 until `IdentityRiskyAgent.Read.All` was granted 2026-07-16) | `RiskyAgents` ✅ enabled | ❌ **none** |
| **Agent risk detections** | `identityProtection/agentRiskDetections` | ✅ **200 on beta** | `AgentRiskEvents` ✅ enabled | ❌ **none** |

All probed as **`graph2otel-poller`** (`2c92ce28-…`) via `g2o-probe` — the only identity whose answers are valid for graph2otel.

## Why these matter

**Workload and agent identities are the gap in most identity monitoring.** graph2otel already ships `entra.risky_users`, `entra.risky_service_principals` (gauge) and `entra.risk_detections` (user risk events) — so we report **which service principals are risky** but **never why**, because `servicePrincipalRiskDetections` is the detection-level detail and nothing polls it. That is half a signal: a gauge with no evidence behind it.

**`RiskyAgents` / `AgentRiskEvents` are a genuinely new surface** — Entra ID Protection now scores **AI agent identities** for compromise risk. graph2otel is a SIEM feed; an emerging identity attack surface with zero coverage is exactly the kind of gap worth closing early. Note the asymmetry today: `agentRiskDetections` was reachable with pre-existing scopes while `riskyAgents` needed a grant — so we could already see the *events* but not *which agents* are flagged. Same half-a-signal shape.

## Proposed shape (respects the cardinality rule — #112)

Per-entity detail (SP object ID, app ID, display name, agent identity, IP, detection timing) is **log-shaped**, never a metric label — a series keyed on a detection ID gets exactly one sample ever, the pathological TSDB case.

- **Gauges** bucketed on bounded enums only: `risk_level`, `risk_state`, `risk_detail`, `detection_type`, `activity`
  - `entra.service_principal_risk_detections.count`
  - `entra.risky_agents.count`
  - `entra.agent_risk_detections.count`
- **Log twins**, one per entity — the reference shape is `entra/risk` (#110): bounded gauge + one log per entity, **from the same fetch, no extra Graph calls**.
  - `entra.service_principal_risk_detection` · `entra.risky_agent` · `entra.agent_risk_event`

**`riskyAgents` / `agentRiskDetections` are beta-only** (v1.0 → 400). So they must be `Experimental`/opt-in, exactly like the filtered sign-in streams — **unless** their blob categories prove viable, which would make them v1.0-stable (see #131). `servicePrincipalRiskDetections` is **v1.0** and can be default-on.

## ⚠️ Cannot be verified on m7kni today — and that is the real risk

Every one of these returns **200 with ZERO rows**:

```
identityProtection/servicePrincipalRiskDetections -> 200, 0 rows
identityProtection/riskyAgents (beta)             -> 200, 0 rows
identityProtection/agentRiskDetections (beta)     -> 200, 0 rows
```

**A mapping bug against an always-empty collection is invisible** — wrong field name, wrong enum, wrong severity scale; the collector reports success forever. That is not hypothetical: the sensitivity-label catalog returns `displayName: null` on every label with the real value in `name` (#126), a trap that only surfaced because real rows existed to look at.

**#129 (synthetic UserRiskEvent) is the mitigation** — it is the only way to get a real risk row on this tenant. This issue should land its mappings **against real data**, or explicitly accept that they are unverified and say so in the code.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `servicePrincipalRiskDetections` collector — v1.0, default-on, gauge + log twin from one fetch
- [ ] `riskyAgents` + `agentRiskDetections` collectors — beta, **`Experimental`/opt-in**, gauge + log twin
- [ ] Scopes declared per collector; `IdentityRiskyAgent.Read.All` documented in SECURITY.md (granted 2026-07-16)
- [ ] **Distinct `CheckpointKey` per stream** — these share the `/identityProtection/` path prefix; without it they collide on one namespace and dedupe each other's events away (the exact bug the 4 sign-in streams hit)
- [ ] `EndpointConfig.PageSize=500` — **Identity Protection caps `$top` at 500, not 1000**; the logpipeline default of 1000 400s
- [ ] Severity mapped on the right scale — `telemetry.Severity` (Info=0/Warn=1/Error=2), **NOT** the OTEL wire scale (#113)
- [ ] Verified against ≥1 real row (via #129) — or the gap explicitly recorded in the code and this issue
- [ ] `make check` green

## Out of scope

- The blob path for these (#89/#131). This issue is the **Graph** collectors; blob is a later source option.
- Guessing field shapes from docs. Today proved the docs wrong twice on this tenant (blob prefix, `displayName`).

Related: #129 (synthetic risk event — the only way to verify), #110 (risk log-twin reference shape), #113 (severity scale), #131 (dual-ship), #89 (categories enabled).

comments.body:
## Investigation: how to generate real rows to verify these mappers (2026-07-19)

Not building blind mappers (CLAUDE.md wire-over-docs). Investigated how to make a **real** row appear in each collection first. Probed live as `graph2otel-poller` from camden.

### Premise re-verified — all three still empty `[live-measured 2026-07-19, #133, n=1 tenant]`

```
v1.0/identityProtection/servicePrincipalRiskDetections -> 200, 0 rows
beta/identityProtection/servicePrincipalRiskDetections -> 200, 0 rows
v1.0/identityProtection/riskyServicePrincipals          -> 200, 0 rows
beta/identityProtection/riskyAgents                     -> 200, 0 rows
beta/identityProtection/agentRiskDetections             -> 200, 0 rows
```

The poller already holds the **read** scopes the collectors need — no read grant required:
`IdentityRiskEvent.Read.All`, `IdentityRiskyUser.Read.All`, `IdentityRiskyServicePrincipal.Read.All`, `IdentityRiskyAgent.Read.All`.

### Synthesis verdict per signal

| signal | synthesizable? | how | gating action |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `servicePrincipalRiskDetections` | **yes, cheap + reversible** | `POST /identityProtection/riskyServicePrincipals/confirmCompromised` on a throwaway SP → writes an `adminConfirmedServicePrincipalCompromised` detection (the analogue of #129's user path). Sets risk `high`; reversible via `dismiss` or deleting the SP. | needs a **write** scope + a tenant mutation (below) |
| `riskyAgents` + `agentRiskDetections` | **blocked, no cheap path** | the confirm-compromise write (`POST /identityProtection/riskyAgents/confirmCompromised`, scope `IdentityRiskyAgent.ReadWrite.All`) needs an **Entra Agent ID identity to exist first** — m7kni has none (`riskyAgents` = 0), and ID-Protection-for-agents may require an **Agent 365** license. | park until an agent identity exists on the tenant |

### Proposed SP-risk synthesis (needs explicit approval — tenant mutation + scope grant)

Keeps the poller read-only; the write is done by `homelab-agentic-mgmt`, not the poller.
1. Create a disposable app registration + its SP (`g2o-sprisk-synth`, clearly labelled DELETE-ME).
2. Grant **`IdentityRiskyServicePrincipal.ReadWrite.All`** to `homelab-agentic-mgmt` (write scope, one-time).
3. `POST /identityProtection/riskyServicePrincipals/confirmCompromised` with the throwaway SP's object id → real `servicePrincipalRiskDetection` row appears within minutes.
4. Read it as the poller, capture the verbatim record, write + test the collector against it.
5. Clean up: `dismiss` the SP and delete the throwaway app registration.

### Recommendation
Build the **`servicePrincipalRiskDetections`** collector (v1.0, default-on) against a synthesized real row per the plan above, once approved. Ship **`riskyAgents`/`agentRiskDetections`** only when an Agent ID identity exists on a tenant to map against — do NOT ship them blind. Sources: Microsoft Learn workload-identity-risk + riskyServicePrincipal:confirmCompromised + concept-risky-agents.

## SP half SHIPPED + live-verified against a synthesized real detection; agent halves stay parked

Data-gate cleared for the service-principal signal by synthesizing a real row (Rob-approved). All live-verified as `graph2otel-poller` from camden.

### Shipped (deployed to camden `:main`, `make check` green)
| SHA | what |
| --- | --- |
| `90b3708` | `entra.service_principal_risk_detections` — log-shaped WindowCollector over `/identityProtection/servicePrincipalRiskDetections` (v1.0, default-on). One log per detection. The SP-risk STATE gauge already ships via `entra.risk`, so this is deliberately not a second gauge. |
| `66ae6d4` | **fix:** removed the `CapWorkloadIdentitiesPremium` gate — see the false-negative note below. |
| `3e0a7b8` | maps `mitre_techniques` from the doubly-encoded `additionalInfo` (the detection enriched to carry `T1078` — Valid Accounts), matching the user-detection twin. |
| `9d50c0b` | **fix to `entra.risk`:** its risky-SP gauge had the same false-negative gate — now emits without WIP too. |

### The WIP capability is a FALSE NEGATIVE on m7kni `[live-measured 2026-07-19, #133]`
License detection reports **no Workload Identities Premium** on m7kni (so `entra.risk` was internally skipping its SP half, and my first cut of the new collector was skipped with `skip_reason: requires workload_identities_premium`), **yet** `GET /identityProtection/servicePrincipalRiskDetections` and `/riskyServicePrincipals` return **200 with real data**, and `confirmCompromised` returns **204**. Gating on the capability hid both signals on the exact tenant where they work. Both now poll unconditionally and degrade gracefully (403 → info-skip, not a failure). This closes a latent bug in `entra.risk` too — its risky-SP gauge was invisible on m7kni.

### Synthesis (executed + cleaned up)
Granted `IdentityRiskyServicePrincipal.ReadWrite.All` to `homelab-agentic-mgmt` (NOT the poller), created a throwaway SP, `confirmCompromised` → real `adminConfirmedServicePrincipalCompromised` detection. Read back the verbatim row (pinned as the test fixture). Gotcha: `POST /servicePrincipals` 400s `NoBackingApplicationObject` immediately after `POST /applications` (Entra replication lag — retry). The detection **enriched over ~25 min** (source/detectionTimingType/displayName/appId/mitreTechniques populated later). **Cleanup done:** risk dismissed + throwaway app deleted. The mgmt write-scope grant persists (revoke if unwanted).

### Still BLOCKED — `riskyAgents` + `agentRiskDetections`
No Entra Agent ID identity exists on m7kni to confirm-compromise, and ID-Protection-for-agents may need an Agent 365 license — so no real row exists to map against, and CLAUDE.md forbids mapping blind. **Unblock condition:** stand up ≥1 Agent ID identity on a tenant; then the same confirmCompromised path works with `IdentityRiskyAgent.ReadWrite.All` (the poller already holds the read scope). **This issue stays OPEN scoped to these two.**

## Agent halves re-checked — still blocked (2026-07-19)

Re-probed the unblock condition live as graph2otel-poller from camden:
```
beta/identityProtection/riskyAgents         -> 200, 0 rows
beta/identityProtection/agentRiskDetections -> 200, 0 rows
```
No Entra Agent ID identity exists on m7kni yet, so there is still no real row to map `riskyAgents` / `agentRiskDetections` against, and CLAUDE.md forbids mapping blind. **Unblock condition (unchanged, not fired):** stand up ≥1 Agent ID identity on a tenant, then the same `confirmCompromised` synthesis path used for the SP half works (`IdentityRiskyAgent.ReadWrite.All`; the poller already holds the read scope). Staying parked, issue open scoped to these two signals.

## Agent halves DONE + deployed + verified on camden (m7kni) — #133 fully closed

Commit `fd7a1fa` (pushed as `99670c8`, `Closes #133`). The two remaining Identity Protection signals — `riskyAgents` + `agentRiskDetections` — now have collectors, mapped against a **real synthesized row**, live on camden (`version=99670c8`).

### Unblock: an Entra Agent ID identity now exists (Agent 365 trial)
The blocker on the last two comments was "no Entra Agent ID identity on m7kni to map against". An Agent 365 trial is now active and real agent identities exist (`testagent`, `robs-blueprint`, a Copilot Studio agent). Synthesised a real detection the same way as the SP half (Rob-approved 2026-07-20):

- `homelab-agentic-mgmt` self-granted **`IdentityRiskyAgent.ReadWrite.All`** (201).
- `POST /beta/identityProtection/riskyAgents/confirmCompromised` `{"agentIds":["7d5472af-…"]}` (the **testagent** identity) → **204**. Body param `agentIds` is undocumented — now live-verified.
- Rows appeared in ~3 min and enriched over ~3 min (empty → `mitreTechniques: T1078`, `source: IdentityProtection`, `detectionTimingType: offline`), exactly like the SP synthesis.

### Built (beta-only → Experimental, read-only `IdentityRiskyAgent.Read.All`, IPC PageSize 500)
- **`entra.risky_agents`** — current-agent-risk STATE: bounded gauge `entra.risky_agents.total{risk_level,risk_state}` + one `entra.risky_agent` log twin per agent. The agent analog of `entra.risk`; ungated (reachability-driven, 403 → graceful skip — same fix as the risky-SP half). Distinct from a metric label per #112.
- **`entra.agent_risk_detections`** — the detection EVENT stream (log-only WindowCollector), the agent analog of `entra.service_principal_risk_detections`. `additionalInfo` is the same doubly-encoded `{Key,Value}` MITRE payload (#142).
- 5 new semconv attrs (`agent_id`, `agent_display_name`, `blueprint_id`, `is_enabled`, `risk_evidence`); mappers pinned against the verbatim rows (`[live-measured 2026-07-20, #133]`). `make check` green; `docs/collectors.md` + signal goldens regenerated.

### Verified in Grafana Cloud (grafanacloud-prom / -logs)
- **Metric** `entra_risky_agents_total{risk_level="high",risk_state="confirmedCompromised"}=1`, `tenant_id` stamped.
- **State twin** `entra.risky_agent`: `agent_display_name=testagent, risk_level=high, risk_state=confirmedCompromised, risk_detail=adminConfirmedAgentCompromised, is_enabled=true, is_deleted=false, is_processing=false, ingest_transport=graph`.
- **Event twin** `entra.agent_risk_detection`: `risk_event_type=adminConfirmedAgentCompromised, risk_evidence="Admin confirmed agent compromised", mitre_techniques=T1078, detection_timing_type=offline, source=IdentityProtection, agent_id=7d5472af-…`.

### Acceptance
- [x] `riskyAgents` + `agentRiskDetections` collectors — beta, `Experimental`/opt-in, gauge/twin + event stream
- [x] Scopes declared (`IdentityRiskyAgent.Read.All`); surfaced in generated `docs/collectors.md`
- [x] Distinct `CheckpointKey` per stream (distinct paths → no override needed); `PageSize=500` (IPC cap)
- [x] Severity on `telemetry.Severity` scale (#113)
- [x] Verified against a real row (synthesized) — not mapped blind
- [x] `make check` green

### Cleanup
Dismissing testagent's risk state now that the collectors have captured the row (a follow-up comment will confirm). The `IdentityRiskyAgent.ReadWrite.All` grant on `homelab-agentic-mgmt` persists, mirroring how the SP-half `IdentityRiskyServicePrincipal.ReadWrite.All` grant was left — revoke if unwanted.

Cleanup confirmed: testagent risk state settled to `riskState: dismissed`, `isProcessing: false` on both `/beta/identityProtection/riskyAgents` and `/beta/identityProtection/agentRiskDetections` (read back as graph2otel-poller). The synthesized detection is no longer an active risk. The `IdentityRiskyAgent.ReadWrite.All` grant on `homelab-agentic-mgmt` remains in place (mirrors the SP-half `IdentityRiskyServicePrincipal.ReadWrite.All` grant); revoke if unwanted.

body:
## Mission

Determine whether the Intune **`Devices`** and **`DeviceComplianceOrg`** diagnostic categories carry **per-device inventory rows** or merely event notifications.

**If `Devices` carries per-device rows, it retires graph2otel's single most expensive poll.** That is the whole reason this issue exists.

## Why this matters more than it looks

`intune.devices` pages the **entire managed-device fleet every hour**. CLAUDE.md records this as the deliberate exception to "never page the full collection", forced by a hard API limit:

> **Intune `managedDevices` has no `$count` segment** (M4, verified live). `GET /deviceManagement/managedDevices/$count` → **HTTP 400** *"No OData route exists that match template ~/singleton/navigation/$count"* — its backend is `DeviceFE/StatelessDeviceFEService`, not the directory OData stack. AND `operatingSystem` is **not** server-`$filter`able. So there is no bounded `$count`/`$filter` slice for the fleet — page the full collection with a trimmed `$select` and bucket/count **client-side**.

On a 10k-device tenant that walk runs against Intune's **elevated Devices throttle tier** every hour. It is the worst poll graph2otel has, and it is currently unavoidable.

## The reasoning this issue exists to test

A recent audit (#130) concluded the page-walk is **"irreducible by design, not by API limitation"**:

> `manageddevices.go:466` emits `e.LogEvent(deviceLogTwin(...))` **per device** — the per-device rows *are* the deliverable, not just an input to a count. Replacing the page-walk with a bounded count would **delete the log twins and violate CLAUDE.md's hard rule**. `managedDeviceOverview` is already implemented as a cross-check (`intune.devices.overview.*`) — and its OS summary sums to **9** against a real fleet of **10** (no Linux bucket), so it could not substitute even if the rule allowed it.

**That reasoning is correct against a bounded count. It does NOT hold against a blob category carrying per-device rows.**

If the `Devices` category emits one row per device, blob serves **both** the log twins **and** the client-side buckets — the exact two things the page-walk exists for. The walk then disappears entirely, with **no** loss of per-entity detail and **no** violation of the cardinality rule. That is a materially different conclusion, and it turns on one unverified fact: **the shape of the blob rows.**

## Do NOT guess the shape — today already proved the docs wrong here

Both categories were enabled on the `microsoft.intune/graph2otel` diagnostic setting on **2026-07-16** (blob-only; no Event Hub). Nothing is verifiable until blobs land.

The docs are **not** a substitute. On this exact storage path today, the documented blob prefix (`resourceId=/tenants/<tid>/providers/...`) was **wrong** — the real one is `tenantId=<guid>/` (#89). Coding to the docs would have produced a collector that finds nothing. **Observe, do not infer.**

## ⏳ Blocked on time — expect a delay

- Azure documents **up to 24h** before data appears in a newly-configured storage destination. In practice #89 saw Entra data in **~15 minutes**, but Intune's cadence is unknown and may differ.
- **An empty container is expected, not broken.** Do not "fix" the diagnostic setting in response to it.
- Check with: `g2o-arrival` (reads the blob account; safe to run any time).

## Questions to answer

1. **Is `Devices` one row per device, or an event notification?** Read the raw JSON Lines.
2. **What fields does a row carry?** Compare against what `manageddevices.go`'s log twin emits. Anything missing means blob cannot fully replace the walk.
3. **What is the push cadence?** Hourly? On-change? On-check-in? This determines whether it can drive a gauge at all, and how stale that gauge would be.
4. **Does it cover the whole fleet, or only changed devices?** A delta-only stream cannot produce a fleet count — it can only maintain one, which is a much harder (stateful) problem.
5. **Does it include the Linux devices** `managedDeviceOverview`'s OS summary misses (9 vs 10)?
6. **Same five questions for `DeviceComplianceOrg`** vs `intune.compliance`.
7. **If `Devices` IS full per-device inventory:** does the fleet walk get **retired**, or kept as the default with blob opt-in? Note the deployment argument — blob needs Azure infra graph2otel otherwise does not, so `graph` almost certainly stays the default regardless.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Raw blob rows for both categories captured and their real shape recorded (field list, not a doc quote)
- [ ] Push cadence and coverage (full fleet vs delta) determined **by observation**
- [ ] Field-by-field comparison against `manageddevices.go`'s log twin and `intune.compliance`'s gauges
- [ ] **Verdict: can blob fully replace the fleet page-walk without losing per-entity detail?** Yes/no with evidence
- [ ] If yes: file the implementation issue; correct #130's "irreducible by design" conclusion
- [ ] If no: record **exactly which field or property** is missing, so this is never re-chased
- [ ] Either way: correct CLAUDE.md's `managedDevices` entry to state what was actually observed

## Out of scope

- Building the consumer (#89) or the metrics path (#128). **This issue is observation only** — its output is a verdict.
- Removing per-device log twins. They are the deliverable; the cardinality rule is not up for negotiation here.

Related: #89 (blob consumer), #128 q6 (this was that question, now split out), #130 (the audit whose conclusion this may correct), #131 (dual-ship — `Devices` may invert it for this collector: blob-only could beat dual).

comments.body:
## Inherited from #131 (closed): this issue now gates graph2otel's single biggest poll saving

#131 closed as *"dual-ship is unnecessary; mutual exclusion was right"* - the mode is structurally empty for every signal it listed, because those are all `WindowCollector`s and **`WindowCollector`s emit zero metrics**, so there is no metric side for Graph to keep serving.

**One case survived that closure, and it lands here**, because it is gated on this issue's question and nothing else.

## `intune.devices` is the only collector where dual-ship would genuinely pay

Dual needs a gauge **and** a log twin **and** a blob category. Across the whole registry, 15 collectors have the shape; exactly **two** also have a blob source - `entra.risk` (`RiskyUsers`/`RiskyServicePrincipals`, zero rows here per #129) and **`intune.devices`** (`Devices`/`DeviceComplianceOrg` - this issue).

`intune.devices` does the full-fleet `managedDevices` page-walk: **graph2otel's most expensive poll**, against Intune's elevated Devices tier, with no `$count` segment and no server-`$filter` on `operatingSystem`. CLAUDE.md calls it *"irreducible BY DESIGN"* - not by API limitation - because `manageddevices.go` emits a **log twin per device**, and those per-device rows ARE the deliverable. A bounded count like `managedDeviceOverview` can never replace them.

**That reasoning is sound against a count. It does not hold against a blob category carrying per-device rows.**

If `Devices` is inventory-shaped, then:

```
today   : page the entire fleet   -> bounded gauges + per-device log twins
dual    : managedDeviceOverview   -> bounded gauges          (ONE call, already fetched)
          blob Devices            -> per-device log twins
```

That replaces a full-fleet page-walk with **a single bounded request**. Not "the load relocates" - the Graph poll genuinely shrinks to one call. It is the strongest saving available anywhere in the project, and **this issue's shape question is the only thing standing in front of it.**

## Two caveats to carry, so nobody over-sells it

1. **`managedDeviceOverview` is not a clean substitute for the walk's own bucketing.** CLAUDE.md records its OS summary summing to **9 against a real fleet of 10** - no Linux bucket. So a dual `intune.devices` either accepts a weaker OS gauge or derives it from blob, which is #128 territory.
2. **`DeviceComplianceOrg` vs `Devices`** may split inventory from compliance state; the saving depends on which carries the per-device rows the twins need. Check both.

## The prior question, which this issue should settle FIRST

**The Intune categories have produced zero containers**, and that is a different signal from "a slow category":

- The 17 Entra categories come from the **`aadiam/graph2otel`** diagnostic setting - **6 containers exist and are actively growing** (blob ingest went live in production 2026-07-16 and consumed 50 blobs / 72MB with zero errors).
- The 3 Intune categories (`Devices`, `DeviceComplianceOrg`, `OperationalLogs`) come from a **separate setting, `microsoft.intune/graph2otel`** - **zero containers**, hours after enablement.

Azure creates a container on first write, so absence still means "nothing written yet" rather than "misconfigured". But **6 of 6 delivering from one setting while 0 of 3 deliver from another** narrows what that can mean considerably. **Verify the Intune diagnostic setting itself before concluding anything about row shape** - the answer may be that it is not delivering at all, in which case the shape question is unanswerable rather than open.

## Suggested order

1. Confirm the `microsoft.intune/graph2otel` diagnostic setting is actually configured and delivering
2. If containers appear: is `Devices` inventory-shaped (per-device rows) or summary-shaped?
3. If per-device: **the `intune.devices` dual case above becomes real** - and it is worth its own issue, not a footnote here
4. Map per this category's own envelope (do **not** reuse a mapper across category families - the envelope is inconsistent across them, and `AuditLogs` was recently confirmed as a *third* distinct pattern that predicts neither MGAL nor SignInLogs)

Refs #131 (closed), #128, #135, #129

Unblocked (live-observed 2026-07-17): both `insights-logs-devices` and `insights-logs-devicecomplianceorg` containers now EXIST on `graph2otelm7kni` — the Intune diagnostic setting is delivering. The shape question this issue asks is answerable now: sample the blobs as `graph2otel-poller` and check whether `Devices` carries per-device inventory.

## Answered: `Devices` IS per-device inventory — but the dual-ship saving this issue was built on does NOT hold

Probed 2026-07-17 ~09:45Z as **`graph2otel-poller`** (appId `2c92ce28-126c-47c1-82b0-410b64502989`, oid `13371536-…`, cert credential, storage audience `https://storage.azure.com`). Blob content read succeeded, so `Storage Blob Data Reader` is correctly granted — this is not the "lists happily, 403s on read" case.

**Evidence class: live-measured (2026-07-17, #132), n=1 snapshot.**

### 1. Layout — verified, not assumed

Both Intune containers use the **`tenantId=` prefix**, same as the Entra categories. Verified per-category rather than inherited:

```
insights-logs-devices/tenantId=4b8c18bd-…/y=2026/m=07/d=17/h=00/m=00/PT1H.json            14,432b  11 lines
insights-logs-devicecomplianceorg/tenantId=4b8c18bd-…/y=2026/m=07/d=17/h=00/m=00/PT1H.json   990b   1 line
insights-logs-devicecomplianceorg/tenantId=4b8c18bd-…/y=2026/m=07/d=17/h=01/m=00/PT1H.json 9,968b  10 lines
```

Append blobs, CRLF-terminated JSON Lines — consistent with the Entra categories.

`insights-logs-operationallogs` **still does not exist**. The Intune setting is delivering 2 of its 3 categories.

### 2. `Devices` is per-device inventory — richer than the Graph poll

10 device records + 1 trailer. **The blob device-id set is exactly the Graph `managedDevices` id set** — 10/10, zero on either side only. `DeviceId` is the same GUID as Graph's `id`, so correlation is free.

Field-by-field, blob `Devices` vs what `intune.devices` selects from Graph (`manageddevices.go:92`):

| Graph `$select` field | blob `properties` field | agreement (n=10) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `DeviceId` | **identical**, 10/10 |
| `deviceName` | `DeviceName` | **identical**, 10/10 |
| `serialNumber` | `SerialNumber` | **identical**, 10/10 |
| `userPrincipalName` | `UPN` | **identical**, 10/10 |
| `complianceState` — `compliant`/`noncompliant`/`unknown` | `CompliantState` — `Compliant`/`Noncompliant`/`Not Evaluated` | same semantics, **different vocabulary** 10/10 |
| `operatingSystem` — `iOS`/`macOS`/`Windows`/`Linux` | `OS` — `iOS/iPadOS`/`MacOS`/`Windows`/`Linux` | same semantics, **different vocabulary** |
| `isEncrypted` — bool | `EncryptionStatusString` — string `"True"`/`"False"` | same value, **different type**, 10/10 |
| `lastSyncDateTime` — RFC3339 `…Z`, second precision | `LastContact` — **no timezone designator**, 7-digit fraction | same instant where the device has not synced since the snapshot |

So the blob covers **8/8** of the poll's selected fields, plus 32 the poll does not collect: `Manufacturer`, `Model`, `OSVersion`, `StorageTotal`/`StorageFree`, `IMEI`, `MEID`, `WifiMacAddress`, `PhoneNumber`, `JailBroken`, `Ownership`, `JoinType`, `SupervisedStatusString`, `ManagedBy`, `DeviceState`, `DeviceRegistrationState`, `CreatedDate`, `InGracePeriodUntil`, `PrimaryUser`, `ManagedDeviceName`, `CategoryName`, `AndroidPatchLevel`, `SkuFamily`, `EasID`, `SubscriberCarrierNetwork`, `UserEmail`, `UserName`, `ReferenceId`, `GraphDeviceIsManaged`, `AADTenantId`, `IntuneAccountId`, `BatchId`, `Stats`.

**On shape alone, blob `Devices` could carry the `intune.managed_device` log twin.** The rest of this comment is why that is not sufficient.

### 3. ⛔ The dual-ship saving as framed does not hold — `managedDeviceOverview` cannot serve the gauges

This issue's proposal was `managedDeviceOverview` (one bounded call) for the gauges + blob `Devices` for the twins. Re-probed the overview singleton live today:

```json
{"enrolledDeviceCount": 10, "mdmEnrolledCount": 5, "dualEnrolledDeviceCount": 3,
 "deviceOperatingSystemSummary": {"iosCount": 4, "macOSCount": 1, "windowsCount": 4, "unknownCount": 0, …},
 "deviceExchangeAccessStateSummary": {…}}
```

Two independent blockers:

1. **`managedDeviceOverview` carries no compliance data at all.** There is no `complianceState` field anywhere in the resource. `intune.devices.count{compliance_state, operating_system}` (`manageddevices.go:476`) therefore **cannot** be served by the overview — the dual mode would drop the compliance gauge entirely, or derive it from blob (= #128, at the cadence in §4).
2. **The OS summary is still wrong.** `iosCount 4 + macOSCount 1 + windowsCount 4 = 9` against `enrolledDeviceCount 10` — the Linux device (`oli`) has no bucket. CLAUDE.md's 9-against-10 claim **re-verified live 2026-07-17**; it has not been fixed upstream.

The caveats this issue listed as "two caveats to carry, so nobody over-sells it" are not caveats — caveat 1 is fatal to the proposal on its own.

### 4. ⛔ Cadence: the blob is a periodic snapshot, and it is NOT hourly

This is the decisive practical finding. `intune.devices` defaults to **hourly** (`manageddevices.go:368`). The blob delivers:

| observation | value |
| --- | --- |
| `Devices` records span | `00:14:37Z` → `00:36:57Z` (one batch, 22 min) |
| `DeviceComplianceOrg` records span | `00:49:26Z` → `01:24:31Z` (one batch, 35 min) |
| blobs since `01:24Z` | **none** — silent for **8.4h** at time of probe (09:50Z) |
| Intune blobs for `d=16` | **none at all** — the Intune categories did **not** backfill (contrast: Entra backfilled ~15h of history) |
| first Intune record | `2026-07-17T00:14:37Z` = **10.0h after enablement** (~2026-07-16T14:15Z) |

**Definitively not hourly** — an hourly feed would have produced ~9 more blobs by now. Observed lower bound on the period is **≥9.6h**; the single batch landing just after 00:00Z is consistent with a **daily ~00:15Z snapshot**, but that is **n=1 and unproven**. Do not record "daily" as fact — re-check after 00:30Z on 2026-07-18 to establish the period.

**Consequence:** replacing the Graph poll with blob is an **hourly → ~daily fidelity downgrade** on the per-device twin. #114 froze "every device is twinned every cycle" precisely so "was device X enrolled on date Y" stays answerable; a daily snapshot still answers that, but the gauges would go from hourly to daily, and there is no way to derive an hourly compliance count from a daily snapshot.

### 5. Traps for whoever maps this (do not inherit a neighbouring category's rules)

1. **A trailer record terminates each batch** — no `DeviceId`, no device fields, `resultType: "Completed"`, and `properties` = `{BatchId, IntuneAccountId, Stats:{RecordCount:10}}`. A mapper that assumes every line is a device emits a garbage row per batch. **`BatchId` does not isolate it** — the trailer shares its batch with a real device record (`b2e8afab-…` = `tablet-office` + trailer). Discriminate on `resultType == "Completed"` / presence of `Stats` / absence of `DeviceId`. `Stats.RecordCount` (=10) is a free completeness check against the rows actually read.
2. **`BatchId` is not one-batch-per-snapshot.** The 10 devices split across 3 BatchIds (6/3/2). Do not treat it as a snapshot key.
3. **The two Intune categories disagree with each other on the same concept** — the field is named `CompliantState` in `Devices` and `ComplianceState` in `DeviceComplianceOrg`, and their vocabularies differ (`"Not Evaluated"` vs `"Not evaluated"` — capital vs lowercase E). `DeviceComplianceOrg` additionally carries a numeric-string code + localized twin (`ComplianceState: "0"` + `ComplianceState_loc: "Not evaluated"`).
4. **Four different OS vocabularies for the same 10 devices:** Graph `iOS`/`macOS` · `Devices.OS` `iOS/iPadOS`/`MacOS` · `DeviceComplianceOrg.OS` `IOS`/`MacOS` · `DeviceComplianceOrg.OS_loc` `iOS`/`macOS`. `osBucketFor` (`manageddevices.go:134`) survives all four by prefix+fold match — verified by inspection, not luck — but the **raw** `operating_system` log-twin attribute would silently change value if the source switched.
5. **`LastContact` has no timezone designator** (`"2026-05-23T08:55:35"`). Must be assumed UTC; a naive local parse backdates or advances it by the host offset.
6. **`properties` is NOT the Graph resource here.** The sign-in categories and AuditLogs each had `properties` ≡ the Graph resource, so the polled mapper was reusable. **`Devices` breaks that pattern** — PascalCase keys, different field names, different enum vocabularies, different types. This is a **third/fourth distinct envelope family**; it needs its own mapper. Do not reuse `mapManagedDevice`-style logic from the polled path.
7. **`resultType`** is `"None"` on device rows and `"Completed"` on the trailer — a fifth per-category quirk.

### 6. `DeviceComplianceOrg` vs `Devices` — the split

Same 10 devices, **identical id sets**. Not an inventory/compliance split — both carry identity + compliance + OS + LastContact. Difference is depth:

- **Only in `DeviceComplianceOrg`:** `ComplianceState`(+`_loc`), `DeviceHealthThreatLevel`(+`_loc`), `ManagementAgents`(+`_loc`), `OwnerType`(+`_loc`), `OS_loc`, `OSDescription`, `DeviceType`, `UserId`, `RetireAfterDatetime`, `AccountId`
- **Only in `Devices`:** the hardware/inventory surface — `Manufacturer`, `Model`, `StorageTotal`/`Free`, `IMEI`, `MEID`, `WifiMacAddress`, `JailBroken`, `Ownership`, `JoinType`, `EncryptionStatusString`, `ManagedBy`, `DeviceState`, `CreatedDate`, +14 more

**`Devices` is the one that carries the twin's fields** (it is the only one with `EncryptionStatusString`, which the gauges need). `DeviceComplianceOrg` is largely redundant against it for this issue's purpose, and adds `DeviceHealthThreatLevel` (`Low`/`Secured`/`Unknown`) as the one genuinely new signal.

### Verdict

**The shape question is answered YES** — `Devices` is per-device inventory and could carry the `intune.managed_device` twin field-for-field. **The dual-ship case built on that answer is NO**, for reasons that have nothing to do with shape:

- `managedDeviceOverview` **cannot** replace the compliance gauge (no compliance data in the resource) — this alone kills "the Graph poll shrinks to one call"
- the overview's OS gauge is still wrong (9/10, no Linux) — re-verified live today
- blob cadence is **≥9.6h observed** (consistent with daily) vs the poll's hourly — a fidelity downgrade, not a free saving
- blob `Devices` needs its **own mapper** (it is not the Graph resource), so this is new code, not a source toggle over shared mappers

**Recommendation: do not build the dual `intune.devices`.** The framing "replaces a full-fleet page-walk with a single bounded request" is not achievable — the bounded request does not carry the data the gauges need. What blob `Devices` *is* genuinely good for is a **separate, additive** signal: the 32 inventory fields the poll does not collect (`Manufacturer`/`Model`/`StorageFree`/`JailBroken`/`Ownership`/`JoinType`), at daily cadence, with **zero** Graph cost. That is a different and smaller proposal than this issue's, and it should be its own issue rather than a rename of this one.

**Blocking unknown before any build:** the exact snapshot period (n=1). Re-check `insights-logs-devices` after **00:30Z on 2026-07-18**.

Refs #131 (closed), #128, #135, #114, #112

## Corroborated + the field-parity angle for the turn-off decision

Re-sampled both containers live 2026-07-18 (`graph2otel-poller`, cert on camden), independent of the 2026-07-17 probe above — same conclusion, plus the `$select` point that decides what to do next.

- `insights-logs-devices` — 30 KB / 2 blobs. **Per-device inventory, confirmed** (`DeviceId`, `DeviceName`, `UPN`, `CompliantState`, `OS`/`OSVersion`, `EncryptionStatusString`, plus `Model`, `Manufacturer`, `Ownership`, `StorageTotal`/`Free`, `WifiMacAddress`, `IMEI`, `JoinType`, `SupervisedStatusString`).
- `insights-logs-devicecomplianceorg` — 23 KB / 3 blobs. Per-device compliance rows (`DeviceName`, `UPN`, `ComplianceState`/`_loc`, `OS`, `DeviceHealthThreatLevel`, `ManagementAgents`, `OwnerType`).

**The overlap is with `intune.devices`' per-device log twin, not `intune.compliance`.** `intune.compliance` is aggregate-only by design (its package doc: never walks per-device×policy children, to keep per-device ids off metric labels), so it has nothing to overlap. `manageddevices.go`'s `intune.managed_device` twin already emits the core identity/compliance fields for the same fleet. So both blob categories are **redundant** with what the polled walk already ships — they do not add a new signal, and (per the answer above) they cannot retire the walk because blob needs Azure infra the walk doesn't.

**The one thing the blobs carry that the twin doesn't** is a handful of fields the current `managedDevicesSelect` `$select` omits: `Model`, `Manufacturer`, `Ownership`, `StorageTotal/Free`, `WifiMacAddress`, `IMEI`, `JoinType` (from `Devices`), and `DeviceHealthThreatLevel` (a Defender signal, from `DeviceComplianceOrg`). These are on the **same** `/deviceManagement/managedDevices` resource at **zero extra Graph cost** — the walk already happens; they're just not selected.

**Recommendation:** if any of those hardware/threat fields have SIEM value, widen `managedDevicesSelect` on the polled collector to capture them — then **turn off both blob categories** (`Devices`, `DeviceComplianceOrg`) on the `microsoft.intune/graph2otel` diagnostic setting. That reaches field parity without standing up a second transport for data the fleet walk already retrieves. Cheap, tiny volume either way; the point is not to double-ingest as a production tenant scales.

`[live-measured 2026-07-18, #132, n=1]`

## Answer: YES — both blob categories carry per-device inventory. `[live-measured 2026-07-18, graph2otel-poller]`

Both `insights-logs-devices` and `insights-logs-devicecomplianceorg` are landing on `graph2otelm7kni` (from the `microsoft.intune/graph2otel` diagnostic setting) with the `tenantId=<guid>/` prefix — same as the Entra categories, no per-setting prefix surprise. Real records sampled:

**`Devices`** (`category=Devices`, `properties`): `DeviceId`, `DeviceName`, `UPN`, `LastContact`, `OS`, `OSVersion`, `CompliantState`, `Ownership`, `ManagedBy` (e.g. `MDE`), `Model`, `SerialNumber`, `Manufacturer`, `CreatedDate`, `DeviceState` (e.g. `Managed`), `UserEmail`, `DeviceRegistrationState`, `ManagedDeviceName`, `EncryptionStatusString`, `JoinType`, `SupervisedStatusString`, `WifiMacAddress`, `StorageTotal`, `StorageFree`, `JailBroken`, `PrimaryUser`, `IntuneAccountId`, `AADTenantId`.

**`DeviceComplianceOrg`** (`category=DeviceCompliance`, `properties`): `AccountId`, `DeviceName`, `ComplianceState` + `ComplianceState_loc`, `OSDescription`, `OS`, `OwnerType` + `_loc`, `DeviceId`, `LastContact`, `ManagementAgents` + `_loc`, `DeviceType`, `InGracePeriodUntil`, `DeviceHealthThreatLevel` + `_loc`, `IntuneAccountId`, `AADTenantId`.

## Disposition

Spike question answered: **yes**, blob carries substantial per-device inventory, so a blob-sourced device signal is viable and would dodge the hourly full-fleet `managedDevices` page-walk (`intune.devices`) — the tenant's heaviest poll.

**Caveat before retiring the page-walk (do NOT skip):** the polled Graph `managedDevice` resource carries a wider field set (~60 fields: EAS activation, Azure AD registration detail, compliance grace, chassis, etc.) than the blob `Devices` category above. A **field-by-field diff** of polled-vs-blob is required before `intune.devices` can be switched to `source: blob` without losing signal. That diff + the source-toggle implementation is follow-up build work (belongs with #135 group F), not this spike.

Closing the spike as answered. The build (blob-source variant + field diff + page-walk retirement decision) is tracked under #135 group F.

## Correction — do NOT act on the "turn off as redundant" recommendation; see #197

Re-opening the reasoning (not the issue): the recommendation above to treat `Devices`/`DeviceComplianceOrg` blob categories as redundant and **turn them off** is small-tenant-biased. It holds only if the hourly full-fleet page-walk is kept. It under-weights the at-scale case this repo actually cares about: a **metrics-via-graph + logs-via-blob split** for `intune.devices`, where the point is to *stop* running the walk (graph2otel's most expensive poll) and serve the per-device twins from blob.

That split is the genuinely-dual case CLAUDE.md flags (`intune.devices` emits both metrics and twins), and #131's "dual mode closed" does **not** cover it (that was for log-only WindowCollectors). Tracked as **#197**.

**Standing instruction: keep `Devices` and `DeviceComplianceOrg` enabled.** They are the candidate log transport for #197, not redundant noise. The spike verdict here (blob can't *fully retire* the walk today, because the cheap overview metric path is lossy — 9 vs 10, no Linux) stands; what's reversed is the leap from that to "so turn the categories off."

> ## ⛔ CLOSED WITH THE OPPOSITE VERDICT (banner added 2026-07-17, #146)
> This body argues that #89/#128's "source must be mutually exclusive" model is wrong and proposes a `dual` mode. **The investigation concluded the reverse**: every signal the dual-ship table lists is a `WindowCollector` emitting **zero metrics**, so `dual` ≡ `blob` for all of them — **#89/#128 were right; mutual exclusion stands** and is enforced by #144's `ConflictsWith` (`7551f59`). **Do NOT act on the "Correct #89 and #128" acceptance items below.** Exactly two collectors are genuinely dual-capable (`entra.risk`, `intune.devices`); the one real win (`intune.devices`) moved to #132. Read the closing comment for the full evidence chain; note the mid-thread comment claiming this issue is "NOT the binding blocker on #135" is retracted one comment later.

## Mission

Research the **dual-ship** model: run **Graph polling and the blob path simultaneously for the same signal**, split by signal type rather than choosing between them.

> **Maintainer framing (verbatim, 2026-07-16):** *"when I talk about dual ship I mean in the context of letting us get real time metrics from API polling but comprehensive log ingest via blob storage after we've built the shipper."*

- **Graph poll → metrics.** Fresh, near-real-time, no ~4-minute Entra pipeline floor, no first-write delay.
- **Blob → logs.** Complete, backfilled, no reporting/IPC throttle ceiling, no beta dependency.

**They are complementary, not redundant.** Each pipeline is fed by the route that actually suits it.

## This CORRECTS the model recorded on #89 and #128

Both currently say **"`source: graph|blob` must be mutually exclusive per collector — both enabled = duplicate records."** That framing assumed dual-ship meant *the same signal twice*, and it is **wrong** for this design.

Under dual-ship there is **no duplication**, because the two routes feed **different pipelines**:

| mode | metrics from | logs from |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `graph` (default, today) | Graph poll | Graph poll |
| `blob` | *(none, unless #128)* | blob |
| **`dual`** | **Graph poll** | **blob** |

The duplication risk is real **only** if both routes emit into the **same** pipeline. `dual` must therefore mean *"Graph stops emitting log twins for this collector; blob stops emitting metrics"* — a **mode**, not a source toggle. **That is the whole design question and it is not yet answered.**

## Why this is attractive

It takes the best half of each route and discards the worst half of each:

| | Graph poll | blob |
| --- | --- | --- |
| freshness | ✅ no ~4-min floor | ❌ ~4–6 min floor (live-measured, #89) |
| throttle ceiling | ❌ reporting 5/10s; **IPC 1 req/s tenant-wide**; Intune elevated Devices tier | ✅ none |
| completeness / backfill | ❌ bounded by lookback | ✅ Azure backfills on enablement |
| beta dependency | ❌ 3 sign-in streams need `/beta` | ✅ first-class categories |
| infra required | ✅ none (app registration only) | ❌ storage account + diagnostic settings + RBAC |

**Metrics want freshness; logs want completeness.** Dual-ship gives each what it wants. It also means **#128 (blob→metrics) is NOT needed for dual-ship signals** — Graph already supplies their metrics fresh. #128 stays relevant only for signals with **no Graph route at all** (`MicrosoftGraphActivityLogs`, `MicrosoftServicePrincipalSignInLogs`, Intune `OperationalLogs`), where blob is the *only* source and a recency-gated counter is the only way to get a metric.

## Questions the spike must answer

1. **Is `dual` a third mode, or two independent per-pipeline source keys?**
   `source: graph|blob|dual` vs `metrics_source:` + `logs_source:`. The latter is more expressive and more config surface. Pick deliberately; both must satisfy #103's registry + drift gate.
2. **Which signals can even do it?** Requires *both* a working Graph collector **and** a diagnostic category. From the #89 audit: the 4 sign-in streams, `AuditLogs`, `ProvisioningLogs`, `UserRiskEvents`, Intune `AuditLogs`. **Not** `MicrosoftGraphActivityLogs` / `MicrosoftServicePrincipalSignInLogs` / Intune `OperationalLogs` (blob-only — no Graph route), and **not** snapshot collectors (no blob equivalent... except possibly `Devices`/`DeviceComplianceOrg`, see below).
3. **Does the Graph poll get cheaper in `dual` mode?** If Graph only needs bounded aggregates, can it use a **narrower `$select`**, a **`$count`**, or a **wider interval** than a full log-fetch needs? **If yes, dual-ship reduces Graph load rather than merely relocating it — that is the strongest version of this argument and it is unverified.**
4. **What happens on blob outage?** Storage unreachable → metrics keep flowing, logs stop **silently**. Needs an explicit staleness signal (`graph2otel.*`), not silence.
5. **Attribute parity.** A metric derived from a Graph poll and a log twin sourced from blob must agree on `event.name` and attribute keys, or correlation breaks. The blob record is the **raw** diagnostic shape; the Graph record is Microsoft's **normalised** shape (`TimeGenerated` vs `time`, etc.). **These are NOT the same schema.** Mapping must converge them.
6. **Does `dual` change the recommended default?** Almost certainly **no** — default stays `graph`-only, since blob needs Azure infra graph2otel otherwise does not. `dual` is opt-in for tenants that already have the storage account.
7. **Medium/large tenants — quantify the crossover.** At what fleet/user size does the Graph log-fetch actually hurt? The IPC 1 req/s ceiling and the Intune elevated Devices tier are the binding constraints. **Give a number, not an intuition.**

## Interaction with the Intune `Devices` question

`Devices` and `DeviceComplianceOrg` were just enabled on the Intune diagnostic setting to test whether they are **inventory-shaped** (#128 q6). **If `Devices` carries per-device rows, it partially inverts this issue for that collector**: blob could serve *both* the log twins *and* the counts, making `blob`-only better than `dual` — and retiring the hourly full-fleet page-walk, graph2otel's single most expensive poll (`managedDevices` has no `$count`, so it walks the whole collection against Intune's elevated tier).

Note the recent audit concluded that walk is "irreducible by design" because the per-device **log twins are the deliverable**, so a bounded count like `managedDeviceOverview` can never replace it. **That reasoning holds against a count. It does NOT hold against a blob category carrying per-device rows.** Settle by observation once the blobs land — do not assume either way.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Spike write-up as a comment: is `dual` a mode or two source keys, and why
- [ ] Per-signal table: `graph` / `blob` / `dual` capable, and the recommended default for each
- [ ] Answer q3 — **does the Graph poll actually get cheaper in `dual`, or just relocated?**
- [ ] Quantify the tenant size at which the Graph log-fetch becomes the binding constraint
- [ ] Schema convergence: prove raw-blob and normalised-Graph records can emit identical `event.name` + attribute keys
- [ ] Blob-outage staleness signal designed (metrics must not mask a silent log stop)
- [ ] Config keys registered per #103's drift gate; `docs/env-vars.md` regenerated
- [ ] **Correct #89 and #128** — the "mutually exclusive" statement is wrong under this model
- [ ] Default stays `graph`-only; `dual` is opt-in and documented as requiring Azure infra
- [ ] `make check` green

## Blocked on

**#89's blob consumer.** Nothing here is testable until blobs can be read. This is a **design spike whose output is a decision**, not code.

Related: #128 (blob→metrics — needed only for blob-only signals, NOT for dual-ship ones), #118 (backfill window), #103 (config drift gate), #105 (active-series cap).
