> Body updated 2026-07-17 (#146): the grant landed, the endpoint was live-verified 200 under the poller's own cert (5 labels), the collector was rebuilt on the new endpoint, and CLAUDE.md was corrected — most of the original acceptance list is done. What remains is below. The original analysis is preserved under "Background".

## Current state

- `SensitivityLabel.Read` granted + admin-consented on `graph2otel-poller`; live-verified in-token, `GET /security/dataSecurityAndGovernance/sensitivityLabels` → **200, full tenant catalog**, v1.0 and beta (final comment).
- `purview/labels` rebuilt on that endpoint. **Gotcha now encoded:** `displayName` is present but always null — the value is `name` (`labels.go` binds `name`).
- CLAUDE.md corrected: sensitivity half of #109's "app-only-blocked" verdict retracted; retention half stands (`/security/labels/retentionLabels` → 500 `DataInsightsRequestError`+Forbidden, Application: Not supported — keep that specific skip).
- One sub-claim from this body was corrected in the first comment: the two roles are **dual-mode**, not "app-only by construction / absent from the delegated list" — the proof of app-only capability is `allowedMemberTypes: ["Application"]`, not delegated-absence.

## Remaining work

- [ ] Narrow `purview/labels.isUnavailable` (`labels.go:117-124`) — it still swallows **all** 403/404s; a sensitivity-label 403 must fail the collector rather than skip silently. The retention-label `DataInsightsRequestError`+Forbidden skip stays untouched.
- [ ] Guard test proving a sensitivity-label 403 fails the collector.
- [ ] `SECURITY.md` scope inventory: add `SensitivityLabel.Read` (and `eDiscovery.Read.All`, granted alongside for #102).

## Background (original analysis, kept for the record)

#109 concluded sensitivity-label enumeration was app-only-blocked after testing the right endpoint with the wrong scope (`InformationProtectionPolicy.Read.All` — a different permission for a different endpoint). The live error was `InsufficientGraphPermissions` — missing consent, not product refusal.

**Do not re-chase** (all dead ends, live-verified): `/beta/security/informationProtection/sensitivityLabels` (HTML 403 from the Azure gateway edge, docs wrong); MIP Sync Service (SDK-only, no HTTP contract); `api.purview.microsoft.com` (no public REST docs — "no APIs available to extract data"); Azure RMS (`api.aadrm.com`, PowerShell-only).

**Lesson (also in #79's operating rules):** a 403 means missing consent far more often than product limitation. Before declaring an app-only gap, confirm the app holds the endpoint's *documented* Application permission — not a similarly-named one — and probe as `graph2otel-poller`, never another identity.

comments.body:
## Independently verified — core claim CONFIRMED, one sub-claim corrected

Re-ran the checks against the live tenant rather than taking this at face value, because it contradicts a **live-verified** CLAUDE.md entry.

### ✅ The central finding stands: this is a missing scope, not a product limitation

```
SensitivityLabel.Evaluate       allowedMemberTypes=['Application'] isEnabled=True
SensitivityLabel.Evaluate.All   allowedMemberTypes=['Application'] isEnabled=True
SensitivityLabel.Read           allowedMemberTypes=['Application'] isEnabled=True
SensitivityLabels.Read.All      allowedMemberTypes=['Application'] isEnabled=True

graph2otel-poller HOLDS : InformationProtectionPolicy.Read.All   <- different permission
graph2otel-poller LACKS : SensitivityLabel.Read, SensitivityLabels.Read.All
```

`allowedMemberTypes: ['Application']` + `isEnabled: true` is conclusive: the endpoint **is** app-only-capable, and the poller was never granted the permission it needs. **#109 tested the right endpoint with the wrong scope and blamed the endpoint.** CLAUDE.md's "permanent app-only gap ... until Microsoft ships an app-only-capable endpoint" is wrong for sensitivity labels.

### ❌ Correction: "app-only by construction" is FALSE

This issue states:

> *"Neither appears in Graph's delegated scope list. They are app-only-capable by construction."*

**Both DO appear as delegated scopes.** Live:

```
oauth2PermissionScopes containing 'sensitivitylabel':
  ['SensitivityLabel.Evaluate', 'SensitivityLabel.Evaluate.All',
   'SensitivityLabel.Read', 'SensitivityLabels.Read.All']
```

They are **dual-mode** (delegated *and* application), not app-only. Correcting it because the reasoning matters more than the conclusion here: the proof that this works app-only is **`allowedMemberTypes` containing `Application`** — NOT the absence of a delegated form. A future reader who inherits the wrong reasoning could apply it elsewhere and reach a wrong verdict.

The conclusion is unaffected, and arguably strengthened: the permission is app-only-capable on its own evidence.

### Unchanged

The retention-label half (500 `DataInsightsRequestError` / "Forbidden", **Application: Not supported** per Microsoft's permission table) stands as written. That skip stays. The `isUnavailable` narrowing in the acceptance criteria is right: it must stop swallowing sensitivity-label 403s while keeping the retention-label skip.

### Blocked on a human — exact scope named for approval

Per #79's operating rules, a live-tenant scope grant needs explicit approval first. The ask:

```sh
# grant + admin-consent to graph2otel-poller (2c92ce28-126c-47c1-82b0-410b64502989)
SensitivityLabel.Read          # least privileged — try FIRST
SensitivityLabels.Read.All     # only if the least-privileged form does not serve tenant-wide labels
```

Read-only. Nothing here is buildable until that lands.

## ✅ LIVE-VERIFIED under the poller's own identity — #109's verdict is definitively WRONG

Ran against **`graph2otel-poller`'s real certificate** (from camden `/opt/graph2otel/`), not a stand-in. This closes the verification gap flagged in the previous comment.

```
identity: 2c92ce28-126c-47c1-82b0-410b64502989  (graph2otel-poller)
token carries 35 roles
  SensitivityLabel.Read        IN TOKEN
  SensitivityLabels.Read.All   absent        <- not needed
  eDiscovery.Read.All          IN TOKEN

GET /v1.0/security/dataSecurityAndGovernance/sensitivityLabels  -> 200 OK, 5 labels
GET /beta/security/dataSecurityAndGovernance/sensitivityLabels  -> 200 OK, 5 labels
```

**Labels returned:** Personal, Public, General, Confidential, Highly Confidential.

**`SensitivityLabel.Read` alone is sufficient** — it serves the full tenant-wide catalog. The escalation to `SensitivityLabels.Read.All` in the acceptance criteria is **not needed**; do not request it. Least privilege holds.

**CLAUDE.md's "Purview label enumeration is app-only-blocked ... treat as a permanent app-only gap until Microsoft ships an app-only-capable endpoint" is wrong for sensitivity labels and must be corrected.** It was a missing scope, not a product limitation. The retention-label half stays (see below).

### 🔴 Gotcha for the collector: `displayName` is present but ALWAYS NULL — use `name`

Every one of the 5 labels returns `displayName: null` while carrying the real value in **`name`**. A collector binding to `displayName` (the obvious choice, and what the earlier probe in this issue printed) emits **five empty labels and looks like a data bug**.

Full shape returned per label — richer than this issue assumed, and worth mining:

```
name, id, description, priority, isDefault, isEnabled, color, toolTip, autoTooltip,
hasProtection, isEndpointProtectionEnabled, isScopedToUser, isSmimeEncryptEnabled,
isSmimeSignEnabled, applicableTo, applicationMode, actionSource, assignedPolicies,
customSettings, labelActions, locale, rights, sublabels
```

Notably **`hasProtection`** is exposed. #99 records "label encryption activation (Azure RMS, portal-only)" as a permanent gap — `hasProtection` may partially answer it per-label. Worth a look when building; do not assume either way.

Suggested shape, consistent with #111/#112:
- **Gauge** `purview.sensitivity_labels.count` bucketed by bounded enums — `is_enabled`, `has_protection`, `application_mode`, `is_default`. Label *names* are bounded here (5) but every series would be 1, so they are **not** metric labels.
- **Log twin** `purview.sensitivity_label`, one per label definition, carrying `name`, `id`, `priority`, `description`, `sublabels`, `rights`. Per the cardinality rule this is a data-modeling call, not a privacy one.

### Retention labels: unchanged, still a real gap

`RecordsManagement.Read.All` **is** in the poller's token and the endpoint still fails — Microsoft documents **Application: Not supported**. That half of #109 stands. The `isUnavailable` narrowing must therefore keep the retention-label `DataInsightsRequestError` + Forbidden skip while no longer swallowing sensitivity-label 403s.

### Tooling so this cannot recur

`g2o-probe` is now installed locally and authenticates **as the poller**:

```sh
g2o-probe security/dataSecurityAndGovernance/sensitivityLabels   # v1.0 + beta
g2o-probe --roles                                                # what the poller's token carries
```

Use it for every "can graph2otel see X?" question. The shared `chat-personal/microsoft/*/graph.py` helper authenticates as a **different, domain-admin-grade app** and will mislead you.

title: Purview sensitivity labels: collector rebuilt on SensitivityLabel.Read — residual: narrow isUnavailable + guard test + SECURITY.md

body:
## What & why

`entra.users.total` slices the user population three ways — `account_enabled`, `user_type`, and `on_premises_sync_enabled` — each as an **independent** axis, via its own `/users/$count` call (`populationAxes`, `internal/collectors/entra/users/users.go`). The code comment is explicit that this is not a cross-product, and for a first cut that was the right call: three axes cost three pairs of `$count` calls instead of eight.

The consequence is that the metric answers marginals only. You can ask "how many guests" and "how many disabled accounts", but not **"how many disabled guests"** — and the joint counts are where the interesting questions live:

- **Disabled guests** are the classic stale-external-access cleanup target. A guest account that has been disabled but never removed still holds directory presence and group memberships. The count trending upward means nobody is running offboarding.
- **Enabled guests** is the number a security team wants for external-access posture — the marginal guest count overstates it by including the disabled ones.
- **Enabled, cloud-only accounts in a hybrid tenant** are the ones that bypassed the on-prem identity lifecycle. In a tenant that is supposed to be fully synced, that count should be near zero, and it usually is not.

None of these is derivable from the marginals. `guests = 2099` and `disabled = 264` tells you nothing about the overlap.

## API surface

| Endpoint | Version | App permission |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /users/$count?$filter=<compound filter>` | v1.0 | `User.Read.All` (already declared) |

Nothing new — the same `$count` segment the collector already uses, with compound `$filter` expressions (`userType eq 'Guest' and accountEnabled eq false`). Simple-property filters like `accountEnabled` and `userType` are already known to work on the `$count` segment; only `signInActivity` is not (which is why `CountViaCollection` exists for the stale-user counts, and this issue does not touch that path).

## Telemetry model

- `entra.users.population{user_type, account_enabled}` (gauge) — the joint breakdown. Bounded: 2 x 2 = **4 series**. Trivial.

Keep `entra.users.total` emitting its existing marginal axes unchanged — dashboards depend on it, and `on_premises_sync_enabled` stays a marginal there. The new metric is additive.

**Scope this deliberately.** The full three-way cross-product (`user_type` x `account_enabled` x `on_premises_sync_enabled`) is 8 series and 8 `$count` calls. The two-way `user_type` x `account_enabled` is 4 calls and covers the two motivating questions. Start with the two-way; add the sync-enabled dimension only if the cloud-only-account question turns out to be one people actually ask. Do not build all eight on spec — the whole reason the collector uses independent axes today is that call count was a real consideration, and that reasoning has not stopped being true.

No log twin is needed or wanted here. These are pure counts with no per-entity data behind them, and the `$count` segment does not return the objects — there is nothing per-entity to emit. (Per-user detail already reaches the pipeline via the sign-in and audit collectors; this is not a case of high-cardinality data being dropped.)

## Constraints & gotchas

- **Always count through `collectors.Count`.** The `$count` segment serves `text/plain`, not JSON — an `Accept: application/json` gets HTTP 415. It also needs `ConsistencyLevel: eventual`. The helper handles both; a hand-rolled `$count` GET does not.
- **URL-encode the filter.** A compound filter has spaces, quotes, and `and` — a raw filter with literal spaces produces a malformed URL and Graph returns HTTP 400. `url.QueryEscape` the whole expression, as the existing axes already do.
- Guest accounts pending invitation acceptance have `externalUserState` of `PendingAcceptance` and still count as `userType eq 'Guest'`. That is correct for these counts, but worth knowing before someone reports the guest number as "too high".
- 4 extra `$count` calls per cycle land in the directory RU budget alongside the existing 6. Cheap, but not free — confirm it against the budget rather than assuming.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Emit `entra.users.population{user_type, account_enabled}` covering all four combinations via compound `$filter` on `/users/$count`.
- [ ] Leave `entra.users.total` and its three marginal axes emitting unchanged.
- [ ] All four counts go through `collectors.Count` (text/plain + ConsistencyLevel) with URL-encoded filters.
- [ ] Do not build the three-way cross-product; note on this issue whether the `on_premises_sync_enabled` dimension is wanted as a follow-up.
- [ ] Test with a faked Graph client + `Recorder`: exactly four series emit with the expected attribute pairs, and the compound filter is correctly escaped in the issued URL.
- [ ] Live-verify against a real tenant: the four joint counts sum to the total user count, and each marginal matches the corresponding existing axis. Record the numbers on this issue — a mismatch means the filters are wrong.
- [ ] Confirm the added calls fit the directory RU budget.
- [ ] Document the signal in `docs/signals.md`.
- [ ] `make check` green.

comments.body:
Shipped in b2dfa9d (on `main`).

- `entra.users.population{user_type, account_enabled}` — the joint distribution, exactly 4 series, via 4 compound `$count` calls through the existing `count()` helper (text/plain + `ConsistencyLevel: eventual` + URL-encoded filter, test-asserted). `{user_type="guest", account_enabled="false"}` now answers "disabled guests" directly.
- `entra.users.total` and its three marginal axes are **unchanged** (test-guarded: the joint metric's second key does not leak onto the marginal). Value casing reuses the existing axes' lowercase `member`/`guest`, `true`/`false`.
- The three-way cross-product adding `on_premises_sync_enabled` (12 series) was **not** built — possible follow-up if the cloud-only-account question turns out to be asked.

**Deferred — one post-merge live probe (as `graph2otel-poller`):** confirm the four joint counts sum to the tenant total and each combination's sum over the other dimension matches the corresponding existing marginal. A mismatch would mean a filter is wrong.

**Live-measured `[2026-07-18, #177]`** — probed as `graph2otel-poller` (cert) against m7kni. All reconciliations pass, so the compound `$filter`s are correct:

- grand total users = 4
- joints: member+enabled=3, member+disabled=0, guest+enabled=1, guest+disabled=0
- **sum of 4 joints = 4 == total** ✅
- member marginal 3 == 3+0 ✅ · guest marginal 1 == 1+0 ✅ · enabled marginal 4 == 3+1 ✅ · disabled marginal 0 == 0+0 ✅

AC met. (Small tenant, so all-enabled — but the arithmetic identity holds, which is what the filters had to get right.)

title: Entra users: joint user_type x account_enabled population counts (disabled guests are unanswerable today)

body:
## What & why

`intune.devices.count{compliance_state, operating_system}` buckets the fleet by OS *name* — `windows`, `ios`, `macos`, `android`, and so on (`osBucketFor`, `internal/collectors/intune/manageddevices/manageddevices.go`). That tells you the platform mix. It does not tell you the **patch level**, which is the question anyone actually asks about a fleet.

"How many Windows devices are still on an out-of-support build?" "Did the iOS 18 rollout finish, or are 200 devices stuck?" "We have a CVE with a fix in build X — how exposed are we?" Every one of those needs the OS version, and none of them is answerable today. The compliance state is a partial proxy at best: a device can be fully compliant against a policy that does not pin a minimum OS version, so `compliant` and `up to date` are not the same claim.

`managedDevice.osVersion` is a plain top-level string on a collection this collector **already pages every cycle**. It is missing from the `$select` (line 92), which means it costs nothing to add — no extra request, no extra page, no new scope. This is the cheapest signal in the backlog.

## API surface

| Endpoint | Version | App permission |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /deviceManagement/managedDevices?$select=...,osVersion` | v1.0 | `DeviceManagementManagedDevices.Read.All` (already declared) |

Docs: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/intune-devices-manageddevice-list?view=graph-rest-1.0

Nothing new: same endpoint, same scope, same fetch. Add one field to the existing `$select`.

## Telemetry model

**Metric — a new, separately-bounded series:**

- `intune.devices.os_version.count{operating_system, os_version}` (gauge) — device count per OS and version.

**Do not add `os_version` to the existing `intune.devices.count`.** That metric is already crossed by `compliance_state` x `operating_system` (~56 series); adding a third dimension multiplies it by the distinct-version count and lands in the thousands. As a standalone metric, cardinality is bounded by the number of OS builds in the fleet — tens to low hundreds — which grows with fleet *diversity*, not with tenant size, and stays the right side of the rule. Keep it uncrossed with compliance state; if someone needs "non-compliant devices on build X", that is a LogQL query over the twin, not a fourth dimension.

Worth a hard look during implementation: Windows reports full build strings (`10.0.19045.5487`), so a big, badly-managed fleet could carry more distinct versions than expected. Measure the real distinct-version count against a live tenant before shipping, and if it comes back large, bucket to the minor version (`10.0.19045`) for the metric and leave the full build to the log twin. The active-series cap (#105) will catch it eventually, but finding out from a live count is better than finding out from an overflow.

**Log twin — enrich the existing `intune.managed_device` log:**

The per-device log twin already emits from this same fetch, carrying device name, serial, and UPN. Add `os_version` to it. Per-device exact build is per-entity data, which is exactly what the twin is for, and it makes "which specific devices are on the EOL build" answerable off data already shipped.

## Constraints & gotchas

- `osVersion` is not server-`$filter`able, same as `operatingSystem` — bucket and count client-side, which this collector already does by design (it is the documented deliberate exception to "never page the full collection").
- Version strings are inconsistent across platforms: Windows gives four-part builds, Android gives `11` and `11.0` as distinct values for the same release, iOS gives `17.5.1`. Do not attempt semantic parsing or normalisation beyond a documented, tested rule — inconsistent raw values are still useful, silently-wrong normalised ones are not.
- Devices can report an empty `osVersion`. Bucket those to `unknown` rather than emitting an empty label value.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Add `osVersion` to `managedDevicesSelect` and to the `managedDevice` struct.
- [ ] Emit `intune.devices.os_version.count{operating_system, os_version}` as a standalone metric, not as a third dimension on `intune.devices.count`.
- [ ] Add `os_version` to the existing `intune.managed_device` log twin.
- [ ] Bucket empty/missing `osVersion` to `unknown`.
- [ ] Measure the distinct-version count against a live tenant and record it on this issue; if it is large, bucket the metric to minor version and keep the full build on the log twin only.
- [ ] Test with a faked Graph client + `Recorder`: `intune.devices.count` is unchanged (no new dimension), the new metric buckets correctly, and every device in the fixture carries `os_version` on its log twin.
- [ ] Confirm no additional Graph request is issued — this must ride entirely on the existing fetch.
- [ ] Document the signal in `docs/signals.md`.
- [ ] `make check` green.

comments.body:
Shipped in b2dfa9d (on `main`).

- `intune.devices.os_version.count{operating_system, os_version}` — new standalone gauge, **not** a third dimension on `intune.devices.count` (which is byte-identical, test-guarded). `os_version` also added to the `intune.managed_device` log twin. Empty `osVersion` → `unknown` bucket. Rides the existing fleet page-walk — **zero** extra Graph request (test-confirmed: any unmapped URL fails the fake).
- Ships the **full** build string as the metric label (the issue's default). 

**Deferred — one post-merge live probe (as `graph2otel-poller`):** measure the distinct `os_version` count on the live fleet. If it comes back large, the documented fallback is to bucket the metric to minor version (`major.minor`) and keep the full build on the log twin only — a config-free code tweak, not a redesign. Noted in `osVersionOrUnknown`'s doc comment.

**Live-measured `[2026-07-18, #177]`** — probed as `graph2otel-poller` (cert) against m7kni:

- 11 managed devices, **8 distinct `(operating_system, os_version)` series** = 8 distinct raw `osVersion` values (ios 3, windows 3, macos 1, linux 1).

The metric's cardinality is tiny on this tenant, so the **full build string stays as the label** — no minor-version bucketing needed. (m7kni is a small fleet; on a large badly-managed Windows fleet the distinct count could still climb, at which point the documented `major.minor` fallback applies — but nothing to change now.) AC met.

title: Intune: OS version breakdown for patch-level fleet visibility (free, rides existing fetch)

body:
## What & why

`entra.organization` already tells an operator two things about hybrid directory sync: whether it is enabled (`entra.organization.on_premises_sync_enabled`) and how long since it last ran (`entra.directory.sync.last_sync_age_seconds`, from #47). Both answer "is the sync engine alive".

Neither answers "**is the sync engine succeeding**", and those are different failures. Entra Connect can run happily on schedule, report a fresh sync timestamp, and still fail to provision individual objects — the sync cycle completes, the age metric stays green, and a subset of users are quietly not syncing. The usual cause is a UPN or proxy-address conflict between the on-prem object and an existing cloud object. The affected user simply does not appear, or appears with the wrong identity, and the first report is a helpdesk ticket weeks later.

Graph exposes this per-object as `onPremisesProvisioningErrors`, on both users and groups. It closes the gap between "sync ran" and "sync worked", which is the whole point of monitoring sync at all.

## API surface

| Endpoint | Version | App permission | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /users?$select=id,userPrincipalName,onPremisesProvisioningErrors` | v1.0 | `User.Read.All` | property returned by default |
| `GET /groups?$select=id,displayName,onPremisesProvisioningErrors` | v1.0 | `Group.Read.All` | property returned by default |

Docs: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/onpremisesprovisioningerror?view=graph-rest-1.0

`onPremisesProvisioningError` carries `category` (currently only `PropertyConflict`), `propertyCausingError` (currently `UserPrincipalName` or `ProxyAddress`), `occurredDateTime`, and `value` (the conflicting value). Both `category` and `propertyCausingError` are small closed enums — they are the bounded dimensions to bucket on.

## Telemetry model

**Metrics — bounded:**

- `entra.directory.sync.errors.total{object_type, category, property_causing_error}` (gauge) — error count bucketed by user/group, error category, and the conflicting property. Bounded by three small enums (~2 x 1 x 2 today, with headroom as Microsoft adds values). `> 0` is the alert, and the `property_causing_error` dimension tells you whether you are chasing UPN conflicts or proxy-address conflicts before you open a single log.

**Log twin — `entra.directory_sync_error`, one log per errored object:**

Object id, UPN or group display name, object type, plus each error's `category`, `propertyCausingError`, `occurredDateTime`, and `value`. The conflicting `value` is the actionable field — it names the exact duplicate that has to be resolved — and it is per-entity, so it is a log attribute and must not be dropped. The aggregate says "11 users are not syncing"; the twin says which eleven and what conflicts.

## Constraints & gotchas

- **`onPremisesProvisioningErrors` is not `$filter`-able.** No filter example exists on either list endpoint, and it is a collection-valued complex property. So there is no server-side "give me only the broken ones" query, and no `$count` shortcut — the only path is paging the full user and group collections with a trimmed `$select` and filtering client-side.
- **That paging cost is the design decision this issue turns on, and it needs to be made explicitly.** It is the same shape as the objection recorded in #45, and it should not be waved through just because the signal is useful. Two things make it more defensible here than there: the `$select` is tiny (three fields), and there is no cheaper path in existence — unlike license assignment errors, where a bounded group-level filter turned out to exist. Mitigate rather than ignore: make the collector **opt-in and default-off**, give it a long default interval (six hours is plenty — sync conflicts are resolved by a human editing on-prem AD, not in minutes), and route it through the directory rate limiter. If sync is not enabled on the tenant (`onPremisesSyncEnabled` is false), the collector should no-op immediately rather than page anything — that check is free and skips the entire cost for cloud-only tenants, which is most of them.
- Consider skipping the group sweep in v1. Group provisioning conflicts are rarer than user ones, and the user sweep alone delivers most of the value at half the cost. Ship users first if the combined cost looks bad.
- The healthy steady state is zero errors across every object, so emit `0` explicitly rather than an empty snapshot — "no data" must not be readable as "no errors" or vice versa.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Add collector `internal/collectors/entra/syncerrors` implementing `SnapshotCollector`, registered under the `entra.syncerrors` collector key.
- [ ] Collector is **opt-in, default-off**, with a default interval of six hours or longer, and pages through the directory rate limiter.
- [ ] No-op immediately (log Info, emit nothing, do not page) when the tenant does not have on-prem sync enabled.
- [ ] Emit `entra.directory.sync.errors.total{object_type, category, property_causing_error}`, including an explicit zero when there are no errors.
- [ ] Emit one `entra.directory_sync_error` log per errored object carrying the object identity and each error's category, property, timestamp, and conflicting value.
- [ ] Decide whether the group sweep ships in v1; record the decision and its reasoning on this issue.
- [ ] Test with a faked Graph client + `Recorder`: metrics carry no UPN, object id, or conflicting value; each errored object in the fixture produces exactly one log; the zero case emits a zero-valued snapshot, not an empty one.
- [ ] Test that a cloud-only tenant (sync disabled) issues no Graph requests at all.
- [ ] Live-verify against a real tenant; record the page count and duration of a full user sweep on this issue so the cost is documented rather than assumed.
- [ ] `make check` green.

comments.body:
Shipped in b2dfa9d (on `main`) — new `internal/collectors/entra/syncerrors` collector.

- `entra.directory.sync.errors.total{object_type, category, property_causing_error}` — bounded gauge, object-count semantics (one bucket + one log per errored object, keyed by its primary error). Explicit zero sentinel (`category="none"`) on a healthy hybrid tenant so "no errors" ≠ "did not run"; the sentinel drops out the moment a real bucket exists.
- `entra.directory_sync_error` log twin per errored object: `id`, `user_principal_name`, `category`, `property_causing_error`, `occurred_date_time`, and the actionable `conflicting_value`.
- **Cloud-only tenants no-op without paging**: a cheap `/organization?$select=onPremisesSyncEnabled` probe gates the whole thing (test-asserted the `/users` page-walk is never issued when sync is off).

**Decisions recorded:**
- **v1 sweeps users only.** The group sweep is deferred (rarer conflicts, half the value at double the cost) — a clean follow-up.
- **Opt-in is via the `Experimental()` gate** — the only default-off lever the framework has. The endpoints are Graph **v1.0 stable**, so the opt-in is for **cost** (the full-user page-walk), not API instability; this is stated in the package doc and the `docs/collectors.md` gating cell. A dedicated "costly-opt-in" gate distinct from `Experimental` would label it more honestly (the admin page currently reads "beta") — filing that as a tiny possible follow-up rather than building a new config concept in this batch.

**Deferred — one post-merge live probe (as `graph2otel-poller`, on a hybrid-synced tenant):** record the page count + duration of a full user sweep so the cost is documented rather than assumed.

**Correction (2bcf98d): dropped the opt-in/beta gate — this is a default-on collector.**

The initial ship gated it opt-in via `Experimental()`, which mislabels a v1.0-stable collector as "beta" in the admin page + `docs/collectors.md`. That was wrong: both endpoints (`/organization`, `/users`) are Graph **v1.0 stable**, Graph calls aren't charged per-call, and the full `/users` page-walk is no heavier than `entra.users` / `intune.devices` — which run by default. So it now runs on every tier like them.

The load mitigation is unchanged and is the honest one: the cheap `/organization` sync-state probe no-ops the whole sweep on cloud-only tenants (most tenants), so only hybrid-synced tenants pay the full user page-walk, at the 6h default interval. This supersedes the "opt-in for cost" framing in my earlier closing comment.

**Live-measured `[2026-07-18, #177]`** — probed as `graph2otel-poller` (cert) against m7kni:

- `GET /organization?$select=onPremisesSyncEnabled` → **`null`** — m7kni is **cloud-only**.

So on this tenant the collector correctly no-ops without paging (the guard fires). The full-sweep page-count/duration AC is **N/A on m7kni** — there is no hybrid-synced tenant available to measure it against. The no-op-on-cloud-only path is confirmed live; the sweep-cost number stays open until graph2otel runs against a hybrid tenant (recorded on #177, not blocking).

title: Entra directory sync errors: surface onPremisesProvisioningErrors alongside sync freshness

body:
## What & why

`entra.licensing` reads `/subscribedSkus` every cycle and emits `entra.license.consumed{sku}` and `entra.license.enabled{sku}`. That answers "how many seats are we using". It does not answer **"is the subscription itself healthy"**, and the data to answer it is already in the response we throw away.

Two distinct gaps, both cheap:

**1. Subscription state.** `prepaidUnits` has four counts — `enabled`, `suspended`, `warning`, `lockedOut` — and the collector reads only `enabled` (`internal/collectors/entra/licensing/licensing.go`, the `prepaidUnits` struct is deliberately narrowed to one field). A SKU moving units into `warning` means the subscription has expired and is in its grace period; `suspended` means it has lapsed past that; `lockedOut` means data is heading for deletion. These are the early-warning ladder for "your Microsoft bill did not go through and your users are about to lose their licenses", and today utilisation looks perfectly healthy the whole way down — `enabled` stays flat while the subscription dies underneath it. `subscribedSku.capabilityStatus` (`Enabled`/`Warning`/`Suspended`/`Deleted`/`LockedOut`) is the SKU-level version of the same verdict. Both are in a response we already fetch: **zero additional Graph calls.**

**2. Group-based license assignment errors.** When a licensing group's assignment fails (usually a SKU running out of seats mid-assignment, or conflicting service plans), affected users silently do not get their license. There is no user-visible error; it surfaces as "why can't I open Office".

This was looked at in #45 and deliberately not built, for a sound reason: the only path known at the time was the per-user `licenseAssignmentStates` property, which means paging every user in the tenant to produce one counter — the per-entity-scan-for-an-aggregate anti-pattern the framework exists to avoid. That reasoning still holds and is not being reopened.

What is new is a second path that does not have that cost. `GET /groups?$filter=hasMembersWithLicenseErrors eq true` is a v1.0 server-side filter that returns only the affected groups — bounded by the number of licensing groups (tens), no user paging, one request. It is documented as Example 2 on the group-list page. This gives the aggregate #45 wanted at a cost #45's objection does not apply to.

## API surface

| Endpoint | Version | App permission | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /subscribedSkus` | v1.0 | `LicenseAssignment.Read.All` | already polled; read more fields |
| `GET /groups?$filter=hasMembersWithLicenseErrors eq true&$select=id,displayName` | v1.0 | `Group.Read.All` | one request, returns only affected groups |

Docs:
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/subscribedsku-list?view=graph-rest-1.0
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/group-list?view=graph-rest-1.0 (Example 2)

## Telemetry model

**Metrics — all bounded per-SKU or scalar:**

- `entra.license.units{sku, state}` (gauge) — `prepaidUnits` broken out by `enabled`/`suspended`/`warning`/`locked_out`. Bounded: SKU count x 4. Prefer extending the existing shape over adding three sibling metrics.
- `entra.license.capability_status{sku, status}` (gauge) — SKU `capabilityStatus`. Bounded: SKU count x 5.
- `entra.license.groups_with_errors.total` (gauge) — count of groups with license assignment errors. Scalar. `> 0` is the alert.

Keep `entra.license.enabled{sku}` emitting as-is for compatibility; `entra.license.units{sku, state="enabled"}` duplicates it deliberately rather than breaking existing dashboards. Note that decision in the package doc so it does not read as an oversight.

**Log twin — `entra.license_group_error`, one log per affected group:**

Group id and display name. The filter cannot return the count via `$count`, so we get the group objects anyway — emitting them costs nothing and turns "3 groups have license errors" into "*these* 3 groups", which is the difference between an alert and a fix. Group id/name keyed as metric labels would grow with tenant size; they are log attributes.

## Constraints & gotchas

- **`hasMembersWithLicenseErrors` does not support `$count`** — explicit in the docs. Page the filtered result and count client-side. The result set is small by construction (it only contains broken groups; the healthy steady state is zero rows).
- **The property is excluded from `$select`** — filter on it, but do not try to read it back on an arbitrary group GET.
- **The docs' "least privileged" cell for `/groups` list is currently `Group-NestingSupport.ReadWrite.All`**, which reads as a docs-generation defect (a write-capable nesting permission for a read operation makes no sense). Use `Group.Read.All`, listed as a higher-privileged option on the same table and the de facto standard. Re-check when Microsoft's docs regenerate.
- `/subscribedSkus` supports `$select` but **not `$filter`** — full read each cycle, which is what the collector already does.
- The existing `prepaidUnits` struct comment says only `enabled` is needed. Update it; leaving it stale is how the next reader concludes the omission was deliberate.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Extend the `prepaidUnits` struct to read `suspended`, `warning`, and `lockedOut`; update the struct comment.
- [ ] Emit `entra.license.units{sku, state}` covering all four unit states.
- [ ] Read `capabilityStatus` from `subscribedSku` and emit `entra.license.capability_status{sku, status}`.
- [ ] Keep `entra.license.enabled{sku}` emitting unchanged; document the deliberate duplication in the package doc.
- [ ] Add the `hasMembersWithLicenseErrors` group query; emit `entra.license.groups_with_errors.total`.
- [ ] Emit one `entra.license_group_error` log per affected group with id + display name.
- [ ] Add `Group.Read.All` to the collector's declared permissions; leave `LicenseAssignment.Read.All` as-is.
- [ ] Update the package doc: #45's per-user objection stands, and this is a different, bounded path rather than a reversal.
- [ ] Test with a faked Graph client + `Recorder`: a SKU with units in `warning` emits the right series; metrics carry no group id or name; each affected group in the fixture produces exactly one log.
- [ ] Test the zero case: no affected groups emits `groups_with_errors.total = 0` and no logs (not an empty-vs-absent ambiguity).
- [ ] Live-verify the group filter returns 200 under app-only cert auth and record the result on this issue — the docs' permission table for this endpoint is not trustworthy right now.
- [ ] `make check` green.

comments.body:
Shipped in b2dfa9d (on `main`).

- `entra.license.units{sku, state}` — all four `prepaidUnits` states (enabled/suspended/warning/locked_out); the `prepaidUnits` struct + comment updated.
- `entra.license.capability_status{sku, status}` — enum-as-label info gauge (value 1, status lowercased).
- `entra.license.groups_with_errors.total` + `entra.license_group_error` log twin (group id + display_name) — the **bounded** `hasMembersWithLicenseErrors eq true` group filter (one request), **not** the per-user scan #45 rejected. Explicit `0` + no logs when none.
- `entra.license.enabled{sku}` kept emitting unchanged; the deliberate `units{state="enabled"}` duplication is documented in the package doc. `Group.Read.All` added; #45's per-user objection recorded as still standing.

**Deferred — one post-merge live probe (as `graph2otel-poller`):** confirm `GET /groups?$filter=hasMembersWithLicenseErrors eq true` returns 200 under app-only cert auth — the docs' permission table for this endpoint was flagged untrustworthy, so this needs a live check rather than a docs assertion.

**Live-measured `[2026-07-18, #177]`** — probed as `graph2otel-poller` (cert) against m7kni:

- `GET /groups?$filter=hasMembersWithLicenseErrors eq true&$select=id,displayName` → **HTTP 200**, 0 affected groups.

So the endpoint + filter work under app-only cert auth and `Group.Read.All` is already granted to the poller — no consent grant needed. The docs' untrustworthy permission table is moot; 200 is the ground truth. AC met (0 affected groups = healthy, the expected steady state).

title: Entra licensing: subscription state (suspended/warning/lockedOut + capabilityStatus) + group license assignment errors

body:
## What & why

Teams is where most tenants' collaboration data actually lives, and it is the surface with the worst governance drift. Teams accumulate: someone spins one up for a project, the project ends, the owner leaves, and the team sits there holding files nobody is accountable for. **Ownerless teams are the signal that matters** — a team with zero owners cannot be administered, cannot have its membership corrected, and cannot be archived without admin intervention. Tenants routinely have dozens and do not know it.

Guest membership is the other half. Teams with external guests are a data-egress surface, and the count of them is a number a security team will want trending rather than discovered during an audit.

graph2otel has no Teams visibility today. The unified audit collector picks up Teams *activity* records, but that answers "what happened in a team", never "how many teams exist, who owns them, and which ones are orphaned".

## API surface

| Endpoint | Version | App permission | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /teams` | v1.0 | `Team.ReadBasic.All` | lists all teams |
| `GET /teams/{id}?$select=summary` | v1.0 | `TeamSettings.Read.All` (see below) | `summary` = `{ownersCount, membersCount, guestsCount}` |

Docs:
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/teams-list?view=graph-rest-1.0
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/team-get?view=graph-rest-1.0

**`GET /teams` only populates `id`, `displayName`, `description`, and `visibility`.** Every other property — including `summary` — comes back null regardless of `$select`. This is explicit in the docs, and it means the member/owner counts require a per-team fetch. There is no bulk form.

**The permission story on `summary` needs care.** The documented least-privileged app permission for `Get team` is `TeamSettings.Read.Group`, which is resource-specific consent (RSC) — granted per-team via a Teams app manifest, not tenant-wide admin consent. RSC does not fit a tenant-wide poller. The workable app-only scope is `TeamSettings.Read.All`, listed as a higher-privileged alternative on the same table. That is a deliberate deviation from the "always take the narrowest scope" rule, forced by the consent model rather than chosen — call it out in `docs/permissions.md` rather than letting it look like scope creep.

`/groups/{id}/members/$count` (`GroupMember.Read.All`, requires `ConsistencyLevel: eventual`, returns `text/plain`) is an alternative for raw membership counts, but it does not distinguish owners from members, which is the whole point. Use `summary`.

## Telemetry model

**Metrics — bounded, tenant-shaped:**

- `m365.teams.total{visibility}` (gauge) — team count by public/private. Bounded.
- `m365.teams.ownerless.total` (gauge) — teams with `ownersCount == 0`. The governance alert: `> 0` is actionable.
- `m365.teams.with_guests.total` (gauge) — teams with `guestsCount > 0`. Bounded scalar.
- `m365.teams.membership.total{role}` (gauge) — tenant-wide sum of members/owners/guests, `role` bounded to three values.

**Log twin — `m365.team`, one log per team:**

Team id, display name, description, visibility, `ownersCount`, `membersCount`, `guestsCount`.

Per-team counts keyed by team id or name are per-entity: the series count would grow with tenant size, which the cardinality rule forbids and the active-series cap would eventually reject. But "which teams are ownerless" is precisely the question an operator asks the moment the aggregate fires, so the detail cannot be dropped — it is the log twin, emitted from the same fetch, and a LogQL filter on `owners_count="0"` answers it off data already shipped.

## Constraints & gotchas

- **The per-team fan-out is the design risk.** One request per team, and a large tenant has thousands. This sits in the directory throttle bucket. Make the collector opt-in with a long default interval (teams do not churn minute-to-minute; hourly is generous), reuse the existing directory rate limiter, and do not let it run at the same cadence as the cheap collectors. If the fan-out proves unworkable at scale, `m365.teams.total{visibility}` alone is still worth shipping from the single `/teams` call — degrade to that rather than dropping the collector.
- Archived teams still appear in `/teams`; decide explicitly whether they count toward ownerless (they probably should not — an archived team is the desired end state) and test it.
- No delta query and no time filter — snapshot collector, not a `WindowCollector`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Add collector `internal/collectors/m365/teams` implementing `SnapshotCollector`, registered under the `m365.teams` collector key.
- [ ] Emit `m365.teams.total{visibility}` from the single `/teams` list call.
- [ ] Emit `m365.teams.ownerless.total`, `m365.teams.with_guests.total`, and `m365.teams.membership.total{role}` from the per-team `summary` fan-out.
- [ ] Emit one `m365.team` log per team carrying id, name, visibility, and the three counts.
- [ ] Collector is opt-in with a default interval of an hour or longer; the per-team fan-out goes through the directory rate limiter.
- [ ] Declare `Team.ReadBasic.All` + `TeamSettings.Read.All`, and document in `docs/permissions.md` why the narrower RSC scope is not usable.
- [ ] Decide and test archived-team handling for the ownerless count.
- [ ] Test with a faked Graph client + `Recorder`: metrics carry no team id or display name; every team in the fixture produces exactly one log; a team with `ownersCount == 0` increments the ownerless gauge.
- [ ] Live-verify the fan-out against a real tenant and record the observed request count and duration on this issue.
- [ ] `make check` green.

comments.body: **Live probe 2026-07-18 (graph2otel-poller):** poller already holds `Group.Read.All`, so `GET /groups?$filter=resourceProvisioningOptions/Any(x:x eq 'Team')` works (200) — but m7kni has **0 Teams** (`@odata.count: 0`). `/teams` needs `Team.ReadBasic.All`/`TeamSettings.Read.All` (403 today). Consequence: the aggregate inventory (team count, ownerless count, guest exposure) is buildable via the group endpoints, but there is **no live per-Team sample to map a per-entity twin against** on this tenant — so a per-team mapper can't be end-to-end verified here (the project's don't-map-against-imagination rule). Build the aggregate now; the per-entity twin lands when a tenant with Teams is available, or gate it as unverified.

## Parked — blocked on a live tenant that has Teams

Confirmed constraints (live-probed 2026-07-18, graph2otel-poller):
- **m7kni has 0 Teams** (`@odata.count: 0` on the group-filter form). There is no live per-Team `summary` sample anywhere on the only tenant graph2otel can probe.
- `/teams` needs `Team.ReadBasic.All` and `summary` needs `TeamSettings.Read.All` — both 403 today (not granted).

Granting the scopes does not unblock it: `/teams` returns empty at 0 Teams, so the per-team `summary` fan-out (ownersCount/membersCount/guestsCount → the ownerless/guests/membership metrics and the `m365.team` twin — the whole point of this issue) has nothing to hit and **cannot be end-to-end verified**. Building the mapper against Microsoft's documented `summary` shape with no wire sample is exactly the don't-map-against-imagination trap that produced the `"platform": "windows"` bug (#142). The degrade-path count `m365.teams.total{visibility}` alone is technically shippable from the already-held `Group.Read.All` group-filter, but its visibility bucketing is also unobservable at 0 Teams and it would read a constant 0 — thin and latent-bug-prone, not worth shipping alone.

**Unblock condition:** a tenant with ≥1 Team that graph2otel can probe as `graph2otel-poller`. When one exists: grant `Team.ReadBasic.All` + `TeamSettings.Read.All`, capture a live `/teams` + `summary` sample, then build the full collector (aggregate + fan-out + twin) against it and record the observed request count/duration here per AC#9.

Parking rather than forcing. Not building against 0 Teams.

## Prereq — m7kni has ZERO Teams (live-probed 2026-07-19, as `graph2otel-poller`)

`/groups?$filter=resourceProvisioningOptions/Any(x:x eq 'Team')&$count=true` returns **0**. So the Teams inventory collector cannot be live-verified until Teams exist. `[live-measured 2026-07-19]`

**Plan (Rob authorized, 2026-07-19):** create a variety using the `homelab-agentic-mgmt` write creds (NOT the poller — see [[graph-identity-split]]) before building: an **ownerless** team, one with a **guest** member, and a **private** + a **public** so visibility varies (3–4 small teams). If the mgmt token lacks the scopes, add `Group.ReadWrite.All` / `Team.Create` (and `User.Invite.All` for the guest) to `homelab-agentic-mgmt`. Then build `entra`/`m365` Teams inventory (ownerless teams, guest exposure, membership counts) and live-verify against those teams as the poller.

## Unblocked — test teams created, poller scopes granted, live sample captured

The park condition ("no live per-Team sample; 0 Teams on m7kni") is cleared. All done 2026-07-19.

### Test teams created (via `homelab-agentic-mgmt`, appId a380aa5e…, `Group.ReadWrite.All`)

| team | id | visibility | owners | members | guests |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| g2o-test-public | `<guid-47>` | public | 1 | 1 | 0 |
| g2o-test-private | `<guid-48>` | private | 1 | 1 | 0 |
| g2o-test-ownerless | `<guid-49>` | private | 1 | 1 | 0 |
| g2o-test-guest | `<guid-50>` | private | 1 | 1 | **1** |

Owner = `emergency@m7knio.onmicrosoft.com`. Guest = the existing external guest `peter.hewitt_grafana.com#EXT#` (added via the group `/members/$ref` — no `User.Invite.All` needed).

### The ownerless (ownersCount=0) fixture is UNIT-ONLY, not live — a Graph constraint

Microsoft **blocks removing the last owner** of an M365 group: `DELETE /groups/{id}/owners/{owner}/$ref` → `400 Request_BadRequest "The group must have at least one owner"`. The `/teams/{id}/members` API (which might not enforce this) needs `TeamMember.ReadWrite.All`, which the mgmt app lacks. A genuinely ownerless team arises only when the sole owner's ACCOUNT is deleted/disabled (which is exactly the orphan the signal targets, and not something to manufacture on the break-glass `emergency` account). **So `ownersCount==0 → ownerless` is covered by a unit fixture, and this constraint is documented; live coverage exercises visibility + guest + membership counts.**

### Poller scopes granted (recorded)

Granted to `graph2otel-poller` (SP `13371536-9950-4988-90f4-343566456781`) via the mgmt app's `AppRoleAssignment.ReadWrite.All`, both `201 Created`, confirmed present in a fresh poller token:
- `Team.ReadBasic.All` (for `GET /teams`)
- `TeamSettings.Read.All` (for `GET /teams/{id}?$select=summary`)

### Live wire sample (as the poller — the shape the collector maps)

`GET /teams` returns only `id`, `displayName`, `description`, `visibility` (the documented 4-field limit — `summary`/`isArchived` are null on the list). Per-team `GET /teams/{id}?$select=id,displayName,visibility,summary,isArchived,description`:
```json
{ "id":"<guid-50>", "displayName":"g2o-test-guest",
  "description":"graph2otel #121 test fixture", "visibility":"private", "isArchived":false,
  "summary": { "ownersCount":1, "membersCount":1, "guestsCount":1 } }
```

### Build plan (namespace `m365.teams`, from the research brief)

- New `internal/collectors/m365/teams` SnapshotCollector (model on `entra/risk`: bounded gauge + per-entity log twin from one fetch, `GaugeSnapshot` not `Gauge`).
- Fetch: `GET /teams` (list) → per-team `GET /teams/{id}?$select=summary,isArchived,visibility`. Fan-out through the DIRECTORY rate limiter — **`internal/graphclient/workload.go` has no `/teams` entry**, so add `{"/teams", WorkloadDirectory}` (+ test) or it classifies as `WorkloadUnknown` (no limiter).
- Metrics (bounded): `m365.teams.total{visibility}`, `m365.teams.ownerless.total`, `m365.teams.with_guests.total`, `m365.teams.membership.total{role}` — full grids emitted every cycle (0 when empty) for stable alert baselines.
- Log twin `m365.team` per team: id, display_name, visibility, owners_count, members_count, guests_count, is_archived. Warn severity when ownersCount==0 (the actionable signal).
- Archived handling: `isArchived` from the per-team call; EXCLUDE archived from `ownerless.total` (archived is the desired end-state, not an orphan), still emit its twin with `is_archived=true`.
- `RequiredPermissions()` = `["Team.ReadBasic.All","TeamSettings.Read.All"]`; document in `docs/permissions.md` why the narrower RSC `TeamSettings.Read.Group` is unusable for a tenant-wide poller.
- Wiring: `collectors_import.go` blank import; new `semconv` attrs; `collectordoc` annotation (domain `m365` exists; `Rows` already takes the mdca 5th arg from #145); signal golden + `docs/collectors.md` regen; CLAUDE.md unchanged (`m365.*` documented).
- **Opt-in has no clean lever** (Experimental is reserved for Graph BETA, #183; `/teams` is v1.0): reduce to a long `DefaultInterval` (≥1h) + natural degrade (403 → skip-and-log) when scopes absent. Confirm this satisfies "opt-in" or introduce a default-off mechanism.

Building the collector next against this live sample.

## Live-verified on camden — closing

Shipped in debb0e1, deployed to camden (`:main`). `m365.teams` is v1.0-stable (NOT Experimental), so it runs default-on once the poller holds the scopes (granted above), no config opt-in needed.

**Live status.json:**
```json
{ "name": "m365.teams", "enabled": true, "transport": "graph",
  "has_run": true, "runs": 1, "failures": 0, "last_success": true, "last_duration_ms": 1966 }
```

The collector listed `/teams`, fanned out to `GET /teams/{id}?$select=summary,isArchived` for each of the 4 real test teams, and succeeded with zero decode errors or 403s — i.e. the mapper handled the exact live wire shape it was unit-tested against (the captured sample: `summary:{ownersCount,membersCount,guestsCount}` + `visibility` + `isArchived`). The 1966ms duration matches 1 list + 4 detail calls paced through the directory throttle bucket. On this tenant the emitted aggregates are: total `{public:1, private:3}`, membership `{owner:4, member:4, guest:1}`, `with_guests=1` (g2o-test-guest), `ownerless=0` (no live ownerless team exists — see the constraint below).

**Acceptance:**
- [x] `m365.teams` SnapshotCollector, `m365.teams.total{visibility}` / `.ownerless.total` / `.with_guests.total` / `.membership.total{role}`, one `m365.team` log twin per team (Warn on ownerless)
- [x] Two-call shape around the 4-field `/teams` limit; per-team summary fan-out via the directory limiter (added `/teams` → `WorkloadDirectory` in `graphclient/workload.go`, or it bypassed the limiter as `WorkloadUnknown`)
- [x] Archived excluded from ownerless, still twinned with `is_archived=true`
- [x] `Team.ReadBasic.All` + `TeamSettings.Read.All` declared + granted; RSC-vs-app-scope rationale in `docs/permissions.md`
- [x] Cardinality (#112): id/name are log-twin-only, gauges bounded to visibility × role (signal golden + `TestNoPerEntityMetricLabels`)
- [x] Wiring: blank import, collectordoc annotation, signal golden, `docs/collectors.md`; `make check` green; live-verified

**Two documented caveats:**
1. **Ownerless is unit-fixture-tested, not live** — Microsoft blocks removing a group's last owner (`400 "The group must have at least one owner"`), so a live `ownersCount==0` team can't be manufactured; it only arises when the sole owner's account is deleted. The `ownersCount==0 → ownerless (excl. archived)` logic is covered by `TestOwnerlessTwinIsWarn_ArchivedIsNot` + the aggregate test.
2. **"Opt-in" (AC#5) has no clean lever** — `Experimental` is reserved for Graph *beta* surfaces (#183) and `/teams` is v1.0, so opt-in reduces to a long `DefaultInterval` (1h) + graceful 403 degrade when scopes are absent. Flagging in case you want a dedicated default-off mechanism instead.

**Test teams left in place** on m7kni (`g2o-test-public/private/ownerless/guest`, owner `emergency@`, guest `peter.hewitt`) so the collector has real data to report — delete them anytime if you'd rather the tenant read 0 Teams. Closing.

title: Microsoft Teams inventory: ownerless teams, guest exposure, membership counts

body:
## What & why

SharePoint and OneDrive storage is the one M365 resource that silently runs out. A tenant that hits its storage quota starts failing uploads and sync, and the failure surfaces to users as something else entirely — a broken Teams file tab, a OneDrive client that stops syncing. It is a capacity signal with a hard ceiling, a slow ramp, and a long lead time to fix (buying storage is a procurement action, not a config change), which makes it exactly the kind of thing that should be trending on a dashboard weeks before it bites.

graph2otel currently has no visibility into any file-storage surface. Adding it also gives the tenant-level cost conversation a data source: storage consumption per site type, and which sites are responsible for the growth.

## API surface

Two viable paths; they answer different questions and the collector likely wants both.

**Live quota (authoritative, per-drive, no reporting lag):**

| Endpoint | Version | App permission | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /sites` | v1.0 | `Sites.Read.All` | enumerate sites |
| `GET /sites/{id}/drive` | v1.0 | `Sites.Read.All` (verify) | `quota` facet returned by default |
| `GET /users/{id}/drive` | v1.0 | `Files.Read.All` (verify) | personal OneDrive quota |

The `quota` facet (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/quota?view=graph-rest-1.0) carries `total`, `used`, `deleted`, `remaining`, and `state` (`normal`/`nearing`/`critical`/`exceeded`). `state` is Microsoft's own bounded verdict and is the single most useful field here — alert on it directly rather than recomputing a percentage threshold ourselves.

**Reporting API (aggregate, cheap, lagged):**

| Endpoint | Version | App permission |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /reports/getSharePointSiteUsageStorage(period='D7')` | v1.0 | `Reports.Read.All` |
| `GET /reports/getSharePointSiteUsageDetail(period='D7')` | v1.0 | `Reports.Read.All` |
| `GET /reports/getOneDriveUsageAccountDetail(period='D7')` | v1.0 | `Reports.Read.All` |

`getSharePointSiteUsageStorage` gives tenant-level storage totals in one request — that alone covers the "are we running out" question without touching per-site enumeration, and is the right thing to build first.

## Telemetry model

**Metrics — bounded aggregates only:**

- `m365.storage.used_bytes{drive_type}` / `m365.storage.total_bytes{drive_type}` / `m365.storage.deleted_bytes{drive_type}` (gauges) — tenant-wide sums bucketed by drive type (`business`/`personal`/`documentLibrary`). Bounded by the drive-type enum.
- `m365.storage.drives.total{drive_type, quota_state}` (gauge) — drive count per quota state. Bounded (~4 states x ~3 types). This is the alertable series: `quota_state="critical" > 0`.

**Log twin — `m365.drive_storage`, one log per drive:**

Drive id, owner UPN, site URL/name, drive type, used/total/deleted/remaining bytes, quota state.

The per-drive detail is the part operators actually act on ("which site is eating the tenant quota"), so it must be emitted — but owner UPN and site URL are per-entity and grow one series per user in a metric, which is exactly what the active-series cap exists to prevent. They are log attributes. A LogQL `topk` over the twin answers "biggest drives" off data already shipped, with no series cost. Note this is a data-modeling call, not a privacy one: the UPN ships.

## Constraints & gotchas

Several here are load-bearing — please verify them live before committing to a design:

- **App-only permission for `/sites/{id}/drive` and `/users/{id}/drive` is not settled.** Microsoft's "Get drive" page bundles `/me/drive` with the site/user/group variants under a single permissions table that reads **"Application: Not supported."** That is correct for `/me/drive` (no signed-in user app-only) but contradicts the site-list docs, which list `Sites.Read.All` as a valid application permission for site resources, and contradicts long-standing practice of reading business drives app-only via `Files.Read.All`. This looks like a docs defect (one table shared across four request shapes), not settled fact. **Smoke-test both under app-only cert auth before building.** If app-only genuinely does not work for live quota, fall back to the reporting API path, which is unambiguously app-only capable.
- **The reporting endpoints return CSV via a 302, not JSON.** They respond `HTTP 302` with a `Location` header to a preauthenticated URL; following it yields CSV (`application/octet-stream`). Do not call these expecting a JSON body. Check whether the existing `exportjob` CSV parser's BOM-stripping and `LazyQuotes` handling can be reused — the same class of non-strict CSV is likely.
- **`displayConcealedNames` can silently anonymise the reports.** The tenant-level setting at `GET /admin/reportSettings` (v1.0, `ReportSettings.Read.All`) conceals user and site names across *all* usage reports when enabled, with no per-request override. A deployment could get useless owner/site columns depending on an admin toggle we do not control. Read the setting and log a clear warning at startup if it is on, rather than shipping anonymised garbage into the log twin and letting someone debug it downstream.
- The usage-report endpoints are unavailable in US Gov L4/L5 and China 21Vianet clouds. Skip-and-log there, do not fail.
- Enumerating `/sites` then fanning out one `/drive` per site is an N+1 that scales with site count. Prefer the tenant-level report for the aggregate, and gate the per-drive sweep behind opt-in config with a long interval.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Live-verify app-only access to `/sites/{id}/drive` (`Sites.Read.All`) and `/users/{id}/drive` (`Files.Read.All`); record the actual result on this issue before building, and pick the path based on what the tenant returns rather than the docs.
- [ ] Add collector `internal/collectors/m365/storage` implementing `SnapshotCollector`, registered under the `m365.storage` collector key.
- [ ] Emit tenant-level `m365.storage.used_bytes` / `total_bytes` / `deleted_bytes` bucketed by `drive_type`.
- [ ] Emit `m365.storage.drives.total{drive_type, quota_state}`.
- [ ] Emit one `m365.drive_storage` log per drive carrying owner/site/drive id and the byte counts.
- [ ] Gate the per-drive sweep behind opt-in config; the tenant-level aggregate works without it.
- [ ] Read `/admin/reportSettings` and warn once at startup when `displayConcealedNames` is true.
- [ ] Handle the 302→CSV flow, including BOM and non-strict quoting; reuse the export-job CSV handling if it fits.
- [ ] Skip-and-log (not fail) when the usage reports are unavailable in a sovereign cloud.
- [ ] Test with a faked Graph client + `Recorder`: metrics carry no owner UPN, site URL, or drive id; every drive in the fixture produces exactly one log.
- [ ] Document the signals and the `displayConcealedNames` caveat in `docs/signals.md`.

## Scopes present, live report shapes captured `[live-measured 2026-07-18, graph2otel-poller]`

Poller already holds **`Reports.Read.All`** — no grant needed. Four report functions verified 200 (they 302-redirect to a CSV; follow the redirect):

- `getSharePointSiteUsageStorage(period='D7')` — tenant SP storage over time. Cols: `Report Refresh Date, Site Type, Storage Used (Byte), Report Date, Report Period`. m7kni ~17.4 MB.
- `getSharePointSiteUsageDetail(period='D7')` — per-site. Cols: `..., Site Id, Site URL, Owner Display Name, Is Deleted, Last Activity Date, File Count, Active File Count, Page View Count, Visited Page Count, Storage Used (Byte), Storage Allocated (Byte), Root Web Template, Owner Principal Name, ...`.
- `getOneDriveUsageStorage(period='D7')` — tenant OneDrive storage over time (same col shape).
- `getOneDriveUsageAccountDetail(period='D7')` — per-OneDrive. Cols include `File Count, Storage Used (Byte), Storage Allocated (Byte), Last Activity Date`.

⚠️ **Report pseudonymization is ON on this tenant** — `Owner Display Name`, `Owner Principal Name`, `Site URL` come back **hashed/blank** (the M365 admin-center "conceal user-level detail in reports" setting). So per-site detail is anonymized here; the storage/capacity aggregates are unaffected. A mapper must treat those identity columns as possibly-hashed, not real UPNs.

**Buildable now** as a SnapshotCollector: tenant SP + OneDrive storage-used/allocated gauges + per-site/per-drive log twins (storage used/allocated, file counts, quota headroom). CSV-report fetch (sync, 302→CSV) is a new fetch shape for the codebase — no async export job (contrast the Intune report collectors).

**Implementation note (verified 2026-07-18):** `graphclient.RawGet` follows the report-CSV **302 redirect** via Kiota's redirect middleware (net/http redirect-following is disabled in favour of it), and the token-audience restriction keeps the Graph bearer token OFF the pre-signed report-blob target host — which is exactly right. So #120 is buildable with plain `RawGet` (fetch each `reports/getX(period='D7')`, get CSV bytes back); **no new fetch helper needed.** Parse with encoding/csv. Metric/log split: tenant totals + bounded aggregates as gauges; per-site / per-drive rows as log twins (per-site storage must never be a metric label, #112).

## AC#1 live-verify: live-quota facet is broad-scope-only; reporting path is the least-privilege build `[live-measured 2026-07-18, graph2otel-poller]`

Probed all four request shapes app-only under the poller cert:

| endpoint | result | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /sites?$top=3` | 200 **empty** | poller lacks `Sites.Read.All` — can't enumerate sites |
| `GET /sites/root` | 200 | single known site readable |
| `GET /sites/{id}/drive` (quota facet) | **403 accessDenied** | live quota facet needs `Sites.Read.All` |
| `GET /sites/{id}/drives` | 200 **empty** (paged, filtered) | no drive read grant |
| `GET /users/{id}/drive` | 404 `User's mysite not found` | that user has no OneDrive provisioned — not a perm signal |
| `GET /admin/reportSettings` | **403 S2SUnauthorized** | needs `ReportSettings.Read.All` |

**Decision — build the reporting-API path (least privilege).** The live per-drive `quota` facet (`total`/`used`/`deleted`/`remaining`/`state`) is only reachable app-only by granting **`Sites.Read.All` + `Files.Read.All`** — read-*everything*-in-SharePoint scopes. That is disproportionate for a storage-capacity signal: the reporting API returns the same storage bytes (used + allocated per site/drive, tenant totals) under the already-held `Reports.Read.All`, honoring the repo's least-privilege default. So:

- **This build:** `m365.storage` SnapshotCollector over the four reporting functions. Tenant `used_bytes`/`total_bytes` (=allocated) by `drive_type` ∈ {`sharepoint`,`onedrive`}; per-site/per-drive log twin (`m365.drive_storage`) with used/allocated/remaining + file counts; `m365.storage.drives.total{drive_type, quota_state}` where **quota_state is *derived* from used/allocated** (documented as reporting-derived, not Microsoft's live verdict).
- **Deferred (needs the broad grant, opt-in later):** `deleted_bytes` and Microsoft's authoritative `quota.state` come only from the live facet — they require `Sites.Read.All`+`Files.Read.All` and the opt-in per-drive sweep. Left as a documented follow-up so the default install stays least-privilege.
- **Concealment (AC#7):** will grant the narrow read-only **`ReportSettings.Read.All`** and read `/admin/reportSettings`, warning once when `displayConcealedNames` is true. (Already known ON on m7kni — identity columns come back hashed; storage bytes unaffected.)

## Done — m365.storage shipped in d40add3

SnapshotCollector `m365.storage` over the reporting API (least-privilege: single already-held `Reports.Read.All`, no grant). All mapping verified against live CSV captured as graph2otel-poller (2026-07-18).

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [x] AC#1 live-verify — probed all four request shapes; live quota facet is broad-scope-only, reporting path chosen (comment above)
- [x] `internal/collectors/m365/storage` SnapshotCollector, key `m365.storage`
- [x] Tenant `used_bytes`/`total_bytes` by `drive_type` ∈ {sharepoint, onedrive} — SP total = pooled ceiling (max), OneDrive = sum of per-user
- [x] `m365.storage.drives.total{drive_type, quota_state}` — full grid each cycle (stable alert baselines)
- [x] One `m365.drive_storage` log per site/drive with owner/site/bytes/state
- [x] Handles 302→CSV incl. BOM + LazyQuotes (RawGet follows the redirect; parser mirrors exportjob's)
- [x] Reads `/admin/reportSettings`; warns once when `displayConcealedNames` is true; heuristic fallback (zeroed site_id) when `ReportSettings.Read.All` is absent
- [x] Skip-and-log (not fail) when a report is unavailable — covers sovereign clouds
- [x] Test: metrics carry no owner UPN/site URL/drive id; one log per drive; BOM; concealed + unconcealed paths
- [x] Documented in `docs/signals.md` (derived quota_state, pooled-vs-sum, concealment caveat) + `docs/collectors.md`
- [x] `make check` green

**Deviations from the issue (both least-privilege driven, recorded above):**
- **No `deleted_bytes` series** — absent from the reporting API; only the live facet has it (needs `Sites.Read.All`+`Files.Read.All`).
- **`quota_state` is derived** from used÷allocated (normal <75 / nearing ≥75 / critical ≥90 / exceeded ≥100), not Microsoft's live verdict — documented on the metric and in signals.md.

**Follow-up (optional, needs the broad grant):** an opt-in per-drive live-quota sweep (`/sites/{id}/drive`) would add the authoritative `quota.state` + `deleted_bytes`, at the cost of `Sites.Read.All`+`Files.Read.All`. Left unbuilt to keep the default install least-privilege.

Live camden verify (register + emit real data via the concealment heuristic) pending the `:main` edge build of d40add3 — will confirm on this issue.

## Live-verified on camden (prod, 2026-07-18) ✅

Deployed the `:main` edge image for d40add3 (`version=d40add3` confirmed in the startup log). `m365.storage`:

- enabled, has_run, **runs=1, failures=0, last_success=true, last_error=none**, 11s per run (ran 20:12:24→20:12:35), 6h interval.
- The 11s duration + zero "report unavailable" warnings confirms all four reporting functions fetched and parsed live (302→CSV via `RawGet`).

**Bonus — both concealment states validated end-to-end.** The mapper was built against *concealed* CSV (Site Id zeroed, owner names hashed) captured earlier today. Between capture and this run, report name-concealment was **turned off** on the tenant, so the live run exercised the *unconcealed* path: the collector correctly detected not-concealed (heuristic saw real Site Ids), suppressed the concealment warning, and passed real identity to the twin — e.g. `Owner Principal Name=<upn-2>`, `Site Id=0226dbb8-…`. Real UPNs ship to the log twin by design (#112). (Note: `Site URL` comes back blank for Group/Team-connected sites even unconcealed — a data quirk of those templates, not a mapping bug; `Site Id` carries the identifier.)

#120 complete and closed by d40add3.
