title: Epic/spike: does graph2otel need a real cache layer (Redis sidecar or similar), or is in-process + a persistent volume enough?

body:
Surfaced by the #114 log twin work, but it is a pre-existing cadence question that the twin only makes expensive.

## The numbers

`entra.mfaregistration` polls `GET /reports/authenticationMethods/userRegistrationDetails` — **one record per user** — at `DefaultInterval() = 15 * time.Minute` (`mfaregistration.go:216`).

With the #114 log twin emitting one record per user per cycle (the decided behaviour — the SIEM is the surviving record, so filtering to posture-failures would break correlation), that means:

| tenant size | logs/hour | logs/day |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1,000 users | ~4,000 | ~96,000 |
| 50,000 users | ~200,000 | ~4,800,000 |

Nearly all of it is byte-identical to the previous cycle. MFA registration posture changes when a human enrolls an authenticator — it does not move on a 15-minute clock.

## Why 15 minutes looks wrong independently of the twin

Comparable snapshot collectors over slow-moving, admin/human-timescale state are hourly:

- `purview.sensitivity_labels` / `purview.retention_labels` — `time.Hour` (`labels.go:170`, `:335`)
- `intune.manageddevices` — `time.Hour` (`manageddevices.go:368`), and that one also pages the full collection per cycle

`entra.risk` is also 15 min (`risk.go:101`), but that is defensible — risk state is exactly the thing you want to know about quickly, and the risky population is small by definition. The whole user directory is neither.

This collector also already carries a documented "known scaling limitation" about `collectors.GetAllValues` on a per-user endpoint. A 15-minute cadence makes that four times worse than it needs to be, for freshness nobody asked for.

## Proposal

Raise `DefaultInterval` to `time.Hour`. Cuts both the Graph paging load and the twin volume 4x, with no realistic signal loss. It is a **default** — an operator who genuinely wants 15-minute MFA posture can still set it in config.

Not done as part of #114 because it changes the **metric's** emission cadence too, which is a behaviour change beyond the log-twin scope and deserves its own decision.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Decision: hourly, or keep 15 min and accept the volume
- [ ] If changed: `DefaultInterval` updated, package doc's volume section updated to match (it currently quotes the 15-min numbers)
- [ ] Sanity-check whether any other per-user/per-device snapshot collector has a cadence out of line with how fast its data actually changes
- [ ] `make check` green

comments.body:
Done in adc6df4 (pushed to main). `DefaultInterval` is now `time.Hour`. `make check` green.

Two things the issue got slightly wrong, worth recording:

**The stated rationale was already self-contradicting.** The old `DefaultInterval` comment claimed a longer interval "matches this exporter's other slow-drifting posture collectors (e.g. conditional access, licensing)" — and then returned 15 minutes. So the comment was describing the change this issue makes.

**And the sibling comparison was wrong.** `entra.licensing` and `entra.conditionalaccess` are *also* 15 minutes (`licensing.go:85`, `conditionalaccess.go:116`), so "drifts slowly" never distinguished this collector from them. They are fine at that cadence because they fetch a few dozen bounded rows. The real distinction is **fetch cost**: this is the only Entra posture collector that pages one row per user, with no delta query, so every cycle was a full read of the user directory. The comment now says that instead.

Answering the third acceptance criterion (other cadences out of line with how fast their data changes): no. The survey came back clean — every other collector that pages a full collection is already hourly (`intune.manageddevices`, `purview.labels`). `entra.risk` is 15 min and stays there: risk state is exactly what you want to know about quickly, and the risky population is small by definition. The bounded-fetch collectors at 15 min are cheap and fine.

Package doc volume figures updated to the hourly numbers (~1.2M/day for a 50k-user tenant, down from ~4.8M), with an explicit warning that lowering the interval in config multiplies both log volume and Graph paging load.

title: perf(collectors): entra.mfaregistration polls the whole user directory every 15 min — hourly is the right default

body:
#110 and #111 fixed the two decode-and-drop collectors found by hand. #112 made the log-twin obligation a hard rule. This issue is the **full audit** of the remaining snapshot collectors against that rule.

> **Revised 2026-07-16.** The first version of this body was written from an incomplete hand sweep and **under-reported the problem** — it listed 2 HIGH items and missed 4 more, including the worst one (`entra.roles`). A fuller audit followed; every claim below has been re-verified against the source directly. It also corrects a wrong call in that fuller audit (`entra.domains` — see MEDIUM).

## Method

38 snapshot collectors (`collectors.Register`, excluding the 11 `RegisterWindow` log collectors). Two already emit a log twin (`intune/defenderreport`, `intune/certinventoryreport`). Roughly 20 are pure `$count`/pre-aggregated-report shapes — no per-entity data ever reaches memory, so there is nothing to drop and no twin to emit. Those are correct as-is and out of scope.

The rest are the genuine gap, in **two distinct mechanisms**:

- **Decode-and-drop** — the rows are already on the wire and the fields simply aren't decoded. The twin costs **zero extra Graph calls** (same as #110). This is most of the list.
- **Never-fetched** — identity is excluded at the `$select` level, so it never crosses the wire. Fixing these means widening `$select`, which has a real cost: CLAUDE.md records that `$select=keyCredentials` on a collection GET is throttled to ~150 req/min per tenant, tighter than the general directory ceiling. Weigh per collector; do not blanket-widen.

## The systemic finding

This is not a set of accidents. `entra/signinactivity:12-13` says the per-item detail "belongs in the logs pipeline (M3/M5), **consistent with the credential-expiry collector's decision**", and `intune/malware:15-16` says "see windowsDeviceMalwareStates for the per-device infection log stream, **deferred to M5**". So there is a **lineage of collectors that consciously deferred their log twin to a milestone and never built it**, each citing the last as precedent. The "PII guidance" framing (#112) then made the deferral look like a principled exclusion rather than unfinished work. That is the actual root cause, and it is why this sweep needs finishing rather than sampling.

## HIGH — verified, worth doing

### `entra.roles` (`internal/collectors/entra/roles/roles.go:185`) — worst offender

Pages `GET /directoryRoles/{id}/members` in full, then uses **only `float64(len(members))`** (`:192`). Every Global Admin's identity is already decoded into memory and thrown on the floor.

"Who is in Global Admin, and when did that change" is one of the most classic security questions there is. Zero extra Graph calls — the data is already in the variable. Cheapest fix with the highest value in the whole sweep.

### `entra.consent` (`internal/collectors/entra/consent/consent.go`)

Pages `oauth2PermissionGrants` + `appRoleAssignedTo`, classifies each against a hard-coded high-privilege allowlist, emits only bucketed counts. `oauth2Grant` decodes `Scope` alone — `principalId`/`clientId`/`resourceId` dropped. The package doc itself calls over-privileged consent "a key attack path in Entra tenants"; illicit consent grant is a well-known real-world Entra attack. A count that cannot name the app is an alert you can't action.

**Design nuance — do not twin every grant.** The doc notes `oauth2PermissionGrants` "can run into the tens of thousands in a large tenant", which is exactly why the per-grant *series* was rejected; a log per grant reimports that volume into Loki. The collector **already classifies** each grant, so emit the twin **only for high-privilege classified grants**. Low volume, high signal, directly serves the attack path the collector exists to watch.

### `intune.malware` (`internal/collectors/intune/malware/malware.go:15`)

The per-device `windowsProtectionState` sweep decodes only booleans/status and drops the device id. The package doc self-identifies the gap: *"see windowsDeviceMalwareStates for the per-device infection log stream, deferred to M5"* — deferred, never built. "Which device has malware" is the archetypal SIEM question.

### `entra.credential_expiry` (`internal/collectors/entra/credentialexpiry/credentialexpiry.go:80`)

`type credential struct { EndDateTime string }` — that is the entire decode. `:84-85` states it "deliberately does not decode appId, displayName, id". So the collector knows *"3 credentials expire in 7 days"* and cannot say **which app**, which makes it unactionable for both outage prevention and incident rotation-priority.

### `entra.signin_activity` (`internal/collectors/entra/signinactivity/signinactivity.go:12`) — beta

Pages `servicePrincipalSignInActivities`/`appCredentialSignInActivities`, drops `app_id`/`app_display_name`/`key_id`. Doc explicitly defers the twin to "M3/M5". Stale/dormant service principals and credentials are a real attack surface.

### `entra.mfaregistration` (`internal/collectors/entra/mfaregistration/mfaregistration.go:116`) — never-fetched variant

Pages `userRegistrationDetails` (one record per user) and already decodes `isAdmin`, `isMfaRegistered`, `isMfaCapable`. So it knows *"2 admins are not MFA-registered"* and cannot say **which two** — arguably the most-asked identity-posture question there is.

Two decisions needed:
- UPN/id/displayName are excluded at the **`$select`** level, so this needs a `$select` widening, not just a struct field.
- **Volume:** one log per user per cycle scales with tenant size. Consider emitting only rows failing a posture check (admin without MFA, not MFA-capable) rather than every user.

## MEDIUM — defensible either way

- **`entra.domains`** (`domains.go:45`) — **the fuller audit called this "pure `$count`, not a match"; that is wrong.** It calls `GetAllValues` on `/domains` (`:91`) and decodes only `{AuthenticationType, IsVerified}`, dropping the domain name/id. The list is tiny and bounded (dozens), so this was never a cardinality problem at all — the same over-correction as #111's label names. "Which domain is unverified / federated" is a genuine trust-surface question. Cheap.
- **`intune.manageddevices`** — never-fetched variant; fleet-wide `$select` excludes device id/name/serial/UPN. Note this collector *already* pages the full collection and buckets client-side (the documented exception in CLAUDE.md), so the rows are already flowing. "Which device is non-compliant/unencrypted/stale."
- **`intune.certificates`** (beta) — drops device/user identity + thumbprint. Failed/expiring certs cause auth/VPN/Wi-Fi outages; thumbprint matters for cert-misuse investigation.
- **`intune.appprotection`** (`:129`, `:137`) — `managedAppRegistrations` flagged-reason rollup (rooted/jailbroken detection) drops `userId`/`deviceTag`. "Which user has a rooted device running a managed app" is a real security signal, not inventory.

## LOW — recommend closing as won't-do

- **`entra.agreements`** (`:94`) — drops userId/UPN/displayName/email/deviceId. "Which users haven't accepted the ToU" is a legal/HR/compliance question, not a security signal — it indicates no compromise, misuse, or active threat. It also fails the independence test the HIGH items pass: **Entra retains the acceptance record with its own timestamp as the audit trail of record**, so graph2otel would not be the only place this data lives — unlike credential expiry or malware detections, where our log pipeline is the only surviving per-entity record. Leave it out.
- **`intune.autopilot`** — serial/displayName of Autopilot identities; IT-ops, not IR.
- **`intune.detectedapps`** — fixed common-app allowlist software inventory; no compromise signal.
- **`intune.gpoanalytics`** / **`intune.endpointanalytics`** — migration readiness / device perf-UX scoring; not SIEM-shaped.
- **`intune.compliance`** (`:357`) — the comment is about per-policy metric attribution, not a per-entity drop. Correct as-is.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Decision recorded on `mfaregistration` volume (all users vs posture-failures only) and its `$select` widening
- [ ] Decision recorded on `consent` scoping (confirm: high-privilege classified grants only)
- [ ] Decision recorded on whether the never-fetched items (`mfaregistration`, `manageddevices`) are worth their `$select` cost
- [ ] `entra.roles` log twin — do this one first, it is nearly free
- [ ] `entra.consent` log twin, scoped as decided
- [ ] `intune.malware` log twin
- [ ] `entra.credential_expiry` log twin
- [ ] `entra.signin_activity` log twin
- [ ] `entra.mfaregistration` log twin, scoped as decided
- [ ] MEDIUM items each either done or explicitly deferred with a reason
- [ ] LOW items closed as won't-do in a comment so a future sweep does not re-litigate them
- [ ] Every fix keeps its existing metric byte-for-byte unchanged, pinned by a test
- [ ] Every "deferred to M3/M5" comment in a collector package doc is either resolved or removed — no collector should still cite a milestone that has passed
- [ ] `docs/pii-cardinality-audit.md` records that the both-directions sweep is complete
- [ ] `make check` green

comments.body:
Body revised — the original was written from an incomplete hand sweep and **under-reported the problem**: 2 HIGH items listed, 4 missed, including the worst one.

What changed:

- **`entra.roles` added as the top item, and it is the worst of the lot.** It pages `/directoryRoles/{id}/members` in full and then uses only `float64(len(members))` (`roles.go:192`). Every Global Admin identity is already decoded into memory and discarded. Zero extra Graph calls to fix; "who is in Global Admin" is about as classic as security questions get. Missed it entirely first time round.
- **`intune.malware`, `entra.credential_expiry`, `entra.signin_activity` added as HIGH** — all verified against source, not taken on trust.
- **`entra.domains` kept at MEDIUM.** A second audit called it "pure `$count`, not a match"; that is wrong — it calls `GetAllValues` on `/domains` (`:91`) and decodes only `{AuthenticationType, IsVerified}`. Verified directly.
- **`entra.agreements` confirmed LOW / won't-do**, on a better argument than I had: Entra retains the ToU acceptance record with its own timestamp as the audit trail of record, so graph2otel would not be the only place that data lives — unlike credential expiry or malware, where our log pipeline is the only surviving per-entity record. That independence test is a good general filter for the rest of this sweep.

**The systemic finding, which is the real point of this issue:** these are not accidents. `signinactivity.go:12-13` defers the twin to "M3/M5" *"consistent with the credential-expiry collector's decision"*, and `malware.go:15-16` defers to `windowsDeviceMalwareStates` "deferred to M5". There is a lineage of collectors that consciously deferred their log twin to a milestone and never built it, each citing the last as precedent — and the "PII guidance" framing (#112) then made that unfinished work look like a principled exclusion. Hence the new acceptance criterion: no collector should still cite a milestone that has passed.

## Decisions recorded — unblocking implementation

Maintainer: fix all HIGH + MEDIUM; LOW stays won't-do.

**On the independence test:** dropped as a discriminator. The observation that "Entra retains the record" applies to essentially every signal here — security.microsoft.com holds the data longer-term regardless — so it does not separate the HIGH items from `agreements`. The reason `agreements` stays out is simply that ToU acceptance **is not a security signal**: it indicates no compromise, misuse, or active threat. Retention was never the real argument.

**Confirmed: graph2otel's log pipeline is the surviving SIEM record.** That is the design premise for every twin below.

### Scoping decisions

1. **`consent` — high-privilege classified grants only.** The collector already classifies each grant against its allowlist. Twinning all grants would reimport into Loki the exact tens-of-thousands volume problem that got the per-grant *series* rejected. Low volume, high signal.
2. **`mfaregistration` / `manageddevices` — twin EVERY row, not just posture-failures.** Since the log pipeline is the surviving record, filtering to "problem rows only" would break the correlation a SIEM exists to do ("was device X enrolled on date Y", "did this user have MFA last month"). Volume scales with tenant size x interval; both already page the full collection, and both package docs will state the volume characteristic explicitly so an operator knows what they are signing up for.
3. **`mfaregistration` / `manageddevices` `$select` widening accepted.** Watch the ~150 req/min `keyCredentials` ceiling noted in CLAUDE.md — it applies to credential `$select` on collection GETs, not these, but re-verify live.

### Frozen seam — all lanes code against this

Reference implementation: `entra/risk` (2c57fdd) and `purview/labels` (f4ed32c).

- Emit via `e.LogEvent(telemetry.Event{Name, Body, Severity, Attrs})` from the **existing** fetch — no new Graph calls.
- Event names are **consts**, referenced by both the emit site and the tests.
- A `setStr(attrs, key, val)` helper omits empty values — absent fields emit no attribute, never `""`.
- All log attrs are **string**-typed (house convention; Loki structured metadata is string on the wire).
- `Timestamp` left **zero** (= poll time) for state feeds — these re-emit each cycle, and stamping with a source timestamp would pile repeats onto one instant.
- Existing metrics stay **byte-for-byte unchanged**, pinned by a test asserting no per-entity attr reaches a metric point.
- Any skip/unavailable path **short-circuits before** the twin — a skipped tenant emits zero logs, not empty ones.

### Frozen event names

| collector | event name |
| --- | --- |
| `entra.roles` | `entra.role_member` |
| `entra.consent` | `entra.consent_grant` |
| `entra.credential_expiry` | `entra.app_credential` |
| `entra.signin_activity` | `entra.app_signin_activity` |
| `entra.mfaregistration` | `entra.user_registration` |
| `entra.domains` | `entra.domain` |
| `intune.malware` | `intune.device_malware_state` |
| `intune.manageddevices` | `intune.managed_device` |
| `intune.certificates` | `intune.device_certificate` |
| `intune.appprotection` | `intune.app_registration` |

Done — sweep complete. b0b75ac (6 Entra) + 4b331b6 (4 Intune) + f4f38ab (exceptions + audit doc), all pushed to main. `make check` green: vet, `-race` tests, 0 lint issues, 0 vulnerabilities.

## Ten collectors twinned

`entra.roles`, `entra.consent`, `entra.credential_expiry`, `entra.signin_activity`, `entra.mfaregistration`, `entra.domains`, `intune.malware`, `intune.manageddevices`, `intune.certificates`, `intune.appprotection` — plus `entra.risk` (#110) and the two Purview label collectors (#111) = twelve total. All 38 snapshot collectors are now accounted for in `docs/pii-cardinality-audit.md`.

**The frozen seam held across six parallel lanes:** all ten event names match the table exactly, and **not one `Gauge`/`GaugeSnapshot`/`Counter` call was touched** in any commit — verified by diffing for metric emit calls, not just by trusting the tests.

## Things found during the work that were not in the plan

- **`entra.roles` was worse than recorded.** The PIM half never decoded `principalId` either, despite it being right there in the response — so "who is ELIGIBLE for Global Admin" was as unanswerable as the standing side. Both halves twinned, discriminated by `assignment_type`.
- **`intune.appprotection` was half-fixed on the first pass** — it twinned `userId`/`deviceTag` but kept dropping `packageId`/`bundleId`, leaving it able to say which user had a rooted device but not which app. Sent back and completed; a tenant's managed-app set is dozens of admin-configured rows, so it was never a cardinality problem either.
- **`entra.credential_expiry` got the secrets call right unprompted** — decodes neither `keyCredential.key` nor `passwordCredential.secretText`, keeps `customKeyIdentifier` (the thumbprint, which is the useful part), and widened `$select` by only `id,appId,displayName` while citing the ~150 req/min ceiling.
- **The two exceptions were still citing the rule #112 rewrote.** `agreements` and `endpointanalytics` justified their drops with "see CLAUDE.md's cardinality/PII rule", which now says the opposite. Both package docs rewritten to state the real reason and mark them audited, so the next sweep neither re-litigates them nor "fixes" them into existence.

## Follow-up filed

**#115** — `entra.mfaregistration` polls the whole user directory every 15 min (`DefaultInterval`, `:216`). With the decided per-user twin that is ~200k logs/hour for a 50k-user tenant, nearly all byte-identical cycle to cycle. Comparable slow-moving collectors are hourly. Not changed here because it also alters the metric's cadence — that deserves its own decision.

## Deferred by decision, recorded so they are not re-litigated

`entra.agreements` (compliance, not security), `intune.endpointanalytics` (ops, not security), `intune.autopilot`, `intune.detectedapps`, `intune.gpoanalytics`. `intune.compliance`'s comment was about per-policy metric attribution, not a per-entity drop — correct as-is.

title: fix(collectors): finish the log-twin sweep — 6 collectors drop the detail that makes them actionable

body:
Found while adding the #110 log twin — my first assertion compared the two scales and failed with `severity = 13, want Warn (1)`, which surfaced this.

## The two scales

- `telemetry.Severity` (internal enum, `internal/telemetry/types.go:24`): `SeverityInfo=0, SeverityWarn=1, SeverityError=2`
- `telemetrytest.LogRecord.Severity` (`internal/telemetrytest/recorder.go:45`): the **OTEL wire value** — `INFO=9, WARN=13, ERROR=17` — assigned at `:232` via `int(rec.Severity())`

Same word, same `int` type, silently different scales. Nothing catches a mix-up at compile time.

## The live bug

`internal/collectors/intune/certinventoryreport/certinventoryreport_test.go:240`:

```go
if logs[0].Severity < int(telemetry.SeverityWarn) {
    t.Errorf("revoked certificate log severity = %+v, want WARN", logs[0])
}
```

This evaluates `13 < 1` → false. It also evaluates `9 < 1` → false for an INFO record. **The assertion can never fail**, so the "revoked certs are WARN" guarantee is untested — the collector could regress to INFO and CI would stay green.

## Approach

The sound idiom already exists and should be the house rule: drive the mapper directly and compare `telemetry.Event.Severity` against `telemetry.Severity`, as `entra/securityalerts` and `entra/securityincidents` do (`ev.Severity != telemetry.SeverityError`). The `entra/risk` test `TestLogTwinSeverityTracksRiskLevel` (added in #110) follows it.

Where an assertion genuinely needs the recorded record rather than the mapper, compare `LogRecord.SeverityText` (`"WARN"`) — unambiguous, no scale to confuse.

Prefer making the mix-up impossible over documenting it. Options, cheapest first:

1. Give `telemetrytest.LogRecord` a typed accessor, or store `telemetry.Severity` alongside the wire value, so the two cannot be compared by accident.
2. Failing that, rename the field to `SeverityNumber` (matching OTEL vocabulary) so `x.SeverityNumber < telemetry.SeverityWarn` reads as obviously wrong.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `certinventoryreport_test.go:240` asserts revoked-cert severity in a way that actually fails when severity regresses — verified by temporarily breaking the collector and watching it go red
- [ ] Sweep every other `_test.go` comparing `LogRecord.Severity` against a `telemetry.Severity` constant; fix each
- [ ] The scale confusion is designed out (typed accessor or rename), not just commented
- [ ] `make check` green

comments.body:
Done in f8e29e3 (pushed to main). `make check` green.

**Designed out rather than patched.** `LogRecord.Severity` is now `SeverityNumber`, typed `log.Severity` instead of `int`, so comparing it against a `telemetry.Severity` no longer compiles. That paid off immediately: the rename let the **compiler** find every affected site in the tree, which both did the sweep for me and confirmed `certinventoryreport_test.go:240` was the only real instance — `manageddevices` already used `SeverityText`, and `signinactivity` had spotted the trap and documented it inline while avoiding it.

**The fix is verified, not asserted.** With the collector's escalation temporarily removed the fixed assertion goes red; restored, green. The old form stayed green through that same regression — which is the whole bug.

**Added the negative case.** `TestCollectDoesNotEscalateSeverityForHealthy`. Without it, a collector that marked *every* certificate WARN would still pass. The old assertion was vacuous in both directions, and only fixing the positive half would have left the weaker gap.

Also swept `autopilotevents_test.go`, which compared `telemetry.Event.Severity` against bare `2`/`0` — correct scale, but raw numbers are exactly the habit that produced this bug, so they use the named constants now.

title: test: LogRecord.Severity vs telemetry.Severity are different scales — one assertion is vacuous, the API is a footgun

body:
The rule is mis-sold in every doc that states it, and the framing has already caused real damage: it produced two collectors that drop useful data on the floor (#110, #111) and it reads to a maintainer as "graph2otel withholds PII from your backend", which is **false**.

## What the rule actually is

graph2otel exports PII by design. `SECURITY.md` enumerates it: UPNs, user object IDs, device names, serials, IMEIs, sign-in IPs and geo, group/role membership, cert thumbprints. Eleven WindowCollectors exist to do exactly that. `unifiedaudit.go:20` says it outright — "these are LOGS, so per-entity detail ... belongs here".

The actual rule is narrower and has nothing to do with privacy:

- **metrics carry aggregates; logs carry entities.**

It is justified by cost and queryability, not confidentiality. Grafana Cloud bills metrics on active series, so a per-UPN series in a 10k-user tenant is 10k series per metric (hence the active-series cap, #105). Series keyed by a sign-in or correlation id have exactly one sample each — the pathological case for a TSDB. And a metric label buys nothing a LogQL `count by` over data we already ship does not.

Calling this "Cardinality & PII guidance" invites exactly the wrong reading: that the boundary is protecting privacy and could be relaxed for a SIEM use case. It cannot be relaxed, and it was never about privacy.

## The missing half — the log-twin principle

The docs state where data must NOT go and never state where it MUST go. That omission is what licensed the drops in #110/#111. The rule needs both halves:

> Per-entity data too high-cardinality for a metric label MUST still be emitted as a **log** — never dropped. "Not a metric label" means "log twin", not "silently discarded".

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `CLAUDE.md` "Cardinality & PII guidance" reframed: data-modeling rule, cost/queryability rationale, log-twin obligation stated as a hard rule
- [ ] `SECURITY.md` "The cardinality boundary rule" likewise; keep the exposure inventory (it is accurate and useful) but stop implying the boundary is a privacy control
- [ ] The genuine content redactions stay clearly separated and keep their real justification — **secrets**, not PII: `auditevents` never emits `modifiedProperties` old/new values because they carry credentials/certs
- [ ] `docs/signals.md` states the metrics-vs-logs split so a user knows which pipeline answers "which user?"
- [ ] `docs/pii-cardinality-audit.md` reconciled with the reframing
- [ ] No collector package doc still cites a "PII" justification for dropping non-PII bounded data

comments.body:
Done in c546147 (pushed to main).

Reframed across `CLAUDE.md`, `SECURITY.md`, `docs/security.md`, `docs/signals.md` and `docs/pii-cardinality-audit.md`. Each now leads with the rule being a data-modeling rule rather than a privacy control, gives the real justification (active-series billing; a correlation-ID series receives exactly one sample; a LogQL `count by` answers the same question off data already shipped), and states the log-twin obligation as a hard rule with `entra/risk` as the reference shape.

`intune/auditevents` package doc rewritten so the one genuine content exclusion carries its real justification — **secrets, not PII**. It now says explicitly that the collector emits actor UPN/id/IP by design, so PII was never the reason those `modifiedProperties` values are dropped, and adds a do-not-"fix"-this note: no SIEM framing justifies shipping a private key to a log backend.

`docs/pii-cardinality-audit.md` records why its original pass missed both bugs — it verified only that nothing leaked *onto* a metric, never that fetched per-entity data reached a pipeline at all. A future pass must check both directions.

Two things worth noting:

- `docs/security.md` is a hand-maintained twin of `SECURITY.md`, not generated, so it needed the same edit — easy to miss.
- The `signals.md` heading was left as `## Cardinality shape` on purpose; renaming it would have dead-linked `security.md:55`. The new framing went into the body instead.

title: docs: the cardinality rule is a data-modeling rule, not a PII exclusion — reframe it and state the log-twin principle

body:
Both Purview label collectors count the catalog but never say **which** labels exist. `purview.labels.count{applicable_to="email"} = 3` cannot tell you whether those three are Public/Internal/Confidential or three flavours of Highly Confidential — so the metric is close to unactionable on its own.

`sensitivityLabel` (`internal/collectors/purview/labels/labels.go:104`) decodes only `ApplicableTo`; `retentionLabel` (`:236`) only three enums. Both comments justify the drop with "they are PII-shaped and must never become metric labels (CLAUDE.md cardinality/PII rule)".

Two things wrong with that:

1. **A sensitivity label name is not PII.** "Confidential" is a tenant-wide policy name, not per-entity data. The `PII-shaped` framing is wrong on the facts.
2. **The metric-label half of the reasoning is right, but the drop does not follow.** The package doc already makes the correct argument against a per-label series (see the `priority` note at `:35` — one series per label, each value == 1, cardinality growing with the catalog, no aggregation value). That argument holds for names too. But "not a metric label" does not imply "not emitted anywhere" — it implies **log twin**.

## Approach

Same shape as #110: emit the catalog as logs from the existing fetch, keep every gauge exactly as-is.

- `purview.sensitivity_label` — one log per label (id, name, priority, applicable_to, description)
- `purview.retention_label` — one log per label (id, name, the three retention enums, descriptions)
- `purview.retention_event_type` — one log per event type (id, name, description); this collector currently emits a bare count and decodes nothing at all (`:345`)

Catalogs drift slowly and the collectors already poll hourly, so the volume is trivial.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All three catalogs emit a per-row log event
- [ ] Every existing gauge unchanged, including the deliberate `priority` / per-label-series exclusion — a test asserts no label name/id reached a metric point
- [ ] `isUnavailable` skip-and-log path still short-circuits before any log twin is emitted (a 403 tenant emits nothing, not empty logs)
- [ ] Package doc corrected: drop the "PII-shaped" claim for label names, state the log-twin split
- [ ] `make check` green

comments.body:
Done in f4ed32c (pushed to main).

All three catalogs now emit a per-row log twin from the existing fetch: `purview.sensitivity_label`, `purview.retention_label`, `purview.retention_event_type` (that last one previously decoded nothing at all and emitted only a bare count). Event names are consts, referenced from both the emit sites and the tests, so a rename cannot silently desync them.

Every gauge is byte-for-byte unchanged — same names, units, descriptions, attribute sets. `priority` stays off the metric (the one-series-per-label argument in the package doc is sound and still holds) and appears only in the log twin.

Both critical constraints are pinned by tests: `TestSensitivityNoPIIInLabels` / `TestRetentionNoPIIInLabels` allow only the bounded dims on metric points, and the `isUnavailable` short-circuit is asserted to emit **zero** log records — a 403 tenant emits nothing rather than empty rows. The live-verified `TestRetentionDataInsightsForbiddenIsSkipped` and `TestRetentionEventTypesFailureDoesNotBlockLabels` were left intact.

`make check` green (0 lint issues, 0 vulnerabilities).

title: fix(collectors): purview label collectors drop the label catalog with no log twin

body:
The `entra.risk` snapshot collector answers "how much risk is live" but not "**who**" — the single question an analyst actually asks. For a SIEM-shaped deployment that is a real hole.

`riskyEntity` (`internal/collectors/entra/risk/risk.go:88`) decodes only `RiskLevel` + `RiskState`. Its comment says every other field — `id`, `userPrincipalName`, `appId`, `displayName` — is "per-entity/PII and deliberately never decoded here". That reasoning is half right: those fields must never become **metric labels**, but dropping them entirely means they reach no pipeline at all. `entra.riskdetections` does not cover this: it is the detection *event* stream, a different endpoint from current risky-user *state*.

## Approach

Emit a **log twin** from the existing fetch. `collectHalf` already pages the whole collection, so this costs zero extra Graph calls, and `telemetry.Emitter` already exposes `LogEvent` (`internal/telemetry/types.go:96`) — a SnapshotCollector can emit both.

Deliberately NOT a WindowCollector: riskyUsers is point-in-time **state**, not an append-only event stream, so a watermark/checkpoint is the wrong shape. Re-emit the current risky set each cycle so "who was risky at 14:00" is answerable from the logs.

- Keep `entra.risky_users.total` / `entra.risky_service_principals.total` exactly as they are — bounded by `risk_level` x `risk_state`. No new metric label.
- Add log events `entra.risky_user` and `entra.risky_service_principal` carrying the per-entity detail as structured attributes.
- Severity tracks risk level (high -> Warn) so the stream is filterable without a query gymnastics.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `riskyEntity` decodes the per-entity fields (id, UPN/appId, displayName, riskLevel, riskState, riskDetail, riskLastUpdatedDateTime)
- [ ] One `entra.risky_user` log per risky user; one `entra.risky_service_principal` log per risky SP
- [ ] Existing gauges unchanged — a test asserts no per-entity attribute leaked onto a metric point
- [ ] Absent fields omitted rather than emitted as empty strings
- [ ] Both halves stay independently license-gated and degrade as they do today
- [ ] Package doc rewritten: it currently states the drop as intentional
- [ ] `make check` green

comments.body:
Done in 2c57fdd (pushed to main).

Both halves now emit the bounded gauge **and** one log per risky entity from the same paged fetch — zero extra Graph calls. Field names verified against the Graph `riskyUser`/`riskyServicePrincipal` resource docs rather than guessed.

Two design calls worth recording, both deliberate:

- **Timestamp left zero (= poll time)**, not set to `riskLastUpdatedDateTime`. This is a state feed, re-emitted each cycle while an entity stays risky; stamping it with the assessment time would pile every repeat onto one instant and make "who was risky at 14:00" unanswerable. The assessment time survives as the `risk_last_updated` attribute.
- **Only `risk_level=high` escalates to Warn.** medium/low are routine background on a real tenant; warning on them would make the severity dimension useless for filtering.

Not a WindowCollector, as planned — riskyUsers is point-in-time state, so a watermark/checkpoint would be the wrong shape.

Tests added: `TestCollectEmitsRiskyUserLogTwin`, `TestCollectEmitsRiskyServicePrincipalLogTwin`, `TestLogTwinOmitsAbsentAttrs`, `TestUnlicensedHalfEmitsNoLogTwin`, `TestLogTwinSeverityTracksRiskLevel`. The metric boundary stays pinned by the pre-existing `TestCollectNoPerEntitySeries`. `make check` green (0 lint issues, 0 vulnerabilities).

Spun out of this work: #113 — the severity assertion idiom used in `certinventoryreport_test.go` compares two different scales and can never fail.

title: fix(collectors): entra.risk drops the risky-entity detail with no log twin

body:
## Summary

The 2026-07-16 live-verify + camden redeploy pass (scopes `AuditLogsQuery.Read.All` / `InformationProtectionPolicy.Read.All` / `RecordsManagement.Read.All` granted to `graph2otel-poller`) surfaced three real defects in the collectors closed under #92 / #97 / #101. All confirmed against the live m7kni tenant with a **fresh** poller token that provably carries the new scopes (so none of this is scope-replication lag).

## Findings (live, fresh-token)

**1. `entra.security_incidents` (#92) — `/security/incidents` caps `$top` at 50.**
`GET /security/incidents?$top=1000` → HTTP 400 `"The limit of '50' for Top query has been exceeded. The value from the incoming request is '1000'."` The logpipeline engine defaults `PageSize` to 1000, so the collector fails every cycle. `?$top=50` → **200 with real data** (live incident id `14`, active). Fix: `EndpointConfig.PageSize = 50`. (Same class as the documented IPC `riskDetections` `$top`=500 cap.)

**2. `m365.unified_audit` (#97) — the audit query API is beta-only on this tenant.**
`POST /v1.0/security/auditLog/queries` → HTTP 404 `UnknownError` (empty message), even with a fresh token carrying `AuditLogsQuery.Read.All`. `POST /beta/security/auditLog/queries` → **201 Created** (returns a query id). Graph's own docs list the endpoint under v1.0, but this tenant only serves it on `/beta` — same beta-only reality as the `signInEventTypes` filter. Fix: set `QueryConfig.BaseURLOverride` to the beta root (collector is already `Experimental`, correct).

**3. `purview.retention_labels` (#101) — app-only data-plane Forbidden, and it errors instead of skipping.**
`GET /security/labels/retentionLabels` and `/security/triggerTypes/retentionEventTypes` → HTTP **500** `DataInsightsRequestError: "DataInsights command(GET) FAILED - Forbidden"` (Exchange Online compliance backend), on **both** v1.0 and beta, with the scope present in the token. This is an app-only limitation (retention data flows through the Exchange compliance data-plane, which blocks the app identity), not a bug we can fix — but the collector currently surfaces it as a `WARN "collector failed"` because `isUnavailable()` only matches `status 403/404`. Fix: treat the specific `DataInsightsRequestError` + `Forbidden` 500 signature as skip-and-log (graceful), staying precise so genuine 500s still surface. Document as a permanent app-only gap.

**4. `purview.sensitivity_labels` (#101) — no app-only endpoint on this tenant (already degrades gracefully).**
`/security/dataSecurityAndGovernance/sensitivityLabels` → 403 `InsufficientGraphPermissions`; every alternate (`/informationProtection/policy/labels`, `/security/informationProtection/sensitivityLabels`, `/informationProtection/sensitivityLabels`, their `/beta` forms) → 400/403 app-only. The collector already skips on 403 (correct). No code change; document the gap.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `entra.security_incidents` sets `PageSize = 50`; live cycle returns 200 + data
- [ ] `m365.unified_audit` targets `/beta`; live create returns 201 and records page
- [ ] `purview.retention_labels` treats the DataInsights `Forbidden` 500 as a graceful skip (no `WARN failed`), genuine 500s still surface
- [ ] CLAUDE.md gotchas added: `/security/incidents` `$top`<=50; auditLogQuery beta-only; purview sensitivity/retention app-only-Forbidden
- [ ] `make check` green; camden redeployed and re-verified

Found on the live camden deployment. Part of #79 / #86.

comments.body:
## Live-verified on camden (2026-07-16, image 5eef26d)

Redeployed camden on the fixed `:main` (07:35Z) and confirmed via `/api/status.json` — every previously-failing collector now reports `last_success=true`, 0 failures:

| collector | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `entra.security_incidents` | 400 `$top=1000` every cycle | ✅ `last_success=true`, runs=1, failures=0 |
| `m365.unified_audit` | 404 on `/v1.0` create | ✅ `last_success=true` (async create→poll→page on `/beta` completed) |
| `purview.retention_labels` | `WARN collector failed` (500) | ✅ `last_success=true` — now `INFO ... skipping` (graceful) |
| `purview.sensitivity_labels` | 403 skip (already fine) | ✅ `last_success=true` |

The camden logs carry no `top=1000` / `status 404` / `limit of '50'` errors post-redeploy; purview retention now logs `INFO "retention labels endpoint unavailable on this tenant; skipping"` instead of erroring. (Row emission for incidents/audit is tenant-data-dependent — the fix verified here is that all four collectors run to success instead of failing every cycle.)

## Authoritative state (2026-07-17, #146) — one of the four findings was overturned

Findings 1–3 **stand**: `/security/incidents` `$top=50`; the M365 audit query API beta-only on this tenant; the retention-label `DataInsightsRequestError`+Forbidden graceful skip.

Finding 4's **sensitivity-label half was WRONG** — *"no app-only endpoint on this tenant / document the gap"* was a **missing scope, not a product limitation**. Overturned in #126 (live-verified 2026-07-16 under the poller's own cert): granting `SensitivityLabel.Read` makes `GET /security/dataSecurityAndGovernance/sensitivityLabels` return 200 with the full tenant catalog; the collector was rebuilt on it. The retention-label half of finding 4 stands (Application: Not supported).

The lesson, now in #79's operating rules: this issue probed the right endpoint holding a *similarly-named* permission (`InformationProtectionPolicy.Read.All`) and blamed the endpoint. Before declaring an app-only gap, confirm the app holds the endpoint's **documented** Application permission, and probe as `graph2otel-poller`.

title: Live-verify fixes: security_incidents $top=50, m365 audit beta-only, purview app-only degradation

body:
## Problem

The msgraph-heavy dependency tree makes goreleaser cross-compilation slow. It surfaces in two places:

- **`goreleaser-snapshot` in `ci.yml`** — runs on **every push/PR** (required check), cross-compiles all 5 targets with `-p 1` and `cache: false`. Cold full compile of the giant tree, 5× serial. This is the recurring cost.
- **`binaries` in `release-please.yml`** — only on real releases (`-p 1`, `--skip=docker`).

Context worth recording: the edge `:main` image path does **not** use goreleaser — it builds from the repo-root `Dockerfile` via `container-publish.yml` (native amd64+arm64 matrix). goreleaser only produces release *download* binaries. So this is about CI-per-push cost and release-binary cost, not edge image speed.

Why we're the outlier: tailscale2otel uses the same 5-target matrix fully parallel with no `-p 1` — it has no msgraph. Our tree OOMs the runner at 5-way parallel, hence `-p 1` (commit 30e38ba), which is now slow.

## Plan (all repo-owned, no shared-actions divergence)

Runtime is Docker/Linux; darwin is only for Apple-Silicon local dev.

- [ ] **Trim the matrix** in `.goreleaser.yaml`: 5 → 3 targets — `linux/amd64`, `linux/arm64`, `darwin/arm64`. Drop windows entirely and Intel-Mac (`darwin/amd64` — build locally). Remove the now-dead windows `format_overrides`.
- [ ] **Enable Go build cache** in the `ci.yml` snapshot job (`cache: false` → `true`) — the msgraph tree compiles once and restores on every subsequent push instead of a cold full build.
- [ ] **Relax `-p 1` → `-p 2`** in both the ci snapshot job and the release-please `binaries` `goreleaser-args` — 3 targets at 2-way concurrency fits memory (far below the 5-way that OOM'd) and roughly halves the serial cost.
- [ ] `make check` green + `goreleaser check` + a snapshot build proving 3 targets.

## Follow-up (out of scope — shared repo)

The shared `rknightion/.github` `binaries.yml` reusable hardcodes `cache: false`, so release builds won't get cross-run caching. Flipping that to `true` would benefit every rknightion Go repo — worth a separate shared-repo PR.

comments.body:
Reopening — the `-p 2` change from the first commit (2b516ae) still OOM-kills the 7 GB standard runner on the msgraph-heavy linker (confirmed on the live run). Course-correcting.

**Root cause:** standard `ubuntu-latest` is 2-core / **7 GB**. The msgraph linker peaks ~3-4 GB per target, so two concurrent builds (`-p 2`) exceed 7 GB → OOM. Larger GitHub runners would fix it but are **billed even on public repos** (~$0.016/min for 4-core) — not free.

**Fix (free, no runner change):** add a ~12 GB swapfile in a pre-step so the linker spills to SSD instead of getting OOM-killed. This makes the build robust at any `-p` / matrix size on the free standard runner.

- [ ] Add swap step to the `goreleaser-snapshot` job in `ci.yml` (I own that workflow).
- [ ] Inject the same swap setup into the release `binaries` job via the shared reusable's existing `pre-cmd` input (chained with the syft/go-licenses installs) — no shared-repo change.
- [ ] **Restore the full 5-target matrix** in `.goreleaser.yaml` (linux/darwin/windows × amd64/arm64, minus windows/arm64) + the windows zip `format_overrides`. Swap makes "cross-compile everything" OOM-safe.
- [ ] Keep `cache: true` and `-p 2`; `make check` + `goreleaser check` + full-matrix snapshot build green.

✅ Verified fixed. The `goreleaser-snapshot` job **succeeded** on the run carrying this change (main @ `519c002`, which includes commit `2a8c833`): the swap step provisioned 12 GiB, and the full 5-target matrix cross-compiled at `-p 2` with **no OOM**.

- Duration: **10m33s** — but this was the **cold-cache** first run (`cache: true` had nothing to restore yet). It's now populated, so subsequent pushes only recompile changed packages instead of the whole msgraph tree ×5, which should cut this substantially.
- If the warm-cache time is still too slow, the remaining levers are `-p 1` (swap-safe, slower) or a paid 4-core runner (~$0.016/min).

title: ci: speed up goreleaser cross-compile (trim matrix, cache, relax -p)

body:
> Body updated 2026-07-17 (#146): the transport question this body used to end on is **decided and built** — the earlier "poll vs pub/sub" analysis moved to background, and the final comment's "do not start the consumer yet" instruction is void (its unblock condition fired: #89 closed with the consumer live in production).

## Mission

Ingest the **full Microsoft Defender advanced-hunting table set** so Loki can serve as the SIEM for endpoint hunting and file-scan telemetry, replacing Sentinel for that workload. Child of #86.

**Status: greenlit for v1** (maintainer decision, 2026-07-16). Config-gated, full table set — *"no point going half in"*.

## Transport — DECIDED: Defender streaming API → the shared Azure Storage account

- #89 closed with **Storage** as the fallback transport; `internal/blobpipeline` (byte-offset engine) is built and live in production reading the Entra categories. See `docs/blob-ingest.md` before touching anything here.
- Defender's streaming API targets the **same storage account** (`graph2otelm7kni`, RG `auditlogs`, uksouth) — a new container set alongside the Entra ones. Marginal infra cost ~£0.
- Streaming is push: it consumes **none** of the tenant-wide advanced-hunting CPU quota shared with the security team's portal queries — the property that killed the polling design (a polling exporter can 429 a human mid-investigation).
- For the record, not to be re-litigated: the streaming API cannot target Log Analytics (Event Hub or Storage only), and per #89's final design the consumer is **read-only** — the `delete-after-7d` lifecycle rule owns retention, the consumer never deletes.

## Scope — the full table set, plus #93's

#93 (`AlertInfo`/`AlertEvidence`) was closed as redundant and absorbed here. `entra.security_alerts` covers the alert *layer* (proven — `g2o-defender-crit` runs on it) but emits only `evidence_count`; evidence detail is a projection of the raw tables, so it belongs here.

Tables in scope (all confirmed queryable live 2026-07-16 under `ThreatHunting.Read.All`; the streaming API ships the same tables):

- `DeviceFileEvents`, `DeviceProcessEvents`, `DeviceNetworkEvents`, `DeviceLogonEvents`
- `IdentityLogonEvents`, `EmailEvents`, `CloudAppEvents`, `UrlClickEvents`
- `AlertInfo`, `AlertEvidence` (absorbed from #93 — the joined alert→evidence view)

## What remains (the actual work)

1. **Enable the Defender streaming-API export** to the storage account for the table set (tenant mutation — needs maintainer approval; name the exact settings first).
2. **Verify the Defender blob layout on real data** before freezing anything — Defender's layout will differ from Entra's (`tenantId=` prefix was itself undocumented, #89), and CLAUDE.md's blob rules say envelopes must be verified per category family, never assumed.
3. **Per-table mappers + collectors** registered via `RegisterBlob`, reusing `blobpipeline` unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Streaming export enabled for the full table list; settings recorded here
- [ ] Blob layout + envelope types verified against live samples per category before mapping (string-vs-int traps, `time` vs event-time binding — CLAUDE.md blob rules)
- [ ] Full table set ingested, config-gated + `Experimental()` — off by default, per-table enable
- [ ] Per-entity detail lands as **log attributes**, never metric labels (#112); any bounded aggregate gets its log twin (#114)
- [ ] Volume documented honestly in the package doc — one endpoint alone emitted 3,003 `FileDeleted` events in 24h via endpoint-DLP (#98)
- [ ] Live-verified against m7kni before close
- [ ] `make check` green

## Constraints

- **Never emit file content or key material.** Hashes (`SHA1`/`SHA256`/`MD5`), paths and URLs are the point and are fine; do not widen into content.
- Highest-volume surface graph2otel would ever touch: the honest v1 story is "config-gated, off by default, here is what it costs".

## Answering "what did you mean by cost — processing or actual $$?"

Fair challenge: I was sloppy. I meant **Loki ingest volume**, which you told me to exclude. Stripped of that, here is the honest answer — and **it is not dollars**.

`POST /security/runHuntingQuery` has **no per-query charge**; it is included with the Defender licence. The binding constraint is a **tenant-wide CPU quota**, verified against [the API docs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-xdr/api-advanced-hunting):

- 30-day lookback only; 100,000-row cap per query; 3-minute query timeout
- ~45+ calls/min per tenant (varies with tenant size)

An exporter that degrades the tool it exists to feed is a bad trade, and no Loki-side tuning fixes it.

**Which makes your pub/sub instinct probably right.** Defender's streaming API pushes the same tables to Event Hub: **no hunting CPU quota consumed at all**, no 30-day ceiling, no 100k cap, no 429-the-analyst failure mode. ### The two standouts

- **`alertinfo` → turn off; `alertevidence` → build.** `alertinfo`'s fields (`AlertId/Title/Category/Severity/ServiceSource/DetectionSource/AttackTechniques`) are a strict subset of what `entra.security_alerts` (`/security/alerts_v2`) already emits — building it duplicates the alert layer over a second transport for zero new fields. `alertevidence` is the opposite: it is exactly the per-entity evidence (`EntityType` User/Ip/CloudLogonSession/CloudLogonRequest, real UPN/`AccountObjectId`/IP/geo/session detail) that `securityalerts.go:122-124` deliberately collapses to a bare `evidence_count`. - **`cloudappevents` — HOLD, do not build as-is.** All 20 sampled records are one macOS endpoint (`MBP16`) repeatedly deleting its own Spotlight index cache (`ActionType=FileDeleted`, `RawEventData.Application=spotlightknowledged.updater`, an `~/Library/Metadata/CoreSpotlight/…` path) surfaced through Defender's Endpoint→MCAS connector — zero security signal in the sample. Still: `cloudappevents` needs an `ActionType`/`Workload` allow-list and a wider multi-hour sample before it earns a mapper. 2. **High-value + high-volume** (the EDR payload the ingest exists for; config-gated + `Experimental`, off by default, per-table enable per AC): `deviceprocessevents`, `devicefileevents`, `devicenetworkevents`, `deviceevents`.
3. **Deferred companions** (build alongside a parent, not standalone): `devicenetworkinfo`, `devicefilecertificateinfo`, `emailurlinfo`, `emailattachmentinfo`, `identitylogonevents`, `deviceimageloadevents`, `identityinfo`.
4. **`cloudappevents`** — parked pending filter + wider sample. **`alertinfo`** — turn off (redundant).

### Wire quirks a mapper must handle (verified across the sampled tables)

- **Event time = `properties.Timestamp`**, distinct from envelope `time` and `_TimeReceivedBySvc` (both arrival/export clocks, seconds–minutes later). Bind `Timestamp`, never `time`.
- **`AdditionalFields` encoding is inconsistent across tables** — a JSON *string* needing a second `Unmarshal` on `deviceprocessevents`/`devicefileevents`/`devicenetworkevents`/`deviceevents`/`devicelogonevents`/`deviceinfo`/`alertevidence`, but a *native* JSON object on `identitylogonevents`/`cloudappevents`. Do not assume one shape.
- **Other stringified-JSON arrays**: `deviceinfo.LoggedOnUsers`, `devicenetworkinfo.IPAddresses/ConnectedNetworks/DnsAddresses` are JSON strings, not native arrays — same double-parse.
- **`alertevidence.AdditionalFields` is polymorphic by `EntityType`** (User/Ip/CloudLogonSession/CloudLogonRequest each carry a different sub-schema) — entity-type-conditional parsing, not one struct.
- **`ProcessCreatedAggregatedReport` is a second logical shape inside `deviceprocessevents`** (Defender's dedup rollup for process-creation storms): most `Initiating*` fields null, `ProcessId=0`. Branch on `ActionType`.
- **Null-vs-sentinel**: most absent values are JSON `null`, but `devicelogonevents.RemoteIP` uses `""`/`"-"` and `deviceregistryevents.RegistryKey` can be `""` on a delete — special-case, don't drop.
- **`DeviceId`** is a stable opaque hash consistent across all Device* tables — good shared join-key attribute.
- **Email family** joins on `NetworkMessageId` across `emailevents`/`emailurlinfo`/`emailattachmentinfo`.

### One constraint to flag on `deviceevents`

`ScriptContent` (inside `AdditionalFields`) can carry an entire multi-KB script body — the one table in the set that could contain a secret pasted into a script. Per the existing `intune.audit_events` secrets carve-out (CLAUDE.md), treat shipping it verbatim as a **named decision point**, not a default either way. Everything else here (hashes, paths, URLs, command lines) is explicitly in-scope per this issue's constraints.

## Decision (maintainer, 2026-07-18): ship `ScriptContent` verbatim

The named `ScriptContent` decision point is resolved: **ship it verbatim**, like every other Defender advanced-hunting field (hashes, paths, command lines).

Rationale: there is no *evidence* of a secret in this field on the wire (CLAUDE.md's rule is to change the secrets exclusion only on observed evidence, not by feel), the OTLP backend is a trusted, scope-limited sink, and the full script body is the primary threat-hunting signal for `DeviceEvents`. The `intune/auditevents modifiedProperties` carve-out stays "exactly one field" — `ScriptContent` is not added to it.

Guardrail (evidence-triggered, not preemptive): if a real credential/key is ever observed inside `ScriptContent` on this tenant, revisit — a hash+length fallback is a trivial later change. Until then, verbatim.

This clears the last open fork inside #106; the rest of the per-table build (full table set, config-gated, `Experimental`, off by default) proceeds as specced.

## Decision (maintainer, 2026-07-18): new `defender.*` namespace

The Defender advanced-hunting tables get their own top-level namespace/domain, **`defender.*`** — not fragmented across `entra`/`intune`/`m365`, and not folded into `m365.*`.

Rationale: it keeps the one coherent advanced-hunting schema (endpoint EDR + email/MDO + identity + alerts) in a single place instead of scattering `DeviceProcessEvents`→intune, `EmailEvents`→m365, `AlertEvidence`→entra; and it matches how #86 itself lists Defender as a **peer** domain ("Entra ID, Intune, Microsoft 365, Defender, and Purview"), not a sub-part of the others. The `entra.security_alerts`/`intune.nagents` precedents predate having a real Defender home; they stay where they are.

Frozen seam for the build:
- Namespace: `defender.*`; collector dir `internal/collectors/defender/*`; collectordoc Domain label `Defender` (5th domain — added to CLAUDE.md namespace list + `docs/signals.md` + the collectordoc Domain set).

### Wire-verified 2026-07-18 (build-first + high-value tranche, cert on camden, `storage.azure.com`)

All containers exist and are actively writing; layout is the same `tenantId=<guid>/y=/m=/d=/h=/m=/PT1H.json` as the Entra categories (blobpipeline prefix reused unchanged). Event time binds `properties.Timestamp` (never envelope `time`/`_TimeReceivedBySvc`). Confirmed per-table quirks against live records:

- **alertevidence** — `AdditionalFields` is a **stringified JSON**, polymorphic by `EntityType` (User/Ip/CloudLogonRequest/CloudLogonSession each a different sub-schema). This is the per-entity evidence `entra.security_alerts` collapses to `evidence_count` — the #93-absorbed gap.
- **deviceregistryevents** — `AdditionalFields` absent (null); rich `Registry*`/`PreviousRegistry*` + full `InitiatingProcess*` family. `RegistryValueName`/`Data` can be null on a key-create; don't drop.
- **devicelogonevents** — `AdditionalFields` stringified JSON; `RemoteIP` uses `""` (not null) sentinel; local/non-Entra logons Entra never sees. macOS + Windows both present on m7kni.
- **deviceinfo** — snapshot (no `ActionType`); `LoggedOnUsers` is a stringified-JSON array (double-parse); Defender-only `ExposureLevel`/`SensorHealthState`/`OnboardingStatus`/`AssetValue`.
- **emailevents** — snapshot-ish per-message; `AdditionalFields` null; MDO delivery/threat fields (`DeliveryAction`/`ThreatTypes`/`DetectionMethods`), zero coverage today.
- **deviceprocessevents/devicefileevents/devicenetworkevents/deviceevents** — the high-volume EDR set; `AdditionalFields` stringified JSON; `deviceevents` carries `ScriptContent` (ship verbatim, decided above) and is a catch-all multi-`ActionType` table.

### Field-emission policy (implementer decision, noted for the record)

Per #106's "full table set / per-entity detail lands as log attributes" — emit the **full documented per-table field set** as log attributes, each key a `semconv.Attr*` constant, sharing constants across tables for the common families (`DeviceId`, `InitiatingProcess*`, account fields). The `AdditionalFields` catch-all is emitted as a single lossless `additional_fields` string attribute (raw JSON) on the Device* tables — nothing dropped, no dozens-of-consts explosion — **except** `alert_evidence`, where it is parsed by `EntityType` because that detail is the whole point of the table. `make check` + a green golden prove behavior per table.

Not ticking "full table set" until the EDR tranche lands.

## EDR tranche shipped — all 9 build-first + high-value + EDR collectors are on main

Commit `75b9d5e`. `make check` green. The high-volume endpoint tables (the payload the ingest exists for) now land alongside the build-first five, each mapped against a **full untruncated** live capture and driven end-to-end into a signals golden:

| collector | table | golden keys |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| `defender.device_process` | DeviceProcessEvents | 45 |
| `defender.device_file` | DeviceFileEvents | 42 |
| `defender.device_network` | DeviceNetworkEvents | 34 |
| `defender.device_event` | DeviceEvents (catch-all) | 24 |

`device_event`'s fixture pins a real **`ScriptContent`** event — Defender for Endpoint on macOS running its own log4j-mitigation scanner (`open_files.py`) — so the "ship `ScriptContent` verbatim" decision is exercised against a genuine script body, not a synthetic one.

The shared engine gained the event-level Account / File-hash / Process stamper families that `device_process` and `device_event` both carry (defined once). All nine `defender.*` collectors are wired (blank imports + collectordoc annotations); `docs/collectors.md` shows 9 rows.

### Acceptance criteria status

- [x] Blob layout + envelope types verified per table against live samples (event time bound to `properties.Timestamp`, never envelope `time`)
- [x] Config-gated + `Experimental()`, off by default, per-table enable
- [x] Per-entity detail as log attributes, never metric labels (all log-only; no metrics emitted)
- [x] `make check` green
- [ ] **Deferred companions** still to build alongside their parents: `device_network_info`, `device_file_certificate_info`, `email_url_info`, `email_attachment_info`, `identity_logon`, `device_image_load`, `identity_info`
- [ ] `alert_info` — **not built** (strict subset of `entra.security_alerts`); `cloud_app_events` — **parked** (needs an ActionType allow-list + wider sample)
- [ ] Package-doc volume note + a final live end-to-end verify (collector actually consuming the containers on camden) before close

The substantive build (the tables carrying unique, high-value signal) is done. Remaining items are the lower-value companions + the turn-off/park calls already decided above, so I'm leaving the issue open but the core is shipped.

## Complete — the full Defender advanced-hunting table set is shipped

Final commit `363548b`. `make check` green. **17 `defender.*` collectors** now live on `main`, every one mapped against a full untruncated live m7kni capture (2026-07-18) and driven end-to-end into a signals golden, all log-only + Experimental + off by default.

### The full set

**Endpoint (EDR):** `device_process`, `device_file`, `device_network`, `device_event` (ScriptContent verbatim), `device_registry`, `device_logon`, `device_image_load`, `device_info`, `device_network_info`, `device_file_certificate`
**Identity:** `identity_logon`, `identity_info`
**Email (MDO):** `email`, `email_url`, `email_attachment`
**Alerts:** `alert_evidence` (the #93-absorbed per-entity evidence)
**Cloud apps:** `cloud_app_event`

### The two originally-parked calls, resolved

- **`cloud_app_events` — BUILT.** Its park condition is discharged: a wider live sample (120 records) showed real security signal — `edit`/`upload`/`change_acl_editors`/`MailItemsAccessed`/OAuth activity across SharePoint/Exchange — not the single-endpoint Spotlight-cache noise the original one-hour sample caught. `raw_event_data` ships verbatim.
- **`alert_info` — NOT built, by decision.** Its fields (`AlertId/Title/Category/Severity/ServiceSource/DetectionSource/AttackTechniques`) are a strict subset of what `entra.security_alerts` already emits; building it would duplicate the alert layer over a second transport for zero new fields.

### Acceptance criteria

- [x] Streaming export enabled for the full table set (18 containers live + writing)
- [x] Blob layout + envelope types verified per table against live samples (event time = `properties.Timestamp`)
- [x] Full table set ingested, config-gated + `Experimental()`, off by default, per-table enable
- [x] Per-entity detail as log attributes, never metric labels (#112); log-only (no metrics emitted)
- [x] Never emit file content/keys — hashes/paths/URLs only (verified per table); the one content field, `DeviceEvents.ScriptContent`, ships verbatim per the explicit maintainer decision
- [x] `make check` green
- [ ] **Deploy-time live-run verify** — the mappers are wire-verified and the pipeline is test-proven, but the deployed binary actually consuming these containers on camden needs the Experimental collectors enabled in the tenant config first (an opt-in ops step). That's the last gate before this is "running in prod", and it's yours to flip when ready.

Two engineering notes for the record: `device_info` + `device_network_info` omit `report_id` (18-digit id that float64 rounds during JSON decode — DeviceId is the exact identity; the small event-table ReportIds stay, exact). `identity_logon`'s `LastSeenForUser` (a nested per-signal counts object) is currently omitted rather than emitted — a minor UEBA-enrichment gap on a companion, not wrong data; easy to add as a `raw`-style field if wanted.

Closing: the build is done — the full table set is shipped, gated, and green. Reopen if you want the `LastSeenForUser` enrichment or want to track the deploy-time live-run here rather than in the collector rollout.

body:
## Summary

Add output-side series governance, matching `tailscale2otel` and `opnsense-exporter`: (a) a **hard cap on active-series cardinality** with an overflow accounting metric, and (b) normalization of emission to **at most ~1 data point per minute (DPM) per unique active series**, regardless of a collector's poll interval. graph2otel currently pushes each series at its collector's cadence with no ceiling on how many distinct series a run can create.

## Why

- **DPM/cost control.** Grafana Cloud bills on active series / DPM. Most collectors poll at 5/15/30/60 min, so a per-series rate near 1/min is already the natural ceiling — but there is no *enforced* cap, and nothing stops a mis-scoped label (see #83's app_name = 341, or the #104 version churn) from multiplying active series unbounded. The siblings cap this deterministically.
- **Blast-radius guard.** A future collector that accidentally puts a per-entity value in a metric label should hit a **bounded overflow** (dropped + counted), not silently balloon the bill.

## Prior art to port

`tailscale2otel/internal/telemetry/cardinality.go` + `catalog.go`:
- `cardinality.metric_limit` config — a hard **per-instrument** max distinct series; series beyond it are dropped.
- self-obs metrics `series_active`, `series_limit`, `series_overflowing` (graph2otel's `internal/telemetry` already documents these names in the M6 dashboard contract but does **not** emit them yet — the self-observability dashboard has placeholder panels).
- `opnsense-exporter` has the equivalent cap; align the config key + semantics.

## Scope

- Config block (e.g. `cardinality.metric_limit`, default a sane cap; `0` = unlimited) layered per the existing koanf precedence, env `G2O_CARDINALITY__METRIC_LIMIT`.
- Enforcement in the telemetry emitter: track active series per instrument, drop + count overflow, emit `graph2otel.series.active` / `.series.limit` / `.series.overflowing` (the self-obs dashboard already references these — wiring them closes that gap).
- Optional DPM normalization: coalesce a series to ≤1 emit/min even if a collector ticks faster (none do today, but the guard is cheap and future-proofs sub-minute collectors / the log-export work).
- Interaction with #104: capping active series also bounds the version-churn blast radius, though #104's proper fix (drop `service_version` from metrics) is still the primary remedy.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `cardinality.metric_limit` config + env, documented in `config.example.yaml` and the Helm values
- [ ] Emitter enforces the per-instrument cap: overflow series dropped and counted
- [ ] `graph2otel.series.active` / `.series.limit` / `.series.overflowing` emitted (unblocks the placeholder panels in the self-obs dashboard)
- [ ] Optional ≤1 DPM per active-series coalescing, off unless a sub-minute source exists
- [ ] Semantics + config key aligned with tailscale2otel / opnsense-exporter
- [ ] Tests: overflow drop + counter; limit=0 = unlimited

Requested pre-v1. Part of #79.
title: Add active-series cardinality cap + ≤1 DPM per-series governance (parity with tailscale2otel/opnsense-exporter)

## Summary

On the live camden deployment, every metric panel that `sum`s across a bounded dimension (device compliance state, OS, encryption, etc.) shows a clean **2× spike lasting ~5–10 min after each redeploy**. Root-caused against live Grafana Cloud data: it is a redeploy artifact of `service.version` being a per-metric resource-attribute label, not a data error.

## Root cause (confirmed live)

`internal/telemetry/provider.go:194` attaches `service.version` (= the build's version string) as an **OTEL resource attribute**, so it becomes a `service_version` **label on every emitted metric**. The camden deployment tracks the `:main` edge image, whose version string is the **git short SHA** — so it changes on *every commit*.

When the container is redeployed onto a newer `:main`:
1. the new process emits its series with `service_version=<new sha>` — a **new series set**;
2. the old process's series (`service_version=<old sha>`) stop receiving samples but **linger in Mimir for the query lookback window** (~5 min) still returning their last value — because an OTLP push that simply stops carries **no staleness signal** (unlike a Prometheus scrape target going down, which is marked stale immediately);
3. dashboard panels `sum by (compliance_state)(…)` aggregate `service_version` away, so they **sum the old + new series** → exactly 2× until the old series ages out.

Live evidence: during the jump window `intune_compliance_devices` carried **two** `service_version` values (`d8067b3` and `fc7238b`); outside it, one (`8267… current`).

This is the OTLP-push-vs-scrape difference the artifact makes visible: scraping self-heals via staleness markers; push does not.

## Why the sibling repos don't show it

`tailscale2otel` also promotes `service.version` to a `service_version` metric label — but it runs **stable release tags**, so it almost never restarts onto a *different* version, and the overlap never happens. We deliberately run `:main` (version = per-commit SHA) and redeploy often, so we hit it constantly.

## Prevention strategies (pick one; recommend #1)

1. **Do not put a per-build-changing value on every metric series.** Keep `service.version` **only** on `graph2otel.build_info` (it already carries `version`) and drop `service.version` from the metrics resource — restarts then reuse the same domain series (no overlap, no doubling) and per-metric cardinality drops. Version stays queryable via a `build_info` join. *(This diverges from ts2otel, correctly, because our deploy cadence is different.)* Keep it on **logs** if wanted (logs are not summed).
2. Pin camden to a **stable release tag** instead of `:main` — rejected, we want `:main`.
3. **Staleness on graceful shutdown**: have the exporter emit a final stale/zero marker per active series on SIGTERM. Hard/fragile with OTLP metrics (no clean per-series stale marker) — not recommended.
4. Dashboard-only: can't cleanly pick "the live version" in PromQL during the overlap; not a real fix.

Related: the broader OTLP-push staleness gap (a series lingers for lookback-delta after the pusher stops) also motivates the active-series DPM cap tracked separately.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `service.version` removed from the **metrics** resource attributes (retained in `graph2otel.build_info`; optionally retained on logs)
- [ ] Redeploy on camden and confirm the `sum`-panels no longer double across the restart
- [ ] Note the OTLP-push staleness behaviour in docs so operators expect a brief flat-line (not a spike) after a restart

Found on the live camden deployment. Part of #79.

comments.body:
## OTel semconv / OTLP→Prometheus standard (researched)

Checked against the OpenTelemetry spec + the Prometheus/OpenMetrics compatibility guide. Verdict: **`service.version` is correct as a resource attribute, but it must NOT be a label on every metric series — its Prometheus home is an info metric (`target_info` / a `*_build_info` gauge).** So "build_info-only" is right for the *series-label surface*.

The spec (OTLP → Prometheus, verbatim intent):
- Only `service.name` (+ `service.namespace`) → `job` and `service.instance.id` → `instance` are promoted to labels.
- **All other resource attributes — including `service.version` — go into a `target_info` metric** (OpenMetrics 1.0 convention), NOT onto every series. "Specific resource attributes *can* be promoted to metric-level labels" but that is an explicit, non-default opt-in.

So the picture for graph2otel:
1. Declaring `service.version` at the OTel **resource** is semconv-correct — keep it. It flows to `target_info`.
2. graph2otel *also* emits `graph2otel_build_info{version=...}` — the classic Prometheus build-info pattern. Correct.
3. The **deviation** is that `service_version` is showing up as a label on `intune_compliance_devices` (and every other series). That only happens when the OTLP pipeline **promotes** the resource attribute to per-series labels (Grafana Cloud's OTLP ingest does this). That promotion is what turns a per-build version into per-series churn → the redeploy doubling.

## Refined fix

Keep version discoverable **only via the info-metric surface** (`graph2otel_build_info` and/or `target_info`), never as a per-series label:
- Preferred: stop the pipeline promoting `service.version` to series labels (so it stays in `target_info`), and query version via a `group_left` join on `build_info`/`target_info`.
- Since backend promotion isn't reliably controllable per-service and `graph2otel_build_info` already carries the version, the robust cross-backend fix is to **not rely on a promoted `service_version` series label at all** — dashboards/alerts should never aggregate over it, and it should not multiply domain series.

Net: version → info metric, matching Prometheus best practice and the OTLP→Prometheus default. This is a real (if version-stable-so-invisible) deviation in **tailscale2otel and opnsense-exporter too**, which deliberately promote `service_version` — filing alignment issues there so all three do the semconv-standard thing regardless of the doubling symptom.

## Verified fixed live (2026-07-16)

Fix `519c002` (drop `service.version` from the metrics resource) is deployed on camden (`:main` = `0ab7ac5`) and confirmed against live Grafana Cloud data.

**AC1 — `service.version` gone from the metrics label surface.** `intune_compliance_devices` now carries only `{__name__, job, service_name, state}` — no `service_version` label on any series. (Version stays queryable via `graph2otel_build_info`; logs keep it, they're never summed.)

**AC2 — no doubling across a redeploy.** `sum(intune_compliance_devices)` across the 07:16:44Z redeploy (`b66596d` → `0ab7ac5`) held **flat at 10** for the entire window — no 2× spike:

```
07:14:00 -> 10   07:17:00 -> 10   07:20:00 -> 10   07:23:00 -> 10
07:15:00 -> 10   07:18:00 -> 10   07:21:00 -> 10   07:24:00 -> 10
07:16:00 -> 10   07:19:00 -> 10   07:22:00 -> 10   07:25:00 -> 10
```

With no per-build `service_version` label, a restart reuses the same domain series, so the old + new series no longer coexist for the lookback window. (This is now a fixed→fixed transition; the one-time doubling only ever happened on the first redeploy onto a fixed image.)

**AC3 — docs.** The OTLP-push staleness behaviour is documented (README "Expect a brief flat-line after a restart, not a gap") so operators expect a short flat-line, not a spike.

Closing. Part of #79.

title: Metric panels double for ~5-10 min after every redeploy (service_version churn on :main + OTLP push staleness)
