## Summary

`internal/config` has no registry/generator today — `config.example.yaml` and the Helm chart's
`values.yaml` are hand-maintained and can silently drift from the actual `koanf`-backed config
struct. Two sibling repos already solve this and are the reference implementations to follow —
adapt whichever pattern fits graph2otel's config shape (it's YAML+env like tailscale2otel, not
CLI-flag-like opnsense-exporter, so the tailscale2otel pattern is the closer analog):

**tailscale2otel** (closer analog — YAML config file + env-var overlay, same as graph2otel):
- No separate name/type/default/description registry struct — instead `config.example.yaml`
  (repo root) is itself the source of truth: YAML-annotated with inline `#` comments per key, and
  locked to the actual `Default()` function
  (`internal/config/config.go`) by two tests: `TestExampleConfigMatchesDefaults` and
  `TestExampleConfigCoversEveryKey` (`internal/config/completeness_test.go`).
- `internal/config/envref.go` parses `config.example.yaml` as a `yaml.Node` AST (walks keys, reads
  `LineComment`s, classifies scalar/list/file-only-map fields) and renders a markdown table
  spliced into `docs/env-vars.md` between `<!-- BEGIN/END GENERATED: env-vars -->` markers.
- The drift gate is a golden-file test, `TestEnvReferenceDocInSync`
  (`internal/config/envref_test.go`) — asserts the rendered doc equals the committed
  `docs/env-vars.md`; runs under plain `go test` (so it's already part of `make check`). Update via
  `go test ./internal/config -run TestEnvReferenceDocInSync -update`, or the wrapper
  `scripts/regen-generated.sh envref`.
- Helm chart `values.yaml`/README/`values.schema.json` are generated via `helm-docs` +
  `helm-values-schema-json`, gated in `.github/workflows/helm.yml` with `fail-on-diff: true` on
  both steps.
- Env var naming is mechanically derived: `TS2OTEL_` prefix + `.`→`__` nesting delimiter,
  uppercased. Structured values (maps/list-of-structs) are marked `FileOnly` — no flat env var.

**opnsense-exporter** (CLI-flag-shaped, less directly applicable but same drift-gate philosophy):
- kingpin `Flag()` declarations across `internal/options/*.go` ARE the live registry; a curated
  `CollectorFlags []CollectorFlag` slice (`internal/options/collectors.go`) additionally maps
  each enable/disable flag to its collector subsystem.
- `scripts/docgen/` walks `kingpin.CommandLine.Model()` to build `docs/configuration.md` +
  CLAUDE.md flag references. `make docs` regenerates; `make docs-check` (`go run ./scripts/docgen
  -check`, diff-only) is the CI drift gate, named "Verify generated docs match code (docgen +
  doclint + registry gate)" in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. A companion test,
  `TestCollectorFlagsCoverAllSwitchFlags`, fails CI if a new `enable-*`/`disable-*` flag is added
  without a matching `CollectorFlags` entry — the "new field, must register it or CI fails"
  guarantee this issue wants for graph2otel's `tenants`/`collectors`/`otlp`/`admin` config keys.

## What / why

Add the equivalent machinery for graph2otel's `internal/config` (koanf, layered defaults < YAML <
env, `G2O_` prefix + `__` nesting per this repo's CLAUDE.md):

1. Make `config.example.yaml` the annotated source of truth (inline comments per key), locked to
   the actual defaults via a completeness test pair analogous to tailscale2otel's
   `TestExampleConfigMatchesDefaults`/`TestExampleConfigCoversEveryKey`.
2. Add a doc generator (parse `config.example.yaml` or walk the config struct directly via
   reflection/tags — either approach is defensible; reflection avoids the "docs.md diverges from
   the struct, not just from the example file" failure mode tailscale2otel's approach still
   allows in principle) that produces a generated config-reference doc.
3. Keep the Helm chart's `values.yaml` (once a Helm chart exists for graph2otel — check current
   deploy assets before assuming one does) in sync the same way, `fail-on-diff` gated in CI.
4. Wire the drift check into `make check` (as a `go test`, matching tailscale2otel — cheapest to
   keep green — or as a dedicated `docs-check`-style Makefile target, matching opnsense-exporter,
   if a struct-reflection generator is chosen instead of a golden-file test) so **`go build ./...
   && go vet ./... && go test -race ./...` and `golangci-lint run` fail on any drift**, per this
   project's own CLAUDE.md mandate that this is the green bar checked before every commit.

## Scope

- `internal/config` registry/generator + `config.example.yaml` annotation pass.
- Helm chart values sync, if/when a chart exists (check current state — CLAUDE.md's v1-skeleton
  note suggests deploy assets may not exist yet; if not, scope this to config.example.yaml +
  docs only and leave a note for when the chart lands).
- Does NOT change any config key, default, or env-var naming — parity/tooling only, zero behavior
  change.

## Feasibility + licensing notes

- Pure tooling — no Graph API, no license/scope implications.
- Both reference implementations are proven in production repos Rob maintains — this is porting
  an established pattern, not inventing one. Prefer the tailscale2otel shape (YAML+env, no CLI
  flags) as the closer structural match; borrow opnsense-exporter's "new field without a registry
  entry fails CI" test idea (`TestCollectorFlagsCoverAllSwitchFlags`) regardless of which
  generator shape is chosen, since it's the actual enforcement mechanism the maintainer wants
  ("forcing an update").

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `config.example.yaml` fully annotated and locked to `internal/config`'s actual defaults via
      a completeness test (`go test` fails if they diverge).
- [ ] A generated config-reference doc exists (e.g. `docs/config.md` or similar), produced by a
      script/generator, not hand-maintained.
- [ ] Drift-check wired into `make check` (or CI equivalent) — a stale generated artifact fails
      the gate, matching this repo's "keep `go build && go vet && go test -race` and
      `golangci-lint run` green ... before claiming work is done" rule.
- [ ] A test analogous to `TestCollectorFlagsCoverAllSwitchFlags` (or equivalent) fails CI when a
      new config key is added without a corresponding registry/doc entry.
- [ ] Helm chart values (if a chart exists) included in the drift gate; otherwise explicitly noted
      as follow-up once the chart lands.
- [ ] `make check` green.

Part of #86.
title: Config registry + generators + drift-check gate (parity with tailscale2otel/opnsense-exporter)

comments.body:
## `eDiscovery.Read.All` GRANTED — and it is **not** sufficient. This is the mirror image of #126.

Granted and consented on `graph2otel-poller` (2026-07-16), then live-verified with the poller's own certificate:

```
identity: 2c92ce28-126c-47c1-82b0-410b64502989  (graph2otel-poller)
  eDiscovery.Read.All   IN TOKEN     <- the scope IS present

GET /v1.0/security/cases                     -> 200 OK          <- parent collection works
GET /v1.0/security/cases/ediscoveryCases     -> 401 UnknownError (empty message)
GET /beta/security/cases/ediscoveryCases     -> 401 UnknownError (empty message)
GET /v1.0/compliance/ediscovery/cases        -> 401 Unauthorized
     "ServiceFabricGraphAuthenticationMiddleware.ValidateToken: ..."
```

### Read this next to #126 — same tenant, same session, opposite outcomes

- **#126 (sensitivity labels)**: 403 `InsufficientGraphPermissions` → the scope was genuinely missing → granting it returned **200**. The "permanent app-only gap" verdict was **wrong**.
- **#102 (eDiscovery)**: the scope is now **in the token**, and it still **401s**. The parent `security/cases` returns 200, so this is not routing and not the token being rejected wholesale — **the eDiscovery data-plane behind Graph is refusing the app identity specifically.**

**Do not repeat #109's mistake in reverse.** #109 saw a permission error and concluded "permanent product gap" when it was a missing scope. The opposite error here would be to see #126's success and assume every Purview 4xx is a scope away from working. **It is not. The scope is present and it still fails.**

### Probable cause — needs confirming, not assuming

`401` (not `403`) with a valid scope in the token, plus the `ServiceFabricGraphAuthenticationMiddleware.ValidateToken` message on the compliance route, points at the **Purview/compliance data-plane rejecting the app-only principal** rather than Graph rejecting the request.

This is exactly the mechanism CLAUDE.md hypothesised for the Purview labels: *"likely need delegated auth or a compliance-role-group membership the app doesn't have"*. That hypothesis was **wrong for sensitivity labels** (#126) but may be **right here**. Microsoft requires an app to be added to an **eDiscovery role group** in the Purview compliance portal — a scope grant alone does not confer eDiscovery access.

### Next step — a portal action, blocked on a human

**Do not grant more Graph scopes; that is not the blocker.** The thing to try:

1. Add `graph2otel-poller` to an **eDiscovery Manager** (or **Reviewer**) role group in the Purview compliance portal (portal-only; no Graph API for role-group membership of a service principal).
2. Re-probe: `g2o-probe security/cases/ediscoveryCases`
3. If it still 401s with the role-group membership in place, **this is a genuine app-only block** — record it as such and close, with the evidence, rather than leaving it open forever.

### Do not roll the scope back yet

`eDiscovery.Read.All` is granted and read-only. Keep it until step 3 resolves — if the role group fixes it, the scope is required. **If this issue is closed as an app-only block, remove the scope** so the poller does not hold a permission it cannot use.

### Tooling

`g2o-probe` (local) authenticates as the poller — use it for the re-probe. The shared
`chat-personal/microsoft/*/graph.py` helper authenticates as a **different, domain-admin-grade app**
and would give a misleading answer here.

## Role-group hypothesis: **CONFIRMED**. Microsoft documents it as a required second step, and names the cmdlets.

The previous comment set the right bar — *"probable cause ... needs confirming, not assuming"* — and
parked on the hypothesis. Confirming it now. It is correct, and it is not a hypothesis: it is
Microsoft's own documented setup procedure, which graph2otel-poller has completed exactly half of.

### The documentation says the permission has two halves

[Set up app-only access for Microsoft Purview eDiscovery by using Microsoft Graph APIs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/security-ediscovery-appauthsetup),
Step 4, verbatim:

> **Permission assignments for your app come in two parts — Microsoft Graph-level permissions, which
> you have already granted, and Purview-level case and role permissions.**

Step 3 is the Graph half: grant `eDiscovery.Read.All` / `eDiscovery.ReadWrite.All` + admin consent.
**That is the half that is done, and it is why the scope sits in the token doing nothing.** Step 4 is
the Purview half, and it is not a Graph scope at all — it is an Exchange/Security-&-Compliance
PowerShell service principal registration plus role-group membership.

This exactly matches the observed behaviour, and explains the detail that ruled out the alternatives:

| Observation | Explained by |
|---|---|
| `eDiscovery.Read.All` present in the token, still fails | Graph half done, Purview half missing |
| `security/cases` → **200**, `security/cases/ediscoveryCases` → **401** | parent is Graph-served; the child hits the Purview data plane, which has never heard of this principal |
| **401**, not 403 | not "you lack a scope" — it is "I cannot identify you", from a service where the SP does not exist |
| `ServiceFabricGraphAuthenticationMiddleware.ValidateToken` on `/compliance/ediscovery/cases` | the compliance data plane rejecting the principal, exactly as the middleware name says |

A missing Graph scope produces `InsufficientGraphPermissions` + 403 (#126's sensitivity labels).
A missing Purview role-group membership produces an unauthenticated-principal 401. **Both were
observed in the same tenant in the same session, and they are different errors because they are
different systems.**

### What it would take — S&C PowerShell, not a scope grant

Per Step 4 of the doc. The poller's **service principal object ID** is
`13371536-9950-4988-90f4-343566456781` (confirmed live — ARM returned it in an authorization error:
*"The client '2c92ce28-126c-47c1-82b0-410b64502989' with object id '13371536-9950-4988-90f4-343566456781'"*).
Note this is the enterprise-app **object** ID, not the appId — the doc calls this out specifically
because using the appId here is the common mistake.

```powershell
Install-Module ExchangeOnlineManagement
Import-Module ExchangeOnlineManagement
Connect-IPPSSession

# register the app with the Purview compliance data plane (this is what does not exist today)
New-ServicePrincipal -AppId "2c92ce28-126c-47c1-82b0-410b64502989" `
                     -ObjectId "13371536-9950-4988-90f4-343566456781" `
                     -DisplayName "graph2otel-poller"
Get-ServicePrincipal

Add-RoleGroupMember -Identity "eDiscoveryManager" -Member "13371536-9950-4988-90f4-343566456781"
Get-RoleGroupMember -Identity "eDiscoveryManager"

# the doc also adds the SP as an eDiscovery case admin
Add-eDiscoveryCaseAdmin -User "13371536-9950-4988-90f4-343566456781"
Get-eDiscoveryCaseAdmin
```

Then re-probe: `g2o-probe security/cases/ediscoveryCases`

**Not run — this mutates the tenant and is outside a read-only spike.** Recording the exact commands
so the human step is a copy-paste rather than a re-derivation.

### Read this against #126 — the two outcomes are both real

- **#126** (sensitivity labels): 403 `InsufficientGraphPermissions` → scope genuinely missing → grant → **200**. "Permanent gap" was wrong.
- **#102** (eDiscovery): scope present → **401** → needs a *non-Graph, non-scope* authorization step.

The previous comment's warning holds and is now evidenced: **do not assume every Purview 4xx is one
grant away.** A 403 usually means missing consent (#126's lesson). A 401 with the scope already in
the token means something other than Graph is refusing you, and no amount of Graph scope will move it.
The error code is the tell, and it was the tell here.

### Status

**Confirmed blocked on a human, with a known and documented unblock.** Not a product limitation, not
an app-only gap — Microsoft explicitly supports this app-only, it just requires the second half of a
two-half setup that only a compliance admin can perform. This is a genuinely different verdict from
"permanent gap": it is buildable the moment Step 4 runs.

`eDiscovery.Read.All` stays granted per the previous comment — it is required, it is read-only, and
it is half of a working configuration rather than a permission the poller cannot use. The
roll-back-if-blocked instruction should now only fire if Step 4 runs and it **still** 401s.
The S&C PowerShell registration (this issue's human step) is batched with the other three maintainer actions in **#148** — exact commands are there, copy-paste ready. Build work stays here.

## App-only `Connect-IPPSSession` does NOT work for this tenant — measured on Windows AND macOS, both fail identically

#148's pre-flight comment asserted item 1 needs no interactive login, on the reasoning that
`homelab-agentic-mgmt` holds `Exchange.ManageAsApp` + Compliance Administrator, "so app-only
`Connect-IPPSSession` works from winsrv". **That was an inference, not a measurement, and the wire
says it is wrong.** Recording it here so the next reader does not re-derive it.

### What was measured (2026-07-17)

| environment | result |
| --- | --- |
| macOS, pwsh 7.6.3, EXO 3.10.0, cert from `mgmt.pfx` via `-Certificate` | `Object reference not set to an instance of an object.` |
| **winsrv (VM 104), Windows PS 5.1, EXO 3.10.0, cert in store via `-CertificateThumbprint`** | **identical NullRef** |

Same module version, same identity, same org, two different operating systems, byte-identical
failure. **The "Connect-IPPSSession is Windows-only, so run it on winsrv" framing is not the
blocker** — Windows was tested directly and fails the same way.

### The failure is post-authentication

`-Verbose` places it precisely:

```
VERBOSE: [ThreadID: #] Trying to acquire token based on UI flow
VERBOSE: [ThreadID: #] Successfully acquired new token for Cert based flow.
VERBOSE: [ThreadID: #] Successfully got a token from AAD
VERBOSE: ConnectionContext Removed
=== EXCEPTION ===
Message : Object reference not set to an instance of an object.
Type    : System.SystemException
   at Microsoft.Exchange.Management.ExoPowershellSnapin.NewEXOModule.ProcessRecord()
```

**Token acquisition succeeds.** The NullRef is thrown while building the cmdlet module from the
service's response — i.e. the compliance endpoint returns something the module cannot handle. This
is the shape of "the service does not recognise this principal", not "auth failed".

### Ruled out, with evidence

- **Not the platform.** Windows reproduces it (table above).
- **Not the cert or the identity.** `Connect-ExchangeOnline` with the *same* pfx on the *same* macOS
  host connects fine and returns live data (`Get-AdminAuditLogConfig` → `UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled: True`).
  Same module, same cert, same app — EXO works, S&C does not.
- **Not a missing role.** Live Graph read of the mgmt SP (`8f35f4e9-5c91-42db-a1f7-d77ada4cc0a2`):
  `['Compliance Administrator', 'Security Administrator', 'Exchange Administrator', 'Purview Workload Content Administrator', 'Teams Administrator']`,
  and `Exchange.ManageAsApp` present = True.
- **Not replication lag.** Those grants date from the 2026-07-14/15 baseline pass — 3 days, well past
  the documented <=24h window. The `purview/CLAUDE.md` note that the NullRef means "SP unknown to
  compliance RBAC, wait up to 24h" has had its wait.

### Probable cause — stated as a hypothesis, not a fact

`purview_grant.py` is described in `chat-personal/microsoft/purview/CLAUDE.md` as registering the app
SP into compliance RBAC via `New-ServicePrincipal` + `Add-RoleGroupMember`. **It does not** — reading
the script, it grants Graph scopes, `Exchange.ManageAsApp`, and the Compliance Administrator directory
role, and contains neither cmdlet. So `homelab-agentic-mgmt` was most likely **never registered in
compliance RBAC**, and the 2026-07-14 baseline landed on a delegated device-code token, which does not
need that registration.

That yields a bootstrap catch-22: `New-ServicePrincipal` is itself an S&C cmdlet, so registering an SP
for app-only access requires an already-working IPPS session. **The delegated token is not merely the
"reliable path today" — for the bootstrap it appears to be the only path.** This is consistent with
`purview_baseline.ps1` taking an `-AccessToken` parameter.

`[live-measured 2026-07-17, #102 / #148]` for the measurements above; the `purview_grant.py`
hypothesis is `n=1` code-reading, not yet proven on the wire.

### Consequence for #148 item 1

Item 1 **does** need an interactive moment after all — a device-code delegated login. The
pre-flight's item-1 simplification is withdrawn. Everything else about item 1 stands: the cmdlets,
and the poller object ID `13371536-9950-4988-90f4-343566456781`, which is **confirmed correct** by
live Graph read of `servicePrincipals(appId='2c92ce28-126c-47c1-82b0-410b64502989')` — the `id`
returned is exactly that value, so the "using appId is the common mistake" trap is avoided.

Next: run the registration under a delegated token, then re-probe
`g2o-probe security/cases/ediscoveryCases` (expect 200; was 401).

## UNBLOCKED — 401 → **200**. Step 4 ran, and the role-group hypothesis is now live-proven.

Ran under a **delegated device-code token** (`rob@m7kni.io`), 2026-07-17, per #148 item 1.

```
=== 1. New-ServicePrincipal ===  CREATED
DisplayName          AppId                                ObjectId
graph2otel-poller    2c92ce28-126c-47c1-82b0-410b64502989 13371536-9950-4988-90f4-343566456781
homelab-agentic-mgmt <guid-53> 8f35f4e9-5c91-42db-a1f7-d77ada4cc0a2

=== 2. Add-RoleGroupMember eDiscoveryManager ===  ADDED   -> members: graph2otel-poller
=== 3. Add-eDiscoveryCaseAdmin ===                ADDED   -> 13371536-9950-4988-90f4-343566456781
```

**Verification, probed as `graph2otel-poller` with its own certificate:**

```
v1.0  security/cases/ediscoveryCases  -> 200, 1 row(s)     (was 401 UnknownError)
beta  security/cases/ediscoveryCases  -> 200, 1 row(s)     (was 401 UnknownError)
v1.0  security/cases                  -> 200, 1 row(s)
```

**No replication wait was needed** — the probe returned 200 on the first attempt, immediately after
the cmdlets. The ≤24h compliance-RBAC replication lag documented in
`chat-personal/microsoft/purview/CLAUDE.md` did not apply to this path.
`[live-measured 2026-07-17, #102 / #148]`

The two-half diagnosis is confirmed end to end: the Graph half (`eDiscovery.Read.All`, granted
2026-07-16) put the scope in the token and changed nothing; the Purview half (`New-ServicePrincipal`
+ role group + case admin) is what moved it from 401 to 200. **`eDiscovery.Read.All` stays granted** —
it is required, and the roll-back-if-blocked instruction is now moot because Step 4 ran and it
worked. This closes as buildable, not as an app-only gap.

## Correction: my own hypothesis from earlier today was WRONG

The previous comment hypothesised — explicitly tagged `n=1` code-reading, not fact — that
`homelab-agentic-mgmt` had "most likely **never** been registered in compliance RBAC", since
`purview_grant.py` contains no `New-ServicePrincipal`. **The wire refutes it.** The very first
`Get-ServicePrincipal` of the session, *before* any cmdlet ran, returned:

```
homelab-agentic-mgmt <guid-53> 8f35f4e9-5c91-42db-a1f7-d77ada4cc0a2
```

mgmt **is** registered in compliance RBAC — registered by something other than `purview_grant.py`,
which is a separate loose end in that workspace, not here. So "the SP is unknown to compliance RBAC"
is **not** the explanation for the app-only NullRef.

**What still stands (measured, not inferred):** app-only `Connect-IPPSSession` NullRefs identically
on winsrv and macOS with the token acquiring successfully, while the delegated token connects on the
first try from the same macOS host with the same module version. Both of those are live-measured and
unaffected by the correction. What is now **open** is *why* app-only fails, given the SP is registered
and holds Compliance Administrator + `Exchange.ManageAsApp`. That is a `chat-personal` tooling
question rather than a graph2otel one, and it does not gate this issue: the delegated path did the
job, and graph2otel itself never needs S&C PowerShell at runtime — it reads eDiscovery over Graph as
the poller, which now works.

Recording the correction rather than quietly dropping it, per the evidence-class rule: a hypothesis
that reaches the right action for the wrong reason is exactly the kind of thing that hardens into
false do-not-redo armor.

## Remaining on this issue

The block is gone; the **build work** (an eDiscovery collector, if one is wanted) is what is left,
and the endpoint now returns real data to design against — 1 live case.

## Doc half landed (`98c1dad`); the collector itself is still open — and this issue is **no longer blocked**.

`docs/data-plane-registration.md` now carries the registration procedure this issue proved out, so the "how do I register a poller app with a non-Graph data plane" knowledge is out of the comments and into a page an operator can follow (#149, closed).

**Restating the state plainly, because the tracker still reads as blocked in two places** and a future session will otherwise re-derive it:

- `security/cases/ediscoveryCases` → **200** as `graph2otel-poller`, v1.0 and beta, 1 live case. `[live-measured 2026-07-17, #102/#148]`
- The 401 was never a scope problem. `eDiscovery.Read.All` was granted and in the token throughout. The S&C data plane did not know the principal.
- `New-ServicePrincipal` + `Add-RoleGroupMember eDiscoveryManager` + `Add-eDiscoveryCaseAdmin` cleared it, under a **delegated device-code** token — app-only `Connect-IPPSSession` NullRefs post-auth on both Windows and macOS, and why remains **unexplained** (the "SP unknown to compliance RBAC" hypothesis was refuted — mgmt *was* registered).
- **No replication wait** — 200 on the first probe, immediately after the cmdlets.
- graph2otel never needs S&C PowerShell at runtime. This is one-time operator setup.

Also corrected `docs/graph-api-gotchas.md`, which still told readers this endpoint "still 401s — the blocker is Purview-side service-principal registration (a human/portal action)". Per the body-freshness rule that was a day stale and would have sent the next reader to file a duplicate blocker.

**What remains here is just the collector**: the eDiscovery case inventory gauge + its log twin. Nothing external gates it.

Two things a future reader should not assume, both marked `[unverified]` in the new doc rather than left implicit:
- Which subset of the three cmdlets is minimally sufficient — they ran as one batch.
- Whether `Reviewer` works instead of `eDiscoveryManager`. Never tested; it is the least-privilege candidate.

## Done — 5d49f57

Built `purview.ediscovery_cases`: a bounded gauge of eDiscovery cases by status + a log twin per case (id, display name, custodial description, external id, real created/closed times), following the `entra.risk` SnapshotCollector shape. TDD'd against the verbatim live case probed as `graph2otel-poller` — no imagination.

**The blocker is gone, confirmed:** the S&C data-plane registration ran 2026-07-17 and `/security/cases/ediscoveryCases` returns 200 with 1 case. Verified again today as the poller. The `needs-rob` framing was stale — nothing external gated the collector, only the collector itself remained.

**Wire traps handled (live, not docs):**
- The auto-created default "Content Search" case has `createdDateTime`/`lastModifiedDateTime` = the .NET zero `0001-01-01T00:00:00Z`. `realDateTime` drops those rather than emit a year-0001 timestamp.
- `closedBy`/`lastModifiedBy` are `identitySet` objects (null on every observed record). Their populated shape has not been seen on the wire, so they are deliberately **not** mapped (#142).

**Opt-in, documented for admins** (per the enable-path requirement): default-off via `Experimental` — not because it's beta (v1.0 GA) but because `eDiscovery.Read.All` alone 401s without the S&C registration. A 401 fails the collector loudly and names the fix. Enable path in `docs/permissions.md` §4b (grant → register → `collectors["purview.ediscovery_cases"].enabled: true`), `config.example.yaml`, and `docs/collectors.md`.

Deploying to camden opted-in next (registration is already live there).

## Deployed + verified live on camden

`version=5d49f57` running. `purview.ediscovery_cases` enabled (opted-in in camden's config) and green on its first run:

```
enabled: true, transport: graph, runs: 1, failures: 0,
last_success: true, last_error: null, last_duration_ms: 3228
```

A 3.2s successful fetch with no 401 confirms both halves work end-to-end: the granted `eDiscovery.Read.All` scope AND the Security & Compliance data-plane registration. The collector emits the gauge + log twin for the tenant's 1 active case ("Content Search"). Fully done.

title: feat(collectors): Purview eDiscovery case inventory gauge

body:
## Summary

Two small, bounded, config-shaped Purview inventories are cleanly Graph-servable today and follow
the exact same pattern as the existing Entra `recommendations`/`securescore` inventory gauges —
lowest-risk, highest-confidence wins in this domain. graph2otel has zero Purview-domain code
today (confirmed via repo-wide grep).

## What / why

- **Sensitivity label definitions** — `GET /security/dataSecurityAndGovernance/sensitivityLabels`
  (`InformationProtectionPolicy.Read.All`, already granted in the tenant checked). Tenant-wide
  label list: id, displayName, rank, `applicableTo` (file/email/site). Gauge:
  `purview.labels.count` by `applicableTo`/rank — bounded by label count, no PII.
- **Retention labels + retention event types** — `GET /security/labels/retentionLabels` and
  `GET /security/triggerTypes/retentionEventTypes` (`RecordsManagement.Read.All`, already granted;
  Microsoft's own "what's new" notes confirm this is readable app-only, no signed-in user
  required). Properties: `behaviorDuringRetentionPeriod`, `actionAfterRetentionPeriod`,
  `retentionTrigger`. Gauge: `purview.retention.labels.count` (+ a small event-types count) — both
  tiny bounded lists, same domain, cheap to bundle in one collector.

## Scope

One new collector package (e.g. `internal/collectors/purview/labels` or similar), metrics only —
bounded gauges, no per-entity detail, no metric-label cardinality risk.

## Feasibility + licensing notes

- Requires Microsoft Purview / Compliance premium licensing (E5 Compliance, or standalone
  Information Protection P1/P2 and Records Management add-ons respectively) — model as new
  `internal/license` capabilities (e.g. `CapPurviewInfoProtection`, `CapPurviewRecordsMgmt`) gated
  off `subscribedSkus` service-plan GUIDs, following the exact pattern already proven for
  `CapEntraP1`/`CapEntraP2`/`CapWorkloadIdentitiesPremium`/`CapIntune` in
  `internal/license/license.go` — not new design, a reusable pattern.
- Both scopes already granted in the tenant checked in this research (confirmed live in the
  Graph activity-log scope dump) — no scope-grant blocker for smoke-testing.
- Both are read-only application permissions.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `purview.labels.count` gauge built, bucketed by `applicableTo`/rank.
- [ ] `purview.retention.labels.count` + retention-event-types count gauges built.
- [ ] New license capabilities added following the existing `internal/license` pattern.
- [ ] Cardinality reviewed: no per-label PII in metric labels (label names may be worth a bounded
      label if cardinality stays low — verify against real tenant label counts before deciding).
- [ ] `make check` green.

Part of #86.

comments.body: Closed by b66596d. Two bounded-gauge collectors (metrics only): `purview.sensitivity_labels` (`purview.labels.count` by applicable_to, from `/security/dataSecurityAndGovernance/sensitivityLabels`) and `purview.retention_labels` (`purview.retention.labels.count` by behavior/action/trigger + `purview.retention.event_types.count`, from `/security/labels/retentionLabels` + `/security/triggerTypes/retentionEventTypes`). **Verified all three are v1.0 GA** (docs source path + `@odata.context`), so not Experimental (secure_score/agreements precedent). **Two collectors, not one** — the catalogs sit behind two entitlements, so new license caps `CapPurviewInfoProtection`/`CapPurviewRecordsMgmt` (MIP_S_CLP1/CLP2 + RECORDS_MANAGEMENT service-plan GUIDs) gate them independently. Dropped the issue's `rank` bucket — the real field is a dense per-label `priority` that would mint per-entity series; bucketed by bounded enums instead. 403/404 → skip-and-log. InformationProtectionPolicy.Read.All + RecordsManagement.Read.All (added to preflight catalog). Tests -race green. Still to do: verify/grant the two scopes on the poller + live-smoke in the ops pass.

body:
> **This body was rewritten 2026-07-17 (#146).** The original body was a park order ("fallback only — do not build") whose every load-bearing "fact" was later measured false, and the issue was then closed won't-do **on the wrong question** (data equivalence, when the right question was ingest fitness), reopened, built, and shipped. The comment chain below is the authoritative history — this body summarizes it and lists what remains.

## Current state — SHIPPED, default-on

`m365.activity` collects the M365 unified audit log over the **O365 Management Activity API** (stable v1.0, 2,000 req/min, subscription→content-blob model): `internal/o365activityclient` + `internal/o365pipeline` + `internal/collectors/m365/activity`. Shipped `98d5583`, AF20024 tolerance `55e3999`, live-verified end-to-end on camden 2026-07-16 (see the final comment for the full verification).

**Latency framing (folded from a deleted pre-reversal comment):** both this API and Graph's `auditLogQuery` sit on the **same unified audit log backend**, so neither has a fresher source (UAL availability is 30min–24h). The Management API's win is **overhead, not backend** — subscription+blob pull avoids the search-job round-trip and its creation 429s (#98). True near-real-time for these signals is streaming only (the #89/#106 path).

Grants on `graph2otel-poller`: `ActivityFeed.Read` + `ActivityFeed.ReadDlp`; subscriptions enabled: `Audit.AzureActiveDirectory`, `DLP.All`; camden additionally runs `Audit.Exchange` + `Audit.SharePoint` + `Audit.General`. `m365.unified_audit` (the beta-only Graph route) is **disabled on camden** — both emit `m365.audit` with the same ids.

## Facts a reader must not take from the original body (all measured false, live, 2026-07-16)

- ~~"15-minute cooldown between subscription-start calls"~~ — never fired; 5 back-to-back 200s. The real trap is **AF20024** (undocumented): re-starting an enabled subscription 400s; it is a success condition and the client treats it as one.
- ~~"Up to 12h latency for first content"~~ — content listed **~2 min** after subscribe, with ~22h of backfill.
- ~~"7-day max blob expiration"~~ — live `contentExpiration` was ~20 days; always read it off the wire.
- Unstated in the body but load-bearing: the list endpoint caps ranges at **24h** (AF20055) — chunk via `o365activityclient.MaxWindow`; `CreationTime` is **not RFC3339** (zone-less); wire enums are PascalCase; **defaults emit zero on a small tenant while reporting 100% healthy** (Exchange/SharePoint carry no content on m7kni — a green tick with an empty checkpoint is the steady state, not a fault).

The doc-vs-wire scorecard ran **6-0 against Microsoft's docs**. Full detail: CLAUDE.md's O365 entries + the comments below.

## Remaining work (the reason this stays open)

- [ ] Emit `user_principal_name` (`UserId` IS the UPN in the classic schema) — biggest convergence gap vs `m365.unified_audit`.
- [ ] Verify `DLP.All` end-to-end — zero rows live; needs a deliberately-triggered DLP match (tenant mutation, needs maintainer).
- [ ] Move the `WindowCollector` adapter from the collector package into `o365pipeline`.
- [ ] `SECURITY.md`: document `POST /subscriptions/start` as the second break in the read-only property (after the reports-export job).

Part of #86.

comments.body:
Closing as **won't-do**, on live evidence rather than assumption — per the maintainer's call to verify the DLP question first.

## The live-verify (m7kni, 2026-07-16)

This issue's own bar: *"do not build unless the live-verify spike shows a material gap"* — specifically `DLP.All` sensitive-data content missing from `auditLogQuery`. CLAUDE.md still flagged that as **open/pending**. So I tested it directly.

`POST /beta/security/auditLog/queries` with `recordTypeFilters: [complianceDLPSharePoint, complianceDLPExchange, dlpEndpoint]` over 2026-07-09 → 07-16:

```
DLP records returned: 5557
record types: {DLPEndpoint: 5557}
first: type=DLPEndpoint op=FileDeleted
auditData keys: [Application, ClientIP, CorrelationIdentity, CreationTime, DeviceName,
                 FileExtension, FileSize, FileType, Hidden, Id, MDATPDeviceId, ObjectId,
                 Operation, OrganizationId, Platform, RecordType, Scope, Sha1, Sha256,
                 SourceLocationType, UserId, UserKey, UserType, Version, Workload]
sensitive-content markers: NONE
```

**Finding 1 — auditLogQuery is NOT blind to DLP.** 5,557 DLP rows came back through Graph. The premise that this API family cannot see DLP data is refuted; the endpoint-DLP stream arrives with full per-event detail (device, user, client IP, file hashes, path metadata).

**Finding 2 — no sensitive-information-type payload on these records.** No `SensitiveInfoTypeData`, no `PolicyDetails`. But read that honestly: **every returned row is `DLPEndpoint`/`FileDeleted` — plain endpoint file activity where no DLP policy matched, so there is no SIT payload to carry.** `ComplianceDLPSharePoint`/`ComplianceDLPExchange` — the record types that *do* carry `PolicyDetails`+`SensitiveInfoTypeData` — returned **zero rows**, which almost certainly means this tenant had no DLP policy matches in the window, not that they are unmirrored.

## Verdict

**No material gap is confirmed, so the issue's own precondition for building is unmet.** Closing.

**The residual unknown, stated honestly rather than buried:** whether `auditLogQuery` carries the SIT/`PolicyDetails` payload on a genuine DLP *policy-match* event is still untested — because m7kni produced no such event to test against. Testing it would require deliberately triggering a DLP match (e.g. writing a synthetic SIT pattern to a monitored location), which is a tenant mutation and out of scope for a spike.

**If this ever matters, that is the exact test**: trigger one match, re-run the query above, and check whether `PolicyDetails`/`SensitiveInfoTypeData` appear on the `ComplianceDLP*` record. Reopen only on that evidence. Do not reopen on the theory alone — the O365 Management Activity API costs a whole second auth model (tenant-wide `ActivityFeed.Read` vs the per-workload least-privilege scopes we have now), and that is a real downgrade to pay for an unproven gap.

## Bonus findings recorded

- **5,557 endpoint-DLP rows in 7 days on a 6-device tenant** (~790/day). Confirms #98's decision to exclude `dlpEndpoint` from `m365.unified_audit`'s `recordTypeFilters` was right — it is high-volume, low-signal noise.
- **The audit query took over 10 minutes to reach `succeeded`.** Worth knowing for `m365.unified_audit` (30-min interval): query completion is far slower than the collector's cadence assumes, which is directly relevant to the in-flight-job-resumability spike — a 10-minute server-side job is a wide window for a container restart to land in.

Closes #100.

## REOPENING — this was closed on the wrong test. Maintainer challenge, and it holds up.

This issue was closed as **"redundant — `security/auditLog/queries` returns the same unified-audit data (5,557 DLP rows live-verified)"**. The data-equivalence claim is true. **It was the wrong question.**

*"Does it return the same rows?"* is not the same as *"is it a better ingest mechanism?"* — and on that question the Management Activity API wins decisively. The CLAUDE.md / do-not-redo entry saying "the O365 Management API is closed, do not propose it" is **wrong and must be removed**; it actively steered a later spike away from this.

### The two are not variants of one API — they are different delivery models

| | `security/auditLog/queries` (what we built) | **O365 Management Activity API** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| model | async **query** → poll status → page records | **subscribe → list content blobs → GET blob** |
| latency | **>10 min per query** (live-verified, #100's own testing) | blobs listed as they become available |
| throttle | **429s on rapid create** (#98) | **2,000 requests/min per tenant** (per-tenant quota, not shared) |
| stability | **beta-only** — `POST /v1.0/security/auditLog/queries` **404s** | **stable v1.0** (`manage.office.com/api/v1.0`) |

### Model detail (from the [API reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/office/office-365-management-api/office-365-management-activity-api-reference))

- **Content types:** `Audit.AzureActiveDirectory`, `Audit.Exchange`, `Audit.SharePoint`, `Audit.General`, `DLP.All`
- **Flow:** `POST /subscriptions/start?contentType=X` → `GET /subscriptions/content?contentType=X&startTime&endTime` → `GET {contentUri}` per blob

- **Endpoint:** `https://manage.office.com/api/v1.0/{tenant_id}/activity/feed/{operation}`
- **Optional webhook push** — irrelevant for us (no inbound endpoint); **poll `/subscriptions/content` instead**, which is fully supported.

### The honest downsides — state them, do not bury them

1. **`POST /subscriptions/start` is a WRITE.** This breaks graph2otel's read-only property, exactly like the reports-export-job exception (M5). It is a subscription, not a data mutation — but it IS a second break and must be documented, not glossed. **`ActivityFeed.Read` is a Read-named role**, so no `ReadWrite` scope is needed; the write is an API operation, not a scope escalation. That is a meaningfully softer break than M5's.
2. **12-hour delay for first content blobs** after a subscription starts. Same class as the blob first-write delay (#89) — plan for it; do not misdiagnose it.
3. **7-day content expiry.** Bounds backfill — consistent with the Loki ceiling and #89's 7-day lifecycle, so not a new constraint.
4. **Blobs are NOT sequential.** *"One content blob can contain actions and events that occurred prior to ... an earlier content blob."* Needs the same watermark + overlap + seen-id dedupe every `WindowCollector` already does. The engine handles this.
5. **New audience + new API surface** — a second non-Graph client alongside #89's blob reader.

## Reverse check: does `auditLogQuery` have anything the Management API does NOT?

Maintainer asked the right question — I had only checked one direction. Verified against the [API reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/office/office-365-management-api/office-365-management-activity-api-reference).

### Coverage: NO gap. The Management API is exhaustive BY CONSTRUCTION.

The five content types are not a curated subset:

```
Audit.AzureActiveDirectory   <- Entra. First-class content type.
Audit.Exchange
Audit.SharePoint
Audit.General                <- "includes all other workloads not included
                                 in the previous content types"   <-- CATCH-ALL
DLP.All
```

**`Audit.General` is an explicit catch-all**, so there is no record type the Management API structurally cannot see. The maintainer's suspicion ("I suspect it doesn't, but worth verifying") is **correct — no coverage gap, and it is guaranteed by the API's own design rather than by us enumerating record types.**

Entra specifically is well covered: the reference's own sample blobs show `"Workload": "AzureActiveDirectory"` records — `PasswordLogonInitialAuthUsingPassword` (sign-ins with `ClientIP`, `LoginStatus`, `UserId`), `Add User.` with full `Actor`/`Target` — the same shape `entra.directory_audits` emits.

### But TWO real asymmetries favour `auditLogQuery` — one is moot, one is not

**1. Retention depth — the audit query API reaches MUCH further back. MOOT for us.**

- Management API: content blobs **expire after 7 days**. Error `AF20051`: *"Content older than 7 days cannot be retrieved."* `/subscriptions/content` also refuses a `startTime` more than **7 days in the past**.
- `auditLogQuery`: searches Purview Audit's full retention — **180 days (Standard), 1 year+ (Premium)**.

**Why it is moot:** graph2otel ships to Loki, which rejects samples beyond ~13 days (the constraint that set #89's 7-day blob lifecycle). A 180-day backfill would be **fetched, mapped, shipped, and rejected**. The Management API's 7-day window sits inside the useful ceiling. This is the same downstream bound already recorded on #118 and #89.

**2. Server-side filtering — genuinely real, genuinely a downgrade.**

- `auditLogQuery`: filter server-side by user, operation, recordType, date range.
- Management API: **no filtering.** You take every blob for the content type and filter client-side.

**This is a real cost, not a moot one.** Subscribing to `Audit.General` on a busy tenant means fetching every Exchange/SharePoint/Teams event to keep the few we want. It is the same shape as the `intune.devices` full-fleet page-walk that CLAUDE.md calls out as the deliberate exception. **Mitigation:** subscribe only to the content types we actually map (likely `Audit.AzureActiveDirectory` + `DLP.All`, **not** `Audit.General`), which bounds the volume to what we want anyway.

### Revised recommendation — not "switch", but "switch with one caveat"

The Management API is better for **continuous ingest** (stable v1.0, 2000 req/min, no 10-min query, purpose-built). `auditLogQuery` is better for **deep historical search** — which graph2otel structurally cannot use, because Loki will not accept the results.

**So: switch `m365.unified_audit` to the Management API and drop the beta + Experimental status.** Keep `auditLogQuery` **only** if a use case appears that needs >7-day lookback — and note that use case cannot be "ship it to Loki".

**Do NOT subscribe to `Audit.General` by default.** Start with `Audit.AzureActiveDirectory`; add `DLP.All` if the DLP verify lands. Adding content types is a config decision with a real volume cost, so it must be explicit, not implied by "subscribe to everything".

- [ ] Spike `POST /subscriptions/start` for **`Audit.AzureActiveDirectory` only**; wait out the 12h; confirm blobs list + fetch under the poller's cert
- [ ] Verify the open DLP question: does `DLP.All` carry sensitive-data detail `auditLogQuery` does not?
- [ ] Confirm client-side filtering volume is acceptable per content type **before** enabling any beyond the first
- [ ] Switch `m365.unified_audit` to this transport; drop `Experimental`; drop `BaseURLOverride`/beta
- [ ] Checkpoint namespace migration — query-API watermark and content-blob cursor are NOT interchangeable
- [ ] CLAUDE.md: **remove** the "O365 Management API closed as redundant" do-not-redo entry
- [ ] CLAUDE.md: record the 7-day content expiry + the no-server-side-filter constraint

```
contentCreated=2026-07-16T06:47:21.100Z
contentCreated=2026-07-16T13:36:38.951Z
```

## FINDING 2: `/subscriptions/content` caps the range at 24 HOURS. This issue does not record it, and it changes the client.

This issue records only the 7-day lookback (`AF20051`). There is a second, much tighter bound:

```
GET /subscriptions/content?startTime=<-9d>&endTime=<now>
-> HTTP 400 AF20055: "Start time and end time must both be specified (or both omitted)
   and must be less than or equal to 24 hours apart, with the start time prior to end time"
```

So `startTime`/`endTime` must both be present or both absent, and be **<=24h apart**. Listing any wider window requires **chunking into <=24h sub-windows client-side**.

This is the same class as the `$top` ceilings already in CLAUDE.md (IPC 500, `/security/incidents` 50): a naive "list from watermark to now" works fine until the collector has been down for over a day, then 400s. Exactly the restart-after-outage case #118 exists for. The client is being built with the chunker in from the start, pinned by a mutation-tested test.


That is ~20 days. This issue says "7-day content expiry" and quotes `AF20051`. ## The record shape, and a security constraint on whoever maps it

One blob, 20 records, `Workloads: {AzureActiveDirectory: 20}`:

```
Operations: {'UserLoggedIn': 8, 'Add app role assignment to service principal.': 6,
             'Update service principal.': 2, 'Update application.': 2,
             'Consent to application.': 1, 'Add app role assignment grant to user.': 1}
```

Top-level keys: `CreationTime`, `Id`, `Operation`, `OrganizationId`, `RecordType` (int), `ResultStatus`, `UserKey`, `UserType`, `Version`, `Workload`, `ObjectId`, `UserId`, `ClientIP`, `AzureActiveDirectoryEventType`, `ExtendedProperties[]`, `ModifiedProperties[]`, `Actor[]`.

**These records carry `ModifiedProperties` with `OldValue`/`NewValue`.** CLAUDE.md's one genuine content exclusion applies directly: emit the **names** of changed properties, never their old/new **values**, which can carry credentials and certificates. `intune/auditevents` already models this and is the shape to copy.

**`ExtendedProperties[].Value` is a JSON-encoded string, not an object** - a nested document inside a string field. Same class of trap as #89's `durationMs`-is-a-string-at-one-level-and-an-int-at-another.

**No rate-limit headers on any response** (no `RateLimit-*`, no `Retry-After`). The 2,000/min ceiling is not observable from the wire, so a client-side limiter is the only control - same as every Graph workload here.

### Two tests in this package were FAKE, and both had the same shape

Worth recording as a finding rather than a footnote, because both passed while the bug was live and one of them existed specifically to defend a wrong belief.

**1. The expiry test encoded my own misreading of the docs.** It asserted `contentExpiration - contentCreated == 7 days` against a fixture built *from the docs*. It passed. It would have passed forever, and it would have defended the 7-day figure against exactly the live measurement that disproved it. Now inverted: it uses the live values (`contentCreated=2026-07-15T20:45:11.875Z`, `contentExpiration=2026-08-05T19:44:14.638Z`) and asserts expiry equals the wire value, does **not** equal `created+MaxLookback`, and exceeds `MaxLookback`. Only a decoder that reads the field passes.

**2. The host-guard tests asserted a symptom, not the property.** They checked "an error occurred, and the message names the host". With the guard removed the client got a **DNS failure that also named the host** - so the tests passed **while the bearer token leaked to the foreign host**. Rewritten to point at a real second `httptest.Server` that records `Authorization` headers and must receive zero requests. Mutating the guard now produces:

```
--- FAIL: TestFetchContentRejectsForeignHost
    content_test.go:419: the foreign host received 1 request(s) carrying
                         [Bearer test-token] — the bearer token leaked
```

**The generalisable lesson: both tests asserted a *symptom* rather than the *property*.** "An error happened" and "the token did not leave" are not the same claim, and only the second one is the thing we care about. 13 mutations were run against this package; these were the two that survived. A test that has only ever passed is decoration - the repo already knows this (#139's gates were mutation-verified for the same reason), but this is the first case where mutation caught a test actively protecting a *wrong belief* rather than merely failing to catch a bug.

### What the client does

Chunks any range into <=24h windows (`MaxWindow`), clamps `startTime` to the 7-day lookback (`MaxLookback`), follows `NextPageUri` with a page cap, dedupes on `contentId` within a call, rate-limits per tenant at the documented 2,000/min (no rate-limit headers exist on the wire, so a client-side limiter is the only control), and types the documented `AF*` error codes with predicates (`IsContentExpired`, `IsInvalidTimeRange` covering AF20030+AF20055, `IsThrottled`, …) rather than blanket-swallowing an HTTP status.

`FetchContent` returns `[]map[string]any` deliberately: a content blob is a union of every workload's schema, so a typed record would be a lie. That places the **`ModifiedProperties` names-not-values exclusion on the mapper**, and the duty is documented at the package level and on the method, pointing at `intune/auditevents` as the model. `ExtendedProperties[].Value` being a JSON-encoded string is documented next to it.

`StartSubscription` carries the read-only-property break in its own doc comment.

### Docs disagreement, recorded rather than resolved

The reference never actually claims a 7-day *expiry*. `AF20051` is a **retrieval** bound ("content older than 7 days cannot be retrieved"); `AF20030`/`AF20055` are a **startTime lookback** bound. The live ~20-day `contentExpiration` contradicts the first, not the second. Only the lookback bound is measured (by the -9d/AF20055 vs -23h/200 probe), so only the lookback bound is encoded. Nothing derives an expiry from a constant. **Unresolved, and deliberately so** - the likeliest explanation is stale doc text, but that is a guess and it is not worth encoding a guess next to the field that disproved the last one.

Also worth flagging on the 24h cap: the reference says a >24h range that *does* return 200 may be **silently partial** - *"these could be partial results and should not be taken into account"*. So the AF20055 400 is the friendly failure. The dangerous one is the request that succeeds and under-reads.

1. m7kni genuinely has no DLP policy matches (this issue's earlier finding: `ComplianceDLPSharePoint`/`ComplianceDLPExchange` returned zero rows; only `DLPEndpoint`/`FileDeleted` came back, which carry no SIT payload because no policy matched).
