## Summary

Every collector already declares its own `DefaultInterval()` (5 min → 24 h, tuned per-signal), the scheduler runs one goroutine-per-collector on independent tickers with only a small startup jitter, and outbound requests are gated by six per-workload token buckets. **No response caching exists anywhere.** No workload realistically risks Graph 429s at documented ceilings even on a 10k-device/user tenant, with one narrower exception (`credentialexpiry`'s `$select=keyCredentials` paging can burst above Microsoft's *actual* undocumented ~150/min sub-ceiling while staying under our modeled client-side bucket). The one clean caching win is `/deviceManagement/managedDevices`, fully paged independently by two collectors every cycle.

## Current state (verified)

**Intervals — per-collector, no global default.** `collector.Collector` requires `DefaultInterval()` (`internal/collector/collector.go:19-20`); registry falls back to it only on a non-positive registration interval (`:68-73`, `:77-87`). Configurable per-collector and per-tenant via `config.CollectorConfig.Interval` → `Config.CollectorSettings` (precedence per-tenant > global > default; `internal/config/config.go:75-79,104-139`, applied `cmd/graph2otel/tenants.go:171,183`). Observed defaults: 5 min (groups, directory_counts, 4 sign-in streams, directory_audits); 10 min (roles, security_alerts); 15 min (bulk Entra directory/policy + provisioning + Intune compliance/enrollment/connectors/audit_events); 20 min (autopilot/enrollment events); 30 min (recommendations, risk_detections, most Intune config collectors); 1 h (secure_score, signin_activity, detected_apps, managed_devices, endpoint_analytics); 6 h (export-job collectors); 24 h (gpo_analytics).

**Scheduler.** One goroutine per entry, own `time.Ticker` (`internal/collector/scheduler.go:120-131,162-171`); one-time startup jitter `[0, 3s)` then immediate first tick (`:138,154-156,174-179`). Stagger is startup-only decorrelation, not continuous phase-spread — same-interval collectors drift back toward coincidence; steady-state bursts are absorbed by the shared per-workload limiter, not scheduler spacing.

**Rate limiters (6 buckets, path-classified `internal/graphclient/workload.go:55-89`, `ratelimit.go:25-47`):** reporting 5/10s; identity-protection 1/s (per-tenant, all apps); directory 50/10s; intune-general 1000/20s; intune-devices 2000/20s; intune-export 48/min.

## Call-volume vs ceiling (1 tenant, 1 cycle, ~49 collectors)

- **reporting / IPC / intune-general / intune-export:** nowhere near ceilings.
- **directory:** `entra.credentialexpiry` fully pages `/applications` + `/servicePrincipals` with `$select=keyCredentials,passwordCredentials` every 15 min (`credentialexpiry.go:75,151-152`) at Graph's default page size (no `Prefer: odata.maxpagesize` anywhere in the client). CLAUDE.md documents `$select=keyCredentials` is Graph-throttled to **~150 req/min per tenant** — tighter than our modeled 300/min bucket. On a large tenant this is the one genuine headroom risk the client-side model doesn't anticipate.
- **intune-devices:** `intune.manageddevices` (hourly) and `intune.malware` (30 min) each independently fully page `/deviceManagement/managedDevices` (~100 pages each on a 10k-device tenant). `malware` also fans out one `.../{id}/windowsProtectionState` per Windows device up to `windowsFleetSweepThreshold=3000` — the largest per-cycle call count in the system, still inside the 6000/min ceiling. Not a throttling risk, but the biggest waste-of-calls candidate.

## Caching / overlap findings

- **`/deviceManagement/managedDevices`** — fully paged independently by `manageddevices.go:314` (`$select=complianceState,operatingSystem,isEncrypted,lastSyncDateTime`) and `malware.go:317` (`$select=id,operatingSystem`). Same collection/tenant, overlapping cadence — a genuine double full-fleet fetch. **The one clean shared-fetch target.**
- Weaker overlaps (different filter/select/cadence, not worth a general cache): `/servicePrincipals` (credentialexpiry vs consent vs directory_counts `$count`), `/applications` (credentialexpiry vs `$count`), `/users|devices|groups` (directory_counts `$count` vs bucketed `$count`-with-`$filter`).

## Recommendation

- **Intervals:** scheme is already well-reasoned + overridable; no default changes. *Document* in `config.example.yaml` how large-tenant operators should widen `intune.manageddevices`, `intune.malware`, `entra.credentialexpiry`.
- **Caching:** build **one narrow per-tick shared fetch** for `/deviceManagement/managedDevices` (union of both `$select` sets, composition-root level `cmd/graph2otel/tenants.go`) — ~50% managedDevices traffic cut on large tenants. A general response-cache layer is **not** justified (other overlaps differ too much in filter/select/cadence). This is API-etiquette, not a throttling fix.
- **Higher priority than caching:** add `Prefer: odata.maxpagesize` (e.g. 999) to `GetAllValues`-based full-collection fetches (managedDevices, applications, servicePrincipals) — cuts absolute page count ~10x on large tenants with no cache, and reduces the `credentialexpiry` real-ceiling exposure.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `config.example.yaml` documents recommended interval overrides for `intune.manageddevices`, `intune.malware`, `entra.credentialexpiry` on 10k+ tenants
- [ ] Add `Prefer: odata.maxpagesize` (or equivalent) to `GetAllValues` full-collection fetches; verify ~10x page-count reduction
- [ ] Per-tick shared fetch for `/deviceManagement/managedDevices` shared by `intune.manageddevices` + `intune.malware`, with a test proving both collectors' metrics are unchanged
- [ ] Confirm whether `credentialexpiry`'s `$select=keyCredentials` paging can exceed Graph's real ~150/min ceiling; if so, narrow its limiter sub-bucket or widen its interval
- [ ] No scheduler-stagger or other `DefaultInterval()` changes — document why (per-collector tuning already exists + is overridable)

From a research spike during the live camden deployment. Part of #79.

> Body updated 2026-07-17 (#146): phases 1–3 were complete but unticked, the fallback framing predated #89's outcome (a **third** option — Azure Storage — won, not LA or Event Hub), and the honest-scope list carried two since-corrected claims. Fixed. The child-issue comment below is the historical worklist; 12 of its 14 issues are closed.

## Mission

Make `graph2otel` capable of **replacing the traditional Microsoft telemetry export pipeline** — diagnostic settings → Log Analytics → Event Hub → an Azure Function → Grafana Cloud — with first-party Graph-API polling (plus the agreed Storage-blob fallback) pushing the same signals as OTLP logs + metrics straight into Grafana Cloud, across **Entra ID, Intune, Microsoft 365, Defender, and Purview**.

## Why

The current pipeline is multi-hop, Azure-Function-bound, and costs money to run. The expensive middle hop is the Azure Function; retiring it is the win.

## Fallback transport (decided — #89, closed)

For signals with no Graph endpoint: diagnostic settings → **Azure Storage account** → `internal/blobpipeline` (byte-offset consumer, read-only, lifecycle-deletion). Live in production, ~£0.85/mo measured. Log Analytics and Event Hub were evaluated and rejected (LA cannot delete or receive Defender streaming; Event Hub = £8.34/mo for ~12s latency gain). Reference: `docs/blob-ingest.md`.

## Honest scope (corrected per #126/#130 — see #79's Honest-scope section for the authoritative list)

Permanent Graph gaps go via the Storage path (`MicrosoftGraphActivityLogs` — already consumed live; `EnrichedOffice365AuditLogs`; Intune `OperationalLogs`; ADFS). Purview **sensitivity** labels are Graph-servable app-only (#126 corrected #109); `NetworkAccessTrafficLogs` has a Graph endpoint but is out of scope with no GSA tenant (#130). Each remaining gap analysis must state plainly what can and cannot be served, so we don't retire an Azure export that's still the only source for something.

## Phase plan

- [x] **Gap analysis** — five domain spikes done; child worklist filed (comment below); 12/14 closed.
- [x] **Highest-value missing log collectors** — shipped: security incidents, unified audit (jobpipeline), `m365.activity` (O365 Management API), blob-sourced MGAL + three sign-in categories, Purview label gauges.
- [x] **Recreate the `entra-security` alert group** — `entra-security-g2o` (6 rules) evaluating in parallel with the legacy group, muted burn-in (`g2o-burnin-silent`); cutover = unmute + retire legacy (#90, closed).
- [ ] **#106** — Defender advanced-hunting tables via the streaming API → Storage (last big build).
- [ ] **#102** — Purview eDiscovery gauge (blocked on a human: Purview-side S&C PowerShell registration).
- [ ] **Coverage validation:** side-by-side graph2otel streams vs `integrations/azure-logexport` for a fixed window; document residual gaps. **This is the real "did we actually replace it?" proof — do not hand-wave it.**
- [ ] **Retire** the Azure-side export (incl. the Function) for domains graph2otel fully covers; unmute `entra-security-g2o` + retire the legacy alert group.

Closes when the four unticked items land. Part of #79.

comments.body:
## Addendum: fallback ingest for signals with no Graph endpoint

Decision from the maintainer: where a log signal has **no Microsoft Graph API endpoint** (e.g. `MicrosoftGraphActivityLogs`, `EnrichedOffice365AuditLogs`, most Intune `OperationalLogs`), a fully acceptable fallback is to ingest it **not from Graph** but from the existing Azure pipeline's data at rest, so the expensive middle hop (the Azure Function) can still be retired:

- **Option A — Log Analytics query + delete-post-ingest.** graph2otel queries the Log Analytics workspace directly (Azure Monitor Log Analytics query API), emits the rows as OTLP logs, and purges the ingested data afterward.
- **Option B — Event Hub / pub-sub sub-client.** graph2otel acts as a *secondary consumer* of the Event Hub the current pipeline already feeds, reading the stream directly.

The real cost pain is the **Azure Function**, not Log Analytics/Event Hub themselves — so either fallback that lets us delete the Function is a win. A research spike will decide which of A vs B is cheaper + lower-effort (tracked as its own child issue). This fallback is the escape hatch for every "no Graph endpoint" gap the domain gap-analyses identify — those gaps are not dead ends, just not Graph-servable.

## Child issues filed (gap-analysis worklist)

Derived from five domain research spikes (Entra/Intune/Defender/M365/Purview) against the live tenant + the current `integrations/azure-logexport` coverage.

**Foundational / cross-cutting**
- #88 — logpipeline: async job-poll collector mode (create → poll → page) — unblocks the auditLogQuery + hunting-shaped APIs
- #89 — spike: fallback ingest strategy (Log Analytics query-and-delete vs Event Hub sub-client) — the escape hatch for every no-Graph-endpoint gap

**Entra**
- #90 — recreate the `entra-security` Grafana alert group on graph2otel-native signals
- #91 — self-instrument graphclient 4xx/5xx as a narrow substitute for the Graph-403-burst rule (that rule's source, `MicrosoftGraphActivityLogs`, has no Graph endpoint)

**Defender**
- #92 — `entra.security_incidents` (Graph `/security/incidents`) collector
- #93 — Defender advanced-hunting collector for `AlertInfo`/`AlertEvidence` parity (`/security/runHuntingQuery`)

**Intune** (gap is largely already closed)
- #94 — docs: Intune `OperationalLogs` is a permanent Graph gap
- #95 — spike: verify `remoteActionAudits`, dedupe vs `intune.audit_events`
- #96 — validate `DeviceComplianceOrg`/`Devices` metric parity (decommission readiness)

**M365 + Purview** (Graph `/security/auditLog/queries` is the primary path, GA)
- #97 — M365 unified-audit collector via Graph `security/auditLogQuery`
- #98 — spike: live-verify auditLogQuery record shape, licensing, latency (M365 + Purview)
- #99 — docs: honest-scope note — signals with no Graph/REST path either way
- #100 — backlog: O365 Management Activity API client (fallback only)
- #101 — Purview sensitivity + retention label inventory gauges
- #102 — Purview eDiscovery case inventory gauge

**Parity (separate track, not log-export)**
- #103 — config registry + generators + drift-check gate (tailscale2otel/opnsense-exporter parity)

Honest-scope permanent gaps confirmed across briefs: `MicrosoftGraphActivityLogs`, `EnrichedOffice365AuditLogs`, most Intune `OperationalLogs` — none Graph-servable; these are the targets for the #89 fallback.

## Coverage validation — done via historical side-by-side (2026-07-20)

The old pipeline is already retired (Function off; `service_name="integrations/azure-logexport"` is silent as of now, last data ~2026-07-06). So a *live* side-by-side is impossible — instead I diffed the old pipelines data from ~14 days ago (still in Loki) against graph2otels current emission. Both queried via gcx against the m7kni stack (`grafana.m7kni.com`, gb-south).

### What the old `integrations/azure-logexport` pipeline carried (24h, 14d ago)

14 diagnostic categories (the `category` stream label). Mapped to graph2otel:

| old category | 24h vol | graph2otel coverage (live event, verified emitting now) |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| AdvancedHunting-CloudAppEvents | 12810 | ✅ `defender.cloud_app_event` (#106 blob) |
| MicrosoftGraphActivityLogs | 10648 | ✅ `entra.graph_activity` |
| MicrosoftServicePrincipalSignInLogs | 1941 | ✅ `entra.signin` (MS-SP blob) |
| AdvancedHunting-DeviceNetworkInfo | 337 | ✅ `defender.device_network_info` |
| ServicePrincipalSignInLogs | 290 | ✅ `entra.signin` (SP blob twin) |
| AuditLogs | 152 | ✅ `entra.directory_audit` (blob) |
| NonInteractiveUserSignInLogs | 138 | ✅ `entra.signin` (non-interactive blob twin) |
| AdvancedHunting-DeviceInfo | 39 | ✅ `defender.device_info` |
| AzureADGraphActivityLogs | 22 | ⚠️ **deprecated Azure AD Graph API** (Microsoft-retired; successor `MicrosoftGraphActivityLogs` IS covered) — not a real gap |
| DeviceComplianceOrg | 13 | ✅ intune device twin (blob, #135-F) |
| Devices | 12 | ✅ intune device twin (blob, #135-F) |
| RequestResponse | 8 | ❌ **out of scope** — an Azure *resource* diagnostic (Document Intelligence, `docintel` sub), not a Graph/identity signal |
| _(empty category)_ | 7 | ❌ resource-diagnostic noise, negligible |
| SignInLogs | 2 | ✅ `entra.signin` (interactive, polled) |

### Verdict: no identity/security-signal regression

**Every Entra / Intune / Defender / M365 identity signal the old pipeline carried is covered by graph2otel and emitting live.** The only non-covered categories are (a) a **deprecated** API whose successor is covered, and (b) two **Azure resource diagnostics** that were never graph2otels Graph/identity mission (they rode the same diagnostic setting incidentally).

graph2otel is in fact a **strict superset**: it is currently emitting **48** log event types (vs the old pipelines 14 categories) — all the other Defender hunting tables (device_process/registry/file/event/image_load/email/identity_*), plus Entra/Intune/M365/Purview signals the old pipeline never had (app_signin_activity, role_member, app_credential, deleted_item, consent_grant, teams, drive_storage, sensitivity_label, ediscovery_case, mdca.discovery_parse, the full intune.device_* set, m365.service_message/health, …).

So the epics **coverage-validation** and **retire-the-Azure-export** items are both satisfied (validation done here; retirement already done by the maintainer).

## Remaining #86 item: the alert cutover (needs a decision)

Live state (gcx, folder `ffo7you47fxtsd`):
- **`entra-security`** — 7 legacy rules.
- **`entra-security-g2o`** — 6 burn-in rules, still muted by mute-timing **`g2o-burnin-silent`** (00:00–24:00). Burn-in has been Normal since 2026-07-16; each g2o rule mirrors a legacy one (`g2o-sp-*` ↔ `entra-signin-*`, `g2o-audit-tamper` ↔ `entra-audit-tamper`, `g2o-defender-crit` ↔ `entra-defender-crit`, `g2o-signin-anomaly` ↔ `entra-signin-anomaly`).

**Cutover = unmute `entra-security-g2o` (delete/disable the `g2o-burnin-silent` mute) + retire the 7 legacy `entra-security` rules.** Since the legacy rules query the now-dead azure-logexport data, they are effectively blind already — but this changes live security alerting, so it needs a deliberate go and a per-rule check that each legacy rule has a live g2o equivalent before removal. Parked pending maintainer approval; not mutating alerting unprompted.

`[live-measured 2026-07-20, #86, gcx historical side-by-side]`

## Alert cutover executed (2026-07-20)

Correction to my earlier comment on where the mute lived: it was **not** the notification policy — the `g2o-burnin-silent` mute was applied **per-rule** via each g2o rules `notification_settings.mute_time_intervals`. So the burn-in rules were genuinely silenced (fired but did not notify) — `g2o-audit-tamper` logged **5,615** Alerting transitions during burn-in (all the grant/token activity), all correctly suppressed.

Done:
- **Deleted 6 legacy `entra-security` rules** that have live g2o equivalents: `cfo7yr86di58gb` (mgmt SP), `entra-signin-intunebrew`, `entra-signin-n8n-namedloc`, `entra-audit-tamper`, `entra-defender-crit`, `entra-signin-anomaly`.
- **Un-muted the 6 `entra-security-g2o` rules** — cleared `g2o-burnin-silent` from each ones `notification_settings` (now `{receiver: irm}`), so they notify live.
- **Deleted** the now-unused `g2o-burnin-silent` mute timing.

Notes:
- **Receiver difference flagged:** the g2o rules notify to receiver **`irm`** (per-rule setting), whereas the legacy security rules routed to **`irm-security`** (via the `severity=critical, source=entra` policy route). Left as-is — a routing decision for the maintainer (may want `irm-security` for parity).
- **`entra-graph403-burst` NOT dropped** — it is a genuine SIEM signal (Graph API 403 burst). Its original def is a Prometheus rule `max(entra_graph_403_5m{appId=~"a380aa5e…|992d4404…|6ad1b334…"}) > 10` — **3 specific tenant apps**, off the now-dead MGAL-derived metric. graph2otel can replicate it: `entra.graph_activity` carries `app_id` + `response_status_code`, and `sum by (app_id)(count_over_time({service_name="graph2otel"} | event_name=\`entra.graph_activity\` | response_status_code=\`403\`[5m]))` works live. Rebuild scope (which apps / external-vs-specific / threshold) pending maintainer confirmation, then the legacy rule is dropped and #86 closes.

Remaining to close #86: rebuild graph403-burst on `entra.graph_activity` + drop the legacy rule.

## Cutover complete — closing the epic

Final alerting state (verified live via gcx):
- **Legacy `entra-security` group: empty** — all 7 rules removed.
- **`entra-security-g2o`: 7 live rules** — the 6 un-muted burn-in rules + the rebuilt `g2o-graph403-burst`. All `health=ok`, not paused, `notification_settings` cleared so they route through the notification policy by their `severity=critical, source=entra` tags -> **`irm-security`** (parity with the old security routing).

### `entra-graph403-burst` rebuilt (scope B) — not dropped blind
Replaced the dead Prometheus rule (`max(entra_graph_403_5m{3 specific appIds}) > 10`, sourced from the retired MGAL metric) with a graph2otel-native LogQL rule **`g2o-graph403-burst`** on `entra.graph_activity`:
`sum by (app_id) (count_over_time({service_name="graph2otel"} | event_name=` + "`entra.graph_activity`" + ` | response_status_code=` + "`403`" + ` [5m])) > 10`
Broadened per maintainer decision from the 3 specific apps to **any app_id** getting a 403 burst (the attack/probing signal), keyed by `app_id` so the alert names the offender. May want threshold tuning if first-party apps (e.g. SharePoint `00000006-…`) churn 403s. Legacy rule deleted.

### Epic close-out
All four remaining items are done:
- [x] #106 (Defender advanced-hunting via Storage) — closed
- [x] #102 (Purview eDiscovery) — closed
- [x] Coverage validation — historical side-by-side proved graph2otel is a **strict superset** of the old `integrations/azure-logexport` pipeline with **no identity-signal regression** (see the 2026-07-20 coverage comment)
- [x] Retire the Azure export + unmute `entra-security-g2o` + retire the legacy alert group — Function already off; cutover done here

graph2otel has **replaced** the traditional Entra/Intune/Defender/M365/Purview log-export pipeline. Closing.

body:
## Summary

`entra.signin_activity` fails at runtime with a 403 because it declares fewer Graph scopes than it actually calls. `RequiredPermissions()` returns only `AuditLog.Read.All`, but the collector's `appSummary` sub-fetch calls `GET /beta/reports/getAzureADApplicationSignInSummary`, which requires **`Reports.Read.All`**. The `check` preflight compares granted scopes against declared scopes, so it passes an app registration that then 403s on this collector's first poll.

## Evidence (live)

`:main` on camden, dedicated app registration granted every scope the collectors declare — this collector still failed:

```
level=WARN msg="collector failed" collector=entra.signin_activity
error="app sign-in summary: GET https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/reports/getAzureADApplicationSignInSummary(period='D7'):
status 403: Authentication_MSGraphPermissionMissing:
The principal does not have required Microsoft Graph permission(s): Reports.Read.All to call this API."
```

`graph2otel_scrape_success_ratio{collector="entra.signin_activity"}` was `0`; after granting `Reports.Read.All` it went to `1`. The other two sub-fetches (`/reports/servicePrincipalSignInActivities`, `/reports/appCredentialSignInActivities`) are fine on `AuditLog.Read.All` — only `appSummary` needs the extra scope, which is why the collector's independent-halves design let the rest emit.

## Fix

`internal/collectors/entra/signinactivity/signinactivity.go` — add `Reports.Read.All` to `RequiredPermissions()`:

```go
func (c *Collector) RequiredPermissions() []string {
    return []string{"AuditLog.Read.All", "Reports.Read.All"}
}
```

Then `check` will flag a missing `Reports.Read.All` up front instead of the collector 403ing at runtime. Also audit the other reporting-workload collectors for the same under-declaration (any collector hitting `/reports/*` beyond the sign-in-activity endpoints).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `entra.signin_activity` declares `Reports.Read.All`
- [ ] `preflight` docs/known-scopes updated if they enumerate this collector's scopes
- [ ] Sweep other `/reports/*` callers for the same gap
- [ ] README/permissions doc lists `Reports.Read.All` under sign-in-activity

Discovered during the live camden deployment. Part of #79.
title: entra.signin_activity under-declares Reports.Read.All (runtime 403, preflight blind)

body:
## Summary

`intune.app_install_status` (the AppInstallStatusAggregate export collector) emits `intune_app_install_status_devices` keyed by `app_name` — and on a live tenant `app_name` is the **entire Intune app catalog**, not the set of admin-deployed apps. On the m7kni lab tenant (6 devices, 6 users) this produced **1870 series from this one collector**:

- distinct `app_name` = **341** (values include store apps: "Icelandair", "Monzo Bank", "23andMe - DNA Testing", "ASDA Scan & Go", "Harvester: Food & Drink", …)
- × `install_state` = 5
- × `platform` = 4

1870 series in a 6-device tenant scales with the app catalog, not the fleet, so a real enterprise (thousands of catalogued apps) yields tens of thousands of series from this collector alone.

## Why this contradicts the audit

`docs/pii-cardinality-audit.md` classifies `app_name` as an "admin-configured object name … bounded by the count of objects an admin has created (dozens–hundreds)" and states free-text label allow-lists are "capped with an `other` leftover". Neither holds here: the aggregate report returns a row per (app, state) for every app Intune knows about, and `app_name` is **not** capped with an `other` bucket. So the audit's PASS for this metric was based on an assumption the live data refutes.

## Note on scope

Not urgent for the maintainer's own lab (Grafana Cloud, no ingest cost) — filing for later investigation, not as a launch blocker. It matters for anyone running this at enterprise scale.

## Options to consider

- Cap `app_name` to a top-N allow-list + `other` bucket (consistent with how the audit says other free-text labels are handled).
- Drop `app_name` from the metric and keep only bounded dims (`install_state`, `platform`), moving per-app detail to the logs pipeline (the export collector already emits per-row logs).
- Gate the per-app_name breakdown behind an explicit config opt-in, off by default.
- Document the cardinality characteristic prominently and leave the choice to the operator.

## Evidence

Live queries against Grafana Cloud (m7kni), `:main` build on camden:
```
count(intune_app_install_status_devices)                       => 1870
count(count by (app_name)(intune_app_install_status_devices))  => 341
count(count by (install_state)(...))                           => 5
count(count by (platform)(...))                                => 4
```

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Decide the cardinality strategy for `intune.app_install_status` (cap / drop label / opt-in / document)
- [ ] Re-run the PII/cardinality audit entry for this collector against live data
- [ ] Update `docs/pii-cardinality-audit.md` so its `app_name` claim matches reality

Discovered during the live camden deployment. Part of #79.

comments.body:
## Shipped: the label is gone, the twin is in - `8765ea2`

`app_name` is gone from the metric, the missing log twin is in, and the gauge is renamed. `make check` green.

| | before | after |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| series on the 6-device m7kni tenant | **1,870** | **~20** |
| bounded by | the Intune app catalog (341 apps) | Microsoft's report schema (5 states x platform enum) |

### This issue's body was wrong, and the reason matters more than the error

The body says *"the export collector already emits per-row logs"*. It emitted **none** - `grep LogEvent` on the package returned nothing. So this was never only a cardinality bug: it was the fetch-rows-bucket-a-count-discard-the-rest shape #112 calls a bug outright, and the per-app detail reached no pipeline at all. Both sibling export collectors (`defenderreport`, `certinventoryreport`) had twins. This was the one the #114 sweep missed.

**Why it was missed is the durable finding.** `docs/pii-cardinality-audit.md` itself claimed this collector emitted "per-device rows". A sweep that read the audit doc rather than the source ticked it off and moved on. **A wrong claim in an audit doc does not merely fail to catch a bug - it hides it from the next audit.** That is also where this issue's own false claim came from: it inherited it.

### The fix

- Metric sums into `install_state` x `platform`. Per-app detail moves to a new `intune.app_install_status` log event carrying app name, id, publisher, platform and the five raw per-state counts.
- Capping `app_name` to a top-N allow-list was considered and rejected: the twin is obligatory under #112 either way, and once the detail is in the logs a LogQL `count by (app_name)` answers the same question off data already shipped. The label buys nothing.
- Guard test asserts the metric's **exact attribute key set**, not a denylist of known-bad keys - so any future unbounded dimension trips it, not just this one.

### Renamed `.devices` → `.installations`, because the old name lied

Summing across apps counts (app, device) pairs, not distinct devices - a device running ten apps contributes ten. An aggregate per-app report cannot yield a device-distinct count, so this is the only bounded aggregate available. `intune.app_install_status.devices` with unit `{device}` would therefore have contradicted its own package doc, and whoever built the first dashboard would have trusted the name.

Now `intune.app_install_status.installations`, unit `{installation}`. Free to do now, checked: **no dashboard or alert references this metric.** It would not have been free later.

### Audit doc: the PASS was an inference, never an observation

The `app_name` PASS is corrected. It classified `app_name` as an "admin-configured object name" and passed it on that basis - an inference about the source data, never an observation of it. The report returns a row per app in the tenant's **catalog**, not the set an admin deployed, and it carried no `"other"` cap despite the doc asserting free-text labels are capped.

Recorded there too: this verdict has now been wrong three times in the same way (#110, #111, and this), and every one was found from live emission or collector source, never from re-reading the doc - which by then asserted the bug did not exist.

title: intune.app_install_status emits unbounded per-app_name cardinality (app catalog, not deployed apps)

body:
## Summary

The shipped dashboards (`dashboards/*.json`) and alert rules (`alerts/graph2otel-alerts.yaml`) reference metric names **without the OTLP→Prometheus unit/type suffixes** that Grafana Cloud's OTLP gateway actually appends. As a result many dashboard panels render blank and at least one primary alert can never fire. Found by deploying `:main` against a live Grafana Cloud stack (m7kni, camden `/opt/graph2otel`) and diffing the panel/alert exprs against the series actually present in Mimir.

The M6 artifact guide flagged this risk ("exact metric-name normalization depends on the operator's OTLP→Prometheus pipeline… queries may need a one-line adjustment") but the artifacts were authored with **no** live Mimir to validate against. There is one now, so here is the confirmed mapping.

## Normalization actually applied by Grafana Cloud

- gauge with unit `1` → `_ratio` (e.g. `graph2otel.scrape.success` → `graph2otel_scrape_success_ratio`)
- gauge with time unit → `_seconds` (`graph2otel.scrape.staleness` → `graph2otel_scrape_staleness_seconds`)
- gauge with percent unit → `_percent` (`entra.secure_score.percentage` → `entra_secure_score_percentage_percent`)
- counter → `_total` (`graph2otel.export.jobs` → `graph2otel_export_jobs_total`)
- histogram → `_seconds_bucket`/`_count`/`_sum`

## Confirmed dashboard fixes (panel blank until corrected)

| dashboard expr uses | live series is |
| --- | --- |
| `graph2otel_scrape_success` | `graph2otel_scrape_success_ratio` |
| `graph2otel_scrape_duration` | `graph2otel_scrape_duration_seconds` |
| `graph2otel_scrape_staleness` | `graph2otel_scrape_staleness_seconds` |
| `graph2otel_build_info` | `graph2otel_build_info_ratio` |
| `graph2otel_tenant_license_tier` | `graph2otel_tenant_license_tier_ratio` |
| `graph2otel_export_jobs` | `graph2otel_export_jobs_total` |
| `graph2otel_http_client_request_duration_bucket` | `graph2otel_http_client_request_duration_seconds_bucket` |
| `entra_secure_score_percentage` | `entra_secure_score_percentage_percent` |
| `entra_mfa_admin_mfa_capable_total` | `entra_mfa_registration_admin_mfa_capable_total` |
| `intune_compliance_policy_version` | `intune_compliance_policy_version_ratio` |
| `intune_config_profile_version` | `intune_config_profile_version_ratio` |
| `intune_enrollment_config_priority` | `intune_enrollment_config_priority_ratio` |
| `intune_enrollment_config_version` | `intune_enrollment_config_version_ratio` |
| `intune_update_ring_pause_state` | `intune_update_ring_pause_state_ratio` |
| `intune_update_ring_rollback_active` | `intune_update_ring_rollback_active_ratio` |

`entra_mfa_admin_mfa_capable_total` is a plain typo (missing `_registration_`); the rest are the missing OTEL suffix.

## Confirmed alert fix

`alerts/graph2otel-alerts.yaml` — the **collector-staleness primary rule** queries `graph2otel_scrape_staleness`; the live series is `graph2otel_scrape_staleness_seconds`. As written the rule matches nothing and never fires. Fix the expr (and audit the other rules against the mapping above).

## Not-a-bug on this tenant (do NOT "fix" by renaming)

These panel names are correct but had no series on the m7kni lab (license/feature-gated or no such objects): `entra_risky_users_total`, `entra_risky_service_principals_total` (P2), `intune_uxa_*` (Endpoint Analytics not onboarded), `intune_wip_policy_count` (WIP deprecated), `intune_malware_overview_by_severity|by_category`, `graph2otel_series_*`, `graph2otel_throttle_*`, `intune_certificate_*`, `intune_autopilot_stale_contact_count`, `intune_app_protection_policy_count`. A couple of these (`graph2otel_throttle_limit_percentage`, `graph2otel_checkpoint_persist_errors`) may themselves gain a `_percent`/`_total` suffix once they emit — verify on a tenant that produces them.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Dashboards corrected per the table and redeployed; panels populate against a live stack
- [ ] Alert staleness rule (and any others) corrected against the mapping
- [ ] A short note in the dashboards/alerts README on the suffix convention actually observed
- [ ] Verified live (m7kni) that corrected panels/alerts resolve

Discovered during the live camden deployment. Part of #79.
title: Dashboards + alerts use pre-normalization metric names (missing OTLP→Prometheus unit/type suffixes)

body:
## Mission

Take graph2otel to **v1.0.0**: a production-quality, multi-tenant Go exporter that pulls every useful Entra ID / Intune / Defender / M365 / Purview signal from Microsoft Graph (or the agreed fallbacks) and pushes OTEL **metrics + logs** via OTLP to Grafana Cloud — far enough to **retire the traditional diagnostic-settings → Log Analytics → Event Hub → Azure Function → Grafana Cloud pipeline**.

This is the parent tracker. **If context is lost mid-effort, a successor resumes from this issue + its comments alone.**

## How to use this tracker

- **The worklist is `gh issue list --state open` — not a list in this body.** Two previous versions of this body enumerated per-issue state and both rotted within a day. This body holds only: mission, current state, a *grouping* of the open set, decisions, and operating rules. Per-issue state lives on each issue.
- **Every open issue is a v1 gate** (maintainer decision 2026-07-16, reaffirmed 2026-07-17 — including the #119–#127 feature backlog). Sole exception: **#78**, Renovate's Dependency Dashboard, permanently open by design; not a gate.
- **Body-freshness rule (applies to every issue in this repo):** when a comment reverses a claim in an issue body, edit the body the same day — a strikethrough + pointer is enough. If you find a body contradicting its comments, the newest comment wins; fix the body before moving on.
- **Any "do not X yet" instruction must name its unblock condition** so a later reader can check whether it has fired. An unconditioned "do not start" caused real damage (#106's stale stop order outlived the thing it was waiting for).
- **Every do-not-redo / verified-fact entry carries its evidence class**: `live-measured (date, #issue)`, `docs-only`, or `n=1`. Docs-only and n=1 entries are cheap to re-open; live-measured ones are not. Wrong verdicts hardened into do-not-redo armor cost this project days (#100, #109, #130).

## Current state (2026-07-17)

- **58 collectors shipped** across Entra / Intune / Defender / M365 / Purview — see `docs/collectors.md` (generated from the registry, drift-gated). Framework: `internal/logpipeline` (watermark window polling), `internal/jobpipeline` + `internal/exportjob` (async jobs), `internal/blobpipeline` (Azure Storage byte-offset ingest), `internal/o365pipeline` + `internal/o365activityclient` (O365 Management Activity API). `make check` green.
- **Live on camden** (`/opt/graph2otel`, tracks the `:main` edge image) as the dedicated least-privilege identity `graph2otel-poller` (cert auth; 30+ read-only Graph app scopes plus 2 O365 Management API roles). Metrics + logs verified in Grafana Cloud (gb-south).
- **Blob fallback ingest is live** (#89, closed): diagnostic settings → Azure Storage account → `blobpipeline` consumer, ~£3.07/mo steady-state (live-measured 2026-07-17, #137; the £0.85 was mid-backfill). Currently reading `MicrosoftGraphActivityLogs` + three sign-in categories; the remaining categories are #135's worklist. `docs/blob-ingest.md` is the reference — read it before touching anything blob-shaped.
- **`m365.activity` shipped default-on** over the O365 Management Activity API (#100 — note its earlier "won't-do" close was reached on the wrong question and reversed; residual items live on the issue).
- **Observability artifacts deployed**: 3 dashboards + 10 alert rules (folder `graph2otel`), Pyroscope profiling, and the `entra-security-g2o` burn-in alert group evaluating in parallel with the legacy group (muted via `g2o-burnin-silent`; cutover = unmute + retire legacy).

## The open set, grouped

State per issue lives **on the issue**; this is only a map. Regenerate the real list with `gh issue list --state open`; the groups below are also queryable as labels (`program/blob`, `kind/gate`, `kind/spike`, `kind/residual`, `kind/feature`, `bug`, `needs-rob`).

- **Blob-ingest program**: #128 (blob→metrics spike), #132 (Intune category shape — the one real dual-ship win, gates the biggest possible poll saving), #134 (three unknown categories), #135 (map the remaining categories), #137 (post-backfill re-measure — quietly gates parts of #135 and #138), #138 (at-least-once dedupe decision), #129 (synthesize a risk event to verify mappings).
- **Correctness / gates**: #140 (emitted-signal drift gate), #141 (provenance attribute + attribute registry), #142 (export-report enum codes), #143 (`tenant_id` docs/dashboards), #126 residual (403-narrowing + guard test), #100 residual, #147 (cold-checkpoint job adoption), #146 (this reorganisation).
- **Build work**: #106 (Defender tables via the Storage path), #102 (blocked on a human: Purview-side S&C PowerShell registration, not a Graph scope), #85 residual (rate-limiter headroom panel + profiling docs), #116 (cache spike — its sequencing gate #117/#118 has lifted), #133 (three uncovered Identity Protection signals), #145 (MDCA Cloud Discovery governance-log collector — silent parse failures), #119–#125 + #127 (feature collectors: M365 service health, SharePoint/OneDrive storage, Teams inventory, licensing state, sync errors, Intune OS versions, joint user counts, sharing posture).
**Recommended order (maintainer-agreed, 2026-07-17):** work `kind/gate` + `bug` before building any more collectors — #140/#141 are one registry approached from two ends, and every collector built after they land is cheaper to verify (same logic as the existing config drift gate). The four maintainer-only tenant actions are batched in **#148**; agents skip anything it gates rather than waiting. Feature collectors (`kind/feature`) come last. Time-ripe checks: #134's 24h observation bar has passed and #137's backfill has had a day to settle — both are cheap to check and #137 unblocks three other items.

- **Fleet-parity / ops tooling** (`program/fleet-parity`, 2026-07-20 audit vs `opnsense-exporter` + `tailscale2otel`): #209–#220. The collector/signal surface is ahead of both siblings and the console/runtime core is at or ahead of parity — these are the **tooling + observability-as-code** gaps only. Release tooling: #209 (notices.sh/sbom.sh + `/licenses`), #210 (pre-commit hook), #214 (helm schema + helm-docs), #216 (coverage→Codacy, `needs-rob` on `CODACY_PROJECT_TOKEN`). Operator console: #211 (config tab), #215 (cardinality tab — data already computed, just unrendered), #217 (pprof-pull `kind/spike`, valid to close won't-do). Config: #212 (`*_file` for OTLP/Pyroscope egress secrets). Docs: #213 (dashboard/alert deploy path). **Observability-as-code tier** (the widest divergence): #218 (dashboards-as-code — metric catalogue + builder + coverage gate + CI, `kind/gate`, folds in #162's log panels), #219 (alert/recording-rule generator), #220 (Microsoft Graph **beta** drift canary, `kind/gate`). See the audit comment below for the full findings, the N/A list, and where graph2otel is ahead.
- **Umbrella**: #86 — closes when #102 + #106 + coverage validation + the Azure-side export retirement all land.
- **Release**: #35 — Gate 0 is "this list empty"; Gate 1 (release mechanics) is on that issue.

## Decisions already made — do not re-litigate

- **Go 1.26.x**, single static binary, distroless container. House style follows tailscale2otel.
- **OTLP push only** (gRPC/HTTP/stdout). No Prometheus scrape endpoint in v1.
- **Multi-tenant from day one** — per-tenant checkpoints, rate limiters, telemetry resource attrs.
- **Raw REST for all collectors** via the `internal/graphclient` helpers + the pipeline engines. `msgraph-sdk-go` remains in the tree for exactly **one** call site (`internal/license/graphclient_adapter.go`, subscribedSkus) — do not add typed-SDK usage, and do not "clean up" that one either. Beta endpoints via `BaseURLOverride` + `Experimental()` opt-in (default off).
- Auth via `azidentity.DefaultAzureCredential`.
- **OTEL core v1.44.0 + sdk/log v0.20.0 as a lockstep pair** (Renovate-grouped).
- **The cardinality rule is a DATA-MODELING rule, not a privacy control** (#112). Metrics carry bounded aggregates; logs carry entities; "not a metric label" means **log twin, never dropped** (#114). PII in logs is by design — graph2otel is a SIEM feed.
- **Fallback transport = Azure Storage blobs** (#89, live-measured; Log Analytics and Event Hub evaluated and rejected — LA cannot delete or receive Defender streaming, Event Hub costs £8.34/mo for ~12s of latency).
- **Graph vs blob is mutually exclusive per collector**, enforced by config `ConflictsWith` (#144). #131 examined the "dual-ship" alternative and closed confirming mutual exclusion was right (only real dual candidate: `intune.devices`, split to #132).
- **OTLP→Prometheus normalization is real and verified**: gauges gain `_ratio`/`_seconds`/`_percent`, counters `_total`; dashboards/alerts must use normalized names (#82).
- **Log attributes are Loki structured metadata, not stream labels** (#90). `{event_name="…"}` matches zero rows silently.
- **Versioning**: release-please from 0.1.0; v1.0.0 needs a manual version override (no `feat!` markers exist, so release-please computes 0.x forever).

## Honest scope — corrected 2026-07-17

- **Permanent gaps, re-audited against the non-Graph first-party API surface** (live-verified as `graph2otel-poller`): `EnrichedOffice365AuditLogs` (Sentinel-side synthesis, no source API), `ADFSSignInLogs`, Intune `OperationalLogs` (fired-alert stream; Graph has only the templates; the dedicated Intune API exposes zero app-only roles), Purview **retention** labels (Application: Not supported), DLP **policy enumeration** (Purview APIs evaluate content, never enumerate policy).
- **Previously claimed as gaps, corrected**: `NetworkAccessTrafficLogs` HAS a beta Graph endpoint that names its own scope (#130 — closed; out of scope until a GSA tenant exists). Purview **sensitivity** labels work app-only with `SensitivityLabel.Read` (#126 — collector rebuilt; bind `name`, not the always-null `displayName`).
- **Escape hatch** for blob-only categories: the Storage ingest path — `docs/blob-ingest.md`.

## Operating rules (for any agent picking this up)

- GitHub issues are the source of truth: read each issue **in full including comments** before implementing; keep it live; close via `Closes #NN`; commit straight to `main` and push (bypass output is expected).
- Strict TDD per CLAUDE.md; std-lib `testing` only; `make check` green as evidence before any issue closes.
- **Validate an issue's premise against the live tenant before implementing** — and probe as `graph2otel-poller`, never another app identity (#109's wrong verdict came from probing with the wrong identity/scope).
- **Wire over docs.** Microsoft's documentation has been wrong on essentially every load-bearing detail on this path (blob layout, timestamp formats, enum casing, latency, expiry, record-type coverage). Never assert an API behavior from docs alone; measure it, then tag the fact `live-measured`.
- Sub-agents never commit; the coordinating thread commits and **verifies every diff itself** — a returned brief is not evidence of correct work.
- Live-tenant mutations (new app registrations, scope grants, diagnostic settings) require naming exact scopes and explicit maintainer approval first.

## History — phase plan (all implementation phases complete)

- [x] **M1 Core framework** (#2–#13)
- [x] **M2 Entra metrics** (#36 #39 #43–#48 #58 #66 #68–#75)
- [x] **M3 Entra logs** (#18–#25)
- [x] **M4 Intune metrics** (#49–#67)
- [x] **M5 Intune logs + export jobs** (#14–#17 #37 #38 #40–#42)
- [x] **M6 Ops & docs** (#26–#34)
- [x] **Cardinality reframe + log-twin sweep** (#110–#115)
- [x] **Hardening + log-export replacement rounds** (#83–#118 — see the consolidated history comment below for the issue→SHA ledger)
- [x] **Blob ingest + O365 Management Activity** (#89, #100, #135 first slice)
- [ ] **Pre-v1 open set** (grouping above)
- [ ] **v1.0.0 cut** (#35)

The phase-completion comments below are the issue→SHA ledger for the ~100 closed issues. Body last rewritten **2026-07-17** (third rewrite; see #146 for why).

## Deferred (parked, need Rob)

- **Codacy coverage** (needs CODACY_PROJECT_TOKEN) — dropped from ci.yml.
- **Claude issue-triage workflow** (needs CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN) — not ported.
- **Prometheus pull bridge** — deliberately out of v1.
- **`entra-security-g2o` cutover** — burn-in group live but muted; unmute + retire the legacy group when confident.

### The M1 gate is met

The **429-retry regression test passes** — a 429 with no `Retry-After` is retried, not surfaced — which is the fix for the latent m365-exporter "silent no-retry" bug (the SDK adapter drops Kiota's default middleware chain when handed a custom client; we re-attach it via `NewCustomTransportWithParentTransport(GetDefaultMiddlewares()...)`). Additionally the auth + Graph-client stack was **verified live end-to-end against a real Entra tenant** (token acquisition, typed `Organization().Get`, and the raw-REST escape hatch all succeeded).

### How it was built

Shared seams frozen first (the `telemetry.Emitter` interface, the collector interfaces, the expanded `config.Config`), then fanned out across parallel sub-agent lanes on disjoint packages, with all wiring/integration/commits on the coordinating thread. `#6`+`#9` were fused into one lane because the donor bakes the self-obs triad into the scheduler (one-file-one-owner). Every lane was std-lib `testing` only, TDD, and gate-green before its issue closed.

- **Collectors config is map-shaped** (`map[string]CollectorConfig` + per-tenant override maps), not the donor's struct-per-collector, because ~40 collectors + per-tenant overrides land in M2–M5.

- **Composition root is intentionally minimal for M1:** run mode boots the telemetry provider + admin server + `build_info` only. - `msgraph-sdk-go` compile cost is real (first build pulls a large tree) but accepted per the M4 decision; the beta-SDK-vs-raw-REST call is deferred to M4 (the raw-REST escape hatch on the instrumented+retrying transport is already available for beta endpoints).

### How it was built

Froze the M2 collector seam first — an `internal/collectors` self-registration registry (a new collector = a new subpackage + one blank-import line, never an edit to shared wiring), shared Graph query helpers (`Count`, `GetAllValues`, `CountViaCollection`, `EventualHeaders`), `graphclient.RawGetWithHeaders`, `Deps.Caps` for license-partial-degrade, and a beta opt-in seam (`collectors.Experimental` + `config.CollectorExplicitlyEnabled`). ### Live verification (the real payoff)

Ran the actual binary against a real Entra tenant (P2-licensed). **All 18 collectors run; ~41 domain metric series emit end to end.** This caught three bugs unit tests structurally couldn't, all fixed + regression-tested:
- `$count` serves `text/plain` → HTTP **415** under `Accept: application/json` (fixed in `collectors.Count`).

Maintainer confirmed each. Net effect: **one issue closed, one greenlit, one rescoped, one pending evidence — plus two new pre-v1 issues surfaced by the discussion.**

The validation it asked for came back positive: `entra.security_alerts` carries `severity`/`category`/`service_source`/`detection_source`/`incident_id` (`securityalerts.go:94-105`) — everything the canonical `entra-defender-crit` rule filters on — and the rule was **actually recreated** on those signals as `g2o-defender-crit` (`health=ok`) in the #90 burn-in. ### #106 — GREENLIT for v1. Full table set, config-gated

Not a scope decision any more. *"No point going half in"* — the bounded-subset option was rejected. `AlertInfo`/`AlertEvidence` absorbed from #93.

**The "cost" question got a real answer, and it changes the design.** I had been vague; asked to be precise (processing or dollars?), the honest answer is **neither**. `runHuntingQuery` has no per-query charge. The binding constraint is a **tenant-wide CPU quota** ([verified](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-xdr/api-advanced-hunting)): 30-day lookback, 100k rows/query, ~45 calls/min, and **at 100% CPU consumption queries are BLOCKED until the next 15-minute cycle** (429).

That quota is **shared with the security team's own Defender-portal queries**. So a polling design's real risk is not money — it is **429-ing a human mid-investigation**. An exporter that degrades the tool it feeds is a bad trade. Which makes the pub/sub instinct likely right: Defender's streaming API pushes the same tables to Event Hub with **zero hunting-CPU consumption**.

### #89 — RESCOPED: evaluation-first spike, still a v1 gate

Two criteria: **cheapest** and **most data**. One transport wins, not both. **Deletion mandatory either way.** Infra provisioning authorised (az CLI; guided UI steps where the API cannot reach). Full context captured on the issue.

Flagged as the likely crux: **the deletion asymmetry.** LA has a real purge API (async, coarse, throttled); Event Hub has no delete at all — "deleted" means checkpointing a consumer group and letting retention expire. If the existing Event Hub already has long retention, **consuming it may reduce no cost at all**, which would undercut the mission. Also flagged: `EnrichedOffice365AuditLogs` is Sentinel-side ML enrichment synthesized downstream, so it may exist in LA and **never reach an Event Hub** — that single fact could decide the transport.

**#89 now gates #106.** Both face the same poll-vs-pub/sub fork; if #89 picks Event Hub, #106 reuses the same infra for ~zero marginal cost. Decided separately, we would maintain two ingest architectures for no reason. **Sequence: #89 evaluates → #106 matches.**

### #100 — live-verifying now

Chose evidence over assumption. An audit query for `complianceDLPSharePoint`/`complianceDLPExchange`/`dlpEndpoint` over a 7-day window is running against the live tenant. Interim finding worth recording: **the query has been `running` for >10 minutes** — the audit query API is far slower than the collector's 30-min interval assumes. Verdict to follow.

## Two new pre-v1 issues from this discussion

- **Async-job resumability + restart data-loss + configurable backfill** (spike running). The concern: `jobpipeline`/`exportjob` create a job then poll it, but the checkpoint stores only `{watermark, overlap_window, seen_ids}` — **no in-flight job id**, so a restart mid-job likely orphans it and re-creates (wasting quota on APIs that 429 hard). Expanded to cover the bigger question: **can logs be lost on restart at all?** Prime suspect is the `MaxWindow` clamp (e.g. `maxWindow = 24h` in unifiedaudit) — if the window is clamped AND the watermark advances to the clamped end, an outage longer than `MaxWindow` **silently skips** the gap forever. Requirement: no log loss on restart, backfill on a **configurable** window. Metrics can stay near-realtime.
- **#116** — cache-layer epic (Redis sidecar or similar). Deliberately framed sceptically: #87 already found the one duplicate read and fixed it **in-process** (`devicefleet.go`), checkpoints are already durable on disk, and graph2otel is **deliberately single-instance** — which is the only thing an external cache is structurally good at. On a huge tenant the bottleneck is likely Graph's own throttles and page-walk time, and **a cache does not make the first fetch cheaper**. Spike must measure before designing; "in-process + a persistent volume is enough" is a successful outcome.

## Fleet-parity audit — graph2otel vs `opnsense-exporter` + `tailscale2otel` (2026-07-20)

Ran a three-way comparison of graph2otel against the two mature fleet exporters across dev/CI/docs
tooling, observability-as-code, and runtime/product architecture (all findings from reading actual
source in the three repos). Filed the gaps as **#209–#220**, all `program/fleet-parity`, milestone M6,
v1.0 gates. This comment is the durable record of *why* each exists so a successor doesn't re-derive it.

### Headline

graph2otel is **not behind on features**. Its collector/signal surface (58+ collectors) is ahead of
both siblings, and its **runtime core is at or ahead of parity** — multi-tenancy, the
SnapshotCollector+WindowCollector model, license/permission skip-gating, checkpoint depth, per-tenant
self-obs, and `config.Secret` redaction all exceed the fleet. The gaps are entirely in **tooling and
observability-as-code**, in three bands:

**Band 1 — cheap parity (mechanical, low risk):** #209 notices.sh/sbom.sh scripts + `/licenses`
(artifacts exist inline in `publish.yml:49-79` / `release-please.yml`; repo already self-flags this at
`publish.yml:46-48`), #210 pre-commit hook + `make install-hooks`, #211 console config tab (secrets
presence-only; `config.Secret` in `internal/config/secret.go` already redacts), #212 `*_file` for the
OTLP token + Pyroscope password (only `mdca.token_file` exists today; tenant auth stays on the
`azidentity` chain — out of scope), #213 deploy-path doc, #214 helm `values.schema.json` + helm-docs.

**Band 2 — high-value self-obs (medium):** #215 console cardinality tab — the data is **already
computed** (`internal/telemetry/cardinality.go`, `CardinalityTracker`, `#105`) and simply not rendered;
cheapest big win. #216 coverage→Codacy (non-gating job; `needs-rob` — needs `CODACY_PROJECT_TOKEN`;
this is the item already parked under "Deferred" in the body). #217 pprof-pull spike (optional; graph2otel
already pushes all profile types to Pyroscope, so pull is additive — a won't-do close is legitimate).

**Band 3 — the real maturity-tier gap, observability-as-code (large):** #218 dashboards-as-code. Today
3 hand-written JSON dashboards, **no builder, no metric-coverage gate, no CI validation** — nothing
forces a new metric onto a panel, the exact drift opnsense's `coverage()` gate exists to prevent.
Two-step: extract a machine-readable metric catalogue (t2o `tools/metricscatalog`), then a builder with
a coverage gate wired into `ci-success` (opnsense `grafana/build_dashboard.py`). Folds in **#162**
(zero log panels ship — build them into the generator). #219 converts the 12 hand-written alerts + 2
recording rules to a single-source generator so they regen-gate (lower priority; the alert *content* and
docs are strong). #220 Microsoft Graph **beta** drift canary — neither the emitted-signal goldens (#140)
nor anything else diffs the upstream Graph surface; scope to beta (v1.0 is contractually stable),
spec-diff against a committed OpenAPI/CSDL snapshot (t2o `tools/apidrift` pattern), not the heavier
opnsense live-payload-golden approach.

### Explicitly N/A — do not force these onto a push-only Graph exporter

- opnsense's **reflected live-payload golden schemas** + `cmd/apidrift` scrape-canary (needs a CI test
  tenant + app creds; #220 does the lighter spec-diff instead).
- **Volatility tiers** (fast/med/slow/cold) — graph2otel's per-collector `DefaultInterval()` + config
  override is the right model; no named tiers needed.
- **Snapshot/scrape decoupling** — N/A, push-only.
- **Console inventory/devices tab** — no cached device inventory to browse in a push model (opnsense's
  devices/OUI view is scrape-model-specific).
- **OTLP trace export** — the span plumbing exists (`scheduler.go` `WithTracer`) but wiring a trace
  exporter is low downstream value; not filed.
- **Prometheus pull bridge** — deliberately out of v1 (already recorded under "Deferred").
- **`_file` for tenant auth** — `azidentity.DefaultAzureCredential`'s own chain is correct; hand-rolling
  `_file` there would be a regression.
- tailscale2otel has **no Makefile at all**, so "graph2otel's Makefile is lean" is not a real gap.

### Where graph2otel is ahead (do not regress while chasing parity)

Native multi-tenancy (per-tenant scheduler/registry/checkpoint/rate-limits), the two-shape collector
model, license/permission gating with skip-reasons on the console, `internal/checkpoint` depth,
per-tenant `graph2otel.scrape.*` self-metrics, thorough `config.Secret` redaction, and **log-derived
recording rules** (`count_over_time` over Loki → recorded Prometheus metric — a pattern neither sibling
has; the #219 generator must keep supporting Loki-datasource recording rules).

### Recommended sequencing (if/when these are worked)

Band 1 is a fast cleanup sweep. Band 3 #218 is the highest-impact and gates #162; it needs the metric
catalogue built first. #216 is blocked on the token (`needs-rob`). #217 and #220 each carry an explicit
scope decision — a won't-do (#217) or beta-only-spec-diff (#220) close is a valid outcome.

## Session 2026-07-22 — #225/#226/#230/#231 closed, and a fabricated finding caught and reverted

`main` @ `d06cb83`, `make check` green. Three commits. Dashboards/alerting (#162, #218, #219) explicitly out of scope for this session.

### The part that matters most: I shipped a wrong finding, then caught it

`9a3efc0` landed a `WithBackdateClamp` on the conclusion that Grafana Cloud silently discards log records backdated beyond **~4h20m**, measured across three sweeps against the live gateway. **That finding was false**, and `65ce1ff` reverts the code built on it.

The error was in the instrument, not the reasoning on top of it: every sweep was **queried within seconds of the push**. Backdated records are indexed through a late-data path (`__time_shard__`) and are not queryable for minutes after being accepted. Re-queried later, **every record recorded as dropped was present** — 15m through 3 days, in both a production-shaped stream and a virgin one. A second, independent error compounded it: one recheck used `count_over_time({…}[24h])`, whose range excludes 2–3 day old records *by the query*, manufacturing a fake cutoff between 12h and 24h.

The real behaviour, stated by the gateway itself:

```text
400 Bad Request: entry for stream '{service_name="…"}' has timestamp too old:
2026-07-08T13:05:10Z, oldest acceptable timestamp is: 2026-07-15T13:05:10Z
```

- Accept window is **exactly 7 days** (`now-168h`).
- Rejection is **loud**, not silent.
- Rejection is **per-entry, not per-batch** — the same push had 12h/1d/2d/3d accepted while only 7d and 14d were refused, so one over-old record cannot poison a batch.

**Why the revert was mandatory, not cosmetic:** with a real 7-day window, a 3h clamp default would have relocated every record aged 3h–7d that the backend accepts perfectly well — `m365.activity`, `intune.epm_elevation_events`, every backfilling window collector — destroying the true event time of records that were never at risk, and doing it invisibly. A worse defect than the one it was built to fix, wearing the appearance of working.

**An empty Loki query is not evidence of a drop. This is the output-side twin of the existing wire-over-docs rule: never attribute an empty result to the world until the instrument has been validated.

Also this session: **#262** (`0d4bd53`, empty-id SeenIDs poisoning in the job/log pipelines), **#251** epic close-out (SecurityAnalyzedMessage handback revoked, verified), **#219** (`66b991d`, alert/recording-rule generator + `make grafana-check` gate).

**Release readiness (details on #35):** the 1.0.0 override is already applied to release PR #80, and the release-please token wiring is confirmed so its CI runs unattended. One release blocker was found and fixed today — `3967630` — the helm-docs README version badge was not being bumped alongside `Chart.yaml`, failing `helm lint + template` (hence `ci-success`) on every release PR; it now bumps atomically via release-please annotations. Once PR #80's CI re-renders green, Gate 1 is the maintainer cut: merge #80, verify the tagged artifacts, review the docs site, publish the announcement, then the burn-in→legacy cutover.

## v1.0.0 shipped — closing the launch tracker (2026-07-25)

The mission is done: graph2otel is a production-quality multi-tenant Graph→OTLP exporter, live on camden, and now cut as **v1.0.0**.

- **Gate 0 empty** — every substantive issue closed (#234 was the last).
- **Gate 1 verified and closed on #35** — v1.0.0 tag + GitHub Release, multi-arch signed GHCR image with SBOM + provenance, 5-platform binaries (checksum-verified, runs and reports `1.0.0`), and the Helm chart OCI at 1.0.0. Release PR #80 merged as `4ac6a0f2`.

Per the tracker's own rule ("closes when v1.0.0 ships"), closing it. The only open issue remaining in the repo is **#78** (Renovate's Dependency Dashboard, permanently open by design).

Post-release follow-ups live on #35 and are yours to run when ready: the release announcement (outbound), a docs-site consistency pass, independent `cosign verify`, and the burn-in→legacy pipeline cutover.

body:
## What & why

Service-principal / credential / app **sign-in activity** (usage & insights). These beta `/reports` endpoints give last-used timestamps per service principal and per app credential (by `keyId`), plus an aggregate app sign-in success/failure summary. Paired with credential expiry (#credential-expiry issue), a "credential that never signs in but is about to expire" or "enabled SP unused for 90 days" is a strong stale-workload compliance signal. **Beta-only** and **P1/P2-gated**.

## Scope

- [ ] Add collector `internal/collectors/entra/signinactivity` implementing `SnapshotCollector` (#6).
- [ ] Poll SP sign-in activity, app-credential sign-in activity, and the app sign-in summary function.
- [ ] Emit days-since-last-use gauges (per-item only near a staleness threshold; aggregate always) and app success/failure counts.
- [ ] Guard behind the beta feature flag; license-gate via #10 (P1/P2).
- [ ] Register under `entra.signin_activity` collector key (#2).

## API surface

| Endpoint | Version | App permission | Pagination | Filter/delta | Throttle bucket |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /reports/servicePrincipalSignInActivities` | **beta** | `AuditLog.Read.All` | nextLink | `$filter`, `$select`; no delta | Reporting (5 req/10s per app per tenant, no Retry-After) |
| `GET /reports/appCredentialSignInActivities` | **beta** | `AuditLog.Read.All` | nextLink | `$filter`, `$select`; no delta | Reporting |
| `GET /reports/getAzureADApplicationSignInSummary(period='D7')` | **beta** | `AuditLog.Read.All` | n/a (function) | period param; no delta | Reporting |

Docs: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/reportroot-list-serviceprincipalsigninactivities?view=graph-rest-beta , https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/appcredentialsigninactivity?view=graph-rest-beta , https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/reportroot-getazureadapplicationsigninsummary?view=graph-rest-beta

## Telemetry model

- `entra.serviceprincipal.signin.last_used_age_days{app_id,app_display_name}` (gauge) — **per-SP only above a configurable staleness threshold**; always emit `entra.serviceprincipal.signin.stale.total{threshold_days}` as the aggregate.
- `entra.app.credential.signin.last_used_age_days{app_id,key_id}` (gauge) — same near-threshold-only rule; aggregate `entra.app.credential.signin.stale.total{threshold_days}`.
- `entra.app.signin.summary.total{result}` (gauge/counter) — `result` ∈ `success|failure`, from the D7 summary.
- Cardinality: per-item series bounded by the staleness threshold set (mirrors the credential-expiry cardinality strategy); aggregate buckets always cheap.

## Constraints & gotchas

- **Beta-only** — wrap behind the beta feature flag; schema subject to change.
- **P1/P2-gated** — usage/insights reports require P1/P2 at the tenant level. Detect via #10, skip-and-log on Free.
- Reporting workload (5 req/10s per app per tenant, **no `Retry-After`**) — the limiter (#5) owns backoff. These endpoints share the reporting bucket with the M3 sign-in log pollers, so budget accordingly.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Tests against the `Recorder` (#8) with a faked Graph client: per-item series emitted only above the staleness threshold; aggregate stale counts and the app success/failure summary emit correctly.
- [ ] Test that the collector is off unless the beta flag is enabled, and skipped-and-logged on a non-P1 tenant (#10).
- [ ] `make check` green.

## Dependencies

- #4, #5, #6, #8, #10 (P1/P2 gate).

comments.body: Done in d4f2cae. `internal/collectors/entra/signinactivity` emits bounded aggregates from the beta usage-insights reports: `entra.serviceprincipal.signin.stale.total` and `entra.app.credential.signin.stale.total` by threshold_days (30|90), and `entra.app.signin.summary.total` by result. Beta + P1/P2 gated (Experimental + RequiredCapability). **The issue's per-SP/per-credential last-used-age gauge was intentionally not emitted** — app_id/app_display_name/key_id as metric labels violate the cardinality rule (the number of stale workloads is unbounded by tenant); that per-item detail belongs in the logs pipeline (M3/M5), consistent with the credential-expiry collector. `AuditLog.Read.All`. **Live-verified end to end** — stale aggregates and the D7 success/failure summary emit against the real tenant.

## What & why

Entra recommendations: Microsoft's own tenant-posture scoreboard (`/directory/recommendations`), giving counts of recommendations by status and priority plus impacted-resource counts. A cheap "what does Microsoft think this tenant should fix" gauge. **Beta-only** — the endpoint lives on `/beta`, so it must sit behind a feature flag and be treated as schema-unstable.

## Scope

- [ ] Add collector `internal/collectors/entra/recommendations` implementing `SnapshotCollector` (#6).
- [ ] Poll `GET /directory/recommendations` (beta); emit counts by status/priority and impacted-resource counts.
- [ ] Guard behind the beta feature flag; do not enable by default.
- [ ] Register under `entra.recommendations` collector key (#2).

## API surface

| Endpoint | Version | App permission | Pagination | Filter/delta | Throttle bucket |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /directory/recommendations` | **beta** | `DirectoryRecommendations.Read.All` | nextLink | `$filter`, `$select`; no delta | Directory |
| `GET /directory/recommendations/{id}/impactedResources` | **beta** | `DirectoryRecommendations.Read.All` | nextLink | `$select`; no delta | Directory |

Docs: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/directory-list-recommendation?view=graph-rest-beta

## Telemetry model

- `entra.recommendations.total{status,priority}` (gauge) — `status` ∈ `active|completedByUser|completedBySystem|dismissed|postponed`; `priority` ∈ `high|medium|low`. Bounded.
- `entra.recommendations.impacted_resources.total{recommendation}` (gauge) — `recommendation` bounded by the (small) recommendation-type catalog.
- Cardinality: bounded by the recommendation catalog. Small.

## Constraints & gotchas

- **Beta-only** — schema subject to change; wrap behind a feature flag and treat any shape change defensively.
- License coverage varies: some recommendation types are feature-gated per P1/P2, so a Free tenant simply sees fewer recommendations rather than an error — no hard single-tier gate, so no #10 dependency (but degrade cleanly if the endpoint 403s on an unlicensed tenant).
- No delta — full read each cycle (bounded catalog).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Tests against the `Recorder` (#8) with a faked Graph client: status/priority counts and impacted-resource counts emit correctly.
- [ ] Test that the collector is off unless the beta flag is enabled.
- [ ] Test graceful handling of a 403/unavailable response (skip-and-log, no crash).
- [ ] `make check` green.

## Dependencies

- #4, #5, #6, #8.

Marked `collectors.Experimental` (opt-in, off by default — beta schema is unstable); a 403/404 is skipped-and-logged, not an error. `DirectoryRecommendations.Read.All`. **Live-verified end to end** (with the beta collector explicitly enabled + the scope granted) — status/priority and impacted-resource counts emit against the real tenant.

## What & why

Terms-of-use agreements posture: count of agreements and per-agreement acceptance counts (accepted vs pending). Useful for compliance programs that require attested terms. Terms of Use is a P1 feature, so the collector degrades gracefully on Free tenants.

## Scope

- [ ] Add collector `internal/collectors/entra/agreements` implementing `SnapshotCollector` (#6).
- [ ] Poll agreements and (aggregate) acceptance counts.
- [ ] License-gate via #10 (P1); skip-and-log otherwise.
- [ ] Register under `entra.agreements` collector key (#2).

## API surface

| Endpoint | Version | App permission | Pagination | Filter/delta | Throttle bucket |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /identityGovernance/termsOfUse/agreements` | v1.0 | `Agreement.Read.All` | nextLink | `$select`; no delta | Directory / governance |
| `GET /identityGovernance/termsOfUse/agreements/{id}/acceptances` | v1.0 | `AgreementAcceptance.Read.All` | nextLink | `$select`; no delta | Directory / governance |

Docs: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/agreement-list?view=graph-rest-1.0

## Telemetry model

- `entra.agreements.total` (gauge) — count of agreements.
- `entra.agreements.acceptances.total{agreement,state}` (gauge) — `state` ∈ `accepted|pending`; `agreement` bounded by the (small) agreement set. Acceptance **events** → logs (M3) if wanted.
- Cardinality: bounded by agreement count. Acceptances scale with users → **aggregate counts, never per-user series**.

## Constraints & gotchas

- Two permissions: `Agreement.Read.All` for the agreements, `AgreementAcceptance.Read.All` for acceptances — request both only if the acceptance gauge is enabled.
- **P1-gated** (Terms of Use is a P1 feature). Detect via #10, skip-and-log on Free.
- No delta — full read each cycle (small collection).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Tests against the `Recorder` (#8) with a faked Graph client: agreement count and per-agreement accepted/pending counts emit correctly.
- [ ] Test that on a non-P1 tenant the collector skips-and-logs.
- [ ] Test that acceptances are aggregated, not per-user.
- [ ] `make check` green.

## Dependencies

- #4, #5, #6, #8, #10 (P1 gate).

comments.body: Done in 22c42d1. `internal/collectors/entra/agreements` emits `entra.agreements.total` and `entra.agreements.acceptances.total` by agreement × state (accepted|declined; there is no 'pending' acceptance record in Graph). Whole-collector P1 gate, bounded, no per-user series. `Agreement.Read.All` + `AgreementAcceptance.Read.All`. **Live-verified end to end** — this also resolves the app-only-auth concern I flagged: the endpoint DOES work under application permissions once `Agreement.Read.All` is granted (the earlier failure was a missing grant, not an unsupported auth model).

## What & why

Tenant authentication-methods **policy** config: which methods (FIDO2, Authenticator, SMS, voice, TAP, etc.) are enabled and their target scope. "Legacy method still enabled tenant-wide" (e.g. SMS) is a direct compliance signal. This is config state, distinct from the registration *report* (which counts users) covered separately.

## Scope

- [ ] Add collector `internal/collectors/entra/authmethodspolicy` implementing `SnapshotCollector` (#6).
- [ ] Poll `GET /policies/authenticationMethodsPolicy`; emit a per-method enabled gauge.
- [ ] Register under `entra.auth_methods_policy` collector key (#2).

## API surface

| Endpoint | Version | App permission | Pagination | Filter/delta | Throttle bucket |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /policies/authenticationMethodsPolicy` | v1.0 | `Policy.Read.All` (or `Policy.Read.AuthenticationMethod`) | single object | `$select`; no delta | Directory / policy |

Docs: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/authenticationmethodspolicy-get?view=graph-rest-1.0

## Telemetry model

- `entra.auth_methods_policy.method.enabled{method}` (gauge, 0/1) — `method` bounded (`fido2|microsoftAuthenticator|sms|voice|temporaryAccessPass|email|...`).
- Optional `entra.auth_methods_policy.legacy_enabled.total` — convenience count of enabled methods flagged legacy (e.g. SMS/voice) for alerting.
- Cardinality: one series per method configuration state — bounded by the method catalog.

## Constraints & gotchas

- Single object — full read each cycle, no delta.
- Method-config **changes** are tracked via directory audits (M3), not here.
- Free to read; no `#10` dependency (some individual method *features* need P1/P2 but reading the policy does not).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Tests against the `Recorder` (#8) with a faked Graph client: per-method enabled gauges emit with the correct bounded `method` values.
- [ ] Test the legacy-method convenience count.
- [ ] `make check` green.

## Dependencies

- #4, #5, #6, #8.

## What & why

Identity Protection current-risk gauges: counts of risky **users** and risky **service principals** by risk level and state. These are the point-in-time "how much risk is live right now" numbers (the discrete risk-detection *events* are a separate log stream in M3). Merged into one collector because both live under `/identityProtection`, share the very-low Identity-Protection throttle bucket, and are individually small — but they carry **two different license gates** (see below).

## Scope

- [ ] Add collector `internal/collectors/entra/risk` implementing `SnapshotCollector` (#6).
- [ ] Poll risky users and risky service principals; emit count gauges by level/state.
- [ ] License-gate each half independently via #10 (risky users → P2; risky SPs → Workload Identities Premium); skip-and-log the ungated half.
- [ ] Register under `entra.risk` collector key (#2).

## API surface

| Endpoint | Version | App permission | Pagination | Filter/delta | Throttle bucket |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /identityProtection/riskyUsers` | v1.0 | `IdentityRiskyUser.Read.All` | nextLink | `$filter(riskLevel, riskState)`, `$count`; no delta | **Identity Protection: 1 req/s per tenant, no Retry-After** |
| `GET /identityProtection/riskyServicePrincipals` | v1.0 | `IdentityRiskyServicePrincipal.Read.All` | nextLink | `$filter`, `$count`; no delta | Same IPC bucket |

Docs: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/identityprotectionroot-list-riskyusers?view=graph-rest-1.0 , https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/identityprotectionroot-list-riskyserviceprincipals?view=graph-rest-1.0

## Telemetry model

- `entra.risky_users.total{risk_level,risk_state}` (gauge) — `risk_level` ∈ `low|medium|high|hidden|none`; `risk_state` ∈ `atRisk|confirmedCompromised|remediated|dismissed|...`. Bounded.
- `entra.risky_service_principals.total{risk_level,risk_state}` (gauge) — same bounded dimensions.
- Cardinality: bounded by level×state. **Aggregate only — never per-user or per-SP series** (identifiers are PII; belong in the risk-detection log stream, M3).

## Constraints & gotchas

- **Identity Protection throttle: 1 request/second per tenant across all apps, NO `Retry-After`.** Serialize via the IPC limiter (#5).
- **Two distinct license gates:** risky users require **P2**; risky service principals require **Workload Identities Premium** (a separate SKU). Detect each via #10 and skip-and-log the unavailable half independently — one may be present without the other. On P1 tenants, risk values may come back `hidden`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Tests against the `Recorder` (#8) with a faked Graph client: level×state counts emit for both users and SPs.
- [ ] Test that each half is skipped-and-logged independently per its license gate (P2 vs Workload ID Premium).
- [ ] Test that calls respect 1 req/s serialization.
- [ ] `make check` green.

## Dependencies

- #4, #5, #6, #8, #10 (P2 / Workload ID Premium gates).
