body:
## What & why

The OAuth consent surface: delegated permission grants (`oauth2PermissionGrants`) and application-role assignments (`appRoleAssignments`). Over-privileged consent — a delegated grant of a high-privilege scope, or an app-role assignment granting a sensitive Graph app role like `Directory.ReadWrite.All` or `Mail.Read` — is a key attack path. Aggregate counts of privileged grants/assignments are the compliance gauge; individual grants are far too numerous for per-series.

## Scope

- [ ] Add collector `internal/collectors/entra/consent` implementing `SnapshotCollector` (#6).
- [ ] Poll delegated grants and app-role assignments; classify against a bounded set of high-privilege scopes/roles.
- [ ] Emit aggregate counts by privilege classification.
- [ ] Register under `entra.consent` collector key (#2).

## API surface

| Endpoint | Version | App permission | Pagination | Filter/delta | Throttle bucket |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /oauth2PermissionGrants` | v1.0 | `Directory.Read.All` | nextLink (can be large) | `$filter(clientId, resourceId)`; delta on `oauth2PermissionGrants` | Directory objects |
| `GET /servicePrincipals/{id}/appRoleAssignedTo` / `/appRoleAssignments` | v1.0 | `Application.Read.All` | nextLink | `$select`; no delta | Directory objects |

Docs: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/oauth2permissiongrant-list?view=graph-rest-1.0 , https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/serviceprincipal-list-approleassignedto?view=graph-rest-1.0

## Telemetry model

- `entra.consent.oauth2_grants.total{privilege}` (gauge) — `privilege` ∈ `high|standard` (classified against a bounded allowlist of sensitive scopes). Optionally total grants as a separate series.
- `entra.consent.app_role_assignments.total{app_role}` (gauge) — count of assignments granting each **sensitive** Graph app role (bounded allowlist, e.g. `Directory.ReadWrite.All`, `Mail.Read`); non-sensitive assignments rolled into an aggregate total.
- Cardinality: bounded by the sensitive-scope/role allowlist. **`oauth2PermissionGrants` can be enormous** (one per user×client×resource) — never a per-grant series; aggregate/scope by privileged classification.

## Constraints & gotchas

- `oauth2PermissionGrants` is potentially very large — page via nextLink and reduce to aggregate counts as you go; delta can cut re-read cost as an optimization.
- New consent events (a log stream of who consented to what) come from directory audits (M3), not here.
- Free tier; no `#10` dependency.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Tests against the `Recorder` (#8) with a faked Graph client: privileged grants and sensitive app-role assignments counted correctly against the allowlist; non-sensitive rolled into aggregate.
- [ ] Test that a large grant set produces only bounded aggregate series (cardinality guard).
- [ ] `make check` green.

## Dependencies

- #4, #5, #6, #8.

comments.body: Done in 02f5ff5 (+ fix 9604905). `internal/collectors/entra/consent` emits `entra.consent.grants.total` by consent_type × privilege (privileged|standard) — 4 bounded series, no per-grant series. Classifies delegated oauth2 grants and app-role assignments against a bounded high-privilege allowlist; resolves app-role assignments resource-side (appRoleAssignedTo on well-known resource SPs) to avoid an unbounded per-SP fan-out. `Directory.Read.All` + `Application.Read.All`. **Live-verified end to end** — this surfaced a real bug: the resource-SP $filter lookup inlined `appId eq '…'` with raw spaces/quotes, which Graph rejects as HTTP 400; the $filter value is now URL-encoded, and both grant classifications emit against the real tenant.

## What & why

Authentication-method / MFA registration posture. The summary functions give tenant-wide gauges — how many users are MFA-registered, MFA-capable, passwordless-capable, SSPR-registered, and counts by method — without paging every user. "% of admins MFA-capable" is a direct compliance KPI. Prefer the summary functions over enumerating `userRegistrationDetails` per user.

## Scope

- [ ] Add collector `internal/collectors/entra/authmethods` implementing `SnapshotCollector` (#6).
- [ ] Poll the `usersRegisteredByFeatureSummary` / `usersRegisteredByMethodSummary` functions for aggregate gauges.
- [ ] License-gate via #10 (report requires P1/P2); skip-and-log otherwise.
- [ ] Register under `entra.auth_methods` collector key (#2).

## API surface

| Endpoint | Version | App permission | Pagination | Filter/delta | Throttle bucket |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /reports/authenticationMethods/usersRegisteredByFeatureSummary(...)` | v1.0 | `AuditLog.Read.All` | n/a (summary) | function params; no delta | Reporting |
| `GET /reports/authenticationMethods/usersRegisteredByMethodSummary(...)` | v1.0 | `AuditLog.Read.All` | n/a (summary) | function params; no delta | Reporting |
| `GET /reports/authenticationMethods/userRegistrationDetails` (optional detail) | v1.0 | `AuditLog.Read.All` | nextLink (per-user) | `$filter(isMfaRegistered, isAdmin, ...)`; no delta | Reporting |

## Telemetry model

- `entra.auth_methods.mfa_registered.total`, `.mfa_capable.total`, `.passwordless_capable.total`, `.sspr_registered.total` (gauges) — from the feature summary.
- `entra.auth_methods.registered_by_method.total{method}` (gauge) — `method` bounded (`fido2|authenticator|sms|voice|tap|...`).
- Optional `{is_admin}` slice for the admin-MFA KPI.
- Cardinality: bounded by method set. **Do not page `userRegistrationDetails` for metrics** — that is a per-user read; use it only if per-user log export is explicitly wanted.

## Constraints & gotchas

- Prefer the summary functions — one call each — over the per-user detail endpoint for the aggregate gauges.
- **P1/P2-gated:** the registration report requires P1/P2. Detect via #10 and skip-and-log on Free tenants.
- Reporting workload (5 req/10s per app per tenant, no `Retry-After`) — the limiter (#5) owns backoff.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Tests against the `Recorder` (#8) with a faked Graph client returning canned summary payloads: feature-summary gauges and per-method counts emit correctly.
- [ ] Test that on a Free tenant (#10 says not P1) the collector skips-and-logs.
- [ ] Test that the per-user detail endpoint is not used for the metric path.
- [ ] `make check` green.

## Dependencies

## What & why

Microsoft Secure Score: the tenant's daily identity/security posture score, plus per-control scores from the control-profile catalog. `entra.secure_score.current` / `.max` and the ratio are a single-number executive posture gauge; per-control scores let you see which controls drag the score down. Score is readable on Free/basic even where remediating a control needs premium features.

## Scope

- [ ] Add collector `internal/collectors/entra/securescore` implementing `SnapshotCollector` (#6).
- [ ] Poll the latest daily score (`$top=1`) and the control-profile catalog.
- [ ] Emit overall and per-control gauges.
- [ ] Register under `entra.secure_score` collector key (#2).

## API surface

| Endpoint | Version | App permission | Pagination | Filter/delta | Throttle bucket |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /security/secureScores?$top=1` | v1.0 | `SecurityEvents.Read.All` | nextLink (recent daily snapshots) | `$top`; no delta | Security workload |
| `GET /security/secureScoreControlProfiles` | v1.0 | `SecurityEvents.Read.All` | nextLink | limited `$filter`; no delta | Security workload |

Docs: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/security-list-securescores?view=graph-rest-1.0

## Telemetry model

- `entra.secure_score.current` (gauge) — latest `currentScore`.
- `entra.secure_score.max` (gauge) — `maxScore`.
- `entra.secure_score.control{control_name}` (gauge) — per-control `controlScores` (control catalog bounded, ~dozens).
- Cardinality: one overall pair + bounded per-control set. `control_name` is tenant-independent.

## Constraints & gotchas

- Use `$top=1` for the latest daily score rather than pulling the ~90-day series each cycle.
- Security workload throttle (moderate) — **not** the 1 req/s Identity-Protection bucket. No special serialization needed beyond the standard limiter (#5).
- Free/basic tier for reading the score; no `#10` dependency.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Tests against the `Recorder` (#8) with a faked Graph client: current/max gauges and a bounded set of per-control gauges emit correctly.
- [ ] Test that only the latest daily score is emitted (not the full retained series).
- [ ] `make check` green.

## Dependencies

- #4, #5, #6, #8.

## What & why

Metrics for **enrollment configuration** — the enrollment restriction / limit / ESP (`windows10EnrollmentCompletionPageConfiguration`) configs that govern how devices enroll. Emit config inventory + priority/version gauges. The enrollment **failure** event stream is a separate logs concern for a later milestone; this collector covers the snapshot config side.

SnapshotCollector, app-only read. v1.0 surface.

## Scope

- [ ] `internal/collectors/intune/enrollment` — poll `deviceEnrollmentConfigurations` (v1.0), emit inventory + priority/version gauges bucketed by config subtype
- [ ] Register under the `intune` rate-limit bucket
- [ ] Enrollment **failure** logs — `enrollmentTroubleshootingEvent` (v1.0 event stream) and the `EnrollmentFailures` export (beta) — are event/log data, deferred to the **M5 milestone**; this issue covers the enrollment-config entities only.

## API surface

| Endpoint | Version | App permission | Pagination | Filter quirks | Throttle bucket |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /deviceManagement/deviceEnrollmentConfigurations` | v1.0 | `DeviceManagementServiceConfig.Read.All` | `@odata.nextLink` | subtypes: enrollment limit, platform restrictions, ESP `windows10EnrollmentCompletionPageConfiguration` — branch on type | Standard Graph |

Docs: [deviceEnrollmentConfiguration v1.0](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/intune-onboarding-deviceenrollmentconfiguration?view=graph-rest-1.0), [enrollmentTroubleshootingEvent v1.0](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/intune-troubleshooting-enrollmenttroubleshootingevent?view=graph-rest-1.0) (M5 log source, referenced for context only).

## Telemetry model

`intune.*` namespace.

- `intune.enrollment_config.count` gauge, attrs `{config_type}` — inventory by subtype.
- `intune.enrollment_config.priority` gauge, attrs `{config_type, config_name}` — surfaces `priority` (note the lowest-wins semantics below).
- `intune.enrollment_config.version` gauge, attrs `{config_name}` — change detection.

Config names/types are bounded (small). No per-device series.

## Constraints & gotchas

- `deviceEnrollmentConfigurations.priority` is **lowest-wins** (counterintuitive) — document it on the gauge so a dashboard doesn't read a high number as "most important."
- Heterogeneous collection (limit / platform-restriction / ESP subtypes) — branch on type.
- The live enrollment-failure stream (`enrollmentTroubleshootingEvent`) and the `EnrollmentFailures` export are two independent overlapping surfaces with different columns/freshness — both are M5 logs concerns, not this collector.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] SnapshotCollector emits config inventory + priority/version gauges against the in-memory **Recorder** with a **faked Graph client** returning mixed-subtype configs; asserts type bucketing and that `version` bumps surface.
- [ ] Test: no enrollment-event/log calls attempted here.
- [ ] Graceful skip-and-log on 403 / missing scope (M1 #9).

## Dependencies

M1 #4 (client factory), #5 (rate limiters — Intune bucket), #6 (SnapshotCollector), #8 (Emitter + Recorder), #10 (license detection / degradation).

## What & why

Privileged-access posture: standing directory-role membership plus PIM active/eligible assignments. Global Admin count, count of **permanent** (non-time-bound) active assignments, and eligible-vs-active ratio per role are the headline "who has privilege and how" compliance gauges. The standing-membership half (`/directoryRoles`) is Free; the PIM half (roleManagement schedule instances) is P2-gated.

## Scope

- [ ] Add collector `internal/collectors/entra/roles` implementing `SnapshotCollector` (#6).
- [ ] Emit standing role-member counts per role.
- [ ] Emit PIM active/eligible assignment counts per role and a permanent-assignment count — P2-gated via #10.
- [ ] Register under `entra.roles` collector key (#2).

## API surface

| Endpoint | Version | App permission | Pagination | Filter/delta | Throttle bucket |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /directoryRoles` , `/directoryRoles/{id}/members` | v1.0 | `RoleManagement.Read.Directory` | nextLink | `$filter`, `$expand`; delta on directoryRole | Directory / roleManagement |
| `GET /roleManagement/directory/roleAssignmentScheduleInstances` (active) | v1.0 | `RoleManagement.Read.Directory` | nextLink | `$filter(principalId, roleDefinitionId)`, `$expand(roleDefinition)`; no delta | Directory / roleManagement |

- `entra.roles.members.total{role_name}` (gauge) — standing/active membership per directory role (`role_name` bounded by the role catalog).
- `entra.pim.assignments.total{role_name,assignment_type}` (gauge) — `assignment_type` ∈ `active|eligible`.
- `entra.pim.permanent_assignments.total{role_name}` (gauge) — active assignments with no end time.

- `$expand=roleDefinition` gives human-readable `role_name` — resolve it once, keep the label bounded to the catalog.

## What & why

Metrics for **Group Policy analytics** — the migration-readiness assessment that scores how much of an imported GPO can move to Intune. Low cardinality (bounded by GPOs/configs, not devices), cheap to poll fully, daily is plenty. Emit `migrationReadiness` and `supportedSettingsPercent` gauges. Beta-only surface (`beta-api` label).

SnapshotCollector, app-only read.

## Scope

- [ ] `internal/collectors/intune/gpoanalytics` — poll `groupPolicyMigrationReports` (beta) for readiness gauges
- [ ] Poll `groupPolicyConfigurations` (beta) inventory (with `$expand=definitionValues` where needed)
- [ ] Register under the `intune` rate-limit bucket
- [ ] Raw GPO XML (`groupPolicyObjectFile.content`) is an input artifact, not telemetry — never emitted. Any per-setting export detail (if it exists) deferred to the **M5 milestone**; this issue covers the migration-report + config entity endpoints.

## API surface

| Endpoint | Version | App permission | Pagination | Filter quirks | Throttle bucket |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /deviceManagement/groupPolicyMigrationReports` (+ `groupPolicySettingMappings`, `unsupportedGroupPolicyExtensions`) | **beta** | `DeviceManagementConfiguration.Read.All` | `@odata.nextLink` | no `$filter` documented | Standard Graph |
| `GET /deviceManagement/groupPolicyConfigurations` (+ `definitionValues`, `assignments`) | **beta** | `DeviceManagementConfiguration.Read.All` | `@odata.nextLink` | `$expand=definitionValues` to get actual values | Standard |
| `GET /deviceManagement/groupPolicyObjectFiles` | **beta** | `DeviceManagementConfiguration.Read.All` | `@odata.nextLink` | `content` is raw GPO XML — not a metric | Standard |

Docs: [groupPolicyMigrationReport beta](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/intune-gpanalyticsservice-grouppolicymigrationreport?view=graph-rest-beta).

## Telemetry model

`intune.*` namespace.

- `intune.gpo.migration_readiness` gauge, attrs `{report_name, readiness}` where `readiness` ∈ none/partial/complete/error/notApplicable.
- `intune.gpo.supported_settings_percent` gauge, attrs `{report_name}` — from `supportedSettingsCount`/`totalSettingsCount`.
- `intune.gpo.config.count` gauge, attrs `{ingestion_type}` from `policyConfigurationIngestionType`.

Report/config names are bounded (dozens–low hundreds). GPO XML never emitted.

## Constraints & gotchas

- **Beta-only** (all three resources) — pin beta endpoints.
- `groupPolicyObjectFile.content` is raw GPO XML (input artifact) — never a metric.
- Migration-report ↔ object-file link is implicit (`groupPolicyObjectId`) — join client-side if needed. `unsupportedGroupPolicyExtensions` explains "why didn't this migrate."
- Low cardinality/frequency — a daily poll is plenty.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] SnapshotCollector emits readiness + supported-settings-percent gauges against the in-memory **Recorder** with a **faked Graph client**; asserts percent is computed from supported/total counts and XML content is never read into telemetry.
- [ ] Test: bounded report-name cardinality; pagination to exhaustion.
- [ ] Graceful skip-and-log on 403 / beta unavailability (M1 #9).

## Dependencies

M1 #4 (client factory), #5 (rate limiters — Intune bucket), #6 (SnapshotCollector), #8 (Emitter + Recorder), #10 (license detection / degradation).

body:
## What & why

Metrics for **management scripts and proactive remediations** — Windows PowerShell scripts, macOS shell scripts, and health scripts (proactive remediations). Emit fleet run-state rollups from `runSummary`/`getRemediationSummary()` as gauges; script objects are inventory. All three surfaces are beta-only, hence the `beta-api` label.

SnapshotCollector, app-only read.

## Scope

- [ ] `internal/collectors/intune/scripts` — poll `deviceManagementScripts` (Windows PS), `deviceShellScripts` (macOS), `deviceHealthScripts` (remediations); a shared `deviceManagementScriptDeviceState`-style type parameterized by OS
- [ ] Emit `runSummary` (success/fail/pending) and `getRemediationSummary()` counts as gauges
- [ ] For health scripts, keep detection AND remediation as separate phases (don't collapse)
- [ ] Register under the `intune` rate-limit bucket
- [ ] Per-device run-state **transitions** (`deviceRunStates` diffed over time, `errorCode`/`errorDescription`) are event/log data → deferred to the **M5 milestone**; this issue covers the summary/rollup functions only.

## API surface

| Endpoint | Version | App permission | Pagination | Filter quirks | Throttle bucket |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /deviceManagement/deviceManagementScripts` (+ `runSummary`) | **beta** | `DeviceManagementScripts.Read.All` (or `DeviceManagementConfiguration.Read.All`) | `@odata.nextLink` | don't `$select` `scriptContent` (base64 config, not telemetry); no documented `$filter` on run states | Standard Graph |
| `GET /deviceManagement/deviceShellScripts` (+ run states) | **beta** | `DeviceManagementScripts.Read.All` | `@odata.nextLink` | as above | Standard |
| `GET /deviceManagement/deviceHealthScripts` (+ `runSummary`, `getRemediationSummary()`, `getRemediationHistory()`) | **beta** | `DeviceManagementScripts.Read.All` | functions return a single summary | don't `$select` detection/remediation script content | Standard |

Docs: [deviceManagementScript beta](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/intune-shared-devicemanagementscript?view=graph-rest-beta), [deviceHealthScript beta](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/intune-devices-devicehealthscript?view=graph-rest-beta).

## Telemetry model

`intune.*` namespace.

- `intune.script.run_summary` gauge, attrs `{script_name, os, run_state}` where `run_state` ∈ unknown/success/fail/scriptError/pending/notApplicable — from `runSummary`.
- `intune.remediation.summary` gauge, attrs `{script_name, phase, state}` where `phase` ∈ `{detection, remediation}` — from `getRemediationSummary()`, keeping the two health-script phases distinct.

Script names are bounded (dozens). Never `deviceRunStates` per device to metrics (scripts × devices = 200k+). Script content is config, not telemetry — never emit it.

## Constraints & gotchas

- **Beta-only** (all three) — pin beta endpoints; isolate errors.
- Health scripts have **two-phase** state (`detectionState` + `remediationState`) — map both, don't collapse into one enum.
- Run states reflect last-known state, not history — for a time series, poll and diff `lastStateUpdateDateTime` (the diff/transition stream is M5); the summary functions are the metric source here.
- Never `$select` `scriptContent`/`detectionScriptContent`/`remediationScriptContent`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] SnapshotCollector emits run-summary + remediation-summary gauges against the in-memory **Recorder** with a **faked Graph client**; asserts detection and remediation phases are separate series and script content is never read.
- [ ] Test: no per-device `deviceRunStates` fetched by this collector; bounded script-name cardinality.
- [ ] Graceful skip-and-log on 403 / beta unavailability (M1 #9).

## Dependencies

M1 #4 (client factory), #5 (rate limiters — Intune bucket), #6 (SnapshotCollector), #8 (Emitter + Recorder), #10 (license detection / degradation).

body:
## What & why

Certificate-lifecycle metrics — a "days until cert expiry" gauge bucketed by issuance state, from `managedDeviceCertificateStates` (PKCS/SCEP per device × cert profile), plus NDES/SCEP connector health. There is no CA-health Graph resource, so this collector also documents that honest gap. Beta-only surface, hence the `beta-api` label.

SnapshotCollector, app-only read.

## Scope

- [ ] `internal/collectors/intune/certificates` — poll `managedDeviceCertificateStates` (beta), emit a days-until-expiry gauge bucketed by collapsed issuance state
- [ ] Poll `ndesConnectors` (beta) for state/staleness (SCEP-via-NDES CA-health proxy) — coordinate with the connectors collector to avoid double-emitting NDES if both poll it
- [ ] Document the missing CA / Cloud-PKI-health gap in code comments / issue closure notes
- [ ] Register under the `intune` rate-limit bucket
- [ ] Fleet-wide cert inventory (`AllDeviceCertificates`, `CertificatesByRAPolicy`) is export-job-only — deferred to the **M5 milestone**; this issue covers the entity certificate-state endpoint only.

## API surface

| Endpoint | Version | App permission | Pagination | Filter quirks | Throttle bucket |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /deviceManagement/managedDeviceCertificateStates` (+ `/{id}`) | **beta** | `DeviceManagementConfiguration.Read.All` | `@odata.nextLink`, `$top` (device × cert profile) | no relationship back to `managedDevice.id` — join by display name (fragile on duplicates) | Standard |
| `GET /deviceManagement/ndesConnectors` | **beta** | `DeviceManagementConfiguration.Read.All` / `ServiceConfig.Read.All` | tiny | no `$filter` | negligible |
| `GET /deviceManagement/userPfxCertificates` | **beta** | `DeviceManagementConfiguration.Read.All` | `@odata.nextLink` | — | Standard |

Docs: [managedDeviceCertificateState beta](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/intune-deviceconfig-manageddevicecertificatestate?view=graph-rest-beta), [ndesConnector beta](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/intune-deviceconfig-ndesconnector?view=graph-rest-beta).

## Telemetry model

`intune.*` namespace.

- `intune.certificate.days_until_expiry` — bucketed **count** gauge, attrs `{state, cert_profile_name}` where `state` collapses the ~20-value `certificateIssuanceState` enum to `{healthy, pending, failed, revoked}`. Aggregate to counts-per-bucket; do NOT emit one series per device certificate.
- `intune.certificate.state.count` gauge, attrs `{state}` — fleet distribution across the collapsed issuance states.
- `intune.ndes_connector.state` / `intune.ndes_connector.heartbeat_age_seconds` gauges.

`certificateThumbprint`, `deviceDisplayName`, `userDisplayName` are unbounded — never metric labels. `cert_profile_name` is bounded.

## Constraints & gotchas

- **Beta-only** — pin the beta endpoint; isolate error handling.
- No `deviceManagementCertificationAuthority` resource — CA health is only inferable via `ndesConnector.state` for SCEP-via-NDES; **Cloud PKI health has no stable public Graph resource** (an honest gap to document, not a bug).
- `managedDeviceCertificateState` has no relationship back to `managedDevice.id` — any device join is by display name and breaks on duplicate device names; treat cert states as their own aggregate rather than joining to devices for metrics.
- Collapse `certificateIssuanceState` (~20 values) to a handful before it becomes a label — cardinality discipline.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] SnapshotCollector emits days-until-expiry bucket counts + state-distribution gauges against the in-memory **Recorder** with a **faked Graph client**; asserts the ~20-value issuance enum is collapsed to the 4-value state label and no thumbprint/device-name appears as a label.
- [ ] Test: pagination to exhaustion; NDES double-emit avoided when connectors collector also runs.
- [ ] Graceful skip-and-log on 403 / beta unavailability (M1 #9).

## Dependencies

M1 #4 (client factory), #5 (rate limiters — Intune bucket), #6 (SnapshotCollector), #8 (Emitter + Recorder), #10 (license detection / degradation).

comments.body: M4 seam decision (Group A — NDES ownership, tracker #79): **#63 is now certificates-only.** To resolve the shared `/deviceManagement/ndesConnectors` endpoint + the metric-name collision with #51, NDES connector health moves entirely to #51 (the general connector-health collector). This collector emits ONLY the certificate-state metrics (`intune.certificate.days_until_expiry`, `intune.certificate.state.count`) from `managedDeviceCertificateStates` + `userPfxCertificates` (both beta). It does NOT poll `ndesConnectors` and does NOT emit `intune.ndes_connector.*`. Scope narrows accordingly; the collector stays beta/`Experimental()` since both cert endpoints are beta-only. The "no CA-health Graph resource exists" honest-gap note still applies and should be documented in the package doc.

Done in 17a1502. `internal/collectors/intune/certificates`, collector `intune.certificates` (beta, Experimental). Certificates-ONLY per the Group A seam decision — no ndesConnectors, no intune.ndes_connector.* (NDES health owned by #51). Emits intune.certificate.days_until_expiry{state,cert_profile_name} (bucketed) + .state.count (certificateIssuanceState collapsed to a bounded set). Live-verified: polls cleanly (0 rows = no device certs on tenant, healthy empty state). No per-device join; documents the no-CA-health-resource gap.

body:
## What & why

Days-until-expiry gauges for the **Apple integration tokens** — APNS certificate (single point of failure for ALL Apple MDM), VPP tokens, and DEP onboarding tokens. If the APNS cert expires, every Apple device loses MDM simultaneously, so this is the tightest-threshold alert of anything in M4. Cheap, tiny, daily-poll snapshot.

SnapshotCollector, app-only read. Mostly v1.0 (APNS + VPP); DEP is beta-only, handled inline with isolated error handling rather than labelling the whole issue beta.

## Scope

- [ ] `internal/collectors/intune/appletokens` — daily poll of APNS certificate, VPP tokens, DEP onboarding settings → days-until-expiry gauges
- [ ] Include a `state`/`lastSyncStatus` dimension so "expiring" is distinguishable from "already broken"
- [ ] Register under the `intune` rate-limit bucket
- [ ] DEP `depOnboardingSettings` is beta — isolate its error handling so a beta failure doesn't drop the APNS/VPP gauges.

## API surface

| Endpoint | Version | App permission | Pagination | Filter quirks | Throttle bucket |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /deviceManagement/applePushNotificationCertificate` | v1.0 | `DeviceManagementServiceConfig.Read.All` | singleton | no meaningful `$filter` | negligible |
| `GET /deviceAppManagement/vppTokens` | v1.0 | `DeviceManagementApps.Read.All` | tiny collection | no meaningful `$filter` | negligible |
| `GET /deviceManagement/depOnboardingSettings` | **beta** | `DeviceManagementServiceConfig.Read.All` | tiny collection | no meaningful `$filter` | negligible |

Docs: [applePushNotificationCertificate v1.0](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/intune-devices-applepushnotificationcertificate?view=graph-rest-1.0), [vppToken v1.0](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/intune-onboarding-vpptoken?view=graph-rest-1.0), [depOnboardingSetting beta](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/intune-enrollment-deponboardingsetting?view=graph-rest-beta).

## Telemetry model

`intune.*` namespace.

- `intune.apple_token.days_until_expiry` gauge, attrs `{type, state}` where `type` ∈ `{apns, vpp, dep}` and `state` is a bounded status enum (VPP `state`, APNS `certificateUploadStatus`, DEP sync status). Token counts are trivial (1 APNS, 1–5 VPP, 1–3 DEP).
- Optionally `intune.apple_token.synced_device_count` gauge for DEP.

`appleIdentifier`/`appleId`/`organizationName` (the owner Apple ID — "who to ping") are few and bounded, so acceptable as a low-cardinality attribute; keep them out if they inflate series unnecessarily.

## Constraints & gotchas

- **APNS cert is a single point of failure** — set the tightest alert threshold on its expiry gauge; its expiry breaks all Apple MDM at once.
- `vppToken.state == assignedToExternalMDM` = non-functional for this tenant even if not expired — the `state` dimension is essential; don't rely on expiry alone.
- `depOnboardingSetting` is **beta-only** — pin the beta version; isolate its errors.
- Long lifetimes (~1yr) — a daily poll is enough; don't over-poll.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] SnapshotCollector emits days-until-expiry gauges for all three token types against the in-memory **Recorder** with a **faked Graph client**, computing days against a fixed clock; asserts the `state` dimension distinguishes expiring from already-broken (`assignedToExternalMDM`).
- [ ] Test: DEP beta failure does not drop APNS/VPP gauges.
- [ ] Graceful skip-and-log on 403 / missing scope (M1 #9).

## Dependencies

M1 #4 (client factory), #5 (rate limiters — Intune bucket), #6 (SnapshotCollector), #8 (Emitter + Recorder), #10 (license detection / degradation).

comments.body: Done in d427cdf. `internal/collectors/intune/appletokens`, collector `intune.apple_tokens`. Live-verified: emits intune.apple_token.days_until_expiry{type,state,token_name} for APNS/VPP/DEP + intune.apple_token.synced_device_count. DEP polled best-effort against /beta with isolated error handling (collector not Experimental overall since APNS/VPP are v1.0). Owns the depOnboardingSetting.dataSharingConsentGranted signal #51 deferred here.

body:
## What & why

Metrics for **Windows malware / Defender state** — the cheap tenant `windowsMalwareOverview` singleton (detected-device counts, per-severity/category summaries) plus per-device `windowsProtectionState` health gauges (signature/scan overdue, real-time protection, tamper protection) for smaller fleets. At scale the per-device path is replaced by exports.

SnapshotCollector, app-only read.

## Scope

- [ ] `internal/collectors/intune/malware` — poll `windowsMalwareOverview` (tenant singleton) as the primary cheap summary gauge set
- [ ] For fleets below a configurable device threshold (~2–3k Windows devices), poll per-device `windowsProtectionState` for protection-health gauges
- [ ] Register under the `intune`/Devices rate-limit bucket
- [ ] Malware **detections** (`detectedMalwareState`/`windowsDeviceMalwareState` — detection timestamps, `threatState`) are event/log data, and fleet-wide rollups (`DefenderAgents`/`UnhealthyDefenderAgents`/`Malware`/`ActiveMalware` exports) are export-job-only — both deferred to the **M5 milestone**; this issue covers the overview singleton + entity protection-state gauges only.

## API surface

| Endpoint | Version | App permission | Pagination | Filter quirks | Throttle bucket |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /deviceManagement/windowsMalwareOverview` | v1.0 | `DeviceManagementManagedDevices.Read.All` | singleton | no filter | negligible |
| `GET /deviceManagement/managedDevices/{id}/windowsProtectionState` | v1.0 | `DeviceManagementManagedDevices.Read.All` | per-device | doesn't batch — 10k devices = 10k+ GETs | Devices tier (~2000/app per 20s) |
| `GET /deviceManagement/windowsDeviceMalwareStates` | v1.0 | `DeviceManagementManagedDevices.Read.All` | `@odata.nextLink` (can be very large) | — | Devices tier |
| `GET /deviceManagement/windowsMalwareInformation/{id}` | v1.0 | `DeviceManagementManagedDevices.Read.All` | `@odata.nextLink` | this is the malware **catalog** (definitions), NOT per-device infection state | Devices tier |

Docs: [windowsProtectionState v1.0](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/intune-devices-windowsprotectionstate?view=graph-rest-1.0), [windowsMalwareOverview v1.0](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/intune-devices-windowsmalwareoverview?view=graph-rest-1.0), [available reports](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/intune-service/fundamentals/reports-export-graph-available-reports).

## Telemetry model

`intune.*` namespace.

- `intune.malware.overview.detected_devices` gauge; `intune.malware.overview.total` gauge; `intune.malware.overview.by_severity` / `by_category` gauges (bounded enums) — all from the overview singleton.
- `intune.defender.protection_state` gauge, attrs `{signal}` where signal ∈ `{malware_protection_enabled, real_time_protection_enabled, signature_update_overdue, quick_scan_overdue, full_scan_overdue, tamper_protection_enabled}` — aggregated counts across polled devices, not per device.
- `intune.defender.product_status` gauge, attrs `{status}` from `productStatus`/`deviceState` (bounded enums).

`displayName` of malware and device identifiers never become metric labels (they belong in the M5 malware log stream).

## Constraints & gotchas

- `windowsMalwareInformation` is the malware **catalog** (definitions), NOT per-device infection state — use `windowsDeviceMalwareState` for infections; don't confuse them.
- Per-device `windowsProtectionState` doesn't batch — above ~2–3k Windows devices, switch to `DefenderAgents`/`Malware`/`ActiveMalware` exports (M5); this collector gates the per-device sweep on a device-count threshold.
- Documented `windowsProtectionState` path nests oddly under `detectedApps/{id}/managedDevices/{id}/...`; the direct `managedDevices/{id}/windowsProtectionState` nav also resolves — verify per tenant.
- 403 on `windowsMalwareInformation` usually means the `DeviceManagementManagedDevices.Read.All` scope isn't consented.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] SnapshotCollector emits overview gauges + aggregated protection-state gauges against the in-memory **Recorder** with a **faked Graph client**; asserts per-device data is aggregated (no device-id label) and the per-device sweep is skipped above the configured threshold.
- [ ] Test: overview-only mode issues zero per-device GETs.
- [ ] Graceful skip-and-log on 403 / missing scope (M1 #9).

## Dependencies

M1 #4 (client factory), #5 (rate limiters — Intune/Devices bucket), #6 (SnapshotCollector), #8 (Emitter + Recorder), #10 (license detection / degradation).

comments.body: Done in d427cdf. `internal/collectors/intune/malware`, collector `intune.malware`. Live-verified (sweep summary: windows_devices=4 ok=3 not_found=1 errored=0). Emits intune.malware.overview.* and intune.defender.protection_state{signal}/.product_status{status} aggregated from per-device windowsProtectionState, gated on a client-side Windows fleet-size threshold. Two live-caught fixes folded in: managedDevices has no `$count` segment / operatingSystem is not server-filterable (switched to client-side count off the paged fleet); per-device windowsProtectionState 404 is a routine no-data condition and no longer fails the collector (protection-state snapshots emit only when ≥1 device returns readable state).

body:
## What & why

Metrics for **Endpoint analytics** (User Experience Analytics / UXA) — score-shaped gauges for device boot/login performance, app health, work-from-anywhere, and (beta) battery/resource/baseline. The tenant Overview singleton gives the headline scores cheaply; per-category collections add boot/login and app-crash detail as periodically-polled metrics tables.

SnapshotCollector, app-only read. This family is **mixed v1.0/beta** (Overview/Startup/AppHealth/WFA are v1.0; Battery/Resource/Baseline are beta) — the beta pieces are gated behind a config flag rather than labelling the whole issue beta.

## Scope

- [ ] `internal/collectors/intune/endpointanalytics` — poll `userExperienceAnalyticsOverview` (v1.0) for per-category score gauges
- [ ] Poll device startup history + app-health performance (v1.0) as bucketed boot/login and crash-rate metrics
- [ ] Gate battery/resource/baseline (beta) behind a "beta features" config flag
- [ ] Register under the `intune`/Devices rate-limit bucket
- [ ] Per-boot / per-device raw rows are high-volume — pull incrementally and aggregate to histograms/buckets; do not emit per-device series. Any fleet-wide raw export deferred to the **M5 milestone**; this issue covers the overview + aggregate collections.

## API surface

| Endpoint | Version | App permission | Pagination | Filter quirks | Throttle bucket |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /deviceManagement/userExperienceAnalyticsOverview` | v1.0 | `DeviceManagementManagedDevices.Read.All` | singleton | most props `$select`/`$orderby` but NOT `$filter` (400); no `$expand` | Standard Graph |
| `.../userExperienceAnalyticsDeviceStartupHistories` | v1.0 | `DeviceManagementManagedDevices.Read.All` | `@odata.nextLink`, `$top` | per-boot rows — pull incrementally | Standard |
| `.../userExperienceAnalyticsAppHealthApplicationPerformance` | v1.0 | `DeviceManagementManagedDevices.Read.All` | `@odata.nextLink` | — | Standard |
| `.../userExperienceAnalyticsBatteryHealthDevicePerformance` / `...ResourcePerformance` / `...Baselines` | **beta** | `DeviceManagementManagedDevices.Read.All` | `@odata.nextLink` | beta — gate behind flag | Standard |

Docs: [userExperienceAnalyticsOverview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/intune-devices-userexperienceanalyticsoverview?view=graph-rest-beta).

## Telemetry model

`intune.*` namespace.

- `intune.uxa.score` gauge, attrs `{category}` — `overallScore`, `deviceBootPerformanceOverallScore`, `appHealthOverallScore`, `workFromAnywhereOverallScore`, plus beta `resourcePerformanceOverallScore`/`batteryHealthOverallScore`; `*HealthState` enum as a companion gauge/attr.
- `intune.uxa.boot_time_ms` / `intune.uxa.login_time_ms` histograms (from startup history `totalBootTimeInMs`/`totalLoginTimeInMs`), attrs `{restart_category}` — bucketed, not per-device.
- `intune.uxa.app_crash_count` gauge, attrs `{app_name}` — from AppHealth; cap cardinality (distinct raw exe names can be large).
- `intune.uxa.battery_health_score` gauge (beta, flag-gated).

`deviceId` and raw device fields never become metric labels.

## Constraints & gotchas

- Requires Endpoint analytics enabled + score maturity — `insufficientData` is **normal, not an error** (handle gracefully; a fresh/small tenant legitimately returns it — coordinate with M1 #10 license/degradation).
- Mixed v1.0/beta within one family — check per entity; don't assume the whole family is beta (or v1.0).
- StartupHistory is per-boot per-device (~300k+ rows/month for 10k devices) — pull incrementally and aggregate to histograms; never one series per device.
- AppHealth cardinality scales with distinct raw exe names — cap/allow-list.
- Battery `model`/`manufacturer` deprecated → `deviceModelName`/`deviceManufacturerName`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] SnapshotCollector emits overview score gauges + bucketed boot/login histograms against the in-memory **Recorder** with a **faked Graph client**; asserts app-crash cardinality is capped and `insufficientData` yields a clean skip (no crash, no bogus zero-score).
- [ ] Test: beta battery/resource collections are skipped when the beta flag is off.
- [ ] Graceful skip-and-log on 403 / missing scope / immature tenant (M1 #9/#10).

## Dependencies

M1 #4 (client factory), #5 (rate limiters — Intune/Devices bucket), #6 (SnapshotCollector), #8 (Emitter + Recorder), #10 (license-tier detection / graceful degradation — the `insufficientData` case).

comments.body: Done in 17a1502. `internal/collectors/intune/endpointanalytics`, collector `intune.endpoint_analytics` (beta, Experimental). Startup/app-health aggregated to histograms (never per-device/per-boot series); app_name capped. Live-caught fix: a tenant that has not onboarded Endpoint Analytics returns 400 ResourceNotFound on every UXA segment — now recognized as feature-not-provisioned and skipped cleanly (Collect returns nil), distinct from the 200-body insufficientData case which is also handled.

body:
## What & why

Metrics for **Windows Update management** — Update rings (v1.0, a subtype of `deviceConfigurations`) plus the beta feature / quality / driver update profiles. Ring-level pause/rollback state and pause-expiry countdowns; profile config for EOL-targeting and driver-approval-backlog alerting. The profiles are beta-only (`beta-api` label); per-device rollout status across all of these is export-only.

SnapshotCollector, app-only read.

## Scope

- [ ] `internal/collectors/intune/updates` — poll Update rings via `deviceConfigurations` filtered to `windowsUpdateForBusinessConfiguration`; pause/rollback + pause-expiry gauges; roll up ring `deviceStatuses` compliance counts
- [ ] Poll `windowsFeatureUpdateProfiles` (beta) — EOL-targeting config gauges
- [ ] Poll `windowsQualityUpdateProfiles` + `windowsQualityUpdatePolicies` (beta, two parallel resources) — config drift
- [ ] Poll `windowsDriverUpdateProfiles` (beta) + `driverInventories` — `newUpdates`/`deviceReporting` gauges + stale-sync alerting
- [ ] Register under the `intune`/Device Config bucket
- [ ] Per-device rollout status/failure reports (`FeatureUpdateDeviceState`, `FeatureUpdatePolicyStatusSummary`, `QualityUpdateDeviceStatusByPolicy`/`...ErrorsByPolicy` — the latter **require `PolicyId`**, `DriverUpdatePolicyStatusSummary`) are export-job-only — fleet-wide detail deferred to the **M5 milestone** export-job subsystem; this issue covers the ring/profile config snapshots + inherited ring `deviceStatusOverview` only.

## API surface

| Endpoint | Version | App permission | Pagination | Filter quirks | Throttle bucket |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /deviceManagement/deviceConfigurations` (`@odata.type eq 'windowsUpdateForBusinessConfiguration'`) + `/{id}/deviceStatusOverview` | v1.0 | `DeviceManagementConfiguration.Read.All` | `@odata.nextLink` | ring-specific props are "Query parameters not supported" — `$filter` on e.g. `qualityUpdatesPaused` 400s; fetch and filter client-side; always check `@odata.type` | Device Config bucket |
| `GET /deviceManagement/windowsFeatureUpdateProfiles` (+ `/{id}/assignments`) | **beta** (v1.0 404) | `DeviceManagementConfiguration.Read.All` | `@odata.nextLink` | only `assignments` is a relationship — no `deviceStatuses` here | Standard |
| `GET /deviceManagement/windowsQualityUpdateProfiles` / `windowsQualityUpdatePolicies` | **beta** | `DeviceManagementConfiguration.Read.All` | `@odata.nextLink` | two parallel resources for the same job — a tenant may use either/both | Standard |
| `GET /deviceManagement/windowsDriverUpdateProfiles` (+ `/{id}/driverInventories`) | **beta** (v1.0 404) | `DeviceManagementConfiguration.Read.All` | `@odata.nextLink` | no documented `$filter` — client-side | Standard |

Docs: [windowsUpdateForBusinessConfiguration v1.0](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/intune-deviceconfig-windowsupdateforbusinessconfiguration?view=graph-rest-1.0), [windowsFeatureUpdateProfile beta](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/intune-softwareupdate-windowsfeatureupdateprofile?view=graph-rest-beta), [windowsQualityUpdatePolicy beta](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/intune-softwareupdate-windowsqualityupdatepolicy?view=graph-rest-beta), [windowsDriverUpdateProfile beta](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/intune-softwareupdate-windowsdriverupdateprofile?view=graph-rest-beta), [available reports](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/intune-service/fundamentals/reports-export-graph-available-reports).

## Telemetry model

`intune.*` namespace.

- `intune.update_ring.pause_state` gauge, attrs `{ring_name, update_type}` from `qualityUpdatesPaused`/`featureUpdatesPaused`; `intune.update_ring.pause_expiry_seconds` gauge (countdown from `*PauseExpiryDateTime`, ≤35 days).
- `intune.update_ring.rollback_active` gauge, attrs `{ring_name, update_type}` from `*WillBeRolledBack`.
- `intune.update_ring.status` gauge, attrs `{ring_name, state}` — rolled-up ring `deviceStatusOverview`.
- `intune.feature_update_profile.eol_target` / config gauges (from `featureUpdateVersion`, `endOfSupportDate`).
- `intune.driver_update.pending_approval` gauge, attrs `{profile_name}` from `newUpdates`; `intune.driver_update.sync_staleness_seconds` from `inventorySyncStatus.lastSuccessfulSyncDateTime`.

Ring/profile/policy names are bounded; never emit per-device series.

## Constraints & gotchas

- Update rings share the heterogeneous `deviceConfigurations` collection — always branch on `@odata.type`; coordinate with the config-profiles collector so rings aren't double-counted.
- All three profile families are **beta-only** (v1.0 404) — pin beta endpoints.
- Quality-update reports require `PolicyId` — no fleet-wide-in-one-call form; that's an M5 concern.
- Feature-update profiles have **no** device-level Graph relationship — per-device status is export-only.
- `newUpdates`/`deviceReporting` are embedded on the driver profile — cheap headline metrics without walking `driverInventories`; don't poll `syncInventory`/`executeAction` tightly (they trigger backend work).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] SnapshotCollector emits ring pause/rollback/expiry gauges + driver pending-approval/stale-sync gauges against the in-memory **Recorder** with a **faked Graph client** (v1.0 rings + beta profiles); asserts pause-expiry countdown against a fixed clock and bounded ring/profile-name cardinality.
- [ ] Test: ring type filter isolates `windowsUpdateForBusinessConfiguration`; no per-device export calls attempted.
- [ ] Graceful skip-and-log on 403 / beta unavailability (M1 #9).

## Dependencies

M1 #4 (client factory), #5 (rate limiters — Intune/Device Config bucket), #6 (SnapshotCollector), #8 (Emitter + Recorder), #10 (license detection / degradation).

comments.body: M4 seam decision (Group B — deviceConfigurations partition, tracker #79): **#59 owns EXACTLY `@odata.type == #microsoft.graph.windowsUpdateForBusinessConfiguration` within `/deviceManagement/deviceConfigurations`** (its update-ring metrics), plus the beta `windowsFeatureUpdateProfiles` / `windowsQualityUpdateProfiles` / `windowsQualityUpdatePolicies` / `windowsDriverUpdateProfiles` families. It MUST filter the deviceConfigurations collection to that one type so it never double-emits with #53. #53 owns everything else in that collection.

Done in 17a1502. `internal/collectors/intune/updates`, collector `intune.updates` (beta, Experimental/opt-in). body:
## What & why

Conditional Access policy posture + named locations. CA policy counts by state (enabled / disabled / report-only) are direct compliance signals — a disabled or report-only policy that should be enforcing is a finding. Named locations (trusted IP ranges, country lists) are the companion config CA policies reference. Merged into one collector because both live under `/identity/conditionalAccess`, share the P1 license gate and the same very-low Identity-Protection throttle bucket, and are individually tiny.

## Scope

- [ ] Add collector `internal/collectors/entra/conditionalaccess` implementing `SnapshotCollector` (#6).
- [ ] Poll CA policies and named locations; emit count gauges by the bounded dimensions below.
- [ ] License-gate via #10 (CA is P1); skip-and-log when the tenant lacks P1.
- [ ] Register under `entra.conditional_access` collector key (#2).

## API surface

| Endpoint | Version | App permission | Pagination | Filter/delta | Throttle bucket |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /identity/conditionalAccess/policies` | v1.0 | `Policy.Read.All` (or `Policy.Read.ConditionalAccess`) | nextLink (small) | `$select`; no delta | **Identity Protection / CA: 1 req/s per tenant, no Retry-After** |
| `GET /identity/conditionalAccess/namedLocations` | v1.0 | `Policy.Read.All` | nextLink | `$select`; no delta | Same IPC/CA bucket |

Docs: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/conditionalaccessroot-list-policies?view=graph-rest-1.0 , https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/conditionalaccessroot-list-namedlocations?view=graph-rest-1.0

## Telemetry model

- `entra.ca.policies.total{state}` (gauge) — `state` ∈ `enabled|disabled|enabled_for_reporting_but_not_enforced`. Bounded.
- `entra.named_locations.total{type,is_trusted}` (gauge) — `type` ∈ `ip|country`; `is_trusted` ∈ `true|false`.
- Full policy JSON is **not** emitted as metrics — policy-change tracking belongs in the directory-audit log stream (M3).
- Cardinality: bounded by state/type — tens of policies at most.

## Constraints & gotchas

- **Identity Protection / CA throttle bucket: 1 request/second per tenant across all apps, and NO `Retry-After` header on 429.** Serialize these calls and rely on the client-side limiter (#5) — this is one of the two binding ceilings in the whole exporter.
- **P1-gated:** Conditional Access is a P1 feature. Detect via #10 and degrade gracefully (skip-and-log), never crash, when the tenant is Free-only.
- No delta on either resource — full read each cycle (both are small).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Tests against the `Recorder` (#8) with a faked Graph client: policy-state and named-location slices emit correctly.
- [ ] Test that when #10 reports "not P1", the collector skips-and-logs rather than erroring.
- [ ] Test that calls respect the 1 req/s serialization (the limiter is invoked; no burst).
- [ ] `make check` green.

## Dependencies

- #4, #5, #6, #8, #10 (P1 gate).

comments.body: Done in 16d4c7b. `internal/collectors/entra/conditionalaccess` emits `entra.ca.policies.total` by state and `entra.named_locations.total` by type × is_trusted (bounded, no per-policy series). Whole-collector P1 gate via `license.CapabilityRequirer`. `Policy.Read.All`. Country named locations (no isTrusted property) treated as is_trusted=false. **Live-verified end to end** on a P1 tenant.

body:
## What & why

Metrics for **Windows Autopilot** — registered device identities (`windowsAutopilotDeviceIdentities`, v1.0) and deployment profiles (`windowsAutopilotDeploymentProfiles`, beta). Gauges by `enrollmentState`/`groupTag`, stale-`lastContactedDateTime` alerting, and profile config snapshots for drift alerting (ESP timeout, white-glove toggled). The profile side is beta-only, hence the `beta-api` label.

SnapshotCollector, app-only read.

## Scope

- [ ] `internal/collectors/intune/autopilot` — poll `windowsAutopilotDeviceIdentities`, gauges by `enrollmentState`/`groupTag`, stale-contact alerting
- [ ] Poll `windowsAutopilotDeploymentProfiles` (beta) + assignments for config-drift snapshot gauges
- [ ] Register under the `intune`/Devices rate-limit bucket
- [ ] Per-device enrollment **events** (`autopilotEvents`, beta) are an event stream → logs, deferred to the **M5 milestone**; this issue covers the device-identity + profile entity snapshots only.

## API surface

| Endpoint | Version | App permission | Pagination | Filter quirks | Throttle bucket |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /deviceManagement/windowsAutopilotDeviceIdentities` (+ `/{id}`) | v1.0 | `DeviceManagementServiceConfig.Read.All` | `@odata.nextLink`, `$top` | `$filter` support undocumented on this collection — validate empirically; `groupTag`/`serialNumber` common in practice but not guaranteed | Devices tier (~2000/app, 4000/tenant per 20s) |
| `GET /deviceManagement/windowsAutopilotDeploymentProfiles` (+ `/{id}/assignments`) | **beta** (v1.0 404) | `DeviceManagementServiceConfig.Read.All` | `@odata.nextLink` | `$filter`/`$search` explicitly NOT supported on most props (400) — `$select`/`$top`/`$skip` only | Standard deviceManagement |

Docs: [windowsAutopilotDeviceIdentity v1.0](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/intune-enrollment-windowsautopilotdeviceidentity?view=graph-rest-1.0), [windowsAutopilotDeploymentProfile beta](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/intune-shared-windowsautopilotdeploymentprofile?view=graph-rest-beta).

## Telemetry model

`intune.*` namespace.

- `intune.autopilot.devices` gauge, attrs `{enrollment_state, group_tag}` — `enrollmentState` ∈ unknown/enrolled/pendingReset/failed/notContacted; `group_tag` is operator-defined but typically bounded (dozens).
- `intune.autopilot.stale_contact.count` gauge, attrs `{group_tag}` — count of identities past a staleness threshold on `lastContactedDateTime`.
- `intune.autopilot.profile.count` gauge, attrs `{device_type, preprovisioning_allowed}`; config-drift-relevant booleans (ESP settings, white-glove) as bounded gauges/attrs.

`serialNumber`, `managedDeviceId`, `userPrincipalName` are unbounded — never metric labels. If `group_tag` cardinality is unbounded in a given tenant, cap or drop it.

## Constraints & gotchas

- The device-identity collection includes historically-registered (retired) hardware unless deleted — it can exceed the live fleet; paginate fully and don't equate it to live device count.
- `azureActiveDirectoryDeviceId` is marked "to be deprecated" — join on `managedDeviceId` instead.
- Deployment profiles are **beta-only** (v1.0 404) — pin the beta endpoint; `language`/`enableWhiteGlove`/`extractHardwareHash` deprecated (May 2024) → `locale`/`preprovisioningAllowed`/`hardwareHashExtractionEnabled` (don't read the old names).
- No `deviceDeploymentStates` resource — coarse per-device outcome is `enrollmentState`; rich per-device outcome is `autopilotEvents` (M5). Effective profile may come from a Policy Set, not a direct assignment.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] SnapshotCollector emits device gauges by state/groupTag + profile config gauges against the in-memory **Recorder** with a **faked Graph client** (v1.0 identities + beta profiles); asserts no serial/UPN label and correct stale-contact count against a fixed clock.
- [ ] Test: pagination to exhaustion; group_tag cardinality cap enforced.
- [ ] Graceful skip-and-log on 403 / beta unavailability (M1 #9).

## Dependencies

M1 #4 (client factory), #5 (rate limiters — Intune/Devices bucket), #6 (SnapshotCollector), #8 (Emitter + Recorder), #10 (license detection / degradation).

Live-verified: emits intune.autopilot.devices{enrollment_state,group_tag}, .profile.count/.assignments/.setting. group_tag cardinality capped. Uses post-May-2024 field names (locale/preprovisioningAllowed/hardwareHashExtractionEnabled).

body:
## What & why

Metrics for **app protection / MAM** policies (iOS/Android managed app protection, targeted app configs, managed app registrations) plus a low-priority legacy flag for **Windows Information Protection (WIP)**. Policy objects become inventory gauges; `managedAppRegistrations.flaggedReasons` (e.g. `rootedDevice`) is a security-relevant signal (surfaced as a bounded count here; per-registration detail → logs in a later milestone).

SnapshotCollector, app-only read.

## Scope

- [ ] `internal/collectors/intune/mam` — poll iOS/Android managed app protections + targeted managed app configs as policy-inventory snapshots
- [ ] Poll `managedAppRegistrations` (paged, cached) and aggregate `flaggedReasons` into a bounded security gauge
- [ ] Low-frequency inventory check for assigned WIP policies, tagged as a deprecated-feature compliance flag
- [ ] Avoid depending on `managedAppStatuses` (legacy quasi-deprecated report shim)
- [ ] Register under the `intune` rate-limit bucket
- [ ] Per-registration detail as a log stream and MAM export rollups (`MAMAppProtectionStatus`, `MAMAppConfigurationStatus`) deferred to the **M5 milestone**; this issue covers the policy-inventory + flaggedReasons aggregate only.

## API surface

| Endpoint | Version | App permission | Pagination | Filter quirks | Throttle bucket |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /deviceAppManagement/iosManagedAppProtections` / `androidManagedAppProtections` / `targetedManagedAppConfigurations` | v1.0 | `DeviceManagementApps.Read.All` | `@odata.nextLink` | — | Standard Intune |
| `GET /deviceAppManagement/managedAppRegistrations` | v1.0 | `DeviceManagementApps.Read.All` | `@odata.nextLink` | `$filter` support undocumented — verify before relying | Standard Intune |
| `GET /deviceAppManagement/managedAppPolicies` / `managedAppStatuses` | v1.0 / beta-quasi | `DeviceManagementApps.Read.All` | small fixed menu of report ids | `managedAppStatuses` payload shape depends on the id — avoid | Standard Intune |
| `GET /deviceAppManagement/windowsInformationProtectionPolicies` / `mdmWindowsInformationProtectionPolicies` | v1.0 (product-deprecated) | `DeviceManagementApps.Read.All` | `@odata.nextLink` | — | Standard Intune |

Docs: [iosManagedAppProtection list](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/intune-mam-iosmanagedappprotection-list?view=graph-rest-1.0), [managedAppRegistration list](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/intune-mam-managedappregistration-list?view=graph-rest-1.0), [windowsInformationProtection v1.0](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/intune-mam-windowsinformationprotection?view=graph-rest-1.0).

## Telemetry model

`intune.*` namespace.

- `intune.app_protection.policy.count` gauge, attrs `{platform, assigned}` — protections + targeted configs; `deployedAppCount`, `pinRequired`, `dataBackupBlocked` as bounded config gauges/attrs.
- `intune.app_protection.flagged_registrations` gauge, attrs `{flagged_reason, platform}` — count of registrations by `flaggedReasons` (e.g. `rootedDevice`). Bounded by the small reason enum; never label by `userId`/`appIdentifier`.
- `intune.wip.policy.count` gauge, attrs `{assigned}` — legacy WIP inventory, tagged deprecated.

`userId`, `appIdentifier`, device identifiers on registrations are unbounded — keep them off metrics (logs only, later milestone).

## Constraints & gotchas

- `managedAppRegistrations` is per app per user per device (50k–100k+) — page and cache; only the aggregated `flaggedReasons` count goes to metrics.
- `managedAppStatuses` is a legacy quasi-deprecated shim (`{displayName,id,version}` schema, payload varies by id) — prefer registrations + protection `deployedAppCount`/`isAssigned`.
- WIP is **product-deprecated** (removed from Windows 24H2+; WIP-without-enrollment ended 2022) — track only as a "migrate to Purview DLP" legacy flag, low frequency.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] SnapshotCollector emits policy-inventory gauges + a bounded `flaggedReasons` count against the in-memory **Recorder** with a **faked Graph client**; asserts no `userId`/device identifier appears as a label.
- [ ] Test: `managedAppRegistrations` paginated to exhaustion and aggregated by reason.
- [ ] Test: WIP policies emit the deprecated-flag gauge.
- [ ] Graceful skip-and-log on 403 / missing scope (M1 #9).

## Dependencies

M1 #4 (client factory), #5 (rate limiters — Intune bucket), #6 (SnapshotCollector), #8 (Emitter + Recorder), #10 (license detection / degradation).

comments.body: Done in 17a1502. `internal/collectors/intune/appprotection`, collector `intune.app_protection` (v1.0). Live-verified: emits intune.app_protection.policy.count + .flagged_registrations (aggregated managedAppRegistration flaggedReasons — never per-user/per-app labels). Live-caught fix: the deprecated WIP endpoints return an empty body ("unexpected end of JSON input"); WIP is now best-effort (empty body = zero policies) and never fails the collector.

body:
## What & why

Inventory metrics for the **mobile app catalog** (`mobileApps`) and **mobile app configuration policies** (`mobileAppConfigurations`). The app catalog is small, device-independent, and cheap to poll fully — counts by app type and publishing state, with change detection off timestamps. App config policies get aggregate status gauges from `deviceStatusSummary`.

SnapshotCollector, app-only read.

## Scope

- [ ] `internal/collectors/intune/mobileapps` — full-collection poll of `mobileApps`, metrics by `@odata.type` / `publishingState`
- [ ] Poll `mobileAppConfigurations` + `deviceStatusSummary` for aggregate config-status gauges
- [ ] Register under the `intune` rate-limit bucket
- [ ] App **install status** (per app × per device) is a deprecated/broken nav-prop surface and fundamentally an export-job product (`DeviceInstallStatusByApp`, `AppInstallStatusAggregate`) — fleet-wide install detail deferred to the **M5 milestone** export-job subsystem; this issue covers the catalog + config-policy summary endpoints only.

## API surface

| Endpoint | Version | App permission | Pagination | Filter quirks | Throttle bucket |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /deviceAppManagement/mobileApps` (+ `/{id}`) | v1.0 | `DeviceManagementApps.Read.All` | `@odata.nextLink`, `$top` | subtypes via `@odata.type` (`win32LobApp`, `iosStoreApp`, `webApp`, …); `$expand=assignments` on the LIST is deprecated — expand per-app | Standard Intune (1000 any / 100 write per 20s per app) |
| `GET /deviceAppManagement/mobileAppConfigurations` (+ `/{id}/deviceStatusSummary`) | v1.0 (verify abstract-resource slug live) | `DeviceManagementApps.Read.All` | `@odata.nextLink`, `$top` | status sub-paths (`deviceStatuses`/`userStatuses`) historically drift from docs — verify live before trusting | Standard Intune |

Docs: [mobileApp v1.0](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/intune-apps-mobileapp?view=graph-rest-1.0), [managedDeviceMobileAppConfigurationUserStatus](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/intune-apps-manageddevicemobileappconfigurationuserstatus?view=graph-rest-1.0), [export-graph-apis](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/device-management/reports/export-graph-apis).

## Telemetry model

`intune.*` namespace.

- `intune.mobile_apps.count` gauge, attrs `{app_type, publishing_state}` — `@odata.type` and `publishingState` are bounded.
- `intune.mobile_app_config.status` gauge, attrs `{policy_name, status}` from `deviceStatusSummary` (complianceStatus enum). Policy count is small.

Catalog is bounded (hundreds–low thousands); `app_type`/`publishing_state` are safe labels. Never emit a series per individual app id, and never per-device install-status series.

## Constraints & gotchas

- `mobileApps` is an abstract base — inspect `@odata.type` for type-specific fields; don't hardcode one shape.
- Avoid `$expand=assignments` on the LIST (deprecated) — expand per-app if assignments are needed.
- App config policy status sub-paths carry the same 2023 backend-routing risk as app-install status — spike a live test before committing to `deviceStatuses`/`userStatuses`; prefer `deviceStatusSummary`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] SnapshotCollector emits catalog counts by type/state + config-policy status gauges against the in-memory **Recorder** with a **faked Graph client** returning mixed-`@odata.type` apps; asserts bounded labels and pagination to exhaustion.
- [ ] Test: no per-device install-status calls are attempted.
- [ ] Graceful skip-and-log on 403 / missing scope (M1 #9).

## Dependencies

M1 #4 (client factory), #5 (rate limiters — Intune bucket), #6 (SnapshotCollector), #8 (Emitter + Recorder), #10 (license detection / degradation).

Live-verified: emits intune.mobile_apps.count{app_type,publishing_state} (branching on @odata.type of the abstract mobileApps base) and intune.mobile_app_config.status{policy_name,status} (via deviceStatusSummary, avoiding the drift-prone deviceStatuses/userStatuses sub-paths). Per-device install status deferred to M5.

body:
## What & why

Inventory metrics for the **Settings Catalog** (`configurationPolicies`), the template-based **deviceManagementIntents**, and **security baselines** — the modern and legacy sides of the same migrating surface. Settings Catalog is Microsoft's forward direction; intents (including security baselines) are migrating into it (`isMigratingToConfigurationPolicy`). This collector polls all three for policy/baseline inventory and, for intents/baselines, the cheap `deviceStateSummary` compliance gauges — while flagging the migration so baseline coverage isn't silently double-counted or dropped.

This is a **merge of three research domains** (Settings Catalog §3, deviceManagementIntents §3, endpoint-security baselines §7) into one issue: they are all beta-only and overlap directly through the intents→Settings-Catalog migration, so tracking them together is the only way to reconcile them without double-counting. SnapshotCollector, app-only read.

## Scope

- [ ] `internal/collectors/intune/settingscatalog` — poll `configurationPolicies` (beta) for policy inventory, bucketed by `platforms`/`technologies`/`templateReference.templateFamily`
- [ ] Poll `intents` (beta) for inventory + `isMigratingToConfigurationPolicy` migration flag + per-intent `deviceStateSummary` compliance gauges
- [ ] Poll `templates?$filter=templateType eq 'securityBaseline'` (beta) + per-template `deviceStateSummary` for baseline secure/notSecure gauges
- [ ] Reconcile intents ↔ configurationPolicies by `templateReference` so a mid-migration tenant (same policy both ways) is not double-counted
- [ ] Register under the `intune`/Device Config bucket
- [ ] Settings Catalog per-device/per-setting status has **no navigation property** — it is export-job-only (`ConfigurationPolicyAggregate` / `ConfigurationPolicyDeviceAggregatesV3`); likewise `DeviceIntentPerSettingStatus` at scale. Fleet-wide per-setting status detail deferred to the **M5 milestone** export-job subsystem; this issue covers the entity/summary endpoints only.

## API surface

| Endpoint | Version | App permission | Pagination | Filter quirks | Throttle bucket |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /deviceManagement/configurationPolicies` (+ `/settings`, `/assignments`) | **beta** | `DeviceManagementConfiguration.Read.All` (endpoint-security-templated also `DeviceManagementEndpointSecurity.Read.All`) | `@odata.nextLink` | `$expand=settings` balloons — GET `.../settings` separately with paging; `PATCH` on `settings` 400s | Device Config v2 bucket |
| `GET /deviceManagement/intents` (+ `deviceStateSummary`) | **beta** | `DeviceManagementConfiguration.Read.All` | `@odata.nextLink`; summary singleton per intent | no documented `$filter` on `deviceStates`; template name via separate `templateId` lookup | Device Config bucket |
| `GET /deviceManagement/templates?$filter=templateType eq 'securityBaseline'` (+ `/{id}/deviceStateSummary`) | **beta** | `DeviceManagementConfiguration.Read.All` | `@odata.nextLink` | `templateType` enum shared across baseline and non-baseline templates — filter carefully | Device Config bucket |

Docs: [configurationPolicy beta](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/intune-deviceconfigv2-devicemanagementconfigurationpolicy?view=graph-rest-beta), [deviceManagementIntent beta](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/intune-deviceintent-devicemanagementintent?view=graph-rest-beta), [securityBaselineDeviceState beta](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/intune-deviceintent-securitybaselinedevicestate?view=graph-rest-beta).

## Telemetry model

`intune.*` namespace.

- `intune.settings_catalog.policy.count` gauge, attrs `{platform, technology, template_family}` — bounded.
- `intune.intent.count` gauge, attrs `{migrating}` (`isMigratingToConfigurationPolicy`).
- `intune.intent.devices` gauge, attrs `{intent_name, compliance_status}` from `deviceStateSummary`.
- `intune.security_baseline.devices` gauge, attrs `{baseline_name, state}` where state ∈ `{secure, notSecure, error, conflict, notApplicable}`.

Baseline/intent/policy names and template families are bounded low-cardinality attributes. Never emit per-device series.

## Constraints & gotchas

- **Beta-only, no v1.0 fallback** for all three — flag as a stability risk for a compliance product; pin the beta endpoint.
- Intents are migrating to `configurationPolicies` — a mid-migration tenant exposes the same policy both ways; reconcile by `templateReference` so you neither double-count nor silently lose baseline coverage.
- Settings Catalog has **no per-device/per-setting status navigation property** — that data is export-job-only, a genuinely different fetch architecture (deferred to M5).
- `templateType` is shared across baseline and non-baseline templates — the `$filter` must isolate `securityBaseline` precisely.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] SnapshotCollector emits policy/intent/baseline inventory + intent/baseline `deviceStateSummary` gauges against the in-memory **Recorder** with a **faked Graph client** (beta payloads); asserts the migration flag drives `intune.intent.count{migrating}` and reconciliation avoids double-counting a policy present both ways.
- [ ] Test: no per-device/per-setting status calls are made (export-only path not attempted here).
- [ ] Graceful skip-and-log on 403 / missing scope / beta unavailability (M1 #9).

## Dependencies

M1 #4 (client factory), #5 (rate limiters — Intune/Device Config bucket), #6 (SnapshotCollector), #8 (Emitter + Recorder), #10 (license detection / degradation).

comments.body: Done in 17a1502. `internal/collectors/intune/settingscatalog`, collector `intune.settings_catalog` (beta, Experimental). Live-verified: emits intune.settings_catalog.policy.count; intents/baselines reconciled by templateReference. Live-caught fix: a per-template `deviceStateSummary` returning 400 "not found for segment" (template type has no summary) is now skipped per-template instead of failing the collector.

body:
## What & why

Metrics for classic **device configuration profiles** (`deviceConfigurations`) — the heterogeneous collection of VPN / Wi-Fi / general-config / update-ring profiles. Emit profile inventory + version-change signals and per-profile deployment-status gauges from `deviceStatusOverview`, without walking per-device status rows. Note: Windows Update rings live in this same collection but have their own collector (feature/quality/driver update profiles issue); this collector covers the general configuration profiles.

SnapshotCollector, app-only read.

## Scope

- [ ] `internal/collectors/intune/configprofiles` — poll `deviceConfigurations` for inventory, bucketed by `@odata.type`, with `version`-change detection
- [ ] Per-profile `deviceStatusOverview` gauges (pending/success/error/failed/notApplicable)
- [ ] Register under the `intune` rate-limit bucket
- [ ] Per-device rows (`deviceStatuses`, `userStatuses`, `deviceSettingStateSummaries`) are per-device×profile → NOT metrics; fleet-wide detail deferred to the **M5 milestone** export-job subsystem — this issue covers inventory + overview only.

## API surface

| Endpoint | Version | App permission | Pagination | Filter quirks | Throttle bucket |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /deviceManagement/deviceConfigurations` (+ `/{id}`) | v1.0 | `DeviceManagementConfiguration.Read.All` | `@odata.nextLink` | heterogeneous collection — settings live on subtypes via `@odata.type` (e.g. `windows10GeneralConfiguration`); always check `@odata.type` | Device Config bucket (2000 any / 200 write per tenant / 20s) |
| `.../deviceConfigurations/{id}/deviceStatusOverview` / `userStatusOverview` | v1.0 | `DeviceManagementConfiguration.Read.All` | singleton per profile | — | fan-out = N profiles |

Docs: [deviceConfiguration v1.0](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/intune-deviceconfig-deviceconfiguration?view=graph-rest-1.0).

## Telemetry model

`intune.*` namespace.

- `intune.config_profile.count` gauge, attrs `{odata_type}` — inventory by profile type.
- `intune.config_profile.status` gauge, attrs `{profile_name, state}` from `deviceStatusOverview`: `pending`, `notApplicable`, `success`, `error`, `failed`. Profile name bounded (single-to-low-double digits typically).
- `intune.config_profile.version` gauge, attrs `{profile_name}` for change detection.

`@odata.type` and profile display names are bounded, low-cardinality attributes. Never emit per-device series.

## Constraints & gotchas

- The collection is heterogeneous (VPN/Wi-Fi/update rings all mixed) — always branch on `@odata.type`; the base type omits subtype settings.
- Overview counts lag actual client check-in by minutes–hours — don't alert on transient mismatches.
- `$expand` on status collections can 400 — hit overview as its own GET, not `$expand`.
- Windows Update ring profiles (`windowsUpdateForBusinessConfiguration`) appear here but are owned by the update-profiles collector — avoid double-emitting; scope this collector to non-update profile types or coordinate the type filter.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] SnapshotCollector emits inventory-by-type + per-profile status gauges against the in-memory **Recorder** with a **faked Graph client** returning a mixed-`@odata.type` collection; asserts type bucketing and bounded profile-name cardinality.
- [ ] Test: `version` bump surfaces on the version gauge.
- [ ] Test: per-device status children are never fetched.
- [ ] Graceful skip-and-log on 403 / missing scope (M1 #9).

## Dependencies

M1 #4 (client factory), #5 (rate limiters — Intune/Device Config bucket), #6 (SnapshotCollector), #8 (Emitter + Recorder), #10 (license detection / degradation).

Separate packages, frozen filter split → both run concurrently.

body:
## What & why

The **compliance** metrics collector — the heart of an Intune compliance product. Emit the tenant-level compliance rollup (the singleton gauge set a dashboard needs), per-policy status overviews, and per-setting compliance summaries, plus a policy-inventory poll that turns `version` bumps into a change-audit signal. Uses the cheap aggregate/overview endpoints throughout and deliberately avoids the per-device×policy×setting status children, which are the primary cardinality bomb.

SnapshotCollector, app-only read.

## Scope

- [ ] `internal/collectors/intune/compliance` — poll `deviceCompliancePolicyDeviceStateSummary` (tenant singleton) as the primary compliance gauge set
- [ ] Poll `deviceCompliancePolicies` for inventory + detect `version` increments (a policy-change signal; the change event itself → logs in a later milestone)
- [ ] Per-policy `deviceStatusOverview` / `userStatusOverview` gauges (bounded by policy count, tens)
- [ ] `deviceCompliancePolicySettingStateSummaries` as per-setting metric source (bounded by unique settings)
- [ ] Register under the `intune` rate-limit bucket
- [ ] Per-device rows (`deviceStatuses`, `userStatuses`, `deviceComplianceSettingStates`, per-device `deviceCompliancePolicyStates`) are device×policy(×setting) cross-products → NOT metrics. On-demand / fleet-wide detail deferred to the **M5 milestone** export-job subsystem (`DeviceNonCompliance`, `DeviceStatusSummaryByCompliacePolicyReport`); this issue covers the summary/overview endpoints only.

## API surface

| Endpoint | Version | App permission | Pagination | Filter quirks | Throttle bucket |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /deviceManagement/deviceCompliancePolicyDeviceStateSummary` | v1.0 | `DeviceManagementConfiguration.Read.All` | none (singleton) | N/A | cheapest call — poll ~5 min |
| `GET /deviceManagement/deviceCompliancePolicies` (+ `/{id}`) | v1.0 | `DeviceManagementConfiguration.Read.All` | `@odata.nextLink` (tens of policies) | base type returns only 6 shared props — request the concrete subtype (e.g. `windows10CompliancePolicy`) for rules; `$expand` on status collections can 400 | Device Config bucket (2000 any / 200 write per tenant / 20s) |
| `.../deviceCompliancePolicies/{id}/deviceStatusOverview` / `userStatusOverview` | v1.0 | `DeviceManagementConfiguration.Read.All` | singleton per policy | — | fan-out = N policies |
| `GET /deviceManagement/deviceCompliancePolicySettingStateSummaries` | v1.0 | `DeviceManagementConfiguration.Read.All` | `@odata.nextLink` | no documented `$filter` | Device Config bucket |

Docs: [deviceCompliancePolicy](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/intune-deviceconfig-devicecompliancepolicy?view=graph-rest-1.0), [deviceCompliancePolicyDeviceStateSummary](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/intune-deviceconfig-devicecompliancepolicydevicestatesummary?view=graph-rest-1.0), [settingStateSummaries list](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/intune-deviceconfig-devicecompliancepolicysettingstatesummary-list?view=graph-rest-1.0), [settingStates list](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/intune-deviceconfig-devicecompliancesettingstate-list?view=graph-rest-1.0).

## Telemetry model

`intune.*` namespace.

- `intune.compliance.devices` gauge, attrs `{state}` for the state summary counts: `compliant`, `nonCompliant`, `inGracePeriod`, `configManager`, `unknown`, `notApplicable`, `remediated`, `error`, `conflict`. This is the tenant-level headline.
- `intune.compliance.policy.devices` gauge, attrs `{policy_name, state}` — per-policy overview counts (`pending`/`success`/`error`/`failed`/`notApplicable`). Policy name is bounded (tens).
- `intune.compliance.setting.devices` gauge, attrs `{setting_name, platform, state}` — from setting-state summaries, bounded by unique settings.
- `intune.compliance.policy.version` gauge, attrs `{policy_name}` — surfaces `version` for change detection.

Never mirror `deviceComplianceSettingStates` (per device per setting per policy, 100k–200k rows) or `deviceStatuses` to metrics.

## Constraints & gotchas

- Base compliance-policy type returns only 6 shared properties — request the platform subtype for actual rules; naive reads look empty.
- Setting-state summaries **aggregate across all policies** checking the same logical setting — you can't attribute a count to one policy without walking per-device states, so don't imply per-policy attribution from the summary.
- Overview counts lag real client check-in by minutes–hours — don't alert on transient mismatches.
- Status lists can return stale rows for deleted/retired devices — cross-check live `managedDevices` before alerting on any per-device path.
- `deviceCompliancePolicyStates` (per device) is omitted from the `managedDevice` relationships table (a docs gap, not a missing endpoint) — verify SDK exposure or fall back to raw REST; out of scope here regardless.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] SnapshotCollector emits the state-summary gauge set + per-policy overview gauges against the in-memory **Recorder** with a **faked Graph client**; asserts the tenant singleton maps to `intune.compliance.devices{state}` and per-policy names stay bounded.
- [ ] Test: `version` bump between polls surfaces on the policy-version gauge.
- [ ] Test: per-setting summaries produce bounded series by unique setting, and per-device status children are never fetched by this collector.
- [ ] Graceful skip-and-log on 403 / missing scope (M1 #9).

## Dependencies

M1 #4 (client factory), #5 (rate limiters — Intune/Device Config bucket), #6 (SnapshotCollector), #8 (Emitter + Recorder), #10 (license detection / degradation).

comments.body: Done in d427cdf. `internal/collectors/intune/compliance`, collector `intune.compliance`. Live-verified: emits intune.compliance.devices{state} (headline), .policy.devices/.policy.users{policy_name,state} (per-policy overview fan-out), .policy.version, .setting.devices{setting_name,platform,state}. No per-device compliance rows. Added .policy.users as its own metric+unit (the Scope checklist requires both device AND user overviews).
