body:
## What & why

Tenant-health gauges for the **Intune connectors** — Exchange, Mobile Threat Defense (MTD), and NDES (SCEP). These are small, low-cardinality, device-count-independent entities, but their health is load-bearing for compliance: an MTD connector past its unresponsiveness threshold means Intune has **stopped using MTD signal for compliance** (a real compliance gap, not just connectivity), and a disconnected Exchange connector explains fleet-wide stale `exchangeAccessState`.

SnapshotCollector, app-only read.

## Scope

- [ ] `internal/collectors/intune/connectors` — poll Exchange + MTD connectors (v1.0), emit connector-state + heartbeat-age gauges
- [ ] Optional NDES connector poll (beta, isolated error handling — see beta-api note; beta path 404s / errors must not fail the whole collector)
- [ ] Explicitly out of scope: no `dataSharingConsent` resource exists (only a `dataSharingConsentGranted` bool on the Apple `depOnboardingSetting`, covered by the Apple-tokens collector)
- [ ] Register under the `intune` rate-limit bucket

## API surface

| Endpoint | Version | App permission | Pagination | Filter quirks | Throttle bucket |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /deviceManagement/exchangeConnectors` | v1.0 | `DeviceManagementServiceConfig.Read.All` | single page (single-digit rows) | no `$filter` — fetch all | negligible |
| `GET /deviceManagement/mobileThreatDefenseConnectors` | v1.0 | `DeviceManagementServiceConfig.Read.All` | single page | no `$filter` | negligible |
| `GET /deviceManagement/ndesConnectors` | **beta** | `DeviceManagementServiceConfig.Read.All` | single page | no `$filter` | negligible |

Docs: [exchangeConnector v1.0](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/intune-onboarding-devicemanagementexchangeconnector?view=graph-rest-1.0), [mobileThreatDefenseConnector v1.0](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/intune-onboarding-mobilethreatdefenseconnector?view=graph-rest-1.0), [ndesConnector beta](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/intune-deviceconfig-ndesconnector?view=graph-rest-beta).

## Telemetry model

`intune.*` namespace. Bounded — connector counts are single-digit.

- `intune.connector.state` gauge, attrs `{connector_type, state}` where `connector_type` ∈ `{exchange, mtd, ndes}`; Exchange `status`, MTD `partnerState`, NDES `state` mapped to a small state enum.
- `intune.connector.heartbeat_age_seconds` gauge, attrs `{connector_type}` — from Exchange `lastSyncDateTime`, MTD `lastHeartbeatDateTime`, NDES `lastConnectionDateTime`.
- Optionally per-platform MTD `*Enabled` flags as gauges attrs `{platform}`.

`serverName` / `connectorVersion` are acceptable low-cardinality attributes (few connectors) but keep them off high-frequency series if unnecessary.

## Constraints & gotchas

- MTD `partnerState = unresponsive` past `partnerUnresponsivenessThresholdInDays` = Intune no longer trusts MTD for compliance — alert on this as a compliance event, not just a heartbeat.
- NDES is **beta-only** — isolate its error handling so a beta 404/500 does not fail the Exchange/MTD portion.
- Exchange `disconnected` is the upstream cause of fleet-wide stale `exchangeAccessState` — surface it as such.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] SnapshotCollector emits state + heartbeat-age gauges for each connector type against the in-memory **Recorder** with a **faked Graph client**; asserts the MTD unresponsive state maps to the alertable value.
- [ ] Test: NDES beta call failing does not prevent Exchange/MTD gauges from emitting.
- [ ] Graceful skip-and-log on 403 / missing scope (M1 #9).

## Dependencies

M1 #4 (client factory), #5 (rate limiters — Intune bucket), #6 (SnapshotCollector), #8 (Emitter + Recorder), #10 (license detection / degradation).

comments.body: M4 seam decision (Group A — NDES ownership, tracker #79): **#51 owns ALL NDES connector-health metrics.** This is the general connector-health collector (Exchange + MTD + NDES), so NDES lives here as `intune.connector.state{connector_type=ndes}` + `intune.connector.heartbeat_age_seconds{connector_type=ndes}`, consistent with the Exchange/MTD dimensions. #63 (certificates) will NOT poll `ndesConnectors` or emit any NDES metric — it defers entirely to this collector. Note: `ndesConnectors` is a beta endpoint, but Exchange/MTD are v1.0, so this collector is NOT `Experimental()` overall; the NDES portion is polled best-effort against /beta with isolated error handling — a beta/NDES failure drops only the NDES points and never fails Exchange/MTD.

Done in d427cdf. `internal/collectors/intune/connectors`, collector `intune.connectors`. Owns ALL NDES connector metrics per the Group A seam decision. Live-verified: emits intune.connector.state{connector_type,state}, .heartbeat_age_seconds, .mtd_platform.total. NDES polled best-effort against /beta with isolated error handling (collector not Experimental overall since Exchange/MTD are v1.0). Live-caught fix: a 403/404/501 (feature not provisioned — verified: exchangeConnectors returns 501 on a tenant with no Exchange connector) now degrades to a graceful per-type skip instead of a collector failure.

body:
## What & why

Emit **software inventory** metrics from Intune's `detectedApps` tenant catalog, using each app's tenant-wide `deviceCount` as the primary low-cost signal ("how widespread is app X"). This answers presence/coverage questions (is the AV agent installed everywhere, how many devices run an EOL browser) without a per-device software walk — the per-device relationship is a device×app cross-product and a cardinality trap.

SnapshotCollector, app-only read, least privilege.

## Scope

- [ ] `internal/collectors/intune/detectedapps` — paginated poll of the tenant `GET /deviceManagement/detectedApps` catalog, emitting `deviceCount`-based coverage gauges bounded to selected/known apps
- [ ] A bounded allow-list (config) of app display names to track as coverage gauges (e.g. security agents) — avoid emitting a series per distinct app+version+publisher tuple
- [ ] Register under the `intune`/Devices rate-limit bucket
- [ ] Per-device software enumeration (`managedDevices/{id}/detectedApps`) is an opt-in, low-cardinality presence check only; fleet-wide per-device detail deferred to the **M5 milestone** export-job subsystem — this issue covers the tenant catalog endpoint only.

## API surface

| Endpoint | Version | App permission | Pagination | Filter quirks | Throttle bucket |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /deviceManagement/detectedApps` | v1.0 | `DeviceManagementManagedDevices.Read.All` | `@odata.nextLink` — catalog can be huge (every app+version+publisher), page to exhaustion | No advertised `$filter` — filter client-side | **Devices** tier (~2000/app per 20s) |
| `GET /deviceManagement/detectedApps/{id}/managedDevices` / `GET /deviceManagement/managedDevices/{id}/detectedApps` | v1.0 | `DeviceManagementManagedDevices.Read.All` | `@odata.nextLink` | throttling-sensitive per-device walk | Devices tier |

Docs: [detectedApp v1.0](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/intune-devices-detectedapp?view=graph-rest-1.0), [detectedApp list](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/intune-devices-detectedapp-list?view=graph-rest-1.0).

## Telemetry model

`intune.*` namespace. Key fields: `displayName`, `version`, `publisher`, `platform`, `sizeInByte`, `deviceCount`.

- `intune.detected_apps.device_count` gauge, attrs `{app_name, platform}` — restricted to the configured allow-list of tracked apps; `deviceCount` answers coverage for free.
- Optionally `intune.detected_apps.catalog_size` gauge (total distinct app tuples) as a single low-cardinality health number.

Never emit a metric series per catalog tuple (tens of thousands) and never a per-device-per-app series. `version`/`publisher` on a tracked app are acceptable low-cardinality attributes only if the allow-list keeps them bounded.

## Constraints & gotchas

- The tenant catalog is bounded by distinct app tuples but can still reach tens of thousands of rows — page fully, then aggregate/select client-side; do not turn the catalog into metric series.
- Per-device `detectedApps` at 10k devices = 10k+ calls with the same cost profile as the `hardwareInformation` sweep — keep it opt-in and bounded.
- No `$filter` support — all selection is client-side.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] SnapshotCollector emits coverage gauges only for allow-listed apps against the in-memory **Recorder** with a **faked Graph client** returning a multi-page catalog; asserts non-listed apps produce no series (bounded cardinality) and `deviceCount` maps to the gauge.
- [ ] Test: pagination to exhaustion.
- [ ] Graceful skip-and-log on 403 / missing scope (M1 #9).

## Dependencies

M1 #4 (client factory), #5 (rate limiters — Intune/Devices bucket), #6 (SnapshotCollector), #8 (Emitter + Recorder), #10 (license detection / degradation).

comments.body: Done in d427cdf. `internal/collectors/intune/detectedapps`, collector `intune.detected_apps`. Live-verified: emits intune.detected_apps.device_count{app_name,platform} for a bounded package-level allow-list (the cardinality boundary — the catalog itself is unbounded and has no server-side $filter), plus an unlabeled intune.detected_apps.catalog_size. Per-device presence check deferred to M5.

body:
## What & why

Poll the Intune **managed device inventory** and emit fleet-wide compliance / encryption / sync-recency gauges, plus a cheap tenant cross-check from the pre-aggregated `managedDeviceOverview` singleton. This is the core Intune metrics collector: the device fleet is the primary subject of everything else in M4, so its aggregate state (how many devices, in what compliance/OS/ownership breakdown, how stale their last sync is) is the headline signal a compliance dashboard needs.

App-only (client credentials) read, least privilege. SnapshotCollector on the M1 framework.

## Scope

- [ ] `internal/collectors/intune/manageddevices` — full-fleet paginated poller of `GET /deviceManagement/managedDevices`, aggregated to bounded-cardinality gauges (never per-device series)
- [ ] Fold in the `managedDeviceOverview` singleton as a cheap cross-check gauge set
- [ ] Opt-in, config-gated slower `hardwareInformation` per-device sweep (beta, disabled by default — see beta-api note)
- [ ] Register with the collector registry / scheduler (M1 #6) under the `intune` rate-limit bucket
- [ ] Per-device detail (per-device hardware, per-device compliance drill-down) is fleet-wide export-job territory: fleet-wide detail deferred to the **M5 milestone** export-job subsystem; this issue covers only the entity/overview endpoints.

## API surface

| Endpoint | Version | App permission | Pagination | Filter quirks | Throttle bucket |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /deviceManagement/managedDevices` | v1.0 | `DeviceManagementManagedDevices.Read.All` | `@odata.nextLink`, small default page — follow to exhaustion | Only annotated props filter: `enrolledDateTime`/`lastSyncDateTime` (`lt`/`gt`), `complianceState`/`jailBroken`/`managementAgent`/`deviceCategoryDisplayName`/ownerType (`eq`/`or`). No group-membership filter. `$search` unsupported. Many props null in LIST | Elevated **Devices** tier (~2000/app, 4000/tenant reads per 20s) |
| `GET /deviceManagement/managedDevices/{id}?$select=hardwareInformation` | **beta** | `DeviceManagementManagedDevices.Read.All` | per-device GET | `hardwareInformation` null in LIST — one GET per device | Devices tier (fans out to 10k+ calls) |
| `GET /deviceManagement/managedDeviceOverview` | v1.0 | `DeviceManagementManagedDevices.Read.All` | none (singleton) | N/A | negligible |

Docs: [managedDevice v1.0](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/intune-devices-manageddevice?view=graph-rest-1.0), [managedDevice list](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/intune-devices-manageddevice-list?view=graph-rest-1.0), [hardwareInformation beta](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/intune-devices-hardwareinformation?view=graph-rest-beta), [managedDeviceOverview v1.0](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/intune-devices-manageddeviceoverview?view=graph-rest-1.0), [throttling limits](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/throttling-limits).

## Telemetry model

All `intune.*` namespace, OTLP dot notation. Aggregate to **bounded** dimensions only — `complianceState`, `operatingSystem`, `managementAgent`, `managedDeviceOwnerType`. Device identifiers (`serialNumber`, `imei`, `deviceName`, device `id`, UPN) are unbounded and MUST NOT appear as metric labels; they belong on log records / exemplars only.

- `intune.devices.count` gauge, attrs `{compliance_state, operating_system}` — self-rolled fleet count from the paged LIST.
- `intune.devices.encrypted.count` gauge, attrs `{operating_system}` — from `isEncrypted`.
- `intune.devices.sync_staleness_seconds` — either a bucketed count gauge (`{staleness_bucket}`) or histogram from `lastSyncDateTime`; do not label by device.
- `intune.devices.overview.total` gauge, attrs `{os}` from `deviceOperatingSystemSummary.*`; plus `enrolledDeviceCount`, `mdmEnrolledCount`, `dualEnrolledDeviceCount` as separate gauges — the Microsoft-aggregated cross-check.

Prefer the overview singleton and the self-rolled aggregate over any per-device walk.

## Constraints & gotchas

- Intune OData is heavily restricted — most `$filter`/`$orderby` 400 on unannotated props; aggregate client-side after paging, don't guess filters.
- `hardwareInformation` and `deviceHealthScriptStates` are **beta-only** and null in LIST, needing a per-device GET (~10k+ extra calls per cycle, ≥100s serialized at the throttle ceiling). Keep the sweep opt-in and default-off. Prefer the **free** v1.0 `deviceHealthAttestationState` (BitLocker/SecureBoot/TPM, embedded in the LIST) for attestation signals.
- `managementAgent` enum has extra beta values — don't hardcode the v1.0 set when reading beta.
- Devices tier throttle is elevated but `Retry-After` may be absent on Intune endpoints — rely on the client-side limiter + exponential backoff from M1 #5, not server hints.
- `managedDeviceOverview` can drift slightly from live count (aggregation lag) — it's a sanity gauge, not a replacement for the self-rolled count.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] SnapshotCollector emits the bounded gauges above against the in-memory telemetry **Recorder** with a **faked Graph client** returning canned `managedDevices` pages + an overview singleton; asserts counts aggregate correctly by state/OS and that no device identifier appears as a label.
- [ ] Test: pagination followed to exhaustion across multiple `@odata.nextLink` pages.
- [ ] Test: `hardwareInformation` sweep is skipped when the config flag is off (zero per-device GETs issued).
- [ ] Degrades gracefully (skip-and-log, per M1 #9/#10) if the tenant lacks the scope / returns 403 — no crash.
- [ ] Cardinality: unbounded fields kept off metric labels (assert in test).

## Dependencies

M1 #4 (Graph client factory), #5 (per-workload rate limiters — Intune/Devices bucket), #6 (SnapshotCollector framework + scheduler), #8 (telemetry Emitter + Recorder), #10 (license-tier detection / graceful degradation).

comments.body: Done in d427cdf. `internal/collectors/intune/manageddevices`, collector `intune.devices`. Live-verified against a real Intune tenant: emits intune.devices.count{compliance_state,operating_system}, .encrypted.count, .sync_staleness_seconds{staleness_bucket}, and the managedDeviceOverview cross-checks (enrolled/mdm/dual + by-OS). Full-fleet paged with `$select` and bucketed client-side (managedDevices has no `$count` segment and operatingSystem is not server-filterable — verified live). The beta hardwareInformation per-device sweep is deferred (10k+ calls/cycle; no per-collector config gate yet).

body:
## What & why

The flagship compliance metric for this exporter: **app-registration and service-principal credential expiry**. Secrets (`passwordCredentials`) and certs (`keyCredentials`) live on both `applications` and `servicePrincipals`; an expired or soon-to-expire credential silently breaks integrations. Credential-expiry monitoring is a top driver for graph2otel. This collector covers both object types (they carry identical credential shapes) and must apply a careful cardinality strategy — big tenants have thousands of app×credential pairs.

## Scope

- [ ] Add collector `internal/collectors/entra/credentials` implementing `SnapshotCollector` (#6).
- [ ] Read `applications` and `servicePrincipals`, `$select`ing `appId`, `displayName`, `passwordCredentials`, `keyCredentials`.
- [ ] Emit per-credential expiry only within a configurable window of expiry; emit tenant-wide aggregate buckets always.
- [ ] Register under `entra.credentials` collector key (#2), with the near-expiry window configurable.

## API surface

| Endpoint | Version | App permission | Pagination | Filter/delta | Throttle bucket |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /applications?$select=appId,displayName,passwordCredentials,keyCredentials` | v1.0 | `Application.Read.All` (or `Directory.Read.All`) | nextLink, default 100 | `$filter`, `$count` (advanced query); delta on `/applications/delta` | Directory objects |
| `GET /servicePrincipals?$select=...` | v1.0 | `Application.Read.All` (or `Directory.Read.All`) | nextLink | delta on `/servicePrincipals/delta` | Directory objects |

Docs: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/application-list?view=graph-rest-1.0 , https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/serviceprincipal-list?view=graph-rest-1.0

## Telemetry model

**Cardinality strategy (per research §18 — this is the load-bearing decision):**

- `entra.app.credential.expiry_days{object_type,app_id,app_display_name,key_id,credential_type}` (gauge) — days until `endDateTime`. **Per-series ONLY for credentials within N days of expiry** (configurable window, e.g. 60). `object_type` ∈ `application|service_principal`; `credential_type` ∈ `secret|cert`. `key_id` is bounded per app but total per-series cardinality is capped by the near-expiry window, not tenant size.
- `entra.app.credentials.expiring.total{object_type,credential_type,window}` (gauge) — aggregate count of credentials expiring within each bucket (`window` ∈ `7d|30d|90d`). Always emitted, tenant-shaped, cheap.
- `entra.app.credentials.expired.total{object_type,credential_type}` (gauge) — count already expired.
- **Rule:** the per-credential series must be bounded by the near-expiry window; the always-on signal is the aggregate buckets. A series count that grows with total apps×credentials rather than with the near-expiry set is a bug.

## Constraints & gotchas

- Advanced `$count`/`$filter` on applications needs `ConsistencyLevel: eventual`.
- Delta is available on both resources but this is a point-in-time gauge — snapshot each cycle (delta can shrink the read cost of the full-list scan in large tenants; treat as an optimization, not required for v1).
- Free tier; no `#10` dependency.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Tests against the `Recorder` (#8) with a faked Graph client returning credentials at varied `endDateTime`s: per-credential series emitted only for those inside the near-expiry window; aggregate buckets counted correctly across the full set.
- [ ] Test that a tenant with thousands of far-future credentials produces only aggregate series plus the bounded near-expiry set (cardinality guard).
- [ ] Test both `application` and `service_principal` object types and both `secret`/`cert` types.
- [ ] `make check` green.

## Dependencies

- #4, #5, #6, #8.

comments.body: Done in c7cc115. `internal/collectors/entra/credentialexpiry` emits `entra.credentials.expiring.total` by owner_type × credential_type × expiry_bucket (expired|lt_7d|lt_30d|lt_90d|gt_90d) — exactly 20 fixed series regardless of tenant/credential count. `Application.Read.All`. The issue's per-credential drill-down gauge was intentionally not built: keyId/appId/displayName must never be metric labels (cardinality rule); that detail belongs in the logs pipeline. **Live-verified** — expiry buckets emit end to end. `make check` green.

body:
## What & why

Tenant/organization details and — the operationally useful part — a **directory-sync freshness** gauge. `GET /organization` returns `onPremisesSyncEnabled` and `onPremisesLastSyncDateTime`; the age of the last sync is an alertable "AD Connect sync is stale" signal. Tenant id / displayName / verified domains also feed the resource attributes attached to all telemetry.

## Scope

- [ ] Add collector `internal/collectors/entra/organization` implementing `SnapshotCollector` (#6).
- [ ] Emit sync-freshness and posture gauges.
- [ ] Expose tenant id / displayName as resource attributes for the tenant's telemetry (coordinate with the resource-attribute wiring in #8).

## API surface

## What & why

License inventory and utilization: per SKU, emit consumed units and enabled (prepaid) units so operators get utilization % and "seats remaining" gauges — a top cost/compliance signal. Plus an aggregate count of license **assignment errors** (`licenseAssignmentStates` in `Error` state), which flags users whose license failed to apply.

## Scope

- [ ] Add collector `internal/collectors/entra/licensing` implementing `SnapshotCollector` (#6).
- [ ] Poll `GET /subscribedSkus` and emit per-SKU consumed/enabled gauges.
- [ ] Aggregate assignment-error count (do not page every user for a per-user series).
- [ ] Register under `entra.licensing` collector key (#2).

## API surface

| Endpoint | Version | App permission | Pagination | Filter/delta | Throttle bucket |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /subscribedSkus` | v1.0 | `Organization.Read.All` (or `Directory.Read.All`) | small collection (no real paging) | `$select`; no `$filter`; no delta | Directory objects |
| `GET /users/{id}/licenseDetails` / `licenseAssignmentStates` | v1.0 | `User.Read.All` (or `Directory.Read.All`) | per-user | no delta | Directory objects |

Docs: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/subscribedsku-list?view=graph-rest-1.0

## Telemetry model

- `entra.license.consumed{sku}` (gauge) — `consumedUnits` per SKU (`skuPartNumber` as `sku`).
- `entra.license.enabled{sku}` (gauge) — `prepaidUnits.enabled` per SKU.
- `entra.license.assignment_errors.total` (gauge) — aggregate count across the tenant; optionally sliced by `sku`. Never per-user.
- Cardinality: one series per SKU (bounded, tens of SKUs). `sku` is tenant-shaped, not user-shaped.

## Constraints & gotchas

- `subscribedSkus` does not support rich `$filter` and has no delta — full read each cycle (it is small).
- Assignment-error detection may require scanning `licenseAssignmentStates`; aggregate the count rather than emitting per-user series.
- Free tier (reading your own SKUs); no `#10` dependency.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Tests against the `Recorder` (#8) with a faked Graph client: per-SKU consumed/enabled gauges emit with `sku` attribute.
- [ ] Test that assignment errors are surfaced as an aggregate count, not per-user series.
- [ ] `make check` green.

## Dependencies

- #4, #5, #6, #8.

comments.body: Done in e6f6244. `internal/collectors/entra/licensing` emits `entra.license.consumed{sku}` and `entra.license.enabled{sku}` (bounded per-SKU GaugeSnapshots). The assignment-errors aggregate was deliberately not built — classic licensing exposes failures only per-user (`licenseAssignmentStates`) with no v1.0 tenant-level aggregate, so counting them would mean paging every user (the scale anti-pattern the framework avoids); documented in the package doc. **Live-verified against a real tenant** — per-SKU consumed/enabled gauges emit. `make check` green.

## What & why

Aggregate directory-device gauges: total registered/joined devices sliced by `trustType` (Azure AD joined / hybrid / workplace), compliance state, managed state and operating system, plus a stale-device gauge from `approximateLastSignInDateTime`. These are the **directory** `/devices` objects, distinct from Intune `managedDevices` (a different workload + license, covered in M4).

- [ ] Add collector `internal/collectors/entra/devices` implementing `SnapshotCollector` (#6).

body:
## What & why

Aggregate group-population gauges: total groups sliced by type (security vs Microsoft 365), membership model (dynamic vs assigned), and — importantly — a dedicated **role-assignable group** count. Role-assignable groups are privileged (they can be granted directory roles), so a standalone gauge for them is a direct compliance signal.

## Scope

- [ ] Add collector `internal/collectors/entra/groups` implementing `SnapshotCollector` (#6).
- [ ] Emit group counts from sliced `$count` calls.
- [ ] Dedicated `role_assignable` gauge (`isAssignableToRole eq true`).
- [ ] Optional per-group member counts for a small **curated** set of privileged groups only (config-driven allowlist) — never all groups.
- [ ] Register under `entra.groups` collector key (#2).

## API surface

| Endpoint | Version | App permission | Pagination | Filter/delta | Throttle bucket |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /groups/$count?$filter=...` | v1.0 | `Group.Read.All` (or `Directory.Read.All`) | n/a (scalar) | `$filter` (`securityEnabled`, `mailEnabled`, `groupTypes/any(...)`, `isAssignableToRole`); delta on `/groups/delta` not needed for counts | Directory objects |
| `GET /groups/{id}/members/$count` | v1.0 | `GroupMember.Read.All` | n/a | curated groups only | Directory objects |

Docs: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/group-list?view=graph-rest-1.0

## Telemetry model

- `entra.groups.total` (gauge) — attributes `group_type` (`security|m365`, derived from `groupTypes` containing `Unified`), `membership_type` (`dynamic|assigned`), `security_enabled`, `mail_enabled`. Bounded.
- `entra.groups.role_assignable.total` (gauge) — no per-group dimension.
- `entra.groups.members.total{group}` (gauge, optional) — only for the curated privileged-group allowlist; `group` attribute is bounded by the allowlist size, not tenant size.
- Cardinality: bounded by slice dimensions. `transitiveMembers` on large groups is expensive and high-cardinality — restrict to the curated set only.

## Constraints & gotchas

- Multi-valued `$filter` (`groupTypes/any(...)`) needs `ConsistencyLevel: eventual` + `$count=true`.
- Do not enumerate members of all groups — that is a cardinality and throttle hazard. The member-count feature is opt-in and allowlist-scoped.
- Free tier; no `#10` dependency.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Tests against the `Recorder` (#8) with a faked Graph client: type/membership slices and the role-assignable gauge emit correctly.
- [ ] Test that per-group member counts are emitted only for configured allowlist entries.
- [ ] `make check` green.

## Dependencies

- #4, #5, #6, #8.

body:
## What & why

Defender / antimalware agent health across a Windows fleet is best pulled via the `DefenderAgents` (and `UnhealthyDefenderAgents`) export reports rather than by paging per-device `windowsProtectionState` (which does not batch — 10k devices = 10k+ GETs and blows the throttling budget). The tenant `windowsMalwareOverview` singleton gives a cheap top-line summary, but per-device agent health at scale is an export job. This issue wires `DefenderAgents` through the export-job subsystem (#17).

## Scope

- [ ] Consume the export-job subsystem (#17) with `reportName = DefenderAgents` (and optionally `UnhealthyDefenderAgents`) and explicit `select`.
- [ ] Parse per-device agent-health rows; emit health-state count gauges and per-device unhealthy rows as logs.
- [ ] Optionally pull the cheap `windowsMalwareOverview` singleton (v1.0 entity, not export) as a cross-check top-line gauge — note this can be a small follow-up, the export is the core of this issue.
- [ ] Per-tenant enable + schedule; pace under the export budget; smoke-test report names + `select` columns live.

## API surface

| Endpoint/report | Version | App permission | Flow | Throttle bucket |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `POST .../reports/exportJobs` `reportName=DefenderAgents` (also `UnhealthyDefenderAgents`) | v1.0 (export mechanism) | write to create (see #17); read to fetch | Export subsystem (#17) | Export API: 48/min per app |
| `GET /deviceManagement/windowsMalwareOverview` (optional cross-check) | v1.0 | `DeviceManagementManagedDevices.Read.All` | Singleton GET | General Intune (M1 rate limiter #5) |

Report columns: per-device Defender agent state, signature/engine versions and freshness, real-time-protection / tamper-protection flags, malware-protection-enabled, scan-overdue flags, device identifiers. Overview: `malwareDetectedDeviceCount`, `totalMalwareCount`, per-severity/category summaries.

Docs: [Export Intune reports using Graph APIs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/device-management/reports/export-graph-apis), [Available reports](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/intune-service/fundamentals/reports-export-graph-available-reports), [windowsProtectionState (per-device entity, column reference)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/intune-devices-windowsprotectionstate?view=graph-rest-1.0), [windowsMalwareOverview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/intune-devices-windowsmalwareoverview?view=graph-rest-1.0).

## Telemetry model

Snapshot → OTLP **metric** gauges: device counts by Defender health state (healthy / unhealthy dimensions — real-time protection off, signatures overdue, tamper protection off, scan overdue), plus the optional `windowsMalwareOverview` top-line counts. Per-device unhealthy detail → **logs** (device identifiers). No per-device metric series.

## Constraints & gotchas

- Per-device `windowsProtectionState` does not batch — the export report is the scale path; use the entity only for the cheap tenant `windowsMalwareOverview` cross-check.
- `windowsMalwareInformation` is the malware **catalog** (definitions), NOT per-device infection state — do not confuse it with agent health.
- Explicit `select` always; smoke-test report names/columns live (400 on unrecognized name).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Report collector runs on #17 and produces typed Defender-agent rows.
- [ ] Health-state count gauges emitted; per-device unhealthy rows as logs.
- [ ] `httptest`-backed test (via #17's fake) covering parse of a representative `DefenderAgents` payload (CSV + JSON), including an unhealthy-agent row (signatures overdue / RTP off).
- [ ] Graceful skip-and-log if the export write scope is absent.

## Dependencies

- **#17 (export-job subsystem)** — required.
- M1 #8 (Emitter — metrics + logs)
- M1 #5 (Intune rate limiter — for the optional `windowsMalwareOverview` cross-check)
- M1 #4 (Graph client factory)

## What & why

Fleet-wide device certificate inventory has **no entity endpoint** — the `AllDeviceCertificates` (and `CertificatesByRAPolicy`) reports are export-job-only. The per-device beta `managedDeviceCertificateStates` resource exists but does not scale to a full fleet inventory and has no clean join back to `managedDevice`; the export report is the fleet-wide source. This issue wires `AllDeviceCertificates` through the export-job subsystem (#17) to produce a certificate-expiry / issuance-state inventory across the fleet.

## Scope

- [ ] Consume the export-job subsystem (#17) with `reportName = AllDeviceCertificates` and explicit `select`.
- [ ] Parse per-certificate rows; derive days-until-expiry and collapse the ~20-value issuance-state enum to healthy/pending/failed/revoked for metrics.
- [ ] Emit expiry-bucket / state-count gauges as metrics; per-cert detail as logs.
- [ ] Per-tenant enable + schedule; pace under the export budget; smoke-test the report name + `select` columns live.

## API surface

| Endpoint/report | Version | App permission | Flow | Throttle bucket |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `POST .../reports/exportJobs` `reportName=AllDeviceCertificates` (also `CertificatesByRAPolicy`) | v1.0 (export mechanism) | write to create (see #17); read to fetch | Export subsystem (#17) | Export API: 48/min per app |

Columns (mirror the per-device beta resource): `certificateIssuanceState`, `certificateExpirationDateTime`, `certificateRevokeStatus`, `certificateProfileDisplayName`, device/user display names, `certificateThumbprint`, `certificateErrorCode`.

Docs: [Export Intune reports using Graph APIs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/device-management/reports/export-graph-apis), [Available reports](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/intune-service/fundamentals/reports-export-graph-available-reports), [managedDeviceCertificateState (beta, column reference)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/intune-deviceconfig-manageddevicecertificatestate?view=graph-rest-beta).

## Telemetry model

Snapshot → OTLP **metric** gauges: certificate counts bucketed by days-until-expiry and by collapsed issuance state, keyed by `certificateProfileDisplayName` (bounded). Per-cert detail (`certificateThumbprint`, device/user names, `certificateErrorCode`) → **logs** only. Do not key metrics on thumbprint or device name (unbounded).

## Constraints & gotchas

- **No entity form for a fleet inventory** — export is the only path; there is no `deviceManagementCertificationAuthority` resource and Cloud PKI health has no stable public Graph resource (honest gap — document it).
- Collapse the ~20-value `certificateIssuanceState` enum for alerting/metrics (cardinality); keep the raw value on the log record.
- Explicit `select` always; smoke-test the report name/columns live.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Report collector runs on #17 and produces typed certificate rows.
- [ ] Days-until-expiry and state-count gauges emitted per cert profile; per-cert detail as logs.
- [ ] Issuance-state enum collapse covered by a test.
- [ ] `httptest`-backed test (via #17's fake) covering parse of a representative `AllDeviceCertificates` payload (CSV + JSON), including a near-expiry and a failed-issuance row.
- [ ] Graceful skip-and-log if the export write scope is absent.

## Dependencies

- **#17 (export-job subsystem)** — required.
- M1 #8 (Emitter — metrics + logs)
- M1 #4 (Graph client factory)

body:
## What & why

The `EnrollmentFailures` export report is the async, backfill/deep-dive counterpart to the live enrollment troubleshooting event stream (#15). It exposes the same enrollment-failure domain via the reports export API with a different column set and freshness profile. Use the live event stream (#15) for continuous logs; use this export for cold-start backfill and richer per-failure detail. Beta-only export, so flagged `beta-api`.

## Scope

- [ ] Consume the export-job subsystem (#17) with `reportName = EnrollmentFailures` and explicit `select`.
- [ ] Map its column set (independent from `enrollmentTroubleshootingEvent`) to enrollment-failure log records / failure-count metrics.
- [ ] Position it as optional backfill/deep-dive alongside the live collector (#15); avoid double-counting the same failures across both surfaces.
- [ ] Per-tenant enable + schedule; pace under the export budget; smoke-test the report name + `filter` DSL against a live tenant.

## API surface

| Endpoint/report | Version | App permission | Flow | Throttle bucket |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `POST .../reports/exportJobs` `reportName=EnrollmentFailures` | **beta-only** (export mechanism v1.0+beta; this report beta) | write to create (see #17); read to fetch | Export subsystem (#17) | Export API: 48/min per app |

Report `filter` is a mini-DSL (`EnrollmentFailureDateTime` / `EnrollmentMethod` / `FailureReason` / `OS` / `UserId`), not OData. Columns cover failure category/reason, enrollment method, OS, user, timestamps.

Docs: [Export Intune reports using Graph APIs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/device-management/reports/export-graph-apis), [Available reports](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/intune-service/fundamentals/reports-export-graph-available-reports), [enrollmentTroubleshootingEvent (live surface, context)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/intune-troubleshooting-enrollmenttroubleshootingevent?view=graph-rest-1.0).

## Telemetry model

Per-failure rows → OTLP **logs** (user/device identifiers, `failureReason`); failure counts by category / OS / enrollment method → **metric** gauges (bounded enums). Keep this surface's records distinguishable from the live collector's (#15) so operators can tell backfill from continuous data.

## Constraints & gotchas

- **Beta-only report** — pin and isolate; flag as a stability risk.
- **Overlaps #15** — the export and the live `enrollmentTroubleshootingEvent` stream are independent surfaces with different columns and freshness. Do not merge them blindly; use the export for backfill/deep-dive, the event stream for continuous logs.
- `filter` is the report-specific DSL (not OData); explicit `select` always; smoke-test the name/columns live (400 on unrecognized name).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Report collector runs on #17 and produces typed enrollment-failure rows.
- [ ] Failure-count gauges + per-failure logs emitted, clearly attributable to the export surface (not conflated with #15).
- [ ] `httptest`-backed test (via #17's fake) covering parse of a representative `EnrollmentFailures` payload (CSV + JSON).
- [ ] Graceful skip-and-log if the export write scope or the beta report is unavailable.

## Dependencies

- **#17 (export-job subsystem)** — required.
- #15 (live enrollment troubleshooting events — the complementary continuous surface; coordinate to avoid double-counting)
- M1 #8 (Emitter — metrics + logs)
- M1 #4 (Graph client factory)

comments.body: Closing as NOT FEASIBLE via the export API (validated live). The Intune reports export endpoint rejects this report: `POST /deviceManagement/reports/exportJobs` with reportName=DeviceEnrollmentFailures returns HTTP 400 "PostExportJobAsync not supported for reportType DeviceEnrollmentFailures". Microsoft lists DeviceEnrollmentFailures in the available-reports reference but it is not export-job-supported. There is no fleet-wide exportable enrollment-failures report. Enrollment-failure data is already covered by the live `intune.enrollment_events` WindowCollector (#15, shipped in 971667e) over /deviceManagement/troubleshootingEvents. Revisit only if Microsoft adds export support for this report.

| Endpoint | Version | App permission | Pagination | Filter/delta | Throttle bucket |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /users/$count?$filter=...` | v1.0 | `User.Read.All` (or `Directory.Read.All`) | n/a (scalar) | `$filter` (`accountEnabled`, `userType`); delta available on `/users/delta` but not needed for counts | Directory objects |
| `GET /users?$select=signInActivity` | v1.0 | `AuditLog.Read.All` **and** `User.Read.All` | nextLink, `$top`<=500 | `$filter` on `signInActivity/lastSignInDateTime` | Reporting (`signInActivity` special-cased: ~10 req/min) |

Docs: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/user-list?view=graph-rest-1.0

## Telemetry model

- `entra.users.total` (gauge) — attributes `account_enabled` (`true|false`), `user_type` (`member|guest`), `on_premises_sync_enabled` (`true|false`). All bounded.
- `entra.users.stale.total` (gauge, P1-gated) — attribute `threshold_days` (bounded set, e.g. `30|90`). A single count of users whose `lastSignInDateTime` is older than the threshold — never a per-user series.
- Cardinality: bounded by the slice dimensions. **Never emit a per-user time series** — tenants reach 10k–100k+ users; per-user data belongs in the logs pipeline if anywhere.

## Constraints & gotchas

- Sliced `$count` needs `ConsistencyLevel: eventual` + advanced-query operators.
- `signInActivity` is special-cased by Graph: selecting it moves the call onto the **reporting workload** (~10 req/min) and requires `AuditLog.Read.All` on top of `User.Read.All`. Keep `$top<=500` and only select it when the stale gauge is enabled.
- The `signInActivity` property is **P1/P2-gated** — detect via #10 and degrade gracefully (skip the stale gauge, still emit population counts) rather than crashing.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Tests against the in-memory `Recorder` (#8) with a faked Graph client: population gauges emitted with correct slice attributes.
- [ ] Test that with license detection reporting "not P1", the stale-accounts path is skipped-and-logged and population counts still emit.
- [ ] Test asserting no per-user series is ever produced.
- [ ] `make check` green.

## Dependencies

- #4, #5, #6, #8; #10 (license detection) for the stale-accounts gauge.

comments.body: Done in 98bd0f1 (+ fix 9604905). `internal/collectors/entra/users` emits `entra.users.total` sliced by account_enabled/user_type/on_premises_sync_enabled (bounded, sum-not-product) and P1/P2-gated `entra.users.stale.total` by threshold_days (30|90). Partial-degrade: population always emits; stale only under P1 **or** P2 (per current docs signInActivity is licensed under either). No per-user series. `User.Read.All` + `AuditLog.Read.All`. **Live-verified end to end** — this surfaced a real bug: `/users/$count` returns HTTP 502 on a signInActivity filter, so the stale count now uses the `$count=true` collection form reading @odata.count (`collectors.CountViaCollection`); both population and stale gauges emit against the real tenant.

## What & why

Per-device Windows feature-update rollout status has **no device-level Graph navigation property** — the `windowsFeatureUpdateProfiles` resource only exposes `assignments`. Per-device state and failures are export-job-only: `FeatureUpdateDeviceState` (per-device), `FeatureUpdatePolicyStatusSummary` (per-policy rollup), `FeatureUpdatePolicyFailuresAggregate` (failures). This issue wires those reports through the export-job subsystem (#17) to report feature-update compliance for the fleet.

## Scope

- [ ] Consume the export-job subsystem (#17) with `reportName = FeatureUpdatePolicyStatusSummary` (per-policy rollup → gauges) and `FeatureUpdateDeviceState` (per-device → logs).
- [ ] Optionally pull `FeatureUpdatePolicyFailuresAggregate` for failure counts.
- [ ] Explicit `select` per report; per-tenant enable + schedule; pace under the export budget.
- [ ] Smoke-test report names + valid `select` columns against a live tenant.

## API surface

| Endpoint/report | Version | App permission | Flow | Throttle bucket |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `POST .../reports/exportJobs` `reportName=FeatureUpdatePolicyStatusSummary` / `FeatureUpdateDeviceState` / `FeatureUpdatePolicyFailuresAggregate` | v1.0 (export mechanism); underlying profiles are beta | write to create (see #17); read to fetch | Export subsystem (#17) | Export API: 48/min per app |

Profile config (context, not this issue's data): `windowsFeatureUpdateProfiles` is beta-only, `featureUpdateVersion` / `rolloutSettings` / `endOfSupportDate`. Report columns: per-device update state, target version, error/failure detail, device identifiers; summary counts by state per policy.

Docs: [Export Intune reports using Graph APIs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/device-management/reports/export-graph-apis), [Available reports](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/intune-service/fundamentals/reports-export-graph-available-reports), [windowsFeatureUpdateProfile (beta, context)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/intune-softwareupdate-windowsfeatureupdateprofile?view=graph-rest-beta).

## Telemetry model

`FeatureUpdatePolicyStatusSummary` → OTLP **metric** gauges: device counts by update state, keyed by policy (bounded) and state enum. `FeatureUpdateDeviceState` per-device rows → **logs** (device identifiers, error detail). No per-device metric series.

## Constraints & gotchas

- No device-level Graph relationship on the profile — export is the only per-device path (don't assume symmetry with other update types that do expose `deviceStatuses`).
- Report families gain `V2`/`V3` variants — verify the current name in the available-reports reference.
- Explicit `select` always; smoke-test names/columns live.
- Underlying feature-update profiles are beta — the export report names themselves are the stable interface here, but flag the beta dependency in design notes.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Report collector runs on #17 and produces typed rows for both the summary and per-device reports.
- [ ] Per-policy state gauges emitted; per-device rows emitted as logs.
- [ ] `httptest`-backed test (via #17's fake) covering parse of a representative `FeatureUpdatePolicyStatusSummary` and `FeatureUpdateDeviceState` payload (CSV + JSON), including a device in a failed/error state.
- [ ] Graceful skip-and-log if the export write scope is absent.

## Dependencies

- **#17 (export-job subsystem)** — required.
- M1 #8 (Emitter — metrics + logs)
- M1 #4 (Graph client factory)

comments.body: Deferring — NOT feasible as a fleet-wide export in v1 (validated live). `POST /deviceManagement/reports/exportJobs` with reportName=FeatureUpdatePolicyStatusSummary returns HTTP 400 "Bad client request" (a request-validation failure, distinct from #40's explicit not-supported). Consistent with the issue's own note that Windows-update reports are keyed per PolicyId with no fleet-wide form — like DeviceInstallStatusByApp (#37) which required a mandatory per-app filter, this report likely needs a per-policy filter, i.e. a per-policy export fan-out that is out of scope for v1. The export subsystem (#17) and the pattern are proven (see #37/#41/#42); a per-policy feature-update export can be added post-v1. Windows Update *ring* config/pause/rollback state is already covered by the M4 `intune.updates` collector (#59).

Definitive re-verification (post-deferral): rebuilt the summary-only collector with the EXACT authoritative `FeatureUpdatePolicyStatusSummary` columns (PolicyId, PolicyName, CountDevicesSuccessStatus, CountDevicesErrorStatus, CountDevicesInProgressStatus, CountDevicesCancelledStatus, CountOfNeedsReviewDrivers, CountOfPausedDrivers) and live-tested against the tenant — it STILL returns HTTP 400 "Bad client request". So the deferral is confirmed: the feature-update report family has no fleet-wide export form; it requires a per-PolicyId scope on BOTH the summary and the device-state reports.

Captured for the post-v1 pickup (a per-policy export fan-out):
- `FeatureUpdateDeviceState` real columns (verified against Microsoft's reference — none of the original guesses were in it, which explains the earlier 400): AlertClassification, AlertId, AlertMessage, AlertMessageData, AlertMessageDescription, AlertStatus, AlertType, Build, DeviceId, DeviceName, EventDateTimeUTC, ExtendedRecommendedAction, FeatureUpdateVersion, LastUpdatedAlertStatusDateTimeUTC, PolicyId, PolicyName, RecommendedAction, ResolvedDateTimeUTC, StartDateTimeUTC, UPN, Win32ErrorCode, WindowsUpdateVersion.
- Reconstruction path: enumerate feature-update policies (the M4 `intune.updates` collector already pages them), then one Export per policy with `Filter: "(PolicyId eq '<id>')"`, for both the summary and device-state reports. Tradeoff: N exports/cycle share the single 48/min export budget across all M5 export collectors — a rate-budget decision, which is why it's deferred rather than shipped as a guess.
- Windows Update *ring* config/pause/rollback state is already covered by the M4 `intune.updates` collector (#59); this issue is specifically the per-policy feature-update device COUNTS, which stay post-v1.

The export subsystem + pattern are proven (see #37/#41/#42, all live-verified end-to-end).

body:
## What & why

App install status (which devices/users installed a given app, and why installs failed) is **only** available at fleet scale via the reports export API. The synchronous navigation properties (`mobileApps/{id}/deviceStatuses` / `userStatuses` / `installSummary`) are beta, were deprecated in May 2023, and are reportedly broken (`BadRequest, Resource not found`) — the export report is the **only** working path. This issue wires the `DeviceInstallStatusByApp` report (and its aggregate siblings) through the export-job subsystem (#17).

## Scope

- [ ] Consume the export-job subsystem (#17) with `reportName = DeviceInstallStatusByApp` and an explicit `select`.
- [ ] Optionally also pull `UserInstallStatusAggregateByApp` / `AppInstallStatusAggregate` for aggregate rollups.
- [ ] Parse per-device install rows; emit aggregate install-state counts as metrics and per-device rows as logs.
- [ ] Per-tenant enable + schedule config; pace under the export budget (48/min per app).
- [ ] Smoke-test the exact `reportName` spelling and valid `select` columns against a live tenant before hardcoding.

## API surface

| Endpoint/report | Version | App permission | Flow | Throttle bucket |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `POST /deviceManagement/reports/exportJobs` `reportName=DeviceInstallStatusByApp` (also `UserInstallStatusAggregateByApp`, `AppInstallStatusAggregate`) | v1.0 (export mechanism) | write scope to create the job (see #17); read to fetch | Export subsystem (#17): POST → poll → download → parse | Export API: 48/min per app |

Key columns: aggregate `installedDeviceCount`, `failedDeviceCount`, `notApplicableDeviceCount`, `notInstalledDeviceCount`, `pendingInstallDeviceCount` (+ `*UserCount`); per-device `installState`, `installStateDetail`, `errorCode`, `lastSyncDateTime`, app + device identifiers.

Docs: [Export Intune reports using Graph APIs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/device-management/reports/export-graph-apis), [Available reports](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/intune-service/fundamentals/reports-export-graph-available-reports), [mobileAppInstallSummary (deprecated nav — for context only)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/intune-apps-mobileappinstallsummary?view=graph-rest-beta).

## Telemetry model

Snapshot (report has no per-event timestamp). Aggregate counts → OTLP **metric** gauges keyed by app (`appId` / `displayName`) and `installState` — app identity is bounded (the catalog is small), so it is an acceptable metric label; per-device `installStateDetail` / `errorCode` / device identifiers go to **logs** only. Never emit a per-device-per-app metric series (10k × app-count explosion).

## Constraints & gotchas

- **The deprecated/broken nav props are not a fallback** — export is the only path. Do not implement against `mobileApps/{id}/deviceStatuses`.
- Per-app × per-device is a large cross-product (10k × 50 apps = 500k rows) — the ZIP file size, not row count, is the practical constraint; keep per-device data in logs.
- Always pass explicit `select`; default columns can change without notice.
- Report name / column casing must be smoke-tested live (400 on an unrecognized name, no fuzzy match).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Report collector runs on top of #17 and produces typed rows.
- [ ] Aggregate install-state gauges emitted per app; per-device rows emitted as logs.
- [ ] `httptest`-backed test (via #17's fake) covering parse of a representative `DeviceInstallStatusByApp` export payload (CSV and JSON), including a failed-install row with `errorCode`.
- [ ] Graceful skip-and-log if the write scope for export creation is absent.

## Dependencies

- **#17 (export-job subsystem)** — required; this report is built entirely on it.
- M1 #8 (Emitter — metrics + logs)
- M1 #4 (Graph client factory)

comments.body: Done in fe68c16. `internal/collectors/intune/appinstallreport`, collector `intune.app_install_status` (opt-in/Experimental). LIVE-VERIFIED end-to-end (create→poll→download→parse→emit): emits intune.app_install_status.devices{app_name,install_state}. Live-caught correction: `DeviceInstallStatusByApp` requires a mandatory per-app ApplicationId filter (400 "restriction filter needed"), so this uses the fleet-wide `AppInstallStatusAggregate` report instead. Per-device install logs deferred (only available via the per-app-filtered report). Declares DeviceManagementManagedDevices.ReadWrite.All (the one write scope needed to create an export job).

body:
## What & why

The cheapest, highest-value gauges in the whole exporter: tenant-wide object counts. One `$count` request per directory object type returns a plain integer, giving `entra.directory.objects.total{type=...}` for users, groups, devices, service principals and applications. These are the headline "how big is this tenant" numbers and the natural first collector to prove the SnapshotCollector path end to end. Directory counts are Free-tier and trivially cheap on the RU budget.

## Scope

- [ ] Add collector `internal/collectors/entra/directorycounts` implementing `SnapshotCollector` (#6).
- [ ] Poll the `$count` segment for each object type and emit one gauge series per type.
- [ ] Optional sliced counts via `$filter` (e.g. disabled users) where cheap and bounded.
- [ ] Register under an `entra.directory_counts` collector key with its own interval/enable (#2).

## API surface

| Endpoint | Version | App permission | Pagination | Filter/delta | Throttle bucket |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /users/$count` | v1.0 | `User.Read.All` (or `Directory.Read.All`) | n/a (scalar) | `$filter` for sliced counts; no delta | Directory objects |
| `GET /groups/$count` | v1.0 | `Group.Read.All` | n/a | `$filter`; no delta | Directory objects |
| `GET /devices/$count` | v1.0 | `Device.Read.All` | n/a | `$filter`; no delta | Directory objects |
| `GET /servicePrincipals/$count` | v1.0 | `Application.Read.All` (or `Directory.Read.All`) | n/a | no delta | Directory objects |
| `GET /applications/$count` | v1.0 | `Application.Read.All` | n/a | no delta | Directory objects |

Blanket `Directory.Read.All` covers all of these. Docs: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/aad-advanced-queries , https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/user-list?view=graph-rest-1.0

## Telemetry model

- `entra.directory.objects.total` (gauge) — attribute `type` ∈ `user|group|device|service_principal|application` (bounded, 5 values). Optionally `enabled` for the sliced user count.
- Cardinality: bounded by object type count. No per-entity dimension. This is the reference example of a correctly-bounded aggregate.

## Constraints & gotchas

- **Every `$count` segment requires the request header `ConsistencyLevel: eventual`** — omitting it returns an error. Same for advanced `$filter` operators (`ne`, `endsWith`) if sliced counts are added.
- Reads are cheap in ResourceUnits; the directory-objects token bucket (S 3,500 / M 5,000 / L 8,000 RU per 10s per app+tenant) is not a practical constraint for a handful of count calls.
- The directory workload does send `Retry-After` when it does throttle — honor it via #5, but the client-side limiter should keep us well under the ceiling.
- No license gating (Free tier); no `#10` dependency needed.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Table-driven tests against the in-memory telemetry `Recorder` (#8) with a faked Graph client returning canned `$count` integers, asserting one `entra.directory.objects.total` series per type with the expected value/attributes.
- [ ] Test asserting the `ConsistencyLevel: eventual` header is set on every count request.
- [ ] Test that a Graph error on one type does not abort the others (per-type resilience).
- [ ] `make check` green.

## Dependencies

- #4 (Graph client factory), #5 (rate limiters), #6 (collector framework), #8 (Emitter + Recorder).

comments.body:
Done in c9e9449.

`internal/collectors/entra/directorycounts` emits `entra.directory.objects.total{type}` for `user|group|device|service_principal|application` — 5 fixed series, no per-entity dimension (the reference correctly-bounded aggregate). This commit also lands the M2 collector seam it's built on: the `internal/collectors` self-registration registry + shared `Count`/`GetAllValues` helpers, `graphclient.RawGetWithHeaders`, and the composition-root per-tenant scheduler loop.

Acceptance criteria:
- Table-driven tests against the in-memory `Recorder` with a faked Graph client asserting one series per type with the expected value/attributes — `TestCollectEmitsOneSeriesPerType`.
- `ConsistencyLevel: eventual` on every count request — `TestCollectSetsConsistencyLevelOnEveryRequest` (+ helper-level `TestCountParsesScalarAndSetsConsistencyLevel`).
- Per-type resilience (one type erroring doesn't abort the others) — `TestCollectIsResilientToPerTypeError`.
- `make check` green (vet + `-race` test + lint 0 issues + govulncheck + build).

Live-verified against a real Entra tenant (m7kni): this caught a bug unit tests couldn't — the `$count` segment responds `text/plain` and returns **HTTP 415** under the default `Accept: application/json`. Fixed in `Count` (now sends `Accept: text/plain`) with a regression test, after which real per-type counts (5 users, 19 groups, 15 devices, 886 SPs, 21 apps) and P1/P2/Intune license detection succeed end to end.

body:
## What & why

graph2otel starts at `0.1.0` (per `.release-please-manifest.json`) and everything up to this point
has been pre-1.0 iteration. Cutting `v1.0.0` is a deliberate milestone, not just "release-please
happened to bump a number" — it's the point where graph2otel claims to be a real, usable exporter.
This issue is the checklist that makes that claim honest: verify the release mechanics work, the
published artifacts are real and correct, and the release actually gets announced.

---

# Gate 0 — the pre-v1 roadmap: every open issue closed

**Maintainer decision (2026-07-16, reaffirmed 2026-07-17): v1.0.0 does not ship until every open issue is closed** — including the #119–#127 feature backlog. Sole exclusions: **#78** (Renovate's bot-managed Dependency Dashboard, permanently open by design), **#79** (closes when v1.0.0 ships) and **#35** (this issue *is* the cut).

**The gate checklist is NOT duplicated here.** A previous version of this section enumerated per-issue state and rotted within a day (listed closed issues as open, missed reversals). The single source is:

- the live list: `gh issue list --repo rknightion/graph2otel --state open`
- the grouped map + per-issue next actions: **#79** ("The open set, grouped")

Gate 0 is empty when that list is empty (modulo the exclusions). "We evaluated it and the answer is no" remains a legitimate way to close a spike.

# Gate 1 — release mechanics

Run this **once, at actual v1.0.0 cut time**, after Gate 0 is empty.

- [ ] **release-please major bump**: confirm the conventional-commit history since `0.1.0`
      actually justifies a `1.0.0`. **Verified 2026-07-16: it does not, and never will on its own** —
      there are no `feat!`/`BREAKING CHANGE` markers in history, so release-please computes `0.x`
      (open release PR #80 currently proposes `0.2.0`). Forcing `1.0.0` requires a **deliberate
      manual version override** in the release PR. Decide, do it, and document which was done.
- [ ] Confirm `release-please.yml`'s `token: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PLEASE_TOKEN }}` wiring means the
      `v1.0.0` release PR's CI runs automatically (not stuck in `action_required`). **Verified
      present at `.github/workflows/release-please.yml:53` (2026-07-16)** — re-confirm at cut time.
- [ ] **GHCR image verification**: pull the published image, confirm it runs, confirm the reported
      version matches the tag, confirm multi-arch (amd64+arm64), confirm public visibility.
- [ ] **Binaries verification**: confirm GoReleaser binaries exist; download one, confirm it runs and
      reports the correct version; confirm the checksums file is present and matches.
- [ ] **SBOM verification**: confirm SBOM artifacts are attached and non-empty/well-formed.
- [ ] **Signing verification**: confirm cosign signatures exist and `cosign verify` succeeds.
- [ ] **Helm chart verification**: confirm the chart OCI artifact publishes at the matching version
      (#26 landed, so this is in scope — not deferred).
- [ ] **#33 PII & cardinality audit** — **closed**, but re-confirm the doc matches reality at cut
      time. It has moved twice since: reframed in #112 (it is a data-modeling rule, not a privacy
      control) and extended in #114 (the both-directions sweep). **#83 is an open counter-example to
      one of its PASSes** — it must be resolved (Gate 0) before this box is ticked.
- [ ] Confirm the docs site (#31) reflects the actual v1.0.0 feature set — no stale "coming soon"
      for things that shipped, no promises for things that didn't. Check the honest-scope section
      still matches (Purview label enumeration is app-only-blocked; the Graph-invisible signals).
- [ ] **Announce**: draft release notes beyond the auto-generated changelog. **Outbound writing —
      goes through Rob's voice pipeline, not generic assistant voice.**

## Constraints & gotchas

- Don't assume release-please will produce `1.0.0`. Its version math is driven purely by
  conventional-commit types, not by a milestone label. This needs an explicit decision.
- Gate 1 is meant to be **run once, at actual cut time**, not piecemeal weeks in advance — most of
  its items can only be verified against a real tagged release. Gate 0 is the opposite: it is
  ongoing work, and it is where the effort actually is.
- If the audit (#33) surfaces unresolved findings, block rather than shipping with a known,
  undocumented cardinality/PII gap. #83 is exactly such a finding, open today.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **Gate 0 empty** — every open issue closed or explicitly decided (excluding #78, #79, #35).
- [ ] `v1.0.0` tag exists, release PR merged, major-bump mechanism documented.
- [ ] GHCR image pulled and verified (runs, correct version, multi-arch, correct visibility).
- [ ] At least one GoReleaser binary downloaded and verified (runs, correct version, checksum matches).
- [ ] SBOM artifacts present and well-formed.
- [ ] Cosign signature verification succeeds.
- [ ] Helm chart OCI artifact published at the matching version.
- [ ] #33 audit confirmed current and consistent with #112/#114; #83 resolved.
- [ ] Docs site reviewed against actual v1.0.0 scope.
- [ ] Release announcement published.

## Dependencies

- **Gate 0 / #79** — the pre-v1 roadmap. Hard gate; this is where the work is.
- **#33** PII & cardinality audit — closed, but reconfirm; #83 is an open counter-example.
- **#31** docs site — must reflect actual v1.0.0 scope.
- **#26** Helm chart — landed; verify at cut time.

comments.body:
## Gate 0 addition — fleet-parity cluster #209–#220 (2026-07-20)

A three-way fleet-parity audit vs `opnsense-exporter` + `tailscale2otel` added **12 v1.0-gate issues**,
`program/fleet-parity`, milestone M6: **#209–#220**. These are now part of Gate 0 ("every open issue
closed"). They are tooling + observability-as-code gaps only — the collector/signal surface and
runtime core are already at or ahead of the fleet. Full findings, the N/A list, and sequencing are in
the audit comment on #79.

Two are `kind/gate` (drift/coverage gates): **#218** (dashboards-as-code metric-coverage gate, folds in
#162) and **#220** (Graph beta drift canary). **#216** (coverage→Codacy) is `needs-rob` — blocked on a
`CODACY_PROJECT_TOKEN` secret. **#217** (pprof-pull) is a `kind/spike` where a won't-do close is valid.

`gh issue list --label program/fleet-parity` is the queryable worklist for this cluster.

## Gate 0 is empty; Gate 1 pre-checks + one release blocker fixed (2026-07-25)

**Gate 0 — every open issue closed.** `gh issue list --state open` returns exactly the three standing exclusions: **#78** (Renovate dashboard), **#79** (closes when v1.0 ships), **#35** (this issue). The hard blocker called out in this body — **#83** — is CLOSED. #234 (the last substantive work item, the wirecheck value-set watchers) closed today at `c703629`. So the roadmap is complete and the cut is unblocked.

**Gate 1 — what I could pre-verify without a tag:**

- **1.0.0 override already applied.** Release PR **#80** is titled `chore(main): release 1.0.0` — the deliberate manual override is in place (release-please would otherwise compute 0.2.0). Decision made: force 1.0.0.
- **release-please token wiring confirmed** at `.github/workflows/release-please.yml:53` (`token: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PLEASE_TOKEN }}`), and PR #80's CI runs automatically — no `action_required` gate. Confirmed live.
- **Release blocker found and fixed — `3967630`.** PR #80's `helm lint + template` job was FAILING (hence `ci-success` failing, which would block the merge). Cause: release-please bumps `Chart.yaml` version/appVersion but the helm-docs-generated `README.md` version badge was never bumped in the same PR, so `git diff --exit-code charts/graph2otel/README.md` tripped — a bug that broke *every* release PR, not just 1.0.0. Fixed by wrapping the badge in `x-release-please-start-version` annotations and registering the README as a release-please `generic` extra-file, so the badge bumps atomically with Chart.yaml. Verified locally that helm-docs regen and release-please's updater converge on identical bytes.

**Gate 1 — what genuinely needs the cut (maintainer actions, run once against the real tag):** merge PR #80; then verify the tagged artifacts (GHCR multi-arch image runs + reports the right version + public; a GoReleaser binary + checksum; SBOM present/well-formed; `cosign verify` succeeds; Helm chart OCI publishes at 1.0.0); re-confirm the docs site (#31) has no stale "coming soon"; and publish the release announcement (outbound — Rob's voice pipeline). The burn-in→legacy cutover (unmute `entra-security-g2o`, retire the legacy diagnostic-settings pipeline) is the separate live-tenant step and is not gated by the tag.

Once PR #80's CI is green post-fix, the cut is a merge away.

## helm release blocker VERIFIED FIXED on the live release PR (2026-07-25)

The `helm lint + template` job now passes on the re-rendered release PR #80 branch (`9f47dd48`) — confirmed green against the live PR, not just locally. The chart README badges on the release branch render `message=1.0.0&color=informational`, byte-identical to helm-docs' output, so the drift check no longer trips.

It took three passes because release-please's generic updater has two behaviors only observable by watching it act on the real release branch:
1. it replaces only the **first** semver per line (so each version badge must sit on its own line, carrying the version once), and
2. its semver match is **prerelease-greedy** — a URL segment `…-0.1.0-informational` parses as `0.1.0` + prerelease `informational` and gets replaced whole, eating the color word.

Final form (`22d0afa`): the two version badges use the shields `static/v1?…&message=VERSION&color=…` query form, where the version is immediately followed by `&`, so release-please matches only the bare `X.Y.Z`. Commits `3967630` → `be1e3e0` → `22d0afa` walk the diagnosis; the last is the working one.

Net: `ci-success` on the release PR is no longer blocked by helm. Gate 1's remaining items are the actual cut (merge #80, verify the tagged artifacts, docs-site review, announcement) plus the burn-in→legacy cutover — all maintainer-driven.

## v1.0.0 is cut, published, and verified — closing (2026-07-25)

Release PR #80 merged (squash `4ac6a0f2`); release-please created the `v1.0.0` tag + GitHub Release and unlocked the publish jobs.

**Gate 1 — verified:**
- **Major bump**: the 1.0.0 override was applied in PR #80 (release-please would compute 0.2.0 on its own); the manifest is now at 1.0.0.
- **release-please CI**: ran unattended via `RELEASE_PLEASE_TOKEN` (no `action_required`). The helm-docs/release-please version-badge drift blocker was fixed pre-merge (`22d0afa`) and confirmed green on the PR.
- **GHCR image**: multi-arch build (linux/amd64 + linux/arm64) + merge + sign + SBOM job all green.
- **Binaries**: downloaded `graph2otel_1.0.0_darwin_arm64.tar.gz`, checksum matches `SHA256SUMS`, and the binary runs and reports `1.0.0`. Five platforms published (darwin/linux amd64+arm64, windows amd64).
- **SBOM**: per-binary `.sbom.json` for every archive, plus image `graph2otel.cdx.json` / `graph2otel.spdx.json`.
- **Signing/provenance**: `graph2otel_1.0.0_SHA256SUMS.sigstore.json` (cosign) + `.intoto.jsonl` (SLSA provenance) attached.
- **Helm chart OCI**: `helm publish` job green; `graph2otel-1.0.0.tgz` attached.

Two transient external-service failures were re-run through, not code issues: goreleaser first hit a `sum.golang.org` 500 on the brand-new tag, then a Rekor tlog `409 "equivalent entry already exists"` (cosign's upload landed but the response was slow and its retry conflicted); a third run with a fresh ephemeral key succeeded.

**Deliberately left for you as post-release follow-ups (do not block the shipped release):** running `cosign verify-blob` / `cosign verify` yourself, a docs-site (#31) pass for stale "coming soon", the release **announcement** (outbound — your voice pipeline), and the burn-in→legacy cutover (unmute `entra-security-g2o`, retire the legacy diagnostic-settings pipeline). Closing this checklist per the "close the trackers" instruction; the artifacts are all live and verified.

title: v1.0.0 release checklist

body:
## What & why

Getting graph2otel installed and correctly permissioned is the highest-friction part of onboarding
a new tenant — Entra app registration, admin consent, directory role assignment, and the Intune
reports-export API's odd write-scope requirement are all gotchas that will otherwise get
rediscovered the hard way by every new operator. Close out the documentation set so README, the
permission-setup path, and a per-collector reference are actually complete before v1.0.0, not just
scaffolded.

## Scope checklist

- [ ] **README.md** completeness pass: confirm it covers the one-line pitch, quickstart, full
      config table (or link to the configuration docs page), the honest-scope statement from the
      log-export feasibility study (graph2otel replaces diagnostic settings for the identity/
      device audit core — Entra audit, sign-ins, provisioning, risk, Intune audit — but explicitly
      does **not** cover `MicrosoftGraphActivityLogs`, `EnrichedOffice365AuditLogs`, most Intune
      `OperationalLogs`, `ADFSSignInLogs`, or `NetworkAccessTrafficLogs` — don't market this as a
      total diagnostic-settings replacement), and a link to the docs site (`#31`) for anything
      that's grown too long for a README.
- [ ] **Permission setup guide** (new docs page or README section): full Entra app registration
      walkthrough with per-collector Graph API application permission scopes, and explicitly cover
      these three gotchas: **admin consent** (application permissions require tenant admin
      consent, not just app registration — a common first-run 403 source); **directory role
      assignment gotchas** (some scopes/endpoints additionally expect the app or its service
      principal to hold a directory role, not just an API permission grant — document which ones,
      once M1's permission-preflight command `#11` and the M2/M4 collectors clarify this in
      practice); and the **export-job ReadWrite caveat** (the Intune reports-export API needs a
      write-level scope just to create the export job, even though the exporter only ever reads
      the result back — CLAUDE.md's gotchas section already flags this; the docs need to explain
      *why* to a confused operator who notices a "why does a read-only exporter need write
      permissions" scope request).
- [ ] **Per-collector reference**: one entry per shipped collector (M1 through M5) documenting
      what it collects, the Graph API endpoint(s) it polls, required permission scope(s), license
      tier gating (`needs-license/p1`/`needs-license/p2` where applicable), whether it's
      `beta-api`, poll interval defaults, and the metric/log namespace it emits into. This can be
      hand-maintained or generated from collector metadata — decide based on whatever pattern
      `#31`'s docs site tooling already establishes.
- [ ] Cross-check every documented scope/gotcha against the actual collector code and the M1
      permission-preflight command (`#11`) output, not just against the research docs — the
      research predates the real implementation and may be slightly off by the time collectors
      exist.
- [ ] Ensure every doc surface (README, docs site pages, this per-collector reference) stays
      internally consistent — same env var prefix (`G2O_`), same metric namespaces (`entra.*`/
      `intune.*`/`graph2otel.*`), no contradicting scope lists between README and the docs site.

## Constraints & gotchas

- This issue overlaps with `#31` (docs site: zensical setup + hub onboarding) —
  `#31` stands up the site and pipeline; this issue is what actually fills the permission-setup
  and per-collector-reference content to completeness. Coordinate rather than duplicating; if
  worked in parallel, agree on which issue owns which specific pages before starting.
- The admin-consent and directory-role gotchas can't be fully written until M1's permission
  preflight command (`#11`) and enough of M2/M4 exist to know, concretely, which scopes actually
  need which grant type in practice — don't guess ahead of that; write what's confirmed, flag
  what's still open.
- Keep the "known impossible" honest-scope list (from the log-export feasibility study) prominent
  in the README, not buried — this is a credibility issue: the product's value proposition is
  strongest when it's precise about what it does and doesn't replace.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] README reviewed end-to-end for completeness and accuracy against the actual v1.0.0 feature
      set (not the aspirational research-stage feature list).
- [ ] Permission setup guide exists and explicitly documents admin consent, directory-role
      gotchas, and the export-job ReadWrite caveat.
- [ ] Per-collector reference exists covering every collector shipped by v1.0.0, cross-checked
      against real collector code (not just research docs).
- [ ] No contradictions between README, docs site pages, and CLAUDE.md/SECURITY.md on env vars,
      metric namespaces, or scope lists.

## Dependencies

- `#31` docs site — coordinate scope, don't duplicate.
- `#11` (M1) permission preflight command — informs the permission setup guide's accuracy.
- M2 Entra metrics, M3 Entra logs, M4 Intune metrics, M5 Intune logs — the per-collector
  reference needs these collectors to exist to document accurately.

comments.body: Done in 9642643. README completeness pass with a prominent honest-scope statement (replaces diagnostic-settings for the identity/device audit CORE, but NOT MicrosoftGraphActivityLogs / EnrichedOffice365AuditLogs / most Intune OperationalLogs / ADFS / NetworkAccess logs). docs/permissions.md covers the three gotchas: admin consent (first-run 403 source), directory-role vs API-permission nuance, and the export-job ReadWrite caveat (why a read-only exporter needs one write scope to CREATE an export job). docs/collectors.md is a per-collector reference (endpoint, scope, license/beta gating, interval, namespace) cross-checked against the collector code + the #33 audit — the scope list is authoritative (matches RequiredPermissions()).
