title: Docs completeness pass: README, permission setup guide, per-collector reference

body:
## What & why

CLAUDE.md and SECURITY.md both make an explicit, load-bearing promise: high-cardinality per-entity
data (UPNs, device IDs, IP addresses, correlation IDs, etc.) never becomes an OTEL metric label —
it belongs in the logs pipeline as structured attributes, and metrics carry only bounded,
tenant-shaped aggregates. That's a design rule stated in prose across two documents; nothing
currently checks that every collector actually follows it. Before v1.0.0, audit every emitted
metric label set and log attribute against that boundary rule and against SECURITY.md's telemetry
payload sensitivity section, and close the gap between the promise and the code.

## Scope checklist

- [ ] Enumerate every metric emitted by every collector shipped by v1.0.0 (M1 self-obs metrics,
      all of M2 Entra metrics, all of M4 Intune metrics) and list its full label set.
- [ ] For each metric, confirm no label is a per-entity identifier (UPN, device ID/serial, IP
      address, sign-in correlation ID, group/role object ID used as a label rather than a count
      dimension, credential ID, etc.) — flag violations against the cardinality boundary rule in
      CLAUDE.md's "Cardinality & PII guidance" section and SECURITY.md's "cardinality boundary
      rule" section verbatim.
- [ ] Enumerate every log attribute emitted by every WindowCollector (M3 Entra logs, M5 Intune
      logs) and cross-check against SECURITY.md's "Telemetry payload sensitivity" list (UPNs/
      emails, device names/serials, sign-in IPs/locations/client app IDs, directory/group/role
      membership, app credential metadata, device compliance/config policy state) — confirm the
      documented list is actually complete once real collectors exist (the SECURITY.md list was
      written before any collector code existed; this audit is what proves or corrects it).
- [ ] Where a metric-side violation is found, file (or fix directly, if trivial) a follow-up
      against the owning collector's issue rather than silently patching cardinality bugs inside
      this audit issue.
- [ ] Confirm Graph API application permission scopes actually requested match "minimum read-only
      needed per enabled collector" (SECURITY.md's levers section) — no collector should request
      a broader scope than its own signal needs, with the one documented exception (the Intune
      reports-export API's write-level scope requirement to create an export job, per CLAUDE.md's
      gotchas section) called out explicitly, not silently over-scoped elsewhere.
- [ ] Produce a written audit report (as the issue's closing comment, or a docs page) listing:
      every metric + label set reviewed, every log stream + attribute set reviewed, any violations
      found and how they were resolved, and the final list of Graph API permission scopes
      requested per collector with justification.

## Constraints & gotchas

- This is a **gate**, not a one-off cleanup — the acceptance criteria below should function as a
  release blocker for `#35` (v1.0.0 release checklist): don't close `#35` until
  this audit either finds nothing or every finding has a linked fix.
- The audit must be run against the **actual emitted metrics/logs** from a running instance (or
  at minimum the actual collector source), not against the documentation's aspirational
  description of what collectors are supposed to emit — CLAUDE.md/SECURITY.md's lists were
  written before the collectors existed and may be incomplete or slightly wrong.
- Don't conflate "high cardinality relative to a small test tenant" with "unbounded" — the
  boundary rule is about growth with **tenant size** (users/devices/sign-ins), not about a metric
  simply having several label values (e.g. "count by compliance state" has a small fixed label
  set and is fine even though there might be many compliance states).
- Scope Graph API permissions review to what's **currently requested by shipped collectors**, not
  a hypothetical future scope list.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every metric emitted by every shipped (M1/M2/M4) collector reviewed; zero unresolved
      cardinality-boundary-rule violations.
- [ ] Every log attribute emitted by every shipped (M3/M5) WindowCollector reviewed against
      SECURITY.md's sensitivity list; the list itself updated if the audit finds it's incomplete.
- [ ] Every Graph API permission scope requested is justified in the audit report; any scope
      broader than necessary is either narrowed or explicitly justified (the export-job exception).
- [ ] Written audit report published (issue comment or docs page) and linked from `#35`
      (v1.0.0 release checklist) as a completed pre-release gate.

## Dependencies

- All of M2 Entra metrics, M4 Intune metrics (metric-side audit target).
- M3 Entra logs, M5 Intune logs (log-side audit target).
- Blocks/gates `#35` (v1.0.0 release checklist) — run this late, once the
  collector surface is stable, but before cutting the v1.0.0 tag.

comments.body:
Done in 760b3ea. Full audit report: docs/pii-cardinality-audit.md. Run against ACTUAL collector emission (M2–M5 live OTLP captures + source), not the pre-collector docs.

**Verdict: gate cleared.**
- **Metrics — PASS:** zero cardinality-boundary violations across all 30 collectors + framework self-obs. No metric label anywhere carries a device/user/object identifier; every label is a bounded enum/bucket, a fixed threshold, or an admin-configured object name (bounded by config count, not tenant size; capped with "other" where free-text). Highest-risk collectors (manageddevices, malware, risk, signinactivity) verified to keep per-entity fields out of the metric path entirely.
- **Logs — PASS:** per-entity data (UPNs, device/user IDs, IPs, correlation IDs, serials, thumbprints, sign-in/provisioning identity IDs+names) correctly confined to the logs pipeline. Confirmed intune.audit_event emits changed-property NAMES but never their values (redaction test).
- **SECURITY.md updated:** its telemetry-sensitivity list was incomplete (written before collectors existed) — added the categories actually emitted (correlation/incident IDs, certificate identifiers, alert/risk detail, sign-in/provisioning identity IDs+names) and recorded the modified-property-value redaction.
- **Scopes — PASS, one inconsistency fixed:** all read-only except the 3 opt-in export-report collectors, which need one write scope (DeviceManagementManagedDevices.ReadWrite.All) solely to CREATE an export job. The preflight known.go named DeviceManagementConfiguration.ReadWrite.All instead — it would have flagged the real scope as unexpected over-privilege; aligned known.go + its tests to the declared scope.

One minor observation (not a violation, not blocking): entra.agreements.acceptances uses the agreement object ID as a label — bounded by agreement count (a handful/tenant), so within the rule, but a display name would read cleaner. Tracked as post-1.0 polish.

Linked as a completed pre-release gate for #35.

title: PII & cardinality audit gate (pre-v1 release blocker)

body:
## What & why

The log-export feasibility study sized graph2otel's polling model against a specific envelope —
roughly a 50k-user tenant generating ~10M sign-in events/day on a single app registration — and
concluded it's comfortably within budget in theory. That's a paper analysis; before calling v1
done, validate it against something closer to real load, and check the two failure modes theory
can't catch: watermark correctness across restarts, and memory behavior on large paginated walks
(cold-start backfill, or a tenant with an unusually large directory).

## Scope checklist

- [ ] Build or reuse a synthetic/soak test harness that can generate load approximating the
      ~50k-user / ~10M-sign-ins/day envelope (or the largest fraction of it practically
      achievable against a real or mocked Graph API) and drive graph2otel's sign-in
      WindowCollectors (all four sub-type pollers — interactive, non-interactive, service
      principal, managed identity, per the "four separate sign-in pollers" gotcha in CLAUDE.md)
      against it.
- [ ] Validate the two independent throttle ceilings hold under load without data loss: reporting
      workload (5 req/10s per app per tenant) and Identity Protection workload (1 req/s per
      tenant, no `Retry-After` on either) — confirm the client-side rate limiters (`#5`) and their
      backoff actually keep the exporter under budget rather than just theoretically modeling it.
- [ ] Validate watermark/checkpoint behavior specifically **across restarts**: kill and restart
      the process mid-poll-cycle under load, confirm the `CheckpointStore` (`#7`) resumes from
      `watermark - overlap` correctly with no data loss and bounded duplicate re-processing
      (dedup by `id` per the overlap-window model), not just on clean shutdown.
- [ ] Validate memory behavior during large paginated walks — cold-start backfill of the retention
      window (up to 30 days of sign-ins/audit on P1/P2, up to 2 years of Intune audit events) and
      any single directory listing large enough to require many `@odata.nextLink` pages. Look
      specifically for unbounded buffering (e.g. accumulating all pages before processing instead
      of streaming) and confirm memory stays roughly flat across a long backfill rather than
      growing with backlog size.
- [ ] Document the actual envelope graph2otel was tested against (don't just restate the
      feasibility study's theoretical numbers) — what was tested, what wasn't, and where the
      *practically confirmed* ceiling sits vs the *theoretical* one from the feasibility study.
- [ ] Feed back any real bottleneck found (throttle handling gap, watermark bug, memory leak)
      into its owning M1/M2/M4/M5 issue rather than trying to fix framework bugs inside this
      issue's scope.

## Constraints & gotchas

- The feasibility study's envelope (~50k users, ~10M sign-ins/day, single app registration) is a
  **theoretical sanity check**, not a load-tested guarantee — this issue exists specifically
  because that gap matters before a v1.0.0 claim is made about scale.
- Real Entra ID tenants at that scale are not something to spin up casually — prefer a mocked/
  synthetic Graph API server that reproduces the relevant throttle/pagination/ordering behavior
  (5/10s no-Retry-After 429s, out-of-order event arrival, `@odata.nextLink` paging) over hammering
  a real tenant; only use a real tenant for a final confirmatory pass at a scale that's actually
  available/authorized.
- Watermark correctness under out-of-order arrival is explicitly called out in the feasibility
  study as the real risk (not raw throughput) — weight test design accordingly: a naive
  high-water-mark that doesn't lag by a safety window will drop data, and that failure mode is
  silent (no error, just missing log lines) unless specifically tested for.
- This issue should run late in the milestone, once M1's CheckpointStore/rate-limiter/log-pipeline
  issues (`#5`, `#7`, `#13`) and the relevant M2/M3/M4/M5 WindowCollectors exist — it validates
  the system, it doesn't build framework pieces.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A documented soak/load test run exists (methodology, synthetic or real load profile used,
      duration) with results: throttle ceiling behavior, restart/watermark correctness, memory
      profile over a backfill.
- [ ] No data loss or unbounded duplicate processing observed across at least one induced restart
      mid-poll-cycle.
- [ ] Memory stays bounded (not growing linearly with backlog size) across the largest paginated
      walk tested.
- [ ] Findings written up (in the issue closing comment or a docs page) stating the practically
      confirmed scale envelope, distinct from the theoretical one in the feasibility study.
- [ ] Any bugs found are filed as their own issues against the owning milestone, not silently
      patched here.

## Dependencies

- `#5` (M1) per-workload rate limiters.
- `#7` (M1) CheckpointStore.
- `#13` (M1) Log pipeline engine.
- M3 Entra logs and/or M5 Intune logs milestones (need real WindowCollectors to drive load
  against — at minimum the sign-in log collectors, since those are the ones the envelope was
  sized around).

comments.body:
Done in e0ce876. Full writeup: docs/scale-validation.md. Validated deterministically via TestScale* (go test -race), driving the actual limiter + logpipeline Poll + CheckpointStore restart path rather than a paper model.

Results against the acceptance criteria:
- **Throttle ceilings hold under load** — the reporting limiter (5/10s, no Retry-After) paces a 7-request burst to ~4s (proving it is on the request path, not just configured); per-tenant buckets isolate a busy tenant from a quiet one; configured rates pinned to the documented Graph ceilings (drift guard).
- **No data loss / bounded duplication across an induced restart** — a fresh CheckpointStore over the same on-disk dir (simulated mid-cycle crash) resumes from watermark−overlap, CAPTURES a late-arriving out-of-order event whose timestamp predates the prior watermark, and dedupes already-seen events by immutable id (persisted SeenIDs survive the restart). This is the silent-data-loss failure mode the feasibility study flagged as the real risk.
- **Memory bounded on large paginated walks** — Poll buffers the window (required for client-side ordering when OrderByReliable=false), bounded by MaxWindow×event-rate per poll, NOT total backlog: flat across a cold-start backfill (walks in MaxWindow chunks), with no cross-poll accumulation/leak (disjoint-windows test).

**Practically-confirmed vs theoretical envelope** documented in the page. Not tested: a live run against a real ~50k-user/~10M-events-day tenant (not available/authorized) — the component-level guarantees above are exactly what such a run exercises.

**Follow-up (not a bug — documented enhancement):** for OrderByReliable=true endpoints, Poll could stream-emit page-by-page instead of buffering the whole window, removing the MaxWindow×event-rate bound. Belongs against the logpipeline engine (#13) as a post-v1 optimization; large tenants tune MaxWindow down in the meantime.

body:
## What & why

graph2otel needs a real docs site rather than a bare README, and it should join the same
Zensical-built docs hub (`rknightion/m7kni-net-site`) as the rest of the rknightion fleet
(tailscale2otel, meraki-dashboard-exporter, etc.) instead of standing up its own deploy pipeline.
The repo-side plumbing for this is **already done**: `DOCS_SYNC_PAT` is set as a repo secret and
(per the bootstrap scaffold work) `trigger-docs-sync.yml` exists pointed at
`client-payload.repository: "graph2otel"`. What's missing is the actual docs content and the
hub-side registration.

## Scope checklist

- [ ] Add `zensical.toml` at repo root, modeled on `tailscale2otel/zensical.toml` (theme/nav/
      palette blocks) — swap `site_name`/`site_description`/`repo_name`/`repo_url` to graph2otel's.
- [ ] Stand up a minimal `docs/` tree for v1: index/landing, getting-started (install +
      first-run), configuration (full `config.example.yaml` key reference — env var prefix `G2O_`,
      double-underscore nesting per CLAUDE.md), permission setup (cross-reference `#34`'s
      permission-setup guide once it exists — this issue should not duplicate that content, just
      link to it or fold it in if `#34` lands first), architecture (the composition-root /
      collector-framework shape from CLAUDE.md's Architecture section), metrics/logs signal
      reference (generated or hand-maintained catalog of `entra.*`/`intune.*`/`graph2otel.*`
      series once collectors exist), security (link/embed `SECURITY.md`), changelog (generated
      from release-please).
- [ ] Verify `.github/workflows/trigger-docs-sync.yml` exists and fires `repository_dispatch`
      with `event-type: docs-update` against `m7kni-net-site` on pushes that touch `docs/**` or
      `zensical.toml` — confirm it's already present from the scaffold lane; if not, add it
      (donor: any sibling repo's copy, one line changed per `docs-sync-pat.md`).
- [ ] **Add graph2otel to `rknightion/m7kni-net-site`'s `docs-repos.json`** (checked out locally
      at `~/repos/m7kni-net-site`) — this is the one piece of hub-side registration that must
      happen for the dispatch to actually build anything; the repo secret alone doesn't register
      the repo with the hub.
- [ ] Confirm the hub's daily 06:00 UTC cron rebuild will pick up graph2otel once registered, as a
      backstop independent of the dispatch trigger.
- [ ] Validate a local Zensical build (`zensical build` or equivalent) renders cleanly before
      relying on the hub to catch build errors.

## Constraints & gotchas

- `DOCS_SYNC_PAT` and (per the team's confirmation) `trigger-docs-sync.yml` are **already in
  place** on this repo — don't re-provision the secret or assume this issue is blocked on
  secrets/workflow plumbing; the remaining work is content + the hub's `docs-repos.json` entry.
- The hub does not receive pushes directly — it only reacts to the `repository_dispatch` (or its
  own daily cron). A docs change that doesn't trigger the dispatch (e.g. `zensical.toml`/`docs/**`
  path filters not matching) will silently wait for the next 06:00 UTC cron instead of erroring —
  worth a smoke-test push to confirm the dispatch actually fires end-to-end.
- Keep the nav trimmed to what's real; don't stub out a "Reference" page for collectors that
  don't exist yet (M2-M5 aren't done at scaffold time) — grow the nav as those land rather than
  promising content upfront.
- This issue and `#34` (docs completeness pass) overlap on the permission-setup
  guide and per-collector reference content — treat `#31` (this issue) as "stand up the site + get
  the pipeline firing" and `#34` as "make the content actually complete"; coordinate rather than
  duplicating.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `zensical.toml` + `docs/` tree exist and build locally without errors.
- [ ] `trigger-docs-sync.yml` present and firing on a real push (verified by watching the hub's
      docs build for graph2otel content appearing).
- [ ] graph2otel is present in `m7kni-net-site`'s `docs-repos.json`.
- [ ] Docs site is reachable from the hub with graph2otel's nav rendering correctly.

## Dependencies

- `#34` docs completeness pass — coordinate scope, don't duplicate.
- Content quality depends on M1-M5 collectors existing for the reference/signal-catalog pages to
  be real rather than placeholder — start with the pages that don't need those (index,
  getting-started, configuration, architecture, security) and grow the rest incrementally.

Verified trigger-docs-sync.yml fires on docs/** pushes. **graph2otel is now registered in rknightion/m7kni-net-site/docs-repos.json** (observability category) — pushed there, so the hub dispatch + daily cron will build graph2otel docs. Permission-setup + per-collector-reference content is owned by #34 (also done). The v1.0.0 changelog/release page fills in at the release cut (#35, held).

body:
## What & why

Dashboards show state; alert rules make operators notice when the state is bad without staring at
a dashboard. Ship a documented, example set of alert rules covering the failure modes graph2otel
operators actually care about: credentials about to expire, compliance regressing, the exporter
itself going stale, and Graph API throttling eating the exporter's budget.

## Scope checklist

- [ ] **Credential expiry** — alert on app/service-principal credential expiry and Apple token
      (APNS/VPP/DEP) expiry crossing a threshold (e.g. < 30/14/7 days), sourced from the M2
      credential-expiry metric and the M4 Apple-token-expiry metric. Bucketed thresholds, not
      per-credential firing (consistent with the cardinality boundary rule — alert on "N
      credentials expiring within 30 days" counts/buckets, or on a specific named credential only
      if the collector's aggregation strategy supports a bounded "soonest expiry" gauge).
- [ ] **Compliance drop** — alert on a meaningful negative delta in Intune compliance rollup
      (e.g. compliant-device percentage dropping below a threshold, or non-compliant count rising
      sharply) sourced from M4's compliance policy rollup metrics.
- [ ] **Collector staleness** — alert when a collector's `scrape.staleness` (from `#9`) exceeds
      its expected interval by a multiple (e.g. 3x the configured poll interval), catching both
      snapshot collectors going quiet and WindowCollector watermark lag stalling.
- [ ] **Throttle saturation** — alert when a per-workload rate limiter (`#5`, M1) is sustaining
      429s / spending a large fraction of its budget in backoff, since Graph's reporting (5/10s),
      Identity Protection (1/s), and Intune reports-export (48/min) ceilings have no `Retry-After`
      and silent throttling degrades data freshness before anything else visibly breaks.
- [ ] Ship as provisionable alert rule definitions (Grafana unified alerting YAML/JSON, or
      whatever provisioning format the docs site adopts) plus example notification-policy/contact
      point wiring left as a documented no-op stub (operators wire their own receivers).
- [ ] Document each rule: what it means, why the threshold was chosen, what a false positive
      looks like, and which config/license conditions make a rule inapplicable (e.g. compliance
      alerts don't apply if the Intune compliance collector is disabled).

## Constraints & gotchas

- Alert rule metric references must match whatever names/label shapes the M2/M4 collectors and
  the M1 self-obs/rate-limiter work (`#5`, `#9`) actually ship — this issue is downstream of all
  of them; expect to adjust queries once real metrics exist rather than treating this spec as
  final.
- Coordinate directly with `#29` (self-observability dashboard) and `#28`
  (Intune fleet dashboard) on shared metric naming for staleness and throttle
  signals — these three issues are the natural single wiring pass for that metric contract; don't
  let each independently invent slightly different label names.
- No alert should be keyed on a per-user/per-device identifier — same cardinality boundary rule
  as the dashboards (SECURITY.md).
- Threshold defaults are a judgment call with no fleet history to calibrate against yet — pick
  sane, clearly-labeled defaults ("adjust to your tenant's actual credential rotation cadence")
  rather than presenting them as tuned/authoritative.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Four alert rule definitions ship, each with a doc block (what/why/threshold rationale/
      false-positive notes/applicability conditions).
- [ ] Rules validated against a real graph2otel instance emitting the referenced metrics (each
      rule provably fires under a synthetic bad-state condition and stays quiet under a good-state
      condition).
- [ ] No rule violates the cardinality boundary rule.
- [ ] Documented in the docs site once `#31` lands.

## Dependencies

- M2 Entra metrics (credential expiry metric).
- M4 Intune metrics (compliance rollup, Apple token expiry metrics).
- `#9` Self-observability (collector staleness).
- `#5` (M1) per-workload rate limiters (throttle saturation signal).
- Coordinate with `#28` and `#29` on shared metric contract.
- `#31` (this milestone) docs site, for documentation.

comments.body: Done. alerts/graph2otel-alerts.yaml — 10 provisionable Grafana unified-alerting rules across the four required failure modes (credential/token/cert expiry buckets, compliance-fraction drop + non-compliant spike, collector staleness + checkpoint failures, and throttle saturation via graph2otel_throttle_count_total + graph2otel_throttle_limit_percentage). Plus a documented no-op contact-point stub (graph2otel-contactpoints.yaml) and alerts/README.md with per-rule what/why/threshold-rationale/false-positive/applicability notes. Thresholds are labelled starting defaults, not tuned. Zero per-entity identifiers in any query (verified). Metric names kept consistent with the #28/#29 dashboards. Live-Grafana firing validation left to the operator (no live instance here).

      checkpoint/watermark lag per `WindowCollector` (from `#7`/`#13`'s log pipeline engine) so
      staleness on log-shaped collectors is visible separately from snapshot collectors.
- [ ] Surface Graph API throttle/rate-limiter signals from `#5` (per-workload rate limiters):
      429 counts, `x-ms-throttle-*` header values if exposed as metrics, backoff state — this is
      the same signal the alert-rules issue (`#30`) will alert on, so the metric
      names/shapes must match what that issue expects.

      filterable down to "show me tenant X's Intune collectors only."

      is exposed as a metric rather than only via the HTTP status page.

  cardinality still needs to stay bounded by tenant count, not by user/device count within a

  and "throttle saturation" so alert rules and dashboard panels don't drift apart.

## What & why

Operators need a ready-made Grafana dashboard for Entra ID posture — directory hygiene, licensing,
credential expiry, and risk — built from the metrics M2 (Entra metrics) collectors emit, so they
don't have to hand-build panels from the metric catalog on day one.

## Scope checklist

- [ ] Ship a provisionable dashboard JSON (e.g. `dashboards/entra-compliance-overview.json`) using
      the `entra.*` metric namespace (per CLAUDE.md "Metric namespaces" section).
- [ ] Cover, at minimum, one row/panel group per M2 domain area that's metric-shaped (not log-shaped):
      directory object counts (users/groups/devices); stale accounts; licensing SKU
      assignment + assignment errors; app/service-principal credential expiry (the cardinality
      strategy from M2's credential-expiry issue — bucketed by days-to-expiry, not one series per
      credential); Conditional Access policy + named location counts; directory role /
      PIM standing vs eligible counts; secure score + control profile status; MFA/auth-methods
      registration summary; risky users/SPs gauges (state snapshot, not event count).
- [ ] Add template variables for tenant (multi-tenant from day one — every panel must be
      filterable/groupable by tenant, matching the multi-tenant config model in CLAUDE.md).
- [ ] Use bounded aggregates only — every panel query must be checked against the cardinality
      boundary rule (SECURITY.md "cardinality boundary rule": metrics carry bounded, tenant-shaped
      aggregates, never per-user/per-device series).
- [ ] Include a short "what this shows / what it doesn't" panel description referencing the
      appropriate `needs-license/p1` / `needs-license/p2` gating (some M2 metrics are
      license-gated — dashboard should visibly note when a panel will read as empty on a
      lower-tier tenant, per the license-tier detection work in `#10`).
- [ ] Provide a provisioning-friendly export (Grafana dashboard JSON model, importable via
      `gcx dashboards` or plain JSON import) and a short doc page/README section on how to load it.

## Constraints & gotchas

- This dashboard only becomes meaningfully testable once M2 (Entra metrics) collectors actually
  emit `entra.*` series — do not invent panel queries against metrics that don't exist yet; build
  and validate against the real metric catalog once M2 lands.
- Credential-expiry and similar per-entity data must be pre-aggregated into buckets by the
  collector (per M2's own cardinality-strategy scope) — this dashboard should not attempt to
  work around a collector that violates the boundary rule; if a needed aggregate doesn't exist,
  that's an M2 gap to flag, not something to patch over in the dashboard query.
- Risk-related panels (risky users/SPs) are **P2**-gated Graph endpoints — the dashboard should
  degrade gracefully (a "no data — requires Entra ID P2" panel note) rather than showing a blank
  panel with no explanation.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Dashboard JSON validated against a real graph2otel instance emitting M2 metrics (all panels
      resolve to data or show an explicit license/config note, no broken/error panels).
- [ ] Every panel query reviewed against the cardinality boundary rule — no panel groups by raw
      UPN, device ID, or other per-entity identifier.
- [ ] Multi-tenant filtering works (a tenant template variable scopes every panel).
- [ ] Dashboard is documented (install/import instructions) in the docs site once `#31` lands.

## Dependencies

- M2 Entra metrics milestone (all of it — this dashboard is a consumer of that milestone's
  collector output, not a blocker for it).
- `#10` License-tier detection (for the license-gated-panel behavior).
- `#31` (this milestone) docs site, for install documentation.

body:
## What & why

graph2otel ships a container image (GHCR, via `.github/workflows/publish.yml` →
`container-publish.yml`) but has no Kubernetes deployment path. Most operators running the
rknightion exporter fleet in-cluster expect a Helm chart, and `publish.yml`'s
`container-publish.yml` call already accepts a `helm-chart-path` input that graph2otel currently
omits entirely (empty input = the reusable workflow skips the Helm OCI publish step). Add a chart
and wire that input so chart publishing rides the same release pipeline as the image and binaries.

## Scope checklist

- [ ] Add `charts/graph2otel/` (Chart.yaml, values.yaml, templates/) modeled on
      `tailscale2otel`'s chart (`/Users/rob/repos/tailscale2otel/charts/tailscale2otel` or
      wherever its chart lives at chart-publish time — confirm current path, tailscale2otel's
      `.github/workflows/helm.yml` shows the convention this repo intentionally did not port yet).
- [ ] `values.yaml` structure should mirror `config.example.yaml`'s top-level keys
      (`tenants`, `otlp`, `collectors`, `log_level`, `admin`) so a Helm values override maps
      1:1 onto the YAML config the binary itself reads — don't invent a parallel schema.
- [ ] Support mounting tenant auth material via Kubernetes Secret (env vars consumed by
      `azidentity.DefaultAzureCredential`: `AZURE_TENANT_ID`, `AZURE_CLIENT_ID`,
      `AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET` or `AZURE_CLIENT_CERTIFICATE_PATH`) — never bake secrets into the
      chart's ConfigMap.
- [ ] Deployment template: single replica (no HA/leader-election in v1 — see CLAUDE.md
      Architecture section), resource requests/limits, `admin` health endpoint wired to
      liveness/readiness probes once `#12` (admin/health endpoint) ships.
- [ ] Chart.yaml version tracks the app version; decide whether release-please should bump it
      automatically (tailscale2otel's `release-please-config.json` has an `extra-files` entry
      bumping `Chart.yaml` — port that pattern once the chart exists, per `hygiene-port.md`'s
      release-please-config.json notes).
- [ ] Wire `.github/workflows/publish.yml`'s `container-publish.yml` call: set
      `helm-chart-path: charts/graph2otel` (and `charts-repo`/`sign`/`sbom` inputs consistent
      with the existing image publish config) — this input is currently omitted per
      `actions-port.md`'s target-file-list notes.
- [ ] Add a chart lint/template-render CI check (helm lint + `helm template` smoke test) —
      either as a new CI job or an addition to the existing `ci.yml`.
- [ ] Document chart install in README/docs site (depends on `#31` docs site landing).

## Constraints & gotchas

- Do not port tailscale2otel's `helm.yml` CI workflow verbatim without checking its current
  shape first — `actions-map`/`actions-port.md` explicitly deferred Helm CI wiring ("NOT ported:
  … helm.yml (until chart)") because no chart existed at scaffold time; this issue is what
  finally makes that port make sense.
- `container-publish.yml`'s `helm-chart-path` input treats an empty string as "skip the Helm OCI
  publish step" — confirm the exact input contract in `rknightion/.github` (pinned SHA
  `65aedb61754e9bf31e947c17409256ba0c58c637`, v1.4.3) before wiring, in case the contract has a
  `charts-repo` requirement.
- graph2otel is single-instance/no-HA by design (CLAUDE.md Architecture) — do not add a
  StatefulSet, leader-election sidecar, or multi-replica default; keep `replicaCount: 1` and
  document why in `values.yaml` comments.
- CheckpointStore (`#7`) is file-based — the chart needs a PersistentVolumeClaim (or documented
  emptyDir-is-lossy warning) for checkpoint state to survive pod restarts; decide and document
  which default the chart ships.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `helm lint charts/graph2otel` and `helm template charts/graph2otel` pass in CI.
- [ ] A release triggers a Helm chart OCI push to GHCR alongside the image, verifiable via
      `helm pull oci://ghcr.io/rknightion/charts/graph2otel --version <tag>`.
- [ ] `values.yaml` documented inline for every key, with tenant secret material clearly marked
      "supply via `existingSecret`, never inline."
- [ ] README/docs mention the chart and a minimal `helm install` example.

## Dependencies

- `#7` CheckpointStore (PVC/persistence decision).
- `#12` Admin/health endpoint (liveness/readiness probe wiring).
- `#31` (this milestone) docs site, for chart install documentation.
- M1 Core framework generally must be far enough along that the binary actually boots against a
  mounted config before the chart is meaningfully testable end-to-end.

comments.body: Done in 271a4d8. `charts/graph2otel` — single-replica deployment (no HA/leader-election by design). values.yaml `config:` mirrors config.example.yaml 1:1 (tenants/otlp/collectors/log_level/admin/checkpoint_dir) → ConfigMap; tenant auth via env from a K8s Secret (existingSecret or chart-created, never in the ConfigMap); optional PVC for the file-based CheckpointStore (documented emptyDir-is-lossy warning); admin health endpoint on liveness/readiness probes. Pipeline: publish.yml `helm-chart-path: charts/graph2otel` (chart rides the release to GHCR OCI alongside the image); ci.yml helm lint + template job (incl. a persistence/existingSecret/admin-disabled render variant); release-please bumps Chart.yaml version/appVersion. `helm lint` (0 failures) + `helm template` pass locally. The release-time OCI-push verification (`helm pull oci://...`) happens on the actual v1.0.0 release cut (#35), which is deliberately not part of this ops/docs pass.

body:
## What & why

Security alerts (`alerts_v2`) is the unified, current-schema security alert stream — it aggregates identity-related alerts surfaced from Entra ID Protection and Microsoft Defender products. Each alert is a discrete event, so it is a `WindowCollector` on #13, checkpointed via #7. It uses the **security workload** (moderate limits — NOT the 1 req/s IPC bucket that risk detections use). Read-only via `SecurityAlert.Read.All`; the legacy `/security/alerts` endpoint is deprecated and avoided.

## Scope

- [ ] `SecurityAlertsCollector` (`WindowCollector`) over `GET /security/alerts_v2`, time field `createdDateTime`, `ge`/`le` filter, `$orderby createdDateTime` (supported), `$top` + nextLink drain via #13.
- [ ] Use `alerts_v2` (current), NOT the deprecated legacy `/security/alerts`.
- [ ] OTLP log record mapping (see Telemetry model).
- [ ] Optional derived counters by severity/status/serviceSource.

## API surface

| Endpoint | Version | App permission | Pagination | Filter/orderby | Retention | Throttle bucket |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /security/alerts_v2` | v1.0 | `SecurityAlert.Read.All` | `@odata.nextLink` | `$filter` (`status`, `severity`, `createdDateTime`, `serviceSource`); `$orderby createdDateTime`; **no delta** | ~30d visible via Graph (per source product) | security workload (moderate; **not** the IPC 1 req/s bucket) |

Docs: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/security-list-alerts_v2?view=graph-rest-1.0 , resource https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/security-alert?view=graph-rest-1.0 , throttling https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/throttling-limits

## Telemetry model

OTLP **log record** per alert; body/timestamp from `createdDateTime`. Structured attributes: `title`, `category`, `severity`, `status`, `serviceSource`, `detectionSource`, `determination`, `classification`, `tenantId`, `id`, `providerAlertId`. Evidence/entity detail (accounts, IPs, devices) as nested structured attributes.

Optional bounded counters: alerts by `severity`, by `status`, by `serviceSource`. **High-cardinality fields (`id`, `providerAlertId`, entity ids/IPs) stay LOG attributes — NEVER metric labels.** Per-tenant resource attributes on every record.

## Constraints & gotchas

- **Security workload, not IPC** — moderate limits, so it does not share the 1 req/s serialization the risk-detections collector needs. Route via #5's appropriate bucket (or default reporting-class backoff if a dedicated security limiter isn't warranted — decide at implementation).
- Watermark on `createdDateTime`, ~10-15 min safety lag, 2-6h overlap, dedupe by `id` (handled by #13). `$orderby createdDateTime` supported. No delta query.
- Data aggregates from Defender/Sentinel sources — identity-sourced alerts require the underlying detection license (P2 for IdP-sourced), but the endpoint itself only needs `SecurityAlert.Read.All`; missing source products simply yield fewer alerts (no hard failure), so no license label on this issue.
- Volume: moderate; depends on which Defender products are enabled in the tenant.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Collector runs on #13 against `alerts_v2` (not the deprecated legacy endpoint).
- [ ] Test: two-page drain via nextLink, each alert emitted once to the in-memory recorder (#8).
- [ ] Test: watermark advance on `createdDateTime` + persist + restart resume from `watermark - overlap` (#7).
- [ ] Test: overlap dedupe (no re-emit across consecutive cycles).
- [ ] Test: out-of-order late arrival inside the overlap window captured, not dropped.
- [ ] Test: no high-cardinality field becomes a metric label on any derived counter.
- [ ] `make check` green (with `-race`).

## Dependencies

- #13, #7, #5 (security-workload limiter), #8, #6, #4.

comments.body:
Done in `d7814ce` (package `internal/collectors/entra/securityalerts`). v1.0 `/security/alerts_v2` (current schema — not the deprecated legacy `/security/alerts`), reporting-class limiter (security workload; `/security/alerts*` added to `ClassifyWorkload`). `ge`/`le`, `$orderby createdDateTime asc`. Maps title / category / severity / status / serviceSource / detectionSource / determination / classification / providerAlertId / evidence_count; alert severity high→Error, medium|low→Warn on the log record.

**Status:** code-complete, unit-verified, `make check` green. Live run against m7kni confirmed the **correct request** but returned **HTTP 403** — the mgmt app doesn't declare `SecurityAlert.Read.All` yet. The collector surfaces the 403 as a WARN and keeps its checkpoint unchanged. Full live data verification pending that scope grant.

**Live verification complete** (`d7814ce`). After granting `SecurityAlert.Read.All` (approved by @rknightion 2026-07-15) the 403 cleared. Re-run against m7kni: security_alerts polls `/security/alerts_v2` cleanly (no error), advances its watermark, writes its checkpoint. 0 records in-window = the tenant has no security alerts in the last hour (healthy state); the request path is fully exercised.

body:
## What & why

Risk detections (Identity Protection) are discrete security events — each detection (anonymous IP, impossible travel, leaked credentials, etc.) is one event. It is a `WindowCollector` on #13, checkpointed via #7. Its defining operational constraint: it lives on the **Identity Protection (IPC) workload**, which is **1 request/second per tenant across ALL apps** with **no `Retry-After`** — so its poller must be serialized through #5's IPC limiter and run slowly. Requires **Entra ID P2** for full detail (P1 downgrades detections to `generic`).

## Scope

- [ ] `RiskDetectionsCollector` (`WindowCollector`) over `GET /identityProtection/riskDetections`, time field `detectedDateTime`, watermark-based filter, `$orderby` treated as weaker/unverified (sort client-side within the drained window), `$top` + nextLink drain via #13.
- [ ] Route through #5's **IPC limiter (1 req/s per tenant, serialized)** — NOT the reporting bucket.
- [ ] OTLP log record mapping (see Telemetry model).
- [ ] License-gate: skip-and-log below P2 via #10 (P1 returns `generic`-only detail — treat as degraded/skip per #10 policy).

## API surface

| Endpoint | Version | App permission | Pagination | Filter/orderby | Retention | Throttle bucket |

## What & why

Non-interactive user sign-ins (token refreshes, silent auth) are for most tenants the **bulk** of all sign-in volume — the largest single log stream graph2otel produces. They are not returned by default from `/auditLogs/signIns`; you must add an explicit `signInEventTypes` filter, and user event types cannot be combined with service-principal/managed-identity types, so this is its own separate `WindowCollector` and poller (on #13, checkpointed via #7, rate-limited via #5's reporting bucket).

> **signInEventTypes filter tier caveat:** the signInEventTypes filter tier (v1.0 vs beta-only) had conflicting evidence during research — verify against live docs at implementation; assume beta until proven otherwise, and note that user-type and servicePrincipal/managedIdentity event types cannot be combined in one $filter (hence separate pollers).

## Scope

- [ ] `SignInsNonInteractiveCollector` (`WindowCollector`) over the sign-ins endpoint with `$filter=signInEventTypes/any(t: t eq 'nonInteractiveUser')`, time field `createdDateTime`, `ge`/`le`, `$orderby createdDateTime asc`, `$top=1000`, following `@odata.nextLink` via the #13 engine.

- [ ] OTLP log record mapping (see Telemetry model); consider filtering to failures/risky if volume is a concern (document as a config lever).

## API surface

| Endpoint | Version | App permission | Pagination | Filter/orderby | Retention | Throttle bucket |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /auditLogs/signIns` + `$filter=signInEventTypes/any(t: t eq 'nonInteractiveUser')` | beta (verify v1.0 at implementation) | `AuditLog.Read.All` (+ `Policy.Read.All` for CA sub-object) | `@odata.nextLink` / `$skiptoken`; default & max 1000/page | `$filter createdDateTime ge/le` AND the `signInEventTypes` filter; `$orderby createdDateTime asc` | 30d P1/P2 | reporting: 5 req/10s per app per tenant, **no Retry-After** |

## Telemetry model

OTLP **log record** per sign-in; body/timestamp from `createdDateTime`. Same attribute set as interactive (`userPrincipalName`, `appDisplayName`, `appId`, `ipAddress`, `clientAppUsed`, `status.errorCode`, `conditionalAccessStatus`, `riskLevelDuringSignIn`, `location.countryOrRegion`, `signInEventTypes`, `id`, `correlationId`).

body:
## What & why

Interactive user sign-ins are the flagship compliance log stream: who signed in, from where, with what result, and whether Conditional Access and MFA were satisfied. This collector is a thin `WindowCollector` on the generic log pipeline engine (#13), checkpointed via #7, rate-limited through the reporting-workload limiter (#5). It captures the **default** slice of `/auditLogs/signIns` (with no `signInEventTypes` filter the endpoint returns interactive user sign-ins only), emitting one OTLP log record per sign-in and optionally deriving bounded counters.

## Scope

- [ ] `SignInsInteractiveCollector` (`WindowCollector`) over `GET /auditLogs/signIns`, time field `createdDateTime`, standard `ge`/`le` filter, `$orderby createdDateTime asc` (reliable here), `$top=1000`, following `@odata.nextLink` to exhaustion via the #13 engine.
- [ ] No `signInEventTypes` filter — the default collection is interactive user sign-ins.
- [ ] OTLP log record mapping (see Telemetry model).
- [ ] Optional derived counters (see Telemetry model), emitted through the Emitter (#8).
- [ ] License-gate: skip-and-log on Free (sign-ins require P1) via #10.
- [ ] Preflight (#11) warns once if `Policy.Read.All` is absent, since `appliedConditionalAccessPolicies` is then silently omitted — warn, don't fail.

## API surface

| Endpoint | Version | App permission | Pagination | Filter/orderby | Retention | Throttle bucket |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /auditLogs/signIns` (default = interactive user) | v1.0 | `AuditLog.Read.All` (+ `Policy.Read.All` to populate `appliedConditionalAccessPolicies`) | `@odata.nextLink` / `$skiptoken`; default & max 1000/page; default order desc | `$filter createdDateTime ge/le`; `$orderby createdDateTime asc`; no `$count`; **no delta** | 7d Free (interactive only) / 30d P1/P2 | reporting: 5 req/10s per app per tenant, **no Retry-After** |

Docs: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/signin-list?view=graph-rest-1.0 , https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/signin?view=graph-rest-1.0 , throttling https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/throttling-limits , retention https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/monitoring-health/reference-reports-data-retention

## Telemetry model

OTLP **log record** per sign-in; body/timestamp from `createdDateTime`. Structured attributes: `userPrincipalName`, `appDisplayName`, `appId`, `ipAddress`, `clientAppUsed`, `status.errorCode`, `conditionalAccessStatus`, `riskLevelDuringSignIn` (returns `hidden` unless P2), `location.countryOrRegion`, `signInEventTypes`; plus `id`, `correlationId`.

Derived counters (optional, bounded): sign-ins by `status.errorCode`, by `conditionalAccessStatus`, MFA-satisfied rate. **High-cardinality fields (`id`, `correlationId`, `ipAddress`, `userPrincipalName`) stay LOG attributes — NEVER metric labels.** Per-tenant resource attributes (tenant id + display name) on every record.

## Constraints & gotchas

- Watermark on `createdDateTime`, safety lag ~10-15 min, generous 2-6h overlap re-query window, dedupe by immutable `id` — out-of-order ingestion is real (all handled by #13).
- Default order is **descending**; poll ascending from the watermark (`$orderby asc` reliable on signIns).
- Reporting workload sends **no `Retry-After`** on 429 — rely on #5's limiter + own exponential backoff, not the SDK retry handler alone.
- Retention is 7 days on Free and sign-ins need P1 regardless; cold-start backfill bounded to 30 days (P1/P2).
- Volume: interactive is the *smallest* sign-in category (non-interactive/SP/MI dwarf it), so this collector is the least throttle-sensitive of the four.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Collector registers and runs on the #13 engine through the reporting limiter (#5).
- [ ] Test: two-page response fully drained via nextLink, each sign-in emitted once as an OTLP log to the in-memory recorder (#8).
- [ ] Test: watermark advances to newest-drained `createdDateTime` minus safety lag and persists (#7); restart resumes from `watermark - overlap`.
- [ ] Test: overlap-window dedupe — a record seen in cycle N is not re-emitted in cycle N+1.
- [ ] Test: an out-of-order late-arriving event inside the overlap window is captured, not dropped.
- [ ] Test: license-gate skip — collector is skipped-and-logged (not crashed) when tier < P1 (#10).
- [ ] Test: no high-cardinality field appears as a metric label on any derived counter.
- [ ] `make check` green (with `-race`).

## Dependencies

- #13 (log pipeline engine), #7 (CheckpointStore), #5 (reporting-workload limiter), #8 (Emitter), #6 (WindowCollector), #4 (transport/retry), #10 (license-gate skip), #11 (preflight for `Policy.Read.All`).

**Live-verified** against the m7kni tenant (app-only cert auth, `AuditLog.Read.All`): 103 `entra.signin` log records emitted across all four streams; four distinct checkpoints written (`#interactive`, `#nonInteractiveUser`, `#servicePrincipal`, `#managedIdentity`) proving the shared-path streams keep independent watermarks; UPN / IP (incl. body:
## What & why

Most fleet-wide Intune compliance / security / app-install / update detail is **only** available as an async export job (`deviceManagement/reports/exportJobs`), or is only sane at scale that way — per-device entity walks blow the throttling budget on a 10k+ fleet. The export API is the linchpin of the Intune log/report side: a generic, reusable subsystem that all export-based report collectors (app install status, feature-update device states, enrollment failures, certificate inventory, Defender agents, and more) build on. This issue delivers that subsystem; the individual reports are separate issues that depend on it.

The client is a generic pipeline parameterized by `reportName` / `select` / `filter`: **POST create job → poll status to terminal → download the pre-signed SAS ZIP → unzip → parse CSV/JSON**. It owns its own rate budget and its own polling backoff, distinct from the entity-polling path.

## Security-review talking point (document prominently)

**A read-only exporter still needs one write-level scope purely to create export jobs.** Reading the exported data back needs only read, but **creating** an export job requires one of `DeviceManagementConfiguration.ReadWrite.All`, `DeviceManagementApps.ReadWrite.All`, or `DeviceManagementManagedDevices.ReadWrite.All`. This is unavoidable per Microsoft's design and must be called out in `SECURITY.md` and the permission preflight (#11) as a genuine least-privilege wrinkle — graph2otel is otherwise entirely read-only, and this is the single scope that breaks that property. Pick and document exactly one such scope; do not request more than one.

## Scope

- [ ] Generic export-job client parameterized by `reportName`, `select`, `filter`, `format`, `localizationType`.
- [ ] Create: `POST /deviceManagement/reports/exportJobs` with the body fields above; handle the `201` + generated `id` + `status: notStarted`.
- [ ] Poll: `GET .../exportJobs/{id}` through `notStarted → inProgress → completed` (or `failed`) with exponential backoff (2–5s initial → 30–60s cap).
- [ ] Download: fetch the temporary pre-signed SAS `url` (no auth on that URL) promptly on `completed`, before `expirationDateTime`.
- [ ] Unzip + parse the CSV/JSON payload into typed rows for the consuming report collector.
- [ ] Own rate budget: **48 requests/min per app** ceiling covering create + every poll + list; a single export polled ~10× before completion burns ~11 of the 48 — schedule accordingly (this is the export budget, separate from the general Intune limiter).
- [ ] Always pass explicit `select` (Microsoft warns default columns can change without notice).
- [ ] Surface `failed` status and SAS-expiry-before-download as distinct, retryable error conditions.

## API surface

| Endpoint/report | Version | App permission | Flow | Throttle bucket |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `POST /deviceManagement/reports/exportJobs` (create) | v1.0 (also beta) | **write** — one of `DeviceManagementConfiguration.ReadWrite.All` / `DeviceManagementApps.ReadWrite.All` / `DeviceManagementManagedDevices.ReadWrite.All` | POST → `201` + `id` + `status` | Export API: 100/tenant/min, **48/min per app**, 8/min per user |
| `GET /deviceManagement/reports/exportJobs/{id}` (poll) | v1.0 (also beta) | read (job created under the write scope above) | Poll to terminal status | Same export budget (each poll counts) |
| `GET <SAS url>` (download) | n/a | none (pre-signed) | Download ZIP, ~6h expiry | Not a Graph call |

Body fields: `reportName`, `filter` (report-specific `eq` string DSL, e.g. `"(OwnerType eq '1')"` — NOT OData `$filter`), `select`, `format` (defaults `csv`; set `json` explicitly), `localizationType` (`LocalizedValuesAsAdditionalColumn` default | `ReplaceLocalizableValues`). Response fields: `id`, `status`, `url`, `requestDateTime`, `expirationDateTime`, `snapshotId`.

Docs: [Export Intune reports using Graph APIs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/device-management/reports/export-graph-apis), [deviceManagementExportJob resource](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/intune-reporting-devicemanagementexportjob?view=graph-rest-1.0), [Available reports (report-name catalog)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/intune-service/fundamentals/reports-export-graph-available-reports), [Graph throttling limits](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/throttling-limits).

## Telemetry model

The subsystem itself is transport, not a domain collector — it produces typed rows for a consuming report collector to model as metrics or logs. It should emit self-obs metrics: export jobs created / completed / failed, poll counts, time-to-completion, and download bytes, keyed by `reportName` (low cardinality). No per-row telemetry originates here.

## Constraints & gotchas

- **`filter` is a report-specific string DSL, not OData** (`"(Column eq 'value')"`); only specific columns are valid per report, and an invalid `reportName` or `select` column 400s with no fuzzy match — smoke-test names/casing against a live tenant before hardcoding.
- **48/min per-app budget is the binding constraint.** Every poll counts; reports that fan out per `PolicyId` multiply round trips. Serialize and pace exports under one shared export limiter.
- SAS `url` is time-limited (~6h) — download promptly; treat expiry as retryable (re-create the job).
- `localizationType` is ignored by `Devices` / `DevicesWithInventory` (legacy) — don't assume it applies everywhere.
- Report schemas gain `V2` / `V3` variants over time — check the available-reports reference for the current name.
- `snapshotId` (a `CachedReportConfiguration` id) is mutually exclusive with `filter` / `select` / `orderBy`.
- No pagination in the REST sense — poll to terminal, then one full-file download.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Generic client compiles against the M1 Graph client factory (#4) and runs under a dedicated export rate limiter (48/min per app) provided by / registered with the M1 rate-limiter set (#5).
- [ ] The write-scope-to-create caveat is documented in `SECURITY.md` and surfaced by the permission preflight (#11).
- [ ] `httptest`-based fake exercising the full POST → poll → download flow, including:
  - [ ] a **slow-completion** case (job stays `inProgress` for several polls, then `completed`) — asserts backoff and eventual download;
  - [ ] a **failed-job** case (`status: failed`) — asserts a distinct, surfaced error and no download attempt;
  - [ ] a SAS-expiry / download-error case — asserts retryable handling;
  - [ ] CSV and JSON parse paths.
- [ ] Explicit `select` is always sent; a missing `select` is a programming error caught in tests.

## Dependencies

- M1 #4 (Graph client factory — instrumented transport)
- M1 #5 (rate limiters — the export 48/min bucket lives here; add if not already present)
- M1 #8 (Emitter — for the subsystem's self-obs metrics)
- Consumed by the export-based report issues (app install status, feature-update device states, enrollment failures, certificate inventory, Defender agents).

comments.body: Done in 971667e. `internal/exportjob` — generic reports export-job client: POST create → poll to terminal (backoff PollInitial→PollMax) → SAS-expiry check → download ZIP → unzip → parse CSV/JSON into []Row. Runner/Request/Row/Poster/Downloader interfaces; ErrJobFailed + ErrSASExpired sentinels; self-obs metrics graph2otel.export.{jobs,poll_count,duration_seconds,bytes} keyed by report_name. Runs on the 48/min export limiter (already classified in graphclient/workload.go). All acceptance criteria met via httptest (slow-completion, failed-job, SAS-expiry, CSV+JSON parse, empty-select guard). The write-scope-to-create caveat is documented on the collectors that use it (each M5 export consumer declares the one write scope). Enabled `graphclient.RawPost` for the POST. Wired into the composition root via `collectors.Deps.Export` (one exporter per tenant). Consumers: #37/#38/#40/#41/#42.

body:
## What & why

Windows Autopilot deployment events (`deviceManagement/autopilotEvents`, the `deviceManagementAutopilotEvent` type) are one record per enrollment / Enrollment Status Page (ESP) attempt, carrying phase timestamps and durations. This is the rich per-attempt view of Autopilot outcomes — far more detailed than the coarse `enrollmentState` on the device-identity resource — and the source for ESP phase-latency and failure analysis. Beta-only, so flagged `beta-api`.

Implemented as a `WindowCollector` on the M1 log pipeline engine (#13), checkpointed on `eventDateTime`.

## Scope

- [ ] Register an `autopilotEvents` `WindowCollector` (beta endpoint) against the M1 log pipeline engine (#13), keyed on `eventDateTime`.
- [ ] Client-side time filtering on `eventDateTime` (no documented server-side `$filter`).
- [ ] Watermark + overlap + id-dedupe model.
- [ ] Emit one OTLP log record per attempt; keep a `phase` dimension so the three phase statuses stay distinguishable.
- [ ] Clamp negative durations (clock skew) before deriving any latency metric.
- [ ] Per-tenant enable + interval config (default 15–30 min; bursty on refresh waves).

## API surface

| Endpoint/report | Version | App permission | Flow | Throttle bucket |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /deviceManagement/autopilotEvents` (`deviceManagementAutopilotEvent`) | **beta-only** (no v1.0) | `DeviceManagementManagedDevices.Read.All` | Paged `@odata.nextLink`, client-side `eventDateTime` filter | General Intune (M1 Intune rate limiter #5) |

Key fields: `eventDateTime`, `deploymentState` / `deviceSetupStatus` / `accountSetupStatus`, `enrollmentState`, `enrollmentType`, `enrollmentFailureDetails`, `deploymentDuration` / `deviceSetupDuration` / `accountSetupDuration` (ISO 8601 — ESP phase-latency histograms), `windowsAutopilotDeploymentProfileDisplayName`, `osVersion`, `deviceSerialNumber`.

Docs: [deviceManagementAutopilotEvent resource (beta)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/intune-troubleshooting-devicemanagementautopilotevent?view=graph-rest-beta), [Graph throttling limits](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/throttling-limits).

## Telemetry model

Event stream → OTLP **logs**, keyed on `deviceId` / `enrollmentType` / `deploymentState`. Optionally derive ESP phase-latency histograms from the `deploymentDuration` family — but keep a `phase` label and clamp negatives first. `deviceSerialNumber` on the log record only. Attributes limited to low-cardinality enums (`deploymentState`, `enrollmentType`, `enrollmentState`, profile display name).

## Constraints & gotchas

- **Beta-only** — no v1.0 fallback. Pin the beta version and isolate error handling; flag as a stability risk in design docs.
- **Durations can be negative** (client clock skew) — clamp to zero before any histogram/metric.
- Three phase statuses (`deviceSetupStatus` / `accountSetupStatus` / overall `deploymentState`) share one enum shape — keep an explicit `phase` dimension, don't collapse them.
- No documented `$filter` / relationships / `$expand` — filter `eventDateTime` client-side; use watermark + overlap + id-dedupe (do not trust server order).
- Multiple events per device on retries (`successOnRetry`) — id-dedupe, and don't treat a later success as erasing an earlier failure record.
- Bursty on refresh waves — overlap window and cadence must tolerate spikes.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Collector registers and runs as a `WindowCollector` on the beta endpoint; watermark persisted per tenant+endpoint via the M1 CheckpointStore (#7).
- [ ] Emits deduplicated OTLP log records; id-dedupe verified across an overlap window.
- [ ] Negative-duration clamp covered by a test.
- [ ] Table-driven tests with an `httptest` fake: multi-page drain; out-of-order arrival captured; duplicate `id` dropped once; retry events (multiple per device) preserved distinctly.
- [ ] Graceful skip-and-log if the beta surface is unavailable / unlicensed.

## Dependencies

- M1 #13 (log pipeline engine)
- M1 #7 (CheckpointStore)
- M1 #6 (collector framework)
- M1 #8 (Emitter)
- M1 #5 (Intune rate limiter)
- M1 #4 (Graph client factory)

comments.body: Done in 971667e. `internal/collectors/intune/autopilotevents`, `intune.autopilot_events` WindowCollector over beta /deviceManagement/autopilotEvents (Experimental/opt-in). LIVE-VERIFIED: polls cleanly (empty window; NoServerFilter filter-less beta fetch did NOT 400). BaseURLOverride=beta + NoServerFilter. Transforms: ISO-8601 phase durations clamped non-negative (clock skew, guard test); distinct deployment/deviceSetup/accountSetup phase statuses preserved (not collapsed); retry records preserved (dedupe by distinct event id).

## What & why

Enrollment troubleshooting events (`deviceManagement/troubleshootingEvents`, the `enrollmentTroubleshootingEvent` type) are the continuous, log-shaped feed of failed device enrollments — one row per failure with a `failureCategory`, `failureReason`, and `correlationId`. This is the Graph-reachable slice of the Intune `OperationalLogs` diagnostic category (the rest of that category has no Graph equivalent), and it is the primary continuous source for "why are devices failing to enrol". A parallel `EnrollmentFailures` export report exists for backfill/deep-dive (tracked separately as an export-job report); this issue is the live event stream.

Implemented as a `WindowCollector` on the M1 log pipeline engine (#13), checkpointed on `eventDateTime`.

## Scope

- [ ] Register a `troubleshootingEvents` `WindowCollector` against the M1 log pipeline engine (#13), keyed on `eventDateTime`.
- [ ] Client-side time filtering on `eventDateTime` (assume no server-side `$filter`).
- [ ] Watermark + overlap + id-dedupe model.
- [ ] Emit one OTLP log record per failed enrollment, correlated on `correlationId`.
- [ ] Per-tenant enable + interval config (default 15–30 min poll; volume tracks failure rate, not fleet size).

## API surface

| Endpoint/report | Version | App permission | Flow | Throttle bucket |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /deviceManagement/troubleshootingEvents` (`enrollmentTroubleshootingEvent`) | v1.0 | `DeviceManagementManagedDevices.Read.All` | Paged `@odata.nextLink`, client-side `eventDateTime` filter | General Intune (M1 Intune rate limiter #5) |

Key fields: `eventDateTime`, `deviceId`, `userId`, `operatingSystem` / `osVersion`, `enrollmentType`, `failureCategory` (`authentication` / `authorization` / `accountValidation` / … / `enrollmentRestrictionsEnforced` / `userAbandonment`), `failureReason`, `correlationId`.

Docs: [enrollmentTroubleshootingEvent resource](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/intune-troubleshooting-enrollmenttroubleshootingevent?view=graph-rest-1.0), [Graph throttling limits](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/throttling-limits).

## Telemetry model

Event stream → OTLP **logs**. Attributes carry low-cardinality dimensions (`failureCategory`, `enrollmentType`, `operatingSystem`); `deviceId` / `userId` / `correlationId` on the log record only, never as metric labels. Optional self-obs counter of failures processed per poll keyed by `failureCategory`.

## Constraints & gotchas

- **Assume no server-side `$filter`** on `troubleshootingEvents` — filter on `eventDateTime` client-side. `$orderby` likewise not to be trusted; use the M1 watermark + overlap + id-dedupe model.
- No delta query — consumer owns the watermark.
- Event volume spikes on onboarding / OS-upgrade waves rather than scaling with fleet size — the poll cadence and overlap window must tolerate bursts.
- `EnrollmentFailures` (the export report) and this live event stream are two independent, overlapping surfaces with different columns and freshness — this collector is the continuous log source; the export is optional beta backfill (separate issue).
- Needs an active Intune license.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Collector registers and runs as a `WindowCollector`; watermark persisted per tenant+endpoint via the M1 CheckpointStore (#7).
- [ ] Emits deduplicated OTLP log records; id-dedupe verified across an overlap window.
- [ ] Table-driven tests with an `httptest` fake endpoint: multi-page drain; client-side `eventDateTime` filtering correct; out-of-order arrival within overlap captured; duplicate `id` dropped exactly once.
- [ ] Graceful skip-and-log without an Intune license.

## Dependencies

- M1 #13 (log pipeline engine)
- M1 #7 (CheckpointStore)
- M1 #6 (collector framework)
- M1 #8 (Emitter)
- M1 #5 (Intune rate limiter)
- M1 #4 (Graph client factory)

LIVE-VERIFIED: polls cleanly (empty window on this tenant = no recent enrollment failures; the filter-less fetch did NOT 400). body:
## What & why

Intune's change-audit stream (`deviceManagement/auditEvents`) is the highest-volume Intune log source and the direct Graph equivalent of the portal audit log / the `AuditLogs` diagnostic-settings category. Every admin/service change (policy create/update/delete, assignment change, remote action, enrollment-config edit) lands here with actor, target resource, and before/after values. Graph retains this for ~1 year, so it is a genuine drop-in replacement for the diagnostic-settings → Log Analytics path for Intune audit, with no workspace to configure.

This collector is a `WindowCollector` on the M1 log pipeline engine (#13): checkpointed watermark on `activityDateTime`, emitted as OTLP logs, one tenant-scoped poller.

## Scope

- [ ] Register an `auditEvents` `WindowCollector` against the M1 log pipeline engine (#13), keyed on `activityDateTime`.
- [ ] Watermark + overlap + id-dedupe model only (see Constraints — server order is not trustworthy here).
- [ ] Emit one OTLP log record per audit event, keyed/correlated on `correlationId`.
- [ ] Redaction pass over `modifiedProperties` before export (secrets/PII — see Constraints).
- [ ] Per-tenant enable + interval config (default 15–60 min poll).
- [ ] Verify the required application permission empirically against a live tenant (docs name is suspect — see API surface).

## API surface

| Endpoint/report | Version | App permission | Flow | Throttle bucket |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /deviceManagement/auditEvents` (+ `/{id}`) | v1.0 | `DeviceManagementApps.Read.All` (surprising for an audit endpoint — verify live; likely a docs artifact) | Paged `@odata.nextLink`, incremental filter on `activityDateTime` | General Intune (~1000 req/20s per app; no guaranteed `Retry-After`) — use the M1 Intune rate limiter (#5) |

Key fields: `activityDateTime`, `activity` / `activityType` / `activityOperationType` / `activityResult`, `actor` (`userPrincipalName` / `applicationDisplayName` / `ipAddress` / `auditActorType`), `resources[]` (`auditResourceType` / `resourceId` / `modifiedProperties[].oldValue` / `newValue`), `correlationId`, `category`.

Docs: [auditEvent resource](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/intune-auditing-auditevent?view=graph-rest-1.0), [List auditEvents](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/intune-auditing-auditevent-list?view=graph-rest-1.0), [Graph throttling limits](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/throttling-limits).

## Telemetry model

Pure event stream → OTLP **logs**. No steady-state metric series (audit rows carry unbounded actor/resource identifiers). Log body carries the human-readable activity; attributes carry low-cardinality dimensions (`activityType`, `activityOperationType`, `activityResult`, `category`) plus `correlationId` and actor identifiers on the log record only. Optional counter of events processed per poll for self-obs, keyed by `activityResult` — not by actor/resource.

## Constraints & gotchas

- **`$orderby` is unreliable on `auditEvents` — never depend on server order.** The v1.0 List page documents no OData options at all; `$filter` on `activityDateTime` works empirically (incremental pulls rely on it) but `$orderby` is unverified and must not be assumed. Correctness comes from the M1 watermark + overlap re-query window + id-dedupe (dedupe on the immutable event `id`), exactly as the feasibility model prescribes. Events can arrive out of order relative to `activityDateTime`, so a naive high-water mark drops data — lag the watermark and re-query an overlap window.
- **No delta query** exists for this endpoint — the consumer owns the watermark.
- **`modifiedProperties` can carry secrets / PII** (certificate- or credential-bearing profiles, UPNs, IPs). Redact before emitting as OTLP log attributes.
- Retention is ~1 year service-side — poll often enough to never lose data to rollover; cold-start backfill can walk up to ~1 year.
- Needs an active Intune license on the tenant.
- `$filter` guessed on unsupported properties 400s — only filter on `activityDateTime`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Collector registers and runs on the M1 scheduler as a `WindowCollector`; watermark persisted per tenant+endpoint via the M1 CheckpointStore (#7).
- [ ] Emits deduplicated OTLP log records (id-dedupe verified across an overlap window).
- [ ] `modifiedProperties` redaction applied and covered by a test.
- [ ] Table-driven tests with an `httptest` fake Graph endpoint: multi-page drain; out-of-order-arrival within the overlap window is captured (not dropped); duplicate `id` across overlapping polls is dropped exactly once; watermark advances only to the newest fully-drained event minus safety lag.
- [ ] Graceful skip-and-log if the tenant lacks an Intune license rather than crashing.

## Dependencies

- M1 #13 (log pipeline engine — the watermark poller this runs on)
- M1 #7 (CheckpointStore — watermark/overlap/seen-ids persistence)
- M1 #6 (collector framework — `WindowCollector` interface, Registry, Scheduler)
- M1 #8 (Emitter — OTLP log export)
- M1 #5 (Intune rate limiter)
- M1 #4 (Graph client factory)

body:
## What & why

The generic watermark poller that every `WindowCollector` (M3 Entra logs, M5 Intune logs) runs on. Since no log-shaped Graph endpoint supports delta queries or reliable server-side ordering, each poll must: query a time window `[watermark - overlap, now - safetyLag]`, order ascending where supported, follow `@odata.nextLink` to exhaustion, dedupe by immutable `id`, emit each record as an OTLP log, and advance the watermark — all backed by the CheckpointStore (#7). This issue delivers that engine once, generically, so the M3/M5 log collectors are thin configurations of it rather than 12 hand-rolled pollers each re-deriving the same subtle correctness logic.

## Scope

- [ ] Add the log pipeline engine (in `internal/collector` or a new `internal/logpipeline`), consumed by `WindowCollector`s.
- [ ] A generic poll routine parameterized per endpoint by: the OData path, the timestamp field name, the filter operator flavor (see below), whether `$orderby` is trustworthy, the OTLP log mapping (record body + attributes), and the workload (for #5's limiter).
- [ ] Each cycle: build `$filter {timeField} <op> {watermark - overlap} and {timeField} <op> {now - safetyLag}`, `$orderby {timeField} asc` **only where reliable**, `$top 1000`; follow `@odata.nextLink` to exhaustion via the SDK `PageIterator`.
- [ ] Dedupe each record against the CheckpointStore seen-ids set (#7); emit non-duplicates as OTLP logs through the Emitter (#8); advance the watermark to the newest fully-drained event timestamp minus `safetyLag`; persist the updated checkpoint.
- [ ] Route requests through the correct #5 rate limiter (reporting vs IPC vs Intune) and rely on #4's transport for retry.
- [ ] Cold-start backfill: walk the retention window in ascending time-sliced pages under the same rate budgets (bounded by each endpoint's retention — see #9 for tier-dependent retention).

## Design constraints

- **safetyLag ~10–15 min; overlap 2–6h** (generous — out-of-order ingestion is real; cheap insurance with id-dedupe). Watermark = last fully-processed event timestamp minus safetyLag. Resume from `watermark - overlap` on restart. (research: log-export-feasibility §5 + "Recommended polling architecture"; checkpoint model in #7)
- **No delta query exists for ANY of these endpoints** (`signIns`, `directoryAudits`, `provisioning`, `riskDetections`, `riskyUsers`, Intune `auditEvents`) — you own the watermark; there is no server cursor. (research: entra-graph-api §0 "No delta for logs"; log-export-feasibility §5)
- **Per-endpoint filter-operator flavor differs — handle all three:**
  - [ ] Standard `ge`/`le` on the time field: `signIns` (`createdDateTime`), `directoryAudits` (`activityDateTime`). `$orderby ... asc` is reliable here. (research: entra-graph-api §8/§9)
  - [ ] **Strict `gt`/`lt` (NOT ge/le)** on `activityDateTime`: **provisioning** (`provisioningObjectSummary`). `$orderby` unreliable — watermark+dedupe only. (research: log-export-feasibility verdict matrix + §"Recommended polling architecture"; entra-graph-api §10)
  - [ ] **`$orderby` unreliable / undocumented** — do NOT trust server order: **Intune `auditEvents`** (v1.0 `List auditEvents` documents NO OData options at all; `$filter` on `activityDateTime` works but is empirically-supported/undocumented — smoke-test against a live tenant; "do not promise `$orderby`"). Watermark+dedupe carries correctness here. (research: log-export-feasibility Intune matrix "AuditLogs" row; intune-graph-api §6 auditEvents)
- **Default order is descending** by the time field on signIns — for polling you want ascending from the watermark; where `$orderby asc` isn't reliable, sort client-side within the drained window before advancing. (research: log-export-feasibility §5)
- **Dedupe by immutable `id` (GUID)** per endpoint — the overlap window is what creates duplicates; the seen-ids set makes it idempotent. Intune's own diagnostic export can duplicate up to 100% of records in 24h, so dedupe is mandatory regardless. (research: log-export-feasibility §5, §"gaps" note)
- **Page size 1000** (default and max) for sign-ins/audits; follow `@odata.nextLink`/`$skiptoken` (opaque). `$skip` is not supported — nextLink only. (research: entra-graph-api §0 Pagination, §8)
- **Four separate sign-in pollers** are required (interactive / non-interactive / servicePrincipal / managedIdentity) because event types can't be combined — that's an M3 concern, but the engine must support running N independent `WindowCollector` instances over the same base path with different `signInEventTypes` filters and independent checkpoints. (research: entra-graph-api §8 "CRITICAL signInEventTypes")
- **Reporting + IPC workloads send NO `Retry-After`** — the engine must go through #5's limiters + own backoff, not rely on the SDK retry handler alone. (research: entra-graph-api §0; #5)
- **PII/cardinality:** log records carry the per-entity detail (UPN, IP, correlationId, id) as structured attributes; these must NEVER become metric labels if the engine also derives counters. (CLAUDE.md cardinality rule)
- **No third-party assertion library** — standard-library `testing`; drive with an `httptest.Server` returning canned paged responses.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A test (against `httptest`) that a two-page response is fully drained via nextLink and every record is emitted as an OTLP log to the in-memory recorder (#8).
- [ ] A test that records within the overlap window already in the seen-ids set are deduped (emitted exactly once across two consecutive poll cycles).
- [ ] A test that the watermark advances to `newest-drained-timestamp - safetyLag` and persists to the CheckpointStore (#7), and that a restart resumes from `watermark - overlap`.
- [ ] A test that an out-of-order late-arriving event (timestamp older than a prior watermark but inside the overlap window) is still captured and not dropped.
- [ ] A test that the `gt`/`lt` (provisioning) vs `ge`/`le` (signIns/audits) filter flavor is emitted correctly per endpoint config, and that an endpoint flagged "orderby unreliable" (Intune auditEvents) sorts client-side rather than trusting server order.
- [ ] A test that requests are routed through the correct #5 rate limiter (reporting vs IPC).
- [ ] `make check` green (with `-race`, since the engine runs concurrently across endpoints).

## Dependencies

- Depends on #4 (transport/retry), #5 (per-workload limiters + backoff), #6 (`WindowCollector` interface), #7 (CheckpointStore watermark/overlap/seen-ids), #8 (Emitter for OTLP logs). License-gated retention windows from #9 inform cold-start backfill bounds.
- Consumed by: every M3 Entra log collector (sign-ins x4, directory audits, provisioning, risk detections, security alerts) and M5 Intune log collectors (auditEvents, enrollment troubleshooting).

body:
## What & why

An operator visibility endpoint: `/healthz` for liveness and a per-collector status page so ops can see live per-collector health ("Intune collector last succeeded 3 polls ago", "sign-ins skipped: requires P1"). Ported from tailscale2otel's admin status pattern. This is the human-facing complement to the self-obs metrics (#9) — the same underlying per-collector state, rendered for a browser/curl without needing a metrics backend wired up.

## Scope

- [ ] Add `internal/admin` (or `internal/app`) with an HTTP server, gated by the `admin` config block from #2 (`Enabled`, `Addr`).
- [ ] `/healthz` — liveness (200 when the process is up and the scheduler is running). Keep it cheap and dependency-free (no Graph call).
- [ ] A per-collector status page (HTML + a JSON variant) surfacing, per collector per tenant: last success time, staleness, last error (if any), enabled/skipped state + skip reason (license/permission), and interval. Read from the same scheduler state that feeds #9.
- [ ] Port the tailscale2otel `admin_status` structure: a `statusdata` model + `statushtml` renderer separated so the JSON and HTML share one source of truth. (donor: `/Users/rob/repos/tailscale2otel/internal/app/admin_status.go` + its `statusdata`/`statushtml`)
- [ ] Bind to the configured `admin.addr`; default disabled or bound to a non-privileged port per #2's default. Clean shutdown with the process (SIGINT/SIGTERM).

## Design constraints

- **Port from tailscale2otel's admin status page** (research: go-stack §3 "Error/partial-failure handling" cites `internal/app/admin_status.go` + `statusdata`/`statushtml`; m365-exporter-lessons §1 notes the per-collector health triad is "the first thing you'll want when something silently stops updating").
- **Reuse #9's per-collector state — do not maintain a second copy.** The scheduler (#6) owns per-collector last-success/duration/error; #9 emits it as metrics and this endpoint renders it. One source of truth.
- **Surface skip reasons** from #9/#10 (license tier) so a "why is this collector not running" question is answerable from the status page, not just from logs. This is what turns partial-failure confusion (m365-exporter-lessons §4 lesson 5) into a glanceable answer.
- **No Graph calls from `/healthz`** — liveness must not depend on an upstream that legitimately throttles/degrades. A degraded collector is shown on the status page, not as a failed healthcheck.
- **Single-instance, no HA** (v1 decision) — this is an ops visibility endpoint, not a clustered control plane. (CLAUDE.md Architecture: "Single-instance, no HA/leader-election in v1")
- **No third-party assertion library** — standard-library `testing`; test handlers via `httptest`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A test that `GET /healthz` returns 200 with the scheduler running (via `httptest`).
- [ ] A test that the status page (JSON variant) reflects a collector's last-success/staleness/error and its enabled-vs-skipped state, driven from injected scheduler state.
- [ ] A test that a skipped collector shows its skip reason (e.g. "requires P2") on the status output.
- [ ] A test that the admin server does not start when `admin.enabled: false`.
- [ ] `make check` green.

## Dependencies

- Depends on #2 (`admin` config block), #6 (scheduler per-collector state), #9 (per-collector self-obs state), and reads skip reasons from #9/#10.
