body:
## What & why

A partially-permissioned service principal is a classic "works for me, 403 for you" trap: some collectors succeed and others silently 403 at runtime, scattered across poll cycles, with no clean startup signal. This issue adds a `graph2otel check` subcommand that validates, per enabled collector per tenant, that the app has the admin-consented permissions it needs — and reports what's missing clearly, up front, instead of leaving operators to reverse-engineer runtime 403s. Directly actioned from the m365-exporter lesson that setup needs two easily-missed manual steps (admin consent, and sometimes a directory role) and would benefit from a preflight command.

## Scope

- [ ] Add a `check` subcommand to `cmd/graph2otel` (e.g. `graph2otel check --config <path>`), separate from the normal long-running poll mode.
- [ ] For each configured tenant, authenticate via #3 and enumerate the app's effective granted application permissions (e.g. read the service principal's `appRoleAssignments` / the OAuth2 app-role grants for the Graph resource, or introspect the token's roles claim).
- [ ] For each enabled collector (per #6 registration + #2 config), know its required Graph application permission(s) — each collector declares them (a `RequiredPermissions() []string` on the collector, or a static registry). Compare required vs granted.
- [ ] Report clearly: per tenant, per collector, OK / MISSING `<permission>`. Exit non-zero if anything required is missing. Group and de-duplicate the missing-permission list so the operator gets a single actionable "grant these and admin-consent" summary.
- [ ] Surface the admin-consent + directory-role caveats in the output/help (some permissions need admin consent after being added; a few surfaces gate on a directory role too).
- [ ] Keep it read-only and side-effect-free (it validates; it does not grant anything).

## Design constraints

- **App-only application permissions, admin-consented** — the permissions to validate are the least-privilege read scopes each collector declares. Representative required scopes from research (per-collector authoritative list comes from the collector itself):
  - Entra: `AuditLog.Read.All` (sign-ins/audits/provisioning/reports), `User.Read.All`/`Group.Read.All`/`Device.Read.All`/`Application.Read.All` or `Directory.Read.All` (directory objects), `Policy.Read.All` (CA/named locations/auth-methods policy), `IdentityRiskyUser.Read.All` + `IdentityRiskEvent.Read.All` (risk), `IdentityRiskyServicePrincipal.Read.All` (risky SPs), `RoleManagement.Read.Directory` (roles/PIM), `SecurityEvents.Read.All`/`SecurityAlert.Read.All` (secure score/alerts), `Organization.Read.All`, `Domain.Read.All`, `Agreement.Read.All`, `DirectoryRecommendations.Read.All`. (research: entra-graph-api per-domain "App permission")
  - Intune: `DeviceManagementManagedDevices.Read.All`, `DeviceManagementConfiguration.Read.All`, `DeviceManagementApps.Read.All`, `DeviceManagementServiceConfig.Read.All`. (research: intune-graph-api §0)
- **Two least-privilege traps to flag (do NOT request these for a read-only exporter):** `DeviceManagementManagedDevices.PrivilegedOperations.All` (remote wipe/retire — huge blast radius, not needed); and the **Reports export API needs a ReadWrite scope just to CREATE an export job** even though we only read the result — that one ReadWrite scope (`DeviceManagementConfiguration.ReadWrite.All` or an Apps/ManagedDevices `.ReadWrite.All`) is unavoidable for M5 exports and must be reported as an expected exception, not silently over-requested. (research: intune-graph-api §0 "two least-privilege traps"; learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/device-management/reports/export-graph-apis)
- **The 403-confusion this prevents** is the documented m365-exporter failure mode: partial permissions -> some collectors 403 at runtime piecemeal. Preflight turns that into one clear pre-run report. (research: m365-exporter-lessons §4 lesson 5, §5 "build a permission-preflight check")
- **No third-party assertion library** — standard-library `testing`. Use a fake Graph client / injected granted-permission set for tests (don't hit a live tenant in CI).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A test that, given a granted-permission set and a set of enabled collectors with declared requirements, the checker reports the correct MISSING list and OK entries (table-driven).
- [ ] A test that the subcommand exits non-zero when a required permission is missing and zero when all are satisfied.
- [ ] A test that the ReadWrite export-scope exception is reported as an expected note (not flagged as over-privilege) when M5 export collectors are enabled.
- [ ] A test that the missing-permission summary is de-duplicated across collectors sharing a scope (e.g. many collectors need `AuditLog.Read.All` -> reported once).
- [ ] `make check` green.

## Dependencies

- Depends on #2 (enabled-collector config), #3 (auth to enumerate granted perms), #4 (Graph client), #6 (collector registration + per-collector `RequiredPermissions`).
- Complements #9 (license-tier detection) — permissions and license are orthogonal gates; both must pass for a collector to run.

body:
## What & why

Graph gates whole data domains behind license tiers, and an unlicensed call fails in confusing ways (empty results, `hidden` fields, or errors) rather than a clean "not licensed". graph2otel must **detect each tenant's license tier and gracefully degrade** — skip collectors the tenant isn't licensed for, with a clear log line and a gauge, and never crash. Example: sign-in logs need Entra ID P1 (Free tenants get nothing via Graph); full risk detail needs P2; risky service principals need Workload Identities Premium; Intune collectors need an Intune license.

## Scope

- [ ] Add license-tier detection (in `internal/graphclient` or a new `internal/license` package). Per tenant, detect which of these apply: **Entra ID P1**, **Entra ID P2**, **Workload Identities Premium**, **Intune** (active Intune/EMS/M365-E3+ license present).
- [ ] Detection approach: read `/subscribedSkus` (already a planned collector) and map service-plan IDs to tiers, and/or probe a cheap representative endpoint per tier and classify the result. Prefer `subscribedSkus` mapping (deterministic, cheap, one call) over probing where possible; fall back to a capability probe for ambiguous cases.
- [ ] Expose per-tenant detected tier as a `graph2otel.*` gauge (e.g. `graph2otel.tenant.license_tier{tenant_id, tier}` = 1) so the tier is visible in telemetry.
- [ ] A registration-time (or startup) gate: each collector declares the minimum license tier it needs; collectors whose tier isn't present for a tenant are **skipped for that tenant** with a single clear log line (`slog.Warn "skipping collector X for tenant Y: requires <tier>"`) and are NOT registered/ticked. Never hard-fail the process.
- [ ] Handle the "fresh/small tenant returns `insufficientData` not an error" case for Intune analytics — treat as not-yet-available, not a failure.

## Design constraints

License gates (research: entra-graph-api §"Premium-license-gated" + per-domain License fields; intune-graph-api §0 Licensing; log-export-feasibility §6 Licensing):
- [ ] **No premium license (Free):** Entra `directoryAudits` and `provisioning` logs are readable (7-day retention only); `/subscribedSkus`, directory counts, apps/SP credential expiry all readable. **Free tenants get NO sign-in logs via Graph** — the sign-in interactive collector must be skipped on Free.
- [ ] **Entra ID P1:** required for ANY sign-in log access via Graph (interactive + beta sub-types), Conditional Access policies + named locations, Terms of Use, provisioning feature, auth-methods reports.
- [ ] **Entra ID P2:** required for full risk detections / risky users / risky sign-ins detail (P1 downgrades detections to `generic`) and 90-day risk retention.
- [ ] **Workload Identities Premium:** required for risky service principals / SP risk detections (a separate SKU from Entra P1/P2).
- [ ] **Intune license:** required for all `deviceManagement/*` collectors (M4/M5). Not Entra premium.
- [ ] **Degrade, never crash** — the explicit design directive: "detect license tier and degrade gracefully (skip sign-ins on Free, skip premium risk detail without P2) rather than hard-fail." (research: log-export-feasibility §6; m365-exporter-lessons §4 lesson 5 on partial-permission confusion)
- [ ] **Retention is not retroactive across upgrades** — a Free->P1 upgrade doesn't recover data older than the Free 7-day window (note for docs / backfill logic, not a blocker here).
- [ ] Emit the tier gauge under `graph2otel.*` with bounded attributes (`tenant_id`, `tier`). (CLAUDE.md namespaces + cardinality)
- [ ] **No third-party assertion library** — standard-library `testing`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A test mapping representative `subscribedSkus` service-plan sets to the correct detected tiers (table-driven: Free / P1 / P2 / Workload-ID-Premium / Intune / combinations).
- [ ] A test that a collector declaring `requires P2` is skipped (not registered) for a P1 tenant and registered for a P2 tenant, with the skip logged.
- [ ] A test that the sign-in collector is skipped on a Free tenant.
- [ ] A test that detection failure / `insufficientData` degrades gracefully (collector skipped or deferred, process does not crash).
- [ ] A test that `graph2otel.tenant.license_tier` gauge is emitted per tenant with the detected tier (in-memory recorder).
- [ ] `make check` green.

## Dependencies

- Depends on #3 (credential), #4 (Graph client to read `subscribedSkus`), #6 (collector registration gate), #8 (tier gauge via Emitter).
- Informs which M2–M5 collectors register per tenant (each declares its required tier).

body:
## What & why

Per-collector self-observability: the first thing an operator needs when a collector silently stops updating. Every collector gets a success/duration/staleness triad plus a process-wide build_info metric, all under the `graph2otel.*` namespace. Ported from tailscale2otel's per-collector self-obs and the m365-exporter "last-update / scrape-duration / scrape-success" triad (called out in the prior-art analysis as "cheap and the first thing you'll want").

## Scope

- [ ] Wire self-obs metrics into the Scheduler (#6), emitted through the Emitter (#8), per collector per tick:
  - [ ] `graph2otel.scrape.success` — 1/0 (or a counter of successes/failures) per collector per tenant, set each tick.
  - [ ] `graph2otel.scrape.duration` — histogram (or gauge) of how long the tick's `Collect`/`CollectWindow` took.
  - [ ] `graph2otel.scrape.staleness` — seconds since the collector last succeeded (so "Intune collector last succeeded 3 polls ago" is directly visible). Derived from a last-success timestamp.
- [ ] `graph2otel.build_info` — a gauge/info metric with value 1 and attributes `version` (from `main.version` via `internal/version`), Go version, and OTEL SDK versions if cheap. One series per process.
- [ ] Attributes on the per-collector metrics: `collector` (name) and `tenant_id` (bounded — number of tenants, not number of entities). No per-entity attributes.
- [ ] Optionally surface the 429/throttle self-obs signals coordinated with #5 (throttle counter per workload/tenant) under the same `graph2otel.*` namespace — align metric names so #5 and this issue don't collide.

## Design constraints

- **Namespace is frozen: `graph2otel.*`** for all self-obs (OTLP dot notation). Domain metrics are `entra.*`/`intune.*` — self-obs must not leak into those. (CLAUDE.md "Metric namespaces")
- **Port the triad near-verbatim:** tailscale2otel emits `scrape.success`/`scrape.duration`/`scrape.staleness` per collector (research: go-stack §3 "Error/partial-failure handling"); m365-exporter's equivalent triad is `m365_collector_scrape_success` / `_scrape_duration_seconds` / `_last_update_seconds_timestamp` (research: m365-exporter-lessons §1, §5 "Copy"). Staleness-since-last-success is the more directly useful form than a raw last-update timestamp — prefer emitting staleness (seconds since last success) computed at emit time.
- **`scrape.success` must reflect reality, not optimism:** the typed-Register compile-safety in #6 exists precisely so a collector can't silently report success while doing nothing. A tick that errors sets success=0 and does NOT advance the last-success timestamp (so staleness climbs). (research: go-stack §3 "typed Register")
- **Cold-start:** don't emit a misleading success/staleness before the first real tick (ties to the #6 cold-start "blip to zero" rule). (research: m365-exporter-lessons §4 lesson 2)
- **Bounded cardinality:** `collector` and `tenant_id` only. Never per-device/per-user. (CLAUDE.md cardinality rule)
- **No third-party assertion library** — standard-library `testing`; assert against the `telemetrytest.Recorder` (#8).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A test that a successful collector tick sets `graph2otel.scrape.success` = 1 and records a `scrape.duration` sample with the `collector`+`tenant_id` attributes (assert via the in-memory recorder).
- [ ] A test that a failing tick sets `scrape.success` = 0 and does NOT reset the last-success timestamp, so `scrape.staleness` increases on the following tick.
- [ ] A test that `graph2otel.build_info` is emitted exactly once with value 1 and carries the `version` attribute wired from `internal/version`.
- [ ] A test asserting the self-obs metrics carry only bounded attributes (no per-entity labels) — e.g. assert the attribute key set.
- [ ] `make check` green.

## Dependencies

- Depends on #6 (Scheduler hooks) and #8 (Emitter + `telemetrytest.Recorder` + `graph2otel.*` namespace).
- Coordinates throttle self-obs metric names with #5.
- Consumed by: admin/health endpoint (#12, which surfaces per-collector status), and the M6 self-obs dashboard.

body:
## What & why

The telemetry provider + `Emitter` facade: the single package that owns OTLP metrics + logs export, so exporter/SDK details never leak into collectors. Collectors call `Emitter.Counter/Gauge/UpDownCounter/...` (and a log emitter) and are unit-testable against an in-memory recorder — they never touch OTLP or SDK types directly. Ported from tailscale2otel's `internal/telemetry/`, which is the only fleet sibling shipping OTEL logs in production. This is the seam the entire collector framework (#6) emits through.

## Scope

- [ ] Add `internal/telemetry` (new package). Port from `/Users/rob/repos/tailscale2otel/internal/telemetry/` (`provider.go`, `emitter.go`) — adapt attribute namespaces to graph2otel.
- [ ] `Provider` wrapping `*sdkmetric.MeterProvider` + `*sdklog.LoggerProvider` (+ optional `*sdktrace.TracerProvider`) behind one struct, exposing a single `Emitter` facade.
- [ ] Protocol selection via a single `Options.Protocol` string resolved once in `provider.go`: `grpc` -> `otlpmetricgrpc`/`otlploggrpc`; `http` -> `otlpmetrichttp`/`otlploghttp`; `stdout` -> `stdoutmetric`/`stdoutlog`. (matches config #2 `otlp.protocol`)
- [ ] Grafana Cloud first-class target: build the Basic-auth header from `otlp.grafana_cloud.{instance_id,token}` automatically.
- [ ] `Emitter` methods for synchronous instruments (Counter/Gauge/UpDownCounter/Histogram) and a log-record emitter, all recorded at poll time.
- [ ] Cardinality limit wired via `sdkmetric.WithCardinalityLimit`, tied to a self-obs `series.active` tracker (coordinate with #9).
- [ ] Add `internal/telemetrytest` with an in-memory `Recorder` (OTEL in-memory metric reader + log exporter) that collectors assert against directly. This is the standard collector-test primitive for all of M2–M5.

## Design constraints

- **The `/v1/metrics` + `/v1/logs` URL-path gotcha (do NOT lose this):** the otlphttp exporter does **not** append `/v1/{metrics,logs}` to the endpoint itself. A bare Grafana Cloud gateway URL silently 404s. Port tailscale2otel's `otlpHTTPURL()` helper that appends the correct path per signal. Add a test. (research: go-stack §3 "OTLP exporter wiring"; CLAUDE.md "OTLP URL-path")
- **OTEL version lockstep — FROZEN PAIR:** `go.opentelemetry.io/otel` core = **v1.44.0** (matches the whole fleet), `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/log` = **v0.20.0**. The log SDK is genuinely pre-1.0 (verified via the Go module proxy — latest v0.20.0) with no minor-version compatibility guarantee; the accepted mitigation is pinning + lockstep bumping (Renovate batches them). Never bump one without the other. (research: go-stack §2 "Logs" + §3; CLAUDE.md "OpenTelemetry dependency lockstep")
- **Cumulative temporality (SDK default) — do NOT switch to delta.** Grafana Cloud metrics = Mimir (Prometheus data model, fundamentally cumulative); graph2otel controls its own instrumentation so there's no delta source to convert. Matches every fleet sibling. (research: go-stack §2 "Delta vs cumulative")
- **Synchronous instruments recorded at poll time** (not async/observable gauges). (research: go-stack §2 "Metrics")
- **Exemplar-reservoir engineering (port the pattern):** give synchronous Counter/Gauge/UpDownCounter a no-op exemplar reservoir view (avoids a per-series `FixedSizeReservoir` allocation that can never be populated when recorded with `context.Background()`); keep the default reservoir only on the one histogram recorded with a real span context. Real cost control for graph2otel's many per-device/per-policy attribute sets. (research: go-stack §3)
- **Metric namespaces (frozen):** self-obs = `graph2otel.*`; exported domain metrics = `entra.*` / `intune.*` (OTLP dot notation). Custom attribute keys go in a small dedicated `internal/semconv`-style constants set (port tailscale2otel's `internal/semconv/attrs.go` pattern), NOT ad-hoc string literals. (research: go-stack §2 "Resource attributes"; CLAUDE.md "Metric namespaces")
- **Cardinality/PII boundary (CLAUDE.md, SECURITY.md):** high-cardinality per-entity data (UPN, device id, IP, correlation id) is a LOG attribute, never a metric label. Metrics carry bounded tenant-shaped aggregates. The Emitter API should make the metric path naturally bounded.
- **No third-party assertion library** — standard-library `testing`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A test asserting `otlpHTTPURL()` appends `/v1/metrics` and `/v1/logs` correctly to a bare gateway URL and does not double-append when a path is already present.
- [ ] A test that each `Options.Protocol` value (`grpc`/`http`/`stdout`) resolves to the correct exporter type without error.
- [ ] A test that the Grafana Cloud Basic-auth header is built correctly from `instance_id` + `token`.
- [ ] A test using the `telemetrytest.Recorder` that an emitted Counter/Gauge shows up with the expected name/attributes/value (this validates the recorder itself, which all later collector tests rely on).
- [ ] A test that an emitted log record is captured by the in-memory log exporter with the expected body/attributes.
- [ ] A test that the cardinality limit is applied (series beyond the limit are dropped/aggregated per SDK behaviour) and the `series.active` tracker reflects it.
- [ ] `make check` green.

## Dependencies

- Depends on #2 (`otlp.*` config).
- Tight seam with #6 (collectors emit through the Emitter) and #9 (self-obs metrics live in the `graph2otel.*` namespace defined here).
- Consumed by: everything that emits telemetry — #6, #9, #10, #13, and all M2–M5 collectors.

body:
## What & why

Every log-shaped Graph endpoint (`signIns`, `directoryAudits`, `provisioning`, `riskDetections`, `riskyUsers`, Intune `auditEvents`) has **no delta query** — there is no server-side cursor, so graph2otel owns the watermark. Events can also arrive **out of order** (an event with an older timestamp appearing after you advanced past it), so a naive high-water mark silently drops data. The CheckpointStore persists, per tenant + endpoint, the watermark plus an overlap window and a bounded seen-ids set, so a restart resumes from `watermark - overlap` and dedupes by immutable `id`. This is the durable state the log pipeline engine (#13) and every `WindowCollector` depend on.

## Scope

- [ ] Add `internal/checkpoint` (new package). File-based store rooted at the `CheckpointDir` config field (#2).
- [ ] Model per (tenant, endpoint): `type Checkpoint struct { Endpoint string; TenantID string; Watermark time.Time; OverlapWindow time.Duration; SeenIDs <bounded set> }`. Namespacing: one file (or one keyed entry) per `(tenantID, endpoint)` — tenant + endpoint form the namespace key.
- [ ] `Load(tenantID, endpoint) (*Checkpoint, error)` (returns a zero/initial checkpoint if none exists) and `Save(*Checkpoint) error` (atomic write: temp file + rename).
- [ ] Bound the `SeenIDs` set to cover the overlap window (evict ids older than the overlap horizon) so it cannot grow unboundedly on a busy tenant.
- [ ] Concurrency-safe: multiple `WindowCollector`s (different endpoints) run on their own goroutines; guard per-key access.
- [ ] JSON on-disk format (human-inspectable), versioned with a schema field for forward compatibility.

## Design constraints

- **Model exactly as the feasibility study specifies:** `{ endpoint, watermark (last fully-processed event timestamp minus a safety lag), overlap_window, seen_ids (bounded set covering the overlap window for dedupe) }`, persisted per tenant per endpoint; on restart resume from `watermark - overlap`. (research: log-export-feasibility §7 "Reliability semantics" + "Recommended polling architecture")
- **Safety lag ~10–15 min; overlap re-query window 2–6h.** Be generous on overlap — out-of-order ingestion is real and a 2–6h overlap with id-dedupe is cheap insurance vs chasing a tight watermark. These are defaults the checkpoint carries; the actual query construction lives in #13. (research: log-export-feasibility §5 "Ordering / late arrival", §"Recommended polling architecture")
- **Dedupe by the immutable `id` (GUID) per endpoint** — duplicate risk comes from the overlap window; the seen-ids set is what makes the overlap idempotent. (research: log-export-feasibility §5 "Duplicate risk")
- **No delta query exists for any of these endpoints** — confirmed by absence of any delta method on the resource docs; there is no server cursor to fall back on. (research: entra-graph-api §0 "No delta for logs"; log-export-feasibility §5)
- **Multi-tenant namespacing mirrors tailscale2otel's CheckpointStore** (which namespaces per-tailnet for its multi-tailnet support) — port that pattern. (research: go-stack §3 "CheckpointStore")
- **Atomic writes** (temp + rename) so a crash mid-write never corrupts a checkpoint. File-based (no DB) matches the single-instance, no-HA v1 decision.
- **No third-party assertion library** — standard-library `testing`; use `t.TempDir()` for the store root.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A test that `Save` then `Load` round-trips a checkpoint (watermark, overlap, seen-ids) for a `(tenant, endpoint)` key.
- [ ] A test that `Load` on a missing key returns a usable zero/initial checkpoint (not an error) so cold start works.
- [ ] A test that two different endpoints for the same tenant, and the same endpoint for two tenants, are stored independently (namespacing).
- [ ] A test that the seen-ids set evicts ids older than the overlap horizon (bounded growth).
- [ ] A test that a simulated crash mid-write (write temp, don't rename) leaves the previous good checkpoint intact (atomicity).
- [ ] A test of concurrent `Save`/`Load` across keys with `-race` clean.
- [ ] `make check` green.

## Dependencies

- Depends on #2 (`CheckpointDir` config field).
- Consumed by: log pipeline engine (#13) and every `WindowCollector` (M3 Entra logs, M5 Intune logs).

comments.body: Done in 6adfce2. File-based CheckpointStore: `Checkpoint{Schema,TenantID,Endpoint,Watermark,OverlapWindow,SeenIDs}` persisted one JSON file per (tenant,endpoint); atomic temp+rename writes; bounded `SeenIDs` id→eventTime set with horizon eviction; cold-start returns a zero checkpoint (not an error); collision-safe sanitized+sha256 filenames; per-key mutex map (-race clean). Std-lib only, 8 tests green, lint clean.

body:
## What & why

The core collector framework: the interfaces, registry, and scheduler that every Entra/Intune collector (M2–M5) plugs into. Ported near-verbatim from tailscale2otel, which solves exactly this shape (poll a vendor API on independent intervals, isolate failures, self-observe per collector). Two typed collector kinds map cleanly onto graph2otel: **`SnapshotCollector`** (fetch current state each tick -> OTEL metric gauges/counters — directory counts, device compliance, license SKUs) and **`WindowCollector`** (fetch a `[from,to]` time window each tick, return a high-water mark for checkpointing -> OTEL logs — sign-ins, audits, risk detections).

## Scope

- [ ] Add `internal/collector` (new package). Port from `/Users/rob/repos/tailscale2otel/internal/collector/` (adapt names/attrs for graph2otel; do not copy verbatim).
- [ ] `Collector` base interface: `Name() string`, `DefaultInterval() time.Duration`. (donor: tailscale2otel `internal/collector/collector.go`)
- [ ] `SnapshotCollector` extends `Collector` with `Collect(ctx) error` (fetch current state, emit metrics via the Emitter facade from #8).
- [ ] `WindowCollector` extends `Collector` with `CollectWindow(ctx, from, to) (highWater time.Time, err error)` (fetch a time window, emit logs, return the new watermark for #7 to persist).
- [ ] `Registry` holding `Entry{ Collector; Interval; InitialLookback; MaxWindow }`. **`Register` takes the TYPED `SnapshotCollector`/`WindowCollector` interface, not the base `Collector`** — so a collector that fails to implement `Collect`/`CollectWindow` is a COMPILE ERROR, not a silent no-op that still reports `scrape.success=1`. This is a deliberate, worth-preserving design decision. (donor: tailscale2otel `internal/collector/collector.go:60-68`)
- [ ] `Scheduler`: one goroutine + ticker PER registered collector. Per-collector failure isolation (one collector erroring never stops the others). Random startup **stagger** delay (`WithStaggerWindow`, default ~3s) so collectors don't hit Graph in lockstep, then each runs at its own configured interval. (donor: tailscale2otel `internal/collector/scheduler.go`, esp. lines ~24-27, ~110-140)
- [ ] Recover panics inside a collector tick so a panicking collector restarts on its next tick rather than crashing the process.
- [ ] Resolve each collector's enabled/interval from config (#2) at registration: disabled collectors are never registered / never get a worker.
- [ ] Optional root span per scrape cycle via a `WithTracer` option (matches tailscale2otel).

## Design constraints

- **Goroutine-per-collector, independent tickers — NOT a single central loop.** Deliberately chosen so one slow/failing Graph collector (e.g. a large Intune device page walk taking tens of seconds) cannot delay or block a fast one (a small settings/policy read). (research: go-stack §3 "Scheduling model"; m365-exporter-lessons §1 confirms the same background-poller-per-domain shape)
- **Typed Register = compile-time safety** — do not weaken `Register` to accept the base `Collector` interface. (research: go-stack §3 bullet on `internal/collector/collector.go:60-68`)
- **Synchronous instruments recorded at poll time** (not async/observable gauges): the poll and the emission happen in the same tick, so there is no fast-tick/slow-poll mismatch to decouple, and synchronous recording is far easier to unit-test against an in-memory recorder. (research: go-stack §2 "Metrics")
- **Cold-start "blip to zero" trap:** do NOT emit a domain's metrics with zero/absent values before its first successful poll. Suppress emission (or mark a distinct "not yet initialized" state) until each collector's first success. (research: m365-exporter-lessons §4 lesson 2)
- **Per-collector self-obs is a separate issue (#9)** but the Scheduler must expose the hooks it needs (per-tick success/duration/timestamp). Design the Scheduler so #9 can attach without re-plumbing.
- **The Emitter facade (#8) is the ONLY thing collectors touch for telemetry** — collectors must never import OTLP/SDK types directly. This is what makes them unit-testable against the in-memory recorder. Freeze the collector<->Emitter seam accordingly.
- **No third-party assertion library** — standard-library `testing`. Port tailscale2otel's test style (in-memory recorder assertions).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A test that registering a type implementing only `Collect` as a `SnapshotCollector` compiles, and (documented, not a runtime test) that a type missing `Collect` fails to compile when passed to `Register` — capture this as a compile-time-safety note + a `// +build`-style example or a doc comment, since you cannot assert a compile error in a normal test.
- [ ] A test that the Scheduler runs each registered collector on its own interval (use short intervals + a fake clock or real short sleeps) and that a collector returning an error does NOT stop the others from ticking.
- [ ] A test that a panic inside a collector tick is recovered and the collector ticks again next interval (process survives).
- [ ] A test that the stagger delay is applied within the configured window (collectors don't all fire at t=0).
- [ ] A test that a config-disabled collector is never ticked.
- [ ] A test asserting a `SnapshotCollector` emits the expected metric to an in-memory recorder and a `WindowCollector` returns an advanced high-water mark.
- [ ] `make check` green.

## Dependencies

- Depends on #2 (per-collector enable/interval config).
- Tight seam with #8 (Emitter facade — collectors emit through it) and #9 (self-obs hooks). CheckpointStore (#7) persists `WindowCollector` watermarks.
- Consumed by: license-tier detection (#10), permission preflight (#11), admin endpoint (#12), log pipeline engine (#13), and every M2–M5 collector.

body:
## What & why

Microsoft Graph throttles **per app per tenant, per workload** — and the two workloads graph2otel leans on hardest (reporting and Identity Protection) **do not send `Retry-After` on 429**, so the SDK's default retry handler (#4) cannot back off correctly for them. Intune has its own tighter ceilings again, and the Intune reports-export API is tighter still. This issue adds per-workload client-side rate limiters that gate requests BEFORE they hit Graph, plus our own exponential backoff for the no-`Retry-After` workloads, and surfaces the `x-ms-throttle-*` headers in logs / self-obs so operators can see throttle pressure. Without these limiters, a single collector on a short interval trips 429s fast and silently drops data.

## Scope

- [ ] Add rate limiting to `internal/graphclient` (or a sub-package) as middleware layered on the transport from #4. One limiter per workload per tenant. Use `golang.org/x/time/rate` token buckets (or equivalent) keyed by `(tenantID, workload)`.
- [ ] Implement these workload buckets with the verified numbers below.
- [ ] Implement **own exponential backoff with jitter** on 429 for the reporting + IPC + Intune workloads (they do not send `Retry-After`). Honor `Retry-After` only when actually present (directory workload does send it).
- [ ] Classify each request into a workload (by request path / builder) so the right limiter applies. Provide a mapping helper.
- [ ] Surface throttle telemetry: log `x-ms-throttle-limit-percentage` (approaching-limit signal) at debug/info, and on 429 log `x-ms-throttle-scope` + `x-ms-throttle-information`. Emit a self-obs signal (counter of 429s per workload/tenant; gauge of last-seen throttle percentage) — coordinate the metric names with #9.

## Design constraints

Verified throttle numbers (research: entra-graph-api §0, intune-graph-api §0, log-export-feasibility §5; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/throttling-limits):

- [ ] **Reporting workload** (`signIns`, `directoryAudits`, `provisioningObjectSummary`, `applicationSignInSummary`, `auditLogRoot`, credential-usage summaries): **5 requests / 10s per app per tenant** (and 122/10s per app across all tenants). **NO `Retry-After` on 429** — own backoff. `GET signInActivity` has its own 10/min limit.
- [ ] **Identity Protection + Conditional Access workload** (`riskDetection`, `riskyUser`, `riskyServicePrincipal`, `conditionalAccessPolicy`, `namedLocation`): **1 request / second per tenant ACROSS ALL APPS** — a very low ceiling. **NO `Retry-After`.** Serialize these calls (bucket of effectively 1 concurrent, 1/s refill).
- [ ] **Directory-objects workload** (users, groups, servicePrincipals, applications, devices, roles): token-bucket on ResourceUnits — S(<50 users) 3,500 / M(50–500) 5,000 / L(>500) 8,000 RU per 10s per app+tenant; 150,000 RU / 20s per app across all tenants. Reads are cheap in RU. This workload **does** send `Retry-After` — the SDK retry handler (#4) largely covers it; a coarse RU-budget limiter is defensive.
- [ ] **Intune general service:** ~**1000 requests / 20s per app per tenant** (any method). The **Devices** service area is elevated: ~**2000 (per-app) / 4000 (per-tenant) reads per 20s**. `Retry-After` NOT guaranteed — own backoff.
- [ ] **Intune reports-export API:** its OWN much tighter throttle — **48 / minute per app** (application auth = graph2otel's ceiling; also 100/tenant/min, 8/user/min). A single export that polls ~10x before completing burns ~11 of the 48/min budget — schedule exports carefully; the per-`PolicyId` update reports fan out. (used by the export-job subsystem in M5)
- [ ] **Buckets are per app PER TENANT** (except IPC which is per tenant across all apps, and the cross-tenant 122/10s / 150k-RU ceilings). Sharding across multiple app registrations gives each app its own reporting bucket — note as a future scale lever, not v1 scope.
- [ ] Backoff must be **exponential with jitter** and must NOT depend on `Retry-After` for reporting/IPC/Intune. (research: log-export-feasibility §5 "recommended polling architecture")
- [ ] **No third-party assertion library** — standard-library `testing`. `golang.org/x/time/rate` is acceptable (std-adjacent, in the fleet).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A test that the reporting limiter admits at most 5 requests per rolling 10s window for a given tenant (use a controllable clock / `rate.Limiter` with injected time, or assert bucket capacity/refill).
- [ ] A test that the IPC limiter serializes to ~1 req/s per tenant and that two apps against the same tenant share the ceiling (per-tenant, not per-app, key).
- [ ] A test that a 429 with NO `Retry-After` triggers our exponential backoff (assert increasing sleep intervals via injected clock), and a test that a 429 WITH `Retry-After` honors the header value.
- [ ] A test that `x-ms-throttle-*` headers on a response produce the expected log fields / self-obs counter increment (assert against an in-memory recorder).
- [ ] A test that requests are classified into the correct workload bucket (table-driven over representative paths: `/auditLogs/signIns` -> reporting, `/identityProtection/riskyUsers` -> IPC, `/deviceManagement/managedDevices` -> Intune-devices, `/deviceManagement/reports/exportJobs` -> export).
- [ ] `make check` green.

## Dependencies

- Depends on #3 (per-tenant credential) and #4 (transport + default retry to layer onto).
- Coordinates self-obs metric names with #8/#9.
- Consumed by: log pipeline engine (#13), all collectors, and the M5 export-job subsystem (export limiter).

body:
## What & why

Build the Graph client factory: an adapter around the official `msgraph-sdk-go` v1.0 SDK that runs Graph calls through **our own OTEL-instrumented HTTP transport** while explicitly re-attaching Kiota's default middleware chain — critically the retry handler.

**This exists to fix a latent bug found in the closest prior art.** cloudeteer/m365-exporter passes its own instrumented `*http.Client` into the Graph SDK adapter. Verified against `kiota-http-go` / `msgraph-sdk-go-core` source: the adapter constructors only install the SDK's default middleware (`RetryHandler`, `RedirectHandler`, `CompressionHandler`, `ParametersNameDecodingHandler`, `UserAgentHandler`, `HeadersInspectionHandler`) **when the passed `httpClient` is `nil`**. Passing any non-nil client silently drops the entire default chain — including the 429/503 + `Retry-After` retry handler — and m365-exporter has no compensating retry logic anywhere (confirmed: zero grep hits for 429/Retry-After/throttle/backoff). Since OTEL instrumentation is the whole point of graph2otel, we WILL pass a custom transport, so we MUST re-attach the default middlewares ourselves or we ship the same silent-no-retry bug. (research: m365-exporter-lessons §2 "Throttling / 429 handling" + §4 lesson 1)

## Scope

- [ ] Add `internal/graphclient` (new package). Add the SDK deps: `github.com/microsoftgraph/msgraph-sdk-go`, `github.com/microsoftgraph/msgraph-sdk-go-core`, `github.com/microsoft/kiota-abstractions-go`, `github.com/microsoft/kiota-http-go` (transitively). (Scaffold intentionally had zero Graph deps; they land here.)
- [ ] Build the middleware chain explicitly: start from `nethttplibrary.GetDefaultMiddlewares()` (kiota-http-go), and add our OTEL HTTP instrumentation middleware into the chain (as a `Middleware` or by wrapping the base `http.RoundTripper` underneath the Kiota middleware pipeline). Construct the `*http.Client` via `nethttplibrary.NewNetHttpRequestAdapter`-compatible client builder so the default middlewares are present.
- [ ] Wire a per-tenant `*msgraphsdk.GraphServiceClient` from the `TenantAuth` credential (#3): `authentication.NewAzureIdentityAuthenticationProviderWithScopesAndValidHosts(cred, []string{GraphDefaultScope}, []string{"graph.microsoft.com"})` -> request adapter built with our custom client -> `GraphServiceClient`.
- [ ] Provide a factory: `NewClient(ctx, tenantAuth) (*Client, error)` returning a struct wrapping the `GraphServiceClient` plus the shared instrumented transport. One client per tenant.
- [ ] Provide a raw-REST escape hatch on the same instrumented+retrying transport for beta endpoints not worth pulling `msgraph-beta-sdk-go` for (mirrors m365-exporter's DEP-onboarding hand-roll) — a helper that does `GET`/`POST` with the same auth + retry, returning the raw body for hand-decoded structs. Beta coverage decision is per-endpoint; do not add the beta SDK module in this issue.
- [ ] Expose the `PageIterator[T]` usage as the standard pagination pattern (helper or documented convention) since collectors will all need it.

## Design constraints

- **The re-attach is the whole point** — do not pass a bare custom client. Use `nethttplibrary.GetDefaultMiddlewares()` and thread OTEL instrumentation into that chain, OR implement equivalent 429/503 + `Retry-After`-aware retry ourselves. The former is strongly preferred (less to get wrong). (research: m365-exporter-lessons §4 lesson 1; Kiota default middleware list verified there)
- **The SDK default retry handler honors `Retry-After` when present** — but the reporting and Identity-Protection Graph workloads do NOT send `Retry-After` (see #5). So this handler covers the directory workload's throttling but is NOT sufficient for reporting/IPC — those need the client-side rate limiters in #5. This issue delivers the transport + default-retry; #5 layers the per-workload limiters on top.
- **`$select` on every list/get call** is throttling hygiene worth building into the convention — fewer bytes, faster, less likely to trip response-size throttling. (research: m365-exporter-lessons §5 "Copy")
- **`ConsistencyLevel: eventual` + `$count=true` gotcha:** advanced queries (`$count`, `$search`, `$filter` with `ne`/`not`/`endsWith`/`any` on multi-valued props, `$orderby`+`$filter`) require BOTH the header and `$count=true` or they silently 400. Surface a helper/convention so collectors don't miss it. (research: entra-graph-api §0 "Advanced query"; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/aad-advanced-queries)
- **SDK compile-time cost is real and known** (msgraph-sdk-go issues #753/#129: golangci-lint 36s->7m13s, tests 7s->8m50s in CI on some setups). Accept it for v1 (matches m365-exporter's production choice); revisit scoped Kiota generation only if CI time becomes a measured blocker. (research: go-stack §1)
- **Unwrap OData errors:** raw Graph errors are opaque `*odataerrors.ODataError`; provide a helper that unwraps to the actual OData error code/message for logging (mirrors m365-exporter's `util.GetOdataError`).
- **No third-party assertion library** — standard-library `testing`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **A test that asserts a 429 response is retried with backoff.** Stand up an `httptest.Server` that returns `429` on the first call (optionally with and without `Retry-After`) then `200`, point the factory's transport at it, issue a request, and assert the request ultimately succeeds and the server saw >1 attempt. This is the regression guard for the m365-exporter latent bug — without the middleware re-attach this test MUST fail.
- [ ] A test asserting the constructed client's middleware chain includes a retry handler (assert `GetDefaultMiddlewares()` members are present, or behaviourally via the 429 test above).
- [ ] A test asserting OTEL HTTP instrumentation is present in the chain (e.g. a span/metric is recorded for an outbound request against an in-memory recorder / test server).
- [ ] A test that the OData-error unwrap helper turns a synthesized `ODataError` into a loggable code+message string.
- [ ] `make check` green (note: first build pulls the large SDK — expect slower CI).

## Dependencies

- Depends on #3 (consumes `TenantAuth` credential + `GraphDefaultScope`).
- Consumed by: rate limiters (#5, which wrap this transport), license-tier detection (#10), permission preflight (#11), log pipeline engine (#13), and every metrics/logs collector in M2–M5.

body:
## What & why

graph2otel authenticates to Microsoft Graph with **app-only client-credentials** (no signed-in user), potentially against several tenants in one process. This issue wires per-tenant credential resolution via `azidentity.DefaultAzureCredential` and the Graph token scope, producing a credential per configured tenant that the Graph client factory (#4) consumes. Getting this right up front avoids leaking secret handling into every collector.

## Scope

- [ ] Add `internal/auth` (new package). For each `TenantConfig` from #2, construct an `azidentity.DefaultAzureCredential` (via `azidentity.DefaultAzureCredentialOptions{TenantID: t.TenantID}`; set the client ID through the credential chain's env, do not invent a config secret).
- [ ] Expose a per-tenant credential holder, e.g. `type TenantAuth struct { TenantID string; Cred azcore.TokenCredential }`, and a constructor `NewTenantAuth(cfg config.TenantConfig) (*TenantAuth, error)` plus a helper that builds all of them from `[]config.TenantConfig`.
- [ ] Pin the Graph scope constant: `const GraphDefaultScope = "https://graph.microsoft.com/.default"`. This is the only scope app-only Graph needs; `.default` means "all admin-consented app permissions".
- [ ] A cheap credential smoke path used by the preflight command (#11): a method that requests a token for `GraphDefaultScope` and surfaces a clear error (tenant unreachable / bad client / consent missing) rather than deferring failure to the first collector call.
- [ ] Document (in package doc + README auth section) the `DefaultAzureCredential` env recipes: secret (`AZURE_TENANT_ID`/`AZURE_CLIENT_ID`/`AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET`), cert (`AZURE_CLIENT_CERTIFICATE_PATH`), workload identity, managed identity.

## Design constraints

- **App-only client credentials only.** Base auth endpoint `https://login.microsoftonline.com/{tenant}/oauth2/v2.0/token`, scope `https://graph.microsoft.com/.default`. All Graph permissions are **application** permissions granted with admin consent. (research: entra-graph-api §0 Auth; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/auth-v2-service)
- **`DefaultAzureCredential` is the sole mechanism** — do not construct `NewClientSecretCredential`/`NewClientCertificateCredential` explicitly. This matches cloudeteer/m365-exporter (`pkg/auth/auth.go`, ~40 lines) and lets the same binary run as a container with env-var secrets or as an Azure workload with managed identity, with zero exporter-specific auth config. (research: m365-exporter-lessons §2 "Authentication")
- **Per-tenant TenantID pinning:** `DefaultAzureCredential` must be scoped to each tenant's GUID via `DefaultAzureCredentialOptions.TenantID`; a single shared app registration across tenants leaves `ClientID` unset in YAML and relies on `AZURE_CLIENT_ID`.
- **SDK versions** (from research go-stack §1 / m365-exporter go.mod, pin to fleet-current at implementation): `github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-go/sdk/azidentity` (~v1.13.x), `.../azcore` (~v1.21.x). Do NOT pull `msgraph-sdk-go` in this package — auth is SDK-agnostic; the Graph SDK dependency lands in #4.
- **Two manual setup steps are a known 403 trap** (document, and let #11 detect): (a) an admin must explicitly *consent* to the app permissions after adding them; (b) some surfaces gate on a directory role too. A partially-permissioned SP fails per-collector at runtime, not at startup — the preflight command (#11) exists to catch this. (research: m365-exporter-lessons §4 lesson 5)
- **No third-party assertion library** — standard-library `testing`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A test that `NewTenantAuth` builds a credential for a valid `TenantConfig` and returns a non-nil `azcore.TokenCredential`.
- [ ] A test that the scope constant equals `https://graph.microsoft.com/.default` (guard against accidental edit).
- [ ] A test that building auth for multiple tenants yields one `TenantAuth` per tenant, each carrying the correct `TenantID`.
- [ ] A test that the token-smoke method wraps an underlying credential error into a clear, tenant-identified error message (use a fake `TokenCredential` returning an error).
- [ ] `make check` green.

## Dependencies

- Depends on #2 (consumes `config.TenantConfig`).
- Consumed by: Graph client factory (#4), permission preflight (#11), license-tier detection (#10).

body:
## What & why

The committed scaffold ships a minimal `internal/config` (koanf layered load: defaults < YAML < `G2O_` env) with a `Config` holding `LogLevel`, `Tenants []TenantConfig` (`TenantID`, `ClientID`), and `OTLP` (protocol/endpoint/grafana_cloud). That is enough to boot but not enough to drive the collector framework: there is no per-collector enable/disable, no per-collector interval override, no per-tenant collector scoping, and no `admin` block. This issue expands the config surface to the full shape every M1 framework piece depends on, keeping the layered-load and secrets-out-of-YAML invariants intact.

Auth material (client secret/cert) is NEVER read through this package — tenants authenticate via `azidentity.DefaultAzureCredential` from its own env vars. `TenantConfig` carries only non-secret identifiers. See #3.

## Scope

- [ ] Add a `Collectors` config block: per-collector `enabled bool` (default true) and optional `interval time.Duration` override, keyed by collector name. Model as `map[string]CollectorConfig{ Enabled *bool; Interval time.Duration }` so "unset" is distinguishable from "false"/"zero" (a nil `Enabled` means "use the default", not "disabled").
- [ ] Add an `Admin` config block: `Enabled bool`, `Addr string` (default `:9090` or similar), consumed by the admin/health endpoint (#12).
- [ ] Add optional per-tenant collector overrides on `TenantConfig` (a tenant may disable a collector the global config enables, or tune its interval) — same `map[string]CollectorConfig` shape, merged over the global collector config at resolution time. Provide a resolver method (e.g. `(c *Config) CollectorSettings(tenantID, collectorName string) (enabled bool, interval time.Duration)`).
- [ ] Add a `CheckpointDir string` field (default e.g. `./checkpoints` or `/var/lib/graph2otel`) consumed by the CheckpointStore (#7).
- [ ] Extend `Validate()`: reject unknown collector names? (No — collectors self-register at runtime and config is loaded before registration; instead validate interval bounds: reject negative/absurdly-small intervals, e.g. `< 1s`). Keep the existing tenant/protocol/log_level checks.
- [ ] Update `config.example.yaml` at repo root to document the new `collectors` and `admin` keys and the per-tenant override shape.
- [ ] Table-driven tests for every new behaviour (see acceptance).

## Design constraints

- **Frozen seams (from the plan's Global Constraints — do not change):** module path `github.com/rknightion/graph2otel`; env prefix `G2O_` with `__` as the nesting delimiter (single `_` preserved within a name), e.g. `otlp.endpoint` -> `G2O_OTLP__ENDPOINT`; top-level YAML keys `tenants`, `otlp`, `collectors`, `log_level`, `admin`.
- **Layered load, secrets out of YAML:** keep the existing koanf order (built-in `Default()` < optional YAML file < `G2O_*` env). Env overrides file. No auth secrets in this struct — `TenantConfig` is `TenantID` + `ClientID` only (secrets come from `DefaultAzureCredential` env vars, see #3).
- **Donor pattern:** model on tailscale2otel `internal/config/` (adapt, do not copy verbatim — env prefix is `G2O_` not `TS2OTEL_`). tailscale2otel already has per-collector interval/enable config and a `Validate()`/`Warnings()` split worth mirroring.
- **Nesting delimiter gotcha:** a collector named e.g. `sign_ins` inside `collectors` must remain addressable via env — confirm koanf's env transform (single `_` preserved, `__` = nesting) does not mangle map keys that themselves contain underscores. Document the resulting env var form in `config.example.yaml`.
- **No third-party assertion library** (house rule, CLAUDE.md): standard-library `testing` only.
- Standard-library `time.Duration` for intervals; koanf/mapstructure decodes duration strings ("5m", "30s") with `WeaklyTypedInput` already enabled — verify duration decode works and add a test.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A test asserting defaults load with an empty `collectors` map and all collectors resolving to enabled + their built-in default interval.
- [ ] A test asserting a YAML `collectors.<name>.enabled: false` disables exactly that collector and leaves others enabled.
- [ ] A test asserting a YAML `collectors.<name>.interval: "10m"` decodes to `10*time.Minute` via `CollectorSettings`.
- [ ] A test asserting a per-tenant override wins over the global collector config (tenant disables a globally-enabled collector; another tenant keeps it enabled).
- [ ] A test asserting `G2O_LOG_LEVEL` env overrides YAML (regression guard on the existing behaviour) and a test that a nested collector key is settable via `G2O_` env.
- [ ] A test asserting `Validate()` rejects a negative/sub-1s interval and still rejects a missing `tenant_id` and duplicate tenants.
- [ ] `config.example.yaml` parses cleanly through `Load()` in a test (round-trip guard so the documented example never drifts from the struct).
- [ ] `make check` green (vet + test + lint + govulncheck + build).

## Dependencies

- Extends the committed scaffold `internal/config/config.go`. No blocking issue dependency — this is the foundation the rest of M1 builds on. Consumed by: auth (#3), collector framework (#6), CheckpointStore (#7), telemetry provider (#8), admin endpoint (#12).

comments.body: Done in 0a88fb0. Config surface expanded to the full M1 shape (map-based `collectors` + per-tenant override maps + `CollectorSettings` resolver + `admin` + `checkpoint_dir`), duration-string decode wired, sub-1s interval validation added, example YAML documents it all with a round-trip guard test. Full `make check` green. This freezes the config seam every other M1 lane builds on.

body:
## What & why

graph2otel is a new exporter that pulls every useful piece of Entra ID and Intune data from the Microsoft Graph API and ships it to Grafana Cloud (or any OTLP endpoint) as OTEL **metrics and logs**. Target use cases: compliance monitoring, log monitoring, and ideally replacing the Entra/Intune → Log Analytics → Grafana Cloud export chain entirely.

This issue tracks the bootstrap session that takes the repo from empty to ready-for-implementation.

## Decisions already made (don't re-litigate)

- **Language: Go** — matches tailscale2otel / genai-otel-bridge / opnsense-exporter house patterns; m365-exporter (inspiration project) is also Go.
- **Export surface: OTLP push only** (gRPC/HTTP) — no Prometheus scrape endpoint in v1.
- Repo hygiene follows the existing rknightion fleet: release-please, renovate, shared central GitHub Actions, docs hub sync.

## Plan

1. Research swarm (parallel agents): m365-exporter lessons; Entra Graph API surface; Intune Graph API surface; feasibility of replacing Log Analytics export via Graph; Go SDK/OTEL design options; CLAUDE.md + CI/actions porting survey.
2. Synthesize research into an architecture direction + v1 scope.
3. Scaffold the repo (Go module, CI, release-please, renovate, CLAUDE.md, docs skeleton, minimal compiling skeleton).
4. Create the full v1 backlog as GitHub issues with milestones/labels, plus a launch tracker issue that orchestrates them.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Research briefs completed for all six lanes
- [x] Feasibility verdict recorded for Graph-API-as-log-export-replacement (incl. limitations)
- [x] Repo scaffold committed: Go module skeleton that builds, CI wired to shared central actions, release-please + renovate, CLAUDE.md, README, docs skeleton
- [x] Full v1 backlog filed as issues with milestones/labels
- [x] Launch tracker issue created linking all backlog issues with phase plan

comments.body:
Research phase complete — all six lanes reported (briefs in gitignored scratch `docs/superpowers/research/`). Key outcomes:

- **Feasibility verdict**: Graph polling fully replaces diagnostic settings for the identity/device audit core (Entra audit, sign-ins, provisioning, risk; Intune audit). Structurally impossible via Graph: MicrosoftGraphActivityLogs, EnrichedOffice365AuditLogs, Intune OperationalLogs, Intune DeviceComplianceOrg (diagnostic-settings-only). Scope claims accordingly.
- **Stack locked**: Go 1.26, msgraph-sdk-go (+azidentity DefaultAzureCredential), OTEL v1.44.0 + logs SDK v0.20.0 lockstep, OTLP push only, koanf config, tailscale2otel collector architecture (SnapshotCollector/WindowCollector + checkpointed watermarks), cumulative temporality.
- **Decisions from Rob**: multi-tenant from day one; Helm chart in v1 backlog; start at 0.1.0; CI extras: notify-new-issue only for now.
- **Critical implementation constraints found**: Graph reporting + Identity Protection workloads send NO Retry-After on 429 (self-backoff required); IPC/CA limit is 1 req/s per tenant across all apps; sign-ins need 4 separate pollers (signInEventTypes can't combine user+SP types); custom http.Client into the Graph SDK silently drops the retry middleware (m365-exporter's latent bug — must re-attach Kiota default middlewares); Intune reports export API is the only source for much fleet detail and needs a ReadWrite scope just to create export jobs (48 req/min/app).

Now executing: scaffold lanes (Go skeleton, hygiene, .github) in parallel, then commit + secrets, then the full backlog + launch tracker.

Bootstrap complete. Scaffold landed in 7d182ad (CI green on shared reusables, release-please @0.1.0, secrets provisioned). Backlog: 74 issues across milestones M1–M6 (#2–#75), all self-contained with API/permission tables, telemetry models with cardinality strategy, throttle constraints, and test-inclusive acceptance criteria. Launch tracker: #79 — the single resumption point for the v1 effort. Closing.
